Coral Beauty Angelfish: A Hardy and Vibrant Reef Tank Favorite The Coral Beauty Angelfish (Centropyge bispinosus) is one of the most popular and beloved dwarf angelfish in the marine aquarium hobby. It’s no surprise, given its stunning coloration—a deep purple body that transitions to a rich reddish-orange, all accented by a brilliant, iridescent electric blue along its fins. Known for its exceptional hardiness and active personality, the Coral Beauty Angelfish is a fantastic choice for both beginner and experienced aquarists. It is generally considered reef-safe and an excellent addition to a community tank. Why the Coral Beauty Angelfish is a Great Choice: Striking Colors: The beautiful blend of purple, orange, and blue makes this fish a true centerpiece in any marine aquarium. Exceptional Hardiness: This species is known for its resilience and ability to adapt well to new environments. Generally Reef-Safe: It is an excellent angelfish for a reef tank, though like all angelfish, it should be monitored with soft corals and clam mantles. Active and Engaging: Its constant movement and foraging behavior add life and energy to your aquarium's rockwork. Quick Facts Scientific Name: Centropyge bispinosus Origin: Indo-Pacific Ocean Max Size: 4 inches Lifespan: 5 years or more Diet: A varied diet of high-quality angelfish pellets, flakes, and frozen foods such as mysis shrimp. Shipping Size: 1-2 inches

Bicolor Angelfish The Bicolor Angelfish (Centropyge bicolor) features a brilliant yellow front half that transitions sharply to a deep royal blue rear . A distinctive blue mask often covers its face, adding to its bold look. While a hardy and very popular aquarium fish, it is territorial so give the guy some rocks to call his own. This fish has been around the trade for a while, with the first live samples brought to Germany by the great naturalist Marcus Bloch in 1787. He then killed, dissected, and named the species. Why the Bicolor Angelfish is a Great Choice: Vibrant Colors: Its striking yellow and blue contrast creates a spectacular, high-impact focal point. Exceptional Hardiness: This species is known for its resilience and ability to adapt well to new environments. Active and Engaging: The Bicolor Angelfish is a constant swimmer, adding a sense of energy and life to your tank. A Bold Personality: Its more territorial nature can make it a captivating and engaging fish to observe. Important Note: The Bicolor Angelfish is not considered consistently reef-safe and may nip at soft corals or clam mantles. It should be kept with caution in a reef tank and is best housed as the only angelfish in the aquarium. Quick Facts Scientific Name: Centropyge bicolor Origin: Western Pacific Ocean Max Size: 6 inches Lifespan: 5 years or more Diet: A varied diet of high-quality angelfish pellets, flakes, and frozen foods. Shipping Size: 2-3 inches

Blueface Angelfish: A Majestic and Elegant Centerpiece The Blueface Angelfish (Pomacanthus xanthometopon) is a breathtakingly beautiful species, renowned for its majestic appearance and graceful swimming. While juveniles display a stunning pattern of concentric white and blue stripes on a dark body, the adult form is a true showstopper. It features a bright yellow body covered in a delicate blue net pattern, a brilliant yellow patch on its forehead, and a striking blue face accented with black lines. Its intelligence and commanding presence make the Blueface Angelfish a prized centerpiece for any large, well-established marine aquarium . Why the Blueface Angelfish is a Great Choice: Iconic Appearance: The vibrant colors and distinct blue-faced pattern make this angelfish instantly recognizable and highly sought-after. Fascinating Transformation: Watching its dramatic change from juvenile to adult colors is a rewarding experience for any aquarist. Graceful and Stately: Its elegant swimming and large size add a sense of majesty and calm to your display. Intelligent and Active: Its engaging personality and constant exploration add a lively dynamic to your tank. Important Note: The Blueface Angelfish is a large fish that requires a minimum tank size of 180 gallons due to its adult size and need for ample swimming room. It is not generally considered consistently reef-safe and is best suited for experienced aquarists. Quick Facts Scientific Name: Pomacanthus xanthometopon Origin: Indo-Pacific Reefs Max Size: 15 inches Lifespan: 10 years or more Diet: A varied diet of high-quality angelfish pellets, flakes, and a variety of frozen foods. Shipping Size: 1-2 inches (juvenile)

Its body is a striking combination of a light gray to white base color with distinct reddish-orange vertical stripes that give it a sophisticated look. It is also known for its graceful swimming and its hardiness , making it a great choice for both intermediate and experienced hobbyists. While generally considered peaceful, its temperament requires monitoring in a community setting, as is common with all angelfish. Why the Eibli Angelfish is a Great Choice: Unique Pattern: Its distinctive striped pattern sets it apart from other dwarf angelfish, making it a beautiful addition. Exceptional Hardiness: This species is known for its resilience and ability to thrive in a wide range of water conditions. Generally Reef-Safe: It is an excellent candidate for a reef tank, though like all angelfish, it should be monitored with soft corals and clam mantles. Active and Engaging: Its constant movement and foraging behavior add life and energy to your aquarium's rockwork. Quick Facts Scientific Name: Centropyge eibli Origin: Indian Ocean Max Size: 4 inches Lifespan: 5 years or more Diet: A varied diet of high-quality angelfish pellets, flakes, and frozen foods such as mysis shrimp. Flameback Angelfish: A Hardy and Fiery Dwarf Angelfish The Flameback Angelfish (Centropyge acanthops) is a captivating and durable species that makes a fantastic addition to almost any marine aquarium . Known for its stunning and unique coloration, this dwarf angelfish features a deep royal blue body that beautifully contrasts with a fiery orange or yellow blaze running along its back. Its hardiness and peaceful nature (for an angelfish) make it a great choice for beginners and a welcome member of a community reef tank . Why the Flameback Angelfish is a Great Choice: Vibrant Colors: The striking combination of blue and orange creates a visually spectacular focal point in your tank. Exceptional Hardiness: This species is known for its resilience and ability to thrive in a wide range of water conditions. Generally Reef-Safe: While some individuals may nip at corals, they are a better candidate for a reef tank than many other angelfish species. Peaceful Temperament: They are less aggressive than many other dwarf angelfish, making them a good tank mate for other non-aggressive fish. Quick Facts Scientific Name: Centropyge acanthops Origin: Western Indian Ocean Max Size: 3 inches Lifespan: 5 years or more Diet: A varied diet of high-quality angelfish pellets, flakes, and frozen foods such as mysis shrimp. Shipping Size: 1-2 inches

Imperator Angelfish: The Imperial & Transformative Centerpiece The Imperator Angelfish (Pomacanthus imperator) also called the Emperor Angelfish is a majestic and highly sought-after fish that serves as a stunning centerpiece in a large marine aquarium . This angelfish is famous for its dramatic transformation from its juvenile to adult stage. The juvenile Emperor Angelfish has a beautiful dark blue body with concentric white and electric-blue stripes. As it matures, the adult Emperor Angelfish displays a brilliant blue and yellow body with a distinct dark mask around its eyes. It is a territorial fish and can be aggressive towards other angelfish and some other tank mates. It is considered reef-safe with caution , meaning it may occasionally nip at soft corals or clams. Why the Emperor Angelfish is a Great Choice: Iconic Appearance: Its beautiful coloration and distinctive "mask" make it a true showpiece. Dramatic Transformation: Its stunning color change from juvenile to adult is fascinating to observe. Adds Energy to the Tank: It adds a lot of energy and graceful movement to a spacious aquarium. Reef-Safe with Caution: It can be successfully housed in many reef tanks if well-fed and monitored. Quick Facts Scientific Name: Pomacanthus imperator Origin: Indo-Pacific Reefs Max Size: 15 inches Lifespan: 10+ years Diet: Omnivore. Feeds on a varied diet of angelfish formulas, sponges, and marine algae. Shipping Size: 2-4 inches

Flame Angelfish: A Striking and Iconic Dwarf Angelfish The Flame Angelfish (Centropyge loricula) is arguably the most popular and recognizable dwarf angelfish in the entire marine hobby. Its breathtaking coloration—a fiery red-orange body accented by bold black vertical stripes and vibrant blue tips on its fins—makes it an instant showstopper. While it is a hardy species, its semi-aggressive nature requires it to be introduced into a well-established tank. Its stunning beauty and active personality make the Flame Angelfish a prized addition to any saltwater or reef aquarium . Why the Flame Angelfish is a Great Choice: Unmatched Color: The intense red and orange colors provide a spectacular focal point for any tank. Hardy and Resilient: This species is known for its durability, allowing it to adapt to a wide range of water conditions. Active Forager: It is an active and engaging fish, constantly picking at rockwork and searching for food. Reef-Safe (with caution): While it is a better candidate for a reef tank than many other angelfish, its temperament should be monitored as it can occasionally nip at corals. Quick Facts Scientific Name: Centropyge loricula Origin: Pacific Ocean Max Size: 4 inches Lifespan: 5 years or more Diet: A varied diet of high-quality angelfish pellets, flakes, and frozen foods. Shipping Size: 1-2 inches

Niger Triggerfish: The Ocean's Vibrant Sentinel The Niger Triggerfish (Odonus niger), also known as the Red Tooth Triggerfish , is a popular and captivating species known for its beautiful colors and, unusually for a triggerfish, its relatively peaceful demeanor. This magnificent fish has a sleek, torpedo-shaped body that can shift from a deep blue to a purple or even greenish hue. Its most striking feature, and the source of its name, is its prominent set of fluorescent red teeth . The Niger Triggerfish is a non-stop, open-water swimmer that adds a dynamic presence to a well-established marine aquarium . While it is one of the most reef-safe triggerfish available, a watchful eye is still recommended with very small invertebrates. Its beauty and unique temperament make it a great choice for a larger community tank. Why the Niger Triggerfish is a Great Choice: Stunning Coloration: Its vibrant blue body and brilliant red teeth provide a unique and beautiful visual display. Peaceful for a Trigger: It is one of the most docile triggers, making it suitable for larger community tanks with peaceful tank mates. Active Swimmer: It adds a lot of energy and movement to the upper and middle sections of the aquarium. Hardy & Resilient: This is a very hardy species that is easy to acclimate and care for. Quick Facts Scientific Name: Odonus niger Origin: Indo-Pacific Reefs Max Size: 12 inches Lifespan: 10+ years Diet: Carnivore. Primarily feeds on meaty foods such as shrimp, krill, and clams. Shipping Size: 2-4 inches

Apistogramma Cacatuoides Double Orange males are beautiful with a dark background or in a planted aquarium. These peaceful dwarf cichlids will get along with each other and other small fish. Quick Facts Scientific Name Apistogramma cacatuoides (double orange variety) Origin Amazon basin (bred in Indonesia) Care Level Easy, a good first apisto Temperament Peaceful (males territorial with each other) Adult Size Males up to 3"; females about 2" Lifespan 3–5 years Diet Omnivore (tiny foods) Water Temperature 75–84°F pH 6.0–7.5 Shipping Size Approx. 1" Care Guide Tank setup: Give them a heater, a gentle filter, dim lighting and lots of plants, driftwood and leaf litter. Add a cave (a coconut shell or small clay pot) for each female. Most apistos prefer soft, slightly acidic water. Feeding: Feed small pellets or flake once or twice a day. They also enjoy frozen foods like bloodworms and brine shrimp. Tankmates: Keep them with small, peaceful fish such as tetras, rasboras, pencilfish, otocinclus and corydoras. A calm school of small "dither" fish helps apistos feel safe enough to come out. Keep one male per tank unless it is large and well planted, and avoid large or boisterous fish. Adults may eat small shrimp and baby shrimp. Breeding: Apistos are cave spawners. The female lays her eggs inside a cave and guards the fry, while the male patrols the territory. One male with several females works well in a planted tank. Good to know: Tank-bred double orange cockatoos are hardy and adaptable. Males show their tallest fins and brightest orange when a female is present.

Cortez Angelfish: A Bold and Beautiful Pacific Gem The Cortez Angelfish (Pomacanthus zonipectus) is a striking and highly sought-after species from the Eastern Pacific. As a juvenile, this fish is an absolute showstopper with its vibrant black body crossed by prominent white and blue vertical stripes . As it matures, it transforms into a handsome adult with a brownish-gray body, a distinctive vertical black band, and vibrant electric blue highlights on its fins. Known for its bold personality and grace, the Cortez Angelfish is a magnificent centerpiece for a large, well-established marine aquarium . Why the Cortez Angelfish is a Great Choice: Dramatic Color Transformation: Its stunning change from a striped juvenile to a bold, banded adult makes for an incredible visual journey. Exceptional Hardiness: This species is known for its resilience and ability to thrive in a well-maintained large tank. Intelligent and Active: Its engaging personality and graceful swimming patterns make it a true showpiece fish. Unique Appearance: The subtle, yet beautiful, colors of the adult make it a unique addition to any collection. Important Note: The Cortez Angelfish is a large and territorial fish that requires a minimum tank size of 180 gallons due to its adult size and need for ample swimming room. It is not generally considered reef-safe and is best suited as the dominant fish in a large community. Quick Facts Scientific Name: Pomacanthus zonipectus Origin: Eastern Pacific Ocean (including the Sea of Cortez) Max Size: 18 inches Lifespan: 10+ years Diet: A varied diet of high-quality angelfish pellets, flakes, and a variety of frozen foods. Shipping Size: 3-4 inches

Ruby Anthias: The Open-Water Reef Aggregator The Ruby Anthias (Paranthias colonus), also known as the Creole Fish , is a unique and fascinating member of the grouper family (Serranidae). Unlike most groupers that hide in caves or stay close to the substrate, this species has evolved a slender, streamlined body and a deeply forked tail, adapting to a life of active, open-water swimming. Sporting a beautiful reddish-brown to olive-pink coloration often accented by small, bright spots along its back, it brings captivating motion and school-like behavior to large marine aquariums. Native to the Eastern Pacific Ocean, ranging from the Gulf of California down to Peru and around the Galápagos Islands, this fish can grow to an impressive maximum length of about 12 to 14 inches (30-35 cm). Because they are high-energy, schooling fish that spend their time cruising the water column in search of food, they require a tremendous amount of swimming space. A minimum aquarium size of 180 gallons is required to house a single specimen, though a much larger tank is necessary if you intend to keep a small group. The Ruby Anthias is generally peaceful toward other fish that are too large to swallow, making it an excellent addition to large community setups or predator-focused tanks. They are hardy and adaptable, but because of their active lifestyle, they require strong water movement, highly efficient filtration, and a tightly fitted lid, as they can be prone to jumping when startled. Diet & Compatibility: Diet: This fish is a dedicated Planktivore . Unlike its ambush-predator grouper cousins, it feeds on zooplankton drifting in the current. In the aquarium, it should be fed a varied diet of meaty frozen foods, including mysis shrimp, krill, finely chopped squid, clams, and high-quality marine pellets. Because of their fast metabolism and constant swimming, they should be fed at least twice a day . Feeding: They are enthusiastic eaters and will quickly learn to rush to the surface during feeding time. Ensure that enough food disperses throughout the water column so all tankmates get a share. Reef Compatibility: It is Reef Safe With Caution . They will completely ignore stony and soft corals, anemones, and polyps. However, they are opportunistic predators and will systematically hunt down and consume small ornamental shrimp, crabs, and very small fish. Temperament: It is Peaceful to Semi-Aggressive . It is peaceful toward larger, robust tankmates such as tangs, large angels, triggerfish, and larger wrasses. It can be kept singly or in a group if introduced simultaneously to a massive system. Avoid housing it with tiny, passive fish like neon gobies or micro-chromis, which may become an accidental snack. Quick Facts Scientific Name: Paranthias colonus Primary Common Name: Ruby Anthias or Pacific Creolefish Other Common Names: Creole Fish, Southern Creole Fish Origin: Eastern Pacific (Gulf of California to Peru) Max Size: 12-14 inches (30-35 cm) Temperament: Peaceful to Semi-Aggressive Diet: Planktivore / Carnivore Minimum Tank Size: 180+ Gallons Reef Compatibility: With Caution (Will eat small invertebrates and tiny fish)

Starry Blenny: The Speckled Algae Patrol The Starry Blenny (Salarias ramosus), also known as the Snowflake Blenny, is a charming and industrious bottom-dweller, prized by aquarists for its striking looks and tireless algae-grazing habits. Its body features a beautiful, mottled dark brown or black base color covered with hundreds of tiny, brilliant white or light blue dots , resembling a night sky of stars. Combined with its expressive eyes and quirky personality, the Starry Blenny is a standout addition to any marine display. This blenny is an excellent member of the clean-up crew, using its specialized comb-like teeth to graze continuously on nuisance filamentous algae and microalgae on live rock and tank glass. It is a perching fish , spending much of its time hopping across the rockwork and observing its surroundings. The Starry Blenny is completely reef safe and generally peaceful, making it compatible with most non-aggressive tank mates. A minimum tank size of 30 gallons is suitable for a single specimen, provided the aquarium is well-established with ample live rock to support grazing. As a dedicated herbivore , this species relies heavily on natural algae growth. While it will accept prepared foods, a varied diet of marine algae sheets (nori), Spirulina, and vegetable matter is crucial to prevent starvation, especially in cleaner tanks. They can be territorial toward other blennies or fish that share a similar diet, so it is best kept alone. Like all blennies, the Starry Blenny is a known jumper , and a secure, tight-fitting lid is mandatory. Quick Facts Scientific Name: Salarias ramosus Common Names: Starry Blenny, Snowflake Blenny, Starry Lawnmower Blenny Origin: Indo-Pacific (Western Central Pacific) Max Size: 5 to 6 inches Temperament: Peaceful (Territorial toward blennies/similar grazers) Diet: Herbivore. Must have constant access to algae supplemented with nori and vegetable matter. Minimum Tank Size: 30 gallons Reef Safe: Yes, excellent for coral systems.

Yellow Boxfish: The Toxic, Gentle Giant The Yellow Spotted Boxfish (Ostracion cubicus) or Spotted Boxfish, is an iconic marine fish easily recognized by its cube-shaped body and distinctive pattern. It is also known by common names such as Cubicus Boxfish or Polka Dot Boxfish. This fish is generally purchased as a stunning juvenile, which features a bright yellow carapace covered in bold black spots. While irresistible when small, the Yellow Boxfish is strictly an expert-only species due to several critical challenges. First, it grows into a large fish, reaching up to 18 inches (45 cm) in the wild. As it matures, its vibrant yellow coloration fades to a more subdued tan, brownish, or blue-green hue, and the spots shrink. Second, and most critically, all boxfish possess a defense mechanism: when severely stressed, threatened, or dying, they release a potent skin toxin called Ostracitoxin (or Pahutoxin) into the water. This venom can quickly kill all other fish in the aquarium, including the boxfish itself. Maintaining a stable, low-stress environment and planning for emergency water changes is essential. Diet & Compatibility: Diet: The Yellow Boxfish is an Omnivore that grazes constantly on benthic algae, small invertebrates, and detritus in the wild. In the aquarium, it requires a varied diet fed multiple times daily to maintain its health and bulk. Offer high-quality frozen meaty foods (e.g., mysis shrimp, chopped squid, clams) and plant matter (e.g., nori/seaweed sheets), often supplemented with vitamins. They are slow, methodical feeders and must not be housed with fast or aggressive tankmates that will outcompete them for food. Toxicity & Stress: Due to the risk of toxin release, the fish requires a massive aquarium (minimum of 180-250+ gallons) with exceptional filtration and a powerful protein skimmer. The large water volume helps to dilute any potential toxin release. Stressors like bullying, netting, or poor water quality are the main triggers. Reef Compatibility: It is Not Reef Safe. While the fish generally avoids sessile corals, it is known to nip at LPS (Large Polyp Stony) corals, soft corals, and especially tubeworms (feather dusters), which it views as food. It will also consume small ornamental shrimp and snails. Temperament & Tankmates: It is generally Peaceful toward non-boxfish species, but it is solitary and should be kept singly unless the system is enormous and allows for multiple, separate territories. Tankmates should be large, peaceful, and non-aggressive to prevent the boxfish from becoming stressed. Avoid boisterous fish or those that may pick at its smooth, sensitive skin. Special Note: Due to its poor maneuverability, ensure that water flow is gentle and that filtration intake tubes are covered to prevent the fish from being sucked against the grates. Never use the water the fish was shipped in when transferring it to the quarantine or display tank. Quick Facts Scientific Name: Ostracion cubicus Primary Common Name: Yellow Boxfish Other Common Names: Cubicus Boxfish, Polka Dot Boxfish, Cube Trunkfish Origin: Indo-Pacific (Widespread) Max Size: 18 inches (45 cm) Temperament: Peaceful (to other large, non-aggressive fish) / Highly Toxic Diet: Omnivore (Constant grazer of algae and meaty foods) Minimum Tank Size: 180–250+ Gallons (Expert Only) Reef Compatibility: Not Reef Safe (May nip corals and consume invertebrates)
Mertensi Butterfly; Tonga - Chaetodon mertensii

Raccoon Butterflyfish: A Classic and Hardy Butterflyfish The Raccoon Butterflyfish (Chaetodon lunula) is a beautiful and exceptionally hardy species that adds a touch of classic elegance to any marine aquarium . It is highly sought after for its distinctive "raccoon mask" pattern: a broad black band across the eyes, followed by a white band behind it. With a graceful, oval body and a yellow-orange base coloration, this fish is a standout. It is known for its peaceful temperament with other fish, making it a great candidate for a community tank with other non-aggressive species. Why the Raccoon Butterflyfish is a Great Choice: Distinctive Appearance: Its iconic black-and-white face mask and vibrant coloration make it an instantly recognizable and attractive inhabitant. Active and Engaging: This species is a resilient fish that will constantly swim and forage, adding life and energy to your tank. Hardy and Resilient: It is known for its durability, making it a good choice for intermediate aquarists. Potential Aiptasia Eater: In some cases, this butterflyfish may feed on pest anemones like Aiptasia, which can be a bonus for some reef keepers. Important Note: The Raccoon Butterflyfish is not considered reef-safe. Its diet in the wild consists of various invertebrates, including coral polyps, and it will often nip at and consume corals, especially when a proper diet is not provided. It is best suited for a fish-only or fish-only-with-live-rock aquarium. Quick Facts Scientific Name: Chaetodon lunula Origin: Indo-Pacific Reefs Max Size: 8 inches Lifespan: 5 years or more Diet: Omnivore. A varied diet of meaty foods such as frozen shrimp and clams, as well as marine algae and prepared foods. Shipping Size: 2-3 inches

Lightning Maroon Clownfish: A Dazzling & Bold Centerpiece The Lightning Maroon Clownfish (Premnas biaculeatus) is one of the most iconic and sought-after designer clownfish in the marine hobby. This unique variant is known for its breathtaking and highly variable web-like pattern of white lines that flash across its vibrant maroon-to-orange body, resembling a lightning storm. Unlike the more peaceful Ocellaris varieties, the Lightning Maroon is a bold and territorial species, making it a spectacular centerpiece for a large, semi-aggressive community tank. Its hardiness and striking looks make it a favorite for experienced aquarists. Important Note: The Maroon Clownfish is known for its aggressive and territorial behavior, especially as it matures. It should be introduced to the tank before more docile species and is best kept as a single specimen or a well-established pair. Why the Lightning Maroon Clownfish is a Great Choice: Breathtaking Appearance: Its one-of-a-kind lightning pattern makes it an unforgettable showpiece. Hardy & Resilient: This captive-bred species is known for its resilience and adaptability, making it a great choice for a well-maintained system. Unique Personality: Its bold and confident nature adds a dynamic presence to the aquarium. Reef-Safe: The Lightning Maroon Clownfish will not harm corals, though it may be territorial with other fish in the tank. Quick Facts Scientific Name: Premnas biaculeatus Origin: Captive-bred (Designer Variety) Max Size: 6 inches Lifespan: 10 years or more Diet: Omnivore. A varied diet of high-quality frozen foods, marine pellets, and algae. Shipping Size: 1.5-2.5 inches

True Percula Clownfish: The Iconic Reef Tank Inhabitant The True Percula Clownfish (Amphiprion percula) is perhaps the most iconic and beloved species in the marine aquarium hobby. Its classic and vibrant appearance features a brilliant orange body with three distinct white stripes , each outlined in a thin black line. Why the True Percula Clownfish is a Great Choice: Iconic Appearance: Its classic orange, white, and black pattern makes it an instantly recognizable and attractive inhabitant. Highly Hardy: This species is incredibly resilient and easy to care for, making it a perfect first fish for a new tank. Peaceful Temperament: It is a great community fish that can coexist with a variety of other species without issues. Reef-Safe: The True Percula Clownfish is completely safe to keep with all types of corals and invertebrates. Quick Facts Scientific Name: Amphiprion percula Origin: Western Pacific Ocean and Great Barrier Reef Max Size: 4 inches Lifespan: 6-10 years Diet: Omnivore. A varied diet of high-quality flakes, pellets, and frozen foods. Shipping Size: 1-2.5 inches

Electric Blue Damselfish: A Brilliant Flash of Color for Your Tank The Electric Blue Damselfish (Pomacentrus coelestis) is a small but vibrant species that adds a brilliant pop of color to any marine aquarium . Its striking appearance features an intense electric blue body contrasted with a beautiful, bright yellow tail , making it a showstopper despite its small size. Known for its exceptional hardiness and active personality, the Electric Blue Damselfish is an excellent choice for both beginner and experienced hobbyists. Exceptional Hardiness: This species is incredibly resilient and easy to care for, making it a perfect first fish for a new tank. Active and Engaging: Its constant movement and foraging behavior add a sense of energy and life to your rockwork. Reef-Safe: The Electric Blue Damselfish is a great candidate for most reef tanks and will not harm corals or invertebrates. Important Note: Like most damselfish, this species can be territorial. It is best to introduce it into a tank with a well-established aquascape to give it a place to hide and claim as its own. Quick Facts Scientific Name: Pomacentrus coelestis Origin: Indo-Pacific Reefs Max Size: 3.5 inches Lifespan: 5 years or more Diet: Omnivore. Red Tail Filefish: The Shy, Colorful Omnivore The Red Tail Filefish (Pervagor melanocephalus), also known as the Black Headed Filefish or Flame Filefish , is a visually appealing and generally peaceful addition to the marine aquarium. This filefish is distinguished by its striking color pattern: the rear portion of its body is typically a bright orange or red, contrasting sharply with its darker, gray to black head and forebody. Its thin, paddle-like tail often features irregular dark stripes. Originating from the Indo-Pacific, this species is relatively small for a filefish, reaching a maximum size of about 4 to 6 inches (10-15 cm). While its peaceful disposition makes it compatible with most non-aggressive tankmates, its omnivorous diet and tendency to graze make it a significant risk in a dedicated reef system. The Red Tail Filefish requires an established, peaceful environment with ample rockwork and is best suited for the intermediate aquarist due to its dietary requirements and often shy nature when newly introduced. Diet & Compatibility: Diet: The Red Tail Filefish is an Omnivore that feeds on algae, small crustaceans, and other benthic invertebrates in the wild. In the aquarium, a varied diet is critical to maintain its health and vibrant coloration. Feeding: It has a small mouth designed for picking at food in crevices, so it needs small, meaty foods (mysis shrimp, enriched brine shrimp, chopped squid) and plenty of marine algae (nori on a clip). It should be fed multiple times per day. Vitamin enrichment is essential to prevent color fading. Temperament: Peaceful and Shy. This filefish can be easily bullied by aggressive fish like Triggerfish or large Angelfish. It should be housed only with other peaceful tankmates. It may show aggression toward other filefish, so it is best kept singly unless a proven mated pair is acquired. Reef Compatibility: NOT Reef Safe. While generally peaceful toward fish, it is known to nip at and consume various sessile invertebrates, including soft corals, stony corals (LPS and SPS polyps), feather dusters, and zoanthids. It should be kept in a Fish-Only-With-Live-Rock (FOWLR) system. Special Notes: Some filefish species are sought after for eating pest anemones like Aiptasia, and while this individual may pick at them, it is not reliably known as a dedicated Aiptasia hunter like its close cousin, the Matted Filefish ( Acreichthys tomentosus ). Quick Facts Scientific Name: Pervagor melanocephalus Primary Common Name: Red Tail Filefish Other Common Names: Blackheaded Filefish, Flame Filefish, Black Headed Leatherjacket Origin: Indo-Pacific Max Size: 4-6 inches (10-15 cm) Temperament: Peaceful / Shy Diet: Omnivore (Meaty and Algae-based foods) Care Level: Intermediate Minimum Tank Size: 50 Gallons Reef Compatibility: No (Will pick at corals and inverts)

Yellow Watchman Goby: The Reef's Natural Sentry The Yellow Watchman Goby (Cryptocentrus cinctus) is a popular and beneficial species that serves as a living sentry in any marine aquarium . Its unique appearance features a bright yellow or grayish body with a series of vibrant iridescent blue or pink spots. This goby is renowned for its charming habit of perching at the entrance of its burrow, often created in a symbiotic relationship with a pistol shrimp . The goby acts as a "watchman," alerting its nearly-blind shrimp partner to danger. This peaceful and captivating fish is an excellent choice for a community reef tank, provided it has a deep sand bed and plenty of rock rubble to maintain its home. Why the Yellow Watchman Goby is a Great Choice: Natural Sand-Sifter: While perching, it also sifts through sand, helping to keep the substrate clean and aerated. Unique Appearance: Its bright yellow color and iridescent spots provide a beautiful splash of color. Beneficial Symbiosis: Can form a captivating partnership with a pistol shrimp, adding an element of natural behavior to your tank. Peaceful Temperament: It's a non-aggressive species that coexists well with other peaceful tank mates. Quick Facts Scientific Name: Cryptocentrus cinctus Origin: Indo-Pacific Reefs Max Size: 4 inches Lifespan: 3-5 years Diet: Carnivore. It feeds on small invertebrates found in the sand, supplemented by high-quality frozen foods. Shipping Size: 1.5-2.5 inches

Bella Goby The Bella Goby (Valenciennea bella) is best known for its constant, active sifting behavior, tirelessly taking in mouthfuls of sand and sifting it through its gills to extract food. It's an excellent choice for a community reef tank and is a perfect "workhorse" fish to help keep your substrate clean, aerated, and free of detritus. Discovered by French zoologish Achille Valencienna, he nick named the fish "bella" which is simply Latin for "beautiful". Why the Bella Goby is a Great Choice: Natural Sand-Sifter: Its continuous sifting behavior helps to keep the sand bed clean and aerated, preventing harmful gas buildup. Stunning Appearance: The elegant blue and yellow markings provide a beautiful, subtle splash of color. Peaceful Temperament: It is a non-aggressive species that coexists well with other peaceful tank mates. Reef-Safe: The Bella Goby is completely safe to keep with all types of corals and invertebrates. Quick Facts Scientific Name: Valenciennea bella Origin: Western Pacific Reefs Max Size: 5 inches Lifespan: 5 years or more Diet: Carnivore. It feeds on small invertebrates found in the sand, supplemented by high-quality frozen foods like mysis shrimp. Shipping Size: 2-3 inches

The Radiata Lionfish (Pterois radiata) is one of the smaller and less common lionfish species in the aquarium trade, distinguished by its elegant, translucent fins and distinctive markings. Also known as the Clearfin Lionfish or Tailbar Lionfish , this species is noted for being the only *Pterois* species lacking spots or bands on its dorsal spines and pectoral fins, which are clear (hence the name). They also feature two distinct horizontal white stripes on the base of the tail (caudal peduncle). Native to the Indo-Pacific and Red Sea, the Radiata Lionfish is a nocturnal and more secretive predator than its larger cousins. It is capable of reaching an adult size of 8 to 10 inches (20-25 cm). Due to their size and predatory nature, a minimum aquarium size of 70 to 75 gallons is recommended, with plenty of live rock to create the caves and overhangs they prefer for daytime hiding. Like all members of the genus, the Radiata Lionfish is equipped with venomous spines . They are a hardy fish once established but require care in handling and diet. Diet & Compatibility: Diet: This fish is a dedicated Carnivore that hunts small fish and crustaceans at night. In captivity, it must be trained to accept a varied diet of frozen meaty foods, such as silversides , krill, and pieces of squid. It often requires live food, like feeder shrimp, initially to encourage feeding. Feed a large meal only 2–3 times per week to maintain a healthy weight. Feeding: Due to their shy and nocturnal nature, they may take longer than other lionfish to adapt to hand-feeding or frozen foods. Persistence is key, often requiring the use of feeding sticks or tongs near their hiding spot. Reef Compatibility: It is Reef Safe With Caution . The Clearfin Lionfish will prey upon nearly all ornamental shrimp, crabs, and very small fish. It will generally leave corals and sessile invertebrates alone. Temperament: It is Semi-Aggressive / Predatory . They are generally peaceful toward larger fish that cannot be swallowed. They are best kept with other semi-aggressive fish that are too large to be considered prey, such as certain triggers, larger angels, and tangs. They are typically solitary. Venomous Spines: The sting is extremely painful. If stung, immediately immerse the affected area in the hottest water you can tolerate (not scalding) for 30-90 minutes, and seek medical attention immediately . Quick Facts Scientific Name: Pterois radiata Primary Common Name: Radiata Lionfish Other Common Names: Clearfin Lionfish, Tailbar Lionfish, Radial Firefish Origin: Indo-Pacific, Red Sea Max Size: 8-10 inches (20-25 cm) Temperament: Semi-Aggressive / Predatory ( Venomous ) Diet: Carnivore (Frozen meaty foods) Minimum Tank Size: 70-75 Gallons Reef Compatibility: With Caution (Eats shrimp and small fish)

Why the Spotted Sharpnose Puffer is a Great Choice: Captivating Personality: Its curious and intelligent behavior makes it a truly interactive and entertaining fish. A varied diet of high-quality frozen foods and pest invertebrates found in the tank. Shipping Size: 1.5-2 inches

Cleaner Wrasse: A Unique & Beneficial Reef Fish The Cleaner Wrasse (Labroides dimidiatus) is a fascinating and highly specialized species that adds a touch of graceful elegance to any marine aquarium . Its unique appearance features a slender, bright blue body with a single, prominent black horizontal stripe that runs from its snout to its tail. This fish is renowned for its symbiotic relationship with other reef inhabitants; it sets up "cleaning stations" where it removes parasites and dead skin from other fish. This behavior is both mesmerizing to watch and highly beneficial for the health of your tank's ecosystem. The Cleaner Wrasse is a peaceful species that poses no threat to corals or invertebrates. Why the Cleaner Wrasse is a Great Choice (with caution): Unique Behavior: Its role as a cleaner fish is one of the most interesting symbiotic relationships you can observe in a home aquarium. Elegant Appearance: Its sleek, blue body and active swimming make it a beautiful and constant presence. Peaceful Temperament: It is a non-aggressive species that coexists well with other peaceful tank mates. Reef-Safe: The Cleaner Wrasse is completely safe to keep with all types of corals and invertebrates. Important Note: Due to their highly specialized diet of parasites and mucus, Cleaner Wrasse can be difficult to acclimate and feed in a home aquarium. They require a well-established tank with a thriving community of other fish to support their natural feeding habits. Quick Facts Scientific Name: Labroides dimidiatus Origin: Indo-Pacific Reefs Max Size: 4.5 inches Lifespan: 5 years or more Diet: Carnivore. Primarily feeds on parasites and mucus from other fish. Shipping Size: 1.5-3 inches

Clown Triggerfish: An Iconic and Bold Centerpiece The Clown Triggerfish (Balistoides conspicillum) is one of the most iconic and sought-after fish in the marine aquarium hobby. Renowned for its breathtaking and intricate coloration, it features a striking black body adorned with large, irregular white spots on its lower half. Its face is a vibrant mosaic of patterns, including a bright yellow mouth and bold markings around its eyes.
