If the aquarium just needs a male or two with all the color, here's the solution. Our current stock is juvenile and will begin demonstrating the bright red colors in another three to four months, but they are from a very good breeder. Quick Facts Scientific Name Apistogramma agassizii (double red variety) Origin Amazon basin (captive-bred) Care Level Moderate Temperament Peaceful (males territorial with each other) Adult Size Males up to 3"; females about 2" Lifespan 3–5 years Diet Omnivore (tiny foods) Water Temperature 76–84°F pH 5.5–7.0 Shipping Size Approx. 1" Care Guide Tank setup: Give them a heater, a gentle filter, dim lighting and lots of plants, driftwood and leaf litter. Add a cave (a coconut shell or small clay pot) for each female. Most apistos prefer soft, slightly acidic water. Feeding: Feed small pellets or flake once or twice a day. They also enjoy frozen foods like bloodworms and brine shrimp. Tankmates: Keep them with small, peaceful fish such as tetras, rasboras, pencilfish, otocinclus and corydoras. A calm school of small "dither" fish helps apistos feel safe enough to come out. Keep one male per tank unless it is large and well planted, and avoid large or boisterous fish. Adults may eat small shrimp and baby shrimp. Breeding: Apistos are cave spawners. The female lays her eggs inside a cave and guards the fry, while the male patrols the territory. One male with several females works well in a planted tank. Good to know: Double red males color up gradually and look their best in a dim, planted tank with a female or two present.

listings.commonName: Mickey Mouse Platy Assorted Colors (Clubhouse of 5)
listings.description: Mickey Mouse Platies might have the mouse ears on their tails instead of their heads, but they can have a club in the aquarium too. Quick Facts Scientific Name Xiphophorus maculatus Origin Southern Mexico and Central America Care Level Easy, good for beginners Temperament Peaceful Adult Size Up to 2" Lifespan 3–4 years Diet Omnivore Water Temperature 70–80°F pH 7.0–8.2 Breeding Livebearer – breeds easily in the aquarium Group Size Sold as a group of 5 Care Guide Tank setup: Platies are hardy and easy to keep. Give them a filter, a lid and plenty of plants. Use a heater to keep the water steady in the 70s. They prefer harder, slightly alkaline water. Feeding: Feed a quality flake or small pellet once or twice a day, only as much as they eat in a couple of minutes. Platies also need some plant matter, so a vegetable flake is a good choice. They also enjoy frozen brine shrimp. Tankmates: Platies get along with most peaceful community fish, such as other livebearers (mollies, guppies and swordtails), tetras, rasboras and corydoras. Avoid large or aggressive fish that may bully or eat them. Breeding: Platies are livebearers, so a tank with males and females will almost certainly have babies (fry). Adults will eat fry, so add dense plants or use a breeding box if you want to raise them. Keeping more females than males gives the females a break from the males' attention. Good to know: Platies are one of the easiest fish to keep, which makes them a great choice for a first aquarium.

Rare purple crystal shrimp, also called purple zebra shrimp, grow in subtropical areas of Taiwan and once in a while find themselves in the aquarium trade, like the ones we brought in. Peaceful and adaptable to most aquarium conditions similar to Neocaridina shrimp, they do not like temperatures over 80 degrees. Purple bands and a green head are what make this shrimp remarkable. Quick Facts Scientific Name Wild-type Taiwanese shrimp (exact species uncertain) Origin Taiwan (wild-collected) Care Level Easy, good for beginners Temperament Peaceful Adult Size Up to 1" Lifespan 1–2 years Diet Omnivore (grazes on algae) Water Temperature 65–78°F pH 6.5–8.0 Water Hardness GH 6–12 (moderately hard) Group Size Does best in a group (breeds readily) Shipping Size Approx. ½" Care Guide Tank setup: Neocaridina are hardy and ideal for beginners. Use a cycled, planted tank with moss, plants and hiding spots, and a sponge filter or a sponge over the filter intake so shrimp aren't pulled in. Keep the water stable. Feeding: Shrimp graze on algae all day. Feed a small amount of quality shrimp food once a day and remove anything uneaten after a few hours. Tankmates: Keep shrimp alone or with tiny, peaceful fish like small rasboras, ember tetras, otocinclus and pygmy corydoras, plus snails. Most fish will eat baby shrimp, and cichlids (even dwarf cichlids like rams and apistogrammas) and larger fish will eat adults. Different Neocaridina colors will crossbreed and lose their color over time. Good to know: Shrimp are very sensitive to copper and many medications. Never treat a tank with shrimp, and check plant fertilizers and treatments for copper.

True Percula Clownfish (Pair) One of the most popular marine aquarium fish, along with it's close cousin and Nemo fame, the False Percula Clownfish, or simply the Percula Clownfish. Also called the Clown Anemonefish, the True Percula only varies a little bit from the more common Percula. True Percula Clownfish feature slightly brighter orange colors and thinner black lines. The True Percula Clownfish can be found in most independent marine aquarium stores and generally available through commercial breeding operations. Scientific Name: Amphiprion percula Origin: Great Barrier Reef (Where Nemo grew up) Max Size: 3 inches Diet: Omnivore Shipping Size: 1 to 3 inches

Not to be confused with the cardinal tetra, these small minnows are related to white clouds, only grow to one inch and are wild-caught in central Vietnam. Brightly colored white, reds and greens on this fish are lovely but hard to pick out until the fish nears its adult size. Peaceful and very adaptable, these fish go well with any other smaller community fish and fancy shrimp. The scientific name comes from Tan Kam Fei, the Boy Scout who discovered the white cloud minnow family. Quick Facts Scientific Name Tanichthys micagemmae Origin Central Vietnam Care Level Easy, good for beginners Temperament Peaceful Adult Size Up to 1" Lifespan 3–5 years Diet Omnivore Water Temperature 64–77°F pH 6.5–7.5 Group Size Does best in a group Shipping Size Approx. ½" Care Guide Tank setup: Give them plants and gentle filtration. These are cool-water fish that do fine at room temperature, and they also do well in outdoor ponds and patio tubs in warm months. Keep a lid on the tank. Feeding: Feed a quality flake or small pellet once or twice a day, only as much as they eat in a couple of minutes. They also enjoy frozen foods like bloodworms and brine shrimp. Tankmates: They get along with other small, peaceful fish like ricefish, danios, small rasboras, and dwarf shrimp, and can share an unheated tank with other cool-water species. Avoid large fish (including goldfish) that may eat them. Good to know: White clouds have been kept in aquariums since the 1930s and are one of the hardiest small fish in the hobby. Males show the brightest color when they display to each other.

Black Dogface Puffer is a very unique and rare puffer. Black Dogface Puffers have a mostly all black body with white fins and a white tail. Black Dogface Puffers also have a white mouth and various white patches on their black bodies. Black Dogface Puffers reach a maximum adult size of around 13 inches and need to be kept in tanks that are at least 90 gallons in size. Black Dogface Puffers are semi-aggressive fish, but shouldn't bother too many other fish in your tank. Black Dogface Pufferfish can bother some smaller fish and eat most inverts. Black Dogface Puffers have also been known to nip at some corals. For these reasons, it is a bad idea to add a Black Dogface Puffer to your reef tank. Shipping Size : 5-6 Inches Regions Found: Indo-Pacific Ocean, Indonesia, Solomon Islands

HG811 Hygger Mini Air Pump The HG811 mini air pump from Hygger is the smallest, quietest air pump on the market. Using piezo electric crystal technology this little pump is amazing. Lots of air for small tanks and no noise. Air stone and tubing included. This thing is only 2 inches. Unbelievable. It can handle all the air required for betta tanks and small aquariums up to 20 gallons.

Magnetic Glass Cleaner The HG815 Hygger Glass Cleaner features a 2" by 4" cleaning surface and ultra strong magnetic force between the glass panel. The cleaner comes with a detachable scraper - in case you don't want to work with any sharp objects. Effective for glass widths found with aquariums up to 200 gallons.

HG010 Aquarium Wave Maker The Hygger HG010 creates waves for the saltwater aquarium or the freshwater aquarium (but generally used for saltwater aquariums). A magnetic power source on the outside of the glass keeps all the power cords out of the water. 12W and 2100 GPH, perfect for 40 gallons to whatever.

HG978 Overhead Aquarium Light 14W and 18W Hygger Overhead Lights Programmable, full spectrum, and expandable from 12 inches to 18 inches for the medium light and 18 inches to 24 inches for the medium/large size. The Hygger programmable, dimmable, full spectrum color changing lights provide beauty and all the light necessary for corals and plants. Perfect for saltwater and freshwater aquariums and at a prices that cannot be beat. (Medium) Top brackets expand on the 14 W unit from 12 inches to 18 inches. (Medium/Large) Top brackets expand on the 18W unit from 18 inches to 24 inches.
Hollow Tree Trunk The perfect natural looking hiding place made from fish safe light weight resin. Only 6.5" long and 2.5" wide, but it's an impactful and practical piece of decor.

Hygger HG092 Protein Skimmer This protein skimmer does the job for small to large marine aquariums. The skimmer is adjustable and hangs on the back of 29 to 125 gallon aquariums. On 7W with maximum flow of 264GPH. Size is 4"x4"x12".

Thai breeders name the fish and aquariumfish.com just passes it along. In this case, we suppose the jade head and multicolored tail resemble the colors of a faraway Asian dragon. In the fish tank, these colors are bright and cherry, and there is little chance that any fire will be breathed. This order comes with one male and one female. Quick Facts Scientific Name Poecilia reticulata Origin Northern South America (captive-bred in Thailand) Care Level Easy Temperament Peaceful Adult Size Up to 2" Lifespan 2–3 years Diet Omnivore Water Temperature 72–82°F pH 7.0–8.0 Group Size Sold as a pair (1 male + 1 female) Shipping Size Approx. 1" Care Guide Tank setup: Give them a heater, a gentle filter and plenty of plants, including some floating plants where babies can hide. Guppies like slightly hard water. Feeding: Feed a quality flake or small pellet once or twice a day, only as much as they eat in a couple of minutes. They also enjoy frozen foods like bloodworms and brine shrimp. Tankmates: Guppies get along with other small, peaceful fish such as platies, mollies, corydoras, small tetras and rasboras. Avoid fin-nippers like tiger barbs and larger fish that could eat them. Breeding: Guppies are livebearers and breed easily. Females give birth to live babies about once a month, and adults will eat the babies, so thick plants give them a place to hide. Good to know: Males carry the bright colors and long tails; females are plainer but needed for breeding.

Wonder Shells Weco Wonder Shells are a 50 year old hobby classic. The wonder shells proved several uses. For instance, this is the most decorative way to remove chlorine from your fish tank. Just drop one in and all the chlorine is instantly removed. Most importantly - made of natural materials, Wonder Shell provides beneficial minerals and electrolytes to aquarium water. Each shell oxygenates, aerates and neutralizes harmful acids in your aquarium water and provide invertebrates with an easily available source of calcium for health shell growth. One large shell treats 20 gallons for one month. Shipping Size: One each in small pack (Small bag fits in any live fish box)

Aqua Derm Weco Aqua Derm repairs damaged skin and fins. Just add a couple of drops to your water and monitor the fish. This is not intended to replace medication. Aqua-Derm is a scientifically-formulated concentrate to provide a synthetic slime coat that will help protect fish from stress and injury due to mating, fighting, contact with pond substrate, netting, handling, or transporting fish. If skin abrasions are present, Aqua-Derm creates a protective bandage over the affected areas that will help resist opportunistic disease organisms, aid the natural healing process and reduce loss of electrolytes from the wound site. Shipping Size: 4 ozs (fits inside a live fish box order)

StaClear Weco StaClear is effective against bacterial-derived conditions that lead to cloudy water. Sta Clear will allow you to enjoy the beauty of your aquarium by keeping your freshwater aquarium water sparkling clear. Shipping Size: 4 oz (fits inside any live fish order box)

Nox-Ich by Weco Nox-Ich is the classic ICH medicine. Proven for more the 50 years, the active ingredient malachite green is especially effective against the most common aquarium parasite, ICH. Add just one drop per gallon to eliminate unwanted visitors to your aquarium. Nox-Ich is also effective against Velvet, Fin Rot, Chilondonella, Trichondina as well as many forms of fungi. Treat every three days until all traced of disease are gone. The process generally takes one week. Use half dose as a preventative. Please remove snails prior to treatment, crustaceans and amphibians are sensitive to aquarium medications. The aquarium is safe for invertebrates three days after treatment. Shipping Size: 4 oz (small bottle easily fits into a live fish order box)

DeChlor Add this product to tap water before adding the fish and all the chlorine will be instantly removed. Over 60 years of experience is packaged into each bottle Weco produces. AquariumFishSale selected Weco for their extraordinary experience with the aquarium hobby. DeChlor is scientifically formulated to protect your fish and aquatic plants from the harmful effects of chlorine and even metals in everyday tap water. Chlorine is instantly removed and chloramines and toxic heavy metals are neutralized. This results in tap water that is safe for your pond, or fresh or saltwater aquarium. Shipping Size: 4 oz bottle (fits into any live fish order box)

Aquarium Fish Nets AquariumFish.com offers fish nets in coarse mesh grade. Coarse mesh nets are perfect for delicate fish handling and skimming debris. Counter intuitive, it is the coarse netting that is less likely to snag gills and fins of fish - fine netting tends to snag. The size of the net refers to the width. Sera mesh is of the highest quality, you will be able to see and feel the difference! The vinyl-coated wire is 3mm (10% thicker) than that of the competition on all net sizes Thicker twisted wire creates a more rigid and stronger net Shipping Sizes: 3 inch, 5 inch, and 8 inch

Squamipinnis Anthias: The Graceful & Colorful Schooler The Squamipinnis Anthias (Pseudanthias squamipinnis) also called the Blue Eye Anthias, or Lyretail Anthias, is a stunning and active species that adds a touch of vibrant color and a mesmerizing schooling effect to any marine aquarium . This magnificent anthias displays a striking sexual dimorphism: males have a brilliant reddish-purple body with an elongated dorsal fin and a forked "lyre-shaped" tail, while females are a beautiful golden-orange. The Squamipinnis Anthias is a very active, open-water swimmer that prefers to be kept in a group, which creates a breathtaking visual display as they swim together. It is completely reef-safe and will not harm corals or invertebrates, making it a fantastic addition to a community tank. Due to its high metabolism, it requires a well-established tank and frequent, small feedings throughout the day. Why the Lyretail Anthias is a Great Choice: Schooling Behavior: Keeping a group of these fish provides a dynamic and engaging visual display. Stunning Coloration: The male's brilliant colors and the female's golden-orange hue make it a true showpiece. Completely Reef-Safe: It will not harm corals, clams, or most other invertebrates. Peaceful Temperament: It is a non-aggressive species that coexists well with other peaceful fish. Quick Facts Scientific Name: Pseudanthias squamipinnis Origin: Indo-Pacific Reefs Max Size: 6 inches Lifespan: 5-7 years Diet: Carnivore. Primarily feeds on meaty foods such as shrimp, krill, and prepared foods. Shipping Size: 2-3 inches

HG021 Hygger Mini Wave Maker Little waves and gentle circulation for small fish tanks - the Hygger Mini wave maker is an easy magnetic mount answer. Only 6W and perfect for 5 gallon to 50 gallon aquariums.

listings.commonName: Hygger Dunker Submersible Aquarium LED Light
listings.description: HG005 - 12W Hygger Submersible Light Programmable, multi-colored lighting options, and FULLY SUBMERSIBLE to light up the tank from any angle - even the bottom of the aquarium. 12W and 20 inches long, suitable for medium to large fish tanks.

Hygger HG033 Clip-on Aquarium Light Designed for small tanks under ten gallons, the Hygger Mini Clip-On Light is 9W and colvers a 16 square inch pattern for live plants. DC powered, effective and attractive.
HG088 Hygger Clip-on Marine Light THe 30W full spectrum LED light is suitable for coral growth and will light up an area of up to 2 feet. Size of the unit is 2"x3"x18". Easy to place and adjust.

HG908 Hygger Mini Sponge Filter The Hygger sponge filter offers mechanical and biological filtration for small aquariums. Easy to use and sets right inside the fish tank. Great even for shrimp tanks, betta tanks, and small community tanks. Appropriate for one gallon to ten gallon fish tanks. It is necessary to have a small air pump, like the hygger mini air pump, to produce the filtration flow. Each box comes with a spare filter, but one will last many many months. Just rinse once per week in dechlorinated water.

The Hygger mini heater offers a continues and accurate read out - simply set to 78 degrees or a little higher or lower depending on the species. Only 10W this little heater can regulate temperatures in tanks up to 10 gallons. Safety features include an auto shut-off when water runs low.

HG073 Hygger Digital Thermometer Large LCD display and very accurate readings along with low and high warning settings. Stylish and unobtrusive display monitor. The unit comes with an extra battery and sticks right onto the outside of the fish tank. Swtich from You can switch between centigrade and fahrenheit (for whatever reason). Suitability: Freshwater Aquarium, Saltwater Aquarium, Turtle Tank, Reptile Tank.

HG009 Internal Corner Filter Hidden unobtrusive filtration and aeration for aquariums up to 15 gallons. The filter is easy to rinse and replace, quite, and adjustable to suit the aquarium size. Mechanical filtration Biological filtration Aeration

HG051 Aquarium Cooling Fan The Hygger cooling fan is a low cost and effective method to keep the upper temperature of the aquarium water just a few degrees lower. Silent and low voltage, the cooling fan mounts right to the side of the fish tank.

HG965 Aquascape Tool Set This set comes complete with straight tweezers, curved tweezers, scissors, substrate spatula and scraper. What? You thought you could use your fingers? Planted tanks take special care, part of the hobby. But good news - Hygger made these stainless steel instruments affordable.

Sera Color Enhancing Flake Food Extra ingredients like spirulina for just a little extra money ensures you are providing all you can for your aquatic pets. Like all SERA products, the color enhancing flake food contains only natural color enhancers and nutrients. Shipping Size: 0.8 ounces, 2.1 ounces, 7.4 ounces

The newest mutant in the GloFish series is stunning. It features a solid hot pink body; in the picture here, these fish are not even under any fluorescence. Otherwise, these fish behave like any other natural angelfish. Quick Facts Scientific Name Pterophyllum scalare (genetically modified) Origin Bred in Florida (genetically modified) Care Level Easy Temperament Semi-aggressive (territorial when pairing) Adult Size Up to 6" long and 8" tall Lifespan 10+ years Diet Omnivore Water Temperature 75–82°F pH 6.0–7.5 Shipping Size Approx. 2" Care Guide Tank setup: Give them tall plants or driftwood, a heater and a gentle filter. Feeding: Feed a quality flake or small pellet once or twice a day, only as much as they eat in a couple of minutes. They also enjoy frozen foods like bloodworms and brine shrimp. Tankmates: Choose peaceful fish too large to swallow, such as larger tetras, corydoras, plecos, rams, gouramis and peaceful barbs. Avoid fin-nippers like tiger barbs, and small fish like neon tetras that adult angels may eat. Breeding: Angelfish pair off and lay eggs on flat surfaces like broad leaves or slate. A breeding pair can become territorial, so give them room and places for other fish to retreat. Good to know: GloFish colors look brightest under a blue or actinic LED light. Care is the same as for any other freshwater angelfish.

Not a lot is known about the breeding of this rare exotic fish. The wild-caught red fin rasbora is small and grows to only about 0.75 inches. Hardy and able to acclimate to flake food, this is a great schooling fish for planted tanks and small community aquariums. Quick Facts Scientific Name Rasbora rubrodorsalis Origin Thailand and Cambodia (Mekong basin) Care Level Easy, good for beginners Temperament Peaceful Adult Size Up to 1¼" Lifespan 5–8 years Diet Omnivore Water Temperature 72–80°F pH 6.0–7.5 Group Size Does best in a group Shipping Size Approx. 1" Care Guide Tank setup: Give them plants along the back and sides, open swimming space in front and a dark substrate. Soft, slightly acidic water and gentle filtration bring out their best color. Feeding: Feed a quality flake or small pellet once or twice a day, only as much as they eat in a couple of minutes. They also enjoy frozen foods like bloodworms and brine shrimp. Tankmates: They get along with most peaceful community fish of similar size, such as tetras, other rasboras, danios, corydoras, gouramis and dwarf shrimp. Avoid large predatory fish that could eat them. Good to know: In a well-planted tank a school of rasboras swims together in the middle of the tank, and their colors deepen as they settle in.

If anyone can figure out why our trade called these the "Mayan" butterfly koi instead of black, gold, and white butterfly koi, we would love to cite the history here. This hybrid koi has a unique color pattern (pictured) along with the distinctive fins of butterfly koi. This color pattern was one of the few that originated in Malaysia and not in Japan. Quick Facts Scientific Name Cyprinus carpio Origin Captive-bred (Malaysia) Care Level Easy Temperament Peaceful Adult Size Up to 2–3 feet Lifespan 25–35 years Diet Omnivore Water Temperature 50–80°F pH 7.0–8.5 Group Size Does best in a group Shipping Size Approx. 5" Care Guide Tank setup: Koi grow large and are best kept in an outdoor pond with strong filtration. They are cool-water fish and do not need a heater. Feeding: Feed a quality koi or goldfish pellet once or twice a day, only as much as they eat in a few minutes. Feed less when the water is cool. Tankmates: Koi get along with goldfish and other pond fish. Good to know: Butterfly koi have long, flowing fins and are a cross between koi and Asian long-finned carp.

The pink solar swordtail, bred in Sri Lanka, is a bright pink and orange fish bred to stand out in the aquarium. Black highlights on the tail really make the colors pop. Quick Facts Scientific Name Xiphophorus hellerii (pink solar) Origin Southern Mexico to Honduras (wild ancestors); bred in Sri Lanka Care Level Easy, good for beginners Temperament Peaceful (males may spar) Adult Size Up to 4–5" (not counting the sword) Lifespan 3–5 years Diet Omnivore Water Temperature 72–79°F pH 7.0–8.0 (hard water) Group Size Keep more females than males Shipping Size Approx. 2" Care Guide Tank setup: Swordtails are active swimmers, so give them plants, open swimming space and a tight-fitting lid, since they are good jumpers. They prefer hard, alkaline water. Feeding: Feed a quality flake or small pellet with some vegetable content once or twice a day. They also enjoy frozen foods like bloodworms and brine shrimp. Tankmates: Swordtails get along with most peaceful community fish of similar size, such as platies, mollies, larger tetras, danios, rainbowfish, gouramis and corydoras. Keep more females than males, since males chase females and may spar with each other. Avoid fin-nippers and large cichlids. Good to know: Swordtails are livebearers and breed readily. Fry are born free-swimming and will be eaten unless there are dense plants or a breeding box for them to hide in. Only males grow the "sword" on the tail.

The male bivittatum killifish stay in their own corners and do well by themselves. Not schoolers, but not fighters either. Quick Facts Scientific Name Aphyosemion bivittatum Origin Cameroon and Nigeria, West Africa Care Level Moderate Temperament Peaceful (males may spar with each other) Adult Size Up to 2" Lifespan 2–3 years Diet Carnivore (meaty foods; takes flake) Water Temperature 72–79°F pH 6.0–7.0 Group Size Pair, or one male with several females Care Guide Tank setup: Use a planted tank with soft, slightly acidic water, a dark substrate, gentle filtration and floating plants. Killifish are expert jumpers, so a tight-fitting lid is a must. Feeding: Feed small amounts of a quality flake or small pellet once or twice a day. They also enjoy frozen foods like bloodworms and brine shrimp. Tankmates: Killifish do well with small, peaceful fish like tetras, rasboras, corydoras and other killifish of similar size. Avoid fin-nippers and large fish. Keep one male per tank unless the tank is large, since males may spar. Good to know: Killifish are egg-layers that spawn readily in plants or spawning mops, and their eggs can be hatched separately.

Sera Guppy Food Veggie based special diet to bring out the colors and vitality in fancy guppies. Feed once or twice per day, no more than they eat within 5 minutes. Also contains fish meal proteins, Shipping Size: 100 ml (1.5 oz)

AquaZen Snail Catcher Like the old lint rollers for clothing, we offer the amazing snail roller for aquariums. The AquaZen Snail Catcher is perfect for that active person that can't sit around and wait for the Sera Snail Trapper to do all the work. The handle extends for larger aquariums. Soft in case you hit any fish, just roll along any surface infected with pesky snails and they fall right into the little collecting bin.

The solid red pristella GloFish is a tight, active schooler and looks even more attractive with a few green pristellas in the classroom. Quick Facts Scientific Name Pristella maxillaris (genetically modified) Origin Farm-raised (genetically modified) Care Level Easy, good for beginners Temperament Peaceful Adult Size Up to 2" Lifespan 3–5 years Diet Omnivore Water Temperature 72–80°F pH 6.0–7.5 Group Size Does best in a group Shipping Size Approx. 1" Care Guide Tank setup: Give them a heater, a filter, plants and open swimming space. A dark substrate and background make the colors pop. Feeding: Feed a quality flake or small pellet once or twice a day, only as much as they eat in a couple of minutes. They also enjoy frozen foods like bloodworms and brine shrimp. Tankmates: GloFish tetras get along with most peaceful community fish of similar size, such as other tetras, danios, rasboras, corydoras and livebearers. Keep them in a group so they don't nip the fins of slow, long-finned fish like bettas. Good to know: GloFish colors look brightest under a blue or actinic LED light, but they are colorful under normal lighting too. GloFish pristellas are gentler than GloFish skirt tetras, so they suit calmer community tanks.

Radican Sword Radican sword, also called marble queen sword, originates in Mexico and will grow to the top and sometimes a little out of the aquarium. Scientific Name: Echinodonus cordifolius Shipping Size: Approx. 6 inches in 2 inch pot

The classic red swordtail will stand out with dark gravel and green plants. Males have yellow and black highlights; females display a bright solid red to orange body. Quick Facts Scientific Name Xiphophorus hellerii (fire red) Origin Southern Mexico to Honduras (wild ancestors); aquarium-bred Care Level Easy, good for beginners Temperament Peaceful (males may spar) Adult Size Up to 4–5" (not counting the sword) Lifespan 3–5 years Diet Omnivore Water Temperature 72–79°F pH 7.0–8.0 (hard water) Group Size Keep more females than males Shipping Size Approx. 2" Care Guide Tank setup: Swordtails are active swimmers, so give them plants, open swimming space and a tight-fitting lid, since they are good jumpers. They prefer hard, alkaline water. Feeding: Feed a quality flake or small pellet with some vegetable content once or twice a day. They also enjoy frozen foods like bloodworms and brine shrimp. Tankmates: Swordtails get along with most peaceful community fish of similar size, such as platies, mollies, larger tetras, danios, rainbowfish, gouramis and corydoras. Keep more females than males, since males chase females and may spar with each other. Avoid fin-nippers and large cichlids. Good to know: Swordtails are livebearers and breed readily. Fry are born free-swimming and will be eaten unless there are dense plants or a breeding box for them to hide in. Only males grow the "sword" on the tail.

listings.commonName: Dumbo Ear Betta Male Veil Tail
listings.description: The Dumbo Betta is one of the most ornate and unusual varieties of Betta splendens. This variety has very enlarged pectoral fins that look like large elephant ears on either side of the betta's head, hence they are called "Dumbo Ears" after the children's story about Dumbo the Elephant. These fins may have similar coloration to the body or may even be a contrasting color. There are many names for the particular betta color patterns, but most are variations of blue and/or red colors. Fish pictured here are representative only. If you are looking for a specific coloration, message us, add to the order notes, or simply allow us to choose one of our favorites for you. When messaging, please note your order number. Quick Facts Scientific Name Betta splendens Origin Thailand (captive-bred) Care Level Easy, good for beginners Temperament Males fight each other; peaceful toward most other fish Adult Size Up to 3" Lifespan 3–5 years Diet Carnivore (meaty foods) Water Temperature 76–82°F (needs a heater) pH 6.5–7.5 Breathes Air Yes – labyrinth fish take air from the surface Shipping Size Approx. 2" Care Guide Tank setup: Give him a heater (bettas are tropical fish), a gentle filter and live or silk plants. Floating plants or a "betta leaf" near the surface give him a place to rest. Keep a lid on the tank and leave a gap of air under it, since bettas breathe from the surface. Feeding: Feed a few betta pellets or a pinch of flake once or twice a day. Bettas overeat easily, so small meals are best. They also enjoy frozen bloodworms. Tankmates: Never keep two male bettas together. A male can live with small, peaceful fish that don't nip fins, such as corydoras, small rasboras, otocinclus and snails. Avoid fin-nippers like tiger barbs and flashy, long-finned fish like fancy guppies. Good to know: The big "dumbo ear" pectoral fins and long tail make these slower swimmers. Keep flow gentle and add resting spots like floating leaves near the surface.

There are two recent color morphs available for the popular algae-eating amano: white and orange. The white, or snow white, amano is a bright white and looks terrific against plants and dark substrate. Quick Facts Scientific Name Caridina multidentata (white variety) Origin Taiwan Care Level Easy Temperament Peaceful Adult Size Up to 2" Lifespan 2–3 years Diet Omnivore (excellent algae eater) Water Temperature 65–80°F pH 6.5–7.8 Water Hardness GH 6–12 Group Size Does best in a group Shipping Size Approx. ½–1" Care Guide Tank setup: Give them a cycled, planted tank with moss, driftwood and hiding spots. Cover filter intakes with a sponge and keep a lid on the tank, since amanos can climb out. Feeding: Amanos eat algae and leftover food. If algae runs low, feed algae wafers or shrimp pellets. Tankmates: Amanos do well with most peaceful community fish, plus other shrimp and snails. Avoid cichlids, goldfish, loaches and other fish large enough to eat them. Good to know: Amano shrimp breed in captivity, but their larvae need brackish water to develop, so they will not overpopulate a freshwater tank.

Hygger HG990 APEX Saltwater Clip-on Aquarium Light Designed to light small tanks or small areas of larger tanks, light and clips to any small to mid-size aquarium. Programmable multi color LED. 22Watts.
Hygger HG107 Reef Light 50Watt focus light for tanks with live coral or for hobbyists who simply enjoy intense lighting.

HG948 Hygger 4 gallon Aquarium Complete The Hygger 4 Gallon Complete Set comes with a curved glass hi visibility 4 gallon tank, removable filter with media, overhead LED full spectrum light, and replacement cartridges for the easy peasy filter system. This is a good quality glass tank with nice lighting, not a cheap plastic tank. Recommended fish include fancy shrimp, endlers, guppies, rasboras, dwarf cichlids, panda cory to name a few. This is a beautiful tank and compatible with freshwater planted or unplanted themes. Too small for salt water fish. Base is 7 1/2 inches wide by 11 inches long. Height 12 inches. Remember a four gallon set weighs about 40 lbs, so make sure it's place on a sturdy stand or table.

5-Gallon Arc-Shaped Aquarium Kit with Light, Filter, Pump for Starters The Hygger 5 Gallon Fashion Complete Set comes with a curved glass 5 gallon tank and a in house curved filter system to bring a bit of style to the room. LED multi color lights and oversized filter will keep your fish happy and your eyes transfixed. 3.2W LED lights Fashion and unique design 5W water pump 5 gallon glass fish tank Touch the switch to control multi-mode lighting
HG038 Small Aquarium Cleaning Kit Scarper, net, straight and angled sponge, a very affordable set to keep on top of the small aquarium (and in it).

4-in-1 multi-function: This comprehensive kit includes a fishnet, algae scraper, two sponges, a tube brush, and a gravel rake, making it the ultimate tool for cleaning and maintaining your aquarium. Telescopic Handle with Secure Buckle: The unique buckle design allows easy stretching and ensures attachments stay firmly in place without falling off. The handle adjusts from 1.95 to 2.95 feet, providing reach for cleaning even the most bottomless 2.65-foot tanks without getting your hands wet. Durable Construction: Crafted from a robust carbon fiber composite, the handle pole is built for longevity, resisting bending and breaking for years. Attachments lock securely onto the pole, ensuring they stay put during cleaning. Minimized Water Intake: Thanks to a scientific structural design, water intake is significantly reduced. The handle poles and connection attachments fit snugly together, preventing water from entering the pole and avoiding messy spills when removed from the aquarium. This feature makes it an ideal cleaning solution for all aquarium enthusiasts.

Apisto Cruzzi The apistogramma cruzzi from the Amazonia region of Peru features a rainbow of subtle colors for the males and females. Dwarf in size and peaceful, these are very nice and fairly rare community species. Since these dwarf cichlids are wild-caught, they will not tolerate pH above 7.5 or temperatures below 72 degrees. In all other aspects, they are hardy and adapt easily to flake food. Quick Facts Scientific Name Apistogramma cruzi Origin Peru (wild-caught) Care Level Moderate Temperament Peaceful (males territorial with each other) Adult Size Males up to 3"; females about 2" Lifespan 3–5 years Diet Omnivore (tiny foods) Water Temperature 76–82°F pH 5.5–7.0 Shipping Size Approx. ¾–1" Care Guide Tank setup: Give them a heater, a gentle filter, dim lighting and lots of plants, driftwood and leaf litter. Add a cave (a coconut shell or small clay pot) for each female. Most apistos prefer soft, slightly acidic water. Feeding: Feed small pellets or flake once or twice a day. They also enjoy frozen foods like bloodworms and brine shrimp. Tankmates: Keep them with small, peaceful fish such as tetras, rasboras, pencilfish, otocinclus and corydoras. A calm school of small "dither" fish helps apistos feel safe enough to come out. Keep one male per tank unless it is large and well planted, and avoid large or boisterous fish. Adults may eat small shrimp and baby shrimp. Breeding: Apistos are cave spawners. The female lays her eggs inside a cave and guards the fry, while the male patrols the territory. One male with several females works well in a planted tank. Good to know: Like all wild apistos, cruzi prefer soft, slightly acidic water and settle in best with dim light and plenty of cover.

Five bright red platies will create a colorful and active display. Very peaceful and hardy, the red platy is a good addition to any community aquarium. Quick Facts Scientific Name Xiphophorus maculatus Origin Southern Mexico and Central America Care Level Easy, good for beginners Temperament Peaceful Adult Size Up to 2" Lifespan 3–4 years Diet Omnivore Water Temperature 70–80°F pH 7.0–8.2 Breeding Livebearer – breeds easily in the aquarium Group Size Sold as a school of 5 Shipping Size Approx. 1¼" Care Guide Tank setup: Platies are hardy and easy to keep. Give them a filter, a lid and plenty of plants. Use a heater to keep the water steady in the 70s. They prefer harder, slightly alkaline water. Feeding: Feed a quality flake or small pellet once or twice a day, only as much as they eat in a couple of minutes. Platies also need some plant matter, so a vegetable flake is a good choice. They also enjoy frozen brine shrimp. Tankmates: Platies get along with most peaceful community fish, such as other livebearers (mollies, guppies and swordtails), tetras, rasboras and corydoras. Avoid large or aggressive fish that may bully or eat them. Breeding: Platies are livebearers, so a tank with males and females will almost certainly have babies (fry). Adults will eat fry, so add dense plants or use a breeding box if you want to raise them. Keeping more females than males gives the females a break from the males' attention. Good to know: Platies are one of the easiest fish to keep, which makes them a great choice for a first aquarium.
Weco Wonder Plants - Freshwater Pro Series Red Cabomba - realistic and keeps its color long term under aquarium lighting and water conditions.
Weco Wonder Plants - Freshwater Pro Series Tonina - natural stemmed plant with lots of space to protect small fish and pretty flowing feature.

Amazon Ruffled Sword (Realistic plastic) Weco Wonder Plants - Freshwater Pro Series - Amazon Sword Amazon sword have long broad leaves and offer a nice contrast to narrow stemmed plants. The plastic will not fade or fall apart and these plants are safe for all aquatic species.
Weco Wonder Plants - Freshwater Pro Series Red Ludwigia - realistic and will not fade or fall apart and designed with fish comfort in mind.
Weco Wonder Plants - Dream Series Magenta Tulips Magenta tulips are popular decorative plants that may not actually live in nature but sure make the aquarium come alive.

Weco Wonder Plants - Dream Series Pink Princess Feather - lovely fantasy colors from the WECO dream series makes aquariums come alive, particularly under lighted night time conditions. All plastic plants offered by AquariumFishSale are fish safe.

Weco Wonder Plants - Dream Series - Fuschia Fern Fuschia Fern - maybe not found in nature but what a pretty plant for the aquarium and these plants do not lose color and the aquarium plastic plants are safe for all aquatic species.
Weco Wonder Plants - Dream Series Orange Pom Pom - part of the WECO dream series, these fantasy plants bring amazing color to the fish tank.

Aquarium Hash Aquarium Hash - not really appropriate for kids aquariums, we do have a few people that do like this selection of whimsy from Weco Products. Don't get too excited - these are only plastic.

Sera Betta Starter Kit Betta can be picky. Don't panic when you see your betta resting on a rock or bottom of the tank, this is normal. With those over developed fins they need to take a break from time to time. But clamped fins, not exited to eat may be signs they are not acclimating to their home. Sera Betta Stater offers peace of mind that you are doing what you can for your pet with the best nutrition with sera bettagran and sera aquatan for improved water conditions.
Sera Goldfish Starter Kit Goldfish, particularly fancy goldfish, look hardy but they do need special care. Sera offers the perfect goldfish food and water conditioner to give your pet a great start.

Sera Tropical Fish Starter Kit Why guess when SERA offers a basic starter kit complete with community fish food and water conditioner. The conditioner takes chlorine out of tap water for water changes and adds back minerals and tannins for fish friendly water.

This fish is for an exclusive club. The largest and most ancient fish species is the sturgeon fish. Smaller than some of its cousins, the Siberian sturgeon is suitable for ponds with an area that does not get much over 75 degrees, or super large aquariums. And suitable for caviar, though the caviar will have to wait a few years. These fish take a long time to grow to maturity and can outlive the owner (if the owner is as old as this writer). Research, research, and be ready if you want to invest in this rare and exotic species. Though endangered in Central Asia due to overpopulation and loss of habitat, these fish are pond raised in Florida and plentiful. Quick Facts Scientific Name Acipenser baerii Origin Siberia and Central Asia (pond-raised in Florida) Care Level Difficult (grows very large) Temperament Peaceful Adult Size Up to 6 feet in the wild; much smaller in ponds Lifespan 30+ years Diet Carnivore (sinking pellets) Water Temperature 50–74°F pH 7.0–7.8 Group Size Single or group Shipping Size Approx. 6" Care Guide Tank setup: Sturgeon are cold-water fish best suited to large outdoor ponds with cool, very clean, well-oxygenated water and a smooth bottom. They do not do well in warm water. Feeding: Feed sinking sturgeon pellets once a day. Sturgeon feed from the bottom and cannot reach floating food. Tankmates: Sturgeon are peaceful and get along with koi and other pond fish, but they can be outcompeted for food, so make sure food sinks to them. Good to know: Sturgeon have no scales, just rows of bony plates, and belong to one of the oldest groups of fish on Earth.

Gold Tiger Scat, African Tiger Scat, or Somalian Tiger Scat: they all refer to the rarest and hardiest of the scat family. The Tiger Scat is tough - these fish thrive in 100 percent freshwater and tolerate a wide pH range. They are very active and need room to swim and grow. Speaking of growing, these guys will grow to 20 inches and eat plants, community flake food, lettuce from the kitchen, and veggie cichlid pellets. Tiger Scats are big and active, but they are VERY PEACEFUL to other fish - they do not harm even the smallest peaceful species. However, they will bump each other constantly as they compete for any veggies in the fish tank. Quick Facts Scientific Name Scatophagus tetracanthus Origin East Africa Care Level Easy Temperament Very peaceful Adult Size Up to 12–16" Lifespan 10+ years Diet Omnivore (needs plant matter) Water Temperature 72–82°F pH 7.0–8.5 Group Size Does best in a group Shipping Size Approx. 1" Care Guide Tank setup: Tiger scats are tough, active swimmers that grow large. They do well in fresh water and also tolerate slightly salty (brackish) water. Give them open swimming space and strong filtration. Feeding: Feed a quality flake or pellet once or twice a day. They also enjoy vegetable foods and frozen foods like brine shrimp. Tankmates: Tiger scats are very peaceful with other fish, even small ones. Good to know: Tiger scats are big eaters of plant matter and will eat soft aquarium plants.

Sera Filter Wool Filter wool gathers floating debris for easy periodic rinsing and absorbs unwanted contaminants in the water. Each bag comes with 3.5 oz of fish safe wool material for any type of filter.

Pogostenum Pogostenum is an open narrow leaf plant that allows small fish to swim through but contributes a very nice branchy green display. Good grower, needs moderate light. Scientific Name: Pogostenum stellatus Shipping Size: Potted or bunched w weight, five inches

HG915-4000 Water Pump The Hygger HG0915 pump moves water at a rate of 1060 gallons per hour for large aquariums, ponds, and fountains. This DC powered pump is even adjustable and comes with controller. Compare to anything found at Home Depot or Lowes.
Cross Flow Pump Sine wave technology creates a wave across the length of the fish tank. Controller adjusts the flow to the desired movement for mid to large size aquariums (20 to 120 gallons).

The Hygger HG908 is a small, single sponge filter that works off a small air pump (not included) and sticks right on the side of the bowl or aquarium. Perfect for goldfish bowls, betta bowls, shrimp tanks and other small aquarium set ups. Key Features Integrates biofiltration, oxygenation, and physical filtration to maintain excellent water quality Super Mini design fits tanks or bowls from 0.5 to 5 gallons, taking up minimal space Enhanced Bio-Filtration to Fine Sponge enhances the surface area for beneficial bacteria, promoting a healthy aquatic environment Sponge is easily removable for cleaning or replacement, rinsed with aquarium water to preserve beneficial bacteria Simple setup and maintenance instructions ensure hassle-free operation for beginners and experts alike What's In The Box? 1x Spare Sponge 1x Suction Cup 1x Single Mini Sponge Filter

Product Features Dual-mag brush, efficient clean, scratch-free felt pad. (Caution: Keep the pad clear of sand to avoid glass scratches.) Double-sided magnetic cleaner: High-quality magnet, firm fit, smooth cleaning for glass up to 5/8″ thick. Detachable scraper: Effective algae removal, easy replacement, safe handling. Auto floating brush: Easily retrieve with magnetic pull, no need to reach in. Correct usage: Ergonomic handle, smooth movement, store separately to avoid sticking. Enhanced Ergonomics for Hygger Aquarium Cleaner Brush: The hygger aquarium cleaner brush features an innovative dual-sided magnetic design that simplifies the cleaning process. It allows you to clean the exterior of the tank while the interior is simultaneously scrubbed, with ease of movement up and down the tank walls. Following the exterior handle, cleaning becomes a hassle-free and enjoyable task, conserving your time and energy. The handle’s grip is designed for a comfortable hold that remains secure even when wet. When released, the magnetic brush floats to the surface, and its powerful magnetic force automatically attaches it to the exterior magnet for continuous cleaning. Fish Tank Cleaning Scrubber Details: This cleaner brush is composed of two magnetic brushes. The inner brush is equipped with a Velcro-hooks surface, ideal for scrubbing algae off the glass, while the exterior brush has a felt pad surface that effectively wipes away dust and water stains from the tank’s exterior. The design permits smooth vertical movement and the ability to navigate around corners to reach the tank’s opposite side. The stainless steel blade’s working surface is thoughtfully crafted with rounded edges, ensuring safety for both the aquarium and the user. Premium Double-Sided Magnetic Cleaner: The hygger aquarium cleaner utilizes high-quality neodymium magnets, ensuring a strong magnetic force that keeps the inner and outer brushes firmly attached. This feature allows for a smooth and effortless cleaning experience, and it is compatible with glass tanks up to 3/8″ in thickness. Easy-to-Replace Scraper: The hygger cleaner, equipped with plastic and stainless steel blades, allows quick scraper changes. To replace the scraper, simply press and push it out. Exercise caution when handling the sharp stainless steel blade to avoid injury. Convenient Auto Floating Feature: If the inner cleaner falls into the water, it is designed to float to the top of the tank. This allows you to quickly retrieve it using the magnetic pull from the outer cleaner without immersing your hand in the water.

Smaller & Stronger Air Pump Hygger fish tank air pump is smaller but stronger in power. It doesn’t take up space in aquariums. It is very suitable for use in both large and small freshwater and saltwater fish tanks. Adjust Air Output The oxygen output can be adjusted manually. You can adjust the appropriate air output by yourself according to the number and the characteristics of the fish, which is more beneficial to the tank creatures. Quiet Air Pump Although it has great power but has a small noise. The Hygger fish tank oxygen pump greatly reduces the noise by four raised rubber feet to isolate the transmission path of the noise, and the thickened ABS plastic seal effectively isolates noise, achieving a more ideal mute effect for household use. Two Pump Sizes to Choose Using the latest power system, the pump volume is very compact, but the oxygen output is increased. A variety of specifications and accessories can be selected according to needs. 2W Single - mini size air pump without accessories 2W is the single air pump, if you already have air stones, hoses, and check valves, and your fish tank height does not exceed 2.6ft, then you can choose this air pump model. 5-30 gallon aquariums 6W Set - double vent air pump with accessories Super powerful air pump with double air outlet, two air stones, two hoses, and complete accessories. when you have a large fish tank, it is recommended to get the 6W pump set. 70-100 gallon aquariums

Coral/Fish Feeding You can use the siphon kit as a coral feeder to feed liquid phytoplankton to corals or other aquatic pets. As a coral feeder, it can be used in marine reef tanks to feed coral directly, and is easy to control, it helps to keep your hands from getting wet. It can also be used in marine reef tanks to feed corals, reefs, anemones, lionfish, and so on, especially when caring for timid fish. The extension pipe allows slow fish feeding without wasting fish feed, it is an effective way to avoid contamination of water with excess fish feed.

Beautiful long tail (veil) angelfish are remarkable in the aquarium. Unless provoked, they generally glide around the middle zone of the fish tank. Marble veils sometimes have a little gold on the body but are primarily black and white. Quick Facts Scientific Name Pterophyllum scalare (veil-fin variety) Origin Amazon basin, South America (captive-bred) Care Level Easy Temperament Semi-aggressive (territorial when pairing) Adult Size Up to 6" long, with extra-long fins Lifespan 10+ years Diet Omnivore Water Temperature 75–82°F pH 6.0–7.5 Shipping Size Approx. 2" Care Guide Tank setup: Give them tall plants or driftwood, a heater and a gentle filter. Feeding: Feed a quality flake or small pellet once or twice a day, only as much as they eat in a couple of minutes. They also enjoy frozen foods like bloodworms and brine shrimp. Tankmates: Choose peaceful fish too large to swallow, such as larger tetras, corydoras, plecos, rams, gouramis and peaceful barbs. Avoid fin-nippers like tiger barbs, and small fish like neon tetras that adult angels may eat. Breeding: Angelfish pair off and lay eggs on flat surfaces like broad leaves or slate. A breeding pair can become territorial, so give them room and places for other fish to retreat. Good to know: Long veil fins are easy targets for fin-nippers and can get infected in dirty water, so keep the water clean and skip nippy tankmates.

The Albino Pacu is a natural mutation of the Red Belly Pacu and often found in the Amazon basin. Quick Facts Scientific Name Piaractus brachypomus Origin South America Care Level Easy (grows very large) Temperament Peaceful Adult Size Up to 30" Lifespan 15–20+ years Diet Omnivore (pellets, vegetables) Water Temperature 72–82°F pH 6.5–7.5 Group Size Single or group Shipping Size Approx. 2" Care Guide Tank setup: Pacu grow very large and fast. Give them open swimming space, strong filtration and a heavy, tight lid. Feeding: Feed a quality pellet once or twice a day. They also enjoy vegetables and fruit. Tankmates: Pacu are peaceful but very large, so keep them only with other large fish. Good to know: Pacu are cousins of piranhas but have flat, human-like teeth for crushing nuts and seeds. They grow very fast, so check their adult size before buying.

The Valentine catfish, or synodontis valentine, is a well known cross of the synodontis decorus and the synodontis multifasciatus. These catfish grow to four inches and have a very pretty body and face pattern - sort of a mix of leopard spots and zebra stripes. Quick Facts Scientific Name Synodontis hybrid Origin Captive-bred hybrid Care Level Easy Temperament Peaceful Adult Size Up to 4–5" Lifespan 10+ years Diet Omnivore Water Temperature 74–80°F pH 6.5–8.0 Group Size Single or group Shipping Size Approx. 1" Care Guide Tank setup: Give them caves, rocks or driftwood to hide in, and good filtration. They are most active at night. Feeding: Feed sinking pellets once a day, ideally in the evening. They also enjoy frozen foods like bloodworms. Tankmates: They get along with most fish of similar size, including many cichlids. They may eat very small fish. Good to know: Synodontis catfish often swim upside down under leaves and driftwood, which is normal behavior.

Maine Mocha Clownfish: A Unique & Hardy Designer Clownfish The Maine Mocha Clownfish (Amphiprion ocellaris) is a popular and striking designer variant of the classic Ocellaris Clownfish. This captive-bred species stands out with its beautiful chocolate-brown body and sharp, contrasting white bands, giving it a rich, sophisticated look. Like its Ocellaris relatives, the Maine Mocha is renowned for its peaceful temperament, hardiness, and entertaining swimming behavior. It's a fantastic choice for a community reef tank and is an ideal fish for both beginner hobbyists and experienced aquarists looking for a unique centerpiece. Why the Maine Mocha Clownfish is a Great Choice: Unique Designer Coloration: Its deep mocha color and crisp white stripes make it a one-of-a-kind addition. Peaceful Temperament: It is a non-aggressive species that coexists well with other peaceful tank mates. Hardy & Resilient: This captive-bred species is known for its resilience and adaptability, making it an excellent choice for a variety of tank conditions. Reef-Safe: The Maine Mocha Clownfish is completely safe to keep with all types of corals and invertebrates. Quick Facts Scientific Name: Amphiprion ocellaris Origin: Captive-bred (Designer Variety) Max Size: 3 inches Lifespan: 10 years or more Diet: Omnivore. A varied diet of high-quality frozen foods, marine pellets, and algae. Shipping Size: 1-1.5 inches

An assorted lot of four should contain at least three different bright color variations. If you wish us to avoid a color or go heavy on a color, please let us know! Quick Facts Scientific Name Aulonocara (assorted line-bred varieties) Origin Lake Malawi, Africa Care Level Easy to moderate Temperament Semi-aggressive (males territorial) Adult Size Up to 5–6" Lifespan 8–10 years Diet Omnivore (meaty foods) Water Temperature 76–82°F pH 7.8–8.6 Group Size Sold as a lot of 4 Shipping Size Medium: approx. 2" · Large: approx. 3" · Jumbo: approx. 4" Care Guide Tank setup: Give them a sand bottom, open swimming space in front and rockwork along the back. Lake Malawi and Lake Tanganyika cichlids need hard, alkaline water; crushed coral or aragonite sand helps hold the pH up. Feeding: Feed a quality cichlid pellet or flake once or twice a day. They also enjoy frozen foods like brine shrimp. Tankmates: Haps do well with peacocks and other haps of similar size, plus robust catfish like synodontis. Keep one male per similar-looking species, with several females, to limit fighting and crossbreeding. Good to know: Males take a year or more to show full adult color, and color best when females are present.

Lot Size: 4 Quick Facts Scientific Name Carassius auratus Origin Japan (now bred in the USA) Care Level Very easy, extremely hardy Temperament Peaceful, very active Adult Size Up to 10" or more in ponds Lifespan 10–15 years; 20+ years in ponds Diet Omnivore Water Temperature 50–75°F (tolerates cold winters in ponds) pH 7.0–8.0 Group Size Sold as a lot of 4 Shipping Size Approx. 3" Care Guide Tank setup: Shubunkins are fast, active swimmers that grow big and produce a lot of waste. They do very well in outdoor ponds; indoors, use a strong filter. Feeding: Feed small amounts of a quality sinking pellet or flake once or twice a day, only as much as they eat in a couple of minutes. They also enjoy frozen foods like bloodworms and brine shrimp. Tankmates: Keep them with other single-tail goldfish like comets and shubunkins, or with koi in a pond. Avoid slow fancy goldfish, which can't compete for food, and tropical fish, which need warmer water. Ponds: This is where they shine. They handle cold winters as long as part of the pond stays deep enough not to freeze solid. Stop feeding when the water drops below about 50°F. Good to know: Shubunkins grow quickly and are well suited to ponds.

AquariumFish.com selected a mix of Pseudotropheus, Melanochromis, and Labeotropheus that will grow well together and display a wonderful mix of colors and patterns. The assortment is a great way to start a new cichlid tank! Lot of 4 Quick Facts Scientific Name Pseudotropheus , Melanochromis and Labeotropheus spp. Origin Lake Malawi, Africa Care Level Moderate Temperament Aggressive (territorial rock-dweller) Adult Size Up to 4–6", depending on species Lifespan 6–10 years Diet Omnivore (needs plant matter) Water Temperature 76–82°F pH 7.8–8.6 Group Size Sold as a lot of 4 Shipping Size Small: approx. 1" · Medium: approx. 2" · Large: approx. 3" Care Guide Tank setup: Use a sand or crushed-coral bottom and stack plenty of rockwork with caves and hiding spots so each male can claim a territory and others can escape. Lake Malawi and Lake Tanganyika cichlids need hard, alkaline water; crushed coral or aragonite sand helps hold the pH up. Feeding: Mbuna are mostly plant eaters. Feed a vegetable-based flake or pellet once or twice a day, and avoid high-protein foods, which can upset their digestion. Tankmates: Keep mbuna with other mbuna of similar size and temperament, stocked in a group to spread out aggression. Avoid mixing them with peaceful peacocks and haps unless the tank is large, and avoid closely related species that look alike, which can crossbreed. Good to know: A mixed group of mbuna spreads out aggression. Adding all fish at the same time, with lots of rockwork, helps them settle in.

The most common colors of oranda goldfish are bright orange, and orange and white. A school of oranda goldfish is striking in the pond or the aquarium with their round bodies and distinctive crowns of different colors. As more colors become available this season, we will add to the description of the assorted group. The Oranda name comes from the Dutch phrase Lionhead because the English aquatic trade thought the origin of this variety was Holland. Nope, all the selective breeding took place in China. Lionhead goldfish also share the bubble formation at the head, called a crown or wen, but have been further bred to remove the dorsal fin so that the round body and bubble formation are more accented. Note: Our stock of Orandas is young and does not have the developed wen seen in the images. The wen develops when they mature. Lot of 4 Quick Facts Scientific Name Carassius auratus Origin China Care Level Easy, good for beginners Temperament Peaceful Adult Size Up to 8" Lifespan 10–15 years, often longer with good care Diet Omnivore Water Temperature 65–75°F (no heater needed in most homes) pH 7.0–8.0 Group Size Sold as a lot of 4 Shipping Size Medium: approx. 2" · Jumbo: approx. 5" Care Guide Tank setup: Orandas produce a lot of waste, so give them plenty of room and a strong filter. Feeding: Feed small amounts of a quality sinking pellet or flake once or twice a day, only as much as they eat in a couple of minutes. They also enjoy frozen foods like bloodworms and brine shrimp. Tankmates: Keep them with other fancy goldfish of similar size and speed. Avoid fast single-tail goldfish like comets and shubunkins, which will outcompete them for food. Also avoid tropical fish, which need warmer water, and fin-nippers. Ponds: Orandas can live in ponds in mild climates, but they are less cold-hardy than comets and shubunkins. Bring them indoors where winters are harsh, and keep them away from fast, aggressive pond fish. Good to know: The wen (crown) keeps growing for the first couple of years and can trap debris, so clean water is the key to a healthy, full wen.

Very easy-to-keep fish for beginners. They are livebearing fish, and the females give birth throughout their lifetime. The balloon shape of this class of fish makes them very appealing in peaceful fish tanks. A group of four will have males and females in the mix. Quick Facts Scientific Name Poecilia sphenops (balloon-bodied aquarium strain) Origin Mexico and Central America (wild ancestors); aquarium-bred Care Level Easy Temperament Peaceful Adult Size Up to 2½–3" Lifespan 3–4 years Diet Omnivore (needs plant matter) Water Temperature 75–82°F pH 7.5–8.5 (hard water) Group Size Sold as a school of 4 Shipping Size Approx. 1½" Care Guide Tank setup: Give them hard, alkaline water with plants and gentle filtration, since balloon mollies are slower swimmers than other mollies. Aquarium salt is optional; they also do well in brackish tanks. Feeding: Feed small amounts of a quality flake that includes vegetable matter once or twice a day. They also enjoy algae wafers. Avoid overfeeding, since balloon mollies are prone to bloating. Tankmates: Mollies get along with most peaceful community fish that like similar hard water, such as platies, swordtails, guppies, danios, rainbowfish, corydoras and plecos. Avoid fin-nippers and soft-water specialists. Keeping more females than males keeps any one female from being harassed. Good to know: The balloon shape comes from a shortened, curved spine bred into this strain, so they swim more slowly. Feed them where they can reach food easily and don't house them with fast, pushy eaters.

Rather than the long, slender body of the Common Goldfish or the Shubunkins, the Fantail Goldfish is one of the more rounded or egg-shaped fancy goldfish. These fish are bred for showing. Their main feature, the split tail fin, is medium in length and slightly forked. To be a good show specimen, the tail fin needs to be completely split, with the two lobes much closer together on top than on the bottom, making it look triangular when viewed from the back. Good show goldfish also have a double anal fin with complete separation. Those whose tail fins are not completely split won't win any prizes, but they still make great pets. Shipping size: approximately 2 inches. Fish pictured here are representative only. If you are looking for a specific coloration, add a note to the order or simply allow us to choose one of our favorites for you! Butterfly koi do not have the specific color patterns of the show koi sought by enthusiasts, but these hybrids feature long, flowing fins and beautiful colors of their own. Quick Facts Scientific Name Cyprinus carpio Origin Captive-bred (Asia) Care Level Easy Temperament Peaceful Adult Size Up to 2–3 feet Lifespan 25–35 years Diet Omnivore Water Temperature 50–80°F pH 7.0–8.5 Group Size Sold as a lot of 4 Shipping Size Approx. 3–4" Care Guide Tank setup: Koi grow large and are best kept in an outdoor pond with strong filtration. They are cool-water fish and do not need a heater. Feeding: Feed a quality koi or goldfish pellet once or twice a day, only as much as they eat in a few minutes. Feed less when the water is cool. Tankmates: Koi get along with goldfish and other pond fish. Good to know: Each lot is an assortment, so colors and patterns will vary.

The beautiful Ryukin Goldfish are a Japanese version of the fantail goldfish. They were developed from the common Fantail Goldfish. Like their Fantail counterpart, they are one of the more rounded or egg-shaped fancy goldfish. The Ryukin Goldfish are easily differentiated from the Fantail by their extremely high back, which is often described as a dorsal hump. The hump starts in the neck region and gives a more pointed appearance to the Ryukin's head. They also have a wider caudal fin than the Fantail. A distinguishing feature common to both the Fantail and the Ryukin Goldfish is their split or double caudal (tail) fin. A long-tailed version of this fish is called the Fringe-tail or Ribbon-tail Ryukin. This fish comes in a variety of colors: red, red and white, tri-color, calico, white, and chocolate. Quick Facts Scientific Name Carassius auratus Origin Captive-bred (Asia) Care Level Easy Temperament Peaceful Adult Size Up to 6–8" Lifespan 10–15 years Diet Omnivore Water Temperature 65–75°F pH 7.0–8.0 Group Size Sold as a lot of 4 Shipping Size Approx. 2–4" Care Guide Tank setup: Give them a strong filter and smooth decorations. Goldfish are cool-water fish and do not need a heater. Feeding: Feed a quality goldfish flake or pellet once or twice a day, only as much as they eat in a couple of minutes. They also enjoy frozen brine shrimp and bloodworms. Tankmates: Keep them with other fancy goldfish. Avoid fast or nippy fish, which outcompete them for food and pick at their fins. Good to know: Each lot is an assortment, so colors will vary.

These fish are fine in community tanks as long as they are not overstocked with many other fish. Mine seems fine with about 20 other fish, though. They eat flakes, pellets and frozen food. This one loves bloodworms. Make sure you feed them some flakes and/or pellets with vitamins and minerals too, though, to maintain good health. As with all livebearers, they are prolific breeders and are best kept in a "harem" ratio of one male to two or three females. This allows the females to have some relief from the males' constant pestering. Males have a modified pointed anal fin known as a "gonopodium", while this fin is held fanned out in females. Mollies are generally brackish water fish, meaning they like a salt level between that of true freshwater and full saltwater (usually with a specific gravity of 1.005 to 1.015). While they can be acclimated to freshwater, they still should have a higher pH, around 7.4 to 7.8, and will benefit from some aquarium salts. My tank is lightly salted at about 1 tablespoon per 10 gallons. Lot Size: 6 Male to female ratio approximately 1:1. Give them plants, open swimming space and good filtration, since they are active and produce a fair amount of waste. Aquarium salt is optional; they also do well in brackish tanks. Feeding: Mollies graze on algae, so feed a quality flake that includes vegetable matter once or twice a day. They also enjoy algae wafers and frozen brine shrimp. Sailfin mollies are robust and colorful livebearers. The male sailfin molly displays a giant dorsal fin to earn his namesake and will show it more often in the presence of females and other males. In the wild these fish can grow to nearly five inches but seldom get larger than three inches in the aquarium. Tank-raised albino pygmy cory are a rare find and very visible in the community fish tank, despite their diminutive size. Like most small fish, they are best kept in small schools of three or more to lower the stress. Quick Facts Scientific Name Corydoras pygmaeus (albino variety) Origin Captive-bred Care Level Easy Temperament Peaceful Adult Size Up to 1" Lifespan 3–4 years Diet Omnivore (bottom feeder) Water Temperature 72–79°F pH 6.0–7.5 Group Size Does best in a group Shipping Size Approx. ½" Care Guide Tank setup: Give them a gentle, sponge-type filter, a heater, fine sand and plenty of plants. Corys are sensitive to salt and some medications (especially copper), so check labels before treating the tank. Feeding: Feed tiny sinking pellets or crushed flake once or twice a day. Make sure the food reaches them before faster fish eat it all. Tankmates: Keep them with other tiny, gentle fish such as small rasboras, ember tetras, shrimp and bettas. Anything big enough to swallow them will. Good to know: Albino pygmy corys are easy to spot in a planted tank and, like regular pygmies, often school in midwater.

The L-519 Honeycomb Pleco, or L-519 Rio Iténez Pleco, is named for its very unique honeycomb color pattern on the body. This pleco originates in Brazil, but the batch we have was bred in the United States for the aquarium trade. Quick Facts Scientific Name Ancistrus sp. L-519 Origin Bolivia and Brazil (captive-bred in the USA) Care Level Easy Temperament Peaceful Adult Size Up to 4–5" Lifespan 10+ years Diet Herbivore (algae wafers) Water Temperature 75–82°F pH 6.0–7.5 Group Size Single, or several with a cave each Shipping Size Approx. 1¼" Care Guide Tank setup: Give them caves, driftwood and good filtration. They are most active at night. Feeding: Feed algae wafers and sinking pellets once a day, ideally in the evening when they are most active. They also enjoy frozen bloodworms. Tankmates: They are peaceful and get along with most community fish. Males may squabble over caves, so give each one its own hiding spot. Good to know: Male honeycomb plecos grow soft bristles on their snout as they mature, while females stay smoother-faced.

Not a true aquatic plant since it is generally partially submerged in the wild, the Brazil sword, or "spath", will tolerate full submersion for a few months but best if leaves can be allowed to grow out of the aquarium. It's not often the guys in Thailand release females for this variation but once in a while they do. Quick Facts Scientific Name Poecilia reticulata Origin Northern South America (captive-bred in Thailand) Care Level Easy Temperament Peaceful Adult Size Up to 2" Lifespan 2–3 years Diet Omnivore Water Temperature 72–82°F pH 7.0–8.0 Group Size Sold as a pair (1 male + 1 female) Shipping Size Approx. 1" Care Guide Tank setup: Give them a heater, a gentle filter and plenty of plants, including some floating plants where babies can hide. Guppies like slightly hard water. Feeding: Feed a quality flake or small pellet once or twice a day, only as much as they eat in a couple of minutes. They also enjoy frozen foods like bloodworms and brine shrimp. Tankmates: Guppies get along with other small, peaceful fish such as platies, mollies, corydoras, small tetras and rasboras. Avoid fin-nippers like tiger barbs and larger fish that could eat them. Breeding: Guppies are livebearers and breed easily. Females give birth to live babies about once a month, and adults will eat the babies, so thick plants give them a place to hide. Good to know: Dumbo ear guppies are named for their oversized, ear-like pectoral fins.
