Please check your local regulations before purchasing. We are unable to ship this species to these states. If you reside in one of the above states and try to checkout with this crayfish in your cart you will be unable to checkout and receive an error message until the crayfish is removed from the cart. We are thrilled to introduce the Blue Dragon Crayfish, an exceptionally rare color morph of Procambarus clarkii. This remarkable crustacean is renowned for its stunning appearance, and it owes its name to a Taiwanese breeder who recognized its resemblance to the timeless beauty of classic blue and white porcelain, a tradition dating back to 10th to 13th century China. Until now, the Blue Dragon Crayfish has been a rarity in the United States, but we are excited to be among the first stores to offer this unique specimen. Its reputation precedes it, thanks to its mesmerizing blue and white coloration. Each individual boasts a distinctive and intricate marbled pattern, blending shades of dark blue and bright white. When you receive these crayfish, they will be young adults with the potential for even more breathtaking coloration. Over the course of 2 to 6 months and through several molts, you will witness their captivating hues intensify, further echoing the elegance of that ancient art form, just as we had previously mentioned. 🦞🔵⚪ Don't miss out on the opportunity to add this rare gem to your collection! Though most crayfish are often reclusive by nature, this particular crayfish is very active by comparison and spends plenty of time exploring the floor of the aquarium in search of food. The Blue Dragon Crayfish is an omnivorous scavenger and will eat most any meaty or plant-based foods. This crayfish should not be kept with ornamental live plants as it will eat them at a surprising rate. It is a skilled climber, so extra care must be taken to ensure that it does not escape its enclosure. As it reaches adulthood, the Blue Dragon Crayfish will become relatively territorial, so it may behave aggressively towards other animals in the tank. It is important that ample hiding places such as rockwork, driftwood, or PVC pipes be provided. This is even more crucial when housing multiple crayfish in the same tank. Due to the size and waste production of this crayfish, a minimum 30-gallon, well-filtered aquarium is necessary for one adult. A larger aquarium can house multiple adults of similar size. This is a very hardy animal, but regular water changes are vital to its optimal health. Other bottom-dwelling invertebrates and fish should not be kept with large crayfish. It is possible to keep mid- and upper-level, fast-swimming fish with the Blue Dragon Crayfish, but crayfish are opportunistic feeders and will generally eat whatever they can catch. As with all of our crayfish, the coloration of the Blue Dragon Crayfish is EXTREMELY high quality. This crayfish may TEMPORARILY change color and hide more than usual after molting, which may occur during shipping. If your crayfish has faded color and you find a molt in the bag or in your aquarium, do not worry; this is normal and the bright color will return in 2 weeks or less What We Like About This Crayfish: Incredible Blue markings and white coloration that makes for a wonderful centerpiece to the aquarium Much more active than many crayfish species Hardy and adaptable Excellent scavenger RECOMMENDED TANK PARAMETERS: Temperature : 65 - 76° F (18 - 24° C) pH : 6.5 - 7.5 KH : 6 - 15 dKH Minimum tank size : 30 gallons CARE INFORMATION: Diet : Omnivorous. High-quality sinking pellets, plants, and freeze-dried or frozen meaty foods will be readily accepted. Cuttlebone should be added to the aquarium to supplement calcium, which will aid in exoskeleton production. Social behavior : Can be aggressive/territorial with its own kind. Crayfish will typically eat whatever they can catch, but since they are slow-moving, they are not often able to harm fast-moving fish. Origin : Tank-bred, but indigenous to Southeastern United States Average adult size : 4 - 5 inches (10 - 12.7 cm) body length, minus claws Average purchase size : Juveniles - 1+ inch (2.5+ cm), Young Adults - 1.5+ inches Recommended Aquatic Arts tank mates : Fast-moving fish (such as Celestial Pearl Danios , Rasboras , Guppies , etc.). While dwarf shrimp can be kept successfully with these crayfish, caution should be exercised, as the crayfish have been known to catch and eat slow, sick, or particularly small shrimp. Cichlids can be aggressive toward crayfish and should not be kept in the same tank. Bottom-dwelling tankmates should definitely be avoided. listings.description: * For the safety of our animals, we now ship live fish exclusively via UPS Next Day Air. If your order contains this item, you will only see UPS Next Day Air as a shipping option during checkout * Cochu’s Blue Tetra ( Boehlkea fredcochui ), also known as the Blue King Tetra, is an excellent choice for many medium to large community aquariums, especially planted aquariums. It is one of the few freshwater aquarium fish that has bright blue coloration. In the case of Cochu’s Blue Tetra, most blue coloration is on the back half of an otherwise nearly transparent body. There is also often pink coloration at the base of the tail. Males are usually more vividly marked than females. Cochu’s Blue Tetras typically occupy the top and middle level of the water column, although they can often be seen swimming and feeding in the middle and bottom levels as well. This tetra is safe with most other peaceful fish, provided that there is plenty of space in the aquarium. It is extremely active, especially at feeding time, so it can be intimidating to slower-moving fish and it may nip at long-finned fish. This harassing behavior is much less likely in a larger aquarium. Larger, peaceful invertebrates can also make good tankmates. This fish could possibly be kept with adult dwarf shrimp, but we do not recommend it in most aquariums due to the extremely active nature of this tetra. Cochu’s Blue Tetra must be kept in schools of 6 or more. Since it is tank-bred, this fish is very adaptable, but its natural habitat contains soft, acidic water that is rich in tannins and leaf litter. Its colors will be brightest with dark substrate. While not a picky eater, Cochu’s Blue Tetra will thrive and remain very colorful on a varied diet of meaty foods. High-quality flake food, pellets, and frozen or freeze-dried tubifex and bloodworms will all be readily accepted. What We Like About This Fish: Bright, neon blue coloration Peaceful disposition with most other fish Very active and noticeable fish in any aquarium Excellent for inhabiting the top of the aquarium RECOMMENDED TANK PARAMETERS: Temperature : 72° - 82° F (22.2° - 27.7° C) pH : 5.5 - 7.6 KH : 5 - 12 dKH Minimum tank size : 25 gallons CARE GUIDELINES: Diet : Omnivorous. Will easily accept high quality dry and frozen foods. Social behavior : Peaceful, schooling/shoaling. Origin : Tank-raised, but indigenous to South America. PLEASE READ: This species is a semi-terrestrial crab. NOT FULLY AQUATIC. Its habitat must be at least half (and preferably more) land with freshwater. It is an ideal paludarium animal. Our Vampire Crabs of different colors are not the same species and should not be kept together. *For the safety of our animals, we now ship Vampire Crabs exclusively via UPS Next Day Air. If your order contains this item, you will only see UPS Next Day Air as a shipping option during checkout * The Rainbow Vampire Crab is a fascinating semi-terrestrial species that is beautifully marked. It is communal with its own species and is an excellent choice for the paludarium, even nano-sized enclosures! The Rainbow Vampire Crab ( Geosesarma golden ) is a small, very colorful, semi-terrestrial species that is native to Java, Indonesia. It inhabits forest areas near streams, rivers, and ponds. It spends most of its time on land, but also often submerges in freshwater, including when it molts. It is communal with its own species, and males typically are larger than females, and also have much larger claws. In nature, the Rainbow Vampire Crab lives in leaf litter and vegetation. In the paludarium, it requires ample land area. It typically will not eat healthy plants, but it will often help keep them clean and it may consume dead leaves. Like most crabs, it needs plenty of cover, especially when molting, so lots of decor is necessary. While it is communal with its own species, it is often aggressive with other types of crabs, including other vampire crab species with which it competes in the wild. It is a skilled climber, so extra care must be taken to ensure that it does not escape its enclosure. Like most crabs, the Rainbow Vampire Crab is an omnivorous scavenger and an opportunistic hunter on occasion. It feeds on filamentous algae and detritus in the paludarium and will also readily accept high-quality dry foods that are rich in plant matter. Fresh and dried vegetables are also excellent food sources, as are insects, worms, and other invertebrates. Due to its opportunistic nature, the Rainbow Vampire Crab might eat other ornamental invertebrates and fish, so its tankmates must be chosen with great care. * IMPORTANT * Please "Choose a Variant" above before adding this crab to your cart. We offer a "B-Grade" variant for these crabs. Our “B-Grade” crabs are simply specimens that are missing legs or claws unless otherwise stated. Loss of appendages is not permanent and happens commonly with crustaceans. They are completely healthy with excellent coloration and will completely regenerate lost appendages within 1 to 2 molts. What We Like About This Crab : Generally peaceful with its own species Fascinating behavior and beautiful coloration Ideal for paludariums Easy to feed Excellent scavenger RECOMMENDED TANK PARAMETERS : Temperature : 75 ° - 82° F (24° - 28° C) pH: 7.5 - 8.0 KH : 4 - 10 dKH Humidity : 75+% Minimum tank size : 5 gallons for a male and 2 females. Larger colonies require larger tanks. CARE GUIDELINES : Diet : Omnivorous. High-quality sinking flakes and pellets, plants/algae, and freeze-dried or frozen meaty foods will be readily accepted. Cuttlebone or a similar material should be added to the aquarium to supplement calcium, which will aid in exoskeleton production Social behavior : Peaceful with its own species. May fight with or prey on other species. Origin : Java, Indonesia Average adult size : 2 inches (5 cm) or less Average purchase size : 1 - 2 inches (2.5 - 5 cm) All Aquatic Arts brand plants and animals come with a 100% live arrival guarantee, plus free email support!

Species Overview The Carnival Vampire Crab is one of the most colorful and eye-catching vampire crab species available in the hobby. Known for its vibrant mix of orange, yellow, purple, and red coloration, this species often appears as though it has been hand-painted. Combined with bright yellow eyes and an active personality, the Carnival Vampire Crab quickly becomes a centerpiece of any paludarium or tropical vivarium. At Aquatic Arts, we especially appreciate Carnival Vampire Crabs for their incredible color diversity and entertaining behavior. These fascinating crabs spend much of their time climbing, exploring, foraging, and interacting with their environment, making them exceptional inhabitants for planted paludariums and bioactive tropical enclosures. Their bright colors create beautiful contrast against green plants, mosses, natural wood, and leaf litter. What We Love About This Crab • Exceptional multi-colored appearance unlike most vampire crab species • Black eyes and a muli color carapace give a great coltrast • Active, curious, and entertaining behavior • Excellent choice for bioactive paludariums and tropical vivariums Quick Care Guide • Care Level: Moderate • Temperament: Generally peaceful with appropriate space and hiding places • Diet: Omnivorous scavenger that readily accepts prepared, frozen, and fresh foods • Source: Wild Collected • Average Adult Size: Approximately 1–1.5 Inches (2.5–3.8 cm) • Average Purchase Size: Approximately 0.75–1 Inch (1.9–2.5 cm) • Activity Level: Most active during morning, evening, and nighttime hours • Group Size: Social species; best maintained in small groups • Aquarium Type: Semi-terrestrial paludarium or vampire crab enclosure • Shrimp Compatibility: Not Recommended Enclosure Parameters • Minimum Enclosure Size: 10 Gallons • Temperature Range: 72–82°F (22–28°C) • Humidity Range: 75–90% • Water Depth: Shallow freshwater area with easy access to land • Water Type: Freshwater • pH Range: 6.5–8.0 • Recommended Land Area: 70–80% • Recommended Water Area: 20–30% Important Information Semi-Terrestrial Species Carnival Vampire Crabs are not fully aquatic crabs and cannot be maintained in a traditional aquarium. This species requires a paludarium-style enclosure that provides both land and water areas. Long-term success depends on providing adequate terrestrial space, proper humidity, and easy access to freshwater. While Carnival Vampire Crabs are generally social with their own kind, we strongly recommend maintaining only a single species of vampire crab per enclosure. Mixing different Geosesarma species can result in territorial disputes, competition for resources, stress, injury, and potential hybridization. listings.description: Live Moina Macrocopa (Water Flea) Culture, Bred By Aquatic Arts Experience the ultimate in live feed with Aquatic Arts' Live Moina Macrocopa (Water Flea) Culture! Perfect for both novice and seasoned aquarists, our live Moina culture is the ideal solution for providing nutritious and live feed to your fish and aquatic pets. What is Moina Macrocopa? Moina Macrocopa, commonly known as water fleas, are small freshwater crustaceans belonging to the order Cladocera. They are part of the larger family of Daphniidae, but Moina are distinct from the more commonly known Daphnia. Here are some key details about Moina Macrocopa: Physical Characteristics: Size: Moina Macrocopa are small, typically ranging from 0.3 to 1.0 mm in length, making them slightly smaller than their Daphnia relatives. Body Structure: They have a transparent, oval-shaped body with a single large compound eye. Their body is covered by a shell called a carapace, and they have a pair of antennae used for swimming. Reproduction: Moina can reproduce both sexually and asexually. Under favorable conditions, they reproduce asexually through parthenogenesis, which allows for rapid population growth. Habitat: Environment: Moina Macrocopa are found in a variety of freshwater environments, including ponds, lakes, and slow-moving rivers. They thrive in nutrient-rich waters and can tolerate a wide range of temperatures and water conditions. Adaptability: They are highly adaptable and can survive in environments with low oxygen levels, making them hardy and easy to cultivate in aquariums. Diet: Feeding Habits: Moina are filter feeders, consuming bacteria, algae, and other small organic particles suspended in the water. This diet makes them an important part of the aquatic food web, as they help control algae levels and recycle nutrients. Key Features: High-Quality Live Feed: Moina Macrocopa are known for their excellent nutritional value, making them a superior choice for feeding fry, small fish, and other aquatic pets. Rich in Protein: These water fleas are an exceptional source of protein, promoting healthy growth and vibrant coloration in your aquatic life. Easy to Cultivate: Our culture comes with simple instructions, making it easy to maintain and cultivate your own live feed supply at home. Chemical-Free: Grown in a controlled environment, our Moina Macrocopa culture is free from harmful chemicals and pathogens, ensuring the safety of your fish and aquatic pets. Natural Behavior Stimulation: Watching your fish hunt and consume live prey encourages natural feeding behaviors, providing both mental and physical stimulation. CLICK HERE to read our blog post for more detailed information on how to keep your culture going! Benefits: Enhanced Growth: The high-protein diet helps fry and small fish grow quickly and healthily. Improved Coloration: Regular feeding with Moina Macrocopa can enhance the natural colors of your fish. Healthier Fish: The live prey encourages natural hunting behavior, leading to more active and healthy fish. Sustainable Feed Source: Cultivating your own Moina culture provides a continuous and reliable source of live feed, reducing the need for processed fish food. Ideal For: Freshwater aquariums Fry and juvenile fish Small fish species Breeders and hobbyists seeking to enhance the health and coloration of their fish Moina Macrocopa vs. Daphnia: Size: Moina Macrocopa are smaller than Daphnia, making them an excellent choice for feeding fry and small fish that might struggle with larger prey. Reproduction Rate: Moina reproduce faster than Daphnia, providing a more consistent and abundant food source for your aquarium. Nutritional Value: Both Moina and Daphnia are highly nutritious, but Moina are particularly rich in protein and fats, which are essential for the rapid growth and development of young fish. Ease of Cultivation: Moina Macrocopa are easier to culture in a wider range of conditions compared to Daphnia, which often require more specific water parameters and care. Environmental Tolerance: Moina can thrive in a variety of water conditions and are more resilient to changes in water quality, while Daphnia are more sensitive and may require more careful monitoring.

listings.description: African Water Fern is an extremely undemanding, yet very elegant plant that thrives in low-light setups! The African Water Fern ( Bolbitis heudelotii ), also known as the Congo Fern or Bolbitis Narrow Leaf, is a popular but uncommon plant that is highly in demand for the freshwater aquarium. Its long, flowing, dark green leaves are very elegant and delicate in appearance. Unlike many plants, the African Water Fern attaches itself to and propagates on aquarium décor as an epiphyte. African Water Fern is relatively rare because it is very slow growing. It only requires low to moderate lighting and nutrient rich soil, although its growth rate can be increased through CO 2 injection/supplementation. It reproduces through rhizome division and the production of offshoots, and it thrives in areas with strong water currents. African Water Fern should not be planted with its rhizome (roots) buried in the substrate because it will rot and recede. Instead, it can be attached to rocks, driftwood, and other decorations in the aquarium, or it can be planted on top of the substrate as long as the roots are not completely buried. Due to its delicate leaves, it should never be housed with large crayfish, medium to large cichlids, goldfish, or any other animals that are prone to picking at plants. CO 2 supplementation is beneficial, but not necessary for this plant. Like most plants, African Water Fern will benefit from supplementation such as Seachem Flourish, Flourish Excel, Nitrogen and other plant supplements. It has phenomenal coloration, it attains a small adult size, and it is a durable, hardy species for the Amazon biotope as well as other planted and community setups! The L134 Leopard Frog Pleco ( Peckoltia compta ), also known as the Imperial Tiger Pleco, is a member of the Loricariidae family of South American suckermouth catfishes. Its bright yellow and black, zebra-like striping combined with its relatively outgoing personality make it a very striking fish for the planted or nano aquarium. The color of the stripes can range from a cream to a yellow color. Like many plecos, the Leopard Frog Pleco has generally been a wild-caught species, but we are proud to be among the first stores to offer tank-raised juveniles at a much lower cost than wild-caught specimens! A generally peaceful and hardy species, the Leopard Frog Pleco is an excellent, undemanding candidate for most aquariums. Unlike the widely-seen Common Pleco ( Hypostomus plecostomus ) and Trinidad Pleco ( Hypostomus punctatus ), which easily reach a monstrous size of 18 to 20+ inches (45 to 51+ cm), the Leopard Frog Pleco grows to a size of only 3.5 to 4.2 inches (8.9 to 10.7 cm). This smaller size makes for a much more manageable (and less messy) pleco that can thrive permanently in a well-maintained aquarium as small as 30 to 40 gallons. Male plecos may be somewhat territorial with other males of their species, but disputes can usually be diffused by providing ample territory and hiding places for each fish. All other tankmates will be generally ignored, although it is possible that small shrimp fry might fall prey to the Leopard Frog Pleco. However, some large-scale shrimp suppliers breed Leopard Frog Plecos in the same pools they use for shrimp breeding. The Leopard Frog Pleco is primarily nocturnal, but will often become active during daytime hours once established in an aquarium with plenty of driftwood, rockwork, and other hiding places. It is not known to eat wood heavily like some plecos ( Panaque sp ., etc.), but it may benefit from some supplementary wood (or bio-film on driftwood). The Leopard Frog Pleco will not bother most plants and it is not an effective algae eater. Feed the Leopard Frog Pleco a diet heavy in meaty foods supplemented with vegetable matter, including high-quality vegetable flakes, sinking algae wafers, and pellets. This omnivorous species requires a high-protein diet rich in meaty foods and will enjoy frozen foods such as bloodworms and Tubifex. listings.commonName: Anubias nana (Anubias barteri var. “nana”) - Bare Root, EXTRA LARGE
listings.description: Anubias nana ( Anubias barteri var. “Nana” ) is a well-known variant of Anubias nana that is well known in the aquarium hobby due to its attractive appearance, durability, and ease of care. Its thick, deep green leaves stand out and provide valuable refuge for aquatic animals. Like virtually all Anubias plants, it is extremely hardy, undemanding, and can thrive in a variety of water parameters. We are offering this plant as an oversized portion with unusually large leaves and a generous size that is at least 3 TIMES the size of most Anubias plants ! Care for Anubias nana is identical to other Anubias plants. Its ideal placement in the aquarium is in the middle ground, and it will look its best under low to moderate lighting. Excessive lighting can result in unattractive, pesky algae growth on its leaves. However, this algae growth can easily be kept under control in an aquarium with a healthy population of shrimp (especially Amano shrimp) that will constantly graze on the algae without harming the Anubias plant itself. Most herbivorous animals will not harm Anubias nana whatsoever, although some bio-fim or ”wood-eating” Panaque genus plecos may “chew” holes in its leaves. Like many Anubias species, this plant is slow and steady in growth and does not seem to respond significantly to CO 2 supplementation. It does best when attached to driftwood or rockwork. It can be planted in the substrate but its rhizome (roots) must not be buried in the substrate because it will rot and recede. It can also be planted emersed in terrariums, paludariums, and viquariums. No aquarium plant distributor/nursery/wholesaler/retailer can or will guarantee their plants to be 100% snail free. We can not guarantee our plants will be snail free. listings.description: Fissidens Nobilis Moss ( Fissidens nobilis ), is a very rare Southeast Asian aquatic moss that is occasionally available for the freshwater aquarium. This plant is a very fluffy, lush green plant with palm-like stems that will attach to most surfaces and can eventually grow into a large mat of impressive size. Like many similar plants, it provides refuge for shrimp and fish fry and makes for an attractive and useful grazing area for shrimp. It can be easily attached to driftwood and rockwork. It is very slow-growing and requires low to moderate lighting. We offer this moss in a solid stainless steel mat form that makes it easy to attach to and begin propagating on rocks, driftwood, or aquarium walls and substrate. The moss is grown outdoors in Taiwan, and may contain a few pest snails or terrestrial bugs (the bugs will not survive or reproduce underwater). Fissidens Nobilis Moss is a very easy plant to keep without much extra care, but like all plants, it can benefit from CO 2 supplementation (although this is not required). Like many mosses, it does not typically respond positively to most chemical plant supplements. Many aquarists report success with this moss purely through keeping a well-maintained aquarium with no supplementation. No aquarium plant distributor/nursery/wholesaler/retailer can or will guarantee their plants to be 100% snail free. We can not guarantee our plants will be snail free. Also known by the names Red Torpedo Barb and Roseline Shark, the Denison’s Barb ( Sahyadria denisonii ) is one of the most strikingly colorful and active fish available for the freshwater aquarium. It has become extremely popular among aquarists over the past few years, and a few commercial breeding programs have been developed to ensure its longevity in the aquarium hobby. The Denison’s Barb is known for its incredible bright red coloration, as well as its peaceful disposition. It is a very hardy species that will thrive in most community and planted aquariums of appropriate size. Care is simple for the Denison’s Barb. It is tolerant of a wide range of water parameters, but it will thrive in an aquarium with ample filtration and moderate to high water flow. This active fish is known to jump occasionally, so a secure aquarium lid is recommended. It will readily eat most high-quality dry foods, but it should also be offered fresh vegetables such as zucchini and cucumber as well as meaty frozen or freeze-dried foods. As stated above, the Denison’s Barb is a peaceful fish, but it will prey on dwarf shrimp and other very small invertebrates. It does not seem to bother most snails, and we have found it to be generally peaceful with most larger shrimp (such as Amano, Flower, Green Lace, and Vampire Shrimp) as long as they are too large to be considered easy prey. The Denison’s Barb is a schooling fish that should be kept in a group of at least 6 to 8 fish. If these requirements are met, the Denison’s Barb is an excellent aquarium fish that is worthy of being the centerpiece of any peaceful aquarium! If your order contains this item, you will only see UPS Next Day Air as a shipping option during checkout * The L201 Snowball Pleco is an uncommon pleco that displays a striking pattern and stays a very manageable size! The L201 Snowball Pleco ( Hypancistrus sp. ), also known as the Orinoco Angel Pleco, is a member of the Loricariidae family of South American suckermouth catfishes. Its black body with large white polka dots makes it a very striking fish for the planted or nano aquarium. A generally peaceful and hardy species, the Snowball Pleco is an excellent, undemanding candidate for most aquariums. Unlike the widely-seen Common Pleco (Hypostomus plecostomus ) and Trinidad Pleco ( Hypostomus punctatus ), which easily reach a monstrous size of 18 to 20+ inches (45 to 51+ cm), the Snowball Pleco grows to a size of only 5.5 to 6.3 inches (14 to 16 cm). This smaller size makes for a much more manageable (and less messy) pleco that can thrive permanently in a well-maintained aquarium as small as 40 gallons. Male plecos may be somewhat territorial with other males of their species, but disputes can usually be diffused by providing ample territory and hiding places for each fish. All other fish tankmates will be generally ignored, although it is likely that dwarf shrimp will fall prey to the Snowball Pleco. However, ornamental snails will not be bothered and large Amano, Green Lace, Flower, and Vampire Shrimp are generally unthreatened by the Snowball Pleco. The Snowball Pleco is primarily nocturnal, but will often become active during daytime hours once established in an aquarium with plenty of driftwood, rockwork, and other hiding places. It is not known to eat wood heavily like some plecos ( Panaque sp ., etc.), but it may benefit from some supplementary wood (or bio-film on driftwood). The Snowball Pleco will not bother most plants and it is not an effective algae-eater. Feed the Snowball Pleco a diet heavy in both meaty and vegetable matter, including high-quality vegetable flakes, sinking algae wafers, and pellets. It will also appreciate being fed some fresh vegetables such as shelled peas, spinach, zucchini and cucumber. Meaty foods such as bloodworms are definitely necessary for this species, especially in comparison to some other “pleco” species. This species requires a well-maintained aquarium with moderate to high water flow in order to thrive. What We Like About This Fish: The Snowball Pleco is an extremely beautiful and very peaceful, hardy addition to almost any aquarium. At a maximum size of 5.5 to 6.3 inches, this is a very practical and manageable fish. This fish will not bother most plants. It will also scavenge and consume most uneaten fish food. The Snowball Pleco is an aquarium fish with a unique appearance as well as plenty of personality. If your order contains this item, you will only see UPS Next Day Air as a shipping option during checkout * The Gold Neon Dwarf Goby ( Stiphodon percnopterygionus ) is a very rare freshwater dwarf goby that is native to Japan, Taiwan, and Micronesia. It is known for the neon blue and neon gold-orange color phases that male specimens display. Females are not as colorful, but are still very attractively marked with horizontal black and cream-colored stripes. This fascinating, peaceful fish is an algae and biofilm grazer that is an excellent candidate for the mature nano aquarium. An aquarium with heavy water flow (10 to 15 times turnover per hour) and very clean, clear water is required for the Gold Neon Dwarf Goby. This fish is native to shallow, clear, fast-flowing waters and it is sensitive to declines in water quality, so regular aquarium maintenance is a must. The Gold Neon Dwarf Goby is a biofilm and algae grazer in nature. It is known to usually accept frozen meaty foods, but such foods should only be fed occasionally. This fish will also sometimes accept high-quality dry foods that are rich in plant matter, but it is absolutely essential that biofilm and algae are naturally available in the aquarium to ensure its long-term health or else it may slowly starve. As long as it is kept in a well-maintained, mature aquarium with good biofilm and algae growth as well as high water flow, the Gold Neon Dwarf Goby is a hardy and entertaining fish. It will not bother aquarium plants. In fact, Anubias species are an excellent plant to keep with this goby because Anubias can foster significant biofilm/algae growth in an aquarium with moderate to high lighting. Most small rasboras, tetras, hillstream loaches, and other small, peaceful fish are good tankmates for the Gold Neon Dwarf Goby. Due to its small size and diet, the Gold Neon Dwarf Goby can also be kept with dwarf shrimp, although it might eat a few of their fry. Dwarf shrimp are particularly good tankmates in larger aquariums where they can find areas of lower water flow. Peaceful bottom-dwelling fish are also a possibility, but care must be taken to make sure that the passive Gold Neon Dwarf Goby is not outcompeted for food. Female Gold Neon Dwarf Gobies will often congregate together, even with other goby species such as the Blue Neon Dwarf Goby. Males seem to be able to differentiate between females of different species during courtship behavior. There are reported cases of the Gold Neon Dwarf Goby spawning in the aquarium, but it is very difficult (if not currently impossible) to raise the fry due to their complex larval stages. In nature, adults spawn and their fry hatch in freshwater, then they are immediately swept downstream to marine ocean waters where they feed and develop. As the fry mature, they swim great distances back to full freshwater streams, often on completely different islands than where they originated. At this point, the fry have become young adults are will soon be sexually mature and exhibit adult coloration. listings.description: This Deluxe Java Moss is among the highest quality available anywhere! This is the famous Java Moss (Taxiphyllum barbieri / Vesicularia dubyana ) which probably needs no introduction. It is certainly the most popular and easy-to-grow live moss in the aquarium hobby. This DELUXE Java Moss is grown completely submerged and is in INCREDIBLE condition with completely deep green color and very long shoots. It is by far the highest-quality Java Moss we have ever sold and the best you fill find anywhere! Java Moss is a vibrant green moss that is particularly excellent for aquariums that house fish, snails, and dwarf shrimp, as it provides biofilm, hiding places, and security for all aquarium inhabitants. If you breed shrimp or fish, the fry will find vital refuge in the plant cover. Java Moss is very low-maintenance; it can be kept in any freshwater aquarium and does not need special supplementation or high-intensity lighting. This Java Moss ships as a loose portion. It can also be grown along the rear glass of your aquarium for an impressive live plant backdrop effect! Java Moss also removes pollutants from the water by reducing nitrates and providing some dissolved oxygen, which will greatly benefit any animals in the aquarium. Plant Profile Cardamine lyrata, also known as Japanese Cress or Chinese Ivy, is an expressive East Asian marsh plant that brings a charming, vine‑like texture to aquascapes. Its light‑green, clover‑like leaves trail along fine, creeping stems, giving tanks a soft, whimsical touch. Highly adaptable, it can form lush midground bushes, creep into a low foreground carpet under high light and CO₂, or float at the surface to create a cozy canopy for fish fry and dwarf shrimp. It's a plant that’s basically happy anywhere you let it grow! *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Clover-like foliage trails and adds visual texture. Dense growth shelters fish fry, shrimp, and shy tank inhabitants. Natural nutrient sponge that helps keep water clarity high. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight (or pot) and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the roots, then strip lower foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stem clumps 1 to 2 inches into substrate, or allow stem clusters to float freely along the water surface. Provide medium-to-high lighting and cooler water temperatures when possible (68–75°F preferred); adding pressurized CO2 encourages lower, creeping horizontal growth. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid drastic environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or rotting in delicate stems. Trim stem shoots with straight scissors anywhere along the stem or pull apart dense clumps to propagate and maintain compact growth. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. As new growth adapts, the plant will shed its firmer land leaves and sprout delicate, ivy-like submerged foliage. Once new shoots develop, trim away old lower growth to encourage branching.

Plant Profile Anubias Heterophylla, or Congo Anubias, is a larger-leaved heavyweight that is ready to bring major tropical structure to your aquascape. While it shares the long, graceful stems seen in Anubias barteri, its impressive foliage stretches nearly double the length, with individual leaves capable of reaching up to 12 inches long. If you've been looking for a bold, low-maintenance centerpiece to add dramatic height and fill out your midground or background, this epiphyte is here to help you pull off a grand layout without breaking a sweat. Key Features & Benefits Massive foliage provides bold height and structural impact for larger aquascapes. Wavy, lanceolate leaf architecture creates a dynamic linear contrast against rounder aquatic plants and heavy rockwork. Durable and leathery leaves withstand the activity of plant-eating fish and active shrimp. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Avoid intense light and ensure good water flow to prevent spot algae on slow‑growing leaves. CO₂ is optional but improves growth and leaf density. Learn more about planting these species by reading our guide on How to Plant Epiphyte Aquatic Plants. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. Its tough leaves are also resistant to plant-eating fish like cichlids or goldfish.

Plant Profile Cyperus Helferi is a striking, grass-like background plant that adds graceful movement and natural elegance to planted aquariums. Characterized by its long, slender green leaves that can reach up to 20 inches in length, it sways gently in the water current to create a dense, flowing backdrop. Despite its dramatic, architectural look, Cyperus Helferi is relatively easy to care for and adapts well to both fully submerged aquarium layouts and emersed setups like paludariums or terrariums. Key Features & Benefits Sways naturally with water flow, adding dynamic movement and scale to medium and large aquariums. Adapts to fully submerged tanks or high‑humidity emersed setups. Hardy rosette provides shelter and reduces line‑of‑sight stress for territorial fish. Care & Planting Instructions Provide medium to high lighting to encourage full, dense foliage and prevent lower blades from deteriorating. Inject pressurized CO2 to accelerate its naturally slow growth rate, though CO2 is optional in low-tech configurations. Maintain stable aquarium parameters and avoid drastic shifts in water quality to prevent your new grass from melting. Master the basics by learning how to properly grow aquarium carpet plants and background foliage to ensure your layout fills in quickly and stays free of algae. As Cyperus Helferi matures, it produces new plantlets around the base of its root system. Simply separate these mature daughter plantlets along with their attached roots using sharp scissors and replant them into the substrate.

Plant Profile Echinodorus horizontalis 'Mini', aka Horizontal Mini Sword, offers all the unique growth habit of the classic Horizontal Sword at roughly half the full-grown scale. True to its name, this dwarf selection produces broad, oblong green leaves on petiole stems that branch outward almost parallel to the substrate, creating a distinctive wide-spreading canopy rather than reaching straight up. Maxing out at a manageable height of around 12 inches, it fits comfortably into midground zones or functions as an architectural background anchor in smaller aquariums. Its hardy nature, bold horizontal leaves, and adaptable care requirements make it an approachable choice for hobbyists looking for structural leaf contrast without overcrowding their display. Key Features & Notes Distinctive horizontal growth habit causes broad foliage to fan out sideways across the midground. Hardy rosette plant that thrives in low-tech environments while offering unique structural layout depth. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Plant the roots deeply into your aquarium soil, keeping the central crown resting just above the substrate line to prevent rot. All Echinodorus are heavy root feeders that rely on rich substrate nutrition; placing root tabs near the base supports steady, healthy leaf development. Supplemental CO2 injection accelerates growth and encourages denser, fuller foliage, though the plant will still grow steadily in low-tech setups. Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf shedding during the initial transition period. Sword plants propagate through side shoots off of their leaves, which can be trimmed and replanted into the substrate. To control the size of your sword plant, you can remove the side shoots and older leaves. Final size and leaf shape depend on whether the plant is grown fully submerged or emersed; please note that individual plants may vary based on tank conditions. Plant Profile Myriophyllum Aquaticum, commonly known as Parrot's Feather or Water Feather, is a fast-growing, highly textured aquatic stem plant native to the lush streams, lakes, and river systems of the Amazon Basin in South America. Its needle-like foliage creates a delicate, feather-like look, and this perennial doesn't just stick to one lane: it thrives in indoor planted aquariums, open-top aquascapes, paludariums, and outdoor water gardens alike. Let it grow emersed above the waterline, and it builds lush, fir-like mini forests right at the surface, while the submerged foliage below keeps things soft, bright-green, and full of gentle movement. *Shipping Restriction Notice: To comply with conservation laws and state environmental regulations, we are unable to sell or ship this plant to the following states: IL, IN, MI, MN, NY, OH, PA, WA, and WI. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Feathery leaf whorls add needle-like texture and movement to background zones. Versatile in submerged aquariums, open-top paludariums, bog gardens, and outdoor ponds. Fast growth acts as a natural nutrient sponge to keep water clean and suppress algae. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight (or pot) and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the roots, then strip lower foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into soil, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower growth. Provide moderate-to-high lighting and clean water conditions; while adaptable without CO2, supplying pressurized CO2 yields faster growth. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim main stem tops with straight scissors once stems reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to easily propagate and expand coverage. Plant Profile Dwarf Nomaphila Siamensis, commonly known as Dwarf Hygrophila Siamensis, is a robust, highly adaptable aquatic stem plant ideal for aquascapers looking for dense, low-growing foliage. Native to Southeast Asia, this popular species features broad, sturdy leaves that form thick midground or foreground bushes. When provided with high-intensity lighting, its leaves develop beautiful red and orange tints while maintaining a tight, compact growth habit that creates immediate visual depth in any aquarium layout. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Forms dense, low bushes under strong lighting, making it an excellent compact midground accent. Foliage responds to intense light by developing subtle red and orange hues, offering natural warmth and contrast to green aquascapes. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip the lower inch of foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them apart so light reaches lower leaves to maintain compact growth. Provide moderate-to-high lighting for steady growth; higher light levels are essential to prevent vertical stretching and to trigger red/orange coloration. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid drastic environmental changes to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the desired height to encourage new lateral side branching and a bushier appearance. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. listings.commonName: Micranthemum Micranthemoides (Pearl Weed) UNS Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Micranthemum Micranthemoides, aka Pearl Weed, is a bright green, soft-textured aquatic stem plant native to North American wetlands. Featuring tiny round leaves that make it look like it's constantly having a good hair day, it grows fast and adapts to just about anything you throw at it: keep it trimmed low for a creeping foreground carpet, let it mound up in the midground, or leave it alone entirely and watch it turn into a towering background bush. Think of it as the low-maintenance friend of the carpeting-plant world, forgiving enough for beginners while still forming a lush green matrix that gives shrimp and fish fry plenty of places to hide. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Versatile growth habit trains into a foreground carpet, midground hedge, or background forest. Beginner-friendly and adaptable to both low-tech and high-tech setups. Dense foliage acts as a natural nitrate sponge and shelter for fry and dwarf shrimp. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide medium-to-high lighting for compact, bushy horizontal carpet growth, or moderate light for looser vertical growth; while adaptable in low-tech tanks, adding pressurized CO2 and quality aquarium soil yields maximum density and speed. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent melting or rotting. Trim stem tops with curved scissors to shape into desired forms, and group several trimmings together to replant into substrate to expand coverage. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Once the gel is removed, separate the dense cluster into smaller clumps or individual stem bundles and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

listings.commonName: Bucephalandra Green Wavy UNS Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Bucephalandra ‘Green Wavy’ is a low-tech, farm-grown aquarium plant featuring bright green ruffled leaves. Growing around 2 to 4 inches tall with leaves averaging 0.75 to 1 inch long, it works well in the foreground or midground as a charming accent that fills in empty spaces between hardscape. Like most Buce species, it attaches directly to rocks and driftwood rather than soil, making it just as easy to run in low-tech setups as it is in humid terrariums or paludariums. Tissue culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab-grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go-to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Notes The wavy margins of the leaves catch the light beautifully, creating a sense of "movement" and great detail even in low-flow areas of the tank. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for planted tanks where other plants might struggle. Unlike many darker or purplish Buce varieties, ‘Green Wavy’ stays a bright, clean green that contrasts beautifully with dark stones like Seiryu or Dragon Stone. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by carefully removing the plantlets from the cup and rinsing away all sterile nutrient gel under lukewarm, dechlorinated water before mounting. Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood with aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as it will rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard low-light aquarium plant setups, CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and a smoother tissue culture transition. Why is my tissue culture Bucephalandra melting after planting? Tissue culture plants undergo an acclimation phase when transitioning to underwater conditions. Maintain stable water parameters, good circulation, and moderate light; as long as the rhizome stays firm, new submerged leaves will emerge. 3. Can tissue culture Bucephalandra be planted in substrate? Yes, you can push the roots into substrate or gravel to help anchor the plantlet. However, you must keep the central horizontal rhizome completely exposed above the substrate line, as burying the rhizome starves it of circulation and causes rot.

Plant Profile For aquascapers wanting to fill out midground gaps with a thick, naturalistic texture, Cryptocoryne lutea delivers without demanding constant attention. Native to the limestone-rich streams of Sri Lanka, this classic favorite showcases vibrant green to bronze-tinted oblong leaves with gracefully wavy margins. As with all crypt plants, this plant can be sensitive to changes in water parameters and doesn’t like to be moved. Choose its location wisely from day one to avoid triggering leaf drop, and this adaptable survivor will slowly expand into a lush, evergreen anchor for your layout. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Bright green to bronze wavy leaves create a lush, dynamic texture in the midground. Hardy species that adapts to a wide range of water conditions once rooted. Compact growth builds a bushy footprint that provides shelter for small fish and shrimp. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Crypt species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. listings.commonName: Bucephalandra Red Mini UNS Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Bucephalandra ‘Red Mini’ is a rare, low-tech aquarium plant with tiny leaves that develop a stunning reddish-purple tint when grown submerged over a long period. Because of its exceptionally small foliage, it's a great pick for adding fine detail to driftwood and stone crevices or adding a tiny pop of deep jewel-toned color to the foreground of planted tanks. Grow it emersed or submerged and attach it to hardscape for best results. Tissue culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab-grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go-to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Notes With consistent care and time, the tiny leaves mature into a rich palette of red and purple that contrasts sharply against neutral hardscape. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for planted tanks where other plants might struggle. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by carefully removing the plantlets from the cup and rinsing away all sterile nutrient gel under lukewarm, dechlorinated water before mounting. Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard low-light aquarium plant setups, CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and a smoother tissue culture transition. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Plant Profile Hemigraphis repanda, commonly called Dragon's Tongue, is a tropical perennial featuring slender, crinkled leaves with serrated margins, deep olive-green upper surfaces, and bold magenta-purple undersides. This terrestrial plant is infamous among aquarists as the poster child for aquarium plant catfishing, as big-box pet stores routinely sell it in submerged tanks where it holds out like a trooper for a few weeks before turning into sad purple soup. Keep it in an emersed setup instead, where its rippled foliage breaks up flat carpets of green moss, and it can actually live its best life alongside other humidity-loving plants. Key Features & Notes Ruffled, wrinkly leaves feature deep olive tops paired with vivid purple undersides. Strictly terrestrial grower that will melt away if planted underwater in an aquarium. Spreading habit fills out midground pockets and contrasts cleanly against pale hardscape. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and gently rinsing the roots in clean water. Tuck the roots into an airy, moisture-retentive tropical soil blend with plenty of bark and perlite, avoiding overly dense soil that turns into soggy mud. Provide moderate to bright indirect light; decent lighting keeps the purple undersides vibrant, but direct scorching sun will burn the rippled leaf tips. Maintain humidity above 70% while ensuring excess moisture can drain out so the root crown doesn't sit in stagnant water. Trim wandering stem tips just above a node with sharp shears to encourage bushier growth and prevent leggy stems. Final size and purple coloration depend entirely on your specific setup conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Hemigraphis repanda are terrestrial plants, and being submerged will result in the death of the plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Clip healthy lateral runners or take a stem cutting containing at least two leaf nodes, then press it into moist tropical soil or sphagnum moss until it roots.

Plant Profile If you're looking to break up the bright green monotony of your aquascape, Cryptocoryne beckettii offers a classic, warm-toned silhouette that never goes out of style. Native to the mineral-rich, fast-flowing limestone streams of Sri Lanka, this long-time hobby favorite showcases oblong leaves with gracefully ruffled margins that shift from deep olive-green to rich reddish-brown. As with all crypt plants, this species can be sensitive to sudden parameter shifts and strongly objects to being relocated once planted. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Reddish-brown oblong leaves with ruffled edges provide a rich visual contrast to surrounding green plants. Can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups where mature plants can potentially produce unique flowering spathes above the water. Thrives in limestone-derived, hard water environments, making it a resilient choice for low-tech community tanks. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel. Maintain moderate to low lighting to prevent unnecessary stress or premature leaf dissolving. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Cryptocoryne species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. Plant Profile Vallisneria gigantea, commonly known as Giant Val, is a massive species for creating lush, jungle-style backgrounds in planted tanks. If you thought standard Vallisneria spiralis grew quickly, this oversized powerhouse takes vertical growth to a whole new level, shooting thick, ribbon-like leaves straight up to the surface until they drape across the top of the glass like a living canopy. It acts as an absolute lifesaver for hiding filter pipes and other equipment that you would rather not look at. Even with its massive scale, it remains one of the most reliable background aquarium plants for beginners with larger tanks who want density without complicated care routines. Key Features & Notes Extra-wide ribbon foliage can grow over 20 inches tall, concealing background equipment. Adapts easily to low-tech environments, though rich nutrients and moderate lighting maximize leaf width and strength. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap surrounding the root crown, taking care not to crush or damage the roots. As heavy root feeders, Vallisneria should be planted deeply into aquarium soil to ensure they anchor securely and absorb vital nutrients. Provide root tab fertilization and reliable lighting to feed these nutrient-loving plants and sustain fast vertical growth. Trim overgrown leaves near the base using sharp aquascaping shears rather than topping them, and snip spreading runner shoots to propagate or control expansion across your planted tank background. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I trim Giant Val when its ribbon-like leaves grow too long for my aquarium? Use sharp aquascaping scissors to cleanly snip individual leaf blades near the water surface at your desired height. To prevent ragged or browning tips, make clean cuts across the blade rather than tearing the foliage, or prune older leaves entirely near the base to thin out dense growth. 2. Is pressurized CO2 required to grow Vallisneria gigantea? Pressurized CO2 is recommended to achieve maximum leaf width, strength, and rapid runner spread. However, it is an easy-to-moderate species that will still adapt and grow reliably in low-tech setups without CO2, provided it receives decent lighting and quality substrate nutrients. 3. How does Giant Val propagate, and how do I control it from spreading across the tank? Giant Val propagates naturally by sending out subterranean lateral runner shoots. To manage its footprint or populate a new area, simply snip the connecting runner chain with scissors once the baby plantlet has developed its own root system, then leave it or replant it elsewhere.

Plant Profile If you are looking to build a sweeping, wild jungle backdrop with a warm splash of color, Vallisneria gigantea 'Rubra' brings impressive drama to the rear of a display. True to its 'Rubra' title, this striking Giant Val variant trades the plain green look of traditional vals for long, ribbon-like leaves infused with reddish-bronze and rich coppery hues. Under moderate to high lighting, the new leaf growth emerges in deep reddish tones before maturing into a bold, multi-toned olive and red canopy across the surface. Growing between 12 and 20+ inches tall, its broad, strap-like blades flow with filter currents, turning large aquariums into vibrant underwater forests in no time. Key Features & Notes Broad, strap-like leaves feature distinct coppery-red to bronze coloration under good lighting. Rapid growth rate and massive scale quickly establish a thick, moving background wall in large aquariums. Spreads reliably via lateral root runners to build a seamless jungle backdrop. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap surrounding the root crown, taking care not to crush or damage the roots. Plant individual crowns into aquarium soil or sand, ensuring the crown rests just above the substrate line to prevent root rot. As heavy root feeders, Giant Vals thrive when root tabs are inserted near the base to encourage quick anchoring and vigorous runner production. Supplemental CO2 injection and moderate-to-high lighting encourage the deepest reddish-bronze pigmentation and fuller leaf width. Trim surface-drifting leaf tips cleanly with sharp aquascaping scissors to prevent shading lower-growing foreground plants. Final color intensity and leaf length depend on your tank lighting and nutrient levels; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. To thin out a dense patch, remove older outer crowns or trim subterranean runner chains rather than cutting whole plant tops down.

Plant Profile Vallisneria nana is a distinct, fine-leaved background species native to northern Australia that brings a refined, sweeping texture to planted aquariums. Unlike the broader, ribbon-like blades of traditional Vallisneria varieties, this species produces ultra-narrow, needle-like green leaves that resemble a tall, flowing hairgrass. Reaching heights of 12 to 20+ inches, its fast growth rate allows it to quickly send out runner shoots across the substrate, forming a dense, continuous wall of foliage. As the long blades reach the water column, they drape across the surface to create a living canopy that moves naturally with filter currents, making it an ideal choice for aquascapers seeking a jungle-style backdrop with a lighter visual footprint. Key Features & Notes Ultra-narrow, hairgrass-like foliage adds a fine, delicate texture to background zones. Rapidly propagates via runner shoots to establish a dense, moving aquatic wall. Drapes gracefully across the water surface under moderate-to-high lighting, creating soft shade and natural motion. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap surrounding the root crown, taking care not to crush or damage the roots. Plant individual crowns deeply into aquarium soil or fine substrate, keeping the base of the crown visible just above the substrate line to prevent crown rot. Provide moderate to high lighting and consistent water-column or substrate nutrients to encourage dense runner propagation. Trim surface-drifting leaf tips cleanly with sharp aquascaping scissors to manage length and prevent shading adjacent plants. Final size and growth density depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Plant Profile Cryptocoryne striolata doesn't need bright colors to catch your eye; its shape does all the talking! Native to the Sarawak region of Borneo, where it naturally clings to riverbed rocks and submerged tree roots, this uncommon species stands out with long, slender stalks topped by compact reddish-brown leaves. As with all crypt plants, this plant can be sensitive to changes in water parameters and doesn’t like to be moved. But once its extensive root system anchors into the substrate, its distinct silhouette and warm earthy tones will mature into a midground or background accent that plays beautifully against traditional green plants. Key Features & Benefits Compact leaves on long petioles create an elevated focal point in midground or background zones. Can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups, where mature plants may produce flowering spathes above water. Ancient Pagoda Stone is a rare natural rock named for its rugged, architectural shape and distinct sedimentary layers formed over thousands of years of natural weathering. This highly sought-after aquascaping stone is a true collector's item, seldom found in the US due to the significant challenges involved in its mining and sourcing. Each unique piece carries its own storied character, offering a sense of history and permanence to any underwater landscape. Ancient Pagoda Stone is also suitable for non-aquarium use and will work beautifully as a sophisticated accent in terrariums, paludariums, or similar enclosures. Stones vary in shape, size, and density. Pieces from packages will range from 5-15 inches Notes: If you are looking for larger stones, a minimum weight may be required. Larger stones = higher weight. Email our team if you need assistance. This is a natural product and has the potential to alter water parameters slightly. We recommend rinsing stones thoroughly before use to remove any natural dust or sediment. Stone coloration darkens when wet.

Seiryu Stone is the undisputed "Godfather" of all stones and the pinnacle of aquascaping materials. As one of the most popular hardscape options available, this grey-blue natural rock is prized for its jagged, craggy, and heavily veined texture that deepens in color when wet. Its silver-gray tones and rough, weathered surfaces make it an incredible focal point, ideal for creating dramatic, natural-looking mountain-style landscapes or minimalist Iwagumi layouts. The endless details found in these stones allow any hobbyist to easily recreate the complexity of nature. Boutique Seiryu is also suitable for non-aquarium use and will work beautifully as a sophisticated accent in terrariums, paludariums, or similar planted enclosures. Stones vary in shape, size, and density. Notes: Seiryu may slightly raise pH and water hardness. Controsoil can help balance that out. We recommend rinsing stones thoroughly before use to remove any natural dust or sediment. Stone coloration darkens when wet.

How do I bring out the reddish-brown coloration on Cryptocoryne Albida Costata? Increasing lighting to moderate-to-high intensity and providing iron-rich substrate fertilizers alongside CO2 injection will draw out richer reddish-bronze hues across its ruffled foliage. 2. Why does moving or uprooting my Crypt cause leaf drop? This species relies heavily on a delicate network of subterranean roots that absorb nutrients from the soil. Plant Profile If you're hunting for a unique center-stage plant, Barclaya Longifolia ( Barclaya longifolia ), often called the Orchid Lily, is an exceptional find. Native to the soft-water streams of Southeast Asia, this rare bulb species belongs to the water lily family, but with a fascinating twist: unlike most lilies that send floating pads to the surface, Barclaya grows completely submerged! It forms an impressive rosette of long, wavy, ribbon-like leaves that radiate outward in deep maroon, olive, and copper-red tones. Reaching anywhere from 8 to 16 inches in height, it creates a sweeping, high-contrast display when placed in the midground or background alongside classic green stem plants and lush carpets. *Important Note: Photo shows a bulb portion after 2 months of growth. Key Features & Benefits Unique fully submerged water lily that stays completely underwater without sending floating pads to the top. Uncommon collector bulb plant that creates a dramatic centerpiece in planted aquariums. Care & Planting Instructions Gently press the bulb halfway into your aquarium soil, making sure the top half remains exposed to the water column to prevent rotting. Bulbs typically range from 0.5 to 1.5 inches upon arrival, so don't worry if it looks small at first, as it will grow larger and establish strong roots once placed in soft, slightly acidic water. As a heavy root feeder, Barclaya Longifolia thrives when provided with plenty of root nutrients; placing root tabs near the bulb in your aquarium soil will directly encourage faster growth and vibrant foliage. Provide moderate to high lighting; while adaptable, supplying pressurized CO2 and regular liquid iron dosing brings out the deepest maroon-red colors. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Keep water parameters stable and avoid sudden changes in water chemistry to prevent leaf melt during transition. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I plant a Barclaya Longifolia bulb properly? Set the bulb gently on top of your aquarium soil and press it in just enough so that it stays anchored, keeping at least half of the bulb exposed above the substrate. Completely burying the bulb can block circulation and cause it to rot before sprouting. 2. What water conditions does Barclaya Longifolia prefer to sprout? Barclaya Longifolia sprouts best in soft, slightly acidic water. Hard or highly alkaline water parameters can slow down sprouting and cause the leaves to turn bronze or dull, so maintaining soft water helps promote deep maroon-red leaves. 3. Why is my Barclaya Longifolia losing its leaves or going dormant? Like many bulbous species in the water lily family, Barclaya Longifolia can occasionally undergo a rest or drop leaves if parameters fluctuate drastically. As long as the bulb remains firm in your aquarium soil, it will rest and send out fresh new foliage once conditions stabilize.

Not sure which Twinstar series fits your budget and plant choices? Read our guide: Which Twinstar LED Light is Best for You? Plant Profile Ranunculus Inundatus, known as River Buttercup, is a creeping aquatic plant that looks like nothing else in the hobby. It has deeply palm-lobed, starburst leaves that sprout from horizontal runners like a forest of tiny green umbrellas, spreading across the substrate via underground runners. It works as an eye-catching foreground carpet or low midground accent, and it's just as happy in submerged setups as it is in emersed Wabi Kusa or dry-start builds, bringing architectural texture that high-tech layouts don't usually get elsewhere. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Unique starburst and umbrella-like leaf shapes introduce bold architectural contrast into foreground and midground zones. Rapidly spreads across the substrate to form a dense foreground carpet. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide high-intensity lighting and pressurized CO2 injection to encourage low, creeping horizontal growth; tall vertical stretching indicates insufficient light, while pale or thin foliage signals a CO2 or micronutrient deficiency. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent leaf melting or root decay. Trim horizontal stolons or upright stems with curved scissors, and replant individual cuttings directly into substrate to propagate and expand coverage. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Why is my Ranunculus Inundatus growing tall and leggier instead of staying low? Ranunculus Inundatus stretches vertically when it receives insufficient lighting. To keep stems short and induce low, horizontal creeping runners across the substrate, increase light intensity and maintain adequate pressurized CO2 levels. 2. Why are the leaves of my River Buttercup turning yellow or thin? Yellowing leaves usually point to a macro or micronutrient deficiency (such as iron or nitrogen), while abnormally thin or fragile foliage typically hints at insufficient CO2 levels in the water column. 3. How do I prepare Ranunculus Inundatus Tissue Culture before planting? Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the dense runner cluster into smaller individual plantlets and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

Plant Profile If you're looking for a clever way to bridge your foreground and midground with warm, earthy color, Cryptocoryne 'Mioya' is a versatile favorite. Hailing from the shaded riverbanks of Sri Lanka's Mi Oya, this variety is celebrated for its slender, gracefully ruffled leaves that shift seamlessly from bright emerald green to deep copper-brown tones. As with all crypts, it can be sensitive to sudden parameter shifts and strongly objects to being moved once planted. Given a permanent home in your substrate, however, its crinkled foliage expands into a lush, dynamic accent that brings high-contrast warmth to dark wood and hardscape setups. Key Features & Benefits Slender, ruffled leaves transition from bright emerald to rich copper-brown, delivering striking color contrast. Can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups where it will periodically produce unique flowering spathes. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Crypt species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I help my Cryptocoryne Mioya recover if it melts? Crypt melt is a standard reaction when shifting water conditions cause old leaves to dissolve so the plant can rebuild foliage adapted to your aquarium. Trim away rotting tissue, keep your water parameters stable, and do not disturb the subterranean root system. For complete recovery steps, check out our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt . 2. Why does moving or uprooting my Crypt cause leaf drop? This species relies heavily on a delicate network of subterranean roots that absorb nutrients from the soil. Uprooting the plant ruptures these fine root hairs and alters its micro-environment, triggering a shock response where the plant drops its leaves to conserve energy. Placing it in a permanent location from day one prevents unnecessary leaf loss. 3. Should I use root tabs or liquid fertilizers for Cryptocoryne Mioya? Root tabs are far more effective than liquid fertilizers for Cryptocoryne species because they draw the overwhelming majority of their nutrition through their roots. While liquid nutrients benefit water column feeders like mosses or stem plants, placing nutrient-rich root tabs inside sand or gravel substrates directly fuels your Crypt's foliage growth.

Plant Profile Proserpinaca Palustris, or Mermaid Weed, is an aquatic stem plant native to the swamps, marshes, and slow-moving waterways of North America. Renowned for its distinctly serrated, comb-like, saw-toothed leaves, this species provides an unmatched visual texture in planted aquariums. Depending on light intensity and nutrient levels, its coloration shifts dynamically from a soft golden-green to fiery copper, amber, and deep ruby-red. Reaching up to 12 inches in height, Mermaid Weed is a great choice for midground focal points and Dutch-style plant streets, where its saw-toothed leaf geometry creates a high-contrast backdrop against fine-leaved or broad-leaved neighbors. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Intricate, saw-toothed, comb-like leaf structure provides striking visual contrast and texture in midground and background zones. Displays a dynamic color gradient from golden-green to brilliant orange and deep ruby-red under high-tech conditions. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide medium-to-high lighting and pressurized CO2 injection; consistent liquid fertilization rich in iron and micronutrients intensifies leaf serration and ruby-red pigmentation. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or leaf shedding. To propagate, trim main stem tops with sharp straight shears and replant the trimmings directly into the substrate. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. How do I turn Proserpinaca Palustris deep red? Achieving deep ruby-red and copper tones on Mermaid Weed requires high-intensity lighting, pressurized CO2 injection, and regular dosing of a trace fertilizer that supplies iron and essential micronutrients. 3.
