Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the cluster into smaller clumps or individual stems and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

Plant Profile Hailing from the lush aquatic habitats of Peru, Echinodorus peruensis is a large-scale sword plant built to make a sweeping background statement. Producing long, elegant green leaves with an elongated, lance-like shape, this South American native shoots up tall, broad rosettes that easily reach up to 20+ inches in height. Its imposing vertical scale makes it an absolute lifesaver for filling out deep background corners or effortlessly concealing bulky aquarium equipment like intake tubes and heaters. Naturally robust and adaptable, it brings classic jungle-style lushness to spacious freshwater aquariums without demanding high-maintenance care or complex technical setups. Key Features & Notes Tall, elongated green foliage creates a dramatic vertical backdrop in medium to large aquariums. Spacious rosette structure easily conceals background equipment and filters. Hardy and adaptable species that thrives in low-tech setups without mandatory CO2 injection. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Plant the roots deeply into your aquarium soil, keeping the central crown resting just above the substrate line to prevent rot. All Echinodorus are heavy root feeders that rely on rich substrate nutrition; placing root tabs near the base supports steady, healthy leaf development. Supplemental CO2 injection accelerates growth and encourages denser, fuller foliage, though the plant will still grow steadily in low-tech setups. Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf shedding during the initial transition period. Sword plants propagate through side shoots off of their leaves, which can be trimmed and replanted into the substrate. To control the size of your sword plant, you can remove the side shoots and older leaves. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I manage the large size of Echinodorus peruensis in a planted aquarium? Because its elongated leaves can grow up to 20+ inches tall, periodically prune the largest or outermost leaves near the base using sharp aquascaping scissors. Yes, Peruvian Sword plants grow vigorously in low-tech setups without pressurized CO2. Providing a nutrient-rich substrate or adding root tabs near the root base, along with moderate lighting, is all it takes to keep it thriving. 3. Will Echinodorus peruensis produce flowers when grown emersed? Yes, when grown emersed in open-top aquariums, paludariums, or Wabi Kusa setups, it will extend tall flowering stems that produce small, delicate white flowers above the waterline.

Plant Profile If you love the sweeping look of classic background plants and want to create that dense, wild jungle backdrop, Vallisneria americana is an incredible choice that brings a unique twist to the table! Like popular varieties such as Vallisneria spiralis or Vallisneria nana , it shoots up long, ribbon-like leaves that reach toward the surface, sending out runners to quickly form a lush, green wall across the rear of your display. What sets this particular Val apart, however, is its distinctive leaf structure: instead of growing completely straight, its long blades naturally twist as they shoot upward. This corkscrew-like habit catches the water current and light in a way that adds dynamic texture and constant motion to your aquascape, giving you that quintessential jungle tank aesthetic with an extra layer of visual detail. Key Features & Notes Distinct spiral-twisted leaves bring unique texture and subtle motion to background zones. Rapidly spreads via root runners to form a dense, natural wall of foliage for a wild jungle look. Shares the bulletproof background utility of other Vallisneria species while offering a more dynamic leaf shape. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap surrounding the root crown, taking care not to crush or damage the roots. Plant individual crowns into aquarium soil or sand, making sure to leave the crown resting just above the substrate line to prevent rot. All Vallisneria species are heavy root feeders; placing root tabs near the base supports strong root anchoring and quick runner production. Trim surface-drifting leaf tips cleanly with sharp aquascaping scissors to manage length and prevent excessive shading of lower-growing plants. Maintain stable water parameters, as sudden environmental changes or liquid carbon additives can cause initial leaf melt. Final size and leaf twist depend on your specific tank conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Yes, Vallisneria americana will grow reliably in low-tech tanks without pressurized CO2, though providing decent lighting and substrate nutrients will help it send out runners much faster. 3. Why are my Vallisneria leaves turning soft or melting after planting? Vallisneria can experience transition melt when introduced to new water chemistry or exposed to liquid carbon supplements. Keep parameters stable and give the root system time to establish, and new twisted growth will quickly emerge.

Plant Profile If you've ever wanted an aquatic plant that looks like an octopus having a bad hair day, Crinum calamistratum is here to steal the show. Native to Central Africa, this quirky bulbous plant sprouts extremely thin, deeply crinkled, dark green leaves that twist, loop, and swirl through the water column. Anchored by an onion-like bulb base, its sprawling tentacle-like foliage can max out at around 40 inches long, making it a dramatic background centerpiece. While it takes its sweet time growing, happy plants under good light may even reward you with elegant white flowers blooming above the surface! Key Features & Notes Thin, deeply crinkled leaves create a wild octopus-like textural display. Unique onion bulb base supports long-term nutrient storage and stability. Slow-growing species that occasionally blooms elegant white flowers above the waterline. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by gently inspecting the bulb and removing any loose organic debris around the base. Plant the bulb so that it is only half-buried in your aquarium soil or substrate; completely burying the bulb can cause it to rot. Avoid moving or uprooting the bulb once buried, as Crinum species dislike root disturbance and take time to settle in. Supplemental CO2 injection and soft water parameters accelerate growth and help encourage flower development. Propagate by gently separating formed daughter bulbs from the main mother bulb once they develop independent root systems. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. How deep should I bury the bulb of Crinum calamistratum? Bury the roots firmly into the substrate, but leave the top half to two-thirds of the main bulb exposed to the water column. Completely burying the bulb can lead to rot. 2. Why are the leaves on my Crinum calamistratum so wavy and crinkled? That deeply ruffled, crimped texture is 100% natural! It’s the signature look of Crinum calamistratum , helping its long ribbon leaves catch light and current without tearing. 3. Can I move Crinum calamistratum around after planting it? It’s best to pick a spot and stick to it. Crinum species grow extensive root systems and really hate having their roots disturbed, often stalling in growth if moved too frequently.

Plant Profile Featuring tall, architectural stems topped with triangular arrowhead leaves, Anubias Hastifolia brings dramatic height and geometric structure to planted tanks. Diverging from the curves of standard Anubias like Anubias Barteri or Anubias Nana , this epiphyte serves up serious pointed drama with its distinct, triangular arrowhead-shaped leaves! Rising on tall petioles, it reaches 6 to 16 inches in height, giving your aquarium an instant weapon of mass decoration for midground and background zones in low-tech aquariums, terrariums, and paludariums. Key Features & Benefits Distinct triangular arrowhead leaf architecture provides striking geometric contrast against round or lanceolate aquatic plants. Thick, durable leaves deter grazing from plant-eating cichlids, snails, and dwarf shrimp. Resilient nature handles a wide range of water parameters in low-tech setups. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Avoid intense light and ensure good water flow to prevent spot algae on slow‑growing leaves. CO₂ is optional but improves growth speed and leaf density. Learn more about planting these species by reading our guide on How to Plant Epiphyte Aquatic Plants. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. While adding CO2 speeds up growth and foliage density, it thrives happily in low-tech aquariums. 3. Is this plant safe for shrimp, snails, and fish? Yes, Anubias Hastifolia is 100% safe for all freshwater fish, shrimp (including sensitive Caridina and Neocaridina), and snails. Its tough leaves are also resistant to plant-eating fish like cichlids or goldfish.

How do I help my Cryptocoryne Pontederiifolia recover if it melts? Crypt melt is a standard reaction when shifting water conditions cause old leaves to dissolve so the plant can rebuild foliage adapted to your aquarium. Trim away rotting tissue, keep your water parameters stable, and do not disturb the subterranean root system. For complete recovery steps, check out our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt . 2. Why does moving or uprooting my Crypt cause leaf drop? This species relies heavily on a delicate network of subterranean roots that absorb nutrients from the soil. Uprooting the plant ruptures these fine root hairs and alters its micro-environment, triggering a shock response where the plant drops its leaves to conserve energy. Placing it in a permanent location from day one prevents unnecessary leaf loss. 3. Should I use root tabs or liquid fertilizers for Cryptocoryne Pontederiifolia? Root tabs are far more effective than liquid fertilizers for Cryptocoryne species because they draw the overwhelming majority of their nutrition through their roots. While liquid nutrients benefit water column feeders like mosses or stem plants, placing nutrient-rich root tabs inside sand or gravel substrates directly fuels your Crypt's foliage growth.

Plant Profile If your aquascape needs a splash of polished, high-gloss greenery, Cryptocoryne undulata delivers serious aesthetic appeal. Hailing from the pristine rivers and streams of Sri Lanka, this timeless staple catches the light with smooth, remarkably glossy leaves that transition from a rich emerald green to deep bronze-red hues depending on your lighting. As with all crypts, it can be sensitive to sudden parameter changes and strongly objects to being moved once planted. Give it a permanent spot in your midground, however, and its sleek, reflective foliage will grow into a lush, self-sustaining focal point that elevates your entire layout. Key Features & Benefits Smooth, glossy leaves with a polished sheen transition from rich emerald green to warm bronze-red under tank lighting. Adapts to emersed high-humidity paludarium displays where mature plants can bloom. Adaptable midground grower that builds dense, compact rosettes without crowding neighboring hardscape. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Crypt species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. Plant Profile Utricularia Graminifolia, affectionately known in the hobby as UG, is a highly sought-after carpeting plant that delivers a vibrant, velvety aesthetic that regular aquarium grasses simply cannot match. This unique species is a carnivorous bladderwort, characterized by thousands of microscopic traps that capture tiny microorganisms in the water column. But don't worry! These traps are completely microscopic, making them 100% safe for dwarf shrimp, fish fry, and all other tank inhabitants. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Bright green foliage creates a dense, velvety carpet across the foreground of your tank. Microscopic carnivorous traps capture water-column microorganisms while remaining completely safe for shrimp and fry. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions and planting. Separate the larger tissue culture mats into small portions and plant each piece about an inch apart, burying them halfway into the substrate. Provide medium to high lighting and ensure it doesn’t get shaded by larger background plants, as this species absolutely demands direct light. Inject pressurized CO2 to drastically increase its growth speed, density, and thickness, though it can technically adapt to low-tech conditions over time. Learn tips and tricks to successfully establish this species by reading our complete guide on how to grow Utricularia Graminifolia (UG). Plant Profile Blyxa Japonica, aka Japanese Bamboo or Bamboo Plant, is native to the sunlit shallow pools and slow-moving streams of East Asia and became a Nature Aquarium staple thanks to Takashi Amano's frequent use of it for dense, grass-like thickets. Despite the stem-plant look, it actually grows in a soft rosette structure, staying rich green under moderate conditions but blushing gold, bronze, and red under high-intensity lighting, CO2, and nutrient dosing. At 4 to 8 inches tall, it's a natural midground centerpiece or transition layer between foreground carpets and background stems. Key Features & Benefits Grass-like, bushy growth adds soft texture to midground and background zones. Blushes gold, bronze, and red under high-intensity lighting and high-tech parameters. Popularized by Takashi Amano for classic Nature Aquarium layouts. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip the lower inch of foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into soil, spacing them about half an inch apart to ensure light reaches lower leaves. Provide medium-to-high lighting and pressurized CO2 injection; consistent fertilization with a liquid macro and micro formula yields robust, compact growth and deep golden-red coloration. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid drastic environmental shifts to prevent leaf melting or root rot. To propagate, snip side shoots, offshoots, or lateral runners that branch off from the base of established plants and replant them directly into the substrate. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Plant Profile Common Name: Marsilea Crenata Marsilea Crenata is a delightful little fern that hails natively from the tranquil rice fields of Asia. Famous in the hobby for its distinct, miniature leaves that closely resemble four-leaf clovers, it offers a whimsical, texture-rich look for your foreground. If you love the aesthetic of Hydrocotyle Tripartita but want an aquatic carpeting plant vastly shorter in stature that won't require constant, aggressive haircuts, this is your alternative. It is highly resilient and handles varying tank environments with ease, gradually spreading out to knit together a fascinating, low-profile carpet. Key Features & Benefits Miniature clover-shaped fronds form a compact, low-profile carpet. A compact alternative to taller creeping plants, as it stays naturally short and hugs the substrate. Tolerates a wide variety of aquarium parameters and water conditions. Care & Planting Instructions Provide medium to high lighting alongside a steady supply of nutrients to help it easily form a dense, uniform carpet across the substrate. Inject pressurized CO2 to encourage faster, more compact horizontal growth, though it remains a highly adaptable species. Keep an eye on its growth habit, as low light conditions may cause the stems to stretch upward slightly in search of light. Propagate the plant effortlessly by cutting new, mature growth along with the attached roots and pressing them back into your substrate. Master the basics by learning how to properly grow aquarium carpet plants to ensure your new layout fills in quickly, evenly, and stays free of algae. Plant Profile Alternanthera Reineckii Rosaefolia, commonly known as Scarlet Temple or AR Rosaefolia, is a classic, highly favored red stem plant originating from South America. Celebrated for its bold, intense magenta-to-scarlet red leaves and distinct white vein-like patterns running along its foliage, this species is a staple focal point in Dutch-style aquascapes and nature aquariums. Growing up to 8–12 inches tall, AR Rosaefolia brings unmatched color contrast and dense, architectural midground or background structure when planted alongside green stem species. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Vibrant magenta and scarlet foliage with subtle light vein patterning provides exceptional color contrast in Dutch-style layouts. Dense leaf structure gives cover and shelter for dwarf shrimp and timid fish. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide medium-to-high lighting. Regular dosing of liquid fertilizers like UNS Plant Food (2–3 times per week) and pressurized CO2 injection are highly recommended to yield maximum ruby-red coloration and prevent stunting. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or rotting. Trim stem tops or side shoots with curved scissors once stems reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and expand your hedge. Plant Profile Eleocharis Vivipara, commonly referred to as Umbrella Hair Grass, is a popular and striking background plant in the aquascaping community. As its common name implies, this species grows tall and slender, eventually arching over near the surface to create a graceful, flowing canopy across the top of the water. Because it grows quite tall, it makes an exceptional background centerpiece for medium and larger aquariums. However, it can also be kept in smaller nano tanks with routine trimming to keep its vertical growth in check. Key Features & Benefits Arching blades form a soft, floating canopy at the surface that fish and shrimp use for shade. Tolerates a wide range of aquarium conditions, suitable for beginners and experienced keepers. Spreads via lateral runners to fill gaps and create a continuous grassy carpet. Care & Planting Instructions Separate into small clumps and press them compactly into a quality aquarium soil to give the roots the perfect head start. Space small portions roughly one inch apart, burying the roots securely into the substrate. Maintain stable aquarium parameters and avoid drastic shifts in water quality to prevent your new grass from melting. Provide medium to high lighting and inject pressurized CO2 to supercharge its density and growth rate, keeping the tall stems thick and vibrant. Plant Profile Echinodorus 'Aflame', also known as the Purple Knight Sword, is a cultivated rosette species valued for its dark, narrow foliage. Native to the tropical Western Hemisphere through its parent lineage, this sword plant produces long, slightly twisted leaves that range in color from deep bronze and dark violet-red to near-black purple under bright lighting. Reaching 4 to 12 inches in height, its compact rosette structure provides a high-contrast centerpiece in midground or background zones. While adaptable across various tank conditions, providing clean water parameters and a steady supply of iron and root nutrients helps maintain its deep purple-red coloration. Tissue culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab-grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go-to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Notes Rare and sought-after cultivar displaying dramatic dark purple, deep crimson, and near-black leaves. Compact growth habit of 4 to 12 inches fits perfectly into midground centerpiece positions. Slow to moderate growth rate keeps its neat rosette shape stable and manageable over time. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by carefully removing the plantlets from the cup and rinsing away all sterile nutrient gel under lukewarm, dechlorinated water before mounting. Plant the roots deeply into your aquarium soil, keeping the central crown resting just above the substrate line to prevent rot. All Echinodorus are heavy root feeders that rely on rich substrate nutrition; placing root tabs near the base supports steady, healthy leaf development. Provide moderate to high lighting; while CO2 injection isn't strictly required, good lighting will enhance its reddish-brown colors. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf shedding during the initial transition period. Sword plants propagate through side shoots off of their leaves, which can be trimmed and replanted into the substrate. To control the size of your sword plant, you can remove the side shoots and older leaves. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. How do I achieve the deepest dark red and purple colors on Echinodorus 'Aflame'? Provide high-intensity lighting directly over the plant, inject CO2, and supplement the root zone with iron-rich root tabs. Higher light and iron levels are essential for driving its leaves to develop deep burgundy, crimson, and near-black tones rather than reverting to olive green. 2. Is Echinodorus 'Aflame' suitable for nano aquariums or smaller midground spaces? Yes, 'Aflame' is one of the more compact sword cultivars available, typically topping out around 4 to 12 inches. Because it grows at a slower pace than standard giant Amazon Swords, it functions beautifully as a midground centerpiece in standard tanks or a dramatic background plant in nano setups. 3. How do I prepare and plant tissue culture portions of Echinodorus 'Aflame'? Gently remove the plant mass from the in vitro cup and wash away the clear nutrient gel under room-temperature water. Carefully separate the clump into individual plantlets and anchor their roots deeply into nutrient-rich soil using fine-tipped tweezers, making sure the leaf crown stays exposed above the substrate.

Plant Profile Helanthium tenellum, commonly known as the Dwarf Chain Sword or Pygmy Chain Sword, is a popular grass-like carpeting plant native to the Americas. Maxing out at around 3 inches tall, its fine, needle-like foliage offers a natural look that bridges the gap between Dwarf Hairgrass and Micro Sword. It spreads by sending lateral runner chains across the substrate, filling in foreground spaces over time to build a lush green lawn. Under moderate to high lighting, the tips of its thin leaf blades often blush with subtle reddish-pink to bronze tones. Tissue culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a clean starting point. Lab-grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or unwanted algae. It’s the go-to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Notes Needle-like green foliage spreads via runner chains to form a dense foreground carpet. Higher light intensity encourages reddish-pink to bronze blushing on leaf tips. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by carefully removing the plantlets from the cup and rinsing away all sterile nutrient gel under lukewarm, dechlorinated water before mounting. Divide the tissue culture mass into small plugs and anchor them deep into your aquarium soil using fine-tipped aquascaping tweezers. Provide moderate to high lighting; higher light levels and supplemental CO2 encourage faster runner production. Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf shedding during the initial transition period. Trim spreading runner shoots with sharp aquascaping scissors to control its footprint or replant plantlets elsewhere. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Echinodorus tenellus ) Common Name(s) Dwarf Chain Sword, Pygmy Chain Sword, Echinodorus Tenellus Family Alismataceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Rosette / Runner plant (Tissue Culture) Care Difficulty Easy to Moderate Light Requirement Moderate to High CO2 Requirement Not required (Recommended for fast spreading) Placement / Usage Foreground Carpet / Midground Accent (Nano tanks) Height / Size 2–3 inches Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Water Parameters pH 6.5–7.5 Propagation Method Separate and replant lateral runner plantlets Origin North & South America Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I prep and plant a UNS Tissue Culture portion of Helanthium tenellum? Remove the plant mass from the cup and gently rinse off the clear nutrient gel under room-temperature water. Use your fingers or scissors to separate the cluster into smaller portions, then plant the small plugs into aquasoil using tweezers. 2. Can Helanthium tenellum form a full foreground carpet without CO2? Yes, it can carpet without pressurized CO2, though spreading will be noticeably slower. Providing a nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs along with moderate lighting will give it the boost it needs to spread across the foreground. 3. What causes the foliage tips to turn bronze or pink? Under higher lighting levels and healthy nutrient levels, Helanthium tenellum naturally develops a warm bronze or reddish blush on the upper halves of its leaves.

Heavy-Duty Stainless Steel Construction: Premium rust-proof stainless steel provides a rigid, sag-free armature that supports up to 22 lbs without compromising structural integrity or visual elegance. Plant Profile The Beginner Plant Pack takes all the guesswork out of starting your first planted tank (or your tenth low-maintenance setup), delivering a curated mix of our absolute favorite, practically indestructible low-tech species. Featuring a hand-picked selection of potted Anubias , lush Aquarium Moss , bulletproof Java Fern , and hardy Cryptocoryne , this starter bundle gives you everything needed to build a complete foreground, midground, and hardscape layout in one go. If you want a resilient, diverse mix of beginner staples without worrying about delicate plants melting into green soup, this bundle is your ultimate shortcut to a lush, low-tech display. Choose Your Pack Style The 5 Pack: Includes at least 1 pot of each plant from the list below for a total of 5 pots. Ideal for 5–10 gallon aquariums (e.g., UNS 5N, 3N, 25C, 30C, 60S, 45U, 45S, 60L). The 10 Pack: Includes 2 or more pots of each plant from the list below for a total of 10 pots. Ideal for 10–20 gallon aquariums (e.g., UNS 40C, 45U, 60U, 60S, 90L, 90LS). The 15 Pack: Includes 3 or more pots of each plant from the list below for a total of 15 pots. Ideal for 20–30+ gallon aquariums (e.g., UNS 60U, 90L). Every Beginner Plant Pack contains a healthy mix selected from the following core categories: Anubias Aquarium Moss Java Fern Cryptocoryne Please note: Specific varieties are hand-selected by our team based on current healthy stock and greenhouse availability. We are unable to fulfill requests for specific individual species, but we guarantee a beautiful, healthy mix! Care & Planting Instructions Prep the epiphytes (Anubias and Java Fern) by removing them from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Attach them directly to driftwood or rocks using super glue gel or thread, keeping rhizomes above substrate to prevent rot. Prep Cryptocoryne by removing rockwool and planting root systems directly into quality substrate or aqua soil. Attach Aquarium Moss to hardscape features using plant glue, thread, or by tucking it into rock crevices. Maintain stable water conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce initial leaf loss. CO₂ is optional; all species included flourish in low-tech, non-CO2 setups under basic lighting. Learn more about planting epiphytic species by reading our guide on How to Plant Epiphyte Aquatic Plants . Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I plant the varieties in the Beginner Plant Pack? Each plant type has slightly different planting needs: Anubias & Java Fern: Remove from pots, clear away rockwool, and attach rhizomes to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe super glue gel or thread. Do not bury rhizomes in substrate. Cryptocoryne: Remove from pot, gently clear rockwool, and press root systems directly into aquarium substrate or soil. Moss: Tie or glue directly onto hardscape features or press into tight crevices. 2. Can I request specific plant varieties in my pack? Because packs are curated based on current greenhouse inventory to guarantee maximum health and freshness, we are unable to accept requests for specific individual species or cultivars. However, every pack is guaranteed to include a healthy mix across the four core categories (Anubias, Java Fern, Cryptocoryne, and Moss). 3. Are the plants in this pack safe for shrimp and fish? Yes, all species included in the Beginner Plant Pack are 100% safe for all freshwater fish, shrimp (including sensitive Caridina and Neocaridina), and snails. Their tough leaf structures (especially Anubias and Java Fern) also make them resistant to plant-eating fish like cichlids or goldfish.

Plant Profile Having trouble deciding which stem plants to choose for your next aquascape? The Dutch Stem Plant Pack takes the guesswork out of building a classic Dutch-style aquarium layout! Hand-selected from our freshest daily inventory, this bundle provides a colorful, high-contrast mix of 5 distinct stem plant species. Characterized by varying leaf textures, growth heights, and vibrant color palettes, this pack is specifically curated to help you sculpt defined plant streets, cascading background hedges, and striking midground focal points. *Form Notice: Photos display these species in both their emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive plants in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . What You Might Receive Each pack includes 5 distinct species selected based on current farm health and availability. Potential species include: Bacopa Monnieri – Sturdy, bright green vertical stems. Ludwigia Arcuata – Fine, needle-like foliage that blushes orange and red. Ludwigia Natans Super Red – Intense, deep crimson-red broad leaves. Ludwigia Senegalensis – Rare, patterned foliage with brick-red hues. Ludwigia Peruensis 'Diamond' – Deep purplish-red centerpiece foliage. Rotala Indica – Compact, rounded stems with pink growing tips. Rotala Rotundifolia Red – Fast-growing, colorful background stem. ...and many other premium aquarium stem plants ! *Note: Species selection is subject to change at any time based on fresh inventory availability. Requests to exchange species or make custom substitutions cannot be accommodated. Available Pack Sizes & Tank Sizing 5 Pack (5 Lead Bunches Total): Includes 1 lead bunch each of 5 distinct stem species. Ideal for 5–10 gallon aquariums (such as UNS 5N, 3N, 25C, 30C, 60S, 45U, 45S, 60L). 10 Pack (10 Lead Bunches Total): Includes 2 lead bunches each of 5 distinct stem species. Ideal for 10–20 gallon aquariums (such as UNS 40C, 45U, 60U, 60S, 90L, 90LS). 15 Pack (15 Lead Bunches Total): Includes 3 lead bunches each of 5 distinct stem species. Ideal for 20–30+ gallon aquariums (such as UNS 60U, 90L). Key Features & Benefits Curated assortment of 5 distinct stem species provides instant color, texture, and height diversity for Dutch-style aquascapes. Offers incredible value and variety for aquascapers looking to plant out midground and background zones efficiently. Fast-growing stem plants act as powerful natural nutrient sponges, helping keep aquarium water clean and suppressing algae growth. Frequently Asked Questions 1. Can I request specific plants for my Dutch Stem Plant Pack? Due to fluctuating farm harvest and inventory levels, species are pre-selected daily to ensure you receive the healthiest plants possible. Requests for specific species, modifications, or exchanges cannot be accommodated. 2. How do I plant the stem bunches once they arrive? Remove the metal lead weight and rubber band or cotton wrap from each bunch. Strip off the bottom 1–2 inches of leaves from each stem, then use planting tweezers to insert individual stems or pairs 1 to 2 inches into your substrate, leaving small gaps between stems for light penetration. 3. Do I need CO2 injection to grow a Dutch stem plant aquarium? While many stem plants in this pack can grow in low-tech setups with moderate light, pressurized CO2 injection alongside quality aquasoil and liquid fertilization is strongly recommended to achieve the dense branching and intense red/orange colors characteristic of true Dutch aquascapes.

Custom-engineered for original UNS rimless glass tanks, these lids maintain high-definition visibility without interfering with lighting or aquascape aesthetics. Sized to leave precise clearance gaps, each lid allows for proper surface gas exchange while providing room for filter pipes, heater cables, and equipment access. Black Lava Rock is a highly porous natural rock that is widely used for both lush planted tanks and African Cichlid setups. This lightweight stone features a color palette ranging from black to gray, offering a rugged aesthetic for any hardscape. The extreme porosity of this natural stone makes it an excellent addition to your aquarium filtration system, as the millions of tiny holes provide massive surface area for beneficial bacteria to colonize. Its coarse texture also makes it a perfect pick for anchoring mosses, ferns, and other epiphytic plants. Black Lava Rock is also suitable for non-aquarium use and will work beautifully as a textured accent in terrariums, paludariums, or similar planted enclosures. You will receive 15LB per order. Sizes cannot be mixed and matched at this time. Notes: Smaller pieces may be slightly buoyant due to their high porosity. This stone is inert and will not alter water parameters. We recommend rinsing stones thoroughly before use to remove any natural dust or sediment. Stone coloration darkens when wet. Check out the Skull Island themed aquascape we did using Black Lava Rock

Spiderwood is known for its wild, multi‑branching shape that instantly adds depth and personality to any aquarium hardscape. This type of driftwood has twisting limbs that make it easy to create a natural, organic look, mimicking the root systems found in riverbanks and forest streams. Whether you stand it upright, lay it on its side, or angle it, each orientation creates a fresh visual story. It’s no surprise that Spiderwood has become one of our favorite driftwood choices here at Buce Plant HQ. Product Features & Benefits Unlike solid logs, Spiderwood features thin, sprawling branches that provide a sense of scale and movement. It is the premier choice for a planted aquarium hardscape, offering endless points to attach moss or small epiphytes. The complex tangles create a perfect "jungle gym" for shrimp and small fish, providing safety and exploration zones. This aquarium wood is easy to reposition and stack, allowing you to build towering vertical structures or low-profile root systems. Size Specifications Photos provided are a representation of what you will receive. As Spiderwood is a natural aquarium hardscape product, please expect variations in shape, weight, and character. Small: 8-12 inches Medium: 12-16 inches Large: 16-20 inches Extra Large: 20-24 inches Preparation & Care Driftwood is a natural product and requires a bit of prep before it’s ready for prime time. Rinse: Thoroughly rinse the piece to remove any dust or debris from transit. The "Float" Phase: Because it is lightweight, Spiderwood will almost certainly float initially. We recommend soaking it in a bucket or boiling it in water until it decides to join the rest of your aquarium hardscape at the bottom of your tank. The "White Fuzz" Phenomenon: It is common for a harmless white biofilm to develop on Spiderwood during the first few weeks. Don't panic, your shrimp and snails will think it’s a five-star buffet. It will eventually disappear on its own. Tannin Release: Spiderwood releases fewer tannins than other aquarium driftwood, but a quick boil will still help it sink faster and keep your water clear. Important note: We recommend rinsing wood thoroughly before adding it to an established aquarium. If you prefer, you may also boil the wood for at least 1–2 hours to help release tannins.

Malaysian Driftwood is a classic aquarium driftwood for a reason, embodying the quintessential, time-tested look that aquascapers know and love. With its rich, dark brown color and deeply craggy texture, this heavy hardwood makes a rock-solid foundation for just about any aquarium hardscape, whether you’re going for a dense jungle vibe, an old-growth forest, or a natural riverbed aesthetic. It’s beginner-friendly, pro-approved, and sturdy enough to anchor an entire planted tank layout from day one. It's proof that sometimes the root of a great aquascape really is the wood you start with! Product Features & Benefits Unlike many other types of aquarium wood, Malaysian Driftwood is exceptionally dense. It is typically "sink-on-arrival," meaning it generally stays submerged without the need for additional weights. The rugged surface provides an excellent anchor point for live plants. It is the perfect substrate for attaching Moss, Anubias, or Bucephalandra to create a lush, planted aquarium hardscape. It provides a natural foraging ground for shrimp and other aquatic pets. Size Specifications Photos provided are a representation of what you will receive. As Malaysian Driftwood is a natural aquarium hardscape product, please expect variations in shape, weight, and character. Extra Small: 3-8 inches Small: 8-12 inches Medium: 12-16 inches Large: 16-20 inches Extra Large: 20-25 inches Preparation & Care A little extra prep goes a long way in maintaining its stunning appearance. Rinse: Thoroughly rinse the piece to remove any dust or debris from transit. Tannin Management: This wood will release natural tannins, giving your water a warm, "tea-colored" tint. This is a natural occurrence, and the effects will subside over time. If you prefer the crystal-clear look, boil the wood for 1–2 hours or soak it in a separate container until the water runs clear. You can also reduce this effect through consistent water changes or through the addition of Aquario Neo Carbon Bag Placement: Once prepped, simply place the wood into your layout. Since it’s denser than a bad dad joke, it should settle into your substrate immediately. Important note: We recommend rinsing wood thoroughly before adding it to an established aquarium. If you prefer, you may also boil the wood for at least 1–2 hours to help release tannins.

Plant Profile Meet Pogostemon Erectus, an eye-catching aquatic stem plant that basically grew its own tiny forest underwater! Needle-like foliage radiates out from central stems in dense, starburst whorls, giving off serious miniature-pine-tree energy. Its crisp, vibrant lime-green color creates striking contrast against broader-leaved green or deep red plants nearby. This one's best suited for experienced hobbyists running high-tech setups, but the payoff is worth it: routine trimming sends the stems branching like crazy, turning individual shoots into a thick, dramatic background forest or a picture-perfect Dutch-style aquarium. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Pine-needle foliage adds textural detail and architectural interest to background zones. Lime-green coloration creates a strong visual focal point and contrasts with red stem plants. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide medium-to-high lighting and pressurized CO2 injection; consistent fertilization with a specialized liquid macro and micro formula yields robust stem growth and prevents bottom leaf yellowing. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or rotting. Trim main stem tops with sharp straight scissors once they reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and thicken the bush. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Pogostemon erectus Common Name(s) Pogostemon Erectus Family Lamiaceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Tissue Culture Stem Plant Care Difficulty Medium to Advanced Light Requirement Medium to High CO2 Requirement Recommended (Essential for compact, dense needle whorls) Placement / Usage Midground / Background Bushing Height / Size 4–12”+ (Cup portion size: 2–3”) Growth Rate Moderate Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 Propagation Method Cuttings (Cut stem tops or lateral shoots and replant) Origin India / Southeast Asia Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I achieve a thick, bushy forest with Pogostemon Erectus? To encourage Pogostemon Erectus to form a dense hedge, routinely trim the main stem tops once established. Each cut site will sprout multiple lateral side shoots, doubling the stem density and creating a tight, cloud-like needle bush. 3. How do I prepare Pogostemon Erectus Tissue Culture before planting? Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the cluster into smaller clumps or individual stems and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

listings.commonName: Riccia Fluitans Tissue Culture - Small Cup
listings.description: Plant Profile Riccia Fluitans is the choice for you if you want to recreate the legendary, high-definition layouts made famous by master aquascaper Takashi Amano. This unique liverwort grows in thick, bright green, interlocking mats that look absolutely striking under bright lights. Because it is rootless, it can either be left free-floating at the surface or tied and glued down to rocks, driftwood, or stainless steel mesh to form a bubbling green carpet. Under strong lighting and a steady supply of carbon dioxide, it will routinely trap oxygen bubbles right at its leaf tips, producing a breathtaking, shimmering phenomenon known as "pearling." Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Vibrant neon-green coloration and fine branching structure deliver a high-end, professionally scaped look. Functions as a floating surface cover for fry or a dense foreground carpet when tied to hardscape. Care & Planting Instructions Rinse away the nutrient gel thoroughly under lukewarm water, separate into small portions, and attach to mesh or hardscape. Maintain a stable aquarium environment and trim regularly to prevent the lower layers from dying off and floating away. Give the plant an occasional light haircut with sharp aquascaping shears to keep its shape neat, compact, and perfectly balanced. Propagate your patch in seconds by cutting or pulling a small clump apart and anchoring it to a new surface in your tank. Add CO2 injection if you want to accelerate growth and unlock the most intense, eye-popping green coloration possible. Manzanita is a beloved, branchy type of aquarium driftwood that is perfect for adding fine, natural detail to your layout. With their delicate, spindly limbs, these versatile pieces are the premier choice for DIY moss trees, intricate root-like depth, or adding subtle texture to a larger aquarium hardscape. Whether you're building a nano tank or layering complex details into a massive planted display, this aquascaping wood makes it easy to weave a sense of organic growth and delicate precision right into your underwater landscape. Product Features & Benefits Manzanita’s naturally thin and twisting limbs allow you to create intricate "tree-top" effects or complex root systems without cluttering your aquarium hardscape. Unlike the heavier "forbidden tea" leaching of other woods, Manzanita is much lighter in tannin content. It’s perfect for hobbyists who want the wood look without a significant shift in water color. Size Specifications Photos provided are a representation of what you will receive. This is a natural aquarium hardscape product; please expect variations in shape, weight, and character. Small: 8-10 inches Medium: 12-15 inches Preparation & Care A little extra prep goes a long way in maintaining its stunning appearance. Rinse: Thoroughly rinse the piece to remove any dust or debris from transit. The Floating Phase: Depending on the size, Manzanita will float a little initially. We recommend soaking it thoroughly or boiling it. A large stone or heavy decor may be placed on top to ensure a non-waterlogged piece of wood stays submerged. Tannin Control: If you want zero tint in your water, a quick 1-hour boil will fast-track the sinking process and remove any remaining surface tannins. You can also reduce this effect through consistent water changes or through the addition of Aquario Neo Carbon Bag Important note: We recommend rinsing wood thoroughly before adding it to an established aquarium. If you prefer, you may also boil the wood for at least 1–2 hours to help release tannins.

Red Lava Rock is the vibrant, earthy counterpart to our classic Black Lava Rock . As a highly porous volcanic stone, it is a versatile staple in the hobby, widely used for both lush planted tanks and African Cichlid setups. This lightweight natural rock features a spectrum of deep brick-red to burnt-orange tones, providing a warm, organic contrast to green aquatic plants. The porosity of this natural stone makes it an excellent addition to your aquarium filtration system; its millions of tiny holes provide a massive surface area for beneficial nitrifying bacteria to colonize. The texture also makes it a perfect pick for anchoring mosses, ferns, and other epiphytic species. Red Lava Rock is also suitable for non-aquarium use and will work beautifully as a textured accent in terrariums, paludariums, or similar bioactive enclosures. Stones vary in shape, size, and density. Notes: If you are looking for larger stones, a minimum weight may be required. Larger stones = higher weight. Email our team if you need assistance. We recommend rinsing stones thoroughly before use to remove any natural dust or sediment. Stone coloration darkens when wet.

Plant Profile Juncus Repens, or Lesser Creeping Rush, is a unique, grass-like aquatic plant native to the wetlands, boggy margins, and shallow waters of North America. It features tufts of flattened, needle-thin leaves growing along creeping stems. Versatile and beginner-friendly, Juncus Repens bridges the gap between carpeting plants and traditional stem species. Under low-to-moderate lighting, it maintains a clean, bright green bushy appearance in the foreground or midground; however, when exposed to high-intensity light and iron supplementation, its leaf tips transform into striking reddish-brown and copper-bronze hues. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Grass-like leaf tufts provide a textural contrast alongside broader-leaved or finely feathered stem species. Foliage shifts from vibrant green to rich copper, red, and brownish-bronze tones when grown under intense light and iron supplementation. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip lower foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stem tufts 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower growth. Provide low-to-high lighting for healthy growth; while extremely easy and undemanding under low light, higher light levels trigger vibrant reddish-brown pigmentation. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters across a wide pH range (6.0–8.0); CO2 injection is not required but will promote faster creeping and denser bushy clusters. Trim stem tops or separate lateral creeping shoots with straight scissors, replanting the trimmings directly into the substrate to propagate. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. As new growth adapts, the plant will shed its stiffer emersed shoots and sprout soft, grass-like underwater foliage. Once new shoots develop, trim away old lower growth to encourage dense branching.

Plant Profile Meet Ceratophyllum Demersum, aka Hornwort or Coontail, the aquatic plant that skipped roots entirely and still somehow thrives everywhere. Found floating in quiet lakes, ponds, and slow-moving streams worldwide, it grows dense, needle-like whorls of stiff green foliage that branch out into bushy arrangements, looking every bit like its raccoon-tail nickname. No roots means it pulls nutrients straight through its foliage instead, turning it into a natural filter that chews through excess nitrates and phosphates before algae gets a chance. It's a favorite for beginners, shrimp keepers, and fish breeders alike, giving fry, shrimplets, and shy tankmates a place to hide out. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in its natural submerged form. Depending on farm availability and seasonality, portion size and branching density may vary slightly. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Needle-like foliage whorls shelter fry and shrimplets, plus grazing biofilm. Fast-growing, rootless habit acts as a natural nutrient sponge, improving water quality and fighting algae. Beginner-friendly and adaptable, thrives floating or anchored without CO2 or soil. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight or rubber bands gently from the stem bases upon arrival. * Note that Hornwort is a rootless species and does not form traditional root systems. To keep Hornwort floating, simply place stems directly onto the water surface where they will freely drift and expand under light. To anchor Hornwort submerged, secure stem bases loosely to hardscape using plant weights or suction cups; avoid burying stem bases deep in dense substrate, as buried portions will decay. Provide low-to-high lighting and stable water parameters; CO2 injection is not required, making it an ideal choice for low-tech setups. Prune oversized or sprawling stems by simply cutting along any stem node with sharp aquatic scissors, and allow trimmings to float to propagate new plants. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Does Hornwort grow roots in aquarium substrate? No, Hornwort is a strictly rootless aquatic plant. Yes, floating is the natural and easiest way to grow Hornwort. Letting it drift along the surface provides excellent shade, absorbs floating nutrients efficiently, and creates a safe sanctuary for fish fry and dwarf shrimp. 3. Why is my Hornwort shedding its needles? Hornwort needle shedding (often called "melting") typically happens when the plant experiences sudden changes in water parameters, extreme temperature swings, or when introduced to a new environment. Keeping parameters stable, providing adequate light, and avoiding harsh chemical treatments will help it adjust quickly and sprout dense new growth.

Plant Profile Myriophyllum Tetrandrum is a delicate aquatic stem plant that closely resembles its relative Parrot's Feather ( Myriophyllum aquaticum ), although this species is better adapted for long-term submerged aquarium growth. Featuring fine, needle-like leaves that radiate in soft, fir-like whorls, it displays a striking contrast between bright lime-green foliage and rich reddish-brown central stems. Unique among many fine-leafed stem plants, Myriophyllum Tetrandrum thrives exceptionally well in moderately hard water conditions. Growing quickly to heights of 4 to 12+ inches, it forms dense, cloud-like green bushes that serve as ideal background filler in nature aquariums and Dutch-style layouts. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Delicate needle-like green whorls contrasted by reddish-brown stems add soft visual texture and movement to background zones. Superior submerged adaptation compared to other watermilfoil varieties, performing exceptionally well even in harder water setups. Fast-growing stem habit acts as an effective natural nutrient sponge to help maintain clean water and prevent unwanted algae. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight (or pot) and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the roots, then strip lower foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. * Myriophyllum foliage is extraordinarily delicate, so handle stems with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems or small stem groups 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower foliage and prevents leggy decay. Provide moderate-to-high lighting and clean water conditions; while adaptable, supplying pressurized CO2 and quality aquarium soil yields much denser, bushier growth and richer stem coloration. See our guide to growing colorful aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or needle shedding. Trim main stem tops with sharp straight scissors once stems reach the desired height, and replant top trimmings or lateral shoots directly into substrate to propagate and expand coverage. Plant Profile Rotala Macrandra Green is a classic green cultivar of one of aquascaping's most beloved stem plants. It's adored by planted tank enthusiasts for its soft, wavy leaves and famously fast growth habit (up to 4 inches a week under optimal conditions). While maintaining a lush, light-green base coloration, its foliage can blush with delicate pink to subtle orange tips when grown under high-tech aquarium conditions with tuned nutrient dosing. Rotala Macrandra Green is a go-to choice for background or midground placement, forming dense, textured bushes that bring movement, color contrast, and that coveted "jungle" look to freshwater aquascapes. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Lush light-green wavy leaves that blush with delicate pink and orange tips under tuned fertilization and high lighting. Fast vertical growth habit quickly creates thick, energetic background or midground hedges in high-tech planted aquariums. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip the lower inch of foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. * Rotala have fragile leaves, so handle with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into soil, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower growth and prevents bottom leaf loss. Provide high-intensity lighting and pressurized CO2 injection; maintain stable phosphate levels (1.5–2.0 ppm) and lean nitrates (10 ppm or less) to encourage pink-blushing leaf tips. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem stunting. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the water surface to encourage dense side branching, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate. Growing up to 12 inches tall, it makes a solid midground focal point in larger aquariums or a background hedge in medium-sized planted tanks, standing out without needing to try too hard. Fast growth rate acts as an excellent nutrient sponge to help stabilize new aquascapes against algae. listings.description: Common Name: Round Leaf Sundew Drosera Rotundifolia is a carnivorous sundew plant that can be found growing in bogs or marshes. The sugary mucilage on the tips of the leaves attract insects which the plant feeds on. This makes Drosera Rotundifolia a great addition to any terrarium or paludarium. Make sure to keep humidity high and never fully submerge the plant. Drosera Rotundifolia, more commonly known as the sundew plant, is a perennial that goes dormant in winter. During its dormancy period, it does best in cool temperatures (between 32-50°F/1-10°C), moist conditions, and some light. It's normal for the leaves to drop during this time, and the plant will grow new ones once it wakes up again in spring. So if you're looking for a low-maintenance plant that doesn't require much attention during the colder months, a sundew plant is a great option. Plant Profile Echinodorus Horemanii Red is a cultivated sword plant valued for its slender, wavy foliage and rich color transitions. Emerging new leaves display bright red to reddish-pink tones before turning dark green while keeping red outlines along the leaf margins. Reaching 8 to 12 inches in height, its narrow upright structure makes it an effective background choice or central midground feature in medium to large aquariums. Because it grows well under low lighting without mandatory CO2 injection, it serves as a beginner-friendly and low-tech plant option for aquarists setting up low-maintenance planted tanks. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Slightly wavy, narrow foliage transitions from red on young growth to dark green with red margins on mature leaves. Upright rosette habit provides tall structural presence in midground and background zones. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Plant the roots firmly into your aquarium soil, ensuring the central crown remains positioned slightly above the substrate line to avoid tissue rot. All Echinodorus are heavy root feeders that rely on rich substrate nutrition; placing root tabs near the base supports steady, healthy leaf development. Provide low to moderate lighting; while CO2 is not required, supplying moderate light and liquid iron supplements helps bring out the red highlights on newly emerging leaves. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters to avoid leaf melting during the transition to submerged growth. To propagate, separate new daughter plantlets that form along the crown or runner stems once they develop independent roots, then replant them into your aquarium soil. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I prepare Echinodorus Horemanii Red Tissue Culture before planting? Rinse the gel completely off the roots in a bowl of room-temperature water. Once clean, divide the cluster into individual plantlets or small clumps and insert the roots into your aquarium soil using fine pinsettes. 2. Is Echinodorus Horemanii Red suitable for low-tech aquariums? Yes, Echinodorus Horemanii Red is a low-tech species that grows well under low to moderate lighting without CO2 injection. Adding root tabs to your aquarium soil helps provide the root nutrition needed for healthy foliage. 3. Why are root tabs recommended for sword plants grown from tissue culture? Echinodorus species absorb most of their nutrients through their root systems rather than relying strictly on liquid fertilizers in the water column. Placing root tabs directly in your aquarium soil supports steady root anchoring and leaf development after planting.

Plant Profile Pogostemon helferi, commonly known in the hobby as 'Downoi' (Thai for "little star"), is a striking aquatic species native to the fast-flowing streams of Thailand. Reaching just 2 to 3 inches in height, it stands out immediately for its unique rosette of heavily crinkled, zig-zag leaves that resemble miniature palm trees or starbursts. Given sufficient lighting and nutrient availability, it stays low and compact, sending out lateral side shoots to form a dense, textured carpet or prominent midground grouping. Its distinct foliage and architectural growth pattern make it a favorite for aquascapers looking to add detailed focal points near hardscape borders. Key Features & Notes Crinkled, starburst-like foliage adds unmatched texture and visual detail to foreground or midground layouts. Compact rosette habit stays low to the substrate, slowly spreading via side shoots into tight clusters. Moderate-to-high lighting and consistent CO2 injection encourage rich green coloration and tight, bushy growth. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Plant individual stems deeply into aquarium soil using fine-tipped tweezers, taking care not to crush the delicate crown or lower leaves. Provide medium to high lighting and pressurized CO2 injection to prevent stems from stretching thin or dropping lower leaves. Avoid sudden, drastic changes in water parameters or light intensity, as Downoi can be sensitive to environmental shocks during transition. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I propagate Pogostemon helferi 'Downoi'? As the plant matures, it develops small side shoots around the base of the crown. Trim these side shoots or the main stem cleanly with aquascaping scissors and replant them directly into nutrient-rich substrate. 2. Can this plant grow without pressurized CO2 injection? While Downoi can survive in well-maintained low-tech tanks with adequate light and nutrients, pressurized CO2 is strongly recommended to achieve its signature compact, starburst growth and vibrant green color. 3. Why are the leaves on my Downoi turning yellow or melting after planting? Downoi can be sensitive to environmental transitions or parameter shifts. Ensure your water chemistry remains stable, provide sufficient substrate nutrition, and avoid disturbing the root system once planted.

Anubias Nana grown on stone Anubias Nana is one of the most popular aquatic plants in the hobby. If you're new to planted tanks and want to try growing for the first time, this is a good one to start with. It's an extremely easy plant to grow and can survive a wide range of water parameters. Like other Anubias plants it can grow in both aquariums and terrariums either submerged or emersed. Anubias Nana is a flowering plant that grows best when the rhizome is attached to a hard surface such as wood or stones. They have low to medium light requirements and can benefit from regular fertilization. CO2 is not necessary but can promote faster growth and more robust leaves. Since its a slow grower, the leaves are susceptible to algae growth if placed under high lighting. Propagation is easy and straightforward; simply cut or pull apart rhizomes to be replanted. Notes: Anubias are strong plants that can thrive in a variety of environments. These epiphytes can be planted above the substrate or attached to hardscape . Burying the rhizome, will cause the plant to melt and die. Do not make drastic changes to the aquarium. Unstable parameters will result in melt and rotting of the aquarium plant. Please be sure to remove this plant from its pot. For instructions on how to properly prep aquarium plants, click here . CO2 injection and quality aquarium soil will yield better growth. Please research appropriately to ensure your plant thrives. Plant Profile Cryptocoryne albida 'Red' brings extraordinary color and rare collector appeal directly to your foreground layout! This aquarium plant is extremely hard to come by and is considered a seasonal item for us. It features narrow red leaves with striped markings similar to Crypt Nuri, cycling through shades of pink to red, though higher light intensity brings out even more of that reddish color. It stays relatively compact, which makes it a great foreground accent that pops against darker hardscape or green neighboring plants. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Slender pink-to-red striped foliage brings intense color and high-contrast texture to foreground zones. Can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups, where mature plants may produce flowering spathes. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel to supply essential subterranean nutrients. Provide medium-to-high light and stable pressurized CO2 injection right from day one to lock in its signature bright red pigmentation and prevent lingering transition shock. Pick its final foreground location carefully before planting; moving this high-demand crypt once it sets roots almost always causes severe melting. Crypt species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I get the brightest red and pink colors out of Cryptocoryne Albida Red? Sufficient light intensity is key to driving vibrant pigmentation, alongside root tab supplementation rich in iron and trace elements. Pressurized CO2 injection also encourages denser foliage growth with more pronounced tiger-stripe patterning. 2. How do I help my Cryptocoryne recover if it melts? Trim away dissolving leaves, maintain stable water parameters, and leave the root system undisturbed so it can rebuild new foliage. Check our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt for full recovery steps. 3. Should I use root tabs or liquid fertilizers? Root tabs are best. Cryptocoryne species are heavy root feeders that draw primary nutrition from the substrate rather than the water column.

Plant Profile Hemigraphis colorata, aka Purple Waffle Plant, is a sprawling tropical perennial with deeply puckered, corrugated leaves that show off dark metallic olive surfaces above and a brilliant, vivid royal purple underneath. This two-toned purple foliage creates an immediate visual punch against hardscape or breaks up endless fields of green plants in midground zones. Like its cousin Dragon's Tongue , Purple Waffle is a classic victim of pet store mislabeling, where it often gets dunked in fully submerged aquariums to masquerade as an aquatic stem, only to drown and melt after a few weeks. Given a humid, emersed setup, those textured ridges will catch the light and add rich color depth! Key Features & Notes Two-toned crinkled foliage pairs dark metallic olive-green tops with vibrant royal purple undersides. Heavily puckered waffle texture catches indirect light and creates bold visual contrast on the tank floor. A strictly terrestrial grower that will melt away if planted fully underwater in an aquarium setup. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Tuck the root system into a loose, airy tropical substrate blend loaded with bark, perlite, and peat moss so moisture stays consistent without turning waterlogged. Provide moderate to bright indirect light; decent light intensity is essential to keep that rich purple pigmentation saturated, but direct scorching rays will toast the leaf edges. Maintain humidity above 70% while ensuring excess water can drain away freely to prevent the lower stems from suffocating. Pinch back spreading branch tips just above a leaf node to keep the mound dense, compact, and tidy. Final size and purple color intensity depend entirely on your specific setup conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Hemigraphis colorata are terrestrial plants, and being submerged will result in the death of the plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Hemigraphis colorata (syn. Hemigraphis alternata ) Common Name(s) Purple Waffle Plant, Red Ivy, Metallic Purple Waffle Family Acanthaceae Plant Type Terrestrial Tropical Perennial / Groundcover Care Difficulty Easy Light Requirement Moderate to Bright Indirect Submersion Suitability Emersed Only (Not for full submersion) Placement / Usage Foreground, Midground, Paludarium Margins Height / Size 6"–12" (15–30 cm) Growth Rate Moderate Humidity Requirement High (> 70% RH) Propagation Method Stem Cuttings / Lateral Runners Origin Southeast Asia (Indonesia) Frequently Asked Questions 1. Can Purple Waffle Plant grow fully submerged in a fish tank? No. Even though fish stores often sell it in submerged display tanks, Purple Waffle is strictly a terrestrial plant that will slowly rot away if kept underwater. 2. How do I keep the purple color vibrant on my Purple Waffle Plant? Provide plenty of bright, filtered indirect light. If kept in lighting that is too dim, the vibrant purple undersides will fade to a dull, washed-out greenish tone. 3. How do you propagate Hemigraphis colorata? Snip a healthy stem cutting or lateral runner with two or three sets of leaves, remove the lowest leaves, and press the cut node into damp sphagnum moss or light soil until roots establish

Made from rugged, ultra‑transparent acrylic that looks like glass but won’t shatter, it’s a clean, high‑performance upgrade for both rimmed and rimless tanks. Key Features & Benefits An integrated bubble counter chamber design lets you track your daily dosing rate easily without adding external inline equipment clutter. The heavy-duty acrylic construction is completely shatterproof, providing vast safety improvements over fragile, easy-to-snap glass alternatives. Specialized micro-hole ceramic membrane technology vaporizes gas into an ultra-fine mist for rapid and efficient plant absorption. The versatile straight-tube geometry installs effortlessly alongside the walls of both rimmed and rimless aquarium configurations. Technical Specifications For maximum efficiency, always place your diffuser in an area with active water movement, such as directly under your filter's outflow stream, to distribute the rising micro-bubbles evenly. Size Disk Diameter Tube Height Tank Size Small 12mm 5.65 inches 13 gallons or less Medium 17mm 5.65 inches Up to 32 gallons Large 24mm 5.65 inches 32 gallons or larger Additional Information Submerge the entire diffuser in clean water for 30 minutes before connecting it to your gas line. This primes the micro-pores of the ceramic membrane, ensuring it produces a fine mist instantly on startup rather than large, wasteful bubbles. Over time, natural organic film or algae can accumulate on the ceramic surface, causing the bubbles to grow larger. When this happens, simply soak the diffuser in standard household bleach for 10 minutes, then rinse it thoroughly with fresh water and a generous dose of aquarium water conditioner to completely neutralize any residual bleach before placing it back in your tank. Plant Profile Dwarf Sagittaria (Sagittaria subulata) brings that fresh‑cut‑lawn energy straight into your tank. This hobby‑favorite foreground plant adds subtle depth to your layout, but it’s versatile enough to stretch into the midground or even background of your aquascape when it’s feeling extra ambitious. Its bright green, wide blades mimic those dreamy riverbank vibes while doubling as a cozy hideout for shrimp and nano fish. It grows happily emersed or submersed, and once it matures, it can even reach the surface and pop out tiny white flowers. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Tolerates hard, alkaline water conditions where other plants might struggle. Provides an excellent foraging ground, shelter, and security for baby fish, dwarf shrimp, and nano inhabitants. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Stick to moderate lighting for standard growth, or upgrade to higher lighting to watch it thrive and potentially bring out beautiful red tones in the leaves. Supplement with iron and other nutrients if you notice the leaves looking sickly and yellow. Grow it with or without pressurized CO2. It doesn't require it to grow, but adding it will make it carpet much faster. Master the basics by learning how to properly grow aquarium carpet plants to ensure your new layout fills in quickly. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth!
