Why is my Dwarf Sagittaria growing tall instead of staying short? Dwarf Sagittaria naturally grows taller in lower lighting conditions as its leaves reach upward for light. Providing stronger lighting will encourage it to stay shorter, produce shorter leaves, and spread horizontally via runners. 2. Does Dwarf Sagittaria require CO2 injection? No, CO2 is completely optional for Dwarf Sagittaria. It is one of the easiest carpeting plants to grow in low-tech setups, though adding pressurized CO2 will significantly increase its carpeting speed and leaf density. 3. Why are the leaves on my Dwarf Sagittaria turning yellow? Yellowing foliage is a common sign of iron or nutrient deficiency. Dwarf Sagittaria feeds heavily through its root system, so placing nutrient-rich root tabs near the plant will restore its bright green color quickly.

Plant Profile If you've ever wished your aquascape had the neat, orderly vibes of a freshly pruned garden hedge, meet Lobelia cardinalis , aka the Cardinal Plant. This species is known for growing sturdy, upright stems packed with thick, rounded leaves that look almost like miniature green spades. While emersed specimens have flowers and deep purple leaf undersides, its underwater persona trades the drama for crisp, bright-green foliage with just a whisper of violet underneath. It's exceptional for sculpting classic Dutch-style "plant streets" or defining clean midground boundaries. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Growth habit ideal for sculpting structured Dutch-style plant streets and midground hedges. Crisp green foliage displays subtle purple and violet undersides. Beginner-friendly and flourishes across aquariums, paludariums, and terrariums. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide moderate-to-high lighting and consistent fertilization; while pressurized CO2 injection is not strictly required, adding CO2 yields thicker stems, vibrant leaf coloration, and faster lateral shoot production. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or rotting. Trim main stem tops with sharp straight scissors to maintain a low street layout, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to easily propagate new shoots. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How is Lobelia Cardinalis used in Dutch-style aquascapes? Lobelia Cardinalis is legendary in Dutch aquascaping for creating "plant streets", sloped rows planted from front to back at an angle. Regular pruning keeps the stems low in the front and taller in the back, creating dramatic visual perspective and depth. 3. How do I prepare Lobelia Cardinalis UNS Tissue Culture before planting? Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the dense cluster into smaller clumps or individual stems and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

Plant Profile The Red Root Floater is a beautiful floating plant with light green leaves that can turn blood red when kept under high light. What makes this plant unique and highly sought after is its striking blood-red roots, setting it apart from the usual brown roots of other aquarium floaters. This small floating fern quickly spreads into thick mats across the surface, making it perfect for low-tech aquariums and paludariums where it creates natural shade to suppress algae growth. Just keep in mind that these floating plants for aquariums prefer low flow and will not survive in a tank with heavy surface agitation. You will receive 2-3 dime-sized plants with a minimum of 2-3 leaves each. Key Features & Benefits Small white flowers bloom along the leaves under strong lighting and stable water parameters. Absorbs excess nitrates and biological waste to starve out nuisance algae. Dense crimson roots provide shelter for shrimp and fry while giving shy fish confidence to explore. Care & Planting Instructions Gently place the plants directly onto the water surface, ensuring the tops of the leaves remain dry. Keep surface agitation minimal, as heavy water flow or splashing filters will trap water on top of the leaves and cause them to rot. Provide adequate lighting to encourage rapid growth and bring out rich coloration. Thin out the floating carpet regularly to ensure light still reaches your submerged midground and stem plants below. Dose liquid fertilizers regularly because floating plants absorb nutrients directly from the water column at an accelerated rate. Click here for an in-depth Red Root Floater Care Guide. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Phyllanthus fluitans Common Name(s) Red Root Floater Family Phyllanthaceae Plant Type Floating Plant / Fern Height / Size Leaves up to 1 in. wide | Roots 1–4 in. long Care Difficulty Easy Light Requirement Low to High (6 to 8 hours daily) CO2 Requirement Not Required Placement / Usage Water Surface Canopy, Livestock Shade Growth Rate Fast Water Parameters pH 6.5–7.5 | Temperature 70°F–82°F (21°C–28°C) Propagation Method Division (Side Shoots / Runners) Origin South America Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I keep my floating aquarium plants from dying due to filter flow and splashing? High water turbulence and constant water resting on the leaves are the main causes of rot in floating aquarium plants. Keep surface flow low, or use an airline tubing loop or floating ring to shield your aquarium floaters from direct filter return or bubbling air stones. 2. Can floating plants help control algae and absorb nitrates in a fish tank? Yes, these aquarium floaters act as incredible biological filters. Because they sit at the surface with direct access to atmospheric carbon dioxide, they grow exponentially faster than fully submerged species, aggressively consuming nitrates, ammonium, and excess nutrients that fuel nuisance algae. 3. Should I trim the hanging roots or thin out excess surface growth? You can trim the long red roots using sharp aquascaping scissors to maintain your desired aesthetic without harming the plant. However, routinely thinning out excess leaves is crucial so that your floating plants do not block all light from reaching your submerged stem and ground plants below.

Plant Profile Bucephalandra ‘Red Blade’ is a compact, low-tech epiphyte prized for its narrow, slightly curly foliage with sharp, distinct tips and a subtle reddish tint that develops once adapted to life underwater. Standing at 1 to 2.5 inches tall, this nano-sized species is uniquely suited for fine detailing, making it a perfect fit for tucking into tight hardscape crevices, wedging between stones, or carpeting the immediate foreground of freshwater aquascapes. Adaptable to both submerged aquariums and high-humidity emersed environments, its rhizomes attach readily to wood or rock, yielding a low-maintenance, textured accent for planted tanks. Key Features & Notes The pointed tips and ruffled leaf margins offer a rugged, aggressive texture that contrasts beautifully with rounder Buce varieties. Under stable conditions and quality LED lighting, the leaves transition from simple greens to a warm, reddish-maroon hue. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for planted tanks where other plants might struggle. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard low-light aquarium plant setups, CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and richer color development. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Why is my Bucephalandra melting? Bucephalandra melt can occur after changes in water chemistry, temperature, or lighting. If the rhizome remains firm, keep it attached to hardscape while the plant acclimates and produces new submerged growth. 2. Can I plant Bucephalandra in substrate? Bucephalandra is an epiphyte, so never bury its rhizome in substrate. Attach it to driftwood or rocks, or wedge the roots into hardscape while keeping the rhizome exposed. 3. Is Bucephalandra ‘Red Blade’ beginner-friendly? Yes. Bucephalandra ‘Red Blade’ is a beginner-friendly, low-light aquarium plant that grows without specialized substrate or pressurized CO₂, making it well suited for low-tech planted aquariums.

Plant Profile Borneo Fern (Trichomanes javanicum) is a terrestrial filming fern native to the shaded rainforest floors and riverbanks of Southeast Asia, prized for its delicate, translucent foliage that seems to shimmer under soft lighting. This species is a non-aquatic epiphyte that thrives exclusively in high-humidity terrariums, vivariums, and paludarium land sections where it can cling to damp rocks or wood. Unbothered by low lighting and slow to overgrow its boundaries, it anchors effortlessly onto damp moss or hardscape to deliver ethereal forest texture. Key Features & Notes Delicate, paper-thin translucent fronds shimmer under terrarium lighting, providing exceptional visual depth and fine texture. Exclusively non-aquatic terrestrial species designed specifically for humid terrariums, vivariums, and paludarium land setups. Do not keep fully submerged long-term. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Borneo Fern is an epiphytic terrestrial fern that should be mounted to damp rocks or wood in humid setups; never bury the horizontal rhizome beneath heavy substrate, as it will rot and decay. Ensure high ambient air humidity (80%+) and moist air circulation to prevent its thin, paper-like foliage from drying out. Avoid placing this fern fully underwater; while it tolerates occasional splashing or high soil moisture, permanent submersion will lead to leaf melt. Final size and foliage pattern depend entirely on your specific enclosure conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Trichomanes javanicum Common Name(s) Borneo Fern, Filmy Fern, Aqua Fern (Terrestrial) Family Hymenophyllaceae Plant Type Terrestrial / Emersed Epiphyte (Filmy Fern) Care Difficulty Easy (Terrarium / Paludarium Environment) Light Requirement Low to Medium CO2 Requirement Not Required Placement / Usage Terrariums, Vivariums, Paludarium Land Section Height / Size 4"–8" (10–20 cm) Growth Rate Slow Environment Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 | High Ambient Humidity Required (Non-Submerged) Propagation Method Rhizome Division Origin Southeast Asia Frequently Asked Questions 1. Can I grow Borneo Fern (Trichomanes javanicum) fully submerged in an aquarium? No. Borneo Fern is a true terrestrial/emersed filmy fern, not a fully aquatic plant. While it is sometimes sold in the aquarium trade under the misnomer "Aqua Fern," keeping it completely underwater long-term will cause the fronds to rot. It is best suited for high-humidity terrariums, vivariums, or paludarium land sections. 2. What is a "filmy fern" and why are the leaves translucent? Filmy ferns (family Hymenophyllaceae) have leaves that are often only one cell layer thick, lacking a dense cuticle layer found in traditional plants. This unique anatomy allows them to absorb water and nutrients directly from humid air and misty surroundings, giving the foliage its delicate, translucent appearance. 3. How do I propagate Borneo Fern? Propagation is simple: use sharp, sterilized scissors to cut the horizontal creeping rhizome into smaller sections, making sure each piece retains at least 3–4 healthy fronds. Attach the divided sections to new hardscape features in your humid enclosure.

listings.description: Plant Profile Utricularia Graminifolia, affectionately known in the hobby as UG, is a highly sought-after aquatic carpeting plant that delivers a vibrant, velvety aesthetic that regular aquarium grasses simply cannot match. Unlike traditional options like Monte Carlo or Dwarf Baby Tears , this unique species is a carnivorous bladderwort, characterized by thousands of microscopic traps that capture tiny microorganisms in the water column. But don't worry! These traps are completely microscopic, making them 100% safe for dwarf shrimp, fish fry, and all other tank inhabitants. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Forms an ultra-dense, velvety foreground lawn with bright green, grass-like foliage. Unique microscopic carnivorous traps capture water-column microorganisms while remaining 100% safe for shrimp and fry. Functions as a distinct alternative to standard carpeting plants for high-tech setups and Wabi Kusa layouts. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions and planting. Use a dry start method or Wabi Kusa setup to give its delicate root system plenty of time to firmly anchor into the substrate before you flood the tank. Separate the larger tissue culture mats into small portions and plant each piece about an inch apart, burying them halfway into the substrate. Provide medium to high lighting and ensure it doesn’t get shaded by larger background plants, as this species demands direct light. Inject pressurized CO2 to drastically increase its growth speed, density, and thickness. Learn tips and tricks by reading our complete guide on how to grow Utricularia Graminifolia (UG). How do I plant Utricularia Graminifolia (UG) tissue culture? Rinse away the gel, separate the mat into small coin-sized plugs, and use fine pinsettes to press each portion halfway into nutrient-dense, fine aquasoil spaced 1 inch apart. 2. Is Utricularia Graminifolia (UG) safe for dwarf shrimp and fish fry? Yes, 100%. Because its roots are delicate, current or livestock can dislodge unanchored plugs. Utilizing the Dry Start Method for 4–6 weeks or keeping initial water column nutrients low will securely root the carpet and prevent tissue melt before flooding.

listings.commonName: Glossostigma Elatinoides Platinum Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Glossostigma Elatinoides 'Platinum' is an extremely rare and highly sought-after variant of regular green Glosso . The leaves of this stunning mutation can range from a vibrant yellow to an almost translucent off-white color, making it an extraordinarily unique foreground choice. Because it is rarely available in the hobby, we are typically only able to secure a handful of cups at a time. This distinctive, pale coloration makes it a fascinating anomaly compared to traditional green and red aquatic plants, allowing it to contrast beautifully and dramatically against darker hardscape like lava rock or driftwood. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Rare yellow-to-off-white foliage creates a high-contrast foreground carpet. Retains the fast-growing, low-profile carpet habit of classic Glossostigma elatinoides. Care & Planting Instructions Remove the tissue culture gel completely before planting by washing it away under cool water or soaking the cup and gently squeezing the gel from the roots with your fingers. Use a dry start method or Wabi Kusa setup to give its tiny, delicate root system plenty of time to firmly anchor into the substrate before you flood the tank. Provide high lighting and heavy CO2 injection to keep this plant hugging the substrate. Keep nutrients balanced and rich; thin leaves hint at a lack of CO2, while any additional yellowing or translucent deterioration can point to a nutrient deficiency. Trim the carpet regularly once it is established, as proper high-tech conditions will trigger rapid horizontal growth. Master the basics by learning how to properly grow aquarium carpet plants to ensure your new layout fills in quickly, evenly, and stays free of algae. Maintaining bright lighting alongside balanced macro and micronutrients is essential. Balanced fertilizing ensures the leaves maintain their unique cream-to-platinum hues.

Plant Profile Rotala Nanjenshan is a delicate natural hybrid aquatic stem plant originating near Nanjenshan, Taiwan. Believed to be a natural cross between Rotala rotundifolia and Rotala wallichii , this unique species combines the hardy growth habit of Rotundifolia with the fine, needle-like leaf structure of Wallichii. Featuring dense whorls of slender, hair-like leaves along flexible stems, it displays a vibrant lime-green coloration that blushes soft pink, orange, and yellow-gold at the growing tips under high-tech aquarium conditions. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Needle-like foliage adds soft, cloud-like texture to midground and background zones. Hybrid origin gives lime-green foliage with blush-pink, gold, and orange growing tips under high lighting. Fast-branching growth perfect for dense hedges and Dutch-style streets with routine pruning. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight (or pot) and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the roots, then strip lower foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. * Rotala leaves are delicate, so handle stems with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems or small stem groups 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower foliage. Provide medium-to-high lighting and soft, acidic water conditions (pH 5.0–7.0); mandatory pressurized CO2 injection and consistent fertilization with iron are essential to maintain needle density and induce pinkish growing tips. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim main stem tops with straight scissors once stems reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and thicken your bush. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Rotala sp. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I get pink and gold growing tips on Rotala Nanjenshan? While Rotala Nanjenshan stays bright green under moderate conditions, developing soft pink, orange, and gold growing tips requires high light intensity, pressurized CO2, soft acidic water, and consistent dosing of liquid micro and macronutrients, particularly iron. 3. How do I transition Rotala Nanjenshan from emersed to submerged growth? When transitioning from emersed to submerged growth, plant bare stems securely into rich substrate under good lighting and pressurized CO2 while keeping water parameters stable. As new growth adapts, the plant will shed its oval land foliage and sprout delicate, needle-like underwater leaves. Once new shoots take root, trim away old lower growth to encourage dense branching.

listings.commonName: Ludwigia Inclinata Cuba Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Ludwigia Inclinata 'Cuba' is a large, showstopping aquatic stem plant native to the swampy wetlands of the Isle of Youth off the coast of Cuba. Prized for its dramatic size and extraordinary leaf morphology, its submerged form produces long, narrow foliage in dense, needle-like whorls that display a marbled swirl of fiery orange, yellow, and deep ruby-red. Reaching an impressive height of 15 to 20 inches, it requires high-tech conditions, including strong lighting, soft acidic water, high iron dosing, and pressurized CO2 to showcase its vivid coloration. Positioned in the midground or background of larger aquariums, its wide, voluminous crown creates an unforgettable centerpiece accent. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Large, voluminous whorled foliage displays a breathtaking marbled mix of yellow, fiery orange, and ruby-red tones. Fast-growing background species that forms a massive, dramatic crown accent in medium-to-large aquariums. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant individual stems 2 inches apart into nutrient-rich aquarium soil, giving each stem ample room for its wide crown. Provide high-intensity lighting and pressurized CO2 injection; consistent fertilization rich in iron and micronutrients is essential to prevent shoot blanching or white leaves. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain soft, acidic water conditions and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or rotting. To propagate, trim healthy stem tops with sharp straight shears and replant them directly into the substrate. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the cluster into smaller clumps or individual stems and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

Plant Profile Born from a rare mutation, Anubias Nana Petite White takes the beloved micro-footprint of standard Anubias Nana Petite and spices it up with spectacular white-to-cream coloration. Unlike fully ghostly variants like Snow White, this variety rocks a gorgeous marbled mix of white and deep green pattern work across its foliage. Because its variegated foliage contains less chlorophyll, it breaks standard low-light Anubias care rules and requires medium to high lighting along with CO₂ injection to thrive. Key Features & Benefits Marbled white and green variegated foliage provides unmatched color contrast in nano tanks and detailed hardscape layouts. Compact dwarf scale stays small (2 to 5 inches), making it an ideal foreground centerpiece or focal accent in tight crevices. Tough, compact leaves naturally resist grazing from plant-nibbling fish, snails, and active dwarf shrimp. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Provide medium to high lighting to compensate for reduced chlorophyll; ensure good water flow to keep variegated leaves free of spot algae. Crypt species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. If you bury its horizontal rhizome beneath aquarium soil, sand, or gravel, the stem will suffocate, rot, and die. Always attach it to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread. 4. Will fish like cichlids or goldfish eat Java Fern Windelov Twisted? Generally, no. Java Fern leaves are thick, fibrous, and contain bitter-tasting compounds that deter most plant-eating fish. While aggressive diggers might knock it off hardscape if not glued securely, they rarely consume the foliage.

Plant Profile Piptospatha Ridleyi is a rare, low-tech aquarium plant belonging to the same family as Bucephalandra, featuring elongated leaves with striking light green markings. Originating from the riverbanks of Borneo, this variety displays a beautiful dark green base color that provides a lush, tropical aesthetic to any layout. Highly versatile, it can be grown submerged or emersed, usually attached to hardscape such as driftwood or rocks rather than being buried in traditional aquarium substrate. It's a great accent for the foreground and midgrounds of planted tanks, where its unique leaf patterns and slender profile can create a colorful colony. Key Features & Notes The distinct light green variegation or markings running throughout the leaf make this a standout collector's item in the hobby. Reaching heights of 4–12 inches, it is an excellent tool for filling vertical space and providing a structural backdrop among hardscape. Like many Araceae species, it prefers low to moderate lighting; high light should be avoided to prevent algae from forming on its slow-growing leaves. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Piptospatha Ridleyi is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy once established, CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and richer color density. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Plant Profile Homalomena sp. Sekadau South is a rare rheophytic aquatic plant native to the shaded streams of Borneo, belonging to the Araceae family alongside Bucephalandra and Anubias . Staying under 6 inches in height, this uncommon collector plant features deep green, glossy leaves with visible venation that bring a distinct tropical rainforest aesthetic to the midground zones of a planted tank. Similar to its Bucephalandra cousins, it develops a creeping rhizome that can be anchored directly onto rocks and driftwood or placed loosely in substrate without burying the rhizome. Because it naturally thrives in shaded forest waters, it is a slow grower that performs best under low to moderate lighting where algae growth on the foliage can be kept in check. Key Features & Notes Broad, textured Araceae foliage introduces a rare and unique visual accent to hardscape structures. Rheophytic growth habit allows the plant to anchor directly onto rocks and driftwood via its creeping rhizome. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Attach the rhizome directly onto rocks or driftwood using aquarium glue or thread, ensuring the main rhizome remains uncovered to avoid rot. Avoid excessive high-intensity lighting to prevent green spot algae from forming on the slow-growing leaves. Supplemental CO2 injection encourages faster growth and stronger root attachment, though it can be adapted to low-tech setups with stable parameters. Maintain consistent water parameters to prevent leaf melting during the initial acclimatization period. listings.commonName: Hygrophila Siamensis Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Nomaphila stricta, also known as Hygrophila siamensis, is a fast‑growing, highly adaptable stem plant that brings a bold splash of green to midground and background layouts. With broad leaves and sturdy vertical stems, it’s the kind of resilient species that shrugs at most freshwater conditions. It grows just as happily fully submerged as it does emersed in paludariums and terrariums. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Rapid growth acts as a natural nitrate sponge for crystal-clear water, deterring nuisance algae. Equally suitable for submerged aquariums or emersed paludarium setups. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide moderate-to-high lighting for steady growth, though pressurized CO2 injection and quality soil will accelerate development and leaf size. Maintain stable water parameters and cooler water temperatures when possible, though the plant adapts easily to tropical aquarium conditions. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the water surface to encourage new lateral side branches. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Once the gel is removed, separate the dense runner cluster into smaller individual plantlets and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

listings.commonName: Helanthium Vesuvius Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Common Name: Echinodorus Vesuvius Helanthium 'Vesuvius', previously known as Echinodorus Vesuvius, features bright green leaves that exhibit a curling growth pattern. When provided with optimal conditions and a clean environment, Helanthium Vesuvius grows at a steady pace and makes for a wonderful background plant choice. It is quite hardy and can be easily propagated by separating plantlets that form via runners. Notes: Echinodorus is a very hardy species of aquatic plants. Most Echinodorus require nutrient-dense soil to thrive as they are heavy root feeders. Tissue culture plants are grown in vitro from a state of the art laboratory specialized in propagating aquatic plants. They provide the best option for those who want to ensure that absolutely zero unwanted pests are introduced into the aquarium. Remove tissue culture gel before planting. Simply wash the gel away or soak the plant in water and squeeze the gel off with your fingers. Do not make drastic changes to the aquarium. Unstable parameters will result in melt and rotting of the aquarium plant. For instructions on how to properly plant tissue culture aquarium plants, click here . CO2 injection and quality aquarium soil will yield better growth. pH: 5-7 Care: Easy Light: Low to Medium Co2: Not necessary Propagation: Split runners and replant

listings.description: Plant Profile If you want a reliable, foolproof way to get that classic backyard-lawn aesthetic inside your aquarium, Eleocharis Pusillis is your go-to choice. Highly popular throughout the hobby, this iconic aquatic grass features ultra-thin, bright green stalks that spread out horizontally by sending out eager runners. It behaves just like a terrestrial lawn, making it incredibly easy to work with, whether you are planting a traditional submerged scape or working on an emersed dry start or Wabi Kusa. It is a fantastic, straightforward option for giving your tank a clean, uniform, and natural look. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Beginner-friendly option that behaves predictably and adapts easily to various tank setups. Forms a classic, vibrant green lawn across your foreground through horizontal underground runners. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions and planting. Use a dry start method or Wabi Kusa setup to give its root system plenty of time to firmly anchor into the substrate before you flood the tank. Maintain stable aquarium parameters and avoid drastic shifts in water quality to prevent your new grass from melting. Provide medium to high lighting and inject pressurized CO2 to supercharge its density and growth rate, keeping it low and compact. Master the basics by learning how to properly grow aquarium carpet plants to ensure your new layout fills in quickly. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Dwarf Hairgrass is one of the easiest carpeting plants in the hobby and will spread in low-tech setups without pressurized CO2. However, injecting CO2 and providing medium-to-high lighting will force the runners to spread much faster and form a noticeably denser lawn. 3. How do I trim Dwarf Hairgrass to keep it looking neat? Once established, use sharp curved aquascaping scissors to mow the grass straight across, about 1 inch above the substrate. Regular trimming encourages the plant to direct its energy into sending out new horizontal runners rather than growing taller blades.

Plant Profile Hedyotis Salzmannii is a fast-growing aquatic stem plant native to the wetlands of South America. Bearing a strong resemblance to Bacopa monnieri , this species features thick, sturdy upright stems lined with pairs of small, rounded green leaves. Reaching 4 to 12 inches in height, its orderly growth habit makes it an effective choice for midground rows, dense background hedges, or Dutch-style plant streets. Because it adapts easily to standard tank conditions without requiring CO2, it is a beginner-friendly and low-tech option for aquascapers seeking a low-maintenance green backdrop. Key Features & Benefits Thick, upright stem structure provides clean geometric lines for midground rows and background hedges. Hardy, fast-growing habit helps outcompete algae by absorbing surplus nutrients from the water column. Versatile species that grows submerged in aquariums or emersed in humid terrarium and paludarium setups. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot or lead wrap and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Use fine-tip pinsettes to insert individual stems 1 inch apart into your aquarium soil so light reaches the lower leaves. Provide moderate to high lighting; while CO2 injection is optional, supplying steady light and liquid fertilization supports faster growth and thicker stem diameter. Maintain stable water parameters to encourage steady root development and prevent lower leaf shedding during transition. To propagate, trim main stem tops with sharp, straight shears and replant the cuttings directly into your aquarium soil. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. How do I make Hedyotis Salzmannii grow thicker in the background? Pruning the stem tops regularly encourages side shoots to branch out from lower leaf nodes. Replanting those trimmed stem tops back into your aquarium soil alongside the parent stems builds a dense, lush green bush over time.

Plant Profile Bacopa Monnieri Variegatus, commonly known as Variegated Moneywort or Variegated Water Hyssop, is a unique and sought-after color variant of the classic Bacopa Monnieri stem plant. This perennial aquatic species is known for its sturdy vertical stems lined with thick, succulent-like oval leaves in opposing pairs and its cream-to-white marbling layered over bright lime-green leaves. Hardy and beginner-friendly, Variegated Moneywort grows just as well submerged in aquariums as it does emersed in open-top setups and paludariums, where it produces pink and white blossoms above the waterline. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Oval foliage features white vein patterns and cream marbling. Beginner-friendly, thrives in low-tech setups without requiring CO2 injection. Sturdy vertical growth adds structured height to midground and background zones. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight (or pot) and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the roots, then strip lower foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. * Bacopa stems can be crisp, so handle with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems or small stem groups 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower leaves. Provide moderate-to-high lighting and clean water conditions; adequate light penetration is required to keep lower leaves healthy and maintain distinct variegation. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim main stem tops with straight scissors once stems reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to easily propagate and expand coverage. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Plant Profile Meet Rotala Bossii, a rare and sought-after aquatic stem plant that shares the delicate form and leaf shape of hobby favorite Rotala rotundifolia, but with a collector's-species status that puts it a cut above the usual suspects. While typically maintaining a lush, bright green color under standard lighting, its upper leaf tips can develop subtle pink, orange, or reddish highlights under high-intensity light and targeted iron fertilization. Growing rapidly with fine vertical stems, it is best placed in the midground or background of the aquarium, where its dense growth habit forms a lively, bushy backdrop. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Slender foliage that maintains a bright green base with delicate pink-orange tip accents under high light. Fast-growing stem structure easily forms dense, bushy midground or background hedges through routine pruning and replanting. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip the lower inch of foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. * Rotala leaves are fragile, so handle stems with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them about half an inch apart so light reaches lower leaves. Provide high-intensity lighting. While adaptable across a wide pH range, adding pressurized CO2 and liquid iron accelerates growth speed and color. Read our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the water surface to encourage new lateral side branching. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard setups, gentle water movement and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and broader fronds. Does Mini Bolbitis on Driftwood prefer strong water flow in the aquarium? Yes! Bolbitis species are rheophytic in nature, originating from fast-moving streams and waterfalls across Southeast Asia. listings.description: Plant Profile Ludwigia Arcuata is a colorful aquatic stem plant celebrated for its slender, needle-like foliage set in opposing pairs along delicate stems that bring remarkable movement, soft texture, and warmth to planted aquariums. While displaying rounded green leaves in its land-grown (emersed) state, transitioning underwater transforms its foliage into fine, pointed blades that blush with shades of vivid yellow, orange, and fiery ruby-red. Highly versatile and adaptable, Ludwigia Arcuata branches readily when pruned, forming lush, colorful midground or background hedges that provide dynamic visual depth. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Fine, needle-like leaves develop a vibrant color spectrum ranging from bright yellow-orange to deep ruby-red. Fast vertical and branching growth habit forms dense, cloud-like background or midground bushes. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. * Ludwigia Arcuata stems can be delicate, so handle with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide medium-to-high lighting and consistent iron supplementation; adding pressurized CO2 yields robust growth and maximizes deep red pigmentation. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or rotting. Trim main stem tops with sharp straight scissors once they reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to easily propagate and expand coverage. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Ludwigia arcuata Common Name(s) Ludwigia Arcuata, Needle Leaf Ludwigia Family Onagraceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Tissue Culture Stem Plant Care Difficulty Easy to Moderate Light Requirement Medium to High CO2 Requirement Optional (Recommended for robust growth & deep red tones) Placement / Usage Midground / Background Bushing Height / Size 10–20”+ Growth Rate Moderate Water Parameters pH 6.5–7.5 Propagation Method Cuttings (Cut stem and replant tops) Origin North America (USA) Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I get my Ludwigia Arcuata to display bright red colors? Achieving deep ruby-red foliage on Ludwigia Arcuata requires high light intensity, regular micronutrient dosing with liquid iron, and a nutrient-rich soil substrate. Adding pressurized CO2 further enhances stem density and coloration. 3. How do I prepare Ludwigia Arcuata Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture before planting? Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the dense cluster into smaller clumps or individual stems and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

Product Overview Aquario Neo Media Soft is a high-performance biological filter media manufactured in South Korea from natural mineral materials fired at high temperatures. Formulated with a slightly acidic nature, Neo Media Soft helps lower and stabilize pH levels in your aquarium. Its multi-pore structure provides an immense surface area for diverse strains of beneficial nitrifying bacteria to thrive, ensuring long-term biological stability and water clarity for planted aquascapes, dwarf shrimp, and South American fish species. Key Features & Benefits Slightly Acidic pH Target (SOFT): Imparts a mild acidic effect to naturally lower and maintain pH levels for soft-water setups. Multi-Pore Microstructure: Features varied internal pore dimensions to host diverse beneficial bacterial strains for a complete, resilient nitrogen cycle. 5-Step High-Temperature Manufacturing: Fired at extreme temperatures using natural Korean minerals to guarantee long-term structural durability without crumbling. Ideal for Soft-Water Livestock: Specially formulated to support aquatic plants, Caridina dwarf shrimp, and South American species like Tetras, Discus, and Angelfish. Versatile Basket Fit: Standard circular shape packs neatly into canister filter trays, HOB chambers, trickle sumps, and internal media baskets. Technical Specifications Precaution: Rinse gently with running water 2–3 times prior to installation. Avoid aggressive washing to prevent excessive mineral dust. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Which aquariums benefit most from Aquario Neo Media Soft? Neo Media Soft is ideal for planted aquascapes, dwarf shrimp tanks (such as Crystal Red Shrimp), and South American species like Tetras, Discus, and Angelfish, all of which thrive in slightly acidic water conditions. 2. How does Neo Media Soft differ from the Neo Media Soft Quad shape? Both feature the exact same pH-lowering acidic chemistry, but this standard model comes in classic cylindrical rings, whereas the Quad variant features a plus-sign (+) cross-section for extra outer surface area and multi-directional water channels. 3. How should I prepare and clean Aquario Neo Media during routine maintenance? Rinse the media gently under clean water 2 to 3 times prior to first use. During routine maintenance every 3 to 6 months, swish the media in a bucket of drained aquarium water to clear accumulated detritus without harming beneficial bacterial colonies.

Plant Profile Crypt Flamingo is one of our favorites here at Buce Plant, and honestly, it's not hard to see why! Ruffled leaves and pink coloration set it apart from the more common crypts out there, making it a rare, highly sought-after pick among collectors. Those exotic pink tones are what give it the edge over the usual green or brown Cryptocoryne species, and new leaves start with a striking blood-red color before naturally softening into a pinkish tint over time. As with all crypts, it can be a bit sensitive to changes in water parameters and doesn't like to be moved, but once established, it will contrast nicely with greener plants in your foreground or midground zones. Key Features & Benefits Exotic pink foliage with ruffled margins introduces a rare, vibrant accent to your aquascape. Can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups where it will periodically produce unique flowering spathes. The depth of the pink color intensifies significantly under higher light levels and CO2 injection. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Crypt species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Cryptocoryne wendtii 'Pink Flamingo' Common Name(s) Crypt Flamingo, Crypt Pink Panther, Crypt Pink Flamingo Family Araceae Plant Type Rosette / Root Feeder Height 2–6" (5–15 cm) Care Difficulty Easy Light Requirement Low to Medium (Moderate to High for best pink color) CO2 Requirement Optional (Recommended to maximize pink intensity) Placement / Usage Foreground / Midground Accent Growth Rate Moderate Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.0 | Temperature 72°F–82°F (22°C–28°C) Propagation Method Rhizome Division / Runner Offshoots Origin Borneo (Cultivated Variety) Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are my Cryptocoryne Pink Flamingo leaves melting away? Transplanting Crypts into new water parameters often triggers a temporary reaction where old leaves dissolve. As long as the root system remains undisturbed in healthy soil, fresh foliage will sprout shortly. Check out our guide on Cryptocoryne melt for step-by-step recovery tips. 2. Can I move my Cryptocoryne to a new spot in the tank later? It is best to leave your Crypt permanently in its original spot. Uprooting an established plant damages its fine root hairs and almost always causes another cycle of leaf melt. 3. Should I use root tabs or liquid fertilizers? Root tabs are best. Cryptocoryne species are heavy root feeders that draw primary nutrition from the substrate rather than the water column.

Plant Profile Alternanthera Reineckii 'Variegatus' is an eye-catching color cultivar of the classic South American stem plant, standing out thanks to delicate ruffled leaf margins paired with intricate variegated vein patterns. Its bright lime-green leaves are accented by vivid pink veins, sturdy magenta stems, and reddish-brown undertones, adding real texture and color depth to any planted aquarium. Growing 4 to 12 inches tall, it works as a midground centerpiece or a colorful background hedge, offering striking contrast against traditional smooth-leaved plants. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Unique ruffled leaf edges deliver unrivaled texture. Distinct appearance creates a captivating midground or background centerpiece. Dense, broad-leafed structure shelters shy fish and dwarf shrimp. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight (or pot) and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the roots, then strip lower foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower growth. Provide medium-to-high lighting. Regular dosing of liquid fertilizers alongside pressurized CO2 injection will enhance stem thickness, maintain compact growth, and bring out intense pink and magenta stem pigmentation. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim main stem tops with straight scissors once stems reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and expand coverage. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Alternanthera reineckii 'Variegatus' Common Name(s) Alternanthera Variegatus, AR Variegated, Variegated AR Family Amaranthaceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Stem Plant Care Difficulty Easy to Moderate Light Requirement Medium to High CO2 Requirement Required (Essential for pink/red stem tones and compact growth) Placement / Usage Midground / Background Centerpiece Height / Size 4–12”+ Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Water Parameters pH 6.5–7.5 Propagation Method Cuttings (Cut stem and replant tops) Origin Central & South America (Cultivar) Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I bring out bright pink and red coloration on Alternanthera Variegatus? While Alternanthera Variegatus displays green leaves under lower light, encouraging bright pink stem coloration and deep magenta leaf undersides requires medium-to-high light intensity, mandatory pressurized CO2, nutrient-rich aquasoil, and regular liquid nutrient dosing with iron. 3. How do I transition Alternanthera Variegatus from emersed to submerged growth? When transitioning from emersed to submerged growth, plant bare stems securely into rich substrate under good lighting and keep water parameters stable. As new growth adapts, the plant will shed its stiffer emersed leaves and sprout soft, ruffled underwater foliage with vivid pink veins. Once new shoots take root, trim away old lower growth to encourage dense branching.

Plant Profile Echinodorus 'Aflame', also known as the Purple Knight Sword, is a cultivated rosette species valued for its dark, narrow foliage. Native to the tropical Western Hemisphere through its parent lineage, this sword plant produces long, slightly twisted leaves that range in color from deep bronze and dark violet-red to near-black purple under bright lighting. Reaching 12 inches in height, its compact structure provides a high-contrast centerpiece in midground or background zones. While adaptable across various tank conditions, providing clean water parameters and a steady supply of iron and root nutrients helps maintain its deep purple-red coloration. Key Features & Benefits Dark foliage displays shades of bronze, deep purple, and violet-red under moderate to high lighting. Compact rosette structure creates high-contrast focal points against green aquatic plants. Hardy background plant suitable for medium and large planted aquarium layouts. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Plant the roots deeply into your aquarium soil, keeping the crown of the plant resting just above the substrate line to prevent rot. All Echinodorus are heavy root feeders that rely on rich substrate nutrition; placing root tabs near the base supports steady, healthy leaf development. Provide medium to high lighting; while CO2 injection is optional, supplying regular liquid iron supplementation and CO2 encourages faster growth and deeper purple tones. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf shedding during the initial transition period. To propagate, allow daughter plantlets to form along flowering runners or separate new shoots along the crown once independent roots sprout, then replant them directly into your aquarium soil. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Echinodorus 'Aflame' Common Name(s) Aflame Sword, Purple Knight Sword, Echinodorus Aflame Family Alismataceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Rosette Sword Plant Care Difficulty Easy to Moderate Light Requirement Medium to High CO2 Requirement Recommended (Enhances growth speed and deep purple hues) Placement / Usage Midground / Background Focal Point Height / Size 4–12”+ Growth Rate Slow to Moderate Water Parameters pH 6.5–7.5 Propagation Method Runner Plantlets / Division Origin Cultivar / Hybrid Variant Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I prep potted Echinodorus Aflame before planting? Remove the plastic pot and unwrap the cotton or foam surrounding the root base under room-temperature water. Inspect the base, snip off damaged outer leaves, and gently insert the roots into your aquarium soil using pinsettes. 2. How do I achieve the darkest purple and red colors on Echinodorus Aflame? Deep purple-red leaf coloration requires moderate to high light levels, iron supplementation in the water column, and nutrient tabs placed in your aquarium soil near the root base. 3. How is Echinodorus Aflame propagated? Unlike stem plants, Echinodorus species grow from a central crown and propagate by producing flowering runners that sprout small daughter plantlets. Once these plantlets form roots, cut them from the runner and plant them into your aquarium soil.

Plant Profile Elodea Najas, widely known as Anacharis Najas or Narrow Leaf Anacharis, is one of the easiest, most resilient aquatic stem plants in the freshwater hobby. Native to South America, this beginner-friendly species features slender, slightly textured, bright green leaves lined along fast-growing vertical stems. Thinner and more delicate in appearance than its popular relative Egeria densa , Elodea Najas thrives under a wide spectrum of conditions. Whether planted directly into substrate or left floating freely in the water column, it acts as an excellent natural shelter for fish fry while outcompeting nuisance algae. *Restricted State Notice: Please be aware that certain species of Anacharis may be classified as restricted or noxious weeds in specific states. It is the responsibility of the customer to review and stay informed of their local and state regulations before purchasing. Key Features & Benefits Nearly indestructible, a rewarding choice for first-time planted aquarium owners. Rapid growth acts as a natural nitrate sponge for crystal-clear water. Anchor in substrate or float freely for cover for fry and shrimp. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip lower foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, or allow stems to float freely along the water surface. Provide low-to-medium lighting for steady growth; while pressurized CO2 injection is not required, keeping water temperatures slightly cooler (68–75°F) yields firmer stems. Maintain stable water parameters and supply basic liquid fertilizers to support rapid leaf development. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the water surface, and simply replant the trimmings into substrate to propagate new stems. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Elodea najas (syn. Egeria najas ) Common Name(s) Anacharis Najas, Elodea Najas, Narrow Leaf Anacharis, Brazilian Waterweed Family Hydrocharitaceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Stem Plant / Floating Plant Care Difficulty Super Easy / Beginner Light Requirement Low to Medium CO2 Requirement Not Required Placement / Usage Background / Floating Cover Height / Size 4–12”+ Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Water Parameters pH 6.5–7.5 | Prefers cooler to moderate water (65–78°F) Propagation Method Cuttings (Cut stem and replant tops) Origin South America Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining adequate light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How does Elodea Najas differ from Egeria Densa (Standard Anacharis)? Elodea Najas features narrower, thinner, and slightly serrated/textured leaves along its stem compared to Egeria densa , which produces broader, smooth green leaves in thicker whorls. 3. Can Elodea Najas grow floating on the water surface? Yes! Elodea Najas takes up nutrients directly from the water column, making it fully capable of thriving as a free-floating plant matrix that offers excellent cover for shrimp and young fish fry.

Plant Profile Don't let the delicate look fool you! Myriophyllum Mattogrossense may have remarkably fine, feathery foliage radiating in soft, pine-like whorls, but this plant can hang with any setup you throw at it. It shows off a crisp, bright lime-green color that occasionally blushes gold under high lighting, all while staying easy to care for and adaptable to a wide range of tank conditions. Routine trimming encourages rapid lateral branching, quickly turning individual shoots into a thick, cloud-like background bush or structured Dutch-style street. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Fine foliage adds soft texture, volume, and movement to midground and background zones. Fast-growing stem habit easily branches into dense, cloud-like hedges when routinely trimmed. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide medium-to-high lighting and pressurized CO2 injection; consistent fertilization with a specialized liquid macro and micro formula yields robust stem growth and prevents bottom leaf yellowing. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or rotting. Trim main stem tops with sharp straight scissors once they reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and thicken the bush. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Myriophyllum mattogrossense Common Name(s) Myriophyllum Mattogrossense, Green Milfoil Family Haloragaceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Stem Plant Care Difficulty Easy to Moderate Light Requirement Medium to High CO2 Requirement Recommended (Encourages dense needle whorls and rapid growth) Placement / Usage Midground / Background Bushing Height / Size 4–12”+ (Cup portion size: 2–3”) Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.0 Propagation Method Cuttings (Cut stem tops or lateral shoots and replant) Origin South America (Mato Grosso, Brazil) Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I achieve a thick, bushy forest with Myriophyllum Mattogrossense? To encourage Myriophyllum Mattogrossense to form a dense hedge, routinely trim the main stem tops once established. Each cut site will sprout multiple lateral side shoots, doubling the stem density and creating a tight, bushy cloud of fine foliage. 3. How do I prepare Myriophyllum Mattogrossense Tissue Culture before planting? Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the cluster into smaller clumps or individual stems and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

Aquarium Thermometer Knowing the temperature of your aquarium is a vital part of keeping your livestock healthy and thriving. This aquarium thermometer provides easy to read and accurate temperatures in both Fahrenheit and Celsius. Use a thermometer and don't risk losing your beloved fish and shrimp!

Derived from the dried husk of the Cholla Cactus, this hollow, porous aquarium wood is a functional powerhouse. Its iconic honeycomb structure isn't just for aesthetics; it serves as a biological factory for biofilm and a high-security nursery for small aquatic life in a planted aquarium. Product Features & Benefits Cholla is famous for stimulating the growth of biofilm, a natural, nutrient-rich film that serves as the primary food source for shrimp and baby fry. The hollow center and perforated walls create the perfect "safe house" for molting shrimp and small fish to hide from larger tank mates. Its unique texture makes it incredibly easy to attach mosses, Anubias, or Bucephalandra. Over time, it can be transformed into a lush, living sunken log that anchors your planted aquarium hardscape. Cholla releases beneficial tannins that slightly lower pH levels, mimicking the natural blackwater environments in which many tropical species thrive. Size Specifications Photos are a representation of the natural variations you will receive. They are cut to 6 inches in length and approximately 1.5-2 inches in diameter. Preparation & Care Rinse: Thoroughly rinse the piece to remove any dust or debris from transit. The Sinking Process: Dry Cholla is very lightweight and will float initially. To get it to stay put, we recommend soaking it in a bucket for 24–48 hours or boiling it for 20 minutes to help it become waterlogged. Safety Disclaimer This tunnel is best suited for freshwater shrimp or small fry. If you have larger, curious fish or other fauna (such as a betta fish) that may try to explore such small crevices, there is a risk they may get caught or stuck in the tunnel. Please be mindful of this before placing it in your aquarium.

Suction cups don’t get much attention, but they keep your whole setup from turning into chaos. Nothing’s worse than finding your CO₂ diffuser floating at the surface or your airline tubing drifting into the middle of your scape. Aquarium Suction Cups fix that with a strong, underwater‑ready grip on both glass and acrylic. The built‑in snap‑on clips hold standard airline and CO₂ tubing snug against the tank wall, keeping everything tidy. Want to mount glass lily pipes instead? Just pop off the tubing clips and use the suction pads as clean, direct glass‑to‑glass mounts. Key Features & Benefits Advanced marine-grade suction design creates a reliable grip on clean glass or acrylic walls without losing suction over time. Keeps utility lines perfectly organized and out of your way during routine maintenance and trimming sessions. Constructed from 100% aquarium-safe, non-toxic polymers that resist premature stiffening under water.

By utilizing world-class Epistar RGB diodes, the Titan 1 eliminates the dull, washed-out hues of standard aquarium lighting, instead saturating your landscape in vibrant, natural color. Whether you’re chasing the deep reds of Ludwigia or the electric greens of a Monte Carlo carpet, this LED aquarium light provides the high-intensity PAR and 9,000K–12,000K color temperature needed to turn your tank into a living masterpiece. Seriously, it’s light-years ahead of the competition. This item qualifies for FREE shipping to the contiguous U.S. Shipping to Alaska or Hawaii? Contact us for a custom shipping quote—we’re here to help! Key Features & Benefits 200 High-Output Epistar RGB Diodes: Intensifies the natural red, green, and blue pigmentation of fish, shrimp, and rare aquatic foliage without artificial color casting. Wide Chassis with Integrated Flat Diffuser: Ensures ultra-even light distribution across the entire substrate, eliminating harsh "hot spots" and shade zones for consistent carpet growth. Lightweight Aluminum Heat Sink: Premium brushed aluminum body acts as a massive passive heat dissipation unit, keeping internal circuitry running cool without noisy cooling fans. Sleek Architectural Pendant Design: Minimalist aesthetic complements high-end rimless glass aquariums. Available in brushed black or anodized silver finishes to match your room's decor. Plant Profile If you have a large tank that needs serious botanical presence, Echinodorus palaefolius is more than ready to step up. Naturally originating from marshy wetland habitats in South America, this giant sword species is famous for its massive scale and fast growth rate. In its submerged state, it produces long, elegant leaves that start out with a subtle reddish tint before deepening into rich, vibrant green foliage that arches toward the light. Because of its sheer size and rapid growth, it commands the background of medium-to-large aquariums, creating a lush jungle feel in no time. Alternatively, if you let it grow emersed or keep it in an open-top tank or paludarium, it transforms with broad, rounded leaves and will reward you with delicate white flowers floating above the waterline. Key Features & Notes Fast growth rate makes it a commanding focal point for large aquariums and tall backgrounds. A versatile species that thrives fully underwater or emersed in open-top tanks, where it often produces lovely white flowers. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Plant the roots deeply into your aquarium soil, keeping the central crown resting just above the substrate line to prevent rot. All Echinodorus are heavy root feeders that rely on rich substrate nutrition; placing root tabs near the base supports steady, healthy leaf development. Supplemental CO2 injection accelerates growth and encourages denser, fuller foliage, though the plant will still grow steadily in low-tech setups. Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf shedding during the initial transition period. Sword plants propagate through side shoots off of their leaves, which can be trimmed and replanted into the substrate. To control the size of your sword plant, you can remove the side shoots and older leaves. Final size and leaf shape depend on whether the plant is grown fully submerged or emersed; please note that individual plants may vary based on tank conditions. Why are the leaves on my new Echinodorus melting or turning yellow? Sword plants are often grown emersed and shed their old emersed leaves when submerged to adapt to underwater growth. Keep water parameters stable and supply root tabs near the base to support new leaves.

Plant Profile If you love the broad, sturdy look of classic sword plants but don't want a single rosette swallowing half your aquarium, Echinodorus 'Harbich' is a hidden gem. Originating as a naturally compact mutation of Echinodorus cordifolius (Radican Sword), this dwarf cultivar caps out at a manageable 9 inches in height. Instead of the massive, arching foliage of its parent, it produces stout, rounded, heart-shaped leaves on short stems that form a neat, dense bush. Young emerging leaves unfurl in subtle reddish to bronze tones before transitioning into a deep, glossy green as they mature. Its compact size makes it a perfect midground focal point or a cozy background choice for smaller setups! Key Features & Notes Compact dwarf habit makes it ideal for midground placement. Broad, rounded heart-shaped leaves give it a uniquely sturdy, architectural silhouette. Emerging foliage shows warm reddish-bronze hues before maturing into vibrant, deep green. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Plant the roots deeply into your aquarium soil, keeping the central crown resting just above the substrate line to prevent rot. All Echinodorus are heavy root feeders that rely on rich substrate nutrition; placing root tabs near the base supports steady growth and sturdy leaf structure. Thrives in low-to-moderate lighting without requiring pressurized CO2, though supplemental CO2 will encourage faster growth and fuller rosette development. Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf shedding during the initial transition period. Final size and coloration depend on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Plant Profile Bringing ruby-red intensity to a manageable scale, Echinodorus 'Red Devil' is a gorgeous hybrid cultivar that proves you don't need a massive 20-inch sword plant to make a bold statement. Produced by crossing multiple Echinodorus species, this compact variant tops around 12 inches tall, making it a fantastic midground centerpiece in medium-to-large tanks or a prominent background feature in nano setups. Newly unfurled leaves emerge in brilliant shades of deep ruby red and rich crimson before slowly maturing into a dark, olive-green base with reddish-brown undertones. Hardy, undemanding, and forgiving across various water conditions, it delivers eye-catching color contrast without requiring complicated high-tech care. Key Features & Notes Compact height fits seamlessly into midground or small background zones. A hardy hybrid cultivar that provides intense color contrast while remaining easy for beginners to maintain. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Plant the roots deeply into your aquarium soil, ensuring the central crown sits just above the substrate line to prevent rot. All Echinodorus are heavy root feeders that rely on rich substrate nutrition; placing root tabs near the base supports steady leaf development and rich pigmentation. Provide moderate-to-high lighting and consistent iron fertilization to achieve the deepest ruby-red leaf tones. Supplemental CO2 is recommended to maximize leaf color and growth rate, though the plant will still grow reliably in low-tech setups. Final size and coloration depend on your specific tank conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Plant Profile Alternanthera Rosanervig, or AR Rosanervig, is a stem plant with vivid pink-to-magenta leaves and distinct light-colored leaf veins. Known for adding immediate visual contrast and warm tones to a planted tank, it’s a great pick for hobbyists branching out from standard green aquatic plants. When provided with medium-to-high lighting, quality aquarium soil, and a consistent nutrient routine, it forms lush midground or background clusters that stay vibrant with minimal fuss. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Vertical stems hold their shape well, making it ideal for structured rows and Dutch-style plant streets. Dense foliage shelters dwarf shrimp and shy fish. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and sponge from the stems, stripping the lower inch of foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. * AR Rosanervig has soft, sensitive stems, so handle carefully during planting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into soil, spacing them apart so light reaches lower leaves. Provide medium-to-high lighting and consistent CO2 injection to accelerate growth and maximize pink coloration. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or rotting in delicate stems. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the surface to encourage new lateral side branching. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Plant Profile If your background looks flat, Hygrophila Angustifolia Rubra is here to flip the script. Native to the tropical waterways of Southeast Asia, this fast-growing, beginner-friendly aquatic stem plant grows long, narrow, willow-like leaves that shift through a gradient of olive-green to rich reddish-copper under moderate to high lighting. Because of its impressive height potential that easily reaches 6 to 12+ inches, it serves as an outstanding background plant that quickly absorbs excess nutrients from the water column, helping to keep algae at bay in newly established or mature aquariums alike. Key Features & Benefits Long, narrow willow-like foliage blushes with warm reddish-copper tones under sufficient light. Fast growth acts as a natural nutrient sponge to keep water clean and suppress algae. Hardy and adaptable across a wide range of temperatures and parameters. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and remove cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip the lower inch of foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower leaves. Provide moderate to high lighting; while adaptable without pressurized CO2, supplying CO2 and regular liquid fertilizer dosing will enhance growth rate, leaf size, and reddish coloration. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid drastic environmental shifts to ensure healthy stem transition. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the desired height to encourage dense side-branching. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details.
