Plant Profile Meet Isoetes Velata Var. Sicula, commonly known as Sicilian Quillwort, a living fossil that's older than your favorite aquascaping trend by a few hundred million years. It's part of the ancient lycophyte family Isoetaceae, and out of the 60 to 150 species in the genus, almost none of them are aquarium-friendly, which makes this one a hobby unicorn. Featuring long, tubular, grass-like fronds that radiate upward from a bulbous root crown, it resembles miniature underwater rush grass. Capable of enduring a broad range of water conditions in nature, from nutrient-poor cold lakes to warm tropical wetlands, it grows slowly to 8 to 15 inches, bringing clean, architectural vertical lines to your midground and background. Key Features & Benefits Quill-like fronds add vertical structure and grassy texture. Rare collector species with high contrast against broad-leaved plants. Hardy and adaptable across a wide range of temperatures and parameters. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight (or pot) and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the roots, taking care not to crush or damage the bulbous root crown. Use fine-tip pinsettes to anchor the root system securely into substrate, ensuring the central root crown remains elevated slightly above the soil surface. Provide medium-to-high lighting and clean water conditions; while adaptable to low-tech tanks, supplying regular fertilization supports steady frond development and vibrant coloration. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent frond melting. Prune damaged or yellowing fronds near the base using sharp aquatic scissors to encourage fresh growth from the central crown. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I plant Isoetes Velata Var. Sicula so it doesn't rot? When planting Isoetes, it is crucial not to bury the central root crown below the substrate line. Push the roots firmly into the soil, then gently pull the plant upward until the base of the quill-like fronds where they meet the crown is fully exposed above the substrate. 2. How does Isoetes Velata Var. Sicula propagate in the aquarium? In nature, Isoetes reproduces via microscopic spores produced at the base of its fronds. In home aquariums, spore propagation is notoriously slow and difficult, which accounts for its rarity. Over time, mature specimens can occasionally be divided at the root crown when side offsets form. 3. Does Isoetes Velata Var. Sicula require CO2 injection? No, CO2 injection is not mandatory for Isoetes Velata Var. Sicula. Because it is naturally adapted to low-nutrient environments, it can thrive in low-tech setups, though providing quality aquasoil, moderate light, and CO2 will noticeably speed up its inherently slow growth rate.

listings.description: Plant Profile Featuring mature, oversized leaf canopies anchored to heavy root systems, the Anubias Barteri Broad Leaf Mother Pot delivers instant jungle scale for large planted tanks. Holding its foliage high on long, sturdy stems, this impressive epiphyte produces massive, broad leaves that are almost double the size of standard Anubias Barteri , with individual leaves easily stretching up to 3 inches long or more! This expansive canopy provides dramatic coverage and lush visual weight, making it an unbeatable choice for filling out background spaces. Mother pots are extra-large, mature specimens containing multiple individual plants (typically 2-4+ plants per pot). Having been cultivated for much longer than standard pot sizes, these robust plants represent the original mother stock used for commercial propagation. Their impressive size and established root systems make them the perfect instant-impact choice for large aquariums or big scaping projects! Key Features & Benefits The extra-large Mother Pot format delivers a massive cluster of mature, fully developed plants in one pot. Massive, broad-leafed foliage creates a lush, wild jungle canopy that offers great contrast against delicate stem plants and hardscape elements. The tough and leathery leaf structure easily resists grazing from large or herbivorous fish. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Avoid intense light and ensure good water flow to prevent spot algae on slow‑growing leaves. CO₂ is optional but improves growth and leaf density. Learn more about planting these species by reading our guide on How to Plant Epiphyte Aquatic Plants. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. What makes a Mother Pot different from a standard potted Anubias? A Mother Pot contains a fully mature, multi-rhizome specimen that has been grown out for months, featuring 15 to 30+ large leaves and an extensive root system, providing an instant display rather than waiting for a small starter plant to grow. 2. How do I anchor a heavy Anubias Mother Pot without burying the rhizomes? If older outer leaves already carry heavy algae, prune them off cleanly at the rhizome base to encourage fresh, compact leaf growth.

Plant Profile Echinodorus 'Red Rubin', commonly known as the Red Rubin Sword, is a vibrant hybrid cultivar with broad, wavy-edged foliage that shifts through striking shades of ruby red, deep purple, bronze, and dark green. Thanks to its hardy, undemanding nature and wide parameter tolerance, it serves as an excellent plant for beginners without requiring specialized high-tech equipment. Each oversized pot contains 2 to 4+ mature Echinodorus Red Rubin plants with well-developed growth, making it a great choice for large aquariums and bigger aquascaping projects. Key Features & Notes Broad, slightly wavy leaf blades display a rich color range from ruby red and gold to deep burgundy and olive green. An adaptable and low-maintenance species that thrives under a wide variety of lighting and water conditions. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Plant the roots deeply into your aquarium soil, keeping the crown of the plant resting just above the substrate line to prevent rot. All Echinodorus are heavy root feeders that rely on rich substrate nutrition; placing root tabs near the base supports steady, healthy leaf development. Provide moderate lighting; while CO2 injection is not strictly required, supplying regular liquid iron supplementation and good lighting will enhance its deepest ruby-red and purple colors. Avoid using copper-based medications in tanks containing Echinodorus species, as sword plants are particularly sensitive to copper. Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf shedding during the initial transition period. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. How do I prune an Echinodorus when it grows too large? Prune older or overgrown outer leaves individually near the root crown using sharp aquascaping scissors. Avoid cutting across leaf blades, as damaged leaf tips will turn brown rather than regrowing. 2. Can this background plant grow in low-tech aquariums without CO2? Yes, this species thrives in low-tech aquariums without pressurized CO2, provided it receives adequate root supplementation and consistent lighting. 3. Why are the leaves on my new Echinodorus melting or turning yellow? Sword plants are often grown emersed and shed their old emersed leaves when submerged to adapt to underwater growth. Keep water parameters stable and supply root tabs near the base to support new leaves.

listings.description: Product Overview The UNS 75P 40.1 Gallon Ultra Clear Rimless Aquarium offers a spacious, medium-sized canvas ideal for creating detailed, nature-inspired aquascapes, Dutch-style planted tanks, and community aquariums. Constructed from 91% Clarity Diamant glass with 8mm panel thickness and signature 45° mitered edges, this tank eliminates green glass distortion to maximize light transmission and present a high-definition view of your aquatic layout. Golden Ratio Depth: Designed with a generous 17.72" front-to-back depth, providing essential breathing room for multi-layered hardscape placement and natural perspective. Signature Laser-Etched Branding: Features a clean, laser-etched UNS logo in the glass corner for an authentic finish that will not peel or fade. Acoustic Leveling Mat Included: Pre-cut dense foam leveling mat absorbs micro-vibrations, levels surface irregularities, and protects against glass stress points. In the unlikely event that your tank arrives damaged or broken by the carrier, we will immediately ship out a replacement at no additional cost to you. Please send photos of the damaged tank in its original shipping box so that we can file a claim with UPS on your behalf. Please allow an additional 2-3 business days in case of potential logistical delays. Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why select a standard proportion tank like the UNS 75P over a shallow or tall format? The 75P offers classic proportions that balance horizontal swimming space with sufficient height for tall stem plants and substantial rock or wood hardscapes. 2. What livestock is best suited for a 40.1-gallon aquarium? The 40.1-gallon volume provides excellent water stability for medium-sized schooling fish (such as Tetras, Rasboras, or Rainbowfish), Corydoras, dwarf cichlids, or large communities of ornamental dwarf shrimp and snails. 3. listings.commonName: Mini Pellia on Stainless Steel Mesh
listings.description: Plant Profile Mini Pellia is a moss-t have liverwort plant that has grown in popularity and demand over the past few years. While technically not a true moss, its thick green fronds cluster together to look just like tiny underwater coral, forming a dense and beautiful cushion! We have pre-attached this premium liverwort to a 3" x 3" stainless steel mesh pad so you can instantly place a lush, heavy carpet exactly where you want it. It is an amazing, texture-rich addition to any aquascape, serving as a premium shady sanctuary or playground where dwarf shrimp and small fish can hang out. Key Features & Benefits Pre-attached stainless steel pad sinks and stays put for zero-hassle carpeting. Unique, coral-like growth pattern creates an ultra-dense, rolling green carpet that adds incredible visual depth. Thick, padded clusters form a shaded sanctuary that coaxes out shy fish and shrimp. Care & Planting Instructions Place the metal mesh pad directly onto your substrate or nestle it snugly into your hardscape where it can receive clean water circulation. Maintain a stable aquarium environment and keep temperatures cool (below 78°F / 25.5°C) to prevent stress, browning, or melting. Give the moss an occasional light haircut with sharp aquascaping shears to keep its shape neat, compact, and perfectly balanced. Propagate your patch in seconds by cutting or pulling a small clump apart and anchoring it to a new surface in your tank. The Dymax PowerHead is an ideal choice for driving internal filters, powering water features, or boosting water circulation in both freshwater planted aquascapes and marine reef systems. If you love the tangled, branchy look of Spiderwood but want a material that doesn't feel as brittle, Amazon Wood is your prime pick. This aquarium wood is muscular, knotty, and full of dramatic twists that give an instant flooded‑rainforest vibe without a million tiny twigs. Its balanced, organic shapes mean there’s no “bad side,” so it looks natural from any angle and suits horizontal roots, vertical canopy pieces, or clean focal points. Forgiving to work with and built to last, it brings untamed character without the fragility. Product Features & Benefits With more character than a standard branch, this driftwood offers deep grooves and rugged knots that provide an immediate sense of age to your aquarium hardscape. Arriving in a lighter, sandy tone, this wood transforms into a rich, darker hue once submerged, perfectly complementing the vibrant greens of aquatic mosses and ferns. Its unique shapes make it equally popular for terrariums and vivariums, providing climbing structures for reptiles or amphibians. Size Specifications Photos provided are a representation of what you will receive. As Amazon Wood is a natural aquarium hardscape product, please expect variations in shape, weight, and character. Small: 4-9 inches Medium: 9-16 inches Large: 15-21 inches Preparation & Care Driftwood is a natural product and requires a bit of prep before it’s ready for prime time. Rinse: Thoroughly rinse the piece to remove any dust or debris from transit. The Floating Phase: This aquarium driftwood is naturally buoyant and will float initially. We recommend soaking it thoroughly or boiling it. A large stone or heavy decor may be placed on top to ensure a non-waterlogged piece of wood stays submerged. Tannin Management: Like most aquarium driftwood, this will release tannins, giving your water a warm, "tea-colored" tint. This is a natural occurrence, and the effects will subside over time. If you prefer crystal-clear water, a 1–2 hour boil is the best way to fast-track the process. You can also reduce this effect through consistent water changes or through the addition of Aquario Neo Carbon Bag Important note: We recommend rinsing wood thoroughly before adding it to an established aquarium.

We recommend rinsing stones thoroughly before use to remove any natural dust or sediment. Stone coloration darkens when wet.

listings.commonName: Mini Christmas Moss on Stainless Steel
listings.description: Plant Profile Tree-t your scape with a little holiday magic all season long by adding this downsized freshwater aquarium moss to your setup. Mini Christmas Moss delivers the same festive spirit as its famous larger cousin , but features much thinner, shorter, and more delicate fronds. These tiny leaves grow horizontally in neat, overlapping layers that perfectly mimic miniature evergreen branches. Pre-cultivated on a weighted 3" x 3" stainless steel mesh pad, this setup allows aquascapers to easily build a low-profile foreground carpet or mount a lush moss wall without the struggle of gluing or tying down loose pieces. Key Features & Benefits Pre-attached 3" x 3" stainless steel mesh pad sinks naturally to establish an instant, low-profile foreground carpet. Ultra-compact, delicate triangular fronds maintain proper visual scale and high-definition texture in nano aquariums. Provides safe hiding, shelter, and grazing areas for freshwater shrimp and nano fish. Care & Planting Instructions Place the metal mesh pad directly onto your substrate for an instant lawn carpet, bend it around curved hardscape, or mount it vertically against your glass. Maintain a stable aquarium environment and avoid sudden water parameter swings to keep your live moss vibrant and healthy. Give the moss fronds an occasional light haircut with sharp aquascaping shears to encourage denser, tighter growth. Propagate in seconds by snipping or pulling clumps apart and securing them to new hardscape surfaces throughout your tank. Optionally supply CO2 injection and low-to-medium LED lighting to accelerate growth rate and enhance deep-green foliage coloration. Plant Profile Java Fern Mother Pot brings instant, established greenery to your aquarium without waiting months for everything to fill in. Each oversized pot contains 2 to 4+ mature Java Fern plants with well-developed growth, making it a great choice for large aquariums and bigger aquascaping projects. Hardy, adaptable, and seriously difficult to offend, Java Fern tolerates a range of water and lighting conditions, making it one of the best aquarium plants for beginners. Think of the Mother Pot as a Java Fern that already did the growing-up part for you. Key Features & Notes Tough, fibrous foliage easily withstands curious nipping from herbivorous fish like cichlids, goldfish, and large snails. Broad vertical fronds create a natural, leafy backdrop that masks equipment while providing territory cover for timid fish. Exceptional hardiness lets it thrive in non-CO2 tanks and low-light environments. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Java Fern Mother Pot is an epiphytic fern that should be attached to rocks or driftwood with aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as it will rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard setups, gentle water movement and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and broader fronds. Master long-term care and troubleshoot common leaf issues by checking out our Java Fern Care Guide . Final size and foliage pattern depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Microsorum pteropus (syn. Leptochilus pteropus ) Common Name(s) Java Fern, Java Fern Mother Pot Family Polypodiaceae Plant Type Epiphyte (Rhizome Fern) Care Difficulty Beginner / Easy (Low-Tech Compatible) Light Requirement Low to Medium CO2 Requirement Not Required (Beneficial) Placement / Usage Midground, Background, Hardscape Accent Height / Size 5"–20" (13–50 cm) Growth Rate Slow to Moderate Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 | Temperature 68°F–82°F (20°C–28°C) Propagation Method Rhizome Division & Adventitious Plantlets Origin Indonesia Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are there small black spots and tiny leaves growing under my Java Fern leaves? Do not panic; your plant is not diseased! Java Fern reproduces naturally through adventitious plantlets. Small dark bumps (sporangia) form along the undersides of mature leaves, sprouting tiny brown roots and mini green fronds. Once these baby plantlets develop 3–4 leaves, you can gently pop them off the mother leaf and glue them elsewhere in your aquarium. 2. Can I plant Java Fern Mother Pot into substrate? No. Java Fern is an epiphyte that absorbs nutrients directly from the water column through its foliage and fine root network. If you bury its horizontal rhizome beneath aquarium soil, sand, or gravel, the stem will suffocate, rot, and die. Always attach it to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread. 3. Why is Java Fern Mother Pot considered one of the best low light aquarium plants for beginners? Java Fern Mother Pot is exceptionally resilient because it does not require specialized substrate, grows reliably under basic LED lighting, and tolerates a massive range of water conditions without needing pressurized CO2 injection. 4. Will fish like cichlids or goldfish eat Java Fern Mother Pot? Generally, no. Java Fern leaves are thick, fibrous, and contain bitter taste compounds that deter most plant-eating fish. While aggressive diggers might knock it off hardscape if not glued securely, they rarely consume the foliage.

listings.commonName: Hygrophila Lancea 'Araguaia' Sp Chai Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Hygrophila Lancea 'Araguaia' Sp. Chai, commonly known as Hygrophila Chai, is an extremely rare and highly coveted pink mutation of the classic Hygrophila lancea 'Araguaia' . Originating as a specialized tissue-culture mutation in Singapore, this collector plant features narrow, elongated leaves characterized by striking olive-red bases with intense pastel pink margins and tips. While it shares the compact, low-growing, bushy structure of standard Araguaia, its breathtaking pink coloration and limited availability make it one of the most prized midground focal points in high-tech aquascaping. Quantity is limited, and supply is infrequent. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Ultra-rare pink variegated mutation featuring olive-red foliage with pastel-pink leaf tips and margins. Short, bushy branching growth habit naturally creates a dense, spreading midground centerpiece or low-growing foreground terrace. Provides unrivaled visual contrast against green mosses and dark hardscape elements. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide high-intensity LED lighting and pressurized CO2 injection. Consistent iron and micronutrient dosing is required to maintain its signature pink coloration and prevent stunting. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim lateral shoots or stem tops with straight scissors, replanting the trimmings directly into the substrate to encourage compact side branching. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Chai Family Acanthaceae / Lythraceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Stem Plant / Compact Bushing Mutation Care Difficulty Medium to Difficult (High-Tech Required) Light Requirement High CO2 Requirement Required (Essential for pink coloration and growth) Placement / Usage Midground Bushing / Foreground Focal Point Height / Size 2–5” Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Water Parameters pH 6.5–7.5 Propagation Method Cuttings (Trim lateral shoots or main stem and replant) Origin Singapore (Cultivated Mutation) Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I maintain the bright pink color on Hygrophila Chai? Hygrophila Chai requires high light intensity, mandatory pressurized CO2, a nutrient-dense substrate, and regular micronutrient/iron dosing. Without intense light and adequate nutrients, the delicate pink margins will fade or stall in growth. 3. How do I prepare Hygrophila Lancea 'Araguaia' Sp Chai Tissue Culture before planting? Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the dense cluster into smaller clumps or individual stem bundles and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

Plant Profile Echinodorus 'Jaguar' is an easygoing sword plant that brings a subtle, spotted pattern into your planted tank. Growing in a classic rosette shape, it produces bright green, oval leaves with rounded tips that are speckled with dark, reddish-brown spots. Maxing out around 16 inches tall, it works great for filling out background corners or adding structure behind midground hardscape in medium to large aquariums. Like most sword plants, it is naturally hardy and doesn't ask for a complex setup to stay healthy! Key Features & Notes Bright green, rounded leaves feature dark speckled spots across new and developing foliage. Hardy rosette growth habit offers dense background coverage and simple maintenance. Adaptable species that grows consistently across a variety of low-tech and high-tech parameters. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Plant the roots deeply into your aquarium soil, keeping the central crown resting just above the substrate line to prevent rot. All Echinodorus are heavy root feeders that rely on rich substrate nutrition; placing root tabs near the base supports steady, healthy leaf development. Supplemental CO2 injection accelerates growth and encourages denser, fuller foliage, though the plant will still grow steadily in low-tech setups. Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf shedding during the initial transition period. Sword plants propagate through side shoots off of their leaves, which can be trimmed and replanted into the substrate. To control the size of your sword plant, you can remove the side shoots and older leaves. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Giving the plant moderate-to-high lighting and placing root tabs near the root base helps keep the dark spots clearly visible against the bright green leaf color. 2. Does Echinodorus 'Jaguar' need CO2 injection to grow well? No, it grows just fine in low-tech setups without pressurized CO2. Good substrate nutrition and decent light are usually all it needs to stay healthy and put out new leaves. 3. How do I keep Echinodorus 'Jaguar' from blocking light to smaller foreground plants? As the plant fills out, simply trim off the larger outer leaves near the root crown with sharp scissors. Thinning it out every so often keeps the size in check and lets light reach the rest of your tank.

Echinodorus Yeni is a rare aquatic sword species that has beautiful red veins on short, round leaves. Like most Echinodorus species, Echinodorus Yeni is easy to grow and a great aquatic plant for beginners. This particular species remains compact when compared to its larger counterparts such as Echinodorus Bleheri or other popular sword species. They are comparable in appearance to Echinodorus Reni, which is a hybrid of Echinodorus Ozelot and Echinodorus Bear. Sword plants should be planted in nutrient-dense aquarium soil as a minimum as they are heavy root feeders. If possible, the addition of a routine dosing schedule, quality aquarium lighting, and clean water will help to encourage quick and healthy growth. Notes: Echinodorus is a very hardy species of aquatic plants. Most Echinodorus require nutrient-dense soil to thrive as they are heavy root feeders. Echinodorus grow fairly large and are more suitable for larger planted aquariums. Do not make drastic changes to the aquarium. Unstable parameters will result in melt and rotting of the aquarium plant. Please be sure to remove this plant from its pot. Remove the cotton surrounding the roots and plant into a quality substrate. For instructions on how to properly prep "potted" aquarium plants, click here . CO2 injection and quality aquarium soil will yield better growth. Please research appropriately to ensure your plant thrives. Common Name: Echinodorus Yeni Family Name: Alismaaceae Leaves: 1-3" pH: 6-7.5 Care: Easy Light: Low-Moderate Co2: Not Required Propagation: Separate new plantlets from the root Growth rate: Moderate

Plant Profile If you're tired of subtle tones, Rotala Rotundifolia Orange Juice (affectionately known as Rotala OJ) is here to add color to your scape. True to its name, this aquatic stem plant features long, narrow leaves that flush a fiery, intense orange when submerged. Highly favored for background placement, planting this species in dense groups forms a dazzling, thick orange bush that adds visual depth, warmth, and contrast with traditional green plants. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Leaf hues shift into vibrant orange tones when provided with strong LED lighting, heavy iron dosing, and complete liquid fertilizers. Easily forms dense, bushy midground or background clusters through routine pruning and replanting. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip the lower inch of foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. * Rotala has fragile leaves, so handle stems with care! Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower growth. Provide high-intensity lighting and pressurized CO2 injection (20–30 ppm) in quality aquarium soil to yield robust growth and maximize color depth. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid drastic environmental changes to prevent leaf melt or rotting in delicate stems. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the surface to promote branching and prevent lower leaves from being shaded out. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Plant Profile Nomaphila Variegatus is a robust, highly attractive aquatic stem plant native to Southeast Asia. Featuring broad green foliage adorned with unique, creamy white-to-light-green variegated vein patterns along slender stems, this species brings exceptional texture and visual contrast to planted aquariums. Highly versatile and beginner-friendly, it flourishes in submerged aquascapes as a terraced midground feature, as well as in open-top tanks and paludariums where its stems break the water surface. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Distinctive variegated leaf patterns provide eye-catching contrast and high aesthetic value in midground stem groups. Fast-growing, hardy stem species that absorbs excess water column nutrients to help deter unwanted algae growth. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight (or pot) and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the roots, then strip lower foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower leaves. Provide moderate-to-high lighting and a steady macro-nutrient fertilizer supply; while CO2 injection is not required, adequate lighting and nutrients prevent growth stunting and maintain strong leaf variegation. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim top shoots with straight scissors to control height and induce lateral side branching, creating a stunning terraced group of stems. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Plant Profile Limnophila Mini Vietnam is a rare and highly prized aquatic stem plant native to the tropical waterways of Southeast Asia. Characterized by its compact stature and starburst whorls of linear, pointed leaves, this species stays significantly smaller than other Limnophila varieties. Under moderate lighting, it displays a crisp, vibrant light green coloration, but under high-intensity light, CO2, and nutrient-rich soil, its foliage reveals attractive reddish-brown central veins. Key Features & Benefits Compact, starburst foliage creates a dense, bushy texture in midground and background zones. Displays vivid light green leaves that develop reddish-brown vein highlights under strong lighting. Fast-branching stem species forms tight, rolling bushes when routinely pruned. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight (or pot) and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the roots, then strip lower foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to insert individual stems 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide moderate to high lighting and clean water conditions; while adaptable, supplying pressurized CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilization yields much tighter leaf whorls and reddish-brown vein accents. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or leaf rot. To propagate, trim main stem tops or developed side shoots with sharp straight shears and replant trimmings directly into substrate. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Plant Profile Instead of picking between standard green and deep red, Nesaea Pedicellata Golden offers a rare third option: gold! Hailing from West Africa, this striking aquatic stem plant pairs greenish-gold leaves with bold, pinkish-red stems for a look you don't see every day. As one of the very few golden-colored species available in the aquascaping hobby, it provides an exceptional pop of color and architectural contrast in midground or background placements. Hardy and versatile, this gem flourishes in both submerged aquariums and emersed setups, developing rich, warm tones under moderate-to-high lighting. Key Features & Benefits Rare greenish-gold leaves contrasting against bright pinkish-red stems introduce a unique color palette to planted tanks. Hardy stem plant that easily forms thick, bushy midground clusters when pruned routinely. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip the lower inch of foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. * Nesaea stems can be fragile, so handle with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1-2 inches into soil, spacing them so light reaches lower leaves. Provide moderate-to-high lighting. Adding pressurized CO2 and a consistent fertilizer regimen enhances growth speed and yields maximum golden-yellow coloration. Maintain stable water parameters and cooler-to-moderate water temperatures (70–78°F) for ideal leaf form and stem development. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the desired height to encourage dense side-branching. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. listings.description: Plant Profile If smooth, pristine foliage feels a little too routine for your aquascape, Anubias Barteri 'Wrinkle Leaf' is here to bring some serious character! True to its name, this uncommon epiphyte takes the classic, dependable round leaves of standard Barteri and gives them a ruffled upgrade. Spanning up to 3 inches long on 4 to 6-inch stems, its broad, crinkled leaves create an immediate pop of tactile depth that makes smooth rocks and plain driftwood look downright boring by comparison. It thrives under low lighting without requiring CO₂ injection, and adapts easily to low-tech submerged setups or humid emersed terrariums. Mother pots are extra-large, mature specimens containing multiple individual plants (typically 2-4+ plants per pot). Having been cultivated for much longer than standard pot sizes, these robust plants represent the original mother stock used for commercial propagation. Their impressive size and established root systems make them the perfect instant-impact choice for large aquariums or big scaping projects! Key Features & Benefits Extra-large Mother Pot format provides multiple mature, fully developed plants in one pot for instant volume and large-scale coverage. Distinctly ruffled, crinkled leaf margins offer an eye-catching, textured look that breaks up monotonous green layouts. Durable foliage naturally resists grazing from fish, snails, and shrimp. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Avoid intense light and ensure good water flow to prevent spot algae on slow‑growing leaves. CO₂ is optional but improves growth and leaf density. Learn more about planting these species by reading our guide on How to Plant Epiphyte Aquatic Plants. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! What is a Mother Pot? A Mother Pot is a fully mature plant specimen consisting of multiple individual plants attached to a well-developed rhizome system. 2. Should I plant Anubias Barteri Wrinkle Leaf Mother Pot as one giant centerpiece or divide it? Both methods work depending on your tank size. You can secure the entire mature root ball directly onto a large central driftwood branch or rock structure, or snip the creeping rhizomes between healthy leaf nodes to create 4 to 8 separate, smaller plants to wedge throughout your hardscape. 3. How do I prevent black beard algae (BBA) or green spot algae on older Anubias mother pot leaves? Because Anubias is a slow-growing epiphyte, mature leaves in a mother pot sit under light for a long time. Place the clump in partial shade beneath taller stem plants or surface floaters, and avoid blasting it with intense, direct lighting. If older outer leaves already carry heavy algae, prune them off cleanly at the rhizome base to encourage fresh, compact leaf growth.

Plant Profile Echinodorus bleheri, universally recognized as the iconic Amazon Sword, is one of the most quintessential background species in the hobby. Characterized by wide, lance-shaped leaves with distinct parallel venation and slightly rippled edges, it forms a dense, architectural rosette that serves as an anchor for planted displays. Each oversized pot contains 2 to 4+ mature plants and delivers instant volume, tall reach, and dense coverage for medium to large aquariums. Its remarkable adaptability to varied water conditions and forgiving nature under low-tech setups solidify its reputation as a classic staple among aquarium plants for beginners. Key Features & Notes Broad, vibrant green foliage with prominent venation provides classic, sweeping background structure. Hardy rosette habit thrives across a wide range of water parameters without requiring pressurized CO2. Amazon sword plants will grow submersed or emersed. Emersed plants produce lovely white flowers. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Plant the roots deeply into your aquarium soil, keeping the crown of the plant resting just above the substrate line to prevent rot. All Echinodorus are heavy root feeders that rely on rich substrate nutrition; placing root tabs near the base supports steady, healthy leaf development. Supplemental CO2 injection accelerates growth and encourages denser, fuller foliage, though the plant will still grow steadily in low-tech setups. Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf shedding during the initial transition period. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Yes, this species thrives in low-tech aquariums without pressurized CO2, provided it receives adequate root supplementation and consistent lighting. 3. Why are the leaves on my new Echinodorus melting or turning yellow? Sword plants are often grown emersed and shed their old emersed leaves when submerged to adapt to underwater growth. Keep water parameters stable and supply root tabs near the base to support new leaves.

listings.commonName: Anubias Barteri Broad White UNS Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Anubias Barteri Broad White is an ultra-rare collector’s gem! Unlike standard green varieties, this farmed mutation boasts broad, creamy-white to pale-green leaves that are larger than Anubias Snow White . If you are looking to turn heads and create a focal point, this white-hot rarity is here to help you pull off an unforgettable aquascape. Its foliage creates an unmatched visual contrast when nested against dark volcanic lava rock, rich Malaysian driftwood, or deep green mosses. Tissue culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab-grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go-to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits The striking creamy white to pale green broad foliage offers a high-contrast accent that brightens dark hardscape crevices and shadowy tank areas. Larger leaves than Anubias Snow White provide a bolder, more prominent structural presence in your midground layout. Care Tips & Preparation Prep the plant by carefully removing the plantlets from the cup and rinsing away all sterile nutrient gel under lukewarm, dechlorinated water before mounting. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the horizontal rhizome completely exposed above substrate to prevent rot. Unlike its green cousins, this sun-seeker lacks heavy chlorophyll! Provide medium to high lighting alongside regular CO2 injection and nutrient dosing to encourage optimal growth and maintain its vivid white leaf coloration. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to ensure your new greenery acclimates smoothly without shedding leaves. Position the plant in areas with balanced water circulation to keep its slow-growing leaves pristine and free of unwanted algae. Master the prep and planting process by checking out a beginner's guide to tissue culture plants to prevent your delicate new plantlets from melting or floating away. Does Anubias Barteri Broad White require higher lighting than standard green Anubias? Yes. Because its white and pale green foliage contains significantly less chlorophyll than traditional green Anubias, Anubias Barteri Broad White requires medium to high lighting. Providing clean light and fertilizer supports photosynthesis and prevents white leaf tissue from melting. 2. How does Anubias Barteri Broad White differ from Anubias Snow White? While Anubias Snow White is a dwarf plant reaching 1 to 3 inches with tiny leaves, Anubias Barteri Broad White grows larger (3 to 5 inches) and features much broader, sweeping leaves that make a stronger midground statement. 3. Is Anubias Barteri Broad White Tissue Culture safe for shrimp and fish? Yes, Anubias Barteri Broad White Tissue Culture is 100% safe for all freshwater fish, dwarf shrimp (including sensitive Caridina and Neocaridina), and snails. Being lab-grown, it is completely free of pesticides, hitchhikers, and pest snails.

Plant Profile Spathiphyllum wallisii, aka Peace Lily, is an adaptable tropical plant native to the humid forest margins and streambanks of Central America. This variety features glossy, green, lance-shaped leaves with distinct parallel veining that fan out from a clumping crown, producing an upright silhouette that adds a structured canopy presence. While its root network excels at pulling dissolved nitrates directly out of aquarium water, keep the crown and foliage elevated into ambient air, because anchoring this marsh plant fully submerged beneath the surface is a fast track to leaf melt and rot. Key Features & Notes Clumping growth habit regularly sends up architectural white spathes under adequate ambient illumination without overtaking tight enclosure footprints. Versatile riparian root system thrives in damp terrarium substrates, paludarium banks, and hanging riparium planters. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots CAUTION: Like most plants in the aroid family, Peace Lilies contain insoluble calcium oxalate crystals that can cause mouth pain, swelling, drooling, and digestive distress if chewed. Keep this plant safely out of reach of curious cats, dogs, and small children. Mount the root system along a wet paludarium bank or inside an aquarium riparium cup, ensuring the roots remain wet while the central crown and petioles stay completely above the waterline. Provide moderate to bright indirect lighting, avoiding unshaded grow lights that scorch leaf tips and bleach dark green pigments. Divide dense root clumps by hand or with sterile shears during maintenance to propagate fresh clusters across multiple tanks. Final size, blooming frequency, and leaf density depend entirely on your specific setup conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Spathiphyllum wallisii Common Name(s) Peace Lily Family Araceae Plant Type Terrestrial / Riparian Clumping Aroid Care Difficulty Easy Light Requirement Moderate to Bright Indirect Submersion Suitability Emersed / Riparian Only (Roots wet, foliage dry) Placement / Usage Paludarium Banks, Riparium Planters, Terrarium Background Height / Size 5.00"–12.00" (13–30 cm) Growth Rate Slow to Moderate Humidity Requirement Moderate to High (50%–80% RH) Propagation Method Rhizome / Clump Division Origin Central America Frequently Asked Questions 1. Can Peace Lilies grow fully submerged in a freshwater aquarium? No. Spathiphyllum wallisii is a terrestrial marsh plant, not a true aquatic plant. Submerging the foliage underwater will cause the leaves to suffocate and melt over several weeks. However, the root system handles being submerged in water indefinitely as long as the crown and stems remain above the surface. 2. Is Spathiphyllum wallisii safe around pets and bioactive terrarium animals? Like many aroids, Peace Lilies contain insoluble calcium oxalate crystals. While safe for aquatic fish when grown riparium-style, chewing on the foliage can cause oral irritation, excessive drooling, and mild digestive discomfort in cats, dogs, or herbivorous terrarium reptiles. Position the foliage out of reach of household pets. 3. How do I get Spathiphyllum wallisii to flower in a paludarium? Peace Lilies produce their iconic white spathes when provided with strong, indirect lighting and consistent root nourishment. In high-humidity setups with adequate air circulation and routine water column feeding, mature specimens can bloom once or twice per year.

Plant Profile Native to the splash zones and rocky banks of Sarawak waterfalls in Borneo, Schismatoglottis Roseospatha looks almost like a hybrid blend of Bucephalandra and narrow-leaf Anubias. It produces lance-shaped, pointed green leaves on slender brownish-yellow stems, eventually showing off tiny speckled white pores and a faint bluish center under stable, full-spectrum lighting. Reaching up to 12 inches tall, it's an effective midground or background accent for breaking up bulky rockwork and wood branches. Whether you're growing it submerged in an aquarium or emersed in a humid terrarium, make sure the rhizome stays completely exposed to open water and air, because burying it in substrate is a fast track to rot. Key Features & Notes Adapted to turbulent river spray, developing strong, clinging root systems that grip tightly to textured stones and wood crevices. Under stable aquarium lighting, leaves develop tiny crystalline white speckles and a subtle bluish midrib accent. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from its pot and clearing all rockwool from the root base . Schismatoglottis is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While hardy and capable of growing in low-tech conditions, consistent water flow and supplemental liquid fertilizers encourage faster root establishment and healthier leaf formation. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Plant Profile Meet Alternanthera Red Broad Leaf, a rare aquatic stem plant that's got a color pattern all its own. Bold crimson-red stems and leaf veins run through broad, lanceolate leaves splashed with greenish-yellow, olive, and rosy-copper, like it couldn't settle on just one shade. Both beginner and experienced aquascapers love it for the same reason: it holds onto those warm reddish tones with way less fuss than most demanding red stem species. It's ready to anchor your midground as a centerpiece or fill in the background as a vibrant hedge in any planted freshwater aquarium. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Broad leaves with red stems and ribs create a multi-toned focal point. Beginner-friendly and holds red coloration far more easily than demanding red species. Dense, broad-leafed structure shelters shy fish and dwarf shrimp. Regular dosing of liquid fertilizers like UNS Plant Food to maintain elevated nitrate and phosphate levels alongside pressurized CO2 injection will prevent dull fading and promote fast growth. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim main stem tops with straight scissors once stems reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and expand coverage. listings.description: Plant Profile Small, serrated leaves with pointed edges give each stem of Gratiola Viscidula a distinct spiky, thorn-like profile underwater. This aquatic plant originates from damp riverbanks and seasonal wetlands across Eastern North America, and its upright bushy habit makes it a versatile choice for foreground carpeting or midground borders. It adapts smoothly to both fully submerged aquarium layouts and emersed growth in humid terrariums or paludariums. Growing reliably under medium lighting without strictly requiring CO2, it serves as a beginner-friendly and low-tech choice for aquascapers adding unique leaf geometry to their layout. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Pointed, serrated leaf blades create a unique spiky texture in foreground carpet and midground areas. Adapts smoothly to fully submerged aquariums or emersed growth in humid terrariums. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small portions or individual stems 1 inch apart into your aquarium soil, ensuring root bases are securely anchored. Provide medium lighting; while CO2 is not mandatory, supplying pressurized CO2 and regular liquid nutrients accelerates growth rate and builds denser carpet clumps. Maintain stable water parameters and good water clarity to encourage steady root development and prevent leaf melting during transition. To propagate, trim main stem tops with sharp, straight shears and replant the cuttings directly into your aquarium soil to expand the carpet group. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Trimming the stems low regularly encourages side shoots to spread horizontally across your aquarium soil into a spiky carpet layer. 3. Is Gratiola Viscidula suitable for low-tech aquariums? Yes, Gratiola Viscidula is an adaptable species that grows well under medium lighting without CO2, though growth will be slower compared to high-tech setups.

Plant Profile Reaching a manageable size compared to its larger relative Echinodorus Big Bear, Echinodorus Small Bear is a desirable hybrid sword plant prized for its compact habit and rich leaf coloration. As new foliage unfurls near the center of the rosette, it displays deep rusty-red, dark burgundy, and copper-brown hues before maturing into a rich, dark olive green. Capping out around 12 inches tall, its moderate proportions make it a standout pick for midground zones or an attractive background anchor in smaller aquariums. Naturally hardy and forgiving across a wide range of water parameters, it offers aquascapers a striking contrast of warm colors without requiring delicate, high-maintenance care. Tissue culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab-grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go-to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Notes Compact growth habit allows it to fit seamlessly into midground or smaller background zones. Striking foliage transitions from deep rusty red and dark burgundy on new growth to dark olive green as it matures. Hardy rosette plant that delivers bold color contrast and lush coverage without demanding delicate high-tech care. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by carefully removing the plantlets from the cup and rinsing away all sterile nutrient gel under lukewarm, dechlorinated water before mounting. Plant the roots deeply into your aquarium soil, keeping the central crown resting just above the substrate line to prevent rot. All Echinodorus are heavy root feeders that rely on rich substrate nutrition; placing root tabs near the base supports steady, healthy leaf development. Provide moderate to high lighting; while CO2 injection isn't strictly required, good lighting will enhance its reddish-brown colors. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf shedding during the initial transition period. Sword plants propagate through side shoots off of their leaves, which can be trimmed and replanted into the substrate. To control the size of your sword plant, you can remove the side shoots and older leaves. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. How does Echinodorus 'Small Bear' differ from Echinodorus 'Big Bear'? Echinodorus 'Small Bear' is a much more compact cultivar, topping out around 6 to 12 inches compared to 'Big Bear', which easily exceeds 16 to 20+ inches. This makes 'Small Bear' far better suited for midground placement in standard aquariums without overwhelming neighboring plants. 2. How do I maintain and enhance the dark burgundy leaf color on Echinodorus 'Small Bear'? Provide moderate-to-high lighting directly over the rosette and place nutrient-rich root tabs near the root base. Higher light levels and consistent iron supplementation encourage newly emerging leaves to develop deep burgundy and rusty-red tones rather than turning solid green. 3. How do I prep and divide tissue culture portions of Echinodorus 'Small Bear'? Gently remove the plant mass from the cup and rinse away the clear gel under room-temperature water. Using your fingers, separate the cluster into small individual plantlets and plant their roots deeply into the soil with pinsettes, making sure the leaf crown remains resting just above the substrate level.

Common Name: Ranalisma Rostratum Ranalisma Rostratum originates from the tropics in Asia. This aquatic plant is still very rare in the trade, difficult to get and is often spelled incorrectly making it more elusive to eager planted tank enthusiasts. This aquatic plant is peculiar in that when it is grown submerged, it appears completely different and its leaves will transform into very narrow blades that resemble a grass-like plant. It features a bright green color and is comparable to the popular aquatic plant, Helanthium Parvulum. When emersed, Ranalisma Rostratum will have much rounder leaves and can sprout small flowers that bear small spiky fruits. In order to grow this plant correctly, high lighting, CO2 injection and a nutrient dense substrate are some of the basic requirements for success. If these factors are provided, this aquatic plant will grow a nice dense lawn of green that will be a beautiful addition to a planted aquarium. Plant Profile Dwarf scale meets intricate geometry in Java Fern Trident Mini, a variation that packs the iconic triple-pronged silhouette of standard Java Fern Trident into compact, narrow fronds. Whether bound to intricate driftwood branches, wedged into stone crevices, or grouped to form miniature bushes, its bright green fork-like leaves provide exceptional detail without overpowering smaller layouts. Unbelievably hardy and tolerant of low light, shifting water chemistry, or plant-nibbling fish, it stands out as a choice for scapers who want striking leaf architecture and high-impact midground detail. Key Features & Notes Tough, fibrous foliage easily withstands curious nipping from herbivorous fish like cichlids, goldfish, and large snails. Miniature, fork-lobed leaf blades offer delicate detail and balanced proportions for nano aquariums, tight rock gaps, and wood branches. Exceptional hardiness lets it thrive in non-CO2 tanks and low-light environments. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Java Fern Trident Mini is an epiphytic fern that should be attached to rocks or driftwood with aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as it will rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard setups, gentle water movement and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and broader fronds. Master long-term care and troubleshoot common leaf issues by checking out our Java Fern Care Guide . What makes Java Fern Trident Mini different from regular Java Fern Trident? Java Fern Trident Mini produces much smaller, narrower fronds with shorter split lobes than standard Trident. This dwarf habit makes it easier to use in nano tanks or tight hardscape gaps without blocking out too much space or light. 2. Why are there small black spots and tiny leaves growing under my Java Fern Trident Mini leaves? Do not panic; your plant is not diseased! Java Fern reproduces naturally through adventitious plantlets. Small dark bumps (sporangia) form along the undersides of mature leaves, sprouting tiny brown roots and mini green fronds. Once these baby plantlets develop 3–4 leaves, you can gently pop them off the mother leaf and glue them elsewhere in your aquarium. 3. Can I plant Java Fern Trident Mini into substrate? No. Java Fern Trident Mini is an epiphyte that absorbs nutrients directly from the water column through its foliage and fine root network. If you bury its horizontal rhizome beneath aquarium soil, sand, or gravel, the stem will suffocate, rot, and die. Always attach it to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread. 4. Will fish like cichlids or goldfish eat Java Fern Trident Mini? Generally, no. Java Fern leaves are thick, fibrous, and contain bitter-tasting compounds that deter most plant-eating fish. While aggressive diggers might knock it off hardscape if not glued securely, they rarely consume the foliage.

Plant Profile Diverging from the compact foliage typical of most Anubias plants, Anubias Glabra brings airiness and sweeping height to planted tanks. Native to West African rainforest streams, it replaces round leaf shapes, like those found on Anubias Barteri or Anubias Nana, with sleek, lanceolate leaf blades that taper into subtle wavy margins. Because its foliage sits atop elongated, flexible petioles, it creates a canopy effect, making it an ideal candidate for midground accenting or soft background fill. Built to handle low-tech setups with minimal maintenance, it thrives fully submerged in aquariums or emersed in humid terrariums and paludariums. Key Features & Benefits Tall leaf canopy provides natural shading and cover for shy fish, shrimp, and bottom-dwelling species. Thick, leathery leaves resist grazing from plant-eating fish, snails, and dwarf shrimp. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Avoid intense light and ensure good water flow to prevent spot algae on slow‑growing leaves. CO₂ is optional but improves growth and leaf density. Learn more about planting these species by reading our guide on How to Plant Epiphyte Aquatic Plants. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. How does Anubias Glabra differ from Anubias Lanceolata or Anubias Congensis? While all three produce narrow, spear-shaped foliage rather than standard round leaves, Anubias Glabra features notably longer, more flexible petioles and slender leaf blades with subtly undulating margins. This gives it an airy, graceful sway in water currents compared to the stiffer, broader leaves. 2. Can Anubias Glabra be planted directly in aquarium soil or sand? No, burying the horizontal rhizome will cause it to rot. To support its tall, top-heavy stems, wedge the rhizome into heavy driftwood or rock crevices; you can tuck the dangling feeder roots into sand, gravel, or aquarium soil as long as the rhizome itself stays exposed above the substrate. 3. Where is the best placement for Anubias Glabra in a planted layout? Reaching up to 16 inches in height, Anubias Glabra is strictly a background anchor or large hardscape centerpiece for tanks 20 gallons and up. Position it behind lower midground plants to create a natural, shaded overhead canopy that provides cover for shy fish without blocking light to the foreground.

This hardy variant is highly prized for its adaptable nature, often displaying shifts in tone that add dynamic visual interest to the layout. Highly versatile, it can be grown submerged or emersed, usually attached to hardscape such as driftwood or rocks rather than being buried in traditional aquarium substrate. It's a beautiful addition to the foreground or midground of freshwater aquascapes, where its slow-growing rhizomes create a dense, colorful colony over time. Product Overview Leveling Mats are an essential safety requirement for any rimless or glass tank setup. Once filled with water, substrate, and heavy hardscape material like rocks or driftwood, an aquarium exerts immense downward pressure on its bottom glass panel. Microscopic debris, stray sand grains, or minor surface imperfections on your stand can create concentrated stress points that lead to cracked glass, leaks, or total seam failure. Designed with high-density acoustic foam, the UNS Leveling Mat cushions the base panel, neutralizing surface irregularities and distributing total aquarium weight evenly across its footprint. Key Features & Benefits High-Density Foam Cushioning: Crafted from durable, dense black foam engineered to absorb stress and cushion the bottom glass panel against microscopic stand imperfections. Non-Slip Surface Stability: The high-grip foam texture prevents the aquarium from shifting or sliding during aquascaping, filling, or routine maintenance. Precise UNS Model Sizing: Pre-cut to match the precise footprints of the Ultum Nature Systems rimless glass tank lineup for a clean, custom fit. Universal Trimmable Design: Highly versatile material that can be easily trimmed with a utility knife or shears to fit non-UNS aquarium brands and custom stand sizes. Discreet Black Finish: Features a low-profile, solid black aesthetic that seamlessly blends between your aquarium base and stand surface. Does a leveling mat replace the need for a level stand? No. Leveling mats are designed exclusively to absorb micro-imperfections, tiny debris, and minor surface texture. They do not compensate for a stand that is structurally out of level. Always ensure your aquarium stand is level and that no part of the aquarium overhangs the edge. 2. Why do rimless tanks specifically require leveling mats? Unlike framed aquariums that sit on a raised plastic perimeter rim, rimless glass tanks rest their bottom glass panel directly on the stand surface. Without a high-density cushion to absorb point pressure, even a single grain of sand beneath the glass can lead to a stress crack over time. 3. Simply measure your tank base and slice along a straight edge for a custom fit.

listings.description: Plant Profile Taxiphyllum sp. Taiwan Moss is a highly sought-after variety that sits in the sweet spot between Java and Willow moss. This rare gem features a horizontal, overhanging growth pattern with feathering fronds that drape over hardscape like a plush green velvet waterfall. Plus, this beginner-friendly plant can serve as a fantastic, five-star aquatic nursery where shy nano fish and dwarf shrimp can safely forage! Key Features & Benefits Pre-attached stainless steel mesh pad lets you drop a lush, ready-to-grow moss carpet directly onto your tank floor without fighting buoyant plants. Unique cascading, overhanging growth habit makes it the perfect decorative choice for covering vertical rocks, masking equipment, or carpeting your foreground. Incredibly versatile survivor easily tolerates everything from chilly cold-water setups to warm tropical aquariums. Care & Planting Instructions Place the metal mesh pad directly onto your substrate or tuck it firmly into your hardscape cracks where it can receive clean water flow. Maintain a stable aquarium environment and avoid sudden, drastic changes to your water parameters to keep your moss looking vibrant and healthy. Give the moss an occasional light haircut with sharp aquascaping shears to keep its shape neat, compact, and perfectly balanced. Propagate your patch in seconds by cutting or pulling a small clump apart and anchoring it to a new surface in your tank. Add CO2 injection if you want to accelerate growth and unlock the most intense, eye-popping green coloration possible. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I keep my Mini Taiwan Moss from turning brown or yellow? Mini Taiwan Moss prefers clean, moving water and stable parameters. Browning usually occurs when organic debris gets trapped inside the fine, cascading fronds or when water chemistry swings abruptly. Gently siphoning debris out during water changes will keep the inner growth green and healthy. 2. How do I use the stainless steel mesh pad in my aquascape? The stainless steel mesh pad is heavy enough to sink right out of the box. You can lay it completely flat on your substrate for an instant carpet, bend the flexible metal around curved rocks or wood, or lean it against a wall to form a vertical green backdrop. 3. How do I stop moss trimmings from spreading everywhere during maintenance? Always turn off your filter pumps and powerheads before trimming moss. Use sharp curved shears to make clean cuts, and immediately scoop or siphon out floating cuttings so they don't take root in unwanted areas of your aquarium.

The wavy leaf edges create a dynamic sense of movement, even in low-flow areas, making it a favorite for detailing rock-to-substrate transitions. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for aquascapes where other plants might struggle. It is perfectly at home fully submerged in an aquarium or emersed in high-humidity terrariums, vivariums, and paludariums. Plant Profile Echinodorus 'Rose' is a cultivated sword plant popular in freshwater aquascaping. Native to tropical regions of the Western Hemisphere through its parent lineage, this hybrid is characterized by wide, oblong leaves with wavy edges and visible leaf veins. Newly emerging leaves display pink and bronze colors before maturing to bright green and dark olive-green as they age. Reaching 10 to 20 inches in height, it works well as a midground centerpiece in larger aquariums or a background option in medium setups. Because it thrives in low to moderate lighting without requiring CO2, it is a beginner-friendly and low-tech plant choice for adding color to a planted tank. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Foliage transitions from pink and bronze on new leaves to dark green as leaves mature. Broad rosette growth provides structural focal points in midground and background areas. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil . All Echinodorus are heavy root feeders that rely on rich substrate nutrition; placing root tabs near the base supports steady, healthy leaf development. Provide low to moderate lighting; while CO2 is not required, supplying moderate light and liquid iron supplements helps maintain the pink and bronze tones on young leaves. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters to avoid leaf melting during the transition to submerged growth. To propagate, separate new daughter plantlets that form along runner shoots or at the base, then replant them directly into your aquarium soil. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I prepare Echinodorus Rose Tissue Culture before planting? Remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant cluster in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once clean, separate the portion into smaller clumps or individual plantlets and insert them into your aquarium soil using pinsettes. 2. Is Echinodorus Rose Tissue Culture suitable for low-tech setups? Yes, Echinodorus Rose is a hardy, low-tech species that grows well without CO2 injection under basic low to moderate lighting. Adding root tabs to your aquarium soil provides the root nutrition needed to sustain steady growth. 3. Why is root feeding necessary for sword plants grown from tissue culture? Echinodorus species rely on extensive root systems to absorb nutrients from the substrate rather than drawing them primarily from the water column. Providing root tabs in your aquarium soil supports healthy root development after planting tissue culture portions.

Plant Profile Anubias Chili is a rare miniature Anubias variety known for its exceptionally small, chili pepper-shaped leaves. Even smaller than Anubias Nana Petite, this variety has a similar appearance to Anubias Pangolino. Its compact size makes it a great choice for nano aquariums, detailed aquascapes, and small spaces in the foreground or midground. Like other Anubias, Anubias Chili is a slow-growing epiphyte that grows best when attached to hardscape such as aquarium wood or stone. It can also be placed above the substrate, as long as its rhizome remains uncovered. This hardy plant does well in low to medium lighting and does not require CO2 injection, making it a good option for low-tech aquariums. Regular fertilization and CO2 can encourage healthier growth, but are not necessary for the plant to thrive. Key Features & Benefits Extremely compact size makes it suitable for nano aquariums and detailed aquascaping. Distinctive leaf shape adds variety to hardscape arrangements. Works well tucked into small crevices between rocks and driftwood. Can be used to create scale and contrast alongside larger-leaved Anubias varieties. Care & Planting Instructions Lighting: Low to medium lighting is ideal. Avoid intense lighting, as the slow growth rate makes Anubias Chili more susceptible to algae buildup on its leaves. CO2: CO2 injection is not required. However, adding CO2 can encourage faster growth and healthier leaf development. Fertilization: Regular dosing of a quality liquid aquarium fertilizer can help support healthy leaf and root development. Since this plant grows slowly, consistent but moderate fertilization is generally sufficient. Placement: Best suited for the foreground or midground, especially in nano aquariums. Attach it to rocks or driftwood where its small leaves can be appreciated up close. Planting: Does not require nutrient-rich substrate. It can grow attached to hardscape in aquariums with inert sand or gravel. Propagation: Propagate by dividing the rhizome into smaller sections. Each section should have healthy leaves, roots, and a rhizome to help it establish successfully. Maintenance: Remove damaged or algae-covered leaves as needed. Avoid making drastic changes to water parameters, lighting, or nutrient levels, as Anubias can be sensitive to sudden changes. Water Parameters: A stable aquarium environment is more important than maintaining exact parameters. Anubias Chili does well across a range of typical freshwater aquarium conditions. Anubias Chili naturally has a very slow growth rate, so it may take several weeks or longer to produce new leaves. Consistent water parameters, adequate nutrients, and appropriate lighting will help support steady growth. CO2 injection can encourage faster growth but is not required.

listings.commonName: Ludwigia Repens Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Ludwigia Repens is an easy, fast-growing midground and background stem plant favored for adding vibrant color to aquascapes without the drama of fussier red species. Featuring oval leaves that grow in alternating pairs along flexible stems, its foliage shifts through shades of gold, orange, and deep red depending on aquarium conditions. When planted in dense bunches of 10 to 12 stems, Ludwigia Repens creates an eye-catching focal point and adds immediate visual depth. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Leaf hues naturally range from olive-gold to vibrant orange and red under medium-to-high lighting and elevated iron dosing. Beginner-friendly red stem plant that delivers bold color contrast in both low-tech and high-tech aquarium setups. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide medium-to-high lighting. While CO2 injection is not strictly required, it yields much thicker stems and richer coloration. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or rotting. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the surface to encourage lower stems to shoot out new side branches. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the dense cluster into smaller clumps or individual stems and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

Best suited for high-tech setups, it thrives under high lighting, pressurized CO2, soft acidic water, and a generous supply of micronutrients. Positioned in the midground or background, its warm golden tones provide a dramatic, high-contrast focal point against deep red and lush green aquatic foliage. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. Delicate, translucent leaf structure creates a soft, fine-textured appearance in high-tech aquascapes. Plant Profile It's time to take a giant leap forward with this adorable, toad-shaped piece of aquarium decor! We have taken a naturally durable coconut shell, carved it into a charming little toad, and dressed it up in a lush, velvety coat of iconic Christmas Moss. Because aquarium moss is beginner-friendly and practically bulletproof, you can easily ditch the tacky plastic ornaments and enjoy a thriving, low-maintenance tank decoration that grows itself. Key Features & Benefits Whimsical, toad-shaped coconut shell naturally sinks out of the box for a creative, established look with zero installation hassle. Organic, carved coconut shell offers a healthy, eco-friendly alternative to synthetic plastic tank decorations. Provides safe hiding, shelter, and grazing areas for freshwater shrimp and nano fish. Care & Planting Instructions Place the coconut toad directly onto your substrate or nestle it among your current hardscape to form an instant shelter and instant pop of green. Maintain a stable aquarium environment and avoid sudden, drastic changes to your water parameters to keep your moss looking vibrant and healthy. Give the moss an occasional light haircut with sharp aquascaping shears to keep its shape neat, compact, and perfectly balanced. Propagate your patch in seconds by cutting or pulling a small clump apart and anchoring it to a new surface in your tank.
