Plant Profile Characterized by its petite, slightly curled leaves and shifting color palette, Bucephalandra ‘Biblis Blue Sky’ adds clean detail wherever you mount it. New growth emerges in warm reddish-brown shades before settling into a deep forest green with subtle blue undertones once established underwater. Staying compact at around 1 to 2 inches in height, it naturally forms dense mini colonies when wedged into hardscape crevices without needing constant trimming. Key Features & Notes Coloration transitions naturally as reddish-brown new leaves mature into deep green with subtle blue highlights under stable lighting. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for planted tanks where other plants might struggle. Adaptable to both fully submerged aquariums and high-humidity terrariums and paludariums. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from its pot and clearing all rockwool from the root base . Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard low-light setups, supplemental CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilizers will yield faster growth and richer blue-green coloration. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Keep water movement steady and conditions stable; as long as the central rhizome stays firm, new submerged leaves will sprout. 3. Can I plant Bucephalandra Biblis Blue Sky in substrate? You can let the roots grow down into gravel or aquarium soil to anchor the plant, but the central horizontal rhizome must remain completely exposed above the substrate line to prevent rot.

Plant Profile Once a classic in the early days of the hobby, this sought-after species stands out with elongated leaves featuring a signature pattern of lightly colored veins set against dark green-to-bronze foliage. As with all crypt plants, it can be sensitive to sudden parameter shifts and strongly objects to being relocated once planted. Given a permanent home in your substrate, however, its compact rosettes mature into an eye-catching, long-lasting accent that adds rich natural texture to your aquascape. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Long, distinctively veined foliage adds high-contrast patterning and texture to midground zones. Can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups, where mature plants may produce flowering spathes. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel to supply essential subterranean nutrients. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth and fuller foliage density, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Crypt species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. While it shares the large leaf profile and rich dark green tones of the popular Skeleton King , it is distinguished by a smooth leaf surface that lacks a heavily ribbed texture. Despite its rarity, it remains a durable species that thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for planted tanks where other plants might struggle. Plant Profile Common Name: Bucephalandra Flamingo Buce ‘Flamingo’ is a rare and striking epiphytic plant characterized by its dark green olive, obovate leaves and vibrant, reddish-pink stems. This unique variety is named for its vivid pink petioles that extend toward the leaf tips, displaying a beautiful contrast against the smooth, glossy foliage, very similar to Buce Pink Lady . Highly versatile, it can be grown submerged or emersed, usually attached to hardscape such as driftwood or rocks rather than being buried in traditional aquarium substrate. It is an exquisite choice for the midground of freshwater aquascapes, where its upright growth pattern and slow-growing rhizomes create a sophisticated focal point within a planted tank. Key Features & Notes Unlike standard green varieties, the "Flamingo" features consistent pink-to-red stems that provide a permanent pop of color regardless of leaf age. This species tends to grow more vertically than creeping varieties, making it ideal for filling gaps behind rocks or along the "trunk" of driftwood trees. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for aquascapes where other plants might struggle. Planting tiny portions deeply into fine aquasoil or growing them emersed using the Dry Start Method for 4–6 weeks will anchor the root system securely before you flood the tank.

listings.commonName: Micranthemum Monte Carlo Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Micranthemum ‘Monte Carlo’ is the ultimate aquatic carpeting plant to give your aquarium that lush, velvety rolling-hill look you’ve been dreaming of. With its tiny, round leaves and bright green color, it pops beautifully against neutral substrates. If you’ve ever struggled to grow notoriously finicky Dwarf Baby Tears (HC) , Monte Carlo is the friendlier, more forgiving alternative you’ve been looking for. It spreads out into a thick, uniform mat, giving you maximum aquascaping rewards without the heartbreak. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Forms a tight, velvety foreground lawn with small, bright green leaves that add an incredible sense of scale and depth to your aquascape. Far easier to cultivate than Dwarf Baby Tears, making it an accessible carpet option for hobbyists of all experience levels. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use a dry start method or Wabi Kusa setup to give its root system plenty of time to firmly anchor into the substrate before you flood the tank. Maintain stable aquarium parameters and avoid drastic shifts in water quality to prevent your new grass from melting. Provide medium to high lighting and inject pressurized CO2 to supercharge its density and growth rate, keeping it low and compact. Master the basics by learning how to properly grow aquarium carpet plants to ensure your new layout fills in quickly. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I plant Monte Carlo tissue culture? Use fine-tip tweezers to bury each portion about halfway into nutrient-dense aquarium soil. Spacing them 1 inch apart helps them connect quickly via runners. 2. Does Monte Carlo need CO2 to form a carpet? While Monte Carlo can technically grow in low-tech setups without CO2, adding pressurized CO2 and medium-to-high lighting is strongly recommended to force it to grow horizontally into a tight, plush carpet instead of growing tall or straggly. 3. Why is my newly planted Monte Carlo floating up? Because tissue culture portions have delicate root systems, fish or water currents can easily dislodge them. Planting small clumps deeply into fine soil or letting the tank grow emersed using the Dry Start Method will anchor the roots securely before flooding.

Plant Profile If you're hunting for a fresh twist on classic dwarf epiphytes, Anubias Nana Paxing brings a totally distinct habit to the table. This relatively new and rare variety sets itself apart by growing almost completely flat in a creeping, horizontal direction. Featuring small, narrow, rich green leaves with a slightly concave curve and a glossy sheen, its growth form stays low to the hardscape, making it a fantastic choice for covering ground, carpeting logs, or tucking into tight rock crevices. Tough, forgiving, and wildly adaptable, it thrives submerged in aquariums or emersed in humid terrarium and paludarium setups. Key Features & Benefits Low-profile creeping habit grows horizontally across wood and stone, creating a distinct hardscape-hugging effect. Small, narrow, concave foliage with a high-gloss finish brings fine, delicate texture to nano tanks and midground details. Tough, compact leaves naturally resist grazing from plant-nibbling fish and active dwarf shrimp. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Avoid intense light and ensure good water flow to prevent spot algae on slow‑growing leaves. CO₂ is optional but improves growth and leaf density. Learn more about planting these species by reading our guide on How to Plant Epiphyte Aquatic Plants. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How is Anubias Nana Paxing different from Anubias Nana Petite? While Anubias Nana Petite forms tight, upright mini rosettes with rounded leaves, Anubias Nana Paxing grows horizontally in a low, flat creeping mat with slender, slightly cupped leaves that hug wood and stone contours instead of growing upward. 2. How do I secure a creeping rhizome like Anubias Paxing so it stays flat against driftwood? Use tiny dabs of aquarium-safe cyanoacrylate gel glue along the underside of the rhizome or wrap it lightly with dark cotton thread so the creeping stem sits flush against the wood, allowing new roots to grip the surface naturally. 3. Why are the glossy leaves on my Anubias Paxing collecting green spot algae? Because its flat, horizontal leaves face directly upward toward your light and grow slowly, intense lighting quickly triggers green spot algae. Keep it in low light or under partial shade from taller plants and maintain steady water circulation.

Plant Profile Bucephalandra ‘Titan’ is a compact, low-tech epiphyte with small, ruffled leaves that sprout from reddish stems along a creeping horizontal rhizome. Depending on your lighting intensity and nutrient stability, the foliage shifts between deep forest green and dark bluish tones with a subtle metallic sheen. Staying around 1.5 to 3 inches tall, its tight, clustering habit works well for detailing foreground hardscape, wedging into rock seams, or layering along driftwood branches. Whether you're growing it fully submerged in an aquarium or emersed in a humid terrarium setup, make sure the central rhizome stays completely exposed to open water and air, because burying it in substrate is a fast track to rot. Key Features & Notes Similar to Buce Catherinae Red , Titan stands out with warm, reddish petioles that contrast nicely against its dark, metallic-tinted foliage. Small, undulating leaf margins add dense, moss-like texture along rocks and wood without sprawling out of control. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for planted tanks where other plants might struggle. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from its pot and clearing all rockwool from the root base . Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard low-light setups, supplemental CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilizers will yield faster growth and richer bluish-dark coloration. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I mount Bucephalandra Titan to hardscape? Gently clean away the rockwool from around the roots, then secure the rhizome directly to porous rock or driftwood using a small drop of cyanoacrylate aquarium glue or cotton thread. Over time, its roots will anchor onto the hardscape surface on their own. 2. Why is my Bucephalandra Titan melting after planting? Sudden swings in water parameters, temperature, or lighting can trigger an acclimation melt as the plant adjusts to your aquarium. Keep water movement steady and conditions stable; as long as the central rhizome stays firm, new submerged leaves will sprout. 3. Can I plant Bucephalandra Titan in substrate? You can let the roots grow down into gravel or aquarium soil to anchor the plant, but the central horizontal rhizome must remain completely exposed above the substrate line to prevent rot.

Plant Profile Cryptocoryne on Driftwood delivers instant aquascaping style without the hassle of delicate substrate planting. Pre-attached to a natural piece of hardscape, this adaptable feature showcases robust rosette foliage that introduces lush, soft textures to your layout. As with all crypt plants, it can be sensitive to sudden changes in parameters and strongly objects to being relocated once it's settled in your tank. Simply place this ready-to-display piece into your midground, and its established roots will continue to anchor into the wood, creating an eye-catching, self-sustaining focal point. Key Features & Benefits Pre-attached to natural hardscape for instant placement without the need for delicate substrate planting. Can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups, where mature plants may produce flowering spathes. Care & Planting Instructions Position the driftwood directly into your midground layout; no rockwool prep or tying required. Ensure the surrounding environment provides steady nutrients via liquid fertilizers or root contact with nutrient-rich substrate. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth and fuller foliage density, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving the driftwood piece repeatedly may trigger leaf loss. Cryptocoryne species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting rhizome offshoots or replanting new plantlets. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Check our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt for full recovery steps. 3. Should I use root tabs or liquid fertilizers? While root tabs work if the driftwood rests directly on nutrient substrate, liquid all-in-one fertilizers or root tabs tucked under the wood base help feed roots clinging to the hardscape.

listings.commonName: Java Fern Trident Mini on Driftwood
listings.description: Plant Profile Java Fern Trident Mini on Driftwood is a pre-mounted hardscape arrangement featuring slender, fork-lobed fronds in a compact, dwarf scale. Pre-attached to natural, aquarium-safe driftwood, this ready-to-drop piece combines the intricate aesthetic of Java Fern Trident with ultimate plug-and-play convenience, eliminating the need to tie or glue individual rhizomes. Virtually bulletproof and delightfully unbothered by parameter swings or curious herbivorous fish, it brings instant structure and natural depth to nano tanks and midground layouts right out of the box. Key Features & Notes Tough, fibrous foliage easily withstands curious nipping from herbivorous fish like cichlids, goldfish, and large snails. Pre-attached to natural driftwood pieces, providing an effortless centerpiece that requires zero gluing, tying, or substrate planting. Exceptional hardiness lets it thrive in non-CO2 tanks and low-light environments. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by rinsing the mounted driftwood piece gently in clean freshwater to remove any loose debris before placing it directly into your aquarium. Java Fern Trident Mini on Driftwood is an epiphytic fern that comes pre-bound to hardscape; position the driftwood directly on top of your substrate or wedged between rocks, ensuring the horizontal rhizome remains exposed and unburied. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard setups, gentle water movement and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and broader fronds. Master long-term care and troubleshoot common leaf issues by checking out our Java Fern Care Guide . Final size and foliage pattern depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual wood shapes and plant arrangements may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Microsorum pteropus 'Trident Mini' (syn. Leptochilus pteropus ) Common Name(s) Java Fern Trident Mini on Driftwood, Mini Trident Java Fern Family Polypodiaceae Plant Type Epiphyte Pre-Attached to Hardscape Care Difficulty Beginner / Easy (Low-Tech Compatible) Light Requirement Low to Medium CO2 Requirement Not Required (Beneficial) Placement / Usage Nano Foreground, Midground, Instant Hardscape Layout Height / Size 3"–5" (7.5–13 cm) Growth Rate Slow to Moderate Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 | Temperature 68°F–82°F (20°C–28°C) Propagation Method Rhizome Division & Adventitious Plantlets Origin Indonesia / Cultivated Variety Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why is the driftwood releasing a slight yellow or tea color into my water? Natural driftwood slowly releases organic compounds called tannins into the water column. These tannins are completely harmless, slightly lower the water pH, and create a natural environment beneficial for soft-water fish like tetras and South American cichlids. You can easily remove the tint with regular water changes or by adding activated carbon / Purigen to your filter. 2. Can I remove the Java Fern Trident Mini from the driftwood piece? Yes. If you wish to detach it later, you can carefully snip the securing thread or cut the roots away from the wood. Once separated, the rhizomes can be re-bound or glued onto other hardscape features in your aquarium. 3. Can I plant the attached driftwood into the substrate? You can rest the driftwood piece on top of your substrate, but you must ensure the green rhizome of the Java Fern remains above the substrate line. Burying the wood so deeply that the rhizome gets covered will cause the fern to rot and die. 4. Will fish like cichlids or goldfish eat Java Fern Trident Mini on Driftwood? Generally, no. Java Fern leaves are thick, fibrous, and contain bitter-tasting compounds that deter most plant-eating fish. Because the plant is already bound firmly to heavy driftwood, it is also much harder for energetic fish to uproot or knock around.

Plant Profile Penthorum Sedoides is a hardy and charming aquatic stem plant native to the wetlands, ditch banks, and river margins of Eastern North America. Characterized by its light green, distinctively serrated leaves that radiate along sturdy central stems, this easy-care species exhibits a naturally compact and bushy growth habit. Highly adaptable to various lighting conditions, Penthorum Sedoides grows upright with wider leaf spacing under low-to-moderate lighting, but under high-intensity light, it transitions into a low, creeping habit that forms dense midground cushions. Key Features & Benefits Light green, serrated leaves add unique texture to midground and background zones. Grows low and creeping under strong light, or tall and upright under moderate light. Easy, slow-to-moderate grower for low-tech tanks, nano aquariums, and nature-style aquascapes. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip the lower inch of foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to insert individual stems 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide moderate lighting and clean water conditions; while CO2 and heavy fertilization are not required, providing CO2 injection promotes faster growth. Maintain stable water parameters to ensure a smooth transition and prevent leaf melting. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and thicken the bush. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Does Penthorum Sedoides require CO2 injection? No, Penthorum Sedoides is a hardy and low-demanding plant that thrives in low-tech aquariums without CO2 injection. However, supplying CO2 along with liquid fertilizer dosing results in denser foliage and a richer green color. 2. How do I get Penthorum Sedoides to grow low and creeping? To encourage Penthorum Sedoides to grow low and spread laterally as a midground carpet, provide strong, direct lighting. Under lower lighting, the stems will grow vertically towards the surface with more spacing between leaf nodes. 3. How do I propagate Penthorum Sedoides? Propagation is simple: snip healthy stem tops or side branches using sharp aquascaping shears and press the cut stems directly into substrate. The newly planted stem cuttings will anchor quickly and establish new root systems.

Plant Profile Mayaca Fluviatilis is what happens when you combine the fine, feathery look of Rotala wallichii and Cabomba . Native to the swamps of the Southern US and South America, this delicate, bushy aquatic stem plant rocks needle-thin, bright green leaves that flow like tiny pine plumes in the current. Highly adaptable and beginner-friendly, planting Mayaca Fluviatilis in large groups creates a stunning, lush background centerpiece that adds remarkable visual depth. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Fine, needle-like green foliage adds soft texture and natural movement to background and midground aquascape zones. Hardy, versatile stem species adapts easily to low-tech tanks while absorbing excess nutrients to support water clarity. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip lower foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. * Mayaca stems are thin and delicate, so handle with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into aquarium soil, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower growth. Provide moderate-to-high lighting to keep lower stem leaves healthy and prevent yellowing or die-off. Maintain stable water parameters and clean water conditions; while CO2 injection is not required, it yields significantly fuller, thicker stems. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the desired height, and replant the trimmings directly into substrate to multiply your stock. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining adequate light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. Why are the lower stems on my Mayaca Fluviatilis turning yellow? Mayaca Fluviatilis requires moderate-to-high lighting to maintain its lower foliage. If lower stems become shaded or lighting is insufficient, the bottom leaves will turn yellow and drop off. Increasing light intensity and spacing stems apart during planting prevents this. 3. How do I transition Mayaca Fluviatilis from emersed to submerged growth? When transitioning from emersed to submerged growth, plant bare stems securely into rich substrate under moderate-to-high lighting and keep water parameters stable. As new growth adapts, the plant will shed its land leaves and sprout soft, needle-thin underwater foliage. Once new shoots develop, trim away old lower growth to encourage dense branching.

Plant Profile Meet Limnophila Aromatica, an aptly named aquatic stem plant known for its vibrant color spectrum and aromatic herbal foliage. Famous for its lanceolate leaves with serrated margins that radiate in whorls, this species displays a palette ranging from olive-green and lime to deep pink, magenta, and rich violet-red. When bruised or pruned, it releases a distinct citrus-herbal aroma, reflecting its traditional culinary use in Vietnamese cuisine. Growing up to 8 to 20 inches tall, Limnophila Aromatica serves as a dramatic centerpiece or colorful background hedge in medium-to-large planted aquariums and Dutch-style layouts. Key Features & Benefits Foliage displays a wide spectrum of colors from lime green to magenta, pink, and deep violet-red. Rapidly forms dense background hedges and structured Dutch-style street layouts. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip the lower inch of foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide medium-to-high lighting and consistent iron dosing; while adaptable without mandatory CO2 injection, supplying pressurized CO2 and rich soil substrate yields robust growth and maximizes vibrant magenta and pink hues. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or rotting. Trim main stem tops with sharp straight scissors once they reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and expand coverage. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Many aquatic stem plants are cultivated emersed (above water) at plant nurseries, producing rounder, thicker green leaves. Once submerged in your aquarium, the plant will transition into its true aquatic form, sprouting delicate, colorful submerged foliage.

Common name: Aponogeton Natans Aponogteon Natans is an aquatic bulb plant with long green wavy leaves that originally comes from stagnant waters in India and Sri Lanka. Like most Aponogeton species, this particular aquatic plant can grow quite large, making it a great addition as a background plant focal plant. With optimal care, Aponogeton Natans flowers frequently and is a great additional to planted aquariums. Half of the bulb should be buried into the substrate to facilitate growth. Avoid completely burying the bulb as this can promote bulb rot. Notes: Do not make drastic changes to the aquarium. Unstable parameters will result in melt and rotting of the aquarium plant. Aponogeton grows fairly large making this aquarium plant suitable for larger planted aquariums. Please be sure to remove this plant from its lead bunch. Remove the cotton surrounding the roots and plant into a quality substrate. For instructions on how to properly prep "bunched" aquarium plants, click here . CO2 injection and quality aquarium soil will yield better growth. Please research appropriately to ensure your plant thrives. Plant Profile Homalomena Silver is a rare rheophytic aroid endemic to Kalimantan, Borneo, featuring spade-shaped, pale green leaves with a noticeable silvery wash. A versatile choice for emersed setups as well as planted aquariums, its lighter tone pops cleanly against dark lava rock, dark wood, or deep green mosses, working well in the foreground or tucked into lower hardscape crevices. Emersed leaves carry a soft, velvety texture that gradually shifts to a smooth, waxy surface once adapted to underwater conditions. Key Features & Notes Bright green foliage with a silvery sheen transitions from velvety emersed to waxy submerged. Versatile growth habit adapts to fully submerged aquariums, humid terrariums, and paludarium margins. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Plant the roots into a quality aquarium soil or airy tropical substrate, keeping the main rhizome exposed above the soil line to prevent rot. Provide low to moderate indirect lighting; supplemental CO2 and gentle water flow encourage denser, faster submerged growth. Maintain humidity above 75% for emersed setups, or ensure clean, stable water conditions when transitioning to fully submerged growth. Trim older or melting transition leaves near the rhizome base with sharp aquascaping scissors to promote fresh growth. Final size and silvery coloration depend entirely on your specific setup conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Use sharp scissors to separate a section of rhizome that contains at least three leaves and viable roots, then replant or attach it to wood or stone.

Plant Profile Hygrophila angustifolia, aka Willow Hygro, is a fast-growing, adaptable aquatic stem plant native to the tropical wetlands and riverbanks of Southeast Asia. Named for its long, narrow, willow-like leaves that sprout in opposite pairs along sturdy vertical stems, this species brings soft movement and green texture, making it an ideal background filler or midground hedge in medium-to-large planted aquariums. Because of its rapid growth rate, Hygrophila Angustifolia serves as an incredible natural filter, absorbing excess nitrates and phosphates from the water column to suppress unwanted algae growth. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Slender, willow-like green leaves introduce elegant texture and gentle movement. Natural nutrient sponge that helps keep water clarity high. Beginner-friendly and adaptable, it thrives in a wide range of aquarium setups. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight (or pot) and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the roots, then strip lower foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower foliage. Provide moderate-to-high lighting and clean water conditions; while adaptable without CO2, supplying pressurized CO2 and regular liquid fertilizers will significantly accelerate growth and stem density. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim main stem tops with straight scissors once stems reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to easily propagate and expand coverage. Plant Profile Limnophila Heterophylla is an easy-to-grow, highly adaptable aquatic stem plant. A favorite among aquascapers for its delicate aesthetic and low-maintenance requirements, this species features finely divided, fan-like whorls of bright green foliage, resembling a refined hybrid between Water Wisteria and Cabomba . Fast-growing and resilient, Limnophila Heterophylla serves as an exceptional background filler or midground accent, rapidly producing dense, feathery green forests even in low-tech planted aquariums. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Delicate, feathery leaf whorls bring soft, lace-like visual texture and vibrant green contrast to background zones. Beginner-friendly and adaptable species that thrives in low-tech setups. Rapid growth acts as a natural nitrate sponge for crystal-clear water. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight (or pot) and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the roots, then strip lower foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower leaf whorls. Provide low-to-moderate lighting and clean water; while adaptable without CO2, supplying pressurized CO2 and a nutrient-rich substrate yields thicker, more lush stem growth. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim main stem tops with straight scissors once stems reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to easily propagate and expand coverage. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Plant Profile Echinodorus grandifolius is known for its massive scale and broad, heart-to-oval-shaped bright green foliage. Unlike many faster-growing sword cultivars, this giant species develops at a steady, moderate pace, allowing aquascapers to enjoy its substantial structure without constantly trimming back runaway growth. Reaching heights of 20+ inches, its expansive leaf blades naturally draw the eye, making it a commanding focal point across background zones in larger aquariums. Thanks to its low lighting demands and forgiving nature, even tolerating cooler, unheated water temperatures, it serves as a hardy, low-maintenance option for beginners. Key Features & Notes Large, heart-shaped leaf blades create a commanding focal point in medium-to-large aquariums. Slower, steady growth rate compared to other sword varieties makes size management far easier. Hardy species that grows reliably without pressurized CO2 injection or high-intensity light. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Plant the roots deeply into your aquarium soil, keeping the crown of the plant resting just above the substrate line to prevent rot. All Echinodorus are heavy root feeders that rely on rich substrate nutrition; placing root tabs near the base supports steady, healthy leaf development. Supplemental CO2 injection accelerates growth and encourages denser, fuller foliage, though the plant will still grow steadily in low-tech setups. Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf shedding during the initial transition period. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Plant Profile Phoenix Moss is a moss-have addition for anyone wanting to add lush elegance and a soft, feather-like texture to their underwater landscape. This gorgeous green plant features delicate fronds that look just like the downy feathers of baby birds, adding brightness and a beautiful three-dimensional depth to any tank. It is highly adaptable and virtually maintenance-free once settled, happily anchoring itself to rocks, driftwood, or even directly into your substrate without the usual headache of constant re-tying. Key Features & Benefits Delicate, feathery fronds add a soft organic texture that makes hardscape look naturally aged. Easily attached to driftwood, rocks, or aquascaping crevices using thread or gel. Incredibly resilient and low-maintenance once established, making it a stress-free choice for any skill level. Care & Planting Instructions Press the golfball-sized portion gently into your substrate, or secure it to your hardscape using dark thread or dabs of aquarium-safe superglue gel. Team Buce Plant Tip: Keep your aquarium temperature on the cooler side, ideally around 77°F, as this species prefers slightly cooler water to stay looking its best. Give the moss an occasional light haircut with sharp aquascaping shears to keep its shape neat, compact, and perfectly balanced. Propagate your patch in seconds by cutting or pulling a small clump apart and anchoring it to a new surface in your tank. Add CO2 injection if you want to accelerate growth and unlock the most intense, eye-popping green coloration possible. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. listings.commonName: Micranthemum Umbrosum Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Common Name: Giant Baby Tears Micranthemum Umbrosum is a bright green, low-growing stem plant perfect for beginners. It is a versatile species which can be used for both foregrounds, midground, and background. Constant pruning will keep it low growing and spread runners horizontally. Leaving it untrimmed will allow it to grow vertically as a background plant. This plant is very easy to grow and can be rampant if it’s not pruned. Its often compared to Pearlweed since they share similar characteristics and growth patterns but the leaves are slightly larger and rounder. The shape and growth of the plant depend on the conditions so you must plan accordingly if you have a specific vision for how it will fit into your aquascape. This plant is similar in appearance to other carpeting plants and can be a low-maintenance alternative if you are having trouble getting foreground coverage in your tank. This plant grows best with moderate light and CO2 levels around 6-14ppm. However, Micranthemum Umbrosum can usually get all the nutrients it needs from a nutrient-enriched substrate and healthy fish colony. For super dense growth, use high light and CO2. Bright light will yield bushy growth, while moderate light yields looser, upward growth. Propagate by trimming the ends of stems, then group several together and bury them together in the substrate. Make sure that other foliage does not cover them. Notes: Tissue culture plants are grown in vitro from a state of the art laboratory specialized in propagating aquatic plants. They provide the best option for those who want to ensure that absolutely zero unwanted pests are introduced into the aquarium. Remove tissue culture gel before planting. Simply wash the gel away or soak the plant in water and squeeze the gel off with your fingers. Mondo Grass does not require too much lighting and is partial to shaded areas as well. We would recommend using it as a background plant choice in a pond/bog style planted aquarium. listings.commonName: Lindernia Rotundifolia Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Lindernia Rotundifolia (commonly called Roundleaf Lindernia or Baby Tears) is a fast-growing, bright green aquatic stem plant native to Asia. Characterized by small, rounded leaves arranged in neat opposing pairs along the stems, it quickly absorbs excess nitrates while building thick, bushy groupings in midground and background zones. This adaptable, beginner-friendly and low-tech species grows reliably both submerged in aquariums and emersed in open-top tanks or humid terrariums, where stems will readily grow past the waterline toward the light. Reaching 6 to 8+ inches in height, it forms dense, vibrant green bushes with regular trimming that contrast well against fine-leaved or red stem plants. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Bright green, rounded leaves grow in opposing pairs along upright stems to form dense midground or background bushes. Fast-growing, beginner-friendly stem plant actively absorbs excess nitrates and thrives in low-tech setups. Adapts smoothly to fully submerged aquariums or emersed growth above the waterline in open-top tanks and terrariums. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small portions or individual stems 1 inch apart into your aquarium soil so light reaches the lower leaves. Provide moderate to high lighting; while pressurized CO2 is not required, adding CO2 injection and balanced liquid fertilizers accelerates growth and keeps stems compact. Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf shedding during the initial transition period. To propagate, trim main stem tops or side shoots with sharp straight shears and replant the cuttings directly into your aquarium soil. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. listings.commonName: Cryptocoryne Pygmaea Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Cryptocoryne pygmaea brings adaptable charm and wide botanical variety directly to your midground layout. Despite its name, this versatile island species expands into a lush rosette with narrow foliage that shifts from bright green to warm brown under aquarium lighting. As with all crypt plants, it can be sensitive to sudden parameter shifts and strongly objects to being relocated once planted. Given a permanent home in your substrate, however, its compact rosettes mature into an eye-catching, long-lasting accent. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Variable green-to-brown foliage creates soft movement and natural texture in midground zones. Can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups, where mature plants may produce flowering spathes. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel to supply essential subterranean nutrients. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth and fuller foliage density, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Crypt species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. This unique lineage replaces classic button-like roundness with elongated, slender foliage ending in a distinct, sharp point. Deep green and exceptionally glossy, its broad lanceolate leaves add a polished, architectural look to midground hardscape layouts. Highly forgiving and adaptable to fluctuating parameters, it delivers high-end hybrid aesthetics with zero high-maintenance stress. By choosing the Tissue Culture version of this plant, you are guaranteed a 100% pest-free, algae-free, and pesticide-free start for your aquarium. Glossy, deep green leaf blades catch ambient light to provide striking visual depth against rocks and wood. The sterile laboratory environment guarantees your new plant arrives completely free of pests. Care & Planting Instructions Remove the plantlets from the cup and rinse away the sterile nutrient gel under lukewarm, dechlorinated water. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Avoid intense light and ensure good water flow to prevent spot algae on slow‑growing leaves. CO₂ is recommended to assist with the tissue culture transition and support healthy growth. Master the prep and planting process by checking out a beginner's guide to tissue culture plants to prevent your delicate new plantlets from melting or floating away. Plant Profile Echinodorus 'Chocolate Marble', often referred to as the Chocolate Marble Sword, is a hybrid cultivar prized for its rich, variegated foliage. True to its name, this unique sword plant produces broad leaves decorated with a mottled pattern of deep chocolate-brown, bronze, and olive-green blotches. Reaching heights between 10 and 16 inches, it makes a handsome midground centerpiece or a standout background plant in medium to large aquariums. Under moderate to bright lighting, its marbling contrast becomes especially pronounced, bringing distinct pattern and warm color to your aquascape. Like most sword plants, it is naturally hardy and adaptable, making it an excellent, low-maintenance option for beginners looking for something a bit different than standard green foliage. Key Features & Notes Broad, marbled leaf blades feature deep chocolate-brown, bronze, and olive-green blotches. Moderate height offers versatile placement as a midground centerpiece or background focal point. Hardy and adaptable rosette habit thrives across a wide range of water parameters. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Plant the roots deeply into your aquarium soil, keeping the crown of the plant resting just above the substrate line to prevent rot. All Echinodorus are heavy root feeders that rely on rich substrate nutrition; placing root tabs near the base supports steady, healthy leaf development. Supplemental CO2 injection and moderate-to-high lighting accelerate growth and sharpen the contrast of the marbled patterns, though the plant will still grow reliably in low-tech setups. Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf shedding during the initial transition period. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I prune an Echinodorus when it grows too large? Prune older or overgrown outer leaves individually near the root crown using sharp aquascaping scissors. Avoid cutting across leaf blades, as damaged leaf tips will turn brown rather than regrowing. 2. How do I maintain and enhance the dark marbling pattern on Chocolate Marble Sword leaves? Provide moderate-to-high lighting and supplement the substrate with iron-rich root tabs. Under low light, the brown and bronze speckling can fade, causing new foliage to emerge in a solid olive-green shade. 3. Will the marbled pattern on emersed leaves change when the plant transitions to underwater growth? Yes. As old emersed leaves drop off, the new submersed leaves will emerge thinner, glossier, and with more defined chocolate-brown and bronze blotches scattered across the foliage.

Topping out around 8 inches in height, it avoids the massive footprints of typical Amazon Swords, making it an ideal midground focal point or accent plant in almost any aquarium size. New leaves emerge with a warm reddish-bronze tint before maturing into various shades of olive green depending on your light levels. Naturally hardy and undemanding, it delivers the iconic rosette style and bulletproof reliability of the sword plant family without taking over your entire layout. Hardy rosette growth habit adapts easily to low light and low-tech parameters without mandatory CO2 injection. Plant the roots deeply into your aquarium soil, keeping the crown of the plant resting just above the substrate line to prevent rot. Plant Profile Common Name: Bucephalandra Kedagang Green Long Buce ‘Kedagang Green Long’ is a striking aquarium plant featuring elongated, slightly ruffled leaves and a bold, vibrant green coloration. Similar to the classic Kedagang variety , this variant is distinguished by its more slender leaf profile and impressive length, providing a unique texture compared to rounded species. Highly versatile, it can be grown submerged or emersed, usually attached to hardscape such as driftwood or rocks rather than being buried in traditional aquarium substrate. It's a great accent for the midground of freshwater aquascapes, where its slow-growing rhizomes gradually expand to create a lush, textured colony. Key Features & Notes The "Green Long" designation refers to its unique slender leaf shape and wavy margins, which catch the water flow beautifully in high-tech setups. This variety maintains a bright, healthy green hue that provides a refreshing contrast against darker stones or red-toned Bucephalandra species. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for aquascapes where other plants might struggle. It is perfectly at home fully submerged in an aquarium or emersed in high-humidity terrariums, vivariums, and paludariums. Care Tips & Preparation Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood . Never bury the rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Carefully remove the plant from its pot and clear away all rockwool from the roots. For a deep dive on prepping potted plants, click here . Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting. Unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance, CO2 injection will yield much faster growth. We recommend researching your specific water chemistry to ensure your plant thrives. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions. Please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Please research appropriately to ensure your plant thrives. Additional Information Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! listings.description: Plant Profile Crypt Flamingo is one of our favorites here at Buce Plant, and honestly, it's not hard to see why! Ruffled leaves and pink coloration set it apart from the more common crypts out there, making it a rare, highly sought-after pick among collectors. Those exotic pink tones are what give it the edge over the usual green or brown Cryptocoryne species, and new leaves start with a striking blood-red color before naturally softening into a pinkish tint over time. As with all crypts, it can be a bit sensitive to changes in water parameters and doesn't like to be moved, but once established, it will contrast nicely with greener plants in your foreground or midground zones. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Exotic pink foliage with ruffled margins introduces a vibrant accent. Can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups where it will periodically produce unique flowering spathes. The depth of the pink color intensifies significantly under higher light levels and CO2 injection. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Crypt species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. Plant Profile Java Fern Philippine Mini is a delicate, compact variation of the classic Philippine Java Fern. Displaying soft-green fronds with a distinctively hammered, textured surface that stay shorter and narrower than traditional Java Fern varieties, it stays at a manageable height of just 3 to 5 inches. Hardy and unbothered by low light or hungry fish, it wedges easily into hardscape gaps and driftwood for instant lushness. This is one of the best choices for beginners seeking refined scale and textured greenery in compact aquascapes. Key Features & Notes Tough, fibrous foliage easily withstands curious nipping from herbivorous fish like cichlids, goldfish, and large snails. Compact height, narrower profile, and hammered leaf texture make it an ideal choice for nano aquariums and filling tight hardscape gaps. Exceptional hardiness lets it thrive in non-CO2 tanks and low-light environments. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Java Fern Philippine Mini is an epiphytic fern that should be attached to rocks or driftwood with aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as it will rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard setups, gentle water movement and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and broader fronds. Master long-term care and troubleshoot common leaf issues by checking out our Java Fern Care Guide . Final size and foliage pattern depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Leptochilus pteropus ) Common Name(s) Java Fern Philippine Mini, Mini Philippine Java Fern Family Polypodiaceae Plant Type Epiphyte (Rhizome Fern) Care Difficulty Beginner / Easy (Low-Tech Compatible) Light Requirement Low to Medium CO2 Requirement Not Required (Beneficial) Placement / Usage Nano Foreground, Midground, Hardscape Accent Height / Size 3"–5" (7.5–13 cm) Growth Rate Slow to Moderate Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 | Temperature 68°F–82°F (20°C–28°C) Propagation Method Rhizome Division & Adventitious Plantlets Origin Indonesia / Cultivated Variety Frequently Asked Questions 1. What makes Java Fern Philippine Mini different from standard Java Fern? Java Fern Philippine Mini produces shorter, noticeably narrower leaves with a softer green color and subtle, hammered leaf texture. Its dwarf stature makes it much better suited for nano tanks or fine hardscape detail than broad, full-sized Java Fern cultivars. 2. Why are there small black spots and tiny leaves growing under my Java Fern Philippine Mini leaves? Do not panic; your plant is not diseased! Java Fern reproduces naturally through adventitious plantlets. Small dark bumps (sporangia) form along the undersides of mature leaves, sprouting tiny brown roots and mini green fronds. Once these baby plantlets develop 3–4 leaves, you can gently pop them off the mother leaf and glue them elsewhere in your aquarium. 3. Can I plant Java Fern Philippine Mini into substrate? No. Java Fern Philippine Mini is an epiphyte that absorbs nutrients directly from the water column through its foliage and fine root network. If you bury its horizontal rhizome beneath aquarium soil, sand, or gravel, the stem will suffocate, rot, and die. Always attach it to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread. 4. Will fish like cichlids or goldfish eat Java Fern Philippine Mini? Generally, no. Java Fern leaves are thick, fibrous, and contain bitter-tasting compounds that deter most plant-eating fish. While aggressive diggers might knock it off hardscape if not glued securely, they rarely consume the foliage.

Lime-green coloration creates a strong visual focal point and contrasts with red stem plants. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Provide medium-to-high lighting and pressurized CO2 injection; consistent fertilization with a specialized liquid macro and micro formula yields robust stem growth and prevents bottom leaf yellowing. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or rotting. Trim main stem tops with sharp straight scissors once they reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and thicken the bush. listings.description: Common Name: Diamond Ludwigia Diamond Ludwigia is a less common Ludwigia variation with very unique coloration. In ideal conditions these plants’ leaves are green on top and red underneath, adding a stunning dimension to the mid-ground of almost any aquascape. Their vivid color creates a superb focal point. Diamond Ludwigia plants have oval, pointed leaves that grow in opposite pairs along the stem. The leaves can be green, gold, orange, or red, depending on tank conditions. These plants are very attractive when planted in bunches of 10-12 stems. In order to achieve the desirable bright colors in your Diamond Ludwigia, you must provide high lighting and nutrient levels. Supplemental iron will bring out more brilliant red tones in the plant. CO2 injection is recommended to see optimal growth and color. The plant can be grown submersed or emersed, and emersed plants will produce delicate yellow flowers. Notes: Tissue culture plants are grown in vitro from a state of the art laboratory specialized in propagating aquatic plants. They provide the best option for those who want to ensure that absolutely zero unwanted pests are introduced into the aquarium. Remove tissue culture gel before planting. Simply wash the gel away or soak the plant in water and squeeze the gel off with your fingers. Do not make drastic changes to the aquarium. Unstable parameters will result in melt and rotting of the aquarium plant. For instructions on how to properly plant tissue culture aquarium plants, click here . CO2 injection and quality aquarium soil will yield better growth. listings.description: Plant Profile Marsilea Hirsuta is a charming dwarf, clover-like foreground plant that brings a unique look to any aquascape. It is a slow-growing carpeting plant that is relatively easy to keep compared to demanding foreground species like Dwarf Baby Tears , making it an excellent alternative for hobbyists wanting a lush carpet without the intense upkeep. When grown under medium to high light, the plant stays low-growing and spreads horizontally, helping you achieve a beautifully dense, turf-style lawn. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Need Dwarf Four Leaf Clover but this listing is out of stock? Check out these other popular variants: Marsilea Angustifolia Marsilea Crenata Key Features & Benefits Dwarf clover-like foliage creates a unique, turf-style lawn across the foreground. More forgiving and easier to cultivate than high-demanding carpets like Dwarf Baby Tears (HC). Horizontal runners form a dense, low-profile carpet under moderate to high light levels. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions and planting. Divide the tissue culture mat into small plugs and plant them spaced an inch apart across the foreground using fine-tip tweezers. Use a dry start method or Wabi Kusa setup to give its root system plenty of time to firmly anchor into the substrate before you flood the tank. Maintain stable aquarium parameters and avoid drastic shifts in water quality to prevent your new grass from melting. Provide medium to high lighting to encourage compact, low-growing horizontal expansion across the substrate (lower lighting causes stems to grow taller). Inject pressurized CO2 to supercharge its density and growth rate, keeping it low and compact. Master the basics by learning how to properly grow aquarium carpet plants to ensure your new layout fills in quickly. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Because tissue culture portions have delicate root systems, fish or water currents can easily dislodge them. Planting small clumps deeply into fine soil or letting the tank grow emersed using the Dry Start Method will anchor the roots securely before flooding.

Plant Profile Aridarum caulescens 'White Fang' is a rare aquarium plant that stands apart from standard riverbank epiphytes with its notably longer, sword-like leaf profile. Larger than its relative 'Sabertooth', it produces thick, narrow leaves measuring 4 to 6 inches that feature a heavy waxy cuticle designed to handle turbulent river currents in the wild. Its thick horizontal stem resembles an Anubias rhizome more than a typical Buce, giving it a stout, architectural presence that works naturally as a bold midground or hardscape accent. Whether grown fully submerged in an aquarium or emersed in a humid terrarium setup, keep the main rhizome exposed to open water and good circulation, as burying it under substrate will quickly rot the plant. Key Features & Notes Long, narrow leaves with a tough, waxy texture resist tearing under high current and easily withstand grazing from bottom dwellers and snails. Forms a larger, more commanding silhouette than most rheophytes, serving as an effective architectural bridge between foreground rocks and background stems. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from its pot and clearing all rockwool from the root base . Aridarum is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While hardy and adaptable to low-tech setups, moderate water flow and pressurized CO2 injection will yield faster root establishment and consistent new growth. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! After cleaning away any packing media or rockwool, secure the thick horizontal rhizome to textured driftwood or porous rock using a couple of dabs of cyanoacrylate glue or cotton thread. Once secured, its roots will slowly grab onto the hardscape surface. 2. Why are the leaves on my Aridarum White Fang melting? Sudden shifts in water parameters, lighting intensity, or temperature can trigger an initial acclimation melt. Maintain steady conditions and clean flow; as long as the stout central rhizome remains firm, it will bounce back with fresh leaves adapted to your aquarium. 3. Can I plant Aridarum White Fang in substrate? You can let the roots grow downward into gravel or aquasoil to pull nutrients, but the main horizontal rhizome must sit fully exposed above the substrate line. If buried, the rhizome will suffocate from lack of water circulation and rot.

This version utilizes a slim, integrated baseplate that slides neatly beneath your rimless aquarium and leveling mat, using the weight of the tank to keep the fixture anchored. The proprietary ColorFull spectrum delivers a beautifully crisp 5100K output, specifically engineered to bring out the deepest green and red pigments in your foliage. It is an extraordinary solution for illuminating small rimless aquariums, open-air Wabi Kusa setups, Aqua Worx Iotas, and desktop terrariums without cluttering your glass rims. Key Features & Benefits Integrated low-profile baseplate slides directly underneath your rimless aquarium and leveling foam mat, offering a hardware-free floating look. Innovative 360-degree swivel arm lets you rotate the entire light panel completely out of the way, giving you unobstructed access for stress-free tank maintenance and plant trimming. Telescoping height adjustability allows you to easily slide the light up or down and adjust angles for highly customized lighting exposure. Fluid 3-level dimming capabilities rely on simple touch-sensitive onboard controls to easily adjust your environment to match your plants' specific needs. Smart ramp up and down feature slowly brightens and dims the light during power transitions, preventing sudden light shocks from stressing your sensitive fish and shrimp. Rust-resistant aluminum housing combined with premium plastic and rubber elements guarantees a pristine finish and superior heat dissipation over a 50,000-hour lifespan. listings.commonName: Rotala Mexicana Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Rotala Mexicana is a highly sought-after aquatic stem plant widely distributed across tropical and subtropical regions of South America, Central America, Africa, and Australia. This fast-growing species features rounded, bright green leaves when grown emersed, which transition into narrow, needle-like foliage with vivid green, salmon, and pink-orange hues when submerged. With its distinctive reddish stems and lush vertical growth habit, Rotala Mexicana makes a great background centerpiece or dense midground hedge when provided with optimal high-tech aquarium conditions. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Thin, narrow underwater foliage displays a dynamic color range from bright green to vibrant pink-orange hues set against reddish stems. Fast vertical growth fills in space and branches into dense hedges with routine pruning. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. * Rotala leaves are fragile, so handle stems with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide high-intensity lighting and pressurized CO2 injection; maintaining balanced macro- and micro-nutrients alongside iron supplementation prevents stunted growth and yields rich pink-orange coloration. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters (acidic to neutral pH 4.5–7.0 preferred) and avoid drastic changes to prevent leaf melt or stem rot. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the water surface, and simply replant the trimmings directly into soil to propagate. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Rotala mexicana (syn. Rotala pusilla ) Common Name(s) Rotala Mexicana, Mexican Rotala Family Lythraceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Stem Plant Care Difficulty Medium / High-Tech Preferred Light Requirement High CO2 Requirement Medium to High (Essential to prevent stunting) Placement / Usage Background / Midground Bushing Height / Size 4–12”+ Growth Rate Fast Water Parameters pH 4.5–7.0 Propagation Method Cuttings (Cut stem and replant tops) Origin South America / Central America / Africa / Australia Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. Why are the tips of my Rotala Mexicana turning black or stunting? Rotala Mexicana is sensitive to nutrient or light deficits. Blackening stem tips or stunted growth typically occur when there is insufficient light, low CO2 injection, or a lack of macro and micronutrients in the water column and substrate. 3. How do I prepare Rotala Mexicana Tissue Culture before planting? Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the dense cluster into smaller clumps or individual stem bundles and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

listings.commonName: Rotala Wallichii Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Common Name: Rotala Wallichii Rotala Wallichii is a popular stem plant with thin fragile leaves that can create luscious forests of green and red when grown in large clusters. High lighting, Co2, and fertilization dosing will turn the leaves a mix of vibrant pink, red, orange and yellow hues. This plant is best kept in large clusters to create a nice bushy background effect. Notes: Rotala has fragile leaves! Be sure to handle with care. Final coloration is ultimately dependent upon the conditions this plant is kept in. This is a live plant meaning size, shape and color may vary. Tissue culture plants are grown in vitro from a state of the art laboratory specialized in propagating aquatic plants. They provide the best option for those who want to ensure that absolutely zero unwanted pests are introduced into the aquarium. Remove tissue culture gel before planting. Simply wash the gel away or soak the plant in water and squeeze the gel off with your fingers. Do not make drastic changes to the aquarium. Unstable parameters will result in melt and rotting of the aquarium plant. For instructions on how to properly plant tissue culture aquarium plants, click here . Do not make drastic changes to the aquarium. Unstable parameters will result in melt and rotting of the aquarium plant. CO2 injection and quality aquarium soil will yield better growth. Please research appropriately to ensure your plant thrives. Plant Profile If you want to add some serious heat to your aquascape without actually burning anything down, we have the moss for you. Flame Moss is known for its upward-pointing attitude, growing in spiraling, vertical shoots that mimic flickering flames. Since we have grown this fiery favorite directly onto a 3" x 3" stainless steel mesh pad, you do not have to play with fire (or messy aquarium glue) to get it to stay put. This unique vertical growth habit can truly ignite your scape, especially if you want to create a dense carpet across your substrate. Key Features & Benefits Pre-attached stainless steel pad naturally sinks, establishing a carpet with no floating. Vertically twisting growth habit resembles flickering flames, adding dramatic architectural height to horizontal surfaces. Dense vertical columns provide a safe foraging forest and shelter for shrimp and fry. Care & Planting Instructions Place the metal mesh pad directly onto your substrate or nestle it firmly at the base of your driftwood where it can receive steady water circulation. Maintain a stable aquarium environment and avoid sudden, drastic changes to your water parameters to keep your moss looking vibrant and healthy. Give the moss an occasional light haircut with sharp aquascaping shears to keep its shape neat, compact, and perfectly balanced. Propagate your patch in seconds by cutting or pulling a small clump apart and anchoring it to a new surface in your tank. Add CO2 injection if you want to accelerate growth and unlock the most intense, eye-popping green coloration possible. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I keep my Flame Moss from turning brown or yellow? Flame Moss prefers clean, moving water and cooler temperatures (under 78°F). Browning usually occurs when organic debris gets trapped inside the dense, vertical shoots or when water temperatures run too high. Gently siphoning debris out during water changes will keep the inner growth green and healthy. 2. How do I use the stainless steel mesh pad in my aquascape? The 3" x 3" stainless steel mesh pad is naturally weighted to sink right out of the box. You can lay it flat on your substrate for an instant vertical carpet, bend the flexible metal around curved hardscape, or attach it vertically to tank walls to form a green backdrop. 3. How do I stop moss trimmings from spreading everywhere during maintenance? Always turn off your filter pumps and powerheads before trimming moss. Use sharp curved shears to make clean cuts, and immediately scoop or siphon out floating cuttings so they don't take root in unwanted areas of your aquarium.

Plant Profile Fittonia albivenis, commonly known as the White Nerve Plant or Silver Fittonia, is a creeping evergreen perennial featuring deep emerald leaves patterned with an intricate web of stark white mosaic venation. In an emersed setup, Fittonia can carpet the tank floor with high-contrast color, fill the gaps between lower hardscape stones, or accent a paludarium waterline. Fittonia is famous among indoor growers as a dramatic "fainter": if the root zone dries out even slightly, the entire stem goes limp and collapses, only to pop fully upright within hours of receiving a thorough misting. Key Features & Notes Dark emerald foliage netted with stark white veins adds high-contrast visual detail to enclosure floors. Low-growing creeping habit spreads across moist substrate to create a tidy, textured carpet. Thrives in high ambient moisture and partial shade with clear warning signs when hydration drops. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Press the root cluster gently into an airy, nutrient-rich tropical substrate mix of bark, sphagnum, tree fern fiber, and perlite; avoid compacting the soil. Maintain humidity above 70% with regular misting, ensuring excess water drains away freely to prevent yellowing leaves and crown rot. Pinch back wandering stem tips with clean shears to prevent leggy growth and encourage bushier, dense lateral branching. Fittonia albivenis are terrestrial plants, and being submerged will result in the death of the plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth!
