Can Fittonia albivenis survive in a closed terrarium? Yes. It thrives in sealed or semi-enclosed glass setups because it relies on consistent air moisture to keep its leaves crisp and hydrated. 2. Why are the leaves on my Fittonia turning yellow and drooping? Yellowing foliage combined with limp stems usually indicates waterlogged, oversaturated soil. Make sure the substrate is loose and has adequate drainage underneath. 3. How do you propagate Fittonia albivenis? Snip a 2 to 3-inch stem cutting just below a leaf node, remove the bottom leaves, and press the cut stem into damp soil or sphagnum moss under high humidity until new roots form.

Plant Profile Fittonia albivenis 'Red', commonly known as the Red Nerve Plant or Net Leaf, is a creeping tropical perennial native to the humid rainforest floors of South America, featuring olive-to-forest-green leaves laced with an intricate mosaic of bold pink-to-red veins. Requiring humid terrestrial conditions, its high-contrast foliage stands out cleanly against light driftwood branches and pale stone, or breaks up uniform mats of green moss along terrarium floors and moist paludarium banks. Fun fact: Fittonia is famously known for wilting dramatically and going limp within hours if the soil dries out, yet visibly perks back up and firms its stems within an hour or two of receiving fresh moisture. Key Features & Notes Dark green ovate foliage is patterned with an intricate network of bright pink-to-crimson veins. Compact, low-creeping habit stays between 3 and 6 inches tall to create an even foreground mat. Requires consistent ambient humidity and moist, well-aerated soil to avoid wilting. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Tuck the root cluster gently into an airy, moisture-retentive tropical substrate mix of peat, sphagnum moss, bark, and perlite across foreground or midground zones. Provide low to medium indirect light; direct sun or intense lighting will bleach the red veining and scorch leaf margins. Keep the substrate consistently moist but never waterlogged, as poor drainage and standing water will cause lower leaves to yellow and roots to rot. Pinch back stem tips just above a leaf node regularly to encourage dense, bushy growth and prevent the stems from getting leggy. Final size and vein color intensity depend entirely on your specific setup conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Fittonia albivenis are terrestrial plants, and being submerged will result in the death of the plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Can Fittonia albivenis Red survive in a closed terrarium? Yes. It thrives in sealed or vented glass enclosures where steady humidity keeps the soil damp and prevents the thin leaves from wilting. 2. Why are the lower leaves on my Red Nerve Plant turning yellow? Yellowing lower leaves typically point to overwatering or compacted soil that lacks drainage. Ensure excess water drains away from the root zone freely. 3. How do you propagate Fittonia albivenis Red? Snip a stem cutting with at least two leaf nodes using sharp shears, remove the lower pair of leaves, and insert the node into moist sphagnum moss or aerated soil under high humidity.

Plant Profile Fittonia albivenis 'Skeleton' is a low-growing tropical evergreen perennial native to the Peruvian Amazon understory, with broad, deep olive-green leaves etched in an intricate web of fine reddish-pink veins. Creeping across shaded substrate flats or tucked against the base of pale driftwood and dark slate, its bone-like lattice pattern breaks up flat expanses of uniform green moss. Grown in moist, airy soil under soft indirect lighting, it forms a low, tidy carpet alongside other humidity-loving plants in terrariums. Key Features & Notes Olive-green foliage showcases an intricate network of fine reddish-pink veins resembling a skeletal frame. Forms a low creeping mat that spreads steadily across moist substrate without climbing aggressively. Adds high-contrast color and texture across shaded foreground pockets in terrariums and paludariums. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Tuck the rooted stems into an airy, nutrient-rich tropical substrate mix of coco coir, peat, and perlite along foreground areas; keep the trailing nodes in contact with damp soil so they can root as they creep. Provide low to medium indirect light or partial shade; harsh direct lighting bleaches the dark leaf surface and scorches the delicate vein markings. Maintain humidity above 70% and keep the soil evenly moist, but ensure proper drainage so water does not sit stagnant around the root base, which causes leaf yellowing. Pinch back growing tips with clean shears to prevent leggy growth and encourage a compact, bushy ground mat. Fittonia albivenis are terrestrial plants, and being submerged will result in the death of the plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Fittonia albivenis 'Skeleton' Common Name(s) Skeleton Nerve Plant, Silver Net Leaf, Mosaic Plant Family Acanthaceae Plant Type Terrestrial Creeping Evergreen Perennial Care Difficulty Easy Light Requirement Low to Medium Indirect Light (Partial Shade) Submersion Suitability Emersed Only (Not for full submersion) Placement / Usage Foreground Carpet, Terrarium Floor, Understory Accent, Paludarium Banks Height / Size 3"–6" (7.5–15 cm) height; spreads horizontally Growth Rate Slow Humidity Requirement High (> 70% RH) Propagation Method Stem Cuttings Origin South America (Amazon Rainforest) Frequently Asked Questions 1. Can Fittonia albivenis 'Skeleton' grow submerged in an aquarium? No. Fittonia is an obligate terrestrial perennial. Submerging the foliage underwater will quickly cause the leaves to turn translucent and rot away. 2. Why are the leaves on my Fittonia turning yellow? Yellowing leaves are almost always a sign of overwatering and waterlogged substrate. Make sure the container drains well so the soil stays moist rather than muddy. 3. How do you propagate Fittonia albivenis 'Skeleton'? Snip a healthy stem cutting just below a leaf node, remove the bottom set of leaves, and press the cut stem into damp soil or moist sphagnum moss inside a closed, humid setup until roots form.

Hakkai Stone is a premium natural rock prized for its dark bluish-green color and smooth, river-worn texture. Also known as Pahai Stone, this stone is adorned with irregular holes and craters produced over centuries by natural erosion, giving it a unique weathered character and the nickname "Bug-Eaten Rock." Its dark coloration provides a visually striking contrast against vibrant green plants, making it a perfect pick for Iwagumi layouts or authentic riverbed-style hardscape designs. While a rare commodity in the planted aquarium hobby, Hakkai Stone is also suitable for non-aquarium use and will work beautifully as a high-end accent in terrariums, paludariums, or similar planted enclosures to achieve a mature, aged look. Notes: Hakkai stone is very heavy. If you are looking for multiple pieces, please increase the amount ordered. If you have any questions, please contact our support team before placing your order. This stone is inert and will not alter water parameters. We recommend rinsing stones thoroughly before use to remove any natural dust or sediment. Stone coloration darkens when wet.

Blue Mountain Seiryu Stone is a darker, bluish-grey variation of the iconic Seiryu stone . This specific variety features a deep, moody tone accented by striking white veins that provide a visually stunning contrast, especially when paired with vibrant green or red aquatic plants. Its signature craggy texture and intricate details allow any hobbyist to easily create a natural-looking, mountainous hardscape or Iwagumi layout . Blue Mountain Seiryu is also suitable for non-aquarium use and will work beautifully as a sophisticated accent in terrariums, paludariums, or similar planted enclosures. Stones vary in shape, size, and density. Pieces from packages will range from 3-10 inches. Notes: Seiryu may slightly raise pH and water hardness. Controsoil can help balance that out. If you are looking for larger stones, a minimum weight may be required. Larger stones = higher weight. Email our team if you need assistance. We recommend rinsing stones thoroughly before use to remove any natural dust or sediment. Stone coloration darkens when wet.

Mountain Stone is a relatively new addition to the world of aquarium hardscaping, offering a unique blend of characteristics from some of the most popular stones in the hobby. Light in coloration, this natural stone is comparable to Dragon Stone in its warm, earthy tones, yet it is exceptionally lightweight, similar to Lava Rock. Its craggy shapes and almost sand-like textures are a perfect pick for creating dramatic cliffs and high-altitude mountainous scenes. We recommend pairing this natural rock with deep green mosses and vibrant red aquatic plants to create a high-contrast look that truly pops. Mountain Stone is also suitable for non-aquarium use and will work beautifully as a weathered accent in terrariums, paludariums, or similar bioactive enclosures. Stones vary in shape, size, and density. Notes: If you are looking for larger stones, a minimum weight may be required. Larger stones = higher weight. Email our team if you need assistance. Stone coloration darkens when wet.

Gobi Desert Stone is a beautiful natural stone with a light greyish-cream hue. Even though it draws similarities to Sand Stone in its coloration and distinct layering, it offers a much smoother texture with patterns that resemble delicate folds or ancient sediment layers. This makes it an excellent choice for creating canyon-style aquascaping layouts, while its light palette ensures the colors of aquarium plants and freshwater fish or shrimp truly pop. Gobi Desert Stone is also suitable for non-aquarium use and will work beautifully in terrariums, paludariums, or similar planted enclosures for a clean, windswept hardscape look. Stones vary in shape, size, and density. Notes: If you are looking for larger stones, a minimum weight may be required. Larger stones = higher weight. Email our team if you need assistance. Stone coloration darkens when wet.

Wolf Stone is a distinctive newer addition to the hobby, characterized by a medium-gray color and an incredibly rough texture. This natural rock is covered in sharp crevices and bumps across its entire surface, making it difficult to find a smooth edge. These features make it a premier choice for "wild" or aggressively styled hardscape layouts, similar in appearance to Seiryu Stone but with its own unique flair. Because of its texture, we do not recommend using it with fragile-finned fish like Bettas, but it looks spectacular when paired with a variety of aquarium plants. Wolf Stone is also suitable for non-aquarium use and will work beautifully in terrariums, paludariums, or similar planted enclosures for a dynamic and wild look. These durable aquarium glass scrapers are fully safe for both freshwater planted aquariums and saltwater reef setups. Designed for maximum versatility, the X-1 and X-3 models feature rotating, adjustable scraper heads and modular length configurations to navigate hard-to-reach corners and deep substrate margins. The compact Nano-Q model is streamlined for smaller displays and nano aquascapes. Key Features & Benefits Ultra-Strong Magnesium Alloy Construction: Crafted from high-strength, rust-resistant materials designed for freshwater and marine aquarium safety. Adjustable & Rotating Scraper Head (X-1 & X-3): Head swivels and locks at various angles to easily navigate around hardscape and tight glass corners. Dual-Function Substrate Flattener: Scraper head reverses to level cosmetic sand and aquasoil along the front glass for a crisp, professional finish. Modular Extension Rod System (X-3 Model): Includes 2 extension rod attachments, allowing 3 adjustable handle length configurations for deep aquariums. Plant Profile Common Name: Anubias Congensis, Anubias Afzelii Anubias Congensis is becoming a major favorite among planted tank enthusiasts looking to break away from standard round-leaved species. Hailing from the tropical streams, rivers, and marshes of West Africa, this bold variety stands out with its long, slender, and sharp lanceolate leaves. Its sleek, upward-reaching habit makes it an exceptional choice for adding architectural height and structural elegance to the midground or background of your aquascape. Adaptable and resilient, it thrives submerged in aquariums or emersed in humid terrariums and paludariums. By choosing the Tissue Culture version of this plant, you are guaranteed a 100% pest-free, algae-free, and pesticide-free start for your aquarium. These plants are grown in-vitro in a sterile laboratory setting, ensuring no unwanted snails or hitchhikers enter your system. While these plantlets start smaller and require more time to mature, they offer the cleanest and most reliable method for establishing a healthy colony in planted tanks. Key Features & Benefits Slender, sharp, lance-shaped foliage offers a dynamic linear contrast against rounder plants like Anubias Nana or Anubias Barteri. Its remarkably durable leaf structure easily withstands the activity of plant-eating fish and shrimp, ensuring your large focal point stays pristine. The sterile laboratory environment guarantees your new plant arrives completely free of pests. Care Tips & Preparation Carefully remove the plantlets from the cup and rinse away the sterile nutrient gel under lukewarm, dechlorinated water before mounting. For instructions on how to properly plant tissue culture aquarium plants, click here . Secure the plant directly to your chosen hardscape elements using aquarium-safe glue or thread. Avoid burying the horizontal stem in gravel or soil because restricting water flow around the rhizome will cause the plant to melt, rot, and die. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to ensure your new greenery acclimates smoothly without shedding leaves. Position the plant away from intense, direct light and ensure healthy water flow to prevent slow-growing leaves from collecting unwanted spot algae. Provide low to moderate lighting and optional carbon dioxide injection to achieve faster growth and more robust leaves, though it will happily thrive without high-tech setups. Master the prep and planting process by checking out a beginner's guide to tissue culture plants to prevent your delicate new plantlets from melting or floating away. Plant Profile If your background layout needs a sense of tranquil flow and dramatic texture, Cryptocoryne balansae creates a stunning canopy that commands attention. Hailing from the fast-flowing, limestone-rich rivers of Southern Thailand, this impressive species has long been a favorite for its towering height and distinctive, heavily puckered (bullated) leaf texture. Its long, ribbon-like leaves stream elegantly in the water current, creating a dynamic backdrop that contrasts beautifully against rigid hardscape materials. As with all crypt plants, this species can be sensitive to changes in water parameters and strongly objects to being relocated once planted. Give it a permanent home at the rear of your tank, however, and its extensive root system will lock in to support healthy, long-lasting foliage that fish love to explore. Key Features & Benefits Tall, bullate ribbon-like foliage delivers dynamic movement and a commanding texture to your background layout. Can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups where it can potentially produce unique flowering spathes. Native riverine history makes it unusually tolerant of hard water, providing hideouts for larger community fish. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel. Provide a calcium supplement to prevent new foliage from growing twisted or deformed because this species originates from high-limestone environments. Provide moderate to high lighting to achieve the attractive puckering effect on the leaves and bring out potential bronze tints. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Cryptocoryne species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Cryptocoryne crispatula var. balansae Common Name(s) Balansae plant, Crypt Balansae Family Araceae Plant Type Rosette / Root Feeder Height 24–36"+ (60–90+ cm) Care Difficulty Medium Light Requirement Moderate to High (Required for ruffling/bronze color) CO2 Requirement Highly Recommended Placement / Usage Background Focal Point Growth Rate Medium Water Parameters pH 6.5–7.5 | Temperature 72°F–82°F (22°C–28°C) Key Nutrients Nitrate, Phosphate, Iron, and highly dependent on Calcium Propagation Method Runner Offshoots / Side Shoots Origin Southern Thailand (Southeast Asia) Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I help my Cryptocoryne Balansae recover if it melts? Crypt melt is a standard reaction when shifting water conditions cause old leaves to dissolve so the plant can rebuild foliage adapted to your aquarium. Trim away rotting tissue, keep your water parameters stable, and do not disturb the subterranean root system. For complete recovery steps, check out our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt . 2. Why are the new leaves on my Crypt Balansae twisting or deformed? Because this species originates from fast-flowing river habitats rich in limestone, it has adapted to require significantly high levels of dissolved calcium. A lack of calcium will directly cause the new leaves to grow twisted, stunted, or severely deformed. It is highly recommended to supplement calcium directly, especially in softer water aquariums, to support healthy structural growth. 3. Should I use root tabs or liquid fertilizers for Cryptocoryne Balansae? Root tabs are far more effective than liquid fertilizers for Cryptocoryne species because they draw the overwhelming majority of their nutrition through their roots. While liquid nutrients benefit water column feeders like mosses or stem plants, placing nutrient-rich root tabs inside sand or gravel substrates directly fuels your Crypt's foliage growth.

Plant Profile Helanthium tenellum, commonly called the Dwarf Chain Sword or Pygmy Chain Sword, is a classic grass-like carpeting plant native to the Americas. Maxing out around 3 inches tall, it features thin, needle-like leaves that look like a mix between Dwarf Hairgrass and Micro Sword. It spreads by sending out lateral runners across the substrate, gradually filling in foreground gaps to form a lush, natural-looking green lawn. Under higher lighting conditions, the tips of its narrow blades often take on a reddish-pink to bronze tint. Easy to manage and quick to establish, it provides a great carpeting option for aquascapers who want grass-like texture without the delicate maintenance requirements of finer carpeting species. Key Features & Notes Narrow, needle-like green blades spread via lateral runner chains to create a grassy carpet. Under higher light intensity, foliage often displays attractive reddish-pink or bronze tips. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Divide the potted portion into small plugs and plant them deep into your aquarium soil using fine-tipped tweezers. All Helanthium species are heavy root feeders that rely on nutrient-rich substrate; placing root tabs near the base supports steady growth and dense spreading. Supplemental CO2 injection accelerates runner production and encourages denser lawn coverage, though the plant will still grow steadily in low-tech setups. Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf shedding during the initial transition period. Trim spreading runner shoots with sharp aquascaping scissors to control its footprint or replant plantlets elsewhere. Final size and growth density depend on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that individual plants may vary based on tank conditions. How does Helanthium tenellum spread across the substrate? It spreads by sending out subterranean runner chains in all directions across the substrate. Each runner produces new baby rosettes every few inches, which eventually form an interconnected, grass-like lawn. 2. What causes the leaf tips of Dwarf Chain Sword to turn reddish or bronze? When grown under high-intensity aquarium lighting with adequate micronutrients and CO2, Helanthium tenellum naturally develops a pinkish-red or bronze color at the tips of its thin leaf blades. 3. Can Helanthium tenellum be grown in low-tech tanks without CO2? Yes, it can grow in low-tech setups without pressurized CO2 injection. While its growth and spreading speed will be slower and the leaves will remain solid green, placing root tabs in a nutrient-rich substrate will keep it healthy.

Plant Profile Common Name: Bucephalandra Brownie Phoenix Brown Buce ‘Brownie Phoenix Brown’ is a beautiful aquarium plant featuring small to medium elliptic leaves with deep green color tones. This variety is distinguished by foliage that is slightly darker than its similar counterpart Brownie Phoenix , providing a sophisticated moody look for detailed layouts. Highly versatile, it can be grown submerged or emersed, usually attached to hardscape such as driftwood or rocks rather than being buried in traditional aquarium substrate. It is an exquisite choice for the foreground or midground of freshwater aquascapes, where its slow-growing rhizomes will gradually sprout new leaves to form a dense, colorful colony within a planted tank. Key Features & Notes True to its name, this variant offers a richer, darker brown and green profile compared to standard varieties, making it perfect for high-contrast scapes. The petite leaf size and predictable growth pattern make it an ideal "filler" plant for the tight crevices between rocks and wood. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for aquascapes where other plants might struggle. It is perfectly at home fully submerged in an aquarium or emersed in high-humidity terrariums, vivariums, and paludariums. Care Tips & Preparation Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood . Never bury the rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Carefully remove the plant from its pot and clear away all rockwool from the roots. For a deep dive on prepping potted plants, click here . Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting. Unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance, CO2 injection will yield much faster growth. We recommend researching your specific water chemistry to ensure your plant thrives. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions. Please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Plant Profile Ludwigia Sphaerocarpa, often referred to as the Spherical Ludwigia, is an aquatic stem plant native to the damp coastal wetlands stretching from Massachusetts down to Eastern Texas. Breaking the mold of typical fast-growing, vertical stem plants, this species grows in a distinctive low, horizontal habit that produces spherical rosettes reminiscent of miniature crowns. It displays a warm color palette ranging from golden-amber to rich orange and deep sunset-red, and its compact growth structure makes it a great pick for foreground-to-midground accents in Dutch-style aquascapes or nature aquariums, where its vibrant round tops provide texture and high-contrast color against carpeting plants. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Unique low-growing horizontal habit forms dense, rosette-like spherical crowns in foreground and midground zones. Leaf coloration ranges from golden-yellow and bright orange to intense sunset-red under strong lighting. A rare North American stem species that provides bold geometric contrast against traditional fine-leaved foliage. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil . Provide medium-to-high lighting and avoid placing this species in shaded areas; strong light penetration is essential for maintaining compact, horizontal growth and vibrant orange-red coloration. Supply pressurized CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilization rich in iron to promote dense crown formation and prevent lower leaf shedding. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable, soft acidic water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or leaf shedding. To propagate, trim main stem tops with sharp straight shears and replant trimmings directly into your aquarium soil. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. How do I prep bunched Ludwigia Sphaerocarpa before planting? Remove the lead weight or rubber band along with the cotton or foam surrounding the lower roots under room-temperature water. Gently inspect the stem bases, trim away any damaged tissue, and use pinsettes to plant individual stems directly into your aquarium soil. 2. Why is my Ludwigia Sphaerocarpa turning dull green and growing leggy? Dull green coloration and tall, stretched stems usually indicate insufficient lighting or shading from larger neighboring plants. Plant Profile Nesaea Crassicaulis is a rare and rewarding aquatic stem plant native to tropical Africa and Madagascar, prized by experienced aquascapers for its bold, reddish-brown to burnt-orange, narrow leaves. When provided with high-tech aquarium conditions, it'll reward you with thick stems and vibrant foliage that creates a striking contrast against green and red aquatic plants alike. Reaching 6–12 inches in height, Nesaea Crassicaulis makes an extraordinary background focal point, bringing a rich, earthy color palette that's hard to find elsewhere. It's a must-have for hobbyists building high-contrast, color-rich planted tanks. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Bold reddish-brown and copper-orange narrow foliage provides a rare color contrast with traditional green and red stem plants. Densely leafed background species that easily branches into thick, colorful bushes through routine pruning and replanting. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip the lower inch of foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push stems 1–2 inches into soil, spacing them apart for light penetration. Provide high-intensity lighting and pressurized CO2 injection; maintaining soft, slightly acidic water with regular iron dosing accelerates growth and yields maximum reddish-brown coloration. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the desired height to encourage dense side branching, and replant trimmings directly into soil to propagate. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when light cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I get my Nesaea Crassicaulis to turn deep reddish-brown? Achieving the rich, deep reddish-brown hues requires strong LED lighting, pressurized CO2 injection, soft water conditions, and consistent micronutrient dosing with liquid iron. Soil-based substrates that lower pH also help optimize nutrient uptake. 3. How do I transition Nesaea Crassicaulis from emersed to submerged growth? When transitioning from emersed to submerged growth, plant bare stems securely into rich substrate under high lighting and keep water parameters stable. As new growth adapts, the plant will shed its firmer land leaves and sprout delicate, reddish-brown submerged foliage. Once new shoots develop, trim away old lower growth to encourage dense branching.

Plant Profile Alternanthera Bettzickiana Green is a vibrant, versatile semi-aquatic plant with lush green foliage popularly featured in terrariums, paludariums, vivariums, ponds, and bog gardens. While not a fully aquatic species for permanent, long-term submersion, it easily adapts as a temporary submerged display in freshwater aquariums, retaining its crisp green leaves for several months before benefiting from a recovery period in emersed growth. Above water, it thrives in high-humidity setups, forming bushy green foliage that brings a fresh, natural aesthetic to moisture-rich terrarium environments. *Semi-Aquatic Notice: For permanent, long-term health and growth, it is best grown emersed in paludariums, terrariums, bog gardens, or moist outdoor ponds. Key Features & Benefits Dense, bright green foliage provides a refreshing, lush aesthetic across terrariums, paludariums, and temporary submerged aquascapes. Highly versatile semi-aquatic species that excels in high-humidity bog environments, vivariums, and water margin planters. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip the lower inch of foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower leaves. Provide medium-to-high lighting for steady growth; keep soil consistently moist in terrestrial/emersed setups or maintain high humidity in closed enclosures. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid drastic environmental changes to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting during submerged periods. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once stems reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into moist soil to propagate new growth. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Can Alternanthera Bettzickiana Green live fully submerged in an aquarium permanently? No. Alternanthera Bettzickiana Green is a true semi-aquatic plant. While it will maintain its lush green appearance underwater for several months as a temporary display, it eventually needs to be moved above water (emersed in a paludarium or terrarium) to recover and grow long-term. 2. How do I care for Alternanthera Bettzickiana Green in a paludarium or terrarium? In emersed setups, keep the substrate consistently moist or water-saturated under medium-to-high lighting. Maintaining ambient humidity above 60% ensures fast, bushy foliage growth. 3. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the base of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from upper leaves. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during planting and ensuring adequate light coverage will keep lower leaves healthy.

Its unique cracks and craggy surfaces provide an ideal surface for attaching mosses or using greening techniques to add maturity to your hardscape. While prized for aquascaping, Manten Stone is also suitable for non-aquarium use and will work beautifully as a high-end accent in terrariums, paludariums, or similar planted enclosures for an authentic, weathered look. Stones vary in shape, size, and density. If you are looking for specific pieces, please increase the amount ordered. Average size ranges from 2-10 inches. Notes: We recommend rinsing stones thoroughly before use to remove any natural dust or sediment. Stone coloration darkens when wet. Great for mountainous aquascapes or Iwagumi layouts!

Spiderwood is known for its wild, multi‑branching shape that instantly adds depth and personality to any aquascape. This Nano version is specifically selected for those twisting tangles and sculptural turns that fit perfectly into smaller tanks. Whether you stand it upright, lay it on its side, or angle it, each orientation creates a fresh visual story. It’s no surprise that Spiderwood has become one of our favorite aquarium driftwood choices here at Buce Plant HQ. Product Features & Benefits The complex network of branches adds immediate depth and energy to your aquarium hardscape without overwhelming the tank. Sized specifically for nano-setups, these pieces allow you to easily maneuver pieces around. The spindly limbs are ideal for anchoring Mosses, Bucephalandra, or Anubias Nana Petite. Wrapping these branches in green creates a stunning, aged "root" look. The numerous nooks and crannies provide essential hiding spots and foraging surfaces for shrimp and fry, encouraging natural behavior. Size Specifications Photos are a representation of the unique, natural character of each piece. Size Range: 5–15 inches Preparation & Care Driftwood is a natural product and requires a bit of prep before it’s ready for prime time. Rinse: Thoroughly rinse the piece to remove any dust or debris from transit. The Floating Phase: It will float initially. We recommend soaking it thoroughly or boiling it. A large stone or heavy decor may be placed on top to ensure a non-waterlogged piece of wood stays submerged. The "White Fuzz" Phase: It is common for a harmless white biofilm to appear on Spiderwood shortly after it's submerged. Don't panic! Your shrimp and snails will think it’s a five-star buffet. It will eventually disappear on its own. Tannin Management: Spiderwood releases fewer tannins than other varieties, but a quick 1-hour boil will still help it sink faster and keep your water crystal clear. Important note: We recommend rinsing wood thoroughly before adding it to an established aquarium. If you prefer, you may also boil the wood for at least 1-2 hours to help release tannins.

Plant Profile If standard Java Ferns feel a bit too vanilla for your low-light aquascape, African Water Fern (Bolbitis heudelotii) is here to fix that. Hailing from the fast-flowing, dramatic rivers of West Africa, this epiphyte rocks semi-translucent, deeply lobed emerald fronds that look less like a standard aquarium plant and more like delicate aquatic stained glass. Reaching a graceful 4 to 8 inches in height, its airy, lacy foliage provides top-tier visual contrast against dark, moody driftwood or rugged stone setups. Key Features & Notes Tough, fibrous foliage easily withstands curious nipping from herbivorous fish like cichlids, goldfish, and large snails. Translucent, lacy emerald fronds bring an elegant, three-dimensional texture to midground and background hardscape arrangements. This plant can be grown emersed or submerged. Exceptional hardiness lets it thrive in non-CO2 tanks and low-light environments. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . African Water Fern is an epiphytic fern that should be attached to rocks or driftwood with aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as it will rot and melt. Position this plant in areas with moderate to high water circulation, as Bolbitis is a rheophytic species that thrives when water currents pass through its fronds. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard setups, gentle water movement and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and broader fronds. Master long-term care and troubleshoot common leaf issues by checking out our Java Fern Care Guide . Final size and foliage pattern depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Bolbitis heudelotii Common Name(s) African Water Fern, Bolbitis Fern Family Dryopteridaceae Plant Type Epiphyte (Rhizome Fern) Care Difficulty Beginner / Easy (Low-Tech Compatible) Light Requirement Low to Medium CO2 Requirement Not Required (Beneficial) Placement / Usage Midground, Background, High-Flow Hardscape Accent Height / Size 4"–8" (10–20 cm) Growth Rate Slow Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 | Temperature 68°F–82°F (20°C–28°C) Propagation Method Rhizome Division Origin West Africa Frequently Asked Questions 1. What makes African Water Fern (Bolbitis heudelotii) different from Java Fern? While both are hardy epiphytes attached to hardscape, African Water Fern belongs to the Dryopteridaceae family and features semi-translucent, deeply lobed pinnate leaves that look like forest ferns. Standard Java Ferns belong to Polypodiaceae and typically produce solid, smooth, or ruffled undivided blades. 2. Why does Bolbitis heudelotii prefer higher water flow in the aquarium? In nature, African Water Fern grows attached to submerged boulders in fast-moving African tropical rivers and waterfalls. Higher water movement delivers constant dissolved oxygen and nutrients to its foliage while preventing algae or particulate matter from settling on its delicate fronds. 3. Can I plant African Water Fern into substrate? No. Bolbitis heudelotii is a strict epiphyte that absorbs nutrients directly from the water column through its foliage and fine root network. If you bury its horizontal rhizome beneath aquarium soil, sand, or gravel, the stem will suffocate, rot, and die. Always attach it to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread.

Plant Profile This Christmas Moss Wreath is ready to deck your aquascape out in style! We have meticulously wrapped classic, tree-like Christmas Moss around a floating ring, complete with a hidden aquarium-safe weight and clear tether line that keeps it standing upright in mid-water. Because aquarium moss is famously beginner-friendly and thrives on minimal attention, you do not need to be a seasoned expert to keep this festive piece looking lush all year round. Key Features & Benefits Adds bold 3D structure and playful swim-through channels without requiring complex hardscape stacking or heavy stones. Provides safe hiding, shelter, and grazing areas for freshwater shrimp and nano fish. Care & Planting Instructions Drop the weighted anchor onto your substrate to let the wreath float upright, adjusting the clear line length to set your perfect viewing height. Maintain a stable aquarium environment and avoid sudden, drastic changes to your water parameters to keep your moss looking vibrant and healthy. Give the moss a light haircut with sharp aquascaping shears occasionally to keep the circle looking clean, uniform, and perfectly manicured. Propagate your patch in seconds by saving the snipped moss pieces and tying or gluing them to hardscape elsewhere in your tank. Add CO2 injection if you want to accelerate growth and unlock the most intense, eye-popping green coloration possible. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I keep my Christmas Moss Wreath from turning brown or yellow? Christmas Moss prefers clean, moving water and cooler temperatures (under 78°F). Browning usually occurs when organic debris gets trapped inside the dense fronds or when water temperatures run too high. Gently siphoning debris out during water changes will keep the inner growth green and healthy. 2. What is the best way to anchor the wreath in my aquarium? The wreath comes complete with a clear tether line and an aquarium-safe weight. Simply drop the weighted anchor onto your substrate (or bury it under your gravel), adjusting the tether line to let the wreath float upright at your preferred water height. 3. How do I stop moss trimmings from spreading everywhere during maintenance? Always turn off your filter pumps and powerheads before trimming moss. Use sharp curved shears to make clean cuts, and immediately scoop or siphon out floating cuttings so they don't take root in unwanted areas of your aquarium.

Cholla Wood is what happens when a prickly desert cactus retires. Derived from the dried husk of the Cholla Cactus, this hollow, porous aquarium wood is a functional powerhouse. Designed specifically as a functional hardscape piece for planted aquariums and shrimp setups, its iconic honeycomb structure serves as a natural factory for biofilm and a safe nursery for small aquatic life. Product Features & Benefits Cholla is famous for stimulating the growth of biofilm, a natural, nutrient-rich film that serves as the primary food source for shrimp. The hollow center and perforated walls create the perfect "safe house" for molting shrimp and small fish to hide from larger tank mates. Its unique texture makes it incredibly easy to attach mosses, Anubias, or Bucephalandra. Over time, it can be transformed into a lush, living sunken log that anchors your planted aquarium hardscape. Cholla releases beneficial tannins that slightly lower pH levels, mimicking the natural blackwater environments in which many tropical species thrive. Preparation & Care Rinse: Thoroughly rinse the piece to remove any dust or debris from transit. The Sinking Process: Dry Cholla is very lightweight and will float initially. To get it to stay put, we recommend soaking it in a bucket for 24–48 hours or boiling it for 20 minutes to help it become waterlogged. Safety Disclaimer This tunnel is best suited for freshwater shrimp or small fry. If you have larger, curious fish or other fauna (such as a betta fish) that may try to explore such small crevices, there is a risk they may get caught or stuck in the tunnel. Please be mindful of this before placing it in your aquarium.

Plant Profile If you’ve ever worried about your ability to keep a live plant alive, rest easy. Najas Indica, affectionately known as Guppy Grass, is nearly indestructible! Whether you let it float lazily along the water surface or anchor it into your substrate like a traditional stem plant, Guppy Grass explodes into a lush, jungle-like sanctuary within weeks. Beyond looking vibrant and cheerful, it acts as a total powerhouse in your aquarium ecosystem by sucking up nitrates, outcompeting stubborn algae, and creating an absolute paradise for timid shrimp and baby fish fry. Key Features & Benefits Dense plant cover creates a tangled matrix that gives fish fry, shrimplets, and shy livestock safe places to hide and forage. Nitrate-absorbing growth removes excess waste from the water column, helping to suppress algae and maintain clarity. Flexible use thrives as a rooted background stem plant or a low‑maintenance floating cover, no CO₂ required. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and the cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base. Gently separate the brittle stems before planting or tossing them into your tank to float. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push stems 1 to 2 inches into soil if you prefer a rooted look, or simply let the plant float freely to form a lush canopy. Provide low-to-medium lighting for steady growth, as this ultra-adaptable species thrives easily without needing pressurized CO2 injection. Maintain stable water parameters, though Guppy Grass easily tolerates a wide range of temperatures, light levels, and water chemistry. Trim overgrown stems with straight scissors whenever the mass gets too thick, or snap stems by hand and toss the cuttings into another tank to multiply your stock. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining adequate light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. Is Guppy Grass better floating or rooted in the substrate? Guppy Grass excels at both! Floating stems absorb nutrients directly from the water column while giving newborn fry and shrimp a surface nursery. Rooting stems in soil creates a dense, bushy background wall that adds classic natural depth to your aquascape. 3. My stem plants arrived with round green leaves, but the new growth looks totally different. Is this normal? Yes! Many aquatic stem plants are cultivated emersed (above water) at plant nurseries, producing rounder, thicker green leaves. Once submerged in your aquarium, the plant will transition into its true aquatic form, sprouting delicate, submerged foliage.

Hygrophila Siamensis Hygrophila Siamensis is a robust aquatic plant that is perfect for beginners trying to grow stem plants for the first time. It is popular and widely available due to its beauty and easy care. This plant can thrive in a wide variety of freshwater aquariums as long as its given some lighting. Like many other stem plants, this plant can grow both emersed and submerged. It is a fast grower and can require frequent trimming when kept under high light with Co2 and the addition of fertilizers. Like most stem plants, propagation can be done simply by cutting along the stem and replanting the cuttings. Family: Acanthaceae Region: Southeast Asia Height: 6-12" pH: 6-7.5 Care: Easy Light: Moderate to High Co2: Not required Propagation: Cut stem and replant Growth rate: Fast

listings.commonName: Java Fern Narrow on Coco Fiber Mat
listings.description: Plant Profile Java Fern Narrow on Coco Fiber Mat delivers a pre-bound 3" x 2" natural coconut fiber mat of sleek leaves about half an inch wide that create an instant, wild-jungle texture without the tedious labor of tying individual rhizomes. Virtually bulletproof and unbothered by parameter swings or curious herbivorous fish, it rests naturally over substrate or wedged between hardscape. It is hands-down one of the best aquarium plants for beginners seeking immediate density, refined leaf texture, and plug-and-play convenience for low-light layouts. Key Features & Notes Tough, fibrous foliage easily withstands curious nipping from herbivorous fish like cichlids, goldfish, and large snails. Pre-attached to a 3" x 2" natural coconut fiber mat, providing a flexible, ready-to-drop pad for effortless placement across substrate or hardscape. Exceptional hardiness lets it thrive in non-CO2 tanks and low-light environments. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by rinsing the coco fiber mat gently in clean freshwater to clear any loose debris before placing it directly into your aquarium. Java Fern Narrow on Coco Fiber Mat is an epiphytic fern pre-bound to hardscape that should be rested directly on top of substrate or hardscape ; never bury the horizontal rhizome beneath sand or soil, as it will rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard setups, gentle water movement and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and broader fronds. Master long-term care and troubleshoot common leaf issues by checking out our Java Fern Care Guide . Final size and foliage pattern depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual mat shapes or foliage densities may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Leptochilus pteropus ) Common Name(s) Java Fern Narrow on Coco Fiber Mat, Narrow Leaf Java Fern Mat Family Polypodiaceae Plant Type Epiphyte Pre-Attached to Natural Mat Care Difficulty Beginner / Easy (Low-Tech Compatible) Light Requirement Low to Medium CO2 Requirement Not Required (Beneficial) Placement / Usage Foreground, Midground, Background Accent Pad Height / Size Mat Dimensions: 3" x 2" | Foliage Height: 3"–8" (7.5–20 cm) Growth Rate Slow to Moderate Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 | Temperature 68°F–82°F (20°C–28°C) Propagation Method Rhizome Division & Adventitious Plantlets Origin Indonesia / Cultivated Variety Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are there small black spots and tiny leaves growing under my Java Fern Narrow leaves? Do not panic; your plant is not diseased! Java Fern reproduces naturally through adventitious plantlets. Small dark bumps (sporangia) form along the undersides of mature leaves, sprouting tiny brown roots and mini green fronds. Once these baby plantlets develop 3–4 leaves, you can gently pop them off the mother leaf and glue them elsewhere in your aquarium. 2. Can I cut the Java Fern Narrow coco fiber mat into smaller pieces? Yes! You can easily cut the 3" x 2" natural coconut fiber pad with sharp scissors to fit tight gaps in your aquascape. Cut sections can be wedged between rocks, attached to driftwood, or placed in different areas of your aquarium. 3. Can I bury the coco fiber mat into substrate? You can rest the mat flat on top of your substrate, but you must ensure the horizontal green rhizomes remain uncovered and exposed to the water column. Burying the mat beneath soil or sand will suffocate the rhizome and lead to rot. 4. Will fish like cichlids or goldfish eat Java Fern Narrow on Coco Fiber Mat? Generally, no. Java Fern leaves are thick, fibrous, and contain bitter-tasting compounds that deter most plant-eating fish. Because the plant is already bound firmly to a weighted mat pad, it is also much harder for energetic fish to uproot.

Common Name: Red Flame Sword Red Flame Sword is a great plant for a quick and easy way to add some color to your aquarium. This plant is easy to keep like other Echinodorus and the leaves will exhibit a bright to blood red coloration. Like most swords, they should be planted directly into the substrate. When using inert substrates such as sand or gravel, it is important to supplement the plants with root tabs as Echinodorus are heavy root feeders. It can be grown both emersed and submerged and often times, new leaves can grow to the top above the water line. Overall, this plant is easy and undemanding and very suitable for larger tanks. Notes: Echinodorus is a very hardy species of aquatic plants. Most Echinodorus require nutrient-dense soil to thrive as they are heavy root feeders. Echinodorus grow fairly large and are more suitable for larger planted aquariums. Do not make drastic changes to the aquarium. Unstable parameters will result in melt and rotting of the aquarium plant. Please be sure to remove this plant from its pot. Remove the cotton surrounding the roots and plant into a quality substrate. For instructions on how to properly prep "potted" aquarium plants, click here . CO2 injection and quality aquarium soil will yield better growth. Please research appropriately to ensure your plant thrives. Family Name: Alismataceae Origin: South Africa Height: 8-12” pH: 6-7.5 Care: Easy Light: Low Co2: Not Required Propagation: Separate new plantlets from the root Growth rate: Slow to Moderate

Plant Profile Big, textured, and refreshingly low-effort, Cryptocoryne usteriana checks every box for a commanding background centerpiece. Native to the limestone-rich riverbeds of the Philippines, this impressive species has long been a prized rarity in the hobby, known for its long, deeply puckered (bullated) foliage that displays a rich green topside and a striking reddish-purple underside. As with all crypt plants, this species can be sensitive to changes in water parameters and strongly objects to being relocated once planted. Once established, however, it anchors the back of your layout with tall, flowing leaves that contrast beautifully against darker hardscape. Key Features & Benefits Large, deeply wrinkled leaves with reddish-purple undersides deliver a bold, tactile background texture. Can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups where it will produce unique flowering spathes. Thrives well in medium to hard water environments once its root system establishes. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Crypt species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Why are my Cryptocoryne Usteriana Green leaves melting away? Transplanting Crypts into new water parameters often triggers a temporary reaction where old leaves dissolve. As long as the root system remains undisturbed in healthy soil, fresh foliage will sprout shortly. Check out our guide on Cryptocoryne melt for step-by-step recovery tips. 2. Can I move my Cryptocoryne to a new spot in the tank later? It is best to leave your Crypt permanently in its original spot. Uprooting an established plant damages its fine root hairs and almost always causes another cycle of leaf melt. 3. Should I use root tabs or liquid fertilizers? Root tabs are best. Cryptocoryne species are heavy root feeders that draw primary nutrition from the substrate rather than the water column.

Plant Profile Egeria Densa, commonly known as Anacharis, is one of the easiest, fast-growing green stem plants available, making it an exceptional choice for beginners and low-tech aquariums. Featuring dense whorls of vibrant green leaves along flexible upright stems, it closely resembles classic waterweed ( Elodea canadensis ) but boasts a noticeably bushier and fuller foliage profile. This resilient species adapts effortlessly to a wide range of water parameters and can either be anchored into substrate or left free-floating to absorb nitrates and suppress unwanted algae growth. *Shipping Restriction Notice: To comply with regional conservation laws, we are unable to sell or ship this plant to the following states: IL, WA, IN, MI, MN, NY, OH, PA, and WI. Key Features & Benefits Hardy green stem plant that tolerates varied water conditions and works well for beginners. Dense foliage absorbs excess nutrients, helping maintain clarity and reduce algae. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip the lower inch of foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower growth. Provide low-to-medium lighting for healthy growth, as pressurized CO2 injection is not required for this adaptable species. Maintain stable water parameters and cooler water temperatures when possible, though the plant adapts well to tropical aquarium temperatures. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the water surface to promote new lateral side branches. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Floating stems provide excellent cover and shade for shy fish, fry, and shrimp. 3. My stem plants arrived with round green leaves, but the new growth looks totally different. Is this normal? Yes! Once submerged in your aquarium, the plant will transition into its true aquatic form, sprouting delicate, submerged foliage.

If you are suffering from some serious decision paralysis because you love moss-t of the varieties out there, we've got you covered. Choosing the perfect green companion for your tank can be tough, so we put together this collector's pack to take the guesswork out of the equation! This bundle is a great educational crash course in aquatic botany, allowing you to see firsthand how different species develop. Some will grow in fluffy, horizontal fans, while others will reach straight for the light like flickering green flames. No matter which varieties land on your doorstep, they all serve as fantastic, highly textured play areas where dwarf shrimp and baby fish fry can safely forage and hang out. Please note: Your five unique varieties will be hand-selected by our team based on our freshest current inventory. We are unable to take requests for specific species, but we promise a beautiful mix! Choose Your Pack Style The Golfball Pack: You will receive one loose, golfball-sized portion of five different moss species. This option is great if you love the hands-on fun of wrapping, gluing, or tying moss onto your own custom driftwood and rocks. The Stainless Steel Pack: You will receive five different moss species pre-attached to their own individual 3" x 3" stainless steel mesh pads. This option is perfect if you want a plug-and-play setup to create an instant carpet on your tank floor. With any Aquarium Moss Collector Pack, you will receive at least 5 different types of moss . Examples of what you may receive are: Christmas Moss Grows in dense, overlapping, triangular fronds that look like miniature pine branches. Java Moss The ultimate hardy classic; grows in a wild, fast-spreading, and highly versatile fashion. Flame Moss Grows distinctively upright in spiraling, vertical shoots that mimic flickering green flames. Peacock Moss Features soft, velvety, fan-shaped fronds that spread out like a peacock's tail. Spiky Moss Grows long, pointed, needle-like fronds for a sharp and deeply textured look. Weeping Moss Naturally droops downward, making it look beautiful draped over elevated driftwood. Fissidens Fontanus (Phoenix Moss) Has incredibly delicate, deep green fronds that resemble soft baby bird feathers. Care & Planting Instructions Place your stainless steel pads directly on the substrate, or use thread or aquarium-safe glue to secure your loose golfball portions to wood, rocks, or filter pipes. Keep your water parameters stable. While mosses are incredibly hardy, sudden and drastic changes to your tank chemistry can cause them to melt. Give the mosses a light trim with sharp aquascaping shears whenever they start looking a bit wild. Trimming actually encourages them to grow back even thicker! Keep your water cool and clean. While these mosses do great in low-tech setups, adding a little CO2 and quality liquid fertilizer will make their colors pop and speed up their growth.

Plant Profile Elatine hydropiper is one of those rare, highly coveted foreground plants that feels like a tiny treasure when you finally get your hands on it. Native to Europe and East Asia, this newer addition to the hobby gets its quirky common name from its distinctive eight stamens. Visually, it looks like a miniature version of Glossostigma Elatinoides , but its leaves stay significantly smaller and naturally hug much closer to the substrate. With its bright, uniform green and micro‑sized profile, it’s perfect for creating a soft, airy carpet for a meadow-inspired look. When kept under optimal conditions, it can even surprise you by producing small, delicate flowers! Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Enjoy an incredibly compact carpet with leaves that stay smaller and tighter to the soil than traditional Glosso. Creates a lush, bright green, and seamless foreground texture that gives nano scapes an airy, natural depth. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions and planting. Divide the tissue culture mat into small portions and plant them spaced an inch apart across the substrate using fine-tip tweezers. Use a dry start method or Wabi Kusa setup to give its tiny root system plenty of time to firmly anchor into the substrate before you flood the tank. Maintain stable aquarium parameters, avoiding any sudden, drastic shifts in water quality to prevent delicate plantlets from melting. Provide high lighting and pressurized CO2 to force compact horizontal growth (vertical stretching indicates inadequate light). Trim established runners regularly to prevent upper layers from shading the lower root network and causing the lawn to dislodge. Master the basics by learning how to properly grow aquarium carpet plants to ensure your new layout fills in quickly, evenly, and stays free of algae. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I plant Elatine Hydropiper tissue culture? Wash away the sterile gel completely under cool water, separate the mat into small coin-sized plugs, and use fine pinsettes to bury each clump deep into fine-grained aquasoil at a 45-degree angle. 2. How is Elatine Hydropiper different from Glossostigma Elatinoides? While both species form creeping foreground lawns with paired leaves, Elatine Hydropiper has significantly smaller leaves, stay lower to the substrate, and grow at a somewhat slower, more controllable pace than Glosso. 3. Why is my newly planted Elatine Hydropiper floating up or growing vertically? Because Elatine Hydropiper has tiny root stems, strong currents or livestock can dislodge unanchored plugs. Vertical stretching means light levels are too low. Increasing light output and starting the carpet via the Dry Start Method will lock roots firmly in place while keeping foliage low.

Plant Profile If you have ever looked at a plant and thought, "Did someone reach into the tank and physically crumple those leaves?" (yeah, we're wincing too), then meet Aponogeton boivinianus. Hailing from the swift, crystal-clear rivers of Madagascar, this bulb species has a hammered, deeply puckered, ruffled texture. New leaves unfurl in translucent shades of pale reddish-green before maturing into thick, leathery, dark olive-green blades that stretch anywhere from 10 to over 20 inches long. Think of it as the opaque, heavily textured cousin of the famous Madagascar Lace plant: instead of open lattice windows, you get a dense, bubbly, wavy curtain of foliage that catches filter flow like a sail. It demands a bit of breathing room and a decent current, making it an absolute showstopper for the background of medium to large aquariums. Key Features & Notes Intensely puckered, "crumpled foil" leaf texture brings dynamic depth and unmatched visual interest. Color shifts naturally from translucent reddish-green on young growth to deep, glossy olive-green on mature foliage. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by inspecting the bulb and clearing any loose, dead organic material around the base. Plant the bulb so that it rests only half-buried in your aquarium substrate; completely burying the bulb traps moisture around the crown and promotes rot. Provide a nutrient-rich aquarium soil or tuck root tabs nearby to support its hungry root system and rapid leaf production. Place in an area with good water flow to replicate its natural river habitat and keep the heavily textured leaves free of settling detritus. Trim yellowing or damaged outer leaves near the base using sharp aquascaping scissors to keep the rosette looking neat. Like many Aponogeton species, it may periodically undergo a rest phase; if it drops leaves, keep parameters stable and allow the bulb time to sprout fresh growth. Final size and leaf texture depend on your specific tank conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Aponogeton boivinianus Common Name(s) Aponogeton Boivinianus, Heavily Ruffled Aponogeton Family Aponogetonaceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Bulb plant Care Difficulty Easy to Moderate Light Requirement Moderate CO2 Requirement Not required (Optional) Placement / Usage Background / Centerpiece Accent Height / Size 10–20+ inches Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 Propagation Method Bulb division or seed reproduction from flowers Origin Madagascar (Africa) Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I bury the Aponogeton boivinianus bulb correctly without causing it to rot? Press the bulb into your substrate until it is only halfway submerged, keeping the top half exposed to open water. This lets the roots dig down for nutrients while keeping the growth crown ventilated and rot-free. 2. Why does Aponogeton boivinianus need water movement in the aquarium? In nature, this species grows in fast-flowing rivers. In an aquarium, water movement prevents organic debris and algae from settling inside the deep, crinkled folds of its textured leaves. 3. How does Aponogeton boivinianus differ visually from the Madagascar Lace plant? While Madagascar Lace features open, see-through lattice windows, Aponogeton boivinianus produces completely solid, opaque leaves with a heavy, bubble-like texture that looks like crumpled metallic foil.

Plant Profile Few aquatic plants command attention quite like Aponogeton madagascariensis , aka the Madagascar Lace plant. Indigenous to the clear, fast-flowing waters of Madagascar, this species produces breathtaking foliage with a skeletonized leaf structure that resembles delicate webbed lace or a high-end underwater fly swatter. Achieving its full potential requires extra attention: moderate-to-high lighting, clean water, steady water movement, and a nutrient-rich substrate are key to keeping its intricate gridwork free of algae or organic debris. When provided with optimal conditions, this species grows vigorously and will frequently reward aquascapers with dramatic, dual-spiked flowers that rise above the surface. Key Features & Notes Intricate, fully skeletonized "lace" leaf blades offer a showstopping visual sight. Produces large, arching foliage ideal for medium-to-large background accent areas. Thrives in clean, well-oxygenated water with good current to keep leaf perforations free of debris. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by gently inspecting the bulb and removing any loose organic debris around the base. Plant the bulb so that it is only half-buried in your aquarium soil or substrate; completely burying the bulb can cause it to rot. Provide a nutrient-dense substrate or place root tabs nearby to fuel rapid leaf growth and encourage flowering. Position the plant in an area with good water flow to prevent floating detritus or algae from settling inside the open leaf grid. Trim off yellowing or damaged leaves near the base using sharp aquascaping scissors to prevent organic decay in the aquarium. Aponogeton bulbs may periodically enter a dormant rest phase where growth slows or stops; maintain stable parameters and allow the bulb time to sprout fresh leaves. Final size and leaf lattice density depend on your specific tank conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Spec Details Scientific Name Aponogeton madagascariensis Common Name(s) Madagascar Lace Plant, Lace Bulb Family Aponogetonaceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Bulb plant Care Difficulty Moderate to Advanced Light Requirement Moderate CO2 Requirement Recommended Placement / Usage Background / Centerpiece Accent Height / Size 8–20+ inches Growth Rate Medium Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 Propagation Method Bulb division or seed reproduction from flowers Origin Madagascar (Africa) Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I plant the Madagascar Lace bulb properly to prevent root or bulb rot? Press the bulb gently into your substrate until it is only halfway buried. Keeping the top half of the bulb exposed to the water column ensures that the shoot crown receives fresh water flow while allowing roots to extend downward into the soil. 2. Why is good water circulation so important for Aponogeton madagascariensis? Because the leaf blades consist of open, lattice-like perforations, slow-moving water allows organic waste, debris, and algae to settle inside the leaf grid. Gentle water flow keeps the delicate foliage clean and well-oxygenated. 3. What should I do if my Madagascar Lace plant loses its leaves and goes dormant? Bulb plants in the genus Aponogeton naturally experience periodic dormant cycles where old leaves drop off. Leave the bulb undisturbed in stable water conditions, and it will sprout a new flush of delicate lace foliage once its rest period ends.

Plant Profile Aponogeton longiplumulosus bridges the gap between two aquatic plant favorites, combining the rapid, hardy bulb growth of the Aponogeton family with the elegant, ruffled texture of Cryptocoryne 'Balansae'. Native to Madagascar's freshwater habitats, this striking bulb plant shoots up long, slender green leaves edged with dramatically crinkled, wavy margins that flow gracefully in filter currents. Reaching anywhere from 8 to 20+ inches tall, its narrow, ribbon-like foliage dances across the upper water column without completely blocking light to lower-growing species. It offers an easy, low-maintenance way to achieve that sought-after, textured Crypt Balansae look in a background plant that establishes quickly and thrives across a wide range of water parameters. Key Features & Notes Long, slender leaf blades feature deeply ruffled, crinkled edges reminiscent of Cryptocoryne Balansae. Fast-growing bulb species easily reaches 8 to 20+ inches to create a lush, flowing background canopy. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by gently inspecting the bulb and removing any loose organic media or debris around the roots. Plant the bulb so that it is only half-buried in your aquarium soil or substrate; completely burying the bulb traps moisture around the crown and promotes rot. Provide a nutrient-rich aquarium soil or place root tabs nearby to support steady leaf production and healthy root development. Position in an area with gentle water circulation to keep its long, wavy leaves clean and moving gracefully. Trim off older or decaying foliage near the base using sharp aquascaping scissors to encourage continuous new growth. Like other members of the Aponogeton genus, it may periodically enter a dormant rest phase where growth slows; maintain stable conditions and new shoots will emerge once rested. Final size and leaf length depend on your specific tank conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. It gives you the same textured, ribbon-like look in the background with the forgiving, adaptable nature typical of the Aponogeton family. 2. How should I plant the Aponogeton longiplumulosus bulb to avoid rot? Press the bulb gently into your aquarium substrate until it is only halfway submerged. Unlike the lattice-like Madagascar Lace ( A. madagascariensis ) or the heavily crumpled, broad-leaved A. boivinianus , A. longiplumulosus features much narrower, slender leaves with distinct ruffled edges, making it ideal for a softer, flowing background effect.

listings.description: Plant Profile Hydrocotyle Japan (Hydrocotyle Tripartita) brings a unique, whimsical texture to your tank with its distinct, clover-like leaves. Made famous by legendary aquascapers like Takashi Amano, this fast-growing favorite is incredibly versatile and can be used in the foreground, midground, or background depending on your vision. Left to its own devices, it will happily grow into wild, compact bushes of vibrant green. It is an exceptionally undemanding and energetic grower, meaning it will gladly take over the entire tank if you don't keep its enthusiastic growth in check! Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Clover-like green foliage that adds a playful, natural texture. Fill in your aquascape rapidly thanks to its fast growth rate, making it an excellent option for quickly blanketing bare spots. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Maintain high lighting and inject pressurized CO2 while frequently trimming new growth to force the plant to stay low and create a tight carpeting effect over your foreground. It grows quickly and requires regular pruning to prevent it from out-competing and overgrowing your other tank inhabitants. Propagate whenever you want by simply cutting the stems anywhere along the shoot and replanting them, or by pulling apart dense clumps and splitting the roots. Trim new shoots anywhere along the stem to encourage the plant to branch out even thicker and more compact. Master the basics by learning how to properly grow aquarium carpet plants to ensure your new layout fills in quickly, evenly, and stays free of algae. Plant Profile ‘Mini Coin’ is a compact, miniature variation within the Bucephalandra family. It features remarkably tiny leaves displaying an array of deep red, purple, and blue hues. Despite its small size, it's highly prized for its pronounced iridescent coloration, provided it receives appropriate care and is placed under aquarium LED lighting. Like other epiphytes, it can grow submerged or emersed and prefers to attach its rhizome to driftwood or rock rather than be buried in substrate. Over time, its thin rhizomes slowly spread into compact, shimmering clusters that make it an excellent choice for nano tanks, possibly ranking as the smallest among known Bucephalandra variations in the aquarium hobby. Key Features & Notes Under stable conditions and quality lighting, the tiny "coin" leaves shimmer with metallic red, purple, and blue tones. As one of the smallest known Buce varieties, it is the gold standard for adding massive scale and detail to even the smallest freshwater aquascapes. It creates very dense, tight clusters that look like a natural "moss" of tiny iridescent leaves when attached to hardscape. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for planted tanks where other plants might struggle. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard low-light aquarium plant setups, CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and richer iridescence. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary.
