listings.commonName: Aquario Neo CO2 - DIY CO2 Kit
listings.description: If you have been wanting to try your hand at high-tech plants but feel completely intimidated by massive gas cylinders, heavy regulators, and confusing electronic solenoids, the Aquario Neo DIY CO₂ Kit is exactly what you are looking for. This all-in-one kit uses a natural, proven bio-fermentation concept to generate a steady stream of carbon dioxide for up to 50–60 days per round. Key Features & Benefits An all-in-one complete starter ecosystem includes the specialized bottle, bio-powders, tubing, and an authentic Neo diffuser right out of the box. Natural yeast-driven bio-fermentation consistently generates a stable supply of essential plant nutrients for up to 50–60 days. An innovative, thick gel-matrix formula ensures a smooth, slow-release gas output that outperforms unpredictable, old-school DIY sugar recipes. The infinitely reusable main reaction bottle can be easily refreshed and reset using the budget-friendly Aquario Neo CO₂ Refill Packs . Product Specifications Product Type: Natural Bio-Fermentation Generator Kit Best Suited For: Aquariums ranging from 10 to 30 gallons. Tank Coverage: Use 1 bottle for every 20 gallons of water volume. For larger layouts, run multiple bottles concurrently. Dosing Life: Approximately 50 to 60 days (Highly dependent on room temperature) Optimal Temperature Range: 68°F to 86°C (Higher ambient temperatures cause the biological reaction to speed up, which increases daily output but shortens the total 60-day lifespan). System Adjustability: Non-adjustable passive flow. Do not use with solenoids, needle valves, or toggle taps, as pressure buildup will damage the bottle. What’s in the Box? 1x Heavy-Duty NEO CO₂ Culture Bottle 1x NEO CO₂ Bio Powder Packet 1x Aquario NEO Acrylic Micro-Bubble Diffuser 1x Flexible Utility Line 2x Clear Securing Suction Cups 1x Sealing Cap O-Ring Step-by-Step Activation & Maintenance Guide Add Water & Shake: Pour 300ml of warm water (around 30°C / 86°F—roughly a 50/50 mix of boiling water and tap water) straight into the bottle with the gel powder. Cap it tight and shake it vigorously at least 100 times until it is thoroughly mixed. Wait 24 Hours: Let the bottle sit completely undisturbed for 24 hours. The mixture will cool down and solidify into a thick, clear gel-like consistency at the bottom of the container. Add the Bio Pack: Open the bottle and pour in 1 packet of NEO CO₂ Bio Powder along with 1 cup (about 200ml) of room-temperature water. Twist the specialized reaction cap onto the bottle. Do not shake the bottle during this step. Hook Up & Diffuse: Connect one end of your flexible tubing to the bottle's reaction cap and the other end directly to your Neo Diffuser. Mount the diffuser low inside your tank using the suction cups and watch your plants begin to bubble! Empty & Repeat: When your gas output slows to a crawl or stops, pour out only the top liquid layer. Put in a Aquario Neo CO₂ Refill Pack and another cup of room-temperature water to activate the next layer. Repeat this cycle until the bottom gel matrix is entirely consumed! Important Safety Guidelines Because this biological process runs 24/7 and cannot be turned off at night, using it on tanks smaller than 10 gallons can risk over-gassing your livestock when the lights are off. If you use this kit on a nano setup, we highly recommend running a small air pump at night, or positioning your filter output to create gentle surface agitation to keep oxygen levels balanced! Never tilt, drop, or shake the bottle while it is actively running. This keeps the acidic fermentation fluid from traveling up the airline and accidentally spilling into your display tank. If any reaction liquid accidentally leaks into your aquarium, don't panic! It is mostly a harmless, minor organic alcohol byproduct, but it can cause a temporary drop in oxygen. Simply perform a swift 30% to 50% water change and run an air pump or adjust your filter output to create heavy surface agitation to clear it up instantly. Wipe away any excess gel material from the inner rim of the bottleneck during your first setup. This prevents debris buildup from jamming your gas ports over time.

The Aquario Neo CO₂ Refill Pack is an inexpensive, mess-free maintenance pouch designed to completely reset your original bottle. Packed with a fresh dose of specialized gel matrix powder and matching active bio-yeast packets, it brings your carbon injection system straight back to peak output so your planted aquascape never suffers from a sudden nutritional slump. Key Features & Benefits An economical maintenance solution lets you reuse your original bottle and diffuser hardware indefinitely. Provides a full 50 to 60 days of steady, automated carbon output to support healthy stem growth and vivid colors. listings.commonName: Aquario Neo Solution 1 - Macronutrient Liquid Fertilizer
listings.description: Product Overview Aquario Neo Solution 1 is a targeted macronutrient liquid fertilizer supplying nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, and magnesium directly to the water column. Plants absorb these elements through cell walls to fuel vegetative growth and photosynthesis. It addresses macro deficiencies that cause stunted stems, slow foliage growth, and premature leaf drop. Selecting the Right Formula (Neo Solution Guide) Aquario Neo Solution offers four formulas to match specific aquatic plant requirements and deficiencies. Use the guide below to select the ideal formula for your setup: Formula Key Composition Primary Effect & Ideal Usage Solution 1 Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium, Magnesium Promotes rapid growth; use when macronutrients are lacking or rapid growth is required. Solution 2 Fe, B, Mo, Ca, Micros, Amino & Humic Acids Balances growth and color; ideal for pale, twisted, or distorted new leaves. Solution K Potassium Promotes photosynthesis; ideal when leaf pinholes are observed. Solution FE Iron Enhances vibrant colors (especially red plants) and corrects pale new leaves. Dosing & Application Instructions Standard Direction: Dose 2 pumps (2mL) for every 5 gallons of aquarium water every 3 days. Adjust Solution 1 application rates based on your specific aquarium setup using the reference table below*: Aquarium Setting Solution 1 Dosage Rate New Aquarium (<30 Days) None (Do not dose) Normal Planted Aquarium 1 mL per 5 Gallons (50% Less) Fast Growth Required / High Light 3 mL per 5 Gallons (50% More) Low Light / Low Plant Mass 1 mL per 5 Gallons (50% Less) Color Enhancement Focus 2 mL per 5 Gallons (Standard Dose) *The recommended dosage assumes regular 20% minimum weekly water changes. Shake well before use. Do not use in dedicated dwarf shrimp breeding tanks. Apply the recommended dosage every 3 days using the calibrated pump dispenser. Adjust application rates upward or downward based on lighting intensity, CO2 levels, and plant biomass. Perform a minimum weekly water change of twenty percent to maintain water column clarity and prevent parameter skew over time. If nuisance algae appears, decrease the dosage volume and increase the frequency of consistent water changes. Keep out of reach of children. listings.commonName: Aquario Neo Solution FE - Liquid Iron Fertilizer
listings.description: Product Overview Aquario Neo Solution FE is a targeted liquid iron fertilizer formulated to supply highly bioavailable chelated nutrients directly to the water column. This essential element plays a critical role in chlorophyll synthesis, enzyme activation, and vivid pigment formation in aquatic foliage. It specifically addresses trace element deficiencies that cause pale or bleached new leaves, helping unlock deep red, pink, and orange pigmentation in demanding stem plants like Ludwigia, Rotala, and Alternanthera species. Selecting the Right Formula (Neo Solution Guide) Aquario Neo Solution offers four formulas to match specific aquatic plant requirements and deficiencies. Use the guide below to select the ideal formula for your setup: Formula Key Composition Primary Effect & Ideal Usage Solution 1 Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium, Magnesium Promotes rapid growth; use when macronutrients are lacking or rapid growth is required. Solution 2 Fe, B, Mo, Ca, Micros, Amino & Humic Acids Balances growth and color; ideal for pale, twisted, or distorted new leaves. Solution K Potassium Promotes photosynthesis; ideal when leaf pinholes are observed. Solution FE Iron Enhances vibrant colors (especially red plants) and corrects pale new leaves. Dosing & Application Instructions Standard Direction: Dose 2 pumps (2mL) for every 5 gallons of aquarium water every 3 days. Adjust Solution FE application rates based on your specific aquarium setup using the reference table below*: Aquarium Setting Solution FE Dosage Rate New Aquarium (<30 Days) None (Do not dose) Normal Planted Aquarium 2 mL per 5 Gallons (Standard Dose) Fast Growth Required / High Light 1 mL per 5 Gallons (50% Less) Low Light / Low Plant Mass 2 mL per 5 Gallons (Standard Dose) Color Enhancement Focus 3 mL per 5 Gallons (50% More) *The recommended dosage assumes regular 20% minimum weekly water changes. Shake well before use. Do not use in dedicated dwarf shrimp breeding tanks. Apply the recommended dosage every 3 days using the calibrated pump dispenser. Adjust application rates upward or downward based on lighting intensity, CO2 levels, and plant biomass. Perform a minimum weekly water change of twenty percent to maintain water column clarity and prevent parameter skew over time. If nuisance algae appears, decrease the dosage volume and increase the frequency of consistent water changes. Keep out of reach of children. listings.commonName: Lobelia Cardinalis Mini Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Common Name: Lobelia Cardinalis, Cardinal Plant Lobelia Cardinalis is an interesting specimen that is native to North America. This specimen can be found growing in marshy conditions in the wild and is characterized by its evergreen leaves with purple undersides. When grown in an aquarium setting, Lobelia Cardinalis typically produces lighter shades of green and will grow to an average height of 3-6", making it suitable for midground placement in a planted tank. When grown above the water's surface, Lobelia Cardinalis will produce scarlet flowers. This specimen is also suitable for outdoor ponds! Quality substrate and nutrients, paired with CO2 injection and low to medium lighting will help with overall growth and health. Lobelia Cardinalis Mini Specifications Please note, all stats are provided as general guidelines. Factors such as height, size and overall success can vary depending on care and environment. They provide the best option for those who want to ensure that absolutely zero unwanted pests are introduced into the aquarium. Remove tissue culture gel before planting. Simply wash the gel away or soak the plant in water and squeeze the gel off, gently. Cryptocoryne do not prefer to be moved once planted. If possible, do not uproot them once planted and established! CO2 injection and quality aquarium soil will yield better growth.

listings.commonName: Rotala Wayanad Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Rotala Wayanad is a relatively rare, delicate aquatic stem plant native to the Wayanad region of India. It's known for slender, needle-like foliage that stays small, with a greenish-yellow color that creates textural contrast when planted alongside broader green or deep red Rotala varieties. It suits nature aquariums, Dutch-style layouts, and nano planted tanks, and branches readily under good care to form fine-leafed midground or background bushes. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Fine, greenish-yellow foliage adds refined texture to planted aquariums. Compact size works for nano tanks or midground/background bushing in larger setups. Fast vertical growth fills in space and branches into dense hedges. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. * Rotala leaves are fragile, so handle stems with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide medium-to-high lighting. Pressurized CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilization yield denser branching and enhance its bright yellow-green tones. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and thicken the bush. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. To encourage Rotala Wayanad to grow into a dense, compact hedge, trim the main stem tops regularly once the plant is established. Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the dense cluster into smaller clumps or individual stems and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

Plant Profile Unlike most Eriocaulon species that grow in low, sea-urchin-like rosettes, Eriocaulon sp. 'Vietnam' is a distinct stem-forming plant native to Southeast Asia. It produces tall upright stems covered in long, narrow, pale green to whitish needle-like leaves that branch into dense lateral shoots over time. Maxing out around 8 inches tall, its fine foliage creates a sea-anemone texture that works well as a midground focal point or background accent in Dutch style aquascapes. It requires specialized care, favoring soft, acidic water, high-intensity lighting, rich substrate, and continuous CO2 injection to maintain steady growth without melting. Key Features & Notes Pale green needle-like foliage forms dense, bushy stem clusters for high visual contrast. Unique upright stem form among Eriocaulon species, making it ideal for Dutch style layouts. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Plant individual stems deeply into an active, acidic aquarium soil using fine-tipped tweezers, making sure stems are spaced slightly apart to allow light to reach lower foliage. Provide high-intensity lighting and continuous CO2 injection to maintain healthy growth and prevent lower leaf rot. Requires soft water parameters and balanced dosing of macro and micro nutrients, including nitrate, phosphate, and iron. Propagate by carefully cutting upper stem tips (around 2 inches long) with sharp scissors and replanting them into the substrate; avoid over-pruning as stems can be sensitive to frequent trimming. Why is Eriocaulon sp. 'Vietnam' considered a difficult plant to keep? It requires strict water parameters, including soft, acidic water (low GH/KH), high light levels, rich active aquasoil, and pressurized CO2. Without these ideal conditions, the lower stems can melt or stall in growth. 2. How does Eriocaulon sp. 'Vietnam' differ from other Eriocaulon species? While most Eriocaulon plants grow as low, rounded rosettes, 'Vietnam' forms true vertical stems with bushy side branching, making it look and handle more like a fine-leaved stem plant. 3. How should I trim and propagate Eriocaulon sp. 'Vietnam'? Use clean, sharp aquascaping scissors to take tip cuttings about 2 inches long from healthy stems, then replant the cuttings into rich soil. Avoid aggressive or frequent pruning, as stems take time to recover from heavy trims.

Plant Profile Weeping Moss on Stainless Steel Mesh is a popular live freshwater aquarium moss prized for its distinctive cascading, downward-growing habit. Known scientifically as Taxiphyllum ferriei 'Weeping', this unique aquatic plant features drooping, feathery fronds that create a natural waterfall effect as they mature. Pre-cultivated on a weighted 3" x 3" stainless steel mesh pad, this setup allows aquascapers to easily establish a low-profile foreground carpet or anchor a flowing accent onto hardscape without the hassle of tying or gluing loose fronds. Key Features & Benefits Pre-attached stainless steel mesh pad sinks naturally to form an instant, low-profile carpet. Signature drooping frond growth creates a soft, cascading waterfall aesthetic that brings visual motion and depth to aquascapes. Dense canopy provides a foraging zone and sanctuary for dwarf shrimp and baby fish fry. Care & Planting Instructions Place the metal mesh pad directly onto your substrate for an instant lawn carpet, or bend and secure it onto hardscape elements. Maintain a stable aquarium environment and avoid sudden water parameter swings to keep your live moss vibrant and healthy. Give the cascading fronds an occasional light haircut with sharp aquascaping shears to encourage denser, tighter growth. Propagate in seconds by snipping or pulling clumps apart and securing them to new hardscape surfaces throughout your tank. Optionally supply CO2 injection and low-to-medium LED lighting to accelerate growth rate and enhance deep-green coloration. Gently siphoning debris off the moss during weekly water changes keeps the inner growth bright green. 2. How do I use the stainless steel mesh pad in my aquascape layout? The 3" x 3" stainless steel mesh pad is naturally weighted to sink right out of the box. You can lay it flat on your substrate for an instant carpet, bend the flexible metal around curved rocks or wood, or mount it vertically against your glass to build a full cascading moss wall backdrop. 3. Use sharp curved aquascaping shears to make clean cuts, and immediately scoop or siphon out floating cuttings so they don't take root in unwanted areas of your aquarium.

Plant Profile Aponogeton henkelianus (aptly named the Henkel’s Lace Plant) looks like nature decided to try its hand at delicate crochet underwater. A close relative of Aponogeton madagascariensis and hailing from the fast-flowing streams of Madagascar, this rare bulb species is easily one of the most eye-catching conversation starters in the hobby. Its broad, see-through, windowpane leaves are riddled with natural holes and lattice-like veining, catching light and current in a way regular leaves just can't match, as they look more like stained glass than foliage! Just give its bulb clean water, good flow, and steady liquid nutrients, and it will reward you with a display that proves fancy aquatic foliage doesn't need to hold back. Key Features & Notes Striking fenestrated foliage creates a delicate, see-through lace pattern with high visual impact. Fast-growing bulb species that rapidly pushes up large, broad leaves to fill out open background space. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by gently inspecting the bulb and removing any loose organic debris around the base. Plant the bulb so that it is only half-buried in your aquarium soil or substrate; completely burying the bulb can cause it to rot. Provide steady water circulation and water-column dosing, ensuring adequate soluble iron levels to keep the delicate lace foliage green and vibrant. Avoid planting directly into overly rich organic substrates, as excess root nutrition can cause brown spots on the foliage; planting near established companion plants like Cryptocoryne can help stabilize soil parameters. Supplemental CO2 injection and moderate-to-high lighting encourage denser leaf production and stronger overall bulb energy. Maintain stable water parameters to prevent premature leaf drop or unexpected bulb dormancy. Final size and leaf density depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual bulbs may arrive sprouting or dormant. How do I plant an Aponogeton bulb correctly? Set the bulb on top of the substrate or press it lightly into sand or gravel so that only the bottom half is resting in the substrate. Never bury the entire bulb or cover the upper crown, as trapping the growth tip under substrate will lead to rot. 2. What should I do if my Aponogeton bulb goes dormant and loses its leaves? Bulb species often undergo natural dormancy periods where leaves die back. If this occurs, leave the bulb undisturbed in stable water conditions or remove it to a cool, dark water bath for a few weeks until new sprouts begin to emerge from the crown. 3. Why are dead brown spots appearing on the lace leaves? Unlike heavy root feeders, Aponogeton henkelianus can react negatively to overly rich organic substrates or iron deficiencies. Ensure soluble iron is available in the water column and that substrate conditions are kept lean and clean.

listings.commonName: Ammannia Gracillis Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Ammania Gracilis is a graceful and large-statured aquatic stem plant native to the tropical riverbanks and wetlands of West Africa. Celebrated for its opposing, wavy-edged leaves that arch elegantly from sturdy central stems, this species is highly valued for bringing warm sunset hues to planted tanks. Depending on light levels and nutrient availability, its foliage displays a stunning spectrum ranging from pale olive-green to blushing pink, salmon, and deep copper-red. Reaching 5 to 8+ inches in height, Ammania Gracilis makes an extraordinary midground centerpiece or background accent when contrasted against bright green foliage. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Elegantly arching, wavy-edged leaves display a vibrant blend of blushing pink, salmon, and deep copper-red. Versatile in submerged aquariums, open-top paludariums, and bog gardens, blooms purple flowers emersed. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide high-intensity lighting. Pressurized CO2 injection (25–30 ppm) alongside elevated phosphates, rich micronutrients/iron, and lean nitrates will yield the most vibrant pink and red leaf coloration. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim main stem tops with straight scissors once stems reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and expand coverage. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! listings.commonName: Anubias Barteri Gigantea Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Anubias Barteri Gigantea is here to remind your tank that size absolutely matters (in this case, at least). Aptly named for its massive profile, this majestic epiphyte produces broad, deep-green, arrow-shaped leaves resting atop tall, sturdy stalks. Individual leaf blades can grow up to 3 inches long, making it an instant centerpiece anchor capable of commanding attention in large aquariums, paludariums, and terrariums alike. Key Features & Benefits Largest of all Anubias varieties, delivering impressive height and arrow-shaped structural foliage for large tanks and centerpiece layouts. The tough and leathery leaves resist grazing from snails or herbivorous fish. The sterile laboratory environment guarantees your new plant arrives completely free of pests. Care & Planting Instructions Remove the plantlets from the cup and rinse away the sterile nutrient gel under lukewarm, dechlorinated water. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Avoid intense light and ensure good water flow to prevent spot algae on slow‑growing leaves. CO₂ is recommended to assist with the tissue culture transition and support healthy growth. Master the prep and planting process by checking out a beginner's guide to tissue culture plants to prevent your delicate new plantlets from melting or floating away. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I plant Anubias Barteri Gigantea Tissue Culture? Attach the plant directly to driftwood or rocks using aquarium-safe super glue gel, thread, or fishing line. While adding CO2 speeds up growth and aids in the tissue culture transition, it is completely optional. 3. Is this plant safe for shrimp, snails, and fish? Yes, Anubias is 100% safe for all freshwater fish, shrimp (including sensitive Caridina and Neocaridina), and snails. Its tough leaves are also resistant to plant-eating fish like cichlids or goldfish.

Plant Profile Azolla Caroliniana, commonly known as Carolina Water Fern, is a tiny and hardy floating fern that brings a captivating, micro-textured look to the water surface. Originating in the Western United States, this fast-growing species forms clusters of tiny, two-lobed leaves along branching stems that naturally split as the plant expands. While mostly emerald green, these unique aquarium floaters can blush with shades of pink, orange, or deep crimson when exposed to medium-to-high lighting. Perfect for low-tech aquariums, paludariums, and outdoor ponds, Azolla creates a vibrant surface carpet that competes heavily against nuisance algae while providing a shaded haven for your aquatic livestock. Please note: Portions may occasionally contain trace amounts of duckweed. Key Features & Benefits Intricate fronds blush with pink, orange, or ruby tones under medium to high lighting conditions. Foliage forms a dense biological carpet that extracts excess nitrates and organic waste to suppress algae. Compact surface canopy offers comfortable overhead shade and protective cover for timid fish, shrimplets, and fry. Care & Planting Instructions Gently place the plants directly onto the water surface, ensuring the tops of the leaves remain dry. Keep surface agitation minimal, as heavy water flow or splashing filters will trap water on top of the leaves and cause them to rot. Provide adequate lighting to encourage rapid growth and bring out rich coloration. Thin out the floating carpet regularly to ensure light still reaches your submerged midground and stem plants below. Dose liquid fertilizers regularly because floating plants absorb nutrients directly from the water column at an accelerated rate. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I keep my floating aquarium plants from dying due to filter flow and splashing? High water turbulence and constant water resting on the leaves are the main causes of rot in floating aquarium plants. Keep surface flow low, or use an airline tubing loop or floating ring to shield your aquarium floaters from direct filter return or bubbling air stones. 2. Can floating plants help control algae and absorb nitrates in a fish tank? Yes, these aquarium floaters act as incredible biological filters. Because they sit at the surface with direct access to atmospheric carbon dioxide, they grow exponentially faster than fully submerged species, aggressively consuming nitrates, ammonium, and excess nutrients that fuel nuisance algae. 3. Should I trim the hanging roots or thin out excess surface growth? Azolla Caroliniana has very short, delicate rootlets that do not require trimming. However, routinely scooping out excess surface growth with a fine-mesh aquascaping net is essential so that your floating plants do not completely block light from reaching your submerged stem and ground plants below.

listings.description: Plant Profile If you're looking to introduce bold architectural shapes to your aquascape, Crypt pontederiifolia delivers a refreshingly distinct silhouette. Native to the lush riverbanks and freshwater tidal zones of Sumatra, this robust species is easily recognized by its long petioles topped with broad, arrowhead-shaped leaves that showcase light-to-olive green topsides and subtle pinkish undersides. As with all crypt plants, this species can be sensitive to sudden parameter shifts and strongly objects to being relocated once planted. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. Extremely hardy and adaptable, thriving across a wide range of low-tech lighting and substrate conditions. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Crypt species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. With its fat, fleshy, rosette-style leaves, it offers a sturdy, unique texture that sets it apart from traditional lawn species like Monte Carlo or Dwarf Baby Tears . It is an exceptional pick for creating a clean, turf-style carpet across the foreground or midground of an aquarium, thriving under low-tech conditions where finicky carpeting species fail. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. Thick, sturdy foliage is resistant to damage from herbivorous fish and active substrate-dwelling inhabitants. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Plant individual clumps spaced roughly 1 inch apart across the substrate so the horizontal runners fill in the gaps into a dense mat. Use a dry start method or Wabi Kusa setup to give its root system plenty of time to firmly anchor into the substrate before you flood the tank. Provide moderate to high lighting to keep the leaves short, fat, and compact (lower lighting will cause the leaf blades to stretch longer). In the tank, it shows off succulent-like, oval leaves in opposing pairs along sturdy vertical stems, with a crisp light-green color that forms clean midground or background columns. Fast-branching habit forms thick, dense hedges that add soft volume and visual depth to aquascapes. Popular Dutch-style and nature aquarium plant ideal for creating high-contrast plant streets. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip the lower inch of foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to insert individual stems 1 to 2 inches deep into nutrient-rich aquarium soil. Provide medium-to-high lighting and pressurized CO2 injection; consistent liquid fertilization with essential macro and micro nutrients ensures lush green foliage and prevents lower leaf loss. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or leaf shedding. Plant Profile Heterogonium pinnatum is an uncommon tropical understory fern featuring elegant, dimorphic fronds with dark purple-brown stipes. A great pick for emersed setups, it provides vertical height for shaded background zones, humid corners, or moist terrestrial margins above a paludarium waterline. Fun fact: this fern completely changes character as it matures, as juvenile plants form compact, wide-lobed green fronds, while mature specimens send up taller, slender fertile fronds with thicker leaf texture. Anchored in loose, well-draining soil under gentle indirect light, it builds a lush forest canopy alongside other humidity-loving plants in terrariums. Key Features & Notes Dimorphic foliage transitions from compact broad juvenile leaves to slender, upright mature fronds. Dark purple-brown stipes provide sharp coloration and structural depth in shaded layouts. Requires shaded indirect light and steady humidity to prevent fronds from crisping or scorching. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Plant into a damp, loose tropical substrate blend rich in bark, tree fern fiber, and perlite, taking care not to bury the central rhizome crown too deep. Provide low to medium indirect light; direct light exposure can scorch the fronds and cause rapid browning. Maintain humidity above 70% while ensuring adequate drainage, as overly waterlogged soil leads to yellowing foliage and root melt. Prune damaged or yellowing fronds close to the rhizome base with sharp shears to encourage fresh fiddleheads. Heterogonium pinnatum is a terrestrial plant, and being submerged will result in the death of the plant. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Plant Profile Pteris ensiformis, commonly known as the Silver Lace Fern or Variegated Brake Fern, is a tropical understory fern featuring pinnate, feather-like fronds patterned with luminous silvery-white centers framed by thin green margins. Anchored in loose, well-draining acidic soil under gentle indirect light, it forms a bright, lacy canopy along midground and background zones or shaded hardscape pockets in emersed setups. This fern does not tolerate frost or being submerged as it will cause the fern to die. Key Features & Notes Silvery-white central variegation framed by deep green borders creates sharp contrast in shaded setups. Upright, feather-like pinnate fronds provide reliable background height and structural depth. Requires shaded indirect light and steady humidity to prevent fronds from scorching or curling. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Plant gently into a loose, airy, slightly acidic tropical soil mix rich in bark, sphagnum moss, and perlite, taking care to keep the central crown exposed just above the substrate line. Provide low to medium indirect light; direct light exposure can scorch the delicate variegated foliage and dry out leaf tips. Maintain humidity above 70% while ensuring excess water drains away freely, as soggy or waterlogged soil causes yellowing foliage. Snip aging or damaged outer fronds close to the rhizome base with sharp shears to promote fresh vertical shoots and maintain airflow. Pteris ensiformis are terrestrial plants, and being submerged will result in the death of the plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. listings.commonName: Bucephalandra Kedagang Round Mini Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Bucephalandra ‘Kedagang Mini Round’ is a vibrant, low-tech aquarium plant that originates from the Kedagang region of Borneo. It features smaller and narrower leaves than the normal Kedagang Round , making it ideal for foreground detailing or tucking into hardscape crevices. For best results, attach it to driftwood or rock rather than burying its rhizome in substrate. It is also highly versatile and can be grown submerged or emersed in a planted tank. Tissue culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab-grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go-to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Notes With consistent care and time, the tiny leaves mature into a rich, jewel-toned palette of red and purple that contrasts sharply against green mosses. As a "mini" variant, it is one of the best species for creating a sense of massive scale in small nano tanks or for detailing intricate crevices in large hardscapes. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for planted tanks where other plants might struggle. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by carefully removing the plantlets from the cup and rinsing away all sterile nutrient gel under lukewarm, dechlorinated water before mounting. Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood with aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as it will rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard low-light aquarium plant setups, CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and a smoother tissue culture transition. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Why is my tissue culture Bucephalandra melting after planting? Tissue culture plants undergo an acclimation phase when transitioning to underwater conditions. Maintain stable water parameters, good circulation, and moderate light; as long as the rhizome stays firm, new submerged leaves will emerge. 3. Can tissue culture Bucephalandra be planted in substrate? Yes, you can push the roots into substrate or gravel to help anchor the plantlet. However, you must keep the central horizontal rhizome completely exposed above the substrate line, as burying the rhizome starves it of circulation and causes rot.

Plant Profile Delivering a sharp, pointed profile in a compact frame, Anubias Spear Leaf offers a distinct alternative to standard round-leaved epiphytes like Anubias Nana Petite . True to its name, this epiphyte features glossy, deep green leaves that taper off into fine, spear-like tips on short stems. Reaching 3 to 5 inches in total height, it fills shadowy hardscape gaps, secures easily onto driftwood branches, and nestles into rock crevices. It grows slowly under low light and thrives submerged in aquariums or emersed in humid terrariums. Key Features & Benefits Sleek, spear-shaped leaves with a glossy sheen bring pointed architectural texture to midground crevices and wood forks. Compact 3-to-5-inch footprint scales cleanly into nano tanks and fine hardscape detailing. Thick, leathery leaves naturally deter grazing from plant-eating fish, snails, and active dwarf shrimp. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Avoid intense light and ensure good water flow to prevent spot algae on slow‑growing leaves. CO₂ is optional but improves growth and leaf density. Learn more about planting these species by reading our guide on How to Plant Epiphyte Aquatic Plants. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. Its tough leaves are also resistant to plant-eating fish like cichlids or goldfish.

listings.commonName: Rotala Macrandra 'Bangladesh' Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Rotala Macrandra 'Bangladesh' is an aquatic stem plant with delicate, wavy-edged leaves that display an exceptionally saturated blood-red to deep crimson color under high-tech conditions. Best suited for experienced hobbyists running high-tech setups, it thrives under high lighting, strong CO2, and elevated phosphate levels. Positioned sparingly as a centerpiece in front of light green background plants or sculpted into a structured Dutch-style street, routine trimming encourages rapid branching and builds an eye-catching focal point. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Intense blood-red and crimson foliage creates an unrivaled focal centerpiece in high-tech aquascapes. Fast-growing stem species that easily branches into dense, colorful hedges when properly pruned. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide medium-to-high lighting and pressurized CO2 injection; consistent fertilization with a specialized liquid macro and micro formula (maintaining 1.5–2.0 ppm phosphate and lean nitrates under 10 ppm) yields robust stem growth and prevents bottom leaf yellowing. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or rotting. Trim main stem tops with sharp straight scissors once they reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and thicken the bush. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Dragon Stone (Ohko) Accent Stones are the perfect solution for hobbyists looking to add finer details and intricate textures to a hardscape. These smaller fragments feature the same iconic, scale-like texture and earthy reds, yellows, and browns as full-sized stones, but in a size that is much easier to manage for nanoscapes or detailed foreground work. Because of their smaller size, these natural stone pieces have great stacking potential, allowing you to build miniature cliffs or fill in gaps between larger boulders for a more cohesive, aged look. Its clay-like composition makes it brittle compared to other rocks, allowing aquatic plants to easily self-attach. These accent pieces are also suitable for non-aquarium use and will work beautifully in terrariums, paludariums, or similar planted enclosures. Pieces from packages will range from 1-3", making them a perfect choice for nano aquarium scapes or adding finer details to an existing scape. Each bag is approximately 2.2 lbs per order. Notes: Dragon Stone is inert and will not influence water parameters. We recommend rinsing stones thoroughly before use to remove any natural dust or sediment. Stone coloration darkens when wet. Dragon Stone can be easily broken into smaller pieces with a chisel and hammer.

Plant Profile Begonia 'Arabian Sunset' is a hybrid cane-type Mallet begonia bred in 1992 with symmetrical, teardrop foliage with ruffled margins that fan out in classic angel-wing pairs in deep metallic green, rich maroon, and glowing sunset-red tones. Strictly suited for emersed conditions, its moody, multi-toned leaves and bright pink floral clusters provide an immediate pop against driftwood branches and deep green mosses. Fun fact: belonging to the specialized Mallet group of cane begonias, its jointed, bamboo-like stems feature swollen nodal rings that store moisture and anchor new growth, functioning in wild tropical ancestors like natural shock absorbers against windy rainstorms. Key Features & Notes Metallic maroon-black ruffled leaves pair with vivid crimson undersides for layered color depth. Produces swollen, bamboo-like cane nodes that regularly sprout clusters of bright coral-pink flowers. Grows as a shrubby upright perennial that provides vertical presence in medium to large enclosures. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Tuck the root cluster into an airy, chunky tropical substrate blend loaded with perlite, pumice, and orchid bark; avoid dense, heavy soils that stay muddy. Provide moderate to bright indirect light; avoid scorching direct light which will bleach the deep metallic maroon tones and crisp the leaf edges. Allow the top inch or two of substrate to dry out between thorough waterings, and ensure the root zone drains freely so the rhizome never sits in stagnant water. Prune tall cane stems just above a swollen node with clean shears to encourage bushy side shoots and keep the canopy balanced. Final size, flowering frequency, and foliar color intensity depend entirely on your specific setup conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. listings.commonName: Eusteralis Stellata / Pogostemon Stellatus Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Pogostemon Stellatus, commonly known as Eustachia stellata or Water Star, is an aquatic stem plant that has narrow, needle-like leaves radiating in dense, star-like whorls, giving it a spiky, textured profile underwater. Native to Southeast Asia and Northern Australia, its color shifts from bright light green to warm orange, pink, and reddish hues at the crown tips under high lighting, pressurized CO2, and steady iron dosing. Reaching 5 to 10+ inches in height, it branches into full, colorful midground or background bushes with routine pruning, adding fine texture and movement alongside broad-leaved species. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Thin, needle-like leaves radiate in star-like whorls from vertical stems, adding fine texture and movement. Foliage shifts from bright green to warm orange, pink, and red hues at the upper tips under high light and iron dosing. Routine pruning encourages dense horizontal branching to fill out midground and background zones. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small portions or individual stems 1 inch apart into your aquarium soil so light reaches the lower leaves. Provide high-intensity lighting, pressurized CO2 injection, and regular liquid fertilization rich in iron and micronutrients to prevent yellowing and bring out orange-red crown tips. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden chemistry shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting during acclimation. To propagate, trim main stem tops or lateral side shoots with sharp straight shears and replant the cuttings directly into your aquarium soil. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Plant Profile Pellionia repens, commonly known as the Trailing Watermelon Begonia or Watermelon Vine, is an evergreen creeping perennial in the nettle family Urticaceae native to the shaded forest floors of Southeast Asia. Despite its common name, this species is not a true begonia; it develops fleshy, trailing stems lined with ovate, dark olive-green leaves marked by contrasting silver-green central marbling and pinkish-purple stems under moderate lighting. Its prostrate vining habit makes it an effective living ground cover or background climber, forming a dense, patterned mat. Key Features & Notes Ovate dark olive leaves feature silvery-green patterned centers and pink-tinted trailing stems. Spreading vining growth habit creates dense ground cover across the floor or climbs damp background walls in terrariums. High humidity tolerance makes it an ideal living carpet alongside mosses in tropical bio-active vivarium plants and paludariums. Care & Planting Instructions Press the root cluster and lower stem nodes gently into a moist, airy tropical substrate mix or pin runners directly against damp sphagnum moss or background panels. Position under partial shade or gentle indirect lighting, avoiding intense direct exposure that bleaches leaf patterns and crisps the foliage. Maintain ambient relative humidity above 70% and keep the soil consistently damp while ensuring excess water drains away freely from the roots. Pinch back growing vine tips regularly with sharp shears to promote lateral branching and maintain a compact, bushy ground cover. Note that Pellionia repens is strictly a terrestrial species, and full underwater submersion will cause the leaves to melt and decay. listings.commonName: Fittonia Albivenis On Clay Moss Ball
listings.description: Plant Profile If you want to inject a quick pop of bright color into your high-humidity setup, this Fittonia on Clay Moss Ball is ready for the job. We have nestled the brightly veined leaves of Fittonia albivenis on top of a weighted terra cotta sphere that is wrapped in a carpet of Christmas Moss. Because this combination is naturally easy to care for, you do not need to bury any roots or use special tools. You can simply place the ball onto the floor of your terrarium, vivarium, or paludarium. The Christmas Moss holds moisture around the base of the Fittonia, helping it grow while creating a neat, rolling green mound. *Fittonia is a terrestrial plant species and will not survive submerged underwater in an aquarium. Depending on current inventory, you may receive a Fittonia in either the Red, White, or Skeleton pattern variation.* Key Features & Benefits Weighted, porous terra cotta ball core provides a sturdy, natural base that sits securely without tipping over or shifting. Stark visual contrast of Fittonia’s colorful, net-like leaf veins against deep-green Christmas Moss creates an eye-catching focal point. Specially adapted for moisture-rich terrestrial environments, making it an ideal fit for high-humidity terrarium displays. Care & Planting Instructions Position the clay ball directly onto your substrate or nestle it among hardscape in terrariums, vivariums, or paludariums above the waterline. Maintain high ambient humidity and mist regularly to keep the Fittonia foliage hydrated and the underlying Christmas Moss damp. Provide low to medium indirect light to prevent the delicate leaf veins from scorching while keeping the moss vibrant and green. Trim back both the Christmas Moss and Fittonia stems occasionally with sharp shears to encourage bushier, more compact growth. Propagate easily by taking clean stem cuttings of the Fittonia or snipping sections of the moss to start new growth points. For the moss, simply trim back overgrown sections with sharp shears and relocate the trimmings to other moist hardscape areas in your enclosure.

listings.commonName: Mini Bolbitis on Clay Moss Ball
listings.description: Plant Profile Need a simple way to add texture to a small setup? The Mini Bolbitis on Clay Moss Ball delivers. We have anchored the delicate, textured fronds of this miniature fern on top of a terracotta sphere that is completely wrapped in a lush carpet of Christmas moss for a seamless green look. Both plants are low‑maintenance, making this a stress‑free upgrade for nano tanks. Key Features & Benefits Pre-attached to a clay sphere, offering an instant plug-and-play centerpiece with zero gluing or tying required. Versatile growth habit thrives fully submerged in aquariums or emersed in high-humidity terrariums, vivariums, and paludariums. Care & Planting Instructions Place the clay ball directly onto your substrate or nestle it among your hardscape layout, ensuring the green fern rhizomes remain completely uncovered to prevent rotting. Maintain a stable aquarium environment and avoid sudden, drastic changes to your water parameters to keep your plant looking vibrant and healthy. Give the moss an occasional light haircut with sharp aquascaping shears to keep its shape neat, compact, and perfectly balanced. Propagate your patch in seconds by cutting or pulling a small clump apart and anchoring it to a new surface in your tank. Add CO2 injection if you want to accelerate growth and unlock the most intense, eye-popping green coloration possible. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Ensure the green rhizome of the fern stays exposed to open water and is never buried beneath soil or gravel. 3. How do I stop moss trimmings from spreading everywhere during maintenance? Always turn off your filter pumps and powerheads before trimming moss. Use sharp curved shears to make clean cuts, and immediately scoop or siphon out floating cuttings so they don't take root in unwanted areas of your aquarium.

listings.commonName: Alternanthera Bettzickiana Red on Clay Moss Ball
listings.description: Plant Profile If you want to inject a blast of fiery color into your scape without the usual high-maintenance drama, this artistic combo is a great pick. We have nestled a vibrant stem of Alternanthera bettzickiana 'Red' onto a 2-inch terra cotta sphere that is wrapped in a velvety cushion of Christmas Moss. Unlike temperamental red aquatic plants that require complex setups, this variety keeps its rich, eye-catching red and deep pink coloration with relative ease when grown in the air. The leaves feature a beautiful, slight waviness and a ruffled, frilled edge that gives the plant immense personality and architectural character. **Alternanthera Bettzickiana Red is a terrestrial plant. It cannot be submerged underwater long-term and does its best in high-humidity setups** Key Features & Benefits Fiery red foliage paired with a deep green moss base provides immediate, eye-catching visual contrast. The combination of stem plant and moss helps absorb excess nutrients from misting water to keep enclosures clean. The porous clay sphere retains moisture to support a healthy microclimate for surrounding roots and moss. Care & Planting Instructions Place the 2-inch clay ball directly onto your damp substrate or nestle it among your hardscape in terrariums, vivariums, or paludariums, keeping the foliage strictly above the water line. As long as the Christmas Moss stays wet and receives light, it will grow easily. Provide regular misting to keep the ambient humidity high and ensure the underlying moss ball remains damp and thriving. While regular aquarium moss handles low light beautifully, the Alternanthera requires high light to display its absolute best red coloration. If lighting is severely lacking, the leaves will dull out to an orange hue. Unlike typical setups that limit nutrients, this plant heavily prefers high nitrates and high phosphates. Regularly dosing a dedicated fertilizer like UNS Plant Food into your misting routine will drastically speed up growth and keep the fiery red coloration at its peak. Snip the top stems of the Alternanthera to encourage a bushier, more compact look. You can press those cuttings right into damp soil to grow new plants, or trim the moss to use elsewhere. listings.commonName: Anubias Nana Golden Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Common Name: Anubias Nana Golden Anubias Nana Golden is the vibrant, chartreuse sibling of the classic Anubias Nana , and it is ready to bring a major golden hour glow-up to your tank. If your current layout is looking a bit too uniformly dark and you are searching for a way to make your hardscape pop, this eye-catching variant is here to help you strike gold. Its bright yellow-green foliage creates a stunning high-contrast focal point when nestled against dark lava rocks, shadowy driftwood, or deep green mosses. By choosing the Tissue Culture version of this plant, you are guaranteed a 100% pest-free, algae-free, and pesticide-free start for your aquarium. These plants are grown in-vitro in a sterile laboratory setting, ensuring no unwanted snails or hitchhikers enter your system. While these plantlets start smaller and require more time to mature, they offer the cleanest and most reliable method for establishing a healthy colony in planted tanks. Key Features & Benefits The bright yellow-green leaves offer an extraordinary color contrast against darker hardscape. Its hardy nature makes it one of the easiest golden-hued plants in the entire hobby. The famously tough and leathery leaves easily resists grazing from large or herbivorous fish. Care & Planting Instructions Remove the plantlets from the cup and rinse away the sterile nutrient gel under lukewarm, dechlorinated water. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Avoid intense light and ensure good water flow to prevent spot algae on slow‑growing leaves. CO₂ is optional but improves growth and leaf density. Master the prep and planting process by checking out a beginner's guide to tissue culture plants to prevent your delicate new plantlets from melting or floating away. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Is this plant safe for shrimp, snails, and fish? Yes, Anubias Nana Golden is 100% safe for all freshwater fish, shrimp (including sensitive Caridina and Neocaridina), and snails. Plant Profile A rare, marbled cultivar among Anubias aquarium plants, Anubias Nana Pinto brings striking white-and-green variegated contrast! Selected through generations of careful cultivation from classic Anubias Nana , this sought-after Anubias features an icy mosaic of cream and forest green splashed across every leaf. This dwarf epiphyte attaches its rhizome directly to driftwood or stone rather than being buried in substrate, delivering high-contrast illumination against dark lava rock, driftwood roots, and deep green mosses in aquariums, terrariums, and paludariums. Key Features & Benefits Marbled white-and-green variegated foliage displays a unique, high-contrast pattern. Compact dwarf footprint under 4 inches makes it one of the premier nano aquarium plants for tight hardscape crevices and desktop layouts. Thick leaves deters nibbling from herbivorous cichlids, goldfish, snails, and active dwarf shrimp. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the horizontal rhizome completely exposed above substrate to prevent rot. Provide clean, medium lighting alongside balanced micro/macro dosing; white leaf tissue lacks heavy chlorophyll and requires adequate light to prevent melting. Maintain stable water parameters and balanced flow to avoid sudden acclimation melt or spot algae accumulation on slow-growing leaves. CO₂ injection is recommended to support steady metabolic rates, accelerate growth, and preserve crisp white marbling. Learn more about planting these species by reading our guide on How to Plant Epiphyte Aquatic Plants. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. While Anubias Pinto is a relatively stable genetic cultivar, prolonged exposure to insufficient lighting or poor nutrient levels can cause new growth to produce higher chlorophyll concentrations (becoming solid green) as an adaptation for survival. Maintaining medium lighting and optional CO₂ encourages each new leaf to retain its marbled white-and-green mosaic. 3. Where is the best placement for Anubias Nana Pinto in a planted tank? Because it reaches only 2 to 4 inches tall, Anubias Pinto belongs in the foreground or low midground. Secure it directly into crevices of hardscape, leaving the rhizome exposed.

Plant Profile Rotala Mexicana is a sought-after aquatic stem plant widely distributed across tropical and subtropical regions of South America, Central America, Africa, and Australia. Historically known under synonyms such as Rotala pusilla , this fast-growing species features rounded, bright green leaves when grown emersed, which transition to narrow, needle-like foliage with vivid green, salmon, and pink-orange hues when submerged. With its distinctive reddish stems and lush vertical growth habit, Rotala Mexicana makes a great background centerpiece or dense midground hedge when provided with optimal high-tech aquarium conditions. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Thin, narrow underwater foliage displays a dynamic color range from bright green to vibrant pink-orange hues set against reddish stems. Fast vertical growth fills in space and branches into dense hedges with routine pruning. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip the lower inch of foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. * Rotala leaves are fragile, so handle stems with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower growth. Provide high-intensity lighting and pressurized CO2 injection; maintaining balanced macro- and micro-nutrients alongside iron supplementation prevents stunted growth and yields rich pink-orange coloration. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters (acidic to neutral pH 4.5–7.0 preferred) and avoid drastic changes to prevent leaf melt or stem rot. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the water surface, and simply replant the trimmings directly into soil to propagate. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Once new shoots develop, trim away old lower growth to encourage dense branching.

Plant Profile Rotala Ceylon is a fast-growing and versatile aquatic stem plant. Featuring slender stems lined with fine, narrow, light-green leaves, this species provides a soft, airy texture and an energetic, bushy habit. Under moderate conditions, it maintains a fresh, neutral lime-green appearance, making it an outstanding background that accentuates darker red plants. When exposed to high-intensity lighting and CO2 injection, its growing tips blush with delicate pink and gold highlights. Highly resilient, Rotala Ceylon quickly regrows into dense hedges after trimming, providing a strong foundation for Dutch-style layouts and nature aquariums alike. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Displays soft pink and golden highlights on growing tips when cultivated under high lighting and nutrient-rich conditions. Rapid growth acts as a natural nitrate sponge for crystal-clear water. Provide medium-to-high lighting and clean water conditions; while easy to maintain without CO2, supplying pressurized CO2 yields significantly faster growth and blush-pink growing tips. Trim main stem tops with straight scissors once stems reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and thicken your bush. How do I transition Rotala Coin Leaf from emersed to submerged growth? When transitioning from emersed to submerged growth, plant bare stems securely into rich substrate under good lighting and keep water parameters stable. As new growth adapts, the plant will shed its rounded, coin-shaped land leaves and sprout slender, colorful underwater foliage. Once new shoots develop, trim away old lower growth to encourage dense branching.

Plant Profile Common Name: Bucephalandra Broad Wavy Buce ‘Broad Wavy’ is a bright green aquarium plant featuring wide, broad leaves with distinctively ruffled margins. As a variant of the popular Green Wavy , this species offers a bigger leaf profile. Highly versatile, it can be grown submerged or emersed, usually attached to hardscape such as driftwood or rocks rather than being buried in traditional aquarium substrate. Broad Wavy is a fantastic choice for adding intricate texture to the midground of freshwater aquascapes, where it will grow into a lush, shimmering carpet of foliage over time. Key Features & Notes Unlike many wild-collected species, this plant is commercially cultivated, making it generally more acclimated to aquarium life and a more eco-friendly choice for hobbyists. The combination of a wider leaf shape and intense ruffling provides a lush, "full" appearance that fills vertical space in the midground effectively. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for aquascapes where other plants might struggle. It is perfectly at home fully submerged in an aquarium or emersed in high-humidity terrariums, vivariums, and paludariums. Care Tips & Preparation Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood . Never bury the rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Carefully remove the plant from its pot and clear away all rockwool from the roots. For a deep dive on prepping potted plants, click here . Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting. Unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance, CO2 injection will yield much faster growth. We recommend researching your specific water chemistry to ensure your plant thrives. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions. Please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Plant Profile Meet Ludwigia Crystal, an extraordinarily rare aquatic stem plant native to the rivers and bogs of Central and South America! Belonging to the Ludwigia inclinata family, this variety is prized for its delicate leaves that showcase a stunning array of orange, salmon, and translucent pink hues. Best suited for midground and background placement in high-tech setups, it requires high lighting, rich nutrients, and robust CO2 injection to reach its full potential. Under proper conditions, it is a fast grower, easily reaching heights of 12” to 16”+, making routine trimming essential to sculpt it into a striking, high-contrast focal point that breaks up traditional green aquascapes. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Unusually translucent, crystal-toned foliage offers exceptional color contrast against green stem plants. Fast-growing stem habit readily branches after trimming to create a dense, colorful midground or background accent. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip the lower inch of foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower growth. Provide medium-to-high lighting and pressurized CO2 injection; consistent fertilization with a specialized liquid macro and micro formula yields robust stem growth and prevents bottom leaf yellowing. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or rotting. Trim main stem tops with sharp straight scissors once they reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and thicken the bush. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Ludwigia inclinata sp. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I achieve a thick, bushy forest with Ludwigia Crystal? To encourage Ludwigia Crystal to form a dense hedge, routinely trim the main stem tops once established. Each cut site will sprout multiple lateral side shoots, doubling the stem density and creating a tight, bushy group. 3. How do I transition Ludwigia Crystal from emersed to submerged growth? When transitioning from emersed to submerged growth, plant bare stems securely into rich substrate under medium-to-high lighting and keep water parameters stable. As new growth adapts, the plant will shed its land leaves and sprout slender underwater foliage. Once new shoots develop, trim away old lower growth to encourage dense branching.

Plant Profile Marsilea Hirsuta is a charming dwarf, clover-like foreground plant that brings a unique look to any aquascape. It is a slow-growing carpeting plant that is relatively easy to keep compared to demanding foreground species like Dwarf Baby Tears , making it an excellent alternative for hobbyists wanting a lush carpet without the intense upkeep. When grown under medium to high light, the plant stays low-growing and spreads horizontally, helping you achieve a beautifully dense, turf-style lawn. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Need Dwarf Four Leaf Clover but this listing is out of stock? Check out these other popular variants: Marsilea Angustifolia Marsilea Crenata Key Features & Benefits Dwarf clover-like foliage creates a unique, turf-style lawn across the foreground. Easier to cultivate than high-demanding carpets like Dwarf Baby Tears (HC). Care & Planting Instructions Maintain high lighting and inject pressurized CO2 while frequently trimming new growth to force the plant to stay low and create a tight carpeting effect over your foreground. Keep a pair of trimming scissors handy, as it grows quickly and requires regular pruning to prevent it from out-competing and overgrowing your other tank inhabitants. Propagate whenever you want by simply cutting the stems anywhere along the shoot and replanting them, or by pulling apart dense clumps and splitting the roots. Maintain stable aquarium parameters and avoid any sudden, drastic shifts in water quality to prevent your new grass from melting. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Why is my Marsilea Hirsuta growing tall instead of carpeting? When Marsilea Hirsuta doesn't receive enough light, it stretches upward toward the surface and grows single, taller leaves. Increasing light intensity will force new leaves to stay low and form classic 2-to-4-leaf clover fronds along horizontal runners. 2. Is Marsilea Hirsuta suitable for low-tech aquariums? Yes, Marsilea Hirsuta is one of the easiest carpeting plants for low-tech tanks without pressurized CO2. While it grows much more slowly without CO2, it will still spread horizontally as long as adequate lighting and root nutrients are provided. 3. How do I propagate Marsilea Hirsuta? Plant it 1 inch apart into substrate using fine tweezers. The plant will naturally send out subterranean runners that connect the plugs into a unified carpet.

Plant Profile Java Moss is moss-tly famous for being the undisputed heavyweight live freshwater aquarium moss of the hobby, and it has earned its reputation for a good reason. This legendary aquatic plant staple can survive almost any water parameter or temperature swing you throw its way. Its deep green, thin, interlocking fronds grow in a wild, free-form pattern that is excellent for softening hard landscape lines or creating a natural, aged look on wood and rocks. We have pre-grown this bulletproof classic onto a weighted 3" x 3" stainless steel mesh pad so you can simply drop it straight to the bottom of your tank to form an instant foreground carpet or moss wall. Key Features & Benefits Pre-attached stainless steel mesh pad sinks naturally to form an instant, low-profile foreground carpet with zero floating. Draping or placing this live moss near hardscape elements gives driftwood and stones a mature, weathered look that mimics wild riverbeds. Fine fronds create a sanctuary and continuous biofilm foraging zone for dwarf shrimp and fry. Care & Planting Instructions Place the metal mesh pad directly onto your substrate for an instant carpet, bend it around hardscape, or mount it vertically against your glass. Maintain a stable aquarium environment and avoid sudden water parameter swings to keep your live moss vibrant and healthy. Give the moss fronds an occasional light haircut with sharp aquascaping shears to encourage denser, tighter growth. Propagate in seconds by snipping or pulling clumps apart and securing them to new hardscape surfaces throughout your tank. Optionally supply CO2 injection and low-to-medium LED lighting to accelerate growth rate and enhance foliage density. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I keep my Java Moss from turning brown or yellow? Java Moss prefers clean water flow and cooler temperatures (under 78°F). Browning usually occurs when organic detritus gets trapped inside the fine, interlocking fronds or when water temperatures exceed 80°F. Gently siphoning debris off the moss during weekly water changes keeps the inner growth bright green. 2. How do I use the stainless steel mesh pad in my aquascape? The 3" x 3" stainless steel mesh pad is naturally weighted to sink right out of the box. You can lay it flat on your substrate to form an instant carpet, bend the flexible metal around rocks and wood, or attach it vertically to glass to start a full moss wall backdrop. 3. How do I stop moss trimmings from spreading everywhere during maintenance? Always turn off all aquarium filter pumps and powerheads before trimming moss. Use sharp curved aquascaping shears to make clean cuts, and immediately scoop or siphon out floating cuttings so they don't take root in unwanted areas of your aquarium.

Product Overview Make choosing the right piece easy with our WYSIWYG (What You See Is What You Get) Driftwood Showpieces. These one-of-a-kind pieces are hand-selected for their unique shape and size and photographed so that what you see is the one that arrives at your door. Perfect for aquariums, terrariums, paludariums, or reptile enclosures, these natural pieces simplify hardscape planning and bring your vision to life without any surprises. Browse our entire collection of WYSIWYG Showpieces About Ancient Wood Characterized by a dense profile and heavily weathered texture, Ancient Wood brings immediate visual weight to your scape. It features an intricate network of deep crevices, valleys, and fissures that offer a dramatic old-growth aesthetic reminiscent of a mature forest riverbed. Approximate Size 27L x 17W x 27H inches The Pen shown is provided for size reference. Additional Information All natural driftwood leaches tannins, creating a temporary yellow or brown "tea-stained" tint. Ancient Wood leaches a heavy amount of tannins for the first 20–40 days. We highly recommend performing frequent water changes during the first few weeks. Driftwood is naturally buoyant and will float initially. To ensure your showpiece stays in place, you can submerge the wood in a separate container until it is fully waterlogged. Alternatively, boiling the wood for 1–2 hours not only speeds up the process but also helps release tannins and sterilizes the piece. You can secure the wood using aquarium-safe glue or weigh it down with a large stone or heavy décor until it remains submerged naturally. Shortly after submersion, a white biofilm may develop on the wood; this is a natural bacterial growth that will disappear on its own or be eaten by shrimp and algae-eaters. We always recommend rinsing your wood thoroughly with fresh water before adding it to an established aquarium, terrarium, or enclosure to remove any surface dust or debris.

Modular Manifold System: An expandable bubble counter manifold lets you split your gas supply seamlessly to feed multiple tanks independently from a single regulator. Dual High-Precision Gauges: Monitors both raw cylinder tank pressure (0–4,000 PSI) and exact working output pressure (0–160 PSI) for complete system transparency.
