Plant Profile Cryptocoryne undulata has smooth, remarkably sleek leaves with subtly wavy edges. Under aquarium lighting, its reflective foliage shifts effortlessly from a vibrant emerald green to warm bronze and deep reddish hues. Native to seasonal riverbanks and flowing streams of Sri Lanka, this low-maintenance plant brings polished elegance to your midground zones. As with all crypt plants, it can be sensitive to sudden parameter shifts and strongly objects to being relocated once planted. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Smooth, glossy green-to-bronze leaves with subtly ruffled edges add texture. Can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups, where mature plants may produce flowering spathes. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel to supply essential subterranean nutrients. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth and fuller foliage density, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Crypt species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. Check our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt for full recovery steps. 3. Should I use root tabs or liquid fertilizers? Root tabs are best. Cryptocoryne species are heavy root feeders that draw primary nutrition from the substrate rather than the water column.

Plant Profile Littorella Uniflora, commonly known as Shoreweed, is an easily recognized, low-growing aquatic carpeting plant native to freshwater shores across Europe, from Iceland to the Black Sea. With its fat, fleshy, rosette-style leaves, it offers a sturdy, unique texture that sets it apart from traditional lawn species like Monte Carlo or Dwarf Baby Tears . It is an exceptional pick for creating a clean, turf-style carpet across the foreground or midground of an aquarium, thriving under low-tech conditions where finicky carpeting species fail. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Fat, fleshy rosette leaves form a unique, thick grass carpet across the foreground. Highly resilient low-tech species that thrives in low light and low CO2 environments. Thick, sturdy foliage is resistant to damage from herbivorous fish and active substrate-dwelling inhabitants. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Plant individual clumps spaced roughly 1 inch apart across the substrate so the horizontal runners fill in the gaps into a dense mat. Use a dry start method or Wabi Kusa setup to give its root system plenty of time to firmly anchor into the substrate before you flood the tank. Provide moderate to high lighting to keep the leaves short, fat, and compact (lower lighting will cause the leaf blades to stretch longer). Inject CO2 and supply nutrient-rich soil or root tabs to accelerate its naturally slow growth rate. Master the basics by learning how to properly grow aquarium carpet plants to ensure your new layout fills in quickly. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Why are the leaves on my Littorella Uniflora growing long instead of staying short? In low-light conditions, Littorella Uniflora stretches its leaves upward toward the light source. Increasing light intensity forces the plant to maintain short, thick, compact leaves that hug the substrate. 3. Is Littorella Uniflora suitable for low-tech tanks without CO2? Yes! Shoreweed is extremely hardy and adapts well to low-CO2 setups. While its growth rate will be slow, it will steadily spread runners and form a healthy lawn over time.

Common Name: Needle Leaf Ludwigia Needle leaf ludwigia is a beautiful plant with delicate green and red leaves. This is an easy plant to keep that adds movement and dimension to the aquarium. Needle leaf plants have thin, pointed leaves that grow in opposite pairs along the whole length of the stem. The leaves can be green or red depending on the amount of iron available in the water. If pruned frequently, this plant will branch out and provide a bushy filler for the mid- or background of your tank. Needle leaf is a versatile plant, but to get the desirable bright red color, you must provide high lighting and nutrient levels. High iron content will bring out more red tones in the plant. CO2 injection is not required for the cultivation of this plant but can help it grow more robustly. The plant can be grown submersed or emersed. When grown emersed, the leaves tend to be round like other types of ludwigia and remain green. When grown under high light and submerged in an aquarium, the leaves turn thin and orange to red depending on nutrient. Dosing UNS Plant and iron supplements will bring out the deep red coloration. Propagation can be achieved by taking cuttings from the main stem of the plant that is replanted into the substrate. Notes: Tissue culture plants are grown in vitro from a state of the art laboratory specialized in propagating aquatic plants. They provide the best option for those who want to ensure that absolutely zero unwanted pests are introduced into the aquarium. Remove tissue culture gel before planting. Simply wash the gel away or soak the plant in water and squeeze the gel off with your fingers. Do not make drastic changes to the aquarium. Unstable parameters will result in melt and rotting of the aquarium plant. For instructions on how to properly prep tissue culture aquarium plants, click here . CO2 injection and quality aquarium soil will yield better growth. Plant Profile Riccia Fluitans is the choice for you if you want to recreate the legendary, high-definition layouts made famous by master aquascaper Takashi Amano. This unique liverwort grows in thick, bright green, interlocking mats that look absolutely striking under bright lights. Because it is rootless, it can either be left free-floating at the surface or tied and glued down to rocks, driftwood, or stainless steel mesh to form a bubbling green carpet. Under strong lighting and a steady supply of carbon dioxide, it will routinely trap oxygen bubbles right at its leaf tips, producing a breathtaking, shimmering phenomenon known as "pearling." Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Vibrant neon-green coloration and fine branching structure deliver a high-end, professionally scaped look. Functions as a floating surface cover for fry or a dense foreground carpet when tied to hardscape. Care & Planting Instructions Rinse away the nutrient gel thoroughly under lukewarm water, separate into small portions, and attach to mesh or hardscape. Maintain a stable aquarium environment and trim regularly to prevent the lower layers from dying off and floating away. Give the plant an occasional light haircut with sharp aquascaping shears to keep its shape neat, compact, and perfectly balanced. Propagate your patch in seconds by cutting or pulling a small clump apart and anchoring it to a new surface in your tank. Add CO2 injection if you want to accelerate growth and unlock the most intense, eye-popping green coloration possible. Master the prep and planting process by checking out a beginner's guide to tissue culture plants to prevent your delicate new plantlets from melting or floating away. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I prepare Riccia Fluitans tissue culture cups before planting? Remove the plant from the tissue culture cup, gently rinse all nutrient gel off the fronds under running lukewarm water, and divide the mat into smaller portions before tying or anchoring them to your hardscape or mesh pads. 2. Why is my submerged Riccia carpet detaching and floating to the surface? Because Riccia Fluitans lacks true roots, it cannot anchor itself to substrate. As the top layer grows thick under light, it shades out the bottom layer, causing it to die off and lose its grip. Frequent, close trimmings with sharp shears are necessary to keep the carpet low and attached. 3. How do I get Riccia Fluitans to pearl (produce tiny oxygen bubbles)? Pearling occurs when the plant undergoes rapid photosynthesis. Providing moderate-to-high lighting alongside steady CO2 injection and adequate liquid micro/macro nutrients will force Riccia to trap oxygen bubbles at its branch tips, creating a shimmering effect.

Plant Profile Rotala H'ra is a sought-after aquatic stem plant hailing from the Gia Lai province in the central highlands of Vietnam. A distinct geographic variant of Rotala rotundifolia , it's known for profuse, narrow, pointed foliage and a growth habit with a mind of its own: instead of growing politely upright like most stem plants, it overhangs, arches, and branches horizontally, doing its own thing. Under high-intensity lighting, pressurized CO2, and tuned fertilization, its foliage transforms into a breathtaking palette of fiery orange, salmon, and deep ruby-red, making it a stellar pick for sweeping midground bushes or dramatic background slopes. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Thin, pointed leaves develop vivid salmon, fiery orange, and intense red tones under high-tech aquarium conditions. Unique cascading and arching growth habit naturally forms lush, overhanging bushes. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. * Rotala leaves are thin and delicate, so handle stems with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide high-intensity lighting and pressurized CO2 (20–30 ppm); combining strong light and regular iron dosing yields the deepest fiery red and orange coloration. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or rotting. Trim stem tops or side shoots with curved scissors once they reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and expand coverage. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Plant Profile Java Fern Needle Leaf is a prized, ultra-narrow cultivar that is one of the rarest low-light aquarium plants available to aquascapers. Virtually bulletproof and delightfully unbothered by neglect, its ultra-thin fronds grow less than half an inch wide, thinner even than Java Fern Narrow Leaf variants, making it nearly impossible for hungry fish to ruin. It is hands-down one of the most mesmerizing aquarium plants for beginners, offering a soft, grass-like texture that anchors onto hardscape and sways gracefully in gentle water flow. Key Features & Notes Tough, fibrous foliage easily withstands curious nipping from herbivorous fish like cichlids, goldfish, and large snails. Ultra-thin, ribbon-like fronds create a fine-textured focal point or dense background contrast that softens hardscape layouts. Exceptional hardiness lets it thrive in non-CO2 tanks and low-light environments. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Java Fern Needle Leaf is an epiphytic fern that should be attached to rocks or driftwood with aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as it will rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard setups, gentle water movement and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and broader fronds. Master long-term care and troubleshoot common leaf issues by checking out our Java Fern Care Guide . Final size and foliage pattern depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Microsorum pteropus 'Needle Leaf' (syn. Leptochilus pteropus ) Common Name(s) Java Fern Needle Leaf, Needle Leaf Java Fern Family Polypodiaceae Plant Type Epiphyte (Rhizome Fern) Care Difficulty Beginner / Easy (Low-Tech Compatible) Light Requirement Low to Medium CO2 Requirement Not Required (Beneficial) Placement / Usage Midground, Background, Focal Hardscape Accent Height / Size 5"–12" (13–30 cm) Growth Rate Slow to Moderate Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 | Temperature 68°F–82°F (20°C–28°C) Propagation Method Rhizome Division & Adventitious Plantlets Origin Indonesia / Cultivated Rarity Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are there small black spots and tiny leaves growing under my Java Fern Needle Leaf leaves? Do not panic; your plant is not diseased! Java Fern reproduces naturally through adventitious plantlets. Small dark bumps (sporangia) form along the undersides of mature leaves, sprouting tiny brown roots and mini green fronds. Once these baby plantlets develop 3–4 leaves, you can gently pop them off the mother leaf and glue them elsewhere in your aquarium. 2. Can I plant Java Fern Needle Leaf into substrate? No. Java Fern Needle Leaf is an epiphyte that absorbs nutrients directly from the water column through its foliage and fine root network. If you bury its horizontal rhizome beneath aquarium soil, sand, or gravel, the stem will suffocate, rot, and die. Always attach it to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread. 3. Why is Java Fern Needle Leaf considered one of the best low light aquarium plants for beginners? Java Fern Needle Leaf is exceptionally resilient because it does not require specialized substrate, grows reliably under basic LED lighting, and tolerates a massive range of water conditions without needing pressurized CO2 injection. 4. Will fish like cichlids or goldfish eat Java Fern Needle Leaf? Generally, no. Java Fern leaves are thick, fibrous, and contain bitter taste compounds that deter most plant-eating fish. While aggressive diggers might knock it off hardscape if not glued securely, they rarely consume the foliage.

Common Name: Brazilian Pennywort Brazilian pennywort can be found growing in the wetlands and marshes of South America. It is characterized by its half-dollar like leaves which can grow into compact bushes of green. This plant is versatile and can be used in the foreground, midground or background. It is undemanding and grows fast, often out-competing and overgrowing the tank if left untrimmed. By frequently trimming new growth and using high light with CO2, the plant can stay low growing and create a carpeting effect over the foreground. Propagate by trimming stems and replanting on pulling apart dense clumps and splitting the roots. New shoots can be trimmed anywhere along the stem which allows the plant to grow thicker and more compact. This version is slightly variegated and can produce variations in color. Variegated species typically require more light when compared to the original species! Plant Profile If your scape is looking a bit static, don't fret! Weeping Moss is highly sought after for its distinct, downward-hanging growth habit that creates a stunning, cascading effect as it matures. While it makes a beautiful carpet on the substrate, its true calling is being wrapped around elevated driftwood branches or vertically stacked rocks to recreate a living green canopy or waterfall. Key Features & Benefits Signature drooping fronds create a soft, cascading waterfall effect. Dense, curtain-like canopy creates a sanctuary where fish and shrimp can forage. Loose portions can be tied, glued, or tucked into hardscape crevices. Care & Planting Instructions Place moss directly onto substrate for a rolling carpet, or secure to elevated hardscape using dark cotton thread or dabs of gel superglue. Maintain a stable aquarium environment and avoid sudden, drastic changes to your water parameters to keep your moss looking vibrant and healthy. Give the moss an occasional light haircut with sharp aquascaping shears to keep its shape neat, compact, and perfectly balanced. Propagate your patch in seconds by cutting or pulling a small clump apart and anchoring it to a new surface in your tank. Add CO2 injection if you want to accelerate growth and unlock the most intense, eye-popping green coloration possible. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I keep my Weeping Moss from turning brown or yellow? Weeping Moss prefers clean, moving water and cooler temperatures (under 78°F). Gently siphoning debris out during water changes will keep the inner growth green and healthy. 2. What is the best way to attach loose Weeping Moss to driftwood branches? Dabbing small dots of gel-based cyanoacrylate superglue (aquarium-safe superglue) directly onto dry hardscape points is the quickest method. Alternatively, wrapping the moss tightly with dark cotton thread allows it to anchor naturally over a few weeks while the thread dissolves. 3. How do I stop moss trimmings from spreading everywhere during maintenance? Always turn off your filter pumps and powerheads before trimming moss. Use sharp curved shears to make clean cuts, and immediately scoop or siphon out floating cuttings so they don't take root in unwanted areas of your aquarium.

Icelandic Lava Stone is widely considered the holy grail of volcanic rock, offering significantly more detail, density, and character than standard black lava . This natural rock features a deep, dark brown hue when submerged and a highly porous surface. Because of its intricate texture, it is a perfect pick for recreating dramatic, mountainous aquascaping layouts, and its porous nature provides an ideal surface for attaching mosses or housing beneficial nitrifying bacteria. Icelandic Lava Stone is also suitable for non-aquarium use and will work beautifully as a bold accent in terrariums, paludariums, or similar planted enclosures. Plant Profile Rorippa Aquatica, aka Water Cabbage, is a unique and captivating aquatic plant. Belonging to the mustard family (Brassicaceae), this undemanding plant features highly variable, bright green leaves that change shape depending on water flow, lighting, and temperature, ranging from deeply lobed, oak-like foliage to smooth, rounded leaves. Compact in stature, it provides a distinctive, cabbage-like visual texture that serves as a foreground accent or midground highlight in planted aquariums, paludariums, and cool-water setups. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Distinctive variable leaf shapes create a unique oak-like or cabbage-like texture. Hardy and adaptable across a wide range of water temperatures and parameters. Compact growth habit makes it ideal for nano aquariums, foreground groups, and midground transitions. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip lower foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower leaves. Provide moderate-to-high lighting and cooler water conditions; while CO2 is not strictly required, supplying pressurized CO2 and regular fertilization encourages faster growth. Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf melting during the transition period. To propagate, cut main stems or mature side shoots and replant them directly into the substrate; individual healthy leaves can also develop adventitious plantlets along their edges. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Why are the leaves on my Rorippa Aquatica changing shape? Rorippa Aquatica is heterophyllous, meaning its leaf structure varies based on environmental conditions. High lighting, strong CO2, and moderate currents produce deeply lobed, laciniate leaves, while lower lighting results in smoother, broader foliage. 2. Can Rorippa Aquatica be propagated from leaves? Yes! In addition to traditional stem cuttings, Rorippa Aquatica can produce adventitious plantlets directly from detached or mature leaves left floating in the aquarium. 3. Does Rorippa Aquatica require CO2 injection? No, Rorippa Aquatica is an easy-care plant that grows well in low-tech setups without CO2 injection. However, supplying CO2 and nutrient-rich soil results in faster growth and much more intricate foliage patterns.

Plant Profile If you're hunting for an uncommon collector's piece that won't make you sweat over strict water parameters, Cryptocoryne axelrodi is an absolute gem. Hailing from the lush tropical waters of Borneo, this elusive species stands out with its slender, strap-like leaves displaying an earthy, greenish-brown hue. As with all crypt plants, this plant can be sensitive to changes in water parameters and doesn’t like to be moved. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Slender greenish-brown foliage brings a rare, naturalistic texture to midground layouts. Uncommon species status makes it a highly sought-after addition for collectors. Resilient once established, thriving even in low-tech setups with minimal lighting. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Crypt species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I prepare this tissue culture plant? Rinse away the nutrient gel under lukewarm water to prevent algae or mold blooms, separate the plant mass into smaller portions, and plant directly into substrate using fine-tip pinsettes. 2. How do I help my Cryptocoryne recover if it melts? Trim away dissolving leaves, maintain stable water parameters, and leave the root system undisturbed so it can rebuild new foliage. Check our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt for full recovery steps. 3. Should I use root tabs or liquid fertilizers? Root tabs are best. Cryptocoryne species are heavy root feeders that draw primary nutrition from the substrate rather than the water column.

Plant Profile Common Name: Anubias Minima Variegated Unlike the classic short, rounded leaves of Anubias Nana, this stunning cultivar produces long, slender foliage with an architectural stretch. The real head-turner here is its striking "marble" variegation, a gorgeous blend of cream, white, and buttery yellow marbling splashed across every leaf as a result of selective propagation over time. Whether tucked into dark hardscape crevices, submerged in an aquarium, or showing off emersed in a humid terrarium, it delivers a high-end collector aesthetic with all the bulletproof hardiness you expect from the Anubias family. Key Features & Benefits Cream, white, and yellow marbled patterns create incredible contrast against dark rocks and green background plants. Long, slender leaf architecture offers a sleek, vertical texture that breaks up round or compact dwarf foliage. Thick leaves deter grazing from plant-eating fish, snails, and active dwarf shrimp. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Unlike its shade-loving green relatives, this variegated variety lacks abundant chlorophyll and requires medium to high lighting to thrive, flourish, and hold its snowy coloration. CO₂ is recommended to support healthy growth and maintain vibrant white coloration. Learn more about planting these species by reading our guide on How to Plant Epiphyte Aquatic Plants. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I plant Anubias Minima Variegated? Attach the plant directly to driftwood or rocks using aquarium-safe super glue gel, thread, or fishing line. Keep the rhizome above the substrate to prevent rot. 2. Does it require CO2 or high lighting? Yes. Unlike standard green Anubias, this variegated variety requires medium to high lighting because its white-marbled leaves lack heavy chlorophyll. It needs more light energy to photosynthesize effectively and maintain its crisp white pattern. CO2 injection is also recommended to support healthy growth and prevent melting. 3. Is this plant safe for shrimp, snails, and fish? Yes, Anubias is 100% safe for all freshwater fish, shrimp (including sensitive Caridina and Neocaridina), and snails. Its tough leaves are also resistant to plant-eating fish like cichlids or goldfish.

Pacific Driftwood brings a mature, untamed character to the planted tank, making it the ultimate choice if you are searching for natural, rugged aquarium driftwood. It’s the rebellious cousin to Malaysian wood, defined by deep knots, weathered tangles, and an aged, river‑worn look. That lived‑in texture makes it ideal for hardscapes that should read like century‑old timber hauled down a fast river. Instead of clean shapes, it offers a chaotic network of twists and crags that demand attention. Use it to build dramatic, wind‑swept river roots or a wild, overgrown jungle layout. Each piece is a unique puzzle of textured paths and hollowed grooves that really branch out your layout. Product Features & Benefits Pacific Wood features a highly textured surface with natural imperfections that provide a realistic, aged look. The unique knots and tangles in each piece provide excellent hiding spots for fry and shrimp, while offering plenty of surface area for beneficial bacteria and biofilm to flourish. Because it offers more "twist" than standard logs but more "bulk" than Spiderwood, it is the ultimate middle-ground for a professional planted aquarium hardscape. Size Specifications Photos provided are a representation of what you will receive. As Pacific Wood is a natural aquarium hardscape product, please expect variations in shape, weight, and character. Extra Small: 6-8 inches Small: 8-12 inches Medium: 12-16 inches Large: 16-20 inches Extra Large: 20-26 inches Preparation & Care Pacific Driftwood is a natural product and requires a bit of prep before it’s ready for prime time. Rinse: Thoroughly rinse the piece to remove any dust or debris from transit. The Floating Phase: Unlike Malaysian wood, Pacific Driftwood is buoyant. It will float initially. To keep it from bobbing like a cork, we recommend soaking it thoroughly or boiling it. A large stone or heavy decor may be placed on top to ensure a non-waterlogged piece of wood stays submerged. Tannin Management: This wood will release natural tannins, giving your water a warm, "tea-colored" tint. This is a natural occurrence, and the effects will subside over time. If you prefer the crystal-clear look, boil the wood for 1–2 hours or soak it in a separate container until the water runs clear. You can also reduce this effect through consistent water changes or through the addition of Aquario Neo Carbon Bag Important note: We recommend rinsing wood thoroughly before adding it to an established aquarium. If you prefer, you may also boil the wood for at least 1–2 hours to help release tannins.

Product Overview Make choosing the right piece easy with our WYSIWYG (What You See Is What You Get) Driftwood Showpieces. Plant Profile Rotala Nanjenshan is a delicate natural hybrid aquatic stem plant originating near Nanjenshan, Taiwan. Believed to be a natural cross between Rotala rotundifolia and Rotala wallichii , this unique species combines the hardy growth habit of Rotundifolia with the fine, needle-like leaf structure of Wallichii. Featuring dense whorls of slender, hair-like leaves along flexible stems, it displays a vibrant lime-green coloration that blushes soft pink, orange, and yellow-gold at the growing tips under high-tech aquarium conditions. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Needle-like foliage adds soft, cloud-like texture to midground and background zones. Hybrid origin gives lime-green foliage with blush-pink, gold, and orange growing tips under high lighting. Fast-branching growth perfect for dense hedges and Dutch-style streets with routine pruning. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. * Rotala leaves are fragile, so handle stems with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide medium-to-high lighting and soft, acidic water conditions (pH 5.0–7.0); mandatory pressurized CO2 injection and consistent fertilization with iron are essential to maintain needle density and induce pinkish growing tips. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim main stem tops with straight scissors once stems reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and thicken your bush. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Rotala sp. 'Nanjenshan' Common Name(s) Rotala Nanjenshan, Nanjenshan Rotala Family Lythraceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Stem Plant (Natural Hybrid) Care Difficulty Moderate Light Requirement Medium to High CO2 Requirement Required (Essential for dense, needle-like whorls) Placement / Usage Midground / Background Bushing Height / Size 5–10”+ Growth Rate Fast Water Parameters pH 5.0–7.0 | Soft Acidic Water Preferred Propagation Method Cuttings (Cut stem and replant tops) Origin Asia (Taiwan) Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I get pink and gold growing tips on Rotala Nanjenshan? While Rotala Nanjenshan stays bright green under moderate conditions, developing soft pink, orange, and gold growing tips requires high light intensity, pressurized CO2, soft acidic water, and consistent dosing of liquid micro and macronutrients, particularly iron. 3. How do I prepare Rotala Nanjenshan Tissue Culture before planting? Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the dense cluster into smaller clumps or individual stem bundles and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

Hygrophila Pinnatifida is a unique plant that originates from India. The leaves can range from brown, purple, red, green or yellow depending on the conditions that its kept in. This plant does best under high lighting with Co2 and fertilization. It has been reported to be susceptible to potassium deficiency, distinguished by small holes in the older leaves. This versatile plant can be grown submerged or emersed, with soil and without. We have tried planting stems directly into soil as well as gluing onto rock/wood. In both instances, the stems will eventually root and anchor itself. Under high lighting, the stems generally stay shorter and more compact while sending out lateral shoots which can be cut and replanted or simply left alone to grow. Cutting the stems horizontally can work as well but in our experience, new growth tends to take longer. Notes: Tissue culture plants are grown in vitro from a state of the art laboratory specialized in propagating aquatic plants. They provide the best option for those who want to ensure that absolutely zero unwanted pests are introduced into the aquarium. Remove tissue culture gel before planting. Simply wash the gel away or soak the plant in water and squeeze the gel off with your fingers. Do not make drastic changes to the aquarium. Unstable parameters will result in melt and rotting of the aquarium plant. For instructions on how to properly plant tissue culture aquarium plants, click here . CO2 injection and quality aquarium soil will yield better growth. Family Name: Acanthaceae Origin: India Height: 5-8” pH: 6-7.5 Care: Medium Light: Medium to High Co2: Recommended Propagation: Cut stem, new growth, or lateral shoots Growth rate: Moderate

Plant Profile Rotala Narrow Leaf Sp. Red is the ultimate cure for a boring, all-green aquascape. Featuring slender leaves that pack a punch of rich red foliage, this vibrant stem plant is a classic staple for Dutch-style layouts and nature aquariums looking for instant color contrast. Crank up the lighting to medium-high, feed it pressurized CO2 with some routine nutrient dosing, and it will happily explode into dense, bushy midground or background clusters before you know it. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Delivers vibrant red coloration and slender leaf texture, making it an ideal background focal point for Dutch-style aquascapes. Fast-growing stem branches into dense bushes through routine pruning, absorbing excess water column nutrients. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip the lower inch of foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. * Rotala has fragile leaves, so handle stems with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push stems 1–2 inches into soil, spacing them apart for light penetration. Provide medium-to-high lighting, pressurized CO2, and balanced water column nutrients. Maintain adequate phosphates (1.5–2.0 ppm) and lean nitrates (10 ppm or less) to maximize deep red tones and prevent stunted growth. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid drastic environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the surface to encourage branching and prevent lower leaves from being shaded out. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when light cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I keep Rotala Narrow Leaf Red looking intensely red? In addition to strong light and pressurized CO2, Rotala Narrow Leaf Red requires specific nutrient balancing to achieve peak red coloration: maintain phosphate levels around 1.5–2.0 ppm while keeping nitrates low (10 ppm or less). Nitrate limitation combined with sufficient iron triggers maximum anthocyanin pigment production. 3. How do I transition Rotala Narrow Leaf Red from emersed to submerged growth? When transitioning from emersed to submerged growth, plant bare stems securely into rich substrate under medium-to-high lighting and keep water parameters stable. As new growth adapts, the plant will shed its rounded land leaves and sprout slender, colorful underwater foliage. Once new shoots develop, trim away old lower growth to encourage dense, bushy branching.

Plant Profile A rare, variegated cultivar of classic Anubias Nana, Anubias Pinto brings striking white-and-green marbled leaves to low-tech planted aquariums. This cultivated gem is the product of generations of careful artificial selection, resulting in a splashy, marbled mosaic of deep green and crisp white on every single leaf. Lacking chlorophyll in its white sections, this dwarf variety requires medium to high light to photosynthesize efficiently and maintain its bright coloration. Reaching a compact 2 to 5 inches, it serves as a dramatic contrast when nestled against dark lava rock, rich driftwood, or deep green mosses in the foreground or midground of aquascapes. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Unique, marbled white-and-green variegated foliage ensures every leaf boasts a distinct pattern. Compact 2-to-5-inch dwarf footprint fits into nano tanks, midground crevices, and detailed hardscapes. Sterile lab-grown tissue culture format guarantees a 100% clean plant free of pest snails and unwanted algae. Care & Planting Instructions Remove the plantlets from the cup and rinse away the sterile nutrient gel under lukewarm, dechlorinated water. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Because its white leaf patches lack chlorophyll, this variety requires medium to high lighting to perform photosynthesis efficiently, stay healthy, and maintain its bold variegated patterns! Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Provide optional carbon dioxide injection to achieve faster growth and more robust leaves. Master the prep and planting process by checking out a beginner's guide to tissue culture plants to prevent your delicate new plantlets from melting or floating away. Yes, compared to green varieties, Anubias Nana Pinto requires medium lighting and benefits from CO2. Its tough leaves are also resistant to plant-eating fish like cichlids or goldfish.

listings.description: Plant Profile Dwarf Hygrophila Corymbosa 'Siamensis' (commonly called Dwarf Hygrophila) is a compact, fast-growing aquatic stem plant native to Southeast Asia. Known for its narrow, lance-shaped bright green leaves and dense branching habit, it brings a clean, lush look to midground and background zones. This hardy, beginner-friendly, and low-tech species adapts easily to a wide range of freshwater parameters, growing reliably both submerged in aquariums and emersed in humid terrariums. Reaching up to 12 inches in height, it forms thick bushes with routine pruning and offers great contrast alongside fine-leaved or red stem plants. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Compact, lance-shaped bright green foliage branches densely into lush midground or background bushes. Hardy, beginner-friendly stem plant thrives in low-tech setups across a wide range of water conditions. Adapts smoothly to fully submerged aquariums or emersed growth in humid terrariums. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small portions or individual stems 1 inch apart into your aquarium soil so light reaches the lower leaves. Provide moderate to high lighting; while CO2 is not required, adding pressurized CO2 and balanced liquid fertilizers accelerates growth and keeps stems full. Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf shedding during the initial transition period. To propagate, trim main stem tops or side shoots with sharp straight shears and replant the cuttings directly into your aquarium soil. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. listings.description: Plant Profile Rotala Green is a classic and highly beloved aquatic stem plant native to the tropical waterways of Southeast Asia. Unlike standard Rotala rotundifolia variations that turn pink or red under high light, Rotala Green retains its vibrant, fresh lime-green coloration even under intense lighting and CO2. Featuring supple central stems lined with delicate, rounded leaves, it exhibits a distinct weeping or drooping growth habit as it reaches toward the light. Prolific and fast-growing, it readily branches after pruning, making it an ideal choice for sculpting dense, rolling background hedges. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Vibrant, fresh lime-green foliage maintains its clean green color under all lighting conditions. Drooping or creeping stem habit branches aggressively when pruned to form thick, sweeping background hedges. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. * Rotala leaves are fragile, so handle stems with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide high-intensity lighting and pressurized CO2 injection (20–30 ppm); consistent fertilization with a liquid macro and micro formula yields robust growth and prevents lower leaf yellowing. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or rotting. Trim main stem tops with sharp straight scissors once they reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and thicken the bush. Plant Profile Ardisia sp. 'Tricolor Type 1' stands out from the forest floor with a distinct blend of deep olive, blush pink, and pale green mapped across prominent leaf veins. Belonging to a massive genus of over 700 species across tropical Asia, this is an obligate terrestrial shrub built entirely for air and damp soil. Tucked between dark lava rock or anchored near the base of driftwood roots, its patterned foliage adds genuine visual depth against solid green moss carpets. Key Features & Notes Showcases patterned multi-toned foliage highlighted by bold, pale venation across the leaf surface. Demands steady humidity above 70% to prevent the decorative leaf edges from drying and curling. Care & Planting Instructions Tuck the cutting or root base into a loose, airy tropical mix of perlite, tree fern fiber, and orchid bark along midground pockets or bank zones shared with paludarium plants. Provide partial shade or moderate indirect lighting, shielding the leaves from intense grow lights that will bleach out the tri-tone coloration. Maintain humidity above 70% in enclosed setups while ensuring the root zone drains freely, as waterlogged soil leads to stem rot. Trim older or damaged lower leaves at the stem base using clean shears to encourage fresh shoots and maintain good air circulation. Note that you will receive a live cutting with 2 to 4 leaves that will root and establish steadily under stable high humidity. Ardisia species are terrestrial plants, and being submerged will result in the death of the plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Ardisia sp. Can Ardisia sp. Tricolor Type 1 grow submerged in an aquarium? No. Ardisia species are terrestrial shrubs. Submerging them underwater will suffocate the leaves, cause the stem to rot, and result in the death of the plant. 2. Why are the edges of my Ardisia leaves turning brown? Crispy or browning leaf edges typically indicate that ambient humidity has dropped below 70% or the plant is sitting in a dry draft. Keep it inside an enclosed setup to maintain consistent moisture. 3. How do you propagate Ardisia sp. Tricolor Type 1? Take a healthy stem cutting containing 2 to 4 leaves and set the lower node into damp sphagnum moss inside a warm, covered container until fresh roots develop.

Plant Profile Ardisia sp. Tricolor Type 2 is a tropical plant featuring textured leaves patterned in shades of rose-red, olive green, and silver-tinted venation. A solid choice for emersed setups, its mottled red and green leaves break up solid green moss walls and stand out against lighter driftwood along the floor or midground of a tank, as well as damp terrestrial banks in a paludarium. New emergent leaves often flush with the deepest red and bronze tones before maturing into complex mottled patterns as the foliage thickens. Key Features & Notes Textured, multi-toned foliage displays striking reddish hues and contrasting network venation. Requires sustained high humidity and airy, well-draining substrate to prevent leaf margin browning. Sturdy growth makes it an ideal midground or background anchor in larger terrariums, vivariums, or paludariums. Care & Planting Instructions Press the stem cutting or root system gently into a loose, airy tropical substrate mix rich in bark, tree fern fiber, and perlite; never bury crowns in compacted soil. Maintain ambient humidity above 75% in enclosed setups to keep sensitive leaf margins from drying out or crisping. Prune tall growth tips just above a node using sharp shears to encourage compact lateral branching and maintain manageable height. Note that you will receive a live cutting with 2 to 4 leaves that will root and establish steadily under stable high humidity. Final size and leaf coloration depend entirely on your specific setup conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Gently siphoning debris out during regular water changes will keep the inner growth green and healthy. 2. How do I use the stainless steel mesh pad in my aquascape? The stainless steel mesh pad is naturally weighted to sink right out of the box. You can lay it completely flat on your substrate for an instant carpet, bend the flexible metal around curved rocks or wood, or attach it vertically to glass to start a full moss wall backdrop. 3. How do I stop moss trimmings from spreading everywhere during maintenance? Always turn off your filter pumps and powerheads before trimming moss. Use sharp curved shears to make clean cuts, and immediately scoop or siphon out floating cuttings so they don't take root in unwanted areas of your aquarium.

Plant Profile Bacopa Australis is a relatively rare and highly desirable aquatic stem plant native to Central and South America (despite its species name referring to southern Brazil). Less common than its popular relatives Bacopa monnieri and Bacopa caroliniana , it features bright green, roundish leaves that closely resemble Micranthemum umbrosum , but with a much hardier and easier care profile. When planted in groups, Bacopa Australis forms soft, dense midground or background bushes that adapt easily to low-tech tanks. When cultivated emersed in paludariums or open-top setups, it produces delicate, tiny pink and white flowers above the surface. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Small, soft green leaves that create a lush, compact bush effect in planted aquariums. Hardy and beginner-friendly species that thrives in low-tech setups while absorbing excess water column nutrients. Blooms charming pink and white flowers when grown emersed in open-top aquariums, paludariums, or terrariums. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip lower foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. * Bacopa leaves can be fragile, so handle stems with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower leaves. Provide moderate-to-high lighting for steady growth, as higher light levels keep the lower stem sections healthy and dense. Maintain stable water parameters and clean water conditions; while CO2 injection is not required, it yields faster growth. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the desired height, and replant the trimmings directly into the substrate to propagate. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. listings.commonName: Lilaeopsis Mauritiana Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Lilaeopsis Mauritiana, better known as the Narrow Leaf Micro Sword, is a sleek and elegant variant of the classic Lilaeopsis Brasiliensis . Hailing natively from the island of Mauritius, this species features distinctly thinner, needle-like leaves that bring a lighter, finer texture to your foreground. If you love the classic look of a grass lawn but want something that offers a more delicate silhouette, this plant is a great choice. It spreads reliably across the substrate, working efficiently to weave a thick, vibrant green carpet. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Establish a soft foreground texture with its ultra-thin, narrow-leaf profile. Enjoy a faster growth rate compared to standard Lilaeopsis Brasiliensis varieties. The sterile laboratory environment guarantees your new plant arrives completely free of pests. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions and planting. Separate into small clumps and press them compactly into a quality aquarium soil to give the roots the perfect head start. Maintain stable aquarium parameters and avoid drastic shifts in water quality to prevent your new grass from melting. Provide medium to high lighting and inject pressurized CO2 to supercharge its density and growth rate, keeping it low and compact. Loved for its easy-going nature, this specific variety of Dwarf Hairgrass is highly sought after because it naturally grows very short and stays beautifully low to the ground with just a little help from regular trimming. It spreads smoothly across your substrate by sending out eager horizontal runners, making it an all-around solid foreground choice that scales perfectly into any aquarium size, from nano cubes to massive displays. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Separate into small clumps and press them compactly into a quality aquarium soil to give the roots the perfect head start. Use a dry start method or Wabi Kusa setup to give its root system plenty of time to firmly anchor into the substrate before you flood the tank. listings.commonName: Pearl Moss Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Pearl Moss is a moss-t have for any small-scale setup, proving that good things come in small packages. While most aquarium mosses grow with long, fuzzy fronds, this species is actually a terrestrial moss relative that has adapted beautifully to life underwater. It is famous for its exceptionally tiny, round leaves that stack tightly together, giving the plant a delicate, glistening look reminiscent of miniature strands of green pearls. Because of this diminutive, slow-growing habit, it's a great pick for nano tanks where larger mosses would quickly overwhelm the layout. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Incredibly small, round leaves stack tightly together to maintain proper scale in nano aquascapes. Unique leaf structure catches light to create a glistening, pearl-like texture and visual depth. Care & Planting Instructions Rinse away the nutrient gel thoroughly under lukewarm water, separate into small portions, and tie or glue onto hardscape. Maintain a stable aquarium environment and keep temperatures cool (65°F–78°F) to prevent stress, browning, or melting. Give the moss an occasional light haircut with sharp aquascaping shears to keep its shape neat, compact, and perfectly balanced. Propagate your patch in seconds by cutting or pulling a small clump apart and anchoring it to a new surface in your tank. Add CO2 injection if you want to accelerate growth and unlock the most intense, eye-popping green coloration possible. Master the prep and planting process by checking out a beginner's guide to tissue culture plants to prevent your delicate new plantlets from melting or floating away. This unique liverwort grows in thick, bright green, interlocking mats that look absolutely striking under bright lights. Because it is rootless, it can either be left free-floating at the surface or tied and glued down to rocks, driftwood, or stainless steel mesh to form a bubbling green carpet. Under strong lighting and a steady supply of carbon dioxide, it will routinely trap oxygen bubbles right at its leaf tips, producing a breathtaking, shimmering phenomenon known as "pearling." Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. Functions as a floating surface cover for fry or a dense foreground carpet when tied to hardscape. Maintain a stable aquarium environment and trim regularly to prevent the lower layers from dying off and floating away. Give the plant an occasional light haircut with sharp aquascaping shears to keep its shape neat, compact, and perfectly balanced. Propagate your patch in seconds by cutting or pulling a small clump apart and anchoring it to a new surface in your tank. Add CO2 injection if you want to accelerate growth and unlock the most intense, eye-popping green coloration possible. listings.commonName: Alternanthera Reineckii 'Mini' Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Alternanthera Reineckii 'Mini', widely known in the hobby as AR Mini, is a compact dwarf cultivar of the iconic South American stem plant. Famous for its intense, ruby-to-magenta red foliage and low-growing, bushy structure, AR Mini is a staple focal point in both Dutch-style aquascapes and nature aquariums. Reaching a manageable height of just 3 to 4 inches, its compact size allows it to be used flexibly as a bold red foreground carpet, a dense midground transition, or a colorful accent in nano aquariums. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Crimson and magenta red foliage adds color contrast to foreground, midground, or nano tank layouts. Compact growth forms dense, bushy red carpets and low hedges, needing less frequent height pruning. Dense leaf structure gives cover and shelter for dwarf shrimp and timid fish species. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide medium-to-high lighting. Regular dosing of liquid fertilizers like UNS Plant Food (2–3 times per week) and pressurized CO2 injection are highly recommended to yield maximum crimson coloration and prevent stunted growth. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim stem tops or side shoots with curved scissors once stems reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and thicken the carpet. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. listings.commonName: Java Fern on Coco Fiber Mat
listings.description: Plant Profile Java Fern on Coco Fiber Mat offers an extra-dense, pre-mounted mat display designed to create an instant lush backdrop or carpet without the tedious labor of tying or gluing individual rhizomes. Pre-bound to a natural, aquarium-safe coconut fiber pad, this arrangement delivers a wall of broad emerald fronds that easily ranks among the most reliable low-light aquarium plants in the hobby. Virtually bulletproof and delightfully unbothered by tough water conditions or plant-grazing fish, it rests naturally over bare substrate or wedged against hardscape to provide immediate structure. Key Features & Notes Tough foliage withstands curious nipping from herbivorous fish like cichlids, goldfish, and large snails. Pre-attached to a flexible, natural coconut fiber mat, allowing for effortless placement across substrate or hardscape without gluing or tying. Exceptional hardiness lets it thrive in non-CO2 tanks and low-light environments. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by rinsing the coco fiber mat gently in clean freshwater to clear any loose debris before placing it directly into your aquarium. Java Fern on Coco Fiber Mat is an epiphytic fern pre-bound to hardscape that should be rested directly on top of substrate or hardscape ; never bury the horizontal rhizome beneath sand or soil, as it will rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard setups, gentle water movement and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and broader fronds. Master long-term care and troubleshoot common leaf issues by checking out our Java Fern Care Guide . Final size and foliage pattern depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual mat shapes or foliage densities may vary. Because the plant is already bound firmly to a weighted mat pad, it is also much harder for energetic fish to uproot.

Because it develops these wide, flat fronds rather than thin needles, it provides an incredible amount of surface area for biofilm to colonize. Plant Profile This is the dark variant of the Skeleton King AKA Dark Achilles. This Bucephalandra is well-titled as the true King of all Buce! This striking aquarium plant features large, thick leaves with prominently raised veins that create a dark, skeletal appearance as they sprout upward from a thick base rhizome. It is a moderately sized plant and forms a compact rosette with leaves held slightly upward and outward, creating the bold look this variety is known for. Highly versatile, it can be grown submerged or emersed, though it is important to note that many hobbyists report leaf melt while transitioning to submerged conditions. Plant Profile Aridarum caulescens 'Sabertooth' is a rare, compact aquarium plant native to the fast-moving waterfalls and boulder-strewn streams of Borneo. Smaller in stature than 'White Fang', this species features slender, sword-shaped leaves with a thick, waxy texture that evolved specifically to hold up against turbulent currents in the wild. Its narrow foliage sprouts tightly from a central creeping rhizome, making it a great natural choice for fine detailing in the foreground, tucking into tight stone crevices, or securing along driftwood. Whether you're growing it submerged in an aquarium or emersed in a humid terrarium setup, make sure the rhizome stays completely exposed to open water and air, because burying it in substrate is a fast track to rot. Key Features & Notes Tough, waxy leaf blades naturally withstand high-flow areas and resist damage from nibbling fish or snails. Petite, narrow foliage creates a sharp, textured contrast when clustered alongside rounded leaves like Anubias Nana Petite or Bucephalandra. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from its pot and clearing all rockwool from the root base . Aridarum is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While hardy and low-maintenance in basic setups, consistent water movement and pressurized CO2 injection will yield faster growth and denser foliage. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. How do I mount Aridarum Sabertooth to hardscape? Gently clean away the rockwool from around the roots, then attach the rhizome directly to porous stone or driftwood using a small drop of aquarium-safe glue or dark cotton thread. Its roots will gradually spread and lock onto the surface. 2. Why are the leaves on my Aridarum Sabertooth melting? Rapid swings in water parameters, light levels, or temperature can cause an initial acclimation melt. Keep conditions stable and provide decent water circulation; as long as the rhizome stays firm and green, it will produce new leaves adapted to your setup. 3. Can I plant Aridarum Sabertooth in substrate? You can let the roots trail down into the soil or gravel to feed, but the central rhizome must sit fully exposed above the substrate line. If you bury that rhizome under gravel or aquasoil, it suffocates and turns to mush.

Plant Profile If you want to add some serious heat to your aquascape without actually burning anything down, we have the moss for you. Flame Moss is known for its upward-pointing attitude, growing in spiraling, vertical shoots that mimic flickering flames. Because of this unique growth habit, it is the ultimate design tool for adding eye-catching vertical texture along your foreground, around the base of driftwood, or as a highly organized carpeting plant. Key Features & Benefits Vertically twisting growth habit resembles flickering flames, adding height to horizontal surfaces. Provides safe hiding, shelter, and grazing areas for freshwater shrimp and nano fish. Easily attached to driftwood, rocks, or aquascaping crevices using thread or gel. Care & Planting Instructions Press the portion gently into your substrate, or secure it to your hardscape using dark thread or dabs of aquarium-safe superglue gel. Maintain a stable aquarium environment and avoid sudden, drastic changes to your water parameters to keep your moss looking vibrant and healthy. Give the moss an occasional light haircut with sharp aquascaping shears to keep its shape neat, compact, and perfectly balanced. Propagate your patch in seconds by cutting or pulling a small clump apart and anchoring it to a new surface in your tank. Add CO2 injection if you want to accelerate growth and unlock the most intense, eye-popping green coloration possible. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I keep my Flame Moss from turning brown or yellow? Flame Moss prefers clean, moving water and cooler temperatures (under 78°F). Browning usually occurs when organic debris gets trapped inside the dense, vertical shoots or when water temperatures run too high. Gently siphoning debris out during water changes will keep the inner growth green and healthy. 2. What is the best way to attach loose Flame Moss to driftwood or rocks? Dabbing small dots of gel-based cyanoacrylate superglue (aquarium-safe superglue) directly onto dry hardscape points is the quickest method. Alternatively, wrapping the moss tightly with dark cotton thread allows it to anchor naturally over a few weeks while the thread dissolves. 3. How do I stop moss trimmings from spreading everywhere during maintenance? Always turn off your filter pumps and powerheads before trimming moss. Use sharp curved shears to make clean cuts, and immediately scoop or siphon out floating cuttings so they don't take root in unwanted areas of your aquarium.

Do you have BBA algae in your planted aquarium? Commonly known as black beard algae, this type of algae typically appears when maintenance is not consistent or thorough enough. Black beard algae attaches and grows on hardscape and can also be found on the leaf edges of slow-growing aquarium plants. Notorious for being one of the most difficult algae to deal with, SL Aqua Z3 BBA Remover aims to eradicate it! This product contains a special formula that works to slow down reproduction and kill spores to eventually remove BBA effectively over time. SL Aqua Z3 BBA Remover will also help with filamentous, blue and brown algae strain removal as well. Pair this product with a consistent maintenance routine and algae problems will be a thing of the past. SL Aqua's Z3 BBA Remover is safe for freshwater applications and will not harm aquarium plants or fish if dosage instructions are followed. Want to learn more about how to get rid of Black Beard Algae? Click for How to Get Rid of Black Beard Algae in the Fish Tank . Notes: For freshwater use only. Do not use in aquariums containing invertebrates or snails. Should be used in addition to a consistent maintenance routine. Please follow dosage guidelines provided below. Volume: 20ml Shelf life: Use within 6 months of opening. Usage Instructions: 2 drops PER 6.6G once per day for 2 weeks. Affected algae will turn white. Perform a minimum of 30% water change every 7 days. Once the 2 week treatment period is up, add 2 drops PER 6.6G once a week for precaution (optional).

listings.description: Plant Profile Circular, umbrella-like green leaves give Hydrocotyle Verticillata its distinct miniature mushroom or lily-pad appearance underwater. Commonly called Whorled Pennywort or Shield Pennywort, this creeping species originates from bogs, marshes, and damp riverbanks across North and South America. Its runner-based growth habit allows it to creep horizontally across the substrate to form foreground carpets or fill gaps in midground aquascapes. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Distinct circular, umbrella-like leaves create unique geometric texture in foreground and midground areas. Adapts smoothly to fully submerged aquariums or emersed growth in humid terrariums. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small portions or individual runner segments 1 inch apart into your aquarium soil, anchoring the root base securely. Provide medium to high lighting; while adaptable without CO2, supplying pressurized CO2 and regular liquid nutrients encourages faster creeping growth and smaller leaf sizes. Maintain stable water chemistry to encourage steady runner development and prevent leaf melting during transition. To propagate, snip horizontal runner stems into sections with sharp shears and replant the runner nodes directly into your aquarium soil to expand carpet coverage. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Once clean, divide the cluster into small clumps or individual runner sections and insert the roots into your aquarium soil using fine pinsettes. 2. How do I keep Hydrocotyle Verticillata low-growing for a carpet layout? Providing high lighting and pressurized CO2 keeps stalks short while pushing horizontal runner growth. Regularly trimming away tall vertical stalks forces the plant to send out low shoots across your aquarium soil. 3. How does Hydrocotyle Verticillata differ from Hydrocotyle Tripartita 'Japan'? While Hydrocotyle tripartita produces clover-like three-lobed leaves that form dense creeping mats, Hydrocotyle verticillata features completely round, peltate umbrella leaves on individual vertical stalks.

Common Name: Ludwigia Marilia Ludwigia Marilia originates from Marilia in the Brazilian states of Sao Paulo. Currently, the exact species of Ludwigia Marilia has not yet been determined. When grown submerged, the leaves are round and can be green with hues of red and orange. Red and orange colors are intensified and concentrated in the shoot tips when grown with high light and CO2 injection. Similar to other Ludwigia species, Ludwigia Marilia can be transitioned to grow emersed above water. When grown emersed, leaves will become more compact and colors may differ. When given the ideal environment, Ludwigia Marilia are considered fast growers. For aquascaping, it is recommended that Ludwigia Marilia be grown in the background to help with coverage and depth. Regular trimming will help keep Ludwigia Marilia compact, and these trimmings can be replanted into substrate for propagation. Notes Ludwigia Marilia can be grown both, submerged and emersed Ludwigia can be very fragile. Be sure to handle this aquarium plant with care. Do not make drastic changes to the aquarium. Unstable parameters will result in melt and rotting of the aquarium plant. CO2 injection and quality aquarium soil will yield better growth. Ludwigia Marilia’s final size, coloration and growth rate are dependent upon the condition of the environment. Photos are a representation of what you will receive and may vary. Please research appropriately to ensure your plant thrives. Plant Profile Rotala Manipurensis is a rare aquatic stem plant native to Southeast Asia and northeastern India. Its leaves narrow into fine, feather-like whorls that blush orange, salmon, and bright pink when grown under high-tech aquarium conditions. Once established, it grows quickly and fills in with dense, layered stems, working well as a midground or background species that adds structural depth, soft movement, and warm color contrast against greener aquascape plants. It's a good pick for aquascapers looking to break up an all-green layout without reaching for the more common red Rotala varieties. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Narrow, fine-textured foliage shifts into striking orange and pink tones under high-intensity lighting and tuned fertilization. Fast vertical growth fills in space and branches into dense hedges with routine pruning. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip the lower inch of foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. * Rotala Manipurensis has fragile leaves, so handle stems with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower foliage. Provide high-intensity lighting, pressurized CO2 injection, and nutrient-rich aquarium soil; adding liquid iron supplementation is key to developing vivid orange and pink coloration. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters (72–84°F) and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the water surface to keep growth compact, and replant trimmings directly into soil to propagate. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I get my Rotala Manipurensis to display bright orange and pink colors? To bring out its signature orange and pink leaf tones, provide high light intensity, pressurized CO2 injection, quality aquarium soil, and regular iron dosing. Lower light levels will cause the plant to remain predominantly olive-green. 3. How do I transition Rotala Manipurensis from emersed to submerged growth? When transitioning from emersed to submerged growth, plant bare stems securely into rich substrate under high lighting and keep water parameters stable. As new growth adapts, the plant will shed its rounded land leaves and sprout narrow, delicate orange-pink underwater foliage. Once new shoots develop, trim away old lower growth to encourage dense branching.

Plant Profile Nesaea Triflora is an eye-catching stem plant native to tropical island regions across Madagascar, Sri Lanka, and Mauritius. What makes this species special is its foliage pattern, featuring smooth, oblong green leaves that sprout in neat pairs along vibrant reddish-pink stems. Deep red veins run through the center of each leaf blade, creating a sharp two-tone color contrast right against the bright green foliage. Reaching up to 8 inches in height, its vertical stems bring organized geometry and warm color tones to midground and background zones. Key Features & Benefits Reddish-pink stems and leaf veins contrast against smooth green leaf blades for a clean two-tone look. Growth habit provides clean structural lines in midground and background layouts. Color shifts from olive-green to rich amber and copper-red under high-intensity lighting and CO2. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip the lower inch of foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push stems 1–2 inches into soil, spacing them apart for light penetration. Provide medium to high lighting and pressurized CO2 injection; consistent liquid fertilization rich in iron highlights the red stem and leaf vein coloration. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf shedding or stem melting during the initial transition period. To propagate, trim main stem tops with sharp straight shears and replant the cuttings directly into your aquarium soil to build a bushier stem group.
