Common name: Ardisia Dino Ardisia Dino is one of 700 species of Ardisia, that originate from Asia. The leaves of Ardisia Dino are large and broad. The name Ardisia Dino comes from its unique reptilian like texture, that will certainly be an eye catcher in any tank! Colors range from light to dark green leaves that have a radiating iridescent sheen. The colors will change depending on the conditions in which the plants are grown in. Originating from tropical rainforest, Ardisia Dino does best in humid and wet environments. The soil should never be allowed to completely dry but be careful not to over water. Over watering can cause root or stem rot, that may lead to death of the plant. Ardisia Dino grows best under bright indirect light. Leaves that are exposed to intense direct light, have a high chance of being burned and damaged. Due to these requirements and growth patterns, Ardisia Dino are best suited as a background plant for terrarium and paludarium set ups. Notes: Ardisia species are terrestrial plants and being submerged will result in death of the plants. Ardisia species should be grown in humid conditions with indirect light. Plants may grow differently depending on the environment in which they are grown in. Additional research should be done to provide optimum growing conditions for the plant to thrive. You will receive a cutting with 2-4 leaves. Photos are a representation of what you will receive. Size, shape and color may vary as this is a live plant. Family Name: Primulaceae Origin: Asia Size: Varies Care: Intermediate Light: Partial Shade Water: Medium Growth rate: Slow

Plant Profile Ardisia Silver is characterized by slender, elongated leaves with serrated margins and a prominent silvery streak running along the central midrib. Strictly suited for emersed conditions, its distinct pale midvein and deep green leaf blades contrast cleanly against dark lava rock, driftwood roots, and solid carpet mosses. While the genus Ardisia contains over 700 recognized species spanning tropical rainforests worldwide, this form stands out for its dynamic leaf development: new growth emerges in a pale, soft green before darkening over time, which makes the silvery central pattern appear sharper and more pronounced over time. Key Features & Notes Elongated serrated foliage develops a pronounced silver streak down the main midrib as it matures. Requires consistent ambient humidity and aerated soil to avoid leaf margin browning and root suffocation. Care & Planting Instructions Press the stem cutting or root base into a loose, airy mix of bark, tree fern fiber, and perlite, taking care not to compact the substrate tightly around the stem. Provide bright indirect or partially shaded light; harsh direct light can scorch the foliage and cause irreversible leaf burn. Maintain ambient humidity above 75% in enclosed setups while ensuring the root zone drains freely, as waterlogged soil can lead to stem and root rot. Prune tall growth tips just above a leaf node using clean shears to encourage compact lateral shoots and maintain balanced scale. Note that you will receive a live cutting with 2 to 4 leaves that will root and establish steadily under stable high humidity. Ardisia species are terrestrial plants, and being submerged will result in the death of the plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Take a healthy stem cutting containing 2 to 4 leaves using clean shears and anchor the lower node into damp sphagnum moss under high humidity until roots form.

Plant Profile Ardisia sp. 'Blue' brings a moody, metallic presence to emersed setups, sporting slender lanceolate leaves washed in a waxy steel-blue sheen with vivid red undersides. Wedged between weathered stones or anchored in driftwood crevices, that cool blue tone cuts right through uniform beds of green plants. Fun fact: that blue cast is pure structural color created by microscopic cell layers that scatter light, an adaptation wild understory species use to soak up faint, filtered rays beneath dense jungle canopies. Keep it under soft, indirect light, and it holds a clean, compact silhouette inside any humid terrarium. Key Features & Notes Slender lanceolate foliage showcases a waxy blue upper sheen paired with contrasting red-striped undersides. Pairs naturally with tropical mosses and other humidity-loving plants in terrariums and vivariums. Care & Planting Instructions Press the stem cutting or root base into a loose, airy tropical soil mix of coarse perlite, tree fern fiber, and bark, taking care not to compact wet soil tightly around the stem. Provide partial shade or moderate indirect lighting; intense direct light will scorch the narrow foliage and destroy the subtle blue leaf sheen. Maintain ambient humidity above 75% in enclosed setups while ensuring the root zone drains freely, as soggy, waterlogged soil can lead to root and stem rot. Snip older or damaged lower leaves at the stem base using sterile shears to encourage compact lateral shoots and maintain balanced scale. Note that you will receive a live cutting with 2 to 4 leaves that will root and establish steadily under stable high humidity. Ardisia species are terrestrial plants, and being submerged will result in the death of the plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Ardisia sp. Can Ardisia Blue grow submerged in an aquarium? No. Ardisia Blue is an obligate terrestrial understory shrub. Submerging its foliage underwater will cause rapid leaf drop and fatal stem rot. 2. Take a healthy stem cutting with 2 to 4 leaves using sterile shears and press the lower node into damp sphagnum moss inside a closed, high-humidity setup until roots form.

Plant Profile Ardisia sp. 'Black Type 1' brings a dark, brooding presence to midground zones, showing off rounded teardrop leaves that shift between near-black olive, deep chocolate, and rich wine red depending on lighting strength. Tucked tightly against pale spiderwood or nestled into shady crevices between dragon stone, its deep, shadow-toned foliage cuts right through standard green moss walls. With warm, steady moisture and gentle indirect light, it maintains a neat, upright silhouette in terrariums or paludariums. Key Features & Notes Rounded teardrop leaves shift from deep forest green to dark wine red under stronger indirect light. Slow, measured growth rate settles neatly into humid emersed setups without taking over. Care & Planting Instructions Tuck the cutting or root base into a loose, airy tropical mix of perlite, tree fern fiber, and orchid bark along midground slopes or bank margins shared with paludarium plants. Provide partial shade or moderate indirect lighting; intense direct rays will burn the dark leaf tissue and cause permanent scorch marks. Maintain humidity above 70% in enclosed setups while ensuring the root zone drains freely, as waterlogged soil leads to stem rot. Trim older or damaged lower leaves near the main stem using clean shears to encourage fresh shoots and maintain good air circulation. Note that you will receive a live cutting with 2 to 4 leaves that will root and establish steadily under stable high humidity. Ardisia species are terrestrial plants, and being submerged will result in the death of the plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Ardisia sp. Can Ardisia sp. Black Type 1 grow submerged in an aquarium? No. Ardisia species are strictly terrestrial understory shrubs. Submerging them underwater will suffocate the leaves, cause the stem to rot, and result in the death of the plant. 2. How do I get more red coloration out of Ardisia Black Type 1? Gradually increase the intensity of your diffused, indirect grow lighting. Brighter ambient light stimulates anthocyanin production, coaxing out richer wine-red hues while avoiding direct scorching. 3. How do you propagate Ardisia sp. Black Type 1? Take a clean stem cutting containing 2 to 4 leaves and insert the lower node into damp sphagnum moss inside a closed, high-humidity container until fresh rootlets develop.

Plant Profile Labisia sp. 'Musim' is an Asian understory shrub that makes a strong midground statement with thick, leathery leaves covered in a distinct reptilian scale pattern. Anchored in loose soil beside dark dragon stone or wedged near the base of driftwood roots, its glossy olive and brown-tinted blades provide heavy visual substance against fine-textured mosses. That thick, waxy cuticle helps the plant shed continuous overhead condensation while holding internal hydration on the tropical forest floor. Given steady warmth, dappled light, and high ambient moisture, it grows at a measured pace alongside other humidity-loving plants in terrariums. Key Features & Notes Thick, leathery ovate leaves display a textured, reptilian scale pattern in shades of green and brown. Requires consistent ambient humidity above 70% to prevent leaf margins from drying and curling. Care & Planting Instructions Tuck the cutting or root base into an open, airy tropical mix of perlite, tree fern fiber, and fine bark chips along the terrarium floor or elevated paludarium banks. Provide partial shade or soft indirect light; direct rays will burn the glossy leaf surface and fade the deeper brown undertones. Maintain humidity above 70% and keep the substrate damp, ensuring proper drainage so water drains away from the crown rather than pooling into stagnant mud. Trim older or damaged lower leaves at the stem base using clean shears to encourage fresh shoots and maintain good air circulation. Note that you will receive a live cutting with 2 to 4 leaves that will root steadily under warm, enclosed conditions. Labisia species are terrestrial plants, and being submerged will result in the death of the plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Labisia sp. Browning leaf margins usually point to dry air or low humidity. Keep the enclosure covered to hold ambient humidity at or above 70%. 3. How do you propagate Labisia sp. Musim? Take a healthy stem cutting with 2 to 4 leaves and set the lower node into damp sphagnum moss inside a closed, humid setup until roots establish.

Plant Profile Java Fern Fishtail is a rare, striking cultivar that is named after its unique leaf fronds that fork into two wide lobes resembling the tail fin of a fish. This variety delivers an eye-catching focal point in midground and background aquascapes. Under stable aquarium conditions, the tips of its vibrant light-green fronds develop glowing orange-to-amber highlights that create a dramatic color contrast in planted tanks. Virtually bulletproof and forgiving across wide parameter ranges, it anchors smoothly onto driftwood or rocks while standing up to hungry fish. Key Features & Notes Tough, fibrous foliage easily withstands curious nipping from herbivorous fish like cichlids, goldfish, and large snails. Unique forked leaf shape with vibrant orange-amber tips adds exceptional visual contrast and structural texture to hardscape compositions. Exceptional hardiness lets it thrive in non-CO2 tanks and low-light environments. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Java Fern Fishtail is an epiphytic fern that should be attached to rocks or driftwood with aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as it will rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard setups, gentle water movement and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and broader fronds. Master long-term care and troubleshoot common leaf issues by checking out our Java Fern Care Guide . Final size and foliage pattern depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Microsorum pteropus 'Fishtail' (syn. Leptochilus pteropus ) Common Name(s) Java Fern Fishtail, Fishtail Java Fern Family Polypodiaceae Plant Type Epiphyte (Rhizome Fern) Care Difficulty Beginner / Easy (Low-Tech Compatible) Light Requirement Low to Medium CO2 Requirement Not Required (Beneficial) Placement / Usage Midground, Background, Focal Hardscape Accent Height / Size 5"–8" (13–20 cm) Growth Rate Slow to Moderate Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 | Temperature 68°F–82°F (20°C–28°C) Propagation Method Rhizome Division & Adventitious Plantlets Origin Indonesia / Cultivated Variety Frequently Asked Questions 1. What makes Java Fern Fishtail different from standard Java Fern? Java Fern Fishtail gets its name from its distinctive leaf architecture, where fronds split at the end into two wide lobes resembling a fish's tail. Additionally, under good lighting and fertilization, the tips of the fronds develop bright orange-amber tones that stand out against the light green foliage. 2. Why are there small black spots and tiny leaves growing under my Java Fern Fishtail leaves? Do not panic; your plant is not diseased! Java Fern reproduces naturally through adventitious plantlets. Small dark bumps (sporangia) form along the undersides of mature leaves, sprouting tiny brown roots and mini green fronds. Once these baby plantlets develop 3–4 leaves, you can gently pop them off the mother leaf and glue them elsewhere in your aquarium. 3. Can I plant Java Fern Fishtail into substrate? No. Java Fern Fishtail is an epiphyte that absorbs nutrients directly from the water column through its foliage and fine root network. If you bury its horizontal rhizome beneath aquarium soil, sand, or gravel, the stem will suffocate, rot, and die. Always attach it to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread. 4. Will fish like cichlids or goldfish eat Java Fern Fishtail? Generally, no. Java Fern leaves are thick, fibrous, and contain bitter-tasting compounds that deter most plant-eating fish. While aggressive diggers might knock it off hardscape if not glued securely, they rarely consume the foliage.

Plant Profile Ophiopogon japonicus 'Green', commonly known as Mondo Grass, is a tough terrestrial evergreen perennial that has caught out generations of aquarists after being mislabeled as an aquarium plant in pet stores. This land-dwelling lily relative belongs strictly on dry ground above the waterline! Planted in damp soil pockets along driftwood or tucked into gaps where rock meets substrate, its dark green, arching ribbons provide a grassy texture that breaks up broad-leaf foliage. Key Features & Notes Arching dark green ribbon foliage forms tidy evergreen tufts that mimic natural woodland grass. Tough underground rhizomes spread steadily to stabilize soil banks without running aggressively. Provides clean linear contrast when grouped with mosses and ferns across humid terrariums. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Divide the clump into manageable tufts and plant into a loose, nutrient-rich tropical substrate mix along terrestrial banks or floor zones; avoid burying the central crown below the soil line. Provide partial to full shade; intense direct lighting will bleach the dark foliage and scorch the slender blade tips. Keep the substrate consistently moist with regular watering and light misting, but ensure proper bottom drainage so water never sits stagnant around the root base. Snip yellowing, wilting, or dried blades close to the crown using clean shears to keep the clump looking tidy and stimulate fresh growth. Ophiopogon japonicus are terrestrial plants, and being submerged will result in the death of the plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Ophiopogon japonicus 'Green' Common Name(s) Mondo Grass, Fountain Plant, Snakesbeard, Lilyturf Family Asparagaceae Plant Type Terrestrial Evergreen Perennial / Grassy Clumper Care Difficulty Moderate Light Requirement Partial to Full Shade (Low to Medium Indirect) Submersion Suitability Emersed Only (Not for full submersion) Placement / Usage Foreground, Midground, Terrarium Floor, Paludarium Banks Height / Size 6"–12" (15–30 cm) Growth Rate Medium Humidity Requirement Moderate to High Propagation Method Rhizome Division Origin East Asia (Japan, Korea, China) Frequently Asked Questions 1. Can Ophiopogon japonicus grow fully submerged in an aquarium? No. Despite often being sold submerged in pet stores, Mondo Grass is an obligate terrestrial plant. Submerging it underwater cuts off gas exchange and will cause the leaves to suffocate and rot within weeks. 2. Why are the tips of my Mondo Grass turning yellow or brown? Yellowing or crispy tips typically signal underwatering, dry air, or light burn from lamps placed too close to the enclosure. Keep the soil evenly moist and position the clump in partial or full shade. 3. How do you propagate Ophiopogon japonicus? Take the plant out of its pot, wash away loose soil, and slice cleanly through the fibrous rhizome mass with sharp shears, ensuring each division retains a cluster of healthy roots and several foliage blades before replanting.

The Dymax CO2 Drop Checker is a great and essential option to monitor the CO2 levels in an aquarium. It is difficult to know how much CO2 is dissolved in the water and too little or too much can have devastating effects on the aquarium. Going off the number of bubbles in a bubble counter is not always a fool proof method to monitor CO2 concentrations in an aquarium. Too little CO2 may promote algae growth and poor plant growth, while too much CO2 will be detrimental to livestock. With the Dymax CO2 Drop Checker, aquarist can easily know when the correct concentration of CO2 has been achieved in the aquarium. Set Up: Start by filling the drop checker half way with the CO2 Indicator Solution. Attach the suction cup to the drop checker Gently place in the tank, being careful not the spill the indicator solution How to Read: Blue- CO2 concentration is too low Green- CO2 concentration is good Yellow- CO2 concentration is too high Be aware that the drop checker takes 1-2 hours to react to the concentration of CO2 in the aquarium. Includes: High Quality Drop Checker Suction cup Dimensions: Small 2 x 1" Large 2.5 x 1.2" **Kits include indicator solution and drop checker**

Product Overview Dymax Clear Mix is a premium macro-porous synthetic polymer adsorbent engineered to eliminate cloudy water, stubborn organic waste, and dark tannin discoloration from aquariums. It polishes water to absolute clarity without stripping essential trace elements, making it an indispensable addition to high-tech planted aquascapes, heavily stocked community tanks, and breeding setups. Key Features & Benefits 5x Higher Efficiency: Outperforms standard filtration media by capturing and holding significantly higher capacities of nitrogenous organic waste. Removes Wood Tannins & Cloudiness: Quickly strips yellow driftwood tannins and floating micro-particles to restore crystal-clear water clarity. Selective Adsorption Action: Target-absorbs organic impurities and waste precursors while having minimal impact on trace elements and plant fertilizers. Regenerable & Reusable: Synthetic polymer beads change color from light tan to dark brown as they exhaust, and can easily be regenerated using a standard household bleach soak. Versatile Media Bag Compatible: Easily packs into fine mesh filter bags for placement in canister filter trays, HOB chambers, or internal media towers. Technical Specifications Avoid using Dymax Clear Mix in specialized blackwater aquarium setups where natural tannin coloration is desired. Specification Details Product Type / Style Macro-Porous Synthetic Polymer Adsorbent Filtration Type Chemical Adsorption & Water Polishing Target Impurities Tannins, Organic Waste, Discoloration, Organic Nitrogen Compounds Reusability Regenerable via Bleach Treatment Water Compatibility Freshwater & Marine Safe What's Included 1x Dymax Clear Mix Polymer Adsorbent Media Container Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I know when my Dymax Clear Mix is exhausted? Dymax Clear Mix visually changes color as it adsorbs organic waste. The polymer beads will gradually darken from a light cream/tan color to deep brown or black, indicating it is time to regenerate or replace the media. 2. How do I regenerate spent Dymax Clear Mix? Soak the dark, exhausted media in a 1:1 solution of household non-scented bleach and water for 24 hours in a well-ventilated area until the beads return to their original light color. Rinse thoroughly, then soak in fresh water treated with a heavy dose of aquarium dechlorinator before placing it back into your filter. 3. Will Dymax Clear Mix strip liquid fertilizers out of my planted tank? No, Clear Mix is specifically formulated to adsorb organic nitrogenous waste and larger organic molecules rather than essential inorganic trace minerals and liquid plant fertilizers. However, this product will remove tannins from the water column, so it should be avoided if tannins are desired in the aquarium.

Plant Profile Bucephalandra ‘Black Tears’ is a beginner-friendly, low-tech aquarium plant featuring slender, elongated, and almost teardrop-shaped leaves, from which it earns its unique name. This variety displays a sophisticated, deep shade of green. Highly versatile, this epiphytic plant can be grown submerged or emersed, usually attached to hardscape such as driftwood or rocks rather than being buried in traditional aquarium substrate. It’s a beautiful addition to the foreground or midground of a planted tank, gradually extending from slender rhizomes to create a lush, vibrant cluster. Key Features & Notes The slender, elongated leaf shape offers a distinct visual departure from the more common round or oval Bucephalandra varieties. Its dark, saturated green foliage provides an excellent backdrop for lighter plants or bright shrimp and fish in a planted tank. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for planted tanks where other plants might struggle. Care & Planting Instructions Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard low-light aquarium plant setups, CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and richer iridescence. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Bucephalandra ‘Black Tears’ is a beginner-friendly, low-light aquarium plant that grows without specialized substrate or pressurized CO₂, making it well suited for low-tech planted aquariums.

This variety is highly prized for its warm color palette and distinct texture, providing a sophisticated look for both low and high-tech setups. It can be grown submerged or emersed, usually attached to hardscape such as driftwood or rocks rather than being buried in traditional aquarium substrate. Bronze Red is a great pick for the midground of freshwater aquascapes, where its slow-growing rhizomes will gradually form a dense, jewel-toned colony within a planted tank. The wavy, ruffled leaf edges provide significant visual texture, making it an excellent plant for breaking up the smooth lines of rocks and wood. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for aquascapes where other plants might struggle. It is perfectly at home fully submerged in an aquarium or emersed in high-humidity terrariums, vivariums, and paludariums. Plant Profile Homalomena humilis is a rare rheophytic aroid with thick, waxy, spade-shaped leaves that shift from soft rose-pink to deep forest green. A relative of Anubias and Bucephalandra, it grows from a creeping rhizome and comes from the fast-flowing streams of Indonesian Kalimantan, where it clings to riverbanks in one of the most biodiverse rainforests on Earth. Tuck it against driftwood or rock, where the pink-to-green leaves give you color against the usual greens, or use it in a lower-light corner where you want some interest without adding a high-demand plant. Key Features & Notes Thick waxy foliage displays a shifting color gradient from soft pink tones to rich emerald green. Dual-growth habit adapts seamlessly to fully submerged aquascapes, enclosed terrariums, and paludarium margins. Compact creeping rhizome anchors securely to stone and wood without sending invasive runners across hardscape. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Secure the rhizome onto driftwood or porous rock using thread or plant glue, or press the roots into an airy tropical mix or aquarium soil while keeping the main rhizome exposed above the substrate line. Provide low to medium indirect lighting; supplemental CO2 in an aquarium setup encourages richer pink tones and faster root anchoring. Maintain humidity above 75% for emersed setups, or provide gentle, clean water circulation when cultivating fully submerged. Trim older or melting transition leaves near the rhizome base with sharp aquascaping scissors to stimulate new shoots. Final size and leaf coloration depend entirely on your specific setup conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Homalomena humilis transitions well underwater, maintaining its thick, waxy leaf texture and compact growth habit when provided with low to medium lighting. 2. Should the rhizome of Homalomena humilis be buried under substrate? No. Burying the central creeping rhizome under substrate can cause it to rot. Attach it directly to wood or stone, or bury only the roots while keeping the rhizome exposed. 3. How do you propagate Homalomena humilis? Use clean aquascaping shears to cut a section of the rhizome containing at least 3 leaves and established roots, then tie or glue the division onto hardscape.

Plant Profile Micranthemum ‘Monte Carlo’ is the ultimate aquatic carpeting plant to give your aquarium that lush, velvety rolling-hill look you’ve been dreaming of. With its tiny, round leaves and bright green color, it pops beautifully against neutral substrates. If you’ve ever struggled to grow notoriously finicky Dwarf Baby Tears (HC) , Monte Carlo is the friendlier, more forgiving alternative you’ve been looking for. It spreads out into a thick, uniform mat, giving you maximum aquascaping rewards without the heartbreak. Key Features & Benefits Forms a tight, velvety foreground lawn with small, bright green leaves that add an incredible sense of scale and depth to your aquascape. Far easier to cultivate than Dwarf Baby Tears, making it an accessible carpet option for hobbyists of all experience levels. Care & Planting Instructions Use a dry start method or Wabi Kusa setup to give its root system plenty of time to firmly anchor into the substrate before you flood the tank. Maintain stable aquarium parameters and avoid drastic shifts in water quality to prevent your new grass from melting. Provide medium to high lighting and inject pressurized CO2 to supercharge its density and growth rate, keeping it low and compact. Master the basics by learning how to properly grow aquarium carpet plants to ensure your new layout fills in quickly. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Micranthemum tweediei 'Monte Carlo' Common Name(s) Monte Carlo Family Phrymaceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Stem / Carpeting Foreground Care Difficulty Easy to Medium Light Requirement Medium to High CO2 Requirement Recommended (Required for tight lawn growth) Placement / Usage Foreground Carpet Height / Size 1-2 inches Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Water Parameters pH 6.0 – 7.5 | Temperature 68°F – 80°F (20°C – 27°C) Propagation Method Cut runners and replant Origin Argentina Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I plant Monte Carlo? Use fine-tip tweezers to bury each portion about halfway into nutrient-dense aquarium soil. Spacing them 1 inch apart helps them connect quickly via runners. 2. Does Monte Carlo need CO2 to form a carpet? While Monte Carlo can technically grow in low-tech setups without CO2, adding pressurized CO2 and medium-to-high lighting is strongly recommended to force it to grow horizontally into a tight, plush carpet instead of growing tall or straggly. 3. Why is my newly planted Monte Carlo floating up? Because tissue culture portions have delicate root systems, fish or water currents can easily dislodge them. Planting small clumps deeply into fine soil or letting the tank grow emersed using the Dry Start Method will anchor the roots securely before flooding.

Plant Profile Ardisia Black Type 2 is a tropical plant featuring thick, elliptical, leathery leaves with dark olive-to-almost-black upper surfaces and rich contrasting pink undersides. A great pick for emersed setups, it contrasts beautifully against lighter hardscape stones and vibrant green terrarium plants across the tank floor and shaded pockets. While the massive genus Ardisia encompasses over 700 species spanning diverse tropical ecosystems worldwide, very few display this degree of dark leaf pigmentation! Key Features & Notes Thick, leathery elliptical foliage features dark olive-black tops with high-contrast pink undersides. Requires sustained high humidity and airy, well-draining substrate to prevent leaf margin browning. Dark coloration makes it an eye-catching focal anchor in midground and background zones. Care & Planting Instructions Press the stem cutting or root base gently into an airy, moisture-retentive tropical substrate mix rich in bark, tree fern fiber, and perlite; never pack down or compact the soil. Maintain ambient humidity above 75% in enclosed setups to keep delicate leaf edges from drying out or crisping. Provide moderate, filtered indirect lighting; exposure to harsh direct light can scorch the dark foliage and cause bleaching. Prune vertical stems just above a leaf node using clean shears to encourage branching and maintain a compact, bushy habit. Note that you will receive a live cutting with 2 to 4 leaves that will root and establish steadily under stable high humidity. Ardisia species are terrestrial plants, and being submerged will result in the death of the plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Ardisia sp. 'Black Type 2' Common Name(s) Ardisia Black Type 2, Ardisia Sp. Can Ardisia Black Type 2 survive in a closed terrarium? Yes. It thrives in enclosed glass setups because sustained ambient humidity prevents its thick, leathery leaves from dehydrating or crisping at the margins. 2. Why are the leaves on my Ardisia Black Type 2 fading or scorching? Direct or overly intense light scorches and fades dark understory leaves. Position the plant under filtered, moderate indirect light for deeper color contrast. 3. How do you propagate Ardisia Black Type 2? Take a stem cutting containing 2 to 4 leaves using clean shears and insert the lower node into damp sphagnum moss or an airy tropical substrate under enclosed humidity until roots anchor.

Product Overview Maintaining high humidity for tropical mosses, terrestrial epiphytes, and emergence zones in paludariums often requires more than passive water evaporation. The UNS Atomizer Mist Maker Kit uses ultrasonic vibrations to transform water into a dense, rolling fog, creating an authentic jungle atmosphere while supplying essential moisture to humidity-loving plants. Compact and easy to conceal behind hardscape, this quiet mist maker adds functional hydration and dramatic visual depth to aquaterrariums and paludariums. Key Features & Benefits Ultrasonic Fogging Action: Produces fine, cool mist via high-frequency vibrations to boost enclosure humidity without raising water temperatures. Automatic Low-Water Protection: Built-in safety sensor automatically shuts off the unit when water drops below 0.5 inches to prevent overheating and dry burning. Splash Guard Protection: The included splash guard keeps water droplets contained within the tank while directing mist outward across your plants. Complete Maintenance Kit: Includes 3 replacement ceramic diffusion plates and a dedicated changing key for easy long-term maintenance. Technical Specifications Attribute Specification Brand Ultum Nature Systems (UNS) Product Line UNS Aquascaping Accessories Tool Type Ultrasonic Fogger / Paludarium Mist Maker Kit Mist Maker Dimensions 2" x 1.5" x 1.5" (5 cm x 3.8 cm x 3.8 cm) Splash Guard Diameter 3.75 inches (9.5 cm) Safety Mechanism Auto-Shutoff Water Level Sensor (Min. 0.5" depth) Ideal For Layout Types Paludariums, Terrariums, Ripariums, & Emerged Moss Walls What's Included 1x Ultrasonic Mist Maker Unit (2" x 1.5" x 1.5") 1x Splash Guard & Atomizer Holder (3.75" Diameter) 1x Power Supply Adapter & Cable 3x Ceramic Diffusion Plates 1x Diffusion Plate Changing Key Installation & Setup Instructions Inspect the Unit: Check all components before installation to ensure the mist maker, splash guard, and power supply are intact. If a part is missing or damaged, contact your Ultum Nature Systems dealer immediately. Submerge to Proper Depth: Position the mist maker (and optional splash guard) in your water reservoir, ensuring the water sensor is submerged at least 0.5 inches below the surface. If not, the water sensor will detect if the water level is too low and shut off the atomizer. Level Alignment: Verify the unit is resting level. If installed at an angle or tilt, water may splash or spray outside the tank during operation. Connect Power: Plug the power cord jack into the unit and plug the power adapter into a wall outlet or timer. Care & Maintenance Instructions Keep water clean and free of large organic debris to prevent buildup on the ceramic disk. Rinse the mist maker housing periodically with fresh tap water to clear mineral crusting. Store unused replacement diffusion plates in a dry place. Ceramic Diffusion Plate Replacement Guide Unplug the unit from power before performing maintenance. Insert the diffusion plate key into the slots of the top retaining ring on the mist maker unit. Turn the key counterclockwise to unscrew and remove the retaining ring and worn diffusion plate. Insert the fresh diffusion plate. Note: Do not remove or disturb the rubber O-ring seated underneath the diffusion plate. Place the retaining ring back on top of the new diffusion plate and tighten clockwise using the key until snug. Frequently Asked Questions 1. How deep should the UNS Atomizer be submerged in water? The top of the mist maker's water sensor must be submerged at least 0.5 inches below the surface. If the water level drops too low, the mist maker will automatically power off to protect the internal ultrasonic disc from damage. 2. How do I know when it's time to change the ceramic diffusion plate? When you notice a significant decrease in fog volume despite maintaining proper water levels, or if the disc shows severe mineral crusting, it is time to replace the diffusion plate using the included key. 3. Can I run the UNS Atomizer continuously on a timer? Yes! Running the atomizer on a digital timer or smart plug (for example, 15 to 30 minutes several times a day) is an excellent way to maintain ideal humidity cycles for sensitive mosses, ferns, and tropical epiphytes without oversaturating your soil.

Plant Profile Common Name: Bucephalandra Brownie Hermes Buce ‘Brownie Hermes’ is a beginner-friendly, low-tech aquarium plant known for its dark green leaves that develop a deep, metallic blue tinge when grown submerged. This variety is highly prized for its moody coloration and refined texture, making it a favorite for adding sophisticated contrast to bright green layouts. Highly versatile, it can be grown submerged or emersed, usually attached to hardscape such as driftwood or rocks rather than being buried in traditional aquarium substrate. Key Features & Notes Under quality full-spectrum LED lighting, the mature dark green foliage reveals a captivating blue iridescence that defines the Brownie series. Its compact nature makes it an ideal "filler" plant for the tight crevices between rocks and wood where larger species might feel out of scale. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for aquascapes where other plants might struggle. It is perfectly at home fully submerged in an aquarium or emersed in high-humidity terrariums, vivariums, and paludariums. Care Tips & Preparation Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood . Never bury the rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Plant Profile The Assorted Hardy Water Lily Pack is the ultimate way to bring classic, vibrant beauty to your indoor water garden or outdoor pond setup. Each grower's choice 5-pack includes an assortment of hardy lily bulbs ready to sprout round floating pads supported by long, elegant stalks. As these aquatic lilies grow, they create a protective floating canopy that shades your water to suppress algae, keeps water temperatures cool, and provides a safe, peaceful shelter for fish. Best of all, as summer arrives, these floating plants for aquariums and ponds reward you with striking, multi-day blossoms ranging in shade from radiant yellow and pink to pure white or deep orange. Key Features & Benefits Assorted 5-pack of hardy bulbs produces iconic floating lily pads and vibrant summer blossoms in yellow, pink, white, or orange. Broad floating leaf canopy provides essential overhead shade that cools water and starves out unwanted algae growth. Extensive surface pads and root structures create an inviting, stress-free sanctuary for pond and aquarium fish. Care & Planting Instructions Plant rhizomes at a 45-degree angle in nutrient-rich substrate, leaving them only partially covered, with the growing tip kept fully exposed to prevent rot. Submerge planted bulbs 1 to 2 feet below the water surface in an area receiving full sun for at least six hours daily to ensure healthy foliage and flowers. Insert aquarium or pond fertilizer tabs into the soil annually to replenish key nutrients for the heavy-feeding root system. Hardy lily bulbs will survive winter underwater as long as the rhizome itself does not freeze solid. Overwinter bulbs in freezing climates by removing them from the water and storing them in a bag filled with damp sand and peat moss at 50–55°F. Remember that water lilies are strictly aquatic plants and will not survive in terrarium or dry environments. Propagate established plants by dividing the rhizomes during routine spring maintenance. How do I plant my Water Lily bulbs properly without causing them to rot? Plant the rhizome at a 45-degree angle in heavy soil or aquatic substrate. Press the bulb into the soil firmly, but make sure the growing tip (where the leaves sprout) remains entirely above the substrate surface. Burying the growing crown completely will trap moisture and cause the rhizome to rot. 2. What should I do with my Water Lilies during cold winter months? Hardy Water Lilies can remain in outdoor ponds over winter as long as the water at depth does not freeze solid into the bulb layer. If you live in a climate where shallow ponds freeze through, lift the bulbs in autumn and store them indoors in a sealed bag filled with damp sand or peat moss at 50–55°F until spring. 3. Why should I trim off flower stalks after my water lily finishes blooming? Once water lily petals drop, the plant naturally shifts its energy toward developing a seed pod. Pruning the spent flower stalk below the water surface with sharp shears prevents the lily from exhausting its nutrient reserves on seed production, directing that energy into growing fresh floating leaves and new flower buds instead.

Plant Profile Bucephalandra ‘Brownie Jade’ is a beginner-friendly, low-tech aquarium plant featuring rounded leaves with pronounced midribs that run through each leaf center. This variety displays older foliage in shades of light to dark green, while newer growth often reveals hints of blue and distinctive shiny white stomata dots. Like other epiphytes, it can grow submerged or emersed and prefers to attach its rhizome to driftwood or rock rather than be buried in substrate. Key Features & Notes The combination of the deep green jade color and tiny silver speckles creates a starry, high-textured look under quality LED lighting. Its medium-sized, rounded leaves offer a soft visual contrast to more jagged or narrow-leaf Buce varieties. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for planted tanks where other plants might struggle. Care & Planting Instructions Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard low-light aquarium plant setups, CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and richer iridescence. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! If the rhizome remains firm, keep it attached to hardscape while the plant acclimates and produces new submerged growth. 2. Can I plant Bucephalandra in substrate? Bucephalandra is an epiphyte, so never bury its rhizome in substrate. Attach it to driftwood or rocks, or wedge the roots into hardscape while keeping the rhizome exposed. 3. Bucephalandra ‘Brownie Jade’ is a beginner-friendly, low-light aquarium plant that grows without specialized substrate or pressurized CO₂, making it well-suited for low-tech planted aquariums.

If you are looking to build an aquascape that feels less like a quiet river scene and more like a rugged, ancient mountain range that time forgot, meet Dragon Wood. Named for its resemblance to Dragon Stone , this aquarium driftwood is the king of texture. It trades the smooth, predictable lines of standard wood for a chaotic, honeycomb-like structure packed with natural craters, deep crevices, and miniature tunnels. Use it to build high‑impact forest layouts or weathered riverbanks that have gone through a millennium of erosion. Dragon Wood will definitely scale your scape to new levels. Product Features & Benefits The natural holes and tunnels aren't just for show! They provide vital hiding spots for shy species like Plecos and shrimp. Dragon Wood is an excellent choice for hobbyists looking to naturally lower their water's pH and hardness, creating a more acidic environment favored by many tropical fish. Ranging from deep earth browns to soft greys, the coloration of this wood will deepen and "mature" over time as it interacts with your water. Size Specifications Photos provided are a representation of what you will receive. As Dragon Wood is a natural aquarium hardscape product, please expect variations in shape, weight, and character. Extra Small: 4-8 inches Small: 8-12 inches Medium: 12-16 inches Large: 16-20 inches Extra Large: 20-24 inches Preparation & Care Because of its unique "holey" structure, Dragon Wood requires a slightly different approach than your standard log. Rinse: Those signature tunnels can sometimes trap dust or debris. Thoroughly rinse the piece to make sure it's clean. The Floating Phase: Dragon Wood is buoyant and will float initially. We recommend soaking it thoroughly or boiling it. A large stone or heavy decor may be placed on top to ensure a non-waterlogged piece of wood stays submerged. Tannin Management: Like most aquarium driftwood, this will release tannins, giving your water a warm, "tea-colored" tint. This is a natural occurrence, and the effects will subside over time. If you prefer crystal-clear water, a 1–2 hour boil is the best way to fast-track the process. You can also reduce this effect through consistent water changes or through the addition of Aquario Neo Carbon Bag Important note: We recommend rinsing wood thoroughly before adding it to an established aquarium. If you prefer, you may also boil the wood for at least 1–2 hours to help release tannins.

listings.description: If you are running a deep micro-tank or an ultra-compact rimless nano setup, finding equipment that fits without causing a massive visual distraction can be a serious challenge. The Aquario Neo CO₂ Extended Diffuser (Tiny edition) solves this perfectly by combining an ultra-small 8mm micro-ceramic disc with an extra-long, 15.65-inch rigid acrylic stem. This extended profile allows you to route your gas lines straight down to the base of your substrate without running ugly, flexible airline loops inside your display glass. Key Features & Benefits The hyper-compact 8mm ceramic disc size is tailor-made for micro layouts, providing maximum gas dissolution with a minimal footprint. The ultra-streamlined design completely removes the built-in bubble counter chamber to give you a pristine, low-profile look. The heavy-duty acrylic body is shatterproof, providing a safe, resilient alternative to notoriously fragile glass diffusers. The extended acrylic body can be gently heated and custom-bent to perfectly wrap around your specific tank rim thickness. Size Disk Size Tube Height Tank Size Tiny 8mm 15.65 inches 8 gallons or less Additional Information Submerge the entire diffuser in clean water for 30 minutes before connecting it to your gas line. This primes the micro-pores of the ceramic membrane, ensuring it produces a fine mist instantly on startup rather than large, wasteful bubbles. Over time, natural organic film or algae can accumulate on the ceramic surface, causing the bubbles to grow larger. When this happens, simply soak the diffuser in standard household bleach for 10 minutes, then rinse it thoroughly with fresh water and a generous dose of aquarium water conditioner to completely neutralize any residual bleach before placing it back in your tank. What’s in the Box? 1x Aquario Neo CO₂ Curved Original Diffuser 2x Clear Suction Cups Team Buce Plant Tips Fine-tuning your CO₂ setup can seem intimidating at first, but the process is far simpler than it appears. And if you’re curious about the science behind why CO₂ makes your buce, stems, and carpets thrive, explore The Mysteries of CO₂ in a Planted Tank Explained for a clear breakdown.

Plant Profile Native to the shaded rainforest streams of Sri Lanka, Lagenandra thwaitesii is the smallest species in its genus. Reaching just 3 to 5 inches tall, its modest stature makes it an ideal low-growing accent for foreground and midground transitions, adding architectural structure and fine leaf texture near hardscape bases and driftwood roots. The slender, bright emerald leaves feature subtly wavy margins, delivering rich Cryptocoryne-like texture near hardscape bases and driftwood roots without taking over the layout. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Slender, wavy-edged foliage creates a distinct, low-profile focal point in the foreground or midground. Slow, steady rosette growth pattern stays tidy and rarely requires frequent trimming. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers under cool water before dividing and planting. Separate the tissue culture cup into smaller plantlet portions and place them into nutrient-rich soil or insert root tabs nearby, as it feeds heavily through its root system. Provide medium to high lighting and inject pressurized CO2 to promote fuller leaf expansion and rich coloration. Maintain stable water parameters and good water clarity to encourage steady root development and prevent leaf melting during transition. To propagate, divide the mature rhizome using sharp, clean aquascaping scissors once the mother plant forms distinct side crowns, and replant the new rosettes into your substrate. Master the basics by learning how to properly grow tissue culture aquarium plants to keep your layout thriving and algae-free. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How is Lagenandra Thwaitesii different from Cryptocoryne species? While visually similar to Cryptocoryne and requiring similar substrate-rich care, Lagenandra Thwaitesii grows outward from a distinct thick rhizome rather than spreading wild subterranean runners, making it much easier to keep contained in specific foreground or midground areas. 2. Can Lagenandra Thwaitesii be grown in cool-water aquariums? Yes. Lagenandra Thwaitesii has a remarkably wide temperature tolerance ranging from 60°F to 85°F, making it suitable for unheated cool-water tanks as well as tropical planted aquariums. 3. How do I propagate Lagenandra Thwaitesii? Once the plant is mature and established, use clean aquascaping scissors to cut through the horizontal rhizome between leaf clusters, making sure each division retains a portion of healthy roots before replanting into the substrate.

The Twinstar Nano Algae Inhibitor is designed to prevent the growth of green algae in the aquarium by eliminating and reducing spore production. This device is safe for live plants, fish and aerobic bacteria. Its microbubbles provide a sterilizing factor that destroys the cell wall of green algae without harming the natural biological environment within an aquarium. Because algae and plants share similar growth requirements, they are constantly in competition with each other. When you reduce the number of algae present in an aquarium, you allow the plant to receive more light and absorb more nutrients. The Twinstar Algae Inhibitor thereby promotes plant growth by reducing algae. The effect may see increases in plant growth up to 50%! The best way to combat algae growth is to achieve a carefully balanced aquarium with proper lighting and nutrient levels. Preventing algae growth from the spore level will give aquarium plants the upper hand in competing for crucial nutrients. Please note, this device will not cure, remove and prevent algae growth alone. It is recommended to use in combination with good maintenance habits for best results. Certified by the Korea National Institute of Fisheries Science for its sterilization effects on thread algae, spot algae, brown algae, and more. Plant Profile If you're hunting for an uncommon collector's piece that won't make you sweat over strict water parameters, Cryptocoryne axelrodi is an absolute gem. Hailing from the lush tropical waters of Borneo, this elusive species stands out with its slender, strap-like leaves displaying an earthy, greenish-brown hue. As with all crypt plants, this plant can be sensitive to changes in water parameters and doesn’t like to be moved. But once settled into its new home, it grows into a highly reliable, low-maintenance midground accent that brings a wild, natural look to your aquascape. Key Features & Benefits Slender greenish-brown foliage brings a rare, naturalistic texture to midground layouts. Uncommon species status makes it a highly sought-after addition for collectors. Resilient once established, thriving even in low-tech setups with minimal lighting. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Crypt species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I help my Cryptocoryne Axelrodi recover if it melts? Crypt melt is a standard reaction when shifting water conditions cause old leaves to dissolve so the plant can rebuild foliage adapted to your aquarium. Trim away rotting tissue, keep your water parameters stable, and do not disturb the subterranean root system. For complete recovery steps, check out our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt . 2. Why does moving or uprooting my Crypt cause leaf drop? This species relies heavily on a delicate network of subterranean roots that absorb nutrients from the soil. Uprooting the plant ruptures these fine root hairs and alters its micro-environment, triggering a shock response where the plant drops its leaves to conserve energy. Placing it in a permanent location from day one prevents unnecessary leaf loss. 3. Should I use root tabs or liquid fertilizers? Root tabs are best. Cryptocoryne species are heavy root feeders that draw primary nutrition from the substrate rather than the water column.

Product Overview SL-Aqua MORE Crayfish is a sinking daily staple pellet for freshwater crayfish that need steady minerals and amino acids to molt cleanly. Built around a balanced blend of natural proteins, essential minerals, and shell-enhancing pigments, this recipe fuels strong exoskeleton growth, active foraging, and vivid carapace coloration. True to the SL-Aqua MORE line, the dense pellets drop straight to the bottom and hold their firm physical shape so crayfish can pick them up with their claws and carry them back into their burrows without the food dissolving into messy dust across your substrate. Offering a few pellets daily delivers complete, bioavailable nutrition while keeping your water clear and your substrate free of decaying waste. Key Features & Notes Firm sinking pellet format drops straight to the bottom and retains its shape so crayfish can carry pieces into burrows without crumbling. Balanced daily recipe packed with amino acids, essential minerals, and natural pigments with zero water-clouding fillers. Supports clean exoskeleton molting, healthy shell density, and vivid coloration in dwarf and standard freshwater crayfish. Feeding Guidelines Feed once or twice daily, offering only what your crayfish can actively consume within one to two hours. Drop pellets near rock caves or driftwood hides so shy crayfish can forage without competing against fast tankmates. Rotate with blanched vegetables, sinking algae wafers, and occasional frozen bloodworms to provide a diverse, balanced diet. Reseal the pouch tightly after each use and store in a cool, dry place away from direct light to keep nutrients fresh. Product Overview SL-Aqua MORE Pacman Frog Food is a finely ground powdered diet crafted specifically for juvenile and adult Pacman frogs ( Ceratophrys species) as a clean, reliable alternative to live insects and rodents. Packed with complete proteins, digestive enzymes, vitamins, and essential minerals without artificial thickeners, this formula supports steady skeletal growth, strong bone density, and vivid skin coloration. When mixed with a splash of water, the powder kneads into a cohesive, firm pellet that holds together cleanly on feeding tongs without crumbling in your terrarium. Frogs will need to be trained to accept this type of food, but once trained, SL-Aqua Pacman food can become the staple food source. Key Features & Notes Finely milled powder mixes with water into firm, customizable pellets that hold their shape on feeding tongs. Complete, balanced formula that works as a replacement for live insects and rodents. Feeding Guidelines Mix one level 0.5g spoonful of powder with half a spoonful of dechlorinated water, then knead into a smooth, firm ball. Offer portions sized to roughly one-third of your frog's mouth width for juveniles, or half the mouth width for adults, using feeding tongs. Gently touch or rub the food ball along the side of the frog's mouth to trigger a natural feeding strike if it hesitates at first. Reseal the pouch tightly after each use and store in a cool, dry place away from direct light to keep enzymes and vitamins fresh. listings.description: Plant Profile Alternanthera Rosaefolia, often affectionately called Magenta Water Hedge, is an iconic aquatic stem plant famous for its bold, magenta-to-ruby-red leaves with rich violet undersides. It's a cornerstone species in classic Dutch-style aquascapes, standing out even among other red and green plants with its striking, high-volume color. Growing 8 to 12 inches tall, its sturdy stems and full-volume foliage deliver knockout contrast wherever you place it, so if your midground or background needs a hedge with some personality, this is it! Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Intense magenta and crimson red foliage introduces bold color contrast into midground and background layout zones. Beginner-friendly and provides vibrant color without extreme maintenance demands. Dense leaves provide shelter and protective cover for skittish fish and dwarf shrimp. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide medium-to-high lighting. Regular dosing of liquid fertilizers like UNS Plant Food (2–3 times per week) and pressurized CO2 injection are highly recommended to yield maximum magenta coloration and prevent stem stunting. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or rotting. Trim stem tops or side shoots with curved scissors once stems reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and expand your hedge. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Alternanthera reineckii 'Rosaefolia' Common Name(s) Alternanthera Rosaefolia Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture, AR Rosaefolia, Magenta Water Hedge Family Amaranthaceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Stem Plant Care Difficulty Medium Light Requirement Medium to High CO2 Requirement Recommended (Essential for rich magenta-red color) Placement / Usage Midground / Background Centerpiece Height / Size 8–12”+ Growth Rate Moderate Water Parameters pH 5.0–7.0 Propagation Method Cuttings (Cut stem, new growth, or lateral shoots) Origin South America Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I keep Alternanthera Rosaefolia Tissue Culture displaying deep red foliage? Providing strong lighting, pressurized CO2, a nutrient-dense substrate, and regular micronutrient dosing with liquid iron ensures intense magenta-red foliage and prevents stem tips from stalling or melting. 3. How do I prepare Alternanthera Rosaefolia Tissue Culture before planting? Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the dense cluster into smaller clumps or individual stems and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

Plant Profile Pogostemon Helferi 'Downoi Red', often called Downoi Red or Little Star, originates from the mineral-rich rivers of Thailand. This distinct strain is recognized for its compact, star-shaped rosette growth and narrow, crinkled leaves with ruffled edges. While standard Downoi displays a bright lime-green color, this red variant develops soft pink to deep red veins running through the centers of its green leaves under targeted care. Reaching 2 to 4 inches in height, its curly leaf structure brings a unique texture to foreground and midground areas. Because its natural habitat features mineral-heavy waters, this species grows well in hard-water aquariums where steady mineral levels and rich root nutrition are present. Key Features & Benefits Crinkled, ruffled foliage forms a distinct starburst rosette pattern in foreground and midground layouts. Pink and red leaf veins contrast against bright green leaf blade surfaces under targeted lighting and nutrients. Adaptable species that can be grown submerged in aquariums or emersed in high-humidity terrariums. Care & Planting Instructions Gently remove the plant from its packaging or container, carefully rinsing away any protective media around the root system with room-temperature water. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant individual stems or small rosettes 1 inch apart into your aquarium soil, ensuring the crown remains above the substrate line. Provide high-intensity lighting and pressurized CO2 injection; consistent dosing of micronutrients, particularly iron, helps develop the pink and red vein coloration. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and good mineral hardness; avoid sudden parameter shifts to prevent leaf melting during transition. To propagate, trim developed side shoots or main stem tops with sharp straight shears and replant the cuttings directly into your aquarium soil. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. How do I maintain a compact growth habit with Downoi Red? Routine pruning of side shoots encourages the plant to branch outwards along the substrate rather than growing tall, helping it form a dense, low-growing bush in your foreground or midground.

listings.commonName: Anubias Minima on Christmas Moss Fiber Mat
listings.description: Common Name: Anubias Minima on Moss Anubias Minima is a unique variety of Anubias. The leaves are long and slender with a bright green coloration. Depending on growing conditions this plant can stay relatively compact or grow quite tall. High light and CO2 injection will help this plant stay more compact. Here, the Anubias Minima is attached onto a fiber mat that is covered in Christmas moss. This combination is ideal for ground coverage and a perfect place for shrimp to feed. Both Anubias Minima and moss are easy plants to care for. They can thrive in low light and CO2 conditions, but will definitely benefit if grown in high light with CO2 injection. It is crucial not to bury the rhizome of the Anubias as this may lead to rot. Trim the moss regularly to achieve a compact growth and to keep ensure that the Anubias Minima does not get outcompeted. Both of these plants can be propagated by cuttings, but be sure to cut the Anubias at the rhizome. Notes: Anubias are strong plants that can thrive in a variety of environments. Anubias are epiphytes can be planted above the substrate or attached to hardscape. Burying the rhizome, will cause the plant to melt and die Do not make drastic changes to the aquarium. Unstable parameters will result in melt and rotting of the aquarium plant. Trim moss to achieve a compact appearance CO2 injection and quality aquarium soil will yield better growth. Please research appropriately to ensure your plant thrives. Care: Easy Light: Low Co2: Not necessary Propagation: Anubias: Separate by rhizome, Moss: Cuttings Growth rate: Slow to moderate

listings.commonName: Anubias Minima on Christmas Moss Tower
listings.description: Plant Profile Think of this clever combo as the Swiss Army knife of your aquascape. The Anubias Minima on Christmas Moss Tower blends long, vibrant green leaves with a thick carpet of moss to deliver a striking focal point that works in multiple orientations. It's a great addition to help you master your layout design, functioning as a majestic vertical pillar or flipping sideways to become a cozy, moss-covered sanctuary for your favorite tank inhabitants, such as small fish or shrimp. Anubias and moss are famously beginner-friendly, so you can skip the learning curve and focus on enjoying your setup. Key Features & Benefits The innovative vertical tower design lets you add immediate height and lush green architecture to your tank. Placing the tower horizontally creates a secret, cozy cave system that offers the perfect stress-free hiding spot for your shyest shrimp and nano fish. Both hardy species used on this tower easily tolerate low light and low carbon dioxide conditions. Care & Planting Instructions Place the tower directly onto your substrate either vertically as a pillar or horizontally as a cave without burying any part of the green Anubias rhizome to prevent the plant from melting or rotting. Occasionally trim the Christmas moss using aquascaping shears to maintain its compact shape. Propagate your thriving tower in the future by cleanly snipping the moss strands or carefully slicing the Anubias' rhizome. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. CO₂ is optional but improves growth and leaf density. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I plant Anubias Minima on Christmas Moss Tower? This plant decor item is pre-assembled, so no planting! 2. Does it require CO2 or high lighting? No. It thrives in low lighting without CO2 injection. While adding CO2 speeds up growth, it is completely optional. 3. Is this plant safe for shrimp, snails, and fish? Yes, it's 100% safe for all freshwater fish, shrimp (including sensitive Caridina and Neocaridina), and snails. Its tough leaves are also resistant to plant-eating fish like cichlids or goldfish.

listings.commonName: Anubias Nana on Christmas Moss Tower
listings.description: Plant Profile Delivering instant vertical structure and dual-plant texture, Anubias Nana on Moss Tower combines two beginner-friendly species into a versatile aquarium plant decor piece that works in multiple orientations. It's a great addition to help you master your layout design, functioning as a majestic vertical pillar or flipping sideways to become a cozy, moss-covered sanctuary for your favorite tank inhabitants, such as small fish or shrimp. Anubias and moss both thrive under low lighting and adapt effortlessly to standard low-tech water parameters. Key Features & Benefits Dual-purpose tower design creates an instant vertical pillar or horizontal cave system for nano fish and shrimp. Pre-bound combination of Anubias Nana and Christmas moss takes all the guesswork out of attaching epiphytes and mosses. Resilient, low-light-tolerant species perform well in a wide range of water parameters. Care & Planting Instructions Place the pre-attached tower directly onto substrate vertically or horizontally; do not bury the Anubias rhizome. Maintain stable water parameters to ensure smooth acclimation and reduce leaf shedding. Avoid intense light and ensure healthy water flow to prevent slow-growing leaves from collecting spot algae. Trim the surrounding moss periodically with sharp shears to maintain a clean shape. CO₂ is optional but improves growth speed and leaf density. No. Both Anubias Nana and Christmas moss thrive in low to moderate lighting without CO2 injection. While adding CO2 speeds up growth, it is completely optional. 3. Is this plant safe for shrimp, snails, and fish? Yes, Anubias and moss are 100% safe for all freshwater fish, shrimp (including sensitive Caridina and Neocaridina), and snails. The hollow tower structure also offers a protected shelter for baby shrimp and shy fish.

Plant Profile Deep-green, glossy leaves with gently ruffled edges give Anubias Barteri Dark Angel its distinctive look. If your tank's foreground or midground zones are feeling a bit too bright or uniform, this dark beauty is here to help you earn your scaping wings by creating visual contrast against lighter hardscape. Better yet, it requires minimal fertilization and practically no trimming, happily pushing out new leaves in low-tech setups as long as you keep its rhizome above the substrate. Key Features & Benefits Deep, glossy dark foliage with gently ruffled margins creates rich visual contrast against lighter hardscape and bright green plants. Compact 3-to-5-inch height fills midground gaps, softens jagged rock edges, and nestles seamlessly into wood forks. Tough, compact leaves naturally resist grazing from plant-nibbling fish and active dwarf shrimp. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Avoid intense light and ensure good water flow to prevent spot algae on slow‑growing leaves. CO₂ is optional but improves growth and leaf density. Learn more about planting these species by reading our guide on How to Plant Epiphyte Aquatic Plants. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How does Anubias Dark Angel compare in size and color to Anubias Nana or Bucephalandra? Anubias Dark Angel shares a compact 3-to-5-inch footprint similar to Anubias Nana, but produces noticeably darker, glossier leaves with subtle wavy margins that mimic the moody palette of dark Bucephalandra cultivars while offering typical Anubias hardiness. 2. Will Anubias Dark Angel keep its dark coloration under low lighting? Yes. Unlike red stem plants that fade without high-PAR lights and CO2, Dark Angel retains its deep, moody green tones under low to moderate lighting, though bright direct light can trigger green spot algae on its slow-growing leaves. 3. Why are older leaves on my Dark Angel showing green spots or fuzzy edges? Because Dark Angel grows slowly, older leaves sit exposed to light for months and readily collect green spot algae or black beard algae if placed directly under strong LEDs. Tuck it into partial hardscape shade and ensure steady water flow across the leaves.

Plant Profile For aquascapers seeking to soften sharp, jagged rockwork without overcrowding compact layouts, Anubias Barteri Petite Round delivers neat, coin-shaped foliage! Its deep green, glossy foliage contrasts beautifully with driftwood, making it a great pick for tucking into crevices for a pop of color. Give it low light and a little patience (it’s slow-growing), and this hardy epiphyte will settle in as a foreground accent or midground detail in low-tech aquariums, terrariums, and paludariums. Key Features & Benefits Miniature profile makes it one of the most versatile nano aquarium plants for smaller layouts. Thick, leathery leaves deter grazing from plant-eating cichlids, snails, and dwarf shrimp. Resilient nature handles a wide range of water parameters in low-tech setups with ease. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the horizontal rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce initial leaf loss. Avoid intense direct light and ensure good water flow to prevent spot algae on slow‑growing leaves. CO₂ is optional but improves growth speed and leaf density. Learn more about planting these species by reading our guide on How to Plant Epiphyte Aquatic Plants. How does Petite Round differ visually from standard Nana Petite? While standard Anubias Nana Petite features elongated, tear-drop leaves with pointed tips, Anubias Petite Round produces distinctly circular, coin-shaped leaves with smooth, cupped margins, providing a softer geometric appearance. 2. Where is the best placement for Anubias Petite Round in a nano tank? Its miniature 1-to-3-inch height makes it ideal for tucking directly into hairline cracks between Seiryu stone, Dragon stone, or tangled driftwood roots in the foreground and midground of tanks under 10 gallons. 3. Can Anubias Petite Round be grown out of water in a terrarium? Yes. Anubias Petite Round thrives emersed in humid terrariums, vivariums, and paludariums. Keep ambient humidity above 75% and ensure the roots and rhizome are mounted to moist wood or moss rather than submerged in soggy soil.

Plant Profile Common Name: Bucephalandra Apple Leaf Buce ‘Apple Leaf’ is a stunning, low-tech aquarium plant prized for its unique teardrop-shaped leaves and vivid green coloration. This variety stays relatively small and compact, making it a versatile choice that functions perfectly as a midground accent in nano setups or a foreground detail in larger layouts. Highly versatile, it can be grown submerged or emersed, usually attached to hardscape such as driftwood or rocks rather than being buried in traditional aquarium substrate. It is an exquisite choice for freshwater aquascapes, where its slow-growing rhizomes create a lush, bright green colony that adds natural beauty to any planted tank. Key Features & Notes Named for its distinct foliage shape, 'Apple Leaf' offers a softer, rounded aesthetic compared to the narrow-leafed variants in the genus. This variety maintains a bright, saturated green hue that provides an excellent high-contrast pop against dark lava rocks or driftwood. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for aquascapes where other plants might struggle. It is perfectly at home fully submerged in an aquarium or emersed in high-humidity terrariums, vivariums, and paludariums. Care Tips & Preparation Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood . Never bury the rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Carefully remove the plant from its pot and clear away all rockwool from the roots. For a deep dive on prepping potted plants, click here . Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting. Unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance, CO2 injection will yield much faster growth. We recommend researching your specific water chemistry to ensure your plant thrives. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions. Please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Please research appropriately to ensure your plant thrives. Additional Information Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only.
