Plant Profile Native to India, Nymphaea stellata , commonly known as the Dwarf Water Lily, is a great pick for hobbyists who want high-impact red foliage with low maintenance. Sprouting directly from a compact bulb, it sends out long, delicate stems topped with distinctly arrow-shaped leaves. These speckled leaf blades shift between warm copper, soft pink, and deep reddish-violet, creating a gorgeous color pop right in the center of your tank. It stays remarkably manageable compared to its giant pond cousins, giving you all the dramatic lily aesthetics without taking over your whole glass box! Key Features & Notes Arrowhead leaves display rich copper, pink, and reddish-violet tones for strong color contrast. Compact bulb growth maxing out around 6 inches tall makes it an ideal midground focal point. Hardy and undemanding species that retains rich red coloration in low-tech tanks without CO2. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by gently clearing any loose debris or rockwool away from the bulb and roots. Set the bulb into your substrate, making sure at least half of the bulb sits above the soil line to prevent rot. As a heavy root feeder, placing nutrient-rich soil or root tabs near the bulb supports steady growth and vivid red leaf pigmentation. Provide moderate lighting; while CO2 injection isn't strictly required, good lighting will enhance its red and pink foliage. Regularly trim long stems that try to reach the water surface if you want to keep the plant growing in a compact midground bush formation. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Propagate by gently separating lateral offshoot plantlets or daughter bulbs once they form independent root systems. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Nymphaea stellata Common Name(s) Dwarf Water Lily, Dwarf Lily Family Nymphaeaceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Bulb plant / True Aquatic Care Difficulty Easy Light Requirement Moderate CO2 Requirement Not required (Optional) Placement / Usage Midground Centerpiece / Foreground Accent Height / Size 4–6 inches Growth Rate Moderate Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 Propagation Method Separate daughter offshoots or side shoots from bulb Origin India & Southeast Asia Frequently Asked Questions 1. How deep should I plant the bulb of Nymphaea stellata? Rest the roots in the substrate, but make sure at least half of the bulb sits completely exposed above the soil. Fully burying the bulb restricts oxygen flow and causes it to rot. 2. How do I stop my Dwarf Water Lily from sending leaves to the surface? If you see a stem shooting straight up toward the waterline, clip it off close to the bulb base with sharp scissors. Regular pruning trains the plant to keep producing shorter, bushier midground foliage. 3. Does Nymphaea stellata need high light and CO2 to stay red? Nope! Unlike many finicky red stem plants, Nymphaea stellata maintains its reddish-pink tones quite easily in standard low-tech setups without pressurized CO2, provided it gets adequate root nutrients.

Plant Profile Echinodorus 'Devil's Eye' gets its striking name from the distinct, high-contrast look of its leaves. What makes this hybrid sword stand out is its foliage color and pattern: newly emerging center leaves unfurl in shades of rich reddish-pink to bronze, marked by a deep red central vein running down the middle of each blade. As the leaves mature, they shift toward an olive-green tone while retaining that prominent dark midrib pattern. Maxing out around 12 inches tall, its moderate size keeps it manageable as a midground centerpiece in medium tanks or a background focal point in smaller aquariums. Like most sword plants, it is naturally hardy and easy to care for as long as it has a nutrient-dense substrate to root into. Key Features & Notes Distinct dark red central vein creates a bold contrast down the length of each leaf blade. Emerging center foliage opens in deep reddish-pink and bronze tones before maturing to olive green. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Plant the roots deeply into your aquarium soil, keeping the central crown resting just above the substrate line to prevent rot. All Echinodorus are heavy root feeders that rely on rich substrate nutrition; placing root tabs near the base supports steady, healthy leaf development. Provide moderate to high lighting; while CO2 injection isn't strictly required, good lighting will enhance its reddish-brown colors. Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf shedding during the initial transition period. Sword plants propagate through side shoots off of their leaves, which can be trimmed and replanted into the substrate. To control the size of your sword plant, you can remove the side shoots and older leaves. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! What gives Echinodorus 'Devil's Eye' its unique look? Its most notable feature is the thick, dark red vein running down the center of each leaf. Combined with young leaves opening in reddish-pink and bronze shades, it creates a striking visual contrast against surrounding green plants. 2. How do I maintain the bright red vein and leaf color on Echinodorus 'Devil's Eye'? Giving the plant moderate-to-high lighting and keeping the substrate rich in nutrients, especially iron, helps keep the central vein defined and encourages vibrant color on newly emerging leaves. 3. Can Echinodorus 'Devil's Eye' grow without CO2 injection? Yes, it grows well in low-tech setups without pressurized CO2. As long as it has good substrate nutrition and decent lighting, it will grow consistently and maintain its unique leaf markings.

Plant Profile Offering a bright, warm color shift compared to typical green sword plants, Echinodorus 'Yellow Sun' is a striking hybrid cultivar that brings fresh contrast to a tank layout. Newly emerging center leaves open in delicate shades of pale red and copper before transitioning into a warm yellow-green hue dappled with subtle brownish specks as they mature. Its balanced rosette habit makes it a versatile midground focal point in medium-to-large aquariums or an attractive background accent in smaller setups. Hardy and adaptable, it brings a cheerful splash of golden-green foliage without requiring fragile or demanding care routines. Key Features & Notes Young leaves open in pale red tones before transitioning into a warm yellow-green with brownish specks. Compact scale of around 12 inches tall makes it ideal for midground focal placement. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Plant the roots deeply into your aquarium soil, keeping the central crown resting just above the substrate line to prevent rot. All Echinodorus are heavy root feeders that rely on rich substrate nutrition; placing root tabs near the base supports steady, healthy leaf development. Supplemental CO2 injection accelerates growth and encourages denser, fuller foliage, though the plant will still grow steadily in low-tech setups. Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf shedding during the initial transition period. Sword plants propagate through side shoots off of their leaves, which can be trimmed and replanted into the substrate. To control the size of your sword plant, you can remove the side shoots and older leaves. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. How do I maintain and enhance the pale red and yellow-green colors on Echinodorus 'Yellow Sun'? Providing moderate-to-high lighting directly over the plant and supplementing the root zone with nutrient-rich soil or root tabs helps encourage bright pale-red inner growth and warm yellow tones throughout the rosette. 2. Can Echinodorus 'Yellow Sun' be kept in low-tech setups without CO2? Yes, it adapts well to low-tech aquariums without pressurized CO2. As long as it receives good root fertilization and adequate lighting, it will grow consistently and maintain healthy foliage. 3. How does Echinodorus 'Yellow Sun' propagate? Over time, healthy plants will produce runner shoots with baby plantlets along floral stalks or divide naturally at the root crown. Once the new plantlets develop roots, you can separate and replant them into the substrate.

Plant Profile If you are looking to create a wall-to-wall green lawn in your aquarium, it is time to tree-t your scape to some holiday magic all season long. Christmas Moss is a legendary aquascaping staple, famous for its deep green, overlapping fronds that naturally grow into the shape of tiny evergreen trees. Instead of struggling with loose pieces that float away, this listing features an extra-large 8" x 4" portion pre-grown onto a 100% aquarium-safe, recycled fiber mat. This ingenious setup allows you to easily craft instant moss carpets and wrap large hardscape sections. Key Features & Benefits Pre-cultivated on a generous 8" x 4" recycled fiber mat for an immediate, low-profile carpet with zero wait time. Recycled, inert fiber backing is completely safe for sensitive dwarf shrimp and fish while providing a secure anchor. Triangular growth pattern adds stunning architectural depth and a mature, cozy forest aesthetic to your aquascape. Care & Planting Instructions Lay the mat flat on your substrate for an instant carpet, or cut the flexible pad to custom sizes to attach to hardscape or walls. Maintain a stable aquarium environment and avoid sudden, drastic changes to your water parameters to keep your moss looking vibrant and healthy. Give the moss an occasional light haircut with sharp aquascaping shears to keep its shape neat, compact, and perfectly balanced. listings.description: Plant Profile Ludwigia Dark Orange is a captivating aquatic stem plant native to the wetlands of North America. Famous for its distinctively veined, oval-shaped foliage that displays a warm spectrum ranging from golden-yellow to rich amber and deep dark orange, this species adds incredible color depth to planted aquariums. Reaching a height of 5 to 10+ inches, it serves as an extraordinary midground accent or background centerpiece. Its orange-red tones intensify under medium-to-high lighting, pressurized CO2, and iron-rich fertilization, making it a favorite choice for Dutch-style plant streets and nature aquascapes alike. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Striking foliage displays a warm color gradient from golden-yellow to deep dark orange with distinct vein patterns. Moderate-growing stem habit branches readily when pruned to form thick, bushy colorful hedges. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. * Ludwigia stems and leaves are delicate, so handle stems with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide medium-to-high lighting and clean water conditions; while adaptable without CO2, supplying pressurized CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilization rich in iron and micronutrients yields the deepest orange-red hues. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or leaf shedding. To propagate, trim main stem tops with sharp straight shears and replant trimmings directly into substrate. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Ludwigia sp. 'Atlantis' / Ludwigia 'Dark Orange' Common Name(s) Ludwigia Dark Orange, Ludwigia sp. Atlantis, Dark Orange Ludwigia Family Onagraceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Stem Plant Care Difficulty Easy to Moderate Light Requirement Medium to High CO2 Requirement Optional / Recommended (Yields richer orange hues and faster branching) Placement / Usage Midground / Background Accent & Dutch Streets Height / Size 5–10”+ (Cup portion size: 2–3”) Growth Rate Moderate Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 Propagation Method Cuttings (Cut stem tops or lateral shoots and replant) Origin North America Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I get Ludwigia Dark Orange to show its deepest orange and yellow colors? Achieving rich dark orange and gold coloration requires medium-to-high light intensity, pressurized CO2 injection, and a reliable fertilizer routine that supplies micronutrients, especially iron. 3. How do I prepare Ludwigia Dark Orange Tissue Culture before planting? Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the cluster into smaller clumps or individual stems and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

Plant Profile Common Name: Bucephalandra Brownie Adinda Buce ‘Brownie Adinda’ is a beautiful and versatile aquarium plant featuring green leaves with prominent central veins and waved margins. This variety is highly prized for its adaptable nature and elegant form, displaying subtle color shifts that vary depending on the specific lighting and nutrient conditions of the tank. Highly versatile, it can be grown submerged or emersed, usually attached to hardscape such as driftwood or rocks rather than being buried in traditional aquarium substrate. It is a fantastic choice for adding intricate texture to the foreground or midground of freshwater aquascapes, where it will slowly grow into a textured, shimmering carpet of foliage. Key Features & Notes The distinct central vein provides a structural look to the foliage, accented by the soft "wave" of the leaf edges for added depth. With a height range of 1–3+ inches, this species fits perfectly into the layout of a nano tank or as foreground detailing in a large display. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for aquascapes where other plants might struggle. It is perfectly at home fully submerged in an aquarium or emersed in high-humidity terrariums, vivariums, and paludariums. Care Tips & Preparation Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood . Never bury the rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Carefully remove the plant from its pot and clear away all rockwool from the roots. For a deep dive on prepping potted plants, click here . Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting. Unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance, CO2 injection will yield much faster growth. We recommend researching your specific water chemistry to ensure your plant thrives. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions. Please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Please research appropriately to ensure your plant thrives. Additional Information Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Ghost Wood delivers a dramatic glow-up the moment it hits the water, making it one of the most stunning choices for an aquascape. Dry, it starts pale and weathered, but once submerged, this aquarium driftwood transforms into a rich, deep mahogany that glows under quality LED lighting. Its smooth, sandblasted trunks and sweeping branches give a clean, sculptural look without the tangle of softer woods, making it ideal for defined, mature layouts. This wood is the one that really comes alive! Talk about a spooktacular glow‑up. Product Features & Benefits Unlike more twiggy varieties, Ghost Wood offers thick, smooth, and flowing lines. The sandblasted surface transitions from a light beige to a vibrant, dark brown once waterlogged, adding a sense of evolution to your planted aquarium hardscape. While a star in the aquarium, Ghost Wood’s clean finish makes it equally popular in vivariums and terrariums, where it won't rot easily in high-humidity environments. This aquarium wood naturally aids in softening the water, creating a comfortable environment for acid-loving fish and shrimp. Size Specifications Photos provided are a representation of what you will receive. As Ghost Wood is a natural aquarium hardscape product, please expect variations in shape, weight, and character. Extra Small: Less than 10 inches Small: 8-12 inches Medium: 12-16 inches Large: 16-25 inches Extra Large: 25-38 inches Preparation & Care Ghost Wood's sandblasted finish means it needs a little prep time. Rinse: Thoroughly rinse the piece to remove any dust or debris from transit. The Floating Phase: This wood is buoyant. Because the pieces are often thick, they require a thorough soak to become fully waterlogged. Tannin Management: Ghost Wood leaches fewer tannins than Malaysian wood, but some tint is still to be expected. This forbidden tea look is easily managed by boiling the wood for 1–2 hours or soaking it in a separate container until the water runs clear. You can also reduce this effect through consistent water changes or through the addition of Aquario Neo Carbon Bag Logistics Note: Due to the impressive size of our Large and Extra Large pieces, additional shipping costs may apply to ensure your "underwater art" arrives in one piece. Important note: We recommend rinsing wood thoroughly before adding it to an established aquarium. If you prefer, you may also boil the wood for at least 1–2 hours to help release tannins.

Grapewood is the ultimate showstopper for land-loving setups. Known for its deeply gnarled trunks, dramatic twists, and rich, sandblasted textures, this wood looks like a piece of living art taken straight from a vineyard. It features incredible contours, deep hollows, and thick, muscular bends that provide a stunning, high-contrast landscape. If you are building an enclosure that needs to look rugged, ancient, and beautifully organic, Grapewood brings the premium, rustic vibes in spades. Now, time for a quick hobbyist reality check: We do not recommend Grapewood for aquarium use. While it looks incredibly tempting to submerge, Grapewood is a much softer wood compared to heavy-duty hardwoods like Mopani or Malaysian Driftwood. When kept underwater long-term, it breaks down quickly, softens into mush, and can throw your water quality into a tailspin. Product Features & Benefits A good pick for reptile terrariums, frog vivariums, and bird enclosures. Packed with dramatic, hollowed-out twists and deep burls that create instant cave networks and climbing routes. Meticulously sandblasted to reveal a smooth, gorgeous grain pattern that looks fantastic under bright enclosure lighting. Size Specifications Photos provided are a representation of what you will receive. This is a natural aquarium hardscape product; please expect variations in shape, weight, and character. Average size: 14-20" Character: Each piece is unique; expect variations in thickness, twist, and knot density.

Plant Profile If you love the classic look of Cryptocoryne beckettii but lack the space for a full-sized bush, Cryptocoryne petchii is an essential freshwater aquarium plant for compact layouts. Native to the stream beds of Sri Lanka, this dependable staple stays comfortably smaller than its relatives, showing off slender olive-brown leaves with striking purple undersides that provide a unique pop of color in planted tanks. As with all crypt plants, this species can be sensitive to sudden parameter shifts and strongly objects to being relocated once planted. Key Features & Benefits Slender olive-brown foliage with rich purple undersides brings vibrant color contrast to midground zones. Compact growth habit makes it an ideal midground or foreground plant for nano and small-to-medium aquariums. Can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups, where mature plants may produce flowering spathes. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth and fuller foliage density, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Crypt species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting subterranean runners or replanting offshoot plantlets. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! What makes Cryptocoryne Petchii different from Cryptocoryne Beckettii? While both feature similar dark earthy tones, Cryptocoryne Petchii remains significantly more compact in height and displays distinct, rich purple pigmentation on the undersides of its leaves, making it far better suited for smaller aquariums and tight midground spaces. 2. How do I bring out the purple undersides on Cryptocoryne Petchii? Providing moderate aquarium lighting and supplementing the substrate with iron-rich root tabs will enhance the contrast between the olive-brown topside and the vibrant purple underside of the foliage. 3. How do I help my Cryptocoryne Petchii recover if it melts after planting? Crypt melt is a standard reaction when shifting water parameters cause old leaves to dissolve so the plant can grow new foliage adapted to your aquarium. Trim away decaying tissue, keep your water conditions stable, and do not disturb the subterranean root mass. For step-by-step recovery tips, check out our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt .

Plant Profile Rotala Colorata (sometimes mislabeled as Rotala indica ) is a vibrant variation of Rotala rotundifolia, popular for coloring up without a fight. Most red aquatic stem plants demand intense lighting and nutrient dosing just to show any color at all, but Rotala Colorata skips that requirement, displaying pink, orange, and red hues even under moderate lighting. Push it further with CO2 injection and iron supplementation, and its leaves shift into scarlet and crimson tones. It pairs beautifully with other Rotala species to form lush, colorful background hedges. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Displays vibrant pink, orange, and red hues more readily than other red stem plants, even under moderate lighting setups. Fast-growing stem habit easily branches into dense, colorful background bushes through routine pruning and replanting. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip the lower inch of foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. * Rotala leaves are fragile, so handle stems with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower leaves. Provide moderate-to-high lighting. Adding pressurized CO2 and iron supplementation maximizes its deep crimson and scarlet pigmentation. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim stem tops or side shoots with straight scissors once they reach the water surface, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I get my Rotala Colorata to display its deepest red colors? While Rotala Colorata blushes easily under moderate light, achieving deep scarlet and crimson tones requires high light intensity, pressurized CO2 injection, low-to-moderate nitrate dosing, and regular iron fertilization. 3. How do I transition Rotala Colorata from emersed to submerged growth? When transitioning from emersed to submerged growth, plant bare stems securely into rich substrate under moderate-to-high lighting and keep water parameters stable. As new growth adapts, the plant will shed its rounded land leaves and sprout delicate, narrow underwater foliage with pinkish-red hues. Once new shoots develop, trim away old lower growth to encourage dense branching.

Species Profile Zebra Nerite Snails ( Neritina natalensis ) are peaceful herbivorous gastropods in the family Neritidae native to coastal brackish and freshwater stream systems across Africa. This species displays a smooth, golden-amber shell accented by bold black zebra-like bands, making them both an aesthetic accent and a dedicated clean-up crew for planted aquariums. They spend their days scouring glass, rocks, and hardscape clean of stubborn film algae, diatoms, and green spot algae without ever taking a bite out of your prized live plants. Because their larvae require brackish water to hatch and develop, they will never reproduce or turn your tank into an out-of-control snail colony, though you should expect them to leave small white calcified egg spots on your favorite driftwood as proof they are settled in. **Note: All livestock orders will come carefully packaged with solid wall Styrofoam insulation and shipped via 1-day shipping only. No extra insulation needs to be added to your cart for your livestock. Key Features & Notes Striped gold and black shell pattern adds visual contrast. Strictly herbivorous diet targets green spot algae, diatoms, and biofilm without damaging aquatic plants. Inability to reproduce in freshwater environments prevents accidental population spikes. Acclimation & Care Instructions Float the sealed transport bag in your aquarium for 15 to 20 minutes to equalize water temperature before opening. Drip-acclimate the snail over 30 to 45 minutes using airline tubing to slowly adjust it to your tank's pH, hardness, and mineral levels. Place the snail upright on flat hardscape or substrate at the bottom; do not drop it upside down, as Nerites struggle to right themselves on soft sand. Maintain stable water chemistry with a pH above 7.0 and sufficient mineral hardness (GH) to prevent shell pitting or calcium erosion over time. Supplement with algae wafers, spirulina disks, or blanched zucchini if your aquarium runs out of natural diatom film and surface algae. Keep a tight-fitting lid on your aquarium, as active Nerites occasionally wander above the waterline on clean-up patrol. Final shell banding patterns and coloration vary naturally between specimens; please note that photos are a representation of healthy stock. Will Zebra Nerite snails eat or damage my live aquarium plants? No. Zebra Nerites have rasping radulas designed strictly for grazing surface films, diatoms, and soft algae off hard surfaces. They lack the jaw strength or interest to chew through healthy plant leaves. 2. Can Zebra Nerite snails reproduce and overrun my freshwater tank? No. While female Nerites frequently lay small, durable white egg capsules on driftwood, stone, and glass, these eggs cannot hatch or develop in freshwater. They require brackish, highly saline water for the veliger larvae to survive, meaning they will never reproduce into a pest infestation in standard freshwater setups. 3. How do I stop my Zebra Nerite snail's shell from eroding or cracking? Shell erosion and pitting happen when snails are kept in acidic or soft water with a low pH (under 7.0) and low calcium/GH levels. Keep your water slightly alkaline and supply adequate dietary calcium through mineral-rich foods, wondershell, or cuttlebone to maintain a thick, healthy shell. 4. What tank mates should I avoid housing with Zebra Nerite snails? Avoid housing Nerites with aggressive snail-eating species such as Clown Loaches, Yo-yo Loaches, Assassin Snails, predatory Crayfish, and large pufferfish. They do exceptionally well alongside peaceful community fish, dwarf shrimp (Neocaridina and Caridina), Otocinclus, and Corydoras.

Species Profile Horned Nerite Snails ( Clithon corona ), also known as Thorny Nerite Snails, are compact herbivorous gastropods in the family Neritidae native to coastal rivers, estuaries, and mangrove zones across Southeast Asia. This species is easily recognized by the array of sharp, thorn-like horns protruding from its spiral shell, which is patterned in varying shades of dark amber, yellow, and black. Their small stature allows them to reach tight hardscape crevices and delicate stem plant foliage that larger snails tumble off of, working non-stop to strip glass and leaves clean of diatoms and stubborn film algae. Because their larvae require high-salinity brackish water to hatch and develop, they will never multiply into a nuisance population in a freshwater planted aquarium. **Note: All livestock orders will come carefully packaged with solid wall Styrofoam insulation and shipped via 1-day shipping only. No extra insulation needs to be added to your cart for your livestock. Key Features & Notes Distinct thorn-like shell spines paired with black and gold striping provide a unique, defensive aesthetic. Petite size allows thorough grazing on delicate plant leaves and tight rock crevices without crushing foreground carpets. Strictly herbivorous feeding habits ensure complete safety around living aquatic plants. Acclimation & Care Instructions Float the sealed transport bag in your aquarium for 15 to 20 minutes to equalize water temperature before opening. Drip-acclimate the snail over 30 to 45 minutes using airline tubing to slowly adjust it to your aquarium water chemistry and mineral levels. Place the snail upright onto flat wood, stone, or hard substrate; take extra care not to drop it upside down into soft sand, as their small footprint makes righting themselves difficult. Handle the shell gently to avoid snapping the delicate ornamental spines protruding from the whorl. Maintain a stable pH above 7.0 and adequate mineral hardness (GH) to keep the shell thick and prevent acid-induced pitting or spine erosion. Supplement their diet with spirulina disks, algae wafers, or blanched vegetables if your aquarium lacks sufficient natural biofilm and diatom growth. Keep a tight lid on your tank, as foraging snails will occasionally venture above the waterline during nighttime grazing patrols. Final spine count, shell patterns, and coloration vary naturally between wild-type specimens; please note that photos are a representation of healthy stock. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy livestock! What are the spikes on the Horned Nerite snail's shell for, and do they grow back if broken? The calcified spines serve as a natural defense mechanism against predatory fish in river environments, making the snail difficult to swallow. If a horn snaps off during transit or maintenance, it will not regenerate, but a broken horn does not harm the snail's health as long as the underlying shell body remains intact. 2. Can Horned Nerite snails reproduce and take over a freshwater aquarium? No. Similar to other Nerite species, female Horned Nerites may occasionally deposit tiny, hard white egg capsules on wood or stone, but these eggs cannot hatch in freshwater. The developing larvae require brackish water with high salinity to survive, ensuring they will never overpopulate your aquarium. 3. Are Horned Nerite snails safe for delicate carpet and stem plants? Yes. Because Horned Nerites stay smaller and lighter than standard Zebra or Tiger Nerites, they can graze across delicate carpeting plants like Micranthemum 'Monte Carlo' or narrow stem leaves without uprooting them or snapping stems under their weight. 4. Which tank mates should not be kept with Horned Nerite snails? Avoid housing them with dedicated snail predators such as Assassin Snails, Clown Loaches, Yo-yo Loaches, Pea Puffers, and predatory Crayfish. They coexist peacefully with dwarf shrimp (Neocaridina and Caridina), Otocinclus, Corydoras, and gentle schooling fish.

Neritina Pulligera, simply referred to as the Black Military Helmet Snail, is a species of freshwater snail that is popular for the planted aquarium. It features a shiny dark brown to black color that resembles a soldier's helmet. This species can be found in fast-flowing freshwater streams or rivers with rocky substrates and as far as brackish waters due to a close proximity to the ocean. The Black Military Helmet Snail is a peaceful species that will happily munch on algae or scavenge left over bits found in the aquarium. This freshwater snail is difficult to breed and is safe to add to the aquarium without concern of excessive reproduction. When choosing tank mates for your Nerites, avoid species that eat snails. These include Loaches, Crayfish, Large Cichlids, Goldfish, and other larger species. We prefer keeping our Nerites in most of our Buce tanks along with Amano Shrimp, Neocardina Shrimp, Caridina Shrimp, Oticinclus, Siamese Algae Eaters, Tetras, Cories, Bettas and other peaceful fish. Key Features & Important Notes Tank-raised specimen. To increase survival rates, please allow 2-3 business days after placing an order to properly prepare live animal shipments. We don't recommend smaller tanks as snails produce a large amount of waste that will add to the tank's bio-load. In the home aquarium, Nerite Snails lay white eggs on tank decorations and plants. However, these eggs won't mature in freshwater. The larvae of these snails require brackish environments with high salinity to undergo proper development. Rearing young snails would involve setting up a separate aquarium, given that adult snails are unable to endure the water conditions required to rear nerite larvae.

Species Profile Assassin Snails ( Clea helena ) originate from flowing, soft-bottomed river systems across Southeast Asia. Sporting a sharp, bumblebee-striped spiral shell and an extendable hunting siphon, they are the hobby's undisputed biological control for nuisance snail infestations. Instead of rasping on glass or grazing diatoms, these specialized carnivores bury themselves down into the substrate like mini trapdoor predators, waiting to ambush pest snails like Pond snails, Bladder snails, and Malaysian Trumpet Snails. They have zero interest in healthy foliage or delicate stems, meaning your aquascape and carpet plants remain pristine and completely undisturbed. Once their target prey is cleared out, they seamlessly transition to cleaning up high-protein fish flakes, sunken pellets, and frozen foods, keeping your layout balanced without ever turning into pests themselves. **Note: All livestock orders will come carefully packaged with solid wall Styrofoam insulation and shipped via 1-day shipping only. No extra insulation needs to be added to your cart for your livestock. Key Features & Notes Bold yellow and dark brown spiral bands provide striking aesthetic contrast across the substrate line. Specialized carnivorous predator that actively hunts down nuisance snails. 100% plant-safe habits ensure no chewing on live stem foliage or uprooting delicate foreground carpets. Acclimation & Care Instructions Float the sealed transport bag for 15 to 20 minutes to equalize water temperatures before opening. Drip acclimate over 30 to 45 minutes using airline tubing to ease them into your tank's GH, KH, and pH levels. Provide fine sand or rounded, loose substrate so they can burrow naturally to hunt and rest. Maintain stable water parameters with a pH between 6.5 and 8.0 and sufficient mineral hardness to support healthy shell structure. Target-feed with bloodworms, carnivore sinking pellets, or protein flakes once pest snail populations dwindle. Exercise caution when keeping with other ornamental mollusks; hungry Assassins may gang up on larger snails like Nerites or Mystery Snails. Shell striping and adult sizing vary naturally between specimens; photos represent healthy stock in mature tanks. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Will Assassin Snails attack dwarf shrimp or baby shrimplets? Healthy, active adult shrimp are far too fast for an Assassin Snail to catch. While an Assassin Snail will gladly scavenge a dead, sick, or dying shrimp, they rarely bother healthy dwarf shrimp like Neocaridina or Caridina. However, we do not recommend keeping them together if you are actively breeding shrimplets. 2. Can Assassin Snails reproduce out of control and become a pest themselves? No. Unlike hermaphroditic pest snails that can reproduce solo and flood your tank with egg clutches, Assassin Snails have distinct sexes and breed at a very slow pace. Females lay single, square-shaped egg capsules on plants or hardscape that take 3 to 8 weeks to hatch. The juvenile snails spend their first several months buried deep in the substrate, meaning you will never see sudden explosive population blooms. 3. What should I feed my Assassin Snails once all the pest snails are gone? Because they are obligate carnivores, they will not graze on algae or green biofilm when prey runs out. Offer them sinking carnivore wafers, protein-rich bottom dweller pellets, and frozen treats like bloodworms or brine shrimp. 4. Are my larger ornamental snails safe with Assassin Snails? It is generally best not to risk keeping prized Nerite, Mystery, or Rabbit Snails in the same aquarium. While a single Assassin may hesitate around a full-sized adult snail, multiple Assassins will readily team up to overwhelm larger snails, especially if their preferred small prey runs low. Keep them alongside peaceful community fish like tetras, Corydoras, and Otocinclus, while avoiding dedicated mollusk predators like loaches or puffers.

Species Profile Tiger Nerite Snails ( Neritina semiconica ) hail from coastal freshwater and brackish stream systems across Africa, sporting an amber-gold shell dotted with deep black dash marks and tire-track bands. In a planted aquarium, they are arguably one of the most reliable workhorses you can employ for algae defense. Unlike bulkier snails that bulldoze foreground stems, Tiger Nerites cruise methodically across glass, Seiryu stone, and driftwood, using their rasping radula to strip away brown diatoms, green dust, and stubborn green spot algae. They have zero interest in healthy foliage, leaving even the most delicate carpet plants completely untouched. While they may occasionally leave behind hard, white sesame-seed-like egg capsules on your favorite hardscape, their larvae require brackish water to develop, so you never have to worry about an accidental population takeover. **Note: All livestock orders will come carefully packaged with solid wall Styrofoam insulation and shipped via 1-day shipping only. No extra insulation needs to be added to your cart for your livestock. Key Features & Notes Amber-gold shell with black dash striping provides natural contrast on dark wood and stone. Dedicated grazer that strips green spot algae, diatoms, and glass films without touching live plants. Cannot reproduce in freshwater, completely eliminating the risk of a pest snail outbreak. Acclimation & Care Instructions Float the sealed transport bag for 15 to 20 minutes to equalize water temperatures before opening. Drip acclimate over 30 to 45 minutes using airline tubing to adjust them slowly to your tank's GH, KH, and pH. Place the snail upright onto a flat rock or solid hardscape; Nerites struggle to right themselves if dropped upside down into soft aquasoil or sand. Maintain alkaline water (pH 7.0+) with sufficient mineral hardness; soft or acidic water will pit and erode their shells over time. Supplement with sinking algae wafers or blanched zucchini if your tank is spotlessly clean or runs out of natural diatoms. Keep a tight lid on your tank; active Nerites often forage right at the waterline and may wander out on nighttime patrols. Shell striping and markings vary naturally between wild-type specimens; photos represent healthy, conditioned stock. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy livestock! Will Tiger Nerite snails eat or damage my aquatic plants? Not at all. Tiger Nerites are strictly herbivorous biofilm and algae grazers. Their mouthparts are designed to scrape soft films and tough diatoms off hard surfaces, lacking the jaw power or inclination to chew through living plant tissue. They will safely browse over delicate stem leaves and dense carpeting without chewing holes or uprooting roots. 2. Can Tiger Nerite snails reproduce and take over my freshwater aquarium? No. While female Nerites will deposit small, tough white egg capsules on wood, rock, and glass, these eggs cannot hatch in freshwater. The larvae require brackish water with high salinity to develop, so your tank will never experience a population explosion or snail infestation. 3. Why is my Tiger Nerite snail flipped over or not moving? Nerite snails have a muscular foot that makes it difficult for them to flip over if they tumble upside down onto loose substrate. Check that your snail is righted onto a stable surface, ensure your water temperature is within the 72°F to 82°F range, and verify that your pH stays above 7.0 to prevent shell erosion and stress. 4. What tank mates work best with Tiger Nerite snails? They do exceptionally well with gentle community fish and dwarf shrimp, including Neocaridina, Caridina, Otocinclus, Corydoras, and small tetras. Avoid housing them with dedicated snail predators like Assassin Snails, Clown Loaches, Yo-yo Loaches, large cichlids, and aggressive freshwater crayfish.

Species Profile Orange Poso Rabbit Snails ( Tylomelania gemmifera "Orange") hail from the ancient, warm, mineral-rich lake systems of Sulawesi, Indonesia. Easily one of the most character-packed critters you can drop into a tank, they sport a vivid sherbet-orange body, a wrinkled elephant-like snout, and a heavy, textured cone shell that looks like a miniature piece of petrified wood. They spend their days bulldozing along the substrate with surprising speed, hoovering up leftover food, detritus, and biofilm like miniature vacuum cleaners. While they love roaming open spaces, they definitely appreciate some shaded hardscape overhangs to retreat to when high-intensity scape lighting gets overwhelming. Unlike pest snails that turn your filter intakes into nurseries overnight, Rabbit Snails reproduce at a leisurely, controlled pace, giving birth to fully formed, single miniature babies every month or so. **Note: All livestock orders will come carefully packaged with solid wall Styrofoam insulation and shipped via 1-day shipping only. No extra insulation needs to be added to your cart for your livestock. Key Features & Notes Bright orange body and long dark cone shell add contrast to substrate and rock lines. Active bottom scavenger that clears uneaten food, decaying plant waste, and biofilm. Reproduces slowly with single live births instead of fast pest snail egg clutches. Acclimation & Care Instructions Float the sealed transport bag for 15 to 20 minutes to equalize water temperatures before opening. Drip acclimate over 45 to 60 minutes using airline tubing to ease them into your tank's GH, KH, and pH levels. Sulawesi natives demand warmth; keep temperatures consistently in the mid-to-high 70s or low 80s; cold water will make them lethargic and suppress their appetite. Maintain hard, alkaline water (pH 7.6+) with plenty of calcium to keep their long cone shells thick, solid, and free of acid pitting. Target-feed with sinking spirulina wafers, blanched zucchini, or protein pellets; a 3-inch snail has a big appetite and can't survive on micro-biofilm alone. Provide soft sand or fine, rounded substrate where possible so their long, heavy shells can trail smoothly without getting wedged. Shell length and shell tip wear vary naturally between individual snails; photos represent healthy, well-fed stock. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy livestock! Temperament Peaceful, curious scavenger Adult Size Up to 3.0" (7.5 cm) Minimum Tank Size 20+ Gallons (Produces noticeable bioload) Water Parameters pH 7.6–8.4 | GH 6–8 | KH 4–8 | 76°F–84°F (24°C–29°C) Freshwater Breeding Yes (Slow live-bearing; single egg sac every 4–6 weeks) Origin Lake Poso, Sulawesi, Indonesia (Tank-raised) Frequently Asked Questions 1. Will Orange Poso Rabbit Snails munch on my live plants or wreck my aquascape? Generally, no, as long as they are well-fed. They do fantastic alongside tough epiphytes like Bucephalandra, Anubias, and Java Ferns. However, because they are big, heavy snails with healthy appetites, a hungry Rabbit Snail will consume soft-leafed plants or tissue culture plantlets. 2. Can Rabbit Snails overpopulate and overrun my tank like Ramshorn or Bladder snails? Not even close. Rabbit Snails are gonochoric (meaning they need both a male and a female to reproduce) and take about a full year just to reach sexual maturity. When they do breed, the female produces a single white capsule every 4 to 6 weeks that hatches into just one or two fully formed mini-snails. 3. Why is my Rabbit Snail inactive or closed up in its shell? Low water temperature is the most common cause. These snails are native to warm Sulawesi lakes and slow down dramatically if temperatures fall below 76°F. Verify your heater is running in their preferred 76°F to 84°F range, check that your pH is safely above 7.5, and review our Rabbit Snail Care Guide if you need troubleshooting steps for water hardness and diet. 4. What tank mates work best with Rabbit Snails? They thrive with gentle community fish and dwarf shrimp that won't pick at their long, fleshy antennae. We keep them alongside Neocaridina and Caridina shrimp, Otocinclus, Siamese Algae Eaters, peaceful tetras, and Corydoras. Skip known snail crushers or nippers like Clown Loaches, Yo-yo Loaches, Assassin Snails, aggressive Cichlids, and Crayfish.

It is common to see this plant in flooded areas in the wild and can be considered invasive in certain areas. This plant features rounded leaves that resemble coins and is a relatively easy plant to care for making it a popular choice amongst beginner hobbyists. This plant features a low growing pattern and will grow moderately, requiring periodic maintenance. Creeping Jenny is known for being a good nitrate indicator and will readily absorb excess in the planted aquarium. When given good conditions, this plant does produce small yellow flowers. listings.commonName: Limnophila Aromatica Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Meet Limnophila Aromatica, an aptly named aquatic stem plant known for its vibrant color spectrum and aromatic herbal foliage. Famous for its lanceolate leaves with serrated margins that radiate in whorls, this species displays a palette ranging from olive-green and lime to deep pink, magenta, and rich violet-red. When bruised or pruned, it releases a distinct citrus-herbal aroma, reflecting its traditional culinary use in Vietnamese cuisine. Growing up to 8 to 20 inches tall, Limnophila Aromatica serves as a dramatic centerpiece or colorful background hedge in medium-to-large planted aquariums and Dutch-style layouts. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Foliage displays a wide spectrum of colors from lime green to magenta, pink, and deep violet-red. Rapidly forms dense background hedges and structured Dutch-style street layouts. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide medium-to-high lighting and consistent iron dosing; while adaptable without mandatory CO2 injection, supplying pressurized CO2 and rich soil substrate yields robust growth and maximizes vibrant magenta and pink hues. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or rotting. Trim main stem tops with sharp straight scissors once they reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and expand coverage. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I achieve bright pink and red coloration on Limnophila Aromatica? While Limnophila Aromatica can grow under moderate conditions as a green-and-pink stem, achieving deep magenta, red, and purple foliage requires high light intensity, regular micronutrient dosing with liquid iron, and a nutrient-rich aquasoil. Adding pressurized CO2 further boosts density and color vividness. 3. How do I prepare Limnophila Aromatica Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture before planting? Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the dense cluster into smaller clumps or individual stems and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

Featuring tiny, deep green leaves that grow in a remarkably tight and dense habit, this epiphyte is a favorite for hobbyists looking to add big impact in nano aquariums. It adapts effortlessly to both submerged aquariums and high-humidity emersed environments, such as terrariums and paludariums. While they look gorgeous through front aquarium glass, they were originally developed for traditional top-down viewing, making them a centerpiece option for shallow rimless planted setups and summer patio tubs alike. Do Javanese Rice Fish need an aquarium heater? Yes. While Japanese rice fish ( Oryzias latipes ) tolerate cold water, Javanese rice fish are tropical natives from Southeast Asia. They need a steady water temperature between 72°F and 82°F to maintain proper immune function, feed normally, and stay active. 2. Can Javanese Rice Fish live in fresh water, or do they require salt? They thrive in standard freshwater planted tanks. They are a euryhaline species, meaning they can tolerate a wide salinity range from pure freshwater to mild brackish environments, but adding salt is not required for general health or breeding. 3. How do Javanese Rice Fish breed in an aquarium? Females carry clusters of fertilized eggs near the anal vent each morning before depositing them into fine-leafed stem plants, mosses, or spawning mops. For a complete walkthrough on water conditions, feeding, and fry collection, check out our comprehensive Japanese Rice Fish Care Guide . 4. Are Javanese Rice Fish safe to keep with dwarf shrimp? Adult Neocaridina and Caridina shrimp are safe alongside them. Because these fish stay near the surface and have very small mouths, they do not bother bottom-grazing adult shrimp. Tiny shrimplets swimming out in open water can be picked off opportunistically, so maintaining dense moss clumps and low-growing ground cover helps maximize shrimplet survival.

listings.description: Plant Profile Bred in Ukraine as a striking hybrid cross between Echinodorus horemanii 'Red' and Echinodorus barthii, Echinodorus 'Red Diamond' delivers rich ruby-red intensity to planted tanks. Under moderate to high lighting, newly emerging leaves unfurl in deep ruby, crimson, and reddish-purple tones that mature into an attractive dark olive green with distinct red veining. Unlike massive sword varieties that easily overwhelm smaller displays, 'Red Diamond' stays at a manageable medium scale, making it a stellar pick for midground zones or a cozy background accent in nano-to-medium aquariums. Tissue culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab-grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go-to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Notes Compact hybrid rosette features bold ruby-red and dark crimson foliage on new emerging leaves. Hardy, medium-scale species that brings intense jewel-toned contrast to midground centerpiece zones. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by carefully removing the plantlets from the cup and rinsing away all sterile nutrient gel under lukewarm, dechlorinated water before mounting. Plant the roots deeply into your aquarium soil, keeping the central crown resting just above the substrate line to prevent rot. All Echinodorus are heavy root feeders that rely on rich substrate nutrition; placing root tabs near the base supports steady, healthy leaf development. Provide moderate to high lighting; while CO2 injection isn't strictly required, good lighting will enhance its deep ruby-red colors. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf shedding during the initial transition period. Sword plants propagate through side shoots off of their leaves, which can be trimmed and replanted into the substrate. To control the size of your sword plant, you can remove the side shoots and older leaves. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. This guarantees that no pest snails, duckweed, hitchhikers, algae spores, or pesticides are introduced into your aquarium. 2. How do I clean and prepare the tissue culture gel before planting? Remove the plant clump from the cup and gently rinse off the clear nutrient gel under room-temperature water. You can then gently separate the rosette clump into individual plantlets using your fingers or tweezers before planting them into the substrate. 3. How do I maintain and enhance the deep ruby-red color on Echinodorus 'Red Diamond'? Provide moderate-to-high lighting directly above the plant and supplement the substrate with iron-rich root tabs. High light levels and carbon supplementation encourage new inner leaves to develop rich crimson and ruby tones rather than fading to dark green.

Plant Profile Built for compact setups and low-tech parameters, Anubias Chili Jalapeno is a rare, bite-sized variation that is here to add some serious flavor and spice to your aquascape. True to its name, this miniature aquatic epiphyte produces small, fleshy leaves in a deep, rich green tone. It grows with a neat, compact habit, making it a great pick for tucking into hardscape gaps or detailing foreground zones. It grows slowly, adapts easily to standard low-tech water parameters, and thrives in aquariums or emersed in humid terrariums. Key Features & Benefits Thick, fleshy miniature foliage introduces a distinct succulent-like texture for small-scale nano aquariums. Compact 1-to-3-inch height fills tiny hardscape gaps without overwhelming surrounding foreground plants. Thick, durable leaf construction naturally resists grazing from plant-eating cichlids, snails, and active dwarf shrimp. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Avoid intense light and ensure good water flow to prevent spot algae on slow‑growing leaves. CO₂ is optional but improves growth and leaf density. Learn more about planting these species by reading our guide on How to Plant Epiphyte Aquatic Plants. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. Keep the rhizome above the substrate to prevent rot. 2. Does it require CO2 or high lighting? No. It thrives in low lighting without CO2 injection. While adding CO2 speeds up growth, it is completely optional. 3. Is this plant safe for shrimp, snails, and fish? Yes, Anubias Chili Jalapeno is 100% safe for all freshwater fish, shrimp (including sensitive Caridina and Neocaridina), and snails. Its tough leaves are also resistant to plant-eating fish like cichlids or goldfish.

Plant Profile Eriocaulon Cinereum is a highly sought-after, rare pipewort native to shallow waters across Asia. Known for its distinct, spiky rosette of needle-like leaves radiating from a central crown, it looks just like a tiny, bright-green sea urchin sitting on your substrate. Erio Cinereum grows in tidy, geometric tufts that reach up to 3 inches in height, serving as a focal point in the foreground and creating architectural contrast against surrounding carpet plants and hardscape bases. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Spiky, hedge-hog rosette structure delivers a distinct sea-urchin aesthetic in the foreground. Compact growth form provides a focal accent that breaks up uniform lawn carpets. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers under cool water before dividing and planting. Use a dry start method or Wabi Kusa setup to allow roots to establish firmly before flooding the aquarium. Provide high-intensity lighting and pressurized CO2 injection alongside soft, slightly acidic water conditions (GH 2–5) to support vigorous growth. Maintain stable water parameters and good water clarity to encourage steady root development and prevent leaf melting during transition. To propagate, wait for mature crowns to naturally split at the base, then use a sharp, sterile blade to separate the daughter rosettes and replant them directly into your aquarium soil to expand the foreground group. Master the basics by learning how to properly grow tissue culture plants to ensure your layout establishes smoothly. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I plant Eriocaulon Cinereum tissue culture? Rinse away the nutrient gel under cool water, separate the cup into individual rosettes, and use pinsettes to push the extensive root base deep into nutrient-rich aquasoil so the crown rests cleanly on the soil surface. 2. Why is Eriocaulon Cinereum considered a difficult species to keep? Erio Cinereum demands soft, acidic water, high light, reliable pressurized CO2, and a nutrient-heavy substrate. In hard water or low-CO2 setups, the delicate needle-like leaves quickly turn white or melt. 3. What should I do if my Eriocaulon Cinereum starts sending up a flower spike? Eriocaulon species often direct energy away from leaf production when flowering under stress. Snipping off emerging flower spikes near the crown base encourages the plant to channel energy back into horizontal crown splitting and leaf growth.

Plant Profile If you love vintage aquascaping classics with a rare modern twist, Cryptocoryne affinis 'Red' brings fantastic nostalgic charm to your tank. Found naturally along the sandy riverbanks of West Malaysia, this historic species was once a staple of the hobby and is making a well-deserved comeback thanks to its distinct brownish-red leaf borders. As with all crypt plants, this plant can be sensitive to changes in water parameters and doesn’t like to be moved. Key Features & Benefits Green foliage with distinctive brownish-red borders offers a unique, high-contrast look in midground zones. Can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups where it will produce unique flowering spathes. Resilient species that adapts to low-tech setups without requiring intense lighting. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Crypt species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Why are my Cryptocoryne Affinis Red leaves melting away? Transplanting Crypts into new water parameters often triggers a temporary reaction where old leaves dissolve. As long as the root system remains undisturbed in healthy soil, fresh foliage will sprout shortly. Check out our guide on Cryptocoryne melt for step-by-step recovery tips. 2. Can I move my Cryptocoryne to a new spot in the tank later? It is best to leave your Crypt permanently in its original spot. Uprooting an established plant damages its fine root hairs and almost always causes another cycle of leaf melt. 3. Do I need root tabs if I already use liquid fertilizers for my Cryptocoryne? Yes. Because Cryptocoryne plants absorb the vast majority of their nutrients through their roots rather than their leaves, providing nutrient-rich aquasoil or root tabs inside sand or gravel is far more effective than relying on water column liquid fertilizers alone.

Product Overview Scrubbing stubborn algae varieties like Black Beard Algae (BBA) or Staghorn off porous hardscape requires an abrasive bristle that can dig into texture without buckling. The Aqua Worx Algae Brush provides targeted scrubbing power to clean rocks, stones, and driftwood across your aquascape. Key Features & Benefits Abrasive Heavy-Duty Bristles: Stiff, durable bristles easily scrub away tough algae types like Black Beard Algae (BBA), Staghorn, and Green Spot Algae (GSA). Porous Hardscape Precision: Designed specifically to penetrate textured surfaces like lava rock, seiryu stone, dragon stone, and intricate driftwood. Targeted Maintenance Leverage: Ergonomic handle offers strong scrubbing control in tight hardscape gaps and low-lying tank zones. Restores Natural Texture: Safely strips surface buildup without damaging dense wood fibers or eroding hardscape detail. Technical Specifications Attribute Specification Brand Aqua Worx Product Line Aqua Worx Maintenance Tools Tool Type Aquarium Hardscape Algae Scrubbing Brush Bristle Material Durable High-Density Abrasive Bristles Ideal For Hardscape Types Rocks (Seiryu, Lava, Dragon), Driftwood (Manzanita, Spider Wood), & Decor Target Algae Types Black Beard Algae (BBA), Staghorn Algae, Green Spot Algae (GSA), & Biofilm Recommended Tank Size Nano to Large Aquariums Care & Maintenance Instructions Rinse the brush head thoroughly with fresh tap water immediately after scrubbing algae or performing liquid spot treatments. Shake off excess water and dry completely before storing to prevent cross-contamination between tanks. Store in a clean, dry location away from high humidity to maintain bristle firmness. Frequently Asked Questions 1. Can I use the Aqua Worx Algae Brush on aquarium glass or acrylic panels? No. This brush features stiff, abrasive bristles intended strictly for hardscape like stone and wood. Using it on glass or acrylic panels may cause micro-scratches. Use dedicated glass scrapers or soft sponges for viewing panels. 2. Is this brush effective when paired with liquid algae spot treatments? Yes. Gently scrubbing BBA or Staghorn with this brush prior to or after liquid spot treatments helps loosen dead organic matter, speeding up algae decay and removal by tank inhabitants like shrimp and snails. 3. How do I identify and treat the root cause of my aquarium algae? While manual scrubbing keeps hardscape clean, balancing lighting, CO2, and nutrient levels is essential for long-term control. Read our comprehensive Aquascaper's Guide to an Algae-Free Tank to identify your algae and restore tank balance.

Plant Profile Java Fern Coral is a stunning newer cultivar that brings a dramatic, reef-like silhouette to the lineup of low-light aquarium plants. Similar to Java Fern Trident in overall structure, this variety stands out with randomized, wildly variable leaf splits that give each frond a unique, branching coral appearance. To make it even more captivating, new emerging growth often displays an attractive pinkish-red flush before maturing into a rich, vibrant green. Key Features & Notes Tough, fibrous foliage easily withstands curious nipping from herbivorous fish like cichlids, goldfish, and large snails. Randomized, coral-like branching fronds featuring pinkish-red young leaves create an eye-catching, multi-colored focal point in midground hardscapes. Exceptional hardiness lets it thrive in non-CO2 tanks and low-light environments. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Java Fern Coral is an epiphytic fern that should be attached to rocks or driftwood with aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as it will rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard setups, gentle water movement and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and broader fronds. Master long-term care and troubleshoot common leaf issues by checking out our Java Fern Care Guide . Final size and foliage pattern depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Microsorum pteropus 'Coral' (syn. Leptochilus pteropus ) Common Name(s) Java Fern Coral, Java Fern Coral Reef Family Polypodiaceae Plant Type Epiphyte (Rhizome Fern) Care Difficulty Beginner / Easy (Low-Tech Compatible) Light Requirement Low to Medium CO2 Requirement Not Required (Recommended for Best Color) Placement / Usage Midground, Focal Hardscape Accent, Nano Layouts Height / Size 3"–6" (7.5–15 cm) Growth Rate Slow Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 | Temperature 68°F–82°F (20°C–28°C) Propagation Method Rhizome Division & Adventitious Plantlets Origin Indonesia / Cultivated Variety Frequently Asked Questions 1. What makes Java Fern Coral different from Java Fern Trident? While both varieties feature branched, lobed fronds, Java Fern Coral has much more randomized, unpredictable leaf splits that resemble natural marine coral structures. Additionally, new growth on Java Fern Coral often emerges with a distinctive pinkish-red hue before transitioning into green. 2. Why are the new leaves on my Java Fern Coral pinkish-red? That subtle pink-to-red flush on young fronds is a natural characteristic of the Coral cultivar! As the leaves mature and harden under your aquarium light, they gradually darken into a deep, healthy green. 3. Can I plant Java Fern Coral into substrate? No. Java Fern Coral is an epiphyte that absorbs nutrients directly from the water column through its foliage and fine root network. If you bury its horizontal rhizome beneath aquarium soil, sand, or gravel, the stem will suffocate, rot, and die. Always attach it to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread. 4. Will fish like cichlids or goldfish eat Java Fern Coral? Generally, no. Java Fern leaves are thick, fibrous, and contain bitter-tasting compounds that deter most plant-eating fish. While aggressive diggers might knock it off hardscape if not glued securely, they rarely consume the foliage.

listings.commonName: Anubias Nana Golden UNS Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Anubias Nana Golden is the vibrant, chartreuse sibling of the classic Anubias Nana , and it is ready to bring a major golden hour glow-up to your tank. If your current layout is looking a bit too uniformly dark and you are searching for a way to make your hardscape pop, this eye-catching variant is here to help you strike gold. Its bright yellow-green foliage creates a stunning high-contrast focal point when nestled against dark lava rocks, shadowy driftwood, or deep green mosses. Tissue culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab-grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go-to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits The bright yellow-green leaves offer an extraordinary color contrast against darker hardscape. Its hardy nature makes it one of the easiest golden-hued plants in the entire hobby. Care & Planting Instructions Remove the plantlets from the cup and rinse away the sterile nutrient gel under lukewarm, dechlorinated water. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Avoid intense light and ensure good water flow to prevent spot algae on slow‑growing leaves. CO₂ is recommended to assist with the tissue culture transition and support healthy growth. Master the prep and planting process by checking out a beginner's guide to tissue culture plants to prevent your delicate new plantlets from melting or floating away. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Anubias barteri var. nana 'Golden' Common Name(s) Anubias Nana Golden Family Araceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Epiphyte (Rhizome) Care Difficulty Easy / Beginner-Friendly Light Requirement Low to Medium CO2 Requirement Recommended for TC transition Placement / Usage Foreground, Nano Hardscape, Midground Crevices Height / Size 3 – 5 inches Growth Rate Slow Water Parameters pH 6.0 – 7.5 | Temperature 68°F – 82°F (20°C – 28°C) Propagation Method Separate by Rhizome Division Origin West Africa / Lab Tissue Culture Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I plant Anubias Nana Golden? Attach the plant directly to driftwood or rocks using aquarium-safe super glue gel, thread, or fishing line. Keep the rhizome above the substrate to prevent rot. 2. Does it require CO2 or high lighting? No. It thrives in low lighting without CO2 injection. While adding CO2 speeds up growth and aids in the tissue culture transition, it is completely optional. 3. Is this plant safe for shrimp, snails, and fish? Yes, Anubias Nana Golden is 100% safe for all freshwater fish, shrimp (including sensitive Caridina and Neocaridina), and snails. Its tough leaves are also resistant to plant-eating fish like cichlids or goldfish.

Plant Profile Alternanthera Reineckii 'Green', widely known in the hobby as AR Green, is a unique and captivating color variation of the iconic red stem plant native to the rivers and wetlands of Central and South America. Featuring vibrant ruby-red central stems lined with soft lime-green leaves that reveal glowing pink undersides, this species offers a breathtaking bi-color contrast in planted aquariums. Reaching 4 to 12 inches in height, its compact upright growth makes it an exceptional choice for midground groupings and Dutch-style plant streets, where the subtle pink undertones add depth and warmth alongside green and deep-red neighbors. Key Features & Benefits Unique dual-tone foliage combines soft green upper leaf surfaces with bright pink undersides and magenta stems. Moderate-growing stem habit easily forms dense, compact midground bushes when routinely pruned. Hardy and adaptable species providing ideal shelter and coverage for shy fish and aquatic shrimp. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight surrounding the root base, then strip lower leaf tips so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to insert individual stems 1 to 2 inches deep into aquarium soil. Provide medium-to-high lighting and pressurized CO2 injection; consistent fertilization rich in iron and micronutrients intensifies pink leaf undersides and prevents leaf deformation. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or leaf shedding. To propagate, trim main stem tops with sharp straight shears and replant the trimmings directly into the substrate. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I prep bunched Alternanthera Reineckii Green before planting? Remove the lead weight or metal band along with the foam wrap surrounding the lower roots. Inspect the base of the stems, gently rinse away any debris in room-temperature water, and snip off any bruised stem bases before inserting individual shoots into substrate using pinsettes. 2. How do I enhance the pink undersides of Alternanthera Reineckii Green? While the upper surface of AR Green remains soft green, maintaining medium-to-high light levels, pressurized CO2, and regular dosing of iron-rich micro-fertilizers will turn the undersides of the leaves a vivid, glowing pink. 3. Why are the lower leaves on my AR Green curling or dropping off? Lower leaf curling or loss is often caused by insufficient light reaching the base of the stems or a deficiency in key nutrients like iron or calcium. Space individual stems 1 inch apart when planting to ensure light reaches the lower foliage.

listings.commonName: Anubias Barteri Petite Round on Lava Stone
listings.description: Plant Profile Skip the superglue and fishing line with Anubias Barteri Petite Round on Lava Stone, which comes pre-bound and ready for instant placement. Featuring dark green, compact leaves with smooth, rounded edges, this charming dwarf variety offers a lush, button-like appearance that fits seamlessly into foreground and midground layouts. Because it arrives established on porous lava rock, it takes all the guesswork out of mounting epiphytes. Growing to a compact height of 2 to 4 inches, it is perfectly suited for low-tech aquariums or humid emersed setups, allowing you to drop a healthy, established accent straight into your aquascape without worrying about buried rhizomes or floating plants. Key Features & Benefits Pre-attached to natural lava rock for instant, hassle-free placement anywhere in your aquarium or terrarium. Compact, smooth, round leaves create a neat, tidy dwarf aesthetic that excels in nano tanks and tight hardscape layouts. Incredibly resilient, low-light tolerant, and tough enough to withstand grazing from active fish, snails, and dwarf shrimp. Care & Planting Instructions Place the pre-attached lava stone directly onto substrate or nestle it into hardscape crevices; do not bury the rhizome. Maintain stable water parameters to ensure smooth acclimation and reduce leaf shedding. Avoid intense light and ensure healthy water flow to prevent slow-growing leaves from collecting spot algae. CO₂ is optional but improves growth speed and leaf density. Learn more about planting these species by reading our guide on How to Plant Epiphyte Aquatic Plants. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth!
