Plant Profile Sitting right between Anubias Nana Petite and standard Anubias Nana in leaf size, Anubias Nana Bonsai fills the gap for nano aquarium plants. It produces small, teardrop-shaped dark green leaves on short, dense stems that form tight clusters. Reaching 2 to 4 inches in total height, it serves as a scaled midground accent for nano tanks or a detailed gap-filler for hardscape. Like all epiphytes, it attaches directly to rock or wood via rhizome. It grows slowly under low light, tolerates a wide range of water parameters, and thrives submerged in aquariums or emersed in humid terrariums. Key Features & Benefits The mid-sized green foliage serves as a transition plant between tiny foreground varieties and larger background species. Its thick and leathery leaves are highly resilient against curious or herbivorous fish. This incredibly hardy specimen easily adapts to a wide variety of water conditions. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Avoid intense light and ensure good water flow to prevent spot algae on slow‑growing leaves. CO₂ is optional but improves growth and leaf density. Learn more about planting these species by reading our guide on How to Plant Epiphyte Aquatic Plants. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. listings.commonName: Anubias Nana Long Wavy on Driftwood
listings.description: Plant Profile Common Name: Anubias Wavy Anubias Nana Long Wavy on Driftwood is a striking variation that is ready to catch some serious waves in your next aquascape. This plant stands out from the crowd with its small, dark green, oblong leaves that feature a beautifully crinkled, wavy texture and a tough, waxy finish. If you want to add instant character to your foreground without the hassle of gluing or tying, this pre-attached combo is here to help you shore up a stunning layout on day one. The porous natural driftwood base is full of perfect nooks and crannies for the roots, making it a highly adaptable centerpiece that transitions flawlessly between fully submerged aquariums and high-humidity terrariums. Key Features & Benefits The unique oblong and heavily waved foliage adds an intricate, ruffled texture to your foreground that stands out sharply against standard smooth leaves. This specimen comes pre-attached to natural driftwood, so you can skip the messy super glue and place it instantly into your aquascape without any floating. Its remarkably tough and waxy leaf structure easily resists grazing from active tank inhabitants, keeping your carefully designed layout completely intact. Care & Planting Instructions Place the attached driftwood piece directly onto your substrate or nestled within your hardscape, ensuring you never bury the horizontal rhizome beneath gravel or soil. Avoid burying the thick horizontal stem in gravel or soil because restricting water flow around the rhizome will cause the plant to melt, rot, and die. Provide low to moderate lighting and optional carbon dioxide injection to achieve faster growth and more robust leaves, though it will happily thrive without high-tech setups. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to ensure your new greenery acclimates smoothly without shedding leaves. Position the plant away from intense, direct light and ensure healthy water flow to prevent slow-growing leaves from collecting unwanted spot algae. Feel free to customize your new hardscape piece by dressing the remaining wood cracks with your favorite aquatic mosses. Master the long-term care and propagation of this unique genus in the comprehensive article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Plant Profile Eliminating the hassle of super glue and thread, Anubias Nana on Driftwood provides an instant hardscape centerpiece for planted tanks. Combining one of the most iconic aquatic epiphytes with a unique piece of natural wood, this pre-attached display allows aquascapers to skip complex prep work entirely. Featuring dense, deep green foliage anchored to natural driftwood (approx. 3-4 inches), it anchors nano tanks and midground layouts with immediate visual texture. Bulletproof and resilient, it adapts effortlessly to low-tech submerged aquariums or humid emersed setups like terrariums and paludariums right out of the box. Key Features & Benefits Pre-attached natural driftwood base allows instant tank placement. Hardy epiphyte adapts to a wide range of water parameters in beginner aquariums. Thick leaves resist grazing from plant-eating cichlids, snails, and active dwarf shrimp. Care & Planting Instructions Place the pre-attached driftwood piece directly onto your substrate or hardscape; never bury the attached plant's rhizome. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Avoid intense direct light and ensure good water flow to prevent spot algae on slow‑growing leaves. CO₂ is optional but improves growth speed and leaf density. Learn more about styling attached epiphytes by reading our guide on How to Plant Epiphyte Aquatic Plants. Plant Profile Anubias Nana Ovalis is a beautifully distinct variation of the classic Anubias family that is ready to bring a softer look to your aquascape. This less common gem stands out with its tall stems and large, dark green, oval-shaped leaves that feature a soft, gently waved texture. If your tank's midground is looking a bit rigid and you want to smooth things over, this hardy epiphyte is the perfect choice to help you round out your design. It is wonderfully versatile, thriving completely submerged, growing emersed in humid terrariums, or even floating freely in bare-bottomed setups. Key Features & Benefits The large, soft, and rounded wavy foliage introduces a unique organic shape and gentle movement that beautifully breaks up aggressive hardscape lines. This incredibly resilient variety boasts a massive pH tolerance range, making it one of the most stable and stress-free options for beginners or varying water types. Its taller stem profile makes it an exceptionally flexible landscaping tool that works brilliantly as an anchor plant for the midground area of your tank. Care & Planting Instructions Carefully remove the plant from its pot and clear away all rockwool from the roots. For a deep dive on prepping potted plants, click here. Secure the plant directly to your chosen hardscape elements using aquarium-safe glue or thread. Avoid burying the thick horizontal stem in gravel or soil because restricting water flow around the rhizome will cause the plant to melt, rot, and die. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to ensure your new greenery acclimates smoothly without shedding leaves. Position the plant away from intense, direct light and ensure healthy water flow to prevent slow-growing leaves from collecting unwanted spot algae. Provide low to moderate lighting and optional carbon dioxide injection to achieve faster growth and more robust leaves, though it will happily thrive without high-tech setups. Read more on securing and styling these plants in your layout by reading our step-by-step guide on How to Plant Epiphyte Aquatic Plants. Plant Profile Anubias Nana Tropica is a popular dwarf epiphyte with rich, dark green, elliptical leaves. Reaching 3 to 5 inches tall, this variety forms a tighter, slightly broader-leaved rosette than standard Anubias Nana, making it a dependable foreground accent, nano centerpiece, or midground filler across driftwood and stone. If you are new to planted tanks and want a foolproof way to get your feet wet, this incredibly forgiving beginner plant is here to help you succeed on your first try. Key Features & Benefits Glossy, dark green elliptical foliage provides a timeless aesthetic that scales easily for nano tanks and large layouts alike. Adapts to diverse water parameters, making it an ideal choice for beginner hobbyists. Durable foliage naturally resists grazing from fish, snails, and shrimp. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Avoid intense light and ensure good water flow to prevent spot algae on slow‑growing leaves. CO₂ is optional but improves growth and leaf density. Learn more about planting these species by reading our guide on How to Plant Epiphyte Aquatic Plants. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. How is Anubias Nana Tropica different from standard Anubias Nana or Nana Petite? Selected by the Danish nursery Tropica, this cultivar sits right between the two in scale. It stays more compact and bushy than standard Anubias Nana with slightly wider, rounder leaf blades, while growing roughly twice the size of miniature Anubias Nana Petite. 2. Can I wedge Anubias Nana Tropica into hardscape cracks instead of gluing it? Yes. Its sturdy rhizome and dense root mass tuck easily into narrow gaps between stone and driftwood. 3. Why are older leaves on my Anubias Nana Tropica developing green spots? Because this cultivar grows slowly, mature leaves sit under your light for months and easily collect green spot algae if positioned directly under high-output LEDs. Place it in partial shade under taller plants or surface floaters.

Plant Profile Ceratopteris Cornuta, commonly known as Broad-leaf Water Sprite, is a classic aquatic fern and a longtime favorite for aquascapers looking to outcompete algae. Whether you float it on the water surface as an intricate canopy or plant it directly into the substrate as a lush background centerpiece, this prolific grower acts as a heavy nutrient sponge, absorbing excess nitrates and waste from the water column. Its branchy, delicate foliage makes it a beloved staple for fish breeders and shrimp keepers, providing endless grazing surfaces and cozy hiding spots for delicate fry and shrimplets. Highly adaptable and forgiving, Water Sprite thrives in soft or hard water alike, making it an excellent, low-maintenance choice for low-tech tanks and paludariums. Key Features & Benefits Branchy foliage creates a lush floating canopy or background bush. Absorbs excess nitrates and biological waste from the water column to suppress algae. Dense leaves offer shelter, shade, and grazing area for timid fish, shrimplets, and newborn fry. Care & Planting Instructions Gently place the plant directly onto the water surface to float freely, or anchor the base into your substrate as a background stem plant. Keep surface agitation moderate to low, ensuring heavy filter currents or spray bars do not constantly submerge floating fronds. Provide low to moderate lighting to maintain steady growth and lush green coloration across the delicate leaves. Thin out or trim the floating fronds regularly using sharp aquascaping scissors to prevent the canopy from completely shading submerged plants below. Propagate by snipping healthy fronds or separating adventitious baby plantlets that naturally form along older leaf edges. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Can I let Water Sprite float on the water surface or does it have to be planted? Water Sprite is extremely versatile and can be grown either way. When left to float on the water surface, it forms delicate fronds that spread horizontally while extending feeder roots into the water column. If you prefer to plant it in substrate, anchor the base gently without burying the crown to grow it as a bushy background fern. 2. How do I propagate new Water Sprite plants? Propagation is effortless because this plant produces tiny plantlets along the edges of mature fronds. You can simply snip off these adventitious plantlets once they grow small roots and place them elsewhere to float, or snip main stems and replant them into your substrate. 3. Why is my floating Water Sprite growing so fast and blocking light? Because floating plants for aquariums have direct access to ambient carbon dioxide in the air, Water Sprite grows exponentially faster at the surface than submerged plants. Regular maintenance and thinning with sharp aquascaping shears are essential to prevent the dense floating mat from blocking light to your foreground and midground plants.

Plant Profile Cryptocoryne wendtii 'Brown Indo' is an easygoing freshwater aquarium plant with warm bronze and brown foliage, making it an easy way to break up an all-green layout or soften the transition against lighter rocks and sand. This Indonesian variant develops darker tones and clearer leaf patterns than the standard brown form when grown submerged. Like most crypts, it dislikes being moved once its roots are settled and can lose leaves if your water parameters change quickly. Given a steady spot in quality substrate, it grows into a clean midground bush that holds its space without crowding out neighboring plants. Key Features & Benefits Bronze and dark brown leaves create natural contrast when set next to bright green stem plants or light hardscape. Beginner-friendly pick that grows well in low-tech setups without high lighting or mandatory CO2 injection. Can be grown emersed in high-humidity paludarium or terrarium setups. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Cryptocoryne species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel to supply essential subterranean nutrients. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth and fuller foliage density, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Cryptocoryne species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting subterranean runners or replanting offshoot plantlets. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. How does the Indonesian variant differ from standard Cryptocoryne Wendtii Brown? The Indonesian variant tends to show a darker, richer brown color on its leaves with more noticeable pattern lines compared to the lighter bronze look of regular Wendtii Brown. 2. Can Cryptocoryne Wendtii Brown Indo thrive in low-tech aquariums? Yes. It handles lower light levels and doesn't require injected CO2, making it a reliable pick for simple low-tech setups as long as the roots have access to nutrients in the substrate. 3. How do I help my Cryptocoryne Wendtii Brown Indo recover if it melts after planting? Crypt melt is normal when moving into a new tank while the plant adjusts to different water chemistry. Siphon or trim away any rotting leaves, keep your water clean and stable, and leave the roots buried in the substrate so new leaves can emerge. For more details, take a look at our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt .

Plant Profile Showcasing a unique architectural growth habit that stands out from typical upright swords, Echinodorus horizontalis is a rare South American species prized for its wide-spreading structure. True to its name, this distinctive plant grows broader than it is tall, extending its firm, heart-shaped (cordate) leaves horizontally on long petioles to form a broad, umbrella-like canopy. Newly emerging leaves open in warm, delicate shades of brownish-pink and coppery-tan before maturing into a solid, light-to-medium green. It serves as a spectacular midground centerpiece or background accent that adds structural depth! Key Features & Notes Signature horizontal canopy extends broad foliage outward parallel to the substrate. Newly unfurled foliage displays warm brownish-pink to coppery-tan tones before maturing to green. Hardy and adaptable species that delivers unique architectural layout depth without requiring high-maintenance care. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Plant the roots deeply into your aquarium soil, keeping the central crown resting just above the substrate line to prevent rot. All Echinodorus are heavy root feeders that rely on rich substrate nutrition; placing root tabs near the base supports steady, healthy leaf development. Supplemental CO2 injection accelerates growth and encourages denser, fuller foliage, though the plant will still grow steadily in low-tech setups. Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf shedding during the initial transition period. Sword plants propagate through side shoots off of their leaves, which can be trimmed and replanted into the substrate. Plant Profile Java Fern on Driftwood offers a complete, pre-mounted hardscape centerpiece featuring one of the most iconic low-light aquarium plants in the hobby. Characterized by its classic broad emerald fronds pre-secured to natural, aquarium-safe driftwood, this ready-to-drop arrangement eliminates the tedious work of tying or gluing individual rhizomes. Virtually bulletproof and delightfully unbothered by tough water conditions or plant-eating fish, it brings immediate structure, height, and natural texture to any aquarium size. Key Features & Notes Tough, fibrous foliage easily withstands curious nipping from herbivorous fish like cichlids, goldfish, and large snails. Pre-attached to natural driftwood pieces, providing an effortless centerpiece that requires zero gluing, tying, or substrate planting. Exceptional hardiness lets it thrive in non-CO2 tanks and low-light environments. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by rinsing the mounted driftwood piece gently in clean freshwater to remove any loose debris before placing it directly into your aquarium. Java Fern on Driftwood is an epiphytic fern that comes pre-bound to hardscape; position the driftwood directly on top of your substrate or wedged between rocks, ensuring the horizontal rhizome remains exposed and unburied. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard setups, gentle water movement and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and broader fronds. Master long-term care and troubleshoot common leaf issues by checking out our Java Fern Care Guide . Leptochilus pteropus ) Common Name(s) Java Fern on Driftwood, Java Fern Mounted Family Polypodiaceae Plant Type Epiphyte Pre-Attached to Hardscape Care Difficulty Beginner / Easy (Low-Tech Compatible) Light Requirement Low to Medium CO2 Requirement Not Required (Beneficial) Placement / Usage Midground Centerpiece, Instant Hardscape Layout Height / Size Small (3"–4"), Medium (5"–6"), Large (7"–8"+) Growth Rate Slow to Moderate Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 | Temperature 68°F–82°F (20°C–28°C) Propagation Method Rhizome Division & Adventitious Plantlets Origin Indonesia Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are there small black spots and tiny leaves growing under my Java Fern leaves? Do not panic; your plant is not diseased! Java Fern reproduces naturally through adventitious plantlets. Small dark bumps (sporangia) form along the undersides of mature leaves, sprouting tiny brown roots and mini green fronds. Once these baby plantlets develop 3–4 leaves, you can gently pop them off the mother leaf and glue them elsewhere in your aquarium. 2. Can I remove the Java Fern from the driftwood piece? Yes. If you wish to detach it later, you can carefully snip the securing thread or cut the roots away from the wood. Once separated, the rhizomes can be re-bound or glued onto other hardscape features in your aquarium. 3. Can I bury the attached driftwood piece in the substrate? You can rest the driftwood piece on top of your substrate, but you must ensure the green rhizome of the Java Fern remains above the substrate line. Burying the wood so deeply that the rhizome gets covered will cause the fern to rot and die. 4. Will fish like cichlids or goldfish eat Java Fern on Driftwood? Generally, no. Java Fern leaves are thick, fibrous, and contain bitter-tasting compounds that deter most plant-eating fish. Plant Profile Cuphea Anagalloidea is a rare, compact stem plant that represents the first species from the Cuphea genus cultivated for aquarium use. Historically confused with Rotala sp. 'Araguaia' or Bacopa sp. 'Red' , this aquatic species produces small, rounded leaves along delicate creeping stems. Under targeted high-tech conditions, the foliage transitions from soft yellow-green to deep orange and bright red tones. Reaching a compact height of 1 to 4 inches, its low growth profile makes it an excellent candidate for foreground-to-midground accent rows or Dutch-style plant streets. Delivering bold color contrast and fine leaf texture right out of the pot, it’s a great pick for experienced hobbyists branching out from standard green aquatic plants. Key Features & Benefits Compact creeping growth habit creates low-profile red and orange accent rows in foreground and midground areas. Foliage color shifts from golden-amber to deep red under strong lighting and consistent nutrient dosing. Rare botanical addition that brings distinct leaf geometry and color depth to high-tech aquascapes. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip lower foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. * Cuphea stems are delicate, so handle each stem with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant individual stems 1 inch apart into your aquarium soil. Provide high-intensity lighting and pressurized CO2 injection; consistent liquid fertilization rich in iron supports vibrant red leaf coloration and prevents lower leaf shedding. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable, soft to moderately hard acidic water parameters (pH below 7.0) and avoid sudden parameter swings, as this demanding species is sensitive to water chemistry shifts. To propagate, trim main stem tops with sharp straight shears and replant the cuttings directly into your aquarium soil. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Key Features & Benefits Striking reddish-orange sunset coloration adds vibrant visual impact to background zones. Creates a distinct focal point and contrasts with green stem plants. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight (or pot) and remove cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the roots, then strip lower foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide medium-to-high lighting and pressurized CO2 injection; consistent fertilization with a specialized liquid macro and micro formula yields robust stem growth and prevents bottom leaf yellowing. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or rotting. Trim main stem tops with sharp straight scissors once they reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and thicken the bush. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Rotala ramosior 'Sunset' Common Name(s) Rotala Sunset, Rotala Ramosior Sunset, Ammannia Sulawesi Family Lythraceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Stem Plant Care Difficulty Medium to Advanced Light Requirement Medium to High CO2 Requirement Recommended (Essential for vivid red/orange coloration) Placement / Usage Midground / Background Centerpiece Height / Size 3–15”+ Growth Rate Medium Water Parameters pH 5.5–7.0 Propagation Method Cuttings (Cut stem tops or lateral shoots and replant) Origin North America Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I achieve a thick, bushy forest with Rotala Sunset? To encourage Rotala Sunset to form a dense hedge, routinely trim the main stem tops once established. Each cut site will sprout multiple lateral side shoots, doubling the stem density and creating a tight, bushy group. 3. How do I transition Rotala Florida Sunset from emersed to submerged growth? When transitioning from emersed to submerged growth, plant bare stems securely into rich substrate under high lighting and keep water parameters stable. As new growth adapts, the plant will shed its land foliage and sprout intense purplish-red underwater leaves. Once new shoots develop, trim away old lower growth to encourage dense branching.

listings.commonName: Alternanthera Reineckii Bronze Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Meet Alternanthera Reineckii Bronze, aka AR Bronze, a hobby favorite whose olive-green to bronze leaf tops and magenta-copper undersides bring a warm, earthy color shift most red stems can only dream of pulling off. And unlike its notoriously high-maintenance red-stem cousins, AR Bronze holds onto its rich tones without demanding a whole routine. Growing 4 to 12 inches tall, it fills in as a dense midground accent or a colorful background hedge that plays beautifully off bright green neighbors. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Bronze, olive, and copper leaf tops with magenta undersides add warm contrast. Beginner-friendly red stem variant that holds color easily. Dense foliage shelters dwarf shrimp and shy fish. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide medium-to-high lighting; regular dosing of liquid fertilizers like UNS Plant Food to maintain healthy nitrate and phosphate levels alongside pressurized CO2 injection will prevent dull orange fading and speed up growth. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or rotting. Trim main stem tops with sharp straight scissors once they reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and expand coverage. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Why are the leaves on my AR Bronze dulling to an orange color? While AR Bronze is easier to keep colorful than other red stems, leaves fading or dulling to a muted orange usually indicate insufficient lighting, low nitrates, or a lack of macro nutrients. Regular dosing with liquid fertilizers like UNS Plant Food restores deep bronze and magenta tones. 3. How do I prepare Alternanthera Reineckii Bronze Tissue Culture before planting? Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the dense cluster into smaller clumps or individual stems and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

Plant Profile Showcasing breathtaking, fully white-to-cream leaves, Anubias White Rose Tissue Culture is an extremely rare and coveted collector's cultivar. Lacking heavy chlorophyll across its ethereal foliage, it introduces an unmatched high-contrast focal point against dark hardscape and standard green flora. With very little information available on this brand-new cultivar, care is assumed to be similar to other Anubias species, especially other variegated forms, requiring steady parameters, gentle lighting, and patience as it adds its ethereal beauty to your aquascape. Key Features & Benefits Stunning, fully white-to-cream foliage provides unparalleled visual contrast impossible to replicate with standard green plants. Compact, slow-growing epiphyte habit makes it an ultimate showstopper for nano aquariums and high-end collector scapes. The sterile laboratory environment guarantees your new plant arrives completely free of pests. Care & Planting Instructions Remove the plantlets from the cup and rinse away the sterile nutrient gel under lukewarm, dechlorinated water. For instructions on planting tissue culture plants, click here . Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Provide gentle, moderate lighting. Variegated and white leaves lack dense chlorophyll, so moderate light combined with stable nutrients will help support healthy growth without scorching the foliage or inviting spot algae Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. CO₂ is recommended to assist with the tissue culture transition and support healthy growth. Master the prep and planting process by checking out a beginner's guide to tissue culture plants to prevent your delicate new plantlets from melting or floating away. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Anubias barteri var. nana 'White Rose' Common Name(s) Anubias White Rose, White Rose Anubias Family Araceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Epiphyte (Rhizome / Tissue Culture) Care Difficulty Moderate Light Requirement Medium CO2 Requirement Recommended for TC Transition Placement / Usage Foreground, Midground Height / Size 2-4 inches Growth Rate Slow (1 leaf every 3-4 weeks) Water Parameters pH 6.0 – 7.5 | Temperature 68°F – 82°F (20°C – 28°C) Propagation Method Separate by Rhizome Division Origin Cultivar / Lab Tissue Culture Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I plant Anubias White Rose Tissue Culture? Attach the plant directly to driftwood or rocks using aquarium-safe super glue gel, thread, or fishing line. Keep the rhizome above the substrate to prevent rot. 2. Does it require CO2 or high lighting? It requires moderate lighting to protect its delicate, white leaves from scorching while still providing enough energy for photosynthesis. CO₂ injection is recommended to help the tissue culture plantlets transition and acclimate successfully. 3. Is this plant safe for shrimp, snails, and fish? Yes, Anubias is 100% safe for all freshwater fish, shrimp (including sensitive Caridina and Neocaridina), and snails. Its tough leaves are also resistant to plant-eating fish like cichlids or goldfish.

listings.commonName: Aqua Worx Omni Aquatic Plant and Coral Super Glue
listings.description: Aqua Worx Omni is an aquarium-safe adhesive that can be used for your favorite aquatic plants or saltwater corals! This adhesive features a gel-like consistency that is simple to use and will securely bind various surfaces together with ease. Packaged in an aluminum tube, this aquarium glue can be kept for extended periods when properly cleaned after each use. Omni is versatile with use and is also suitable for simple repairs to aquarium decor. As with all adhesives, we recommend allowing the glue to fully cure before placing the finished product in water! Basin Wood is a newer addition to the aquascaping hobby, prized for its exceptionally high-detail surface. Characterized by a rugged landscape of deep grooves, tight knots, and weathered twists, it offers more texture than almost any other aquarium driftwood. Whether you’re looking for a standout centerpiece for a nano-tank or a detailed accent to tuck into a larger aquarium hardscape, Basin Wood provides a mature, ancient look right out of the box. Product Features & Benefits The basin-like deep grooves and whorls are a dream for plant enthusiasts. These crevices act as natural planting pockets for epiphytes like Anubias, Bucephalandra, or Ferns, allowing for a seamless planted aquarium hardscape. With its substantial width and height, Basin Wood offers a chunky architectural presence that provides stability to your layout. It pairs beautifully with stones like Seiryu or Dragon Stone for a cohesive river-bottom look. The intricate surface isn't just for show, as it provides a massive amount of surface area for beneficial bacteria and acts as a natural playground for shrimp and small bottom-dwellers. While perfect for driftwood aquariums, its rugged aesthetic also makes it a top-tier choice for high-humidity terrariums and paludariums. Size Specifications Photos provided are a representation of what you will receive. This is a natural aquarium hardscape product; please expect variations in shape, weight, and character. Length: 10–14 inches Width: 5–7 inches Height: 5–7 inches Preparation & Care Driftwood is a natural product and requires a bit of prep before it’s ready for prime time. Rinse: Thoroughly rinse the piece to remove any dust or debris from transit. The Floating Phase: It will float initially. We recommend soaking it thoroughly or boiling it. A large stone or heavy decor may be placed on top to ensure a non-waterlogged piece of wood stays submerged. Tannin Management: Like most aquarium driftwood, this will release tannins, giving your water a warm, "tea-colored" tint. This is a natural occurrence, and the effects will subside over time. If you prefer crystal-clear water, a 1–2 hour boil is the best way to fast-track the process. You can also reduce this effect through consistent water changes or through the addition of Aquario Neo Carbon Bag Important note: We recommend rinsing wood thoroughly before adding it to an established aquarium. If you prefer, you may also boil the wood for at least 1–2 hours to help release tannins.

Basin Wood is a newer addition to the aquascaping hobby, prized for its exceptionally high-detail surface. Characterized by a rugged landscape of deep grooves, tight knots, and weathered twists, it offers more texture than almost any other aquarium driftwood. Whether you’re looking for a standout centerpiece for a nano-tank or a detailed accent to tuck into a larger aquarium hardscape, Basin Wood provides a mature, ancient look right out of the box. Product Features & Benefits The basin-like deep grooves and whorls are a dream for plant enthusiasts. These crevices act as natural planting pockets for epiphytes like Anubias, Bucephalandra, or Ferns, allowing for a seamless planted aquarium hardscape. With its substantial width and height, Basin Wood offers a chunky architectural presence that provides stability to your layout. It pairs beautifully with stones like Seiryu or Dragon Stone for a cohesive river-bottom look. The intricate surface isn't just for show, as it provides a massive amount of surface area for beneficial bacteria and acts as a natural playground for shrimp and small bottom-dwellers. While perfect for driftwood aquariums, its rugged aesthetic also makes it a top-tier choice for high-humidity terrariums and paludariums. Size Specifications Photos provided are a representation of what you will receive. This is a natural aquarium hardscape product; please expect variations in shape, weight, and character. Length: 12-16 inches Width: 10-12 inches Height:7-9 inches Preparation & Care Driftwood is a natural product and requires a bit of prep before it’s ready for prime time. Rinse: Thoroughly rinse the piece to remove any dust or debris from transit. The Floating Phase: It will float initially. We recommend soaking it thoroughly or boiling it. A large stone or heavy decor may be placed on top to ensure a non-waterlogged piece of wood stays submerged. Tannin Management: Like most aquarium driftwood, this will release tannins, giving your water a warm, "tea-colored" tint. This is a natural occurrence, and the effects will subside over time. If you prefer crystal-clear water, a 1–2 hour boil is the best way to fast-track the process. You can also reduce this effect through consistent water changes or through the addition of Aquario Neo Carbon Bag Important note: We recommend rinsing wood thoroughly before adding it to an established aquarium. If you prefer, you may also boil the wood for at least 1–2 hours to help release tannins.

Plant Profile If you've ever wanted a freshwater aquarium plant with a personality as unpredictable as the weather, Cryptocoryne Florida Sunset is ready for the spotlight in your planted tank. A hybrid variant of Cryptocoryne wendtii , this colorful midground species refuses to settle for just one look: each leaf displays a shifting gradient of emerald green, warm gold, and subtle pastel pinks depending on your tank's lighting and nutrient levels. As with all crypt plants, this species can be sensitive to sudden parameter shifts and strongly objects to being relocated once planted. Because it is a slow grower, planting in groups is ideal when filling out midground zones. Key Features & Benefits Shifting foliage gradients of green, gold, and pink make every rosette unique in your aquascape. Adaptable nature makes it a stress-free choice for low-tech tanks once the root system establishes. Compact midground growth provides dense structural coverage without overtaking neighboring plants. Can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups, where mature plants may produce flowering spathes. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Crypt species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I bring out the pink and gold colors in Cryptocoryne Florida Sunset? Providing moderate aquarium lighting and rich iron-focused root tab supplementation encourages the foliage to shift from standard green to vibrant gold and soft pastel pink tones. 2. How should I plant Cryptocoryne Florida Sunset for the best visual impact? Because it grows at a slow-to-moderate pace, planting 2–3 pots in a tight cluster in your midground creates a fuller, multi-colored bush effect faster than planting a single isolated rosette. 3. How do I help my Cryptocoryne Florida Sunset recover if it melts after planting? Crypt melt is a standard reaction when shifting water conditions cause old leaves to dissolve so the plant can grow new foliage adapted to your aquarium. Trim away decaying tissue, maintain stable water conditions, and do not disturb the subterranean root mass. For complete recovery steps, check out our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt .

Plant Profile Common name: Buce Kayu Lapis Buce ‘Kayu Lapis’ is a rare and distinctive epiphytic plant featuring very thin, almost needle-like, glossy green leaves with heavily undulate margins and robust rhizomes that are nearly as thick as the delicate foliage itself. This variety is easily identified by its oblong, slightly serrated foliage, which often draws visual comparisons to a miniature Hygrophila Pinnatifida due to its unique edges. Kayu Lapis can be grown submerged or emersed, usually attached to hardscape such as driftwood or rocks rather than being buried in traditional aquarium substrate. Its patient growth habit and iridescent potential under quality lighting create a high-value foreground focal point in a planted tank. Key Features & Notes The slender, serrated leaf profile provides a stark visual contrast to the rounded or oval leaves of common Bucephalandra species. Due to its exceptionally slow growth rate, this variety is harder to obtain and highly prized among collectors, justifying its higher price point. While primarily a lush, glossy green, the foliage can display a sophisticated metallic shimmer when placed under high-quality aquarium LED lighting. Like its Bornean relatives, Kayu Lapis is not difficult to care for, but it requires stable conditions and time to reach a mature, sizeable portion. Care Tips & Preparation Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood . Never bury the rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting. Unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance, CO2 injection will yield much faster growth. We recommend researching your specific water chemistry to ensure your plant thrives. Plant Profile Bolbitis Heteroclita on Moss Ball delivers an effortless, plug-and-play hardscape accent. We have anchored the broad, deep-green fronds of this hardy Asian water fern on top of a Christmas moss-covered sphere for a seamless green look. This slow-growing epiphyte stays compact at 2 to 4 inches, making it a versatile, beginner-friendly midground piece for planted aquariums, terrariums, and paludariums alike. Simply drop the weighted moss sphere directly into your layout for instant volume and textured green detail. Key Features & Notes Tough, fibrous foliage easily withstands curious nipping from herbivorous fish like cichlids, goldfish, and large snails. Pre-attached to a lush Christmas Moss-covered sphere for an instant, drop-in hardscape accent that requires no gluing or substrate planting. Exceptional hardiness lets it thrive in non-CO2 tanks and low-light environments. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the mounted moss ball by rinsing it gently in clean freshwater to clear any loose debris before placing it directly into your aquarium. Bolbitis Heteroclita on Moss Ball is a pre-mounted epiphyte arrangement designed to sit directly on top of your substrate, wedged into hardscape crevices, or placed among rocks and wood. Ensure the horizontal rhizome of the fern remains exposed and is never buried beneath heavy substrate or gravel. Position this plant in areas with moderate water circulation, as Bolbitis and moss species both appreciate gentle flow to keep foliage free of debris. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because overall environmental stability supports smooth acclimation. While this piece is hardy and low-maintenance in standard setups, gentle water movement and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster fern and moss growth. Final size and moss density depend on your specific tank conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual sphere shapes may vary slightly. Do I need to remove the Bolbitis Heteroclita from the moss ball? No! This product comes pre-assembled as a ready-to-use centerpiece. You can simply place the weighted moss ball onto your aquarium floor or nestle it between rocks and wood right out of the box. 2. Can I propagate or detach the fern later if I want to move it? Yes. If you eventually decide to separate the fern, you can carefully snip the securing thread or cut the rhizome free. Once detached, the Bolbitis rhizome can be glued onto other hardscape, and the remaining moss ball will continue growing on its own. 3. Can I bury the moss ball in aquarium substrate? No. The moss ball should rest on top of your gravel, sand, or aqua soil. Burying it beneath the substrate will suffocate both the Christmas Moss and the Bolbitis rhizome, causing them to rot and die. 4. Will fish or shrimp bother the Bolbitis Heteroclita on Moss Ball? Freshwater shrimp and grazing fish love moss balls because they provide an ideal surface for biofilm and micro-algae growth. Meanwhile, the thick, fibrous leaves of the Bolbitis are unpalatable to most plant-eating fish, making this arrangement both functional and durable.

Plant Profile Selaginella moellendorffii is a terrestrial lycophyte that forms an upright, bushy thicket of bright green, branching fronds, creating immediate structural depth across the floor of the scape. Tucked into shaded pockets between dark lava rock or anchored around driftwood bases, its fine fan-like texture softens rigid hardscape lines. Unlike thinner-leaved relatives that wilt at the slightest dip in moisture, this species carries a thicker, waxier cuticle that gives it added resilience against temporary humidity fluctuations. Key Features & Notes Branching, fan-shaped bright green fronds create a dense, bushy understory mound. Thick, waxy cuticle offers greater resilience than thinner-leaved spikemoss species. Versatile terrestrial groundcover that knits cleanly across humid terrariums and paludariums. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Set the rooted clump into a few inches of moist, well-aerated tropical soil mix containing coco coir, tree fern fiber, and perlite so the rootlets have ample room to establish. Provide low to medium indirect lighting; direct light will scorch the branching fronds, while deep shadow can cause thin, leggy stems. Maintain humidity above 70% and keep the substrate damp, but make sure the container has adequate drainage because waterlogged, stagnant mud leads to yellowing foliage. Trim back wandering tips or leggy growth using clean shears to direct growth into a compact, bushy shape. Selaginella moellendorffii are terrestrial plants, and being submerged will result in the death of the plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Selaginella moellendorffii Common Name(s) Moellendorff's Spikemoss, Club Moss Family Selaginellaceae Plant Type Terrestrial Primitive Lycophyte / Bushy Spikemoss Care Difficulty Easy Light Requirement Low to Medium Indirect Light (Partial Shade) Submersion Suitability Emersed Only (Not for full submersion) Placement / Usage Foreground, Midground Understory, Hardscape Base Crevices Height / Size 3"–10" (7.5–25 cm) Growth Rate Slow to Moderate Humidity Requirement High (> 70% RH) Propagation Method Division / Stem Cuttings Origin Asia Frequently Asked Questions 1. Can Selaginella moellendorffii survive underwater in an aquarium? No. Selaginella moellendorffii is an obligate land plant. Submerging it in an aquarium will prevent respiration, causing the stems and foliage to melt away within days. 2. Why are the lower fronds on my spikemoss turning yellow? Yellowing lower fronds are a common sign of overwatering and waterlogged substrate. Ensure excess water drains cleanly away from the roots so the soil stays damp rather than muddy. 3. How do you propagate Selaginella moellendorffii? Divide an established clump into smaller sections with intact roots, or snip mature branching stems and press the lower portions into moist sphagnum moss inside an enclosed, humid container until new roots develop.

Plant Profile Known across the hobby as the Peacock Fern or Peacock Spikemoss, Selaginella willdenowii grabs attention the second light catches its delicate, branching fronds at an angle, flashing an electric metallic-blue iridescence across deep green foliage. It is strictly a terrestrial lycophyte built for the damp understory floor and humid open air; submerging this plant in an aquarium will rot the thin fronds and kill the crown. Woven between tall driftwood roots or trained up a damp back wall, its fine, fern-like sprays soften harsh stone transitions and fill vertical space without forming heavy bulk. Key Features & Notes Branching, fern-like fronds cast an electric blue metallic sheen under soft indirect lighting. Can scramble and climb upward along wood or damp backgrounds with regular trimming. Thrives in high humidity and porous, aerated soil across vivariums and paludariums. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Plant the rooted base into a light, airy tropical soil mix of coco coir, tree fern fiber, and perlite along midground or background zones, or gently anchor the climbing stems against damp cork bark. Provide low to medium indirect light or partial shade; direct sun or intense grow lights will wash out the vivid blue iridescence and scorch the delicate leaves. Maintain humidity above 75% and keep the soil evenly damp, but provide adequate bottom drainage to prevent muddy, stagnant water that leads to yellowing foliage. Prune stem tips with clean shears to direct growth, encourage bushier branching, or keep its upright reach compact. Final height, climbing habit, and blue sheen intensity depend entirely on your specific setup conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Selaginella willdenowii are terrestrial plants, and being submerged will result in the death of the plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Fully submerging it underwater will quickly suffocate the delicate fronds and rot the plant. 2. Why are the fronds on my Peacock Spikemoss turning yellow? Yellowing fronds generally indicate overwatering and poor soil drainage. Ensure excess water drains cleanly away from the roots so the substrate remains damp rather than soggy. 3. How do you bring out the best blue color in Selaginella willdenowii? Keep the plant under soft, dappled shade and consistent high humidity. Intense or direct light washes out the optical cell structure that produces the metallic blue sheen.

listings.commonName: Utricularia Graminifolia Tissue Culture - Small Cup
listings.description: Common Name: UG, Utricularia Graminifolia UG is a highly sought after foreground plant that can produce a grass-like lawn of carpet. This carnivorous plant is like an aquatic grass, with thin stalks growing from roots that spread horizontally by sending our runners. This listing is for one small cup of Utricularia Graminifolia. High lighting and CO2 injection are not always necessary to grow UG but it will definitely increase the growth speed and thickness of the foreground. This plant can grow submerged or emersed in dry start aquariums and Wabi Kusa. Simply separate larger mats into small portions and plant each an inch or so apart halfway into the substrate. After several weeks, the plant will send our runners all around and a lush foreground of grass can be created. Notes: Utricularia Graminifolia is notorious for being finicky in a planted aquarium. An established environment has been said to yield better growth. Tissue culture plants are grown in vitro from a state of the art laboratory specialized in propagating aquatic plants. They provide the best option for those who want to ensure that absolutely zero unwanted pests are introduced into the aquarium. Remove tissue culture gel before planting. Simply wash the gel away or soak the plant in water and squeeze the gel off with your fingers. Do not make drastic changes to the aquarium. Unstable parameters will result in melt and rotting of the aquarium plant. For instructions on how to properly plant tissue culture aquarium plants, click here . CO2 injection will yield better growth. Family Name: Lentibulariaceae Origin: Asia Height: 1-2.5” pH: 6-7.5 Care: Medium Light: Medium to High Co2: Recommended Propagation: Cut patches and replant Growth rate: Moderate to Fast

This compact epiphyte replaces traditional round-leaf profiles with a ruffled look that contrasts dramatically with smoother hardscape. Tissue culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab-grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Avoid intense light and ensure good water flow to prevent spot algae on slow‑growing leaves. CO₂ is optional but improves growth and leaf density. Plant Profile Aquascapers seeking rare variegated foliage for planted tanks will find their match in Anubias Giant Stardust. While retaining the distinct, starry veining of its predecessor, this celestial cultivar boasts an expanded leaf size that makes a major statement across foreground and midground layouts. Its defining feature is a striking pattern of white center veins running down subtly speckled, light green leaves. Attached directly to rock or wood via rhizome, it provides contrast when mounted against dark volcanic stone or driftwood. Because its white-veined leaves contain reduced chlorophyll, providing medium lighting alongside optional CO₂ injection will support healthy growth and maintain its brilliant pattern. Key Features & Benefits Speckled foliage provides brightness against dark hardscape elements. Larger size makes it a versatile midground layout anchor for nano tanks and standard aquascapes alike. Thick leaves resist grazing from plant-eating cichlids, snails, and dwarf shrimp. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Provide medium lighting to support photosynthesizing variegated leaves while ensuring good water flow to prevent spot algae. CO₂ is recommended to support faster growth and preserve crisp leaf contrast. Learn more about planting these species by reading our guide on How to Plant Epiphyte Aquatic Plants. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I plant Anubias Giant Stardust? Attach the plant directly to driftwood or rocks using aquarium-safe super glue gel, thread, or fishing line. Keep the rhizome above the substrate to prevent rot. 2. Does it require CO2 or high lighting? While it can survive under low light, medium lighting and CO2 injection are recommended. Because its variegated leaves have less chlorophyll, brighter light and added carbon help maintain its distinctive white veining and prevent leaf melting. 3. Is this plant safe for shrimp, snails, and fish? Yes, Anubias Giant Stardust is 100% safe for all freshwater fish, shrimp (including sensitive Caridina and Neocaridina), and snails. Its tough leaves are also resistant to plant-eating fish like cichlids or goldfish.

Plant Profile The Hadi Red Pearl Sword ( Echinodorus 'Hadi Red Pearl' Variegated ) stands out as a highly sought-after variegated Amazon Sword cultivar in the hobby. This rare specimen showcases broad, spade-shaped green leaves marbled with brilliant white splashes and fiery crimson markings throughout each leaf blade. Reaching a compact to moderate height of 4 to 9 inches, its bold variegated foliage provides an eye-catching focal point in midground or background zones. Hardy and beginner-friendly, the Hadi Red Pearl Sword adapts easily to a wide range of tank environments while offering aquascapers an extraordinary mix of color, pattern, and architectural structure. Key Features & Benefits Rare variegated foliage features a captivating marble pattern of bright white streaks and rich red speckles over vibrant green leaves. Hardy, easy-care rosette plant that brings strong structural presence to aquarium layouts. Versatile species suitable for submerged aquariums as well as emersed terrarium and paludarium setups. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Plant the roots deeply into your aquarium soil, keeping the crown of the plant resting just above the substrate surface to prevent rot. All Echinodorus are heavy root feeders that rely on rich substrate nutrition; placing root tabs near the base supports steady, healthy leaf development. Provide low to moderate lighting; while adaptable under basic low-tech conditions, supplying moderate light and regular liquid iron supplementation helps maintain crisp white and red leaf variegation. Keep water parameters stable and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent leaf melting during the transition period. To propagate, gently separate developed daughter plantlets that form along the base or flowering runners once they sprout independent roots, then replant them directly into your aquarium soil. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I prep potted Echinodorus Hadi Red Pearl Variegated before planting? Carefully remove the plastic pot and peel away the cotton or rockwool wrapping from the roots under room-temperature water. Inspect the base, snip off any damaged outer leaves, and gently insert the roots into your aquarium soil using pinsettes. 2. How do I preserve the white and red variegation on my Hadi Red Pearl Sword? Maintaining clear white markings and rich red spots requires moderate lighting and steady root nutrition. Supplying root tabs inside your aquarium soil ensures the plant receives sufficient iron and trace elements to keep new leaves vividly marbled. 3. Why is root feeding essential for Echinodorus species? Amazon Sword plants are heavy root feeders, meaning they absorb nutrients primarily through their extensive root system rather than relying strictly on liquid fertilizers in the water column. Providing root nutrition directly in your aquarium soil supports strong root anchors and lush leaf growth.

Plant Profile Buce ‘Boyan Mini Narrow’ is a compact, low-tech epiphyte prized for its deep green, slender leaves and prominent central vein running down each leaf. Standing at less than 1 to 2 inches tall, this nano-sized species is uniquely suited for tucking into tight hardscape crevices, wedging between stones, or carpeting the immediate foreground of freshwater aquascapes. Adaptable to both submerged aquariums and high-humidity emersed environments, it attaches readily to wood or rock without requiring burial in substrate, yielding a low-maintenance, detailed accent for planted tanks of any size. Key Features & Notes The Mini Narrow designation refers to its petite size and thin leaf shape, making it one of the best choices for adding fine texture to small-scale layouts. With quality LED lighting and stable nutrients, the deep green foliage can develop a shimmering metallic sheen that enhances its visual depth. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for planted tanks where other plants might struggle. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard low-light aquarium plant setups, CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and richer iridescence. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! If the rhizome remains firm, keep it attached to hardscape while the plant acclimates and produces new submerged growth. 2. Can I plant Bucephalandra in substrate? Bucephalandra is an epiphyte, so never bury its rhizome in substrate. Attach it to driftwood or rocks, or wedge the roots into hardscape while keeping the rhizome exposed. 3. Is Bucephalandra ‘Boyan Mini Narrow’ beginner-friendly? Yes. Bucephalandra ‘Boyan Mini Narrow’ is a beginner-friendly, low-light aquarium plant that grows without specialized substrate or pressurized CO₂, making it well-suited for low-tech planted aquariums.

Product Overview Ultum Nature Systems Controsoil Black is a volcanic ash-based aquarium soil from Japan designed to support healthy planted tanks. Selecting the right substrate is foundational not only for aquatic plants to flourish, but also for maintaining optimal water parameters for sensitive livestock like dwarf shrimp and tropical fish. While other substrates might leach excessive ammonia (NH3) and trigger the dreaded "new tank syndrome", resulting in cloudy water and aggressive initial algae spikes, Controsoil keeps initial ammonia release minimal while buffering alkaline water to a slightly acidic pH below 7.0. This natural parameter control simplifies early tank maintenance and creates a stable aquatic ecosystem right out of the bag without daily water changes as the tank establishes itself. Offered in Extra Fine (~1mm), Fine (~3mm), and Normal (~5mm) granule sizes, it provides the ideal foundation for anchoring delicate foreground carpeting species or building a high-impact aquascape for heavy root-feeding plants. This item qualifies for FREE shipping to the contiguous U.S. Shipping to Alaska or Hawaii? Contact us for a custom shipping quote—we’re here to help! Key Features & Benefits Natural soil and volcanic ash composition absorbs impurities and maintains water clarity from initial setup. Natural parameter control buffers alkaline water below 7.0 pH and lowers total hardness for soft-water species. Controlled low ammonia release prevents initial algae blooms while simplifying early aquarium establishment. Durable granule structure resists breakdown over time to prevent compaction and encourage deep root growth. Usage & Application Guidelines Do not rinse this aquarium soil before placing it into your tank. Distribute the granules to achieve a depth of two to three inches sloping toward the back glass to support root systems and build visual perspective. Fill the aquarium gently by pouring water over a plate or plastic wrap to keep the substrate layer undisturbed. Monitor pH and KH levels while cycling your aquarium, ensuring ammonia and nitrites read zero before introducing livestock. Quick Facts & Specifications Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Granule Size Comparison Attribute Specification Extra Fine (~1mm) Ideal Application & Plants: Foreground carpet plants (HC Cuba, Monte Carlo) & nano tanks (<10 gal) Key Advantage: Easiest anchoring for delicate root systems; prevents plant floating Fine (~3mm) Ideal Application & Plants: Small-to-medium stem plants, Crypts & mid-size tanks (10–20 gal) Key Advantage: Versatile all-around granule size for general aquascaping Normal (~5mm) Ideal Application & Plants: Large stem plants, Swords & larger aquariums (20+ gal) Key Advantage: Maximizes water circulation and oxygenation around deeper roots Substrate Volume & Tank Sizing Guide Bag Size Recommended Tank Setup Estimated Bed Coverage 1 Liter ~2 Gallons / 8 Liters (e.g., UNS 20C Cube) ~2 inch depth in nano setups 3 Liters ~9 Gallons / 34 Liters (e.g., UNS 45U) ~2 to 2.5 inch bed depth 10 Liters ~20 Gallons / 75 Liters (e.g., UNS 60U) ~2 to 3 inch sloping bed depth Frequently Asked Questions 1. Do I need to rinse this aquarium substrate before adding it to my tank? No, you should never rinse aquarium soil before adding it to your setup. Rinsing breaks down the delicate volcanic granules, washes away beneficial structural elements, and creates unnecessary cloudiness in the water column. 2. How much substrate do I need for my aquarium size? To calculate the required volume in liters, multiply the length of your aquarium by the width and desired substrate depth in inches, then divide the total by 60. For example, a standard tank measuring 24 inches long by 12 inches wide with a 2-inch bed requires approximately 9.6 liters of soil. 3. How does this substrate affect my water parameters? UNS Controsoil Black gently buffers alkaline water to a slightly acidic pH below 7.0 while lowering overall water hardness. This creates an optimal soft-water environment for aquatic plants, freshwater dwarf shrimp, and tropical fish. 4. Can I combine Controsoil with aquarium sand in the same aquascape? Yes, combining aquarium soil with decorative aquarium sand is a popular technique for high-contrast aquascaping layouts. You can place soil in the rear or planting zones for root growth and cosmetic sand in the foreground or pathway areas for visual contrast.

Plant Profile Ammannia Sp. Sulawesi is a rare and captivating aquatic stem plant native to the tropical, soft-water habitats of Sulawesi, Indonesia. Celebrated for its unique coloration and distinct upright growth habit, this species features slender leaves that display a rich spectrum of sunset orange, warm pink, olive green, and copper hues along its central stem. Ideal for intermediate to advanced aquascapers, Ammannia Sp. Sulawesi forms breathtaking vertical background hedges and midground focal points when planted in dense clusters under high-tech aquarium conditions. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Unique sunset colors of pink, copper, orange, and olive green bring visual interest. Strict vertical growth habit naturally forms clean, structured background hedges and Dutch-style layouts. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight (or pot) and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the roots, then strip lower foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower leaves. Provide medium-to-high lighting and stable water conditions. Pressurized CO2 injection and regular liquid nutrient dosing with iron are essential to ensure successful transition, strong root development, and vivid coloration. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim main stem tops with sharp straight scissors once established, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and expand coverage. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Ammannia sp. 'Sulawesi' Common Name(s) Ammannia Sulawesi, Ammannia Sp. Sulawesi, Nesaea Sulawesi Family Lythraceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Stem Plant Care Difficulty Intermediate to Advanced Light Requirement Medium to High CO2 Requirement Required (Essential for healthy roots and coloration) Placement / Usage Midground / Background Centerpiece Height / Size 4–12”+ Growth Rate Medium Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.2 | Prefers Soft Water Propagation Method Cuttings (Cut stem and replant tops) Origin Indonesia (Sulawesi) Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I get Ammannia Sp. Sulawesi to display bright orange and pink colors? Achieving vibrant orange, pink, and copper shades on Ammannia Sp. Sulawesi requires high light intensity, mandatory pressurized CO2, nutrient-rich soil, and regular supplementation of liquid micro and macronutrients, particularly iron. 3. How do I transition Ammannia Sp. Sulawesi from emersed to submerged growth? When transitioning from emersed to submerged growth, plant bare stems securely into rich substrate under strong lighting, high CO2 injection, and soft water conditions while keeping parameters completely stable. As new growth adapts, the plant will shed its stiffer emersed foliage and sprout soft, colorful underwater leaves. Once new shoots take root, trim away old lower growth to encourage dense branching.

Common Name: Amazon Sword Average Size: 13-15" Amazon sword plants are very common in the aquarium hobby, being that they are beautiful and easy to care for. They offer excellent and attractive coverage to the background of an aquascape. These plants have short stems that grow in a rosette, bearing long and ovoid leaves with a pointed tip. Their leaves are dark or bright green in color with prominent veins and slightly wavy shape. Amazon sword plants can get pretty huge, making them a great fit for a large tank. Their large leaves can easily restrict light to other plants if they are not pruned regularly. These plants propagate through side shoots off of their leaves, which can be trimmed and replanted into the substrate. To control the size of your Amazon sword plant you can remove the side shoots and older leaves. With a nutrient rich substrate these plants will tolerate most lighting conditions, but moderate to high lighting is ideal. CO2 injection is not necessary but will help the plant grow faster if desired. Amazon sword plants will grow submersed or emersed. Emersed plants produce lovely white flowers. Notes: Echinodorus is a very hardy species of aquatic plants. Most Echinodorus require nutrient-dense soil to thrive as they are heavy root feeders. Echinodorus grow fairly large and are more suitable for larger planted aquariums. Do not make drastic changes to the aquarium. Unstable parameters will result in melt and rotting of the aquarium plant. Please be sure to remove this plant from its pot. Remove the cotton surrounding the roots and plant into a quality substrate. For instructions on how to properly prep "potted" aquarium plants, click here . CO2 injection and quality aquarium soil will yield better growth. Please research appropriately to ensure your plant thrives. Family Name: Alismataceae Origin: South America Height: 4-20” pH: 6.5-7.5 Care: Easy Light: Moderate Co2: Not necessary Propagation: Adventitious shoots Growth rate: Fast

Plant Profile Common Name: Bucephalandra Theia Green, Buce Theia Green Buce ‘Theia Green’ is a distinctive epiphytic plant known for its vibrant green foliage and highly textured, undulate leaf margins. While closely related to the Buce Theia variety, this variant is distinguished by its ruffled edges, which provide a more complex and architectural look compared to the flatter and smoother leaves of its counterpart. Theia Green can be grown submerged or emersed, usually attached to hardscape such as driftwood or rocks rather than being buried in traditional aquarium substrate. It's a great pick for the foreground or midground of aquascapes, where it will slowly grow from rhizomes to form a dense colony over time. Key Features & Notes The undulate margins create a wavy effect that catches the light and water flow, making it stand out among smoother-leafed species. This variety maintains a bright, healthy green hue that provides a refreshing contrast against dark stones or blue-tinted Bucephalandra. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for aquascapes where other plants might struggle. It is perfectly at home fully submerged in an aquarium or emersed in high-humidity terrariums, vivariums, and paludariums. Care Tips & Preparation Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood . Never bury the rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Carefully remove the plant from its pot and clear away all rockwool from the roots. For a deep dive on prepping potted plants, click here . Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting. Unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance, CO2 injection will yield much faster growth. We recommend researching your specific water chemistry to ensure your plant thrives. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions. Please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Please research appropriately to ensure your plant thrives. Additional Information Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Plant Profile Selaginella uncinata, widely known as Peacock Spikemoss, is a trailing tropical lycophyte featuring delicate, fern-like scale foliage that displays a metallic-blue iridescence under filtered light. A great pick for emersed setups, this terrestrial plant serves as a spreading groundcover carpet across damp tank floors, lower hardscape ledges, and moist shoreline banks in paludariums. Fun fact: its blue sheen is not caused by blue pigment, but by microscopic optical structures in the upper leaf cells that refract and bend light in shaded environments. Key Features & Notes Delicate fern-like scale foliage exhibits a vivid metallic-blue iridescence under indirect lighting. Spreading groundcover habit roots along creeping stem nodes to carpet moist hardscape and soil. Requires consistent ambient humidity and moist, well-aerated substrate to prevent branch dieback. Care & Planting Instructions Press trailing stem portions gently onto moist, well-draining substrate or tuck stems into damp sphagnum moss across foreground terrain and lower hardscape ledges. Maintain ambient humidity above 75% while ensuring the substrate remains aerated and damp; yellowing foliage typically signals waterlogged, anaerobic soil. Trim wandering stem tips with sharp shears to manage spread and encourage dense lateral branching across the foreground. Final size and blue iridescence depend entirely on your specific setup conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Selaginella uncinata are terrestrial plants, and being submerged will result in the death of the plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only.
