Plant Profile Java Fern Gold Sparkle is a vibrant, rare cultivar that brings a golden-green contrast to the lineup of low-light aquarium plants. Characterized by its unique color progression, new leaves emerge in brilliant lime-to-golden shades that create a glowing sparkle before maturing into a deep emerald hue as the fronds age. Staying compact at 3 to 5 inches in height, this epiphyte is completely unbothered by parameter swings, low lighting, or hungry herbivorous fish, making it an ideal choice for filling empty midground spaces or hardscape nooks. Key Features & Notes Tough, fibrous foliage easily withstands curious nipping from herbivorous fish like cichlids, goldfish, and large snails. Dynamic color evolution features golden-lime emerging growth that matures into a rich emerald foliage canopy, adding visual depth to midground layouts. Exceptional hardiness lets it thrive in non-CO2 tanks and low-light environments. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Java Fern Gold Sparkle is an epiphytic fern that should be attached to rocks or driftwood with aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as it will rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard setups, gentle water movement and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and broader fronds. Master long-term care and troubleshoot common leaf issues by checking out our Java Fern Care Guide . Final size and foliage pattern depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Microsorum pteropus 'Gold Sparkle' (syn. Leptochilus pteropus ) Common Name(s) Java Fern Gold Sparkle, Gold Sparkle Java Fern Family Polypodiaceae Plant Type Epiphyte (Rhizome Fern) Care Difficulty Beginner / Easy (Low-Tech Compatible) Light Requirement Low to Medium CO2 Requirement Not Required (Beneficial) Placement / Usage Midground, Focal Hardscape Accent, Nano Layouts Height / Size 3"–5" (7.5–13 cm) Growth Rate Slow to Moderate Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 | Temperature 68°F–82°F (20°C–28°C) Propagation Method Rhizome Division & Adventitious Plantlets Origin Indonesia / Cultivated Variety Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are the new leaves on my Java Fern Gold Sparkle lighter in color? That bright, golden-green coloration on young leaves is the signature trait of the 'Gold Sparkle' cultivar! As the fronds mature and harden off, they gradually deepen into a rich emerald green, creating a multi-toned, sparkling contrast across the plant bundle. 2. Why are there small black spots and tiny leaves growing under my Java Fern Gold Sparkle leaves? Do not panic; your plant is not diseased! Java Fern reproduces naturally through adventitious plantlets. Small dark bumps (sporangia) form along the undersides of mature leaves, sprouting tiny brown roots and mini green fronds. Once these baby plantlets develop 3–4 leaves, you can gently pop them off the mother leaf and glue them elsewhere in your aquarium. 3. Can I plant Java Fern Gold Sparkle into substrate? No. Java Fern Gold Sparkle is an epiphyte that absorbs nutrients directly from the water column through its foliage and fine root network. If you bury its horizontal rhizome beneath aquarium soil, sand, or gravel, the stem will suffocate, rot, and die. Always attach it to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread. 4. Will fish like cichlids or goldfish eat Java Fern Gold Sparkle? Generally, no. Java Fern leaves are thick, fibrous, and contain bitter-tasting compounds that deter most plant-eating fish. While aggressive diggers might knock it off hardscape if not glued securely, they rarely consume the foliage.

How do I prepare tissue culture Bucephalandra for planting? Gently remove the plant from its plastic cup, rinse off all the nutrient gel under lukewarm water, and separate the plant into smaller clumps before attaching them to driftwood or rock using aquarium-safe glue or thread. 2. Why is my tissue culture Bucephalandra melting after planting? Tissue culture plants undergo an acclimation phase when transitioning to underwater conditions. Maintain stable water parameters, good circulation, and moderate light; as long as the rhizome stays firm, new submerged leaves will emerge. 3. Can tissue culture Bucephalandra be planted in substrate? Yes, you can push the roots into substrate or gravel to help anchor the plantlet. However, you must keep the central horizontal rhizome completely exposed above the substrate line, as burying the rhizome starves it of circulation and causes rot.

Product Overview SL-Aqua MORE Snow is a sinking food for freshwater dwarf shrimps that need steady vegetable fiber, trace minerals, and a low-stress grazing surface. Made from compressed soybean hulls, these supplementary pellets are rich in structural fiber plus calcium, phosphorus, magnesium, and potassium. They sink immediately and expand into soft, snow-like flakes on the substrate so adults and tiny shrimplets can graze side by side. As the plant fibers slowly break down underwater, they naturally cultivate beneficial mycelial fungi and biofilm without releasing ammonia or clouding your tank, making it a steady, self-replenishing food source while you are away for a long weekend. Key Features & Notes Proprietary vegetable protein and high-fiber blend enriched with minerals and trace elements with no water-clouding binders. Supports healthy gut motility, clean exoskeleton molts, and higher juvenile survival rates in Caridina and Neocaridina colonies. Feeding Guidelines Feed two to three times per week as a dietary supplement, offering only what your shrimp colony can finish within a few hours. Rotate with high-protein sticks, mineral supplements, and bacterial biofilm powders to provide a diverse, balanced diet. Reseal the pouch tightly after each use and store in a cool, dry place away from direct light to keep plant fibers crisp and fresh. Plant Profile Eleocharis Vivipara, commonly referred to as Umbrella Hair Grass, is a popular and striking background plant in the aquascaping community. As its common name implies, this species grows tall and slender, eventually arching over near the surface to create a graceful, flowing canopy across the top of the water. Because it grows quite tall, it makes an exceptional background centerpiece for medium and larger aquariums. However, it can also be kept in smaller nano tanks with routine trimming to keep its vertical growth in check. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Arching blades form a soft, floating canopy at the surface that fish and shrimp use for shade. Tolerates a wide range of aquarium conditions, suitable for beginners and experienced keepers. Spreads via lateral runners to fill gaps and create a continuous grassy carpet. Care & Planting Instructions Separate into small clumps and press them compactly into a quality aquarium soil to give the roots the perfect head start. Space small portions roughly one inch apart, burying the roots securely into the substrate. Maintain stable aquarium parameters and avoid drastic shifts in water quality to prevent your new grass from melting. Provide medium to high lighting and inject pressurized CO2 to supercharge its density and growth rate, keeping the tall stems thick and vibrant. Master the basics by learning how to properly grow aquarium carpet plants to ensure your new layout fills in quickly. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Eleocharis Vivipara forms "daughter plantlets" at the tips of its tall blades. Yes, but it requires regular maintenance. Because it easily exceeds 12 inches in height, routinely trimming the tallest arching blades will prevent it from creating a dense surface canopy that blocks light from reaching smaller foreground plants.

Common Name: Hygrophila Araguaia Hygrophila Araguaia is an uncommon aquarium stem that can be commonly seen in the foreground to the midground area of the aquarium. When grown submerged and kept under proper conditions, Hygrophila Araguaia develops a reddish brown tone that can includes purple notes as well, making it an extremely ornamental addition to the layout. Its appearance resembles that of a stem plant but it grows in short bushes which can add a nice bush effect to the midground of your aquarium. Plant Profile Pogostemon Stellatus Dassen features narrow, needle-like foliage that arranges itself in dense whorls around thick central stems, creating vibrant shades of orange, pink, and bright red under targeted care. Its fine-textured foliage and rapid branching habit make it a strong candidate for background hedges and colorful focal points in medium to large aquariums. While adaptable once settled, providing moderate to high lighting along with pressurized CO2 helps maintain its vibrant color and prevents lower leaf shedding. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Dense whorls of needle-like foliage transition from orange to pink and deep red under strong lighting. Tall vertical growth habit creates dense background hedges and colorful architectural structure. Adapts smoothly to fully submerged aquariums or emersed growth in humid terrariums. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant individual stems or small portions 1 inch apart into your aquarium soil, ensuring lower stems receive adequate light penetration. Provide moderate to high lighting and pressurized CO2 injection; consistent liquid fertilization rich in iron supports vibrant orange and red foliage. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water chemistry and consistent nutrient dosing to prevent stem tip melting or leaf stunting during transition. To propagate, trim main stem tops with sharp straight shears and replant the cuttings directly into your aquarium soil to encourage bushier side shoots. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Because this species grows tall and forms thick tops, trim the tops regularly and space individual stems at least 1 inch apart in your aquarium soil to ensure light penetrates down to the lower leaf whorls.

Species Profile Full Red Albino Guppies ( Poecilia reticulata ) are a domestic strain bred for deep, uniform crimson saturation accented by pinkish-red albino eyes. In typical guppy strains, the males claim all the glory while females remain mostly plain, but Full Red Albinos break the mold with females carrying an impressive wash of red across their bodies and fins as well. They spend their days cruising the upper and middle water column, and they are deeply peaceful, active community fish that will not nibble live plants or disrupt foreground carpets, though their flowing finnage means they appreciate calm currents over high-pressure surface flow. While they bring relentless energy and vivid contrast to an aquascape, you will want a fitted lid overhead, as their energetic surface feeding can quickly turn into accidental jumps. **Note: All livestock orders will come carefully packaged with solid wall Styrofoam insulation and shipped via 1-day shipping only. No extra insulation needs to be added to your cart for your livestock. Key Features & Notes Solid ruby-red body and fin coverage paired with true albino red eyes contrast against green plants. Active upper-level swimmer that stays plant-safe and leaves carpet plants rooted. Both males and females display rich red coloration, making colonies visually striking from any angle. Acclimation & Care Instructions Float the sealed transport bag for 15 to 20 minutes to equalize water temperatures before opening. Drip acclimate over 30 to 45 minutes using airline tubing to ease them into your tank's GH, KH, and pH levels. Keep water slightly alkaline (pH 7.0 to 8.0) with moderate mineral hardness to support fin health and avoid spinal curvature. Maintain gentle to moderate filter flow; heavy current will tire out males carrying large, flowing delta tails. Fit your aquarium with a secure lid; surface-oriented guppies can jump when spooked or during feeding rushes. Feed a varied diet of micro pellets, high-quality spirulina flakes, and frozen baby brine shrimp or daphnia once or twice daily. Fin length and red intensity develop with maturity and diet; photos represent conditioned adult stock. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy livestock! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Poecilia reticulata Common Name(s) Full Red Albino Guppy, Albino Full Red Family Poeciliidae Care Difficulty Easy Diet Omnivore (Micro pellets, flakes, frozen brine shrimp, daphnia) Plant Safe Yes (Safe with aquatic plants and carpets) Temperament Peaceful upper-to-mid column swimmer Adult Size 1.0"–1.5" (2.5–3.8 cm) Minimum Tank Size 10+ Gallons (Best in groups of 4 to 6+) Water Parameters pH 7.0–8.0 | GH 8–15 | KH 4–10 | 74°F–80°F (23°C–27°C) Freshwater Breeding Yes (Prolific livebearer) Origin South America (Tank-bred domestic strain) Frequently Asked Questions 1. Are Full Red Albino Guppies safe to keep with dwarf shrimp? Adult Neocaridina and Caridina shrimp are completely safe, but guppies are curious omnivores that will gladly snack on tiny newborn shrimplets if given the chance. If you plan to colony-breed shrimp in the same aquarium, pack the layout with dense mosses like Java Moss or Christmas Moss and dense stem thickets so baby shrimp have reliable shelter. 2. Do Albino guppies have special water quality requirements compared to wild-type guppies? Because they are a refined domestic strain carrying albino genetics, they are slightly more sensitive to poor water quality and cold water swings. Keep your temperature steady between 74°F and 80°F, ensure your water has good mineral hardness (GH 8+), and avoid soft, acidic water that can stress their immune systems and cause fin clamp. 3. How do I raise fry and manage breeding colonies in a planted tank? Guppies are prolific livebearers, giving birth to free-swimming fry every 30 days or so. Adults will naturally hunt newborn fry unless you supply thick surface floaters or moss. If you want a full walkthrough on water chemistry, feeding schedules, and colony management, explore our comprehensive Guppy Care Guide . 4. What tank mates should I avoid housing with Full Red Albino Guppies? Steer clear of fin-nipping or aggressive schooling fish like Tiger Barbs, Serpae Tetras, and large cichlids, as their long ornamental fins make easy targets. They pair best with peaceful tank mates such as Corydoras, Otocinclus, small peaceful rasboras, and clean-up crews like Nerite snails and Amano shrimp.

listings.commonName: Rotala Vietnam Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Common Name: Vietnamese Rotala, Rotala Vietnam This species of Rotala grows in the shallow waters and wet ground of its native Vietnam. With moderate light, it will grow into a plant with green, needle-like leaves and a red stem, while intense light will give the leaves a lovely golden color. CO2 injection, iron, and a micronutrient-rich substrate are necessary to help the plant grow its best, and it will quickly have long shoots growing along the water’s surface if it is not trimmed. The top and lateral shoots can be cut and replanted to propagate the Rotala. Its size and shape make the Vietnamese Rotala excellent in the midground or background, depending on how frequently you trim it, and its color will contrast well with green as well as red/pink plants, especially if planted in a tank dominated by other stem plants. Notes: Rotala has fragile leaves! Be sure to handle with care. Final coloration is ultimately dependent upon the conditions this plant is kept in. This is a live plant meaning size, shape and color may vary. Do not make drastic changes to the aquarium. Unstable parameters will result in melt and rotting of the aquarium plant. Plant Profile Rotala indica ‘Green’, often swapped with Rotala rotundifolia ‘Green’, is a popular bright, true‑green stem plant that refuses to blush red no matter how much light you shine on it. Unlike other Rotala varieties that turn pink or red, this resilient variation retains its color regardless of aquarium lighting or nutrient levels, making it a go-to choice for aquascapers seeking an all-green background or midground contrast. When grown submerged, its leaves become slender and narrow, bending gracefully to form dense, weeping bushes when pruned routinely. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Maintains a bright green coloration even under high-intensity lighting. Branches into dense, bushy background hedges through routine trimming and replanting. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip the lower inch of foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. * Rotala leaves are fragile, so handle stems with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower leaves. Provide medium-to-high lighting for steady growth, as pressurized CO2 injection is not strictly required but yields significantly bushier growth and thicker stems. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid drastic environmental changes to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the water surface to promote new lateral side branches. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Rotala rotundifolia 'Green' Common Name(s) Rotala Indica Green, Rotala Rotundifolia Green, Rotala Green Family Lythraceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Stem Plant Care Difficulty Easy to Moderate Light Requirement Medium to High CO2 Requirement Recommended (Yields bushier growth) Placement / Usage Background / Midground Bushing Height / Size 5–12”+ Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 Propagation Method Cuttings (Cut stem, new growth, or lateral shoots) Origin Asia / Cultivated Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining adequate light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. Will Rotala Indica Green turn red under high light and CO2? No. Rotala Indica Green is specifically selected for its ability to stay bright green regardless of light intensity or nutrient levels, making it ideal for aquascapers who want guaranteed green foliage without accidental blushing. 3. How do I transition Rotala Indica Green from emersed to submerged growth? When transitioning from emersed to submerged growth, plant bare stems securely into rich substrate under medium-to-high lighting and keep water parameters stable. As new growth adapts, the plant will shed its rounded, coin-shaped land leaves and sprout slender, bright green underwater foliage. Once new shoots develop, trim away old lower growth to encourage dense branching.

Plant Profile Rotala Colorata (sometimes mislabeled as Rotala indica ) is a vibrant variation of Rotala rotundifolia, popular for coloring up without a fight. Most red aquatic stem plants demand intense lighting and precise nutrient dosing just to show any color at all, but Rotala Colorata skips that requirement, displaying pink, orange, and red hues even under moderate lighting. Push it further with high-intensity light, CO2 injection, and iron supplementation, and its slender leaves shift into scarlet and crimson tones. Fast-growing and easy to propagate, it pairs beautifully with other Rotala species to form lush, colorful background hedges. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Displays vibrant pink, orange, and red hues more readily than other red stem plants, even under moderate lighting setups. Fast vertical growth fills in space and branches into dense hedges with routine pruning. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. * Rotala leaves are fragile, so handle stems with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide moderate-to-high lighting; adding pressurized CO2 and iron supplementation maximizes its deep crimson and scarlet pigmentation. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim stem tops or side shoots with straight scissors once they reach the water surface, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I get my Rotala Colorata to display its deepest red colors? While Rotala Colorata blushes easily under moderate light, achieving deep scarlet and crimson tones requires high light intensity, pressurized CO2 injection, low-to-moderate nitrate dosing, and regular iron fertilization. 3. How do I prepare Rotala Colorata UNS Tissue Culture before planting? Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the dense cluster into smaller clumps or individual stem bundles and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

Common Name: Rotala Macrandra The Rotala Macrandra, commonly known as the Giant Rotala, is a beautiful red plant from Asia. Rotala is highly demanding, needing high-intensity lighting, no shade, and high Co2 injection. To prevent shading, the individual stems must be planted far enough apart for the lower leaves to get enough light. Once established the plant grows quickly: up to 4” per week, in ideal conditions. To achieve a slight red tint, ensure that this Rotala has plenty of phosphates (1.5 - 2.0 ppm) and not too much nitrate. (10ppm or less.) An incorrect amount of either of these nutrients will lead to stunted growth or discolored leaves. Common Name: Limnophila Vietnam Limnophila Vietnam is a unique aquatic stem plant that features slender leaves that fan out into a star shape along the central stem. When grown in optimal conditions, Limnophila Vietnam produces a delicate look that pairs well with both stone and driftwood aquascape layouts. Its care is intermediate and suitable for aquarists who have some experience keeping aquarium plants. A standard baseline of good maintenance habits, CO2 injection, quality aquarium soil and moderate lighting are essential for this aquatic plant. Softer water and a dosing regiment that includes macro and micro nutrients will encourage healthier growth and overall sucess. Limnophila Vietnam can be propagated the same as other aquatic stems by simply trimming along the stem and replanting into the soil. Notes: Tissue culture plants are grown in vitro from a state of the art laboratory specialized in propagating aquatic plants. They provide the best option for those who want to ensure that absolutely zero unwanted pests are introduced into the aquarium. Remove tissue culture gel before planting. Simply wash the gel away or soak the plant in water and squeeze the gel off with your fingers. Do not make drastic changes to the aquarium. Unstable parameters will result in melt and rotting of the aquarium plant. For instructions on how to properly plant tissue culture aquarium plants, click here . CO2 injection and quality aquarium soil will yield better growth.

Plant Profile Meet Rotala Rotundifolia, a popular and well-recognized aquatic stem plant that brings vibrant life and energy to any aquascape! Featuring long, supple stems lined with delicate, narrow foliage, it creates a sweeping, soft visual movement in your tank. While primarily displaying a fresh, bright lime-green coloration under standard conditions, it has the potential to produce stunning golden-pink, peach, and reddish tones at its upper tips when grown under strong lighting and CO2. It’s a prolific grower that readily branches out after pruning, making it a favorite for both beginners and experienced aquascapers looking to build thick, bushy background hedges or structured Dutch-style plant streets. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Delicate green-to-pink foliage adds soft texture and dynamic visual detail to background zones. Fast-growing stem habit produces prolific side shoots when trimmed to create dense hedges. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide medium-to-high lighting and pressurized CO2 injection; consistent fertilization with a specialized liquid macro and micro formula yields robust stem growth and prevents bottom leaf yellowing. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or rotting. Trim main stem tops with sharp straight scissors once they reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and thicken the bush. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Plant Profile Anubias Jungle Star is an exciting new arrival to the aquascaping scene! This rare, small-to-medium variety features incredibly rich, dark green foliage with beautifully rounded edges, growing in a dense and compact habit. If you are looking to add some dramatic depth to your tank, its moody tones are perfect for creating a striking contrast against lighter stones, driftwood, and bright green background plants. It is a star performer that effortlessly adjusts to both submerged aquariums and high-humidity emersed setups. Key Features & Benefits Deep, dark green foliage provides stark visual contrast against lighter stones, driftwood, and bright green companion plants. Compact 3-to-5-inch growth habit makes it well-suited for midground placement in standard tanks or centerpieces in nano layouts. Thick, resilient leaf structure withstands variable water conditions and resists grazing from herbivorous fish and snails. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Avoid intense light and ensure good water flow to prevent spot algae on slow‑growing leaves. CO₂ is optional but improves growth and leaf density. Learn more about planting these species by reading our guide on How to Plant Epiphyte Aquatic Plants. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. How do I plant Anubias Jungle Star? Attach the plant directly to driftwood or rocks using aquarium-safe super glue gel, thread, or fishing line. Keep the rhizome above the substrate to prevent rot. 2. Does it require CO2 or high lighting? No. It thrives in low lighting without CO2 injection. While adding CO2 speeds up growth, it is completely optional. 3. Is this plant safe for shrimp, snails, and fish? Yes, Anubias is 100% safe for all freshwater fish, shrimp (including sensitive Caridina and Neocaridina), and snails. Its tough leaves are also resistant to plant-eating fish like cichlids or goldfish.

listings.commonName: Cryptocoryne Spiralis Red UNS Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Cryptocoryne spiralis 'Red' brings sweeping movement and warm, brownish-red hues to your midground and background layouts. This stunning variety features long, slender ribbon-like leaves that create a dense canopy, offering excellent cover and security for aquarium livestock. As with all crypt plants, it can be sensitive to sudden parameter shifts and strongly objects to being relocated once planted. Given a permanent home in your substrate, however, it'll stand out against the green of typical aquascape plants over time. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Slender, brownish-red ribbon-like foliage delivers dynamic movement and rich color to background zones. Can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups, where mature plants may produce flowering spathes. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel to supply essential subterranean nutrients. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth and fuller foliage density, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Crypt species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. How do I prepare this tissue culture plant? Rinse away the nutrient gel under lukewarm water to prevent algae or mold blooms, separate the plant mass into smaller portions, and plant directly into substrate using fine-tip pinsettes. 2. How do I help my Cryptocoryne recover if it melts? Trim away dissolving leaves, maintain stable water parameters, and leave the root system undisturbed so it can rebuild new foliage. Check our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt for full recovery steps. 3. Should I use root tabs or liquid fertilizers? Root tabs are best. Cryptocoryne species are heavy root feeders that draw primary nutrition from the substrate rather than the water column.

Plant Profile Bringing a wild, spotted pattern to classic sword plant structure, Echinodorus 'Leopard' is an eye-catching hybrid cultivar with mottled foliage. Newly emerging leaves open in bright, vibrant green and are heavily dappled with dark reddish-brown to maroon spots, giving the plant its distinct "leopard print" appearance. As the foliage expands and matures, these striking spots soften into a subtle marbling against a deep green backdrop, resulting in a dynamic, multi-patterned look across the entire rosette. Reaching an impressive height of up to 16+ inches, its substantial footprint makes it an ideal midground accent in large aquariums or a prominent background centerpiece in medium setups. Key Features & Notes Distinct leopard-like spotted pattern decorates newly emerging light green foliage. Hardy and adaptable species that delivers unique pattern contrast without requiring complex high-tech care. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Plant the roots deeply into your aquarium soil, keeping the central crown resting just above the substrate line to prevent rot. All Echinodorus are heavy root feeders that rely on rich substrate nutrition; placing root tabs near the base supports steady, healthy leaf development. Supplemental CO2 injection accelerates growth and encourages denser, fuller foliage, though the plant will still grow steadily in low-tech setups. Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf shedding during the initial transition period. Sword plants propagate through side shoots off of their leaves, which can be trimmed and replanted into the substrate. To control the size of your sword plant, you can remove the side shoots and older leaves. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I maintain and enhance the dark spots on Echinodorus 'Leopard'? Provide moderate-to-high lighting directly over the plant and place nutrient-rich root tabs near its roots. Higher light levels and consistent iron supplementation ensure newly emerging leaves develop distinct, dark reddish-brown spots rather than faint markings. 2. Why are the spots on the outer leaves lighter than the inner leaves? This is a natural growth pattern for Leopard Swords. Freshly unfurled center leaves display dark, intense spots, which gradually lighten and blend into a subtle marbling effect as the leaf blade matures and expands. 3. Can Echinodorus 'Leopard' grow in low-tech aquariums without CO2? Yes, it grows easily in low-tech setups without pressurized CO2. Providing a nutrient-dense substrate or adding root tabs, along with decent lighting, is all it needs to maintain steady growth and attractive spotted foliage.

listings.commonName: Bucephalandra Sintang Green UNS Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Buce ‘Sintang Green’ is a small-leafed aquarium plant featuring bright green foliage that produces a subtle, attractive sheen when lit by quality LED lighting. This particular variation is highly prized for its compact growth habit, making it an excellent choice for detailing the midground or foreground of freshwater aquascapes. This plant can be grown submerged or emersed, usually attached to hardscape such as driftwood or rocks rather than being buried in traditional aquarium substrate. It's a great choice for any planted tank, where it will slowly sprout from thin rhizomes to create a dense, lush green colony that stands out against darker hardscape. Tissue culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab-grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go-to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Notes The "Sintang Green" variety offers a brighter, more classic green palette compared to the darker or brownish Buce variants. Its predictable, compact growth makes it ideal for filling gaps between rocks or wood without overgrowing the layout. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for planted tanks where other plants might struggle. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by carefully removing the plantlets from the cup and rinsing away all sterile nutrient gel under lukewarm, dechlorinated water before mounting. Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard low-light aquarium plant setups, CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and a smoother tissue culture transition. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. How do I prepare tissue culture Bucephalandra for planting? Gently remove the plant from its plastic cup, rinse off all the nutrient gel under lukewarm water, and separate the plant into smaller clumps before attaching them to driftwood or rock using aquarium-safe glue or thread. 2. Why is my tissue culture Bucephalandra melting after planting? Tissue culture plants undergo an acclimation phase when transitioning to underwater conditions. Maintain stable water parameters, good circulation, and moderate light; as long as the rhizome stays firm, new submerged leaves will emerge. 3. Can tissue culture Bucephalandra be planted in substrate? Yes, you can push the roots into substrate or gravel to help anchor the plantlet. However, you must keep the central horizontal rhizome completely exposed above the substrate line, as burying the rhizome starves it of circulation and causes rot.

Common Name: Rotala Rotundifolia This species of Rotala grows in the shallow waters and wet ground of its native Vietnam. With moderate light, it will grow into a plant with green, needle-like leaves and a red stem, while intense light will give the leaves a lovely golden color. CO2 injection, iron, and a micronutrient-rich substrate are necessary to help the plant grow its best, and it will quickly have long shoots growing along the water’s surface if it is not trimmed. The top and lateral shoots can be cut and replanted to propagate the Rotala. Its size and shape make the Vietnamese Rotala excellent in the midground or background, depending on how frequently you trim it, and its color will contrast well with green as well as red/pink plants, especially if planted in a tank dominated by other stem plants. Notes: Tissue culture plants are grown in vitro from a state of the art laboratory specialized in propagating aquatic plants. They provide the best option for those who want to ensure that absolutely zero unwanted pests are introduced into the aquarium. Remove tissue culture gel before planting. Simply wash the gel away or soak the plant in water and squeeze the gel off with your fingers. Do not make drastic changes to the aquarium. Unstable parameters will result in melt and rotting of the aquarium plant. For instructions on how to properly plant tissue culture aquarium plants, click here . CO2 injection and quality aquarium soil will yield better growth.

Plant Profile Bucephalandra ‘Catherinae Green’ is a rare, beginner-friendly aquarium plant variant that features short stalks and narrow, wavy leaves. This variety develops a deep, emerald green coloration once fully adapted to growing underwater and maintains a low-growing, compact profile. Like other epiphytes, it can grow submerged or emersed and prefers to attach its rhizome to driftwood or rock rather than be buried in substrate. It's a small addition with an outsized amount of detail once established in the foreground or midground in a planted tank. Key Features & Notes The slender, rippled leaves provide a distinct fine-leaf texture that is ideal for adding detail to complex hardscape layouts. While many Buce variants turn dark or purple, Catherinae Green maintains a rich, vibrant green that contrasts beautifully against dark stones or wood. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for planted tanks where other plants might struggle. Care & Planting Instructions Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard low-light aquarium plant setups, CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and richer iridescence. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Why is my Bucephalandra melting? Bucephalandra melt can occur after changes in water chemistry, temperature, or lighting. If the rhizome remains firm, keep it attached to hardscape while the plant acclimates and produces new submerged growth. 2. Can I plant Bucephalandra in substrate? Bucephalandra is an epiphyte, so never bury its rhizome in substrate. Attach it to driftwood or rocks, or wedge the roots into hardscape while keeping the rhizome exposed. 3. Is Bucephalandra ‘Catherinae Green’ beginner-friendly? Yes. Bucephalandra ‘Catherinae Green’ is a beginner-friendly, low-light aquarium plant that grows without specialized substrate or pressurized CO₂, making it well-suited for low-tech planted aquariums.

Plant Profile Hygrophila odora is a rare aquatic stem plant with deeply lobed green leaf blades native to the marshy riverbanks and tidal bogs of West Africa. Its thick central stems and intricate foliage make it a standout choice for midground focal points and structured background groupings. Requiring soft water, strong lighting, and pressurized CO2 injection to maintain crisp leaf detail underwater, it offers an engaging challenge for experienced aquascapers. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Deeply pinnatifid leaf margins create an intricate hybrid look between Water Wisteria and Hygrophila Pinnatifida. Adapts smoothly to fully submerged aquariums or emersed growth in humid terrariums, producing delicate bluish-purple flowers. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant individual stems or small clumps 1 inch apart into your aquarium soil, anchoring the thick stem bases securely. Provide medium to high lighting and pressurized CO2 injection; keeping water soft and supplying balanced water-column nutrients prevents leaf melting and stunted growth tips. Maintain stable water chemistry to encourage steady root development and prevent stem decay during transition. To propagate, trim main stem tops or side shoots with sharp straight shears and replant the cuttings directly into your aquarium soil. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Hygrophila odora Common Name(s) Hygrophila Odora Family Acanthaceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Aquatic Stem Plant Care Difficulty Medium to Advanced Light Requirement Medium to High CO2 Requirement Required (Essential for healthy submerged leaf formation) Placement / Usage Midground Focal Point / Background Accent Height / Size 6–14”+ (Cup portion size: 2–3”) Growth Rate Moderate Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 (Prefers soft to moderately soft water) Propagation Method Stem Cuttings (Trim stem tops or side shoots and replant) Origin West Africa Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I prepare Hygrophila Odora Tissue Culture before planting? Rinse the nutrient gel completely off the roots in a bowl of room-temperature water. Once clean, divide the cluster into individual stems or small clumps and insert the roots into your aquarium soil using fine pinsettes. 2. Why is Hygrophila Odora considered a demanding plant in the aquarium? In submerged settings, Hygrophila Odora requires soft water, pressurized CO2, high light levels, and consistent nutrient dosing to prevent its leaves from deteriorating or losing their pinnatifid shape. 3. How does Hygrophila Odora look when grown emersed? When grown above water in a terrarium or paludarium, Hygrophila Odora develops upright stems covered in fine short hairs and can bloom with light bluish-purple flowers under warm, humid conditions.

How do I choose the best aquarium filter flow rate for my specific tank size? A reliable rule of thumb for selecting a filter for aquariums is aiming for a turnover rate of 4 to 5 times your total tank volume per hour. For instance, a 2.6-gallon pico aquarium benefits most from an aquarium filter rated around 10 to 15 GPH to ensure thorough mechanical filtration and biological filtration without creating overwhelming currents for small livestock. 2. How can I make my filter intake safe for baby shrimp and fry? Installing a fine stainless steel mesh intake guard or a pre-filter sponge directly over the metal inflow pipe prevents tiny dwarf shrimp and newly hatched fry from getting pulled into the suction line. This simple addition keeps delicate livestock safe while trapping large leaf debris before it reaches your main filter chamber. 3. How should I layer my media for maximum water clarity and biological stability? Water should always pass through coarse mechanical filter pads first to trap floating particulate matter, followed by porous biological media like biological ceramic rings or porous stone matrix for beneficial bacteria colonization. Chemical filtration media like activated carbon or specialty resin pads should sit at the very end of the flow path to strip discolorations and odors without clogging prematurely.

Spiderwood is a beloved choice among aquascaping enthusiasts for its intricate, multi-branching shape and natural beauty. But let’s face it: nothing’s more frustrating than carefully placing the perfect branchy centerpiece only to watch your new aquarium driftwood pop up and float around like a runaway pool noodle. Our Spiderwood on Slate comes pre‑mounted to a flat slate base, so there is no need for balancing rocks or using unsightly suction cups. Just drop it in, bury the slate, and the substrate locks it solid so your wood stays exactly where you want it. It’s the easiest way to root your design. Product Features & Benefits Spiderwood is notoriously buoyant, but the integrated slate base acts as a built-in anchor. Known for its "wild" and twisting limbs, it offers the perfect framework for attaching Moss, Anubias, or Bucephalandra, creating a lush forest look. The slate base is thin enough to be easily concealed by gravel or soil, giving the appearance that the wood is growing naturally out of your aquarium hardscape. Size Specifications: Average sizing (L x W x H) Photos provided are a representation of what you will receive. As Spider Wood is a natural aquarium hardscape product, please expect variations in shape, weight, and character. Small - 7 x 11 x 9" Medium - 10 x 9 x 13" Large - 21 x 11 x 13" Preparation & Care Even with a slate base, Spiderwood requires a little attention to ensure it looks its best in your aquarium with wood. Rinse: Thoroughly rinse the piece to remove any dust or debris from transit. The "Biofilm" Phase: It is completely normal for a harmless, white fuzzy biofilm to appear on the branches during the first few weeks. Your shrimp and snails will consider this a delicacy and clear it up in no time. Tannin Management: Spiderwood is a low-tannin wood, but it may still add a slight amber tint to the water. This is a natural occurrence, and the effects will subside over time. If you prefer the crystal-clear look, boil the wood for 1–2 hours or soak it in a separate container until the water runs clear. You can also reduce this effect through consistent water changes or through the addition of Aquario Neo Carbon Bag Important note: We recommend rinsing wood thoroughly before adding it to an established aquarium. If you prefer, you may also boil the wood for at least 1–2 hours to help release tannins.

listings.commonName: Hydrocotyle Sibthorpioides Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Common Name: Lawn Marsh Pennywort Tissue culture plants are grown in vitro from a state of the art laboratory specialized in propagating aquatic plants. They provide the best option for those who want to ensure that absolutely zero unwanted pests are introduced into the aquarium. Hydrocotyle Sibthorpioides is characterized by its clover-like leaves which can grow into compact bushes of green. It's similar to Hydrocotyle Japan except the leaves are rounder. This plant is versatile and can be used in the foreground, midground or background. It is undemanding and grows fast, often out-competing and overgrowing the tank if left untrimmed. By frequently trimming new growth and using high light with CO2, the plant can stay low growing and create a carpeting effect over the foreground. Propagate by trimming stems and replanting on pulling apart dense clumps and splitting the roots. New shoots can be trimmed anywhere along the stem which allows the plant to grow thicker and more compact. Remove tissue culture gel before planting. Simply wash the gel away or soak the plant in water and squeeze the gel off with your fingers. Family Name: Araliaceae Origin: Asia Height: 5-10" pH: 6.5-7.5 Care: Easy to Moderate Light: Medium Co2: Required Propagation: Cut stem and replant Growth rate: Moderate to Fast

Marsh Stone is a natural rock comparable to Hakkai Stone , with the key difference being a lighter color palette of light grey and white tones. It features smoother, semi-rounded edges and a water-worn shape, making it a perfect pick for authentic river-style aquascapes. Its grooves and crevices are ideal for attaching aquarium mosses or epiphytic plants, adding a layer of mature detail to your hardscape. Whether used in a minimalist Iwagumi layout or a mixed hardscape with driftwood, Marsh Stone contrasts against a variety of aquatic plant species. It is also suitable for non-aquarium use and will work beautifully in terrariums, paludariums, or similar planted enclosures. Stones vary in shape, size, and density. Notes: If you are looking for larger stones, a minimum weight may be required. Larger stones = higher weight. Email our team if you need assistance. This is a natural product and has the potential to alter water parameters slightly. We recommend rinsing stones thoroughly before use to remove any natural dust or sediment. Stone coloration darkens when wet.

listings.commonName: Hydrocotyle Tripartita Mini Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Common Name: Hydrocotyle Japan Mini Hydrocotyle Tripartita Mini is a smaller, more compact variation of the regular Hydrocotyle Japan . This versatile favorite is instantly recognizable by its charming, bright green, clover-shaped leaves. If you are looking for an undemanding plant that grows fast, this is your MVP. Depending on your tank size, it can effortlessly transition from a creeping foreground carpet to a bushy midground accent or background filler. Left untrimmed, it will happily take over the tank, but with regular styling, it forms gorgeous, dense cushions of dense greenery. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Miniature, bright green clover‑shaped leaves add texture to the foreground or midground. Fast‑growing stem species that quickly fill gaps and cover open substrate. Can grow as a low creeping lawn, midground cushion, or hardscape accent. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters into aquarium soil. Use a dry start method or Wabi Kusa setup to give its root system plenty of time to firmly anchor into the substrate before you flood the tank. Maintain stable aquarium parameters and avoid drastic shifts in water quality to prevent your new grass from melting. Provide medium to high lighting and inject pressurized CO2 while frequently trimming new growth to keep the plant low-growing and force a tight carpeting effect. Trim new shoots anywhere along the stem or pull apart dense clumps to split the roots, which actually coaxes the plant into growing even thicker. Master the basics by learning how to properly grow aquarium carpet plants to ensure your new layout fills in quickly. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Hydrocotyle tripartita 'Mini' Common Name(s) Hydrocotyle Japan Mini, Tripartita Mini Family Araliaceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Stem / Creeping Carpet Care Difficulty Easy to Moderate Light Requirement Medium to High CO2 Requirement Recommended (Required for low-growing carpet) Placement / Usage Foreground, Midground, or Hardscape Accent Height / Size 1-3 inches (Can reach 5-10" if untrimmed) Growth Rate Fast Water Parameters pH 6.5 – 7.5 | Temperature 68°F – 80°F (20°C – 27°C) Propagation Method Cut stems and replant or divide clumps Origin Asia, Australia, New Zealand Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I make Hydrocotyle Tripartita Mini grow as a carpet instead of growing tall? High lighting, consistent CO2 injection, and regular aggressive trimming are key. Trimming the top growth forces the plant to send out horizontal side-shoot runners that stay low and creep along the substrate. 2. Can I attach Hydrocotyle Tripartita Mini to hardscape like wood or rocks? Yes! While it easily roots into aquarium soil, its creeping stems can also be wedged into driftwood crevices or attached with aquarium-safe glue to create cascading green cushions over hardscape elements. 3. Why is my newly planted Hydrocotyle Tripartita Mini floating up? Because tissue culture portions have delicate root systems, fish or water currents can easily dislodge them. Planting small clumps deeply into fine soil or letting the tank grow emersed using the Dry Start Method will anchor the roots securely before flooding.

Plant Profile Show your aquarium some serious love with a seasonal piece that is guaranteed to steal hearts. We have carefully attached Christmas Moss around a durable, heart-shaped floating ring, paired with a hidden aquarium-safe substrate weight and a clear tether line to keep it floating perfectly upright in mid-water. Loved for its deep forest-green color and its signature frond-like, overlapping growth patterns that resemble pine tree branches, each heart wreath provides secure shelter where shy fish and dwarf shrimp can hide! Key Features & Benefits Upright floating heart design creates a striking mid-water portal and a stunning holiday centerpiece. Adds instant three-dimensional depth and a playful swim-through channel to your tank. Provides safe hiding, shelter, and grazing areas for freshwater shrimp and nano fish. Care & Planting Instructions Drop the pre-attached weighted anchor onto your substrate to let the heart float upright, adjusting the clear line length to set your perfect viewing depth. Maintain a stable aquarium environment and avoid sudden, drastic changes to your water parameters to keep your moss looking vibrant and healthy. Give the moss an occasional light haircut with sharp aquascaping shears to keep its shape neat, compact, and perfectly balanced. Propagate your patch in seconds by saving the snipped moss pieces and tying or gluing them to hardscape elsewhere in your tank. Add CO2 injection if you want to accelerate growth and unlock the most intense, eye-popping green coloration possible. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I keep my Heart Shaped Christmas Moss Wreath from turning brown or yellow? Christmas Moss prefers clean, moving water and cooler temperatures (under 78°F). Browning usually occurs when organic debris gets trapped inside the dense fronds or when water temperatures run too high. Gently siphoning debris out during water changes will keep the inner growth green and healthy. 2. What is the best way to position the floating heart wreath in my tank? The heart wreath comes equipped with a clear tether line and an aquarium-safe weight. Simply place the weight on your substrate (or hide it under your gravel layer) and adjust the line length so the heart hovers gracefully at your desired water depth. 3. How do I stop moss trimmings from spreading everywhere during maintenance? Always turn off your filter pumps and powerheads before trimming moss. Use sharp curved shears to make clean cuts, and immediately scoop or siphon out floating cuttings so they don't take root in unwanted areas of your aquarium.

Plant Profile Rotala Wayanad is a relatively rare, delicate aquatic stem plant native to the Wayanad region of India. It's known for slender, needle-like foliage that stays small, with a greenish-yellow color that creates textural contrast when planted alongside broader green or deep red Rotala varieties. It suits nature aquariums, Dutch-style layouts, and nano planted tanks, and branches readily under good care to form fine-leafed midground or background bushes. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Fine, greenish-yellow foliage adds refined texture to planted aquariums. Compact size works for nano tanks or midground/background bushing in larger setups. Fast vertical growth fills in space and branches into dense hedges. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. * Rotala leaves are fragile, so handle stems with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide medium-to-high lighting. Pressurized CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilization yield denser branching and enhance its bright yellow-green tones. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and thicken the bush. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Rotala sp. 'Wayanad' Common Name(s) Rotala Wayanad Family Lythraceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Stem Plant Care Difficulty Medium Light Requirement Medium to High CO2 Requirement Medium to High (Recommended for bushy growth) Placement / Usage Midground / Background Bushing / Nano Tank Height / Size 5”+ Growth Rate Fast Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 Propagation Method Cuttings (Cut stem and replant tops) Origin Asia (India) Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I achieve a bushy look with Rotala Wayanad? To encourage Rotala Wayanad to grow into a dense, compact hedge, trim the main stem tops regularly once the plant is established. Each cut point will produce multiple lateral side shoots, doubling the stem density of the bush. 3. How do I prepare Rotala Wayanad UNS Tissue Culture before planting? Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the dense cluster into smaller clumps or individual stems and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

Aquario Neo Clean is a water conditioner designed to remove small substances in the water column that contribute to cloudiness. Neo Clean's formula works regardless of tank temperature or pH and results in crystal clear water, improving the view and overall enjoyment. We recommend having Aquario Neo Clean on hand whenever your tank needs a little more clarity! In an aquarium, Aquario Neo Clean can help remove both organic and inorganic particles that cause cloudy or hazy water. These often come from: Substrate dust – stirred up during tank setup or planting Sand fines – tiny particles from sand that don’t settle easily Rock debris – particles released when adding hardscape Mineral dust – from crushed lava rock, liquid additives, or other hardscape materials Metal or salt traces – sometimes introduced from tap water or additives Uneaten food particles Fish waste debris Decaying plant matter (small pieces broken off) Fragments of dead algae Neo Clean binds these tiny suspended particles so they clump together, making them easier for your filter to remove or allowing them to settle out of the water column. It's especially helpful in new tank setups or after major rescapes when water often looks cloudy from disturbed materials. Dosage and Usage Notes: 5ml treats 80 Liters (approximately 21 gallons) 1 capful = 5ml on the 300 ml bottles 1 capful = 10ml on the 1000 ml bottles Shake well before use This product may slightly lower tank pH Perform a 30-50% water change 1-3 hours after dosing if concerned about pH fluctuation or to remove cloudiness after particles bind. Aquario Neo Clean is intended for aquarium use only. Keep out of children's and pets' reach. How do I choose the best aquarium filter size for my nano tank? Why is my HOB filter making a rattling noise, and how do I fix it? Vibration against the tank rim is the primary cause of noise in hang-on-back filters. listings.description: Plant Profile Staurogyne Bihar is a unique and captivating aquatic stem plant native to the tropical region of Bihar, India. Originally misidentified as a Hygrophila species, it was officially reclassified into the Staurogyne genus after flowering. Submerged in the aquarium, it produces deeply lobed, pinnatifid-like leaves that strongly resemble Hygrophila pinnatifida . Displaying a rich spectrum of deep green, olive, and reddish-brown tones under high lighting, its textured, palm-like foliage and spreading stem habit make it an extraordinary choice for midground focal points, background accent groups, and paludarium setups. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Distinctive lobed pinnatifid-like foliage provides rich texture and visual contrast. Displays olive green to warm reddish-brown tones under strong light and balanced nutrient dosing. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide medium-to-high lighting and clean water conditions; supplying pressurized CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilization yields faster growth and richer reddish-brown tones. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or leaf rot. To propagate, trim main stem tops or developed side shoots with sharp straight shears and replant trimmings directly into substrate. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How is Staurogyne Bihar different from Hygrophila Pinnatifida? While submerged Staurogyne Bihar leaves strongly resemble Hygrophila pinnatifida in shape, Staurogyne Bihar grows as a true substrate-rooting stem plant rather than an epiphyte that attaches to hardscape, and its leaves tend to grow somewhat larger and broader. 2. Can Staurogyne Bihar be grown without CO2 injection? Yes, Staurogyne Bihar can be kept in moderate-light, low-tech setups without CO2 injection. However, supplying pressurized CO2 along with nutrient-rich soil and higher lighting yields much faster growth, tighter leaf nodes, and reddish-brown coloration. 3. How do I prepare Staurogyne Bihar Tissue Culture before planting? Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the cluster into smaller clumps or individual stems and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

listings.description: Common Name: Helanthium Tenellum Broad Leaf Helanthium Tenellum is a carpeting grass-like plant that bears close resemblance to a mix between dwarf hair grass and micro swords. The AIO ATO consists of a water reservoir, float valve sensor, and a pump mechanism to transfer water from the reservoir into the aquarium. The float valve sensor detects the drop in water level caused by evaporation, triggering the pump to add freshwater from the reservoir back into the aquarium until the desired water level is reached. Using an AIO ATO has several advantages, including reducing the need for manual water top-offs, making it easy to maintain stable water parameters, and preventing salinity fluctuations due to evaporation. Its automated functionality also helps alleviate the risk of substantial water level fluctuations, which can be detrimental to sensitive aquarium inhabitants and marine life. This feature ensures consistent water parameters, reducing stress on your aquarium's inhabitants and supporting their health and well-being. Prevents Salinity Fluctuations: Water evaporation can lead to changes in salinity, which can be harmful to delicate marine organisms. The AIO ATO's precise water level regulation prevents these fluctuations, creating a more stable and favorable environment for sensitive corals, fish, and other aquatic life. Save Time and Effort: With the UNS AIO ATO, the need to perform frequent manual water top-offs is eliminated. This automated system saves you valuable time and effort, allowing you to focus on other aspects of aquarium care. Compact and Efficient Design: The AIO ATO features a modern, space-saving design that easily integrates into your home aquarium setup. Its efficient operation ensures that water is added only when necessary, minimizing water wastage and maximizing use case effectiveness. Plug-and-Play Installation: The UNS AIO ATO is designed for user-friendly installation. Simply set up the water reservoir close to your aquarium, attach the float valve sensor, and connect the pump mechanism to your aquarium with the included fittings. The straightforward setup ensures a hassle-free experience for both novice and experienced aquarium enthusiasts. Aquarium leveling mats are an essential safety requirement for any rimless or glass tank. Once a planted tank is filled with water, dense substrate, and heavy hardscape like rocks or driftwood, it exerts immense pressure on the bottom glass panel. Even the strongest glass is susceptible to external stress, and uneven surfaces or a single grain of debris on your stand can create pinpointed pressure. Over time, this concentrated stress can lead to catastrophic cracked glass, leaks, or total tank failure. The UNS Leveling Mat serves as a high-density cushion, absorbing these imperfections and distributing the aquarium's weight evenly across its surface. Key Features and Benefits UNS mats are crafted from high-density, absorbent foam that cushions the bottom glass panel, neutralizing minor surface irregularities. The material provides a high-grip surface that prevents the aquarium from shifting or sliding during the initial installation or routine maintenance. While these are cut to fit the UNS tank lineup, they are highly versatile and can be easily trimmed with a utility knife to fit any other aquarium brand. Safety Reminder: Leveling mats are designed to absorb micro-imperfections; they are not a substitute for a structurally level stand. Always ensure your aquarium is placed on a flat, weight-bearing surface and that no part of the glass hangs over the edge. Common Name: Diamond Ludwigia, Ludwigia Diamond, Ludwigia Peruensis Diamond Ludwigia is a less common Ludwigia variation with very unique coloration. In low tech conditions, these plants’ leaves can be green on top and red underneath, adding a stunning dimension to the mid-ground of almost any aquascape. However, with CO2 and high light, the leaves can completely turn to a deep purplish red. Their vivid color creates a superb focal point. Diamond Ludwigia plants have oval, pointed leaves that grow in opposite pairs along the stem. The leaves will range from green, gold, orange, or red, depending on tank conditions. These plants are very attractive when planted in bunches of 10-12 stems. In order to achieve the desirable bright colors in your Diamond Ludwigia, you must provide high lighting and nutrient levels. Supplemental iron will bring out more brilliant red tones in the plant. CO2 injection is recommended to see optimal growth and color. The plant can be grown submersed or emersed, and emersed plants will produce delicate yellow flowers. Propagation can be achieved by taking cuttings from the main stem of the plant that are replanted into the substrate. Notes: Tissue culture plants are grown in vitro from a state of the art laboratory specialized in propagating aquatic plants. They provide the best option for those who want to ensure that absolutely zero unwanted pests are introduced into the aquarium. Remove tissue culture gel before planting. Simply wash the gel away or soak the plant in water and squeeze the gel off with your fingers. Do not make drastic changes to the aquarium. Unstable parameters will result in melt and rotting of the aquarium plant. For instructions on how to properly plant tissue culture aquarium plants, click here . CO2 injection and quality aquarium soil will yield better growth. Species Profile The Orange Eye Blue Tiger (OEBT) is one of the most mesmerizing varieties in the shrimp hobby. It is a genetic morph achieved by extensive selective breeding of the Caridina Tiger shrimp. Good quality specimens have deep blue bodies, dark tiger stripes, and bright orange eyes. The highest-grade specimens are solid blue shrimp that eliminate or greatly diminish the Caridina Tiger striping. Lower grades may have translucent bodies, patchy patterns, and brown eyes. As aquatic pets, OEBTs are active scavengers that bring a unique "alien" aesthetic to the shrimp aquarium. They are a soft-water species, thriving in slightly acidic environments with zero carbonate hardness. Because of their distinct look and the intensive line-breeding required to maintain their color, they are a prized centerpiece for any dedicated shrimp tank. **Note: All livestock orders will come carefully packaged with solid wall Styrofoam insulation and shipped via 1-day shipping only. No additional insulation is needed for your livestock. Key Features & Notes Tank-raised specimens displaying stunning blue bodies with glowing orange eyes. Relentless clean-up crew that continuously grazes on biofilm and algae. Provides an ideal centerpiece choice as peaceful dwarf shrimp for aquariums and low-bioload setups. Care Specifications Maintain stable, soft, acidic water conditions using an active buffering substrate to support sensitive Caridina health. Keep water parameters strictly free of copper-based medications or heavy metals. Supplement their diet with plant-based shrimp pellets, spirulina, and blanched vegetables to ensure proper minerals for molting when natural algae is low. Line genetics produce offspring of varying color grades, making culling and selection essential if maintaining deep blue lines. L-Number: L144 Common Name: Longfin Blue Eye Lemon Bristlenose Pleco Scientific Name: Ancistrus sp. Genus: Ancistrus Wild Origin: South America Average Shipped Size: 1-1.5in Adult Size: 4-5in **Note: All livestock orders will come carefully packaged with solid wall Styrofoam insulation and shipped via 1-day shipping only. No extra insulation needs to be added to your cart for your livestock. The Longfin Blue Eye Lemon Bristlenose Pleco is immediately distinguishable in the hobby, with its bright yellow body and blue eyes. Sub-adult Bristlenose plecos develop multiple bristle-like appendages on their facial region. These appendages grow on both males and females, but males tend to have more pronounced and lengthier growth. This species is generally peaceful and tolerant of a range of water parameters. Compared to the monstrous growth potential of the Common Pleco, its smaller size makes it suitable for mid-sized community aquariums and it grows to a max size of 4-5 inches. Male plecos can be slightly territorial with other males, but issues can be resolved by providing plenty of hiding places for each male to mark as his own. The Blue Eye Lemon Bristlenose pleco generally does not bother other tankmates, but it may prey on dwarf shrimp from time to time. Key Features & Important Notes Tank raised specimen Unsexed juveniles Bright, bold colors To increase survival rates, please allow 2-3 business days after an order is placed to properly prepare live animal shipments. Recommended Water Parameters Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. We encourage you to do thorough research before committing to keeping any livestock. Temperature Range: 72-80 F pH: 6.5-7.5 KH: 6-10 Recommended Tank Size 30 gallons. Tank size is relative and various factors should be considered when determining tank size. Factors include maintenance schedules, tank mates, desired colony size, and more. Diet Requires a mainly plant matter-based diet. While not a heavy wood-feeder, it benefits from supplemental wood grazing. Feed high-quality vegetable flakes and sinking algae wafers, as well as fresh vegetables like shelled peas, spinach, zucchini, and cucumber. Breeding Juvenile Blue Eye Lemon Bristlenose Plecos are impossible to differentiate by sex, but as they mature, distinct gender characteristics emerge. Males develop prominent odontodes on their pectoral fins and heads, as well as long and pronounced whisker growth. Females have smaller, less noticeable whisker growth. Females display rounder body shapes, while males possess broader, shorter heads. Full maturity might take up to 2 years, so patience is necessary if you're looking to form breeding pairs from a group. To prepare for breeding, ensure the adult breeders are well-conditioned with a diet of live and frozen foods beforehand. The simplest breeding method involves isolating a pair in a dedicated tank filled with ample caves. Pipes or plant pots make great make-shift "caves". Cave entrances should be slightly larger than the fish so the female has enough room to lay her eggs. Maintain well-oxygenated water and keep the pH under 6.5. The spawning of the fish is induced by factors such as low air pressure and water changes. The male picks a preferred spawning site and actively defends it. He entices the female to the site, though egg-laying might occur days later. Post-spawn, the female plays no further role and is chased away by the male. He handles parenting duties, safeguarding, and fanning the eggs with his fins. Once hatched, fry feed off their yolk sacs initially. Once consumed, provide newly hatched fry with algae wafers, baby brine shrimp, micro-worms, or crushed flakes.
