Genus: Hypancistrus Wild Origin: South America Average Shipped Size: 1.2-1.3in Adult Size: 5-6in **Note: All livestock orders will come carefully packaged with solid wall Styrofoam insulation and shipped via 1-day shipping only. No extra insulation needs to be added to your cart for your livestock. The King Tiger Pleco belongs to the South American suckermouth catfish family. This particular species is easily recognized by its distinct striped pattern that spans its entire body. The King Tiger Pleco is smaller than the Common Pleco, making it suitable for most standard-sized aquariums. Plecos are relatively peaceful and do not generally bother other tankmates, but may prey on dwarf shrimp from time to time. King Tiger Plecos tend to prefer warmer temperatures that may not be suitable for other popular livestock options. The King Tiger Pleco tends to be active at night, but once it adapts to an aquarium featuring ample driftwood, rock formations, and hiding spots, it can display activity during the daytime. While not known for being a heavy wood consumer like certain plecos, it may benefit from supplemental wood consumption and has been observed to feed on bio-film that grows on driftwood. It typically doesn't disturb most plants and isn't a proficient algae consumer. Key Features & Important Notes Unsexed juveniles Bright, bold pattern To increase survival rates, please allow 2-3 business days after an order is placed to properly prepare live animal shipments. Temperature Range: 72-84°F pH: 6.5-7.5 KH: 6-10 Recommended Tank Size 40 gallons. Tank size is relative and various factors should be considered when determining tank size. Factors include maintenance schedules, tank mates, desired colony size, and more. Diet Requires a mainly carnivorous diet. Feed meaty and high-protein foods like bloodworms or tubifex worms. Supplement with driftwood for biofilm-grazing. Commercially-available protein-rich foods like Repashy Gel Diets and Fluval Bug Bites will also be accepted. Breeding Juvenile King Tiger Plecos are impossible to differentiate by sex, but as they mature, distinct gender characteristics emerge. Males develop prominent odontodes on their pectoral fins and heads, while females might have smaller, less noticeable ones. Females display rounder body shapes, while males possess broader, shorter heads. Full maturity might take up to 2 years, so patience is necessary if you're looking to form breeding pairs from a group. To prepare for breeding, ensure the adult breeders are well-conditioned with a diet of live and frozen foods beforehand. The simplest breeding method involves isolating a pair in a dedicated tank filled with ample caves. Pipes or plant pots make great make-shift "caves". Cave entrances should be slightly larger than the fish so the female has enough room to lay her eggs. Maintain well-oxygenated water and keep the pH under 6.5. The spawning of the fish is induced by factors such as low air pressure and water changes. The male picks a preferred spawning site and actively defends it. He entices the female to the site, though egg-laying might occur days later. Post-spawn, the female plays no further role and is chased away by the male. He handles parenting duties, safeguarding, and fanning the eggs with his fins. Once hatched, fry feed off their yolk sacs initially. Once consumed, provide newly hatched fry with algae wafers, baby brine shrimp, micro-worms, or crushed flakes.

listings.description: Species Profile Shadow Black King Kong Shrimp were selectively bred by crossing Blue Bolt shrimp with Black King Kong Shrimp. This unique lineage results in the "Shadow" effect, which is a distinct blue iridescent hue that glows beneath the white pigment of the shrimp. The "Mosura" grade is highly coveted, defined by a primarily white body and a striking black "crown" or "mask". This combination offers a sophisticated, high-contrast look that stands out in a shrimp tank. Because they are a highly bred Taiwan Bee variety, they are more sensitive than standard shrimp and require a disciplined approach to water stability. They are best suited for the intermediate to advanced hobbyist who can provide the soft, acidic conditions necessary for their vibrant colors and health. **Note: All livestock orders will come carefully packaged with solid wall Styrofoam insulation and shipped via 1-day shipping only. No additional insulation is needed for your livestock. Key Features & Notes Tank-raised unsexed juveniles displaying the coveted Mosura pattern. Elite Taiwan Bee strain prized for its high-grade pigmentation and high-contrast visual appeal. Relentless clean-up crew that continuously grazes on biofilm and algae. Peaceful, social behavior makes them an ideal choice for aquariums. Care Specifications Maintain stable, soft, acidic water chemistry using an active buffering substrate to support sensitive Caridina health. Keep water parameters strictly free of copper-based medications or heavy metals. Species Profile The Golden Bee Shrimp is a unique and ethereal variety belonging to the Crystal Bee group. Unlike the banded Crystal Red or Black shrimp, the Golden Bee has been selectively bred for a solid, opaque body color that ranges from a warm, creamy orange-yellow to a brilliant snow-white or golden-white tone. Because they lack the dark pigment of their cousins, they provide a bright, clean aesthetic that "glows" in a well-lit shrimp aquarium, especially when paired with lush green mosses or dark dragon stone. Caring for Golden Bees requires a disciplined approach to water chemistry. Unlike hardier species, these freshwater shrimp are notably delicate and do not tolerate poor water quality or abrupt fluctuations. For their well-being, ensure that the aquarium water remains soft and slightly acidic. Even trace amounts of ammonia or nitrite can be fatal to these sensitive aquatic pets, making them a rewarding challenge for the intermediate to advanced hobbyist. **Note: All livestock orders will come carefully packaged with solid wall Styrofoam insulation and shipped via 1-day shipping only. Species Profile The Red Nose Shrimp is one of the most peculiar and charming "oddball" freshwater shrimp. Named for their incredibly long, needle-like red rostrum, these shrimp resemble Pinocchio. Their bodies are primarily translucent, often accented with a subtle yellow or red stripe running the full length of the back. While their appearance is whimsical, their work ethic is serious, as Red Nose Shrimp are widely considered to be on par with Amano Shrimp for their ability to consume hair algae and various other nuisance algae types. Red Nose Shrimp are unique not just in looks, but in behavior. Unlike many dwarf shrimp that stay glued to the substrate, Red Nose Shrimp are active swimmers and can often be seen hovering in the water column like tiny helicopters. They are peaceful and social, making them a fantastic addition to a community shrimp aquarium. Important Care Tip: It is important to have a lower water level or aquarium lid with this variety, as they are also known to be jumpers! **Note: All livestock orders will come carefully packaged with solid wall Styrofoam insulation and shipped via 1-day shipping only. No additional insulation is needed for your livestock. Key Features & Notes Tank-raised unsexed juveniles featuring an elongated red rostrum and clear body with subtle striping. Powerhouse algae eater capable of tackling tough hair algae, thread algae, and biofilm. Unique hover-swimming capability that keeps them buoyant and active throughout the water column. Peaceful, social behavior making them ideal community tankmates and peaceful dwarf shrimp for aquariums. To increase survival rates, please allow 2 to 3 business days after an order is placed to properly prepare live animal shipments. Species Profile The Bloody Mary Shrimp ( Neocaridina davidi ) is the ultimate expression of red, and no, you do not have to chant their name into a mirror three times to see them appear in your shrimp tank. While often compared to high-grade Fire Red Cherry Shrimp, these freshwater aquarium shrimp are genetically and physically distinct. In most red varieties, the pigmentation is concentrated in the shell; however, Bloody Marys feature deep red tissue beneath a crystal-clear shell, resulting in an intense, liquid-like crimson glow. You can also spot these tiny critters by their noticeably shorter rostrum (nose) compared to standard cherries. Spooky name aside, these active freshwater shrimp spend their days haunting hardscape and foliage to graze on biofilm and soft algae without damaging delicate plant tissue, popping vividly against dark aquarium soil and lush green mosses. **Note: All livestock orders will come carefully packaged with solid wall Styrofoam insulation and shipped via 1-day shipping only. Active, plant-safe grazer that continuously scours biofilm and soft algae without uprooting delicate carpet runners. Hardy Neocaridina strain with a distinctive short rostrum that adapts smoothly to conditioned tap water. Care Specifications Maintain clean, well-filtered water with stable GH and KH levels to ensure problem-free molting cycles. Keep water parameters strictly free of copper-based medications or heavy metals. Species Profile Blue Rili Shrimp ( Neocaridina davidi ) are selectively bred freshwater aquarium shrimp known for their striking piebald patterning, combining deep midnight-blue and dark carbon patches with translucent midsections. Bred from stable carbon lines, these tiny critters bring visual variety to planted layouts, creating high-contrast depth against light sand, dark aquarium soil, and lush green mosses. Each individual displays a slightly different pattern of color distribution, making every colony look diverse. Their adaptable Neocaridina genetics allow them to thrive in standard conditioned tap water, and their peaceful nature makes these freshwater shrimp an easy addition to dedicated nano colonies and community setups. **Note: All livestock orders will come carefully packaged with solid wall Styrofoam insulation and shipped via 1-day shipping only. No extra insulation needs to be added to your cart for your livestock. Key Features & Notes Distinct piebald color blocking pairs deep midnight blue and carbon-black patches with crystal-clear midsections. Active, plant-safe grazer that continuously scours biofilm and soft algae without uprooting delicate carpet runners. Hardy Neocaridina strain that adapts smoothly to conditioned tap water and establishes self-sustaining colonies. Care Specifications Maintain clean, well-filtered water with stable GH and KH levels to ensure problem-free molting cycles. Keep water parameters strictly free of copper-based medications or heavy metals. Supplement their diet with plant-based shrimp pellets, spirulina, and blanched vegetables to ensure proper minerals for molting when natural algae is low. Provide textured hardscape like lava rock or mosses to maximize surface area for beneficial biofilm growth and shrimplet shelter. Leave molted shells in the tank so fry and adults can ingest essential minerals for growth. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy livestock! Species Profile The Snowball Shrimp is a clean, minimalist favorite in the freshwater shrimp hobby. Known for their translucent-to-pure-white bodies, they offer a bright pop of contrast against dark volcanic substrates or deep green mosses. Unlike many other shrimp varieties, Snowball Shrimp do not have a complex grading scale because they have been bred to produce a consistent, opaque white color. They are named after the female's bright white eggs, which resemble tiny snowballs when she is berried. Snowball Shrimp are energetic scavengers that work around the clock as a natural clean-up crew, grazing on biofilm and nuisance algae. While they belong to a different species than the standard Red Cherry (N. davidi), their care requirements are identical, making them an excellent beginner shrimp. They are peaceful, social, and a fantastic way to add a bright, "frozen" aesthetic to your shrimp aquarium. **Note: All livestock orders will come carefully packaged with solid wall Styrofoam insulation and shipped via 1-day shipping only. Plant Profile Ready to drop the hammer on boring aquascapes? Hailing from Poland, Java Fern 'Thor's Hammer' is a rare cultivar that brings the thunder to your midground zones. Featuring sleeker, narrower leaves than standard Java Fern , its fronds branch out at the tips into distinct, hammer-shaped crests, offering a bolder, blockier take on the finely branched tips seen on Java Fern Windelov . This bulletproof epiphyte thrives under dim lighting, laughs in the face of parameter swings, and remains delightfully unbothered by curious fish looking for a snack. Key Features & Notes Tough, fibrous foliage easily withstands curious nipping from herbivorous fish like cichlids, goldfish, and large snails. Unique crested leaf tips and slender fronds add texture and detail. Exceptional hardiness lets it thrive in non-CO2 tanks and low-light environments. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Java Fern 'Thor's Hammer' is an epiphytic fern that should be attached to rocks or driftwood with aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as it will rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard setups, gentle water movement and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and broader fronds. Master long-term care and troubleshoot common leaf issues by checking out our Java Fern Care Guide . Final size and foliage pattern depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Microsorum pteropus 'Thor's Hammer' (syn. Leptochilus pteropus ) Common Name(s) Java Fern Thor's Hammer, Thor Java Fern Family Polypodiaceae Plant Type Epiphyte (Rhizome Fern) Care Difficulty Beginner / Easy (Low-Tech Compatible) Light Requirement Low to Medium CO2 Requirement Not Required (Beneficial) Placement / Usage Foreground, Midground, Focal Hardscape Accent Height / Size 5"–8" (13–20 cm) Growth Rate Slow to Moderate Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 | Temperature 68°F–82°F (20°C–28°C) Propagation Method Rhizome Division & Adventitious Plantlets Origin Poland (Cultivated Variety) / Native to Asia Frequently Asked Questions 1. What makes Java Fern 'Thor's Hammer' different from regular Java Fern? Unlike standard Java Fern which features smooth, undivided leaf blades, 'Thor's Hammer' boasts narrower fronds that split and crest into distinct, hammer-shaped tips at the ends. It is an extremely rare variant originating from selective cultivation in Poland. 2. Why are there small black spots and tiny leaves growing under my Java Fern 'Thor's Hammer' leaves? Do not panic; your plant hasn't been smitten by lightning! Java Fern reproduces naturally through adventitious plantlets. Small dark bumps (sporangia) form along the undersides of mature leaves, sprouting tiny brown roots and mini green fronds. Once these baby plantlets develop 3–4 leaves, you can gently pop them off the mother leaf and glue them elsewhere in your aquarium. 3. Can I plant Java Fern 'Thor's Hammer' into substrate? No. Java Fern 'Thor's Hammer' is an epiphyte that absorbs nutrients directly from the water column through its foliage and fine root network. If you bury its horizontal rhizome beneath aquarium soil, sand, or gravel, the stem will suffocate, rot, and die. Always attach it to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread. 4. Will fish like cichlids or goldfish eat Java Fern 'Thor's Hammer'? Generally, no. Java Fern leaves are thick, fibrous, and contain bitter-tasting compounds that deter most plant-eating fish. While aggressive diggers might knock it off hardscape if not glued securely, they rarely consume the foliage.

Plant Profile Bucephalandra ‘Kedagang Mini’ is a stunning miniature aquarium plant featuring small leaves that display a deep, saturated reddish-brown hue. This particular variant is highly prized for its tiny scale, making it an essential choice for adding intricate detail and rich color to smaller layouts. Highly versatile, it can be grown submerged or emersed, usually attached to hardscape such as driftwood or rocks rather than being buried in traditional aquarium substrate. Place it in the foreground of your aquascape, and it will slowly form a dense, colorful carpet. Key Features & Notes As one of the smaller Kedagang variants, this plant is perfect for creating a sense of massive scale in tiny nano tanks or tight crevices. Under quality aquarium LED lighting, the foliage maintains a dark reddish-brown color that provides a moody, sophisticated contrast to bright green mosses. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for planted tanks where other plants might struggle. Care & Planting Instructions Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard low-light aquarium plant setups, CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and richer iridescence. Plant Profile Bucephalandra ‘Peacock’ is a beginner-friendly, low-tech aquarium plant distinguished by its rounded leaves and prominent midribs that run through each leaf center. Key Features & Notes The combination of a strong midrib and tiny "silver" spots (stomata) gives this plant a unique, starry appearance under LED lighting. It is an ideal choice for planted tanks where other plants might struggle. Care & Planting Instructions Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard low-light aquarium plant setups, CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and richer iridescence. Plant Profile Hailing from the freshwater streams of Madagascar, Aponogeton ulvaceus is one of the most expressive bulb plants you can add to a display. Visually, it feels like a blend between the ruffled leaves of Aponogeton Longiplumulosus and the translucent structure of the Madagascar Lace Plant . It grows in a full rosette, pushing out wide, delicate, pale green leaves that twist and spiral as they stretch upward toward the light. Maxing out around 20 inches tall, its flowing leaf blades catch filter currents easily and create a soft, undulating backdrop in medium to large setups. While it grows at a manageable pace, giving it a rich root zone and steady flow will keep its foliage healthy and vibrant over time. Key Features & Notes Translucent pale green foliage twists and ripples to create dynamic texture in the background. Large rosette growth habit maxing out around 20 inches tall fills out background corners. Hardy bulb base stores nutrients to support long-term foliage production. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by gently clearing away any loose rockwool or debris around the bulb base and roots. Plant the roots into a nutrient-dense aquarium soil, keeping the top sprouting tip of the bulb exposed above the substrate line to prevent rot. All Aponogeton species are heavy root feeders; placing root tabs near the bulb base provides the extra boost needed for full leaf development. Ensure good water circulation throughout the tank, as steady flow helps clear debris from its delicate leaf surfaces. Provide low to moderate lighting; while CO2 injection isn't strictly required, supplemental CO2 supports denser foliage growth. Maintain stable water conditions to prevent leaf shedding or premature dormancy during seasonal parameter shifts. Propagate by allowing daughter plantlets to form along mature flower stalks or by dividing offshoot bulbs once fully rooted. How deep should I plant the bulb of Aponogeton ulvaceus? Bury the root system into your soil, but make sure the top sprouting tip of the bulb sits just above the substrate. Burying the entire bulb restricts water exchange around the crown and can cause rot. 2. Does Aponogeton ulvaceus go through a dormancy period? Like many wild Aponogeton species, it may occasionally drop its leaves and rest for a few weeks. If this happens, leave the bulb in place with stable water conditions, and it will eventually sprout fresh foliage. 3. Can Aponogeton ulvaceus grow in low-tech aquariums without CO2? Yes, it grows well in low-tech aquariums without pressurized CO2. Providing a quality, nutrient-dense substrate or adding root tabs will give it plenty of fuel to grow steady, healthy leaves.

When you are injecting pressurized CO₂, finding the sweet spot is a delicate balancing act. Too little gas stalls plant growth, while too much can be fatal to your fish and shrimp. The UNS Drop Checker takes the guesswork out of the equation by giving you a permanent, easy-to-read, color-coded window into your tank's chemistry. Available in two sleek glass styles, it shifts colors automatically based on your water's pH fluctuations caused by dissolved gas. Key Features & Benefits Provides a continuous, real-time visual safety check so you can monitor your gas dosing safety at a quick glance. The high-clarity glass construction blends seamlessly into your aquascape without creating an eyesore or distraction. Available in two distinct mounting styles (In-Tank Suction or Over-the-Rim Hang) to perfectly match your aesthetic preferences. The all-in-one kit includes a starter 15ml bottle of high-purity indicator solution so you can protect your livestock right out of the box. The Color Guide: How to Read Your Levels Because CO₂ drops the pH of your water as it dissolves, the indicator solution changes color to tell you exactly where you stand. Note: Readings are not instant. Please allow a minimum of 1 hour for the solution to accurately reflect your current tank levels. Blue (Low): Your carbon levels are too low. Your plants may stall out, allowing opportunistic algae to take hold. Green (Optimal): The sweet spot! Carbon levels are perfectly sufficient for lush, high-tech plant growth and safe for your livestock. Yellow (High): Danger zone. Your CO₂ levels are too high and are posing an immediate risk to your fish and shrimp. Turn down your regulator immediately. Product Specifications Material: Lab-Grade High-Clarity Glass Solution Bottle Volume: 15ml included ( Replacement 30ml bottles are available for separate purchase ). Fluid Lifespan: For maximum accuracy, we recommend replacing the indicator fluid inside the glass every 4 to 6 weeks, or whenever the solution begins to fade in color. Technical Specifications UNS Drop Checker SD Compatible with all aquariums. Installed in-tank via suction cups. UNS Drop Checker HD Compatible with aquarium rims up to 10mm thick. Installed on the aquarium rim. What’s in the Box? 1x Premium Glass UNS Drop Checker (Choose SD or HD style) 1x 15ml CO₂ Indicator Fluid Bottle 1x Clear Suction Cup (Included with SD style only)

However, if you are using different filter tubing, hose clamps need to be used for security.* Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I choose the best aquarium filter flow rate for my specific tank size? A reliable rule of thumb for selecting a filter for aquariums is aiming for a turnover rate of 4 to 5 times your total tank volume per hour. For instance, a 12-gallon nano aquarium benefits most from an aquarium filter rated around 50 to 60 GPH to ensure thorough mechanical filtration and biological filtration without creating overwhelming currents for small livestock. 2. How can I make my filter intake safe for baby shrimp and fry? Installing a fine stainless steel mesh intake guard or a pre-filter sponge directly over the metal inflow pipe prevents tiny dwarf shrimp and newly hatched fry from getting pulled into the suction line. This simple addition keeps delicate livestock safe while trapping large leaf debris before it reaches your main filter chamber. 3. How should I layer my media for maximum water clarity and biological stability? Water should always pass through coarse mechanical filter pads first to trap floating particulate matter, followed by porous biological media like biological ceramic rings or porous stone matrix for beneficial bacteria colonization. Chemical filtration media like activated carbon or specialty resin pads should sit at the very end of the flow path to strip discolorations and odors without clogging prematurely.

listings.description: Plant Profile Bacopa Salzmannii Purple (aka Bacopa Purple) is a sought-after aquatic stem plant native to the tropical Americas and Southeastern United States. Most Bacopa species stay green, but this one doesn't get the memo! Instead, it produces purple and magenta foliage when grown under optimal aquarium conditions. Featuring rounded, succulent-like leaves set along sturdy vertical stems, it doesn't demand perfect conditions to hold its color (unlike a lot of high-color stem plants), making it a solid pick for beginners. It works well as a midground or foreground focal point, adding dark-purple contrast against greener neighbors in a planted aquascape. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Deep purple, violet, and magenta leaves deliver uncommon color. Vertical stems and rounded leaves form structured midground terraces through routine pruning and replanting. Hardiness and adaptability make it a rewarding purple choice for both high-tech and modest planted tanks. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide medium-to-high lighting and consistent liquid or root fertilization; adding pressurized CO2 injection and iron supplementation maximizes its deep purple pigmentation. Maintain stable water parameters and clean water conditions to support fast root attachment and steady growth. Trim stem tops or lateral shoots with straight scissors, and simply replant trimmings or basal runners into substrate to propagate new shoots. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining adequate light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I get my Bacopa Salzmannii Purple to turn deep purple? While this variety naturally possesses purple tendencies, reaching its intense, rich violet-purple coloration requires medium-to-high light intensity, pressurized CO2 injection, micronutrient dosing with liquid iron, and a nutrient-dense substrate. 3. How do I prepare Bacopa Salzmannii Purple Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture before planting? Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the dense cluster into smaller clumps or individual stem bundles and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

Plant Profile Lagenandra Keralensis is a rare rhizome species native to the heavily shaded, flooded stream banks of Kerala, India. It produces broad, textured oval leaves with an earthy color blend of rich bronze, deep olive green, and warm brown. Reaching 5 or more inches in height with a slow-growing rosette habit, it serves as a midground accent in planted aquariums and emersed terrariums. While CO2 and moderate lighting help showcase its deepest bronze hues, Lagenandra Keralensis is hardy and adaptable, making it a beginner-friendly and low-tech option for aquascapers seeking a low-maintenance, unique alternative to classic Cryptocoryne species. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Rare bronze, brown, and deep green foliage brings rich earthy color tones and broad leaf texture to midground zones. Hardy, slow-growing rhizome species that builds a sturdy, low-maintenance rosette structure over time. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Plant the roots firmly into your aquarium soil, taking care to keep the central rhizome resting slightly above the substrate surface to prevent rot. As a heavy root feeder, Lagenaria keralensis thrives when provided with root nutrition; placing root tabs directly near the root base in your aquarium soil encourages steady root development and healthier leaf structure. Provide medium lighting and good water circulation; while adaptable in low-tech setups, supplying pressurized CO2 and soft water parameters yields faster growth and richer bronze tones. Keep water parameters stable and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent temporary leaf melting during transition. To propagate, use a sharp blade to divide the rhizome into smaller sections (ensuring each piece has several leaves and healthy roots attached) and replant them back into your aquarium soil. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I plant Lagenandra Keralensis Tissue Culture without causing rhizome rot? After rinsing away the tissue culture gel, insert the root cluster into your aquarium soil using pinsettes, but ensure the central horizontal rhizome remains resting slightly above the soil surface. Burying the rhizome completely can restrict oxygen flow and cause the plant base to rot. 2. Is Lagenandra Keralensis suitable for beginner low-tech aquariums? Yes, Lagenandra Keralensis is a hardy, beginner-friendly species that can easily adapt to low-tech tanks without pressurized CO2. While its growth rate is naturally slow, maintaining stable water chemistry and basic lighting will keep it thriving. 3. How do I prepare Lagenandra Keralensis Tissue Culture before planting? Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the cup into smaller portion clumps and plant them into your aquarium soil using fine pinsettes.

Plant Profile Assorted Echinodorus Plant Pack brings together a curated mix of hardy rosette sword plants in the family Alismataceae, native to riverbanks and wetlands across South America. Known throughout the hobby as Amazon Swords, these plants develop extensive root systems and grow into substantial midground or background centerpieces and fill out empty vertical space in medium and large aquariums without needing pressurized CO2 or intense lighting. Just plant them deeply into quality aquarium soil or tuck root tabs underneath their crowns, because starving an Amazon Sword in inert gravel is a guaranteed way to end up with yellow, pinhole-riddled leaves. Key Features & Benefits Curated assortment of hardy, beginner-friendly Amazon Sword varieties offers diverse leaf shapes, textures, and colors. Thrives in low-tech setups with low to moderate lighting and adapts smoothly to a wide range of water parameters. Adapts to both fully submerged aquariums and emersed setups in humid terrariums or paludariums. Potential Varieties Included in This Pack: Echinodorus Martii Major Echinodorus Ozelot Green Echinodorus Ozelot Echinodorus Cordifolius Echinodorus Rose Echinodorus Red Phoenix Echinodorus Narrow Mini Echinodorus Grandifolius Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Plant the roots deeply into your aquarium soil, keeping the crown of the plant resting just above the substrate line to prevent rot. All Echinodorus are heavy root feeders that rely on rich substrate nutrition; placing root tabs near the base supports steady, healthy leaf development. Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf shedding during the initial transition period. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Echinodorus spp. Common Name(s) Amazon Sword, Echinodorus Assorted Pack Family Alismataceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Rosette Aquatic Plant Care Difficulty Easy Light Requirement Low to Moderate CO2 Requirement Not Required (Grows reliably without CO2; injection boosts growth rate and color) Placement / Usage Midground / Background Focal Point Height / Size 4–20”+ (Varies by cultivar) Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 Propagation Method Adventitious Plantlets / Runner Division Origin South America Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are my newly planted Amazon Swords melting or turning translucent? Most Echinodorus are grown emersed above water at nurseries and naturally shed their stiffer, rounded land leaves after submersion. Keep the crown healthy in aquarium soil, trim away decaying outer leaves, and new submerged foliage will emerge within a couple of weeks. 2. Do Amazon Swords need root tabs if I use aquarium soil? While fresh aquarium soil supplies plenty of initial nutrients, Echinodorus species are heavy root feeders that quickly deplete local reserves. Adding root tabs every few months keeps larger swords growing steadily without nutrient deficiencies. 3. How do I propagate Echinodorus plants? Healthy, established Amazon Swords send up long flowering stalks that sprout miniature daughter plantlets along the nodes. Once these baby plants develop their own root systems, snip them off the runner and plant them directly into your aquarium soil.

Plant Profile Holding holy-grail status among aquatic plant collectors, Echinodorus Iguazu is easily one of the rarest and most sought-after sword plants in the entire aquascaping hobby. Originally discovered near the majestic Iguazu Falls region in South America, this legendary species is instantly recognizable by its thick, leathery, deep emerald-green leaves that form a remarkably tight, compact rosette. Unlike traditional fast-growing Amazon Swords that rapidly skyrocket toward the surface, 'Iguazu' stays exceptionally low-slung, expanding in a wide, circular pattern with stout, heart-shaped leaf blades. Key Features & Notes Extremely rare collector's species with thick, leathery, dark emerald-green foliage in a rounded rosette habit. Compact and broad growth form makes it a pristine centerpiece for midground placement. Hardy and slow-growing variety that maintains its size and shape without frequent pruning or maintenance. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Plant the roots deeply into your aquarium soil, keeping the central crown resting just above the substrate line to prevent rot. All Echinodorus are heavy root feeders that rely on rich substrate nutrition; placing root tabs near the base supports steady, healthy leaf development. Supplemental CO2 injection accelerates growth and encourages denser, fuller foliage, though the plant will still grow steadily in low-tech setups. Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf shedding during the initial transition period. Sword plants propagate through side shoots off of their leaves, which can be trimmed and replanted into the substrate. To control the size of your sword plant, you can remove the side shoots and older leaves. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Echinodorus 'Iguazu' Common Name(s) Echinodorus Iguazu, Iguazu 2009 Sword Family Alismataceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Rosette plant / Rare Species Variant Care Difficulty Medium Light Requirement Low to Moderate CO2 Requirement Not required (Recommended) Placement / Usage Midground Centerpiece Height / Size 4–15+ inches Growth Rate Slow Water Parameters pH 5.5–9.0 Propagation Method Separate new plantlets from the root crown or adventitious shoots Origin South America (Iguazu Falls region) Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why is Echinodorus Iguazu considered so rare and valuable in the aquarium hobby? Echinodorus 'Iguazu' grows much slower than virtually all other sword plants, producing new leaves only every few weeks. Because it cannot be mass-propagated overnight, available specimens are limited, making it a highly prized holy-grail plant for collectors. 2. What substrate and lighting conditions work best for Echinodorus Iguazu? It thrives best in nutrient-rich aquarium soil supplemented with root tabs, as its thick root system absorbs heavy nutrients from the base. Low-to-moderate lighting is ideal; excess light isn't necessary and can invite algae onto its slow-growing, leathery leaves. 3. Can Echinodorus Iguazu be kept in smaller midground zones? Yes, its compact growth habit and slow growth rate make it a stunning midground centerpiece in medium-to-large aquariums, or an impressive focal point in smaller setups where fast-growing Amazon Swords would quickly outgrow the space.

Covering a comprehensive full-spectrum range of approximately 400 to 700 nm, this light places a heavy emphasis on the critical red and blue wavelengths necessary for robust photosynthesis while beautifully maintaining the green and yellow rays. Key Features & Benefits Integrated Bluetooth App Control: Connects effortlessly to the My Chihiros app so you can customize light schedules, dimming percentages, and gentle sunrise/sunset curves. Targeted 8,000K Plant-Growing Spectrum: Delivers high-PAR energy with pronounced red and blue wavelengths to promote dense, rapid carpeting and stem plant growth. Three-Row LED Array: Blankets your entire aquascape with a smooth, completely uniform light spread that virtually eliminates dark corners and visual shadows. Transparent Acrylic Legs: Clamps securely onto your aquarium rim, providing a highly stable mount while blending invisibly into your room's decor. Low-Profile Heat Sink Architecture: Aluminum shell acts as a structural heat sink, efficiently drawing warmth away from the circuitry to guarantee long-term performance. Technical Specifications Please review the model specifications below to select the ideal light length and PAR output for your aquarium footprint. How do I program daily lighting schedules and dimming on the Chihiros A II Series? The Chihiros A II features built-in Bluetooth connectivity. Simply download the free My Chihiros App (iOS & Android) to program custom photoperiods, adjust brightness intensity levels, and set smooth sunrise and sunset ramping cycles. 2. Is the Chihiros A II light strong enough to grow light-demanding stem plants and carpet plants? Yes! The A II Series outputs high PAR energy in an 8,000K spectrum designed specifically to fuel demanding carpet species (like Dwarf Baby Tears and Monte Carlo) and vibrant red stem plants when paired with proper nutrient dosing and CO2 injection. 3. Are the transparent acrylic mounting legs adjustable? The transparent acrylic legs fit securely over rimless tank glass up to 8mm thick, providing a clean, subtle floating aesthetic above your aquarium display.

Product Overview The Chihiros Nova 1 LED Light is a high-output pendant fixture engineered to deliver exceptional light penetration for deep aquariums and high-tech aquascapes. Packing 126 watts of energy into a compact square footprint, this localized light source utilizes 61 high-density LEDs to project 3,800 lumens straight down through the water column. Designed to overcome the shadow limitations of traditional linear light strips, the Nova 1 produces extreme PAR levels at the substrate level to support demanding carpeting plants, vibrant red stems, and dense hardscape layouts while casting a natural sun-shimmer effect across your tank. Key Features & Benefits 126W Concentrated Pendant Array: Punches high-PAR light energy through deep water columns, delivering the intensity needed for demanding foreground carpet plants and red stems. My Chihiros App Control: Built-in Bluetooth connectivity lets you program custom color channels, adjust intensity thresholds, and set automated 24-hour daily lighting schedules. Natural Sunlight Shimmer Effect: Single point-source illumination creates dancing light reflections and dramatic shadows reminiscent of natural sunlight hitting an open stream. Sunrise & Sunset Ramping: Gradually brightens and dims the light over set timeframes to emulate natural day cycles and prevent livestock from startling. WiFi Hub Compatible: Pairs with the optional Chihiros WiFi Hub for remote, cloud-based lighting management from anywhere. Compact Modern Aesthetic: Packs 61 dense LEDs into a sleek square housing that keeps the top of your rimless aquarium open and uncluttered. What size tank is a single Chihiros Nova 1 LED light suitable for? A single Nova 1 pendant is optimized to cover a footprint up to 24" x 24" (60 x 60 cm) with high PAR intensity. For longer aquariums (such as 36-inch or 48-inch tanks), using two or more Nova 1 units spaced evenly will ensure complete edge-to-edge light coverage without dim spots. 2. Can I control the Chihiros Nova 1 away from home? Out of the box, the light connects directly to the My Chihiros app via Bluetooth within short range. To control schedules, color spectrums, and power levels remotely over Wi-Fi when away from home, you can pair the fixture with an optional Chihiros Wi-Fi Hub. 3. Does the Chihiros Nova 1 come with mounting legs or a stand? No. The Nova 1 is engineered purely as a hanging pendant fixture. You will need to pair it with the dedicated Chihiros Nova 1 Mounting Arm Stand to secure it above your rimless tank.

listings.commonName: Chihiros RGB Vivid Mini LED Light
listings.description: Product Overview The Chihiros RGB Vivid Mini LED Light is specifically scaled down to cater to small-to-medium high-tech displays. Packing 5,000 lumens into a sleek 14-inch frame, this point-source light utilizes 80 premium RGB 3-in-1 LED chips to blast intensive photosynthetic energy deep through the water column. For a different look, you can convert this fixture into an open-air floating display by adding the Chihiros RGB Vivid Mini Hanging Kit . Key Features & Benefits Intense 75W Point-Source Power: Pushes high-PAR energy through dense hardscapes and deep water columns, driving vigorous growth in demanding carpeting plants and red stems. RGB 3-in-1 Diode Technology: Mixes red, green, and blue light directly at the chip source to bring out deep, vibrant natural pigments in foliage, fish, and freshwater shrimp. Natural Shimmer Effect: Single-source point lighting creates dynamic, natural sunlight shimmer patterns across your substrate and hardscape. Full Bluetooth App Customization: Pairs seamlessly with the free My Chihiros App on iOS and Android to set custom color channel balances, dimming thresholds, and daily photoperiods. Gradual Sunrise & Sunset Ramping: Gently ramps lighting intensity up and down over a designated timeframe, creating a smooth transition that keeps skittish livestock from startling. Anodized Aluminum Unibody Heat Sink: Premium metal housing acts as a heavy-duty passive heat sink, pulling heat away from high-density electronics for a 50,000-hour operational lifespan. Technical Specifications Please check your aquarium dimensions carefully to ensure an optimal light spread over your layout. Attribute Specification Brand Chihiros Aquatic Studio Model RGB Vivid Mini LED Light Fixture Dimensions (L x W x H) 14.0" x 5.51" x 1.40" (35.6 x 14.0 x 3.6 cm) Tank Width Compatibility 16" to 24" (40 to 60 cm) Aquariums Power Consumption 75 Watts Luminous Flux 5,000 Lumens LED Configuration 80 Pieces (Full-Spectrum RGB 3-in-1) Expected Lifespan ~50,000 Hours Operating Voltage AC 100–240V, 50–60Hz Control Method Integrated Bluetooth (My Chihiros App) What's Included 1x Chihiros RGB Vivid Mini LED Light Fixture 1x Set of Glass Rim Mounting Brackets 1x Integrated Smart Bluetooth Controller 1x Heavy-Duty Power Adapter & Cable Unit Frequently Asked Questions 1. Can I suspend the Chihiros RGB Vivid Mini overhead as a hanging pendant? Yes! While the fixture includes glass rim-mounting brackets by default, you can add the Chihiros RGB Vivid Mini Hanging Kit to suspend the light from overhead light stands or ceiling mounts. 2. How do I control color settings and timers on the Vivid Mini? The light features built-in Bluetooth connectivity. Simply download the free My Chihiros App on your smartphone to adjust individual red, green, and blue color channels, set total power percentages, and schedule automated sunrise/sunset routines. 3. Are light shades available to block side glare? Yes! To prevent eye glare when sitting near your tank, you can add the matching Chihiros RGB Vivid Mini Light Shade or the Pendant Shade Kit .

Key Features & Benefits Custom-Tailored Fit: Engineered specifically for the RGB Vivid Mini to slide smoothly into factory housing channels for a flush, seamless finish. Complete Anti-Glare Comfort: Intercepts harsh horizontal light spill, keeping bright diode glare out of your eyes when viewing your aquascape from a desk or couch. Effortless Tool-Free Mounting: Installs onto both front and rear tracks in seconds without requiring screws, clips, or extra hardware. Sleek Matte Black Aesthetic: Frame-matching finish creates an architectural boundary that masks raw diode exposure for a clean, gallery-style look. Complete Front & Rear Set: Ships as a complete matching two-panel set to provide balanced coverage across both sides of your pendant. Technical Specifications Please double-check your light fixture model before purchasing. Important Note: This listing is for the shade accessory kit only. Will this light shade fit the Chihiros RGB Vivid II or Vivid II Mate? No. The Vivid Mini has a smaller housing profile. How do I attach the shades to my Chihiros Vivid Mini light? Installation is completely tool-free! listings.commonName: Chihiros RGB Vivid Mini Pendant Light Shade
listings.description: Product Overview Control light spread and maximize your viewing comfort with the Chihiros RGB Vivid Mini Pendant Light Shade. When a powerful light is suspended over an open-top aquarium, a significant amount of light can spill into the surrounding room. Specially engineered as a direct fit for the Chihiros RGB Vivid Mini Pendant LED Light , this accessory functions as a targeted shade that redirects stray rays downward into your aquascape. Key Features & Benefits Effective Anti-Glare Protection: Prevents harsh horizontal light spill from striking your eyes, making your surrounding living room, bedroom, or office workspace much more comfortable for daily viewing. Clean Architectural Aesthetic: Sleek geometric silhouette creates a polished boundary around your suspended pendant while masking raw diode exposure for a high-end gallery finish. Precision Direct-Fit Construction: Engineered specifically for the Vivid Mini Pendant housing to attach seamlessly without compromising airflow or fixture balance. Enhanced Focus & PAR Efficiency: Keeps escaping light directed straight into the water column, increasing localized light levels where your aquatic plants need it most. Technical Specifications Please review your light model before purchasing. Please note that this listing is for the shade accessory kit only. The Chihiros RGB Vivid Mini Pendant LED Light fixture is sold separately. listings.commonName: Chihiros RGB Vivid2 LED Light - Black 10th Anniversary Edition
listings.description: Product Overview The special‑release Chihiros RGB Vivid2 LED Light (10th Anniversary Edition) brings serious power and polish to any high‑tech aquascape and even sports a commemorative 10‑year badge to mark the milestone. Built for deep tanks, demanding layouts, and showpiece Dutch‑style setups, this upgraded pendant pushes out a massive 12,200 lumens through a dense grid of 160 RGB LEDs. By blending red, green, and blue into one unified light cone, it delivers incredibly even PAR coverage that hits all the key plant receptors while flooding your tank with crisp, lifelike clarity. Key Features & Benefits Massive 130W Power Output: Drives 12,200 lumens of ultra-bright light, guaranteeing intense depth penetration for aquariums ranging from 24 to 35 inches in length. Integrated Bluetooth App Control: Pairs seamlessly with the My Chihiros app, allowing you to control custom timers, sunrise/sunset cycles, and color channel mixing wirelessly from your smartphone. Gradual Sunrise & Sunset Ramping: Steps lighting levels up and down over set timeframes to emulate natural day cycles and keep livestock safe from sudden light shock. Active Internal Fan Cooling: Constantly monitors and regulates running temperatures, protecting the internal electronics to extend overall operational life. Spliceable Layout Flexibility: Allows advanced hobbyists to seamlessly mount multiple units side-by-side to deliver uniform, edge-to-edge PAR over extra-large display tanks. IP43 Moisture-Resistant Construction: Safeguards internal circuitry against routine water splashes, heavy condensation, and rising humidity. Technical Specifications Please review the specifications below to ensure proper fitment for your aquarium display. Important Installation Note: This hanging pendant listing includes the main light fixture, integrated power cables, and hanging hardware. The over-tank metal suspension bar stand is sold separately. Attribute Specification Brand Chihiros Aquatic Studio Model RGB Vivid2 LED Light (Black 10th Anniversary Edition) Fixture Type Hanging Overhead Pendant LED Light Dimensions (L x W x H) 13.98" x 5.51" x 1.38" (35.5 x 14.0 x 3.5 cm) Power Consumption 130 Watts Luminous Flux 12,200 Lumens LED Count & Type 160 Pieces (High-Density 3-in-1 RGB) Ideal Aquarium Length Single Unit: 24" to 35" (60–90 cm) Cooling System Active Internal Smart Fan Cooling Waterproof Protection Rating IP43 Moisture & Splash Guard Control Connectivity Built-In Bluetooth (My Chihiros App) What's Included 1x Chihiros RGB Vivid2 LED Light Fixture - Black 10th Anniversary Edition 1x Pendant Stainless Steel Hanging Wire Kit 1x Built-In Bluetooth Controller Unit 1x Power Supply Adapter & Cable Unit Frequently Asked Questions 1. How does a single Chihiros RGB Vivid2 pendant cover my tank? A single RGB Vivid2 pendant provides intense PAR and wide beam coverage for aquariums 24 to 35 inches in length (60–90 cm). For tanks 48 inches or longer, installing two units side-by-side will ensure edge-to-edge coverage without shadows. 2. Does the 10th Anniversary Edition include a mounting stand? No. The light includes the suspension hanging cable kit designed to hang from ceiling mounts or over-tank bars. If you need a tank-mounted stand, you can pair it with the Chihiros Light Hanging Bar Stand . 3. Is the internal cooling fan noisy? No. The active internal fan is temperature-controlled and engineered for ultra-quiet operation, automatically ramping up only when needed to protect the 130W LED circuitry from overheating.

The Chihiros TDS Meter is a compact digital water quality tester engineered to deliver fast, highly accurate total dissolved solids readings by measuring electrical conductivity. Essential for RO Water Remineralization: Perfect for checking purified reverse osmosis water after adding mineral salts to reach exact GH/KH targets. Simple One-Touch Operation: Submerge the titanium alloy probe into water for instant, reliable readouts on the clear LCD screen. Compact & Portable Pen Design: Lightweight, pen-style footprint fits comfortably in your pocket or maintenance toolkit for quick spot-checks. Are batteries included with the Chihiros TDS Meter? No. The Chihiros TDS Meter requires 2x LR44 coin cell batteries, which are sold separately. 2. Why is measuring TDS important for freshwater aquariums? TDS measures the overall concentration of dissolved minerals, salts, and organic compounds in your water column. Monitoring TDS prevents mineral build-up over time and ensures you remineralize RO water to the exact safety thresholds required for delicate dwarf shrimp and plants. 3. Does a TDS meter measure pH or GH/KH directly? No. A TDS meter measures total dissolved solids based on electrical conductivity in PPM. listings.commonName: Cryptocoryne Wendtii Sindoor UNS Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Cryptocoryne wendtii 'Sindoor' introduces a striking flush of rare, warm color directly to your midground layout. Developed through targeted lab cultivation from Wendtii Brown, this vibrant cultivar is celebrated for producing intense maroon to blush-pink tones under moderate aquarium lighting and nutrient-rich substrate. As with all crypt plants, it can be sensitive to sudden parameter shifts and strongly objects to being relocated once planted. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Vibrant maroon to pink foliage adds rare, high-contrast color and texture to midground zones. Can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups, where mature plants may produce flowering spathes. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel to supply essential subterranean nutrients. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth and fuller foliage density, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Crypt species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. How do I prepare this tissue culture plant? Rinse away the nutrient gel under lukewarm water to prevent algae or mold blooms, separate the plant mass into smaller portions, and plant directly into substrate using fine-tip pinsettes. 2. How do I help my Cryptocoryne recover if it melts? Trim away dissolving leaves, maintain stable water parameters, and leave the root system undisturbed so it can rebuild new foliage. Cryptocoryne species are heavy root feeders that draw primary nutrition from the substrate rather than the water column.

listings.description: Plant Profile Hydrocotyle Tripartita Mini is a smaller, more compact variation of the regular Hydrocotyle Japan . This versatile favorite is instantly recognizable by its charming, bright green, clover-shaped leaves. If you are looking for an undemanding plant that grows fast, this is your MVP. Depending on your tank size, it can effortlessly transition from a creeping foreground carpet to a bushy midground accent or background filler. Left untrimmed, it will happily take over the tank, but with regular styling, it forms gorgeous, dense cushions of dense greenery. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Show off a distinct, texture-rich look with miniature, bright green clover-shaped leaves. A fast-growing, hardy species that quickly fills out bare spots and adapts to a wide range of tank setups. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use a dry start method or Wabi Kusa setup to give its root system plenty of time to firmly anchor into the substrate before you flood the tank. Use high light and inject pressurized CO2 while frequently trimming new growth to keep the plant low-growing and force a tight carpeting effect. Trim new shoots anywhere along the stem or pull apart dense clumps to split the roots, which actually coaxes the plant into growing even thicker. Keep your aquascaping scissors handy, as its fast growth rate means it can out-compete other plants and overgrow the tank if left untrimmed. listings.description: Plant Profile If you're looking for a broad-leaved specimen plant that brings rich, broad-leaf texture, Lagenandra meeboldii 'Green' is a great freshwater aquarium plant for midground zones. Native to the seasonally flooded swamp beds of India, this Cryptocoryne relative sports lush, broad, heart-shaped leaves in a striking emerald-green hue. This species thrives when anchored into a nutrient-rich substrate where its heavy root system can settle permanently. Given stable water parameters and consistent root feeding, its rosettes mature into a dense, long-lasting focal point that adds substantial structural presence to planted tanks. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Broad heart-shaped emerald foliage provides strong structural presence and leaf contrast in midground zones. Adapts to emersed high-humidity paludarium displays where mature plants can bloom. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, making sure the main crown remains slightly above the substrate surface to prevent rotting. Insert root tab fertilizers directly near the plant base if using inert sand or gravel substrates. Inject pressurized CO2 and maintain moderate lighting to encourage faster leaf output and fuller rosette density. Propagate established plants by carefully separating offshoot plantlets from the subterranean rhizome using sharp aquascaping scissors. If initial leaves melt during acclimation, trim away decaying tissue, maintain stable water parameters, and allow the subterranean root mass to generate fresh submerged leaves. Check our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt for full recovery steps. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How does Lagenandra Meeboldii Green differ from Cryptocoryne species? While closely related to Cryptocoryne and requiring similar substrate care, Lagenandra plants grow systematically outward from a central rhizome without spreading aggressive subterranean runners, making them much easier to manage in controlled midground layouts. 2. Can Lagenandra Meeboldii Green be planted in low-tech aquariums? Yes. Lagenandra Meeboldii Green is highly adaptable and will grow reliably in low-tech planted tanks with moderate light and root tab fertilization, though adding CO2 speeds up root establishment and foliage production. 3. How do I prevent Lagenandra Meeboldii Green from melting after planting? Wash away all nutrient gel completely, plant the roots firmly while keeping the crown exposed, and avoid making drastic water chemistry changes. If melting occurs, trim dissolving leaves and leave the root mass undisturbed so it can send up new aquatic growth.

listings.commonName: Micranthemum Tweediei 'Pearl White' UNS Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Micranthemum Tweediei 'Pearl White' is a unique, lighter-variegated mutation of standard Micranthemum 'Monte Carlo' . It shares the same forgiving nature and crawling growth habit as regular Monte Carlo, but features pale green to creamy white leaf accents that pop against dark aquasoil. If you've ever wanted the plush, rolling-hill carpet of Dwarf Baby Tears without the high-maintenance headache, Pearl White Monte Carlo offers that same low-growing, fine-leaved texture with far more durability. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Light cream and pale-green variegated foliage creates a striking high-contrast foreground carpet. Far easier to cultivate and establish than finicky carpeting species like Dwarf Baby Tears. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers under cool water before parting it out into manageable portions and planting. Divide the tissue culture mat into small clumps and plant them spaced roughly 1 inch apart using fine-tip tweezers. Use a dry start method or Wabi Kusa setup to give its delicate root system plenty of time to firmly anchor into the substrate before you flood the tank. Provide medium to high lighting and inject pressurized CO2 to force the stems to crawl horizontally into a tight carpet (insufficient light causes tall, leggy growth). Maintain stable aquarium parameters and avoid drastic water quality shifts to prevent new growth from melting. Master the basics by learning how to properly grow aquarium carpet plants to ensure your new layout fills in quickly and stays free of algae. How do I plant Pearl White Monte Carlo tissue culture? Wash away the nutrient gel under running water, break the mat into small coin-sized portions, and use fine pinsettes to insert each clump halfway into fine-grained aquasoil spaced 1 inch apart. 2. How do I maintain the unique pale white/variegated leaf color? Maintaining bright lighting alongside balanced micronutrients and CO2 is essential. If light intensity drops too low, the plant will produce more green chlorophyll to compensate, causing it to lose its distinct white variegation. 3. Why is my newly planted Pearl White Monte Carlo floating up? Because tissue culture portions have fine, delicate roots, strong water flow or inquisitive bottom-dwellers can easily pull them up. Planting tiny clumps deep into soil at a 45-degree angle or starting the tank using the Dry Start Method will lock the roots in place before filling.

Cueva Stone is also suitable for non-aquarium use and will work beautifully as a bold accent in terrariums, paludariums, or similar planted enclosures to achieve a rugged, weathered aesthetic. Stones vary in shape, size, and density. Important Notes: This is a natural product and has the potential to alter water parameters slightly. Some even have subtle streaks of rusty orange for added character! Because of this unique coloration, it stands out beautifully when paired with a dark substrate or with lush green or red plants. This stone is also suitable for non-aquarium use and will work beautifully in terrariums, paludariums, or similar planted enclosures to achieve a bright, clean aesthetic. Stones vary in shape, size, and density. Important Notes: This is a natural product and has the potential to alter water parameters slightly. Patagonia Stone is a porous, roughly textured natural rock with a rugged aesthetic similar to lava stone. This stone is also suitable for non-aquarium use and will work beautifully in terrariums, paludariums, or similar planted enclosures to achieve a weathered, rocky look. Species Profile Mixed Caridina Culls are a great choice for hobbyists interested in a mix of different shrimp varieties, colors, and patterns. Caridina Culls are primarily male. These shrimp are non-aggressive and suitable for community tanks that contain peaceful livestock and shrimp-only tanks. These freshwater shrimp adapt quickly and spend most of their time eating algae and biofilm off plants, aquarium glass, substrate, and hardscape. **Note: All livestock orders will come carefully packaged with solid wall Styrofoam insulation and shipped via 1-day shipping only. No extra insulation needs to be added to your cart for your livestock. Key Features & Notes Tank-raised specimens showcasing an assortment of colors, patterns, and line-breeding variations. Assortments consist primarily of male specimens, making them ideal for budget-friendly clean-up crews or display tanks. Relentless clean-up crew that continuously grazes on biofilm and algae. Care Specifications Maintain stable, soft, acidic water chemistry using an active buffering substrate to support sensitive Caridina health. Keep water parameters strictly free of copper-based medications or heavy metals. Supplement their diet with high-quality vegetable-based shrimp pellets, spirulina wafers, and blanched greens for shell health. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to maintain stable parameters to ensure a healthy, thriving colony! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Caridina sp. Common Name(s) Caridina Culls, Mixed Caridina Culls, Mystery Caridina Care Difficulty Intermediate Adult Size 1.25" (3.0 cm) Diet Omnivore / Biofilm & Algae Scavenger Minimum Tank Size 5 Gallons Temperature Range 70°F–75°F (21°C–24°C) pH Range 6.0–6.8 General Hardness (GH) 4–5 dGH Carbonate Hardness (KH) 0–1 dKH Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) 120–140 ppm Lifespan 1–2 Years Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I properly acclimate my new freshwater shrimp to prevent shock? Dwarf shrimp are sensitive to sudden shifts in water parameters and total dissolved solids (TDS). Always drip acclimate new arrivals over 1 to 2 hours before releasing them into your tank. Follow our step-by-step tutorial in 7 Easy Steps to Drip Acclimate Shrimp and Fish for the perfect drip rate setup. 2. What substrate is best for keeping dwarf shrimp healthy? It depends on the species! Neocaridina species thrive in inert substrates like gravel or sand, while Caridina species like Mixed Caridina Culls require active aquasoils that buffer pH down and pull KH near zero. Learn how to select the right foundation for your aquarium shrimp in our Best Substrate for Shrimp Guide . 3. How do I get my colony to start breeding? Because Caridina Culls consist primarily of males, they are intended as clean-up crews and display livestock rather than breeding stock. 4. Are dwarf shrimp easy to care for if I am a beginner? While Neocaridina species are great for beginners, Caridina species require soft-water conditions (low KH, low TDS, and active buffering soil). If you are just starting out, get a complete overview of parameters, diet, and setup requirements in our Freshwater Aquarium Shrimp Care Guide .

Plant Profile Popularly known as the Melon Sword, Echinodorus osiris is a classic South American favorite celebrated for its broad, wavy-edged foliage and subtle golden-red tones. Emerging center leaves unfurl in shades of soft amber, bronze, and warm crimson before maturing into a rich, deep olive green with distinct veining across the rosette. Its sturdy, rounded leaves create a full, lush canopy that functions beautifully as a midground centerpiece in larger aquariums or a focal background anchor in medium setups. Tissue culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab-grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go-to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Notes Classic Melon Sword species producing broad, wavy leaves with rich amber and crimson emerging growth. Hardy rosette plant that delivers full, lush coverage for background or midground centerpiece placement. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by carefully removing the plantlets from the cup and rinsing away all sterile nutrient gel under lukewarm, dechlorinated water before mounting. Plant the roots deeply into your aquarium soil, keeping the central crown resting just above the substrate line to prevent rot. All Echinodorus are heavy root feeders that rely on rich substrate nutrition; placing root tabs near the base supports steady, healthy leaf development. Provide moderate to high lighting; while CO2 injection isn't strictly required, good lighting will enhance its reddish-brown colors. Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf shedding during the initial transition period. Sword plants propagate through side shoots off of their leaves, which can be trimmed and replanted into the substrate. To control the size of your sword plant, you can remove the side shoots and older leaves. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Echinodorus osiris Common Name(s) Melon Sword, Echinodorus Osiris Family Alismataceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Rosette plant / Species (Tissue Culture) Care Difficulty Easy to Moderate Light Requirement Moderate to High CO2 Requirement Not required (Recommended for best red tones) Placement / Usage Midground Centerpiece / Background Accent Height / Size 5–10+ inches Growth Rate Moderate Water Parameters pH 6.5–7.5 Propagation Method Separate new plantlets from the root crown or adventitious shoots Origin South America (Brazil) Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why is Echinodorus osiris commonly referred to as the Melon Sword? The name "Melon Sword" comes from the unique shape and color of its foliage. As young leaves emerge, they display a warm, melon-pink to amber-red blush on broad, rounded leaf blades before maturing into deep olive green. 2. How do I encourage deep reddish-bronze leaves on Echinodorus osiris? Provide moderate-to-high lighting directly over the plant, inject CO2, and supplement the substrate with nutrient-rich root tabs. Higher light intensity combined with sufficient iron ensures newly emerging center leaves display vibrant golden-red hues. 3. How do I prep and plant UNS Tissue Culture Echinodorus osiris? Gently remove the plant mass from the cup and wash away the clear nutrient gel under room-temperature water. Using your fingers, separate the cluster into individual plantlets and anchor their roots deeply into the substrate using pinsettes, ensuring the growth crown remains resting just above the soil line.

Plant Profile Aglaonema Simplex, commonly known as the Malayan Sword, is a resilient Asian tropical aroid featuring upright, lance-shaped deep green foliage. It flourishes under low to moderate lighting, making it a forgiving choice for shaded corners where other humidity-loving plants might struggle to maintain steady growth. Planted into rich, damp substrate, it establishes a clean background profile in humid layouts or along damp paludarium shorelines without demanding aggressive pruning or constant maintenance. Key Features & Notes Upright lanceolate foliage provides a strong vertical green backdrop in shaded setups. Tolerates low light and high air moisture, making it ideal for closed glass setups. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions and planting. Divide the cluster into smaller plantlets and press roots gently into a rich, well-draining soil mix or moist paludarium shoreline bank. Maintain humidity levels above 70% to keep leaf tips healthy and prevent newly transplanted tissue culture plantlets from wilting. Trim older lower leaves near the stem base with sharp shears to promote fresh vertical shoots and maintain good air circulation. Final size and leaf coloration depend entirely on your specific setup conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Aglaonema Simplex are terrestrial plants, and being submerged will result in the death of the plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Aglaonema Simplex Common Name(s) Malayan Sword, Chinese Evergreen Family Araceae Plant Type Terrestrial Tropical Aroid Care Difficulty Easy Light Requirement Low to Moderate (Indirect) Submersion Suitability Emersed / Paludarium Only (Not for full submersion) Placement / Usage Midground, Background, Riparium Banks Height / Size 4"–12"+ (10–30+ cm) Growth Rate Slow Humidity Requirement High (> 70% RH) Propagation Method Stem Cuttings / Root Division Origin Southeast Asia Frequently Asked Questions 1. Can this plant survive in a fully enclosed glass jar or sealed terrarium? Yes. Aglaonema Simplex thrives in sealed or semi-enclosed glass containers where ambient humidity remains high. Ensure the soil is aerated so water does not sit stagnantly around the main root crown. 2. How do I prevent mold from growing on tissue culture plants during transition? Rinse away 100% of the nutrient agar gel before planting, as leftover gel acts as a food source for mold. Introducing springtails and maintaining moderate air movement further keeps fungal growth away. 3. How do I propagate Aglaonema Simplex when it outgrows my tank? Once a stem matures and develops clear root nodes, take a clean cutting just below a node and replant it directly into damp substrate or sphagnum moss under high humidity.

Common Name: Bacopa Purple, Purple Bacopa, Bacopa Salzmannii Purple Bacopa Salzmannii Purple is a beautiful aquatic stem plant that provides a variety of colors. Depending on the environment in which it is grown, Bacopa Salzmannii has the potential to produce deep reddish-violet tones, making it a unique addition to any aquarium. This aquarium plant is relatively undemanding but grows slowly, requiring patience. Like other forms of Bacopa, Bacopa Salzmannii Purple exhibits upright growth with minimal branching. To create a bushy look, regular trimming will be necessary. Bacopa is fantastic for beginners due to its forgiving and hardy nature. Most varieties don't need CO2 injection and this species will do fine in moderate lighting levels. Key Features & Important Notes: Tissue culture plants are grown in vitro from a state of the art laboratory specialized in propagating aquatic plants. They provide the best option for those who want to ensure that absolutely zero unwanted pests are introduced into the aquarium. Remove tissue culture gel before planting. Simply wash the gel away or soak the plant in water and squeeze the gel off with your fingers. Bacopa is extremely hardy aquarium plants and is a great beginner choice. However, its leaves are fragile and should be handled with care. For instructions on how to properly plant tissue culture aquarium plants, click here . CO2 injection and quality aquarium soil will yield better growth. Please research appropriately to ensure your plant thrives. Plant Profile Micranthemum 'Monte Carlo' originates from Argentina and is one of the best carpeting plants in the aquascaping hobby. When provided with ample lighting and nutrients, Monte Carlo forms a remarkably lush green carpet consisting of small, rounded, bright green leaves. It is immensely popular because it beautifully resembles the tight look of Hemianthus Callitrichoides (HC/Dwarf Baby Tears) , but is far more forgiving and significantly easier to cultivate. This variant comes pre-mounted on a heavy-duty stainless steel sheet to weigh it down and prevent pesky floating. Even better, the flexible mesh sheet can be gently bent to accommodate sloped aquascapes, rolling hills, and uneven substrates rather than just flat surfaces, offering excellent support until the plant establishes a deep root system. Key Features & Benefits Micranthemum Monte Carlo is pre-attached to a 3 x 1.25" stainless steel sheet. Produces small, bright green carpets similar to Dwarf Baby Tears (Hemianthus callitrichoides), but with larger leaves and a hardier growth rate. Grows submerged in aquariums or emersed in dry-start setups and Wabi Kusa arrangements. Care & Planting Instructions Place the pre-mounted sheet directly onto your substrate or gently press it down into slopes where you want your carpet to begin. Provide moderate to high lighting paired with consistent CO2 injection to maintain dense, low-growing, compact behavior. Vertical stretching or yellowing leaves typically indicate a lack of proper lighting or a nutrient deficiency, while thinning leaves hint at a lack of CO2. Perform regular trimmings once the plant becomes fully established and happy to ensure the lower layers continue to receive light and oxygen. Refrain from making drastic or sudden changes to your aquarium parameters, as unstable water conditions can contribute to plant melt and rotting.
