Plant Profile Among Anubias species, Anubias Heterophylla Supernova stands out for aquascapers craving architectural height. True to its cosmic name, this impressive aquatic epiphyte stands out from standard varieties like Anubias Barteri or Anubias Nana with green foliage that stretches nearly twice the length of typical leaves. With extra-long, beautifully waved leaf blades and intricate venation, it's one of the largest specimens in the genus, reaching 8 to 16+ inches tall. It serves as a massive focal point for midground and background hardscape in low-tech aquariums, terrariums, and paludariums. Key Features & Benefits Expansive leaf canopy creates natural shading and cover for shy fish, shrimp, and bottom-dwelling species. Thick, durable leaves deter grazing from plant-eating cichlids, snails, and dwarf shrimp. Resilient epiphyte nature handles a wide range of water parameters. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Avoid intense light and ensure good water flow to prevent spot algae on slow‑growing leaves. CO₂ is optional but improves growth speed and leaf density. Learn more about planting these species by reading our guide on How to Plant Epiphyte Aquatic Plants. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. How do I plant Anubias Heterophylla Supernova? Attach the plant directly to driftwood or rocks using aquarium-safe super glue gel, thread, or fishing line. Keep the rhizome above the substrate to prevent rot. 2. Does it require CO2 or high lighting? No. Anubias Heterophylla Supernova is a classic low-light plant that thrives without specialized CO2 equipment. While added CO2 will speed up growth and foliage density, it thrives happily in low-tech aquariums. 3. Is this plant safe for shrimp, snails, and fish? Yes, Anubias Heterophylla Supernova is 100% safe for all freshwater fish, shrimp (including sensitive Caridina and Neocaridina), and snails. Its tough leaves are also resistant to plant-eating fish like cichlids or goldfish.

listings.description: Plant Profile Helanthium Tenellum Micro is a miniature, grass-like plant that looks like a beautiful blend of dwarf hair grass and traditional micro swords. This particular variation boasts a much smaller blueprint than standard Helanthium Tenellum , making it an absolute dream for scaling down nano tanks with a clean, trimmed-down look. As a heavy root feeder, it loves a nutrient-rich environment where it can aggressively send out lateral runners. Given the right care, these runners weave together tightly to blanket your foreground with slender green blades. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Produces short, blade-like leaves suitable for nano aquarium foregrounds. Spreads via underground runners to form a dense carpet. Root-heavy feeder that draws nutrients primarily from the substrate. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions and planting. Use a dry start method or Wabi Kusa setup to give its root system plenty of time to firmly anchor into the substrate before you flood the tank. Plant in high-quality, nutrient-dense aquarium soil or use root tabs, as this species relies heavily on root feeding. Maintain stable aquarium parameters and avoid drastic shifts in water quality to prevent your new grass from melting. Provide medium to high lighting and inject pressurized CO2 to maximize its growth speed and encourage tight, horizontal expansion. Master the basics by learning how to properly grow aquarium carpet plants to ensure your new layout fills in quickly, evenly, and stays free of algae. Plant Profile Rotala Wayanad is a relatively rare, delicate aquatic stem plant native to the Wayanad region of India. It's known for slender, needle-like foliage that stays small, with a greenish-yellow color that creates textural contrast when planted alongside broader green or deep red Rotala varieties. It suits nature aquariums, Dutch-style layouts, and nano planted tanks, and branches readily under good care to form fine-leafed midground or background bushes. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Fine, greenish-yellow foliage adds refined texture to planted aquariums. Compact size works for nano tanks or midground/background bushing in larger setups. Fast vertical growth fills in space and branches into dense hedges. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip the lower inch of foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. * Rotala has fragile leaves, so handle stems with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower leaves. Provide medium-to-high lighting. Pressurized CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilization yield denser branching and enhance its bright yellow-green tones. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and thicken the bush. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Rotala sp. 'Wayanad' Common Name(s) Rotala Wayanad Family Lythraceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Stem Plant Care Difficulty Medium Light Requirement Medium to High CO2 Requirement Medium to High (Recommended for bushy growth) Placement / Usage Midground / Background Bushing / Nano Tank Height / Size 5”+ Growth Rate Fast Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 Propagation Method Cuttings (Cut stem and replant tops) Origin Asia (India) Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I achieve a bushy look with Rotala Wayanad? To encourage Rotala Wayanad to grow into a dense, compact hedge, trim the main stem tops regularly once the plant is established. Each cut point will produce multiple lateral side shoots, doubling the stem density of the bush. 3. How do I transition Rotala Wayanad from emersed to submerged growth? When transitioning from emersed to submerged growth, plant bare stems securely into rich substrate under medium-to-high lighting and keep water parameters stable. As new growth adapts, the plant will shed its broader land leaves and sprout slender, greenish-yellow underwater foliage. Once new shoots develop, trim away old lower growth to encourage dense branching.

Product Overview Aquario Neo Media Soft Quad is a high-performance biological filter media manufactured in South Korea from natural mineral materials fired at high temperatures. Featuring a unique plus-shaped (+ Quad) cross-section, Neo Media Soft Quad increases available surface area for beneficial bacterial strains while naturally lowering pH levels. It ensures optimal flow dynamics and long-lasting biological stability for planted tanks, Caridina shrimp, and South American fish species. Key Features & Benefits Slightly Acidic pH Target (SOFT): Helps lower and stabilize pH levels, creating the ideal water chemistry for planted aquascapes and soft-water livestock. Plus-Shaped (+ Quad) Geometry: Increases outer surface area and creates varied internal flow channels to maximize biological contact and prevent filter media clogging. Multi-Pore Microstructure: Features diverse pore sizes to support diverse strains of nitrifying bacteria, ensuring a resilient and complete nitrogen cycle. 5-Step High-Temperature Manufacturing: Fired at extreme temperatures using natural Korean minerals to guarantee structural durability without crumbling. Ideal for Delicate Livestock: Formulated specifically to support aquatic plants, dwarf shrimp (such as Crystal Red Shrimp), and South American species like Tetras, Discus, and Angelfish. Technical Specifications Precaution: Rinse gently with running water 2–3 times prior to installation. Avoid aggressive washing to prevent excessive mineral dust. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Specification Details Product Line Aquario Neo Media Premium Series Variant / Chemistry SOFT (Acidic pH Effect) Media Shape Quad (+ Cross Shape) Country of Origin Made in South Korea Target Inhabitants Aquatic Plants, Caridina/Neocaridina Shrimp, South American Fish What's Included 1x Pack Aquario Neo Media Soft Quad Biological Filter Media Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why should I choose the Quad shape over standard round filter rings? The Quad (+ cross) shape provides significantly more surface area than traditional smooth cylinder rings. Its structural geometry creates multi-directional water friction, ensuring water passes evenly through the media basket with minimal channel bypass. 2. How does Neo Media Soft affect aquarium pH? Neo Media Soft naturally imparts a mild acidic effect to the water column. While tank objects (like hardscape rocks and substrate) and source water parameters also play a role, it actively helps prevent pH spikes in soft-water setups. 3. How often should I clean or replace Aquario Neo Media? Rinse the media gently in a bucket of drained aquarium water every 3 to 6 months during routine filter maintenance. Because of its durable, high-temperature manufacturing, it does not need frequent replacement and can last for years.

Product Overview Aquario Neo Media Pure Quad is a high-performance, pH-neutral biological filter media manufactured in South Korea from natural mineral materials fired at high temperatures. Featuring a unique plus-shaped (+ Quad) cross-section, Neo Media Pure Quad provides maximum surface area for beneficial bacterial strains without affecting your tank's acidity or alkalinity. It ensures optimal water flow dynamics and long-lasting biological stability for planted aquascapes, shrimp tanks, cichlid setups, and saltwater displays alike. Key Features & Benefits True pH-Neutral Chemistry (PURE): Will not raise or lower your water's pH, ensuring completely stable water parameters across all aquarium setups. Universal Aquarium Compatibility: The ultimate all-around biological media for planted tanks, dwarf shrimp, community fish, African cichlids, and marine reef systems. Technical Specifications Precaution: Rinse gently with running water 2–3 times prior to installation. Avoid aggressive washing to prevent excessive mineral dust. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Why should I choose the Quad shape over standard round filter rings? The Quad (+ cross) shape provides significantly more surface area than traditional smooth cylinder rings. Its structural geometry creates multi-directional water friction, ensuring water passes evenly through the media basket with minimal channel bypass. 2. Will Aquario Neo Media Pure alter my aquarium's pH over time? No, the Pure formula is entirely pH-neutral. It will not raise or lower your pH, allowing your substrate, hardscape, or water source to determine your exact water chemistry naturally. 3. How should I prepare and clean my Aquario Neo Media during maintenance? Rinse the media gently in clean water 2 to 3 times before first use. During routine maintenance, gently swish the media in a bucket of drained aquarium water every 3 to 6 months to clear trapped debris without harming beneficial bacterial colonies.

listings.description: Plant Profile Meet Rotala Rotundifolia Blood Red, aka Rotala Blood Red, an overachiever when it comes to color! It produces some of the deepest, fiery crimson hues you'll find anywhere in the Rotala family, with slender leaves similar in shape to Rotala H'ra . While standard variants need nitrate limitation just to think about turning pink or orange, Blood Red skips the fussy diet and holds onto its intense, saturated red even under moderate nutrient levels. Growing in a clean vertical line, it's a natural centerpiece for midground streets and background hedges in high-tech nature tanks and Dutch-style aquascapes. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Blood-red and ruby foliage delivers unmatched color saturation in midground and background zones. Upright growth habit makes it easy to sculpt into hedges and forests. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. * Rotala leaves are thin and delicate, so handle stems with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide high-intensity lighting and mandatory pressurized CO2 injection; supplemental liquid iron dosing further enhances its signature deep red color and prevents pale growth tips. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or leaf rot. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and thicken the bush. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Rotala rotundifolia 'Blood Red' Common Name(s) Rotala Rotundifolia Blood Red, Rotala Blood Red Family Lythraceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Tissue Culture Stem Plant Care Difficulty Moderate to Advanced Light Requirement High CO2 Requirement Required (Essential for vibrant blood-red color) Placement / Usage Midground / Background Bushing Height / Size 4–8”+ Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 | Temp 72–84°F Propagation Method Herbaceous stem cuttings (Cut stem tops and replant) Origin Southeastern China Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I get my Rotala Blood Red to achieve its deepest coloration? Achieving its maximum blood-red potential requires high light intensity, mandatory pressurized CO2, a nutrient-rich aquarium soil, and regular supplementation of liquid iron and micronutrients. Under insufficient lighting, leaves will fade to a muted orange or green. 3. How do I prepare Rotala Rotundifolia Blood Red UNS Tissue Culture before planting? Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the dense cluster into smaller clumps or individual stems and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

Species Profile Singa Blue Tail Guppies ( Poecilia reticulata ) are an eye-catching domestic fancy strain known for rich, layered blue tones. While males carry the deepest saturation and widest tail spread, females also show subtle cool-toned iridescence, making a small colony look cohesive rather than lopsided. Their flowing delta fins look best framed by dark hardscape and dense green background plants, though their broad tails mean they handle gentle to moderate water movement much better than high-pressure surface flow. Because their active top-feeding habits can lead to sudden leaping sprints, a tight-fitting aquarium lid is strongly recommended. **Note: All livestock orders will come carefully packaged with solid wall Styrofoam insulation and shipped via 1-day shipping only. No extra insulation needs to be added to your cart for your livestock. Key Features & Notes Vivid royal and metallic blue tones throughout the tail fin provide cool-toned contrast against green foliage. Active upper-level swimmer that remains plant-safe and leaves delicate foreground carpets rooted. Peaceful social nature thrives in small groups and integrates smoothly into calm community layouts. Acclimation & Care Instructions Float the sealed transport bag for 15 to 20 minutes to equalize water temperatures before opening. Drip acclimate over 30 to 45 minutes using airline tubing to ease them gently into your tank parameters. Keep water slightly alkaline (pH 7.0 to 8.0) with moderate mineral hardness to support fin integrity and avoid spinal issues. Maintain gentle to moderate filter circulation; heavy surface turbulence will tire out males trailing large caudal fins. Equip your aquarium with a snug-fitting lid; surface-oriented guppies can jump when startled or during morning feeding. Feed a varied diet of high-quality micro pellets, spirulina flakes, and frozen baby brine shrimp once or twice daily. Blue saturation depth and tail fin spread vary naturally between individuals and develop further with age and quality diet. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy livestock! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Poecilia reticulata Common Name(s) Singa Blue Tail Guppy, Blue Tail Guppy Family Poeciliidae Care Difficulty Easy Diet Omnivore (Micro pellets, flakes, baby brine shrimp, daphnia) Plant Safe Yes (Safe with aquatic plants and carpets) Temperament Peaceful upper-to-mid column swimmer Adult Size 1.0"–1.5" (2.5–3.8 cm) Minimum Tank Size 10+ Gallons (Best in groups of 4 to 6+) Water Parameters pH 7.0–8.0 | GH 8–15 | KH 4–10 | 74°F–80°F (23°C–27°C) Freshwater Breeding Yes (Prolific livebearer) Origin South America (Tank-bred domestic strain) Frequently Asked Questions 1. Are Singa Blue Tail Guppies safe to keep with dwarf shrimp? Adult Neocaridina and Caridina shrimp are safe to cohabitate with them. However, guppies are opportunistic omnivores and will readily hunt tiny newborn shrimplets in open water. If you want to sustain a breeding shrimp colony in the same setup, incorporate plenty of dense hiding zones like Java Moss, Christmas Moss, or thick ground cover. 2. What water chemistry is ideal for keeping guppy fins healthy? Fancy guppies require clean water with moderate mineral hardness (GH 8+) and a stable pH between 7.0 and 8.0. Soft, acidic setups tend to erode slime coats, weaken dorsal and tail structure, and lead to fin clamping over time. Regular partial water changes and consistent mineral levels are key to keeping their blue tail patterns clean and vibrant. 3. How often do guppies breed, and how do I raise the fry? Female guppies drop free-swimming fry roughly every 30 days under stable conditions. Adults will naturally hunt newborn fry in open water, so you will want floating plant cover like Salvinia or Water Lettuce to give fry a fighting chance. If you want a complete breakdown on fry care, nutrition, and water management, take a look at our comprehensive Guppy Care Guide . 4. What tank mates should I avoid housing with Singa Blue Tail Guppies? Avoid fin-nipping or boisterous schooling fish like Tiger Barbs, Serpae Tetras, and large cichlids, as the long, colorful tails on male guppies are prime targets. Great community pairings include pygmy Corydoras, Otocinclus, small rasboras, and peaceful clean-up crews like Nerite snails or Amano shrimp.

The Ultum Nature Systems Foresta Plant Holding System is a space-saving solution designed for plant collectors, propagators, and hobbyists looking to create a unique vertical display. Modeled after the UNS 90L aquarium dimensions, this system utilizes a vertical orientation to maximize plant capacity while keeping the lower footprint open for additional scaping, storage, or display. Whether you are showcasing rare specimens or managing large-scale propagation, the Foresta Holding System provides the specialized infrastructure needed to maintain a thriving emersed environment. This system is centered around a rear wall that promotes consistent water and mist circulation, ensuring optimal plant health and nutrient delivery. It accommodates 90 pots at an upright angle, while the lower section provides space for an additional 42 pots, allowing for a maximum capacity of 132 plants. Key Features and Important Notes The UNS Foresta Plant Holding System is engineered for modularity and high-capacity plant management. High-Capacity Vertical Wall: The rear cascading wall holds 90 pots partially emersed. It can also be customized as a living moss wall or adorned with hardscape for a naturalistic look. Adjustable Lower Trays: Includes two lower plant trays (21 pots each) featuring adjustable legs. This provides the flexibility to display plants at various preset heights or customize your propagation setup. Dual UNS Atomizers: Two included electronic misters generate a constant cooling fog to maintain high humidity levels, essential for tropical specimens and emersed growth. Sliding Glass Doors: Two precision-fit sliding doors allow for easy organization and maintenance while sealing in moisture and humidity. Precision Flow Control: Features a ball valve Y-fitting, allowing users to easily control and adjust the water flow across the waterfall wall. Filtration Compatibility: Includes an overflow fitting and is pre-configured for optional bulkhead sets to seamlessly integrate with the UNS Delta 90 Canister Filter . Product Dimensions Overall Dimensions: (LxWxH): 35.43" x 11.81" x 31.5" (90 x 30 x 80cm) Front Panel Height: 4.72" (12cm) Standard Footprint: Compatible with the UNS 90L Aquarium Stand Product Specifications Total Pot Capacity: 132 Units (90 Wall / 42 Base) Water Distribution: Cascading Waterfall Wall with Ball Valve Adjustment Humidity Control: Dual Ultrasonic Atomizers & Sliding Glass Doors Plumbing Requirements: Compatible with standard 1/2" (12/16mm) inflow/outflow pipes or the UNS Delta 90 system . What’s in the Box? 1x UNS Foresta Plant Holding System - 132 2x Plant Holding Trays (21 pots each) 2x UNS Atomizers & Power Supplies 2x Glass Sliding Doors 1x Ball Valve Y-Fitting & Internal Plumbing Components Optional Add-On Equipment UNS Delta 90 Canister Filter and UNS Nimbus Misting Device We recommend running this system with the Delta 90 Canister Filter - Neo Flow pipes are included with the Delta 90 and are required to plumb the holding system. Any standard 1/2" (12/16mm) inflow/outflow pipe combo may also be used. 1 Nimbus Misting Device can power up to 4 individual Plant Holding Systems if doors are kept primarily shut. listings.description: Plant Profile Christmas Moss is here to keep the evergreen aesthetic going all year long. Famous for its deep, bold green color and distinct triangular fronds that resemble tiny evergreen trees, this absolute staple is the ultimate secret weapon for creating a mature, beautifully aged aquascape. It attaches easily to driftwood and other hardscape, fills in gaps naturally, and creates a soft, inviting environment for shrimp and fry! This beginner-friendly moss is low-maintenance, high-impact, and always ready to deck your tank. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Tree-like growth pattern makes it easy to create realistic bonsai trees and lush forest layouts. Hardy and adaptable species that thrives across a wide range of water conditions and experience levels. Dense, shady structure provides crucial shelter and foraging grounds for dwarf shrimp and fry. Care & Planting Instructions Rinse away the nutrient gel thoroughly under lukewarm water, separate into small portions, and tie or glue onto hardscape. Maintain a stable aquarium environment and avoid sudden, drastic changes to your water parameters to keep your moss looking vibrant and healthy. Give the moss an occasional light haircut with sharp aquascaping shears to keep its shape neat, compact, and perfectly balanced. Propagate your patch in seconds by cutting or pulling a small clump apart and anchoring it to a new surface in your tank. Add CO2 injection if you want to accelerate growth and unlock the most intense, eye-popping green coloration possible. Master the prep and planting process by checking out a beginner's guide to tissue culture plants to prevent your delicate new plantlets from melting or floating away. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Vesicularia Montagnei Common Name(s) Christmas Moss, Xmas Moss Family Hypnaceae Plant Type Moss Care Difficulty Easy Light Requirement Low to Medium CO2 Requirement Optional (Accelerates growth & density) Placement / Usage Hardscape Attachment (Wood & Stone), Bonsai Canopy, Foreground Cushion Growth Rate Slow to Moderate Water Parameters pH 6.0–8.0 | Temperature 65°F–78°F (18°C–25°C) Propagation Method Division (Cut, separate, or pull clumps apart) Origin Southeast Asia Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I prepare Christmas Moss tissue culture cups before planting? Remove the plant from the tissue culture cup, gently rinse all nutrient gel off the fronds under running lukewarm water, and divide the mass into smaller portions before anchoring or tying them to your hardscape. 2. How do I keep my Christmas Moss from turning brown or yellow? Christmas Moss prefers clean, moving water and cooler temperatures (under 78°F). Browning usually occurs when organic debris gets trapped inside the dense fronds or when water temperatures run too high. Gently siphoning debris out during regular water changes will keep the inner growth green and healthy. 3. How do I stop moss trimmings from spreading everywhere during maintenance? Always turn off your filter pumps and powerheads before trimming moss. Use sharp curved shears to make clean cuts, and immediately scoop or siphon out floating cuttings so they don't take root in unwanted areas of your aquarium.

Species Profile Lace Double Sword Guppies ( Poecilia reticulata ) are a domestic strain bred for their snakeskin lace body patterning and twin sword extensions on the top and bottom edges of the tail fin. Rather than dragging a heavy delta tail through the water, males stay nimble and active, cruising the upper and mid levels of the tank. They are peaceful community fish that leave plants alone, so your delicate stems and foreground carpet runners stay rooted. Because they spend most of their time feeding near the surface and can easily jump when startled, you will want to keep a tight-fitting lid on the tank. **Note: All livestock orders will come carefully packaged with solid wall Styrofoam insulation and shipped via 1-day shipping only. No extra insulation needs to be added to your cart for your livestock. Key Features & Notes Intricate lace filigree patterning paired with upper and lower swordtail extensions adds detailed contrast to mid-water scapes. Active, agile swimmer that remains plant-safe and leaves delicate foreground carpets rooted. Peaceful social nature thrives in small groups and integrates smoothly into calm community layouts. Acclimation & Care Instructions Float the sealed transport bag for 15 to 20 minutes to equalize water temperatures before opening. Drip acclimate over 30 to 45 minutes using airline tubing to ease them gently into your tank parameters. Keep water slightly alkaline (pH 7.0 to 8.0) with moderate mineral hardness to support strong sword fin rays and prevent fin rot. Maintain gentle to moderate filter circulation; while more agile than heavy delta tails, they still appreciate calm resting pockets. Equip your aquarium with a snug-fitting lid; surface-oriented guppies can jump when startled or during morning feeding. Feed a varied diet of high-quality micro pellets, spirulina flakes, and frozen baby brine shrimp once or twice daily. Lace pattern density and swordtail length develop naturally with age and a balanced, protein-rich diet. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy livestock! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Poecilia reticulata Common Name(s) Lace Double Sword Guppy, Double Swordtail Guppy Family Poeciliidae Care Difficulty Easy Diet Omnivore (Micro pellets, flakes, baby brine shrimp, daphnia) Plant Safe Yes (Safe with aquatic plants and carpets) Temperament Peaceful upper-to-mid column swimmer Adult Size 1.0"–1.5" (2.5–3.8 cm) Minimum Tank Size 10+ Gallons (Best in groups of 4 to 6+) Water Parameters pH 7.0–8.0 | GH 8–15 | KH 4–10 | 74°F–80°F (23°C–27°C) Freshwater Breeding Yes (Prolific livebearer) Origin South America (Tank-bred domestic strain) Frequently Asked Questions 1. Are Lace Double Sword Guppies safe to keep with dwarf shrimp? Adult Neocaridina and Caridina shrimp are safe to cohabitate with them. However, guppies are opportunistic omnivores and will readily hunt tiny newborn shrimplets in open water. If you want to sustain a breeding shrimp colony in the same setup, incorporate plenty of dense hiding zones like Java Moss, Christmas Moss, or thick ground cover. 2. What water chemistry is ideal for keeping guppy fins and sword extensions healthy? Fancy guppies require clean water with moderate mineral hardness (GH 8+) and a stable pH between 7.0 and 8.0. Soft, acidic setups tend to erode slime coats, weaken delicate sword fin rays, and lead to fin clamping over time. Regular partial water changes and consistent mineral levels are key to keeping their lace patterns and sword rays clean and sharp. 3. How often do guppies breed, and how do I raise the fry? Female guppies drop free-swimming fry roughly every 30 days under stable conditions. Adults will naturally hunt newborn fry in open water, so you will want floating plant cover like Salvinia or Water Lettuce to give fry a fighting chance. If you want a complete breakdown on fry care, nutrition, and water management, take a look at our comprehensive Guppy Care Guide . 4. What tank mates should I avoid housing with Lace Double Sword Guppies? Avoid fin-nipping or boisterous schooling fish like Tiger Barbs, Serpae Tetras, and large cichlids, as the long swordtail points on males make tempting targets. Great community pairings include pygmy Corydoras, Otocinclus, small rasboras, and peaceful clean-up crews like Nerite snails or Amano shrimp.

Dragon Stone, also known as Ohko Stone, is one of the most iconic pieces of natural rock in the hobby. Named for its incredible scale-like texture, these natural details and crevices give your hardscape an aged, ancient look that simply cannot be duplicated with artificial decorations. Dragon Stone displays a beautiful array of earthy colors ranging from reds and yellows to deep browns. Its unique clay-like composition makes it relatively brittle compared to other stones, which allows aquatic plants and mosses to easily self-attach to its craggy surface. This natural stone is also suitable for non-aquarium use and will work beautifully as a dramatic accent in terrariums, paludariums, or similar planted enclosures. Pieces from packages will range from 3-10". Be advised that requests for pieces 8" or larger require a minimum purchase of 10 pounds. Notes: Dragon Stone is inert and will not influence water parameters. We recommend rinsing stones thoroughly before use to remove any natural dust or sediment. Stone coloration darkens when wet. Dragon Stone can be easily broken into smaller pieces with a chisel and hammer.

Species Profile Blue Tuxedo Albino Guppies ( Poecilia reticulata ) are a domestic fancy strain selectively bred for soft pastel iridescence and classic tuxedo patterning, accented by true albino pinkish-red eyes. Males display a striking two-tone body with an iridescent blue tuxedo patch contrasting against a creamy peach-and-white base. While their flowing fins look beautiful framed by lush stem plants and dark hardscape, their lightweight build means they prefer gentle surface movement over high-power flow. Because their active top-level feeding can lead to sudden leaping sprints, a tight-fitting aquarium lid is strongly recommended. **Note: All livestock orders will come carefully packaged with solid wall Styrofoam insulation and shipped via 1-day shipping only. No extra insulation needs to be added to your cart for your livestock. Key Features & Notes Two-tone blue tuxedo pattern paired with soft pastel hues and albino red eyes delivers gentle contrast against green foliage. Active upper-level community fish that remains plant-safe and leaves foreground carpeting undisturbed. Peaceful social nature thrives in small groups and integrates smoothly into calm community layouts. Acclimation & Care Instructions Float the sealed transport bag for 15 to 20 minutes to equalize water temperatures before opening. Drip acclimate over 30 to 45 minutes using airline tubing to ease them smoothly into your tank's GH, KH, and pH levels. Maintain slightly alkaline, mineral-rich water (pH 7.0 to 8.0, GH 8+) to maintain strong dorsal support and prevent fin clamp. Provide gentle to moderate filter circulation; heavy surface turbulence will tire out males trailing long tail fins. Equip your aquarium with a snug-fitting lid; surface-oriented guppies can jump when startled or during morning feeding. Feed a varied diet of high-quality micro pellets, spirulina flakes, and frozen baby brine shrimp once or twice daily. Blue shimmer depth and fin length vary naturally between individuals and develop further with age and good nutrition. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy livestock! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Poecilia reticulata Common Name(s) Blue Tuxedo Albino Guppy, Albino Blue Tux Guppy Family Poeciliidae Care Difficulty Easy Diet Omnivore (Micro pellets, flakes, baby brine shrimp, bloodworms) Plant Safe Yes (Safe with aquatic plants and carpets) Temperament Peaceful upper-to-mid column swimmer Adult Size 1.0"–1.5" (2.5–3.8 cm) Minimum Tank Size 10+ Gallons (Best in groups of 4 to 6+) Water Parameters pH 7.0–8.0 | GH 8–15 | KH 4–10 | 74°F–80°F (23°C–27°C) Freshwater Breeding Yes (Prolific livebearer) Origin South America (Tank-bred domestic strain) Frequently Asked Questions 1. Are Blue Tuxedo Albino Guppies safe to keep with dwarf shrimp? Adult Neocaridina and Caridina shrimp are safe to cohabitate with them. However, guppies are curious, opportunistic feeders that will snack on tiny newborn shrimplets if they catch them in open water. If you want to maintain a thriving shrimp colony in the same tank, plant dense thickets of fine moss, subwassertang, and carpeting plants so baby shrimp have reliable cover. 2. Do albino guppy varieties need special care compared to wild-type guppies? Because albino domestic lines have refined genetics, they are slightly more sensitive to poor water conditions and cold water dips. Keep your temperature steady between 74°F and 80°F, provide moderate mineral hardness (GH 8+), and avoid overly soft, acidic setups that can compromise their slime coat and fin health. 3. How often do guppies breed, and how do I raise the fry in a planted scape? Female guppies can drop a new batch of free-swimming fry every 30 days. Adults will opportunistically hunt their own fry in open water, so you will want plenty of surface floaters, moss clumps, or a dedicated nursery setup if you plan to raise them. For full details on water requirements, feeding fry, and colony breeding tips, review our complete Guppy Care Guide . 4. What tank mates should I avoid pairing with Blue Tuxedo Albino Guppies? Avoid fin-nipping or boisterous schooling species like Tiger Barbs, Serpae Tetras, and large cichlids, as they will target the flowing tails of the males. Stick with gentle tank mates such as pygmy Corydoras, Otocinclus, peaceful micro-rasboras, and clean-up crews like Nerite snails or Amano shrimp.

No extra insulation needs to be added to your cart for your livestock. Black Metal Cobra guppies are primarily solid black in color with a unique pattern that runs along its body. Like other guppies, females lack color when compared to males but are equally a great addition to any planted tank or peaceful community aquarium. Guppies typically inhabit the upper areas of the aquarium, but will periodically swim to other ares of the aquarium. Guppies are peaceful and should be kept with other non-aggressive tank mates. They do best in groups with an absolute minimum of 3 . Plant Profile Some plants make you work for good color, but Cryptocoryne spiralis 'Red' just needs proper lighting and time. Originating from the riverbeds of India, this variety is prized for its slender, strap-like leaves that flush with an intense brownish-red hue under proper lighting. Like all crypts, it can be sensitive to changes in water parameters and doesn't like to be moved, but once settled into its new home, it becomes a low-maintenance midground accent that contrasts beautifully against greener plants. Key Features & Benefits Slender brownish-red leaves introduce rich color contrast to midground and background zones. Can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups where it will produce unique flowering spathes. Dense foliage offers valuable shelter for shrimp, fry, and small community fish. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Crypt species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Cryptocoryne spiralis 'Red' Common Name(s) Crypt Spiralis Red Family Araceae Plant Type Rosette / Root Feeder Height 5–10"+ (13–25+ cm) Care Difficulty Easy Light Requirement Low to Medium CO2 Requirement Optional (Recommended to intensify red coloration) Placement / Usage Midground / Background Accent Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Water Parameters pH 6.5–7.5 | Temperature 72°F–82°F (22°C–28°C) Propagation Method Rhizome Division / Runner Offshoots Origin India Frequently Asked Questions Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are my Cryptocoryne Spiralis Red leaves melting away? Transplanting Crypts into new water parameters often triggers a temporary reaction where old leaves dissolve. As long as the root system remains undisturbed in healthy soil, fresh foliage will sprout shortly. Check out our guide on Cryptocoryne melt for step-by-step recovery tips. 2. Can I move my Cryptocoryne to a new spot in the tank later? It is best to leave your Crypt permanently in its original spot. Uprooting an established plant damages its fine root hairs and almost always causes another cycle of leaf melt. 3. Do I need root tabs if I already use liquid fertilizers for my Cryptocoryne? Yes. Because Cryptocoryne plants absorb the vast majority of their nutrients through their roots rather than their leaves, providing nutrient-rich aquasoil or root tabs inside sand or gravel is far more effective than relying on water column liquid fertilizers alone.

Plant Profile Limnophila Aromatica Mini is a compact variant of the classic Rice Paddy Herb native to the tropical wetlands of Southeast Asia. Celebrated for its serrated, star-like whorls of foliage, this mini aquatic stem plant stays more compact and tightly branched than its full-sized relative. Under high-tech aquarium conditions, its narrow leaves transition from bright olive-green into brilliant hues of deep pink, magenta, and ruby red with vibrant purple leaf undersides. When cultivated emersed in open-top aquariums or paludariums, it can produce fragrant foliage and charming pink or purple flowers above the surface. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Foliage displays a spectrum of colors from green to pink, magenta, and red with purple undersides. Compact structure makes it easier to manage in the midground and background. Produces pink or purple blossoms when grown above water. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip lower foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push stems 1–2 inches into soil, spacing them apart for light penetration. Provide moderate-to-high lighting, pressurized CO2 injection, and regular iron dosing to yield maximum pink and red coloration. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid drastic environmental changes to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim main stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the desired height, and replant trimmings into the substrate to encourage dense side branching. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when light cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I get my Limnophila Aromatica Mini to show bright pink and red colors? Providing high light intensity along with pressurized CO2 injection, nutrient-rich soil, and consistent iron supplementation is key to developing its deep magenta, pink, and ruby-red leaf coloration. 3. How do I transition Limnophila Aromatica Mini from emersed to submerged growth? When transitioning from emersed to submerged growth, plant bare stems securely into rich substrate under moderate-to-high lighting and keep water parameters stable. As new growth adapts, the plant will shed its thicker emersed leaves and sprout soft, serrated, colorful submerged foliage. Once new shoots develop, trim away old lower growth to encourage dense branching.

Plant Profile The Red Tiger Lotus ( Nymphaea zenkeri ) is a stunning water lily that brings an instant splash of rich color and bold shape to any tank. What makes it so special is its dramatic foliage: broad, deep crimson-red wavy leaves covered in variegations of orange, bronze, and brown. It offers incredible contrast when set against bright green carpet plants or delicate stem background hedges. If you keep up with regular pruning, it will stay low and produce a full, bushy rosette of submerged leaves right in your midground. But if you let it stretch its legs, it'll send long stems up to the surface to form classic floating lily pads. These floating leaves add a lovely, natural pond vibe to the top of your tank while creating comfortable shade and cover for shy fish below. This listing includes the plant's bulb. Over time, the bulb may soften and melt as it is replaced by established roots Key Features & Benefits Hardy bulb plant that thrives across a wide range of water conditions, making it great for beginners and seasoned aquascapers alike. Vibrant crimson foliage marked with speckled patterns creates a showstopping centerpiece in any aquarium. Versatile growth habit lets you trim it low for a bushy midground look or let it float to create natural surface lily pads. Care & Planting Instructions Gently press the bulb into your substrate about halfway down, leaving the top half exposed to prevent rot; roots will quickly anchor down into the soil. Use fine-tip pinsettes to anchor developing root shoots into aquarium soil or use root tabs, as Tiger Lotus plants are heavy root feeders. Provide moderate to high lighting and clean water conditions; while CO2 is not required, supplying CO2 and iron-rich fertilizer brings out the deepest ruby-red leaf tones. Maintain stable water parameters to give your lotus a smooth transition and prevent initial leaf melting. To control growth, simply trim off long surface runner stems at the base to encourage the plant to produce shorter, compact submerged leaves. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Nymphaea zenkeri Common Name(s) Red Tiger Lotus, Tiger Lotus, Water Lily Family Nymphaeaceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Aquatic Bulb / Tuber Plant Care Difficulty Easy Light Requirement Moderate to High CO2 Requirement Optional / Not Necessary (Enhances color and leaf size) Placement / Usage Midground / Background Centerpiece Height / Size 4–12”+ (Can send floating leaves up to the surface) Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 Propagation Method Tuber Offshoots / Daughter Bulbs (Separate small side bulbs) Origin Africa Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I plant a Red Tiger Lotus bulb correctly? Place the bulb gently on top of your substrate or press it about halfway down so the bottom roots are anchored. Never bury the entire bulb beneath the soil, as burying the top growth point will cause the bulb to suffocate and rot. 2. How do I keep my Tiger Lotus from taking over the water surface? If you prefer a bushy submerged plant rather than surface lily pads, simply clip off any long stem shoots as soon as they start heading toward the surface. Consistently trimming surface runners signals the bulb to focus its energy on growing short, dense leaves underwater. 3. Why are the leaves on my Red Tiger Lotus turning bronze or green? Color intensity depends mostly on light levels and nutrient availability. Under lower light and without supplement dosing, leaves may appear more bronze or muted green. Boosting light intensity and adding iron supplements or root tabs will bring out those brilliant crimson and speckled patterns.

listings.commonName: Cryptocoryne Wendtii Brown Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Give Cryptocoryne wendtii 'Brown' a permanent spot in your substrate, and its dark foliage will reward you with a lush, self-sustaining clump that contrasts beautifully against lighter hardscape and green aquatic plants. Native to the mineral-rich streams of Sri Lanka, this iconic classic sports deep bronze-to-chocolate leaves with textured, slightly dimpled, wavy margins, an earthy focal point that breaks up the monotonous sea of green without adding strict maintenance to your routine. Like all crypts, though, it can be sensitive to sudden parameter shifts and strongly objects to being moved once planted, so choose its home wisely from the start. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Deep bronze and chocolate foliage with wavy margins adds rich earthy contrast. Can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups, periodically producing flowering spathes. Versatile and tolerant of hard water, great for community tanks and cichlid setups alike. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Crypt species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I prepare this tissue culture plant? Rinse away the nutrient gel under lukewarm water to prevent algae or mold blooms, separate the plant mass into smaller portions, and plant directly into substrate using fine-tip pinsettes. 2. How do I help my Cryptocoryne recover if it melts? Trim away dissolving leaves, maintain stable water parameters, and leave the root system undisturbed so it can rebuild new foliage. Check our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt for full recovery steps. 3. Should I use root tabs or liquid fertilizers? Root tabs are best. Cryptocoryne species are heavy root feeders that draw primary nutrition from the substrate rather than the water column.

listings.description: Plant Profile Anubias Mini Coin is an absolute dream for nano enthusiasts, and as the name implies, it is right on the money if you love tiny details. This diminutive variety features exceptionally small, vibrant green leaves that look almost like miniature clovers or the highly sought-after Bucephalandra Mini Coin . It grows slowly under low light, tolerates a wide range of water parameters, and thrives submerged in aquariums or emersed in humid terrariums. Product Overview Dr. Tank #4 BBA Remover is a dissolvable tablet treatment designed to target stubborn black brush algae, also known as black beard algae , on aquarium hardscape and plant leaves. Rather than dosing the entire water column blindly, you dissolve these tablets into a liquid spray for precise spot-treating right where those dark tufts take hold. The active solution weakens the algae cells upon direct contact, causing the black tufts to turn red and break down within 48 hours. Because black beard algae usually points to fluctuating CO2 levels or excess organic waste, this treatment works best alongside regular water changes, filter cleaning, and consistent tank maintenance rather than acting as a permanent standalone fix. Key Features & Notes Dissolves in clean water to create a targeted spot-treatment spray that weakens and breaks down stubborn black beard algae. Compatible with hardy aquatic plants and established bio-filters, though tanks with sensitive plant species require a partial water change right after dosing. Dosing & Usage Instructions Dissolve 1 tablet per 20 mL of clean water in a spray bottle and wait approximately 1 hour for the tablet to break down completely. Turn off your aquarium filter and water pumps for 30 minutes to stop water flow, then spray at least 2 mL of the mixed solution directly onto each affected patch of algae. Perform a 1/3 water change immediately after application if you keep delicate or sensitive aquatic plants, and do not exceed the maximum daily dose of 1 tablet per 13 gallons (50 liters) to protect fish, shrimp, and snails. Watch for the treated algae tufts to turn red within 48 hours as they die off, then manually siphon out the decaying debris during your routine weekly maintenance. Pair your spot treatments with steady CO2 injection, regular substrate vacuuming, and filter cleanings to keep black beard algae from returning. For freshwater ornamental aquarium use only. Keep out of reach of children and pets, and never exceed the recommended daily dosage. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! listings.description: Plant Profile Common Name: Bucephalandra Lamandau, Bucephalandra Lamandau Mini Purple Buce ‘Lamandau’ is a beginner-friendly, low-tech miniature variation within the Bucephalandra family featuring remarkably tiny leaves that display a diverse array of rainbow hues, from deep pink to purple. This variety is highly prized for its pronounced iridescent coloration, possibly ranking as one of the smallest known Bucephalandra variations in the planted tank hobby. Highly versatile, it can be grown submerged or emersed, usually attached to hardscape such as driftwood or rocks rather than being buried in traditional aquarium substrate. Lamandau shines in the foreground of freshwater aquascapes, where it will slowly sprout from thin rhizomes to create a dense, shimmering colony that adds immense detail to nano setups. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Notes Its exceptionally small leaf profile makes it the perfect tool for creating a sense of massive scale in small professional aquascapes. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for aquascapes where other plants might struggle. It is perfectly at home fully submerged in an aquarium or emersed in a humid terrarium. This flexibility makes it a favorite for diverse paludarium builds. Care Tips & Preparation Carefully remove the plantlets from the cup and rinse away the sterile nutrient gel under lukewarm, dechlorinated water before mounting. For instructions on how to properly plant tissue culture aquarium plants, click here . Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood . Never bury the rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting. Unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new aquarium plants. While hardy, CO2 injection and quality water flow will yield much faster and more robust plant growth during the transition phase. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions. Additional Information Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! listings.commonName: Mini Pellia on Stainless Steel Mesh - Small
listings.description: Plant Profile Mini Pellia, also known as Coral Moss, is a highly prized liverwort that has surged in popularity among aquascapers and breeders alike. Unlike traditional stringy mosses, Mini Pellia develops thick, deep green, coral-like lobes that form lush, velvety cushions over hardscape and substrate. We have pre-attached this slow-growing favorite onto a 2" x 2" stainless steel mesh pad so you can easily drop it straight into your tank to establish an instant carpet or ground anchor. It is an exceptional choice for adding fine architectural detail and high-end texture to nano aquascapes, while providing a safe, biofilm-rich grazing habitat for dwarf shrimp and fry. Key Features & Benefits Pre-attached stainless steel pad naturally sinks, establishing a carpet with no floating. Thick, coral-like frond structure adds a unique, high-definition velvety texture that mimics ancient, weathered terrain. Dense, cushiony canopy traps organic matter and fosters beneficial biofilm for shrimp and fry to safely forage. Care & Planting Instructions Place the metal mesh pad directly onto your substrate, or bend and secure it onto rocks and driftwood surfaces. Maintain a stable aquarium environment and keep water temperatures cool (under 78°F / 25.5°C) to prevent stress, browning, or melting. Give the plant an occasional light haircut with sharp aquascaping shears to keep its shape neat, compact, and perfectly balanced. Propagate your patch in seconds by cutting or pulling a small clump apart and anchoring it to a new surface in your tank. Add CO2 injection if you want to accelerate growth and unlock the most intense, eye-popping green coloration possible. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Riccardia chamedryfolia Common Name(s) Mini Pellia, Coral Moss Family Aneuraceae Plant Type Liverwort on Mesh Pad Care Difficulty Easy Light Requirement Low to Medium CO2 Requirement Optional (Recommended for optimal growth & density) Placement / Usage Foreground Carpet, Hardscape Accent, Nano Tank Feature Dimensions 2 x 2 inches (5.1 x 5.1 cm) Growth Rate Slow Water Parameters pH 6.0–8.0 | Temperature 65°F–78°F (18°C–25.5°C) Propagation Method Division (Cut, rip, or pull clumps apart) Origin Southeast Asia Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I keep my Mini Pellia from melting or turning brown? Mini Pellia is sensitive to high temperatures and rapid changes in water chemistry. Avoid placing it in aquariums with water temperatures above 80°F–83°F, as extreme heat will cause rapid melting. Keeping parameters stable and temperature cool ensures vibrant green fronds. 2. How do I use the stainless steel mesh pad in my aquascape? The 2" x 2" stainless steel mesh pad is naturally weighted to sink right out of the box. You can lay it flat on your substrate for an instant carpet, bend the flexible metal around curved rocks or wood, or attach it vertically to glass to start a full green backdrop. 3. How do I stop plant trimmings from spreading everywhere during maintenance? Always turn off your filter pumps and powerheads before trimming Mini Pellia. Use sharp curved shears to make clean cuts, and immediately scoop or siphon out floating cuttings so they don't take root in unwanted areas of your aquarium.

Plant Profile Pearl Moss is a moss-t have for any small-scale setup, proving that good things come in small packages. While most aquarium mosses grow with long, fuzzy fronds, this species is actually a terrestrial moss relative that has adapted beautifully to life underwater. It is famous for its exceptionally tiny, round leaves that stack tightly together, giving the plant a delicate, glistening look reminiscent of miniature strands of green pearls. Because of this diminutive, slow-growing habit, it's a great pick for nano tanks where larger mosses would quickly overwhelm the layout. Key Features & Benefits Pre-attached 3" x 3" stainless steel pad sinks immediately to establish a green carpet. Incredibly small, round leaves stack tightly together to maintain proper scale in nano aquascapes. Unique leaf structure catches light to create a glistening, pearl-like texture and visual depth. Care & Planting Instructions Place the metal mesh pad directly onto your substrate or nestle it firmly into your hardscape layout where it can receive clean water circulation. Maintain a stable aquarium environment and keep temperatures cool (65°F–78°F) to prevent stress, browning, or melting. Give the moss an occasional light haircut with sharp aquascaping shears to keep its shape neat, compact, and perfectly balanced. Propagate your patch in seconds by cutting or pulling a small clump apart and anchoring it to a new surface in your tank. Add CO2 injection if you want to accelerate growth and unlock the most intense, eye-popping green coloration possible. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Plagiomnium cf. affine Common Name(s) Pearl Moss Family Mniaceae Plant Type Moss on Mesh Pad Care Difficulty Easy to Medium Light Requirement Low to Medium CO2 Requirement Optional (Accelerates growth & density) Placement / Usage Foreground Carpet, Nano Hardscape Accent, Crevice Filler Dimensions 3 x 3 inches (7.6 x 7.6 cm) Growth Rate Slow Water Parameters pH 5.0–8.0 | Temperature 65°F–78°F (18°C–25.5°C) Propagation Method Division (Cut, separate, or pull clumps apart) Origin Asia / Europe (Cultivated Combo) Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I keep my Pearl Moss on Stainless Steel from turning brown or yellow? Pearl Moss prefers clean, well-oxygenated water and cooler temperatures (under 78°F). Browning usually occurs when organic debris gets trapped inside the compact leaf strands or when water temperatures run too high. Gently siphoning debris out during regular water changes will keep the inner growth green and healthy. 2. How do I use the stainless steel mesh pad in my aquascape? The 3" x 3" stainless steel mesh pad is naturally weighted to sink right out of the box. You can lay it completely flat on your substrate for an instant carpet, bend the flexible metal around curved rocks or wood, or attach it vertically to glass to form a full moss wall backdrop. 3. How do I stop moss trimmings from spreading everywhere during maintenance? Always turn off your filter pumps and powerheads before trimming moss. Use sharp curved shears to make clean cuts, and immediately scoop or siphon out floating cuttings so they don't take root in unwanted areas of your aquarium.

listings.commonName: Ludwigia Palustris Sphaerocarpa Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Native to damp coastal wetlands from Massachusetts down to eastern Texas, Ludwigia palustris sphaerocarpa grows up to 12 inches tall and stays compact with regular trimming for midground clusters or foreground accents. Its low-growing, horizontally creeping stems topped with dense red and orange crowns set Ludwigia Sphaerocarpa apart from typical stem plants. It adapts smoothly to both fully submerged aquariums and emersed setups in humid terrariums, developing its richest red-orange hues under strong light, pressurized CO2, and steady nutrient dosing. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Horizontal creeping growth forms low, dense crowns of red and orange foliage. Moderate growth rate requires less frequent trimming than fast-growing stem varieties. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small portions or individual stems 1 inch apart into your aquarium soil, choosing an unshaded spot where light reaches the lower leaves. Provide medium to high lighting and pressurized CO2 injection; consistent liquid fertilization rich in iron brings out vibrant red and orange tones. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters to avoid leaf shedding or stem melting during the initial transition period. To propagate, trim main stem tops or creeping side shoots with sharp straight shears and replant the cuttings directly into your aquarium soil. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I prepare Ludwigia Sphaerocarpa Tissue Culture before planting? Rinse the nutrient gel completely off the roots in a bowl of room-temperature water. Once clean, divide the cluster into small clumps or individual stems and insert the roots into your aquarium soil using fine pinsettes. 2. Why is my Ludwigia Sphaerocarpa staying green instead of turning red? Ludwigia Sphaerocarpa reverts to olive-green when shaded by hardscape or taller plants. Planting it in an open, well-lit area with pressurized CO2 and regular iron supplementation brings out its red and orange crown colors. 3. How does Ludwigia Sphaerocarpa grow differently from standard Ludwigia species? Instead of shooting straight upward like Ludwigia repens , this variety grows at a moderate pace with a low, horizontal creeping habit that builds bushy midground mounds when trimmed regularly.

listings.commonName: Pogostemon Helferi Platinum Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Pogostemon Helferi 'Platinum' is an eye-catching, ultra-rare variation of the classic aquatic plant, Pogostemon Helferi (famously known in the hobby as Downoi or "Little Star"). Like the original species, Helferi Platinum features iconic, elongated leaves with uniquely crinkled, ruffled edges that look almost alien in texture. The key difference lies in its extraordinary coloration: while standard Downoi displays bright green foliage, the Platinum mutation offers a luminous, pale cream to nearly white appearance. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Features pale cream to off-white leaves that contrast with dark substrates and green foliage. Crinkled, wavy leaf margins form a compact, textured rosette suitable for foreground or midground placement. Suitable for low-tech, high-tech, and emersed setups. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions and planting. Use a dry start method or Wabi Kusa setup to give its root system plenty of time to firmly anchor into the substrate before you flood the tank. Maintain stable aquarium parameters and avoid drastic shifts in water quality to prevent delicate stems from melting. Provide high lighting and consistent CO2 injection to keep growth compact, low-growing, and vibrant in tone. Prune side shoots or top crowns once established to encourage denser bushiness and propagate new plantlets into bare spots. Master the basics by learning how to properly grow aquarium carpet plants to ensure your new layout fills in quickly, evenly, and stays free of algae. How do I keep the unique cream-white color on Pogostemon Helferi Platinum? Maintaining strong, high-intensity lighting alongside pressurized CO2 injection and precise dosing of macro and micro nutrients is required. Strong light preserves the pale cream-to-platinum hues without causing leaf deterioration. 2. Why is my Pogostemon Helferi Platinum melting after planting? Pogostemon Helferi species are sensitive to sudden changes in water parameters, GH/KH fluctuations, or low CO2 levels. Keeping water chemistry stable and utilizing soft, slightly acidic water prevents tissue melt during the adaptation phase.

Product Overview UNS Plant Food MIN is a moderately concentrated liquid plant fertilizer specially formulated for aquatic plants. Ideal for new aquariums, low-tech setups, or tanks with heavy bioloads, this formula provides balanced nutrition without overloading the water column. When used as directed, UNS Plant Food MIN is safe for most freshwater fish, dwarf shrimp, and snails. Key Benefits & Target Deficiencies Delivers balanced soluble potash, magnesium, and chelated micronutrients for low-tech and newly established tanks. Prevents deficiencies like leaf yellowing, pinholes, and pale growth during acclimation. Invertebrate-safe, no dangerous copper concentrations, safe for shrimp and snails. Promotes steady cellular growth and healthy foliage without fueling algae when paired with active substrates or heavy fish loads. Dosing & Application Instructions Dose 1 pump per 5 gallons of aquarium water every other day. Apply this recommended dosage consistently for low-tech aquariums, Iwagumi layouts, and paludariums to maintain steady water column nutrients. Apply this recommended dosage every other day for newly established tanks with nutrient-rich aquarium soil to support root and leaf development. Perform a weekly thirty to fifty percent water change to maintain clear water and prevent parameter skew over time. Disclaimer: Crystallization may occur when the fertilizer is stored in colder temperatures due to the high concentration of the formula. This does not impact the quality or effectiveness of the product. Allow the product to reach room temperature and gently shake the bottle to help dissolve the crystals. listings.description: Product Overview Aquario Neo Solid No CO2 Plants Tab is a specialized substrate root fertilizer engineered for low-tech planted aquariums running without pressurized carbon injection. Manufactured using advanced slow-release technology, these substrate tabs optimize root zone chemistry and jump-start nutrient-depleted soils, plain gravel, or sand beds without releasing excess nutrients into the water column. Selecting the Right Formula (Neo Plants Tab Guide) Tab Type Key Composition Target Deficiency Symptoms Primary Effect & Ideal Usage Tab 1 Nitrogen, Phosphoric Acid, Potassium Phosphate or Potassium Deficiency: Red leaves turning green, old leaves melting away, or holes forming in old leaves. Comprehensive fertilizer promoting quick growth; ideal when a general nutrient shortage occurs or when growing red plants. Tab K Potassium Potassium Deficiency: Distinct pinholes forming in older foliage or yellowing leaf borders. Promotes photosynthesis; ideal for restoring osmotic balance and plant tissue strength. Tab Fe Iron Iron Deficiency: New leaves lack color, turn white, or red aquatic plants lose rich coloration. Enhances color development; resolves new leaf chlorosis and boosts red plant vibrancy. Tab St. Long Organic Fertilizer Blend Calcium Deficiency: Abnormal, twisted, or stunted new growth tissue. Long-lasting slow-release organic formula; ideal for heavy root feeders, established soils (>1 year), or rescaping. Solid / No CO2 Tab Substrate Carbon & Organic Nutrients Carbon Shortage: Sluggish growth rates in low-tech aquariums without gas injection. Provides substrate-based carbon support; ideal for low-tech setups without pressurized CO2. Dosing & Application Instructions Push tabs deep into the substrate, 1 to 2 inches beneath the surface. Do not use with other root tabs. Aquario Neo Solid works best with substrates that do not already contain high nutrient levels. Keep out of reach of children. Technical Specifications Attribute Specification Product Type Slow-Release Substrate Root Fertilizer Primary Nutrients Delivered Substrate Carbon & Organic Nutrients Form Solid Substrate Tabs Package Quantity 100+ Tabs per Bottle Target Uptake Substrate Root Zone Uptake Lifespan / Duration Approximately 2 Months per Application Substrate Compatibility Active Aquasoil, Sand, Gravel, and Inert Substrates Livestock Safety Fish, Snail, and Dwarf Shrimp Safe When Buried Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why should I use Aquario Neo Solid No CO2 instead of standard root tabs? Low-tech aquariums without pressurized CO2 injection process nutrients at a much slower rate. Aquario Neo Solid No CO2 is uniquely calibrated to provide steady substrate-level carbon and organic nutrition that low-tech root systems can easily absorb without spiking water column chemistry or triggering algae outbreaks. 2. Can Aquario Neo Solid No CO2 trigger algae growth? Because the nutrients are engineered for slow-release burial within the substrate, nutrients remain localized around the plant roots rather than leaching into the open water column, drastically reducing the risk of fueling surface or glass algae. 3. How does Solid No CO2 fit into the rest of the Aquario Neo Plants Tab lineup? Aquario Neo Solid No CO2 supplies essential substrate carbon support and organic nutrients for low-tech tanks without gas injection. In contrast, Tab 1 serves as a broad macro nutrient source, Tab K supplies targeted potassium to fix leaf pinholes, Tab Fe delivers iron to correct pale leaves and boost red coloration, and Tab St. Long provides long-lasting organic nourishment for depleted or aging aquasoil.

Your regulator's electronic solenoid valve is the absolute heart of automated carbon dosing. The electronic solenoid gives you the power to plug your regulator into a standard light timer or smart plug, automating your daily gas cycle. If your current solenoid is buzzing excessively, running dangerously hot, or stuck permanently open or closed, this official UNS Solenoid Replacement lets you swap out the dead electrical coil and restore a safe, automated routine in minutes. listings.commonName: Lagenandra Keralensis Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Lagenandra Keralensis is a rare rhizome species native to the heavily shaded, flooded stream banks of Kerala, India. It produces broad, textured oval leaves with an earthy color blend of rich bronze, deep olive green, and warm brown. Reaching 5 or more inches in height with a slow-growing rosette habit, it serves as a midground accent in planted aquariums and emersed terrariums. While CO2 and moderate lighting help showcase its deepest bronze hues, Lagenandra Keralensis is hardy and adaptable, making it a beginner-friendly and low-tech option for aquascapers seeking a low-maintenance, unique alternative to classic Cryptocoryne species. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Rare bronze, brown, and deep green foliage brings rich earthy color tones and broad leaf texture to midground zones. Hardy, slow-growing rhizome species that builds a sturdy, low-maintenance rosette structure over time. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Plant the roots firmly into your aquarium soil, taking care to keep the central rhizome resting slightly above the substrate surface to prevent rot. As a heavy root feeder, Lagenaria keralensis thrives when provided with root nutrition; placing root tabs directly near the root base in your aquarium soil encourages steady root development and healthier leaf structure. Provide medium lighting and good water circulation; while adaptable in low-tech setups, supplying pressurized CO2 and soft water parameters yields faster growth and richer bronze tones. Keep water parameters stable and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent temporary leaf melting during transition. To propagate, use a sharp blade to divide the rhizome into smaller sections (ensuring each piece has several leaves and healthy roots attached) and replant them back into your aquarium soil. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Lagenandra keralensis Common Name(s) Lagenandra Keralensis Family Araceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Tissue Culture Rhizome Rosette Plant Care Difficulty Easy to Moderate Light Requirement Medium CO2 Requirement Optional / Recommended (Encourages faster growth and deeper bronze hues) Placement / Usage Midground Centerpiece & Transition Zones Height / Size 5”+ (Cup portion size: 2–3”) Growth Rate Slow Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 Propagation Method Rhizome Division / Rosette Separation Origin India (Kerala) Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I plant Lagenandra Keralensis Tissue Culture without causing rhizome rot? After rinsing away the tissue culture gel, insert the root cluster into your aquarium soil using pinsettes, but ensure the central horizontal rhizome remains resting slightly above the soil surface. Burying the rhizome completely can restrict oxygen flow and cause the plant base to rot. 2. Is Lagenandra Keralensis suitable for beginner low-tech aquariums? Yes, Lagenandra Keralensis is a hardy, beginner-friendly species that can easily adapt to low-tech tanks without pressurized CO2. While its growth rate is naturally slow, maintaining stable water chemistry and basic lighting will keep it thriving. 3. How do I prepare Lagenandra Keralensis Tissue Culture before planting? Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the cup into smaller portion clumps and plant them into your aquarium soil using fine pinsettes.
