If you are tired of the standard teardrop-shaped leaves and want to flip the script on your next layout, this epiphyte is ready to help you strike gold with your aquascape. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Circular leaf shape offers a geometric contrast against pointed or lanceolate aquatic plants. Tall stem structure provides impressive verticality, making it an ideal midground anchor or soft background centerpiece. The sterile laboratory environment guarantees your new plant arrives completely free of pests. Care & Planting Instructions Remove the plantlets from the cup and rinse away the sterile nutrient gel under lukewarm, dechlorinated water. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Avoid intense light and ensure good water flow to prevent spot algae on slow‑growing leaves. CO₂ is optional but improves growth and leaf density. Master the prep and planting process by checking out a beginner's guide to tissue culture plants to prevent your delicate new plantlets from melting or floating away. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Anubias barteri var. 'Golden Coin', Anubias barteri var. 'Round' var. nana Common Name(s) Anubias Golden Coin, Anubias Barteri Round Family Araceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Epiphyte (Rhizome) Care Difficulty Easy / Beginner-Friendly Light Requirement Low CO2 Requirement Not Required but Beneficial Placement / Usage Midground, Background Height / Size 4-6 inches Growth Rate Slow Water Parameters pH 6.0 – 7.5 | Temperature 68°F – 82°F (20°C – 28°C) Propagation Method Separate by Rhizome Division Origin West Africa Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I plant Anubias Barteri Round (Golden Coin)? Attach the plant directly to driftwood or rocks using aquarium-safe super glue gel, thread, or fishing line. 2. Does it require CO2 or high lighting? No. It thrives in low lighting without CO2 injection. While adding CO2 speeds up growth, it is completely optional. 3. Is this plant safe for shrimp, snails, and fish? Yes, Anubias is 100% safe for all freshwater fish, shrimp (including sensitive Caridina and Neocaridina), and snails. Its tough leaves are also resistant to plant-eating fish like cichlids or goldfish.

Product Overview Ultum Nature Systems Controbase delivers a porous pumice base substrate engineered to nourish heavy root-feeding species and eliminate anaerobic dead zones beneath planted tank substrate layouts. Laying down this foundational layer prevents root suffocation and stops expensive stem plants from stalling out over time. Packed with slow-releasing Nitrogen, Potassium, Phosphorus, and trace minerals, these porous 6–8mm pumice granules actively drive water circulation, promote oxygen exchange, and build massive beneficial bacteria colonies. Pre-packaged in reusable mesh filter bags, Controbase lets you stack and sculpt dramatic aquascaping slopes before capping the base with your primary layer of aquarium soil, sand, or gravel. Key Features & Benefits Porous pumice granule composition enhances subsurface water circulation and prevents anaerobic soil compaction. Infused base nutrients deliver steady Nitrogen, Potassium, Phosphorus, and trace minerals directly to root zones. Pre-filled mesh filter bags allow clean installation, easy removal, and simple stacking to build substrate elevation. High microporosity provides expansive surface area for beneficial bacteria colonization to strengthen biological filtration. Usage & Application Guidelines Do not wash or rinse Controbase mesh bags before placement. Place the mesh bags as is into the bottom of the empty tank, keeping them away from the front viewing glass. Stack additional bags toward the rear corners to easily sculpt dramatic sloping hills and hardscape elevation. Cover completely with a minimum of two inches of aquarium soil, sand, or gravel to prevent clouding and lock in nutrients. Pair with active aquarium soil for heavily planted setups or cosmetic sand for low-demand, light-planting layouts. Do I need to rinse this aquarium substrate before adding it to my tank? No, you should never wash or open the Controbase mesh bags. Place the mesh bags directly onto the bottom glass as they come out of the package; washing will rinse away essential infused nutrients and disturb the microbial carrier. 2. How much substrate do I need for my aquarium size? For standard base coverage up to 20 gallons, a single 2-liter bag containing 4 mesh pouches is sufficient. For larger displays up to 114 gallons, the 8-liter option with 16 pouches provides enough volume to build base slopes across the entire footprint. 3. How does this substrate affect my water parameters? UNS Controbase slowly releases Nitrogen, Potassium, and Phosphorus directly into the root zone while remaining safely capped beneath your primary substrate bed. When covered properly with at least 2 inches of soil or sand, it prevents parameter spikes in the open water column. 4. Can I combine UNS Controbase with aquarium sand in the same aquascape? Yes, combining Controbase with decorative aquarium sand is an ideal strategy for low-maintenance or cosmetic setups. It allows you to build substrate height and supply root-zone oxygenation without exposing raw soil along the front glass edge.

Plant Profile Aridarum nakamotoi is a rare, slow-growing aquarium plant hailing from the fast-flowing streams and riverbanks of Kalimantan, Borneo. Closely related to Bucephalandra and Aridarum caulescens, this species stands out with its glossy, elongated green leaves that carry distinct wavy margins along each blade. Its modest stature and subtle undulating foliage make it a great choice for adding fine detail to hardscape-heavy zones. Whether you're growing it submerged in an aquarium or emersed in a humid terrarium setup, make sure the rhizome stays completely exposed to open water and air, because burying it in substrate is a fast track to rot. Key Features & Notes Glossy, elongated leaves with undulating wavy margins provide clean texture without overcrowding nearby plants. Adapted to swift-moving currents, producing resilient, clinging roots that grip securely to stones and textured driftwood. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from its pot and clearing all rockwool from the root base . Aridarum is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While hardy and adaptable to basic low-tech tanks, moderate water movement and pressurized CO2 injection will yield faster root establishment and denser foliage. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Plant Profile Homalomena sp. 'Jambi' is a rare tropical aroid native to the rainforest stream basins of Jambi Province on the island of Sumatra, featuring glossy, broad-bladed foliage supported by distinctive ruffled pinkish petioles. A great pick for humid emersed setups, its rich green foliage stands out sharply against lighter stones or surrounding carpets of low mosses along the enclosure floor. Fun fact: the characteristic winged frills along the stems are a specialized wild adaptation designed to channel heavy tropical rainwater directly down toward the root crown while providing structural reinforcement against river currents during flash floods. Key Features & Notes Distinctive ruffled petioles support broad, glossy green leaves that hold up well in high moisture. Integrates cleanly into midground soil pockets or hardscape crevices without aggressive spreading. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Tuck the roots into a loose, airy tropical substrate mix rich in bark, tree fern fiber, and perlite, ensuring the central rhizome remains resting slightly above the soil surface. Provide low to moderate indirect lighting; direct light exposure will scorch the glossy leaves and bleach the green coloration. Maintain ambient humidity above 75% in well-draining soil so root zones stay damp without sitting in stagnant water. Prune older or melting outer leaves near the petiole base using sharp aquascaping shears to stimulate fresh central shoots. Final size and ruffled stem texture depend entirely on your specific setup conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. A practical pick for emersed setups, its deep foliage contrasts cleanly against lighter hardscape like driftwood branches or pale stones, filling in shaded floor pockets or moist terrestrial sections along a paludarium waterline. This slow-grower stays compact and produces anise-scented oils within its crushed leaf stems to naturally deter plant pests. Rooted in loose, damp substrate, it pairs easily with other humidity-loving plants in terrariums without crowding out neighboring mosses or slow growers. Key Features & Notes Sturdy broad tropical foliage creates a bold structural accent on shaded enclosure floors. Thrives in high ambient humidity with strong resistance to common understory leaf melts. Compact clumping growth habit stays manageable without sending invasive runners across your hardscape. Maintain ambient humidity above 70% while ensuring adequate drainage to prevent standing, stagnant water from choking the lower roots. Trim damaged or aging outer leaves close to the petiole base using sharp shears to preserve airflow around the central crown. Plant Profile Homalomena sub-hasei is a rare tropical aroid native to the shaded forest floors of Sumatra that features compact, elongated green leaves covered in unique hair-like textured spikes. It’s a sleeper hit for terrarium plant collectors, thriving in high-humidity setups where its fine leaf texture can be appreciated up close. While it tolerates lower light levels well, keeping roots moist without letting the substrate turn waterlogged is essential for long-term health. It brings a cozy, layered jungle vibe to humid vivariums and paludarium shorelines without trying to take over the whole tank. Key Features & Notes Elongated green foliage with hair-like leaf spikes adds unusual texture to tropical setups. Needs high humidity and damp, aerated substrate for steady leaf production and to prevent edge crisping. Compact terrestrial footprint fits terrarium floors, moist hardscape crevices, and damp paludarium margins. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Press the root system gently into an open, airy tropical substrate mix rich in bark, coconut coir, and perlite along damp terrarium floors or paludarium banks. Maintain humidity levels above 70% while ensuring adequate bottom drainage so roots remain moist rather than submerged in stagnant water. Trim damaged or aging lower leaves near the petiole base with sharp shears to encourage fresh growth and maintain air circulation around the crown. Note that Homalomena species can experience a brief adjustment period after shipping; keep humidity high and avoid overwatering while new roots establish. Plant Profile Josefia intricata is an uncommon aroid native to the riverbanks of Indonesian Borneo, known for long, pendant leaves that hang like miniature Anthurium foliage etched in deep, quilted veins. This is strictly a terrestrial, rock-dwelling plant that lives above the waterline; dropping it underwater in an aquarium will drown the leaves and rot the crown. Strapped into moist rock crevices or perched on high driftwood branches, those drooping blades soften vertical hardscape and contrast sharply against flat carpets of green moss. Key Features & Notes Elongated pendant leaves showcase intricate, textured venation resembling miniature Anthurium foliage. Demands constant high humidity above 80% to keep the cascading leaf tips supple and healthy. Naturally anchors into rock crevices and wood joints across terrariums and paludariums. Care & Planting Instructions Tuck the root base into porous rock fissures, mount it onto driftwood with a small wad of sphagnum moss, or plant it into an airy tropical mix of perlite, tree fern fiber, and bark; avoid compacting heavy, soggy soil around the crown. Provide moderate indirect lighting or filtered shade; intense, direct light will scorch the narrow foliage and fade the rich leaf texture. Maintain humidity above 80% with consistent misting while ensuring the root zone has excellent drainage, as stagnant, waterlogged roots lead to fungal rot. Snip older or declining lower leaves near the base using clean shears to preserve plant vigor and keep airflow moving through the foliage. Josefia intricata are terrestrial plants, and being submerged will result in the death of the plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Plant Profile Labisia sp. 'Jangkang' is an obligate terrestrial plant from the rainforest floor of Borneo, known for wide oval leaves stamped with a distinct turtle-shell pattern of neon veins. Planted strictly above the waterline at the base of spiderwood or wedged into soil pockets between dark stones, that geometric pattern cuts right through solid green carpets in emersed setups. Key Features & Notes Deep oval foliage displays an intricate turtle-shell pattern highlighted by pale neon veins. Adds structural weight to shaded corners in terrariums and paludariums. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by clearing any loose packing media from the roots and rinsing the stem gently in clean water. Tuck the cutting or root base into an airy, chunky tropical substrate blend of perlite, tree fern fiber, and bark; leave enough space for its roots to anchor without compacting wet soil around the stem. Provide partial shade or moderate indirect lighting; direct light will scorch the detailed vein patterns and bleach the rich leaf color. Maintain humidity above 70% in enclosed setups and keep the substrate damp, ensuring excess water drains away freely so the roots never sit in stagnant mud. Trim older or damaged lower leaves near the main stem using clean shears to encourage fresh growth and maintain airflow around the base. Note that you will receive a live cutting with 2 to 4 leaves that will root and establish steadily under stable high humidity. Plant Profile Leea zippeliana sp. Papua is an understory tropical shrub native to the lowland rainforests of New Guinea, featuring large, compound leaves with serrated margins and an intricate, mottled surface texture reminiscent of snake skin. Its patterned foliage provides a visual contrast against lighter driftwood branches and green mosses, filling out midground zones, background corners, or elevated terrestrial shelves in larger tanks. Fun fact: plants in the genus Leea produce distinctive pearl bodies, which are tiny, nutrient-rich spherical sap droplets along the stems and leaf undersides, that in the wild serve as food rewards to recruit ants for natural pest defense. Key Features & Notes Compound serrated foliage displays a distinctive textured pattern reminiscent of snake skin. Grows as an upright branching shrub, making it ideal for background coverage in taller terrariums or vivariums. Thrives alongside tropical mosses and ferns under steady humidity and bright indirect light. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. CAUTION: This plant's sap contains microscopic calcium oxalate crystals, which can cause skin irritation, contact dermatitis, and harm if ingested. Wear gloves when trimming, wash hands immediately after handling, and position the plant safely out of reach of pets and children. Plant the root base into a loose, airy, well-draining tropical substrate mix of coarse bark, pumice, and sphagnum moss; avoid dense soils that stay waterlogged. Allow the top 2 to 3 inches of substrate to dry slightly between thorough waterings, keeping the lower root zone moist while maintaining ambient humidity between 50% and 80%. Maintain warm enclosure temperatures between 68°F and 77°F (20°C–25°C) under bright, indirect lighting; intense direct light will scorch the leaf margins. Prune tall growth tips just above a stem node using clean pruners to encourage bushy lateral branches and keep height in check. Final size and foliar pattern depend entirely on your specific setup conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Plant Profile Schismatoglottis sp. Mamasa is a tropical aroid native to the forest floors of Southeast Asia, featuring elongated foliage marked with silvery-green patterning. While often grouped alongside amphibious species, this is a terrestrial and riparian plant that belongs in high-humidity enclosures rather than fully underwater. Submerging it completely in an aquarium is a fast track to melted leaves, but giving it a moist root zone inside a glass tank is where it actually shines. Its compact footprint makes it a reliable choice for scapers adding structured foliage to terrariums or damp paludarium shorelines. Key Features & Notes Silver and green variegated foliage adds structural contrast to tropical backgrounds and terrarium floors. Riparian growth habit requires high ambient humidity and damp, well-draining substrate rather than full underwater submersion. Compact growth stays manageable without aggressive creeping or crowding out neighboring plants. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Press the roots gently into a loose, airy tropical soil mix or damp moss bank along a paludarium waterline; never submerge the foliage entirely underwater. Maintain ambient humidity above 65% to keep leaf margins from drying out or crisping at the tips. Trim yellowing lower leaves near the base with sharp shears to maintain air circulation around the main stem. Plant Profile Ludwigia Pantanal is one of the most coveted red aquatic stem plants in the entire hobby! Native to the nutrient-rich, soft-water wetlands of the South American Pantanal, this rare variant features supple central stems enveloped by dense whorls of narrow, needle-like foliage. Under high-tech aquarium conditions, its crown radiates an intense gradient of fiery orange, magenta, and saturated ruby-red. Best suited for advanced hobbyists running high-tech setups, it requires high lighting, soft acidic water, rich soil nutrients, and heavy CO2 injection. Key Features & Benefits Intense ruby-red and orange needle whorls deliver unmatched visual prestige in high-tech aquascapes. Fast-growing foliage creates dense, brilliant red hedges when properly pruned. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight (or pot) and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the roots, then strip lower foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. * Ludwigia stems can be fragile, so handle with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide high lighting and pressurized CO2 injection; consistent fertilization with a specialized liquid macro and micro formula (in soft acidic water) yields robust stem growth and prevents bottom leaf yellowing. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or rotting. Trim main stem tops with sharp straight scissors once they reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and thicken the bush. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Verticillata 'Pantanal' from emersed to submerged growth? When transitioning from emersed to submerged growth, plant bare stems securely into rich substrate under high lighting and keep water parameters stable. As new growth adapts, the plant will shed its land foliage and sprout intense purplish-red underwater leaves. Once new shoots develop, trim away old lower growth to encourage dense branching.

Plant Profile Java Fern 'Soft' offers a fresh, elegant twist on a timeless favorite, widely celebrated as one of the most uniquely textured low-light aquarium plants in the hobby. Featuring gently ruffled, flowing green fronds, it softens hardscape layouts while delivering the same bulletproof hardiness as classic Java Fern . Staying compact at 3 to 5 inches in height, it serves as an exceptional focal point or midground accent that sways gracefully in water currents while shrugging off low light, parameter swings, and hungry fish. Key Features & Notes Tough, fibrous foliage easily withstands curious nipping from herbivorous fish like cichlids, goldfish, and large snails. Elegantly ruffled fronds create a soft, flowing visual texture that breaks up heavy hardscape lines in midground arrangements. Exceptional hardiness lets it thrive in non-CO2 tanks and low-light environments. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Java Fern 'Soft' is an epiphytic fern that should be attached to rocks or driftwood with aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as it will rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard setups, gentle water movement and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and broader fronds. Master long-term care and troubleshoot common leaf issues by checking out our Java Fern Care Guide . Final size and foliage pattern depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Microsorum pteropus 'Soft' (syn. Leptochilus pteropus ) Common Name(s) Java Fern Soft, Soft Java Fern Family Polypodiaceae Plant Type Epiphyte (Rhizome Fern) Care Difficulty Beginner / Easy (Low-Tech Compatible) Light Requirement Low to Medium CO2 Requirement Not Required (Beneficial) Placement / Usage Midground, Focal Hardscape Accent, Soft Scape Layouts Height / Size 3"–5" (7.5–13 cm) Growth Rate Slow to Moderate Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 | Temperature 68°F–82°F (20°C–28°C) Propagation Method Rhizome Division & Adventitious Plantlets Origin Indonesia / Cultivated Variety Frequently Asked Questions 1. What makes Java Fern 'Soft' different from standard Java Fern? Java Fern 'Soft' is distinguished by its delicately ruffled, undulating leaf margins. While standard Java Fern has flat, smooth fronds, the 'Soft' cultivar features gentle ripples along the foliage that give it a lighter, more dynamic texture in gentle water flow. 2. Why are there small black spots and tiny leaves growing under my Java Fern 'Soft' leaves? Do not panic; your plant is not diseased! Java Fern reproduces naturally through adventitious plantlets. Small dark bumps (sporangia) form along the undersides of mature leaves, sprouting tiny brown roots and mini green fronds. Once these baby plantlets develop 3–4 leaves, you can gently pop them off the mother leaf and glue them elsewhere in your aquarium. 3. Can I plant Java Fern 'Soft' into substrate? No. Java Fern 'Soft' is an epiphyte that absorbs nutrients directly from the water column through its foliage and fine root network. If you bury its horizontal rhizome beneath aquarium soil, sand, or gravel, the stem will suffocate, rot, and die. Always attach it to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread. 4. Will fish like cichlids or goldfish eat Java Fern 'Soft'? Generally, no. Java Fern leaves are thick, fibrous, and contain bitter-tasting compounds that deter most plant-eating fish. While aggressive diggers might knock it off hardscape if not glued securely, they rarely consume the foliage.

Why would I need the L-Clip Bracket? The stock bracket included with the Z Light Tiny is designed for standard thin-walled nano tanks. The optional L-Clip Bracket expands the clamp width to fit thick glass walls from 12mm up to 20mm, allowing you to use the Z Light as an accent light on large display aquariums.

Plant Profile Sagittaria platyphylla (Delta Arrowhead) is a freshwater aquarium plant native to the southeastern US, from central Texas to Florida and up to southern Illinois. It forms dense colonies in ponds and slow streams; submerged leaves are ribbon‑like, while emergent leaves range from narrow and pointed to oval. During its blooming period, Sagittaria platyphylla can produce small, white, three-petaled flowers, typically flowering from late spring through early autumn. Fairly uncommon in the hobby, it’s an undemanding choice for larger, low‑tech aquariums. Key Features & Benefits Produces broad, strap-like leaves that contrast visually with fine-leaved stem plants. Suitable for low-tech, high-tech, and emersed setups. Thick leaves offer shelter and line-of-sight breaks for shrimp and fish. Care & Planting Instructions Plant in nutrient-dense aquarium soil or insert root tabs near the root base, as this species relies heavily on substrate nutrients. Provide low to moderate lighting for steady submerged growth, or supply stronger lighting to encourage faster runner production. Inject pressurized CO2 to accelerate leaf expansion and density, though CO2 remains completely optional in low-tech setups. Maintain stable aquarium parameters and avoid drastic shifts in water quality to prevent leaf melting. Master the basics by learning how to properly grow aquarium carpet plants and midground foliage to ensure your layout fills in quickly, evenly, and stays free of algae. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Due to its taller height (8–16 inches) and broad, strap-like leaves, Sagittaria Platyphylla works best as a midground accent in large aquariums or a background plant in small-to-medium nano tanks. 2. Providing a nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs is much more important for its long-term health. 3. How does Sagittaria Platyphylla propagate? Sagittaria Platyphylla propagates by sending out thick underground runners that pop up as new daughter plantlets. Once the daughter plants develop a few leaves and roots, simply snip the connecting runner and replant them elsewhere.

Plant Profile Ophiopogon pusillus, widely recognized by scapers as Dwarf Mondo Grass, is an evergreen perennial native to East Asia that forms dense, fountain-like tufts of slender, arching dark green foliage. Its fine grass-like blades create an immediate visual contrast against pale driftwood branches, light river stones, or flat sheet mosses along the enclosure floors and moist paludarium banks. Fun fact: despite its convincing ornamental grass disguise, it actually belongs to the asparagus family (Asparagaceae). Key Features & Notes Arching, dark green ribbon foliage forms tidy, fountain-like tufts that add grassy scale. Strictly terrestrial grower that will deteriorate and rot if planted underwater in an aquarium. Pairs naturally as a clumping floor accent with other humidity-loving plants in humid setups. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Divide the cluster into smaller plugs if desired, and press the fibrous roots into a loose, well-draining tropical soil blend of bark, pumice, and perlite, keeping the crown level with the soil line. Provide partial shade or moderate indirect lighting; avoid harsh direct light, which will scorch the narrow blades and bleach their deep green color. Maintain steady ambient humidity while keeping the root zone evenly moist, ensuring excess water drains away freely so the rhizome base never sits in stagnant mud. Snip aging or yellowed outer blades near the soil line using sharp scissors to keep clumps compact and clean. Ophiopogon pusillus are terrestrial plants, and being submerged will result in the death of the plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. No. Even though fish stores often sell Mondo Grass submerged in display tanks, it is strictly a terrestrial perennial and will slowly drown and rot if kept underwater. 2. How do you propagate Ophiopogon pusillus in a terrarium? Lift an established clump and divide the root mass and rhizome into smaller rooted sections using clean shears, then replant each division into moist, aerated substrate. 3. Why are the leaf tips turning yellow or brown on my Mondo Grass? Brown or yellowing tips generally point to waterlogged substrate in a poorly drained drainage layer, exposure to intense direct lighting, or dry air drafts.

Plant Profile Common Name: Homalomena Broad Sekadau South Homalomena sp. ‘Broad Sekadau South’ is a rare, low-tech aquarium plant belonging to the same family as Bucephalandra and featuring uniquely broad, structural foliage. This variety is highly sought after for its unique appearance and adaptability, performing exceptionally well in low to moderate lighting environments. Highly versatile, it can be grown submerged or emersed, usually attached to hardscape such as driftwood or rocks rather than being buried in traditional aquarium substrate. It's a great pick for the midground or background of freshwater aquascapes, where its larger profile provides a lush, broad presence. Key Features & Notes As a close relative of Bucephalandra, this Homalomena variant offers a similar ease of care but with a much bolder, more substantial leaf presence. Reaching heights of 4" or more, it is an excellent tool for filling vertical space and creating "shrub-like" details among rocks and wood. Like Anubias, it is a slow grower that thrives in shaded areas. Excessive light should be avoided to prevent algae from forming on its broad leaf surfaces. It is a fantastic candidate for high-humidity ripariums, paludariums, and terrariums, where it can be grown emersed as a striking marginal plant. Care Tips & Preparation As an Aridarum-type epiphytic plant it should be attached to rocks or driftwood . Never bury the rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Carefully remove the plant from its pot and clear away all rockwool from the roots. For a deep dive on prepping potted plants, click here . Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting. Unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance, CO2 injection will yield much faster growth. We recommend researching your specific water chemistry to ensure your plant thrives. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions. Please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Please research appropriately to ensure your plant thrives. Additional Information Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Plant Profile Homalomena sp. 'Sekadau South' is a rare and striking aquarium plant native to Borneo, highly appreciated for its unique combination of deep green foliage and vivid red stems. This species features elliptic, elongated leaves that provide a bold architectural look, making it a standout focal point in any aquatic layout. Highly versatile, it can be grown submerged or emersed, usually attached to hardscape such as driftwood or rocks, similar to the care requirements of Bucephalandra and Anubias. It's a great pick for the midground or background of freshwater aquascapes, where its moderate growth rate and height of 4+ inches add significant depth within a planted tank. Key Features & Notes Contrasting reddish-pink petioles support deep green foliage, giving it a two-tone appearance that stands out along hardscape joints. The broader, lance-shaped leaves provide structural variety next to narrow-leaf epiphytes or fine carpeting plants. Develops a strong clinging root system suited for moderate to high water movement in river-style layouts. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for planted tanks where other plants might struggle. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Homalomena is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant can adapt to standard setups, moderate lighting and pressurized CO2 injection will yield noticeably faster leaf development and richer stem color. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I mount Homalomena Narrow Sekadau South to hardscape? After gently removing the rockwool and rinsing the root base, attach the plant to driftwood or stone using cyanoacrylate aquarium glue or cotton thread. Make sure the binding holds the plant firmly without pinching the main stem or rhizome. 2. Why is my Homalomena dropping leaves after being planted? Homalomena often sheds older emersed leaves when adjusting to submerged aquarium conditions or shifts in water hardness. Keep water flow steady and parameters consistent; as long as the rhizome remains firm, new submerged leaves adapted to your water will replace them. 3. Can I plant Homalomena Narrow Sekadau South in substrate? You can let the roots dig down into soil or gravel to feed, but the central rhizome must sit fully exposed above the substrate line. Covering the rhizome cuts off oxygen flow and leads to rot.

Plant Profile Homalomena ‘Broad Cuneate Red Stem’ is a flowering aquarium plant belonging to the same family as Bucephalandra and originating from the waters of Borneo. This variety is highly prized for its broad, spade-shaped leaves and striking deep red stems that provide a bold color contrast against typical green foliage. Highly versatile, it can be grown submerged or emersed, usually attached to hardscape such as driftwood or rocks rather than being buried in traditional aquarium substrate. It's a great pick for the midground or background of freshwater aquascapes, where it will slowly sprout from thick rhizomes to create a lush, architectural presence within a planted tank. Key Features & Notes The vibrant red petioles (stems) offer a distinct visual pop that remains vivid even under moderate lighting conditions. Unlike the smaller leaves of most Bucephalandra, this Homalomena provides larger, broad leaves that help fill vertical space in your aquascape. Similar to Anubias, it is a hardy plant that thrives in areas with consistent water flow and is very resistant to herbivorous fish. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Homalomena is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood with aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as it will rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy once established, CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and stronger stem coloration. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Homalomena 'Broad Cuneate Red Stem' can be grown fully submerged underwater or emersed in high-humidity setups like paludariums, terrariums, and vivariums. 3. How do I prevent Homalomena rhizome rot? Never bury the rhizome under sand or aquasoil. Attach the roots to hardscape using aquarium-safe glue or thread, leaving the thick main rhizome fully exposed to clean water flow.

listings.commonName: Adiantum Sp. and Moss on Driftwood
listings.description: Plant Profile Adiantum sp., the classic Maidenhair Fern, comes pre-attached to mossy driftwood so you can place it straight into your hardscape. Its fan-shaped, light green leaflets sit on wiry black stems, softening heavy rockwork and contrasting cleanly against dark wood. In the wild, those paper-thin leaves are naturally water-repellent, shedding droplets instantly so the foliage never stays waterlogged. Set it where its roots stay damp under soft indirect light, and it easily holds its own in an emersed setup. Key Features & Notes Pre-attached to weathered driftwood with living moss for immediate placement without glue or thread. Fan-shaped light green leaflets on wiry dark stems soften hard edges in terrariums. Thrives in high humidity along damp ledges and splash zones favored by paludariums. Care & Planting Instructions Set the driftwood base directly onto damp substrate or wedge it securely into hardscape joints where the moss stays in contact with moisture; never bury the fern's crown or rhizome in dense, muddy substrate. Provide medium indirect light or filtered shade; direct rays will scorch the paper-thin leaflets and turn them brittle within hours. Maintain humidity above 75% and keep the wood and moss consistently damp, but avoid letting the fern's crown sit submerged in deep, stagnant water. Snip yellowed or dried fronds near the wood surface with clean shears to encourage fresh fiddleheads to uncoil from the rhizome. Final size, wood shape, and moss coverage depend entirely on your specific setup conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual pieces may vary. Adiantum species are terrestrial plants, and being submerged will result in the death of the plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Can Adiantum on Driftwood be submerged in an aquarium? No. While the moss might hold on underwater, Maidenhair Ferns are strictly terrestrial plants. Submerging the fronds underwater will suffocate the plant and cause the foliage to rot away. 2. What should I do if the Maidenhair Fern fronds dry out or turn crispy? Maidenhair leaflets shrivel quickly if humidity drops or the roots dry out. Mist thoroughly, make sure the moss on the wood stays damp, and clip off dry fronds down at the rhizome so new fiddleheads can sprout. 3. Can this pre-mounted driftwood be used in a riparium setup? Yes, provided only the bottom of the wood rests in the water to draw moisture upward, keeping the fern's crown and lacy fronds elevated completely in the open air.

listings.commonName: Rotala Rotundifolia Blood Red Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Meet Rotala Rotundifolia Blood Red, aka Rotala Blood Red, an overachiever when it comes to color! It produces some of the deepest, fiery crimson hues you'll find anywhere in the Rotala family, with slender leaves similar in shape to Rotala H'ra . While standard variants need nitrate limitation just to think about turning pink or orange, Blood Red skips the fussy diet and holds onto its intense, saturated red even under moderate nutrient levels. Growing in a clean vertical line, it's a natural centerpiece for midground streets and background hedges in high-tech nature tanks and Dutch-style aquascapes. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Blood-red and ruby foliage delivers unmatched color saturation in midground and background zones. Upright growth habit makes it easy to sculpt into hedges and forests. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. * Rotala leaves are thin and delicate, so handle stems with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide high-intensity lighting and mandatory pressurized CO2 injection; supplemental liquid iron dosing further enhances its signature deep red color and prevents pale growth tips. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or leaf rot. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and thicken the bush. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I get my Rotala Blood Red to achieve its deepest coloration? Achieving its maximum blood-red potential requires high light intensity, mandatory pressurized CO2, a nutrient-rich aquarium soil, and regular supplementation of liquid iron and micronutrients. Under insufficient lighting, leaves will fade to a muted orange or green. 3. How do I prepare Rotala Rotundifolia Blood Red Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture before planting? Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the dense cluster into smaller clumps or individual stems and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

Featuring 3 stacked shallow all-in-one tanks, this system allows for easy access and unrestricted plant growth, all housed in a durable aluminum stand that saves space without compromising stability. Each tank has its own filtration system and adjustable flow control, so you can tailor water circulation to your plants' needs. Its versatile design seamlessly integrates into any setup. Key Features Durable Aluminum Cabinet – Built to last with a sleek, modern design. Plant Profile Dendroconche annabellae, historically classified as Lecanopteris annabellae, is an uncommon epiphytic fern native to Papua New Guinea that creeps along vertical hardscape and branch forks using thick rhizomes wrapped in dark brown scales. The sterile leaves (which don’t produce spores) are small, round, and stay close to the surface they grow on, like tree trunks. The fertile leaves (which produce spores) start with a similar round base but then grow into long, thin, tail-like shapes that stick out and carry the spore-producing structures. Key Features & Notes Creeping rhizomes clothed in dark brown scales produce both rounded clasping leaves and elongated fertile fronds. Naturally epiphytic habit thrives when secured to damp wood or rock rather than planted in heavy dirt. Adds natural canopy detail when grouped with climbing mosses and ferns. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Mount the scaly rhizome directly onto rough driftwood, cork bark, or porous rock using cotton thread or plant glue with a thin pad of damp sphagnum moss beneath the roots; never bury the creeping rhizome under soil, as burying it will suffocate the plant and cause it to rot. Provide moderate, filtered indirect lighting; avoid intense, concentrated light that can scorch the delicate sterile shield leaves. Maintain humidity above 75% with regular misting, keeping the mounting media evenly moist while ensuring plenty of air circulation so moisture does not sit stagnant. Propagate by dividing mature creeping rhizomes with clean shears, ensuring each division retains viable roots and an active growing tip. listings.description: Plant Profile Bucephalandra ‘Sanggau Mini Wavy’ is a low-tech, sought-after aquarium plant known for its compact size and distinctive, petite wavy-edged leaves. This variety’s small stature allows for immense versatility, seamlessly integrating into complex hardscape designs to add a sense of refined scale. Highly versatile, it can be grown submerged or emersed, usually attached to hardscape such as driftwood or rocks rather than being buried in traditional aquarium substrate. It is an exquisite choice for the foreground of freshwater aquascapes, where it will slowly sprout from thin rhizomes to create a dense, detailed colony within a planted tank. Tissue culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab-grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go-to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Notes The "Mini Wavy" foliage provides a high level of detail, making it perfect for recreating the look of a natural riverbank on your hardscape. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for planted tanks where other plants might struggle. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by carefully removing the plantlets from the cup and rinsing away all sterile nutrient gel under lukewarm, dechlorinated water before mounting. Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard low-light aquarium plant setups, CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and a smoother tissue culture transition. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Why is my tissue culture Bucephalandra melting after planting? Tissue culture plants undergo an acclimation phase when transitioning to underwater conditions. Can tissue culture Bucephalandra be planted in substrate? Yes, you can push the roots into substrate or gravel to help anchor the plantlet. listings.commonName: Rotala Rotundifolia Manipurensis Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Rotala Manipurensis is a rare aquatic stem plant native to Southeast Asia and northeastern India. Its leaves narrow into fine, feather-like whorls that blush orange, salmon, and bright pink when grown under high-tech aquarium conditions. Once established, it grows quickly and fills in with dense, layered stems, working well as a midground or background species that adds structural depth, soft movement, and warm color contrast against greener aquascape plants. It's a good pick for aquascapers looking to break up an all-green layout without reaching for the more common red Rotala varieties. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Foliage shifts into striking orange and pink tones under high-intensity lighting and tuned fertilization. Fast vertical growth fills in space and branches into dense hedges with routine pruning. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. * Rotala Manipurensis has fragile leaves, so handle stems with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower leaves. Provide high-intensity lighting and pressurized CO2 injection. Adding liquid iron supplementation is key to developing vivid orange and pink coloration. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters (72–84°F) and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the water surface to keep growth compact, and replant trimmings directly into soil to propagate. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I get my Rotala Manipurensis to display bright orange and pink colors? To bring out its signature orange and pink leaf tones, provide high light intensity, pressurized CO2 injection, quality aquarium soil, and regular iron dosing. Lower light levels will cause the plant to remain predominantly olive-green. 3. How do I prepare Rotala Manipurensis Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture before planting? Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the dense cluster into smaller clumps or individual stem bundles and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

listings.description: Plant Profile Thick vertical stems lined with narrow green leaves give Hygrophila Pogonocalyx Hayata a clean, bushy look that fills in midground and background zones quickly. This fast-growing stem plant originates from the tropical riverbanks and marshlands of Taiwan, and its appetite for water-column nutrients makes it a great natural helper for soaking up excess nitrates and keeping algae at bay! Growing reliably under low to moderate lighting without strictly requiring CO2, it serves as a beginner-friendly and low-tech choice for aquascapers adding fast-growing greenery to their layout. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Sturdy vertical stems and narrow green foliage quickly build dense midground and background hedges. Fast growth rate helps absorb excess water column nutrients to support overall tank stability. Adapts smoothly to fully submerged aquariums or emersed growth in humid terrariums. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant individual stems or small clumps 1 inch apart into your aquarium soil, ensuring the root bases are anchored securely. Provide low to moderate lighting; while CO2 injection is optional, supplying steady light and liquid nutrients encourages thicker stem growth and fuller side branching. Maintain stable water temperatures between 72°F and 82°F (22°C to 28°C) to prevent lower leaf shedding during transition. To propagate, trim main stem tops with sharp straight shears and replant the cuttings directly into your aquarium soil to expand the background group. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I prepare Hygrophila Pogonocalyx Hayata Tissue Culture before planting? Rinse the nutrient gel completely off the roots in a bowl of room-temperature water. Once clean, divide the cluster into small clumps or individual stems and insert the roots into your aquarium soil using fine pinsettes. 2. Is Hygrophila Pogonocalyx Hayata suitable for low-tech aquariums? Yes, Hygrophila Pogonocalyx Hayata is a hardy, adaptable stem plant that thrives in low-tech setups under moderate lighting without CO2 injection. 3. How do I keep Hygrophila Pogonocalyx Hayata bushy in the background? Pruning the stem tops regularly encourages side shoots to sprout from lower leaf nodes. Replanting those trimmed stem tops back into your aquarium soil alongside the parent stems rapidly builds a thick, bushy hedge.

Manzanita is a branchy type of driftwood that’s perfect for adding fine detail to your aquascape. The pieces are sandblasted to show off their natural twists and textures, and they’re denser and tougher than Spiderwood, so they hold up well over time. It pairs beautifully with aquatic mosses and epiphytic plants in planted tanks, giving your scape a sculptural, natural look. Go ahead and branch out your design! Product Features & Benefits Manzanita’s naturally thin and twisting limbs allow you to create intricate tree-top effects or complex root systems. Unlike the heavier leaching of other woods, Manzanita is much lighter in tannin content. These branches are just as popular in terrariums and paludariums as they are in planted aquarium hardscapes, providing sturdy climbing structures that won't rot quickly in high humidity. The smooth, pale surface serves as a beautiful high-contrast anchor for green mosses and epiphytes like Anubias. Size Specifications Photos provided are a representation of what you will receive. This is a natural aquarium hardscape product; please expect variations in shape, weight, and character. Extra Small: 6-9 inches Small: 10-16 inches Medium: 16-20 inches Large: 20 -36 inches Extra Large: 36+ inches Preparation & Care Driftwood is a natural product and requires a bit of prep before it’s ready for prime time. Rinse: Thoroughly rinse the piece to remove any dust or debris from transit. The Floating Phase: Depending on the size, Manzanita will float a little initially. We recommend soaking it thoroughly or boiling it. A large stone or heavy decor may be placed on top to ensure a non-waterlogged piece of wood stays submerged. Tannin Management: While low in tannins, a quick boil can help fast-track the sinking process and ensure your water stays crystal clear. You can also reduce this effect through consistent water changes or through the addition of Aquario Neo Carbon Bag Important note: We recommend rinsing wood thoroughly before adding it to an established aquarium. If you prefer, you may also boil the wood for at least 1–2 hours to help release tannins.

listings.description: Plant Profile Bacopa Monnieri 'Platinum', commonly known as Variegated Moneywort or Water Hyssop, is a rare and striking variegated cultivar of the classic hobby staple. Characterized by thick, rigid vertical stems lined with opposite pairs of rounded, fleshy leaves, this variety displays a marble-like pattern of crisp mint green and pale cream-white tones. Exceptionally hardy and adaptable, it easily reaches 4 to 12 inches in height. Perfect for beginners and experienced aquascapers alike, Bacopa Platinum serves as a low-maintenance, high-contrast accent in midground and background zones. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Rare variegated foliage displays a beautiful, high-contrast mix of cream-white and mint-green tones. Thick, upright columnar stems form structured vertical accents in midground and background zones. Hardy and adaptable species ideal for beginners; can be grown submerged or emersed in paludariums, where it produces tiny white flowers. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. * Bacopa leaves are fragile, so handle stems with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide moderate to high lighting to ensure light reaches the lower stems and prevents leaf shedding; while CO2 is not strictly required, supplying pressurized CO2 injection and regular fertilization promotes thicker stems and bolder cream variegation. Maintain clean water conditions and stable water parameters to encourage steady root development. To propagate, simply cut main stems with sharp straight shears and replant trimmings directly into substrate; cut stems will readily anchor and sprout new growth. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I maintain strong cream variegation on Bacopa Platinum? Variegated plants like Bacopa Monnieri 'Platinum' require moderate-to-high lighting to maintain their pale cream-and-green leaf patterns. Under low lighting, stems may grow leggy and leaf variegation may become less pronounced. 3. Can Bacopa Monnieri Platinum be grown out of water? Yes! Bacopa Monnieri Platinum transitions very easily to emersed growth in terrariums, paludariums, or open-top setups, where it forms creeping terrestrial mats and produces delicate white-to-pink flowers.

Common name: Hygrophila Pinnatifida 'UK' This variant of Hygrophila Pinnatifida originates from the Uttara Kannada district in Karnataka, India—hence the abbreviation “UK,” which refers to its region of collection, not the United Kingdom. The UK variety displays a more intense red coloration and noticeably deeper, more defined lobes on its leaves. With its unique foliage and enhanced coloration, Hygrophila Pinnatifida 'Uttara Kannada' is an excellent choice for hobbyists looking to add depth and contrast to their planted aquariums. Care does not differ greatly from the original form. This plant does best under high lighting with Co2 and fertilization. It has been reported to be susceptible to potassium deficiency, distinguished by small holes in the older leaves. Plant Profile Anubias Emerald Bloom is an easy-care aquarium plant with broad, heart-shaped emerald leaves that add bold texture to midground and background zones in planted tanks. Growing 5–8+ inches tall, it excels at filling awkward gaps or creating a dense canopy for sheltering shy fish or shrimp. Extremely resilient and simple to maintain, it adapts smoothly to low-tech submerged setups or humid emersed terrariums without demanding high lighting or CO₂ injection. Attach it to rock or driftwood, keeping the rhizome above the substrate to prevent rot. Key Features & Benefits Large, heart-shaped emerald green leaves easily fill substantial gaps. Tough, compact leaves naturally resist grazing from plant-nibbling fish and active dwarf shrimp. Forgiving growth adapts to low-tech environments without requiring specialized lighting or CO₂ injection. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Avoid intense light and ensure good water flow to prevent spot algae on slow‑growing leaves. CO₂ is optional but improves growth and leaf density. Learn more about planting these species by reading our guide on How to Plant Epiphyte Aquatic Plants. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! What is the growth pattern of Anubias Emerald Bloom? Unlike varieties that produce long, creeping rhizomes with widely spaced leaves, Emerald Bloom grows in an exceptionally tight, compact habit, producing dense clusters of rich emerald foliage that resemble a flowering rosette. 2. Does Anubias Emerald Bloom actually flower underwater? Yes! Like other members of the Araceae family, mature Anubias Emerald Bloom specimens regularly produce creamy-white spadix flowers (spathes) completely submerged beneath the surface when tank conditions remain clean and stable. 3. How should I trim and maintain Anubias Emerald Bloom as it clusters? Due to its dense leaf clusters, trim away older, outer leaves at the base of the petiole using sharp aquascaping scissors to encourage internal water flow and prevent organic debris from settling within the center of the crown.

Cholla Driftwood is the dried husk of the Cholla cactus and a go‑to for shrimp tanks. It provides cozy cover and grows tasty biofilm that shrimp and fry happily graze on. Its porous surface is perfect for attaching mosses, Buce, and Anubias, giving your tank a natural, lived‑in vibe (and your shrimp their very own all‑you‑can‑eat buffet). Driftwood will leech tannins into the water, causing a tea colored tint in the water. This is normal and will reduce over time. Boiling wood before use will reduce tannin leeching while ensuring pieces are waterlogged to prevent floating. Size Specifications: Photos provided are a representation of what you will receive. Cholla is a natural driftwood, colors, shape, and size differences will occur and are to be expected. Larger, curious fish or other fauna (such as a betta fish) run the risk of getting caught in holes or hollowed openings of Cholla. Please be mindful of this before placing it in your aquarium.

listings.commonName: Eriocaulon Buergerianum Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Eriocaulon Buergerianum is a rare aquatic pipewort native to Asia, prized among experienced aquascapers for its compact, tufted rosette foliage. Similar to Eriocaulon Cinereum , this species grows in neat, spiky tufts that resemble miniature sea urchins rather than forming creeping horizontal mats. Reaching 1 to 3 inches in height, its distinct geometric silhouette makes it a great pick for accenting hardscape bases and foreground transition zones in high-tech setups. This is a finicky species that needs soft, acidic water, high lighting, and heavy root feeding to establish properly underwater. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Spiky, hedgehog rosette structure delivers a distinct geometric accent in the foreground. Compact growth breaks up uniform carpet lawns. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers under cool water before dividing and planting. Push the roots deep into fine, nutrient-dense substrate using fine-tip tweezers, leaving the crown exposed. Use a dry start method or Wabi Kusa setup to allow the extensive root system to anchor firmly before flooding the aquarium. Provide high-intensity lighting, consistent pressurized CO2 injection, and soft, acidic water parameters (GH 2–5, low TDS) with nutrient-heavy soil, as this species is extremely finicky and will quickly melt in hard water or low-tech setups. Maintain stable water parameters and good water clarity to encourage steady root development and prevent leaf melting during transition. To propagate, wait for mature crowns to naturally split at the base, then use a sharp, sterile blade to separate the daughter rosettes and replant them directly into your aquarium soil to expand the foreground group. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I plant Eriocaulon Buergerianum tissue culture? Rinse away the nutrient gel under cool water, separate the cup into individual rosettes, and use pinsettes to push the root base deep into nutrient-rich aquasoil so the crown rests cleanly on the soil surface. 2. Why is Eriocaulon Buergerianum considered a high-difficulty plant? Erio Buergerianum requires intense lighting, high CO2, and soft, acidic water with aquarium soil. It draws the majority of its nutrients through its roots and will experience severe leaf melt or die-off if kept in hard water or nutrient-poor substrate. 3. What should I do if my Eriocaulon Buergerianum begins to flower? If an emerging flower spike appears, snip it off near the base of the crown using sharp curved shears. This redirects the plant's metabolic energy back into crown splitting and fresh leaf production.

listings.commonName: Bucephalandra Brownie Phoenix Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Bucephalandra ‘Brownie Phoenix’ is a beginner-friendly, low-tech aquarium plant prized for its resilience and its ability to develop deep, fiery tones under proper lighting. This variety is a slow-growing species that thrives in both submerged and emersed conditions, provided that humidity levels remain high to prevent the foliage from drying. Highly versatile, it can be grown attached to hardscape such as driftwood or rocks rather than being buried in traditional aquarium substrate. It is an exquisite choice for the foreground or midground of freshwater aquascapes, where its compact rhizomes will slowly create a dense, colorful colony within a planted tank. Tissue culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab-grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go-to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Notes True to its name, this variant can display stunning reddish and bronze highlights when maintained under quality full-spectrum LED lighting. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for planted tanks where other plants might struggle. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by carefully removing the plantlets from the cup and rinsing away all sterile nutrient gel under lukewarm, dechlorinated water before mounting. Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard low-light aquarium plant setups, CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and a smoother tissue culture transition. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Why is my tissue culture Bucephalandra melting after planting? Tissue culture plants undergo an acclimation phase when transitioning to underwater conditions. Maintain stable water parameters, good circulation, and moderate light; as long as the rhizome stays firm, new submerged leaves will emerge. 3. Can tissue culture Bucephalandra be planted in substrate? Yes, you can push the roots into substrate or gravel to help anchor the plantlet. However, you must keep the central horizontal rhizome completely exposed above the substrate line, as burying the rhizome starves it of circulation and causes rot.

Your solenoid is the electronic gateway of your CO₂ system. When your timer clicks off at night, the solenoid is supposed to shut tight to prevent midnight gas spikes and deadly pH drops while your livestock is sleeping. If you notice that bubbles continue to trickle out of your diffuser long after the power has cut out, your internal spring mechanism has likely worn down or gotten stuck. Instead of replacing your entire expensive regulator, the UNS Solenoid Spring Switch Replacement is a quick, inexpensive fix that restores a 100% airtight closure every single time the power shuts off. Key Features & Benefits Instantly fixes leaking regulators by ensuring the solenoid internal valve fully closes the second the power drops. Universal dual compatibility works seamlessly with both the UNS Mini and UNS Pro Dual Stage Regulator models. Preventing gas leaks protects your fish, shrimp, and bio-filter from dangerous, suffocating pH fluctuations. Product Specifications Product Type: Regulator Internal Mechanical Repair Part Regulator Compatibility: Fits UNS Mini Dual Stage and UNS Pro Dual Stage Regulators Core Function: Mechanical spring-assisted internal shutoff valve Listing Type: Includes replacement spring switch piece ONLY (Note: Main electronic solenoid body and regulator are not included with purchase).

Species Profile White Medaka Rice Fish ( Oryzias latipes ), often referred to as Shiro Medaka, are a classic Japanese domestic strain known for their clean, porcelain-white to silvery translucent bodies. In a planted aquarium, they cruise the upper third of the water column, standing out clearly against dark soil, hardscape, and dense green stems. While they look sharp through front aquarium glass, Medakas have a long history of being appreciated from above, making them just as well suited for shallow indoor ponds and patio tubs as standard glass aquariums. Because they feed actively right at the surface and can easily leap when startled, keeping a secure lid on the tank is essential. **Note: All livestock orders will come carefully packaged with solid wall Styrofoam insulation and shipped via 1-day shipping only. No extra insulation needs to be added to your cart for your livestock. Key Features & Notes Porcelain-white body with subtle silvery iridescence contrasts against dark substrate and green foliage. Active top-dwelling nano schooler that stays plant-safe and leaves carpet plants rooted. Cold-tolerant and adaptable nature thrives in unheated indoor tanks, heated community setups, or outdoor tubs. Acclimation & Care Instructions Float the sealed transport bag for 15 to 20 minutes to equalize water temperatures before opening. Drip acclimate over 30 to 45 minutes using airline tubing to ease them into your tank's GH, KH, and pH levels. Equip your tank with a snug lid or generous floating plant cover; active Medakas can leap when startled. Provide gentle surface circulation; strong filter turbulence can easily exhaust these small surface swimmers. Feed crushed flakes, micro pellets, or baby brine shrimp once or twice daily to match their small, upturned mouths. Keep in groups of 6 or more to encourage confident schooling behavior and reduce stress. White opacity and silver sheen vary naturally between individual fish and intensify under bright lighting. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy livestock! Do White Medaka Rice Fish require an aquarium heater? Not in a standard indoor room. Japanese Medakas are eurythermal and handle wide temperature ranges with ease, thriving at typical room temperatures between 64°F and 74°F without a heater. They also work well in heated community aquariums up to 78°F or unheated outdoor mini ponds in spring and summer. 2. Are White Medakas safe to keep with dwarf shrimp? Adult Neocaridina and Caridina shrimp are safe to house with them. Medakas stay close to the waterline and have small upturned mouths, rarely interacting with shrimp grazing on hardscape or substrate. Free-swimming newborn shrimplets at the surface can be eaten, so having dense moss and low ground cover provides plenty of protection for your colony. 3. How do Medaka Rice Fish spawn, and how do I raise the fry? Females carry clusters of fertilized eggs near their anal vent in the morning, depositing them into fine-leafed plants, mosses, or yarn mops. For a complete breakdown of setting up breeding tubs, collecting egg mops, and raising fry, explore our comprehensive Japanese Rice Fish Care Guide . 4. What tank mates work best with White Medaka Rice Fish? They do best with calm, non-aggressive species that occupy the middle and bottom layers of the tank. Good pairings include pygmy Corydoras, Otocinclus, small rasboras, and clean-up crews like Nerite snails or Amano shrimp. Avoid aggressive surface feeders or fin-nippers that could harass them or outcompete them during feeding time.

Plant Profile If you're looking to bring wild, high-contrast patterns into your aquascape, Cryptocoryne spiralis 'Tiger' is a contender. Originating from the soft, slow-moving waterways of India, this distinctive variant has earned its stripes in the hobby thanks to its long, ribbon-like leaves covered in bold, tiger-like variegated patterns. As with all crypt plants, this plant can be sensitive to changes in water parameters and doesn’t like to be moved. But once settled into its new home, it'll become a low-maintenance, contrasting background accent. Key Features & Benefits Ribbon-like leaves with tiger-stripe patterning add unique visual depth and movement. Can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups where it will periodically produce unique flowering spathes. Resilient once established, displaying deeper bronze and red accents under higher light and CO2. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Crypt species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth!
