How do I help my Cryptocoryne Spiralis 'Tiger' recover if it melts? Crypt melt is a standard reaction when shifting water conditions cause old leaves to dissolve so the plant can rebuild foliage adapted to your aquarium. Trim away rotting tissue, keep your water parameters stable, and do not disturb the subterranean root system. For complete recovery steps, check out our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt . 2. Why does moving or uprooting my Crypt cause melt? This species relies heavily on a delicate network of subterranean roots that absorb nutrients from the soil. Uprooting the plant ruptures these fine root hairs and alters its micro-environment, triggering a shock response where the plant drops its leaves to conserve energy. Placing it in a permanent location from day one prevents unnecessary leaf loss. 3. Should I use root tabs or liquid fertilizers for Cryptocoryne Spiralis 'Tiger'? Root tabs are far more effective than liquid fertilizers for Cryptocoryne species because they draw the overwhelming majority of their nutrition through their roots. While liquid nutrients benefit water column feeders like mosses or stem plants, placing nutrient-rich root tabs inside sand or gravel substrates directly fuels your Crypt's foliage growth.

Plant Profile Bucephalandra ‘Pygmy’ is a versatile, low-tech aquarium plant featuring small to moderately sized foliage that can produce a wide variety of colors depending on aquarium conditions. This hardy variant is prized for its adaptable nature, often displaying shifts in tone that add dynamic visual interest to the layout. Like other epiphytes, it can grow submerged or emersed and prefers to attach its rhizome to driftwood or rock rather than be buried in substrate. Over time, its thin rhizomes slowly spread into compact, shimmering clusters that serve as a dense, colorful colony in the foreground or midground of freshwater aquascapes. Tissue culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab-grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go-to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Notes Depending on your lighting and nutrient schedule, 'Pygmy' can transition through various shades of green, bronze, and subtle metallic hues. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for planted tanks where other plants might struggle. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by carefully removing the plantlets from the cup and rinsing away all sterile nutrient gel under lukewarm, dechlorinated water before mounting. Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard low-light aquarium plant setups, CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and smoother tissue culture transition. listings.description: Plant Profile Myriophyllum Ussuriense is what happens when delicate foliage decides to be a background powerhouse. This rare aquatic stem plant, native to the quiet rivers, wetlands, and lakes of East Asia, grows soft, feathery, pine-like whorls along supple central stems, bringing lime-green color and movement to the tank. Plant it in dense, bushy groups, and it does exactly what it was built for: filling in midground gaps, forming background hedges, or lining up into detailed Dutch-style streets. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. Easy and versatile stem habit that branches rapidly when pruned to build tight, cloud-like bushes. listings.commonName: Nesaea Pedicellata 'Golden' Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Instead of picking between standard green and deep red, Nesaea Pedicellata Golden offers a rare third option: gold! Hailing from West Africa, this striking aquatic stem plant pairs greenish-gold leaves with bold, pinkish-red stems for a look you just don't see every day. As one of the very few golden-colored species available in the aquascaping hobby, it provides an exceptional pop of color and architectural contrast in midground or background placements. Hardy and versatile, this gem flourishes in both submerged aquariums and emersed setups, developing rich, warm tones under moderate-to-high lighting. Key Features & Benefits Rare greenish-gold leaves contrasting against bright pinkish-red stems introduce a unique color palette to planted tanks. Hardy stem plant that easily forms thick, bushy midground clusters when pruned routinely. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. * Nesaea stems can be fragile, so handle with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil . Provide moderate-to-high lighting. Adding pressurized CO2 and a consistent fertilizer regimen enhances growth speed and yields maximum golden-yellow coloration. Maintain stable water parameters and cooler-to-moderate water temperatures (70–78°F) for ideal leaf form and stem development. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the desired height to encourage dense side-branching. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Featuring long, delicate stems lined with dense, narrow foliage, this species delivers rapid growth and a lush, vibrant appearance. Under standard lighting, it maintains a fresh, bright green coloration, but when grown under high-intensity light and pressurized CO2, its upper leaf tips blush with soft golden and pink hues. Exceptionally striking when planted in dense clusters, Rotala sp. 'Myanmar' responds vigorously to routine trimming, making it an ideal choice for sculpting full, bushy background hedges or structured Dutch-style plant streets. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. Plant Profile Alternanthera Amabilis Tricolor did not want to pick just one color, so it picked three. Young plants start with modest, spade-shaped leaves with wavy margins in a simple lime-green, but grow it under high-tech conditions, and it hits its stride, developing a full tricolor blend of rosy pink, crimson red, and warm golden-yellow across the foliage. Reaching 4 to 12 inches tall, it makes a dynamic midground centerpiece or lush background hedge, perfect for filling open spaces in aquascapes, terrariums, and paludariums. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Textured spade-shaped leaves with wavy margins create rich foliage density. Displays vibrant tricolor variegation including green, pink, red, and golden-yellow highlights. Dense growth habit shelters dwarf shrimp and shy fish. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight (or pot) and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the roots, then strip lower foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower foliage. Provide medium-to-high lighting. Regular dosing of liquid fertilizers alongside pressurized CO2 injection will optimize plant health, prevent leaf melt, and bring out vibrant red, pink, and yellow tricolor patterns. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim main stem tops with straight scissors once stems reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and expand coverage. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Common Name: Bucephalandra Kapuas Bucephalandra Kapuas is a compact epiphyte featuring dark, moody foliage and a subtle metallic sheen. This Buce variant displays narrow, ruffled oval-shaped leaves that range from deep green to brownish hues, often developing richer coloration under stronger lighting. Ideal for nano tanks, shrimp setups, and detailed hardscape work, Bucephalandra Kapuas adds texture and depth without overwhelming a layout. A reliable choice for aquascapers looking for hardy structure and understated color contrast. Like other epiphytic aquatic plants, Kapuas grows from a rhizome and should be attached to rock or driftwood. It thrives in low to medium light and does well in both low-tech aquascapes and CO2-injected aquariums. While growth is slow, stable water parameters and regular fertilization will encourage fuller, healthier clumps over time. Notes: Bucephalandra is an epiphytic aquarium plant, and prefers to be attached to aquarium hardscape. Do not cover the rhizome when planting the Bucephalandra in substrate. This will cause melt and rot. Please be sure to remove this plant from its pot. Remove the rockwool surrounding the roots and attach it to the hardscape. For instructions on how to properly prep "potted" aquarium plants, click here . Bucephalandra’s final size, coloration, and growth rate are dependent upon the condition of the aquarium. Photos are a representation of what you will receive and may vary. Do not make drastic changes to the aquarium. Unstable parameters can result in melt and rotting of the aquarium plant. CO2 injection will yield better growth. Please research appropriately to ensure your plant thrives. Plant Profile Common Name: Bucephalandra Grappa Red (Mini) Buce ‘Grappa Red’ (Mini) is a vibrant aquarium plant characterized by its short, slender, teardrop-shaped leaves and reddish stems. This variety is most notable for the red and coppery undertones that emerge on the foliage when the plant is grown under high-quality aquarium LED lighting. Highly versatile, it can be grown submerged or emersed, usually attached to hardscape such as driftwood or rocks rather than being buried in traditional aquarium substrate. It's a colorful accent for the foreground of freshwater aquascapes, where its miniature size allows it to fit perfectly within the tight nooks and crannies of your hardscape for fine-scale detailing. Key Features & Notes Under optimal conditions, the leaves develop a warm, metallic copper sheen that provides a unique contrast to the standard greens and blues of other Bucephalandra species. True to its name, the petioles (stems) display a distinct reddish hue, adding an extra layer of color to the plant’s overall profile. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for aquascapes where other plants might struggle. It is perfectly at home fully submerged in an aquarium or emersed in high-humidity terrariums, vivariums, and paludariums. Care Tips & Preparation Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood . Never bury the rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting. Unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance, CO2 injection will yield much faster growth. We recommend researching your specific water chemistry to ensure your plant thrives. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions. Please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Please research appropriately to ensure your plant thrives. Additional Information Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. The multi-chamber sump features a prefilter baffle to trap larger solids on filter floss, reducing the frequency of filter sock replacement. This African hardwood is the undisputed heavyweight champion of the aquascaping world. Famous for its extreme density and a striking, two‑toned contrast of sandy tan and deep chocolate brown, Mopani looks less like a piece of timber and more like a rugged, ancient relic sculpted by the elements. If you want a hardscape that brings an immediate sense of weight, permanence, and prehistoric history to your aquarium, this is truly the wood that knocks out the competition. Product Features & Benefits Unlike almost any other driftwood, Mopani is so dense that it typically sinks immediately. This makes it a go-to for hobbyists who want to skip the "weighing it down" phase and get straight to aquascaping. Mopani has a unique, contrasting color palette with light tan highlights and deep chocolate-brown shadows. Its smooth areas paired with gnarled, "knotty" textures add instant depth to a driftwood aquarium. Because it is exceptionally hard, Mopani breaks down much more slowly than other woods. It provides a long-lasting foundation for a planted aquarium hardscape, especially when used as a base for mosses and ferns. Its durability and striking look make it just as popular for reptile enclosures and terrariums, providing a sturdy, non-rot surface for climbing and basking. Size Specifications Photos provided are a representation of what you will receive. Mopani is a natural aquarium hardscape product; please expect variations in shape, weight, and character. Small: 7-10 inches Medium: 10-16 inches Large: 16-22 inches Preparation & Care A little extra prep goes a long way in maintaining its stunning appearance. Rinse: Thoroughly rinse the piece to remove any dust or debris from transit. The Tannin Powerhouse: Mopani is very rich in natural tannins. While these are beneficial for the health of your fish and help naturally lower pH, they will produce a dark "tea-colored" tint. If you prefer crystal-clear water, we strongly recommend boiling the wood for 1–2 hours or soaking it in a bucket for several days before use. You can also reduce this effect through consistent water changes or through the addition of Aquario Neo Carbon Bag Important note: We recommend rinsing wood thoroughly before adding it to an established aquarium. If you prefer, you may also boil the wood for at least 1–2 hours to help release tannins.

Engineered for aquascapers and planted tank hobbyists who demand a clean, equipment-free viewing panel, this high-precision external inline heater combines smart electronic thermal monitoring with a compact, leak-proof housing. Key Features & Benefits In-Line Canister Integration: Mounts externally on canister filter return hosing to keep your display tank 100% free of visible heating equipment. Even Heat Distribution: Warmed outflow water circulates rapidly throughout the entire aquarium, eliminating cold spots and thermal stratification. High-Precision Electronic Control: Smart internal temperature sensors maintain stable thermal conditions to protect delicate fish, dwarf shrimp, and plants. Dual Hose Compatibility: Available in standard 12/16mm and 16/22mm hose barb fittings to seamlessly integrate with popular canister filter systems. Space-Saving Compact Footprint: Sleek 3.19" x 2.40" x 5.51" body mounts neatly inside or behind your aquarium display cabinet. Should I install the Chihiros Heater Pro on the inflow or outflow tubing of my canister filter? Always install the heater on the outflow (return) line carrying clean, filtered water back to the aquarium. Installing it on the inflow side exposes the heating element to raw debris and detritus from the tank, which can cause clogging or uneven heating. 2. What size inline heater do I need for my UNS Delta canister filter? Choose the 12/16mm model for UNS Delta 30, Delta 60, and Delta 90 filters. The larger sizes (Large and Dew-Shaped) work wonderfully as miniature Walstad-style pico aquariums, glass propagation jars, or small rimless desktop shrimp vessels when filled with water. 3. listings.commonName: Ludwigia Senegalensis Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Meet Ludwigia Senegalensis, a rare aquatic stem plant that looks like it was painted, not grown. Oval, slightly reflexed leaves show off an intricate, lattice-like mosaic of brick-red, copper, and orange marbling over a golden-green base, giving it a leaf pattern unlike almost anything else in the hobby. Because it's tough to find commercially, experienced hobbyists chase it down specifically to build an unforgettable centerpiece or midground Dutch street, planting it in dense, well-lit groups where that lattice detail really gets to shine. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Lattice-like leaf pattern in brick-red, copper, and golden orange. Rare African species with standout leaf architecture for midground zones. Compact growth, ideal for high-contrast focal points and Dutch-style streets. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. * Ludwigia stems can be fragile, so handle with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate. Provide high-intensity lighting. Pressurized CO2 injection and regular liquid nutrient dosing, especially iron and micronutrients, are strongly recommended to prevent leaf decay and bring out intense red vein marbling. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim main stem tops with straight scissors once stems reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and expand your bush. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Ludwigia senegalensis Common Name(s) Ludwigia Senegalensis, Ludwigia sp. 'Guinea' Family Onagraceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Stem Plant Care Difficulty Moderate / Advanced Light Requirement Medium to High (High light required for intense patterning) CO2 Requirement Recommended (Essential for strong stem health and red tones) Placement / Usage Midground / Background Focal Point Height / Size 4–8”+ Growth Rate Moderate Water Parameters pH 6.5–7.5 Propagation Method Cuttings (Cut stem and replant tops) Origin Africa Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I bring out the intricate red leaf pattern on Ludwigia Senegalensis? Achieving distinct, brick-red patterned foliage on Ludwigia Senegalensis requires high light intensity, pressurized CO2, nutrient-rich soil, and regular supplementation of liquid micronutrients, particularly iron! In low light, the pattern fades and stems become prone to melting. 3. How do I prepare Ludwigia Senegalensis Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture before planting? Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the dense cluster into smaller clumps or individual stem bundles and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

listings.commonName: Anubias Barteri 'Round Leaf' Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Also affectionately known in the hobby as Anubias Golden Coin, this fast-rising favorite swaps out the standard pointed leaf shape for charming, coin-like circular foliage. Resting atop tall, graceful stems similar to classic Anubias Barteri, its broad, coin-shaped leaves bring a playful geometry and rich green texture that instantly softens heavy rockwork and dark driftwood. Thriving across a wide range of water parameters with minimal effort, this bulletproof beauty makes a standout midground or background accent that pays major visual dividends. By choosing the Tissue Culture version of this plant, you are guaranteed a 100% pest-free, algae-free, and pesticide-free start for your aquarium. These plants are grown in-vitro in a sterile laboratory setting, ensuring no unwanted snails or hitchhikers enter your system. While these plantlets start smaller and require more time to mature, they offer the cleanest and most reliable method for establishing a healthy colony in planted tanks. Key Features & Benefits Circular leaf shape offers a unique geometric contrast against traditional pointed or lanceolate aquatic plants. Legendary Anubias hardiness ensures it effortlessly adapts to low-tech setups, varying water conditions, and active tank mates. The sterile laboratory environment guarantees your new plant arrives completely free of pests. Care & Planting Instructions Remove the plantlets from the cup and rinse away the sterile nutrient gel under lukewarm, dechlorinated water. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Avoid intense light and ensure good water flow to prevent spot algae on slow‑growing leaves. CO₂ is recommended to assist with the tissue culture transition and support healthy growth. Master the prep and planting process by checking out a beginner's guide to tissue culture plants to prevent your delicate new plantlets from melting or floating away. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Anubias barteri var. 'Round' / 'Golden Coin' Common Name(s) Anubias Barteri Round, Anubias Golden Coin Family Araceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Epiphyte (Rhizome / Tissue Culture) Care Difficulty Easy / Beginner-Friendly Light Requirement Low to Medium CO2 Requirement Recommended for TC Transition Placement / Usage Midground, Background Height / Size 4-8 inches Growth Rate Slow (1 leaf every 3-4 weeks) Water Parameters pH 6.0 – 7.5 | Temperature 68°F – 82°F (20°C – 28°C) Propagation Method Separate by Rhizome Division Origin Africa / Lab Tissue Culture Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I plant Anubias Barteri Round Tissue Culture? Attach the plant directly to driftwood or rocks using aquarium-safe super glue gel, thread, or fishing line. Keep the rhizome above the substrate to prevent rot. 2. Does it require CO2 or high lighting? No. It thrives in low lighting without CO2 injection. While adding CO2 speeds up growth and aids in the tissue culture transition, it is completely optional. 3. Is this plant safe for shrimp, snails, and fish? Yes, Anubias is 100% safe for all freshwater fish, shrimp (including sensitive Caridina and Neocaridina), and snails. Its tough leaves are also resistant to plant-eating fish like cichlids or goldfish.

listings.description: Common Name: Eriocaulon Aquaticum Eriocaulon Aquaticum is known for its rosette growth and fine, grass-like leaves. Its vibrant green color and compact growth makes it an ideal aquarium plant for the foreground or midground area in high-tech planted tanks. Native to North America, Eriocaulon Aquaticum grows best in soft, slightly acidic water with strong light and CO2 injection. It is a great choice for intermediate to advanced aquarium hobbyists looking for unique, ornamental plants for their aquascapes. Tissue culture plants are grown in vitro from a state of the art laboratory specialized in propagating aquatic plants. They provide the best option for those who want to ensure that absolutely zero unwanted pests are introduced into the aquarium. Remove tissue culture gel before planting. Simply wash the gel away or soak the plant in water and squeeze the gel off with your fingers. Plant Profile Myriophyllum Elatinoides 'Snowflake', commonly known as Watermilfoil, is a fast-growing aquatic stem plant prized for its remarkably fine, needle-like foliage that radiates in symmetrical whorls along tall central stems, resembling the soft branches of an underwater pine or fir tree. Displaying a crisp, bright lime-green color, this versatile species excels as a textured background or midground filler. Under medium to high lighting and pressurized CO2, it grows rapidly into dense, fluffy thickets that bring depth, volume, and natural movement to both high-tech and low-tech aquascapes. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Feathery, needle-like pine-whorl foliage adds soft, pine-tree texture and visual movement to background zones. Fast-growing stem habit easily branches into dense, cloud-like hedges when routinely trimmed. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. * Myriophyllum foliage is extraordinarily delicate, so handle stems with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide medium-to-high lighting and clean water conditions; while adaptable without CO2, supplying pressurized CO2 injection yields significantly faster growth and denser needle whorls. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or rotting. Trim main stem tops with sharp straight scissors once they reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and expand coverage. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Each cut site will sprout multiple lateral side shoots, doubling the stem density and creating a tight, bushy cloud of fine foliage. 3. Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the cluster into smaller clumps or individual stems and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

Plant Profile Myriophyllum aquaticum 'Roraima' (commonly called Water Milfoil) is a fast-growing stem plant cultivar with feathery, pine-like whorls of fine foliage that shift from bright yellow-orange to deep copper-red under high-tech tank lighting. Reaching impressive heights of 20 to 30 inches, its bushy stems and fine leaf texture make it an ideal choice for filling out background zones and creating dense, colorful hedges in medium to large aquariums. Growing reliably under medium to high lighting, it tolerates a wide range of water parameters and is a beginner-friendly option for adding feathery texture to layouts. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Feathery, pine-like leaf whorls transition from golden-yellow to rich copper-red under moderate to high lighting. Fast vertical growth habit quickly builds dense background hedges and absorbs excess water column nutrients. Adapts smoothly to fully submerged aquariums or emersed growth in humid terrariums. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small portions or individual stems 1 inch apart into your aquarium soil so light penetrates down to lower stem nodes. Provide medium to high lighting; while CO2 is optional, supplying pressurized CO2 and regular liquid iron supplementation deepens copper-red leaf tones and increases growth density. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water chemistry and prune upper stems regularly to prevent upper branches from shading neighboring plants. To propagate, trim main stem tops with sharp straight shears and replant the cuttings directly into your aquarium soil to encourage side shoots. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Once clean, divide the cluster into small stem portions or individual stems and insert the roots into your aquarium soil using fine pinsettes. 2. How do I bring out the orange and red colors in Myriophyllum Roraima? While foliage remains yellow-green under basic light, supplying high light intensity, pressurized CO2 injection, and a consistent liquid dosing routine rich in iron turns upper leaf whorls deep copper-red. 3. How often should I trim Myriophyllum Roraima in the background? Because Myriophyllum Roraima is a fast grower, trim the upper stems every few weeks using sharp shears. Replanting those trimmed tops into your aquarium soil quickly builds a thick, bushy hedge.

Plant Profile Davallia repens, commonly known as the Creeping Rabbit's Foot Fern, is an epiphytic woodland fern that lives perched on bark and stones rather than buried in mud or sunk underwater. Strapped onto damp spiderwood branches or tucked into rock joints, its fuzzy, scaly rhizomes crawl outward and unfurl triangular, lacy green fronds that soften harsh hardscape seams. In wild tropical canopies, those hairy creeping rhizomes act like sponges, soaking up mist droplets and atmospheric moisture during cloudbursts so the plant can survive dry spells between rains. Key Features & Notes Fuzzy, scaly rhizomes creep across hardscape to anchor naturally without needing soil. Triangular lacy green fronds provide an airy canopy texture across rockwork and wood. Thrives when mounted above the waterline in humid vivarium plants and paludarium setups. Care & Planting Instructions Mount the furry rhizome onto rough driftwood, cork bark, or porous stone using cotton thread or plant-safe glue with a thin pad of damp sphagnum moss; never bury the creeping rhizome under soil, as burying it will rot the plant. Provide low to medium indirect light or filtered shade; direct sun or intense grow lights will scorch the delicate pinnae and turn the fronds crispy. Maintain humidity above 75% and keep the mounting media damp, but provide gentle airflow and avoid letting heavy water droplets puddle on the leaves for long periods. Snip older, yellowing fronds close to the creeping rhizome using clean shears to stimulate fresh fiddleheads and maintain plant vigor. Note that this plant is shipped bare root, and each order includes an active cutting with 2 to 4 leaves ready to establish. Davallia repens are terrestrial plants, and being submerged will result in the death of the plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Davallia repens (syn. Humata repens ) Common Name(s) Creeping Rabbit's Foot Fern, Dwarf Rabbit's Foot Family Davalliaceae Plant Type Epiphytic / Lithophytic Creeping Fern Care Difficulty Easy to Moderate Light Requirement Low to Medium Indirect Light (Partial Shade) Submersion Suitability Emersed Only (Not for full submersion) Placement / Usage Epiphyte Mounts, Driftwood Branches, Rock Crevices, Background Walls Height / Size Fronds 2"–4" (5–10 cm); rhizome creeps indefinitely Growth Rate Slow to Moderate Humidity Requirement High (> 70% RH) Propagation Method Rhizome Division Origin Tropical Asia, Africa, and Pacific Islands Frequently Asked Questions 1. Can Davallia repens grow submerged in an aquarium? No. Davallia repens is strictly an epiphytic land fern. Submerging the foliage or rhizomes underwater cuts off gas exchange and will cause the plant to turn translucent and rot within days. 2. Can I plant the rhizome of Davallia repens into potting soil? No. Burying the furry rhizome under damp soil suffocates the growth points and leads directly to rhizome rot. Instead, fasten it on top of wood or rock with a thin layer of damp sphagnum moss. 3. Why are the fronds on my Creeping Rabbit's Foot Fern turning brown or crispy? Crispy or curling fronds indicate low ambient humidity or excess direct lighting. Keep the enclosure sealed to hold humidity above 70% and move the fern out of hot lighting hotspots.

Built-In Cascade & Waterfall Wall: Integrated rear wall that continuously circulates water through vertical plant pads to nourish root systems and foster natural moss growth. listings.commonName: Rotala Macrandra Mini Butterfly UNS Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Meet Rotala Macrandra 'Mini Butterfly', a dwarf stem plant native to the sunlit, soft-water wetlands of India that packs all the color of classic Rotala macrandra into a much smaller footprint. In its emersed form, the leaves tend to grow horizontally and remain green. Submerged under high-tech conditions, it grows upright into glowing crimson stems that make green foliage nearby look almost dull by comparison. Best suited for experienced hobbyists running high-tech setups, it thrives under high lighting, soft water, low nitrates, and generous iron dosing. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Vivid red-magenta dwarf foliage adds dramatic color contrast and fine textural scale to midground and background zones. Fast-growing mini stem species that branches rapidly when pruned to build tight, cloud-like hedges. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. * Rotala leaves are fragile, so handle stems with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. This species prefers soft, slightly acidic water, medium-to-high lighting, and CO₂ levels maintained between 15–25 ppm. Note that pale leaves or white markings are clear signs of an iron deficiency. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or rotting. To propagate, trim healthy tops or side shoots and replant them directly into the substrate. Regular pruning encourages fuller, bushier growth. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Rotala macrandra 'Mini Butterfly' Common Name(s) Butterfly Mini, Rotala Macrandra Mini Butterfly, Rotala Mini Butterfly Family Lythraceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Dwarf Stem Plant Care Difficulty Difficult / Advanced Light Requirement High (Essential to prevent lower leaf melting) CO2 Requirement Required (15–25 ppm essential for health and red-magenta color) Placement / Usage Midground / Background Centerpiece & Dutch Street Height / Size 8–11”+ (Cup portion size: 2–3”) Growth Rate Fast Water Parameters pH 5.0–7.5 (Soft acidic water preferred) Propagation Method Cuttings (Trim side shoots or stem tops and replant) Origin Asia (India) Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I achieve a thick, bushy forest with Rotala Macrandra Mini Butterfly? To encourage Rotala Macrandra Mini Butterfly to form a dense hedge, routinely trim the main stem tops once established. Each cut site will sprout multiple lateral side shoots, doubling the stem density and creating a tight, bushy red cluster. 3. How do I prepare Rotala Macrandra Mini Butterfly Tissue Culture before planting? Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the cluster into smaller clumps or individual stems and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

listings.commonName: Rotala Sp. Pearl UNS Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Rotala sp. Pearl is an exceptionally delicate and miniature variation of Rotala, perfectly suited for nano aquariums and detailed aquascapes! Featuring small, compact foliage along slender stems, this unique species displays an enchanting mix of fresh green, soft purple, and vibrant pink hues when grown under high lighting and CO2. Because of its tiny leaf structure, it is ideal for creating dense midground mounds or soft background bushes without overwhelming smaller tank layouts. Plant Profile Meet Persicaria praetermissa, commonly known as Ruby Smartweed, a rare, fast-growing aquatic stem plant native to the tropical and subtropical marshes, riverbanks, and wetlands of Asia and Australia. It stands out with slender, spearhead- to arrow-shaped leaves featuring distinct basal lobes, a leaf geometry that gives it a textural contrast most stem plants can't match. Grown emersed, it keeps things green, but take it underwater, and it transforms, developing rich reddish-brown, copper, and deep magenta tones instead. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Distinct spear-head leaf shape develops rich copper, reddish-brown, and magenta tones under submerged conditions. Versatile across submerged aquariums, paludariums, and open-top bog gardens. Rapid growth acts as a natural nitrate sponge for crystal-clear water. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight (or pot) and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the roots, then strip lower foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower leaves. Provide medium-to-high lighting; while adaptable, adding pressurized CO2 and regular liquid nutrient dosing with iron yields significantly faster growth, larger leaves, and deeper reddish-brown pigmentation. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim main stem tops with straight scissors once stems reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and expand coverage. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. As new growth adapts, the plant will shed its stiffer emersed foliage and sprout soft, brightly colored underwater leaves with reddish-brown highlights. Once new shoots take root, trim away old lower growth to encourage dense branching.

Plant Profile Dipteracanthus elastica, affectionately known as the Bubble Plant, is a terrestrial plant sporting deep green, pillowy leaves that look like they were individually inflated with an air pump. Its quilted, bubble-wrap texture contrasts cleanly against flat carpet mosses, smooth river stones, or pale driftwood along enclosure floors and moist paludarium margins. As it settles into loose, aerated substrate under indirect light, it shifts from a neat, compact mound into a lazy creeper in enclosed humid setups. Key Features & Notes Distinctly puckered, bubble-textured foliage adds immediate dimensional contrast on the tank floor. Starts as a tidy clumping mound before naturally trailing across damp hardscape and substrate. Strictly terrestrial grower that will drown and rot if dropped underwater in an aquarium. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and gently clearing all loose media from the roots. Tuck the root cluster into a loose, airy tropical soil blend loaded with bark, perlite, and pumice, keeping the crown sitting right at the soil line so it stays well-aerated. Provide moderate to bright indirect light; direct rays will roast the puckered leaf blisters, while overly dark corners will make the stems stretch out looking leggy. Maintain humidity above 70% while keeping the soil evenly damp rather than waterlogged, as wet, stagnant mud will turn the lower leaves yellow in a hurry. Pinch back wandering stem tips with clean shears to encourage denser lateral mounds and keep it from wandering into your neighbors' territory. Final size and leaf puffiness depend entirely on your specific setup conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Dipteracanthus elastica are terrestrial plants, and being submerged will result in the death of the plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Submerging it underwater will quickly rot the bubble leaves and drown the root system. 2. Why are the leaves on my Bubble Plant turning yellow and mushy? Yellowing, soft leaves almost always mean the soil is too soggy or lacks drainage. Make sure the substrate is chunky and airy so excess water escapes freely. 3. How do you propagate Dipteracanthus elastica? Snip a trailing stem cutting with a couple of leaf pairs, remove the bottom set of leaves, and press the bare node into moist sphagnum moss or damp tropical substrate until it roots.

Plant Profile Cryptocoryne spiralis 'Jwala' brings dynamic, ribbon-like texture and rich color to your midground layout. This striking cultivar stands out with narrow, slightly curled leaves that shift from bright emerald to deep bronze and reddish tones under moderate lighting. As with all crypt plants, it can be sensitive to sudden parameter shifts and strongly objects to being relocated once planted. Given a permanent home in your substrate, however, its compact rosettes mature into an eye-catching, long-lasting accent that adds rich natural texture to your aquascape. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Narrow, curled leaves with green to reddish-bronze tones add dynamic texture to midground zones. Can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups, where mature plants may produce flowering spathes. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel to supply essential subterranean nutrients. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth and fuller foliage density, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Crypt species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. Species Profile Komachi Medaka Rice Fish ( Oryzias latipes ) are a prized Japanese domestic strain inspired by the classic Kohaku coloration of ornamental koi, featuring distinct patches of fiery orange set against a clean, milky porcelain-white base. In a planted aquarium, they cruise the upper third of the water column, adding bold two-tone contrast against dark substrate, driftwood, and lush green stem plants. They are peaceful nano schoolers that leave live foliage alone, ensuring delicate carpet runners and stem leaves stay rooted. While they look clean through front aquarium glass, Medakas have a long history of being appreciated from above, making Komachis especially well suited for shallow rimless tanks, mini ponds, and outdoor patio tubs where their split color blocking is on full display. Because they feed actively right at the surface and can easily leap when startled, keeping a secure lid on the tank is essential. **Note: All livestock orders will come carefully packaged with solid wall Styrofoam insulation and shipped via 1-day shipping only. No extra insulation needs to be added to your cart for your livestock. Key Features & Notes Two-tone orange and milky white pattern creates vivid contrast in both front and top-down views. Active top-dwelling nano schooler that stays plant-safe and leaves carpet plants rooted. Cold-tolerant and adaptable nature thrives in unheated indoor tanks, heated community setups, or outdoor tubs. Acclimation & Care Instructions Float the sealed transport bag for 15 to 20 minutes to equalize water temperatures before opening. Drip acclimate over 30 to 45 minutes using airline tubing to ease them into your tank's GH, KH, and pH levels. Equip your tank with a snug lid or generous floating plant cover; active Medakas can leap when startled. Provide gentle surface circulation; strong filter turbulence can easily exhaust these small surface swimmers. Feed crushed flakes, micro pellets, or baby brine shrimp once or twice daily to match their small, upturned mouths. Keep in groups of 6 or more to encourage confident schooling behavior and reduce stress. Orange marking placement and white density vary naturally between individual fish and intensify under bright lighting. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy livestock! How do I bring out the best color contrast on Komachi Medakas? Full-spectrum overhead lighting and a dark background or substrate make the two-tone pattern pop the most. Direct top-down light helps define the line between the milky white body and orange patches. Offering carotenoid-rich foods such as baby brine shrimp, cyclops, and quality spirulina-based micro foods will also help keep the orange patches rich and saturated. 2. Do Komachi Medaka Rice Fish require an aquarium heater? Not in a standard indoor room. Japanese Medakas are eurythermal and handle wide temperature ranges with ease, thriving at typical room temperatures between 64°F and 74°F without a heater. They also work well in heated community aquariums up to 78°F or unheated outdoor mini ponds in spring and summer. 3. How do Medaka Rice Fish spawn, and how do I raise the fry? Females produce small bunches of eggs that hang from their vent like tiny grape clusters before they brush them off into floating plant roots or artificial yarn mops. For a complete breakdown of setting up breeding tubs, collecting egg mops, and raising fry, read our Japanese Rice Fish Care Guide . 4. Are Komachi Medakas safe to keep with dwarf shrimp? Adult Neocaridina and Caridina shrimp are safe to house with them. Medakas stay close to the waterline and have small upturned mouths, rarely interacting with shrimp grazing on hardscape or substrate. Free-swimming newborn shrimplets at the surface can be eaten, so having dense moss and low ground cover provides plenty of protection for your colony.

Species Profile Miyuki Black Medaka Rice Fish ( Oryzias latipes ) are an eye-catching Japanese domestic strain bred for their deep, smoky charcoal base and metallic dorsal sheen. The Miyuki trait produces an electric, reflective blue-silver light line along the dorsal ridge that cuts sharply across the dark body when hit by overhead illumination. While they look sleek through front aquarium glass, Japanese rice fish were historically developed to be appreciated from above, making this dark metallic morph especially well-suited for shallow rimless setups, mini ponds, and summer patio tubs. Because they feed actively right at the surface and can easily leap when startled, keeping a secure lid on the tank is essential. **Note: All livestock orders will come carefully packaged with solid wall Styrofoam insulation and shipped via 1-day shipping only. No extra insulation needs to be added to your cart for your livestock. Key Features & Notes Smoky charcoal body paired with a metallic dorsal line stands out in front and top-down views. Active top-dwelling nano schooler that stays plant-safe and leaves carpet plants rooted. Cold-tolerant and adaptable nature thrives in unheated indoor tanks, heated community setups, or outdoor tubs. Acclimation & Care Instructions Float the sealed transport bag for 15 to 20 minutes to equalize water temperatures before opening. Drip acclimate over 30 to 45 minutes using airline tubing to ease them into your tank's GH, KH, and pH levels. Equip your tank with a snug lid or generous floating plant cover; active Medakas can leap when startled. Provide gentle surface circulation; strong filter turbulence can easily exhaust these small surface swimmers. Feed crushed flakes, micro pellets, or baby brine shrimp once or twice daily to match their small, upturned mouths. Keep in groups of 6 or more to encourage confident schooling behavior and reduce stress. Charcoal depth and dorsal line intensity vary naturally between individual fish and deepen under strong overhead light. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy livestock! How do I get the metallic line and black base to look their best? Strong overhead lighting is key for bringing out the Miyuki dorsal sheen. Because the reflective light line runs along the spine, direct downlighting causes it to shine against the dark charcoal body. Using lighter gravel, sand, or bright green carpeting plants can also create a high-contrast background that makes their dark coloration stand out even more. 2. Do Miyuki Black Medaka Rice Fish require an aquarium heater? Not in a standard indoor room. Japanese Medakas are eurythermal and handle wide temperature ranges with ease, thriving at typical room temperatures between 64°F and 74°F without a heater. They also work well in heated community aquariums up to 78°F or unheated outdoor mini ponds in spring and summer. 3. How do Medaka Rice Fish spawn, and how do I raise the fry? Females produce small bunches of eggs that hang from their vent like tiny grape clusters before they brush them off into floating plant roots or artificial yarn mops. For a complete breakdown of setting up breeding tubs, collecting egg mops, and raising fry, read our Japanese Rice Fish Care Guide . 4. Are Miyuki Black Medakas safe to keep with dwarf shrimp? Adult Neocaridina and Caridina shrimp are safe to house with them. Medakas stay close to the waterline and have small upturned mouths, rarely interacting with shrimp grazing on hardscape or substrate. Free-swimming newborn shrimplets at the surface can be eaten, so having dense moss and low ground cover provides plenty of protection for your colony.

Horn Wood is a dense, high-character natural driftwood. Think Spider Wood’s wild branching energy mixed with the sturdy, no‑nonsense attitude of Pacific Driftwood. With warm tones and bold, antler‑like protrusions, these nano pieces prove that big personality can absolutely come in small packages. Product Features & Benefits The signature "horn-like" protrusions offer sharp, clean lines that provide immediate contrast and drama to your layout. It’s an ideal aquarium wood for creating focal points that catch the eye. The rough, aged texture of Horn Wood is tailor-made for attaching aquatic mosses, Ferns, or Bucephalandra. The crags allow plant roots to grip easily, creating a lush, professional planted aquarium hardscape. Many pieces feature flat bases or sturdy trunks, making them exceptionally easy to stack or lean against stones. Combine several pieces to create a complex "sunken forest" effect. Size Specifications Photos provided are a representation of what you will receive. This is a natural aquarium hardscape product; please expect variations in shape, weight, and character. Nano Range: 4–10 inches (Average) 5-Pack: Recommended for nano-tanks and aquariums up to 10 gallons. 10-Pack: Best for larger setups, providing the variety needed to create a cohesive, wide-scale forest look. Preparation & Care Driftwood is a natural product and requires a bit of prep before it’s ready for prime time. Rinse: Thoroughly rinse the piece to remove any dust or debris from transit. The Floating Phase: It will float initially. We recommend soaking it thoroughly or boiling it. A large stone or heavy decor may be placed on top to ensure a non-waterlogged piece of wood stays submerged. Tannin Management: Like most aquarium driftwood, this will release tannins, giving your water a warm, "tea-colored" tint. This is a natural occurrence, and the effects will subside over time. If you prefer crystal-clear water, a 1–2 hour boil is the best way to fast-track the process. You can also reduce this effect through consistent water changes or through the addition of Aquario Neo Carbon Bag Important note: We recommend rinsing wood thoroughly before adding it to an established aquarium. If you prefer, you may also boil the wood for at least 1–2 hours to help release tannins.

Plant Profile Persicaria hydropiper is a fast-growing aquatic stem plant native to moist riverbanks, marshes, and shallow waters across Asia, Europe, and North America. Its slender, elongated leaves echo Alternanthera Reineckii 'Rosaefolia ' in shape, but the real draw is the color show: under submerged aquarium conditions, its foliage turns soft, displaying a captivating blend of bright green, soft pink, and deep reddish tones. Equally suited for emersed growth in paludariums, vivariums, and bog gardens, Persicaria Hydropiper thrives in wet marginal soils where it produces vivid green and magenta leaves. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Lanceolate foliage mixes lime green, soft pink, and vivid magenta. Versatile across submerged aquariums, paludariums, and open-top bog gardens. Fast growth acts as a natural nutrient sponge, keeping water clean and suppressing algae. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight (or pot) and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the roots, then strip lower foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower growth. Provide medium-to-high lighting and consistent aquarium soil fertilization; while adaptable, adding pressurized CO2 and regular liquid nutrient dosing yields significantly faster growth, larger leaves, and deeper pink-to-red leaf pigmentation. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim main stem tops with straight scissors once stems reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and expand coverage. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Persicaria hydropiper / Polygonum sp. Common Name(s) Persicaria Hydropiper, Water Pepper, Marsh Pepper Smartweed Family Polygonaceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Stem Plant / Marginal Bog Plant Care Difficulty Easy to Moderate Light Requirement Medium to High CO2 Requirement Recommended (Enhances growth rate and pink/red tones) Placement / Usage Midground / Background Bushing / Paludarium Marginal Height / Size 4–12”+ Growth Rate Fast Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 Propagation Method Cuttings (Cut stem and replant tops) Origin Widespread (Asia, Europe, North America) Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I bring out pink and red coloration on Persicaria Hydropiper? While Persicaria Hydropiper remains predominantly green under lower lighting, providing medium-to-high light intensity, pressurized CO2, a nutrient-rich aquarium substrate, and regular dosing of liquid micro and macronutrients (especially iron) will bring out deep pink, magenta, and red foliage tones. 3. How do I transition Persicaria Hydropiper from emersed to submerged growth? When transitioning from emersed to submerged growth, plant bare stems securely into rich substrate under good lighting and keep water parameters stable. As new growth adapts, the plant will shed its stiffer emersed foliage and sprout soft, brightly colored underwater leaves with pink highlights. Once new shoots take root, trim away old lower growth to encourage dense branching.

Famous for its variegated leaves that display a magenta-to-deep-pink body accented by bright, silvery-white leaf veins, this variety brings detail and visual texture to planted aquariums. Slightly softer and more delicate in stem structure than standard Alternanthera reineckii variants, AR Rosanervig functions as a captivating background plant in nano setups or a dramatic midground focal point in larger, high-tech Dutch and nature aquascapes. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Bold foliage with distinct light-colored veins provides visual interest and contrast. Densely leaved plants offer protective cover for sensitive dwarf shrimp and shy fish. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. * AR Rosanervig stems are soft and delicate, so handle with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide medium-to-high lighting. Adding pressurized CO2 injection and regular micronutrient dosing with liquid iron ensures maximum pink coloration and strong vein contrast. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or rotting. Trim stem tops or side shoots with curved scissors once stems reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and thicken the bush. It’s incredibly versatile and willing to travel to all corners of your tank if given the opportunity. Just a heads up: when it’s happy, it grows quickly, so you'll get to enjoy a little therapeutic underwater landscaping to keep your foreground looking perfectly manicured. listings.description: Common Name: Rotalia ramosior Florida, Rotala Florida Rotala Florida Sunset, is as its name implies, a plant most easily found in Florida, USA. Considered to be a rare stem plant, Rotala Florida Sunset is highly coveted and is not the easiest species to propagate successfully. Its most distinctive and attractive feature is the plant's captivating purple leaves. High light and CO2 injection, additionally regular fertilization are all required for this plants beauty to reach its fullest potential. Rotala Florida Sunset grows slower when compared to other species and will require time and patience to achieve good coverage. We recommend placing Rotala Florida Sunset as a background or midground plant. Its vivid purple coloration will be an attention grabber and bring depth to your aquascape. Rotala Florida Sunset can be grown in both submerged and emersed conditions, although a transition period will be required. To keep Rotala Florida Sunset nice and compact, regular trimming will need to be performed. Notes: You may receive this plant in its emersed or submerged form depending on availability and seasonality. Click to learn more about Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants for Aquascaping . Rotala has fragile leaves! Be sure to handle with care. Intensity of coloration, final size, and growth rate is largely based on the conditions this plant is kept in. This is a live plant meaning size, shape and color may vary. Please be sure to remove this plant from its wrap. Remove the foam surrounding the roots and plant into a quality substrate. For instructions on how to properly prep “bunched“ aquarium plants, click here . Do not make drastic changes to the aquarium. Unstable parameters will result in melt of the aquarium plant. High CO2 injection and quality aquarium soil/sufficient nutrients will yield better growth. Please research appropriately to ensure your plant thrives. listings.commonName: Bucephalandra Sekadau Bukit Betung UNS Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Bucephalandra sp. ‘Sekadau Bukit Betung’ is a rare gem celebrated for its deep green foliage and elegant leaf structure. It features leaves with a slight waviness along the margins, creating a sophisticated texture that captures water movement beautifully. Under good lighting, its foliage can display varied iridescent hues of blue, purple, and bronze. Like other epiphytes, it can grow submerged or emersed and prefers to attach its rhizome to driftwood or rock rather than be buried in substrate. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Notes When given proper care and full-spectrum LED lighting, the dark mature foliage shifts to reveal deep metallic purples, blues, and warm bronze tones. The subtle, fluid ripples along the edges of the leaves provide an organic, textured appearance that softens harsh hardscape lines. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for planted tanks where other plants might struggle. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard low-light aquarium plant setups, CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and richer iridescence. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Bucephalandra sp. 'Sekadau Bukit Betung' Common Name(s) Buce Sekadau Bukit Betung, Sekadau Bukit Betung Family Araceae Plant Type Epiphyte (Rhizome) Care Difficulty Beginner / Easy (Low-Tech Compatible) Light Requirement Low to Medium CO2 Requirement Not Required (Accelerates growth & color density) Placement / Usage Midground Focal Point, Hardscape Crevices, Foreground Detail Height / Size 2"–4" (5.0–10.0 cm) Growth Rate Slow Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 | Temperature 68°F–80°F (20°C–26°C) Propagation Method Rhizome Division (Separate with sharp shears) Origin Borneo (Sekadau Region) Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why is my Bucephalandra melting? Bucephalandra melt can occur after changes in water chemistry, temperature, or lighting. If the rhizome remains firm, keep it attached to hardscape while the plant acclimates and produces new submerged growth. 2. Can I plant Bucephalandra in substrate? Bucephalandra is an epiphyte, so never bury its rhizome in aquasoil, sand, or gravel. Attach it to driftwood or rocks, or wedge the roots into hardscape while keeping the rhizome exposed. 3. Is Bucephalandra sp. ‘Sekadau Bukit Betung’ beginner-friendly? Yes. Bucephalandra sp. ‘Sekadau Bukit Betung’ is a beginner-friendly, low-light aquarium plant that grows without specialized substrate or pressurized CO₂, making it well suited for low-tech planted aquariums.

Will the micro-electrolysis mist from the Chihiros Doctor 5 harm my filter's beneficial bacteria? Great for tanks that contain stem plants or species that require good nutrition levels for proper growth. Key Features & Benefits A true all-in-one macro and micro formula bundles nitrogen, phosphate, potassium, iron, and trace minerals, so you don't need secondary bottles. Tailored specifically for non-CO₂ layouts to encourage steady leaf development without overloading the water column. Plant Profile Aquascapers seeking dense fanned foliage among Anubias aquarium plants will find a standout accent in Anubias Nana Peacock. Offering an elegant architectural twist on classic Anubias Nana , this variant is celebrated for its lush, deep green leaves that radiate outward on compact, short petioles to mimic an open peacock tail. Reaching a manageable 3 to 5 inches in height, this aquatic epiphyte attaches its rhizome directly to driftwood or rockwork rather than being buried in substrate. Extremely resilient in low-tech setups, it's a great pick for filling empty hardscape crevices in the foreground or midground of planted aquariums, terrariums, and paludariums. Key Features & Benefits Gracefully fanned leaf arrangement produces a full, rounded rosette effect that softens rigid hardscape junctions. Thick foliage deters grazing from herbivorous cichlids, goldfish, snails, and active dwarf shrimp. Thrives in low-light environments, maintaining rich deep green coloration without specialized equipment. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the horizontal rhizome completely exposed above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable water conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce initial leaf loss. Avoid intense direct light and ensure steady water flow to prevent slow-growing leaves from collecting spot algae. CO₂ is optional but improves growth speed, leaf thickness, and foliage density. Learn more about planting these species by reading our guide on How to Plant Epiphyte Aquatic Plants. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Anubias barteri var. nana 'Peacock' Common Name(s) Anubias Nana Peacock, Anubias Peacock Family Araceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Epiphyte (Rhizome) Care Difficulty Easy / Beginner-Friendly Light Requirement Low to Medium CO2 Requirement Not Required but Beneficial Placement / Usage Foreground Accent, Hardscape Crevices, Midground Focal Point Height / Size 3 – 5 inches Growth Rate Slow (1 leaf every 2-3 weeks) Water Parameters pH 6.0 – 7.5 | Temperature 68°F – 82°F (20°C – 28°C) Propagation Method Separate by Rhizome Division Origin West Africa / Cultivar Frequently Asked Questions 1. How does Anubias Nana Peacock differ from standard Anubias Nana? While standard Anubias Nana features an upright, staggered creeping growth habit along the rhizome, Anubias Nana Peacock develops tightly grouped petioles that fan outward symmetrically in a rosette-like display. This distinctive fanned arrangement gives it a denser, bushier presence in hardscape crevices. 2. Where is the best placement for Anubias Nana Peacock in an aquarium? Because it reaches 3 to 5 inches in height with a broad, radiating spread, it excels as a midground focal point in medium-to-large aquascapes or as a bold foreground anchor in nano tanks. Wedge it directly into rock fissures or driftwood crotches where its fanned canopy softens abrupt hardscape lines. 3. Can Anubias Nana Peacock be grown emersed in high-humidity setups? Yes. Anubias Nana Peacock adapts exceptionally well to emersed growth in humid terrariums, vivariums, and paludariums. Keep ambient humidity levels consistently above 70% and mist the foliage periodically to prevent the broad leaf blades from drying out.

listings.commonName: Bucephalandra Brownie Ghost UNS Tissue Culture
listings.description: Common Name: Bucephalandra Brownie Ghost Tissue culture plants are grown in vitro in a state-of-the-art laboratory specialized in propagating aquatic plants. They provide the best option for those who want to ensure that absolutely zero unwanted pests are introduced into the aquarium. Buce Brownie Ghost is a beautiful variant in the Bucephalandra family group. This aquatic plant is, like almost all Buce, very hardy and can be grown submerged in an aquarium or emerged in a terrarium or paludarium. Like other Bucephalandra species, Brownie Ghost doesn't require too much light and adapts quickly to a wide range of water parameters. Its care is similar to that of Cryptocoryne and Anubias species. It features beautiful coloration that can vary depending on its environment and will easily attach itself to aquarium hardscape material such as stones or aquarium driftwood. If given optimal care, Buce Brownie Ghost can grow to be very beautiful and will also provide a safe haven for smaller aquatic life such as shrimp, fish, and fry! Like all Buce, this aquatic plant grows extremely slowly, and it can take almost half a year for this tissue culture cup to grow in. It can be propagated by cutting the rhizome and attaching it to driftwood and rocks using super glue gel or thread. Important Notes: Bucephalandra is an epiphytic aquarium plant, so it can be attached to aquarium hardscape. Do not plant Bucephalandra in substrate and cover the rhizome. This will cause it to melt and rot. Bucephalandra’s final size, coloration, and growth rate are dependent upon the condition of the aquarium. Photos are a representation of what you will receive and may vary. Tissue culture plants are grown in vitro from a state of the art laboratory specialized in propagating aquatic plants. They provide the best option for those who want to ensure that absolutely zero unwanted pests are introduced into the aquarium. Remove tissue culture gel before planting. Simply wash the gel away or soak the plant in water and squeeze the gel off with your fingers. Do not make drastic changes to the aquarium. Unstable parameters will result in melt and rotting of the aquarium plant. For instructions on how to properly plant tissue culture aquarium plants, click here . CO2 injection will yield better growth. Plant Profile Buce ‘Mini Dark Needle’ is a low-tech, small aquarium plant featuring slender, dark green leaves and striking reddish sheaths on its stems. This variety is highly prized for its needle-like foliage and its ability to adapt to a wide range of water parameters while maintaining a very compact profile. As an epiphyte, it prefers to latch onto wood or stone, whether it’s grown emersed or underwater. It's a beautiful addition to the foreground of a planted tank, where it will slowly sprout from its central rhizome to create a dense, textured colony. Key Features & Notes The thin, pointed leaves provide a unique fine-leaf texture that is perfect for adding intricate detail to small-scale hardscape. The contrast between the deep green leaves and the reddish sheaths adds a subtle but sophisticated pop of color to your planted tank. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for planted tanks where other plants might struggle. Care & Planting Instructions Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard low-light aquarium plant setups, CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and richer iridescence. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth!
