Why is my Bucephalandra melting? Bucephalandra melt can occur after changes in water chemistry, temperature, or lighting. If the rhizome remains firm, keep it attached to hardscape while the plant acclimates and produces new submerged growth. 2. Can I plant Bucephalandra in substrate? Bucephalandra is an epiphyte, so never bury its rhizome in substrate. Attach it to driftwood or rocks, or wedge the roots into hardscape while keeping the rhizome exposed. 3. Is Bucephalandra ‘Mini Dark Needle’ beginner-friendly? Yes. Bucephalandra ‘Mini Dark Needle’ is a beginner-friendly, low-light aquarium plant that grows without specialized substrate or pressurized CO₂, making it well suited for low-tech planted aquariums.

Plant Profile Saxifraga stolonifera, commonly called Strawberry Begonia, is a perennial plant with rounded, scallop-edged leaves covered in fine, velvety hairs with silvery veins and reddish-purple undersides. Because it cannot survive underwater, it is planted strictly above the waterline, growing well along elevated rock ledges, hardscape pockets, or upper terrestrial slopes where its trailing habit can drape naturally. As the plant matures and spreads, its thin thread-like stolons flush a distinct pinkish-red, helping it stand out cleanly against carpets of green mosses and darker hardscape. Key Features & Notes Matures with trailing pinkish-red stolons that create a natural contrast against solid green foliage. Velvety scalloped leaves feature silvery midrib veining paired with soft reddish-purple undersides. Produces miniature daughter plantlets along runners that easily root into nearby damp substrate. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all packing media from the roots. Tuck the root cluster into an airy, well-draining tropical substrate mix of pumice, bark, and perlite on an elevated slope or rock pocket; avoid low, waterlogged soil zones. Provide moderate to bright indirect lighting; harsh direct light can scorch the fuzzy leaf blades, while overly dim conditions reduce leaf color contrast. Water the base directly when the top inch of soil feels dry to the touch, and avoid spraying water directly onto the fuzzy crown to prevent fungal melt. Allow stolon-borne plantlets to develop visible roots before snipping the runner thread to plant them independently. Saxifraga stolonifera are terrestrial plants, and being submerged will result in the death of the plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Saxifraga stolonifera Common Name(s) Strawberry Begonia, Creeping Saxifrage, Strawberry Geranium Family Saxifragaceae Plant Type Terrestrial Stoloniferous Perennial Care Difficulty Easy Light Requirement Shaded Light to Bright Indirect Submersion Suitability Emersed Only (Not for full submersion) Placement / Usage Midground, Hardscape Pockets, Paludarium Upper Banks Height / Size 3"–6" (7.5–15 cm) height; runners trail 18"+ Growth Rate Medium Humidity Requirement Moderate to High (50%–75% RH) Propagation Method Stolon Offsets / Plantlets Origin East Asia (China, Japan, Korea) Frequently Asked Questions 1. Can Saxifraga stolonifera grow fully submerged in an aquarium? No. Saxifraga stolonifera is strictly a terrestrial plant. Submerging its foliage underwater will quickly cause the fuzzy leaves and crown to rot. 2. Why are the fuzzy leaves on my Strawberry Begonia rotting in a terrarium? Crown rot typically happens when excess water sits directly on the fuzzy leaf surfaces or when the soil remains constantly waterlogged. Plant it in an elevated, well-draining spot with gentle airflow. 3. How do you propagate Saxifraga stolonifera? Pin the baby plantlets growing along the ends of the pink stolons directly onto damp soil or sphagnum moss until roots anchor, then clip the connecting runner.

Plant Profile Bacopa Monnieri 'Platinum', commonly known as Variegated Moneywort or Water Hyssop, is a rare and striking variegated cultivar of the classic hobby staple. Characterized by thick, rigid vertical stems lined with opposite pairs of rounded, fleshy leaves, this variety displays a marble-like pattern of crisp mint green and pale cream-white tones. Exceptionally hardy and adaptable, it easily reaches 4 to 12 inches in height. Perfect for beginners and experienced aquascapers alike, Bacopa Platinum serves as a low-maintenance, high-contrast accent in midground and background zones. Key Features & Benefits Rare variegated foliage displays a beautiful, high-contrast mix of cream-white and mint-green tones. Thick, upright columnar stems form structured vertical accents in midground and background zones. Hardy and adaptable species ideal for beginners; can be grown submerged or emersed in paludariums, where it produces tiny white flowers. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. * Bacopa leaves are fragile, so handle stems with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to insert individual stems 1 to 2 inches deep into aquarium soil. Provide moderate to high lighting to ensure light reaches the lower stems and prevents leaf shedding; while CO2 is not strictly required, supplying pressurized CO2 injection and regular fertilization promotes thicker stems and bolder cream variegation. Maintain clean water conditions and stable water parameters to encourage steady root development. To propagate, simply cut main stems with sharp straight shears and replant trimmings directly into substrate; cut stems will readily anchor and sprout new growth. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Bacopa monnieri 'Platinum' Common Name(s) Bacopa Monnieri Platinum, Variegated Moneywort, Water Hyssop Family Plantaginaceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Stem Plant Care Difficulty Easy Light Requirement Moderate to High CO2 Requirement Optional / Not Necessary (Recommended for faster growth) Placement / Usage Midground / Background Accent Height / Size 4–12”+ Growth Rate Slow to Moderate Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 Propagation Method Cuttings (Cut main stems or lateral shoots and replant) Origin Widespread / Cosmopolitan Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I prep bunched Bacopa Monnieri Platinum before planting? Remove the lead weight or metal band along with the cotton or foam surrounding the lower roots under room-temperature water. Gently inspect stem bases, trim away any bruised tissue, and use pinsettes to plant individual stems directly into substrate. 2. How do I maintain strong cream variegation on Bacopa Platinum? Variegated plants like Bacopa Monnieri 'Platinum' require moderate-to-high lighting to maintain their pale cream-and-green leaf patterns. Under low lighting, stems may grow leggy and leaf variegation may become less pronounced. 3. Can Bacopa Monnieri Platinum be grown out of water? Yes! Bacopa Monnieri Platinum transitions very easily to emersed growth in terrariums, paludariums, or open-top setups, where it forms creeping terrestrial mats and produces delicate white-to-pink flowers.

Plant Profile Having trouble deciding which crypts to choose for your next aquascape? The Assorted Cryptocoryne Plant Pack offers a collection of versatile, low-maintenance species to fill out your aquascape with rich texture and natural color. Known for their hardiness once rooted, crypts are ideal for low-light setups, community tanks, and betta aquariums. Each bundle provides hand-selected potted plants that adapt across foreground, midground, and background placements. As with all crypt plants, they can be sensitive to sudden parameter shifts and strongly object to being relocated once planted. Given a permanent home in your substrate, however, their sturdy stems mature into an eye-catching, long-lasting display that adds rich structural depth. What You Might Receive Each pack includes 5 distinct species selected based on current farm health and availability. Potential species include: Cryptocoryne Wendtii Green – Classic, bright green midground favorite with slightly wavy edges. Cryptocoryne Lucens – Slender, upright bright green foliage that forms neat rosettes. Cryptocoryne Wendtii Brown – Rich bronze and dark chocolate-tinted leaf surfaces. Cryptocoryne Mioya – Ruffled-edge leaves that transition from emerald to copper-brown. Cryptocoryne Tropica – Heavily textured, hammered brown leaves for compact accents. Cryptocoryne Lutea – Elegant green-to-bronze leaves with gracefully wavy margins. Cryptocoryne Beckettii – Reddish-brown, ruffled foliage that creates warmth in low-tech setups. ...and many other premium Cryptocoryne species ! *Note: Species selection is subject to change at any time based on fresh inventory availability. Requests to exchange species or make custom substitutions cannot be accommodated. Available Pack Sizes & Tank Sizing 5 Pack (5 Pots Total): Includes 1 pot each of 5 distinct Cryptocoryne species. Ideal for 5–10 gallon aquariums (such as UNS 5N, 3N, 25C, 30C, 60S, 45U, 45S, 60L). 10 Pack (10 Pots Total): Includes 2 pots each of 5 distinct Cryptocoryne species. Ideal for 10–20 gallon aquariums (such as UNS 40C, 45U, 60U, 60S, 90L, 90LS). 15 Pack (15 Pots Total): Includes 3 pots each of 5 distinct Cryptocoryne species. Ideal for 20–30+ gallon aquariums (such as UNS 60U, 90L). Key Features & Benefits Curated assortment of 5 distinct Cryptocoryne species provides instant color, texture, and height diversity for low-tech aquascapes. Offers incredible value and variety for aquascapers looking to plant out foreground and midground zones efficiently. Hardy, root-feeding rosette plants thrive across low to medium lighting, making them ideal for betta tanks and community aquariums. Frequently Asked Questions 1. Can I request specific plants for my Assorted Cryptocoryne Plant Pack? Due to fluctuating farm harvest and inventory levels, species are pre-selected daily to ensure you receive the healthiest plants possible. Requests for specific species, modifications, or exchanges cannot be accommodated. 2. How do I plant the potted crypts once they arrive? Remove each plant from its plastic pot and carefully peel away the cotton rockwool surrounding the roots. Gently separate individual rosettes or keep them in small clumps, then use planting tweezers to push the subterranean root system deep into quality aquarium soil or sand with root tabs. 3. Do I need CO2 injection to grow an Assorted Cryptocoryne aquarium? No, Cryptocoryne species are adaptable and thrive in low-tech setups without pressurized CO2. While CO2 injection and nutrient-dense soil will accelerate growth speed and leaf density, standard low-to-medium lighting and rich substrate nutrients are more than enough to achieve healthy, long-term growth.

Plant Profile Java Fern Windelov 'Hybrid' is an extraordinary cultivar that fuses distinctive characteristics from both traditional Windelov and Coral varieties into one striking low-light aquarium plant. Featuring broader, fatter leaf blades than classic Java Fern or standard Windelov , its fronds terminate in randomized, outward-branching split tips that create an organic, bushy look. Staying compact at 3 to 5 inches in height, it serves as an exceptional textured centerpiece in midground hardscape layouts or high-humidity terrarium environments. Key Features & Notes Tough, fibrous foliage easily withstands curious nipping from herbivorous fish like cichlids, goldfish, and large snails. Fatter leaf blades with randomized, outward-branching split tips combine Windelov and Coral traits for a bushy, organic aesthetic. Exceptional hardiness lets it thrive in non-CO2 tanks and low-light environments. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Java Fern Windelov 'Hybrid' is an epiphytic fern that should be attached to rocks or driftwood with aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as it will rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard setups, gentle water movement and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and broader fronds. Master long-term care and troubleshoot common leaf issues by checking out our Java Fern Care Guide . Final size and foliage pattern depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Leptochilus pteropus ) Common Name(s) Java Fern Windelov 'Hybrid', Windelov Hybrid Fern Family Polypodiaceae Plant Type Epiphyte (Rhizome Fern) Care Difficulty Beginner / Easy (Low-Tech Compatible) Light Requirement Low to Medium CO2 Requirement Not Required (Beneficial) Placement / Usage Midground, Focal Hardscape Accent, Terrariums Height / Size 3"–5" (7.5–13 cm) Growth Rate Slow to Moderate Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 | Temperature 68°F–82°F (20°C–28°C) Propagation Method Rhizome Division & Adventitious Plantlets Origin Indonesia / Cultivated Hybrid Variety Frequently Asked Questions 1. What makes Java Fern Windelov 'Hybrid' different from standard Windelov? The Windelov 'Hybrid' features noticeably wider, fatter leaf blades compared to the slender fronds of standard Windelov. Additionally, its split tips branch outward in a more randomized, organic fashion reminiscent of Java Fern Coral, creating a denser, fuller bush in your aquascape. 2. Why are there small black spots and tiny leaves growing under my Java Fern Windelov 'Hybrid' leaves? Do not panic; your plant is not diseased! Java Fern reproduces naturally through adventitious plantlets. Small dark bumps (sporangia) form along the undersides of mature leaves, sprouting tiny brown roots and mini green fronds. Once these baby plantlets develop 3–4 leaves, you can gently pop them off the mother leaf and glue them elsewhere in your aquarium. 3. Can I plant Java Fern Windelov 'Hybrid' into substrate? No. Java Fern Windelov 'Hybrid' is an epiphyte that absorbs nutrients directly from the water column through its foliage and fine root network. If you bury its horizontal rhizome beneath aquarium soil, sand, or gravel, the stem will suffocate, rot, and die. Always attach it to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread. 4. Will fish like cichlids or goldfish eat Java Fern Windelov 'Hybrid'? Generally, no. Java Fern leaves are thick, fibrous, and contain bitter-tasting compounds that deter most plant-eating fish. While aggressive diggers might knock it off hardscape if not glued securely, they rarely consume the foliage.

Common Name: Water Poppy Hydrocleys nymphoides is an aquatic plant known for its glossy green leaves and bright yellow, poppy-like flowers. Found in shallow waters, it's a beautiful and functional choice for ponds or paludariums that have an emersed section. Water poppies add texture and simultaneously help filter water, ensuring your setup is clean and healthy. This plant is generally easy to care for, but needs strong lighting. In outdoor settings, it prefers full sun exposure for a minimum of 6 hours. If you plan on growing it indoors, we recommend placing it in an area that receives plenty of light to support growth. Once it takes off, trim it regularly to manage its spread. It can be propagated easily by trimming along its runners and replanting. Notes: While Water Poppies can float, they grow best when planted in nutritious aquarium soil. Plant them in shallow areas of your setup and if needed, add extra nutrients with root tabs or an aquatic plant fertilizer. Not frost-hardy. In colder climates, keep your plant indoors and provide good lighting. Photos are a representation of what you will receive and may vary. Please research appropriately to ensure your plant thrives. Plant Profile Pre-attached to a natural piece of driftwood, this adaptable classic features slender, ruffled leaves that transition from rich emerald green to warm copper-brown tones. As with all crypt plants, it can be sensitive to sudden changes in parameters and strongly objects to being relocated once it's settled in your tank. Place this ready-to-display piece into your midground, however, and its established roots will continue to anchor into the wood, creating a lush, self-sustaining focal point that brings dynamic texture to your layout. Key Features & Benefits Pre-attached to natural hardscape for instant placement without the need for delicate substrate planting. Can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups, where mature plants may produce flowering spathes. Care & Planting Instructions Position the driftwood directly into your midground layout; no rockwool prep or tying required. Ensure the surrounding environment provides steady nutrients via liquid fertilizers or root contact with nutrient-rich substrate. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth and fuller foliage density, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving the driftwood piece repeatedly may trigger leaf loss. Cryptocoryne species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting rhizome offshoots or replanting new plantlets. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I plant Cryptocoryne Mioya on Driftwood? There is no planting required. Simply place the entire driftwood piece directly onto your substrate or nestle it into your existing hardscape layout. 2. How do I help my Cryptocoryne recover if it melts? Trim away dissolving leaves, maintain stable water parameters, and leave the root system undisturbed on the wood so it can rebuild new foliage. Check our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt for full recovery steps. 3. Should I use root tabs or liquid fertilizers? While root tabs work if the driftwood rests directly on nutrient substrate, liquid all-in-one fertilizers or root tabs tucked under the wood base help feed roots clinging to the hardscape.

Plant Profile Davallia parvula is a miniature epiphytic fern prized by scapers for its micro-divided, lace-like fronds and distinctive hairy rhizomes. Growing across moist rock faces and tree bark in nature, it is a versatile pick for collections of terrarium plants that need fine, moss-like texture without aggressive rambling. Its creeping rhizomes anchor securely across damp wood, cork bark, or background walls while fronds unfurl in airy layers. As one of the most adaptable humidity-loving plants for enclosed glass, it creates a soft, aged aesthetic when given bright indirect light and good airflow. Key Features & Notes Micro-divided fronds and fuzzy creeping rhizomes create a dense, natural moss-like texture. Epiphytic habit allows easy mounting onto damp driftwood, background panels, and porous stone. Compact growth rate keeps foliage neat without crowding out neighboring slow-growing species. Care & Planting Instructions Affix the creeping rhizome onto damp driftwood, lava rock, or cork bark using thread or plant glue, keeping the main hairy stem exposed rather than buried deep in soil. Maintain humidity between 65% and 85%, ensuring the rhizome stays damp while allowing delicate fronds to dry slightly between mistings. Snip yellowing or older outer fronds close to the rhizome with sharp shears to encourage fresh fiddleheads and improve airflow. Note that each bare-root order includes an established rhizome portion with 2 to 4 healthy fronds ready for mounting. Davallia parvula are terrestrial plants, and being submerged will result in the death of the plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Can Davallia parvula survive in a closed terrarium? Yes. It thrives in high-humidity glass enclosures when mounted on wood or rock, provided foliage is not kept constantly waterlogged. 2. Should the fuzzy rhizome of Davallia parvula be buried under soil? No. Burying the rhizome causes it to rot. Fasten it directly onto moist wood, rock, or sphagnum moss with the top exposed. 3. How do you propagate Davallia parvula? Cut a section of healthy creeping rhizome that contains at least two healthy fronds and roots, then pin it to damp moss until established.

listings.commonName: Drosera Spatulata 'Lovellae' Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Drosera spatulata 'Lovellae' is a compact, vibrant carnivorous plant named for its spoon-shaped (spatulate) leaves lined with glistening, dew-like glandular tentacles. While traditional aquatic foreground plants rely on substrate nutrients, sundews evolved in nutrient-poor bogs across Australasia and Asia, perfecting a clever biological workaround: catching their own snacks. The sticky mucilage droplets act as a natural flypaper to trap fungus gnats and fruit flies, digesting them for nitrogen while adding a gleaming texture to high-humidity setups. This species is strictly an emersed grower designed for humid terrariums, vivariums, and paludarium shorelines. Tissue Culture cups ensure your setup gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, or unwanted mold. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained enclosure. Key Features & Benefits Spoon-shaped leaves covered in sticky, dew-like tentacles function as a natural insect trap for fungus gnats. Compact, subtropical species that does not require a winter dormancy period, making it easy to keep indoors year-round. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers under cool water before planting. Plant in low-nutrient, acidic substrates such as pure peat moss mixed with perlite or silica sand (avoid regular potting soil or fertilized aquasoil, as mineral salts will burn its roots). Water exclusively with distilled water, reverse osmosis (RO) water, or clean rainwater. Tap water minerals will cause the plant to decline over time. Provide strong, bright lighting to coax out deep red coloration and support fast rosette expansion. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Drosera spatulata 'Lovellae' Common Name(s) Spoon-Leaf Sundew, Round-Leaf Sundew Family Droseraceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Terrestrial Carnivorous Rosette Care Difficulty Easy Light Requirement Moderate to High (Bright indirect to direct grow light) Placement / Usage Terrarium Foreground / Paludarium Shoreline (Emersed Only) Height / Size 1-3 inches Growth Rate Fast Water Parameters pH 4.5 – 6.5 (Low TDS) | Temperature 65°F – 80°F (18°C – 27°C) Propagation Method Division of adventitious shoots or seed production Origin Australasia, East Asia Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I plant Drosera Spatulata 'Lovellae' tissue culture? Rinse away the nutrient gel with distilled or RO water, divide the rosette clumps carefully, and use tweezers to set each plantlet into a damp peat-and-perlite mixture in a high-humidity container. 2. Can Drosera Spatulata 'Lovellae' be grown fully submerged underwater in an aquarium? No. Drosera spatulata is an emersed bog plant and will drown if fully submerged underwater. It thrives on damp soil in terrariums, vivariums, or paludarium land sections where its leaves remain exposed to air. 3. Why isn't my Drosera producing sticky dew on its leaves? A lack of dew is usually caused by low ambient humidity or insufficient lighting. Increasing light levels and enclosing the plant in a high-humidity terrarium environment will trigger the tentacles to produce glistening droplets within a few days.

listings.commonName: Drosera Spatulata 'Labill' Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Drosera spatulata 'Labill' Aquatic Farmer Tissue Culture, commonly known as the Spoon-Leaf Sundew, is a compact carnivorous plant native to sunny, nutrient-poor bogs across the Asia-Pacific region. It forms neat, low-lying rosettes of spoon-shaped leaves densely lined with glistening, sticky glandular tentacles that turn vibrant reddish-pink under bright lighting. In a setup with damp, mineral-free soil, its dewy traps serve as a natural controller for stray gnats while adding a unique functional highlight to humid vivarium layouts and open terrarium displays. Key Features & Notes Spoon-shaped rosette leaves feature dewy, sticky tentacles that blush vivid red in bright light. Compact size makes it an excellent carnivorous accent for damp, high-humidity setups. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers under cool water before planting. Press the small rosettes gently into nutrient-poor, acidic substrate like pure sphagnum moss or a peat moss and perlite blend; avoid standard potting soils or fertilizers. Maintain high ambient moisture and keep the substrate consistently damp using distilled, reverse osmosis, or rainwater to protect sensitive roots. Provide moderate to bright indirect lighting to encourage rich crimson leaf coloration and active mucilage production. Drosera spatulata are terrestrial plants, and being submerged will result in the death of the plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Drosera spatulata 'Labill' Common Name(s) Spoon-Leaf Sundew, Round Leaf Sundew Family Droseraceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Terrestrial Carnivorous Rosette Care Difficulty Easy Light Requirement Moderate to Bright (Indirect) Submersion Suitability Emersed Only (Not for full submersion) Placement / Usage Foreground, Moist Moss Beds, Bog Layouts Height / Size 1"–3" (2.5–7.5 cm) Growth Rate Fast Humidity Requirement Moderate to High (> 60% RH) Propagation Method Flower Stalk Cuttings / Leaf Offsets Origin Asia-Pacific / Australasia Frequently Asked Questions 1. What kind of water should I use for Drosera spatulata? Always use mineral-free water such as distilled, RO (reverse osmosis), or rainwater. Tap water containing minerals or dissolved salts will build up in the substrate over time and burn the delicate root system. 2. Can Drosera Spatulata 'Labill' be grown fully submerged underwater in an aquarium? No. Drosera spatulata is an emersed bog plant and will drown if fully submerged underwater. It thrives on damp soil in terrariums, vivariums, or paludarium land sections where its leaves remain exposed to air. 3. How do I propagate Drosera spatulata as it grows? Drosera spatulata propagates easily by forming offset rosettes around the base, producing seeds from flower stalks, or producing plantlets along leaf cuttings placed on damp sphagnum moss.

listings.commonName: UNS Pro Aquascaping Tools - Black Straight Pinsettes
listings.description: Product Overview There is a special kind of heartbreak in watching a newly planted stem float straight back to the surface the second you pull your fingers out of the tank. But fear not, these UNS Pro Black Straight Pinsettes (10" / 25cm) exist so you can stop playing stem-plant tag. Crafted from rust-resistant stainless steel with a sleek matte black finish, these 10-inch aquarium tweezers give you the vertical reach and downward leverage needed to anchor tissue cultures, hairgrass plugs, and deep-root stems straight into aquasoil without disrupting your surrounding hardscape layout. Key Features & Benefits Straight-Tip Accuracy: Ideal for general aquascaping and planting straight down into open substrate, providing direct downward force without slipping. Serrated Precision Grip: Micro-serrations at the tips hold plant stems securely without crushing delicate foliage or root structures. Ergonomic Comfort: Features an expanded finger contact area and balanced spring tension to reduce hand fatigue during long planting sessions. Matte Black Protective Finish: Formulated for high corrosion resistance and a clean, modern aesthetic that looks great in any aquascaping toolkit. Technical Specifications Attribute Specification Brand Ultum Nature Systems (UNS) Product Line UNS Pro Aquascaping Tools Tool Type Straight Aquascaping Pinsettes / Tweezers Overall Length 10 inches (25 cm) Material High-Grade Stainless Steel Finish / Color Matte Black Corrosion-Resistant Coating Tip Design Straight with Fine Micro-Serrations Ideal For Plant Types Stem Plants (Rotala, Ludwigia), Carpeting Plants, Tissue Culture Recommended Tank Size Nano to Medium Aquariums Care & Maintenance Instructions Rinse thoroughly with fresh tap water immediately after using in aquariums, especially after water changes or dosing liquid fertilizers. Wipe completely dry with a soft cloth between uses to extend the life of the black finish and prevent mineral staining. Store in a clean, dry tool holder or rack away from high-humidity areas to maintain optimal spring tension. Frequently Asked Questions 1. When should I use straight pinsettes instead of curved pinsettes? Straight pinsettes are best for vertical planting in open areas and deep substrate beds. They allow you to apply direct, downward pressure when inserting root-heavy stem plants or hairgrass plugs. Curved pinsettes, on the other hand, are better for reaching under overhanging rocks, driftwood, or tight hardscape crevices. 2. Will the black coating peel or leach chemicals into my aquarium water? No. UNS Pro Tools feature a durable, inert coating specifically tested for aquarium safety. It will not leach harmful chemicals or harm sensitive inhabitants like dwarf shrimp or fish fry. To preserve the finish, avoid using abrasive scrubbers when cleaning. 3. How do I prevent stems from pulling back out of the soil when I remove the tweezers? Hold the stem near the roots with the pinsettes at a slight 45-degree angle, push deep into the aquasoil, open the tips slightly, and wiggle the tool gently side-to-side as you pull upward. The surrounding substrate will collapse over the roots, holding the plant securely in place.

Plant Profile Common Name: Bucephalandra Nanga Pinoh Buce ‘Nanga Pinoh Tangerine’ is a low-tech, beginner-friendly aquarium plant featuring oblong leaves with gently wavy edges and subtly colored stems. This variety displays a vibrant, bright green coloration that provides a refreshing pop of contrast against darker hardscape or substrate. Highly versatile, this epiphytic plant can be grown submerged or emersed, usually attached to hardscape such as driftwood or rocks rather than being buried in traditional aquarium substrate. It’s a beautiful addition to the midground in a planted tank, where its moderate size allows it to create a dense, textured colony. Key Features & Notes The "Tangerine" variant is prized for its bright green leaves and warm-toned stems, offering a lighter aesthetic than many darker Buce species. The gentle ruffling along the leaf margins adds organic detail and a sense of "movement" to your hardscape layout. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for planted tanks where other plants might struggle. It is perfectly at home fully submerged in an aquarium or emersed in a high-humidity terrarium, vivarium, or paludarium. Care Tips & Preparation Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood . Never bury the rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Carefully remove the plant from its pot and clear away all rockwool from the roots. For a deep dive on prepping potted plants, click here . Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting. Unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance, CO2 injection will yield much faster growth. We recommend researching your specific water chemistry to ensure your plant thrives. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions. Please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Please research appropriately to ensure your plant thrives. Additional Information Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Family Name: Araceae Origin: Borneo (Endemic) Skill Level: Easy Growth Rate: Slow Light: Low to Medium CO2: Not necessary but recommended pH Range: 6.0 – 7.5 Propagation: Divide the rhizome with sharp scissors

Plant Profile Selaginella pulvinata is an evergreen lycophyte characterized by densely tufted branches that grow in tight rosette-like rosettes, eventually forming an intertwined, woody trunk reminiscent of a miniature cypress tree. Thriving strictly in humid terrestrial conditions, its rich green scaly foliage provides immediate scale and depth when nestled into crevices of dark lava rock or tucked against driftwood. Native to exposed limestone rock faces, this species is a true resurrection plant, as during periods of low moisture, its branch tips curl tightly inward into dry, claw-like yellowish clusters to protect the growing crown, unfurling back into flat, vibrant emerald rosettes within hours of receiving water. Key Features & Notes Intertwined stems and exposed rootlets mature into a distinct miniature tree-like profile. Curling resurrection habit allows fronds to close during brief dry spells and reopen with moisture. Pairs naturally alongside trailing mosses and humidity-loving plants in terrariums or vivariums. Care & Planting Instructions Tuck the root base into a well-draining, airy substrate mix of bark, pumice, and sphagnum moss, or wedge it directly into hardscape crevices where water cannot pool stagnant around the crown. Provide low to moderate indirect lighting; harsh direct light can scorch the tips and trigger prolonged curling. Maintain humidity above 70% while ensuring adequate ventilation, as perpetually soggy or waterlogged roots will lead to yellowing fronds and stem melt. Trim damaged or dead lower branchlets near the base with sharp shears to maintain a tidy rosette form. Selaginella pulvinata are terrestrial plants, and being submerged will result in the death of the plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Selaginella pulvinata Common Name(s) Cushion Spikemoss, Resurrection Spikemoss Family Selaginellaceae Plant Type Lycophyte / Rosette Spikemoss Care Difficulty Easy Light Requirement Low to Medium (Indirect / Filtered) Submersion Suitability Emersed Only (Not for full submersion) Placement / Usage Midground, Hardscape Crevices, Paludarium Rock Ledges Height / Size 2"–6" (5–15 cm) Growth Rate Slow to Moderate Humidity Requirement High (> 70% RH) Propagation Method Division / Stem Cuttings Origin East Asia Frequently Asked Questions 1. Can Selaginella pulvinata survive in a closed terrarium? Yes. It thrives in enclosed glass containers as long as it is planted in loose, gritty substrate with good drainage rather than waterlogged soil. 2. Why are the fronds on my Selaginella pulvinata curling up and turning brown? Inward curling fronds indicate low ambient humidity or a dry root zone. Mist the plant thoroughly or increase enclosure humidity to prompt the rosettes to reopen. 3. How do you propagate Selaginella pulvinata? Carefully separate individual rooted rosettes from the parent cluster during maintenance, or take short stem branchlets and anchor them onto damp, porous rock or moss.

Plant Profile Selaginella sp. 'Brown', commonly known as Spikemoss, features feathery, branching microphylls that take on warm bronze and earthy brown undertones under moderate lighting. It can creep laterally to form a dense, mossy mat or scramble upward across textured background moss walls and wet hardscape in emersed setups like terrariums or paludariums. While it demands steady moisture, it is strictly an emersed species requiring constant air circulation, because letting the roots sit in stagnant, waterlogged mud or submerging it underwater is a fast track to rot. Key Features & Notes Feathery, scale-like microphylls display warm bronze and earthy brown tones. Scrambling growth habit easily scales damp background panels and hardscape. High humidity tolerance allows steady growth in shaded, low-light zones. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Anchor the root cluster or stem runners against damp sphagnum moss, background foam, or an airy tropical substrate mix, keeping the foliage above the water line. Position under low to moderate indirect lighting, avoiding intense direct beams that scorch the delicate foliage and bleach its bronze coloration. Maintain ambient relative humidity above 75% while ensuring the substrate drains freely, as stagnant, soggy soil can cause yellowing and root rot. Prune spreading runners regularly with sharp shears to control its footprint or redirect climbing stems along background panels. Note that Selaginella species are strictly terrestrial and cannot survive submerged underwater in an aquarium. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Selaginella sp. 'Brown' Common Name(s) Spikemoss, Brown Spikemoss Family Selaginellaceae Plant Type Terrestrial Lycophyte / Creeping Spikemoss Care Difficulty Easy Light Requirement Low to Moderate Indirect Submersion Suitability Emersed Only (Not for full submersion) Placement / Usage Terrarium Floor, Living Backgrounds, Vivarium Walls Height / Spread Height: 4.00"–6.00" (10–15 cm) | Spreading climber Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Humidity Requirement High (> 75% RH) Propagation Method Stem Cuttings & Runner Division Origin Tropical Africa & Brazil Frequently Asked Questions 1. Can Selaginella sp. Brown grow submerged in an aquarium? No. Selaginella sp. Brown is a terrestrial spikemoss, not an aquatic plant. Submerging its delicate fronds underwater cuts off oxygen exchange, causing the entire plant to melt and disintegrate within days. 2. Why are the fronds on my Selaginella turning yellow or mushy? Yellowing, translucent, or mushy foliage typically indicates waterlogged, stagnant soil around the roots. Ensure your planting medium contains perlite, pumice, or tree fern fiber for aeration, and empty standing water pools from the bottom of your setup. 3. How do I get Selaginella sp. Brown to climb a background wall? Pin fresh runners directly against a damp background made of hygrolon, cork bark, or epiweb using stainless steel floral pins or small toothpicks. In high ambient humidity, the stems will anchor into the surface with adventitious roots within a few weeks.

listings.commonName: Aquario Neo Solution Complex - Liquid Fertilizer
listings.description: Aquario Neo Solution Complex is a complete, all-in-one fertilizer for planted aquariums. It provides key nutrients such as nitrogen, potassium, phosphate, and magnesium, while also supplying essential trace elements like iron, boron, molybdenum, and calcium to support healthy, balanced aquatic plant growth. Its formula is enriched with Neo Booster Plants, enhancing nutrient absorption and promoting more vibrant coloration. This convenient solution combines the benefits of Neo Solution 1 and 2 in a single product. Dosage & Directions 1 capful (on 300ml bottles) = 5ml Shake well before use. listings.commonName: Aquario Neo C Plants - Water Conditioner
listings.description: Aquario Neo C Plants is a specialized water conditioner designed for planted aquariums. Its formula neutralizes chlorine and heavy metals while supporting overall tank and aquatic plant health. Formulated with Neo Essence and Neo Booster Plants, this water conditioner contains organic carbon, natural amino acids, and chelating agents that support nutrient uptake, helping aquatic plants grow faster, strong, and with richer color. While an improvement in growth will be noticeable, Neo C Plants itself is not a fertilizer. Instead, it supports the ability to absorb nutrients already readily available in the water. Beyond plant benefits, Neo C Plants promotes a balanced environment by supporting beneficial bacteria, improving fish digestion and reducing oxidative stress. Natural humic acid in the formula boosts livestock activity and bacterial performance, while natural minerals and betaine contribute trace elements and digestive support for resilience. This product is safe to use with your existing fertilizer routine and CO2 system! Usage and Notes: One capful (5ml) treats 200 Liters of tap water (approximately 52 gallons). When dosing directly into the tank, use it according to the capacity of the tank. If treating water that is added, dose according to the volume of water being added to the tank. Plant Profile Samolus parviflorus ‘Red’ is a hardy stem plant with soft red, orange, and bronze foliage that slowly builds into compact, full bushes. Give it medium to high light, and it leans into its pinks and reds; keep light low, and it settles back into greens and oranges. Under richer nutrients and brighter conditions, its leaves round out and deepen into lush crimson‑and‑copper tones, making it an easy way to slip midground color into Dutch‑style and nature layouts. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Soft red, copper, and orange foliage forms lush midground bushes and focal points. Slow-to-moderate growth, low-maintenance, and easy to keep neatly shaped. Hardy, flexible care, adds warm accent color without extreme maintenance. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stem clusters 1 to 2 inches into nutrient-rich substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower growth. Provide moderate-to-high lighting. While adaptable under medium light, adding pressurized CO2 and iron supplementation encourages rounder leaves and deeper red tones. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Propagate by separating dense stem clusters or trimming shoot tops with straight scissors, replanting trimmings directly into the substrate. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Samolus parviflorus 'Red' Common Name(s) Samolus Parviflorus Red, Red Samolus Family Primulaceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Stem Plant Care Difficulty Easy to Intermediate Light Requirement Moderate to High CO2 Requirement Recommended (Essential for fuller, redder leaves) Placement / Usage Midground Bushing Height / Size 4–8”+ Growth Rate Slow to Moderate Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 Propagation Method Separate clusters / Stem Cuttings Origin South China / Cultivated Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I get my Samolus Parviflorus Red to display deep red colors? Providing stronger lighting, pressurized CO2, a nutrient-dense aquarium soil, and regular iron dosing encourages deeper, richer red and copper hues. Under low lighting or poor nutrients, the foliage may revert to thinner, greener growth. 3. How do I transition Samolus Parviflorus Red from emersed to submerged growth? When transitioning from emersed to submerged growth, plant bare stems securely into rich substrate under moderate-to-high lighting and keep water parameters stable. As new growth adapts, the plant will shed its land foliage and sprout fuller, colorful underwater leaves. Once new shoots develop, trim away old lower growth to encourage compact branching.

listings.commonName: Bucephalandra Nanga Pinoh UNS Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Buce ‘Nanga Pinoh’ is a low-tech aquarium plant featuring narrow, elongated leaves with subtle ruffled edges and a deep green hue that can take on a bluish sheen under quality lighting. Because of its compact growth, this hardy epiphyte is ideal for tucking into dark hardscape crevices or attaching onto driftwood. Like all other Buce, it thrives submerged or emersed as long as its rhizome remains unburied, making it a beginner-friendly choice for adding lasting color and visual depth to the foreground or midground of planted tanks. Tissue culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab-grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go-to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Notes With moderate lighting and proper nutrients, the elongated leaves of Nanga Pinoh can display a stunning metallic blue luster. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for planted tanks where other plants might struggle. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by carefully removing the plantlets from the cup and rinsing away all sterile nutrient gel under lukewarm, dechlorinated water before mounting. Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood with aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as it will rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard low-light aquarium plant setups, CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and a smoother tissue culture transition. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Bucephalandra sp. 'Nanga Pinoh' Common Name(s) Buce Nanga Pinoh UNS Tissue Culture, Nanga Pinoh TC Family Araceae Plant Type Epiphyte (Tissue Culture) Care Difficulty Beginner / Easy (Low-Tech Compatible) Light Requirement Low to Medium CO2 Requirement Recommended for TC transition (Accelerates growth) Placement / Usage Foreground Detail, Midground Accent, Hardscape Crevices Height / Size 0.5"–1.5" (1.0–3.5 cm) Growth Rate Slow Water Parameters pH 6.0–8.0 | Temperature 68°F–80°F (20°C–26°C) Propagation Method Rhizome Division (Separate with sharp shears) Origin Borneo (Endemic / Lab Cultivated) Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I prepare tissue culture Bucephalandra for planting? Gently remove the plant from its plastic cup, rinse off all the nutrient gel under lukewarm water, and separate the plant into smaller clumps before attaching them to driftwood or rock using aquarium-safe glue or thread. 2. Why is my tissue culture Bucephalandra melting after planting? Tissue culture plants undergo an acclimation phase when transitioning to underwater conditions. Maintain stable water parameters, good circulation, and moderate light; as long as the rhizome stays firm, new submerged leaves will emerge. 3. Can tissue culture Bucephalandra be planted in substrate? Yes, you can push the roots into substrate or gravel to help anchor the plantlet. However, you must keep the central horizontal rhizome completely exposed above the substrate line, as burying the rhizome starves it of circulation and causes rot.

listings.commonName: UNS Stainless Steel Algae Brush Set
listings.description: Product Overview Scrubbing stubborn algae off hardscape surfaces without scratching your rockwork or damaging intricate driftwood detail requires the right bristle for the job. The UNS Stainless Steel Algae Brush Set includes two specialized cleaning tools engineered specifically for hardscape maintenance. Precision-crafted from durable stainless steel, this 2-pack set equips you with both hard and soft bristle options to strip away tough green spot algae, black beard algae, and organic buildup across your entire layout. Key Features & Benefits Dual-Brush Cleaning Set: Comes as a 2-pack featuring one hard-bristle brush and one soft-bristle brush for tailored algae removal. Abrasive Stone Brush: Hard, wavy bristles aggressively strip away stubborn green spot algae, spot treatment residue, and crusty buildup on rocks and hard stones. Gentle Surface Brush: Softer bristles clean delicate driftwood, wood crevices, and decor without gouging soft wood fibers or scratching surfaces. Stainless Steel Construction: Forged from durable, corrosion-resistant stainless steel for long-lasting performance during routine water changes. Technical Specifications Attribute Specification Brand Ultum Nature Systems (UNS) Product Line UNS Aquascaping Tools Tool Type Aquarium Algae Scrubbing Brush Set (2-Pack) Overall Length 5.91 inches (15 cm) Material Stainless Steel Handle & Specialized Bristles Included Brushes 1x Hard Bristle (Stones/Rocks) & 1x Soft Bristle (Wood/Decor) Ideal For Algae Types Green Spot Algae (GSA), Black Beard Algae (BBA), & Biofilm Buildup Recommended Tank Size Nano to Large Aquariums Care & Maintenance Instructions Rinse thoroughly with fresh tap water immediately after scrubbing algae or using during liquid spot treatments. Wipe completely dry with a soft cloth after each use to prevent mineral buildup and extend brush life. Store in a clean, dry tool holder or rack away from high-humidity areas to maintain bristle integrity. Frequently Asked Questions 1. Which brush should I use on dragon stone, seiryu stone, or lava rock? Use the hard-bristle brush for hard aquascaping stones like Seiryu stone, Lava rock, or Dragon stone. The wavy, stiff bristles dig into porous stone surfaces to scrub away persistent green spot algae and black beard algae. 2. Can I use these brushes on aquarium glass or acrylic panels? No. These brushes are specifically designed for hardscape elements like rocks, stones, and driftwood. Using metal or abrasive scrubbing brushes on glass or acrylic tank walls can cause surface scratches. Use dedicated glass scraper blades or soft algae sponges for tank panels. 3. How do I identify the algae in my tank and fix the root cause? While manual scrubbing keeps hardscape clean, balancing light, CO2, and nutrient levels is key to long-term prevention. Check out our comprehensive Aquascaper's Guide to an Algae-Free Tank to identify your specific algae type and restore balance to your aquarium.

listings.commonName: UNS Pro Aquascaping Tools - Grey Straight Scissors
listings.description: Product Overview Doing heavy bulk trimming with awkward, cheap scissors will leave your wrists sore and your plant stems crushed. But fear not, the UNS Pro Grey Straight Scissors (10" / 25cm) will help you execute clean, razor-sharp cuts across your aquascape with total comfort. Precision-crafted from rust-resistant stainless steel with a clean matte grey finish, these 10-inch aquascaping straight scissors feature an upgraded Pro tail grip (finger rest) to give you extra finger support, reduced hand fatigue, and superior leverage during long maintenance sessions. Key Features & Benefits Straight Blade Precision: Ideal for major stem plant trimming, background shaping, and open-water foliage maintenance before moving on to fine detailing. Ergonomic Pro Tail Grip: Features an integrated finger rest extension that provides an additional point of leverage and control to minimize hand strain during extended trimming sessions. Razor-Sharp Shearing Blades: Precision-ground edges slice cleanly through thick stem groups without crushing plant stems or tearing vascular tissue. Wipe completely dry with a soft cloth between uses to protect the blade edge, extend the life of the finish, and prevent mineral staining. Store in a clean, dry tool holder or rack away from high-humidity areas to maintain optimal blade alignment and tension. Frequently Asked Questions 1. When should I use straight scissors instead of curved scissors? Straight scissors are designed for vertical cutting, open-water trimming, and major background stem plant shaping. They allow you to apply a direct, linear shearing force when topping dense stem plant forests. Curved scissors, on the other hand, are better for horizontal trimming parallel to the substrate, such as cutting low-growing foreground carpet plants. 2. What does the Pro tail grip (finger rest) actually do? The tail grip is an extended finger rest located on the upper finger loop. It gives your index or middle finger a solid place to rest, distributing the squeezing pressure across your whole hand rather than focusing it all on two finger tips. This dramatically increases cutting stability and prevents hand cramping during long maintenance sessions.

listings.commonName: Eriocaulon sp Quinquangulare Red UNS Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Eriocaulon sp. 'Quinquangulare' Red is a rare collector plant that brings a distinct look to high-tech aquascapes. Native to tropical wetland environments across Asia, this species is best suited for experienced hobbyists who enjoy working with specialized plants. It forms a neat, spiky rosette of narrow leaves displaying a color gradient that shifts from deep red and maroon near the base to warm orange and lighter green toward the tips. Reaching 3 to 5 inches in height, its round, needle-like shape works well as a midground focal point. Because it relies on soft water, strong lighting, pressurized CO2, and stable parameters, it grows best in established tanks where conditions remain consistent. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Narrow, spiky leaves form a starburst rosette pattern that works well as a midground focal point. Color gradient shifts from deep red and maroon at the base to orange and green near the leaf tips. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to insert individual rosettes or small clumps into your aquarium soil, making sure the root bases are anchored while the leaves remain exposed to light. Provide high-intensity lighting and pressurized CO2 injection; regular dosing of liquid iron and micronutrients supports healthy root growth and maintains the red and orange foliage. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain soft, acidic water conditions and keep water parameters steady to prevent root melting or leaf decay during transition. To propagate, wait for an established, healthy parent plant to form daughter rosettes, then carefully divide and replant them into your aquarium soil. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Eriocaulon sp. 'Quinquangulare' Red Common Name(s) Eriocaulon Quinquangulare Red, Red Pipewort Family Eriocaulaceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Tissue Culture Rosette / Pipewort Care Difficulty Difficult / High-Tech Light Requirement High CO2 Requirement Required (Essential for growth and leaf color) Placement / Usage Midground Focal Point Height / Size 3–5” (Cup portion size: 2–3”) Growth Rate Slow Water Parameters pH 5.0–6.8 (Soft, acidic water preferred) Propagation Method Division of Established Rosettes Origin Asia (Vietnam) Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I prepare Eriocaulon Quinquangulare Red Tissue Culture before planting? Rinse the gel completely off the roots in a small bowl of room-temperature water. Once clean, divide the cluster into individual plantlets and use fine pinsettes to place them into your aquarium soil. 2. What water parameters work best for Eriocaulon Quinquangulare Red? This plant prefers soft, acidic water, strong lighting, and continuous CO2 injection. Keeping parameters stable in a mature tank helps lower the risk of leaf or root melt. 3. How do I bring out the deep red color in this plant? Maintaining strong lighting along with pressurized CO2 and iron supplementation encourages the base of the leaves to develop rich red and maroon tones.

listings.description: Plant Profile Hygrophila Lancea 'Araguaia' Sp. Chai, commonly known as Hygrophila Chai, is an extremely rare and highly coveted pink mutation of the classic Hygrophila lancea 'Araguaia' . Originating as a specialized tissue-culture mutation in Singapore, this collector plant features narrow, elongated leaves characterized by striking olive-red bases with intense pastel pink margins and tips. While it shares the compact, low-growing, bushy structure of standard Araguaia, its breathtaking pink coloration and limited availability make it one of the most prized midground focal points in high-tech aquascaping. Quantity is limited, and supply is infrequent. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Ultra-rare pink variegated mutation featuring olive-red foliage with pastel-pink leaf tips and margins. Short, bushy branching growth habit naturally creates a dense, spreading midground centerpiece or low-growing foreground terrace. Provides unrivaled visual contrast against green mosses and dark hardscape elements. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide high-intensity LED lighting and pressurized CO2 injection; consistent iron and micronutrient dosing is required to maintain its signature pink coloration and prevent stunting. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim lateral shoots or stem tops with straight scissors, replanting the trimmings directly into the substrate to encourage compact side branching. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Chai Family Acanthaceae / Lythraceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Stem Plant / Compact Bushing Mutation Care Difficulty Medium to Difficult (High-Tech Required) Light Requirement High CO2 Requirement Required (Essential for pink coloration and growth) Placement / Usage Midground Bushing / Foreground Focal Point Height / Size 2–5” Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Water Parameters pH 6.5–7.5 Propagation Method Cuttings (Trim lateral shoots or main stem and replant) Origin Singapore (Cultivated Mutation) Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I maintain the bright pink color on Hygrophila Chai? Hygrophila Chai requires high light intensity, mandatory pressurized CO2, a nutrient-dense substrate, and regular micronutrient/iron dosing. Without intense light and adequate nutrients, the delicate pink margins will fade or stall in growth. 3. How do I prepare Hygrophila sp. Chai Tissue Culture before planting? Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the dense cluster into smaller clumps or individual stems and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

Plant Profile Selaginella kraussiana 'Aurea', commonly known as Golden Clubmoss or Golden Spikemoss, features delicate, fern-like scale foliage flushed with luminous golden-yellow highlights. While often mistaken for a true moss or miniature fern, spikemosses belong to an ancient lineage of vascular plants called lycophytes that predate the dinosaurs by hundreds of millions of years. Rooted in loose, damp tropical soil under gentle indirect light, it forms a dense, shingled ground layer that can carpet foreground zones, soften the edges of hardscape, or cover the bank along a paludarium waterline. Key Features & Notes Delicate feathery foliage displays striking chartreuse-gold tones that brighten shaded setups. Low-profile creeping habit roots along trailing stem nodes to form a dense living carpet. Thrives in high ambient humidity and filtered light with manageable, slow-to-moderate spread. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Press the trailing stems gently onto a moist, well-draining tropical substrate mix of bark, sphagnum moss, and perlite across the foreground floor. Maintain humidity above 75% while ensuring the soil remains aerated and damp; yellowing leaves typically indicate waterlogged, anaerobic substrate. Trim wandering stem tips with sharp shears to control its footprint and stimulate dense lateral branching across the hardscape. Final size and golden leaf intensity depend entirely on your specific setup conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Selaginella kraussiana are terrestrial plants, and being submerged will result in the death of the plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Can Selaginella kraussiana 'Aurea' survive in a closed terrarium? Yes. It thrives in sealed or semi-enclosed glass containers where constant high humidity keeps its fine trailing fronds hydrated and supple. 2. Why are the stems on my Golden Spikemoss turning yellow or limp? Yellowing, mushy foliage indicates overwatering and poor drainage. Ensure the soil mix remains airy and that roots are never resting in stagnant water. 3. How do you propagate Selaginella kraussiana 'Aurea'? Snip a trailing stem cutting that contains visible micro-roots or nodes and lay it flat across moist sphagnum moss or tropical soil under high humidity until rooted.

Plant Profile If your hardscape is looking a little bare, it is time to spruce things up with your very own underwater holiday forest. This clever design features lush, textured Christmas Moss pre-wrapped around a heavy base, giving you a miniature pine tree that stays anchored at the bottom of your tank. It is an incredibly forgiving, beginner-friendly option for anyone looking to build a thriving layout with minimal effort. Tucking these little trees into rocky gaps or creating a winding pathway of greenery provides a haven for shrimp and shy fish to feel comfortable. Key Features & Benefits Pre-attached weighted base stands upright in substrate without floating away, making installation fast and hassle-free. Combining multiple trees easily builds a stunning 3D evergreen forest aesthetic, adding incredible scale and depth to nano tanks. Dense canopy offers essential shelter and constant biofilm grazing grounds for dwarf shrimp and fry. Care & Planting Instructions Position the weighted base directly onto your sand, or wedge the trunk securely into hardscape gaps to blend it seamlessly into your layout. Maintain a stable aquarium environment and avoid sudden, drastic changes to your water parameters to keep your moss looking vibrant and healthy. Give the moss an occasional light haircut with sharp aquascaping shears to keep its shape neat, compact, and perfectly balanced. Propagate your patch in seconds by cutting or pulling a small clump apart and anchoring it to a new surface in your tank. Add CO2 injection if you want to accelerate growth and unlock the most intense, eye-popping green coloration possible. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. How do I keep my Christmas Moss Tree from turning brown or yellow? Christmas Moss prefers clean, moving water and cooler temperatures (under 78°F). Browning usually occurs when organic debris gets trapped inside the dense fronds or when water temperatures run too high. Gently siphoning debris out during water changes will keep the inner growth green and healthy. 2. What is the best way to place and secure the moss tree in my aquascape? Since the tree comes pre-assembled with a heavy, weighted base, simply drop it onto your substrate or bury the base slightly under sand or gravel to keep it standing firmly upright. No additional glues or ties are needed. 3. How do I stop moss trimmings from spreading everywhere during maintenance? Always turn off your filter pumps and powerheads before trimming moss. Use sharp curved shears to make clean cuts, and immediately scoop or siphon out floating cuttings so they don't take root in unwanted areas of your aquarium.

Plant Profile Bucephalandra ‘Sanggau’ is a low-tech, beginner-friendly aquarium plant that features compact, wavy leaves that display a range of dark green to iridescent blue tones in quality lighting. This variety's slightly ruffled foliage and variable coloration add a dynamic texture to the foreground or midground of a planted tank. Highly versatile, it can be grown submerged or emersed, usually attached to hardscape such as driftwood or rocks rather than being buried in traditional aquarium substrate. Tissue culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab-grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go-to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Notes Under full-spectrum LED lighting, the "Sanggau" variant can develop a stunning blue sheen on its mature, ruffled leaves. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for planted tanks where other plants might struggle. It is perfectly at home fully submerged in an aquarium or emersed in high-humidity terrariums, vivariums, and paludariums. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by carefully removing the plantlets from the cup and rinsing away all sterile nutrient gel under lukewarm, dechlorinated water before mounting. Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood with aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as it will rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard low-light aquarium plant setups, CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and a smoother tissue culture transition. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I prepare tissue culture Bucephalandra for planting? Gently remove the plant from its plastic cup, rinse off all the nutrient gel under lukewarm water, and separate the plant into smaller clumps before attaching them to driftwood or rock using aquarium-safe glue or thread. 2. Why is my tissue culture Bucephalandra melting after planting? Tissue culture plants undergo an acclimation phase when transitioning to underwater conditions. Maintain stable water parameters, good circulation, and moderate light; as long as the rhizome stays firm, new submerged leaves will emerge. 3. Can tissue culture Bucephalandra be planted in substrate? Yes, you can push the roots into substrate or gravel to help anchor the plantlet. However, you must keep the central horizontal rhizome completely exposed above the substrate line, as burying the rhizome starves it of circulation and causes rot.

Product Overview APT 1 Zero by 2HR Aquarist is a concentrated daily fertilizer made for planted aquariums. The formula supports strong growth and vibrant color without extra nitrates or phosphates, making it ideal for new tanks or heavily stocked aquariums where fish waste already supplies a steady source of nutrients. In a fish-heavy setup, APT 1 Zero provides essential macronutrients for balanced plant nutrition while helping to minimize algae issues. Key Benefits & Target Deficiencies Delivers 5.5% soluble potash, magnesium, and triple-chelated iron for critical plant uptake. Prevents potassium pinholes, yellowing, and pale growth. Invertebrate-safe with no dangerous copper concentrations, safe for shrimp and snails. Promotes vibrant pigmentation and cellular strength without fueling algae from excess nitrates. Dosing & Application Instructions Dose 3mL or 0.1 fluid ounces per 26 US gallons or 100 liters of total water volume daily using the included calibrated pump, which dispenses 1mL per press. Apply this recommended dosage consistently at any time of day for low-tech aquariums with active aquarium soil. Apply this recommended dosage daily for high-tech aquariums with high lighting and pressurized carbon dioxide. Perform a weekly thirty to fifty percent water change to maintain clear water and prevent parameter skew over time. Plant Profile If you are tired of mosses that just look like green fuzz, it is time to upgrade to some serious botanical architecture. What makes this slow-growing plant truly unique is its growth style: it develops into miniature, structural rosettes that look like tiny, hand-carved green roses or miniature umbrellas popping up on the forest floor. Native to the damp, shaded woodlands of Asia, Umbrella Moss brings a dramatic, high-end, forest-floor texture to humid setups that typical carpet mosses simply cannot replicate. **Umbrella Moss is a terrestrial plant and it will not survive submerged in water.** Key Features & Benefits Each stem forms a distinct rosette-shaped crown (0.5 to 1.5 cm) resembling tiny, hand-carved green roses or miniature umbrellas. Specially adapted for terrestrial displays, offering a bold architectural accent for high-humidity land setups. Slowly expands into dense, tiered clusters that add instant height, visual depth, and a lush forest floor aesthetic. Care & Planting Instructions Position the moss clusters directly onto damp substrate, or wedge them securely into hardscape crevices above the waterline. Maintain consistent high ambient humidity and keep the foliage damp through regular misting to protect rosettes from drying out. Provide medium, indirect lighting to keep the rosettes vibrant while avoiding direct, scorching light sources. Give the moss an occasional light haircut with sharp shears to remove old foliage and keep the growth cluster neat and compact. Propagate by gently separating established clusters and pressing them into new areas of damp substrate or hardscape. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Rhodobryum giganteum Common Name(s) Umbrella Moss, Giant Rose Moss Family Bryaceae Plant Type Terrestrial Moss Care Difficulty Easy to Medium Light Requirement Medium (Bright, indirect light) Placement / Usage Terrarium, Vivarium, or Paludarium Feature (Above Waterline) Growth Rate Slow Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 | Temperature 72°F–82°F (22°C–28°C) Propagation Method Division (Gently separate moss clusters) Origin South Asia Frequently Asked Questions 1. Can Umbrella Moss be fully submerged underwater in an aquarium? No, Umbrella Moss is a terrestrial moss species. It cannot survive submerged underwater long-term and must be kept above the waterline in humid enclosures like terrariums, vivariums, or paludariums. 2. How do I maintain high humidity for Umbrella Moss without rotting it? Umbrella Moss needs continuous moisture and high ambient humidity, but it should never sit in stagnant, waterlogged soil. Keep the substrate damp and well-draining, and mist the rosettes regularly while maintaining gentle air circulation in the enclosure. 3. How do I prune and propagate Umbrella Moss clusters? To propagate, carefully pull apart established rosette clumps into smaller sections and press them into fresh, damp substrate or hardscape cracks. Use fine curved aquascaping shears to trim away any older, yellowing stems to promote clean new growth.

This unique architectural growth adds instant verticality, realistic scale, and incredible depth to terrariums, vivariums, and paludarium land sections. *Tree Moss is a terrestrial plant species and will not survive submerged underwater in an aquarium.* Key Features & Benefits Erect stems topped with spreading green branches naturally replicate the structural look of tiny woodland trees. Specially adapted for terrestrial displays, offering a bold architectural accent for high-humidity land setups. Common Name: Rainbow Marcgravia Marcgravia sintenisii is a stunning tropical vine from the rainforests of South America. Its shingling leaves showcase a captivating gradient, shifting from red to orange to green, adding a vibrant splash of color to any terrarium or paludarium. The vines naturally climb toward the light, creating graceful, vertical displays. This terrestrial plant thrives in low to medium light and prefers its roots and growing surfaces to stay slightly moist, while avoiding prolonged water on the leaves. With the right care, Marcgravia sintenisii rewards plant enthusiasts with striking coloration and elegant, cascading growth. Key Features & Important Notes: Shingling plants do best in environments with vertical surfaces to climb. This is not an aquarium plant. Submerging it completely will result in the death of this plant. Photos are a representation of what you will receive. Size, shape and color may vary as this is a live plant. Additional research on Marcgravia sintenisii care should be done to provide optimum growing conditions for the plant to thrive.

Hygrophila salicifolia is an aquarium plant that is great for all skill levels. Often compared to Water Wisteria, this fast-growing Hygro is just as hardy while offering a more upright growth habit, making it an excellent choice for filling out the background of a planted aquarium. Like many aquatic plants, it may experience some initial melt as it adjusts to a new tank. Give it time to establish healthy roots and it will quickly rebound. Once settled, Hygrophila salicifolia grows vigorously and adapts well to a wide range of water conditions. As long as aquarium parameters remain reasonably stable, this plant will continue producing new growth with minimal effort. Plant Profile Eriocaulon 'Feather Duster' brings an unmistakably soft, airy texture to planted aquariums, earning its playful name. Growing in dense, compact rosettes, it sends out dozens of needle-thin, grassy, bright-green blades that fan outward like a miniature pom-pom, though it won't actually dust your hardscape for you. Its fine foliage sways gently in the current and adds crisp visual contrast when paired next to bulky stones or broad-leaved stems. While it appreciates a bit of patience and consistency, such as good lighting and steady CO2, it is more forgiving than many other rare Eriocaulon varieties, making it a rewarding focal point for midground or background zones. Key Features & Notes Slender bright-green blades grow in dense grassy rosettes for fine visual contrast. More adaptable than rare Eriocaulon species while thriving with CO2 and active substrate. Care & Planting Instructions Plant the delicate white roots gently into nutrient-rich active substrate using fine-tipped tweezers, making sure the central crown sits right at the substrate surface to prevent rot. Provide moderate to high lighting alongside continuous CO2 injection to encourage compact growth and dense rosette formation. Maintain soft, slightly acidic water parameters and dose balanced macro and micronutrients regularly. Minimal pruning is needed; snip away older outer leaves near the base as new foliage emerges from the center. Propagate by carefully dividing mature multi-crown clumps at the root base once side shoots develop independent roots. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How deep should I plant Eriocaulon 'Feather Duster' in the substrate? Bury only the white root system, keeping the green central growth crown resting right above the substrate line. Burying the crown too deeply can cause the rosette to rot. 2. Does Eriocaulon 'Feather Duster' require CO2 injection? Pressurized CO2 is strongly recommended. While it can survive in well-maintained low-tech tanks with active soil, steady CO2 and moderate-to-high lighting keep its grassy rosettes compact, healthy, and vibrant. 3. How do I propagate Eriocaulon 'Feather Duster'? As a rosette matures, it will naturally split into multiple distinct growth crowns at the base. Once each crown has its own healthy roots, gently pull or slice them apart and replant them separately.
