Plant Profile Common Name: Bucephalandra Artemis Buce ‘Artemis’ is a striking and relatively rare aquarium plant prized for its unique dark green tones and subtle iridescent highlights. This variety features small, elongated, and slightly wavy leaves that grow in a distinct palm tree-like formation, adding an architectural flair to the layout. Highly versatile, it can be grown submerged or emersed, usually attached to hardscape such as driftwood or rocks rather than being buried in traditional aquarium substrate. Its size and subtle silver sheen make it a beautiful accent to the foreground or midground of a planted tank, where it will slowly sprout from rhizomes to create a dense, textured cluster. Key Features & Notes Under moderate to high lighting, the foliage develops a metallic, silvery sheen that contrasts beautifully against dark hardscape. The unique leaf arrangement mimics the look of miniature palm trees, making it a perfect tool for creating scale in nano aquariums. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas. It is an ideal choice for aquascapes where other plants might struggle. It is perfectly at home fully submerged in an aquarium or emersed in high-humidity terrariums, vivariums, and paludariums. Care Tips & Preparation Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood . Never bury the rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Carefully remove the plant from its pot and clear away all rockwool from the roots. For a deep dive on prepping potted plants, click here . Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting. Unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance, CO2 injection will yield much faster growth. We recommend researching your specific water chemistry to ensure your plant thrives. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions. Please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Please research appropriately to ensure your plant thrives. Additional Information Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Family Name: Araceae Origin: Borneo (Endemic) Skill Level: Easy Growth Rate: Slow Light: Low to Medium CO2: Not necessary but recommended pH Range: 6.0 – 8.0 Propagation: Divide the rhizome with sharp scissors

Plant Profile Hottonia Palustris is a stem plant native to quiet waters across Europe and Western Asia. This species produces deeply divided, fan-shaped green leaves that branch out along upright stems, creating a soft, feathery texture underwater. The delicate foliage provides visual contrast against broad-leaved species in midground and background placements. It adapts smoothly to both fully submerged aquarium setups and emersed growth in humid terrariums, where it occasionally produces small lavender flowers above the water surface. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Feathery, fan-shaped leaves create a soft texture in midground and background layouts. Adapts smoothly to fully submerged aquariums or emersed growth in humid terrariums. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small portions or individual stems 1 inch apart into your aquarium soil, ensuring lower leaves receive light. Provide low to moderate lighting; while CO2 is not strictly required, supplying pressurized CO2 and regular liquid fertilizers encourages thicker stem tops and faster growth. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden water chemistry shifts to prevent leaf melting during transition. To propagate, trim main stem tops with sharp straight shears and replant the cuttings directly into your aquarium soil to encourage side shoots. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Hottonia palustris Common Name(s) Hottonia Palustris, Featherfoil, Water Violet Family Primulaceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Aquatic Stem Plant Care Difficulty Easy Light Requirement Low to Medium CO2 Requirement Optional / Recommended (Promotes bushy top growth) Placement / Usage Midground / Background Textured Accent Height / Size 4–12”+ (Cup portion size: 2–3”) Growth Rate Moderate Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 Propagation Method Stem Cuttings (Trim stem tops or side shoots and replant) Origin Europe, Asia Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I prepare Hottonia Palustris Tissue Culture before planting? Rinse the nutrient gel completely off the roots in a small bowl of room-temperature water. Once clean, divide the cluster into small clumps or individual stems and insert the roots into your aquarium soil using fine pinsettes. 2. Is Hottonia Palustris suitable for low-tech aquariums? Yes, Hottonia Palustris grows well in low-tech setups under moderate lighting without CO2 injection, though leaves may grow slightly looser and stems will stretch taller toward the light. 3. How do I keep Hottonia Palustris bushy in the midground? Regularly trimming the top stems encourages lower nodes to sprout multiple lateral side shoots. Replanting the trimmed tops back into your aquarium soil alongside parent stems creates a dense green bush over time.

This low-growing aquatic plant originates from South America and features small, spade-shaped leaves perfect for filling in the foreground or midground of an aquascape Like most variegated plants, it thrives under stable lighting, CO2, and nutrient levels to keep its lighter patches vibrant rather than faded. Vertical, thin growth indicates insufficient light, yellowing leaves suggest a nutrient deficiency, and thinning leaves point to low CO2. When grown under optimal conditions, this plant can grow quickly and will need regular trimming. These trimmings can be replanted to propagate new plants. Notes: Staurogyne Repens is a great coverage plant, commonly used as a foreground or midground plant Staurogyne Repens can be grown in both submerged and emersed environments Tissue culture plants are grown in vitro in a state of the art laboratory specialized in propagating aquatic plants. Plant Profile Murdannia Keisak, widely known in the hobby as Marsh Dewflower or Asian Spiderwort, is an uncommon aquatic stem plant native to the tropical wetlands and marshes of Asia. Featuring slender, upright stems with narrow, lance-shaped leaves, this bamboo-like species spreads in an organic, free-flowing growth habit. Unlike the strictly uniform structures of traditional Rotalas or Ludwigias, Murdannia Keisak provides a soft, intentional wildness that mimics natural riverbanks and marshlands. Reaching 2 to 8+ inches in height, it serves as an extraordinary accent for nature-style aquascapes, biotope tanks, and open-top paludariums. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Bamboo-like, narrow foliage brings an organic, wild grassy texture to nature aquariums and biotopes. Versatile semi-aquatic stem plant that thrives both submerged underwater and emersed in paludariums or bog gardens. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to plant small stem clusters 1 inch apart into aquarium soil. Provide medium-to-high lighting and clean water conditions; while adaptable without CO2, supplying pressurized CO2 injection will yield significantly faster growth. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden parameter swings to prevent stem melting or rotting. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the desired height to encourage dense side-branching. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Murdannia keisak Common Name(s) Marsh Dewflower, Asian Spiderwort, Murdannia Keisak Family Commelinaceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Stem Plant Care Difficulty Medium Light Requirement Medium to High CO2 Requirement Optional / Recommended (Promotes faster, fuller stem growth) Placement / Usage Midground / Background Accent & Paludariums Height / Size 2–8”+ (Cup portion size: 2–3”) Growth Rate Fast Water Parameters pH 5.0–7.5 Propagation Method Cuttings (Cut stem tops or side shoots and replant) Origin Asia Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. Can I grow Murdannia Keisak without CO2 injection? Yes, Murdannia Keisak is an adaptable species that can be grown successfully in low-tech aquariums without CO2 injection. However, supplying CO2 along with aquasoil will result in thicker stems, faster growth, and much denser foliage. 3. How do I prepare Murdannia Keisak Tissue Culture before planting? Carefully remove the gel from the roots by washing the plant in a bowl of room-temperature water or gently rinsing it under a tap. Once the gel is removed, separate the cluster into smaller clumps or individual stems and plant them into substrate using fine pinsettes.

listings.commonName: Hydrocotyle Tripartita Mini Variegated UNS Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Hydrocotyle tripartita Mini Variegated is a downsized, highly sought‑after twist on the ever‑popular Hydrocotyle Tripartita (Hydrocotyle Japan) . With its tiny clover‑shaped leaves and splashy green‑and‑cream variegation, it brings instant personality and a pop of pattern to any aquascape. Under good conditions, it forms tight, compact bushes that add tons of texture and visual charm. And thanks to its impressive versatility, you can put it to work pretty much anywhere! Let it trail as a foreground carpet, grow it into a dense midground mound, or let it spill gracefully over driftwood and rocks for that effortless, cascading accent every planted tank secretly wants. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Offers distinct, ultra-small clover-like leaves with beautiful variegated patterns. Regular trimming produces dense, compact mounds that offer cover and grazing surfaces for shrimp and small fish. Care & Planting Instructions Remove the tissue culture gel completely before planting by washing it away under cool water. Divide the dense tissue culture mat into smaller clumps or individual stems to plant them into the substrate. Provide moderate to high lighting combined with consistent CO2 injection and frequent trimmings to force the plant to stay low-growing. Trim new shoots anywhere along the stem to encourage the plant to split, which results in much thicker, bushier, and more compact growth. Maintain stable aquarium parameters and avoid drastic shifts in water quality to prevent your new grass from melting. Master the basics by learning how to properly grow aquarium carpet plants to ensure your new layout fills in quickly, evenly, and stays free of algae. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Family Name: Araliaceae Origin: New Zealand, Australia Height: 1–4+ inches (Varies heavily based on trimming) Placement: Foreground, Midground, or Hardscape Accent pH: 6.5–7.5 Temperature: 68–80°F Care Level: Easy to Moderate Light Requirements: Moderate to High CO2: Recommended (Helps maintain low, compact growth) Propagation: Cut stems and replant or split dense clumps Growth Rate: Fast

listings.description: Product Overview The UNS Dual AIO Media Tower Replacement Filter Media set is an official media refill package engineered specifically for the UNS Dual AIO Media Tower. Key Features & Benefits Direct OEM Refill Set: Tailored specifically to drop into the compartments of the UNS Dual AIO Media Tower with zero bypass. Dual Mechanical & Biological Action: Includes mechanical sponges to trap fine particulate waste and high-surface-area Bio Blocks to support beneficial nitrifying bacteria. Restores Water Clarity: Prevents sludge buildup and maintains proper water turnover to keep your aquascape balanced and clear. Sized for Modular Chambers: Pre-shaped media components ensure fast and easy maintenance during routine filter cleanings. How often should I replace or clean the media in my UNS Dual AIO Media Tower? Rinse the mechanical filter sponges in drained aquarium water every 2 to 4 weeks during routine water changes. Plant Profile Bucephalandra ‘Neo’ is a low-tech, compact aquarium plant known for its clean form and subtle iridescent highlights. This variety features narrow, wavy leaves that grow in tight clusters, displaying a rich color palette that ranges from deep green to blue-green with warm red undertones. It's a fantastic choice for adding refined detail and structure to the foreground or midground of freshwater aquascapes, where it will slowly grow to form a lush, shimmering carpet of foliage. Grow it emersed or submerged and attach it to hardscape for best results. Key Features & Notes Under quality LED lighting, ‘Neo’ develops a sophisticated metallic sheen that adds incredible depth and dimension to its foliage. Unlike larger variants, this species stays low and tight to the hardscape, making it perfect for maintaining scale in nano aquariums. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for planted tanks where other plants might struggle. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard low-light aquarium plant setups, CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and richer iridescence. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! 'Neo' Common Name(s) Buce Neo, Bucephalandra Neo Family Araceae Plant Type Epiphyte (Rhizome) Care Difficulty Beginner / Easy (Low-Tech Compatible) Light Requirement Low to Medium CO2 Requirement Not Required (Accelerates growth & color density) Placement / Usage Foreground Detail, Midground Accent, Nano Hardscape Crevices Height / Size 1"–2.5" (2.5–6.0 cm) Growth Rate Slow Water Parameters pH 6.0–8.0 | Temperature 68°F–80°F (20°C–26°C) Propagation Method Rhizome Division (Separate with sharp shears) Origin Borneo (Endemic) Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why is my Bucephalandra melting? Bucephalandra melt can occur after changes in water chemistry, temperature, or lighting. If the rhizome remains firm, keep it attached to hardscape while the plant acclimates and produces new submerged growth. 2. Can I plant Bucephalandra in substrate? Bucephalandra is an epiphyte, so never bury its rhizome in substrate. Attach it to driftwood or rocks, or wedge the roots into hardscape while keeping the rhizome exposed. 3. Is Bucephalandra ‘Neo’ beginner-friendly? Yes. Bucephalandra ‘Neo’ is a beginner-friendly, low-light aquarium plant that grows without specialized substrate or pressurized CO₂, making it well-suited for low-tech planted aquariums.

A swing check valve is a simple yet essential safeguard for sump-based reef aquariums designed to prevent backflow through your return line. Built for reliability and ease, the internal flap-style mechanism supports high flow rates in the saltwater aquarium with minimal resistance and requires very little pressure to open, keeping your system running efficiently. The clear PVC body makes it easy to visually confirm whether the valve is opened or closed at a glance, while the double union design allows for quick removal, cleaning, or part replacement without cutting into your plumbing. While swing check valves provide an extra layer of protection, they’re best used alongside proper sump capacity. When your return pump is running, the internal flap opens to allow strong, unrestricted flow back into the display. If the flow stops during maintenance or a power outage, the valve closes automatically and helps prevent water from siphoning back into your sump. Key Features & Benefits Flap-style design - To handle high flow rates, the valve opens with minimal pressure and maintains smooth, unrestricted water movement Double join union - For easy installation on standard PVC piping Transparent, clear-PVC body - To easily monitor valve operation with a clear view of open and closed positions Metal-free composition - For safety in freshwater and saltwater aquariums

A gate valve is the go-to solution when your reef aquarium plumbing demands precision. Built for smooth, incremental adjustments, it gives you the control needed to fine-tune flow exactly where you want it, especially in saltwater systems where stability and silence matter most. Designed with a full-bore flow path, the internal spool can be fully opened without restricting water movement, allowing your system to run at full capacity when needed. When it’s time to dial things in, the gradual open-and-close mechanism makes it easy to achieve a perfectly balanced siphon, ideal for full siphon drain lines. This uPVC gate valve features slip fittings for easy installation and is constructed to ensure airtight sealing, strong pressure resistance, and long-term corrosion durability, making it a reliable choice for both freshwater and saltwater aquariums. Whether you’re tuning a drain line or controlling flow to equipment, it offers consistent performance you can count on. Key Features & Benefits: Gate valves allow for precision flow control for fine adjustments Its full-bore design allows unrestricted flow when fully open Ideal for silent siphon tuning in reef overflow systems Created with an airtight, pressure-resistant, and corrosion-resistant valve core Smooth operation for stable, consistent performance A simple aquarium upgrade that makes a noticeable difference to give you the control to run your system quietly, efficiently, and exactly how you want it.

Star Wood brings a bold, architectural feel to your aquascape with its long, straight branches and naturally pointed tips. It has the smooth, clean texture of Manzanita Wood, but with sharper edges that create a bolder, more directional look in a scaped tank. Unlike the twisting formations seen in traditional Manzanita Driftwood, Star Wood grows in straighter lines, making it perfect for building structured layouts, dramatic slopes, or branching designs that guide the eye across your scape. Think of it as Spider Wood reimagined into fewer tangles and more intention. Each piece is easy to work with and ideal for attaching epiphytes like Bucephalandra, Anubias, or moss, giving you plenty of creative freedom while maintaining a clean, cohesive layout. Key Features & Benefits Long, straight branches provide strong visual flow Smooth texture with sharper, more defined tips Great for structured, modern aquascapes Easy to attach aquatic plants and mosses Size Specifications Photos provided are a representation of what you will receive. This is a natural aquarium hardscape product; please expect variations in shape, weight, and character. Small: 16-19" Medium: 20-24" Large: 24-28" Preparation & Care Proper aquarium driftwood prep goes a long way Rinse: Thoroughly rinse the piece to remove any dust or debris from transit. The Floating Phase: Depending on the size, Star Wood will float a little initially. We recommend soaking it thoroughly or boiling it. A large stone or heavy decor may be placed on top to ensure a non-waterlogged piece of wood stays submerged. Tannin Control: If you want zero tint in your water, a quick 1-hour boil will fast-track the sinking process and remove any remaining surface tannins. You can also reduce this effect through consistent water changes or through the addition of Aquario Neo Carbon Bag Important note: We recommend rinsing wood thoroughly before adding it to an established aquarium. If you prefer, you may also boil the wood for at least 1–2 hours to help release tannins.

listings.description: Product Overview Ultra Fresh Baby Turtle Nutri Sticks are floating micro sticks made for hatchling and juvenile aquatic turtles with shell sizes between 1 to 2.5 inches, including Red-Eared Sliders, Musk Turtles, Mud Turtles, and Diamondback Terrapins. The tiny sticks float reliably on the surface and soften within seconds so small mouths can easily bite them without scattering fine debris across the water. Nymphoides Hydrophylla ‘Taiwan’ is a pretty forgiving, low-tech aquarium plant that shines with stable nutrients and regular trimming to keep its fast growth in check. Moderate to high lighting allows it to stay compact and vibrant, while lower light will cause it to stretch toward the surface. CO2 isn’t required, but it makes a noticeable difference. Expect denser, more controlled growth compared to larger, more surface-reaching leaves without it. Best placed in the midground to background, this rosette plant works well as a soft focal point or for adding layered texture in natural-style layouts. It spreads quickly through runners, sending out new plants horizontally, and will often produce floating leaves if left untrimmed, adding interest to both submerged and emersed portions of a freshwater aquascape. This aquatic plant can provide excellent natural cover for fish and shrimp, especially when allowed to grow a bit more freely. In smaller tanks, it may need regular trimming to prevent it from shading out surrounding plants. Under the right conditions, Nymphoides Taiwan may reward you with small yellow flowers at the surface. Key Features & Important Notes: Nymphoides is a strong nutrient feeder, especially through the roots, so it responds really well to a nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs. Please be sure to remove this plant from its pot. Remove the rockwool surrounding the roots and attach it to the hardscape. For instructions on how to properly prep "potted" aquarium plants, click here . The plant’s final size, coloration, and growth rate are dependent upon the condition of the aquarium. Photos are a representation of what you will receive and may vary. Do not make drastic changes to the aquarium. Unstable parameters can result in melt and rotting of the aquarium plant. CO2 injection will yield better growth. Please research appropriately to ensure your plant thrives. Family Name: Nymphaeaceae Origin: Asia Height: 4-6” pH: 6-7.5 Care: Easy to moderate Light: Moderate CO2: Not necessary Propagation: Cut side shoots Growth rate: Medium to Fast

listings.commonName: Anubias Nana Pangolino on Lava Stone
listings.description: Plant Profile Anubias Nana Pangolino is a true crown jewel for miniature aquascapes, originating from the shaded riverbanks of West Africa. Even smaller than the popular Anubias Nana Petite , its tiny green leaves overlap beautifully to resemble the scales of a pangolin or the coveted Bucephalandra Mini Coin . Coming pre-attached to a porous piece of natural Lava Stone, this beginner-friendly gem adds instant texture and effortless character to your tank from day one. Key Features & Benefits Micro-sized foliage provides extremely small leaf scale, making it ideal for nano layouts and high-detail focal points. Pre-attached natural lava stone base enables placement into the aquarium without gluing. Thick, leathery leaves deter grazing from fish, snails, and active dwarf shrimp. Care & Planting Instructions Place the attached lava stone directly onto your substrate or nestled within your hardscape, ensuring you never bury the horizontal rhizome beneath gravel or soil. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Avoid intense light and ensure good water flow to prevent spot algae on slow‑growing leaves. CO₂ is optional but improves growth and leaf density. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Anubias barteri var. nana 'Pangolino' Common Name(s) Anubias Nana Pangolino on Lava Stone, Anubias Pangolino Family Araceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Epiphyte (Rhizome) Care Difficulty Easy / Beginner-Friendly Light Requirement Low CO2 Requirement Not Required but Beneficial Placement / Usage Foreground, Nano Hardscape Crevices Height / Size 1-2 inches Growth Rate Slow (1 leaf every 3-4 weeks) Water Parameters pH 6.0 – 7.5 | Temperature 68°F – 82°F (20°C – 28°C) Propagation Method Separate by Rhizome Division Origin Cultivar / West Africa Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I plant Anubias Nana Pangolino on Lava Stone? Place the pre-attached lava stone directly onto substrate or wedge it into hardscape crevices. Keep the central rhizome fully exposed to open water movement to prevent rot. 2. Does it require CO2 or high lighting? No. It thrives in low lighting without CO2 injection. While adding CO2 speeds up growth, it is completely optional. 3. Is this plant safe for shrimp, snails, and fish? Yes, Anubias Nana Pangolino on Lava Stone is 100% safe for all freshwater fish, shrimp (including sensitive Caridina and Neocaridina), and snails. Its tough leaves are also resistant to plant-eating fish like cichlids or goldfish.

Plant Profile Hemianthus callitrichoides ‘Cuba White’ is a rare little gem in the carpeting‑plant world, best known for having the smallest, most delicate leaves in the hobby and featuring a striking, creamy, pale white to variegated coloration that sets it apart from standard Dwarf Baby Tears. Because of its petite size and bright, standout color, HC Cuba White shines in nature‑style scapes, nano tanks, and high‑detail foregrounds where contrast really matters. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Create a high-impact, meticulous foreground with an uncommon look. Exceptionally tiny leaves that maximize visual scale, making even the smallest nano tanks look massive and highly detailed. Care & Planting Instructions Ensure you thoroughly wash away or soak off the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before dividing and planting. Separate into small clumps and press them compactly into a quality aquarium soil to give the roots the perfect head start. Use a dry start method or Wabi Kusa setup to give its root system plenty of time to firmly anchor into the substrate before you flood the tank. This specialized variant is best suited for experienced hobbyists who can provide the strict high-tech environment it requires. Expect a more patient grow-out and adaptation period compared to standard green Dwarf Baby Tears due to the lack of chlorophyll in its variegated leaves. Provide high-intensity lighting and ensure it receives completely unobstructed, direct light. Inject pressurized CO2! This requirement is necessary to sustain its unique coloration and prevent stunting. Maintain stable aquarium parameters, avoiding any sudden, drastic shifts in water quality to prevent your new grass from melting. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Hemianthus callitrichoides 'Cuba White' Common Name(s) HC Cuba White, Dwarf Baby Tears White, White HC Family Scrophulariaceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Stem / Carpeting Foreground Care Difficulty Difficult Light Requirement High CO2 Requirement Required (Mandatory for maintaining coloration) Placement / Usage Foreground Carpet Height / Size 0.5-1 inch Growth Rate Slow to Moderate Water Parameters pH 6.0 – 7.5 | Temperature 68°F – 82°F (20°C – 28°C) Propagation Method Cut runners and replant Origin Cultivated Variant Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I plant Dwarf Baby Tears White tissue culture? Use fine-tip pinsettes to push each portion deep into fine aquasoil at a 45-degree angle. Leave only a few leaves showing above the surface so they don't float. 2. Why does Dwarf Baby Tears White grow slower than standard green HC Cuba? Because of its white and variegated foliage, the plant contains significantly less chlorophyll than traditional green plants. This reduces its photosynthetic efficiency, resulting in a slower growth rate that demands high lighting, steady dosing, and pressurized CO2 to thrive. 3. Can I grow Dwarf Baby Tears White without pressurized CO2? No. This variegated variant is exceptionally delicate. Without pressurized CO2 injection, strong lighting, and pristine water stability, the plant will quickly stunt, lose its white coloration, or completely melt away.

Scientific Name: Poecilia Reticulata Common Name: Moscow Black Guppy **Note: These guppies are sold in breeding pairs (one male and one female per order). To ensure they arrive happy and healthy, all live fish are packed in solid-wall Styrofoam insulation and shipped via 1-Day Shipping only. No need to buy extra insulation; we've got it covered. If you want to add an elegant and dramatic look to your tank, the Black Moscow Guppy is a great choice. These freshwater fish are famous for the midnight-black coloration that covers them from nose to tail fin. They create a breathtaking, stark contrast against vibrant green aquarium plants or a light-colored sand substrate, making them a favorite for aquascapers. Behavior Black Moscow Guppies are celebrated for their energetic, non-aggressive personalities. While they are typically top-level swimmers, they will actively explore the mid and lower areas of the tank throughout the day. Their exceptionally peaceful temperament makes them perfect candidates for community aquariums. They can be safely housed with other non-aggressive species. While mature dwarf shrimp are typically safe, guppies may naturally snack on tiny shrimp fry. If you are breeding shrimp, we highly recommend adding dense aquarium plants and mosses to provide adequate coverage and survival hiding spots. Guppies thrive best when kept in groups of at least 4 to 5 to encourage natural social behavior. Also, they are known to test their limits! Always keep a tight lid on your tank so they don't accidentally jump out! Breeding Because these are sold as a male and female pair, you will likely see some baby guppies (fry) in the near future! Guppies are livebearers, meaning they give birth to free-swimming young rather than laying eggs. Diet Guppies are enthusiastic omnivores and aren't picky eaters at all. To keep their coloration rich and their fins healthy, we recommend a varied diet of high-quality micro-pellets or tropical flakes and occasional treats of baby brine shrimp or bloodworms. Species Profile Ocean Blue Shrimp are a premium freshwater shrimp variety prized for their vibrant blue coloration and eye-catching patterns. Their bodies display varying shades of blue, ranging from light sky blue to deep navy, often accented by darker markings that create a unique appearance from shrimp to shrimp. Best suited for intermediate to advanced shrimp keepers, these Caridina thrive in mature aquariums with stable, soft water parameters and minimal fluctuations. Peaceful and active, they spend their days grazing on biofilm, algae, and microorganisms found on hardscape, substrate, and plant surfaces while adding constant movement and color to the aquarium. Like other Caridina shrimp, Ocean Blue Shrimp prefer soft, slightly acidic water and are sensitive to sudden changes in water chemistry. A well-established aquarium with plenty of mosses, botanicals, and natural grazing surfaces will help support long-term health and encourage natural behaviors. Their brilliant blue coloration contrasts beautifully against dark substrates, driftwood, and vibrant green aquatic plants, making them a standout addition to planted aquariums. Ideal for dedicated Caridina setups, shrimp-focused aquascapes, and hobbyists looking to showcase a unique and highly sought-after shrimp variety. **Note: All livestock orders will come carefully packaged with solid wall Styrofoam insulation and shipped via 1-day shipping only. No additional insulation is needed for your livestock. Key Features & Notes Tank-raised specimens showcasing vibrant blue coloration. Selective Caridina variety prized for its captivating color gradient and individual expression across every specimen. Relentless clean-up crew that continuously grazes on biofilm and algae. Peaceful, social behavior for community aquariums. Care Specifications Maintain stable, soft, acidic water chemistry using an active buffering substrate to support sensitive Caridina health. Keep water parameters strictly free of copper-based medications or heavy metals. Supplement their diet with plant-based shrimp pellets, spirulina, and blanched vegetables to ensure proper minerals for molting when natural algae is low. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to maintain stable parameters to ensure a healthy, thriving colony! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Caridina cf. cantonensis Common Name(s) Ocean Blue Shrimp, Ocean Blue Bee Shrimp Care Difficulty Intermediate to Advanced Adult Size 1.0" (2.5 cm) Diet Omnivore / Biofilm & Algae Scavenger Minimum Tank Size 5 Gallons (10+ Gallons Recommended) Temperature Range 60°F–72°F (15°C–22°C) pH Range 5.8–6.2 General Hardness (GH) 4–5 dGH Carbonate Hardness (KH) 0–1 dKH (Best at 0) Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) 100–120 ppm Lifespan 1–2 Years Frequently Asked Questions 1. How do I properly acclimate my new freshwater shrimp to prevent shock? Dwarf shrimp are sensitive to sudden shifts in water parameters and total dissolved solids (TDS). Always drip acclimate new arrivals over 1 to 2 hours before releasing them into your tank. Follow our step-by-step tutorial in 7 Easy Steps to Drip Acclimate Shrimp and Fish for the perfect drip rate setup. 2. What substrate is best for keeping dwarf shrimp healthy? It depends on the species! Neocaridina species thrive in inert substrates like gravel or sand, while Caridina species like Ocean Blue Shrimp require active aquasoils that buffer pH down and pull KH near zero. Learn how to select the right foundation for your aquarium shrimp in our Best Substrate for Shrimp Guide . 3. How do I get my colony to start breeding? As long as water parameters remain stable, temperatures stay in the low 70s, and adequate food is present, dwarf shrimp will breed naturally. To maximize baby shrimplet survival rates and learn how to support berried females, read our complete guide on How to Breed Freshwater Shrimp . 4. Are dwarf shrimp easy to care for if I am a beginner? While Neocaridina species are great for beginners, Caridina species like Ocean Blue Shrimp require precise soft-water conditions (low KH, low TDS, and active buffering soil). If you are just starting out, get a complete overview of parameters, diet, and setup requirements in our Freshwater Aquarium Shrimp Care Guide .

Plant Profile Aglaonema simplex, commonly known as the Malayan Sword or Chinese Evergreen, is a durable aroid in the family Araceae native to the damp tropical lowlands of Southeast Asia. This species features broad, lance-shaped deep green leaves supported by sturdy upright petioles, creating a dense architectural silhouette that adds natural height and vertical structure along paludarium shorelines, background terrarium borders, and open-top riparium planters. While its thick root network readily establishes in wet gravel, aquarium water, or damp tropical soil, make sure its foliage and growing crown remain elevated into ambient air, because submerging this plant entirely underwater is a fast track to leaf melt and rot. Key Features & Notes Broad lanceolate foliage provides dense vertical greenery and structural scale for background zones in emersed setups. Hardy root system adapts to wet substrates, riparium baskets, and damp moss banks without demanding pressurized CO2. High shade tolerance allows steady leaf production under low to moderate lighting. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Anchor the root network into a hanging riparium planter, along an emersed paludarium bank, or in an airy tropical substrate mix, keeping the foliage entirely above the waterline. Position under low to moderate indirect lighting, avoiding intense direct rays that bleach foliage pigments and scorch leaf tips. Maintain ambient relative humidity above 60% and ensure root zones receive adequate water flow to avoid stagnant, anaerobic conditions. Trim yellowing lower leaves near the main stem base using sharp shears to encourage fresh shoots and maintain air circulation around neighboring vivarium plants. Final size, leaf spread, and growth speed depend entirely on your specific setup conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Can Aglaonema Simplex grow fully submerged in a freshwater aquarium? No. Aglaonema simplex is a terrestrial and riparian plant rather than a true aquatic species. Keeping its leaves permanently submerged underwater will suffocate the foliage, causing the leaves to melt and decay within a few weeks. 2. Can I grow Aglaonema Simplex with bare roots in aquarium water? Yes. Suspending the roots in open aquarium water using a rim planter, hang-on-back breeder box, or riparium cup works well. The roots absorb dissolved fish waste and nitrates while the leaves remain dry in the air above. 3. How do I propagate Aglaonema Simplex when it outgrows my enclosure? Mature plants produce lateral stem offshoots and basal crowns. Use a sterile razor or shears to separate an established shoot with several attached root nodes, then place the cutting into moist sphagnum moss or an airy potting mix until established.

Plant Profile Pearl Moss is a moss-t have for any small-scale setup, proving that good things come in small packages. While most aquarium mosses grow with long, fuzzy fronds, this species is actually a terrestrial moss relative that has adapted beautifully to life underwater. It is famous for its exceptionally tiny, round leaves that stack tightly together, giving the plant a delicate, glistening look reminiscent of miniature strands of green pearls. Because of this diminutive, slow-growing habit, it's a great pick for nano tanks where larger mosses would quickly overwhelm the layout. Key Features & Benefits Incredibly small, round leaves stack tightly together to maintain proper scale in nano aquascapes. Unique leaf structure catches light to create a glistening, pearl-like texture and visual depth. Care & Planting Instructions Place the moss directly onto your substrate, or secure it to your hardscape using dark thread or dabs of aquarium-safe superglue gel. Maintain a stable aquarium environment and keep temperatures cool (65°F–78°F) to prevent stress, browning, or melting. Give the moss an occasional light haircut with sharp aquascaping shears to keep its shape neat, compact, and perfectly balanced. Propagate your patch in seconds by cutting or pulling a small clump apart and anchoring it to a new surface in your tank. Add CO2 injection if you want to accelerate growth and unlock the most intense, eye-popping green coloration possible. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I keep my Pearl Moss from turning brown or yellow? Pearl Moss prefers clean, well-oxygenated water and cooler temperatures (under 78°F). Browning usually occurs when organic debris gets trapped inside the compact leaf strands or when water temperatures run too high. Gently siphoning debris out during regular water changes will keep the inner growth green and healthy. 2. What is the best way to attach loose Pearl Moss to driftwood or rocks? Dabbing small dots of gel-based cyanoacrylate superglue (aquarium-safe superglue) directly onto dry hardscape points is the quickest method. Alternatively, wrapping the moss tightly with dark cotton thread allows it to anchor naturally over a few weeks while the thread dissolves. 3. How do I stop moss trimmings from spreading everywhere during maintenance? Always turn off your filter pumps and powerheads before trimming moss. Use sharp curved shears to make clean cuts, and immediately scoop or siphon out floating cuttings so they don't take root in unwanted areas of your aquarium.

Species Profile Ramshorn Snails ( Planorbella duryi ) are hardy freshwater gastropods characterized by their flat, coiled spiral shells resembling a ram's horn, coming in color morphs ranging from wild brown and leopard spots to vibrant red, pink, and blue. Often unfairly labeled merely as "pest snails," they are actually one of the most efficient, non-stop cleaning crews you can introduce to a planted tank. They cruise across hardscape, glass, and plant foliage to consume brown diatoms, soft algae films, and decaying plant matter before it fouls your water column. Crucially, their rasping mouthparts are not strong enough to chew through healthy plant foliage, so your high-tech stem plants and delicate carpeting runners remain untouched. Because their reproduction rate directly tracks how much uneaten fish food and organic debris lingers in the tank, they act as the ultimate real-time barometer for your system's nutrient balance. **Note: All livestock orders will come carefully packaged with solid wall Styrofoam insulation and shipped via 1-day shipping only. No extra insulation needs to be added to your cart for your livestock. Quantity: Each order includes 10 Ramshorn Snails. Shell color and size may vary slightly, as each snail is a unique live animal. Key Features & Notes Distinctive spiral-coiled shell adds organic shapes and color variety across the substrate and hardscape. Relentless detritivore that recycles uneaten fish food, diatoms, and dying plant matter before ammonia spikes occur. Completely safe with live aquatic plants, feeding strictly on decaying foliage rather than healthy growth. Acclimation & Care Instructions Float the sealed transport bag for 15 to 20 minutes to equalize water temperatures before opening. Drip-acclimate over 30 to 45 minutes using airline tubing to adjust them smoothly to your tank's GH, KH, and pH. Maintain a stable pH above 7.0 with ample mineral hardness; acidic water will degrade and pit their thin spiral shells. Control feeding habits responsibly; excessive leftover fish food and organic waste will trigger rapid population growth. Supplement with sinking algae wafers, calcium blocks, or blanched zucchini if kept in super clean display tanks. Avoid using copper-based plant treatments, algaecides, or medications in aquariums housing ornamental snails. Color morphs and shell patterns vary across specimens; photos represent healthy stock in mature planted setups. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy livestock! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Planorbella duryi Common Name(s) Ramshorn Snail Family Planorbidae Care Difficulty Easy Diet Omnivore / Detritivore (Biofilm, diatoms, decaying plant matter, sinking pellets) Plant Safe Yes (Safe with all live plants; only targets dying or melting tissue) Temperament Peaceful clean-up crew Adult Size Up to 1.0" (2.5 cm) Minimum Tank Size 5+ Gallons Water Parameters pH 7.0–8.2 | GH 6–18 | KH 3–15 | 68°F–82°F (20°C–28°C) Freshwater Breeding Yes (Prolific hermaphroditic egg layers) Origin North America (Tank-raised) Frequently Asked Questions 1. Will Ramshorn Snails eat healthy aquatic plants or tear up carpeting? No. Ramshorn Snails lack the radular jaw strength to break down healthy living plant cells. If you see a cluster of them congregating on a leaf, they are consuming dying, rotting, or melting tissue, or grazing micro-algae films off the surface. They do you a favor by trimming dead weight before it decays into the water column. 2. How do I stop Ramshorn Snails from taking over my planted tank? Their population is directly tied to the tank's food supply. They do not multiply out of nowhere; high populations are a sign of overfeeding, excessive detritus accumulation, or melting plants. Dial back your feeding schedule, vacuum out stubborn detritus, and their population will naturally balance out into a modest, manageable cleanup crew. 3. How do Ramshorn Snails reproduce in an aquarium? Ramshorn Snails are hermaphroditic, meaning any two mature snails can breed together. They lay small, flat, jelly-like egg clutches on glass, hardscape, and plant leaves that hatch into self-sufficient baby snails within 1 to 3 weeks. 4. What tank mates should I pair with Ramshorn Snails? They cohabit peacefully with standard planted tank fauna, such as Neocaridina shrimp, Otocinclus, Corydoras, Siamese Algae Eaters, and small schooling tetras. If you want to keep their numbers in check, species like Assassin Snails or small loaches will readily hunt them. Avoid keeping them with dedicated mollusk predators like pea puffers or crayfish unless intended as live food.

Species Profile Purple King Kong Shrimp are a rare and highly sought-after Caridina shrimp prized for their deep purple bodies accented by crisp white bands. Their unique coloration can range from deep violet to nearly black, depending on genetics, lighting, and water conditions, creating a striking contrast against aquatic plants and dark substrates. As an advanced shrimp variety, they require stable water parameters and are best kept in mature, well-established aquariums. Unlike hardy Neocaridina shrimp, Purple King Kong Shrimp thrive in soft, slightly acidic water and benefit from active buffering substrates designed for Caridina. A heavily planted aquarium with mosses, fine-leaved plants, and plenty of natural biofilm will help them feel secure while providing constant grazing opportunities. **Note: All livestock orders will come carefully packaged with solid wall Styrofoam insulation and shipped via 1-day shipping only. No additional insulation is needed for your livestock. Key Features & Notes Rare, selectively-bred Caridina shrimp with vibrant purple coloration. Best suited for established aquariums with stable water parameters. Excellent scavengers that continuously graze on biofilm, algae, and decaying plant matter. To increase survival rates, please allow 2 to 3 business days after placing an order to properly prepare live animal shipments. Care Specifications Maintain clean, well-filtered water with stable GH and KH levels to ensure problem-free molting cycles. Keep water parameters strictly free of copper-based medications or heavy metals. Supplement their diet with plant-based shrimp pellets, spirulina, and blanched vegetables to ensure proper minerals for molting when natural algae is low. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to maintain stable parameters to ensure a healthy, thriving colony! How do I properly acclimate my new freshwater shrimp to prevent shock? Dwarf shrimp are sensitive to sudden shifts in water parameters and total dissolved solids (TDS). Always drip acclimate new arrivals over 1 to 2 hours before releasing them into your tank. Follow our step-by-step tutorial in 7 Easy Steps to Drip Acclimate Shrimp and Fish for the perfect drip rate setup. 2. What substrate is best for keeping dwarf shrimp healthy? It depends on the species! Neocaridina species thrive in inert substrates like gravel or sand, while Caridina species like Purple King Kong Shrimp require active aquasoils that buffer pH down and pull KH near zero. Learn how to select the right foundation for your aquarium shrimp in our Best Substrate for Shrimp Guide . 3. How do I get my colony to start breeding? As long as water parameters remain stable, temperatures stay in the low 70s, and adequate food is present, dwarf shrimp will breed naturally. To maximize baby shrimplet survival rates and learn how to support berried females, read our complete guide on How to Breed Freshwater Shrimp . 4. Are dwarf shrimp easy to care for if I am a beginner? While Neocaridina species are great for beginners, Caridina species like Purple King Kong Shrimp require precise soft-water conditions (low KH, low TDS, and active buffering soil). If you are just starting out, get a complete overview of parameters, diet, and setup requirements in our Freshwater Aquarium Shrimp Care Guide .

Plant Profile Common Name: Bucephalandra Dark Sky Bucephalandra Dark Sky is a great choice for adding some contrast to your aquascape. Its elongated oval leaves have a deep, glossy finish that helps it stand out next to lighter green plants. The dark foliage also makes its reddish stems more noticeable, giving the plant a little extra character without being too flashy. Like other Bucephalandra, it's a slow grower that does best when attached to rock or driftwood instead of planted in the substrate. Whether you're filling out a nano tank or adding detail to a larger layout, Bucephalandra Dark Sky fits in easily. Plant Profile Managing a large tank means you need plants that can actually fill the space, and Crypt aponogetifolia doesn't disappoint. Native to the fast-flowing, limestone-rich rivers of the Philippines, this impressive species has long been revered by hobbyists for its towering size and distinctive, heavily bullated (hammered) leaf texture. Long, ribbon-like leaves stream elegantly in the water flow, reaching heights that easily canopy across huge tanks. Like all crypts, it can be sensitive to changes in water parameters and doesn't like to be moved, but once settled into its new home, it becomes a low-maintenance background accent. Key Features & Benefits Bullate ribbon-like foliage creates an impressive backdrop in larger aquariums. Can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups where it will periodically produce unique flowering spathes. Thrives well in low-tech setups, enduring hard water and moderate lighting with ease. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Crypt species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. How do I help my Cryptocoryne Aponogetifolia recover if it melts? Crypt melt is a standard reaction when shifting water conditions cause old leaves to dissolve so the plant can rebuild foliage adapted to your aquarium. Trim away rotting tissue, keep your water parameters stable, and do not disturb the subterranean root system. For complete recovery steps, check out our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt . 2. Can I move my Cryptocoryne to a new spot in the tank later? It is best to leave your Cryptocoryne permanently in its original spot. Uprooting an established plant damages its fine root hairs and almost always causes another cycle of leaf melt. 3. Should I use root tabs or liquid fertilizers for Cryptocoryne Aponogetifolia? Root tabs are far more effective than liquid fertilizers for Cryptocoryne species because they draw the overwhelming majority of their nutrition through their roots. While liquid nutrients benefit water column feeders like mosses or stem plants, placing nutrient-rich root tabs inside sand or gravel substrates directly fuels your Crypt's foliage growth.

Plant Profile Meet Ludwigia Inclinata var. Verticillata 'Meta', aka Ludwigia 'Meta', a highly sought-after aquatic stem plant that treats its own leaves like a canvas. Fine, narrow foliage arranges itself in dense, needle-like whorls, starting soft yellow-green under standard conditions. But give it high-intensity lighting, pressurized CO2, and consistent fertilization, and it'll cycle through fiery orange, salmon, and ruby-red for a texture and color combo that's hard to look away from. This variety is ideal for high-tech nature aquariums and Dutch-style layouts as Ludwigia 'Meta' forms sweeping, bushy hedges in midground and background zones when planted in dense clusters with regular trimming. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Needle-like leaves in whorls show orange, salmon, and deep red. Dense branching forms lush bushes and Dutch-style streets with routine pruning. Rare Colombian stem variant adds fine texture and warm color contrast. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip lower foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower leaves. Provide high-intensity lighting. Mandatory pressurized CO2 injection and regular liquid iron dosing are required to maximize growth speed and bring out vivid red and orange leaf pigmentation. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim main stem tops with straight scissors once stems reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and expand your bush. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stems slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining strong light penetration will keep lower foliage healthy. 2. How do I get Ludwigia Inclinata 'Meta' to display bright orange and red colors? Achieving vivid orange and red coloration on Ludwigia 'Meta' requires high light intensity, mandatory pressurized CO2 injection, nutrient-rich soil, and regular supplementation of micronutrients with liquid iron. Under low light, the foliage will remain predominantly green or pale yellow. 3. How do I transition Ludwigia Inclinata 'Meta' from emersed to submerged growth? When transitioning from emersed to submerged growth, plant bare stems securely into rich substrate under high lighting and pressurized CO2, keeping water parameters stable. As new growth adapts, the plant will shed its broader land foliage and sprout needle-like, colorful underwater whorls. Once new shoots take root, trim away old lower growth to encourage dense branching.

Plant Profile Cryptocoryne Spiralis ‘Nari’ is a striking Crypt variety known for its long, narrow leaves and distinctive, slightly twisted growth. Its deep green foliage adds height and movement to the aquarium, making it an excellent choice for the background or midground of larger planted tanks. Like other Cryptocoryne species, ‘Nari’ is relatively undemanding once established. It appreciates nutrient-rich substrate and consistent conditions, but does not require high lighting or CO2 to grow. Given time to settle in, it can develop into a dense cluster of slender leaves that creates a natural, grass-like appearance. Key Features & Benefits Long, narrow leaves with a naturally twisted growth pattern add height, texture, and movement A relatively undemanding Cryptocoryne that thrives under low to moderate lighting Benefits from nutrient-rich substrate and root fertilization to support healthy root development and new growth Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away or soak off the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before dividing and planting. Plant Cryptocoryne ‘Nari’ directly into the substrate, making sure the roots are buried while keeping the crown of the plant above the substrate. Provide low to moderate lighting and consistent water parameters while the plant establishes. CO2 is not required, but can encourage faster growth and fuller development. Avoid frequently uprooting or moving the plant after planting, as Cryptocorynes can take time to establish and may experience “Crypt melt” when introduced to a new environment. Feed the roots with nutrient-rich substrate or root tabs to encourage strong root development and healthy new growth. Allow the plant to grow naturally without frequent trimming. Remove older or damaged leaves at the base as needed to keep the plant looking healthy. Propagate established plants by separating the daughter plants that develop from runners and replanting them individually. Learn how to prevent Cryptocoryne melt to help your new Cryptocoryne acclimate successfully and establish healthy new growth. Plant Profile Schismatoglottis Prietoi is a compact aquatic aroid from the Philippines, known for its bright green, elliptic leaves and dense, low-growing habit. Often compared to miniature Anubias, its soft, wavy-edged leaves give it a distinctive look, while its tendency to spread by runners makes it especially useful for filling in the foreground and midground. Unlike many Anubias species, Schismatoglottis Prietoi is best planted directly into the substrate rather than attached to hardscape. It is an undemanding plant that can thrive under low lighting without CO2, although consistent nutrients and moderate lighting can encourage faster, fuller growth. Key Features & Benefits Compact, bright green leaves with gently wavy edges create a lush, textured appearance An easy, low-light plant that is well suited to low-tech aquariums Naturally spreads through runners, allowing it to form dense groups over time Faster growing than many similar Anubias varieties once established Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away or soak off the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before dividing and planting. Gently separate the plant into smaller portions if needed, taking care to preserve the roots and growing points. Plant Schismatoglottis Prietoi directly into the substrate, making sure the roots are buried. While Schismatoglottis Prietoi can grow attached to porous materials such as Lava Rock, it does not naturally adhere to hardscape like epiphytes. Planting it in substrate is the preferred method. Provide low to moderate lighting and stable water parameters while the plant establishes. CO2 is not required, but supplementation can encourage faster and more vigorous growth. Provide a consistent supply of nutrients through the water column and substrate to support healthy root development and new growth. Avoid frequently disturbing or moving the plant after planting. Schismatoglottis Prietoi can take some time to establish before producing vigorous new growth. Remove older, damaged, or melting leaves at the base as needed to maintain a healthy appearance. Allow established plants to spread naturally through runners. Once daughter plants have developed their own roots and several leaves, separate them from the runner and replant them individually. Holey Rock is a naturally porous limestone known for its unique holes, cavities, and textured surface. Its light, neutral color creates a clean contrast with green aquarium plants, dark substrates, and other aquascaping materials, making it a versatile choice for freshwater aquariums. Use Holey Rock to create natural-looking rock formations, add height and depth to your aquascape, or build detailed hardscape layouts with plenty of texture. The irregular holes and crevices give each piece a distinctive appearance and can be used to create more complex-looking rock structures. As a limestone-based aquarium rock, Holey Rock may naturally increase water hardness and pH. Keep this in mind when planning an aquascape for fish, shrimp, or other aquatic livestock that require soft or acidic water. Each piece is naturally unique, so size, shape, color, and the number of holes will vary. Notes: Naturally occurring variations make every piece different Porous structure gives the rock its characteristic pitted appearance Limestone composition can contribute calcium and carbonate to aquarium water May not be ideal for aquariums that require tightly controlled or very low mineral levels Holey Rock is natural limestone and may affect water chemistry. Test your aquarium water after adding the rock, particularly when keeping species that require soft or acidic water.

listings.description: Echinodorus 'Big Bear' is a large, eye-catching Amazon Sword variety known for its broad, slightly ruffled leaves and substantial size. Its bold appearance makes it a natural centerpiece plant for larger aquariums, where it can create a dense focal point in the background or midground. This tissue culture version is grown in a sterile laboratory environment, making it free from algae, pests, and unwanted hitchhikers. Once established in the aquarium, 'Big Bear' can develop into a large, full plant with impressive leaves that add plenty of visual weight to a planted tank. Key Features & Benefits: Broad, substantial leaves create a bold focal point Can grow into a large specimen suited to spacious aquariums Dense growth provides cover for fish and other aquarium inhabitants Works well as a centerpiece or background plant Tissue culture is grown in a sterile environment and arrives free of algae and pests Care Tips & Preparation: Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots before separating the plant into smaller portions for planting. Plant each portion into nutrient-rich aquarium soil, keeping the crown of the plant above the substrate to prevent rot. Give the plant time to establish its root system after planting. Some leaf melt can occur as the plant transitions from tissue culture to submerged growth. Provide low to moderate lighting and consistent fertilization to support healthy new growth. Root tabs are highly recommended, as Echinodorus are heavy root feeders that benefit from nutrients available directly in the substrate. Plant Profile Mayaca Fluviatilis is a delicate stem plant known for its slender stems and extremely fine, bright green leaves. Its soft, feathery appearance brings plenty of texture and movement to an aquascape, especially when planted in groups to create a dense background. This aquatic stem plant is surprisingly adaptable despite its delicate appearance. With proper lighting and nutrients, individual stems can grow into a lush, bushy cluster that adds depth without visually overwhelming the rest of the scaped tank. Tissue culture aquarium plants are grown in a controlled laboratory environment and arrive free of algae, pests, and other unwanted organisms, making them a convenient option for establishing a clean planted aquarium. Key Features & Benefits Extra fine, needle-like leaves create a soft, feathery texture Bright green color adds contrast against broader-leaved aquarium plants Works especially well when planted in groups for a fuller appearance Thin stems can be delicate, so handle the plant gently when dividing and planting Grows well as a background plant but can be trimmed shorter for midground use Care & Planting Instructions Remove the plant from the cup and gently wash away all nutrient gel with clean water. Separate the tissue culture into several small portions rather than planting the entire clump together. Plant individual portions into nutrient-rich aquarium substrate, leaving enough space between them for light to reach the lower stems. Mayaca Fluviatilis plants prefer moderate to high lighting. Insufficient light can cause the lower leaves to yellow and fall away. Regular fertilization will help support healthy, consistent growth. CO2 is not required, but adding CO2 can encourage denser growth and help the plant develop into a fuller bush. Some leaf loss can occur as the plant adjusts to aquarium conditions. New submerged growth should develop as it acclimates. Once established, trim the taller stems and replant the healthy cuttings to create a denser group. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when light cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Why are the lower stems on my Mayaca Fluviatilis turning yellow? Mayaca Fluviatilis requires moderate-to-high lighting to maintain its lower foliage. How do I transition Mayaca Fluviatilis from emersed to submerged growth? As new growth adapts, the plant will shed its land leaves and sprout soft, needle-thin underwater foliage. Once new shoots develop, trim away old lower growth to encourage dense branching.

Unlike thin, branch-heavy woods, these pieces have substantial sections of wood with extensions that give them a bold, sculptural look. The oversized pieces are well suited for larger aquariums where hardscape will make a strong presence without relying on a collection of smaller branches. Product Features & Benefits Thick, irregular sections give Rasamala Root a heavier visual presence than fine, branchy driftwood. Natural, uneven surfaces create variation throughout each piece. The dense shape works well for filling larger aquariums without needing to combine numerous pieces of wood. The textured surface provides plenty of areas for attaching mosses and epiphytic plants like Anubias and Bucephalandra. Each piece has a completely different shape, with variations in thickness, curves, texture, and overall structure. Size Specifications Photos provided are a representation of what you will receive. This is a natural aquarium hardscape product; please expect variations in shape, weight, and character. Rinse: Thoroughly rinse the piece to remove any dust or debris from transit. The Floating Phase: Rasamala Driftwood will float initially. We recommend soaking it thoroughly or boiling it. A large stone or heavy decor may be placed on top to ensure a non-waterlogged piece of wood stays submerged. Product Overview Keep aquarium glass clear of stubborn algae and buildup with the UNS Pro Algae Scraper. Designed for smooth, controlled cleaning, the Pro Algae Scraper combines a precision blade with an extendable handle to provide the reach needed for routine aquarium maintenance without sacrificing control. Unlike traditional algae scrapers that require screws or tools to change the blade, the UNS Pro Algae Scraper features a quick-release blade holder that allows blades to be removed and replaced in seconds. Available in two sizes, the adjustable design makes it easy to choose the right amount of reach for everything from compact planted aquariums to deeper tanks and hard-to-reach areas. Key Features & Benefits Quick-Release Blade Holder: Swap scraper blades in seconds without screws or additional tools, making blade replacement fast and straightforward. Extendable Handle: Add extra reach when cleaning deeper aquariums, back panels, or areas that are difficult to access comfortably. How can I prevent trapping sand and scratching my glass near the substrate line? When scraping near aquasoil or cosmetic sand beds, stop the blade about 0.5 inches above the substrate line. Avoid pushing the blade directly into sand to prevent trapping abrasive grains beneath the blade edge.

Plant Profile Bucephalandra ‘Shine Blue’ is a low-tech aquarium plant known for its blue-green leaves and subtle blue iridescence. The leaves have gently undulating edges and can develop a deeper blue sheen under suitable aquarium lighting. Like other Bucephalandra varieties, Shine Blue is a slow-growing epiphyte that can be attached to rocks and driftwood, making it a natural fit for detailed freshwater aquascapes. Key Features & Notes Blue-green leaves develop a subtle metallic blue sheen that becomes more noticeable under aquarium lighting. Gently undulating leaf margins add texture and detail to rocks, driftwood, and other hardscape. Slow growth makes Shine Blue a good choice for aquascapes that don't require frequent trimming. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for planted tanks where other plants might struggle. Care & Planting Instructions Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard low-light aquarium plant setups, CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and richer iridescence. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I get more blue color from Bucephalandra Shine Blue? Stable aquarium conditions and appropriate lighting can help bring out the blue-green coloration and iridescent sheen of Shine Blue. Individual plants can vary in coloration depending on their growing conditions.

listings.commonName: Bucephalandra sp. White UNS Tissue Culture
listings.description: Plant Profile Bucephalandra sp. ‘White’ is a rare Bucephalandra variety known for its pale green to silvery-white leaves and compact growth. Its light coloration provides strong contrast against dark rocks, driftwood, and other green aquarium plants, making it a unique choice for detailed aquascapes. Like other Buce, it is a slow-growing rhizome plant that can be attached to hardscape rather than planted in the substrate. This variety is more sensitive than many common Bucephalandra and may require stable conditions, consistent nutrients, and appropriate lighting to maintain its pale coloration. It can be grown fully submerged in freshwater aquariums and is best suited to foreground or midground placement where its unusual color can stand out. Tissue cultures provide a clean, lab-grown start that is free from algae, snails, and other common aquarium hitchhikers. Once removed from the cup, the plant can be divided into smaller portions and attached to rocks or driftwood to establish throughout an aquascape. Key Features & Notes Leaves have a distinct pale, almost frosted appearance that sets this variety apart from darker green Bucephalandra. New growth can emerge lighter before developing more coloration as the leaves mature. Forms a compact clump over time rather than sending out tall vertical growth. Mature plants can develop multiple leaf sizes within the same clump, giving established specimens a more layered appearance. The unusual light coloration makes it easy to distinguish from more traditional green Buce varieties. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by carefully removing the plantlets from the cup and rinsing away all sterile nutrient gel under lukewarm, dechlorinated water before mounting. Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood with aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as it will rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard low-light aquarium plant setups, CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and a smoother tissue culture transition. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Why is my tissue culture Bucephalandra melting after planting? Tissue culture plants undergo an acclimation phase when transitioning to underwater conditions. Maintain stable water parameters, good circulation, and moderate light; as long as the rhizome stays firm, new submerged leaves will emerge. 3. Is Bucephalandra sp. ‘White’ actually white? Its leaves can range from pale green to silvery-white rather than being pure white. Coloration varies with growing conditions and individual plants.

Detail Root is a versatile aquarium driftwood with a fine, root-like structure that makes it easy to add smaller details and natural texture to an aquascape. Each pack includes 20 pieces of thin, irregular natural wood that can be arranged individually or layered together to create the look of exposed roots, dense branches, or a more intricate hardscape. Product Features & Benefits Fine, root-like pieces add detail to larger hardscape layouts. Multiple shapes and lengths make it easy to build layered, natural-looking structures. Works well for creating root systems, overhangs, and transitional areas between rocks and substrate. Natural texture provides plenty of surfaces for attaching mosses and epiphytic plants like Anubias and Bucephalandra. Each piece is naturally unique, with variations in shape, thickness, curves, and branching. Preparation & Care Driftwood is a natural product and requires a bit of prep before it’s ready for prime time. Rinse: Thoroughly rinse the piece to remove any dust or debris from transit. The Floating Phase: Driftwood may float initially. We recommend soaking it thoroughly, boiling it, or tucking it into larger hardscape structures so the root stays submerged. Tannin Management: While low in tannins, a quick boil can help fast-track the sinking process and ensure your water stays crystal clear. You can also reduce this effect through consistent water changes or through the addition of Aquario Neo Carbon Bag Important note: We recommend rinsing wood thoroughly before adding it to an established aquarium. If you prefer, you may also boil the wood for at least 1–2 hours to help release tannins.

Plant Profile Anubias barteri 'King' is a large Anubias variety known for its broad leaves and cream-white marbling. With leaves that can reach around 4–8 in, this epiphytic plant makes an excellent centerpiece for larger aquariums. Its bold size and variegated coloring give it a distinctive look while retaining the hardy nature Anubias is known for. Key Features & Benefits Broad, rounded leaves with irregular cream-white marbling Mature leaves develop a distinctive variegated pattern Thick, substantial leaf structure Large overall size compared to many other Anubias varieties Dense, compact growth from a sturdy rhizome Works well as a focal point among smaller-leaved plants Particularly suited to larger aquascapes where its size can stand out Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the horizontal rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce initial leaf loss. Avoid intense direct light and ensure good water flow to prevent spot algae on slow‑growing leaves. CO₂ is optional but improves growth speed and leaf density. Learn more about planting these species by reading our guide on How to Plant Epiphyte Aquatic Plants. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth!
