Plant Profile Willow Moss is the choice for you if you want to swap out messy, unruly growth for an elegant, cascading aesthetic. While it shares some hardy DNA with its cousin Java Moss, this species sets itself apart with graceful, delicate fronds that flow downward, beautifully mimicking the sweeping branches of a willow tree. It is an exceptional layout choice for softening up the jagged edges of rockwork or draping over driftwood to create a forest or tree canopy look. It creates a dense, luxurious texture that serves as a playground and a safe shelter where shrimp and shy fish fry can confidently forage and hang out. Key Features & Benefits Drooping fronds cascade downward to add soft movement and organic depth. Spreads over hardscape elements to quickly give stones and driftwood a mature, weathered look. Dense, delicate weave of branches creates an ideal surface area for beneficial biofilm. Care & Planting Instructions Secure the loose moss portions to your chosen hardscape surfaces, like driftwood branches or porous rocks, using thin thread or aquarium-safe glue. Maintain a stable aquarium environment and avoid sudden, drastic changes to your water parameters to keep your moss looking vibrant and healthy. Give the moss an occasional light haircut with sharp aquascaping shears to keep its shape neat, compact, and perfectly balanced. Propagate your patch in seconds by cutting or pulling a small clump apart and anchoring it to a new surface in your tank. Plant Profile Living up to its regal name, Echinodorus 'Marble Queen' brings a variegated look to the sword plant family. This rare cultivar produces broad, heart-shaped to oval green leaves intricately marbled with creamy-white and pale yellow streaks across the entire blade. Maxing out around 12 inches tall, its balanced proportions make it an eye-catching centerpiece in midground zones or a prominent background feature in medium aquariums. Its hardy nature, undemanding care requirements, and contrasting leaf patterns make it a stunning collector-grade addition that brightens up any planted layout without requiring high-maintenance effort. Key Features & Notes Striking marbled foliage displays creamy white and pale yellow patterns across rich green leaves. Broad, heart-shaped leaf structure creates a dramatic focal point in midground or background zones. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Plant the roots deeply into your aquarium soil, keeping the central crown resting just above the substrate line to prevent rot. All Echinodorus are heavy root feeders that rely on rich substrate nutrition; placing root tabs near the base supports steady, healthy leaf development. Provide moderate to high lighting; while CO2 injection isn't strictly required, good lighting will enhance its variegated contrast. Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf shedding during the initial transition period. Sword plants propagate through side shoots off of their leaves, which can be trimmed and replanted into the substrate. To control the size of your sword plant, you can remove the side shoots and older leaves. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Plant Profile Alternanthera Reineckii, known in the hobby simply as AR, is a classic red aquatic stem plant that's been putting other red plants to shame with how easy it is to keep colorful. Beginners and experienced aquascapers alike reach for this one because it holds rich ruby-red and magenta coloration far more reliably than other red stems, no complicated dosing schedule required. Broad, lanceolate leaves grow in opposing pairs along stems reaching 4 to 12 inches tall, making it a natural midground centerpiece or background hedge for anyone who wants bold color contrast in their freshwater aquarium without the high upkeep. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Beginner-friendly red stem choice that maintains rich coloration more easily than traditional high-demand red plants. Dense foliage shelters dwarf shrimp and shy fish. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight (or pot) and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the roots, then strip lower foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push stems 1–2 inches into soil, spacing them apart for light penetration. Provide medium-to-high lighting. Regular dosing of liquid fertilizers like UNS Plant Food to maintain healthy nitrate and phosphate levels alongside pressurized CO2 injection will prevent dull orange fading and speed up growth. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim main stem tops with straight scissors once stems reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to propagate and expand coverage. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. As new growth adapts, the plant will shed its stiffer land leaves and sprout vibrant, rich red underwater foliage. Once new shoots take root, trim away old lower growth to encourage dense branching.

Plant Profile Alternanthera Bettzickiana Red, commonly known as the Red Calico Plant, is a bold and adaptable semi-aquatic species native to Central and South America. Highly favored for terrariums, paludariums, vivariums, ponds, and bog gardens, this striking plant features vibrant pink-to-red stems and green-to-yellow leaves that turn a vivid, fiery red under high-intensity lighting. While not a permanently aquatic species, it is often used as a long-lasting temporary submerged display in freshwater aquariums, maintaining its eye-catching colors and developing root systems underwater for several months before benefiting from an emersed recovery period. *Semi-Aquatic Notice: For permanent, long-term health and growth, it is best grown emersed in paludariums, terrariums, bog gardens, or moist outdoor ponds. Key Features & Benefits Bold color palette ranging from green and yellow to vivid pink and deep red. Versatile semi-aquatic species that excels in high-humidity bog environments, vivariums, and water margin planters. Provides excellent protective cover and shelter for sensitive fauna species. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight (or pot) and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the roots, then strip lower foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them so light reaches lower leaves. Provide medium-to-high lighting for intense pink and red coloration; keep soil consistently moist in terrestrial/emersed setups or maintain high humidity in closed enclosures. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid drastic environmental changes to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting during submerged periods. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once stems reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into moist soil to propagate new growth. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Plant Profile Buce ‘Green Wavy’ is a low-tech, entry-level aquarium plant featuring bright green ruffled leaves that develop into a dense, bushy appearance over time. This farm-grown variety is prized for its unique tendency to branch naturally without trimming, making it a favorite for those seeking a low-maintenance yet lush aesthetic. Highly versatile, it can be grown submerged or emersed, usually attached to hardscape such as driftwood or rocks rather than being buried in traditional aquarium substrate. It's a beautiful addition to for the foreground or midground of freshwater aquascapes, where it will slowly sprout from thin rhizomes to create a textured, iridescent colony within a planted tank. Key Features & Notes Unlike some Buce variants that grow in a single line, 'Green Wavy' branches frequently, creating a full and shrub-like look very quickly. The bright green leaves feature distinctly wavy margins that catch the light, providing great visual detail even in low-flow areas. This is one of the most durable species in the hobby and thrives in shaded areas . It is an ideal choice for planted tanks where other plants might struggle. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant that should be attached to rocks or driftwood using aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as this will cause the plant to rot and melt. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard low-light aquarium plant setups, CO2 injection and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and richer iridescence. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Plant Profile Micro Sword (Lilaeopsis Brasiliensis) is an exceptional choice for beginners wanting to tackle an underwater carpet for the very first time. Growing in thick, beautifully arching tufts, this hardy species can transform your foreground into a wild, lush field when planted in dense groups. It is incredibly versatile and works just as well as a compact midground or background filler in nano aquariums, thanks to its dense growth profile. It maps out your substrate by pushing out horizontal runners. Key Features & Benefits A beginner-friendly species that is highly forgiving for first-time carpet growers. Achieve a wild, natural meadow look in your tank with its unique, arching tufts of green. Versatile profile works as a foreground carpet or scales up beautifully into a nano midground backdrop. Give this plant room to spread naturally, as it grows by sending out runners horizontally throughout the substrate. Keep the growth short and compact by maintaining high light and CO2 parameters, creating a manicured underwater lawn of green. Propagate simply like other foreground plants by cutting out portions from the horizontal shoots and replanting the clumps that you cut out. Plant Profile Hydrocotyle Japan (Hydrocotyle Tripartita) brings a unique, whimsical texture to your tank with its distinct, clover-like leaves. Made famous by legendary aquascapers like Takashi Amano, this fast-growing favorite is incredibly versatile and can be used in the foreground, midground, or background depending on your vision. Left to its own devices, it will happily grow into wild, compact bushes of vibrant green. It is an exceptionally undemanding and energetic grower, meaning it will gladly take over the entire tank if you don't keep its enthusiastic growth in check! Key Features & Benefits Clover-like green foliage that adds a playful, natural texture. Fill in your aquascape rapidly thanks to its fast growth rate, making it an excellent option for quickly blanketing bare spots. Keep a pair of trimming scissors handy, as it grows quickly and requires regular pruning to prevent it from out-competing and overgrowing your other tank inhabitants. Propagate whenever you want by simply cutting the stems anywhere along the shoot and replanting them, or by pulling apart dense clumps and splitting the roots. Maintain stable aquarium parameters and avoid any sudden, drastic shifts in water quality to prevent your new grass from melting. Plant Profile Cabomba aquatica, commonly known as Yellow Fanwort or Giant Cabomba, is renowned for its captivating, delicate aesthetic that instantly softens an aquascape. Its standout feature is its intricate foliage, where each stem produces opposite pairs of fine, finely divided, fan-shaped leaves that spread out in precise, circular whorls along slender upright stalks. In healthy conditions, the delicate needle-like segments radiate outward in bright lime green to subtle yellow-green tones, creating a cloud-like, feathery texture underwater. When planted in tight clusters in the midground or background, these lush plumes merge into a thick, pillow-soft wall of greenery that sways elegantly with water circulation. Compared to some of its finicky reddish relatives, Cabomba aquatica offers a far more forgiving experience while delivering that prized, highly detailed foliage style. Key Features & Notes Feathery, fan-shaped leaves arranged in circular whorls create a soft, cloud-like visual texture. Vibrant lime-to-yellow-green foliage adds bright contrast and fine detail to background groupings. Hardier and more forgiving than red Cabomba species, making it an accessible choice for fine-leaved stem lovers. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the lead wrap or pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Plant individual stems into aquarium soil using fine-tipped tweezers, spacing them slightly apart to ensure light reaches the lower fan blades. Provide moderate-to-high light to keep the fan whorls compact and prevent the lower stem portions from shedding leaves. Propagate by trimming the upper stem tops with sharp aquascaping scissors and replanting them directly into the substrate. Maintain clean water conditions and avoid sudden parameter fluctuations to prevent delicate leaf shedding. Final density and leaf color depend on lighting and nutrient availability; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Plant Profile Native to the lush marshlands and limestone streams of Southeast Asia, Crypt Blassii is known for large, oval-shaped leaves with deep olive-green tops and rich purple-red undersides, the kind of bold tropical flair that instantly upgrades an aquatic garden. As with all crypts, it can be sensitive to changes in water parameters and doesn't like to be moved. But once its roots settle into your substrate, it becomes a robust, eye-catching midground anchor worth the setup effort. Key Features & Benefits Broad oval foliage features striking olive-green topside coloration paired with rich purple-red undersides. Originates from mineral-rich marshlands, offering exceptional structural hardiness once established in the substrate. Lush rosette growth forms a grand midground centerpiece that creates excellent natural shelter for shy fish. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Crypt species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. Because Cryptocoryne plants absorb the vast majority of their nutrients through their roots rather than their leaves, providing nutrient-rich aquasoil or root tabs inside sand or gravel is far more effective than relying on water column liquid fertilizers alone.

Its structural rosettes pair beautifully alongside broad-leaved Anubias or fine-textured stem plants. 3. How do I help my Cryptocoryne Sri Lanka recover if it melts after planting? Crypt melt is a standard reaction when shifting water conditions cause old leaves to dissolve so the plant can grow new foliage adapted to your tank. Trim away decaying tissue, maintain stable water conditions, and do not disturb the subterranean roots. For complete recovery steps, check out our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt .

Plant Profile If you're looking for a dependable, beginner-friendly staple to fill out your midground, Cryptocoryne walkeri is an enduring classic that delivers rich natural texture with minimal effort. Native to the fast-flowing, limestone-bed streams of Sri Lanka, this adaptable species sports lance-shaped foliage ranging from vibrant green to warm bronze tones. As with all crypt plants, this species can be sensitive to sudden parameter shifts and strongly objects to being relocated once planted. Key Features & Benefits Sturdy lanceolate leaves in shades of green and bronze add timeless natural elegance to midground zones. Can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups where mature plants can potentially produce unique flowering spathes above the water. Native limestone stream origins make it highly resilient and capable of thriving in a wide variety of hard or soft water parameters. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel. Ensure adequate calcium levels in the water column or substrate to support strong leaf structural integrity. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Crypt species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. Plant Profile Pogostemon Stellatus is a classic aquatic stem plant prized for its fine-textured, star-like whorls of foliage and versatile color range. Displaying vibrant hues from light green and golden-orange to deep pink and magenta, this species brings continuous movement, flow, and structural dimension to midground and background zones. When pruned routinely, Pogostemon Stellatus branches into dense, colorful bushes that serve as dramatic focal points in both Dutch-style and nature aquarium layouts. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Thin, needle-like foliage radiates out from vertical stems, adding distinct star-like texture and visual motion to planted aquariums. Leaf colors dynamically shift into bright pink, orange, and deep red tones under moderate-to-high lighting and consistent iron dosing. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight (or pot) and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip the lower inch of foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. * Stems can be fragile, so handle with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into soil, spacing them so light reaches lower leaves. Provide moderate-to-high lighting. Adding pressurized CO2 injection and iron supplementation accelerates growth and yields rich red and pink coloration. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the surface to encourage lower stems to shoot out new side branches. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Plant Profile Heteranthera zosterifolia, also known in the aquascaping community as Stargrass, is a popular and fast-growing aquatic stem plant native to the tropical marshes, ponds, and slow-moving streams of Brazil and South America. Named for its bright green, star-like leaf whorls that radiate outward from central stems, this species is highly valued for bringing soft texture and dynamic visual energy to planted aquariums. Under moderate lighting, Stargrass grows upright with an elegant, loose habit, while under intense light and CO2, it forms remarkably dense, sprawling bushes that can be sculpted into lush midground mounds or background hedges. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Distinct star-shaped leaf whorls deliver a vibrant lime-green color and unique, high-energy visual texture. Versatile growth habit easily pruned into dense midground bushes or grown tall as a lush background hedge. Fast growth acts as a powerful natural nutrient sponge to help absorb excess nitrates and prevent algae. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight (or pot) and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the roots, then strip lower foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push small groups of stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower foliage and prevents shading. Provide moderate-to-high lighting and clean water conditions; while adaptable without CO2, supplying pressurized CO2 (6–14 ppm) and liquid fertilization yields exceptionally dense, bushy horizontal growth. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim main stem tops with curved scissors once stems reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into substrate to easily propagate and expand coverage. Plant Profile The Red Tiger Lotus ( Nymphaea zenkeri ) is a stunning water lily that brings an instant splash of rich color and bold shape to any tank. What makes it so special is its dramatic foliage: broad, deep crimson-red wavy leaves covered in variegations of orange, bronze, and brown. It offers incredible contrast when set against bright green carpet plants or delicate stem background hedges. If you keep up with regular pruning, it will stay low and produce a full, bushy rosette of submerged leaves right in your midground. But if you let it stretch its legs, it'll send long stems up to the surface to form classic floating lily pads. These floating leaves add a lovely, natural pond vibe to the top of your tank while creating comfortable shade and cover for shy fish below. Prefer to sprout your own? Grab the bulb! Key Features & Benefits Vibrant crimson foliage marked with speckled patterns creates a showstopping centerpiece in any aquarium. Versatile growth habit lets you trim it low for a bushy midground look or let it float to create natural surface lily pads. Care & Planting Instructions Gently remove the plant from its lead bunch wrap or potted foam. Use fine-tip pinsettes to anchor developing root shoots into aquarium soil or use root tabs, as Tiger Lotus plants are heavy root feeders. Provide moderate to high lighting and clean water conditions; while CO2 is not required, supplying CO2 and iron-rich fertilizer brings out the deepest ruby-red leaf tones. Maintain stable water parameters to give your lotus a smooth transition and prevent initial leaf melting. To control growth, simply trim off long surface runner stems at the base to encourage the plant to produce shorter, compact submerged leaves. Plant Profile Vallisneria 'Contortionist', widely known as Corkscrew Val, brings a delightfully tight, spiraled texture to the rear of your aquascape. While it shares the signature fast growth rate and runner-propagating habits of Vallisneria americana (Jungle Val), it differs noticeably in scale and leaf morphology. Unlike the broad, loosely wavy blades of Jungle Val, Corkscrew Val produces narrower, more tightly twisted leaves that resemble spiraled ribbons or springy tendrils as they shoot upward. It swiftly spreads via root runners to create a dense, dancing curtain of green foliage that adds dynamic motion to any background. Key Features & Notes Tight, corkscrew-like spirals offer a distinct and dramatic texture compared to broader Vallisneria varieties. More compact, narrower leaf blades compared to giant V. americana , making size management in medium tanks easier. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap surrounding the root crown, taking care not to crush or damage the roots. Plant individual crowns gently into aquarium soil or fine substrate, keeping the base of the crown visible just above the substrate line to prevent rot. All Vallisneria species are heavy root feeders; placing root tabs near the base supports strong anchoring and continuous runner production. Trim surface-drifting leaf tips cleanly with sharp aquascaping scissors to control height and prevent shading nearby plants. Maintain stable water chemistry, as Vallisneria can be sensitive to sudden parameter swings or liquid carbon supplements. Final size and leaf curl intensity depend on your specific tank conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Plant Profile Water Lettuce is a classic, recognizable floating plant, popular in both ponds and aquariums for its resemblance to an open head of lettuce, minus the salad bowl. Shrimp keepers and aquascapers love it for its long, feather-like root systems that drape deep into the water column, offering endless surface area for beneficial biofilm grazing and a haven for timid livestock. It's also a fast grower, acting as a powerhouse nitrate sponge and making it a great biological filter for tanks housing water-parameter-sensitive species. Just keep in mind its dense canopy blocks overhead light fast, so it pairs best with low-light submerged plants like crypts and bucephalandra. Key Features & Benefits Green velvety leaves form attractive rosettes that create a floating garden effect. Long roots provide abundant coverage, shade, and biofilm grazing space for shrimp and fry. Absorbs excess nitrates and organic waste to suppress nuisance algae growth. Care & Planting Instructions Gently place the plants directly onto the water surface, ensuring the tops of the leaves remain dry. Keep surface agitation minimal, as heavy water flow or splashing filters will trap water on top of the leaves and cause them to rot. Provide adequate lighting to encourage rapid growth and bring out rich coloration. Thin out the floating carpet regularly to ensure light still reaches your submerged midground and stem plants below. Dose liquid fertilizers regularly because floating plants absorb nutrients directly from the water column at an accelerated rate. Plant Profile Bolbitis Heteroclita (Asian Water Fern) bridges the gap between delicate water ferns and classic Java Fern , featuring broad, deep-green fronds with a distinctively rugged leaf structure. Native to humid riverbanks across Southeast Asia, this slow-growing epiphyte stays compact at 2 to 4 inches, making it a versatile midground accent for planted aquariums, terrariums, and paludariums alike. Serving as the ultimate low-stress starter plant, this bulletproof fern thrives under dim lighting, laughs in the face of parameter swings, and remains unbothered by curious fish looking for a snack. Key Features & Notes Tough, fibrous foliage easily withstands curious nipping from herbivorous fish like cichlids, goldfish, and large snails. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Bolbitis Heteroclita is an epiphytic fern that should be attached to rocks or driftwood with aquarium-safe glue or thread; never bury the horizontal rhizome in substrate, as it will rot and melt. Position this plant in areas with moderate to high water circulation, as Bolbitis species thrive when water currents pass gently through their fronds. Avoid making drastic changes to your water parameters or lighting because unstable conditions are the primary cause of leaf melt in new specimens. While this plant is hardy and low-maintenance in standard setups, gentle water movement and regular liquid fertilizing will yield much faster growth and broader fronds. Final size and foliage pattern depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. What makes Bolbitis Heteroclita different from Bolbitis Heudelotii? While Bolbitis Heudelotii (African Water Fern) features finely divided, translucent, pinnate leaves, Bolbitis Heteroclita produces broader, thicker foliage that more closely resembles standard Java Fern. It also tends to grow more compact in submerged aquarium conditions. 2. Can I plant Bolbitis Heteroclita directly into substrate? No. Bolbitis Heteroclita is a true epiphyte that absorbs nutrients directly from the water column through its fronds and root network. Burying its horizontal rhizome in soil, sand, or gravel will cause the stem to suffocate, rot, and die. Always attach it to rocks or driftwood using plant glue or thread. 3. Can Bolbitis Heteroclita be grown in terrariums or paludariums? Yes! Bolbitis Heteroclita adapts exceptionally well to emersed growth. When kept in high ambient humidity (80%+), it makes a fantastic choice for humid terrariums, vivariums, and paludarium land sections mounted onto wet rocks or moss walls. 4. Will fish like cichlids or goldfish eat Bolbitis Heteroclita? Generally, no. Bolbitis leaves are thick, fibrous, and bitter-tasting, making them naturally unappealing to herbivorous fish. While rowdy diggers might knock unbound plants off hardscape, they rarely consume the foliage.

Plant Profile Hydrocotyle Sibthorpioides, commonly known as Lawn Marsh Pennywort, is a charming little aquatic plant native to Asia with delicate, rounded, clover-like leaves. It's often compared to the popular Hydrocotyle tripartita 'Japan' , but produces distinctively rounder foliage. It's also refreshingly easy to work with: run it as a low-growing foreground carpet under high light and CO2, let it bush out in the midground, or just let it trail across your hardscape and see where it ends up. Thanks to its fast growth rate, it's a great option when you want lush greenery filling in your freshwater aquascape sooner rather than later. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Rounded clover-like leaves create unique visual texture across foreground carpet, midground, or hardscape zones. Rapidly fills in empty space while helping absorb excess water column nutrients. A versatile growth pattern can be trained into a tight foreground carpet. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stem clusters 1 to 2 inches into nutrient-rich substrate, spacing them slightly apart to encourage lateral running shoots. Provide medium-to-high lighting. While adaptable, providing pressurized CO2 injection and intense light keeps growth low, dense, and carpet-like. Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim runner shoots anywhere along the stem with curved scissors to encourage thicker, more compact branching. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. When transitioning from emersed to submerged growth, plant bare stem clusters securely into nutrient-rich substrate under medium-to-high lighting and keep water parameters stable. As new growth adapts, the plant will shed its stiffer emersed foliage and sprout delicate, round underwater leaves. Once new runners spread, trim away old lower growth to encourage a dense carpet.

Plant Profile If you're looking to create the natural look of a miniature grassy meadow without the high-light maintenance of demanding carpeting species, Cryptocoryne lucens is a foolproof aquarium plant for low-tech setups. Native to Sri Lanka, this freshwater favorite sports narrow, bright emerald-green leaves set against rich brown stems that form lush, reed-like thickets when planted in groups. As with all crypt plants, this species can be sensitive to changes in water parameters and strongly objects to being relocated once planted. Key Features & Benefits Slender emerald-green foliage creates a natural, grassy reed effect in foreground and midground zones. Hardy and adaptable, making it an excellent low-maintenance choice for low-tech aquarium setups. Can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups, where mature plants may produce flowering spathes. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Cryptocoryne species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel to supply essential subterranean nutrients. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth and fuller foliage density, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Cryptocoryne species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting subterranean runners or replanting offshoot plantlets. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. Plant Profile Vallisneria 'Torta', commonly known as Torta Val, is a compact dwarf variant that brings the iconic spiraled look of Vallisneria into smaller aquascapes. As a smaller sibling to Vallisneria Contortionist (Corkscrew Vallisneria) , it produces tight, spring-like twisted foliage with a noticeably shorter height profile. This manageable scale makes it a fantastic background option for nano tanks, or a dynamic midground-to-background transitional plant in larger setups where standard Jungle Vals would easily overpower the space. Like all members of the Val family, it spreads readily via underground runners to create a lush, dancing curtain of green foliage without requiring constant maintenance or delicate handling. Key Features & Notes Compact height makes it an ideal dwarf alternative to larger Corkscrew and Jungle Val varieties. Tightly twisted, spiraled leaf structure adds dynamic texture and motion to midground and background zones. Spreads steadily via runner shoots to form dense, low-maintenance thickets of grass-like foliage. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap surrounding the root crown, taking care not to crush or damage the roots. Plant individual crowns into aquarium soil or fine substrate, making sure to leave the crown resting just above the substrate line to prevent rot. All Vallisneria species are heavy root feeders; placing root tabs near the base supports strong root anchoring and quick runner production. Trim surface-drifting leaf tips cleanly with sharp aquascaping scissors to manage height and prevent shading lower-growing plants. Maintain stable water parameters, as sudden environmental changes or liquid carbon additives can cause initial leaf melt. Final size and spiraling intensity depend on your specific tank conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Vallisneria species can experience transition melt when introduced to new water chemistry or exposed to liquid carbon supplements. Plant Profile Vallisneria spiralis is a classic aquatic runner species that is a go-to choice among tall aquarium plants for establishing a sweeping, grass-like background in planted tanks. Once established, it rapidly shoots long vertical leaves toward the surface, draping across the top of the water column to form a natural living canopy while swaying gently with the filter current. As one of the most reliable aquarium plants for beginners, it will happily form a dense jungle backdrop as long as you do not mind trimming leaves that breach the water surface and drift across the top. Key Features & Notes Long ribbon-like foliage grows tall to conceal heaters, filter pipes, and background equipment. Adapts well to low-tech tanks, though root fertilizers and moderate light promote faster growth. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap surrounding the root crown, taking care not to crush or damage the roots. As heavy root feeders, Vallisneria should be planted deeply into aquarium soil to ensure they anchor securely and absorb vital nutrients. Provide root tab fertilization and reliable lighting to feed these nutrient-loving plants and sustain fast vertical growth. Trim overgrown leaves near the base using sharp aquascaping shears rather than topping them, and snip spreading runner shoots to propagate or control expansion across your background zones. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Plant Profile Bacopa Caroliniana Red is a hardy, easy-to-grow aquatic stem plant recognized for its thick, oval leaves and upright growth habit. While typically displaying bright olive-green foliage in low-tech setups, the tips of new growth transform into striking hues of pink, bronze, and red when supplied with strong lighting and micronutrient dosing. It serves as an ideal background species for beginners seeking to introduce color contrast without demanding high-maintenance care. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Foliage tips naturally develop rich pink and reddish tones under moderate-to-high lighting paired with micronutrient and iron supplementation. Tolerates a wide range of water conditions and thrives without requiring mandatory CO2 injection. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip the lower inch of foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. * Bacopa leaves are fragile, so handle stems with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them apart so light reaches lower leaves. Provide moderate-to-high lighting. Pressurized CO2 injection will accelerate growth rate and yield fuller stems. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters to support steady growth and prevent leaf melt or rotting in fragile stems. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the water surface to promote new lateral branching. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Plant Profile Didiplis Diandra is a refined aquatic stem plant native to the ponds, lakes, and slow-moving streams of the southeastern United States. Its delicate, needle-like leaves grow in cross-shaped whorls along slender stems, forming soft, cloud-like bushes that look almost too delicate to be this easy to keep. It holds a fresh olive-green color under moderate conditions, but crank up the lighting, add CO2 and iron supplementation, and the growing tips blush with orange, salmon, and ruby-red tones, creating a stunning visual accent in midground or background zones. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Needle-like foliage blushes orange, salmon, and red under high lighting and tuned fertilization. Dense branching forms soft, geometric bushes, great for Dutch-style streets with routine pruning. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems or small stem groups 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing them slightly apart so light reaches lower leaves. Provide moderate-to-high lighting; adding pressurized CO2 and regular iron dosing maximizes growth speed and brings out vivid red leaf tips. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid drastic environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or stem rotting. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the desired height, and replant trimmings directly into the substrate to propagate and expand your bush. Plant Profile Salvinia Cucullata is a less common floating plant with small, nickel-sized leaves and a signature trick: unique pouch-like, hooded folds that trap air pockets to keep it buoyant, no gimmicks required. Unlike many other aquarium floaters, it skips the long, trailing root systems draping into the water column, instead rapidly forming dense, compact mats across the surface. That makes it ideal for low-tech tanks and paludariums, where the natural shade it creates helps keep nuisance algae in check while giving your livestock a peaceful canopy to live under. Key Features & Benefits Hooded leaves with air pouches create a three-dimensional texture across the water surface. Short, compact root structure provides a sleek look that will not entangle taller background stems or snag swimming fish. Absorbs excess nitrates and waterborne nutrients to help starve out algae. Care & Planting Instructions Gently place the plants directly onto the water surface, ensuring the tops of the leaves remain dry. Keep surface agitation minimal, as heavy water flow or splashing filters will trap water on top of the leaves and cause them to rot. Provide adequate lighting to encourage rapid growth and bring out rich coloration. Thin out the floating carpet regularly to ensure light still reaches your submerged midground and stem plants below. Dose liquid fertilizers regularly because floating plants absorb nutrients directly from the water column at an accelerated rate. How do I keep my floating aquarium plants from dying due to filter flow and splashing? High water turbulence and constant water resting on the leaves are the main causes of rot in floating aquarium plants. Keep surface flow low, or use an airline tubing loop or floating ring to shield your aquarium floaters from direct filter return or bubbling air stones. 2. Can floating plants help control algae and absorb nitrates in a fish tank? Yes, these aquarium floaters act as incredible biological filters. Because they sit at the surface with direct access to atmospheric carbon dioxide, they grow exponentially faster than fully submerged species, aggressively consuming nitrates, ammonium, and excess nutrients that fuel nuisance algae. 3. Should I trim the hanging roots or thin out excess surface growth? Unlike other floaters, Salvinia Cucullata maintains naturally short roots that rarely require trimming. However, routinely thinning out excess leaf coverage is crucial so that your floating plants do not completely block light from reaching your submerged stem and ground plants below.

Plant Profile Lagenandra Meeboldii 'Red' brings the classic Crypt look with a color palette that doesn't play by Crypt rules. It develops broad, oval-shaped leaves that showcase a blend of dusty green, olive, rich red-violet, and bright purple-pink, often all on the same leaf. Fresh new foliage unfolds in a soft pastel pink before maturing into deep reddish-brown tones. Native to the shady streams and damp riverbanks of Southwestern India, this eye-catching member of the Araceae family shares close ties with both Bucephalandra and Cryptocoryne. Reaching 5 or more inches in height with a wide-spreading habit, Lagenandra Meeboldii 'Red' makes an unforgettable, low-maintenance centerpiece for midground zones in both high- and low-tech aquariums. Key Features & Benefits Vibrant multi-tonal foliage shifts from soft pastel pink on new leaves to rich red-violet, purple, and olive-green on mature growth. Hardy, easy-care rhizome plant that looks like a lush hybrid of Homalomena and Cryptocoryne wendtii . Thrives both submerged in aquariums and emersed in humid terrariums or paludariums. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Plant the roots firmly into your aquarium soil, taking care to keep the main central rhizome resting slightly above the substrate surface to prevent rot. As a heavy root-feeding species, Lagenandra Meeboldii 'Red' responds to root nutrition; placing root tabs directly near the roots in your aquarium soil encourages fuller foliage and faster growth. Provide low to medium lighting; while it easily adapts to lower light, moderate lighting and regular liquid iron supplementation will help bring out those vivid violet and pink undertones. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Keep water parameters stable and avoid sudden changes in water chemistry to prevent temporary leaf melting during transition. To propagate, use a sharp blade to carefully slice the thick rhizome into smaller sections (ensuring each piece has several leaves and healthy roots attached) and replant them back into your aquarium soil. Like many members of the Araceae family, Lagenandra can shed a few leaves when adjusting to new water parameters. As long as the rhizome remains firm in your aquarium soil, leave it in place! It will quickly adapt and sprout fresh new leaves.

Plant Profile Hydrocotyle Leucocephala, better known as Brazilian Pennywort, is the ultimate fast-growing multitasker from South America’s wetlands. Featuring iconic, half-dollar-shaped circular leaves along creeping stems, this bulletproof plant brings a fun, coin-like texture to any tank. It’s absurdly versatile: anchor it in the substrate, weave it through driftwood, or just let it float at the surface. Give it routine haircuts, and it’ll happily stay put as a tight midground bush or a unique, creeping foreground carpet. Provide medium lighting for steady growth; higher light intensity paired with pressurized CO2 injection encourages lower, creeping horizontal growth. Maintain stable water parameters and supply quality liquid fertilizers to support rapid leaf development. High light encourages shorter leaf stalks and forces runners to grow horizontally along the substrate rather than reaching vertically. 3. How do I transition Hydrocotyle Verticillata from emersed to submerged growth? When transitioning from emersed to submerged growth, plant bare stems securely into rich substrate under medium-to-high lighting and keep water parameters stable. As new growth adapts, the plant will shed its firm land leaves and sprout delicate, compact underwater foliage. Once new shoots develop, trim away old lower growth to encourage dense branching.

Plant Profile Echinodorus 'Big Bear', commonly known as the Big Bear Sword, is a distinctive hybrid cultivar with wide, olive-green leaves marked with dark red splotches and marbling. Living up to its name, it produces a robust, broad rosette that brings a grounded, focal presence to background zones in planted tanks. Under submerged conditions, younger inner leaves display the most vivid reddish-brown mottling before maturing into a deep, patterned green. As a low-maintenance species that tolerates low lighting and basic aquarium setups, it serves as an excellent option among aquarium plants for beginners managing medium-to-large aquariums. Key Features & Notes Broad green foliage heavily patterned with red splotches provides unique mottled visual contrast. Dense, wide rosette structure offers full background coverage that easily hides heaters and filter pipes. Thrives under low light and low-tech parameters without requiring mandatory CO2 injection. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Plant the roots deeply into your aquarium soil, keeping the crown of the plant resting just above the substrate line to prevent rot. All Echinodorus are heavy root feeders that rely on rich substrate nutrition; placing root tabs near the base supports steady, healthy leaf development. Supplemental CO2 injection accelerates growth and encourages denser, fuller foliage, though the plant will still grow steadily in low-tech setups. Maintain stable water parameters to prevent leaf shedding during the initial transition period. Final size and coloration depend entirely on your specific aquarium conditions; please note that photos are a representation, and individual plants may vary. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I prune an Echinodorus when it grows too large? Prune older or overgrown outer leaves individually near the root crown using sharp aquascaping scissors. Yes, this species thrives in low-tech aquariums without pressurized CO2, provided it receives adequate root supplementation and consistent lighting. 3. Why are the leaves on my new Echinodorus melting or turning yellow? Sword plants are often grown emersed and shed their old emersed leaves when submerged to adapt to underwater growth. Keep water parameters stable and supply root tabs near the base to support new leaves.

listings.description: Plant Profile If you want to trade your bare substrate for a vibrant, classic golf-course look, Dwarf Hair Grass (Eleocharis Parvula Mini) is a great pick. This hobby favorite features thin, bright green blades that spread horizontally by sending out runners, creating a realistic, grass-like lawn that your shrimp and nano fish will happily call home. It’s incredibly versatile and willing to travel to all corners of your tank if given the opportunity. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Need Dwarf Hair Grass but this listing is out of stock? Check out these other variants: Dwarf Hair Grass - Eleocharis Belem Dwarf Hair Grass - Eleocharis Pusillis Key Features & Benefits This is a fast-spreading species that quickly fills out empty substrate! Thrives submerged in aquariums or emersed in dry-start setups and Wabi Kusa layouts. Provides shelter and foraging surfaces for dwarf shrimp and fry. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Plant the hairgrass in small clumps spaced a couple of inches apart to give the runners plenty of room to fill in gaps. Use a dry start method or Wabi Kusa setup to give its root system plenty of time to firmly anchor into the substrate before you flood the tank. Maintain stable aquarium parameters and avoid drastic shifts in water quality to prevent your new grass from melting. Provide medium to high lighting and inject pressurized CO2 to supercharge its density and growth rate, keeping it low and compact. Master the basics by learning how to properly grow aquarium carpet plants to ensure your new layout fills in quickly. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I plant Dwarf Hair Grass tissue culture? Separate the mat into small clumps (about 5–10 blades each), and plant them roughly an inch apart using fine-tip tweezers into the substrate. 2. Do I need CO2 injection and high-tech lighting to grow a carpet? Adding pressurized CO2 and medium-to-high lighting is strongly recommended to force it to grow horizontally into a tight, plush carpet instead of growing tall or straggly. 3. How do I plant a carpet without the stems floating to the top? Because tissue culture portions have delicate root systems, fish or water currents can easily dislodge them. Planting small clumps deeply into fine soil or letting the tank grow emersed using the Dry Start Method will anchor the roots securely before flooding.

Plant Profile Glossostigma elatinoides, affectionately known as Glosso to hobbyists, is an absolute classic from New Zealand that helped define the iconic look of aquarium carpets. Its small, round, bright‑green leaves create a gorgeous contrast against darker substrates and instantly brighten up a layout. Give it the right balance of light and nutrients, and Glosso will reward you by stitching itself into a pristine, low‑growing sheet of green that hugs the bottom of your tank like a tiny velvet blanket living its best life. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Form a dense, classic carpet of small, round, vibrant green leaves. An energetic grower that quickly blankets bare substrate areas when provided with optimal conditions. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Separate into small clumps and press them compactly into a quality aquarium soil to give the roots the perfect head start. Use a dry start method or Wabi Kusa setup to give its root system plenty of time to firmly anchor into the substrate before you flood the tank. Provide medium to high lighting and inject pressurized CO2 to supercharge its density and growth rate, keeping it low and compact. Maintain stable aquarium parameters and avoid drastic shifts in water quality to prevent your new grass from melting. Master the basics by learning how to properly grow aquarium carpet plants to ensure your new layout fills in quickly, evenly, and stays free of algae. How do I plant Glossostigma tissue culture without it floating up? Using fine-tip pinsettes, push each clump deep into nutrient-rich aquasoil at a 45-degree angle, leaving only the top leaves sticking out above the surface. 2. Why is my Glossostigma growing tall and leggy instead of hugging the substrate? Vertical growth is a clear indicator of insufficient lighting. Glosso needs strong, direct PAR light and steady CO2 injection to force it to spread horizontally via lateral runners rather than reaching upward toward the light source. 3. How often does Glossostigma need to be trimmed? Because Glosso is a fast grower under proper conditions, it requires routine trimming every few weeks. Mowing the mat short prevents lower layers from being shaded out, which can cause the carpet to detach from the substrate and float.

Plant Profile Anubias Barteri is a classic that brings bold, structural elegance to any aquascape layout. Featuring broad, deep green leaves on tall stems, this epiphyte is slightly larger than Anubias Nana, making it ideal for midground and background placement. It is extraordinarily hardy, adapting effortlessly to a wide range of water parameters while thriving fully submerged in aquariums or emersed in humid terrariums. If you want an indestructible centerpiece plant with a timeless look, Anubias Barteri is a proven staple that never goes out of style. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Deep green foliage adds visual weight and structure to tanks. Legendary hardiness ensures it withstands grazing from cichlids, goldfish, snails, and active dwarf shrimp. Care & Planting Instructions Remove the plantlets from the cup and rinse away the sterile nutrient gel under lukewarm, dechlorinated water. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the rhizome above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable conditions to support smooth acclimation and reduce leaf loss. Avoid intense light and ensure good water flow to prevent spot algae on slow‑growing leaves. CO₂ is optional but improves growth and leaf density. Master the prep and planting process by checking out a beginner's guide to tissue culture plants to prevent your delicate new plantlets from melting or floating away. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! How do I plant Anubias? Attach the plant directly to driftwood or rocks using aquarium-safe super glue gel, thread, or fishing line. 2. Does it require CO2 or high lighting? No. It thrives in low lighting without CO2 injection. While adding CO2 speeds up growth and aids in the tissue culture transition, it is completely optional. 3. Is this plant safe for shrimp, snails, and fish? Yes, Anubias is 100% safe for all freshwater fish, shrimp (including sensitive Caridina and Neocaridina), and snails. Its tough leaves are also resistant to plant-eating fish like cichlids or goldfish.

Plant Profile Rare and richly patterned, Cryptocoryne nurii is a favorite among collectors! Its ruffled, lance-shaped leaves transition from deep olive green to warm bronze-red, often accentuated by pinkish stems and subtle tiger patterning, bringing extraordinary aesthetic appeal directly to your midground layout. Like all crypt plants, it can be sensitive to sudden parameter shifts and strongly objects to being relocated once planted. Tissue Culture cups ensure your aquascape gets a super clean starting point. Lab‑grown and fully sterile, it arrives without pests, snails, duckweed, or any unwanted algae. It’s the go‑to option for anyone who wants peace of mind when adding fresh greenery to a carefully maintained setup. Key Features & Benefits Patterned olive-to-bronze ruffled foliage with pinkish-red stems adds rare, high-contrast collector detail to midground zones. Can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups, where mature plants may produce flowering spathes. Care & Planting Instructions Thoroughly wash away the nutrient gel from the roots with your fingers before parting it out into manageable portions. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel to supply essential subterranean nutrients. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth and fuller foliage density, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Crypt species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. Why is Cryptocoryne Nurii considered rare and more challenging than other crypts? Cryptocoryne Nurii has a very slow growth rate and is particularly sensitive to parameter swings during its initial acclimation phase. Maintaining stable water chemistry and providing rich root nutrition are key to long-term success. 2. How do I help my Cryptocoryne recover if it melts? Trim away dissolving leaves, maintain stable water parameters, and leave the root system undisturbed so it can rebuild new foliage. Check our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt for full recovery steps. 3. Should I use root tabs or liquid fertilizers for Cryptocoryne Nurii? Root tabs are recommended! Cryptocoryne Nurii is a heavy root feeder that absorbs primary nutrition directly from the substrate rather than the water column.

Plant Profile Pearl Weed, also known as Pearl Grass, is a versatile, bright green stem plant highly favored for its exceptional adaptability in aquascapes. Depending on your pruning routine, Pearl Weed can serve as a dense foreground carpet, a bushy midground accent, or a lush background group. When grown under bright lighting with frequent trimming, it creeps horizontally along the substrate, offering a low-maintenance alternative to delicate carpeting plants without requiring complex high-tech setups. Key Features & Benefits Versatile stem plant that can be trained as a low foreground carpet or grown tall as background cover. Dense green foliage provides shelter for dwarf shrimp and fish fry. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and remove cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip the lower inch of foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. Group several small stems together and use fine-tip pinsettes to push them 1 to 2 inches into substrate, spacing groups about half an inch apart. Provide medium-to-high lighting to encourage dense, bushy growth; higher light intensity promotes horizontal creeping and tighter leaf spacing. Maintain stable water parameters, as Pearl Weed easily extracts necessary nutrients from quality aquarium soil and liquid fertilizers. Trim stems aggressively with curved or straight scissors to shape into dense hedges or maintain a low foreground carpet. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Hemianthus micranthemoides Common Name(s) Pearl Weed, Pearlweed, Pearl Grass Family Scrophulariaceae Plant Type / Taxonomy Stem Plant Care Difficulty Easy / Beginner Light Requirement Medium to High CO2 Requirement Not Required (Recommended for dense carpet growth) Placement / Usage Foreground / Midground / Background Height / Size 2–6”+ Growth Rate Medium to Fast Water Parameters pH 6.0–7.5 Propagation Method Cuttings (Trim tops and replant stem groups) Origin North America Frequently Asked Questions 1. Why are the lower leaves falling off my stem plants? Lower leaf loss (leggy stems) usually occurs when lighting cannot reach the bottom of the plant due to overcrowding or shading from larger plants. Spacing individual stem groups slightly apart during initial planting and maintaining adequate light penetration will keep lower leaves healthy. 2. How do I get Pearl Weed to grow as a foreground carpet? To train Pearl Weed into a low carpet, provide strong lighting and trim the top leaves frequently. Regular trimming forces the plant to send out horizontal runners along the substrate rather than growing upward toward the surface. 3. My stem plants arrived with round green leaves, but the new growth looks totally different. Is this normal? Yes! Many aquatic stem plants are cultivated emersed (above water) at plant nurseries, producing rounder, thicker green leaves. Once submerged in your aquarium, the plant will transition into its true aquatic form, sprouting delicate, submerged foliage.

Plant Profile If you're looking for a bright, foolproof staple to fill out your layout, Cryptocoryne wendtii 'Green' is one of the most reliable aquascaping classics available. Native to the nutrient-rich stream beds of Sri Lanka, this ubiquitous favourite is celebrated for its lush rosettes of vibrant green, slightly wavy foliage that introduces soft movement and fresh color to midground zones. As with all crypt plants, this species can be sensitive to sudden parameter shifts and strongly objects to being relocated once planted. Key Features & Benefits Bright green foliage with ruffled margins adds vibrant color to midground zones. Adapts to emersed high-humidity paludarium displays where mature plants can bloom. Hardy and adaptable, one of the easiest crypts for beginners and low-tech tanks. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots . Use fine-tip pinsettes to push roots deep into quality aquarium soil, as Crypt species are heavy root feeders. Insert root tab fertilizers if using an inert substrate like sand or gravel. Inject pressurized CO2 for faster growth, though not required for long-term health. Choose a permanent spot from day one; moving an established plant will likely trigger leaf loss. Cryptocoryne species can be grown emersed in high-humidity setups or submerged in aquariums. Propagate by splitting the rhizome or replanting new growth shoots. Don't discard the plant if leaves dissolve early on; see our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt to help your plant recover smoothly. How do I help my Cryptocoryne Wendtii Green recover if it melts? Crypt melt is a standard reaction when shifting water conditions cause old leaves to dissolve so the plant can rebuild foliage adapted to your aquarium. Trim away rotting tissue, keep your water parameters stable, and do not disturb the subterranean root system. For complete recovery steps, check out our guide to managing Cryptocoryne melt . 2. Can I move my Cryptocoryne to a new spot in the tank later? It is best to leave your Crypt permanently in its original spot. Uprooting an established plant damages its fine root hairs and almost always causes another cycle of leaf melt. 3. Do I need root tabs if I already use liquid fertilizers for my Cryptocoryne? Yes. Because Cryptocoryne plants absorb the vast majority of their nutrients through their roots rather than their leaves, providing nutrient-rich aquasoil or root tabs inside sand or gravel is far more effective than relying on water column liquid fertilizers alone.

Plant Profile Rotala Rotundifolia Red is the quintessential background flex for a reason. Originating from Southeast Asia, this fan-favorite stem plant sports delicate stems and thin leaves that make dark hardscape and green foliage look ten times better. When planted in dense groups and provided with strong lighting, quality aquarium soil, and iron supplementation, Rotala Rotundifolia Red transforms into a dazzling, thick red bush in your aquascape. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Leaf hues shift into intense ruby-red tones when provided with high-intensity LED lighting, heavy iron dosing, and complete fertilizers. Fast-growing stem structure easily forms dense background bushes and absorbs excess water column nutrients to help suppress algae. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip the lower inch of foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. * Rotala has fragile leaves, so handle stems with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push individual stems 1 to 2 inches into soil, spacing them about half an inch apart to ensure light reaches lower foliage. Provide high-intensity lighting and pressurized CO2 injection (20–30 ppm) to yield robust growth and maximize red pigmentation. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid drastic environmental changes to prevent leaf melt or rotting. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the surface to promote branching and prevent lower leaves from being shaded out. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. My stem plants arrived with round green leaves, but the new growth looks totally different. Is this normal? Yes! Once submerged in your aquarium, the plant will transition into its true aquatic form, sprouting delicate, colorful submerged foliage.

Plant Profile Ludwigia Repens is an easy, fast-growing midground and background stem plant favored for adding vibrant color to aquascapes without the drama of fussier red species. Featuring oval leaves that grow in alternating pairs along flexible stems, its foliage shifts through shades of gold, orange, and deep red depending on aquarium conditions. When planted in dense bunches of 10 to 12 stems, Ludwigia Repens creates an eye-catching focal point and adds immediate visual depth. *Form Notice: Photos display this plant in both its emersed (above-water) and submerged forms. Depending on nursery availability and seasonality, you may receive this plant in either form. Learn more about what to expect by reading our guide on Emersed vs. Submerged-Grown Aquatic Plants . Key Features & Benefits Leaf hues naturally range from olive-gold to vibrant orange and red under medium-to-high lighting and elevated iron dosing. Beginner-friendly red stem plant that delivers bold color contrast in both low-tech and high-tech aquarium setups. Care & Planting Instructions Remove lead weight and cotton wrap (or foam) surrounding the base, then strip the lower inch of foliage so bare stems anchor cleanly into soil without rotting. * Ludwigia stems can be fragile, so handle with care during preparation. Use fine-tip pinsettes to push stems 1–2 inches into soil, spacing them apart for light penetration. Provide medium-to-high lighting. While CO2 injection is not strictly required, it yields much thicker stems and richer coloration. See our guide to growing red aquarium plants . Maintain stable water parameters and avoid sudden environmental shifts to prevent leaf melt or rotting. Trim stem tops with straight scissors once they reach the surface to encourage lower stems to shoot out new side branches. Read our trimming & propagation guide for details. Plant Profile Featuring deeply ribbed foliage that mimics real coffee plant leaves, Anubias Barteri Coffeefolia is a distinctive, textured standout among Anubias aquarium plants. A sought-after cultivar of standard Anubias Barteri , this variant is renowned for its corrugated leaf ridges and dramatic bronze-to-copper new shoots that gradually transition into deep emerald green. Reaching up to 7 inches in height with wide, prominent leaf blades, this epiphyte anchors its rhizome onto rock or wood rather than taking root in substrate. Thriving under low to moderate lighting, it provides structural depth and tactile contrast as a midground anchor in planted aquariums, terrariums, and paludariums. Key Features & Benefits Deeply rippled, corrugated leaf surface creates distinctive visual and tactile depth in planted aquascapes. Broad structure establishes a prominent midground anchor that bridges foreground carpeting and tall stems. Thick, rugged foliage easily resists nibbling from boisterous fish, herbivorous cichlids, goldfish, and snails. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by removing it from the pot and clearing all rockwool from the roots. Attach to hardscape using aquarium‑safe glue or thread; keep the horizontal rhizome completely exposed above substrate to prevent rot. Maintain stable water conditions to support smooth acclimation and protect developing leaf buds. Position in moderate water circulation and avoid excessive direct lighting to prevent algae accumulation on slow-growing leaf ridges. CO₂ is optional but significantly accelerates leaf production and deepens leaf ribbing. Learn more about planting these species by reading our guide on How to Plant Epiphyte Aquatic Plants. Master long-term care and propagation with the article All About Anubias Aquarium Plants. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Team Buce Plant encourages you to do thorough research to ensure healthy growth! Attribute Specification Scientific Name Anubias barteri var. Why are the new leaves on my Anubias Coffeefolia brownish-red? This copper, reddish-brown hue is a normal, healthy characteristic of emerging Anubias Coffeefolia leaves. As the leaf unfurls and strengthens its cuticle layer under light, it synthesizes chlorophyll and transitions into its permanent glossy forest-green color. 2. How do I prevent algae from collecting inside the corrugated leaf ridges of Coffeefolia? Due to the ribbed indentations on Coffeefolia foliage, debris and green spot algae can settle in low-flow areas or under direct, intense light. Mount the plant in partial shade, such as beneath taller stem plants or hardscape overhangs, and maintain moderate, continuous water movement across the crown. 3. Can Anubias Coffeefolia be used as a background plant in smaller tanks? Yes. Because its broad leaves span 2 to 3 inches across on 4-to-7-inch stems, it forms a full, dense canopy that can easily serve as a background anchor in tanks 10 to 20 gallons, while functioning as a midground focal point in larger setups.

Plant Profile This Spiky Moss on Stainless Steel is moss-tly about high-definition texture, giving your tank a sharp, detailed look that will spruce up your aquascape. True to its name, this cousin of Christmas Moss grows longer, pointier, and spikier fronds that closely resemble a miniature fir tree. We have grown this versatile plant directly onto a 3" x 3" stainless steel mesh, so you do not have to worry about tying it down or watching it float away. Unlike other aquarium mosses that carpet flatly, this one reaches upward to create a dense, vertical thicket, making it a great choice for creating rich green carpets or lining background walls. Key Features & Benefits Pre-attached stainless steel pad sinks and stays put for zero-hassle carpeting. Sharp, spiky texture creates a distinct visual contrast against softer foliage and smooth stones. Creates a safe habitat for freshwater shrimp and baby fish to hide and forage. Plant Profile Native to the fast-flowing coastal rivers of Thailand, Crinum thaianum, commonly known as the Thai Onion Plant, is an a-peel-ing aquatic species anchored by a smooth, plump, off-white onion bulb that sprouts thick, leathery, dark green foliage with distinctively wavy, undulating edges and prominent, raised veins running down each blade. Maxing out at an impressive 60 inches long, these rubbery green ribbons twist, arch, and stream across the water surface to form a dramatic jungle canopy in taller displays. Under prime conditions, it may even blossom with fragrant, star-shaped white flowers above the waterline! Hardy background giant that occasionally blooms white flowers above the waterline. Care & Planting Instructions Prep the plant by gently inspecting the bulb and removing any loose organic debris around the base. Plant the bulb so that it is only half-buried in your aquarium soil or substrate; completely burying the bulb can cause it to rot. Avoid uprooting or moving the bulb once established, as Crinum species dislike root disturbance. Provide moderate to high lighting; while CO2 injection isn't strictly required, good lighting will enhance its crinkled growth. Heavy root feeder that thrives in nutrient-dense soil or with root tabs placed near the base. Propagate by carefully separating mature daughter bulbs from the primary bulb once independent roots form. Quick Facts Listed information should be treated as general guidelines only. Water Conditions: Temperature : 72-82°F (22-28°C). pH : 6.5-7.5. It prefers slightly acidic to neutral water. Hardness : Soft to moderately hard water (3-8 dGH). Substrate: Nutrient-rich : Amazon swords have extensive root systems and benefit from a nutrient-rich substrate like aquarium soil or planted tank substrate. Root Tabs : Supplementing with root tabs every few months can help provide essential nutrients. Planting and Placement: Depth : Plant the Amazon sword deeply enough to cover the roots, but keep the crown (where the leaves meet the roots) above the substrate to prevent rot. Placement : Place in the midground or background of the aquarium due to its size. Maintenance: Trimming : Remove yellowing or damaged leaves regularly to promote new growth and maintain the plant's appearance. Fertilization : Regular fertilization with liquid fertilizers and root tabs can help support robust growth. Amazon swords are heavy feeders. Water Changes: Perform regular water changes (20-30% weekly) to maintain water quality and support plant health. Propagation: Amazon swords propagate through runners and side shoots. Separate the new plantlets from the mother plant once they develop a few leaves and roots, then plant them in the substrate. Common Issues: Nutrient Deficiencies : Yellowing leaves may indicate a lack of nutrients, especially iron. Regular fertilization and root tabs can prevent this. Algae : Maintain a balance of nutrients and light to prevent algae overgrowth. By providing the right conditions and care, Amazon swords will thrive and become a centerpiece in your aquarium, offering both beauty and functionality as a natural habitat for your fish.

Seachem MetroPlex is a versatile and effective medication specifically designed to treat a variety of external and internal protozoan and bacterial infections in aquarium fish. This dual-action formula makes MetroPlex a comprehensive treatment for a range of conditions affecting both freshwater and marine fish. MetroPlex comes in a powdered form, allowing for easy and accurate dosing. The medication is designed to be easily absorbed, making it an effective choice for treating both internal and external infections. Aquarium hobbyists appreciate MetroPlex for its convenience and the brand's commitment to producing high-quality products for aquatic health. Whether dealing with conditions like hexamita, hole-in-the-head disease, or other protozoan and bacterial issues, Seachem MetroPlex is a trusted solution that aids in the recovery and well-being of aquarium fish when used as directed.

Symptoms can include white stringy feces, scratching or flashing, erosion of head or lateral line tissue, wasting, disinterest in food, or rapid breathing or gasping, ParaCleanse does not treat Nematodes or Roundworms. For these parasites, try Fritz Expel-F Active ingredient: Metronidazole and Praziquantel
