Other shipping methods void our Live Arrival Guarantee for fish.

Buce Kedagang Mini Round Bucephalandra Kedagang Mini Round is a beautiful, slow growing freshwater aquarium plant that's perfect for adding a little extra detail to your aquascape! Unlike some of the larger Buce varieties, Kedagang Mini Round stays nice and compact with small, rounded leaves that can develop gorgeous shades of green, red, and purple depending on your aquarium's conditions! Its smaller size makes it a great choice for nano tanks, foreground accents, or filling in those little spaces between rocks and driftwood. Like other Buce aquarium plants , Kedagang Mini Round is hardy, easy to care for, and doesn't require a fancy setup to thrive. It grows well in low to medium lighting and doesn't need CO2, making it an awesome option for beginners or anyone keeping a low-tech planted aquarium. One of the things we love about Buce Kedagang Mini Round is how much detail it can add to an aquascape without taking up much room! Bucephalandra Kedagang Mini Round is an epiphytic plant, meaning it grows best attached to driftwood, rocks, or other aquarium decorations rather than being buried in the substrate. Just secure the plant to your hardscape and let its roots naturally attach over time. Just be sure to keep the rhizome exposed, as burying it can cause the plant to rot. How to Care for Bucephalandra Kedagang Mini Round Scientific Name: Bucephalandra sp. Kedagang Mini Round Common Name: Buce Kedagang Mini Round, Kedagang Round Mini Bucephalandra Kedagang Mini Round does best in stable, well-established freshwater aquariums. While it's a pretty low maintenance plant, adding CO2 and regular liquid fertilizer can encourage healthier growth and bring out more of its unique coloration. Like many Bucephalandra varieties, some leaf melt is normal when introducing the plant to a new aquarium, especially if it was previously grown emersed. As long as the rhizome remains healthy, it can recover and produce new submerged growth. Care Level: Easy Light Requirements: Low to Medium Growth Rate: Slow Placement: Foreground, Driftwood, or Rocks Temperature: 68-80°F pH: 6.0-7.5 CO2: Not Required (beneficial, but optional) Propagation: Rhizome division Please Note: All live plants may contain snails or snail eggs. We intentionally keep beneficial snails in our plant systems because they help consume algae, leftover food, and decaying plant matter.

listings.description: Lace Java Fern Lace java fern "Windelov" is a great low light plant that is extremely hardy. It does not require much to thrive making it the perfect addition to any planted shrimp tank. You will receive one portion of lace java fern. Usually, this will include one plant with at least 4 leaves. Portion size may vary. Main Benefits: Low light plant for easy maintenance Helps convert toxins in the water and heavy metals into safe organics Promotes oxygen rich water Provides hiding places for shrimp and baby shrimp More Information: Lace java fern is another hardy plant. It is an aquatic fern that grows very well under low light. It can be easily attached to driftwood or rocks. The large green leaves look best attached to driftwood and growing up or down a branch. Often times, we will find lace java fern growing out of our sponge filters due to tiny plantlets breaking away from the mother. It propagates by either cutting the rhizome, horizontal shoots or by plantlets growing from the underside of leaves. Lace java fern is extremely hardy and can survive in even hard water. We grow it with little attention under low light and no fertilizer dosing. It is a great plant for beginners. With all our plants, we mainly just allow them to float in the water or settle where they like. They do not need special soil or anything excessive. Lace java fern will accept most water parameters and thrive in stable conditions.

Dwarf Water Lily | Bulb Aquarium Plant The dwarf lily is an amazing beginner plant. The lily comes with a bulb that you do not want to bury completely (max half way burred). The bulb will usually have multiple plants growing from it. These plants can be separate from the bulb or left attached to it. The lily will send out new leaves higher and higher until they reach the surface. Trim the leaves at the length you want them to stay and it will encourage the plant to only grow that high. The dwarf lily will absorb a lot of excess nutrients in the water which makes it an ideal addition to any low light nano tank. You will receive one (1) plant with one bulb or three (3) bulbs that are unsprouted. Usually, the bulb with have multiple plants. Portion sizes may vary. Santa Crystal Red Shrimp You will receive Santa pattern Crystal Red Shrimp, also known as Santa CRS. The Santa CRS you will receive will be sub-adults, having a size of around half of an inch (.5 inches). Santa Crystal Red shrimp are specifically bred to be mostly red with a white head. These shrimp are line-bred by one of Taiwan's famous breeders, Carbon Chen. This line breeds very true and is among one of the highest quality Santa lines in the world. Crystal red shrimp are stunning in color and pattern. They are the red mutation of the wild bee shrimp. Most hobbyists refer to crystal red shrimp as CRS. The CRS is an entry-level freshwater shrimp for the Caridina genus. When a hobbyist is making the transition from Neocaridina to Caridina, the crystal red shrimp is a great option to start with. While crystal red requires a lower PH, they can still live in conditions that are slightly alkaline (PH above 7). The grading scale for CRS is somewhat difficult to comprehend at first. Here are the grades in order of highest to lowest: SSS, SS, S, A, B, and C. The higher the grade (SSS), the less red the shrimp will have. So, a C-grade shrimp will be almost all red while an SSS-grade shrimp will be almost completely white. The other way to grade the shrimp is by color and how solid the color is versus being transparent in color. Shrimp with poor color are usually culled (separated) from the colony. Here are the tank conditions we keep our CRS at: Tank Parameters PH: 6.6 to 6.9 GH: 5 to 7 KH: 0 to 2 TDS: 130 to 160 Temp: 68 to 74 Tank Equipment Filter: Matten Filter Substrate: Brightwell Rio Escuro or Cafe Soil , Fluval Shrimp Stratum Water: RO/DI Water remineralized with Shrimple GH Decor: Malaysian Driftwood , Java Moss , and Indian Almond Leaves

Grapevine is a unique wood for the aquarium and is more recently catching on in the aquarium hobby. Unlike other woods, Grapevine is very light and will take time to sink. You will have to boil or cure the grapevine to get it to sink. The second reason we use grapevine, or any driftwood for that matter, is because it creates surface area . What we mean is this, shrimp need places to hide, graze and sit on. By adding driftwood to an aquarium, one can more than double the surface area in a tank. The final main benefit we see from using Grapevine is the tannins . These tannins leach from the driftwood into the water column carrying a multitude of anti-fungal and antibacterial properties. It is important to note that some types of plecos will eat the spider wood because it is soft compared to other driftwood types. listings.commonName: API GH & KH General & Carbonate Hardness Test Kit
listings.description: Aquarium Test Kit for GH & KH The most important parameters in any shrimp tank are GH and KH. These two measurements will directly affect the Ph in an aquarium and what types of fish or shrimp you will be able to keep. GH stands for general hardness and this measurement can be raised by using a product called Salty Shrimp GH+. KH stands for carbonate hardness and you can raise this measurement with Salty Shrimp GH and KH+. KH is what directly influences the stability of Ph in an aquarium so for soft water shrimp it is import to keep KH under 3. Important Points: GH and KH are the most important parameters for Shrimp Keeping GH is general hardness KH is carbonate hardness A low KH increases the chance of Ph swings Low levels of KH need active substrate to control PH Low GH is suitable for most Caridina Shrimp High GH is suitable for most Neocaridina Shrimp

This fish is unique in its variation of light and dark colored bands similar to a panda. This fish can be housed with a wide variety of tank mates especially nano and non-aggressive species. Please Note: All fish shipments have a 100% Live Arrival Guarantee when shipping with Overnight (1 Day) option. All other options void our Live Arrival Guarantee for fish. This fish is a peaceful omnivorous species of sucker-mouth cat that mostly feeds on bio-film, however, it can be fed a high quality frozen food such as baby brine shrimp and will readily accept it. This fish will max out around 3 inches in size. We feed our panda garra with algae based foods such as Northfin kelp wafers, and bio-film additive Bacter A.E.. We also feed frozen baby brine shrimp to enhance their diet. Avoid adding too many tannins in the water as it can hinder the growth of bio-films and algae beneficial to this fish. Salt and Pepper Cory The habrosus corydoras, often referred to as the Salt and Pepper Pygmy Cory, is a tiny schooling species of catfish that should be kept in groups of at least 5. Species of this corydoras are often very active swimmers, the entire group can be found schooling but will use driftwood and plants for cover if feeling threatened. The habrosus cory can be housed with a large variety of fish, especially nano species, including dwarf shrimp. On occasion they can be seen eating dwarf shrimp fry, but the adults are usually safe. These corydoras will display a light grey/tan body with blotches of silver and black broken striping. This broken stripe helps distinguish this species from the very similar species corydoras pygmaeus which has a solid stripe. These corydoras are a very comparable to larger species in that they scavenge the bottom of the aquarium for prepared food and microorganisms. These fish will readily accept dry and frozen foods. Shadow Mosura Shrimp Shadow Mosura shrimp have a black pattern on their head and blue bodies with their genetic line coming from a cross between Blue Bolt and Black King Kong Taiwan Bees. The Blue Bolts provide their blue color which is referred to as a "shadow" gene. When breeding these shrimp you will get a variety of black head patterns with some black markings possible on their body. The shades of blue on their bodies will vary but can be selectively bred for a deep blue all-over coloration. The Shadow Mosura is a beautiful variety of Taiwan Bee that can make a great addition to a mixed caridina tank or kept alone and selectively bred. Pacific Wood Pacific wood is very similar in looks to Malaysian Driftwood with a mix of Mopani wood. It is a dense wood that should sink within 3-4 days. Boiling the wood is always recommend and will help it to sink quicker. You will be receiving one (1) piece of Pacific Driftwood that will be between 6 to 10 inches in length. All pieces of wood will be unique in shape with no more than 1 to 2 cut edges. Key Features: Essential for Shrimp Breeding Creates Surface Area for Bio-film and Bacterial to Grow Releases Beneficial Tannin into the Water which Simulates the Natural Habitat of Shrimp Provides Hiding Places for Shrimp Natural Feeding Ground for Shrimp of all Types More Information: When asked, “What is the most essential part to a successful shrimp tank?” we will always respond with three key factors: leaf matter, java moss, and a piece of driftwood. As far as driftwood goes, Malaysian driftwood is our number one choice yet there are plenty of other great options such as Mopani, Spider and Pacific wood. The reason we use driftwood is because it creates surface area . What we mean is this, shrimp need places to hide, graze and sit on. By adding driftwood to an aquarium, one can more than double the surface area in a tank. The best thing about Pacific driftwood specifically is it is dark thus when all that algae we normally hate grows on it, we don’t know and can’t see it. Therefore, we won’t clean the algae off the driftwood so in return we are providing a natural and nearly unnoticeable food source for the shrimp. The final main benefit we see from using driftwood is the tannins it releases. These tannins leach from the driftwood into the water column carrying a multitude of antifungal and antibacterial properties. Although most people prefer clear aquarium water, here at Flip Aquatics we find that the slight discoloration adds character to the tank and allows the shrimp to feel more comfortable.

Assorted Bucephalandra | Potted or Bare Root Our Assorted Bucephalandra features a variety of low-growing, slow-growing plants native to Borneo. These hardy plants thrive in most aquarium setups with minimal light and fertilization. For the brightest colors and fastest growth, add CO₂ injection, stronger lighting, and good water circulation, but they’ll still do well under basic care. Plants may arrive potted or with bare roots, depending on availability. Each rhizome will continue to grow new leaves over several months, so be patient, Bucephalandra adds value through its long-lasting, steady growth. To propagate your Buce, simply cut the rhizome into sections and attach each piece to driftwood or rock with thread or aquarium-safe glue. New leaves will sprout from each section, letting you build a lush carpet or a striking accent over time. Main Benefits: Low to medium light plant for easy maintenance Easy to attach to decoration in the tank for easy growth Provides hiding places for shrimp and baby shrimp Unique and uncommon plant for your aquarium More Information: You will receive a random piece of Bucephalandra, will usually contain a minimum of 3-4 leaves.

Bucephalandra Godzilla Bucephalandra Godzilla is one of those aquarium plants that really stands out from other Buce varieties! Unlike the smaller, compact Bucephalandra you might be used to seeing, Buce Godzilla has longer leaves with beautiful wavy edges and a slightly textured appearance. It's a great way to add some extra height and texture to your aquascape without having to worry about a plant taking over your tank. Like other Bucephalandra aquarium plants , Buce Godzilla is hardy, slow-growing, and pretty easy to care for, making it a great choice for beginners and experienced hobbyists alike. It does well in low to medium lighting and doesn't require CO2, so it's perfect for low-tech planted aquariums. Its larger leaves make it especially nice for filling in spaces between driftwood and rocks or adding a little extra greenery to the midground of your tank. One of our favorite things about Buce Godzilla is how easy it is to incorporate into just about any aquascape. You don't even need to plant it in substrate! Simply attach it to driftwood or rocks and let the roots naturally anchor themselves over time. Just be sure to leave the rhizome exposed, as burying it can cause the plant to rot. How to Care for Bucephalandra Godzilla Scientific Name: Bucephalandra sp. Godzilla Common Name: Buce Godzilla Bucephalandra Godzilla is a hardy freshwater aquarium plant that thrives in stable, well-established tanks. While it doesn't need much to grow, added CO2 and regular fertilization can encourage healthier, fuller growth. Like other Bucephalandra varieties, it's also normal to experience some leaf melt when first introducing the plant to a new aquarium, especially if it was previously grown emersed. As long as the rhizome remains healthy, the plant can recover and produce new submerged leaves. Care Level: Easy Light Requirements: Low to Medium Growth Rate: Slow Placement: Midground, Driftwood, or Rocks Temperature: 68-80°F pH: 6.0-7.5 CO2: Not Required (beneficial, but optional) Propagation: Rhizome division Please Note: All live plants may contain snails or snail eggs. We intentionally keep beneficial snails in our plant systems because they help consume algae, leftover food, and decaying plant matter.

Red King Kong Extreme | Taiwan Bee You will receive red king kong extreme Taiwan bee. The red king kong you receive will have very little white color. Most of our red king kong extremes only have white on the tail. We sell all Taiwan Bee shrimp at about half an inch. The smaller they are, the easier it is to acclimate them to a new aquarium. The shrimp will reach breeding age within a month of receiving them. Red King Kong shrimp are a type of Taiwan bee. They are from the genus Caridina and tend to be more difficult to keep compared to cherry shrimp or other aquarium shrimp. Taiwan Bees were considered some of the hardest to keep and breed freshwater shrimp in the past. Between 2009 and 2014, hobbyists were able to stabilize the Taiwan bee shrimp line to have more stability. By adding in new genetic pools, the Taiwan bee shrimp is much easier to keep and breed in current days. For a hobbyist ready to take their hobby to the next level, these shrimp are a great place to start. Mixing Taiwan Bees It is great to be aware of the fact that all Taiwan Bee shrimp can be kept in the same tank with out risk of hybridizing. All Taiwan Bee shrimp share similar genetic lines so they will produce shrimp that look similar to the parents. Red King Kongs, Red Pandas, Black King Kongs, Black Pandas and Blue Bolts can all be kept in the same aquarium. Otocinclus Catfish for Sale Otocinclus catfish, often called “Otos,” are known as some of the best algae-eating fish for freshwater aquariums. Native to South American rivers, these small catfish are prized for grazing algae off glass, plants, and decorations—making them an essential part of any tank’s cleanup crew. They have distinctive black markings and a mottled appearance, easily standing out among nano fish. Are Otocinclus Sensitive Fish? At Flip Aquatics, we supplement their diet with Bacter AE and ShrimpFit and quarantine new arrivals for at least two weeks. When properly cared for, Otocinclus are beginner-friendly and easy to keep. Live Arrival Guarantee All Otocinclus Catfish orders are backed by our 100% Live Arrival Guarantee . We use proven shipping methods to ensure your fish arrive healthy. Stable water conditions, especially during the first week, are crucial. They do best in mature aquariums with established algae and biofilm, along with plenty of cover from plants, driftwood, and rocks. Frequently Asked Questions How many Otocinclus should I keep together? They do best in groups of 3 or more to reduce stress and promote natural behavior. Otos are peaceful and enjoy being part of a small school. Do Otocinclus eat algae? Yes, they are excellent at eating soft green algae and diatoms. Hillstream Loach for Sale Hillstream loaches are the most visually unique algae eaters in the aquarium hobby. When we import them, they often come in as either scientific name Pseudogastromyzon myersi or Sewellia lineolata , also known as the reticulated hillstream loach. This species features a striking appearance, and the graphic mottled pattern adds to its extraordinary beauty. The reticulated hillstream loach does not have a conventional resemblance to typical fish, as its specialized body structure is adapted for life in fast flowing streams with very strong currents. Although, we occasionally receive other related species so please be aware of this when ordering. Why Buy Our Hillstream Loaches When you purchase hillstream loaches from us, you benefit from our commitment to quality and animal heath. Here’s why buying from us is the best choice for your aquarium: 100% Live Arrival Guarantee : We ensure your fish arrive healthy and vibrant, or we’ll make it right. Overnight Shipping: Fast, reliable delivery to get your hillstream loaches to you as quickly as possible. Shipped Within One Week: We carefully prepare and ship your order within one week from the time you place it. Strict Quarantine Practices : Our fish are quarantined for two or more weeks before sale to ensure they are healthy and free from disease. Expert Care and Handling: Our experienced team provides the best care to maintain the health and vitality of your hillstream loaches. Customer Support: We are here to help with any questions or concerns before and after your purchase. Choose us for peace of mind and the highest quality hillstream loaches available. Natural Habitat and Origins The Reticulated Hillstream Loach comes from fast-flowing, oxygen-rich streams in Asia. It lives among smooth river rocks that provide shelter and food by growing algae and other tiny organisms. To keep them healthy in your aquarium, create a setup that copies their natural home. Use powerheads to make strong water currents and connect airline tubing to bring in fresh air, keeping the water full of oxygen. Keep the water temperature below 75°F because cooler water holds more oxygen. It's important to avoid tropical aquarium setups for this reason. Add different sizes of river rocks so the loach can graze on algae and detritus, just like in the wild. Feed them high quality flake food and sinking carnivore pellets to give them the nutrients they need. This peaceful fish makes a great addition to any tank, offering interesting behavior and helping keep the aquarium clean. SPECIES VARIATIONS The Reticulated Hillstream Loach stands out among aquarium fish thanks to its graphic mottled pattern, which adds further visual interest and sets it apart from the classic piscine shape. This species, also known as the Butterfly Hillstream Loach or Tiger Hillstream Loach, is admired for its gorgeous wing-like finnage and extremely hydrodynamic shape. The streamlined body shape helps them navigate fast moving streams. Hillstream loach species, including the reticulated variety, are peaceful and visually striking, ideal for freshwater hobbyists seeking unusual aquarium inhabitants. Thrive in established aquariums with strong currents, contributing to algae control and balance. Important to maintain high water quality, avoidance of high water temperatures is critical to their success. Adapted to oxygen-rich environments created by powerheads and strong water movement. Feed on a variety of small foods including sinking algae wafers, finely crushed flake food, frozen foods like bloodworms and tubifex worms, and specialty powdered foods designed to support their health and nutrition. Graze on biofilm and algae on various smooth surfaces, providing beneficial algae control and aquarium cleanliness. Feature unique physical traits like a flattened body and graphic mottled pattern, adding extraordinary beauty and visual interest. Their peaceful temperament and beneficial foraging make them essential for maintaining a balanced tank. Their unusual appearance and behavior offer endless fascination for aquarists of all experience levels. WHAT DO HILLSTREAM LOACHES EAT? These loaches are primarily algae eaters, spending most of their time grazing on biofilm and algae-covered surfaces. To supplement their diet, we feed them finely crushed flake food (NorthFin Kelp Flake). To help with their protein intake, we feed them small frozen foods such as baby brine shrimp and daphnia. The two essential food sources for Hillstream Loaches are GlasGarten ShrimpFit and Bacter AE. While these products are designed for shrimp, they both work great for picky algae eaters to help support their gut health. At Flip Aquatics, we feed our hillstream loaches a variety of foods, including: Frozen Foods: baby brine shrimp, daphnia, and cyclops NorthFin Kelp Flake (finely crushed) GlasGarten Bacter AE GlasGarten ShrimpFit Finely crushed, unsalted canned green beans WATER PARAMETERS Our water parameters are listed below and suggested tank setup for hillstream loaches. Maintain the following water conditions for optimal health: pH: 7.2 - 7.5 General Hardness (GH): 4 - 6 Carbonate Hardness (KH): 2 - 4 Total Dissolved Solids (TDS): 100 - 150 ppm Temperature: 70 - 74°F For the tank setup, we suggest: Minimum tank size of 10 gallons or more Substrate consisting of sand or other smooth materials to protect their delicate undersides Decor such as driftwood or smooth lava rock to provide ample surface area for grazing and hiding Adding natural additives like Indian Almond Leaves or Alder Cones to help replicate their natural environment and support water quality FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS DO HILLSTREAM LOACHES EAT SNAILS? No, hillstream loaches do not eat snails. They are extremely peaceful and won't bother adult snails. They might eat a snail egg here and there, but you'll never see them actively hunting anything besides algae and biofilm. ARE HILLSTREAM LOACHES GOOD ALGAE EATERS? Yes, hillstream loaches are excellent algae eaters. They spend most of their time grazing on glass, rocks, and decorations. While they aren't great at handling hair algae, they do a fantastic job on soft surface algae and biofilm. ARE HILLSTREAM LOACHES AGGRESSIVE? No, hillstream loaches are not aggressive. They are playful and may chase each other around, especially males, but it's rarely true aggression. They're very social and do best when kept in small groups. Regular maintenance is required to ensure your Goby lives a long and healthy life. The ideal conditions for the Blue Neon Stiphodon Goby Native to Japan, Taiwan, and Micronesia the Blue Neon Goby is found in shallow, fast-moving water and is particularly sensitive to declines in water quality. Ensure your tank is set up with ample organic structures where algae and biofilm can grow as this is essential to its health and longevity. If multiple males are present, ensure the tank is large enough to provide ample territory. Please Note: All fish shipments have a 100% Live Arrival Guarantee when shipping with Overnight (1 Day) option. All other options void our Live Arrival Guarantee for fish. What we feed our Gobys The Blue Neon Goby is an algae and biofilm grazer, and so these foods should be readily available to ensure their long-term health and happiness. A Goby enjoys plant based foods. We supplement their diet with a mix of fresh vegetables and Northfin Veggie, Community, Bug Pro, and Northfin Kelp Wafers to ensure a balanced and nutritious diet. We also feed our Gobys prepared algae wafers and let them graze on natural algae and bio-film. This can be supplemented by using Bacter A.E. which can be found by clicking here . Our Tank Parameters Ph: 5.5 to 7 Gh: 8 to 16 Kh: 4 to 8 TDS: 180 to 250 Temp: 70 to 74

Siamese Algae Eater The Siamese Algae Eater or Crossocheilus oblongus is a unique fish to add to your aquarium due to its very active habits and unmatched love of various aquarium algae, including but not limited to black beard algae. It is recommended that these fish be kept in a group of at least 5 to 6, when adult size to spread out aggression. These fish are a great beginner fish due to its acceptance of a wide variety of water parameters and ability to handle lower temperatures. It is not uncommon for these fish to jump so a tank with a lid is highly recommended. Please Note: All fish shipments have a 100% Live Arrival Guarantee when shipping with Overnight (1 Day) option. All other options void our Live Arrival Guarantee for fish. The Siamese Algae Eater can reach a max size of 7 inches and is a great community fish in a well established tank with peaceful fish. And is plant safe. It should be kept in slightly larger tanks size of 40 gallons or more. The Siamese Algae Eater consumes many natural food sources but will accept prepared foods with lots of vegetable matter such as kelp wafers. It is good practice to provide fresh cut vegetables such as cucumber and zucchini. listings.commonName: Orange Von Rio Tetra | Flame Tetra
listings.description: Flame Tetra - Von Rio Flame Tetra The Flame Tetra, Hyphessobrycon flammeus , is a bright, colorful freshwater fish that brings a beautiful orange and yellow glow to a peaceful community aquarium. Also known as the Von Rio Flame Tetra , this species has been loved in the aquarium hobby for years thanks to its color, hardiness, and easygoing personality. Flame Tetras stay small, usually reaching around 2 inches as adults, but they really stand out when kept in a group. Their warm orange body color looks especially good in planted tanks, darker aquascapes, and setups with driftwood or botanicals. One of the reasons the Von Rio Flame Tetra is such a great beginner fish is its ability to adapt to a wide range of water parameters. They are peaceful, active, and do best in groups of 6 or more . The larger the group, the more comfortable they feel, and the better their natural schooling behavior looks in the tank. While Flame Tetras are peaceful community fish, we would not recommend them for shrimp breeding tanks . They may leave larger adult shrimp alone, but baby shrimp are small enough to become an easy snack. If you are trying to grow a shrimp colony, this probably is not the best fish to add. The Orange Von Rio Flame Tetra does well with other peaceful community fish like rasboras, corydoras, small tetras, danios, and other nonaggressive tank mates. They enjoy a planted aquarium with both open swimming space and areas to explore. We feed our Flame Tetras a mix of frozen, live, and prepared foods including live baby brine shrimp, frozen daphnia, frozen baby brine, cyclops, and NorthFin flake foods. All other options void our Live Arrival Guarantee for fish. Threadfin Rainbowfish Threadfin Rainbowfish are an amazing addition to any planted aquarium. This rainbow is very distinguishable from other rainbowfish due to their long feather like extensions displayed on the males in the species. Males will display green, red, and blue body coloration in the right lighting, this color can extend into its long fins. As the adults get larger the colors can become even more vibrant. This species does well in schools of 6 or more but can be bred in groups of 3 in some cases. Unlike most rainbowfish it is better to keep these in tanks with lower flow/turbulence. Please Note: All fish shipments have a 100% Live Arrival Guarantee when shipping with Overnight (1 Day) option. All other options void our Live Arrival Guarantee for fish. This species is very community friendly and can even be housed with adult shrimp species if grown up in the same tank. You will still need to watch for aggression if keeping with large adult shrimp. We still recommend you keep shrimp separate from this species to eliminate risks. These rainbowfish will max out around 2.5 inches in size. The scientific name for the Threadfin Rainbow is Iriatherina werneri We feed our Threadfin Rainbowfish a mix of frozen foods, live baby brine shrimp, and flake foods. Our Tank Parameters Ph: 5 to 8 Gh: 10 to 16 Kh: 6 to 10 TDS: 180 to 250 Temp: 72 to 86 Tank Recommendations Leaves: Indian Almond or Guava Wood: Mopani or Malaysian Cones: Alder Cones

Dwarf Hairgrass Dwarf Hairgrass (Eleocharis acicularis) is a popular choice for creating lush, natural carpets in aquariums. Dwarf hairgrass has fine, grass-like blades, forming a soft, green lawn that adds depth and vibrancy to any aquascape. Dwarf Hairgrass is an excellent choice for aquarists looking to enhance the foreground of their tank. Dwarf Hairgrass will spread and grow faster provided a nutrient rich soil (our favorite soils can be found by clicking here. ), CO2, and high lighting. Dwarf Hairgrass spreads through runners creating a dense, visually appealing carpet that promotes a healthy aquatic environment by oxygenating the water and providing shelter for small fish and shrimp. Dwarf Hairgrass requires little pruning (especially if being used as a carpet plant) and can be easily propagated by dividing clumps or allowing it to spread naturally across the substrate. Dwarf Hairgrass has a compact, vibrant growth that enhances the overall aesthetic of your aquarium while also supporting ecological balance. You will receive one (1) potted plant. Portion size may vary. Scientific Name: Eleocharis parvula Common Names: Dwarf Hairgrass, Hair Grass How to care for Dwarf Hairgrass- Light Requirements: Medium/High Care Level: Easy/Medium CO2: Recommended if carpeting look is desired *All Plants may contain snails or snail eggs. We keep them in all of our tanks for the benefits they provide.*

It is great to use in aquarium to help prevent algae, provide shade for inhabitants, increase surface area and to reduce nitrates. Duckweed can also be use for shrimp food when blended into a paste and dried (add in spirulina powder to enrich it). You will receive one (1) portion of duckweed. One portion of giant duckweed will contain 10+ floating plants. Salvinia Minima Enhance your aquarium with Salvinia Minima, also known as Water Spangles, a versatile floating plant that adds both beauty and functionality to your aquatic environment. With its delicate, velvety leaves, Salvinia Minima creates a natural canopy on the water's surface, providing shade and shelter for your fish and shrimp. Salvinia Minima is a low-maintenance floating plant that helps to reduce excess nutrients, improving water quality and contributing to a balanced ecosystem. Ideal for beginners and experienced aquarists alike, Salvinia Minima is the perfect choice for adding a touch of green to the surface of your aquarium. Salvinia Minima is an extremely fast-growing floating plant with a unique textured leaf. Neka Driftwood - Natural Aquarium Wood for Nano Tanks Neka Driftwood is a great option if you're looking for natural aquarium wood to add to your freshwater tank! Similar in appearance to Pacific Driftwood, Neka Wood has a beautiful mix of dark and light coloration, with each piece having its own unique shape. This aquarium driftwood is especially great for nano tanks, shrimp tanks, and planted aquariums . Not only does it look good, but it also provides extra surface area for beneficial bacteria and biofilm to grow, giving shrimp a natural place to graze, explore, and hide! Neka Wood is a fairly dense driftwood that will often sink within a few days of being added to water, although some pieces may take longer. We recommend soaking or boiling the wood before adding it to your aquarium to help it become waterlogged faster. Neka Driftwood Sizes Each order includes one (1) piece of natural Neka Driftwood in your selected size: Approximately 3-6 inches Approximately 6-12 inches Every piece of Neka Wood is unique! Shapes, colors, and textures will vary, and pieces will have no more than 1-2 cut edges. Benefits of Neka Driftwood for Aquariums Great for Shrimp Tanks: Creates additional surfaces for shrimp to graze on and explore. Encourages Biofilm Growth: Provides surface area for biofilm and beneficial bacteria to develop. Natural Hiding Spots: Gives shrimp, shrimplets, and small fish places to feel secure. Releases Tannins: May release natural tannins that give aquarium water a slight brown tint. Perfect for Aquascaping: Adds a natural look to nano aquariums, planted tanks, and shrimp setups. Why We Recommend Driftwood for Shrimp Tanks One of the questions we get asked all the time is, "What's the most important thing for a successful shrimp tank?" Our answer usually comes down to three things: leaf litter, Java Moss, and driftwood! Why driftwood? It's all about surface area! Shrimp spend a HUGE amount of time grazing throughout the aquarium. By adding driftwood, you're giving them more places to explore while creating extra surfaces for biofilm and natural food sources to develop. Another thing we love about Neka Driftwood is its darker coloration. As biofilm and algae grow on the wood, they tend to blend in with its natural appearance. That means your shrimp can enjoy grazing without the wood looking out of place in your aquascape. And don't forget about tannins! Neka Driftwood may release natural tannins into your aquarium, giving the water a slight tea-colored tint. While some hobbyists prefer crystal-clear water, we actually love the natural look tannins can create in a shrimp tank! How to Prepare Neka Driftwood Before adding Neka Driftwood to your aquarium, we recommend giving it a good rinse to remove any loose debris. You can also soak the wood in clean water or boil it, if the piece is suitable, to help it become waterlogged faster. Some pieces may float at first, so don't worry if your driftwood doesn't sink right away! Most pieces will eventually become waterlogged, although the time can vary. Please Note: Natural driftwood may release tannins that temporarily discolor aquarium water. Each piece is unique and may vary from the product photos in shape, size, and coloration.

The Gold Ring Danio Gold Ring Danios are small, active freshwater fish with an awesome pattern that really starts to stand out once you get a group together! Their gold to tan bodies are covered in dark spots, giving the Gold Ring Danio a completely different look from the striped danios most people are used to seeing. They're peaceful, hardy, and always on the move, making them a great addition to community tanks! Also known as the Gold Ring Tinwini Danio , these fish stay small, reaching around 1.5 inches as adults. While you can see some schooling behavior in smaller groups, we really recommend keeping Gold Ring Danios in groups of 10 or more . A larger school helps them feel more comfortable and lets you see much more of their natural behavior! Gold Ring Danios are also a great option for beginner fish keepers because they're hardy, adaptable, and aren't picky when it comes to food. We feed ours a varied diet of live and frozen foods, including daphnia, baby brine shrimp, and cyclops, along with NorthFin Community, Veggie, and Bug Pro. We wouldn't recommend Gold Ring Danios for a shrimp tank if your goal is to grow your colony. Like most small fish, they'll take advantage of the opportunity to snack on tiny baby shrimp. The Blue Tetra Fish The Blue Tetra is a great mid to upper level water occupying fish, best suited for medium to large tanks. We recommend keeping them in tanks of 20 gallons or larger due to their active nature and ability to reach nearly 2 inches in size. This Tetra enjoys slightly acidic water that has tannins, driftwood, and or leaf litter. This tetra has a unique appearance, with a mostly clear body with a light to bright blue coloration taking up its back half. This tetra is relatively peaceful but can be aggressive while feeding, tank mates should be picked with caution. We do not recommend keeping them with smaller invertebrates or long finned fish due to that reason. This fish does best while kept in small to medium size groups, 6 or more is ideal. The scientific name for the Blue Tetra is: Boehlkea fredcochui . We feed our Blue Tetras a mix of Northfin Community and Veggie., and freshly hatched baby brine shrimp. They also get an occasional treat of frozen foods such as daphnia, cyclopods and blood worms. listings.description: Long Fin White Cloud Minnow The Long fin white cloud is a great addition to any aquarium, planted or un-planted. The long fin has the same appearance as the regular white cloud except that the adults fins are elongated. This difference makes them appear flashier and more desirable to hobbyists. The long fin white cloud has great color contrast displaying white to gold coloration with red coloration on its fins and tail. The color stands out even more then the regular white cloud. They show schooling behavior in small groups, this behavior is very evident in larger groups of 10 or more. Please Note: All fish shipments have a 100% Live Arrival Guarantee when shipping with Overnight (1 Day) option. All other options void our Live Arrival Guarantee for fish. The white cloud is great for small tanks from 10 gallons and up. The white cloud minnow can reach a size of 1.5 inches and is a great community and beginner fish do to its adaptability to a large range of water parameters. We would not recommend keeping them with shrimp if trying to grow your colony as they can target baby shrimp easily. The scientific name for the White Cloud Minnow is: Tanichthys albonubes "Long Fin" We feed our White Clouds a mix of frozen foods including daphnia, baby brine and cyclops. Cardinal Tetra Fish The Cardinal Tetra is one of the aquarium hobbies most popular schooling fish. This is due to their striking blue and red color that stands out great in any aquarium. They look closely to a Neon Tetra yet the differences are evident. The Cardinal tetra is a bit larger than the Neon Tetra to start. Cardinals come from warmer water than Neon Tetras. In coloration, the Cardinal Tetra’s red line runs the whole length of the body. The red in the Neon Tetra only goes from the tail to about the middle of the body then the color changes to silver. Finally, Cardinal Tetras enjoying warmer water makes them a great choice for aquariums that house Discus ( Symphysodon aequifasciatus ) or one of the many color strains of Rams ( Mikrogeophagus ramirezi ). They are a stunning addition to aquariums because of their high contrast against planted tanks and dark substrates. We recommend them to anyone that wants an easy to care for and beautiful fish. They prefer to be kept in schools of 5 or more to make them feel the most comfortable. Please Note: All fish shipments have a 100% Live Arrival Guarantee when shipping with Overnight (1 Day) option. All other options void our Live Arrival Guarantee for fish. The Cardinal Tetra originally came from the warmer streams of South America. To replicate their natural habitat, the use of rock work, plants, and driftwood should be included in the aquarium. They also enjoy tannins in their water, so the use of Indian Almond or Guava leaves is highly recommended. We would not recommend keeping this fish with shrimp colonies due to the likeliness of the cardinal tetra eating baby shrimp and potentially picking at adult shrimp. The scientific name for the cardinal tetra is: Paracheirodon axelrodi We feed our Cardinals a mix of frozen foods including daphnia, baby brine, cyclops, and Bloodworms. Crystal Shrimp - Pure Black Line You will receive Pure Black Line shrimp, also known as PBL. The shrimp you will receive will be sub-adults, having a size of around half of an inch (.5 inches). The dwarf shrimp generally range from S to SS grade in pattern. The Pure Black Line Crystal Shrimp (PBL) was introduced into the US market in early 2014. What separated PBL from normal crystal black shrimp was the fact that they were pure. Meaning, they had never been bred with golden bee shrimp to enhance the shrimp coloration. It is common practice for crystal breeders to use golden shrimp to enhance the overall white coloration of their crystal colonies. Therefore, PBL were developed through selective breeding over many generations. Neon Blue Rasbora | Blue Axelrodi Neon Blue Rasbora (Sundadanio axelrodi), also called the Blue Axelrodi Rasbora, is a small freshwater fish with a solid metallic blue body. These delicate rasboras are extremely sensitive when imported because they can be prone to parasites, so we hold them for a minimum of 14 days and run them through a parasite cleanse before listing them for sale. Once they’re healthy, blue neon rasboras become much easier to care for, but we still do not recommend them for beginners. This species is characterized by its vibrant coloration, peaceful temperament, and active schooling behavior, making it a unique addition to nano aquariums. Blue neon rasboras can grow up to 1 inch in length, making them ideal for small tanks. They are native to blackwater streams and peat swamps in Borneo, Sumatra, and other parts of Indonesia. In the wild, you can find these fish in slow-moving, tannin-rich waters surrounded by dense vegetation. Natural Habitat The Blue Axelrodi Rasbora originates from the Greater Sunda Islands in Indonesia and thrives in true black‑water conditions with soft, acidic water rich with natural botanicals . In a well‑planted aquarium, these small neon blue rasboras will show their best behavior. To support their natural needs, it is important to provide plenty of cover, botanicals, and soft water to mimic their native environment. They feel most at home among leaf litter and alder cones, where these guys school together as a group of at least four fish, displaying their metallic blue bodies. By recreating this type of black‑water setup, it helps ensure their well‑being, enhances their vitality, and reduces the chances of this delicate fish becoming stressed. Diet for Blue Neon Rasboras Feeding Blue Neon Rasboras is simple once you know their favorites. We focus on three main types of fish food and try to rotate them daily. Our favorite food type is live daphnia because it doesn’t foul the water and helps prevent bloating. The next type we offer is a mix of Northfin Flake Foods , but be sure to smash the flakes into tiny pieces so these small fish can easily eat them. For optimal health and vibrant color, it is recommended to provide a variety of live or frozen foods such as baby brine shrimp, cyclops, or frozen daphnia. They will also accept pellets but be sure to choose very fine pellets (small size) so the rasboras can consume them without trouble. Blue Neon Rasboras may take some time to learn to accept new foods, especially dried options, so patience and consistent feeding are important as they gradually adapt. Suggest Tank Setup Blue neon rasboras do best in a 10‑gallon tank size or larger with ample room for schooling. We recommend keeping them in group sizes of at least four to help them feel secure. Blue neon rasboras do best with plenty of aquarium plants like vallisneria or dwarf sag. They prefer a pH around 7—though they do well anywhere between 6.5 and 7.5—and add aquarium botanicals like alder cones or Indian almond leaves to create gentle black‑water conditions. This simple setup makes it possible for your blue neon rasboras to thrive and display their bright metallic color. The best approach is to maintain a well-planted, stable environment to encourage natural behaviors and potential breeding. When introducing new fish to the tank, be sure to acclimate them gradually to the water parameters to reduce stress and ensure their health. Our Tank Parameters for Blue Neon Rasboras pH: 7.2 - 7.5 GH: 4 - 6 KH: 2 - 4 TDS: 100 - 150 Temperature: 70 - 74°F Why Buy from Us? Flip Aquatics leads the way in animal care. All orders ship overnight to keep stress on the fish low and ensure their health. The smaller they are shipped the easier it is to acclimate them to a new aquarium. The shrimp will reach breeding age if not already within 1-2 months of receiving them. The term "shadow" references the noticeably blue hue compared to the normal white in black panda/king kong shrimp. This blue can be selectively bred for when keeping blue bolts and black panda/king kongs in the same aquarium. The blue in these shrimp usually become more vivid with age! Shadow Panda and King Kong shrimp are black Taiwan bees. They are from the genus Caridina and tend to be more difficult to keep compared to cherry shrimp or others. Taiwan Bees were considered some of the hardest to keep and breed freshwater shrimp in the past. Between 2009 and 2014, hobbyists were able to stabilize the Taiwan bee shrimp line to have more stability. By adding in new genetic pools, the Taiwan bee shrimp is much easier to keep and breed in current days. For a hobbyist ready to take their hobby to the next level, these pet shrimp are a great place to start. Mixing Taiwan Bees It is great to be aware of the fact that all Taiwan Bee shrimp can be kept in the same tank with out risk of hybridizing. All Taiwan Bee shrimp share similar genetic lines so they will produce shrimp that look similar to the parents. Red King Kongs, Red Pandas, Black King King Kongs, Black Pandas and Blue Bolts can all be kept in the same aquarium. The following parameters are how we keep our Taiwan Bees: Tank Parameters Ph: 5.5 to 6.7 Gh: 3 to 6 Kh: 0 to 1 TDS: 90 to 120 Temp: 68 to 72 Tank Equipment Filter: Matten Filter Substrate: Brightwell Rio Escuro or Cafe, ADA Amazonia Water: RO/DI Water remineralized with Salty Shrimp Gh+ Decor: Malaysian Driftwood, Java Moss and Indian Almond Leaves

Red Pencil Fish The Red Pencilfish (Nannostomus beckfordi) is a popular smaller pencil fish with reddish top half of the fish then a black line, followed by a white underbelly. The male’s “nose” has a red spot on it. Both have bluish/white colored bottom fins. They come from Guyana, Suriname, and French Guiana, plus the eastern Amazon drainage in Amapá and Pará states, Brazil. These are captive raised with emphasis on increased red coloration. They are perfect community fish with other similar sized fish. They grow to the adult size of less than 1.5 inches. They make a perfect addition to a 10-gallon tank or larger with like sized calm fish such as small tetras and rasboras. They enjoy being around live plants, so those are a plus. It is encouraged that they be kept in groups of 10 or more so they feel comfortable in their aquarium. In a group of males and females, the males will have brighter colors as they display to the rest of the group. Please Note: All fish shipments have a 100% Live Arrival Guarantee when shipping with FedEx Overnight (1 Day) option. All other options void our Live Arrival Guarantee for fish. To replicate their natural habitat, the use of rock work, plants, and driftwood should be included in the aquarium. They also enjoy tannins in their water, so the use of Indian Almond or Guava leaves is highly recommended. They enjoy having a shaded aquarium so keeping floating plants is encouraged to cut down the light reaching them. Gentle filtration is encouraged using a sponge filter. We would not recommend keeping this fish with shrimp colonies due to the likeliness of the red pencilfish eating baby shrimp. The scientific name for the red pencilfish is: Nannostomus beckfordi ‘Red’ They are omnivores by nature. We feed our red pencilfish a mix of frozen foods including daphnia, baby brine, cyclops, and bloodworms. Weather Loach The Dojo Loach, often referred to as the Weather Loach, because people say they can predict the weather. When the air pressure around them changes, like before a storm or even on a sunny day, then they start wiggling and swimming more. This happens because their bodies can sense even the tiniest shifts in the water as the air pressure rises or falls. It’s almost like they’re telling you, “Rain is coming” or “The sky will clear up soon” These loaches can grow as long up to about ten inches, so they need a long tank with soft sand or fine gravel to dig and explore. They accept a wide range of water temps between 59-77F. Dojo Loaches are peaceful and enjoy being in small groups, where you can watch them burrow together and play in the sand. We care for every Dojo Loach in our tanks for at least 14+ days before shipping. When it’s time to ship them to you, we bag each fish in a breather bag to prevent sloshing, tuck them into boxes lined with eco‑foam, and ship it overnight. Every order comes with our 100% live arrival guarantee . If your Dojo Loach doesn’t arrive healthy and active, just let us know and we’ll make it right. We’re here to help you before, during, and after your purchase so both you and your new loaches can be happy. Please Note: Dojo loaches are illegal to own and purchase in Illinois, Michigan, Minnesota, and New York. We urge you to be responsible and refrain from releasing any aquatic life into local waterways. Our Tank Parameters: pH: 6.5 to 7.1 Gh: 8 to 12 Kh: 2 to 4 Temp: 72 to 80 Tank Recommendations: Rock: Smooth rock (round in shape) Leaves: Indian Almond or Guava Cones: Alder, Giant Alder, Birch or Casuarina Plants: Java Ferns, Anubias, Sagittaria, Cryptocorene

Kuhli Loach Fish Kuhli Loaches are one of those fish that might be a little weird looking at first… but in the best way possible! They have a long, eel or snake like body and they wiggle all over the tank. Honestly so fun to watch once they get comfortable! These peaceful bottom dwellers spend most of their time exploring the substrate, hiding in plants, and cruising around driftwood or caves. Kuhli loaches are also natural scavengers, so they’ll help clean up leftover food around the aquarium. Just keep in mind, they still need to be fed a good diet of their own! Kuhli Loaches do best in groups of 6 or more. When they’re kept in a group, they feel safer, act more naturally, and you’re way more likely to see them out and about. For the best kuhli loach care, we recommend a soft sand substrate as they like to burrow, peaceful tank mates, and plenty of hiding spots. Plants, driftwood, caves, and leaf litter are all great options. Since they like to burrow and dig around, sand is usually a better choice than rough gravel. With the right setup, Kuhli Loaches can live for years and make such a fun addition to a peaceful community aquarium! Red Root Floaters Red Root Floaters, scientifically known as Phyllanthus Fluitans, are prized for open aquariums, featuring slender stems and distinctively hairy, centrally arched floating leaves. Red Root Floaters have reddish roots that draw nutrients directly from the water, though they require careful maintenance, demanding specific lighting and water conditions along with additional fertilizer for optimal growth. Despite their water-repellent leaves, Red Root Floaters are sensitive to dripping water, thriving best in open tanks with no lids. Enhanced lighting intensifies their red hue and accelerates growth, but they require harder water as light increases. Successful cultivation may yield rare white flowers and green fruits, rewarding enthusiasts. Red Root Floaters care includes, maintaining constant high humidity, low-flow water and regular fertilization with trace elements sustains their robust growth, ensuring their vitality in aquarium settings. Baby Tears The Baby Tears plant ( Micranthemum Umbrosum ) is a real eye-catcher in any aquarium and looks fantastically in the front or middle part of the tank. The Baby Tears plant is often used as a carpeting plant, covering the entirety of the aquarium floor, but can also be used in the foreground as an individual plant. This delicate plant shouldn't be underestimated, as the baby tears plant can be quite demanding in terms of lighting and care. Because of this, the Baby Tears plant is perfect for aquarium keepers have already been in the hobby for a while, looking for a slightly more challenging plant. What is the Baby Tears Plant? The Baby Tears plant is light-hungry but otherwise undemanding. Aquarists love the Baby Tears plant, primarily because of its bright green colour, which stands out beautifully from other species. The Baby Tears plant can be used for a wide range of applications and decoration, making it suitable for all types of aquariums. With increasing light intensity, the growth becomes flatter, leading to carpet growth. The plant reacts relatively quickly to inadequate lighting with holes in the leaves, and the stems become brittle. If the shoots do not receive enough light at the base, they become glabrous and can also break. How to Care for the Baby Tears Plant Under the right conditions, the Baby Tears plant will grow rapidly. They require lots of light to grow adequately, but other than that, they can be rather forgiving. The Baby Tears plant can grow in both slightly acidic and alkaline waters. They can also grow just fine in both hard and soft water, as long as the water is clean. Care Level: Medium Lighting: High CO2: reccommended if carpeting Fertilizer or Shrimp Safe Fertilizer *All Plants may contain snails or snail eggs. Glossostigma Aquarium Plant Glossostigma ( Glossostigma elatinoides ) is a very small, lawn-forming aquarium plant with crawling shoots and spatula-shaped leaves, which is wildly popular in Japanese-styled aquaria. The Glossostigma leaves have a distinct midrib, while the veins of the leaves are fan-shaped, similar to the leaves of the ginkgo tree. Despite their size, these plants shouldn't be underestimated, as they do require adequate care to grow properly. For whom is the Glossostigma suited? While the Glossostigma certainly isn't the most challenging aquarium plant to grow, it does require a certain level of care that beginners may not be able to offer it. To grow well, it requires sufficient amounts of light, CO 2 , as well as trace elements which can be supplemented through fertilizers. It is easy to recognize whether the Glossostigma is getting enough light: At insufficient levels, the plant will start to gain height, while with sufficient levels, it will begin to cover the floor of your tank rather quickly. What are they like? These small plants will, under the right conditions, form a beautiful green lawn at the bottom of your aquarium, which is precisely why they are so popular. They make for a lovely decorative addition to your tank, and they are especially popular among hobbyists who keep freshwater shrimp. The ideal conditions for the Glossostigma As previously mentioned, the Glossostigma requires a lot of intense light to thrive, as well as adequate CO 2 and trace elements. They grow best in waters that as slightly acidic, and have a wide temperature tolerance from 4 °C – 30 °C. The hardness of the water doesn't matter for the growth of these green beauties. *All Plants may contain snails or snail eggs. We keep them in all of our tanks for the benefits they provide.*

Italian Val The Italian Val is a popular and widely recognized aquarium plant known for its rapid growth and ease of care, making it suitable for aquarists of all skill levels. With its band-shaped leaves and dense green stands, it quickly fills up the tank, providing a lush green backdrop. This plant requires minimal maintenance and is often chosen by beginners as their first aquatic plant. Regular trimming may be necessary to prevent it from overtaking the tank. It thrives in temperatures ranging from 18°C to 28°C and prefers slightly alkaline water with moderate hardness. Overall, the Italian Val is an excellent choice for aquarists looking to add vibrant greenery to their aquarium without the need for specialized care. Crinum Calamistratum The Crinum Calamistratum is a very graceful bulbous plant with dark green leaves that are strongly curled and crimped at the edges. The numerous firm and leathery leaves are reminiscent of the arms of an octopus. The bulbous appearance of the leaves will add a unique touch to the green in your aquarium, and on top of that, they are incredibly easy to care for, making them suitable for beginners. Crinum Calamistratum is suited for beginners, especially for those who do not want their plants to dominate their tanks fully. Crinum Calamistratum grows at a rather slow pace and does not require any special care to be healthy. What is Crinum Calamistratum like? When the Crinum Calamistratum reaches the surface in open aquaria, they sometimes form beautiful white flowers, adding a gracious touch to the appearance of your tank. Crinum Calamistratum has slow growth that allows them to easily co-exist with other plants, so long as they can receive sufficient lighting. The Ideal Conditions for the Crinum Calamistratum The Crinum Calamistratum is very forgiving when it comes to the conditions in your aquarium. They can thrive in both slightly acidic and alkaline waters at temperatures between 12 °C – 30 °C, and the hardness of your water doesn't really matter much. They don't require intensive lighting, and supplementation with fertilizer is generally not required. *All Plants may contain snails or snail eggs. In areas with a lot of shade, they will die rather quickly. They require soft water and thrive at a temperature between 72 – 78 °F. Brazilian Pennywort Brazilian Pennywort (Hydrocotyle leucocephala) is a versatile and fast-growing plant that adds a unique touch to any aquarium. Brazilian Pennywort has vibrant green, coin-shaped leaves create a striking contrast against other plants and provide a lush, floating appearance. Whether rooted in the substrate or left to float freely, Brazilian Pennywort can thrive in various water conditions and light levels, making this aquarium plant an ideal choice for beginners and seasoned aquarists. Brazilian Pennyworts ability to grow quickly and adapt to different environments helps improve water quality by absorbing excess nutrients. Perfect for adding height and texture to your aquarium, Brazilian Pennywort can be used as a background plant or to create shaded areas for fish and shrimp. Brazilian Pennywort has delicate trailing stems that can even grow above the waterline, adding a natural, overhanging effect to your aquascape. With minimal maintenance required, this aquarium plant is a beautiful and functional addition that promotes a healthy ecosystem while enhancing the visual appeal of your aquatic setup. Scientific Name: Hydrocotyle Leucocephala Common Name : Brazilian Pennywort Caring for Brazilian Pennywort Care Level: Easy Light: Low-Medium CO2 : Recommended if carpeting effect is desired Fertilizer or Shrimp Safe Fertilizer Propagation : Stem plant, cut and replant stem Note: Please do additional research on your plant to ensure its health. *All Plants may contain snails or snail eggs. We keep them in all of our tanks for the benefits they provide.*

Mid Grade Red Galaxy Pinto Shrimp There is very little information out there about these beautiful shrimp called the Galaxy Pinto. My understanding is that the name originated from the breeder when he or she observed that the shrimp was showing white speckles on the body which looked like a galaxy with many stars. The galaxy pinto is a rather expensive shrimp in the hobby with a range of prices between $50 and $200 each on average. Price is determined by color, size and sex. Since the galaxy pinto is a cross between tiger shrimp and Taiwan bee shrimp, it is not an easy pattern to replicate or reproduce. Therefore, many hobbyists are willing to pay the money to skip year of hard work that went into creating this amazing shrimp. The galaxy pinto comes in two colors: red and black. The red variation sells for a higher price as red is more desirable to most hobbyists. This can also be observed with crystal red shrimp and red cherry shrimp. While color has a lot to do with the price, pattern is also very important. The lowest grade of galaxy pintos is one that has very little white. As the white coloration increases, the higher the value goes. With very little black or red coloration, these shrimp can demand prices of $300 to $400 each. Tank Parameters Ph: 5.5 to 6.7 Gh: 3 to 6 Kh: 0 to 1 TDS: 90 to 120 Temp: 68 to 72 Tank Equipment Filter: Matten Filter Substrate: Brightwell Rio Escuro or Cafe Soil, ADA Amazonia Water: RO/DI Water remineralized with Salty Shrimp GH+ Decor: Malaysian Driftwood, Java Moss and Indian Almond Leaves

listings.commonName: Red Fancy Tiger Shrimp - High Grade
listings.description: High Grade Red Fancy Tiger Shrimp You will receive red fancy tiger shrimp that will differ in pattern, these patterns will be bold and represent our high grade selection. The great thing about Red Fancy Tiger shrimp is that they vary in pattern so drastically, all are so beautiful. We sell tiger shrimp usually around half an inch. The smaller they are, the easier it is to acclimate them to a new aquarium. The shrimp will reach breeding age within a month of receiving them. Red fancy tiger shrimp are a mix between tiger shrimp and crystal red shrimp. We keep these shrimp at the parameters below. In our experience, these shrimp are very hardy and have done really well for us. Through importing these guys, we have lost very few. The red fancy tiger is a must have for all aquarium shrimp hobbyist. The contrast between the red and white is very appealing. They are a great change from the typical red and white patterns found in crystal red dwarf shrimp. Black Lava Rock for Aquariums | Black Carved Lava Rock Lava rock in general is one of the best rocks to use in a shrimp tank. Lava rock is extremely porous which provides tons of surface area to grow biofilm and beneficial bacteria. Lava rock will create natural feeding grounds for shrimp and especially baby shrimp. Black carved lava rock is ideal for an aquarium because it adds character. The holes add depth to the aquarium and provide natural decoration to include in any aquascape. Our black carved lava rock comes in 3 sizes and is great for shrimp tanks: Small: 1.5-2 inches Medium: 2.5-4 inches Large: 5-6 inches Key Benefits Will not increase Ph Provide natural feeding ground for shrimp and other algae eaters Provides hiding places for baby shrimp Beautiful texture for aquascaping For best results we recommend rinsing rocks before addition to an aquarium. Although all pieces are cleaned, it is natural for rock to create additional dust during shipping. You will receive one (1) hand selected piece of carved lava rock. Each piece is inspected and packaged with care to help protect the character of each rock. *Each piece is different. The stones you receive will not be identical to the product pictures although are accurate examples of what you will receive.*

Indian Almond Bark You will be receiving a 40g pack of Indian almond tree bark also known as catappa tree bark. The bark is an essential part of breeding and keeping freshwater shrimp. Although, they are also beneficial to bettas, Apistogrammas and Corydoras species for their healing properties and ability to lower the pH. The Indian Almond Tree Bark is a great alternative to leaves. While it doesn't break down as quick, it releases a lot of tannin into the water. Each 40g pack has at least one log shaped piece of bark making it a great hiding place for shrimp or other small species. Key Features: Provides Natural Food Source for Ornamental Shrimp Releases Tannin into the water which contains Healing Properties Lowers the pH slightly Anti-fungal Properties to help fight off Infection Creates Additional Hiding Places to Reduce Stress of Aquarium Inhabitants

Orange Rili Shrimp Orange Rili Neocaridina shrimp are the orange variety of rili shrimp which means they have an orange carapace, a clear midsection, and an orange tail. These beautiful shrimp were developed from Orange Pumpkin Neocaridina , and their stunning coloration and unique patterns provide a vibrant pop of color to any shrimp tank. Orange Rili shrimp thrive in standard Neocaridina parameters, with a pH above 7. Any inert substrate will work well in their habitat. Providing natural cover and surface area for biofilm to grow—using materials like wood , leaves , and cones —will benefit both these shrimp and their offspring. Including mosses and other live plants in their tank setup is also recommended. They enjoy consuming NorthFin foods, biofilm, and algae. Common Name: Orange Rili Shrimp or sometimes called Orange Sukura Shrimp Scientific Name: Neocaridina Davidi vs. "Rili" Genus: Neocaridina Our Tank Parameters: Ph: 7.0 to 7.6 Gh: 7 to 15 Kh: 2 to 8 TDS: 150 to 350 Temp: 68 °F to 72 °F What we feed: Northfin Veggie Northfin Community Northfin bug pro Kelp Wafers Tank Recommendations: Minimum tank size: 4 g allons , but 20 gallons recommended Compatible tank mates: Micro rasboras , Pygmy cories , plecos Filter: Matten Filter Substrate: Pool Filter Sand, Inert Substrate , or any substrate that will not alter pH Water: RO/DI Water remineralized with Shrimple GH/KH+ Wood and Botanicals: Alder Cones , Malaysian Driftwood , Java Moss, and Indian Almond Leaves

Yellow Neocaridina Yellow Neocaridina shrimp are bright yellow in color and are stunning in any shrimp tank. They thrive in any general Neocaridina parameters with a pH above 7. Any inert substrate will work in their tank. Providing natural cover and surface area for biofilm to grow on with woods, leaves, and cones will be beneficial for these shrimp and their offspring. Mosses and other live plants should be included in their tank setup. They will eat any shrimp specific manufactured foods, biofilm, and algae. We offer both imported and USA bred yellow Neocaridina shrimp. Our USA bred shrimp are smaller at 1/2 an inch in size or less. All imported shrimp are 1/2 and inch or bigger on average.
