Buce Theia Bucephalandra Theia is a beautiful, beginner-friendly Buce that stands out with its broad leaves and cool iridescent shimmer! Depending on your aquarium's lighting and water conditions, the foliage can range from deep olive green to rich reddish-brown, with the blue sheen becoming especially noticeable under quality LED lighting. Its slow growth and compact size make it an excellent choice for adding color and texture to the foreground or midground of planted aquariums. Bucephalandra Theia is an epiphytic plant and should be attached to driftwood, rocks, or other hardscape rather than planted directly into the substrate. Burying the rhizome can cause it to rot, so it's important to keep the rhizome exposed while allowing the roots to naturally anchor themselves. Over time, it will slowly spread along the rhizome and develop new leaves. One of the reasons Buce Theia is so popular is its ability to thrive in lower light and shaded areas where many other aquarium plants struggle. It doesn't require CO2 to grow, but added CO2 and regular fertilization will encourage faster growth, improved coloration, and a healthier plant overall! Like many Bucephalandra varieties, it's normal to experience a small amount of leaf melt after introducing it to a new aquarium as it adjusts to its new environment. Bucephalandra Theia is a hardy freshwater aquarium plant that rewards patience with beautiful growth and unique coloration. Whether you're creating a nature-style aquascape or simply looking for an easy, colorful accent plant, this Buce is an excellent choice. Care Level: Easy Lighting Requirement: Low to Medium CO2: Not Needed, but Beneficial Growth Rate: Slow Origin: Borneo Tank Placement: Foreground – Midground Propagation: By cutting the rhizome *All plants may contain scuds, snails, or snail eggs. We keep them in all of our tanks for the benefits they provide.* ```

Gold Marble Angelfish The Gold Marble Angelfish is a beautiful freshwater angelfish that combines bold black, white, silver, and shimmering gold marbling into one stunning fish. Their tall, graceful fins and unique pattern make them a true centerpiece in larger community aquariums. Every Gold Marble Angelfish develops its own distinct markings, so no two fish look exactly alike. Gold Marble Angelfish are one of the hardier freshwater angelfish , making them a great choice for hobbyists looking to keep cichlids for the first time. While they're generally peaceful, they can become territorial as they mature, especially when they pair off to breed. They do best with other peaceful community fish that are too large to be considered food and appreciate heavily planted aquariums with driftwood, open swimming space, and gentle water flow. When it comes to feeding, Gold Marble Angelfish aren't picky. They'll readily accept high-quality flakes, pellets, frozen foods, and live foods. Feeding a varied diet helps maintain their vibrant coloration and supports healthy growth throughout their long lifespan. Care Guide Scientific Name: Pterophyllum scalare Common Name: Gold Marble Angelfish Gold Marble Angelfish thrive in stable, well-maintained aquariums with plenty of vertical swimming space. As they mature, they'll appreciate taller aquariums with plants and décor that provide natural territories without overcrowding the tank. Care Level: Easy Temperament: Semi-Peaceful (Can be territorial when breeding) Origin: South America Diet: Omnivore (Flake, Pellet, Frozen & Live Foods) Max Size: Up to 6 inches Lifespan: Up to 12 years Recommended Tank Size: 30+ Gallons Shipping Size: Approximately 1.5-3 inches

Their rich, solid red coloration paired with almost glowing orange eyes creates a look that's hard to miss! It is a color combination you simply do not see very often, which is why these shrimp have become so sought after by Caridina keepers. Like other high grade Caridina shrimp, Orange Eye Red Devil Shrimp thrive in stable, well-established aquariums with soft, slightly acidic water and consistent water parameters. Their deep red color sometimes become even richer as they mature, while their signature orange eyes remain one of the defining features that make this selectively bred shrimp so unique. They are known for their bold red coloration paired with beautiful galaxy-style snowflake spotting, giving each shrimp its own unique pattern. No two Red Galaxy Snowflakes look exactly the same, which is part of what makes this line so fun. Some may show heavier galaxy coverage across the body, while others have a cleaner red look with scattered white snowflake-style markings. Azolla Caroliniana Azolla Caroliniana has quite a few names, like Azolla Fairy Moss. Some people call it a Water Fern or Mosquito Fern, which is fine... but we think Fairy Moss is way cooler. We saw this plant a few years back and KNEW we had to get it on the site one day because it's one of the cutest floating plants we've ever seen! Azolla Fairy Moss is a tiny floating plant that grows in little clusters across the surface of the water. Honestly, it kind of looks like tiny green snowflakes floating around your tank or pond! Under stronger lighting, Azolla can even develop pretty pink, orange, or reddish tones, which makes it even more fun! This fast-growing floating plant does great in aquariums, ponds, summer tubs, shrimp tanks, and fry setups. It provides shade, surface cover, and cozy hiding spots for shy fish, baby fish, and shrimp. Like most floating plants, it does best with gentle water flow and doesn't love being pushed around by heavy surface agitation. Azolla Caroliniana is easy to care for and grows quickly once it settles in, so you may need to thin it out from time to time. It does best under medium to high lighting and thrives in a wide range of pH levels and temperatures, though it is not a big fan of cold water. If you want a floating plant that feels a little more unique than the usual options, Azolla Fairy Moss is such a fun pick! Key Features of Azolla Fairy Moss Tiny floating plant with a fairy moss or snowflake appearance Also known as Azolla Caroliniana, Fairy Moss, Mosquito Fern, or Water Fern Perfect for aquariums, ponds, summer tubs, shrimp tanks, and fry setups Provides shade and cover for shy fish, fry, and shrimp Can develop pink, orange, or red coloration under stronger lighting Fast-growing and beginner-friendly Prefers gentle water flow with minimal surface agitation May arrive with small amounts of duckweed mixed in Care Guide for Azolla Caroliniana Scientific Name: Azolla caroliniana Common Names: Azolla Fairy Moss, Fairy Moss, Mosquito Fern, Water Fern Care Level: Easy pH: 5.0-8.0 Light: Medium to High CO 2 : Not Required Growth Rate: Fast Placement: Floating Plant Note: Please do additional research on your plant to ensure it thrives in your aquarium. *All plants may contain snails or snail eggs. We intentionally keep snails in our plant systems because of the many benefits they provide.*

Aponogeton Crispus Plant Aponogeton Crispus is one of those plants that brings instant jungle vibes to a planted aquarium. It's known for its long, wavy, light green leaves that can look slightly see-through under the right lighting. It has a soft, flowing appearance that adds a ton of movement to the background of any aquarium. This plant can get pretty big, so it is best used as a background plant or in a larger aquarium where it has room to show off. Once it settles in, Aponogeton Crispus grows quickly and can become a stunning centerpiece plant. Care is easy overall, but like many aquarium plants, it does not love sudden changes. Large swings in water parameters, lighting, or nutrients can cause melting or leaf loss. Don't panic if it experiences some transition melt after being added to your aquarium. Keep conditions stable, provide a nutrient-rich substrate, and it should bounce back with healthy new growth. Aponogeton Crispus does best in softer, slightly acidic water but can adapt to a variety of conditions as long as the aquarium remains stable. CO2 injection and a quality aquarium soil can help it grow fuller and faster, but patience is the biggest key to success. Key Features of Aponogeton Crispus Beautiful wavy green leaves with a soft, flowing appearance Excellent background plant for larger planted aquariums Can grow 12–24 inches or more Easy to care for once established Fast-growing under good conditions Thrives with stable water parameters and a nutrient-rich substrate CO 2 and quality aquarium soil can encourage faster growth Aponogeton Crispus Care Guide Scientific Name: Aponogeton crispus Family: Aponogetonaceae Care Level: Easy Placement: Background Height: 12-24+ inches pH: 6.0-7.5 Lighting: Low to High CO2: Optional, but beneficial Growth Rate: Fast Propagation: Seeds and may self-pollinate when flowering Leaf melt during shipping or after planting is completely normal for bulb plants like Aponogeton Crispus. As long as the bulb remains firm and healthy, the plant will typically send out fresh new leaves once it acclimates to your aquarium. *All plants may contain snails or snail eggs. They trace back to Stan Shubel , one of the most respected guppy breeders in the hobby, who spent decades selectively breeding guppies beginning in the 1940s. This line has stood the test of time for a reason. Our Green Delta Guppies come from a local hobbyist breeder who's worked hard to keep this line pure, preserving the body shape, flowing delta tail, and beautiful green coloration that made these guppies so well known in the first place. The males have a really unique look with soft green iridescence that almost glows when the light hits them just right. It's a color you don't see very often, and it's one of those fish that looks even better in person. Like most guppies, they're peaceful, active, and easy to keep, making them a great fit for planted tanks and community aquariums. Whether you're just getting into guppies or you're someone who appreciates the history behind different strains, Green Delta Guppies are a really neat fish to own. They combine beautiful genetics with decades of careful breeding, and that's something pretty special. Zebra Danio Fish Zebra Danios are one of those fish that make a tank feel alive instantly! They're small, active schooling fish that usually grow to around 2 inches, but don't let their size fool you because these guys are always on the move! They get their name from the bold stripes that run across their bodies, giving them that classic zebra look. They're honestly just fun to watch, especially when you have a group darting around together! Zebra Danios are also super hardy, which makes them a great choice for beginners . They can adapt to a wide range of water conditions and are usually not picky when it comes to food. That being said, they still do best in a stable, well-maintained aquarium. We recommend keeping Zebra Danios in groups of 6 or more so they feel comfortable and show off their natural schooling behavior. They do great in community tanks with other peaceful fish, especially when they have a mix of open swimming space and plants to explore. Our Tank Parameters pH: 6.8 to 7.2 GH: 4 to 8 KH: 2 to 4 Temp: 72 to 80°F Tank Recommendations Leaves: Indian Almond Leaves or Guava Leaves Wood: Malaysian Driftwood , Pacific, Neka, or Spiderwood Cones: Alder Cones , Giant Alder Cones , Birch, or Casuarina Cones Key Features Hardy, beginner-friendly fish Grows to around 2 inches Active schooling fish Best kept in groups of 6 or more Great for peaceful community aquariums Loves open swimming space with plants around the tank

Smudge Spot Cory | Violet Corydoras The Smudge Spot Cory is such a fun little Corydoras species, and honestly, the name fits perfectly. These fish have a bold dark “smudge” near the back half of the body, right before the tail, that can show up with a bluish or purplish tone. That is why you may also see them called Violet Corydoras They usually grow to about 1.5-2 inches as adults, so they stay a really nice size for community tanks. They are small enough to work in many setups, but still big enough to be easy to spot as they wiggle around the bottom! Like most corys, Smudge Spot Corys are peaceful, social, and fun to watch. They spend their day cruising along the bottom of the tank, sifting through the substrate, and hanging out with their group. They are not aggressive at all, which makes them a great choice for peaceful community aquariums. Our Tank Parameters pH: 7.2 to 7.6 GH: 4 to 8 KH: 2 to 4 TDS: 160 to 180 Temp: 70 to 74°F Tank Setup for Cory Similis Cory Similis are highly social fish, so we recommend keeping them in groups . A group of 6 or more is a great place to start, but with corys, bigger groups are almost always more fun . They feel safer with friends and are way more likely to show off their natural behavior when they have a little crew. Fine sand is our favorite substrate for corys because they love to sift through it looking for food. They will shove their little faces into the sand like they have very important business to attend to, and it's one of the best parts of keeping them! Smooth gravel can work too, but avoid anything sharp since corys spend so much time on the bottom. They also appreciate a peaceful tank with plants, driftwood, leaf litter, and some open areas for foraging. You may occasionally see them dart up to the surface for a quick gulp of air and then zoom right back down. That is totally normal cory behavior and just adds to their goofy little personality. Feeding Smudge Spot Corys Smudge Spot Corys are omnivores, but they should not be treated like “cleaner fish” that can live off scraps. They may help pick up leftover food, but they still need to be fed like any other fish. A good diet for Violet Corydoras should include sinking foods like quality pellets, wafers, frozen foods, and occasional live foods. We really like using NorthFin foods like NorthFin Community , NorthFin Nano Bits , because they are high quality, easy to feed, and give them a more balanced diet than just whatever happens to hit the bottom of the tank. Feed them after lights out or target feed near the bottom if faster fish are stealing everything first. Quick Care Info Scientific Name: Corydoras similis Common Names: Smudge Spot Cory, Violet Corydoras, Cory Similis Natural Range: Rio Madeira tributaries, Brazil Source: Aquarium Bred and Raised Estimated Size at Shipping: 0.75-1 inch Adult Size: Around 1.5-2 inches Sold As: Unsexed Diet: Omnivore Temperament: Peaceful Best Kept In: Groups of 6 or more Tank Placement: Bottom dweller Live Arrival Guarantee All fish orders are covered by our 100% Live Arrival Guarantee when shipped with Overnight shipping. Metallic Silver Endler The Metallic Silver Endler is a small, colorful livebearer with a bright metallic silver shine that REALLY stands out when the light hits it. These little fish may stay small, but they bring a ton of color and movement to planted tanks, nano tanks, and peaceful community aquariums. Metallic Silver Endlers are active, peaceful, and beginner friendly. Like other Endlers, they're constantly on the move, exploring the aquarium, looking for food, and showing off their metallic coloration. They do best in groups and appreciate an aquarium with live plants, open swimming space, and peaceful tank mates. They're also pretty hardy and can adapt to a range of water parameters, making them a great option for both newer and experienced hobbyists. What We Feed Metallic Silver Endlers We feed our Endlers a mix of frozen, live, and prepared foods, including live baby brine and black worms. We also supplement their diet with NorthFin Veggie, Community, and Bug Pro to give them a varied diet. Our Tank Parameters for Endlers pH: 6.5 to 7.8 GH: 6 to 18 KH: 2 to 6 TDS: 100 to 200 Temperature: 72 to 80°F Metallic Silver Endler Tank Recommendations Plants: Java Moss, Guppy Grass, Hornwort, or other beginner-friendly plants Leaves: Indian Almond Leaves or Guava Leaves Wood: Malaysian Driftwood, Mopani, or Spiderwood Cones: Alder Cones Other: A planted tank with plenty of cover is especially helpful if fry are present Quick Facts About Metallic Silver Endlers Scientific Name: Poecilia wingei Common Name: Metallic Silver Endler Adult Size: Around 1 inch Temperament: Peaceful and active Care Level: Easy Minimum Tank Size: 10 gallons Best Kept In: Groups Tank Level: Middle to upper water column Diet: Omnivore Great For: Nano tanks, planted tanks, and peaceful community aquariums Breeding: Livebearer 100% Live Arrival Guarantee All fish shipments have a 100% Live Arrival Guarantee when shipping with our Overnight (1 Day) option. All other options void our Live Arrival Guarantee for fish.

Cory Crumbles | KatsAquatics Cory Crumbles are a high-protein sinking food made specifically with corys and other bottom-feeding dwellers in mind! Instead of dropping one wafer into the tank and watching everyone pile on top of each other, these are designed to break apart and scatter across the bottom , giving your fish more room to search, sift, and forage for their food! Each crumble is made with ingredients like wild-caught fish, black soldier fly larvae, krill, egg, brewer's yeast, spirulina, kelp, and alfalfa. That gives your bottom dwellers a good mix of both animal and plant-based ingredients, which is especially nice for omnivores like Corydoras. Break one apart over the tank and you'll end up with everything from larger chunks to tiny pieces that work their way between plants, rocks, and substrate. Instead of every fish fighting over the same wafer, they get to actually hunt around the bottom for their dinner. They're also handmade in the USA and formulated by a biologist , rather than being mass produced into perfectly identical pellets. Key Features: High-protein sinking food made for Corys and other bottom feeders Crumbles into different-sized pieces for fish big and small Helps spread food throughout the aquarium instead of creating one crowded feeding spot Encourages natural searching, sifting, and foraging behavior Made with wild-caught fish, black soldier fly larvae, krill, and egg Includes spirulina, kelp, alfalfa, and other plant-based ingredients Berry-shaped portions make it easy to control how much you feed Great for corys, plecos, loaches, catfish, and other omnivorous bottom feeders Biologist-formulated and handmade in the USA Great food to rotate into a varied diet How to Feed Take one Cory Crumble and break it apart with your fingers over the aquarium, spreading the pieces around different areas of the tank. You can leave larger pieces for bigger fish or crumble it finer for smaller corys and other little bottom dwellers. Adjust how much you use based on the number and size of fish you're feeding. Feed only what your fish can finish within a few hours and remove anything that goes uneaten. One little crumble can turn the whole bottom of your tank into a feeding ground!

Green Cobra Endlers Green Cobra Endlers are small, colorful livebearers with a bright green metallic shine and cobra-like patterning. They are active little fish that add a lot of movement to planted tanks, nano aquariums, and peaceful community setups. Like other Endlers, Green Cobra Endlers are hardy, beginner-friendly, and easy to enjoy. They do best in groups and really stand out in planted tanks with driftwood, darker backgrounds, and plenty of places to explore. Green Cobra Endlers are peaceful, but they are very active. We recommend keeping them with other peaceful fish that do not mind extra movement in the tank. Since Endlers are livebearers, males and females kept together may produce fry. listings.commonName: Black Metal Snakeskin Guppy | Poecilia Reticulata
listings.description: Black Metal Snakeskin Guppies Black Metal Snakeskin Guppies are SO cool. These guys have a dark bodies almost resembling a normal Black Metal Guppy but they have this stunning snakeskin patterning, some of them look like they even get into the lace patterning on their tails. They have that bold guppy look, but with a darker, moodier color that just feels a little different from your average guppy. They are active, hardy, and always out doing something, which makes them really fun to watch. Black Metal Snakeskin Guppies are great for planted tanks, beginner setups, and peaceful community aquariums where you want color, movement, and a fish with a little extra personality. Like other guppies, they are beginner-friendly and do best in stable, established aquariums. They are peaceful, but they are also very active, so we recommend keeping them with other peaceful fish that do not mind extra movement in the tank. Quick Facts Adult Size: Around 1.5-2 inches Temperament: Peaceful, active Care Level: Easy Tank Level: Middle to upper water column Diet: Omnivore Great For: Planted tanks, beginner tanks, and peaceful community aquariums Note: Guppies are livebearers and may produce fry Please Note: All fish shipments have a 100% Live Arrival Guarantee when shipping with our Overnight (1 Day) option. All other options void our Live Arrival Guarantee for fish. What We Feed Our Guppies We feed our guppies a mix of frozen, live, and prepared foods, including live baby brine shrimp and black worms. We also supplement their diet with NorthFin foods like NorthFin Veggie, NorthFin Community, and NorthFin Bug Pro. Our Tank Parameters pH: 7.2 to 8.2 GH: 8 to 12 KH: 4 to 6 TDS: 150 to 200 Temp: 72 to 80 Why We Like Black Metal Snakeskin Guppies These guys are just flat out cool. The dark metallic color mixed with the snakeskin pattern gives them such a unique look, and when they are swimming around a planted tank, they really pop. They are easy to keep, fun to feed, and a great option if you want a guppy that feels a little more bold and different.

Shrimp Dinner 2 GlasGarten Shrimp Dinner 2 is an everyday shrimp food designed to give your shrimp a balanced mix of nutrients in one easy meal. It contains a blend of algae, plants, minerals, and other natural ingredients to help support healthy growth, molting, coloration, and breeding. This shrimp food comes in small pads that hold together well in the aquarium , giving your shrimp plenty of time to gather around and graze without the food immediately falling apart. This makes Shrimp Dinner 2 a great staple food for both Neocaridina and Caridina shrimp colonies. How Much Shrimp Dinner 2 Should You Feed? Feed 1-2 times per day, offering only as much as your shrimp can finish within a few hours. The amount you need will depend on the size of your shrimp colony, so start small and adjust from there. As always with shrimp… less is usually better than overfeeding! Shrimp Dinner 2 Ingredients Chlorella algae, spirulina algae, kelp, spinach, molluscs and crustaceans, vegetable protein extracts, cereals, minerals, nettle, walnut leaves, yeast extract, herbs, and fennel.

Protein XP GlasGarten Protein XP is a high-protein aquarium food made for shrimp, snails, crayfish, crabs, and omnivorous fish. With 42% protein , it's especially useful when your shrimp need some extra protein to support healthy growth, breeding, egg development, and growing shrimplets. Protein is particularly important for young shrimp since they grow and molt much more frequently than adults. Protein XP combines both animal and plant-based proteins along with vitamins, minerals, amino acids, omega 3 fatty acids, and other nutrients to help support healthy development. This high-protein shrimp food is a great option to work into your feeding rotation if you're breeding shrimp, raising shrimplets, or simply looking to add some extra protein to your shrimp's diet. How Much Protein XP Should You Feed? Protein XP can be fed once daily, offering only as much as your animals can finish within a few hours. If you're using it as a protein supplement alongside other foods, feed it every 2–3 days instead. As with any shrimp food, start with a small amount and adjust based on the size of your colony and how quickly they finish it. You don't need much! Protein XP Ingredients Krill, spinach, insects, vegetable protein extracts, grains, bacterial protein from Corynebacterium glutamicum , peppers, lupine, kelp, minerals, decapsulated Artemia eggs, mannan oligosaccharides (MOS), beta glucan, papaya leaves, and flower pollen. Who Is Protein XP Good For? GlasGarten Protein XP is great for shrimp, snails, crayfish, crabs, and omnivorous fish . It's especially useful for breeding shrimp colonies and growing shrimplets with higher protein needs.

Wabenmuster Bushynose Pleco The Wabenmuster Bushynose Pleco , also called the Honeycomb Bristlenose Pleco , is one of those plecos you just don’t see every day. Their dark body is covered in a whitish-yellow geometric pattern that gives them this really cool honeycomb look. “Wabenmuster” translates from German to “honeycomb pattern,” which honestly fits them perfectly. That patterning covers the body and fins, making them stand out from more common bristlenose plecos. We get these from one of our local breeders who specializes in some seriously cool plecos , and he actually taught us something interesting about them. You might notice they don’t have an L-number like a lot of other plecos in the hobby. From what our breeder explained to us, when these fish first showed up in Europe, their exact collection location wasn’t known, so they never received an L-number. Pretty cool! They are an Ancistrus species, so they stay much more manageable than some of the giant plecos you see in the hobby. That makes them a really cool option if you want something more unusual without needing a massive aquarium. Quick Facts Basic Info Scientific Name: Ancistrus sp. “Wabenmuster” Common Names: Wabenmuster Bushynose Pleco, Wabenmuster Bristlenose Pleco, Honeycomb Bristlenose Pleco Adult Size: Approximately 4-5 inches Origin: Tank raised Care Care Level: Easy Temperament: Peaceful Minimum Tank Size: 20 gallons Tank Level: Bottom Shrimp Safe: Generally safe with adult shrimp. They typically don’t bother shrimplets either, but plenty of cover is recommended. Good For: Peaceful community tanks, pleco keepers, and planted aquariums with driftwood Please Note: All fish shipments have a 100% Live Arrival Guarantee when shipping with Overnight (1 Day) option. All other options void our Live Arrival Guarantee for fish. Feeding Wabenmuster Plecos are omnivores, but their diet should focus heavily on vegetable-based foods, algae, biofilm, and quality sinking foods. Algae wafers, spirulina-based foods, NorthFin Kelp Wafers, zucchini, cucumber, and other veggie-based options are all great choices. They can also be offered small amounts of meatier foods occasionally, but those should not make up the majority of their diet. And don’t forget the driftwood . We recommend keeping real driftwood in the aquarium for Ancistrus to graze on and explore. Recommended Parameters Temperature: 75-82°F pH: 6.0-7.5 KH: 2-12 Tank Recommendations Wood: Driftwood is highly recommended Hides: Pleco caves, wood piles, and shaded areas Substrate: Sand or smooth gravel Plants: Hardy plants that can handle pleco activity Other: Stable, established aquariums are best

L306 Pleco | L306 Blood Red Tiger Pleco The L306 Blood Red Tiger Pleco , also known as the Takutu Tiger Pleco , is seriously one of the coolest tiger plecos out there! These guys have bold banding that can develop beautiful reddish-brown to red coloration, giving them that classic tiger pleco look with a little extra attitude. Unlike many L-number plecos, the L306 Pleco is actually a formally described species Panaqolus claustellifer . They originate from the Takutu and Rio Branco drainages of Brazil and Guyana, and the fish offered here are F3 tank raised from wild caught great-grandparents . These L306 Blood Red Tiger Plecos have been selectively bred for increased red coloration and some really unique pattern traits, including broken or discontinuous bars. Basically, they are not your average pleco. Like other Panaqolus plecos, the Blood Red Tiger Pleco is a wood eater, also called xylophagous. That means they need real driftwood in the tank to graze on. It is not just decoration for them. It is an important part of their care and digestion. L306 plecos stay at a manageable size compared to many larger pleco species, making them a really unique option for established aquariums with stable water, hiding spots, and plenty of wood. They are a great choice for hobbyists who want something a little more rare, a little more bold, and definitely not your average pleco. Quick Facts Basic Info Scientific Name: Panaqolus claustellifer Common Names: L306 Blood Red Tiger Pleco, Takutu Tiger Pleco Adult Size: Approximately 4 inches Origin: F3 tank raised from wild-caught great-grandparents Care Care Level: Moderate Temperament: Peaceful to mildly territorial Tank Level: Bottom Driftwood Required: Yes Good For: Established aquariums, pleco keepers, and peaceful community tanks with proper hiding spots Please Note: All fish shipments have a 100% Live Arrival Guarantee when shipping with our Overnight (1 Day) option. All other options void our Live Arrival Guarantee for fish. What We Feed Plecos L306 Blood Red Tiger Plecos are primarily herbivorous and xylophagous, so driftwood, vegetable-based foods, and algae-based sinking foods should make up most of their diet. Supplemental protein can be offered occasionally, but it should not be the main part of their diet. We feed our Plecos a mix of NorthFin Veggie and NorthFin Community foods. Their main foods are NorthFin Kelp Wafers and unsalted green beans. For L306 Blood Red Tiger Plecos, we also recommend keeping plenty of driftwood in the aquarium so they can naturally graze the way they are meant to. Recommended Parameters pH: 6.0-7.5 Temp: 78-84°F Tank Recommendations Wood: Driftwood is required for this species Hides: Caves, wood piles, and shaded areas Substrate: Sand or smooth gravel Plants: Hardy plants that can handle pleco activity Other: Stable, established tanks are best

Position pieces upright to recreate tree bases and exposed root systems, or turn and combine them to create networks that travel across the substrate. Mosses, Bucephalandra, Anubias, and other epiphytes can be worked between the smaller roots to soften the structure as the aquascape grows in. If you want deep, metallic color for your planted aquarium, consider trying Bucephalandra Shine Blue. Its oval-shaped leaves develop jewel-like blue and green tones with a speckled sheen that becomes especially noticeable under certain aquarium lighting. Compact and slow-growing, Bucephalandra Shine Blue is easy to work into both low-tech and advanced aquascaping styles. Attach it to crevices and grooves in driftwood or stone, where it can establish over time and grow into dense, eye-catching groups. Like Anubias, Bucephalandra is a hardy rhizome plant but offers a wider range of unique colors and foliage.

Not a typical Anubias! Anubias Barteri 'King' features broad leaves marbled with irregular patches of cream, yellow-green, and deep green. Its variegation gives this aquatic plant a unique appearance, with each leaf developing its own distinctive pattern. Unlike smaller Anubias varieties, it produces larger, more substantial foliage that makes an eye-catching addition to planted aquariums and paludariums. As new leaves emerge, their coloration and variegation may change, making each plant a little different from the next. As with all variegated plants, patterns, coloration, and markings may vary between individual specimens and are not guaranteed to remain consistent with new growth. Plants may arrive with different amounts of cream, yellow, and green foliage than pictured.

Rotala macrandra 'Green' offers a softer palette of soft green foliage that can develop rosy pink and orange tones. Its broad, slightly wavy leaves give this stem plant a fuller, more fluffy appearance compared to finer-leaved Rotala varieties. Among the many forms of Rotala Macrandra, green varieties are considered more forgiving than red, variegated, and miniature counterparts. That said, they still require stable environments with consistent CO2 injection, medium lighting, and regular fertilization. When grown in favorable conditions, this aquarium stem plant grows quickly and will more readily branch after trimming.

Looks familiar… Around here, it has another job. We've been using brushes like this in our aquariums for years. You've probably spotted one in our videos, so it probably doesn't need much of an introduction. This brush is one of our go-to tools for cleaning aquarium edges, corners, and those spots that need a little extra attention and a softer touch. Made with a natural bamboo handle and soft nylon bristles, it's ideal for gently brushing away buildup on aquarium glass and hardscape or combing out hair algae. Dimensions: Approx. 6.8 × 0.5 × 0.6 in Care Note: Rough stone surfaces can wear down the soft bristles quickly. Use a light touch to help extend the brush's life.

Add fresh, vibrant greenery to your planted aquarium with Isoetes Lacustris. This aquatic plant features long, slender, slightly fleshy leaves with a reed-like appearance that emerge from a compact, rosette-like base. Its bright green foliage grows in upright clusters, creating a soft, grassy texture that complements a variety of aquascaping styles. Unlike traditional aquarium hairgrass that spreads through runners, Isoetes Lacustris has a more concentrated, clump-like growth habit, making it easier to maintain defined groups of greenery throughout an aquascape. Its flowing foliage adds natural movement and height to the midground, offering an attractive alternative to conventional grass-like aquarium plants. Isoetes Lacustris benefits from moderate lighting, a nutrient-rich substrate, and stable aquarium conditions. Supplemental CO2 is not always necessary, although growth and overall success can vary between setups.

Add shimmering color and lively movement to your planted aquarium or pond with Galaxy Medaka Rice Fish (Oryzias latipes). Known for their silvery-white bodies, iridescent blue eyes, and subtle metallic sheen, these Japanese Rice Fish catch the light beautifully as they swim. Their active swimming behavior, reflective coloration, and unique top-down viewing appeal make them a fun addition to a variety of aquatic setups. Whether kept indoors or outdoors, Galaxy Medaka are rewarding to care for and easy to enjoy. Unlike many traditional aquarium fish, Medaka tolerate cooler temperatures and adapt well to planted aquariums, patio ponds, planted tubs, and indoor pond setups. Their peaceful nature, low bioload, and hardy disposition make them a great option for beginners while still being appreciated by experienced hobbyists and breeders. Medaka Highlights Beginner Friendly: Hardy and adaptable, Medaka are often recommended for newer hobbyists looking for an active and easy-care fish. Top-Down Viewing: One of the most enjoyable aspects of keeping Medaka is viewing them from above. Their reflective coloration and movement are ideal for shallow aquariums, ponds, and planted tubs. Peaceful Temperament: Medaka coexist well with other peaceful livestock and are an excellent choice for community aquariums and ponds. Medaka are social fish that should be kept in groups whenever possible. A group of six or more fish is recommended, with 10 gallons providing a practical starting point for a small group. They prefer gentle water movement and will appreciate floating plants, live aquatic plants, or additional cover, especially in outdoor setups. They may occasionally jump, so a lid or adequate plant cover is recommended. Stocking Recommendations As a practical guideline, a group of six Medaka can be kept in a well-maintained 10-gallon aquarium. Larger aquariums and ponds naturally provide more stability and swimming space. Avoid overcrowding as this can increase stress and make maintaining water quality more difficult. Feeding Medaka are omnivores and readily accept quality pellets, flakes, frozen, and live foods. Feed only what they can consume in a few minutes and remove excess. Avoid overfeeding to help maintain water quality. If kept in outdoor setups, they will happily munch on mosquito larvae too! Arrival & Acclimation For best results, introduce new fish into a mature, cycled aquarium or pond. Float the sealed bag to help match temperatures before gradually acclimating the fish to the new water conditions. Once in the aquarium, pond, or quarantine tank, give them time to settle in! Avoid significant changes or unnecessary handling during this time. Care & Compatibility Temperament: Peaceful Diet: Omnivore Group Size: 6 or more Important Information: If using tap water, always treat with a quality dechlorinator. Stable water conditions, regular maintenance, and appropriate stocking levels will help support long-term health and success. As with all live animals, natural variation in color, pattern, and size should be expected.

Add a ready-made arrangement of hardy greenery to your aquarium with an Anubias Nana Petite Bowl! Featuring live Anubias Nana Petite nestled in a terracotta-colored bowl, this piece of aquarium decor offers an easy way to incorporate live aquatic plants into your freshwater aquarium. Available in two sizes, these planted bowls can be placed directly into an aquarium as a standalone accent or incorporated among driftwood, rocks, and other aquatic plants. Nana Petite's adaptability and manageability adds a vibrant pop of green with little fuss. Size (⌀): Small: 2.5" Large: 3" Each Anubias Nana Petite Bowl includes the bowl and live plant that may vary in size. Anubias size, color, and growth will naturally vary between individual pieces and may continue to fill in after being added to your aquarium.

Add a lush Weeping Moss dome to your planted aquarium. Live Weeping Moss (Vesicularia ferriei) is attached to a rounded dome, creating a dense tuft of live aquatic moss that's ready to place into an aquarium immediately. Place it directly into the foreground or midground, tuck it between hardscape, or use it as a simple source of greenery in breeding and shrimp tanks. As the moss continues to grow, its naturally drooping fronds will extend beyond the dome, creating a soft, cascading appearance. Great for grazing, added coverage, or anyone who wants an easy way to add moss without wrapping or working with loose moss! Approximate Dome Size: 3⌀ x 2" Tall

Create a forest-floor-inspired look in your terrarium or paludarium with Heterogonium Pinnatum. Native to tropical Asia, this fern features deeply lobed fronds that add natural texture and soft greenery throughout a planted display. Its delicate yet sizeable foliage makes it a solid choice for filling gaps in tropical environments. Heterogonium Pinnatum grows from a creeping rhizome that gradually spreads across substrate and moist surfaces, producing new fronds along its length. Its spreading growth habit makes it an excellent choice for the midground of paludariums, terrariums, and vivariums, where it can be planted alongside mosses, driftwood, and other tropical foliage. This tropical fern prefers high humidity, consistent moisture, and moderate, indirect lighting. A well-draining substrate and gentle airflow help support healthy growth while preventing stagnant conditions. In paludariums, Heterogonium Pinnatum can be grown above the waterline or along consistently moist margins.

UNS Controsoil is our recommended aquasoil for beginners and one of the most versatile planted aquarium substrates available. Made from a blend of natural soil and volcanic ash, it features a low-nutrient composition and impurity-absorbing properties that give aquascapers greater control over when and how nutrients are introduced into the aquarium. The result is a cleaner, more predictable start that’s easier to manage, making Controsoil a popular choice for both first-time planted tank hobbyists and experienced aquascapers alike. Best For - Beginner planted aquariums - Shrimp tanks - Hobbyists who want more control over nutrient introduction - Low-tech and high-tech planted aquariums Why Choose Controsoil? Clean and Easy to Use: Controsoil arrives ready to use with no rinsing required and produces significantly less debris for clearer water. Beginner-Friendly Start: Its lower nutrient composition helps reduce ammonia spikes during the initial stages of an aquarium, creating a more predictable startup experience for new hobbyists. Maintains Granule Structure Longer: The granules are designed to hold their shape over time, making Controsoil less likely to break down into "mud". Buffers Aquarium Water: Brings the water column to a slightly acidic pH that is commonly preferred by tropical fish, shrimp, and live aquatic plants. Two Colors and Three Granule Sizes: Choose between black or brown substrate colors and three granule sizes to accommodate everything from carpeting plants to large root-feeding species. Excellent for Dry Start Method (DSM): Its stability, cleanliness, and structure retention make it a popular choice for dry start methods and planted aquarium layouts that require extended establishment periods. Choosing a Granule Size Extra Fine: Tiny spheres look best in nano tanks. Their size helps miniature aquatic plants like Hemianthus Callitrichoides (HC) grow healthy, established roots. Fine: A solid all-purpose aquarium plant soil. It works for a variety of aquascaping purposes. Normal: Larger granules can help build slope and achieve desired substrate height. Perfect for large root plants like Echinodorus. For nutrient-demanding aquatic plants, try adding UNS Controbase first and layering UNS Controsoil on top! How Much Controsoil Do I Need? As a general guideline: - One 3L bag is suitable for most aquariums up to 5 gallons - One 10L bag is suitable for most aquariums up to 20 gallons For aquascapes with significant slopes, elevated hardscape, or thicker substrate layers, additional substrate may be required. Quick Substrate Calculator (Tank Length × Tank Depth × Desired Substrate Height in Inches) ÷ 60 = Liters of Controsoil Needed

Bacopa Caroliniana or Bacopa Red for short, is a lovely aquarium stem plant characterized by delicate, flower-like clusters of light green leaves. When grown in high tech planted aquariums, it may develop pink and red colors! A staple in the hobby, it adds a whimsical effect to aquascapes and is great for midground planting. Alternatively, this aquatic plant can be grown as a paludarium or terrarium plant above water and may bloom tiny purple and blue flowers. Bacopa Red is a great starter plant because it does not require CO2 injection and will grow with a nutrient-rich environment alongside clean water. We recommend moderate light as low lighting may result in slow or leggy growth. Common Name Bacopa Red Care Easy Lighting Medium CO2 Optional Suggested Placement Midground Propagation Trim stems and plant Growth Rate Slow Height 4-12"

Microsorum pteropus 'Windelov', more commonly known as simply Java Fern Windelov, is a popular variation for planted aquariums and aquascaping. This aquatic fern is often picked by beginner aquarists thanks to its easy care and bold green color. This family of plants are very versatile, provide great coverage, fill empty space in layouts well, and can handle considerable amounts of neglect. Its versatility makes it suitable for aquariums, terrariums, vivariums, and paludariums. Windelov is easily recognized for its split ends and bushy appearance. Recently reclassified as Leptochilus pteropus , this plant is still widely known in the aquarium hobby as Microsorum pteropus. Java Fern plants are epiphytic and will grow happily when attached to aquarium driftwood, aquascaping stones, or any aquarium decor. We recommend providing it with clean water, low to medium lighting, and good flow for starters. A quality aquatic plant fertilizer paired with CO2 injection will be beneficial in the long run and can help promote quicker, bushier growth. Propagation is easy and straightforward; simply cut or pull apart rhizomes to be replanted/reattached.

Microsorum Pteropus, commonly known as Java Fern, is a classic aquarium plant in the planted tank hobby. A fantastic choice for beginner aquarists, Java Fern has earned a reputation for being nearly bulletproof as it almost requires some effort to kill and will tolerate a wide range of aquarium conditions. Microsorum Pteropus is an epiphytic plant making it versatile with placement. This aquarium plant will happily grow attached to aquarium driftwood or when placed in the crevices of an aquascape layout. Its bright green, broad foliage is a great way to fill in areas lacking coverage. Like most aquarium plant species, Java Fern can be grown in low tech conditions, but the addition of CO2 injection will produce a noticeable difference in growth rate and appearance. Recently reclassified as Leptochilus pteropus , this plant is still widely known in the hobby as Microsorum pteropus. Microsorum Pteropus can be attached directly to driftwood, rocks, or any aquarium decoration using thread or glue. Make sure to keep the rhizomes above your substrate or the plant can begin to rot. Propagation is easy and straightforward; simply cut or pull apart rhizomes to be replanted/reattached.

Bolbitis Difformis ‘Mini' is a small-leafed aquarium fern. This variation is slow growing, but its foliage is delicate and naturally bushy, making it a solid pick if you're looking for a plant to fill in your aquascape's empty spaces. Mini Bolbitis is also an epiphyte and can be attached to driftwood or gently wedged into gaps between the hardscape. New growth is an interesting view as it sprouts in the form of fiddle leaf heads from its rhizome. While Mini Bolbitis can be grown in an aquarium, it takes a very long time to adapt and grow well. We find it's much happier in marginal conditions where its roots remain close to the water source, but its leaves remains above surface. Similar to terrestrial ferns, Baby Leaf Bolbitis will appreciate good humidity and filtered light. If you have a paludarium or emersed section in your aquascape, try this aquatic fern out. It will provide beautiful texture and color to your planted setup in exchange for low effort. A total of 2 Mini Bolbitis pots were used in our 3 gallon planted tank below:

Ludwigia Arcuata AKA Needle leaf Ludwigia is a beautiful aquarium stem plant with delicate green and red leaves. It is easy to grow and adds movement and dimension to a planted tank. Its leaves are thin and pointed, hence its name, and grow along the entire length of the stem. Coloration is dependent upon water properties and can be improved with CO2 injection, moderate lighting and a liquid plant fertilizer. Like other stem plants, it can grow very fast when conditions are optimal. Grab a pair of quality aquascaping scissors for regular trimming! We recommend this one for nature style aquascapes, Dutch style aquariums and more. If you're interested in a different growing form, try planting it in a terrarium-like setup! Propagation is easy. Simply cut the stems and replant into quality aquasoil Common Name Needle Leaf Ludwigia Care Easy Lighting Medium to High CO2 Optional Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate Height 10-20"

Ludwigia glandulosa, also known as Diamond Ludwigia, is a less common species that offers intense, vibrant color — perfect for aquarists who want magenta, purple, red, or pink aquarium stem plants. Its coloration is unique, with green tops and richly colored undersides. The oval, pointed leaves grow in opposite pairs along the stem which may also vary in color depending on the tank's condition. This aquatic stem plant is especially attractive when planted in generous groups, adding bold color and texture to any planted tank. We recommend it for hobbyists who appreciate large, colorful plants — ideal for Dutch-style tanks or spacious nature-style aquascapes. To achieve its most vivid colors, provide high lighting, CO2, and a balanced source of micro and macronutrients. Propagation is simple: cut healthy stems from the main plant and replant them in quality aquasoil. Common Name Ludwigia Diamond Care Moderate Lighting High CO2 Optional Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate Height 6-8+"

Ludwigia Natans, commonly referred to as Ludwigia Super Red is a staple in the aquascaping hobby for any aquarist who enjoys red aquatic plants. Generally easy going, Ludwigia Super Red is a good first red plant for beginners who are interested in growing red aquatic plants in their tanks. Ludwigia Super Red is a prolific grower and is characterized by small rounded leaves with pointed tips that grow in an offset pattern along the main stem. Coloration can vary and is dependent upon tank conditions. Coloration will vary from green to dull oranges to deep red tones. Because this plant can be a little more sparse, it is common to bunch them in groups of 10 or more for aesthetic appeal. Regular pruning and replanting will aid in producing dense bushes. Common Name Ludwigia Super Red Care Easy Lighting Medium CO2 Optional Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Fast Height 6-20+"

Micranthemum Umbrosum is a bright green, low-growing stem plant perfect for beginners. It is a versatile species and can be used for nearly any placement within a planted tank. Constant pruning will keep it low growing while leaving it untrimmed will result in vertical growth. As it grows quickly, it is quick to get unruly if consistent trims are not performed. Overall, the shape and growth of the plant is dependent upon tank conditions so please be sure to plan accordingly if you have a specific look in mind. Moderate light and CO2 injection are favorable, but it is a forgiving plant and will be fine as long as high-quality substrate is used. Propogate by trimming the ends of stems, grouping them together and planting. Be sure that they are not covered by other plants. Common Name Giant Baby Tears Care Easy Lighting Medium CO2 Optional Suggested Placement Midground Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate Height 2-6" Our bunched stem plants are all kept and grown in high-quality substrate by Marfied Controsoil . Vesicularia Montagnei, more commonly known as Christmas Moss or X-mas Moss is arguably one of the most popular aquatic mosses commonly used in the planted aquarium hobby. Originating from Asia, Christmas Moss is closely related to Java Moss, another extremely popular aquatic moss, and is comparable in appearance with only slight differences in its fronds. Like other aquarium mosses, Christmas Moss is extremely hardy and versatile with usage. Aquarium moss provides excellent shade and coverage for shrimplets and skittish fish who commonly search for refuge. Alternatively, it can be used to mimic foliage on Bonsai-style driftwood or attached sparingly to other types of driftwood for an aged look in the planted tank. Aquarium moss may also be grown in emersed conditions or found wrapped as the base on Wabi Kusa setups! Aquarium Moss is a fantastic choice for beginner aquarists and will tolerate a wide range of aquarium conditions and water parameters. Once established, Christmas Moss is a prolific grower and may require regular pruning to ensure it does not take over the aquarium. Manual removal is best, but if trimming is required, we recommend turning off filters and pumps to prevent the moss spreading to unwanted areas. Average size per small portion is a golfball while large portion is tennis ball. he stainless steel mesh measures roughly 3" x 3" and comes pre-attached with moss, ready to use for creating a moss carpet.

Java Moss (Vesicularia Dubyana) Java Moss is one of the best aquarium plants or aquatic mosses for beginners and those who are looking for an easy aquatic plant for a low-tech planted aquarium. Well-regarded for its unmatched resilience, Java Moss will grow in nearly any freshwater aquarium. Its deep green color and fine fronds soften aquascapes, creating a lush, natural forest-like appearance in planted aquariums. Its adaptability makes it a top aquarium moss for low-tech aquariums, where it can grow without CO2 injection or intense lighting. Alternatively, Java Moss is great for shrimp tanks, breeding setups and more as its growing style provides the perfect habitat for coverage and security. Java Moss is also commonly used to cover small stones for aquascaping accents in planted aquariums. Aquarium mosses also make great makeshift foliage for bonsai driftwood to produce underwater tree aquascapes and more. The addition of CO2 injection and higher lighting will encourage faster and more robust growth. Once established, Java Moss may need routine maintenance to prevent it from overtaking the aquarium. We recommend pulling or removing manually. If using aquascaping tools, try turning off the filter as aquarium moss will grow anywhere it lands! Average size per small portion is a golfball while large portion is tennis ball. he stainless steel mesh measures roughly 3" x 3" and comes pre-attached with moss, ready to use for creating a moss carpet.

Loved for its mini size, it can be difficult to find an easy care red aquarium stem plant that retains its color and also fits in nano planted aquariums. When happy, its colors get bolder and the undersides of its leaves deepen, providing in vibrant contrast. Alternanthera plants are great for many popular aquascape styles including nature-style or Dutch aquariums that feature manicured groups of aquatic stem plants. AR Mini is resilient and often gets categorized with true low tech plants. It can adapt, but lack of nutrients and light can be detected by leggy growth and dulled color. If you’re able, plant this one in a planted tank with CO2 injection, moderate to high light and good flow. Dosing with a liquid aquatic plant fertilizer or using a nutritious aquasoil will speed up growth and really bring those vivid colors Alternanthera plants are known for. Propagation is easy and can be done by trimming anywhere along the stem and replanting into the soil. Common Name AR Mini Care Easy to Moderate Lighting Medium to High CO2 Required Suggested Placement Midground Propagation Trim stems and plant Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 4-12"+

Cryptocoryne beckettii is a long-standing favorite aquarium plant in the hobby. Its slightly wavy leaves range from deep green to brown depending on tank conditions. It has a more upright growth pattern but doesn’t get overly large, making it a great midground aquatic plant for planted aquariums. Its varying color pairs well with finer plants like mosses or ferns, where its broader leaves help break up texture. Like other Cryptocoryne species, it can be susceptible to crypt melt during the initial stages, but with stable conditions will generally recover without issue. It’s well suited for low light setups as long as parameters remain consistent without major swings. Plant it in nutrient-rich aquarium soil or supplement with root tabs. CO2 injection isn’t required, but will improve overall growth and density. A solid, easy-going aquarium plant that fits into a wide range of aquascapes, especially if you’re going for a more natural, biotope-style or slightly darker look.

Grow a unique Cryptocoryne in your planted aquarium with Crispatula Tonkinensis. This aquatic plant features long, thin leaves and easy care that is ideal for low light aquascapes. Its care is similar to other varieties and is generally low-maintenance once established. Cryptocoryne feed via root system, making a nutrient-dense aquasoil or root tab supplementation beneficial for long-term health. CO2 injection isn't required, but we recommend it whenever possible. Once mature, Cryptocoryne produce plantlets that can be gently divided and replanted into the soil.

Cryptocoryne wendtii 'Brown' is a classic aquarium plant valued for its warm, earthy tones and hardy nature. Its leaves can develop colors ranging from olive-green to bronze and reddish-brown depending on tank conditions. Its care remains similar to other Crypt species while offering a way to introduce color and contrast without the demands of more sensitive plant species. As it matures, it forms a compact rosette that will eventually produce plantlets that can be left to spread naturally or divided and replanted as needed. A true midground plant, Wendtii Brown creates natural texture and transitions to other zones of a planted aquarium. It will grow in a range of conditions and while it doesn't require intense lighting or CO2 injection, supplying it can speed up growth and support long-term health. Like many Cryptocoryne, it is susceptible to Crypt melt and an intial adjustment period after planting. With stable conditions, it typically recovers and once established, is very adaptable.

Crypt. Walkeri is a reliable choice for a variety of planted aquarium setups. Often recommended for beginners, this aquatic plant is undemanding and doesn't have strict care requirements. Like other Cryptocoryne, we recommend ensuring the aquarium is fully cycled. Low to medium lighting is sufficient and regular fertilization is beneficial. When mature, Cryptocoryne Walkeri will produce little plantlets that be gently divided and replanted into the substrate.

Add intricate pattern and dimension to your planted aquarium with Cryptocoryne Nurii. This popular Crypt develops narrow leaves with a gradient of olive green to bronze-red tones, sometimes accented with distinctive markings that add another layer of visual texture. Known for its slow growth, Cryptocoryne Nurii is a plant for the patient aquascaper. Its compact growth and patterned foliage make it especially rewarding when grown in a visible area where it can be appreciated up close. Plant it at the base of an aquascape or use it as a unique transition to other zones of a planted aquarium. Cryptocoryne Nurii can adapt to both low-tech and more advanced planted aquarium setups with low to medium lighting. CO2 injection isn't required but can support stronger growth. Like other Cryptocoryne, give this one time to establish a solid root system before moving or propagating it.

Alternanthera Rosaefolia is a variation of the commonly used Alternanthera Reineckii. Like most Alternanthera species used in the planted tank hobby, AR Rosaefolia is no stranger to bold color and can be commonly seen in Dutch aquascapes due to its bright color palette. This aquarium stem plant is easily recognized by a unique white venation found on its leaves. Just like other aquarium stems, AR Rosaefolia does best in a planted tank with quality lighting and CO2 injection. When provided with optimal conditions, this plant will easily breach the surface with the potential to bloom small flowers above water. Propagation can be done by snipping anywhere along the stem and replanting into the substrate.

Cardamine Lyrata is a marsh plant that originates from Asia. It grows in a clover-like pattern similar to Hydrocotyle. If planted in an aquarium that has high lighting and CO2, this aquarium plant has the tendency to grow in dense bushes that are great to feature in any aquascape layout. It can also be grown floating and provides extra coverage for fry, shrimp or skittish fish. Propagate by trimming stems and replanting into nutrient-dense aquasoil. If left to grow without maintenance, you may need to separate it by pulling apart dense clumps and splitting the roots! Common Name Japanese Cress, Chinese Ivy Care Easy to Moderate Lighting Medium CO2 Required Suggested Placement Midground Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 5-10"

Pogostemon Helferi was discovered in Thailand, close to the border of Burma. Its name 'Downoi' means little star in Thailand due to its leaf shape and overall look. Unusual and distinctive, this aquatic plant is compact with curly leaves and has vivid green coloration. If kept under proper conditions with good lighting and quality substrate, Downoi forms side shoots with small roots that have the capability to turn into a lush foreground carpet. Common Name Downoi Care Moderate Lighting Medium to High CO2 Required Suggested Placement Midground Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate Height 3-10"

Eleocharis Parvula Mini, more commonly known as Dwarf Hair Grass or Hair Grass Mini is a staple foreground plant that resembles a lawn of grass in a backyard. This aquarium plant is the epitome of underwater lawns and its thin stalks grow vertically from roots that spread by sending runners horizontally. High lighting and CO2 injection are not necessarily required to grow Dwarf Hair Grass but are highly recommended as it produces a highly noticeable difference in growth rate and overall lush factor. To plant, gently separate the plant into small portions and plant each portion an inch or so apart halfway into the substrate. Once established, regular trimming will be required as once it sends runners out, the plant grows quickly.

Cryptocoryne Petchii, also known as Cryptocoryne Becketii Petchii, is a moderately sized variety of Cryptocoryne Beckettii that originates from Sri Lanka. This aquatic plant features varying color that includes olive-brown tones and slightly fluted leaves that can develop deep purple undersides. Final size, color and overall form weigh heavily on the environment in which the plant is kept. It is hardy in nature and is suitable for low tech planted aquariums or in shaded areas of high-tech setups once mature. To help it establish healthy roots, choose a nutrient-dense substrate or provide root tabs. While it isn't required, the addition of CO2 will support better growth and form.

Cryptocoryne Lucens is a unique aquatic plant that is typically seen in the midground area of a planted aquarium. This particular species grows slender leaves that retain a rich light green hue throughout. Its leaf shape is softly rounded at the tips and larger groups are great for creating tufts or thick grassy bushes where additional texture is desired. Like other Cryptocoryne, C. Lucens is hardy when established. It can take some time to establish during the initial planting period, but once it sends down roots, it is adaptable to a range of water conditions. As heavy root feeders, use a nutrient-dense aquarium soil or supplement with root tabs. Keep water parameters stable and your plant will slowly spread in no time. Once ready, plantlets can be gently divded and replanted as desired.

Cryptocoryne willisii is a less common Crypt with narrower, grass-like green leaves and a more compact growth habit compared to most other species. It has a clean, simple look that works well if you’re trying to create a more natural, low-profile aquascape. Like many Crypts, it can take a little time to get going after planting. Not much may happen at first, but once it settles in, it starts to spread and will produce plantlets that can be divided and replanted as desired. Size wise, it is generally a little smaller, making it a good plant for midground areas in nano planted aquariums. Overall, this one is a nice choice if you're looking for something smaller and unique but still easy to care for. Once established, it is suitable for low light setups and high-tech aquariums as well.

Cryptocoryne wendtii ‘Tropica’ is a darker, more textured variation of the classic wendtii, known for its longer, crinkled leaves and deeper green to bronze coloration. It has a slightly more pronounced look compared to standard wendtii types, making it a nice option if you want more texture and color variation without increasing care requirements. As a rosette, it slowly grows outwards, creating soft, textured patches along the base of hardscape layouts that transition well into other zones of a planted aquarium. Like other Cryptocoryne, it's slow to moderate growing and easy to care for once it settles in. Lower light is sufficient and CO2 isn't required, but can be beneficial for overall health, color and form. A solid, low-maintenance plant that offers texture and varying coloration.

Hydrocotyle Sibthorpioides is a fantastic midground aquatic plant choice! Remove this plant from its growing medium before planting. Click here to shop all aquarium plants! Hydrocotyle Sibthorpioides is characterized by its clover-like leaves similar to Hydrocotyle Japan except its leaves are rounder and much smaller. Just as versatile, it can be used in the foreground, midground or background placement. Care requirements are minimal but should be trimmed frequently to avoid unruly overgrowth. Propagate by trimming stems and replanting or pulling apart dense clumps and splitting the roots. New shoots can be trimmed anywhere along the stem thus allowing the plant to grow thicker and more compact. Common Name Lawn Marsh Pennywort Care Easy to Moderate Lighting Medium CO2 Required Suggested Placement Midground Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 5-10"

Lilaeopsis Novaezelandiae AKA Micro Sword is a great choice for beginners who are trying to grow a carpeting plant for the first time. Its appearance is similar to dense wild grass and can create a stunning underwater lawn. This plant grows by spreading runners horizontally throughout the substrate. Lighting and CO2 injection are essential in keeping the growth short and compact. Propagation is simple, trim portions from of horizontal shoots and replant. Common Name Micro Sword Care Easy to Moderate Lighting Medium to High CO2 Required Suggested Placement Foreground Propagation Trim and plant runners Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 1-3” Ultum Nature Systems tissue culture plants are grown in-vitro by laboratories who specialize in propagating aquatic plants. There is a huge selection of plant species that have been propagated this way. This is truly the best option for those who want absolutely zero unwanted pests, algae and pesticides. This makes them perfect for shrimp keepers and any planted tank enthusiasts alike. NOTE: It is important to remove the tissue culture agar gel before planting. Simply wash the gel away, divide, and plant.

Anubias Barteri is a top selling easy aquatic plant for planted aquariums, terrariums and more. Like others in the family, this plant will grow in a wide range of conditions, making it a top recommendation for anyone new to aquascaping. It is a moderately sized plant and its broad, rich green leaves are great for filling open space in aquariums, terrariums or paludariums. Due to its size, we recommend it as a nice midground and background plant in larger setups since its leaves are capable of growing more than 3" long. Anubias are flowering plants that grow best when the rhizome is attached to a porous surface such as driftwood or stone. It benefits from consistent fertilization but light requirements are minimal as its leaves are susceptible to algae growth when placed under high lighting. CO2 is optional, but can promote faster growth and robust leaves when used. If you are a houseplant hobbyist and like tropical aroids like Philodendron or Monstera, try out Anubias!

Grow a dense, low-profile aquarium carpet in your planted tank with Glossostigma elatinoides. Better known as Glosso, this carpeting plant develops bright green, tear-drop shaped leaves and stays very compact under certain conditions, making it ideal for Iwagumi aquascapes and other layouts where a clean, open foreground is part of the goal. Glosso grows best with strong lighting, CO2 injection, and consistent fertilization. When light is insufficient, it's growth will become noticeably leggy as it tries to reach upward rather than spreading horizontally along the substrate. It can be grown in lower-tech setups, but slower growth and a less compact carpet may be expected. Once established, Glosso grows at a moderate pace and periodic trimming will be needed to maintain a tidy look. Below is an Ultum Nature Systems 5N 4.6 gallon nano tank featuring Glossostigma Elatinoides in the foreground:

Micranthemum ‘Monte Carlo’ has become one of the most popular carpeting plants in the planted aquarium hobby. Its compact growth, bright green color, and forgiving nature make it ideal for lush foreground coverage in planted aquariums. Compared to Hemianthus callitrichoides (HC Cuba), Monte Carlo is generally easier to grow while still producing thick, beautiful carpets when given the right conditions. Recent botanical classification identifies Monte Carlo as Micranthemum tweediei, but it remains widely known in the aquarium hobby simply as “Monte Carlo”. Its small, rounded leaves work for a range of aquascaping styles, from minimalist Iwagumi layouts to nature aquariums. Beyond being grown as a carpet plant, Monte Carlo can also be planted between hardscape to soften transitions, create natural overhangs, or creep gently over driftwood. It’s available in several different forms, including potted plants, tissue culture, and more. Many are grown emersed, so some transition is normal as they adapt to submerged growth. Before planting, we recommend separating the plant into small portions to encourage quicker rooting and more even growth across the foreground. While Monte Carlo can be grown in lower lighting, moderate to strong lighting, nutrient-rich substrate, and CO₂ injection will produce a noticeably denser carpet and quicker spread. Once established, it spreads moderately and bounces back well from regular trimming, making it easy to maintain a healthy, thick aquarium carpet. Below is a mature Iwagumi aquascape featuring a healthy Monte Carlo carpet. This video demonstrates the dense, healthy growth Monte Carlo is known for while showing how easily trapped detritus can be removed during routine aquarium maintenance!

Bucephalandra Green Wavy, commonly referred to as simply Buce Green Wavy, is a classic species of Bucephalandra commonly seen in the planted aquarium hobby. This variation of Buce is relatively easier to obtain since it is typically farmed instead of collected from the wild now. Buce Green Wavy is an eye-catching specimen, offering rich green leaves with a ruffled shape and smooth texture. Like most Bucephalandra plants, Green Wavy is epiphytic and will grow happily attached to aquarium driftwood or stones in an aquascape layout. Low to medium lighting with partial shade is perfect for most Buce species and while this plant will tolerate other conditions associated with keeping a low-tech aquarium, we highly recommend providing Buce with CO2 injection and a quality source of nutrients to boost growth, help the plant outcompete algae and produce the iridescent hues Bucephalandra are known for. Overall, Bucephalandra Green Wavy is a suitable plant for most beginner aquarists that have the basics of aquarium keeping down. Buce's stem and rhizome should not be covered or glued when planting as this can cause damage to the plant.

Staurogyne Repens is a low-growing aquatic plant that originates from South America. Typically shortened to S. Repens, Staurogyne Repens is a popular midground aquatic plant choice in planted tanks for its naturally bushy, compact growth pattern and bright green color. This aquarium plant has a smaller leaf size making it a suitable choice for nano-sized aquariums. These factors make Staurogyne Repens an all around popular plant for aquascaping. Staurogyne Repens grows respective to the environment it is planted in so it is best to be mindful of conditions such as lighting, nutrients and CO2 injection. Depending on the aquarium, Staurogyne Repens has also been used as a foreground aquarium plant. However, this application will require more frequent pruning to maintain the desired look! We recommend medium to high lighting to keep this plant low-growing and bushy. CO2 injection is also favorable to promote quicker, more robust growth. Propagation is simple and can be done by trimming along the stems and replanting into a quality, nutrient-dense aquarium soil.

Hemianthus Callitrichoides, sometimes referred to as dwarf baby tears, HC Cuba or simply HC, is the smallest carpeting plant in the planted tank hobby. Offering some of the tiniest leaves in the hobby, HC is both capable and responsible for creating lush foregrounds seen in many famous aquascapes utilizing Iwagumi style layouts. This plant requires much patience as its root system is miniature and takes a considerable amount of time to anchor into the substrate. The dry start method is sometimes recommended to combat this as it will allow the plant to root, reducing the hassle that comes with floating plants in a freshly filled aquarium. If successful, patience and care will reward generously. Although some have had success growing HC in smaller tanks using liquid carbon, this species requires CO2 injection to truly thrive. It can be quite difficult to grow lush without it. For long term thick carpets, CO2 and consistent fertilization is recommended to maintain a nice foreground. Below is an Ultum Nature Systems 45U 9 gallon tank featuring Hemianthus Callitrichoides in the foreground:

Hydrocotyle Tripartita is a popular midground aquarium plant! Remove this plant from its growing medium before planting. Click here to shop all aquarium plants! Hydrocotyle Tripartita, sometimes referred to as Hydrocotyle Tripartita Japan, is a commonly used aquarium plant species in the planted tank hobby. Made popular by the creator of aquascaping, Takashi Amano, Hydrocotyle Tripartita Japan is easily recognized by its clover-shaped foliage that has the potential to produce dense bushes or delicate vines throughout a planted aquarium tank. This aquarium plant's bright green hue and unique leaf shape makes it a great ornamental species that is commonly used in the midground or background area of the aquarium. Hydrocotyle Tripartita is typically undemanding, but sufficient lighting should be provided or growth tends to be leggy and sparse as the plant stretches towards the light source. We recommend medium to high lighting, CO2 injection and a basic aquarium plant fertilizer to start. From there, tweaks may be made depending on the overall tank and goals. When well-established, Hydrocotyle Tripartita is a quick grower and will outpace many aquatic plant species making regular maintenance a must. Propagation is easy and can be done by snipping the plant anywhere along the stem and replanting it into quality, nutrient-dense aquarium soil. Common Name Hydrocotyle Japan Hydrocotyle Tripartita Japan Care Easy to Moderate Lighting Medium CO2 Required Suggested Placement Midground Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 5-10+"

Cryptocoryne wendtii 'Green' is a classic and widely used aquatic plant known for its deep green leaves and adaptable nature. A popular choice for beginer and experienced aquascapers, it offers a natural look and easy introduction to live plants. As it grows, it forms a compact rosette that spreads outwards. Its leaves gently arch as it matures, creating a soft layered effect that works well in midground areas or as a natural transition between foreground and background plants. Cryptocoryne wendtii 'Green' is suitable for a range of aquarium conditions and adapts well to low tech settings as well. Stable conditions seem to be the most important factor to ensure fuller, healthier growth. Like many Cryptocoryne species, it slowly forms plantlets that can be left to spread naturally or gently divided and replanted as desired.

Cryptocoryne Wendtii Brown 'Indo' is a hardy Crypt featuring silky foliage in varying shades of brown. This Indonesian variant resembles traditional Cryptocoryne Wendtii Brown but develops darker, richer tones with natural color variation depending on its growing environment. Relatively undemanding once established, Cryptocoryne Wendtii Brown 'Indo' is a great choice for beginners or anyone looking to add deeper, earthy color to a planted aquarium. It can be grown submerged or emersed and develops at a moderate pace under suitable conditions. Once established, new plantlets can gradually develop around the mother plant. Allow them to mature before separating and replanting for propagation.

Cryptocoryne wendtii 'Mi Oya' is a less common variety of Cryptocoryne wendtii native to specific parts of Sri Lanka. Its slender, slightly ruffled leaves develop a varying color palette that includes shades of green, copper, and reddish-brown. Like other Cryptocoryne, it works well throughout the midground of a planted aquarium, where its size and texture can help transition the foreground into taller background growth. Cryptocoryne wendtii 'Mi Oya' is relatively undemanding but needs time to establish a healthy root system after planting. Once settled, it becomes surprisingly easy to manage and cultivate, making it an approachable choice for beginner aquascapes.

We love Crypt Parva! Cryptocoryne Parva is considered one of the smallest variations within the Cryptocoryne family. This small aquarium plant offers bright green color and a low-growing profile that makes it best for accents in the foreground of a planted aquarium or as a carpeting aquarium plant. It is also a top pick for nano planted tank or small aquariums. It is a notoriously slow grower, making patience a requirement for heavy coverage. However, it is one of the few species that doesn't transform into an entirely different plant, making it great for aquascapers who value uniformity. Once planted, it benefits from being left alone, as frequent repositioning or uprooting can slow its development. This little Crypt doesn't require CO2, but we recommend it whenever possible.

Originating from Australia, Ranunculus Inundatus is a low growing aquatic plant that creeps horizontally by sending runners. Individual stems can be trimmed along the horizontal shoots and replanted directly into the substrate. High lighting and CO2 injection are necessary to keep this plant growing low. Nutrient deficiency results in yellowing leaves and vertical growing thin stalks are an indication of lack of lighting. While thin leaves may hint that there is a lack of CO2. When kept in proper conditions, this plant grows quickly and will require regular trimming.
