This makes them perfect for shrimp keepers and any planted tank enthusiasts alike. NOTE: It is important to remove the tissue culture agar gel before planting. Simply wash the gel away, divide, and plant.

If you're looking for a more approachable way to bring red tones to your planted aquarium, consider trying Alternanthera Reineckii. Commonly shortened to AR, this aquarium stem plant is comparatively forgiving, making it a longtime favorite for hobbyists experimenting with colorful aquatic plants. Its broad, saturated leaves fill open space easily, giving Alternanthera a heavier visual presence when compared to fine-leafed stem plants. As the plant matures, trimming encourages the development of offshoots that create a more layered, bushy appearance while adding color and coverage for small aquarium livestock. Easygoing by red plant standards, Alternanthera Reineckii is a great choice for beginners looking to introduce stronger color into their aquascape.

Proserpinaca Palustris, commonly referred to as Mermaid Weed, is a unique aquatic stem plant with saw-toothed edged leaves. It provides fantastic texture and vibrant green color in planted aquariums and is also ideal as a pond plant. Its flowing behavior is best for the background zone in planted aquariums and it fills space excpetionally well. Propagation is simple like other stem plants: just cut the stem and replant the trimmings. Common Name Mermaid Weed Care Easy to Intermediate Lighting Medium to High CO2 Required Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim & Replant Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 4-12"+

Bucephalandra Red Mini, shortened to Buce Red Mini, is a variation of Bucephalandra that is typically now farmed and more readily available in the planted aquarium trade. This small-leafed Bucephalandra has a varying color palette that includes red, bronze, green and purple tones with its final coloration determined by various factors. In the wild, Bucephalandra is a marginal plant and can be found along streams in both submerged and emerged conditions. Growth methods will produce noticeable differences in appearance and iridescent color tones are typically produced in what most would consider a high-tech planted tank setup. This includes quality LED lighting, CO2 injection, ample circulation and a quality source of nutrients. Bucephalandra Red Mini, like most Buce, is a slow-grower and will take time to produce impressive results. Slower growth makes Bucephalandra a more coveted genus. Buce Red Mini, amongst others, is a welcome species in the Buce enthusiast's collection. All Bucephalandra are epiphytic and will grow happily attached to aquarium driftwood or in between hardscape crevices.

Few aquarium plants are as flexible as Micranthemum Micranthemoides, aka Pearl Weed. This longtime hobby favorite develops tiny, bright green leaves along fine stems that can be trimmed in any shape you can think of. Keep it pruned low for a dense foreground or creeping mass, shape it into rounded midground bushes, or let the stems gain height to create a soft green background. Its size and flexibility make Pearl Weed especially ideal for nano aquariums. Under stronger lighting, growth becomes more compact with shorter spacing between leaves and increased branching. In open areas, stems may even begin creeping horizontally along the substrate. Lower lighting tends to produce longer, leggier growth instead. Pearl Weed is also quite forgiving. It grows without CO2 injection, tolerates a wide range of aquarium conditions, and can access nutrients through the substrate and water column. Once established, don't let its tiny leaves fool you—this plant grows rapidly. Regular trimming encourages more branching and is the key to developing the dense, manicured bushes Pearl Weed is known for. Why So Many Names? Pearl Weed has traveled through the aquarium hobby under several scientific names, including Micranthemum micranthemoides and Hemianthus micranthemoides. More recent botanical identification recognizes Hemianthus glomeratus, although the older names remain widely used on plant labels and throughout the aquarium trade. Pearl Weed should not be confused with Monte Carlo (Micranthemum tweediei), another small-leaved aquarium plant with a distinctly different growth habit.

Anubias Nana Petite is arguably the most popular variation of Anubias used in the planted aquarium hobby. Easily recognized for its smaller foliage and rich green tones, Anubias Nana Petite is commonly used in planted aquariums of all styles. This variation of Anubias retains a bulletproof reputation in being an aquarium plant where effort is required to kill it. This quality makes it a fantastic choice for beginner aquarists who are building confidence with keeping live aquatic plants in the aquarium. At the same time, the overall appearance is equally loved by seasoned experts who have been keeping planted tanks for some time. Anubias Nana Petite requires seldom maintenance and is very easy to care for. This aquarium plant is typically available in plentiful portions making it a great filler where coverage is needed. Like most Anubias, Anubias Nana Petite will tolerate a wide range of aquarium conditions and also has the ability to thrive in both aquarium and terrarium-like enclosures. Anubias Nana Petite will sometimes produce blooms and is an epiphytic grower, meaning it can be easily attached to aquarium driftwood and stones. Low to medium light is sufficient, but the addition of CO2 injection and a nutrient source will produce a noticeable difference in growth and overall health. Propagation may be done by gently separating plants from the rhizome and reattaching or replanting.

Anubias Nana Golden is the golden variant of Anubias Nana. Similar to other Anubias, it's a great choice for beginners due to its easy care and overall hardiness. It also has the ability to thrive in both aquariums and terrariums set ups. It's a flowering plant that grows best when the rhizome is attached to hardscape material such as wood or stone. Regular fertilization is favorable and low to medium lighting is sufficient as high lighting will promote the growth of algae on its leaves. CO2 is not required but promotes faster growth and robust leaves. Propagation is straightforward; simply cut or pull apart rhizomes to be reattached.

Rotala Rotundifolia is arguably one of the better-known aquarium stem plants. Originating from Southeast Asia, there are now many variations of Rotala Rotundifolia readily available in the planted tank hobby. Rotala Rotundifolia Red is a popular one with color tones varying from pink to orange, yellow and deep reds with final coloration determined by the overall aquarium's condition and parameters. Like most Rotala species, this aquarium stem plant is a prolific grower and will require routine maintenance to keep up with growth. If frequent maintenance is not a concern, we recommend Rotala to aquarists who are looking for relatively easy aquarium plants that grow quickly and will easily fill available space in a planted tank. We recommend growing this plant in a nutritious substrate with medium lighting, CO2 injection and a quality aquatic plant fertilizer. Don't forget to have a good pair of premium aquascaping scissors at the ready for your aquarium stem plants! Rotala wallichii is a favorite among aquascapers who want to add soft movement, and color to planted aquariums. Its fine, feathery foliage contrasts beautifully against broader-leaf stem plants and hardscape, making it especially useful for adding variable texture and breaking up heavier areas of a layout. When grown in groups, Rotala wallichii develops into vibrant clusters of pink, orange, red, and magenta hues. It is commonly used as a background aquatic plant in nature-style and Dutch-style aquascapes where color and texture are important. This species is more demanding than many common stem plants and grows best with strong lighting, CO2 injection, and regular fertilization. With proper care, Rotala wallichii is a treat for the eyes and a solid addition to any colorful planted aquarium. Bacopa Monnieri, commonly known as Moneywort, is a classic aquarium stem plant that’s easily recognized by its thick, upright stems and small, rounded leaves. Its fleshy, bright green foliage grows in opposite pairs along each stem, creating a neat, structured appearance. An easygoing favorite among beginners, Bacopa Monnieri adapts well to a variety of planted aquarium conditions, including low-tech setups without CO2 injection. When grown above the waterline, it occasionally blooms, producing small, delicate flowers. This versatility makes Moneywort suitable for aquariums, terrariums, paludariums, and other planted displays that combine aquatic and emersed growth.

Add warm color to your planted aquarium without demanding care requirements with Ludwigia Ovalis. This easy stem plant develops oval leaves with pointed tips in alternating paris along gently angled stems. Its color ranges from green to golden orange and vibrant red tones depending on growing conditions. Ludwigia Ovalis looks especially attractive when grown in groups of several stems, where regular trimming can encourage branching and a full bushy look over time. Stronger lighting and a liquid fertilizer will help with richer pigmentation, while CO2 injection can support faster growth. Common Name Oval Ludwigia Care Moderate Lighting Medium to High CO2 Optional Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Fast Height 15-30"

Ludwigia Repens is an easy aquarium stem plant that provides beautiful pops of color to a planted aquarium. Ludwigia Repens typically retains its reddish hues without too much finicking, making it a great introduction into keeping red aquarium plants. Leaf coloration will range from green to orange and red depending on the environment in which it is grown. Like most aquarium stem plants, Ludwigia Repens is a prolific grower once it is happy in the aquarium and will require regular pruning to keep its growth under control. A great addition to all aquascape layouts or when used in a Dutch Style planted aquarium. The installation of a pressurized CO2 system is not required, but is favorable in promoting quicker, more robust growth in the planted tank. Propagation is easy and this plant may be trimmed anywhere along its stem and replanted into quality aquarium soil intended for aquatic plant propagation. Common Name Ludwigia Repens Care Moderate Lighting Medium to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Fast Height 10-25+"

Alternanthera Bettzickiana is a colorful ornamental plant recognized for its vibrant foliage in shades of green, pink, red, and purple. Common in the aquarium hobby, Alternanthera Bettzickiana is not considered a true aquatic plant and is better suited for emersed environments where its roots can remain consistently moist while its foliage grows above the waterline. Its compact, colorful growth makes it an excellent option for paludariums, terrariums, Wabi Kusa, and other planted displays that provide high humidity and access to moisture without keeping the entire plant permanently submerged. Good lighting and consistent access to nutrients can help support healthy growth and maintain stronger coloration. Alternanthera Bettzickiana may survive underwater temporarily, but it should not be expected to maintain healthy long-term growth when fully submerged. For best results, grow it emersed or along the moist margins of an aquatic setup.

Overview: Seachem Prime is a liquid water conditioner that will remove harmful chlorine, chloramine and detoxify other harmful elements found in tap water. It is best to use Prime in new water before it is added into aquarium tanks. Prime is a complete and concentrated conditioner for both fresh and saltwater. Prime removes chlorine, chloramine and detoxifies ammonia. Prime converts ammonia into a safe, non-toxic form that is readily removed by the tank’s biofilter. Prime may be used during tank cycling to alleviate ammonia/nitrite toxicity. Prime detoxifies nitrite and nitrate, allowing the biofilter to more efficiently remove them. It will also detoxify any heavy metals found in the tap water at typical concentration levels. Prime is non-acidic and will not impact pH. Use at start-up and whenever adding or replacing water. Prime also contains a binder which renders ammonia, nitrite, and nitrate non-toxic. It is very important to understand how those two functions work together. All dechlorinators operate through a chemical process known as reduction. In this process, toxic dissolved chlorine gas (Cl 2 ) is converted into non-toxic chloride ions (Cl-). The reduction process also breaks the bonds between chlorine and nitrogen atoms in the chloramine molecule (NH 2 Cl), freeing the chlorine atoms and replacing them with hydrogen (H) to create ammonia (NH 3 ). Typically, dechlorinators stop there, leaving an aquarium full of toxic ammonia! Seachem takes the necessary next step by including an ammonia binder to detoxify the ammonia produced in the reduction process. Prime promotes the natural production and restoration of the slime coat rather than relying on artificial or non-native slime compounds.

Overview: Seachem Stability is a liquid water conditioner that will help speed up new tank cycles by breaking down organic wastes which include ammonia, nitrites, and nitrates. Can also be used after filter cleaning reducing the risk of "recycling" already established tanks. Stability will rapidly and safely establish aquarium biofilter in freshwater and marine systems, thereby preventing the #1 cause of livestock death: "new tank syndrome". Stability is formulated specifically for aquariums and contains a synergistic blend of aerobic, anaerobic, and facultative bacteria which facilitate the breakdown of waste organics, ammonia, nitrite, and nitrate. The bacteria employed by Stability are non-sulfur fixing and will not produce toxic hydrogen sulfide. Stability is completely harmless to all aquatic organisms as well as aquatic plants, as a result there's no danger of overuse. Stability is the culmination of nearly a decade of research and development and represents the current state of the art in natural biological management.

Hardy and adaptable, Cryptocoryne Lutea is a great choice for beginner-friendly planted aquariums, low-tech setups, or aquascapes that need reliable midground coverage without demanding care requirements. Its rich coloration, natural knots, and grooved surfaces make it ideal for attaching aquatic plants such as Anubias, Bucephalandra, mosses, and aquatic ferns. Available in a wide range of sizes, Pacific Wood works equally well in nano aquariums, nature-style aquascapes, and larger planted aquarium layouts. Compared to many branch-style driftwoods, Pacific Wood features a denser structure, making it easier to position and typically quicker to become fully waterlogged. Its naturally occurring shapes have made it a longtime favorite among both first-time aquascapers and experienced hobbyists. A fine-leaved aquatic stem plant features slender stems lined with narrow, needle-like leaves, creating a soft, airy appearance. Its delicate foliage makes an attractive addition to planted aquariums, especially when grouped with other popular aquatic stem plants. Rotala Mexicana is a variable species, with growth habits and coloration that can differ depending on the form and aquarium conditions. Stronger lighting, consistent fertilization, and supplemental CO2 are recommended to support healthy growth. Like other aquarium stem plants, healthy cuttings can be trimmed and replanted to encourage fuller groups or expand existing plantings.

Create a flowing, submerged meadow with Potamogeton Gayi. This South American aquatic stem plant develops narrow, slightly translucent leaves in different shades of olive green, orange, and reddish-brown depending on aquarium conditions. Its ribbon-like foliage is delicate and creates natural movement throughout an aquascape. Although a stem plant, Potamogeton Gayi grows a little differently. It spreads beneath the substrate and produces upright stems that gradually form dense groups of foliage. Its relatively easy to grow and adapts well to a range of aquarium conditions. CO2 isn't required, but will help support healthier form and faster growth.

listings.commonName: Plant Pile - Iwagumi Aquarium Plant Bundle
listings.description: Aquascaping and planted tanks go hand in hand, with many styles that are popular for different reasons. Iwagumi layouts hold a special place with our team. This plant pack includes carpeting plants ideal for an Iwagumi aquarium, pre-bundled to suit different rimless tank sizes. What aquatic plants are best for Iwagumi aquascapes? Traditional Iwagumi planted tanks typically feature one to three plant species. Carpet plants like Micranthemum 'Monte Carlo', Hemianthus Callitrichoides (HC), Glossostigma Elatinoides, and hair grass varieties are the most common choices. All of these plants grow low and compact in a horizontal manner. The goal is to complement the hardscape layout, not overshadow. How many plants do I need to grow an aquarium carpet? It depends — everyone’s preferences, layout style, and budget are a little different. To make it easier, we’ve put together safe, bundled aquarium plant packs sized for common tank dimensions to help you get started. Check the recommendations for your tank below, and if you’re unsure or have questions, feel free to email our team — we’re happy to help as best we can. Size Tank Volume Plants Included Tank Recommendations NANO 2 - 5G [5] UNS 5N Nano Rimless Tank MED 10 - 15G [10] UNS 45U Standard Rimless Tank LRG 18 - 30G [20] UNS 60U Standard Rimless Tank What is Iwagumi? It’s an art form that is inspired by ancient Japanese and Chinese rock garden formations that replicate natural landmarks. This style of aquascaping focuses on meticulous placement of rocks, followed by a minimal selection of aquatic plants. Plants chosen should compliment the rock layout, not outshine. If you’re interested in learning more about the basics of Iwagumi aquascaping, we have a full in-depth blog article here .

Add warm, sunset-inspired color to your planted aquarium with Rotala H'ra. Notably popular among aquascapers, this colorful aquarium stem plant displays shades of orange, pink, and red throughout its delicate, narrow leaves. Its fine texture contrasts nicely when grouped with other aquatic plants, while its naturally overhanging growth pattern gives it a soft, flowing appearance. Rather than growing strictly upright, Rotala H'ra has a tendency to branch outward and spread horizontally, allowing its stems to hug hardscape and flow naturally throughout an aquascape. With regular trimming, new side shoots develop along the stems, gradually creating fuller, more colorful bushes. Healthy cuttings can also be replanted to expand existing groups or establish new ones. Strong lighting, consistent fertilization, and CO2 injection encourage more compact growth and richer pigmentation. Like many other Rotala varieties, H'ra can easily outpace other aquatic plants, making regular pruning important for maintaining its shape and preventing lower portions from becoming shaded.

Add delicate texture and fresh lime-green color to your planted aquarium with Mayaca Sellowiana. Native to tropical South America, this aquatic stem plant features narrow, needle-like leaves that grow closely along its stems, creating a compact, finely textured appearance. When planted in groups, its dense foliage develops into soft, bushy clusters that contrast beautifully with broader-leaved plants and colorful red stems. Mayaca Sellowiana is an attractive choice for the midground or background of planted aquariums, where its bright green foliage can help soften transitions between surrounding plants. Its compact growth also makes it an interesting option for smaller aquascapes. Under favorable conditions, it can grow quickly, requiring regular trimming to maintain its shape and prevent overcrowding. While not considered especially difficult, Mayaca Sellowiana benefits from consistent aquarium conditions. Medium to high lighting, softer water, regular fertilization, and supplemental CO2 help support healthy, dense growth.

Add bright color and delicate texture to your planted aquarium with Ludwigia Crystal. This beautiful stem plant develops long, slender leaves with a light, airy growth habit that stands apart from broader-leaved Ludwigia varieties. Foliage can remain vibrant green while developing hints of orange and reddish-pink under stronger lighting and suitable growing conditions. Ludwigia Crystal works especially well grouped throughout the midground of larger planted aquariums or used as a background plant in nano tanks. Its fine foliage creates a soft transition between heavier plant growth and hardscape, while established groups can add plenty of volume without appearing overly dense.

Add fine texture and color to your planted aquarium with Ludwigia Brevipes. Native to the USA, this stem plant closely resembles Ludwigia Arcuata but leans on the larger side. Depending on growing conditions, foliage can range from fresh green to warm orange-red tones that contrast beautifully against surrounding green plants. It works especially well throughout the midground and background, where regular trimming encourages stems to branch into denser groups. Adaptable and relatively easy to grow, Ludwigia Brevipes can be kept across a range of water conditions. Strong lighting, consistent fertilization, and CO2 injection are recommended for bushier growth and stronger coloration. Without supplemental CO2, growth may remain thinner with less branching and more subdued color.

Rich magenta foliage and deep purple undersides give Alternanthera Reineckii Lilacina its signature color. A longtime favorite in the planted aquarium hobby, AR Lilacina develops elongated leaves along upright stems, bringing a darker, moodier palette to a group of colorful stem plants. Its combination of height and pigmented foliage makes Lilacina especially ideal for Dutch-style aquascapes, where contrasting groups of plants are used to create distinct blocks of color and texture. Given room to grow, stems can readily reach the water's surface and may continue into emersed growth, where flowers can occasionally develop above the waterline. Medium to high lighting, a nutrient-rich substrate, consistent fertilization, and CO2 injection support stronger growth and more pronounced coloration. Regular trimming can be used to control taller stems and encourage branching, while healthy cuttings can be replanted to gradually develop a fuller group.

A relative belonging to the Lava Rock family, Icelandic Lava Stone features similar characteristics paired with added detail, ,character and texture. Just as porous, but slightly denser than regular Lava Stone, Icelandic Lava Stone offers added texture that makes this aquascaping stone perfect for recreating scenic mountain aquascapes. Its porous surface is favorable for attaching aquarium moss and epiphytic aquarium plants such as Anubias, Bucephalandra and ferns and a rougher texture makes this stone suitable for stacking. Icelandic Lava Stone is versatile and we can see it being used for popular aquascaping styles from Iwagumi to Pond-style and more. Shown below is approximately 20lbs of Icelandic Lava Stone in a shallow 10 gallon planted aquarium tank:

Ohko Stone, more commonly known as Dragon Stone, is a best selling freshwater aquarium hardscape. It is easy to recognize by its color and scale-like texture. Its warm palette features a mix of brown and golden-orange hues that make bright green aquatic plants and vivid pink or red stem plants really pop in nature-style planted tanks and Iwagumi layouts. Dragon Stone is a lightweight rock that's easy to stack, arrange and adjust when aquascaping. Its clay-like composition makes it relatively soft and easy to break into smaller pieces if needed. Its natural shapes work well in many common aquascape layouts, with plenty of nooks that offer surfaces for attaching aquatic plants or mosses, while also providing shelter for sensitive or shy freshwater fish and shrimp. Best of all, Dragon Stone is aquarium-safe and one of the few inert natural rocks that won't alter water parameters. A great aquarium hardscape for beginners and seasoned planted tank hobbyists! Shown in the video below is approximately 25 pounds of Ohko Dragon Stone in a 15 gallon aquarium:

Maple Stone features deep, reddish-brown tones and a porous texture. Its color alone makes it the perfect choice for aquascapers who are looking for unique hardscape that is not commonly seen or used in planted aquariums. Maple Stone's porosity provides a perfect surface for aquarium moss, terrestrial moss or epiphytic aquatic plants such as Anubias, Bucephalandra and Ferns to self-attach over time. The bold color combination provides beautiful contrast in any planted aquarium or terrarium setup.

Bahai Stone, similar to our favorite, Ryouh Stone, is a much rounder rock in texture. The stones are primarily grey charcoal colored with characteristics that include white marbling and rounded grooves and edges. Just like Ryuoh, Bahai Stone can be used to create softer Iwagumi rock layouts but is versatile and can mimic a range of looks depending on use such as a natural calm river bed. It also complements well with aquarium driftwood such as Pacific Wood or Spider Wood. Its dark coloration would look beautiful when paired with wispy green plants such as Eleocharis Parvulus Mini. Bahai Stone is rare in North America and availability is extremely limited.

Boiling aquarium driftwood will speed up waterlogging and the release of tannins! Click here to shop all hardscape! Tree Branch Driftwood is perfect for creating a cascading forest look within nano to standard sized aquarium tanks. When used as accents in larger aquariums, this particular hardscape material is perfect for detailed roots and branches. Featuring extremely branchy stems and groups of small branches, these are perfect for attaching various species of aquatic mosses for an underwater tree aquascape. Alternatively, the numerous groups of tiny branches provide plenty of space for rhizome plants such as Anubias and Bucephalandra species to attach themselves to. Measurements: Available in 3 different sizes. Nano: 4 - 6" recommended for 4 - 10 gallon aquarium tanks. Medium: 7 - 12" recommended for 10 - 20 gallon aquarium tanks. Large: 12 - 18" recommended for 20+ gallon aquarium tanks. TIP 1: Driftwood is buoyant and can float during initial stages. S oaking, boiling, or using a stone will help keep wood in place. TIP 2: Tannins leeched from wood will provide a natural tint to water, but will gradually dissipate based on the frequency of water changes.

Easily mistaken for a type of aquarium driftwood, because of its texture and coloration, Petrified Wood Stone is actually a popular hardscape rock choice used in the aquarium hobby that features layering characteristics. Compositionally speaking, Petrified Wood Stone is essentially the fossilized remains of terrestrial vegetation and results when trees or tree-like plants are turned into stone through permineralization. Versatile, Petrified Wood Stone can be used in aquarium tank setups, reptile setups, terrariums, and vivariums safely. With its distinct look, the use of aquatic plant species provides a nice contrast and can be used to create unique aquascape layouts in planted aquarium tanks.

Add delicate texture and subtle color to your planted aquarium with Didiplis Diandra. This aquatic stem plant features slender, needle-like leaves that grow densely along its upright stems, creating soft, bushy groups of foliage. Typically bright green, its leaves can develop warm orange and reddish tones under stronger lighting, offering a beautiful contrast against surrounding aquatic plants. Didiplis Diandra looks especially attractive when planted in groups, where its fine foliage creates a fuller, more natural appearance. Depending on aquarium size and regular trimming, it works well in the midground or background of an aquascape. Its stems can grow quickly, making it a solid choice for hobbyists who enjoy shaping and maintaining their planted tanks.

Add soft, feathery texture to your planted aquarium with Myriophyllum Tetrandrum. This aquatic stem plant features delicate, needle-like leaves that flow outward in fine whorls, creating a full yet wispy appearance. Its bright lime-green foliage contrasts beautifully against its reddish-brown stems, making it an eye-catching addition to planted aquariums. This aquarium stem plant looks especially beautiful when planted in large groups, where its delicate texture can add organic movement to an aquascape.

Add autumn-inspired color to your planted aquarium with Myriophyllum Tuberculatum. This colorful aquatic stem plant features delicate, feathery foliage in warm shades of copper, orange, and rusty red, reminiscent of changing leaves in the fall. Its fine texture and rich coloration create a beautiful contrast against surrounding green aquatic plants, making it an attractive addition to the midground or background of an aquascape. Myriophyllum Tuberculatum is a more demanding stem plant that benefits from stronger lighting, consistent fertilization, and supplemental CO2 injection to maintain healthy growth and saturated coloration. Under favorable conditions, it grows quickly and will require regular trimming to maintain shape.

Add soft, feathery greenery to your planted aquarium with Myriophyllum Mattogrossense. Native to South America, this fast-growing aquatic stem plant features finely divided, bright green leaves that spread outward in delicate, fan-like whorls. Its lush foliage creates a soft, bushy appearance, making it an excellent choice for filling the background of an aquascape. One of the easier Myriophyllum species to maintain, Myriophyllum Mattogrossense adapts well to a variety of aquarium conditions, including medium-light setups without CO2 injection. When planted in groups, its fine texture creates a beautiful contrast against broader-leaved aquatic plants. Under favorable conditions, its stems can grow quite tall, making regular trimming important for maintaining a compact, full appearance. Although considered an easier Myrio, this aquarium stem plant benefits from consistent fertilization, stronger lighting and supplemental CO2.

Rotala 'Bonsai' is characterized by dense and compact growth pattern. Dependent upon lighting provided, its tips can achieve a reddish coloration. It is also often described as a moderately growing cousin of Bacopa Caroliniana. When frequent trimming is performed, Rotala Bonsai grows dense and bushy and provides a beautiful display in any planted aquarium tank. Rotala Bonsai can thrive in a wide range of tank conditions. However, to bring the best out of this plant, CO2, rich fertilizer and substrate is recommended. Common Name Ammania Bonsai Care Moderate to Hard Lighting Medium to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate Height 5-20"

Add vibrant pink and reddish tones to your planted aquarium with Cryptocoryne Albida Red. This rare Cryptocoryne develops narrow leaves with intense coloration and markings similar to Cryptocoryne Nurii, making it a standout choice for collectors and planted aquarium hobbyists looking for something less common. Cryptocoryne Albida Red is an extremely slow-growing plant that rewards patience once established. Its coloration can range from pink and red to deeper earthy tones depending on growing conditions. Suitable for both low-tech and more advanced planted aquariums, it performs well under low to moderate lighting. CO2 injection is not required but can be provided to support stronger growth. Like other Cryptocoryne, allow the plant time to establish a healthy root system after planting and avoid unnecessary moving or disturbance while it settles in.

Originating from South America, Sagittaria Subulata is an aquarium plant commonly used for aquascaping and planted tanks. Its easy care makes it a great choice for aquascapers who are looking for a capeting aquatic plant for a low tech tank. Its generally hardy and grows well with minimal care requirements. Once it has established good roots, it will need to be regularly pruned to maintain a low, thick appearance. Depending on the aquarium, it has the capability to grow tall and may even send long shoots to the water's surface with a small white flower bloom. Dwarf Sag grows by spreading runners horizontally throughout the substrate. It is not a fussy plant in terms of lighting or CO2 injection. Propagation is simple, trim portions of its horizontal shoots and replant into quality aquasoil. Plant Care & Information

Limnophila Heterophylla is an easy aquatic stem plant that adapts well to a wide range of aquarium conditions. It’s especially popular in low-tech tanks since it requires little care while still offering a unique look. Its bright green color stands out, and its lacy, ornamental foliage adds great texture. We recommend this plant for beginner aquascapers as a background choice, though it’s a solid option for any skill level. This aquarium stem plant doesn’t require CO2 injection, but like all aquatic plants, it will benefit if provided. In high-tech setups, it grows quickly and will need regular pruning. It can be grown both submersed and emersed. Common Name Limnophila Heterophylla Care Easy Lighting Low to Medium CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Slow Height 4-12"

Lobelia cardinalis can be found growing wild in North America. Known as Cardinal Plant for short, it is a versatile aquatic plant that is commonly used in planted aquariums, nano tanks, and aquascaping projects. It is typically cultivated in marshy, bog-like environments and is easily recognized for its dark green leaves with purple undersides. In planted tanks, its foliage is typically a lighter green and its bush-like growth makes it a great midground plant in layouts. It is very versatile with growing conditions and can be planted in both submerged or emersed environments. Above water, it may also bloom scarlet red flowers from time to time. While it isn't considered an advanced plant, it will appreciate moderate to high lighting levels, nutrient-dense aquarium soil and CO2 when possible. Once established, trim is periodically to encourage off-shoots for a bushier result. Propagate by trimming stems and replanting or pulling apart dense clumps and splitting the roots. Common Name Cardinal Plant Care Easy to Moderate Lighting Low CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Midground and Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate Height 7-12"

Barclaya Longifolia is an uncommon aquatic bulb plant. When it sprouts, this aquarium plant puts out long red leaves that can become quite large and is a sight to see when paired with bushes of colorful aquatic stem plants. Barclaya Longifolia does not require high light and CO2 injection, but growth will slow and color is less vibrant and more of a bronze tone. Whenever possible, we highly recommend planting it in planted tanks that utilize quality light, CO2 injection and a regular dosing schedule of essential fertilizers. The difference that will result will be very noticeable and the plant will reveal healthy leaves that are a deep maroon hue. Common Name Barclaya Longifolia Care Easy Lighting Low to Medium CO2 Optional Suggested Placement Midground Propagation Separate rhizome and plant Growth Rate Slow Height Varies

Blyxa Japonica - A classic aquatic plant used for aquascaping Blyxa Japonica is a true aquatic plant that is naturally found in nutrient-rich, stagnant waters like swamps, marshes and other slow-moving bodies of water. This aquarium stem plant was made popular in the aquarium community by Takashi Amano and his curated use of its grass-like appearance. Medium in height, Blyxa Japonica is a suitable midground aquarium plant or as a background aquatic plant in smaller nano planted tanks. This aquarium stem plant forms bushy growth naturally, thanks to its compact growing pattern and will provide beautiful motion and color nuance to any planted aquarium. When Blyxa Japonica is planted in an aquarium with CO2 injection and moderate to high light levels, this aquarium stem starts to exhibit red and golden hues that weave in between its primary green and yellow leaves. This quality produces visual interest and subtle contrast against a backdrop of other aquarium plants. Commonly believed to be a difficult stem plant, Blyxa Japonica is relatively hardy once mature and can adapt to soft and harder water conditions. Some melt can be expected, but effects can be mitigated through consistent care and quality aquarium plant fertilizers. For best results, Blyxa Japonica should be planted an a nutrient-rich, CO2 injected planted aquarium. Slightly different from other species of grass-like midground and foreground aquatic plants, Blyxa Japonica doesn't produce long runners. Instead, side shoots are produced and are easily divided from the mother plant with quality aquascaping tools. It is a bit more difficult to plant due to its buoyancy, but overall this aquatic plant is not as invasive, since it tends to bush over itself as it grows. Common Name Blyxa Japonica / Blyxa Care Easy to Moderate Lighting Medium to High CO2 Required Suggested Placement Midground Propagation Separate and replant Growth Rate Moderate Height 3-6"

Vallisneria Nana is an easy-care jungle val known for its thin, rich green leaves that grow tall with ease, much like other Vallisneria species. Its height and overall size make it a great choice for larger planted aquariums or even freshwater ponds. With more of a grass-like appearance, Val Nana brings a soft, flowing texture to the background and works beautifully in a variety of aquascape styles. Consider this wispy aquatic plant for your tank's backdrop! Propagation is simple as they spread via side shoots and are easily separated. Regular pruning is recommended to maintain its growth. It is a heavy root feeder and will anchor itself into quality aquasoil if given the opportunity.

Phyllanthus Fluitans, more commonly known as Red Root Floaters, is quite similar to Salvinia aquatic floating plants but features only one leaf on each node instead of two. Leaf color is dependent upon the choice of LED aquarium lighting used and can range from green to a brownish red hue. However, its most notable feature is the tufts of roots that have a nice red coloration, hence the common name. Phyllanthus Fluitans is extremely easy to care for and if given optimal conditions, the plant grows extremely quick and will sprout small white flowers. Red Root Floaters also provide many benefits when added into a planted aquarium tank. This aquatic floating plant provides natural cover for shrimp, skittish fish and even fry as well as another source of natural water filtration as the roots help absorb excess nutrients in the water rather quickly. Portion Size: 10-15 leaves

Add long, bright green grass-like leaves to your planted aquarium! Its appearance is similar to Vallisneria Nana and Giant Hairgrass. Generally easy to care for, it provides another solid option for filling in the background of an aquascape.

Juncus Repens is part of Juncaceae family and is the only species that is commonly kept in planted aquarium tanks. Featuring long stems with narrow leaves, Juncus Repens seemingly appears as a hybrid between stem and rosette aquatic plants. As the rest of the species family is generally kept as pond plants, Juncus Repens can be grown submersed or emersed. Typically non-demanding, Juncus Repens is considered a low maintenance aquatic plant that will adapt fairly well to a wide range of aquarium conditions. Its coloration is usually green, but when provided with quality aquarium lighting, the aquatic plant can exhibit tinges of rich red-brown hues. Propagation is simple and can be done by trimming the stem above the node and replanting in a quality aquarium substrate.

Aponogeton Madagascariensis, commonly known as Madagascar Lace Plant, is an ornamental aquatic plant for large planted tanks or freshwater ponds. Its signature lace-like leaves feature a mixed color palette that includes shades of greens, browns and purplish-red hues. Its texture combined with color makes it a focal point in any aquarium setup. Important Note: This listing includes a bulb that may or may not be sprouted at the time of purchase. Please ensure you are prepared to care for either option. Its bulb serves as an energy hub for healthy growth. Provide a nutrient-rich substrate or supplement with root tabs to support this aquarium plant’s development. While relatively hardy, it can be more selective with water quality than other Aponogeton varieties. When cared for properly, Madagascar Lace can outgrow many other aquatic plants. It grows well with moderate lighting and strong water flow, making it a rewarding choice for hobbyists looking for a statement plant in a large planted aquarium! Common Name Madagascar Lace Care Easy Lighting Low to Medium CO2 Optional Suggested Placement Background Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 8-20+"

Rotala Macrandra Red is a highly sought-after species that is characterized by its bold deep red to magenta hues. It makes for a beautiful background plant in medium to larger planted aquariums and as a mid to background choice. Quality lighting, CO2, and soft water are essential to promote growth. Beyond this, micronutrients are required if intense deep colors are desired. When provided with optimal conditions, this aquatic plant is an amazing addition to any planted tank. Individual stems should also be given sufficient space when planted as planting them too closely together will render the lower leaves void of light. Rotala Macrandra Red is very demanding and can be difficult to keep, but results are well worth the extra effort and rewarding if successful. Common Name Rotala Macrandra Care Difficult Lighting High CO2 Required Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate Height 8-16 " Our bunched stem plants are all kept and grown in high-quality substrate by Marfied Controsoil . A strict fertilizer dosing regime and CO2 are provided in their holding tanks.

Cyperus Helferi is a tall grass-like plant that can be grown submerged or emerged. Its leaves are long and thin and can grow up to 20+ inches long. Given its height, this aquatic plant makes a wonderful background choice for larger planted aquarium tanks. Cyperus Helferi is low maintenance and will adapt to a wide range of aquarium conditions as long as the temperature is not too high. Propagation is simple as they spread via side shoots and are easily separated. Regular pruning is recommended as this species can grow to the height of your aquarium easily and will also anchor deep into substrate if given the opportunity to do so. Common Name Cyperus Helferi Care Easy Lighting Medium to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Background Propagation Divide and plant Growth Rate Slow Height 8-20"

Rotala Nanjenshan is described as a hybrid cross between Rotala Rotundifolia and Rotala Wallichi. It features dense stems with very thin leaves that give it a bushy appearance. Rotala Nanjenshan can be difficult to keep as it requires quality aquarium lighting and CO2 injection to thrive. It is also fairly fragile and should only be planted in an aquarium with smaller docile fish species as overly active or aggressive swimmers have the potential to damage the aquatic plant. If successful in keeping this aquatic plant, Rotala Nanjenshan grows dense and will require regular pruning to keep it in tip-top shape. Common Name Rotala Nanjenshan Care Moderate Lighting Medium to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Fast Height 5-10"

Grow your own dwarf aquarium lily with Nymphaea stellata! Starting from a small bulb, this aquatic plant develops a cluster of delicate, arrow-shaped leaves in shades of reddish-bronze, pink, and green. Its colorful submerged foliage creates a gradient among surrounding aquatic plants, making it an interesting statement plant even in smaller aquariums. As the lily matures, long, slender stems may begin reaching toward the water's surface, eventually producing rounded, floating lily pads. These leaves create a natural canopy that provides shade and coverage for aquarium fish and fry. If you prefer a more compact appearance, stalks can be easily trimmed. To plant, position the bulb on top of the substrate with any existing shoots facing upward. As roots develop, they'll naturally anchor the bulb in place. Avoid burying the entire bulb. If you’re unsure, sometimes we just place it floating in between hardscape until roots appear! Please Note: This listing is for one bulb only. Bulbs may arrive with or without existing leaves. Any existing foliage may be delicate or damaged during transit, but new growth can develop as the bulb establishes settles into your aquarium.

Add a soft, natural touch to your planted aquarium with Bacopa Australis. Compared to other Bacopa varieties like Bacopa Monnieri, this stem plant features smaller, more delicate stems and leaves in bright, fresh shades of green. Under stronger lighting, its foliage may develop subtle reddish tones, adding a little extra color to its otherwise lush green palette. While Bacopa Australis can grow upright, its stems are capable of spreading horizontally under certain conditions, resulting in low, cushion-like groups throughout an aquascape. Bacopa Australis is relatively easy to grow and adapts well to a variety of aquarium conditions, including low-tech setups without CO2 injection. It can also grow emersed, occasionally producing small, delicate flowers above the waterline.

Crinum Calamistratum is a bulbous aquatic plant with thin, curly rich green foliage. Its unique leaves add beautiful motion to planted tanks and can grow extremely long when provided with the right conditions. Calamistratum is considered a hardier Crinum species and requires less light than others, making it well-suited for planted aquariums with low to moderate lighting. Although it grows slowly, it will eventually produce small bulbs that can be separated and replanted for propagation. Crinum calamistratum is also unique in that it can thrive in brackish aquariums with low salt concentrations. It’s not particularly tasty to herbivorous fish and is typically safe from plant munchers! Common Name Crinum Calamistratum Care Easy to Moderate Lighting Moderate CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Background Propagation Divide and plant Growth Rate Moderate Height 8-12+"

Microsorum pteropus ‘Narrow Leaf’, also known as Java Fern Narrow Leaf, is a slimmer variation of the classic Java Fern. Its long, narrow leaves stay relatively thin, giving it a cleaner, more streamlined look compared to broader varieties. It grows well in low light conditions and is very forgiving across a wide range of aquarium parameters. Recently reclassified as Leptochilus pteropus , this plant is still widely known in the aquarium hobby as Microsorum pteropus. Like other Java Ferns, this plant is epiphytic and can be attached directly to driftwood, rocks, or aquarium decor using thread or glue. Make sure to keep the rhizome above the substrate to prevent rot. Propagation is easy—simply cut or divide the rhizome and reattach as needed.

Microcarpaea Minima Merrill is a rare aquatic stem plant that grows similar to Micranthemum Micranthemoides Pearlweed. It has been widely distributed throughout Asia and can be seen used in some of the top aquascapes. Microcarpaea can be kept as a foreground plant with frequent trimming or as a mid to background plant depending on aquarium size. If left untrimmed, this aquatic plant tends to grow bushy with small needle-like leaves that will add a touch of bright lime green to planted tanks. We recommend that Microcarpaea Minima Merrill be planted in an already established planted aquarium as it has a tendency to melt and wither if stable water parameters are not present. Anubias nana Pangolino is one of the smallest Anubias varieties available! Still rare to see, this aquatic plant is known for its tiny leaves that are smaller than Anubias nana petite, which makes it ideal for nano planted aquariums or for adding detail work to larger aquascapes. This plant offers the same easy care and durablility as other Anubias, making it suitable for nearly all setups. It sprouts new growth from its rhizome and will grow best when attached to driftwood or stone. You can also tuck it into small gaps and crevices in the hardscape layout where it will naturally anchor itself over time. Growth is very slow, but that's part of its charm! As it develops, it creates a dense, miniature look that works well for detailed layouts or when paired with other tiny-leaf plants. CO2 isn't required for this plant, but can help support better health. Overall, Anubias nana Pangolino is a true gem for aquascaping and planted aquariums!

Hygrophila Pinnatifida is a relatively rarer aquatic plant in the aquarium hobby. This aquarium plant features a mix of green and bronze hues on its signature serrated leaves. Depending on tank conditions, H. Pinn can develop a varying color palette. A classic plant to use in aquascape layouts, Hygrophila Pinnatifida makes a beautiful addition to any planted aquarium tank. Its care requirements aren't too difficult so long as the water is kept clean and quality aquarium lighting is provided. To achieve compact growth, trim your plant regularly and use brighter lights. In low light settings, it may grow leggy. In addition, this unique aquatic plant can be attached to aquarium hardscape such as driftwood or rock instead of being planted directed in planted tank substrate. Common Name Hygrophila Pinnatifida Care Moderate Lighting Moderate to High CO2 Recommended Aquascape Placement Midground Propagation Trim and replant Growth Rate Moderate Size 3-6”

Lilaeopsis Mauritiana, a variety of Micro Sword, is similar to Lilaeopsis Brasiliensis in appearance with easier care requirements. Its chubby, short blade-like leaves help create the look of an underwater lawn or grassy hedges at the base of an aquascape. Thanks to its easygoing nature, Lilaeopsis Mauritiana is well suited for beginner aquascapers and lower-maintenance planted aquariums. Try it out if you value manageability or are growing a carpeting plant for the first time. As the plant develops, it spreads horizontally through runners that can be trimmed and replanted for propagation.

Echinodorus Horemanii Red is a variant of the classic aquarium sword plant that features a beautiful color spectrum. Possessing a unique growth pattern, Echinodous Horemanii Red's leaves are red when new and slowly turn greener as they age. Just like other aquarium sword variants, this aquatic plant should be planted directly into a quality aquarium substrate to encourage growth as swords are known for heavily absorbing nutrients via their root system. This plant can be grown emersed and submerged and is typically very adaptive to a wide range of aquarium tank conditions. Propagation is simple. Separate and replant. Once established, regular trimming will be required. Common Name Echinodorus Horemanii Red Care Easy Lighting Medium to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant runners Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 8-12" Tissue culture plants are grown in-vitro by laboratories who specialize in propagating aquatic plants. Anubias Nana Bonsai is another species in the Anubias family. It falls between Anubias Nana Petite and Anubias Nana in terms of sizing. Just like the rest of the Anubias species, it's a great choice for beginners due to its easy care and overall hardiness. This plant is almost indestructible in any planted aquarium tank and can survive in a wide range of environments. However, if presented with optimal conditions, this plant will thrive and results will be rewarding. Best when used as a mid-ground plant attached to stones or wood as an accent or centerpiece depending on tank size. We recommend Anubias Nana Bonsai for any size aquarium. It's a flowering aquatic plant that grows best when the rhizome is attached to hardscape material such as wood or stone. Regular fertilization is favorable and low to medium lighting is sufficient as high lighting will promote the growth of algae on its leaves. CO2 is not required but promotes faster growth and robust leaves. Propagation is straightforward; simply cut or pull apart rhizomes to be reattached.

Bucephalandra or Buce for short, is a popular epiphytic plant the is commonly used in the aquascaping and planted aquarium tank hobby. This genus is well-known for its adaptability, hardiness and stunning coloration when grown in healthy aquarium conditions. In the wild, Bucephalandra are often found in fast-flowing bodies of water and are suitable for a wide variety of planted setups. Buce can be grown submerged in the aquarium, as well as emersed in a hybrid planted tank, terrarium, paludarium or vivarium. Bucephalandra are available in a wide variety of shapes, sizes and colors. They are relatively low maintenance, hardy and versatile with placement. From green to purple, wrinkled to flat leaves, and everything in between, this unique aquatic plant is a fantastic addition to any planted setup. There might even be an additional surprise from time to time, so if you're feeling daring and love a mystery, the Buce Plant Bag is for you. Boiling aquarium driftwood will speed up waterlogging and the release of tannins! Click here to shop all hardscape! Tiger Wood is the perfect centerpiece-type aquarium driftwood. Its spindly stump-like form and complex root structure emulates an underwater tree appearance. Combined with its varying brown tones, it also is a top contender for a biotope aquarium. With its twists and turns, Tiger Wood provides plenty areas of shade and shelter for skittish fish and fry to dwell. All aquarium driftwood will discolor water. This is normal, harmless and is caused by tannins. Tannins are what give aquarium water a brown or tea colored tint. This can be commonly seen in black water aquariums or biotope aquarium setups. Some hobbyists prefer this look and there are also benefits to having tannins in your water. Some benefits include softer water while also providing an environment that more closely mimics most tropical species environments found in the wild. The color will lighten and dissipate over time with routine water changes and maintenance. If you do not prefer this look, you can remove tannins from your aquarium with this product! Anubias Nana Snow white is unique variation in the Anubias plant family. Its small, rounded leaves are nearly void of the classic green color, making it stand out in any planted aquarium or aquascape. We've noticed that the mutation is not fully stable and hints of green typically return as the plant matures. This results in a brilliant marbled look, which is actually better for long-term health as chlorophyll is essential for photosynthesis. Like other rhizome aquarium plants, it is epiphytic and will grow best attached to natural stone or driftwood. Its light color palette is beautiful and contrasts well against other live aquatic plants. Overall, it is slow-growing and delicate, so allow it to establish before attempting to propagate! If you like variegated plants, or rare plants for aquascaping, give this one a try.

Homalomena Sekadau South is a rare flowering aquatic plant that belongs to the same family as Bucephalandra. Because of its rarity, the likelyhood of a local fish store carrying this plant is slim to none. Similar to Buce, it's quite easy to care for and can be grown submerged or emersed. Homalomena doesn't require that much aquarium lighting to thrive as it is a slow growing and excessive lighting can cause algae growth on its leaves, much like Anubias and Buce. Common Name Homalomena Sekadau Care Moderate Lighting Medium to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Attach to wood or stone Propagation Separate rhizome Growth Rate Moderate Height 4"+

Add rare color to your planted aquarium with Ludwigia White / Pink (Ludwigia inclinata var. verticillata 'White'). This aquarium stem plant develops dense whorls of narrow leaves in cream-white to pale pink tones, creating a dramatic contrast against traditional green and red aquatic plants. Ludwigia White / Pink is a demanding plant best suited for experienced aquascapers and high-tech planted aquariums. Strong lighting, CO2 injection, consistent fertilization, and a nutrient-rich substrate are recommended to support healthy growth and maintain its characteristic pale coloration. Its delicate appearance comes with less room for inconsistent conditions than more forgiving Ludwigia varieties.

Microsorum pteropus ‘Narrow Leaf Mini’, also known as Java Fern Narrow Leaf Mini, is a compact variation of the classic Java Fern with shorter, slender leaves. Compared to standard Narrow Leaf, this version stays smaller while maintaining the same signature narrow leaf shape. Recently reclassified as Leptochilus pteropus , this plant is still widely known in the aquarium hobby as Microsorum pteropus. Its smaller size makes it especially useful for nano planted aquariums, where it can be used in the midground or even background without overwhelming the layout. Like other Java Fern varieties, it is very easy to care for and grows well in low light conditions. It is tolerant of a wide range of water parameters, making it a great choice for beginner setups. As an epiphytic plant, it can be attached directly to driftwood, rocks, or aquarium decor using thread or glue. Be sure to keep the rhizome above the substrate to prevent rot. Propagation is simple—just cut or divide the rhizome and reattach as needed. Over time, it will continue to grow into a dense, natural-looking cluster.

Microsorum pteropus ‘Trident’, also known as Java Fern Trident, is a popular aquarium plant used in aquascaping and terrariums. Like other Java Fern varieties, it’s easy to care for and maintains its appearance with very little effort. Its slender, deep green leaves branch out into multiple tips, giving it a more detailed, textured look compared to standard Java Fern. Recently reclassified as Leptochilus pteropus , this plant is still widely known in the aquarium hobby as Microsorum pteropus. Its unique, forked growth creates a fuller appearance, making it a great choice for filling in sparse areas or adding contrast to broader-leaf plants in a layout. Java Fern Trident is ideal for low tech planted aquariums and low light setups, making it a great option for beginners. As an epiphytic plant, it can be attached to driftwood, rocks, or aquarium decor using thread or glue. Be sure to keep the rhizome above the substrate to prevent rot. When mature, propagation is simple—just cut or divide the rhizome and reattach as needed. With time, it will continue to grow into a dense, natural-looking cluster.

Tonina Belem is a unique aquatic plant that features a vertical stem with thin leaves shooting out to the side. Found in shallow waters in the wild, Tonina Belem is an advanced aquatic plant that is not recommended for novice planted aquarium hobbyists as it has very particular care requirements. Soft water and a slightly acidic quality substrate is a must and high-quality aquarium LED lighting along with CO2 injection is required to grow this aquatic plant properly. Tonina Belem also needs a consistent dosing schedule and an ample supply of iron and micronutrients. Tonina Belem grows vertically and will produce lateral shoots if provided with enough light, but often times, most aquatic stem plant species grow at a quicker pace leaving most Tonina species susceptible to being covered, resulting in a lack of lighting received. Propagation is simple and similar to other aquatic stem plants. You can simply cut off the shoots using clean aquascaping tools and replant the cut portion back into a quality substrate. This aquatic plant species requires patience and know-how to keep. If given optimal conditions, this aquatic plant is a beautiful addition to any planted aquarium tank and can most commonly be seen in Dutch Style planted aquariums for its unique foliage style. Common Name Tonina Belem Care Advanced Lighting High CO2 Required Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate Height 3-10" Our bunched stem plants are all kept and grown in high-quality substrate by Marfied Controsoil . A strict fertilizer dosing regime and CO2 are provided in their holding tanks.

Tonina Fluviatilis is another aquatic plant species in the Tonina aquatic plant family. This specific species is a beautiful ornamental stem plant that is characterized by its bright green color, unique foliage, and slight shimmer when submerged in an planted aquarium tank. Similar to Tonina Belem, Tonina Fluviatilis prefers to be kept in soft water with a slightly acidic aquarium substrate. Belonging to the Eriocaulaceae family, Tonina species are not recommended for the beginner hobbyists and are considered an advanced aquatic plant choice in the planted tank hobby. Additional care requirements include, quality aquarium LED lighting, CO2 injection and an ample supply of macro and micronutrients. Because Tonina Fluviatilis's growth is moderate, other aquatic stem plant species have the potential to outgrow and cover the plant, resulting in a lack of light available. Propagation is simple and similar to other aquatic stem plants. You can simply cut off the shoots using clean aquascaping tools and replant the cut portion back into a quality substrate. This aquatic plant species requires patience and know-how to keep. If given optimal conditions, this aquatic plant is a beautiful addition to any planted aquarium tank and can most commonly be seen in Dutch Style planted aquariums and even Blackwater Biotopes. Common Name Tonina Fluviatilis Care Advanced Lighting High CO2 Required Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate Height 3-7" Our bunched stem plants are all kept and grown in high-quality substrate by Marfied Controsoil . A strict fertilizer dosing regime and CO2 are provided in their holding tanks.

Hygrophila Siamensis is an aquatic stem plant that features greenish-bronze foliage. Generally easy to grow, Hygrophila Siamensis is a good choice for beginner hobbyists as this aquatic plant species adapts well to a wide range of water parameters and aquarium sizes. It can be grown submerged or emersed and if given optimal conditions, Hygrophila Siamensis will produce small purple-blue flowers. Although Hygrophila Siamensis is very hardy, this aquatic plant thrives with the addition of quality aquarium lighting and a normal dosing schedule of macro and micronutrients. We recommend using this aquatic plant in the midground or background of any planted tank. It is a fast grower and will easily begin to grow out of the tank, so frequent pruning is necessary to keep its growth structured to preference. Propagation is simple as well. Simply cut off a shoot and replant it into a quality aquarium substrate.

Add a splash of color to your planted aquarium with Bacopa Monnieri Variegatus, a lightly variegated form of the popular Moneywort stem plant. Its upright stems feature pairs of small, rounded leaves with a mix of light green, cream, and pale yellow tones. The irregular variegation creates a soft contrast against surrounding green aquatic plants, making it an interesting addition to the midground of planted aquariums. Like standard Bacopa Monnieri, this variety is relatively easy to grow and adapts well to a range of aquarium conditions. CO2 injection is not required, although adequate lighting and consistent nutrients help support healthy growth. Regular trimming encourages branching, and healthy stem cuttings can be replanted to create fuller groups.

Limnophila Mini Vietnam is an exotic aquatic stem plant that is still relatively rare in the hobby. Featuring a lovely bright green hue, Limnophila Mini Vietnam has star-shaped foliage that stays on the smaller side making it ideal as a midground aquatic plant choice in planted aquarium tanks. It's also a great choice for aquarists who are in the search of mini aquatic plants. When provided with quality aquarium lighting, Limnophila Mini Vietnam can produce a faint purplish-red coloration that is sure to pop against other aquatic plant species. Like all other aquatic stem plants, once it is given optimal care, this aquatic plant can grow at a quick pace requiring consistent trims to achieve the bushy effect that is sought after by planted tank enthusiasts. We recommend this plant for aquarists looking for a unique background or midground aquatic plant. Pruning is simple and can be done by replanting trimmed stems into quality aquarium soil. Common Name Limnophila Sp. Mini Vietnam Care Medium Lighting Medium to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 5-10" Our bunched aquatic stem plants are all kept and grown in high-quality substrate by Marfied Controsoil . A strict fertilizer dosing regime and CO2 are provided in their holding tanks.

Vesicularia sp. Little Triangle, more simply known as Triangle Moss, is an aquatic moss species that is characterized by its dense shoots and unique triangular growth outline. Its foliage is a beautiful green hue and is similar to another popular aquatic moss species, Mini Christmas Moss, but with an ascending behavior. Also known as San Jiao Moss, Little Triangle Moss's care is similar to that of other aquatic moss species. This unique aquarium moss provides for a much more natural look in a planted aquarium. It can adapt to a wide range of aquarium tank conditions and can be readily attached to aquarium driftwood and rocks. We recommend using it in a jungle or forest aquascape layout for additional character, depth, and contrast. Common Name Vesicularia Sp. Little Triangle Delicate Fern Moss Thuidium Moss Care Easy Lighting Low to Medium CO2 Optional Suggested Placement Attached to rock or wood Propagation Cut or pull apart Growth Rate Varies Height Varies

Glossostigma Elatinoides Platinum, commonly known as Glosso for short, is an extremely rare variant of the common green Glosso seen often in the aquarium trade. Glosso Platinum features foliage that is multiple shades lighter hence its name. Its peculiar color pattern provides a different aesthetic when used as a foreground plant. Because of its rarity, availability is still extremely limited. Like its popular cousin, Glossostigma Elantinoides Platinum mimics the same growth patterns and is growing in popularity in nature aquarium style planted tanks. Platinum Glosso has a tendency to grows upwards if lighting is poor or if other plants or hardscape overshadow it. When planting, small clumps should be placed half an inch apart from each other to help the plants grow together more quickly. CO2 addition and soft water will promote growth significantly. This plant can grow quickly and will require regular trimming when kept under proper conditions. Helanthium Vesuvius, previously known as Echinodorus Vesuvius, is a cultured aquatic plant species derived from Helanthium Angustifolia. Helanthium Vesuvius features thin leaves in a soft green hue. Its interesting growth pattern exhibiting a twisting behavior makes this aquatic plant a unique addition to the main aquatic plant family. Helanthium Vesuvius is quite hardy and will grow at a steady pace and pruning on a normal basis is necessary. Just like other rosette species, this particular aquatic plant is beautiful in groups or by itself. Marsilea Hirsuta is a carpeting foreground aquatic plant choice. It is well-known for its foliage that resembles a four-leaf clover. Once the plant is submerged, its growth pattern is susceptible to change depending upon the planted aquarium tank's parameters. New leaves sprouted are brown coloration and should not be mistaken for rotting or dead leaves as they will gain color upon maturing. Marsilea Hirsuta is generally hardy and easy to keep and grow. It can adapt to most aquarium conditions and will spread steadily if given optimal conditions. This plant grows by spreading runners horizontally throughout the substrate. Lighting and CO2 injection are essential in keeping the growth short and compact. Propagation is simple, trim along the runners and replant. Eriocaulon sp. ‘Vietnam’ is a less common aquatic plant, known for its bright green, grass-like leaves. It resembles Eriocaulon sp. ‘Goias’ but can be distinguished by its size and slightly arched leaves. Although this genus has a reputation for being difficult to grow, this variety is relatively forgiving and often considered one of the easier Eriocaulon species. Still, it requires the basics: quality aquasoil, good lighting, CO₂ injection, and a complete nutrient source with both micro- and macronutrients. When healthy, it forms dense tufts that resemble grass, making it an excellent midground choice in a planted tank. Successfully growing this plant rewards you with a unique and beautiful addition to your aquascape. If you’re looking for a reliable plant to grow at the base of stones, Eriocaulon are solid contenders! Common Name Eriocaulon Vietnam Care Advanced Lighting High CO2 Required Suggested Placement Midground Propagation Separate and replant Growth Rate Moderate Height 4-7"

Rotala Bossii is an uncommon variant in the Rotala family. This aquatic stem plant is similar to its popular cousin, Rotala Rotundifolia, but will remain purely green in coloration even if provided with conditions that are known to bring out red hues. Rotala Bossii has a similar growth pattern and has the potential to produce bushy and hanging growth. If kept under proper conditions, Rotala Bossii is a fast growing aquatic stem plant and will require consistent pruning to prevent the bottom leaves from dying off due to lack of lighting and to keep it growing lush. Common Name Rotala Bossii Care Moderate Lighting Medium to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Fast Height 15-30 "

Gratiola Viscidula is an aquatic plant that is still relatively new to the planted aquarium hobby. Hailing from North America, Gratiola Viscidula is known for its thorn-like leaves with a bright green hue. Gratiola Viscidula is an easy aquarium plant and doesn't require too much in order to thrive. Clean water and quality aquarium lighting are a good start. Slow growing, this aquatic plant is ideal for a midground choice. Alternatively, it can be used for a foreground aquatic plant choice if it is kept trimmed low enough. Common Name Gratiola Viscidula Care Easy Lighting Medium to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Midground Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Slow Height 1-3”

While its new name is Helanthium Bolivianum, most hobbyists still refer to this aquatic plant as its former, Echinodorus Bolivianum. This aquatic plant is characterized by its light green leaves with a slender shape. Just like other rosette species, this particular aquatic plant is beautiful in groups or by itself. Propagation is also fairly simple and can be done by separating via the runners and replanting into a quality aquarium substrate. Helanthium Tenellum is a grass-like aquatic plant that is commonly used for its carpeting tendencies. Its appearance is similar to other aquatic plant species such as Dwarf Hair Grass and Lilaeopsis Novaezelandiae (Micro Swords) and propagates by sending out runners as well. Helanthium Tenellum is generally easy to keep and will spread readily if given optimal conditions. We recommend using it as a foreground or midground choice. It can even be used as a short background aquatic plant choice in smaller nano-sized aquarium tanks. Just like other rosette species, this particular aquatic plant is beautiful in groups or by itself. Propagation is also fairly simple and can be done by separating via the runners and replanting into a quality aquarium substrate. Pearl Moss (Plagiomnium cf. affine) is a unique semi-aquatic moss that offers a different look compared to more common species like Java Moss or Christmas Moss. Its bright green color and small, pearl-like fronds create a delicate texture that works especially well in nature-style aquascapes, emersed Wabi Kusa displays, and forest-inspired terrariums. This moss is often used to soften hardscape and add instant greenery to planted aquariums and terrariums. Attach it to driftwood, rocks, or tuck it into crevices where it can gradually develop into mossy patches over time. It pairs particularly well with branches, roots, and small stones where it helps soften transitions and create the subtle details that make an aquascape feel more natural and established. From a distance it blends into the layout, but rewards a closer look. Pearl Moss grows slowly and will do best in stable conditions. Grow it in lightly shaded areas that receive good circulation. In a planted aquarium, CO2 injection will support fuller growth. With patience, Pearl Moss develops into a beautiful accent that adds texture, color, and character to planted aquariums and terrarium layouts. Moss Mat: Pre-grown on 3x5" mat with holding tray Stainless Steel Mesh: Pre-grown on 3x3" mesh

listings.commonName: UNS Bar Pro Light Hanging Kit
listings.description: The answer to your light hanging needs. This kit is constructed from rust-proof stainless steel and designed specifically for aquarium use without compromising quality or function. The Ultum Nature Systems Light Hanging Kit can be attached directly to the back/side of an aquarium cabinet stand or onto the wall. The ability to adjust the amount of light over your aquarium is an overlooked necessity in the planted aquarium hobby. By providing the ability to raise or lower the fixture to the desired height, this aquarium light hanging kit allows the user to control the light intensity and coverage spread to suit specific needs. If aquatic plants are receiving more light than they’re able to utilize for photosynthesis, algae develop and grow rapidly. The amount of light required for aquatic plant growth directly correlates to the amount of CO2 and fertilizers present in a planted aquarium. Having an overpowered light fixture on a tank with low CO2 and fertilization is a guaranteed recipe for algae. The additional light energy which plants are unable to use without the lacking nutrients will quickly be consumed by algae. By raising the light higher, algae growth will be reduced significantly or eradicated while still providing aquatic plants with adequate lighting to photosynthesize. Echinodorus Hadi Red Pearl Echinodorus Hadi Red Pearl is a beautiful Amazon Sword variety, easily recognized by broad green leaves that are highlighted with reddish-pink hues. This aquatic plant is a great choice for adding subtle color to low tech planted tanks. Alternatively, sword plants are great focal plant choices for Wabi Kusa setups. Amazon Sword plants are a top choice for beginner aquascapers thanks to their easy care and adaptability. Hadi Red Pearl is considered one of the smaller species within the Echinodorus family, but like most in this group, it still grows significantly larger than many other aquarium plants. We recommend these plants for aquariums that offer plenty of room for healthy development. Aquarium sword plants grow best in nutrient-rich substrate, as they primarily absorb nutrients through their root systems. Support optimal growth with CO2 injection and a liquid plant fertilizer or root tabs that contain both macro and micronutrients. Propagating amazon sword plants can be done by gently separating plantlets from the mother and replanting into the soil! Common Name Echinodorus Hadi Red Pearl Care Easy Lighting Low to Medium CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant runners Growth Rate Slow to Moderate Height 4-8"

Finest bubbles produced Budget-friendly Durable shatterproof acrylic construction Air stone diffusers efficiently distribute oxygen in an aquarium. The NEO Air Stone Diffuser from Aquario features microscopically small holes resulting in very fine and thorough bubble diffusion. The microbubbles produced from its large surface area effectively increases the amount of dissolved oxygen in an aquarium tank. Sleek and sturdy, the Neo Air Stone Diffuser is made from transparent acrylic and is not easily broken when performing aquarium maintenance. Similar to other diffusers, users are able to place it in the corner of a planted aquarium securely with the provided suction cup. TIP: Soak the diffuser in water for 30 minutes before use to produce smaller bubbles. TIP: When bubble diffusion is slowed, soak it in bleach for 10 minutes and rinse with water thoroughly to ensure any residual bleach is gone.
