Neo Media by Aquario is a high-quality filter media that is constructed at high temperatures with natural materials sourced in Korea. Using advanced technology, Aquario's Neo Media provides fine, yet unobstructed large pores within the filter medium allowing a variety of beneficial bacteria to live and thrive. The generous space aids in smooth water flow and allows sufficient nutrients and oxygen to reach beneficial aquarium bacteria. This results in a thriving bacterial ecosystem inside of the Neo Media, keeping filtration cycles stable through thorough filtration and media longevity. Neo Media by Aquario goes through a grueling 5 step manufacturer process in order to produce high-quality aquarium tank filter media and is available in three different forms, making it suitable for any aquarium tank. HOW TO USE: Gently rinse with clean water 2-3 times. Do NOT wash excessively. PH changes can vary depending upon water source and objects inside the tank. NEO Media requires routine cleaning as do other filter media. Natural materials used results in varying shape and sizes. Keep out of the reach of children and pets. Specifications Media Type pH Recommendations SOFT Slightly acidic NEO Media SOFT has its own slight acidity. Recommended for slightly acidic environments. Perfect for: aquatic plants, shrimp, and tropical fish species such as Tetras, Rasboras, Angel Fish, Discus, Gourami, Bettas etc. NOTE: Formulated with dormant bacteria for quick aquarium cycling. PURE Neutral NEO Media PURE is a true neutral filter medium and has little effect on pH. Will not raise the pH of an acidic aquarium tank and will not lower the pH of an alkaline aquarium tank. Perfect for: all aquarium tanks and inhabitants. HARD Alkaline NEO Media HARD has an alkaline nature. Ideal for alkaline environments such as aquarium tanks containing brackish fish, African Cichlids, and marine life or corals. NOTE: Formulated with dormant bacteria for quick aquarium cycling.

Taxiphyllum 'Flame' AKA Flame Moss is rarer species of aquatic moss that is slowly gaining popularity within the planted tank community. This aquarium moss exhibits a creeping upright growth that resembles an underwater campfire or bonfire, earning its name, Flame Moss. Its growth pattern makes it perfect for using it on any horizontal surface such as small stones or at the base of aquarium driftwood. Flame Moss is similar to other aquatic mosses in that it requires very little care, is great for beginners and experts alike, and can adapt to a wide range of aquarium tank conditions. Aquarium moss makes for a wonderful safe haven by providing cover for shrimp and fry and can also cultivate areas for live food sources. Featuring a vibrant green hue, it makes a lovely addition to any planted tank. Flame Moss is a unique choice and although it doesn't require much, it will benefit from CO2 injection like all aquatic plant species.

Aquario Neo Soil is our top substrate recommendation for planted aquariums and is beautifully balanced for both beginners and experienced hobbyists growing advanced aquatic plants. Made from volcanic soil, Neo Soil buffers water to a slightly acidic pH, creating an environment ideal for fish health and aquatic plant growth. Its formula is optimized for lush plant growth, with several experiments showing the ability to grow carpeting aquarium plants like Hemianthus callitrichoides or Eleocharis ‘mini’ (hair grass varieties) in 60–90 days without additional fertilizers or additives. This premium aquasoil contains specialized bacteria, activated by water contact, that help break down pollutants that can build up within substrates. Its double-layer structure makes it lighter than other substrates and creates surface area for beneficial bacteria to reproduce in bulk. Overall, Aquario Neo Soil offers many benefits to planted tanks from nano aquariums to large show tanks, and is suitable for all skill levels. Neo Shrimp Soil shares the same core features but uses a gentler formula tailored for sensitive shrimp species. Designed specifically for dedicated shrimp tanks, the blend is adjusted to support healthy shell development and vivid coloration. The Shrimp version prioritizes stable water parameters and helps prevent sudden spikes that can be fatal for Sulawesi, Caridina, and Neocaridina shrimp. Neo Soil Highlights - No rinsing required! - When using this substrate, we recommend 30% water changes 1—3 times weekly after initial setup. - Avoid mixing your aquarium soils due to differences in composition and ingredients. - Results can vary depending on planted tank conditions, maintenance routines, aquarium plant choice and more. - We recommend CO2 injection and moderate lighting when using this substrate. Below is our Ultum Nature Systems 45U 9 gallon tank using Aquario Neo Soil: How much substrate do I need for my aquarium? The general rule of thumb is one 3L bag for every 5 gallons of water. If you have a large aquarium, one 10L bag for every 20 gallons of water is a good starting point. [Tank Length x Tank Depth x Desired Substrate Height (inches)] / 60 = Total liters of Controsoil required

Marsilea Crenata, commonly known as Dwarf Four-Leaf Clover, is a hardy aquarium plant recognized for its distinctive clover-like foliage. Its small, bright green leaves grow atop slender stalks, creating a soft, meadow-like appearance that brings a natural touch to the foreground of planted aquariums. One of the most interesting characteristics of Marsilea Crenata is how its appearance can vary depending on growing conditions. Emersed plants often develop taller stalks with recognizable clover-like leaves, while submerged growth may become shorter and more compact, sometimes producing chubby, rounded leaves. It spreads through creeping runners that produce new stalks and roots along the substrate. Over time, this growth can develop into a natural-looking carpet, although its height and density will vary with lighting and maintenance. Transition Note: Emersed-grown plants may lose some older foliage as they adjust to submerged conditions. New underwater growth may differ in height and leaf shape from the plant's original appearance.

Anubias Barteri Coffeefolia is a beautiful variant of the popular Anubias family that is characterized by its unique foliage. Its leaves feature a ribbed pattern with an offset coloration to make it pop when submerged in a planted aquarium tank. Similar to other Anubias, it's a great choice for beginners due to its easy care and overall hardiness. This aquatic plant is almost indestructible in any planted aquarium tank and will survive in a range of environments. However, if presented with optimal conditions, this plant will thrive. It's best when used as a mid-ground plant attached to stones or wood as an accent or centerpiece depending on tank size. We recommend Anubias Barteri Coffeefolia for larger sized aquariums and for those looking for a much more unique rhizome aquatic plant. Another added benefit of this aquatic plant is that herbivorous fish such as goldfish species will not munch on it! It's a flowering plant that grows best when the rhizome is attached to aquarium hardscape material such as driftwood or stone. Regular fertilization is favorable and low to medium lighting is sufficient as high lighting will promote the growth of algae on its leaves. CO2 is not required but promotes faster growth and robust leaves. Propagation is straightforward; simply cut or pull apart rhizomes to be reattached.

Anubias Round Leaf is a variant of Anubias Barteri that features rounded heart-shaped leaves. Commonly known as Anubias Golden Coin and Anubias Coin Leaf, this aquatic plant is similar in size and care to that of Anubias Barteri Nana. Compared to other Anubias, it is also very hardy and easy to keep making it ideal for all hobbyist levels. Anubias Round Leaf can adapt to almost any planted aquarium tank and will survive in a range of environments. If given optimal conditions, this aquatic plant thrives and makes a great addition to any planted aquarium tank. Also like other species of Anubias, Anubias Round Leaf is a slow grower, but patience is rewarded. As an epiphyte, this aquatic plant does best when attached to a hard surface such as aquarium driftwood or rocks. It can also be wedged into cracks available within the hardscape layout. Another added benefit of this plant is that herbivorous fish such as goldfish species rarely munch on it! It's a flowering plant that grows best when the rhizome is attached to hardscape material such as wood or stone. Regular fertilization is favorable and low to medium lighting is sufficient as high lighting will promote the growth of algae on its leaves. CO2 is not required but promotes faster growth and robust leaves. Propagation is straightforward; simply cut or pull apart rhizomes to be reattached.

Anubias Nana Thick Leaf is a less common variant of Anubias. This particular variation features small, rounded dark green foliage that is slightly wavy. Just like other Anubias, it is also very hardy and easy to keep making it ideal for all hobbyist levels. Anubias Thick Leaf will appreciate an aquarium tank with good circulation as this aquatic plant can be susceptible to algae growth on its leaves, but can adapt to almost any planted aquarium tank and will survive in a range of environments. If given optimal conditions, this aquatic plant will grow quicker and larger. Also like other species of Anubias, Anubias Thick Leaf is a slow grower, but patience is rewarded. As an epiphyte, this aquatic plant does best when attached to a hard surface such as aquarium driftwood or rocks. It can also be wedged into cracks available within the hardscape layout. Another added benefit of this plant is that herbivorous fish such as goldfish species rarely munch on it! It's a flowering plant that grows best when the rhizome is attached to hardscape material such as wood or stone. Regular fertilization is favorable and low to medium lighting is sufficient as high lighting will promote the growth of algae on its leaves. CO2 is not required but promotes faster growth and robust leaves. Propagation is straightforward; simply cut or pull apart rhizomes to be reattached.

Bolbitis Heudelotii is a beautiful aquatic plant that features sheer dark green foliage that exhibits a flowing growth pattern. Commonly known as African Water Fern, Bolbitis Heudelotii is increasing in popularity within the planted tank hobby but remains relatively uncommon and one of the more difficult aquatic plants to find. Bolbitis Heudelotii is generally undemanding but does prefer an aquarium tank with a higher flow as this aquatic plant's natural habitat provides a quick-moving current. Similar to its popular relative, Bolbitis Difformis Mini, Bolbitis Heudelotii should be attached to a hard surface such as aquarium driftwood or stone. Burying the rhizome will result in rot and the aquatic plant will not survive. Optimal conditions include CO2 injection, strong, flow, and slightly acidic water properties. As one of our personal favorites, Bolbitis Heudelotii provides a delicate and elegant appearance to a planted aquarium tank. We recommend using this aquatic plant in larger sized aquarium tanks, but it can also be used in a nano-sized aquarium tank as well given its slower growth pace. This aquatic plant would look beautiful paired with a darker aquarium driftwood along with other darker hued aquatic plants. If successful, Bolbitis Heudelotii propagates through the division of its rhizome. Gently separate and reattach.

The Twinstar Algae Inhibitor effectively reduces the growth of common algae, such as green algae and more, in planted aquariums. Safe for aquarium plants, freshwater fish, shrimp, and beneficial bacteria, the device works silently without disrupting balance or affecting life in the tank. It eliminates spores in their early stages, ultimately preventing further development before algae becomes visible to the eye. With algae growth reduced, aquatic plants take center stage. They are able to photosynthesize more efficiently and absorb nutrients, resulting in stronger, healthier growth that naturally outcompetes algae in the water column. Dense plant growth offers several benefits—not only is it rewarding to see plants thrive, but it also increases oxygen levels, supporting overall aquarium balance and health. For best results, we recommend installing this device during the setup of a new aquarium, when algae is non-existent, for a boosted jumpstart. Comparative tests with Glossostigma elatinoides and Rotala indica showed growth increases of up to 50% in Glosso and 40% in Rotala. This listing includes 15-16LB per order. Black Lava Rock is a popular aquascaping stone that is commonly used in all types of freshwater aquarium setups. Loved for its porous texture, it’s arguably one of the best rocks to pair with epiphytic aquarium plants and mosses. You’ll often see easy aquatic plants like Anubias, Bucephalandra, moss, or ferns attached to this type of aquarium hardscape. Our favorites are Mini Pellia and Fissidens Fontanus! Its lightweight density makes it easy to stack or balance when creating structured aquascape layouts. And because it’s relatively light, you’ll get more volume per pound compared to denser stones. It works wonderfully on its own or as a base foundation underneath your favorite aquarium wood. It is also very easy to break down if you need smaller pieces for layout accents or nano aquariums. Overall, Lava Rock is versatile and offers many benefits. Aside from its use as a hardscape layout material, it’s also great for cultivating a healthy colony of beneficial bacteria for better aquarium health and balance.

Cryptocoryne Pink Flamingo is an interesting aquatic plant that's known for its signature pink-red color and ruffled leaves. Easily a focal point in any planted tank, its new growth is vibrant and gradually deepens in tone as it matures, creating a display of varying shades on a single plant. This makes it a wonderful pick for aquarium hobbyists who enjoy oddball plants or species with unique character. Like most Cryptocoryne, C. Pink Flamingo can be susceptible to melt during its initial adjustment period and may require a bit of extra care during this time. Allow it to establish strong roots in a nutrient-rich aquasoil before attempting to propagate or relocate. Once established, Cryptocoryne plants are rather hardy and adaptable. While it isn't required, this aquatic plant will enjoy and experience much better growth in a planted tank that is fully established with CO2 injection and high lighting.

Marsilea Angustifolia is a carpeting foreground aquatic plant choice. It is well-known for its foliage that resembles a four-leaf clover. Its smaller and narrower size makes this aquatic plant perfect for nano planted aquariums. Once the plant is submerged, its growth pattern is susceptible to change depending upon the planted aquarium tank's parameters. New leaves sprouted are brown coloration and should not be mistaken for rotting or dead leaves as they will gain color upon maturing. Marsilea Angustifolia is generally hardy and easy to keep and grow. It can adapt to most aquarium conditions and will spread steadily if given optimal conditions. This plant grows by spreading runners horizontally throughout the substrate. Lighting and CO2 injection are essential in keeping the growth short and compact. Propagation is simple, trim along the runners and replant. There is a huge selection of plant species that have been propagated this way. This is truly the best option for those who want absolutely zero unwanted pests, algae and pesticides. This makes them perfect for shrimp keepers and any planted tank enthusiasts alike. NOTE: It is important to remove the tissue culture agar gel before planting. Simply wash the gel away, divide, and plant.

Anubias Minima is a popular aquatic plant that is frequently used in all types of planted aquariums. Like other Anubias it can grow in a multitude of environments varying from aquariums to terrariums. Anubias Minima features long, slender leaves with a deep green coloration loved by planted tank hobbyists. This plant is suitable as a midground and background aquatic plant as the leaves are capable of growing quite long. This Anubias variant is a flowering plant that grows best when the rhizome is attached to a hard surface such as wood or stone. It benefits from consistent fertilization but light requirements are minimal as its leaves are susceptible to algae growth when placed under high lighting. CO2 is optional, but can promote faster growth and robust leaves when used.

Echinodorus Bleheri, commonly referred to as Amazon Sword is a bright green aquatic plant that is known for its behemoth size. Echinodorus Bleheri is generally easy to keep and great for beginners. Aquarium Sword species are heavy root feeders and so long as nutrient-rich quality aquarium substrate is provided, it will do well in a wide range of planted aquarium tank conditions. As mentioned, this aquatic plant can grow quite large and regular pruning will be necessary for allowing light to filter through to the aquatic plant's bottom leaves. We recommend this aquatic plant for beginners as well as experienced hobbyists who have larger aquarium tanks suitable for its size. Propagation is simple. Separate and replant.

Alternanthera Reineckii Rosanervig is anything but subtle! Its leaves can develop beautifully saturated shades of hot pink, magenta, and deep red, contrasted by a signature pattern of lighter veins running throughout the foliage. When grown in a stable environment, this contrast becomes especially pronounced, giving individual leaves almost as much visual interest as the plant's overall color. AR Rosanervig develops a relatively compact, bushy form compared to larger Alternanthera varieties. Regular trimming encourages offshoots and denser growth, while stronger lighting helps maintain a more compact form. Under insufficient lighting or inconsistent nutrient availability, growth may become leggier and its vivid coloration more subdued. Its stems can also be somewhat delicate, so handle them carefully when planting, trimming, or replanting cuttings. Strong lighting, consistent fertilization, and CO2 injection support the intense pigmentation this variety is known for. Given the right conditions, Rosanervig can easily become one of the most vividly colored plants in an aquascape. Common Name AR Rosanervig Care Easy to Moderate Lighting Medium to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Midground Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 4-12"

Isoetes Velata Var. Sicula is still a relatively rare aquatic plant in the aquarium hobby due to its more complex process of propagation by spores. Also known as a quillwort, Isoetes Velata Var. Sicula is one of the few that is suitable for use as an aquatic plant in an aquarium setting. In the wild, Isoetes Velata Var. Sicula is found in wetlands, each with varying conditions such as cold bodies of water with little nutrition. Because of this, Isoetes Velata Var. Sicula is highly adaptable to a wide range of planted aquarium tank conditions, but it also a slow grower. Its foliage is compact and a rich green coloration that stands up, curved or straight. Not too much information is readily available regarding Isoetes Velata Var. Sicula. When used in aquaria, it would make a beautiful background aquatic plant choice in a variety of planted aquarium tanks. A strict fertilizer dosing regime and CO2 are provided in their holding tanks.

Myriophyllum Elatinoides Mini is a beautiful aquatic plant that is easy to recognize by its bright green wispy, feather-like foliage. It is the perfect miniature aquarium stem plant for aquascapes that need a decorative focal point. It is small in size, making it suitable for nano planted tanks or as another addition to larger planted aquariums. Give it a good spot under moderate to high lighting and it will quickly produce small fluffy bushes. CO2 injection, nutrient rich aquasoil and regular dosing with a liquid aquatic plant fertilizer will improve growing speed and form. Myriophyllum Elatinoides 'Mini' is similar to Aquaticum (Parrot's Feather), but in a miniture size! Common Name Myrio Elatinoides 'Mini' / Watermilfol Care Difficult Lighting Medium to High CO2 Required Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Fast Height 6-12"

Add intricate pattern and rich color to your planted aquarium with Ludwigia Senegalensis. Previously known as Ludwigia sp. 'Guinea', this distinctive stem plant develops patterned foliage with lighter veining that contrasts beautifully against deeper red tones under strong aquarium lighting. It can be grown submerged or emersed, developing upright stems underwater and a more creeping growth habit above the surface. Although many Ludwigia are known for being beginner-friendly, Senegalensis is quite the opposite. This more demanding species requires strong lighting, CO2 injection, and consistent fertilization to maintain healthy growth and its characteristic coloration. Give individual stems enough space for light to reach the lower foliage, as inadequate lighting or nutrient deficiencies can quickly affect the plant's appearance.

listings.commonName: UNS Cube Glass Aquarium Stabilizing Tank Mat
listings.description: Stabilizing leveling mats are essential and strongly advised when having a planted aquarium tank. Fully filled planted tanks are quite heavy and most, if not all, the weight is placed on the bottom glass panel resulting in a good amount of stress. Premium rimless glass aquarium tanks are constructed to withstand this so long as the surface they are placed on is level. Unfortunately, this is not true in most cases and the use of a leveling mat is crucial to help offset and absorb surface imperfections that have the potential to crack the bottom glass panel via stress points. Stabilizing tank mats are cost-effective and prevent the worst from happening! These aquarium tank mats are made from premium, absorbent material to ensure your planted aquarium tank doesn't slip, slide or move during or after setup. Tested to withstand considerable turbulence, these aquarium stabilizing tank mats by Ultum Nature Systems are the perfect solution for your planted aquarium. They are sleek, cut to size and ready to place beneath most aquarium tanks. Enjoy peace of mind knowing your planted tank and its inhabitants are safe on their stand, counter, nightstand or console. Mat thickness is 5MM. TIP: These stabilizing mats will fit other rimless aquariums in similar sizing and may also be cut to size. These leveling mats are not meant to be used over small gaps. Please ensure your stand can fully hold your aquarium with no part of the aquarium hanging over the edge. Cutting any excess foam material will keep your setup looking clean! Be sure to use a sharp blade and handle with caution if the mat needs to be trimmed further. listings.commonName: UNS Pro CO2 Dual Stage Regulator
listings.description: The UNS Pro CO2 Dual Stage Regulator is designed for hobbyists looking for a long-term, professional-grade CO2 solution for planted aquariums. Featuring dual gauges for monitoring both working pressure and remaining cylinder pressure, it makes it easy to track CO2 levels and anticipate when a cylinder is running low. Included manifold blocks allow a single CO2 cylinder to supply multiple planted aquariums, making the Pro Regulator an ideal choice for expanding aquarium collections, fish rooms, and advanced aquascaping systems. Best For - Medium to large planted aquariums - Long-term CO2 systems - Hobbyists using refillable CO2 cylinders - Multi-aquarium setups - Aquascapers looking for more control and consistency Why Choose the UNS Pro Regulator? Dual-Stage Reliability: Dual-gauge regulators are sometimes referred to as dual-stage thanks to an extra fail-safe stage that prevents “end-of-tank dump” (a sudden release of CO2 when a cylinder is running low). This built-in feature keeps CO2 levels more stable and helps prevent sudden fluctuations. Expandable for Multiple Aquariums: The included bubble counter manifolds allow CO2 to be distributed across multiple planted aquariums from a single cylinder. Additional manifolds can be added as your aquarium collection grows (we recommend up to 8 splits). Compatible with Standard Refillable Cylinders: Designed for use with CGA-320 CO2 cylinders ranging from 2.5LB to 20LB, providing a practical long-term solution with fewer refills and lower operating costs compared to disposable options. Beautiful Design: Finished in an anodized Space Grey, the Pro Regulator offers a clean appearance that complements planted aquarium equipment and cabinetry. The UNS Pro Dual Stage Regulator is intended for hobbyists ready to invest in a dedicated pressurized CO2 system. While larger than cartridge-based alternatives, it offers greater stability, longer refill intervals, and the flexibility to expand over time. Product Compatibility - Standard CGA-320 CO2 cylinders (UNS Pro Cylinders) - CO2-proof tubing - Aquarium diffusers - Inline diffusers - Bubble counters What’s Included - UNS Pro CO2 Dual Stage Regulator - CGA-320 Adapter - 2 Bubble Counter Manifolds - Power Adapter - Assorted O-Rings (extra replacements included) - Installation Tools Learn about other CO2 regulators and find the best solution for your planted aquarium. Titan 1 by Ultum Nature Systems is a premium planted aquarium LED lighting solution. It is a beautiful, high-rendering RBG LED system for planted aquarium tanks that will light up an aquascape with unparalleled views of aquatic plants and freshwater fish and shrimp species. Equipped with 200 of the latest technology RGB LED bulbs and an output of 90 watts, Titan 1 by Ultum Nature Systems provides the optimal spectrum necessary for growing lush and healthy aquatic plants while intensifying the myriad of hues found in a planted aquarium tank that is displayed by freshwater fish, shrimp, and aquatic plants. With a wide body design, Ultum Nature System’s Titan 1 is able to provide a uniform spread of light to an entire planted aquarium tank. This ensures that all aquatic plants are able to absorb light efficiently and effectively, promoting even and healthy growth. Coming in at a mere 5.3LBs, Titan 1 also sports lightweight and slim measurements while remaining a powerful unit, making it suitable to hang from a fixture or ceiling. It’s paired with a reinforced waterproof wire that is unobtrusive to the eye while establishing a safe, secure power supply to the main lighting unit. Available in brushed black aluminum and brushed silver aluminum, both colorways are an eye-catching finish that's sure to complement interior design within the home while fusing seamlessly with a planted aquarium tank and providing an essential contribution to the health and success of a nature aquarium tank. Each unit is built with precision using high-grade materials such as aircraft grade aluminum guaranteeing beautiful aesthetic, durability and product longevity that is suitable for everyday use. Modernly designed with purposefully exposed heat dissipation fins, Titan 1 allows for maximum airflow ensuring the aquarium tank below remains at a stable temperature. With efficient heat dissipation and LED technology, Ultum Nature System's Titan 1 emanates minimal heat when compared to dated lighting sources such as metal halides and can be boasted as an energy saving unit. There are many advantages of utilizing an RGB wavelength for a freshwater planted aquarium tank. An optimal spectrum ensures that all colors found in a planted tank are highlighted equally and evenly. Red wavelengths are meant to brighten red toned aquatic plant species such as Ludwigias, Rotalas and Alternanthera species. This also applies to boldly colored freshwater shrimp and fish! With green being one of the most important colors in achieving an ethereal underwater world, green wavelengths are essential for enhancing the green seen in most aquatic plants. Last but certainly not least, blue wavelengths help to encourage the onset of photosynthesis in aquatic plants and aid in producing the appearance of crystal clear water. One unit will illuminate a 60-90CM aquarium tank beautifully. For aquarium tanks larger, two or more units are advised to ensure that all aquatic plants receive sufficient lighting. The recommended hanging height is at least 12 inches above an aquarium tank and the suspension wires included are 38 inches long.

These clear suction cups are designed for aquarium tank use and have small clips attached to the back making them perfect for holding airline tubing and pressure proof CO2 tubing against the aquarium tank. These aquarium suction cups will adhere to glass aquarium tanks and acrylic tanks. You will receive 6 aquarium suction cups in one order.

Blyxa Aubertii, sometimes referred to as Roundfruit Blyxa, is a true aquatic plant species that are normally found in a wide variety of habitats such as rice paddies and streams. Blyxa Aubertii is still relatively rare despite being used in the planted tank hobby for quite some time and is most readily available through trading. This aquatic plant is generally easier to keep and hardier when compared to its more known counterpart, Blyxa Japonica. However, Blyxa Aubertii still does best when provided with quality aquarium LED lighting, CO2 injection, quality aquarium soil, and a regular fertilizer regime. If dosed with iron, this aquatic plant also has the potential to gain deep reddish tones but should be handled with care as it has fragile leaves. We recommend using this aquatic plant in conjunction with grass-like plants such as Cyperus Helferi, Potamogeton Gayi and more. Propagation is simple and can be done by separating side shoots that grow from the mother aquatic plant and replanting into quality aquarium soil. A strict fertilizer dosing regime and CO2 are provided in their holding tanks.

Eriocaulon Quinquangulare is a relatively new aquatic plant species introduced to the aquarium hobby and can be quite difficult to keep. Its color pattern makes it highly coveted, sporting a maroon reddish base that lightens to green shades further up each individual leaf. Notorious for being more difficult to keep, Eriocaulon Quinquangulare is no exception and is recommended to be kept by experienced hobbyists only. Eriocaulon Quinquangulare requires high lighting, nutrient-dense aquarium soil and CO2 injection to thrive. Its growth pattern looks like dense little tufts that resemble grass, making it a perfect midground aquatic plant choice or at the foot of stones such as Ryuoh or Seiryu in an Iwagumi style aquascape layout. Fairly sensitive to shipment, Eriocaulon Quinquangulare is often grown in its emersed form as it tends to be hardier in this form. If successful in keeping Eriocaulon Quinquangulare, propagation can be done simply by splitting the plant gently from the adult plant and rewards will be worth the risk. Common Name Eriocaulon Quinquangulare Red Care Advanced Lighting Moderate to High CO2 Required Aquascape Placement Midground Propagation Separate and replant Growth Rate Slow Size 4-7”

Eriocaulon Dong Ha is a rare sight in the planted tank community. Difficult to obtain, there is little-known information about this aquatic plant. Being part of the Eriocaulon family, Eriocaulon Dong Ha is not an exception to the shared characteristics and can be quite difficult to keep. This aquatic plant has a finnicky nature and requires particular care in order to properly grow and thrive. Soft water, nutrient-dense aquarium soil, quality aquarium LED lighting, CO2 injection and a consistent supply of micro and macronutrients are key to its survival and growth. Eriocaulon Dong Ha possesses features similar to E. Vietnam and E. Polaris, but is unique in its own right. Erio Dong Ha sports a small size, narrow leaves and the classic "tuft" look with a beautiful green coloration. If able to grow it, this aquatic plant makes a beautiful addition as a midground aquatic plant choice in planted aquarium tanks. Common Name Eriocaulon Dong Ha Care Advanced Lighting High CO2 Required Suggested Placement Midground Propagation Separate and replant Growth Rate Moderate Height 3-5" Our bunched stem plants are all kept and grown in high-quality substrate by Marfied Controsoil . A strict fertilizer dosing regime and CO2 are provided in their holding tanks.

Mini Pellia (Riccardia chamedryfolia) is a popular moss-like aquatic plant for planted tanks and aquascaping. Its compact, bushy growth and deep green color are an awesome alternative to standard aquarium moss. Like aquatic moss, it can be attached to driftwood, stone, or other hardscape and will eventually secure itself, providing a unique look. Though a slow grower, Mini Pellia rewards patience with dense, cushion-like mats that offer beautiful texture in aquascapes. It’s one of our favorites, and we notice freshwater shrimp and fish enjoy it too! It is suitable for all aquarium sizes, from nano aquariums to larger planted tanks. This aquarium plant does best in moderate lighting and stable water parameters. For fluffier growth, provide it with CO₂ and watch it puff up! Few things beat a healthy patch of Mini Pellia! Approximate size per portion is 3" x 3" attached to stainless steel. Common Name Riccardia Chamedryfolia / Coral Moss Care Easy Lighting Low to Medium CO2 Optional Suggested Placement Attached to rock or wood Propagation Cut or pull apart Growth Rate Varies Height Varies

Echinodorus Magdalenensis is another variant in the Echinodorus family that is closely related to Echinodorus Quadricostatus. It is commonly referred to as Helanthium Qudricostatus Var. Magdalenensis as well. The best way to differentiate this aquatic plants is through the appearance of their seeds and natural habitat. Echinodorus Magdalenensis features a light green hue on its elongated foliage that is shaped like a sword. This aquatic plant is fairly hardy and makes a great addition to the mid-ground of a planted aquarium tank. It can also be utilized as a foreground aquatic plant choice in large aquarium tanks as Echinodorus Magdalenensis has the potential to form dense tufts if given the chance. Although this aquatic plant can adapt to a wide range of aquarium tank parameters, Echinodorus Magdalenensis will show deficiencies through yellowing leaves if the lighting is too weak or the substrate isn’t nutritious enough. Echinodorus Magdalenensis is a flowering species and has the ability to produce small, white flowers above the water’s surface if the care provided is optimal. Common Name Echinodorus Magdalenensis Care Easy to Moderate Lighting Low to Medium CO2 Optional Suggested Placement Varies Propagation Trim stems and plant Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 3-7+"

These aquarium lily pipes are constructed from surgical grade stainless steel providing a sleek appearance that is extremely durable and resistant to scratches and unsightly rust during maintenance. In addition to a solid build, these stainless steel lily pipes have the ability to withstand acidic and alkaline water parameters and will keep their shape through normal wear and tear. Unlike their glass lily pipe counterparts, stainless steel lily pipes are usually lesser prone to algae coverage. The inflow pipe is constructed with thin slits ensuring that aquarium water stays clean from large debris while keeping smaller freshwater fish and shrimp species safe from being vacuumed into an aquarium filter. Stainless steel lily pipes provide ample flow and circulation ensuring the aquarium tank is aerated properly. listings.commonName: Ultum Nature Systems Bar Light Hanging Kit
listings.description: BAR by Ultum Nature Systems offers a simple solution for all your light-hanging needs. Made from rust-resistant stainless steel, the unit is lightweight and installs easily without tools. It clamps directly onto your tank’s rim and can be used to turn any aquarium light into a pendant-style fixture. BAR can be used individually for puck-style aquarium LEDs (such as Kessil lights) or in pairs for standard aquarium lighting. Designed specifically for aquariums, this light hanging kit combines a simple design with reliable, straightforward performance. Proper lighting is essential for a healthy planted aquarium yet is often overlooked. The UNS BAR allows precise height and depth adjustments, enabling aquascapers to fine-tune light intensity and coverage for their specific setup. This control helps ensure aquatic plants receive the right amount of light without overexposure. Light that is too intense can lead to unwanted algae growth, especially when CO2 and nutrients are limited or imbalanced. With this light hanging kit, raising the fixture can effectively reduce algae while still providing enough output for photosynthesis. Easily achieve optimal lighting to support healthy plant growth and maintain a balanced planted aquarium. Seiryu Stone is one of the most popular hardscape stones for planted aquariums. Easily recognized by its signature bluish-grey hue, these natural rocks feature jagged edges and dramatic grooves that make them perfect for aquascaping. Seiryu Stone accent rocks include smaller pieces that are great for creating a more natural and balanced look. Try placing them at the base of your hardscape to mimic natural landscapes. They're easy to work with and add finishing touches that complete forest-style, Iwagumi, or any layout that features sand as the primary substrate. They can also be used to tie aquatic mosses or attach plants like Anubias and Bucephalandra, adding a mature, established look to newly planted tanks! Accent stones are without limit and can be used in both large aquarium setups and planted nano tanks! Each order contains 3LB of Seiryu Rock ranging from 1-3 inches.

Amazon Wood combines the textured surfaces of several popular aquarium driftwoods into one versatile hardscape material. Characterized by natural knots, grooves, and varied branching structures, it provides an ideal surface for aquatic mosses and rhizome plants while offering moderately sized pieces that work well for medium and large aquascapes or planted aquarium layouts with protruding wood pieces. Its varied brown coloration creates natural contrast within planted aquariums, while the shape of each piece makes it easy to combine multiple sections into a cohesive hardscape. For aquascapers looking to create larger driftwood layouts without sacrificing natural appearance, Amazon Wood offers an excellent balance of texture, scale, and flexibility. Best For - Aquariums 10 gallons and larger - Nature-style aquascapes - Rhizome and moss-covered hardscape pieces Natural Variation Amazon Wood is a natural wood and each piece is unique. Variations in shape, structure, coloration, and overall dimensions are normal and part of what makes each piece one of a kind. Custom size and shape requests cannot be guaranteed. Used commonly within the aquarium hobby, these heat packs are great for ensuring that your aquatic plants, aquarium fish and more stay warm and safe during transit. Heatpacks warm up quickly and are ready to use within 3-5 minutes of simply opening the package. They do not require any shaking or kneading and last for the time advertised. One heat pack warms up substantially and can increase the temperature around 20 degrees Fahrenheit in a 1cu. ft. box. For each additional heat pack added, the temperature raises in 10-degree increments. These heat packs are also eco-friendly and their contents are biodegradable. Perfect for those who live in colder areas. Available in 40 hours and 72-hour packs. Heat pack brand and packaging may vary. NOTE : When adding to cart, please specify if you would like us to activate the heat pack for your order, or if you would like it unopened. If no note is added, the heat pack will be used.

Staurogyne Sp. Bihar is an aquatic plant that was originally mistaken as a Hygrophila species. Upon seeing its flowering characteristics, it was suggested that this aquatic plant belonged to the Staurogyne genus. When grown submerged, it features foliage that is slightly lobed, resembling an aquarist’s favorite, Hygrophila Pinnatifida. Staurogyne Bihar’s coloration varies with a mix of olive greens to reddish brown hues. More readily available in the aquarium hobby here in the states, this aquatic plant is still considered to be quite rare and is almost non-existent in European countries as well. Common Name Staurogyne Bihar Care Moderate to Difficult Lighting Medium to High CO2 Required Suggested Placement Midground Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 4-7”

Black Mountain Seiryu Stone is a wonderful stone commonly used for aquascaping. Similar to its popular relative, Seiryu Stone, Black Mountain Seiryu earns its name due to its charcoal grey, almost black color with blueish undertones. Black Mountain Seiryu Stone also offers similar texture and characteristics such as grooves, interesting shapes, and more making it a good pair when using brightly colored aquarium plants. Application is very versatile and like normal Seiryu, Black Mountain Seiryu works wonderfully alone or paired with aquarium driftwood in planted aquarium tanks.

Anubias Broad White is an extremely rare aquatic plant variant of the very popular Anubias family. There is still little information known about this particular aquatic plant variant. It is also known by other names such as Anubias White. Because this variant of Anubias is fairly difficult to get and not always readily available, it makes the list of highly sought after aquatic plants for planted tank enthusiasts. Anubias Broad White features beautiful mutations that result in lighter greens to almost completely white, hence the nickname. Anubias Broad White is extremely similar to Anubias Nana Snow White, but the leaves are slightly larger and equally provides an uncommon aesthetic in planted tanks while remaining just as easy to care for as the more common species such as Anubias Nana Petite. With patience and consistent care, this aquatic plant will also produce marbled white leaves that will contrast beautifully amongst other aquatic plant choices. This aquatic plant is suitable as a midground plant choice. Anubias Broad White will benefit from fertilization and quality light. It is still a slow grower and care should be taken as its leaves are susceptible to algae growth when placed under too high lighting. CO2 is optional, but recommended as it will help encourage faster growth and robust leaves.

Originating from Italy, Rotala Rotundifolia Orange Juice is a created mutation by propagating specific aquatic stems under particular conditions. Similar in leaf shape and growth characteristics to its popular counterpart, Rotala Rotundifolia, Rotala Rotundifolia Orange Juice displays varying shades of orange hues, earning its name. Like all Rotala species, Rotala Orange Juice can be grown submerged or emersed. When growing this aquatic stem plant emerged, its usual thin pointed leaves begin to fatten up and round off. Whether this aquatic plant is grown submerged or emersed, Rotala Rotundifolia Orange Juice provides beautiful contrast against green aquatic plant species. Like all red, pink and orange plants, this aquatic stem plant does well when provided with high lighting, CO2, and fertilization dosing. High iron supplementation will increase the intensity of the plant. If kept under proper conditions, Rotala Rotundifolia Orange Juice is a fast growing plant and will require consistent pruning to prevent the bottom leaves from dying off due to lack of lighting and to keep it growing lush. Common Name Rotala Orange Juice Rotala Rotundifolia Orange Juice Care Moderate Lighting Medium to High CO2 Optional Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Fast Height 15-30 "

Ammania 'Bonsai' is characterized by dense and compact growth pattern. Dependent upon lighting provided, its tips can achieve a reddish coloration. It is also often described as a moderately growing cousin of Bacopa Caroliniana. When frequent trimming is performed, Ammania Bonsai grows dense and bushy and provides a beautiful display in any planted aquarium tank. Ammania Bonsai can thrive in a wide range of tank conditions. However, to bring the best out of this plant, CO2, rich fertilizer and substrate is recommended. Nymphoides hydrophylla ‘Taiwan’ is a fast-growing aquatic plant known for its bright, translucent green leaves and distinct lily-like appearance. Originating from regions in Asia and Africa, this species develops a dense rosette with stems and leaves sprouting upward, creating fullness and gentle, flowing motion in planted aquariums. As it matures, it can quickly fill out space with its wide, rounded leaves, producing a lush, layered appearance. It easily becomes a focal point in an aquascape, contrasting well against fine-textured plants while adding movement and some natural enrichment for aquatic life. Once established, regular maintenance is recommended. Thinning older and surface leaves will help prevent excessive shading and encourage healthy development below. Propagation is simple, as new plantlets naturally form from mature leaves—gently separate and replant or share with fellow aquascapers. Pairs Well With - Fine-leaf stem plants to create varying textures and contrast - Aquatic mosses and epiphytes to soften surrounding areas - Branching driftwood to support natural, flowing appearance - Wabi Kusa inspired aquascapes with a large, single focal specimen

Lagenandra Meeboldii Red is a beautiful aquatic plant that is commonly compared to Cryptocoryne species due to similar appearance through medium-sized, broad leaves. Lagenandra Meeboldii Red is fairly hardy but does require quality aquarium lighting to develop a rich coloration. If provided with optimal conditions, this aquatic plant will grow relatively wide and will fill up a good amount of space within a planted aquarium tank with beautiful foliage ranging in shades of greens, oranges, reddish-bronze, and even violet tones. New leaves on this aquatic plant are pale pink and will slowly color up as the aquatic plant matures. Lagenandra Meeboldii Red does not produce underground runners but has a thick rhizome. Propagation can be done by gently splitting and replanting into quality aquarium soil. Common Name Lagenandra Meeboldii Red Lagenandra Meeboldii Pink Care Moderate Lighting Medium to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Attach to wood or stone Propagation Separate rhizome Growth Rate Moderate Height 4"+

Heteranthera Zosterifolia, commonly known as Stargrass, is a beautiful aquarium plant that exhibits dense, bushy growth of its bright green foliage. A great midground aquatic plant choice, Heteranthera Zoserifolia does best when planted in groups and provided with high-quality aquarium lighting. This aquatic plant grows extremely quick when it is placed in optimal conditions and will require frequent trimming to ensure that lower parts of the aquatic plant are not shaded from the light. Consistent trimming will encourage the beautiful bushy growth that is favored by planted tank enthusiasts. Heteranthera Zosterifolia also has the potential to grow emersed and will occasionally sprout small blue flowers above the water's surface. Propagation is also fairly simple and can be done by separating and replanting into a quality aquarium substrate.

Myriophyllum Guyana is a beautiful aquarium plant that is still relatively difficult to obtain in the planted tank hobby. This smaller aquatic plant species, like other Myriophyllum, features wispy, feather-like foliage that retains a vivid green hue. If provided with optimal conditions such as quality aquarium tank lighting, nutrient dense aquarium soil and a regular fertilizing routine, Myriophyllum Guyana branches willingly and has the capability to produce a dense and lush bush. Its moderate growth pace also makes this aquatic plant a perfect choice for nano-sized planted aquarium tanks as it will be much easier to keep under control when compared to fast-growing aquatic stem plants. Great for a decorative focal point, we recommend using Myriophyllum Guyana as a beautiful midground in a larger planted aquarium tank or as the background in a nano-sized planted aquarium tank.

Ranalisma Rostratum is a small aquatic plantain that is still very rare and seldom seen in the planted tank hobby. With the ability to grow emersed and submerged, Ranalisma Rostratum displays complete opposite forms dependent upon the environment it is grown in. When grown emersed, this aquatic plant sprouts small, spoon-shaped leaves that almost resemble a member of the Echinodorus family. It will also produce small white flowers that bear little hedgehog shaped fruit forms. However, when placed underwater, Ranalisma Rostratum transforms into almost a grass-like aquatic plant that will send bright green runners, producing an aquatic lawn that is close in appearance to aquatic plants like Helanthium Tenellum. In order to provide the best conditions, high aquarium lighting, CO2 injection, fertilizer routine, and nutrient-rich aquarium substrate should be utilized. Just like other rosette species, this particular aquatic plant is beautiful in groups or by itself. Propagation is also fairly simple and can be done by separating via the runners and replanting into a quality aquarium substrate. Common Name Ranalisma Rostratum Ranalisma Rostrata Care Easy to Moderate Lighting Medium to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Foreground to Midground Propagation Trim and plant runners Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 3-6” Our potted aquatic plants are kept under strict fertilizer dosing regimes and are provided with CO2 injection in their holding tanks.

Desert Stone is a planted aquarium tank hardscape choice in the aquarium hobby. Similar in appearance to its popular counterpart, Dragon Ohko Stone, Desert Stone features a golden orangeish coloration along with small craters here and there that are spread across the surface but are not as distinct or consistent. Desert stone is not as fragile and crumbly when compared to Dragon stone but doesn't lack any jagged texture and characteristics making it the perfect choice for planted tank enthusiasts looking for a similar look who don't particularly love the dust that comes with Ohko Stone. Desert Stone's texture is similar to Black Lava Rock and Icelandic Lava Rock making it a great canvas for aquatic plants such as Anubias, Bucephalandra and moss species to anchor themselves to.

Lindernia Rotundifolia, commonly known as Roundleaf Lindernia, is a small aquatic stem plant found in tropical regions. Recognized for its rounded foliage, bright green coloration, and upright growth habit, this undemanding plant is a great choice for beginners. Lindernia Rotundifolia can also be grown emersed, where it may produce small bluish-white flowers and spread readily under favorable conditions. Similar in appearance to Bacopa Monnieri, this aquarium stem plant looks especially cute when planted in groups, creating neat bushes of bright green foliage. Its compact growth makes it a great midground choice in planted aquariums or a background plant in nano-sized setups.

Staurogyne Porto Velho has its place in the European aquarium hobby but is still generally rare within other countries. Hailing from South America, Staurogyne Porto Velho is a beautiful aquatic plant that features narrow leaves with a pointed tip. Its coloration is a beautiful greyish-green hue with light hints of a purple shade. Staurogyne Porto Velho grows moderately when provided with optimal conditions and will develop a creeping growth pattern when provided with quality aquarium lighting, CO2 injection, and a nutrient dense aquarium soil. Comparable to its popular counterpart, Staurogyne Repens, Staurogyne Porto Velho is quickly becoming a new favorite within the planted tank hobby. It is suitable as a midground aquatic plant choice or even a foreground aquatic plant as it has the potential to spread nicely and low to the substrate level. Staurogyne Porto Velho will also be referred to as Hygrophila sp. Roraima at times, but they are the same aquatic plant. With the ability to grow submerged and emersed, Staurogyne Porto Velho is a great choice for anyone who wants a lovely pop of green in their respective aquascape setups. Add bold color and fine texture to the background of your planted aquarium with Ludwigia Inclinata 'Cuba'. This classic stem plant develops long stems lined with narrow leaves that can display striking shades of orange and red when grown submerged, creating a colorful contrast against broader green foliage. Ludwigia Inclinata 'Cuba' can grow quickly and develop into a substantial group, making it best suited for the background of larger planted aquariums where its stems have room to spread. Its growth can naturally angle outward rather than remaining completely vertical, while regular trimming encourages branching and helps maintain a fuller, more controlled shape.

Hygrophila lancea ‘Araguaia’ is a distinctive stem plant known for its narrow, textured leaves and deep reddish-brown to purple tones. Often sought after for its unique form, it brings a different character to planted aquariums compared to more traditional stem plants, with a slightly creeping growth pattern and tightly spaced foliage. As it develops, it forms compact clusters of angled stems that can be shaped into dense, bushy hedges with regular trimming. Its fine, structured appearance adds contrast against other plants while introducing additional texture an aquascape. When grown under optimal conditions, its coloration intensifies, producing richer red and purple hues. Hygrophila benefits from stable, nutrient-rich environments and responds best to higher lighting and CO2 injection. While it can be slightly sensitive during the initial establishment phase, consistent care will encourage steady growth and branching. Pruning and replanting healthy stems helps maintain a compact, controlled form in the midground. Its color and texture can be used to break up green-dominant layouts or create layered transitions between foreground and background plants.

Eleocharis Belem, also known simply as Hair Grass, Japanese Hair Grass and a multitude of other names, is a carpeting aquarium plant that has been used for years! Typically used to grow a carpet for aquascaping, this form of hair grass is similar to Eleocharis Parvula, but with a slightly curved tips. Its low growth is compact and great for nano aquariums to long tanks and more. Hair grass is considered an easy care aquatic plant and is suitable for low tech planted aquariums or setups without CO2. While it isn't required, adding CO2 will significantly boost growing rate and plant thickness! So, if you want an aquarium carpet fast, consider adding it. Additional care includes good tank lighting, nutritious aquasoil and a liquid aquatic plant fertilizer. If you're using sand, consider adding some root tabs to provide micro and macronutrients. Planting is easy and can be done by separating into small portions and using aquascaping tweezers! Space each portion an inch or so apart halfway into the aquarium substrate. Once your hairgrass is mature, it will need regular trims to maintain low, uniform growth! Hair grass plants grow through runners but Eleocharis Belem isn't as invasive and will be easier to maintain. The image below features an Ultum Nature Systems 75P planted aquarium tank utilizing Eleocharis Belem.

Several pieces of Pacific Wood and Elephant Skin Stone were strategically stacked to create levels of depth within a 20C by Ultum Nature Systems. Measuring out to be a 2.1 gallon cube aquarium tank, the 20C doesn't give ample room, but we love a challenge and this aquarium tank is the perfect solution for tight spaces! Utilizing higher substrate levels, we formed fine natural sand into a steep slope before placing our hardscape materials inside, giving the illusion of a much deeper aquarium tank. For an aquascape layout as such, we would recommend leaving the aquarium driftwood bare and playing up the little spaces and cracks between the hardscape layout. Epiphytic aquatic plants such as Anubias and Bucephalandra species would fit perfectly! Alternatively, the fine natural sand can also be replaced with nutrient-dense aquarium soil and planted with an aquatic foreground like Hemianthus Callitrichoides or Eleocharis Parvula Mini. In the background, we would choose a bush aquatic stem plant such as Hemianthus Micranthemoides or Rotala Bonsai to complete the aquarium tank. Modeled after a 2-gallon cube tank. Microsorum pteropus ‘Trident Mini’, also known as Java Fern Trident Mini, is a compact version of the popular Java Fern Trident. It features thin, forked leaves that create a more detailed, textured look while staying smaller in overall size. Recently reclassified as Leptochilus pteropus , this plant is still widely known in the aquarium hobby as Microsorum pteropus. Like other Java Fern varieties, it is easy to care for and grows well in low light conditions, tolerating a wide range of aquarium parameters. Its smaller size makes it especially versatile, working well in nano aquariums or as a detailed accent in larger planted tanks. The fine, branching leaf structure pairs nicely with other popular easy aquatic plants like Anubias, Bucephalandra or standard Java Fern, helping add contrast and color to an aquascape. As an epiphytic plant, it can be attached to driftwood, rocks, or aquarium decor using thread or glue. Be sure to keep the rhizome above the substrate to prevent rot. Propagation is simple—just divide the rhizome and reattach as needed.

Microsorum Pteropus AKA Java fern is a staple aquascaping plant! Java Fern Flaming, as its name implies, features vibrant green color with crinkled leaves that resemble a flame. Equally hardy as other varieties, this Java Fern is a little smaller, making it suitable for nearly all tank sizes. Its care is comparable to other rhizome plants like Anubias, Bucephalandra or Cryptocoryne, making it a top pick for beginners as well. Recently reclassified as Leptochilus pteropus , this plant is still widely known as Microsorum pteropus. If you're looking to add more texture and character to your planted aquarium, consider Java Fern Flaming. It does the job while being easy to care for, grow and share with fellow hobbyists when mature. To grow it, attach it to driftwood or any porous surface. CO2 isn't required, but will go a long way in improving overall health and form.

Anubias Nana Petite is a top seller! Its charming miniature size has quickly become a favorite for aquascaping. Its small, deep green leaves are naturally compact, making it ideal for planting along the base of a layout. Like other Anubias, it is slow-growing but adapts well to low-light conditions, making it perfect for low-tech planted tanks. Its signature green hue works beautifully in nearly all aquascaping styles and easily fills gaps or holes in hardscape layouts. As an epiphytic aquarium plant, it can be attached directly to stones or driftwood. Its hardiness and easy care make it a top pick for both beginner and experienced hobbyists looking for compact, attractive greenery for any freshwater aquarium. It can also thrive in terrariums, paludariums, and similar setups. Propagation is straightforward; simply cut or pull apart rhizomes to be reattached. Tissue culture plants are grown in sterilized conditions! This is the only way to guarantee a pest-free, snail-free start for your planted aquarium.

Bucephalandra sp. 'Pygmy' Bucephalandra Pygmy is a beautiful small-leafed aquatic rhizome that offers iridescent blue, green and purple tones in a planted aquarium. It offers easy care and can grow well in low light tanks, making it a beginner-friendly choice. Like other buce, Pygmy Buce is suitable for both freshwater tanks and terrarium-like setups. It is an epiphyte, and will happily grow attached to your favorite driftwood, rocks, tank decor or within the cracks and gaps of your aquascape. When grown in groups, bucephalandra are beautiful gems and create lovely focal points that also provide safety for aquatic pets like shrimp and small tropical fish. Its small size also makes it perfect for a wide range of aquarium tank sizes. Try it in your nano planted tank or your largest freshwater aquarium. Bucephalandra comes in many varieties, shapes, colors and looks best when kept in clumps in a planted aquarium tank.

listings.commonName: UNS Long Glass Aquarium Stabilizing Tank Mat
listings.description: Stabilizing leveling mats are essential and strongly advised when having a planted aquarium tank. Fully filled planted tanks are quite heavy and most, if not all, the weight is placed on the bottom glass panel resulting in a good amount of stress. Premium rimless glass aquarium tanks are constructed to withstand this so long as the surface they are placed on is level. Unfortunately, this is not true in most cases and the use of a leveling mat is crucial to help offset and absorb surface imperfections that have the potential to crack the bottom glass panel via stress points. Stabilizing tank mats are cost-effective and prevent the worst from happening! These aquarium tank mats are made from premium, absorbent material to ensure your planted aquarium tank doesn't slip, slide or move during or after setup. Tested to withstand considerable turbulence, these aquarium stabilizing tank mats by Ultum Nature Systems are the perfect solution for your planted aquarium. They are sleek, cut to size and ready to place beneath most aquarium tanks. Enjoy peace of mind knowing your planted tank and its inhabitants are safe on their stand, counter, nightstand or console. Mat thickness is 5MM. TIP: These stabilizing mats will fit other rimless aquariums in similar sizing and may also be cut to size. These leveling mats are not meant to be used over small gaps. Please ensure your stand can fully hold your aquarium with no part of the aquarium hanging over the edge. Cutting any excess foam material will keep your setup looking clean! Be sure to use a sharp blade and handle with caution if the mat needs to be trimmed further. Malaysian Driftwood is one of the most recognizable and widely used driftwoods in aquascaping. Known for its deep coloration, natural texture, and substantial presence, it has long been a cornerstone of nature-style planted aquariums and the freshwater aquarium hobby. Its mixed surface textures and organic form help create a natural environment for tropical fish, shrimp, and aquatic plants while providing a timeless look when paired with vivid greenery. Naturally larger and heavier than many other driftwoods, Malaysian Driftwood excels as a foundation and centerpiece hardscape choice, lending the ethereal, nature-inspired appearance that many aquascapers strive to achieve. Best For - Nature-style aquascapes - Aquascapers seeking a timeless, natural aesthetic - Statement driftwood Natural Variation Malaysian Driftwood is a natural wood and every piece is unique. Variations in shape, structure, coloration, and overall dimensions are normal and part of what makes each piece one of a kind. Custom size and shape requests cannot be guaranteed. Mini Taiwan Moss (Taxiphyllum alternans) is a rarer and beautiful aquarium moss with a delicate texture and soft green color. Similar to Weeping Moss, it features horizontal, overhanging growth and adds natural texture and visual interest to any planted aquarium. Its compact size is perfectly scaled for all tank sizes, especially nano aquariums and smaller aquascapes. Like other mosses, care is relatively simple. It adapts well to low-tech tank settings and can grow nicely in shaded areas of higher-light aquascapes. Use aquatic moss to cover unnatural gaps in a planted tank layout or attach it to hardscape materials. Incorporating moss adds character, softens hard edges, and gives instant maturity to freshly planted tanks. Provide Mini Taiwan Moss with clean, stable water parameters and gentle flow as a baseline. CO2 injection will help it grow fuller and form the dense, fluffy tufts seen in popular aquascapes. Propagation is easy—simply separate a portion and reattach or reposition as desired. If you’re trimming moss, we recommend turning off the filter first to prevent unwanted spread and easier clean up! Below is a 40 gallon aquarium with Taiwan Moss:

A simple and longterm solution to an age-old problem that's easy to install! This high-quality brass permaseal provides a secure and permanent connection between an aquarium CO2 regulator and cylinder. Constructed from high-quality materials, using a permaseal will ensure that there are no more leaks and will void the use for plastic nylon CO2 o-ring washers. Using a CO2 Brass Perma-Seal will ultimately reduce countless costly refills and will allow aquatic plants to fully benefit from a continuous supply of CO2 in a planted aquarium tank.

Small details can help make an aquascape feel complete. Driftwood Detail Roots are thin, branchy pieces of aquarium driftwood that can be used to create root-like systems, trailing vines, and other natural details throughout a hardscape layout. Whether you're creating a sprawling forest scene or doing some serious detail work, these little pieces can add the finishing touch. Weave them between stones, wrap them around larger pieces of driftwood, or trim and position them to create a more organic look. Leave them bare, or try wrapping them in aquatic moss for extra texture and greenery. What's Included: 20 pieces of Driftwood Detail Roots

Our recommended choice for hidden hardware Also perfect for maximum CO2 diffusion in aquarium tank sizes 50 gallons and larger Can be completely disassembled for ease of maintenance This inline aquarium tank CO2 diffuser features quality build material, simple design, and beautiful functionality. Inline CO2 aquarium tank diffusers are built to be discrete and lessen the amount of visible equipment within a planted aquarium tank, optimizing the viewer's experience. This inline aquarium tank CO2 diffuser is meant to be installed outside of a planted aquarium by connecting the diffuser to the outflow tubing of an external canister filter. Installation is quick, but care should be taken to ensure it is connected to the outflow tubing. Connecting it to the inflow has the potential to harm canister filters by trapping CO2 gas bubbles in the canister filter and motor. Once installed, this inline aquarium tank CO2 diffuser provides extremely fine microbubbles of CO2 and will be readily absorbed by aquatic plants encouraging lush and healthy growth. Built to last, this inline CO2 diffuser can be completely taken apart easily for routine cleaning and replacement parts are available to ensure increased longevity and use. Best of all, these inline diffusers pair well with all of our Dymax aquarium lily pipe options! Specifications: M1 Fits: 12/16MM (1/2" and 13MM) filter tubing M2 Fits: 16/22MM (5/8" and 17MM) filter tubing Notes: Cleaning can be done carefully by allowing the diffuser to soak in 3 parts water and 1 part bleach. DO NOT scrub the ceramic ring. This inline CO2 diffuser requires a minimum of 30 psi working pressure. Pair with pressure proof tubing only. Do not use it in combination with weaker tubing material. Doing so has the potential to burst. Avoid touching the ceramic and handle the diffuser gently when installing. TIP: Keep a spare ceramic ring! When performing maintenance for the original one, it's possible to simply swap it out for the spare to ensure CO2 supply is consistent and without any downtime.

Bring bold color and dramatic foliage to your planted aquarium with Tiger Lotus (Nymphaea zenkeri). Its broad lilypad-like leaves can develop shades of green, red-brown, pinkish red, and deep maroon with darker spotting, creating a colorful focal point that stands out easily among surrounding aquatic plants. Tiger Lotus can develop into a substantial plant, sending long stems upward with leaves blooming along the water's surface. Allow them to grow for a more organic appearance, or regularly trim taller growth to encourage the plant to stay fuller and more compact below the surface. If allowed to spread across the surface, its larger leaves may eventually shade plants growing underneath. Give Tiger Lotus plenty of room to develop, particularly in larger planted aquariums where its size and distinctive foliage can become a prominent part of the aquascape.

Echinodorus Rose is a lovely hybrid between two well-known aquatic sword plants, Echinodorus Horemanii Red and Echinodorus Horizontalis. Growing to heights of around 7-12 inches, Echinodorus Rose is on the smaller side of the usual Echinodorus family, but don’t let its smaller size fool you! This aquatic plant is characterized by beautifully ranging hues of greens, reds, and bronzes. Newly sprouted leaves appear pink and will fade out into a deeper hue once mature. Like most aquatic swords, Echinodorus Rose should be planted in a quality aquarium soil as Echinodorus species absorb a majority of their nutrients through their roots. Other than providing a nutritious bottom, Echinodorus Rose is a great beginner aquatic plant as these aquatic plants are undemanding, hardy and will adapt to a wide range of aquarium tank parameters. While this aquatic sword is on the smaller side, this aquatic plant will still grow larger than most, making it a good background aquatic plant in nano aquarium tanks or as a midground-background in larger planted aquarium tanks. No matter the choice, Echinodorus Rose will still require periodic pruning to ensure that it does not shade the rest of the aquatic plants within the aquarium tank. Propagation is simple as well. Gently separate the plant and replant the divided portions into a quality aquarium substrate. Common Name Echinodorus Rose Care Easy Lighting Medium to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant runners Growth Rate Moderate Height 7-12" Tissue culture plants are grown in-vitro by laboratories who specialize in propagating aquatic plants. There is a huge selection of plant species that have been propagated this way. This is truly the best option for those who want absolutely zero unwanted pests, algae and pesticides. This makes them perfect for shrimp keepers and any planted tank enthusiasts alike. NOTE: It is important to remove the tissue culture agar gel before planting. Simply wash the gel away, divide, and plant.

Add an cute pop of greenery to your planted aquarium with Banana Plant (Nymphoides aquatica). Named for the cluster of thick, banana-shaped tubers at its base, this aquatic plant develops rounded green foliage that creates an instantly recognizable look in freshwater planted aquariums and ponds. Banana Plant can stay relatively compact with leaves growing closer to its base or send longer stems toward the water's surface, where it can develop floating, lily-like foliage. Its unique growth habit makes it an easy statement plant for planted aquariums, especially when given some open space to show off its unusual shape. When planting, keep the banana-shaped tubers partially exposed rather than completely burying them beneath the substrate.
