Bucephalandra Catherinae Red, or Buce Catherinae for short, is a unique aquatic plant from one of the most popular families in the aquascaping hobby. Characterized by its ruffled, thin leaves and varying colors, it makes an excellent addition to any planted aquarium. It offers a distinct look and makes a great accent plant for nano aquariums, terrariums or small scale planted setups. Like other Bucephalandra species, it is hardy and adaptable to a wide range of aquarium conditions. Because of this, Buce are commonly associated with low-tech planted aquariums. Their easy care and forgiving nature make them great beginner plants, but the results are even better when given higher levels of care. You’ll notice differences in color and form with CO2 injection, good flow, moderate lighting, and regular liquid fertilizer dosing. Simply attach it to your favorite hardscape with a porous surface, and you’re good to go!

Bucephalandra Dark Skeleton King, also known as Bucephalandra Dark Achilles, is a beautiful species in the Bucephalandra family. Boasting large foliage and rich coloration, Bucephalandra Dark Skeleton King's leaves feature a distinct pattern on its leaves that earns its name. Like all Bucephalandra species, Buce Dark Skeleton King has a hardy nature and is fairly adaptable to a wide range of aquarium tank parameters. It can be grown submerged or emersed and grows exceptionally well in low-tech conditions without lacking in unique character. Under optimal conditions, this Buce plant will develop an extremely dark contrasty mix of greens, blues, and purple hues. Bucephalandra Dark Skeleton King's care is comparable to that of Anubias species and while it grows slowly, if given proper care, patience will be generously rewarded. Buce Dark Skeleton King is a good choice for beginner aquarists and also provides refuge for smaller freshwater aquarium tank inhabitants such as smaller shrimp or fry. Bucephalandra can also be used in many ways and does not require being planted in aquarium tank substrate.

Anubias Stardust is a rare variant in the Anubias family. Comparable in size and appearance to Anubias Nana Petite, Anubias Stardust is slightly smaller with unique foliage. Anubias Stardust's leaves have lightly colored veins and varying specks of white scattered across, resembling dust speckles. When kept in a planted aquarium tank under proper lighting, its leaves are illuminated and provide a unique personality to a nature aquarium. Just like all Anubias, Anubias Stardust is fairly easy to care for and will adapt well to a wide range of aquarium tank parameters. This particular species requires a little more light to keep its signature character but is generally hardy and comparable in care to Bucephalandra and aquatic fern species. Overall, Anubias Stardust is a great aquatic plant choice to add to any planted aquarium tank and will give a beautiful pop of contrast against alternative aquatic plant species and aquarium tank hardscape. Another great feature is its ability to thrive in both aquariums and terrarium-like setups. Anubias Stardust is a flowering aquatic plant that grows best when the rhizome is attached to hardscape material such as wood or stone. Propagation is straightforward; simply cut or pull apart rhizomes to be reattached.

Homalomena insignis is a tropical aroid in the same family as Bucephalandra and Anubias, known for its broad, semi-waxy leaves and shifting color tones. Depending on conditions, it can display deep green and olive hues, with the potential to develop soft coral or pink tones that stand out nicely against darker plants. While it’s often grouped with aquatic plants, Homalomena insignis is better suited for paludarium or terrarium-style setups. It grows best with its roots kept moist or lightly submerged, while the leaves remain above water in a humid environment. It’s a relatively easy plant to care for and adapts well to low to medium lighting. Given the right conditions, it develops into a lovely, tropical accent that adds a different texture compared to fully aquatic species. Homalomena insignis is a good option if you’re looking to branch out from traditional aquarium plants and add something a little more unique to a high-humidity setup.

Homalomena humilis is a tropical aroid with thick, waxy leaves and a mix of green and pink tones that can shift depending on its environment. It has a bold, slightly glossy look that stands out nicely against more common green plants. While it’s often grouped with aquatic species like Bucephalandra, Homalomena humilis is better suited for paludarium or terrarium-style setups. It grows best with its roots kept moist or lightly submerged, while the leaves remain above water in a humid environment. It’s relatively easy to care for and does well in low to medium lighting. Overall, it is a great option if you’re looking to add something a little different to a high-humidity setup, especially if you like the look of Buce or Anubias but want something less common.

Bucephalandra Theia is a beautiful species within the Bucephalandra group. This specific species features long, thin leaves that are slightly wavy and bold in coloration. Like all Bucephalandra species, Buce Theia can be grown submerged in an aquarium tank or emersed in terrarium, paludarium and vivarium-like setups. Bucephalandra as a species is very hardy and can adapt to a wide range of aquarium tank parameters. Those who are already familiar with Bucephalandra Catherinae may see similarities between the two as Buce Theia resembles a larger leaf version of Catherinae. Buce doesn't require excessive light either, making it an all-around wonderful choice for expert enthusiasts and beginner hobbyists alike. Bucephalandra Theia's care is comparable to that of Anubias species and its growth behavior is similar in that this aquatic plant does not need to be planted in aquarium soil to grow properly. Bucephalandra Theia is also a flowering species and it will do great simply being attached to aquarium hardscape material such as aquascaping stones or aquarium driftwood. Pruning is simple as well. All you need to do is separate the rhizome and replant.

Schismatoglottis Roseospatha is a stunning epiphyte hailing from the southern regions of Sarawak, Borneo. Characterized by its rich green, low gloss leaves, this aquatic plant is commonly found attached to rocks in the wild along rainforest streams. Although Schismatoglottis Roseospatha is already recognized in the aquarium hobby, this aquatic plant is still incredibly difficult to obtain. Schismatoglottis Roseospatha itself is generally undemanding and its care can be compared to the popular Bucephalandra and Anubias families. Even though it is unnecessary, Schismatoglottis Roseospatha, like most aquatic plants, will benefit greatly from routine fertilizer and CO2 injection along with quality aquarium LED lighting. Similar to Bucephalandra, Schismatoglottis Roseospatha is a slow grower but it will reward those who are patient. We recommend using this aquatic plant in minimally planted aquarium tanks such as a blackwater biotope aquarium tank setup. Another benefit of this aquatic plant is that it is a rheophyte, meaning it can withstand strong currents and will remain firmly attached to its foundation. In the wild, Schismatoglottis Roseospatha gets flooded for a short period of time and can be grown both submerged in an aquarium tank and emersed in alternative setups. If grown emersed, care should be taken to provide as much humidity as possible in the surrounding environment. Plant Care & Information

Bucephalandra Skeleton King is the original Skeleton King species in the Bucephalandra family. Boasting the same large foliage and rich coloration, Bucephalandra Skeleton King's leaves feature a distinct pattern on its leaves that earns its name. Like all Bucephalandra species, Buce Skeleton King has a hardy nature and is fairly adaptable to a wide range of aquarium tank parameters. It can be grown submerged or emersed and grows exceptionally well in low-tech conditions without lacking in unique character. Under optimal conditions, this Buce aquatic plant will produce varying hues that contrast well in a planted aquarium tank. Bucephalandra Skeleton King's care is comparable to that of Anubias species and while it grows slowly, if this aquatic plant is given proper care, having patience will be generously rewarded. Buce Skeleton King is a good choice for beginner aquarists and also provides refuge for smaller freshwater aquarium tank inhabitants such as smaller shrimp or fry. Bucephalandra can also be used in many ways and does not require being planted in aquarium tank substrate.

Bucephlandra Pink Lady is another species in the Bucephalandra family. Considered to be quite rare, Bucephalandra Pink Lady or just Buce Pink Lady for short is characterized by a soft pink stem with beautiful leaves that vary in different shades. This particular Buce species has the potential to grow larger than a lot of Bucephalandra species. Similar in care to other Bucephalandra species, Anubias species, and aquatic fern species, Bucephalandra Pink Lady is undemanding and does well in a wide range of aquarium tank parameters. Despite its hardy nature, Bucephalandra species do even better when provided with a clean, balanced environment with appropriate aquarium LED lighting, CO2 injection and a regular fertilizing schedule. The ease of care along with a variety of shapes, sizes, and colors makes Bucephalandra a favorite amongst beginner hobbyists and experienced enthusiasts. Bucephalandra Pink Lady, too, can be grown submerged in a planted aquarium tank or kept emersed in terrarium-like setups. Propagation is simple and can be done by gently separating the rhizome and replanting it within the crevice of an aquascape layout or attaching it to aquarium stone or aquarium tank driftwood.

Anubias Chili is a very rare species belonging to the ever popular Anubias family. Extremely coveted, Anubias Chili is another aquatic plant that belongs in any Anubias enthusiast's collection. This aquatic plant is characterized by tiny leaves with the signature Anubias green hue. Anubias Chili earns its name as its leaves are unmistakenly shaped like little chili peppers. This aquatic plant grows dense and its care is comparable to other aquatic plant species such as Bucephalandra, Java Ferns and Cryptocoryne. As an Anubias species, Anubias Chili has a hardy nature and works well in low-tech planted aquarium tank setups as well as high-tech planted aquarium tank setups. It can be grown submerged or emersed in terrarium-like setups as well. In terms of size, Anubias Pangolino is still one of the smallest leafed Anubias plants. However, both Anubias Chili and Pangolino compared Nana Petite, are approximately half the size. As a whole, Anubias species can adapt to a wide range of aquarium tank parameters and is a wonderful aquatic plant choice for hobbyists of all skill levels. It is, however, slow growing like most Anubias plants, but will do better when provided with a light fertilizing routine, clean water, quality aquarium tank lighting, and CO2 injection. No different from the rest, Anubias Chili is also a flowering plant that grows best when the rhizome is attached to hardscape material such as aquarium wood or aquascaping stone. Propagation is straightforward; simply cut or pull apart rhizomes to be reattached.

Grow a lush, fine-textured aquarium carpet with Elatine hydropiper. Its tiny, vibrant green leaves resemble a miniature Glossostigma while remaining comparable in size to HC Cuba, making it an excellent choice for detailed aquascapes and nano planted aquariums. Given stable conditions, it gradually develops into a dense foreground carpet that is ideal for both stone and driftwood layouts. Elatine hydropiper performs best in high-tech planted aquariums with medium to high lighting and added CO2. It prefers cooler, stable water temperatures and is less tolerant of prolonged heat than many other carpeting plants. As the carpet matures, routine trimming helps maintain its low, compact appearance and encourages healthy new growth.

Bolbitis Difformis is the larger leaf form of its popular counterpart, Bolbitis Difformis Mini or Bolbitis Difformis Baby Leaf. Like other aquatic Bolbitis, Bolbitis Difformis is an aquatic fern that features leafy foliage that is unique in appearance and rich in coloration. This aquatic plant is fairly slow growing yet easy to maintain and keep within a planted aquarium tank. Bolbitis Difformis’s care is comparable to that of Anubias, Bucephalandra and Cryptocoryne species. While this aquatic fern doesn’t require CO2, the addition of CO2 injection along with soft water and quality lighting helps to promote growth immensely. Bolbitis Difformis does best when attached to aquarium hardscape material such as aquarium driftwood or aquascaping stone. Care should be taken to ensure it is not planted directly into aquarium substrate as this can cause the aquatic plant to rot. Once settled in an aquarium tank, Bolbitis Difformis can be propagated easily by separating the aquatic plant gently along the horizontal rhizome.

Fissidens Fontanus is one of our favorite aquarium mosses! This delicate gem features rich green hues and soft, feathery fronds. It is a very delicate live moss that may look matted when balled up, but once it attaches to aquarium driftwood or stones—it really shines, offering a unique texture that sets it apart from other aquatic mosses. Fissidens moss is easy to care for and doesn't demand much in exchange for fluffy growth. Like all plants, its form and growth speed is noticeably different with CO2 injection and moderate lighting. However, it won't fuss if kept in low light or low-tech planted tanks. When established, it forms fuzzy, cushioned patches that offer excellent hiding spots for tiny freshwater livestock like shrimplets and fry. So, if you're looking for a low-maintenance aquarium plant for your aquascape that doesn't skimp on texture and, try Fissidens! You'll soon see for yourself why its a moss every aquascaper loves.

Bucephalandra Biblis Blue is a wonderful species belonging to the Bucephalandra family. Bucephlandra Biblis Blue, sometimes referred to as Buce Biblis Pink Green is a smaller species of Bucephalandra that works exceptionally well in planted nano aquarium tanks. Bucephalandra Biblis features small curly leaves that vary in shades of green, reddish-brown, and more. This particular species of Bucephalandra grows in dense clumps and with proper care will grow steadily making it a beautiful addition to any planted aquarium tank. Like all Bucephalandra species, Buce Biblis is an easy-going aquatic plant with a forgiving nature. While it is not necessary, providing this species with CO2 injection, quality aquarium tank lighting, and light fertilizer will yield healthier and lush growth. Given this aquatic plant's easy-going nature, it is a great choice for beginner aquarists, and care can be comparable to other popular aquatic plant species such as Anubias and Java Ferns. Bucephalandra can also be used in many ways and does not require being planted in the aquarium tank substrate. Simply attach it to aquarium hardscape material such as aquarium driftwood, aquascaping stones or aquarium decor. Alternatively, it can also be placed in the crevices of an aquascape layout.

Cryptocoryne Affinis is a distinctive Cryptocoryne native to western Malaysia, where it can be found growing densely in groups. Once more widespread within the aquarium hobby, this species has become less commonly available over time, making it an interesting find for Cryptocoryne enthusiasts and collectors. When grown submerged, Cryptocoryne Affinis develops smooth foliage ranging from olive green to deeper brown tones. Lighter veining creates a distinct pattern across the upper surface of the leaves, while contrasting coloration underneath adds another layer of visual interest. Its final size and growth habit can vary considerably depending on the environment in which it is grown. Relatively undemanding once established, Cryptocoryne Affinis can adapt to lower-light planted aquarium setups and appreciates plenty of time to develop a healthy root system. Like other Cryptocoryne, choose its placement thoughtfully and avoid unnecessary moving or sudden changes while the plant settles in.

Echinodorus Horizontalis Mini is one of our personal favorite aquatic sword plants in the hobby. Rarely available in the trade now, Echinodorus Horizontalis Mini is more commonly traded amongst planted aquarium tank enthusiasts. Echinodorus Horizontalis Mini features a soft green hue with rounded leaves. New growth displays a brownish-pink tone and later matures into the same green color. This aquatic sword plant is on the smaller side of the Echinodorus family and is suitable for smaller sized planted aquarium tanks. Like all aquatic sword species, Echinodorus Horizontalis Mini is easy to keep, fairly hardy and needs a minimum of a nutrient-rich aquarium substrate as these species of aquatic plant are heavy root feeders. Aside from this, Echinodorus species are fairly tolerable of varying water parameters and lighting conditions. While this little aquatic sword grows more compact, it is still a larger aquatic plant in general and should be pruned periodically to ensure smaller aquatic plants are not shaded from the light provided. Propagation is simple. Separate and replant. Bucephalandra Godzilla is a lovely species of Bucephalandra! Easily recognized by beautiful ruffled leaves that vary in bold reddish-brown tones, Bucephalandra Godzilla later gains even deeper coloration as the aquatic plant matures. When provided with optimal conditions, Bucephalandra Godzilla produces dense bushes of Buce that will frequently flower, making for a beautiful addition to any planted aquarium tank. Like most Bucephalandra plants, Buce Godzilla is epiphytic and will grow happily attached to aquarium driftwood or stones in an aquascape layout. Low to medium lighting with partial shade is perfect for most Buce species and while this plant will tolerate other conditions associated with keeping a low-tech aquarium, we highly recommend providing Buce with CO2 injection and a quality source of nutrients to boost growth, help the plant outcompete algae and produce the iridescent hues Bucephalandra are known for. Overall, Bucephalandra Godzilla is a suitable plant for most beginner aquarists that have the basics of aquarium keeping down. Buce's stem and rhizome should not be covered or glued when planting as this can cause damage to the plant.

Cryptocoryne Wendtii Green Gecko is a hardy, beginner-friendly Crypt that develops lush foliage in varying shades of green. Its coloration can shift depending on growing conditions, adding subtle variation throughout its compact, leafy growth. Adaptable and relatively undemanding, Cryptocoryne Wendtii Green Gecko grows well across a wide range of planted aquarium conditions and is an excellent choice for low-tech setups. A nutrient-rich substrate or regular root fertilization can support fuller, healthy growth, while CO2 injection can be provided but is not required. Once established, new plantlets can gradually develop around the mother plant and spread into a fuller group. Allow new growth to mature before separating and replanting individual plantlets for propagation.

Cryptocoryne Yujii is a rare, slow-growing Cryptocoryne that develops a tight rosette with leaves ranging from green to reddish-brown tones. Its dense growth and coloration give this uncommon Crypt plenty of character when established in a planted aquarium. With patience and consistent care, Cryptocoryne Yujii can be grown in both submerged and emersed conditions. Like other Cryptocoryne, allow the plant plenty of time to establish a healthy root system and avoid unnecessary moving or disturbance while it settles in. CO2 injection isn't required with Crypts but we find it to be beneficial in supporting healthier growth and easing the transition from emersed to submerged growth.

Like most other aquarium stem plants, Pogostemon Erectus also relies heavily on a nutrient-rich planted aquarium substrate. If provided with optimal planted aquarium conditions, this plant will grow vigorously and will not mind frequent trimming. Helanthium Tenellum is generally easy to keep and will spread readily if given optimal conditions. We recommend using it as a foreground or midground choice. It can even be used as a short background aquatic plant choice in smaller nano-sized aquarium tanks. Just like other rosette species, this particular aquatic plant is beautiful in groups or by itself. Propagation is also fairly simple and can be done by separating via the runners and replanting into a quality aquarium substrate. High lighting and CO2 injection are not necessarily required to grow Echinodorus Tenellus , but is highly recommended for quicker and fuller growth. To plant, simply separate larger mats into small portions and plant each portion an inch or so apart half way into the substrate. Once established, regular trimming will be required. Bucephlandra Flamingo is an exceptional Buce species! Bucephlandra Thick Brown is a fairly rare species of Buce. Bucephalandra Thick Brown is characterized by varying shades displayed on its smaller, rounded leaves. Being of a smaller size, Bucephalandra Thick Brown shares the same care requirements as other species within the same family. This aquatic plant works great in nano aquarium tanks and can be used as ornamental pieces in larger planted aquarium tanks. Care requirements are comparable to other popular aquatic plant families such as Anubias , Cryptocoryne , and aquatic ferns . Bucehalandra Thick Brown is undemanding and will adapt to a wide range of aquarium tank parameters. Despite its hardy nature, Bucephalandra species do even better when provided with a clean, balanced environment with appropriate aquarium LED lighting, CO2 injection and a regular fertilizing schedule. The ease of care along with a variety of shapes, sizes, and colors makes Bucephalandra a favorite amongst beginner hobbyists and experienced enthusiasts. Bucephalandra Thick Brown can be grown submerged in a planted aquarium tank or kept emersed in terrarium-like setups. Propagation is simple and can be done by gently separating the rhizome and replanting it within the crevice of an aquascape layout or attaching it to aquarium stone or aquarium tank driftwood. Placement for this aquatic plant is versatile adding to its overall allure!

Create a dynamic mosaic of color across the water's surface with Ludwigia Sedioides. Commonly known as Mosaic Plant or Floating Ludwigia, this unusual aquatic plant develops lily-like rosettes with small, geometric leaves that fan outward from a central point. Depending on growing conditions, foliage can range from green to vibrant shades of red, creating its signature mosaic-like appearance. Unlike traditional stem plants, Ludwigia Sedioides grows at the water's surface while remaining rooted in the substrate below. Give it plenty of open surface area and gentle water movement so its floating foliage can spread naturally. Regular trimming can help control its coverage and prevent mature growth from shading aquatic plants underneath. Its size and spread is especially well suited for larger planted aquariums and freshwater ponds where its distinctive surface growth can be fully appreciated. Important: Ludwigia Sedioides is highly susceptible to losing some or all of its leaves during transit. Leaf loss does not necessarily indicate that the plant has died. Healthy stems can produce new growth once planted and provided with suitable growing conditions.

Alternanthera Rosaefolia Mini packs the saturated color of larger Alternanthera into a noticeably smaller form. Its leaves can display a mix of red, magenta, pink, and purple tones, creating a colorful mass of foliage without the larger proportions of traditional Alternanthera Reineckii. Its smaller stature makes Rosaefolia Mini especially useful in nano aquariums or anywhere a lower, bushier group of colorful stems is preferred. Frequent trimming encourages branching and helps develop dense growth, creating both visual impact and additional cover for shrimp and small aquarium fish. Rosaefolia Mini is relatively approachable for such a colorful plant, although stronger lighting, CO2 injection, consistent fertilization, and a nutrient-rich substrate will support denser growth and more pronounced coloration. Healthy stem cuttings can be replanted into the substrate to expand the group or maintain its shape over time.

Nesaea Pedicellata Golden is an aquatic stem plant that is still relatively uncommon in the planted aquarium hobby. Derived from the original species, Nesaea Pedicellata Golden is a cultivar that has vibrant golden-green leaves that run along a bright pink stem. It is a moderately sized plant and can be planted in the midground of your aquascape or in the background if you have a smaller tank. Nesaea is pretty easy to grow if your aquarium has CO2 injection, good aquasoil and moderate to high lighting conditions. When your soil is aged, consider introducting a gentle aquatic plant fertilizer to sustain healthy, vibrant growth. Like all aquarium stem plants, Nesaea Pedicellata Golden will need to be trimmed regularly to achieve a bushy look and to prevent lower parts of the plant from becoming overly shaded. Common Name Golden Nesaea Nesaea Pedicellata Golden Ammannia pedicellata Care Easy to Moderate Lighting Medium to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Midground or Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 5-12"

Anubias is a popular genus in the planted aquarium hobby. This family of smaller aroids have a bulletproof reputation in the planted tank community for being extremely hardy, adaptable and tolerant of many aquarium conditions. Their classic look and minimal care requirements make them a favorite amongst seasoned aquarists and beginner hobbyists alike. Anubias are epiphytic and grow well when attached to porous hardscape such as aquarium driftwoods and stones. Because of this, these aquatic plants are perfect for filling in bare areas of an aquascape or wherever additional greenery is desired. It should be noted that Anubias are slow growers, so an established aquarium is ideal, if possible, as they can be more susceptible to algae growth on their leaves when compared to other aquarium plants. Despite the hardy reputation, Anubias plants will appreciate a well-maintained environment with clean water, CO2 injection and low to medium lighting. Care should be taken to ensure the rhizome is not buried as this will cause damage to the plant. When ready for propagation, gently split the rhizome and reattach elsewhere. If being planted for an emersed setup, sufficient moisture should be provided to ensure the plant does not dry out.

Ludwigia Palustris Super Red is a slight variation of Ludwigia Palustris. Ludwigia Palustris Super Red is an easy to keep species that features oval leaves with bolder reddish-orange coloration. This aquatic stem plant is ideal for midground aquatic plant choices as well as the background. When planted in groups, Ludwigia Palustris Super Red provides beautiful pops of color against darker green colored aquatic plants. It also aids in adding movement and dimension to any planted aquarium tank. Coloration is dependent upon the care and deeper hues can be achieved by providing Ludwigia Palustris Super Red with quality aquarium LED lighting, CO2 injection, premium aquatic plant fertilizer, and quality aquarium soil. If optimal conditions are provided, regular trimming will be needed in order to keep this aquatic stem plant growing lush and full. Like most aquatic stem plants, Ludwigia Palustris Super Red can be grown submerged in a planted aquarium tank or emersed in a terrarium-like setup. Propagation is similar to all aquatic stem plants. Simply cut the stems and replant into a quality aquarium substrate.

Echinodorus Ozelot Red is a decorative aquatic plant in the Echinodorus family. This particular species is a decorative hybrid between Echinodorus Barthii and Echinodorus Schluteri. Echinodorus Ozelot Red features large reddish-brown leaves with dark spot markings all throughout. These appear darker on newly sprouted leaves but Echinodorus Ozelot Red retains this interesting pattern into maturity. Like most Echinodorus species, Echinodorus Ozelot Red is great for beginners and is fairly undemanding in care. Just like other aquarium sword variants, this aquatic plant should be planted directly into a quality aquarium substrate to encourage growth as swords are known for heavily absorbing nutrients via their root system. This plant can be grown emersed and submerged and is typically very adaptive to a wide range of aquarium tank conditions. Propagation is simple. Separate and replant. Once established, regular trimming will be required. Common Name Echinodorus Ozelot Red Echinodorus Ozelot Care Easy Lighting Medium CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant runners Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 8-12"

Featuring the Ultum Nature Systems Mini Dual Stage Regulator paired with a disposable CO2 cartridge (a dynamic duo we use often!), this setup offers a reliable and approachable introduction to CO2 injection for nano and small planted tanks. With all essential components included, the Nano CO2 Kit is best for hobbyists with small tanks, or anyone looking to introduce CO2 without the complexity of larger pressurized setups. With up to a 6-way split, one CO2 cylinder can be used to supply each planted aquarium tank, cutting down on cost while remaining efficient and ensuring aquatic plants are receiving essential CO2. Easy to install and built from quality stainless steel, this CO2 regulator splitter doesn't require any tools aside from a strong wrench arm and provides lasting rust-free durability. Why CO2 injection is important in a planted aquarium tank: 3 main factors contribute to the optimal growth of aquatic plants. These factors include nutrients, light and carbon dioxide (CO2). If any of these are unbalanced, the results are algae growth or the withering of aquatic plants. The introduction of CO2 in a planted aquarium tank allows aquatic plants to thrive and grow more efficiently, while also giving them the ability to outcompete algae for nutrients. Lagenandra Keralensis is a rare species that is similar to its more popular counterpart, Lagenandra Meeboldii Red. Lagenandra Keralensis, sometimes referred to as Lagenandra Meeboldii Kerala, features similar foliage as regular Meeboldii Red but is more narrow in width and longer in length. Coloration is varying shades of greens, reds, and bronze but will vary depending on the aquarium tank it is kept in. Other than this, there is very little information available on this aquarium plant, but it can be assumed that many care requirements will be similar to the regular Lagenandra Meeboldii Red . Quality aquarium tank lighting and CO2 injection are recommended along with a nutrient dense aquarium soil. As this species is known to grow quite large, we recommend this aquarium plant for larger sized aquarium tanks as a background aquatic plant choice. If grown emergent, thoroughly moist aquarium soil along with sufficient humidity should suffice for proper growth. Common Name Lagenandra Meeboldii Red Long Lagenandra Keralensis Red Lagenandra Meeboldii Kerala Care Moderate Lighting Medium to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Attach to wood or stone Propagation Separate rhizome Growth Rate Moderate Height 4"+

Eleocharis Pusilla, more simply known as Hair Grass, is a beautiful aquarium plant that is used commonly in aquascaping for its low-growing, lawn forming abilities. Eleocharis Pusilla is a generally undemanding foreground aquatic plant choice and will readily produce reliable ground coverage in an aquarium tank. With foliage resembling blades of grass, Eleocharis Pusilla has a bright green color that pops against darker aquatic plants. This aquarium plant will grow without high-light and CO2 injection, but we highly recommend implementing these factors as it will aid in quicker and lusher growth. Eleocharis Pusilla grows via runners and will quickly spread if conditions are optimal. To prevent this aquarium plant from growing in unwanted areas of a planted aquarium tank, frequent trimming and maintenance will be required once the aquarium plant takes off.

Hygrophila Difformis, commonly known as Water Wisteria or Water Sprite, is a fast-growing stem plant with bright green foliage. Beginner hobbyists flock to this aquarium plant for its easy care, undemanding nature, and quick growth. We also recommend this aquarium plant for beginners who are looking to transition to keeping live aquarium plants for the first time and are looking for an easy-going choice that will fill their aquarium tank readily. Hygrophila Difformis, aka Water Wisteria, does not require too much care and can adapt to a wide range of aquarium tank parameters. Water Wisteria also does well to help absorb excess nutrients in the water column, helping to outcompete algae and preventing its growth. As Hygrophila Difformis grows very quickly, it has the potential to grow unruly if not maintained and pruned regularly. We recommend this aquarium plant for the midground and background aquatic plant choices in a planted tank. Propagation is simple and trimmed stems can be replanted into quality aquarium soil. Common Name Hygrophila Difformis Water Wisteria Water Sprite Care Easy Lighting Low to Medium CO2 Optional Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Fast Height 10+”

Scrophulariaceae Limnophila Sp is a very rare aquatic stem plant with little information known about it. Very similar to Limnophila Mini Vietnam, Scrophulariaceae Limnophila Sp is a low-growing aquatic stem plant that does not grow tall like most aquatic stem plants such as Rotala and Ludwigia species. This unique growing pattern makes this aquarium plant suitable for mid-ground placement in a planted aquarium tank. Although Scrophulariaceae Limnophila Sp does not grow tall and out of control, it will still need adequate aquarium led lighting, CO2 injection and nutrient dense aquarium soil to grow well. Consistent trims will yield a bushy effect that is sought after by planted tank enthusiasts. We recommend this plant for aquarists looking for a unique aquatic stem plant. Pruning is simple and can be done by replanting trimmed stems into quality aquarium soil. Common Name Scrophulariaceae Limnophila Care Medium Lighting Medium to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Midground to Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate Height 5-10" Tissue culture aquatic plants are grown in-vitro by laboratories who specialize in propagating aquatic plants. There is a huge selection of plant species that have been propagated this way. This is truly the best option for those who want absolutely zero unwanted pests, algae and pesticides. This makes them perfect for shrimp keepers and any planted tank enthusiasts alike. NOTE: It is important to remove the tissue culture agar gel before planting. Simply wash the gel away, divide, and plant.

Anubias Nangi is a relatively unknown species of Anubias in the aquarium hobby. Featuring the signature Anubias green tone, Anubias Nangi is a smaller species with the same robust, hardy nature and tough leaves. Like all Anubias, Anubias Nangi is fairly easy to care for and will adapt well to a wide range of aquarium tank parameters and is generally hardy and comparable in care to other Anubias, Bucephalandra, Cryptocoryne and aquatic fern species. Overall, Anubias Nangi is a great aquatic plant choice to add to any planted aquarium tank or Anubias enthusiast's collection and will give a beautiful pop of contrast against alternative aquatic plant species and aquarium tank hardscape. Another great feature is its ability to thrive in both aquariums and terrarium-like setups. Anubias Nangi is a flowering aquatic plant that grows best when the rhizome is attached to hardscape material such as aquarium driftwood or aquascaping stone. Propagation is straightforward; simply cut or pull apart rhizomes to be reattached. It benefits from consistent fertilization but light requirements are minimal as its leaves are susceptible to algae growth when placed under high lighting. CO2 injection is optional but can promote faster growth and robust leaves when used.

This product qualifies for FREE SHIPPING! Check valves are an essential piece of equipment when implementing CO2 injection or air pump in a planted aquarium tank. Check valves are used to prevent the backflow of water to air pumps and CO2 regulators. The Precision Check Valve is an extremely durable piece of equipment constructed from solid materials that is designed to handle high pressure, preventing aquarium water from siphoning into parts it shouldn't and increasing overall product longevity. Unlike plastic CO2 check valves that deteriorate due to gas pressure and easily broken glass pieces, this precision check valve provides extreme durability and is ideal for longterm use without having to be replaced every few months.

Equipped with 200 of the latest technology RGB LED bulbs and an output of 90 watts, Titan 1 by Ultum Nature Systems provides the optimal spectrum necessary for growing lush and healthy aquatic plants while intensifying the myriad of hues found in a planted aquarium tank that is displayed by freshwater fish, shrimp, and aquatic plants. With a wide body design, Ultum Nature System’s Titan 1 is able to provide a uniform spread of light to an entire planted aquarium tank. This ensures that all aquatic plants are able to absorb light efficiently and effectively, promoting even and healthy growth. Coming in at a mere 5.3LBs, Titan 1 also sports lightweight and slim measurements while remaining a powerful unit, making it suitable to hang from a fixture or ceiling. It’s paired with a reinforced waterproof wire that is unobtrusive to the eye while establishing a safe, secure power supply to the main lighting unit. Available in brushed black aluminum and brushed silver aluminum, both colorways are an eye-catching finish that's sure to complement interior design within the home while fusing seamlessly with a planted aquarium tank and providing an essential contribution to the health and success of a nature aquarium tank. Each unit is built with precision using high-grade materials such as aircraft grade aluminum guaranteeing beautiful aesthetic, durability and product longevity that is suitable for everyday use. Modernly designed with purposefully exposed heat dissipation fins, Titan 1 allows for maximum airflow ensuring the aquarium tank below remains at a stable temperature. With efficient heat dissipation and LED technology, Ultum Nature System's Titan 1 emanates minimal heat when compared to dated lighting sources such as metal halides and can be boasted as an energy saving unit. There are many advantages of utilizing an RGB wavelength for a freshwater planted aquarium tank. An optimal spectrum ensures that all colors found in a planted tank are highlighted equally and evenly. Red wavelengths are meant to brighten red toned aquatic plant species such as Ludwigias, Rotalas and Alternanthera species. This also applies to boldly colored freshwater shrimp and fish! With green being one of the most important colors in achieving an ethereal underwater world, green wavelengths are essential for enhancing the green seen in most aquatic plants. Last but certainly not least, blue wavelengths help to encourage the onset of photosynthesis in aquatic plants and aid in producing the appearance of crystal clear water. One unit will illuminate a 60-90CM aquarium tank beautifully. For aquarium tanks larger, two or more units are advised to ensure that all aquatic plants receive sufficient lighting. The recommended hanging height is at least 12 inches above an aquarium tank and the suspension wires included are 38 inches long.

Cryptocoryne Wendtii Pink is a beautiful form of Cryptocoryne in the species family. Sporting shades of greens and pink, Cryptocoryne Wendtii Pink is a great midground aquatic plant choice in a planted aquarium tank. Its foliage provides a wonderful contrast in texture and color against common green aquarium plants or can be used for a lovely tonal contrast amongst groups of red aquatic plants. Like most Cryptocoryne, Cryptocoryne Wendtii Pink is fairly forgiving and will adapt to a wide range of aquarium parameters if given the chance. We recommend planting it in nutrient-dense aquarium soil and allowing the aquatic plant to establish before making any changes. Once established in an aquarium tank, Cryptocoryne Wendtii Pink, along with other cryptocoryne, is extremely hardy and will grow at a steady rate. Care includes low to medium aquarium lighting and clean water. CO2 injection and aquarium plant fertilizers will yield quicker growth and better coloration and is a good addition when possible. Cryptocoryne species are a staple in the planted tank hobby for good reason! Propagation is simple and baby plants can be separated from the mother and replanted in quality aquarium soil.

Echinodorus Chocolate Marble is a relatively unknown species in the Echinodorus family. Care for Echinodorus Chocolate Marble is comparable to that of Anubias, Bucephalandra, Cryptocoryne and Java Fern species aka fairly simple. Its simple care makes this aquatic plant type a great choice for beginner hobbyists or for those who enjoy aquariums and are interested in keeping live aquatic plants for the first time. Like all aquatic sword species, Echinodorus Chocolate Marble is easy to keep, fairly hardy and needs a minimum of a nutrient-rich aquarium substrate as these species of aquatic plant are heavy root feeders. Aside from this, Echinodorus species are fairly tolerable of varying water parameters and lighting conditions. Also known for their sizeable attributes, Echinodorus tend to be larger aquatic plants in general and work well for larger sized aquarium tanks. Microsorum pteropus ‘Philippines Mini’, also known as Java Fern Philippines Mini, is a compact and decorative Java Fern with very narrow, slender leaves and a fresh green color. Its leaf shape is similar to Java Fern Narrow Leaf, but even finer, giving it a more delicate look. Recently reclassified as Leptochilus pteropus , this plant is still widely known in the aquarium hobby as Microsorum pteropus. However, like others, it is very hardy and easy to care for, making it a great introductory aquatic plant. It tolerates low light conditions and a wide range of water parameters, including brackish setups. Its smaller size makes it especially ideal for nano aquariums or as a fine-textured accent plant in larger planted aquariums. When grouped, it creates a soft, natural look and can provide a secure place for smaller fish and shrimp. As an epiphytic plant, it can be attached to driftwood, rocks, or aquarium decor using thread or glue. Be sure to keep the rhizome above the substrate to prevent rot. Occasional trimming of older leaves will help keep the plant looking clean and encourage healthy growth.

Bucephalandra Kedagang Green is a beautiful variant in the Bucephalandra aquatic plant family. The term Kedagang describes Bucephalandra variants that are quite rare and small in size. Bucephalandra Kedagang Green displays ruffled leaves that display an array of green hues with a slight speckly and iridescent sheen when placed under quality aquarium LED lighting. Like most Bucephalandra species, Bucephalandra Kedagang Green is a great aquatic plant for beginners due to its easy care, undemanding nature and ability to adapt to a wide range of aquarium tank parameters. Bucephalandra comes in many varieties, shapes, colors and looks best when kept in clumps in a planted aquarium tank. This aquatic plant prefers lower lighting and will grow nice and dense if favorable conditions are provided. The stem and rhizome should not be covered when planting as this will cause the plant to rot and wither. It is best to attach or wedge Bucephalandra on or between aquarium hardscapes such as aquarium driftwood and aquascaping rocks.

Cryptocoryne Flamingo or Crypt Flamingo for short is highly sought after pink Crypt aquarium plant. New leaves tend to stay hot pink and gradually subdues over time into a vibrant pink that would match well with any aquatic plant. Like all Cryptocoryne , Crypt Flamingo is generally easy to plant to maintain once established in a planted aquarium. This aquatic plant will enjoy and experience much better growth in a planted tank that is fully established with CO2 injection and high lighting.

Marimo Moss Balls (Aegagropila linnaei / Cladophora aegagropila) aren’t actually moss! They’re a rare, slow-growing algae that naturally forms into soft, velvety green spheres. In the wild, Marimo grows at the bottom of lakes in Japan, where water currents tumble the algae into its signature moss ball shape. The name Marimo directly translates to “seaweed ball” in Japanese, and it’s arguably the only algae species welcomed openly in freshwater aquariums. Marimo Balls are very much alive and make a unique, moss-like addition to any freshwater aquarium or planted tank. They’re often used in low light tanks for greening, an aquascaping technique where moss is attached to driftwood and rocks to create an aged, natural look. Simply pull the ball apart and gently wedge into cracks or attach with a very small amount of adhesive. Marimo Balls are also decorative on their own and are often kept in glass jars or similar containers. They’re great for betta fish tanks, shrimp setups, and more. If your Marimo floats, it likely has air trapped inside. Squeeze it gently to release and drop it back in! Quick and easy examples of the greening method and how to unball a Marimo Moss Ball: How to care for a Marimo Ball Marimo Balls require very little maintenance. They prefer cooler water temperatures below 76°F. In still water or under stronger lighting, you may need to manually rotate them occasionally to ensure all sides receive light. Otherwise, they’re fine in low light, tolerate a wide range of water parameters, and can even survive in slightly brackish water. Their hardy nature and minimal care makes them a top beginner “aquarium plant”! Common Name Marimo Ball Care Easy Lighting Low to Medium CO2 Optional Suggested Placement Loose / Attached to hardscape Propagation Gently separate Growth Rate Varies Height Varies

Limnophila Aromatica is a beautiful aquatic stem plant. Hailing from Asia, Limnophila Aromatica features large, narrow green leaves with a purple hue on its underside. Limnophila Aromatica is quite large when cared for properly and makes a great addition to the background of larger planted aquarium tanks. This aquatic stem plant's coloration depends greatly on the type of environment it is kept in and quality aquarium LED lighting along with CO2 injection promotes healthy growth significantly. Like other aquatic stem plants, Limnophila Aromatica is easy to propagate and can be done by cutting at the stem and replanting it into quality aquarium soil. This aquatic plant can grow at a quick pace requiring consistent trims to achieve the bushy effect that is sought after by planted tank enthusiasts. We recommend this plant for aquarists looking for a unique background aquatic plant! It is also said that Limnophila Aromatica earns its name from the scent it gives off when its leaves are crushed! Common Name Limnophila Aromatica Limnophila Hippuridoides Care Medium Lighting Medium to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 7+"

Hygrophila Compact is a lovely midground aquatic plant choice! Showcasing very compact, low growth, Hygrophila Compact is derived from the original species Hygrophila Corymbosa with leaves that sit close to its stem. Foliage is large and bold with varying coloration depending on the aquarium tank it is grown and kept in. Color tones can vary from bold brownish reds and pinks to shades of green. As mentioned, Hygrophila Compact makes a wonderful choice as a midground aquatic plant choice due to its interesting growth habits. This aquarium plant will readily form dense, compact bushes and will fill out sparse areas in a planted aquarium tank with ease. This aquarium plant requires medium levels of quality aquarium LED lighting and the addition of CO2 injection aids in promoting quicker more robust growth. Weak lighting can result in Hygrophila Compact growing upwards towards the light. This can be combated by providing higher light settings and ensuring it is trimmed to encourage low-growing habits. Hygrophila Compact is quite undemanding but can be susceptible to nutrient deficiencies. Common Name Hygrophila Corymbosa Compact Hygrophila Compact Hygrophila Nomaphila Siamensis Care Easy Lighting Medium to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Midground Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate Height 3-5”

Add a natural filtration powerhouse to your planted aquarium with Salvinia Cucullata. This fast-growing floating fern develops soft green, cup-like leaves across the water's surface while its relatively short root system stays more compact than many other aquarium floaters. Beyond its unique appearance, Salvinia Cucullata actively absorbs available nutrients from the water column as it grows, making it a useful addition to planted aquariums and ponds. Its floating coverage and dangling roots also provide added shelter for shrimp, fry, and other small aquarium livestock. When conditions are right, Salvinia Cucullata can multiply quickly and spread across large areas of the water's surface. Regularly remove excess growth to maintain open areas for gas exchange and prevent the plants below from becoming heavily shaded.

Pistia Stratiotes, commonly called Water Lettuce, is a free-floating aquatic plant that is commonly used as an ornamental plant in water gardens, ponds and aquariums. Wedge-shaped, soft green leaves sprout from the center in an overlapping pattern and are covered with water-repellent hairs. Similar to other floating plants commonly used in the aquarium hobby, Pistia Stratiotes is quick growing and can easily cover the surface area of a planted aquarium tank if left to self-propagate without maintenance. Regular pruning should be performed to ensure aquarium plants below are not shaded from the lighting source. Sporting long, feathery roots, Pistia Stratiotes works great in helping to absorb excess nutrients in the water column and preventing algae blooms. Smaller fish and shrimp species also tend to find shelter within this plant's root structure.

Aridarum Caulescens 'White Fang' is an aquatic plant with care requirements similar to its better-known counterpart, Aridarum 'Saber Tooth'. This species features elongated, slender leaves with a thick texture, waxy appearance, and soft green coloration. Its hardy foliage can withstand stronger water currents without sustaining damage. The leaves emerge from an Anubias-like rhizome, and the plant can be propagated similarly to Anubias, Bucephalandra, and Java Fern. Aridarum Caulescens 'White Fang' prefers low to medium lighting and is known for its extremely slow growth rate. Although patience is required, its gradual development can be rewarding. Like other epiphytic aquatic plants, its rhizome should not be buried in the substrate, as this can cause the plant to rot. Instead, we recommend attaching Aridarum Caulescens 'White Fang' to aquarium hardscape, such as driftwood or aquascaping rocks, where it can establish itself naturally.

Bucephalandra Catherinae Red Mini is a beautiful dwarf variant of the well-known Bucephalandra Catherinae Red. This species of buce exhibits a low-growing pattern that is paired with small, ruffled leaves. Buce Catherinae Red Mini sometimes referred to as simply Buce Catherinae Mini is a wonderful choice for nano-sized aquascape layouts and does well when attached to hardscape material such as aquarium driftwood and aquascaping stones . Also due to its small size, Buce Catherinae Red Mini is great for creating scale and producing fine, delicate details in a planted aquarium tank. Like all Bucephalandra species, Buce Catherinae Red Mini is a great species to add to any enthusiast's collection and is generally undemanding. This bucephalandra species is very forgiving in a wide range of aquarium tank parameters, prefers low-medium aquarium LED lighting and does not need much fertilization. Implementing CO2 injection in the planted aquarium tank will aid in boosting growth speed and producing more robust foliage. Given this aquatic plant's easy-going nature, it is a great choice for beginner aquarists and its care is comparable to other popular aquatic plant species such as Anubias and Java Ferns .

Bucephalandra Paris is a medium-sized species of Bucephalandra that features hardy leaves with varying color tones. With its mismatched stem color, Bucephalandra Paris is a beautiful, ornamental aquatic plant that would work well in the midground of a planted aquarium tank. Similar in care to other Bucephalandra species, Anubias species, and aquatic fern species, Bucephalandra Paris is undemanding and does well in a wide range of aquarium tank parameters. Despite its hardy nature, Bucephalandra species do even better when provided with a clean, balanced environment with appropriate aquarium LED lighting, CO2 injection and a regular fertilizing schedule. With additional effort in care, Bucephalandra Paris, like many others, rewards the owner with robust growth and intensified coloration that is highly sought-after by many planted aquarium tank enthusiasts. Buce's ease of care along with a variety of shapes, sizes, and colors makes Bucephalandra a favorite amongst beginner hobbyists and experienced enthusiasts. Bucephalandra Paris, too, can be grown submerged in a planted aquarium tank or kept emersed in terrarium-like setups. Propagation is simple and can be done by gently separating the rhizome and replanting it within the crevice of an aquascape layout or attaching it to aquarium stone or aquarium tank driftwood.

The Glass Aqua Wabi Kusa Starter Kit is a complete, pre-curated setup designed to cultivate your own Wabi Kusa. A Japanese-inspired art form, Wabi Kusa features aquatic plants grown out of water, often on a substrate ball. The imperfect nature of this aquascaping style results in an organic, natural planted display that many aquascapers have come to enjoy. Unlike traditional aquariums, Wabi Kusa setups require minimal equipment and space, making them an approachable and rewarding way to enjoy aquatic plants in a new form. With the included rimless tank, lighting, and substrate, this kit provides everything needed to create your own inspired plant display. Whether molded into a classic Wabi Kusa soil ball or used as a base substrate, this setup offers flexibility in design while maintaining the necessary environment for emersed aquatic plant growth. Looking for plants to get started? Pair this kit with our Wabi Kusa Mystery Plant Bag for a curated selection of compatible species. What this Kit is Best For - Wabi Kusa and emersed plant displays - Plant enthusiasts looking for an easy tank display - Desktop or small-space nature displays - Aquascapers experimenting with emersed growth techniques - Unique, gift-ready plant setups What Makes Wabi Kusa Different This type of planted display requires minimal equipment when compared to traditional aquariums and focuses on humidity and moisture instead of filtration. It offers a wonderful hybrid and good starting point between aquarium and terrariums. A key design principle is being able to find the beauty in imperfection! When a variety of aquatic plant species are grown together and allowed to naturally intertwine, the result is organic and quite lovely! We recommend any plant lover to give this style a try. What’s Included - UNS 16T tall rimless glass aquarium - UNS 16T flush fitting glass lid - Black leveling mat - Aqua Worx SOL magnetic LED light with stand - UNS Controsoil substrate Kit Tank Model Dimensions (IN) W x D x H Volume (GAL) 16T Ultum Nature Systems 16T 6.29 x 6.29 x 9.45 1.6 Getting Started Step 1: Add Controsoil and shape it into a mound or form a classic Wabi Kusa ball Step 2: Use aquascaping tweezers to plant your selected species directly into the soil mound or ball Step 3: Lightly mist and place the lid to retain humidity. Open daily for 5-10 minutes to allow airflow and monitor moisture levels. Remove dead or damaged leaves to prevent mold growth. As plants transition from submerged to emersed growth, they often develop thicker leaves and more rigid structure over time.

Pogostemon Sampsonii is a beautiful aquatic plant species that is still extremely difficult to obtain in the planted aquarium tank hobby and is considered a rarity. Sometimes referred to as Pogostemon Cf. Pumilus, Pogostemon Sampsonii features relatively compact growth that is perfect for achieving bushy sections in the midground of a planted aquarium tank. Pogostemon Sampsonii's leaves are crisp green in coloration and are slightly waved with softly serrated edges. These leaves sit fairly close in proximity to each other and sprout from Pogostemon Sampsonii's thicker stem. Pogostemon Sampsonii can be compared to Limnophila Aromatica Wavy in appearance but differs slightly in color, density, and overall care. This aquatic stem plant is relatively demanding and will require some experience in keeping aquatic plants to ensure it thrives properly. Factors such as quality aquarium tank LED lighting, CO2 injection from a pressurized system and specialized aquatic plant fertilizer are recommended. On top of this, a consistent and thorough maintenance routine should be followed to ensure water is kept clean within the planted aquarium tank. Propagation for Pogostemon Sampsonii is similar to any other aquatic stem plant and can be done by cutting the stem and replanting it into quality, nutrient-dense aquarium soil. Like some aquatic stem plants and aquarium plants in general, Pogostemon Sampsonii can be grown in emersed conditions. Sufficient humidity should be provided to ensure it does not dry out and wither. Pogostemon Sampsonii is a unique aquatic plant and would be a wonderful additional to any planted aquarium tank. Alternatively, we'd recommend utilizing it in a pond-style aquarium tank setup! Common Name Pogostemon Cf Pumilus Pogostemon Sampsonii Care Moderate to Difficult Lighting Medium to High CO2 Required Suggested Placement Midground Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 5-10”

Polygonum Sao Paulo is an amazing aquatic plant species that presents a deep magenta hue that is not commonly found in planted aquarium tanks. Sometimes cross-referenced as Persicaria Kawagoeanum or Persicaria Sp Sao Paulo, Polygonum Sao Paulo features bold coloration, quick upright growth and is a unique addition to any planted aquarium tank. Polygonum Sao Paulo, also known as Sao Paulo Smartweed, is relatively demanding and will require some experience in keeping aquatic plants to ensure it thrives properly. To keep this aquatic stem plant in tip-top shape, ample aquarium tank LED lighting, CO2 injection and a consistent maintenance routine should be provided to ensure optimal conditions for lush growth. If successful, Polygonum Sao Paulo breaks the water surface fairly easy and will reward you with frequent flowering. Propagation for Polygonum Sao Paulo is similar to any other aquatic stem plant and can be done by cutting the stem and replanting it into quality, nutrient-dense aquarium soil. Like some aquatic stem plants and aquarium plants in general, Polygonum Sao Paulo can be grown in emersed conditions and resembles the popular bamboo look that is highly coveted! Polygonum Sao Paulo, when provided with optimal conditions is a very deeply colored plant that looks similar to the popular Purple Bamboo. Sufficient humidity should be provided to ensure it does not dry out and wither. Polygonum Sao Paulo is a unique aquatic plant and would be a wonderful addition to any planted aquarium tank. Alternatively, we'd recommend utilizing it in a pond-style aquarium tank setup! Common Name Persicaria Sp Sao Paulo Sao Paulo Smartweed Care Moderate to Difficult Lighting Medium to High CO2 Required Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 5-10+”

Cryptocoryne Tropica Hybrid is a slight variation of the well-known Cryptocoryne Tropica. Sporting relatively broad leaves, Cryptocoryne Tropica Hybrid varies a little in coloration and tends to have lighter hues when compared to the original version of this aquatic plant. Like most Cryptocoryne, Crypt Tropica is robust and fairly hardy once it is established in a planted aquarium tank. Cryptocoryne species can take time to adjust and can be extremely sensitive to displacement and changes in water parameters during this period so care should be taken to leave this aquarium plant undisturbed for a short duration. Cryptocoryne Tropica Hybrid is suitable for smaller sized planted aquarium tanks and works well as a midground aquatic plant choice. When provided with CO2 injection, low to medium aquarium tank LED lighting and light fertilization, Cryptocoryne Tropica produces beautiful, compact growth. An alternative use for this aquatic plant is within emersed conditions. As long as sufficient humidity is provided, Cryptocoryne Tropica Hybrid works well and will grow in terrarium-like setups such as vivariums, paludariums and more. Propagation is simple and can be done by separating new plantlets from the mother plant and replanting it into quality aquarium soil intended for aquatic plant keeping.

Rotala Wallichii is a popular species of stem plant that is characterized by its thin leaves. Although fragile, it is a great choice when creating lush clusters of green and red that resemble an ornate woodland forest. This plant does well when provided with high lighting, CO2, and fertilization dosing and it will give you a vibrant mix of pink, red, yellow and orange hues. It's a beautiful choice for a background plant. Common Name Rotala Wallichii Care Moderate Lighting Medium to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Fast Height 10-30"

Hakkai Stone, also known as Pa-Hai Stone or Bug Eaten Stone, is a best selling aquarium stone! It’s easy to spot thanks to its signature mix of blue, grey and subtle green undertones. Combine this with its smooth, rounded shape and naturally eroded grooves, Hakkai is an absolute gem for aquascaping! Its unique features and soft color are the result of years of natural weathering, which also contributes to its rarity and limited availability when compared to other popular stones used for planted aquariums. On the density scale, it is one of the heaviest used in the hobby. If you've checked out our general calculation for how many pounds you need for your planted tank, we recommend ordering extra, if possible, to receive multiple pieces and a wider variety of sizes. It is also inert, making it a safe choice that won’t alter parameters. If you enjoy river-style aquascapes, Iwagumi layouts or calming nature aquariums, Hakkai Stone will be the first stone we recommend. Pair it with delicate or grass-like aquatic plants to complete the look. Shown below is a UNS 90L (20-gallon long) planted aquarium featuring Hakkai Stone.

Blue Mountain Seiryu Stone is a unique type of Seiryu Stone that is mainly darker, medium gray with a blueish tinge. Along with a difference in coloration, Blue Mountain Seiryu also features defined, lightly colored veins running throughout the stone. This difference in tone provides a larger contrast when paired with different species of aquarium plants. Just like the classic Seiryu Stone , Blue Mountain Seiryu Stone can be used to create Iwagumi style aquascape layouts. This aquascaping stone is still very versatile and with some creativity, can produce a wide variety of looks in a planted aquarium tank.

This aquascaping rock features a porous surface, distinct shape and earthy tones that pair well with vivid aquatic plants. Mountain Stone's gritty texture offers good grip and is a perfect foundation for attaching aquatic mosses or epiphytic aquarium plants such as Anubias and Bucephalandra. Along with Mountain Stone's porous surface comes low density. This aquarium rock is very lightweight when compared to heavier choices such as Seiryu or Hakkai Stone. You'll receive a wider range of pieces without sacrificing quality and character! They're easy to stack and retain structural integrity, making it a solid freshwater aquarium rock for scaping cliff-inspired aquascapes or creating caves, canyons and mountainous hardscape layouts.

Wolf Stone is a planted tank aquarium rock that is almost a hybrid between Elephant Skin Stone and Icelandic Lava Stone . Elephant Skin Stone features more rounded edges while Wolf Stone provides more of a sharper jagged texture, varying color tones and is relatively porous like Icelandic Lava Stone. Wolf Stone's porous surface also makes it a great contender for attaching aquarium plants such as aquatic mosses, Anubias , and Bucephalandra . Another added benefit is another area is presented for beneficial bacteria to build colonies that are essential for a balanced planted aquarium tank. We recommend pairing Wolf Stone with species such as Mini Christmas Moss , Java Moss , Mini Pellia and Fissidens Fontanus for a beautiful, aged look. A simple foreground aquarium plant or fine natural sand along with a minimal choice of other aquatic plants would complete the look.

Our favorite tool for keeping aquarium tank glass clear and clean! Adjustable sizing to be suitable for a wide range of planted aquarium tanks Comes with 10 razor-sharp refill blades for increased product longevity Algae scrapers are an essential tool in the aquascaper's arsenal. These handy tools are primarily used for aiding in the removal of algae from the aquarium tank's glass surfaces, but may also be used to flatten the substrate in a straight line for a clean appearance. Available in 3 models, there is a size for every aquarium tank. Depending on the size of aquarium tanks kept, each model offers varying length and degree of adjustability. Constructed from strong, durable materials, these algae scrapers are suitable for use in both freshwater planted aquarium tanks as well as saltwater reef, coral and marine aquariums. With a sleek form, these algae scrapers are great for cleaning hard to reach areas in a planted aquarium and simple to clean. Coming with 10 replacement blades, these algae scrapers are sure to last and will clean many aquarium tanks to come! Important Note: Algae Scraper Extension rod is compatible with the Qanvee X3 aquarium algae scraper only. CO2 Cartridge Bottle Base Hanger This CO2 Cartridge Bottle Hanger ensures that the CO2 Cartridge stays in an upright position. Crafted to fit the CO2 replacement cartridge bottle perfectly, this bottle hanger is essential to prevent liquefied gas leaking into a CO2 aquarium regulator. This CO2 Cartridge Bottle Hanger will prevent unnecessary gas build-up and potential danger to the user and aquarium inhabitants. Why CO2 injection is important in a planted tank: 3 main factors contribute to the optimal growth of aquatic plants. These factors include nutrients, light and carbon dioxide (CO2). If any of these are unbalanced, the results are algae growth or the withering of plants. The introduction of CO2 in a planted aquarium allows plants to thrive and grow more efficiently, while also giving them the ability to outcompete algae for nutrients. No matter what type of planted aquarium setup you have, we recommend CO2 injection for better aquarium plant growth. Note : Works for 90-95G mini disposable CO2 cartridges.

listings.commonName: Twinstar Reactor Algae Inhibitor Replacement Disk
listings.description: The Twinstar Reactor is a replacement disk for the Twinstar Algae Inhibitor line. To clean the Twinstar Algae Inhibitor disk, we recommend doing so with the Twinstar Reactor Calcium Cleaner . The Twinstar Algae Inhibitor effectively inhibits the growth of different strains of algae such as green algae amongst others. This device does so without any negative impact on the aquarium tank ecosystem and is safe for aquatic plants, freshwater fish and shrimp species, and beneficial bacteria. The Twinstar Algae Inhibitor works by eliminating algae spores during the early stages, ultimately preventing it from growing. With the reduction of algae growth, aquatic plant growth is encouraged and aquatic plants are able to remain healthy and compete with algae for excess nutrients in the water column. This further starves algae strains and prevents it from reproducing. It is best to install this device during the initial setup of an aquarium when algae are non-existent. The results of a comparative test with Glossostigma and Rotala Indica revealed that Glossostigma's growth increased up to 50% and Rotala Indica increased up to 40%. Every Ultum Nature Systems Aquarium Tank Stand comes fully assembled and is ready to use right out of the box. Presenting a simple cut, these aquarium tank stands are minimal in appearance and fit in perfectly with modern design in any designated space. Nesaea Crassicaulis is a beautiful aquatic stem plant that features a striking color palette when grown in optimal planted aquarium tank conditions. Similar to other species in the same family, Nesaea Crassicaulis also requires a good amount of quality aquarium LED lighting along with CO2 injection and more specific water parameters to promote lush, boldly colored growth. These factors make this aquarium plant slightly more advanced and not recommended for beginner hobbyists. When planting, Nesaea Crassicaulis should be planted in quality aquarium soil with enough space between each stem to ensure lower levels receive an ample amount of lighting as well. Lack of lighting can result in dull coloration as well as the rotting of the lower portions. This aquarium plant can also be grown in emersed conditions. When emersed, it can be easily confused for an aquarium plant in the Ammania family, but submerged conditions will produce finer narrow-leafed growth. We recommend planting Nesaea Crassicaulis in the midground of a planted aquarium tank. The style of this aquatic stem plant would work well for a classic Nature Aquarium Style planted aquarium or in a Dutch Style planted aquarium as well. The slight variation in deep orange and bronze tones would add a lovely contrast to groups of red, magenta and green aquarium stem plants. Simple to propagate, Nesaea Crassicaulis can be treated the same as other aquatic stem plants: simply cut the stem and replant the trimmings into quality aquarium soil. Common Name Nesaea Crassicaulis Ammannia Crassicaulis Thick-Stemmed Nesaea Care Moderate to Advanced Lighting Medium to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Midground or Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 5-12" Our bunched stem plants are all kept and grown in high-quality substrate by Marfied Controsoil . A strict fertilizer dosing regime and CO2 are provided in their holding tanks.

Ludwigia Sphaerocarpa, also known as Roundfruit Primrose Willow, is a rare form that isn't commonly seen in aquascaping. Native to wetlands of North America, this aquatic stem plant is perfect for high tech planted aquariums and aquascapers who enjoy growing challenging aquatic plants. It features a unique growth pattern that is compact and almost rosette-like, and spreads horizontally before growing upwards. When grown in a planted tank with strong lighting, CO2 and a regular dosing routine, Sphaerocarpa develops a vivid color palette that includes orange, brown and rich red tones. Its intense color will surely stand out in any aquascape. It is on the slower side of growth, but patience will be generously rewarded! Provide it with nutrient-rich aquarium substrate and make sure to trim it regularly to encourage new growth and branching behavior. If you're looking for a unique aquarium plant that isn't commonly seen, try this one out. Common Name Roundfruit Primrose Willow / L. Pilosa Care Moderate to Advanced Lighting High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Midground or Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 5-12"

Java Fern Needle Leaf belongs to the Microsorum genus and is easy to spot thanks to its distinctive, slender appearance. This popular choice for planted aquariums features narrow, ribbon-like leaves and is just as low maintenance as other Java Fern plants. It tends to grow a little denser, making it a great pick for aquascapes using driftwood and tanks of all sizes. Care requirements are minimal, and its hardiness makes it a natural favorite for both beginner and experienced aquascapers. Recently reclassified as Leptochilus pteropus , this plant is still widely known in the hobby as Microsorum pteropus. But, if you’re looking for live aquarium plants for a low-tech tank or your first aquascape, Java Fern Needle Leaf is a perfect fit. Its care is similar to other beginner-friendly aquatic plants like Anubias, Bucephalandra, Cryptocoryne and mosses. For a healthy start, plant your Java Fern in established setups with mature cycles — Good tank maintenance and clean water are key and help prevent common issues with plants in general. While optional, providing CO2 injection and a liquid aquatic plant fertilizer are great for overall health and boosting growth speed. Propagation is simple! When your fern is ready, gently separate it at the base rhizome and reattach it.

Ludwigia Twister is a unique species in the Ludwigia family. Just as its name describes, this odd aquarium plant features curled leaves that are presented in tight spirals sprouting from the stem. With such a unique appearance, Ludwigia Twister, sometimes also referred to as Ludwigia Curly, makes for a great ornamental aquatic plant. As Ludwigia Twister is still considered a rarity, there is limited information available regarding its care. However, it has been observed to be similar to Ludwigia Inclinata Cuba. When provided with quality lighting, CO2 injection and proper nutrients, Ludwigia Twister grows at a fast pace like most aquarium stem plants and will require regular pruning to encourage bushy, branching growth. Propagation is simple and can be done the same as any other aquarium stem plant. Simply cut the stem using quality aquascaping tools and replant them into a quality substrate. Ludwigia Twister can also be grown in both submerged aquarium settings or in emersed conditions. If optimal health is reached, this aquarium plant will also produce small yellow flowers above the water's surface.

Aponogeton Natans is a lovely aquarium plant that can be found in the waters of India and Sri Lanka. Because its native environment features temporarily stagnant waters, Aponogeton Natans naturally produces floating leaves. However, when kept in an aquarium, Aponogeton Natans produces large, slightly ruffled leaves making it a great choice for planted aquarium tanks that offer space and a large surface area. This aquarium plant's overall structure is quite delicate and should be handled with care. Because it can grow quite large, we also recommend this aquarium plant for larger sized aquarium tanks in the background area. Similar to other plants in the same family, Aponogeton Natans is relatively easy to keep and is forgiving in nature. This aquatic plant has minimal requirements and will do fine in low to moderate aquarium lighting as long as substantial flow and water circulation is provided. Common Name Aponogeton Natans Care Easy Lighting Low to Medium CO2 Optional Suggested Placement Background Growth Rate Moderate Height 8-20"

Manten Stone is a beautiful aquarium hardscape. Characterized by rugged texture and a varying natural color palette, Manten Stone is a highly-coveted aquarium hardscape rock that is commonly used in Iwagumi style aquascape layouts and miniature mountainous hardscape layouts. Manten Stone can also be used beautifully in classic nature style aquariums as an accent or to support aquarium driftwood pieces. Manten Stone's realistic and unpredictable features are valued immensely by modern-day aquascapers as its notorious inconsistency is the key feature for producing realistic scenes in a planted aquarium tank. Hailing from high elevation mountainsides, Manten Stone is typically recognized as inert. This means that it will not impact water chemistry and is a safe choice for even sensitive freshwater aquatic life. Even so, we always encourage that water is tested and stones are cleansed thoroughly to ensure safe practices. With its varying color tones and unique form, Manten Stone makes for a perfect main hardscape choice or as an accent to any planted aquarium tank. When placed under quality aquarium LED lighting, this stone really shows off its colors and is a treat to see for all aquarists. Watch the video below to see how Manten Stones appear in the foreground of a Ultum Nature Systems 45U planted aquarium:

Rotala Red Cross, sometimes referred to as Rotala Araguaia Red Cross, is an interesting species in the Rotala family that exhibits bold color tones and a unique growth pattern. Considered an advanced aquarium plant, Rotala Red Cross features thin leaves that sprout from the main stem with a varying color palette of greens, yellow and red tones with colors being more intense towards the top parts of the stems. Depending on the condition it is kept in, Rotala Red Cross may produce a slight twist in its leaves making it a unique Rotala species to add to any planted aquarium tank. Like many species of Rotala, Rotala Red Cross is suitable for the mid to background areas of a nature aquarium and should be planted in areas that receive plenty of aquarium LED lighting. CO2 injection along with quality aquarium soil is recommended as well to promote lush growth. Propagation is simple and can be done by trimming along the stem and replanting in quality aquarium soil. Common Name Rotala sp. Red Cross Rotala Araguaia Red Cross Care Difficult Lighting High CO2 Required Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate Height 4-12 " Our bunched aquarium stem plants are all kept and grown in a high-quality aquarium substrate . A strict fertilizer dosing regime and CO2 injection are provided in their holding aquarium tanks.
