The Assorted Rhizome Bundle is an easy way to add variety to a planted aquarium with species that naturally attach to driftwood, stone, and other hardscape materials. Each bundle includes a random selection of rhizome plants such as Bucephalandra, Anubias, and Java Fern, making it a convenient option for aquascapers looking to introduce texture, detail, and life throughout an aquascape. Rhizome plants are known for their versatility and ability to flourish in both low tech tanks and advanced setups alike. Because they are attached rather than planted in substrate, they're perfect for driftwood-focused layouts and filling in empty spaces where additional greenery is desired. Rotala Macrandra Pink is a highly sought-after species that is characterized by its beautiful hues. Just like Rotala Macrandra Red, Rotala Macrandra Pink makes a wonderful choice as a background aquarium plant or for any aquascape that needs a little color variation. Being part of the Macrandra family, Rotala Macrandra Pink is no exception and is a fairly difficult aquarium plant to keep happy, making it suitable for aquarists with a good amount of experience under their belt. Like most Rotala species, Rotala Macrandra Pink prefers soft water and with quality aquarium LED lighting, CO2 injection and nutrient-dense aquarium soil. This Rotala species has the potential to grow quite large as well so it should be grown in medium to larger sized planted aquarium tanks, avoiding nano planted tanks. Individual stems should be given sufficient space when planting as planting too compact will result in the lower portions of the aquarium plant void of light. Rotala Macrandra Pink is very demanding and can be difficult to keep, but results are well worth the extra effort and are rewarding if successful. Characterized by its thick stem, Ammania Gracilis offers beautiful pink, orange to red hues for relatively undemanding care. This aquarium plant's leaves are sprouted opposite of each other along the stem and offer good texture from its wavy appearance. Add flowing greenery to your planted aquarium with Pogostemon Stellatus 'Octopus'. This fast-growing aquatic stem plant features long, bright green leaves that sprout along the central stem. Its loose, flowing growth creates soft, bushy groups of foliage that add organic movement and texture to the midground or background of an aquascape. Pogostemon Stellatus 'Octopus' is a more forgiving species within the genus family, making it an approachable choice for hobbyists who enjoy its delicate, feathery appearance. Botanical Note: Commonly sold as Pogostemon stellatus 'Octopus', this plant is now correctly identified as Pogostemon quadrifolius. The original trade name remains widely used and accepted in the aquarium hobby.

We're excited to now offer the Wabi Kusa Mystery Plant Bag! Hand-selected by our team, we've chosen a mixture of aquarium plants that grow well in emersed conditions, provide different textures, transition smoothly and are relatively hardy in nature. Try your hand at creating your own Wabi Kusa with our Wabi Kusa Mystery Plant Bag! Wabi Kusa Mystery Plant Bag Includes 1x Randomly Selected Echinodorus Aquatic Plant 2x Randomly Selected Aquarium Moss 1 Randomly Selected Potted Plant 1 Randomly Selected Bunched Stem Plant Wabi Kusa is a recent trend within the aquascaping community. Presenting a new challenge, Wabi Kusa calls for the growth of aquarium plants in their emersed forms. Designed to allow even the most space-challenged households to participate and become active in the art of aquatic plant keeping, Wabi Kusa typically involves various aquarium plant species, a nutritious base and a simple glass container for holding and displaying the creation. Our Wabi Kusa Mystery Plant Bag contains select, but random aquarium plants that are fit to thrive in a Wabi Kusa style setting. Aquarium plants chosen are suitable for growing in emersed conditions and are hardy during the transition phase so long as correct care is provided. What is Wabi Kusa? Wabi Kusa does not have a literal translation but alludes to the creation of a tangible item that envokes a natural feeling through an aesthetic, imperfectly beautiful arrangement of plants. In simpler terms, a Wabi Kusa is typically a ball of nutritious aquarium soil compacted together and adorned by aquarium plants. The finished Wabi Kusa is then placed into the container of choice and allowed to grow naturally with little disturbance as nature intends. Why We Love Wabi Kusa: Wabi Kusa is relatively easy to care for and require a minimal amount of maintenance. A great choice for those with limited space! Wabi Kusa setups are easy to move and typically on the smaller side. Rearrange your space without worrying about dealing with wires and equipment that comes with planted aquarium tanks. Wonderful way to introduce the art of aquatic plant keeping to beginner aquarists. Wabi Kusa will attract even terrestrial plant lovers! It can be transitioned back to submerged form for an instant aquascape piece. Wabi Kusa should be kept in a sealed container to trap moisture and humidity. Air out and allow essential gas exchange to occur by opening the container once per day for 5-10 minutes.

Vesicularia Sp. Mini Christmas Moss is a lovely aquatic moss that is commonly seen in the planted aquarium hobby. This aquarium moss presents a lighter green tone and densely ramified growth, making it a great contender for bushy patches along porous stone or aquarium driftwood. Like other aquarium mosses, Mini Xmas Moss provides shade and coverage for shrimp and tropical fish searching for refuge. Mini Xmas Moss's appearance provides a delicate texture to help soften an aquascape layout that otherwise has sharp edges and straight lines. It can be attached to hardscape material to create tree-like structures, cover unnatural cuts, simply left free-floating or placed in the foreground. It is quite forgiving and can be grown in a wide range of aquarium conditions and water parameters. In addition, it is often quite sought after for its compact growth and look as compared to other aquatic mosses.

Eleocharis Vivipara offers wispy background coverage in nature style aquariums or river inspired aquascapes. Remove this plant from its growing medium before planting. Click here to shop all aquarium plants! Eleocharis Vivipara is similar in foliage texure to the popular carpeting aquarium plant, Eleocharis Parvula aka Hair Grass. Eleocharis Vivipara, sometimes referred to as Umbrella Hair Grass, is a much taller variation of Eleocharis and offers excellent background coverage that will sometimes droop over and create a beautiful effect when it has reached the aquarium's water surface. We recommend this plant in river-style planted aquariums or in nature style aquarium tanks. It offers a semi-chaotic appearance and is extremely natural in any planted tank. A Glass Aqua favorite for background plant choice in a wide range of aquascacpes! A pressurized CO2 system is not required to grow Eleocharis Vivipara, but will promote quicker, lush growth. Once established, Eleocharis Vivipara is a prolific grower and will happily spread to all areas of an aquarium. To prevent this, regular trimming will be essential in maintaining this plant's growth! Taxiphyllum sp. 'Spiky Moss', commonly known as Spiky Moss, is an Asiatic aquarium moss recognized for its upright growth and larger, vibrant green, branched fronds and shoots. This aquarium moss grows best on vertical surfaces, where its distinctive branching pattern can fully develop. However, like other aquarium mosses, it is versatile with placement and looks great when planted in small tufts to create a bushy, carpeting effect. Fast-growing and adaptable, Spiky Moss will grow even under very low light conditions. It is quite forgiving and can be grown in a wide range of aquarium conditions and water parameters.

Taxiphyllum sp. 'Peacock,' commonly known as Peacock Moss, is a popular aquatic moss used in aquariums and terrariums. Native to Southeast Asia, it does best in slow-moving or still waters and can be found encursted on rocks, driftwood and other submerged natural surfaces. It features rich green color and delicate, feathery fronds, making it a favored choice for aquascaping and terrarium building. Peacock Moss also provides excellent shade and coverage for shrimp, fish and other microfauna. It can be attached to hardscape material to create tree-like structures, cover unnatural cuts or simply left free floating or placed in the foreground. After it establishes itself in a healthy planted aquarium tank, it grows to be quite thick as opposed to the more common Java Moss. It is quite forgiving and can be grown in a wide range of aquarium conditions and water parameters.

The slender and sharp leaves of Anubias Congensis Mini differentiates this particular Anubias from that of the much more common Barteri or Nana variants. It is a perfect addition to the mid-ground of standard planted aquarium tanks thanks to its leaf size and deep green coloring. Similar to other Anubias, it's a great choice for beginners due to its easy care and overall hardiness. It also has the ability to thrive in both aquariums and terrariums set ups. It's a flowering plant that grows best when the rhizome is attached to hardscape material such as wood or stone. Regular fertilization is favorable and low to medium lighting is sufficient as high lighting will promote the growth of algae on its leaves. CO2 is not required but promotes faster growth and robust leaves. Propagation is straightforward; simply cut or pull apart rhizomes to be reattached.

This distinctive stem plant develops oblong, gently wavy leaves in shades of gold, orange, and red, creating strong contrast against surrounding green foliage. Ludwigia Inclinata is a more demanding Ludwigia best suited for experienced hobbyists and high-tech planted aquariums. Strong lighting is important for healthy growth and coloration, while CO2 injection and consistent fertilization are highly recommended to support its best form. When given suitable conditions, its colorful foliage makes a striking addition to the midground or background of an aquascape.

Microsorum pteropus ‘Petite’, more commonly known as Java Fern Petite, is a smaller, compact form of the classic Java Fern. It features slightly wavy, narrow leaves that give it a softer look compared to other slender varieties like Narrow Leaf. Recently reclassified as Leptochilus pteropus , this plant is still widely known in the aquarium hobby as Microsorum pteropus. Like other Java Fern varieties, it is hardy, easy to care for, and well suited for aquarists of all skill levels. Its smaller size makes it especially useful for nano aquariums, where it can be used as a main plant, or as a detailed accent in larger planted tanks. Java Fern Petite is great for filling in open spaces and adds a natural, layered look to aquascapes. As an epiphytic plant, it can be attached to driftwood, rocks, or aquarium decor using thread or glue. Be sure to keep the rhizome above the substrate to prevent rot. Propagation is simple—just divide the rhizome and reattach as needed.

Pogostemon Deccanensis is a beautiful aquarium stem plant that is still relatively new in the hobby. Similar to Pogostemon Erectus, Pogostemon Deccanensis offers a delicate touch to the midground or background of planted aquarium tanks. Pogostemon Deccanensis is characterized by needle-like, thin leaves that are light green in coloration. Like most aquarium stem plants, Pogostemon Deccanensis does best when provided with quality aquarium LED lighting, CO2 injection, nutrient-dense aquarium soil, and a fertilizing routine. When planting Pogostemon Deccanensis, care should be taken to ensure space is left in between to ensure lower levels of the aquatic stem receive adequate lighting. If optimal conditions are provided, frequent trimming will be required to ensure Pogostemon Deccanensis is kept tidy. Pruning will also encourage bushy growth! Rotala Rotundifolia Platinum is a relatively new species of Rotala available in the planted aquarium hobby. This aquatic plant staple is a variation of the classic aquarium plant, Rotala Rotundifolia, but with a very intense change in hue. Rotala Rotundifolia Platinum, sometimes referred to as Rotala White, is extremely picky and most suitable for experienced aquarists. Sufficient aquarium LED lighting, CO2 injection, nutrient-dense aquarium soil, soft water, and an aquatic plant fertilizer are suggested for its care. It is slightly tinted to help disguise organic matter and waste that accumulates in tubing over time and is compatible with both metal and glass filter pipes! Echinodorus Reni is a common, well-known species in the Echinodorus aquatic plant family. This aquarium plant exhibits an easy-going nature and is safely one of the smallest red-toned Echinodorus species available in the aquarium hobby ranging from 5-10 inches tall. Similar to other reddish hued Echinodorus, Echinodorus Reni also offers a bold reddish-brown tone that would look beautiful in any planted aquarium tank while providing lovely contrast when used strategically with placement. Like other aquatic sword species, Echinodorus Reni is not too picky but does require a nutritious aquarium soil intended for aquatic plant propagation along with sufficient aquarium LED lighting. CO2 injection is not required but will help boost growth and overall health! Aside from this, Echinodorus species are fairly tolerable of varying water parameters in a planted aquarium tank. Pruning should be done frequently depending on the size desired and to ensure other aquarium plant species are not shaded from lighting. Propagation is simple. Separate and replant.

Rotala Rotundifolia Green, also known as simply Rotala Green is a very popular aquatic stem plant within the planted aquarium tank hobby. Belonging to the popular Rotala family, Rotala Green is commonly found in the midground of larger planted aquarium tanks or as the background in nano planted aquarium tanks. A lovely bright green coloration can be observed throughout the stem and its thinly rounded leaves. Rotala Rotundifolia Green is quite hardy, not too demanding and will do well if provided with high-quality aquarium LED lighting along with CO2 injection. Like all aquatic stem plants, Rotala Green should be given room when planted to ensure all parts of the plant are receiving adequate light. If ideal conditions are provided, Rotala Green grows at a quick pace and will readily produce side shoots that can be trimmed and replanted. To achieve lush, bush-like growth, Rotala Green should be trimmed often to promote this look! Propagation is simple. Like all aquatic stem plants, gently snip the aquatic plant along the stem and replant it into quality aquarium soil. Common Name Rotala Green Care Moderate Lighting Medium to High CO2 Optional Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Fast Height 15-30 " Our bunched aquarium stem plants are all kept and grown in high-quality substrate by Marfied Controsoil. A strict fertilizer dosing regime and CO2 are provided in their holding aquarium tanks. NOTE: We always recommend quarantining all new arrivals as safe practices before placing them in your aquarium.

Homalomena Silver is a distinctive aroid known for its thick, elongated leaves and soft silver-green coloration. Similar in appearance to Homalomena Humilis, this plant features compact foliage with a subtle silvery sheen that becomes especially noticeable under certain aquarium lighting. Its muted coloration and waxy leaf texture make it an attractive addition to aquascapes and planted displays. When grown emersed, Homalomena Silver may develop soft, slightly fuzzy foliage that takes on a smoother, glossier appearance under different growing conditions. This slow-growing plant prefers low to medium lighting and benefits from stable conditions. Excessive lighting may encourage algae growth on its leaves, particularly in submerged setups.

Homalomena Sungai is part of a rare family of flowering aquatic plants within the same realm as Bucephalandra and Aridarum. When grown emersed, Homalomena produces softer, fuzzy foliage that slowly transitions to a glossy and waxy state once transitioned to a submerged environment. Because of its rarity, the likelihood of a local fish store carrying this plant is slim to none. Homalomena species don't require excessive aquarium lighting to thrive as it is slow-growing and excessive lighting can cause algae growth on its leaves, much like Anubias and Buce. Homalomena is generally found in fast-flowing rivers across parts of Asia and South America and can often also be found as a common houseplant. Common Name Homalomena Sungai Care Moderate Lighting Low to Medium CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Attach to wood or stone Propagation Separate rhizome Growth Rate Slow to Moderate Height 4"+ Our potted plants are kept under strict fertilizer dosing regimes and are provided with CO2 injection in their holding tanks.

Fill your planted aquarium with lush, bright green foliage with Ceratopteris thalictroides, commonly known as Water Sprite. This fast-growing aquatic fern features finely divided, lacy leaves that spread outward as the plant matures, creating soft, whimsy greenery. Its naturally bushy growth makes it a great choice for filling open spaces in the midground or background of an aquascape. One of Water Sprite's most useful characteristics is its versatility. It can be planted directly into aquarium substrate or left floating at the water's surface, where its trailing roots and leaves provide additional coverage for fish, fry, and shrimplets. Its rapid growth also allows it to absorb nutrients directly from the water column, helping maintain a balanced system. Water Sprite is an easy, adaptable aquarium plant suitable for beginners and experienced hobbyists alike. It grows well in a variety of aquarium conditions without requiring CO2 injection, although adequate lighting and consistent nutrients support healthy growth. Under favorable conditions, Water Sprite can grow quite large, making regular trimming or removal of excess growth important for keeping it manageable.

Anubias Heterophylla is a classic Anubias species that offers a medium to large sizes Anubias in a planted aquarium tank. In its natural habitat, Anubias can be found growing on rocks close to stream edges partially emersed and submerged making it a great choice for both aquarium tanks and terrarium-like, emersed setups. Anubias Heterophylla, like most Anubias, is quite forgiving in nature and is easily loved by hobbyists of all skill levels due to its hardy nature and ability to adapt well to a wide range of aquarium tank parameters. Anubias Heterophylla is a bold green in hue and its leaves are fairly large with a slight wave. It has the potential to grow much larger when kept in its emersed state and will stay on the smaller side when kept in an aquarium fully submerged. Like other Anubias, Bucephalandra and Java Ferns, Anubias Heterophylla does best when attached securely to aquarium hardscape such as aquascaping stones or aquarium driftwood. Alternatively, it can also be placed between cracks in an aquascape layout and it will attach itself overtime. Care should be taken to ensure its roots are not glued when attaching as this can promote the rotting of the plant. Anubias benefits from consistent fertilization but light requirements are minimal as its leaves are susceptible to algae growth when placed under high lighting. CO2 is optional but can promote faster growth and robust leaves when used. This anubias is available in tissue culture form! Tissue culture plants are grown in sterilized conditions. This is the only way to guarantee a pest-free, snail-free start for your planted aquarium.

Cryptocoryne Hudoroi is a beautiful aquarium plant in the Cryptocoryne family that offers a unique midground accent in a planted aquarium tank. Sprouting from a rosette, Cryptocoryne Hudoroi features large, oblong foliage that varies in deep shades of green, reddish-brown and a slight bronze depending on the environment in which it is planted. Crypt Hudoroi's slightly ruffled leaves offer both interesting texture and contrast in a planted aquarium tank and their size provides a valuable refuge for smaller organisms in the tank. Like most Cryptocoryne species, Cryptocoryne Hudoroi does not prefer to be disturbed and care should be taken when deciding placement to ensure it is not moved in the foreseeable future as Crypt melt is a known phrase for good reason! Moderate, quality aquarium LED lighting is preferred along with CO2 injection and a nutrient-dense aquarium soil for good growth and the aquarium should be established if possible before adding Cryptocoryne Hudoroi as a newly set up tank can also lead to the melt of this aquarium plant. Propagation is simple and can be done by gently separating the mother plant into smaller portions and replanting into quality aquarium soil intended for aquatic plant propagation and growth.

Cryptocoryne Usteriana is a classic aquarium plant in the Cryptocoryne family that offers great coverage with an ornamental appearance in a planted aquarium tank. On the larger side, Cryptocoryne Usteriana features long leaves that, with the correct care, will offer a deep green hue with a rich Burgandy underside. Crypt Usteriana's leaves are slightly embossed and can easily reach lengths of up to 20" making this Cryptocoryne suitable for larger planted aquarium tanks. In optimal conditions, Cryptocoryne Usteriana is a lovely aquarium plant and is a treat to view! Like most Cryptocoryne species, Cryptocoryne Usteriana does not prefer to be disturbed and care should be taken when deciding placement to ensure it is not moved in the foreseeable future as Crypt melt is a known phrase for good reason! Moderate, quality aquarium LED lighting is preferred along with CO2 injection and a nutrient-dense aquarium soil for good growth and the aquarium should be established if possible before adding Cryptocoryne Usteriana as a newly set up tank can also lead to the melt of this aquarium plant. Propagation is simple and can be done by gently separating and replanting new growth into quality aquarium soil intended for aquatic plant propagation and growth.

Echinodorus Red Rubin is a beautiful hybrid of Echinodorus Horemanii Red and Barthii. This aquarium plant offers bold coloration and is suitable as a focal point or centerpiece aquarium plant in larger planted aquarium tanks. Echinodorus Red Rubin also exhibits horizontal growth if the lighting is strong enough and can grow quite wide. This should be kept in mind when deciding on placement. New growth displays a green tone and later matures into deep, bold red hues provided that optimal conditions and care are met. This aquatic sword plant is on the larger spectrum of the Echinodorus family and is suitable for planted aquarium tanks with ample space for it to spread its leaves. Like all aquatic sword species, Echinodorus Red Rubin is easy to keep, fairly hardy and needs a minimum of a nutrient-rich aquarium substrate as these species of aquatic plants are heavy root feeders. Aside from this, Echinodorus species are fairly tolerable of varying water parameters and lighting conditions. Given that this aquatic sword grows fairly large and robust, pruning periodically will be required to ensure smaller aquatic plants are not shaded from the light provided. Propagation is simple. Separate and replant. Common Name Amazon Sword Echinodorus Red Rubin Care Easy Lighting Low to Medium CO2 Optional Suggested Placement Background Propagation Separate and Replant Growth Rate Moderate Height 4-15+"

Black Forest Spider Wood is characterized by its signature dark, charcoal brown hue. This unique feature sets it apart from other aquascaping driftwoods such as normal Spider Wood which is lighter in color and only becomes brown in color once waterlogged. Black Forest Spider Wood, however, will become darker and darker as time passes. As a result, this bold aquarium wood provides a much darker-toned and mysterious planted aquarium atmosphere along with beautiful contrast against boldly colored aquatic plants. In addition, this Spider Wood releases a minimal amount of tannins that would otherwise tint aquarium water for a longer period of time. Wild twists and turns along with knots define this aquarium wood. Its natural root-like look is commonly sought after by enthusiasts. Black Forest Spider Wood works well on its own as a centerpiece or when complemented with smaller stones at the base of any scape. Measurement Range: Provided measurements are rough estimates. This driftwood is 100% natural, so dimensions may vary by a few inches. Please use them as general guidelines. SIZE DIMENSIONS NANO 1-4” ~ Nano tanks, cube tanks and most tanks. S 4-6” ~ Nano tanks, cube tanks, shallow tanks. M 6”+ ~ Standard aquariums and larger. Tanks with protruding pieces.

Bucephalandra Broad Wavy or Buce Broad Wavy is yet another a farm-grown variant of the extremely popular and classic aquarium plant, Bucephalandra Green Wavy. As its name implies, the characteristic ruffle-edged leaves are overall slightly larger than those seen on the original Bucephaandra Green Wavy. Coloration is similar and offers a bold green hue that provides lovely contrast to the midground of a planted aquarium tank. Form factor and overall size categorize this Buce species as a medium-sized aquarium plant that would work in the midground of a planted aquarium tank. Like other Bucephalandra, Buce Broad Wavy is versatile with placement and will grow well when attached to aquarium hardscape such as aquascaping stones and aquarium driftwood. Bucephalandra prefers lower lighting, substantial flow and will grow nice and dense if favorable conditions are provided. While CO2 injection is not required, the use of it helps promote quicker growth and lovely coloration. The stem and rhizome should not be covered when planting and over-gluing of roots will be extremely detrimental to its growth and survival.

Bucephalandra Dark Green Wavy or Buce Dark Green Wavy is a unique mutation of the popular classic, Bucephalandra Green Wavy. Characterized by ruffled-edged leaves, Bucephalandra Dark Green Wavy is extremely similar but features a darker, richer hue, as its name suggests. Other than the difference of coloration, both Buce Dark Green Wavy and Green Wavy are similar in size making this particular aquarium plant a great addition to planted tanks of all sizes. Like other Bucephalandra, Buce Dark Green Wavy is versatile with placement and will grow well when attached to aquarium hardscape such as aquascaping stones and aquarium driftwood. Bucephalandra prefers lower lighting, substantial flow and will grow nice and dense if favorable conditions are provided. While CO2 injection is not required, the use of it helps promote quicker growth and lovely coloration. The stem and rhizome should not be covered when planting and over-gluing of roots will be extremely detrimental to its growth and survival.

Cryptocoryne Sri Lanka is a relatively uncommon aquarium plant in the Cryptocoryne family that can provide good coverage for fish and shrimp in planted tanks. Its foliage is long and droopy, but with good flow, can add extra movement and interest in freshwater aquariums. We consider it to be medium in size, making it a good low light plant for tanks over 10 gallons. With consistent and patient care, its leaves will deepen in color and contrast nicely with its burgundy stalk. Like others in this family, plant it and try not to move or propagate it until it's established. Make sure you're using a good aquarium light, CO2 injection and nutrient rich aquarium soil or a liquid plant fertilizer for healthy growth. Patience is key with Cryptocoryne plants! If you're looking for a unique addition to your planted tank, consider giving this one a try.

This large-sized aquarium sword plant species features prominent red-brown spots that speckle every leaf. This contrast in the leaves combined with its rather large size makes it a perfect addition to larger planted aquarium tanks. Like all aquatic sword species, Echinodorus Ozelot Green is easy to keep, fairly hardy and needs a minimum of a nutrient-rich aquarium substrate as this species of aquatic plant are heavy root feeders. Aside from this, Echinodorus species are fairly tolerable of varying water parameters and lighting conditions. While this little aquatic sword grows more compact, it is still a larger aquatic plant in general and should be pruned periodically to ensure smaller aquatic plants are not shaded from the light provided. Propagation is simple. Separate and replant. Common Name Ozelot Sword Care Easy Lighting Low to Medium CO2 Optional Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant runners Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 18 - 22"

Murdannia keisak is a unique aquatic stem plant known for its bamboo-like appearance. Its bright green leaves add grassy texture and offer a soft, organic look that works well in planted aquariums, indoor ponds, and Wabi Kusa plant displays. Its growth is naturally upright and straight but will readily branch out and spread when trimmed back. With the ability to grow in submerged, marginal, or emersed conditions, Murdannia keisak is a versatile choice for a variety of planted setups. When grown fully submerged in aquariums, the plant may develop subtle red tones under stronger lighting and with CO2 injection. When healthy, it grows quickly, making it a great option for aquascapers looking for a fast-growing plant that offers a refreshing alternative to more common stems. Its distinctive leaf shape adds variety and texture to planted layouts while helping fill space in newly established planted tanks.

Lobelia cardinalis can be found growing wild in North America. When grown in captivity, this plant is cultivated in marshy and bog-like environments resulting in the plant's leaves displaying a dark green coloration with purple undersides. When used in a planted aquarium tank, Lobelia Cardinalis is a striking light green and makes a lovely midground or background aquatic plant choice dependent upon the size of the aquarium tank being utilized. Highly versatile, Lobelia Cardinalis can also be grown in outdoor garden pond setups and when grown above the water's surface, it produces flowers with a deep scarlet red coloration. Propagate by trimming stems and replanting or pulling apart dense clumps and splitting the roots. Common Name Cardinal Plant Care Easy to Moderate Lighting Low CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Midground and Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate Height 7-12" Ultum Nature Systems tissue culture plants are grown in-vitro by laboratories who specialize in propagating aquatic plants. There is a huge selection of plant species that have been propagated this way. This is truly the best option for those who want absolutely zero unwanted pests, algae and pesticides. This makes them perfect for shrimp keepers and any planted tank enthusiasts alike. NOTE: It is important to remove the tissue culture agar gel before planting. Simply wash the gel away, divide, and plant.

The Dymax Flexz LED Light is the perfect lighting solution for nano planted aquarium tanks. Boasting an ultra-slim body, the Dymax Flexz offers a clean look while remaining unobtrusive or distracting when viewing the planted aquarium. Equipped with a classic clip-on base and classic gooseneck, the Flexz LED light can be quickly secured to glass panels of a rimless aquarium tank and easily adjusted to a variety of height and angle preferences. Additional features include smart-touch to power the unit on and off or change the color temperature to all blue, white or mixed. The light itself offers a simple swivel feature and can easily be moved out of the way during maintenance without fussing with the height or angle. Versatile for any aquarium hobbyist, the Dymax Flexz Nano LED light is compatible with a range of aquarium keeping styles and is suitable for both freshwater and marine/saltwater aquariums. This aquarium LED light fixture will provide your aquarium fish and aquatic plants the perfect amount of illumination and contrast without bulky, unattractive aesthetic. COLOR: Black TIP: The Dymax Flexz LED Light can be mounted on the left, right or back aquarium tank panels allowing more space for other aquarium equipment or tank lids. listings.commonName: Aquario Neo CO2 Diffuser - Extended Special
listings.description: Maintain a clean, streamlined look for your planted aquarium with the Extended Special Neo CO2 Diffuser. Designed with an extended diffuser pipe, this model positions the tubing connection near the top of the aquarium for a clean, vertical presentation. Its compact Special diffuser body reduces the amount of visible equipment without sacrificing ultra-fine CO2 diffusion. Constructed from durable, transparent acrylic, every Neo CO2 Diffuser blends naturally into planted aquariums while efficiently distributing CO2 to support healthy aquatic plant growth. Best For - Clean, organized CO2 tubing installation - Rimless planted aquariums - Minimizing visible aquarium equipment - Minimalist aquascapes What’s Included - Aquario Neo CO2 Diffuser - Extended Special - 2x Suction Cups - 2x Practice Tubes - Flexible Rubber Insert Usage Tips Soak the diffuser in clean water for approximately 30 minutes before first use to prime the disc for fine bubble diffusion. Add vibrant color and delicate texture to your aquascape with Pogostemon Stellatus. This aquatic stem plant features long, narrow leaves that radiate outward in star-like swirls, displaying shades of green, pink, and reddish-purple under certain conditions. Its intricate foliage and color range makes it an eye-catcher in planted aquariums, especially when grown amongst other leaf shapes and textures. It is a more demanding species, requiring strong lighting, CO2 injection, consistent micro and macro fertilization, and stable water conditions to matain good form. When mature, regular trimming will support branching, creating bushy groups and wider coverage.

Cryptocoryne retrospiralis is a taller, more slender Crypt with long, slightly ruffled leaves that can range from green to bronze depending on your setup. It has a more grass-like look compared to most other Crypts, which makes it a nice option if you're looking for vertical coverage and easy-care. This plant can grow fairly tall over time, so it’s best suited for the midground to background, especially in larger tanks. Once it settles in, it forms a natural, flowing group that adds movement without feeling too heavy or dense. Its unique look and hardy nature pair especially well with biotope or blackwater-style aquariums. Like most Cryptocoryne, it doesn’t like being moved around once planted. It may go through a short adjustment period, but once established it becomes very easy to care for and continues to grow steadily. Cryptocoryne plants are suitable for lower-tech setups, but stronger lighting and CO2 will bring out better growth and fuller leaves. Overall, Cryptocoryne Spiralis is a good choice if you’re looking for a low-maintenance plant that adds height and a more natural, slightly wild look to the aquascape.

Egeria Densa (Anacharis) - Fast growing aquarium stem plant Egeria Densa, sometimes called Anacharis or Brazilian Waterweed, is a popular aquarium stem plant for freshwater and planted aquarium hobbyists. As its name suggests, Egeria Densa can grow at a rapid rate that makes it ideal for various aquarium-related uses. Whether you're a beginner aquascaper looking for an easy aquatic plant or looking for an aquarium plant that can provide extra coverage for young aquatic livestock, Egeria Densa is a solid pick. Its fast growing nature can be attributed to its ability to absorb excess nutrients in the water, making it an aquarium plant powered source of natural filtration. Plant Egeria Densa in the background of a planted aquarium, leave it as a floating aquarium plant or add it to your outdoors as a pond plant. Egeria Densa is extremely versatile and supports a healthy aquarium or pond.

Similar to Val Spiralis, this jungle val adds extra visual interest to planted tanks. Combined with its easy care and adaptable nature, Vals are a popular pick for hobbyists of all skill levels. This aquarium plant is hardy, but grows best with low to moderate lighting and a nutrient-dense aquarium soil. CO2 injection isn't required, but will boost growth rate and overall appearance. In aquascaping, Vallisneria Spiralis Leopard creates a dense backdrop that works lovely in planted aquariums. Vallisneria Torta is a classic Vallisneria species. Well-known for its slightly spiralized, green leaves, Vallisneria Torta is also rightly referenced to as corkscrew val. Similar to other Vallisneria aquarium plants, Vallisneria Torta is easy to keep and relatively undemanding with care making it a great aquarium plant for beginner hobbyists. Because it can grow fairly large, Vallisneria Torta is suitable as a mid to background choice in a planted tank. If favorable conditions are provided, this aquatic plant will self-propagate and spread quickly making routine pruning necessary. Basics such as quality aquarium lighting, CO2 injection and aquarium soil intended for aquatic plant propagation will yield the best results. The use of root tabs or fertilizer will also help as Vallisneria absorb a lot of nutrients in the aquarium. Propagation is simple as it spreads via side shoots and is easily separated. Regular pruning is recommended as this species can grow to the height of your aquarium easily and will also anchor deep into the substrate if given the opportunity to do so.

Aridarum Narrow is a beautiful aquarium plant with long, slender, medium-sized leaves. Similar in care to Bucephalandra, Aridarum Narrow is relatively easy-going and adapts well to low-tech planted tank conditions. Its leaves are thick, dark green in coloration and can vary depending on the environment it is placed in. Like other Aridarum species, Aridarum Narrow does well with good flow and can be attached to hardscape material using thread, superglue or by simply placing it in the gaps of a hardscape layout. Propagation is similar to Anubias, Bucephalandra and Java Fern species. Aridarum prefers low to medium lighting and is notorious for growing extremely slow. However, if patience is administered, growth can is very rewarding. Like other epiphytic aquatic plants, Aridarum Narrow should not have its stem and rhizome covered when planting as this can cause the plant to die.

Hassle-free and budget-friendly CO2 injection solution Comes with everything you’ll need Ideal for beginners and hobbyists alike The video below demonstrates how to properly setup Aquario Neo CO2: Additional Information: The Neo CO2 Kit is designed for aquariums between 10 to 30 gallons. Using this kit for nano aquarium tanks runs the risk of providing excessive CO2 resulting in the depletion of oxygen. This can be potentially deadly for livestock. However, this kit can be used in smaller aquarium tanks if oxygen is provided via air pump, air stone or surface agitation. The life of the Neo CO2 Kit varies depending on the temperature. The recommended usage temperature ranges from 68° to 86°. As a general rule of thumb, this kit will last between 30 to 50 days during winter and 40 to 60 days during summer. Gas output is not adjustable. The use of needle valves, solenoids, or other CO2 adjusting devices is not recommended as this can cause damage to the Nature Bottle. Do not tilt or shake the bottle during operation in order to prevent reaction liquid from siphoning into the aquarium. It is normal for minor amounts of alcohol to be produced from the kit solution: this is harmless. In the event that any reaction liquid leaks into the aquarium, an oxygen deficiency can occur. A simple 30-50% water change will correct the issue as well as introducing an air pump to degas the CO2. Clean and remove any gel that forms on the bottleneck before initial use to prevent build-up or blockage of the gas outlet. If any reaction liquid is found inside the flexible tubing, simply clean with lukewarm water. The video below demonstrates how to properly reset Aquario Neo CO2: Why CO2 injection is important in a planted tank: 3 main factors contribute to the optimal growth of aquatic plants. These factors include nutrients, light and carbon dioxide (CO2). If any of these are unbalanced, the results are algae growth or the withering of plants. The introduction of CO2 in a planted aquarium allows plants to thrive and grow more efficiently, while also giving them the ability to out-compete algae for nutrients. No matter what type of planted aquarium setup you have, we recommend CO2 injection for better aquarium plant growth. Usage Instructions: Step 1: Water Add 300ml of warm water. Do not add water that is too hot as it may damage the bottle and impact performance. Step 2: Shake Tighten the cap and shake well to ensure the solution is thoroughly mixed. Step 3: Wait Allow the Neo CO2 bottle to sit for 24 hours without interruption or disturbance. The liquid will thicken to a gel-like consistency. After 24 hours, invert the bottle to ensure that the liquid is fully solidified. If not, wait another hour and check again. Step 4: Activate Remove cap and clean off any gel that remains on the bottleneck. Add 1 packet of Neo CO2 Bio followed by 1 cup (200ml) of lukewarm, room temperature water around 77°. Reinstall the cap onto the bottle, no shaking is required. Connect flexible tubing on one end of the reaction cap and the other through the suction cup and onto the diffuser. Place the diffuser into your aquarium and wait. Step 5: React During initial use, CO2 gas output will fluctuate; however, the reaction speed will stabilize and slow down over time. The Neo CO2 Bottle will continue to work for up to 60 days depending on room temperature. Step 6: Repeat When CO2 output slows down or stops completely, remove the cap and pour the liquid out. Repeat steps 4 through 5 until the gel is fully consumed. Includes: NEO CO2 Bio Powder Refill Bag

Fittonia Albivenis is a beautiful terrestrial plant that is best known for its striking foliage and prominent leaf vein pattern. Fittonia are also a popular house plant choice and are equally known for their dramatic behavior when sudden changes in environment occur. This dramatic behavior may appear in the form of extreme droopiness and wilted leaves, causing many to believe their plant is a goner. However, in most cases, a thorough water and the addition of a humidity dome for a day or two and your Fittonia will look like a brand-new plant. Small to medium in size, Fittonia Albivenis has a horizontal, creeping growth pattern making it great for ground coverage. Fittonia plants do best when kept in bright, indirect light or in an area with dappled sunlight and decent humidity levels, making it a suitable choice for wabi-kusa style planted setups or terrarium enclosures. Propagation is simple and can be done through stem cuttings. Fittonia Albivenis is NOT an aquarium plant. Submerging this plant in an aquarium will kill it! PLANARIA AND HYDRA Planaria are small off-white, worm-like creatures with a spade-shaped head. They are relatively small and are typically caused by poor tank maintenance, dirty substrate and excess nutrients in the water from overfeeding. While harmless, they are unsightly and can cause swings in water parameters if left to proliferate. Hydra is typically caused by cross-contamination and poor maintenance. Similar to jellyfish, Hydra's tentacle-like extremities possess stinging cells that allow Hydra to immobilize, kill and feed on smaller aquatic life such as shrimplets and even small nano fish. A Hydra has no brain, no circulatory or respiratory system, nor even any musculature, yet it poses a real danger to small freshwater aquarium livestock. Notes: Do not use this product in an aquarium tank that contains ornamental snail species. Treatment cycles last roughly 1 week. Do not change water or perform aquarium tank maintenance during this time. Once treatments are done, please ensure that any killed planaria and hydra are removed to prevent spikes in water parameters. A 50% water change should be done following treatments. Size: 10g

Why we like SL Aqua Ion Exchange Resin: Keeps water crystal clear Can be recharged and reused multiple times Removes cloudiness and discoloration caused by tinting agents such as tannins from driftwood Removes excess ammonia, nitrate, nitrite, and other impurities that are potentially harmful to aquarium livestock Visibly darkens when a recharge is necessary Product comes ready to use in an aquarium safe nylon bag Cleaning and Recharge Instructions: 1. Mix bleach and clean water in a 1:1 ratio. Add the bag to the solution. 2. Allow the bag to soak in the solution for a minimum of 24 hours. 3. Once the bag has lightened visibly, rinse the bag thoroughly in dechlorinated water. 4. After rinsing, allow the bag to soak in a new container of dechlorinated water for an additional 8 hours, minimum. 5. Rinse thoroughly again, and it is ready to reuse!

listings.commonName: ONF Flat Nano Lighting Stand Kit
listings.description: Please note: This item is final sale and cannot be returned or exchanged. This listing includes the ONF Stand ONLY - Light not included. Pair this stand kit with an ONF Flat Nano LED Light! Click here to shop all lighting! The ONF Flat Nano Lighting Stand Kit is an accessory designed to convert the ONF Flat Nano original and Flat Nano + LED Lights into freestanding lights. Using the ONF Flat Nano Lighting Stand Kit allows the ONF Flat Nano lights to be used without mounting it to the rim of a rimless aquarium tank. With the ONF Flat Nano Lighting Stand conversion kit, the ONF Flat Nano + or ONF Flat Nano can be used on both planted aquarium tanks or as a desktop plant light that is capable of growing a wide variety of plants such as terrestrial succulents, cacti, jewel orchids and more. Size: Base measures approximately 9 x 7” ONF Flat Nano Lighting Stand Kit paired with the ONF Flat Nano + LED Light being used on an Ultum Nature Systems 16T tank below:

This product qualifies for FREE SHIPPING! Tropica Nutrition Capsules are planted aquarium root tabs designed to be an extra source of nutrition for aquarium plants. Packed with an abundance of macronutrients, Tropica Plant Care Nutrition Capsules include nitrogen, phosphorus, iron as well as vital micronutrients making them perfect for use in both rich or inert aquarium substrates. Alternatively, Tropica Plant Care Nutrition Capsules are designed for use in aged planted aquarium tanks where nutrients are depleted or for aquarium plants showing signs of nutrient deficiency. These capsules offer convenience and prevent the hassle of replacing aquarium soil. Tropical Plant Care Nutrition Capsules are perfect for use with heavy root feeding aquatic plants or for hobbyists who prefer to introduce fewer nutrients in aquariums with less aquatic plant mass or nutritional requirements. 10 nutrient capsules per pack DIRECTIONS: Insert Tropica Nutrition Capsules using aquascaping tweezers deeply into substrate and close to aquarium roots. NOTE: Tropica Nutrition Capsules will slowly deplete in approximately 2 months time, reinsert when necessary based on aquarium plant growth and health. TIP: Great for fast-growing aquatic plants such as Glossostigma, Rotala and heavy root feeders such as Echinodorus, Cryptocoryne, and Vallensinera.

Keep your aquarium glass and aquascaping tools clean with the Ultum Nature Systems Microfiber Towel. Made from ultra-soft microfiber, this reusable towel is designed to gently wipe away water spots, fingerprints, and moisture without leaving behind lint or scratches from the fabric itself. Its generous size makes it convenient for everyday aquarium maintenance, whether you're drying stainless steel aquascaping tools after trimming plants, wiping down aquarium glass, or cleaning up water around your setup. The soft, absorbent material is gentle on delicate surfaces and can be washed and reused for regular maintenance. Product Specifications Dimensions: 15 × 15" (38x38cm) Material: Microfiber Machine wash with cool water. Allow to air dry or tumble dry on low. Always check your towel for trapped sand or debris before wiping aquarium glass to help reduce the risk of accidental scratches.

Rotala Macrandra 'Mini' is a highly sought-after species that is characterized by its unique leaf shape and deep red to magenta hues. It makes for a beautiful background plant in nano planted aquariums and as a midground choice in larger planted aquariums. Quality lighting, CO2, and soft water are essential to promote growth. Beyond this, micronutrients are required if intense deep colors are desired. Individual stems should also be given sufficient space when planted as planting them too closely together will render the lower leaves void of light. A diamond in the rough, Rotala Macrandra 'Mini' is very demanding and can be difficult to keep, but results are well worth the extra effort and rewarding if successful. Common Name Rotala Mini Butterfly Rotala Macrandra Mini Red Rotala Macradra Mini Care Moderate Lighting High CO2 Necessary Suggested Placement Midground to Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate Height 6 - 10 " Tissue culture plants are grown in-vitro by laboratories who specialize in propagating aquatic plants. There is a huge selection of plant species that have been propagated this way. This is truly the best option for those who want absolutely zero unwanted pests, algae and pesticides. This makes them perfect for shrimp keepers and any planted tank enthusiasts alike. NOTE: It is important to remove the tissue culture agar gel before planting. Simply wash the gel away, divide, and plant.

Rotala macrandra is a highly sought-after species characterized by its vivid color and signature leaf shape. It makes for a beautiful background plant in medium to larger planted aquariums. This is one of the easier macrandra varietals to cultivate, with some of the others being quite picky with parameters and requirements. Start by providing strong lighting, CO2 injection and a nutrient-dense aquasoil. Soft water is a plus! When provided with stable conditions, this aquatic plant is an amazing addition to any planted tank. Individual stems should also be given sufficient space when planted, as planting them too closely together will deprive the lower leaves of light. Rotala macrandra plants can be more difficult to grow, but the results are well worth the extra effort and rewarding if successful. Common Name Rotala Macrandra Care Difficult Lighting High CO2 Required Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate Height 8-16 "

listings.commonName: UNS Substrate System - Soil, Sand & Base (Black)
listings.description: The UNS Substrate System is a complete, layered foundation designed to support healthy plant growth while creating a clean, natural aquascape layout. Combining nutrient-rich Controbase, buffering Controsoil, and decorative Controsand, this system brings together the essential components needed for a balanced planted aquarium. This configuration features UNS Controsoil (Black), offering strong contrast and depth that enhances plant color and hardscape detail. Paired with your choice of Controsand and preferred soil granule size, the system is available in several combinations to suit both the visual style and planting needs of your aquascape. Configure Your System Choose Your Sand / Gravel Style - Bora: Light, neutral, fine-grain sand that creates strong contrast - Maui: Black, fine-grain sand that pairs well with darker themed aquascapes - Monterey: Chunkier, neutral gravel. Balanced and versatile - Santa Fe: Earthy-toned pebble-like gravel that’s great for riverbed or shallow water edge-inspired layouts Choose Your Soil Granule Size - Extra Fine: Ideal for carpeting plants and detailed layouts - Fine: All-purpose and accommodates most aquatic plants - Normal: Larger granule best for large species such as Echinodorus or Vallisneria How It Works A complete layered blend! This substrate system is designed to be used in three layers: 1. Controbase (Bottom Layer) Provides essential nutrients to support root development and long-term plant health and consistent growth. 2. Controsoil (Middle Layer) Buffers water parameters while supplying an ideal base for aquatic plants to absorb nutrients and establish groups. 3. Controsand (Top Layer / Decorative) Adds texture and contrast to the layout. Separates planted and open areas within the aquascape. What’s Included - 1x 10L UNS Controsoil Black (granule size varies by selection) - 1x 8L UNS Controsand (type varies by selection) - 1x 2L UNS Controbase This system simplifies substrate selection by combining compatible materials into a single, proven setup. It supports strong plant growth while giving you flexibility to shape the visual layout of your aquarium using sand and soil contrast. Best For - Planted aquariums with defined foreground and background zones - Aquascapes that combine sand paths with planted areas - Hobbyists looking for a balanced and reliable substrate foundation for planted aquariums Important Information: We recommend rinsing Controsand before use. Do not rinse Controsoil or Controbase! This substrate system is designed for freshwater planted aquariums.

Our solid choice for tropical community fish such as Tetras and Rasboras. Hikari Micro Wafers were developed through extensive research into the nutritional needs and feeding habits of these species. Whether nano or larger fish, all can benefit from a Hikari diet. Their unique floating-then-sinking behavior allows fish to feed at all levels of the aquarium. Hikari Micro Wafers also contain high levels of vegetable matter and essential minerals to promote overall health and vibrant coloration. Product Highlights - All-purpose daily fish food - Natural formula for easy digestion - Natural color-enhancing formula Size: 0.70oz Feeding Guidelines: Feed 1-2 times daily in small portions that can be consumed within a few minutes. Remove uneaten food to prevent excess waste. Looking for the right food for your livestock? Browse our full collection of aquarium foods.

Bucephalandra Variegated Marble is a rare Green Wavy mutation variant in the Bucephalandra aquatic plant family. Its usual ruffled wavy leaves are still very apparent; however, the standout feature of this plant is its unique and highly visible variegated white marbling throughout the brilliant green leaves. This Buce will definitely be an attention-grabber in any planted aquarium tank. Like most Bucephalandra species, Bucephalandra Variegated Marble is a great aquatic plant for beginners due to its easy care, undemanding nature and ability to adapt to a wide range of aquarium tank parameters. Bucephalandra comes in many varieties, shapes, colors and looks best when kept in clumps in a planted aquarium tank. This aquatic plant prefers lower lighting and will grow nice and dense if favorable conditions are provided. The stem and rhizome should not be covered when planting as this will cause the plant to rot and wither. It is best to attach or wedge Bucephalandra on or between aquarium hardscapes such as aquarium driftwood and aquascaping rocks.

The Advanced Check Valve by Ultum Nature Systems is extremely durable and designed to handle high pressure while preventing the backflow of aquarium water into essential aquarium equipment. Backflowing w ater can cause permanent damage to air pumps and CO2 regulators. The Advanced Check Valve is simple to install and easy to work with, preventing stuck tubing and eliminating any need to cut for removal. The Advanced Check Valve is ideal for longterm use and is a cost-effective option when choosing aquarium equipment. Suitable for use with planted aquarium CO2 equipment and aquarium air pumps.

Aponogeton Boivinianus is a large bulb-type aquarium plant that is best for large planted aquariums or freshwater ponds. When established, this aquatic plant grows impressive foliage that surpasses 2 feet in length. Older leaves deepen to a rich green, while new growth is lighter green with brown hues until it matures. Planting methods vary. Some prefer to partially plant the bulb directly into nutrient-rich aquasoil with the growing tip right above the surface. Others will vouch for allowing it to remain floating above the substrate and have had success that way as well. Important Note: This listing does not include fully mature plants. Please ensure you are prepared to care for the option chosen during purchase. If planting in soil, we recommend starting with a nutrient-dense planted aquarium substrate like Aquario Neo Soil or supplementing with nutrient root tabs. Aponogeton plants go through periods of dormancy. During this stage, it may shed its leaves, but will eventually grow back. In natural settings, these large aquarium plants are found in fast-flowing waters. Provide similar conditions for best results. Its size, movement and general hardiness make it a great focal plant for river-themed biotope aquascapes, ponds or large planted tanks. Common Name Aponogeton Boivinianus Care Easy Lighting Medium CO2 Optional Suggested Placement Background Propagation Divide side shoots Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 20"+

Create a soft, textured layer of greenery across your aquarium with Salvinia Natans. This fast-growing floating fern develops pairs of small, pocket-like green leaves that spread along the water's surface, while its short root structure keeps growth relatively compact below. Salvinia Natans can gradually form dense floating mats, making it a great option for adding surface coverage to planted aquariums, ponds, and paludariums. As it grows, it absorbs available nutrients directly from the water column while creating shaded areas and added cover for small aquarium livestock. When conditions are right, Salvinia Natans can spread quickly across the water's surface. Regularly remove excess growth to maintain open areas and prevent dense mats from blocking too much light from aquatic plants below.

The Assorted Cryptocoryne Bundle is an easy way to add variety and discover different Cryptocoryne species without selecting individual plants. Each bundle includes a random selection of live Cryptocoryne plants, making it a convenient option for filling a planted aquarium with hardy, adaptable plants while introducing natural color, texture, and leaf shape. Cryptocoryne are popular planted aquarium plants known for their adaptability, diverse foliage, and low-maintenance care. Depending on the species, they can be used throughout the foreground, midground, or background and are suitable for both beginner and experienced hobbyists. What's Included The Assorted Cryptocoryne Bundle includes a random mix of five different Cryptocoryne varieties. Available in 5, 10, and 15 packs, each bundle contains five varieties in single, double, or triple quantities depending on the pack size selected. Plants are chosen randomly based on availability and may change at any time. Important Information: Photos are representative of what you may receive. With live plants, natural variations in size, leaf shape, and coloration should be expected. Newly introduced Cryptocoryne may experience "crypt melt" when adjusting to a new environment. We recommend planting them in fully cycled, mature tanks to mitigate transitional stress.

listings.commonName: UNS Pro Inline CO2 Diffuser Bundle
listings.description: Maintain consistent CO2 diffusion in your planted aquarium with the UNS Pro Inline CO2 Diffuser and Ceramic Disc bundle. It pairs the inline diffuser with an extra replacement ceramic disc, ensuring you’re ready to get started while keeping a spare on hand for routine maintenance. Designed for use with pressurized CO2 systems and external canister filters, the inline diffuser produces a fine mist that is distributed throughout the aquarium through the filter’s outflow lily pipe. Because the diffuser remains outside the display, it helps maintain a clean appearance. An extra ceramic disc makes routine cleaning quick and convenient, allowing you to rotate between discs during maintenance so a clean diffuser is always ready when you need it. What’s Included - UNS Pro Inline CO2 Diffuser - UNS Inline Diffuser Ceramic Disc Compatibility Guide Model Tubing Size Filter Recommendation 12mm (1/2”) 1/2" Tubing (12/16mm) UNS Blitz 32oz UNS Delta 30, 60 and 90 ADA Super Jet ES-600 Eheim Classic 2213 16mm (5/8”) 5/8" Tubing (16/22mm) UNS Delta 120 20mm (1”) 1” Tubing (20/25mm) Eheim 2262

Microsorum pteropus ‘Black Forest’, also known as Java Fern Black Forest, is a less-common and unique variation known for its pronounced leaf veining and slender shape. Its deeper color and more prominent veins give it a high-contrast look compared to classic Java Fern, making it a great pick for adding visual appeal to planted aquariums. Recently reclassified as Leptochilus pteropus , this plant is still widely known in the aquarium hobby as Microsorum pteropus. Like other Java Ferns, it is very hardy and adapts to varying water parameters, making it suitable for both beginners and experienced aquarists. Its slender leaves and added texture make it a great pick for the midground area of a planted aquarium. Use it to fill in gaps of an aquascape or as a supporting species. As an epiphytic plant, it can be attached to driftwood, rocks, or aquarium decor using thread or glue. Ensure the rhizome is kept above substrate to prevent rot. When the plant is mature, propagation is easy and can be done by dividng the main rhizome and reattaching plantlets as desired.

There is no difference between Left and Right kits other than which side the hanging kit will be installed on. To use this hanging solution on tanks larger than 36"(90CM) please purchase one of each (L&R) to install on both sides of the aquarium cabinet A solid solution for pendant-style LED aquarium lights. The Square light hanging kit by ONF features beautiful, minimal construction that allows it to be attached to any side of an aquarium cabinet and adjusted multiple ways to ensure the lighting used is to preference. ONF's Square Light Hanging Kit offers 8 adjustments for over-tank depth placement and easy adjustment to accommodate different heights as well. The kit comes with several items for versatile use on tanks that range from 24-36" in length. To use this light hanging kit on tanks larger than 90CM or 36", simply purchase one LEFT and one RIGHT to install on both sides of larger aquarium tank cabinets. To finish the look, rubber cable strips are included ensuring the light's cable is kept sleek, organized, and hardly noticeable. Kit Includes: Mounting Hardware 2 Hanging Bars (24" & 36") Cable Strips Check it out in action on some of our popular planted aquarium tank setups! Bucephalandra Biblis is a unique Buce aquarium plant that features narrow ruffled leaves with metallic dark green to red-brown color tones. This is the perfect easy aquarium rhizome plant to add to a planted aquarium for an extra pop of color. This particular Bucephalandra will grow to be about an average of 4 inches in height. This aquatic plant prefers low to medium lighting and will grow nice and dense if favorable conditions are provided. CO2 injection along with a good maintenance schedule will promote quicker, more robust growth. The stem and rhizome should not be covered when planting as this will cause the plant to rot and wither. Given this aquatic plant's easy-going nature, it is a great choice for beginner aquarists, and care can be comparable to other popular aquatic plant species such as Anubias and Java Ferns. Bucephalandra can also be used in many ways and does not require being planted in the aquarium tank substrate. Simply attach it to aquarium hardscape material such as aquarium driftwood, aquascaping stones or aquarium decor. Alternatively, it can also be placed in the crevices of an aquascape layout.

Bucephalandra Kedagang Round Mini is a smaller version of the popular Bucephalandra Kedagang Round. It features dark green coloration with bluish, purplish, and reddish iridescent undertones with proper aquarium LED lighting. Because of its growth and size, Buce Kedagang Round Mini is the perfect easy aquarium plant for nana planted aquariums and larger planted tanks that require aquatic plant details throughout. This aquatic plant prefers low to medium lighting and will grow nice and dense if favorable conditions are provided. CO2 injection along with a good maintenance schedule will promote quicker, more robust growth. The stem and rhizome should not be covered when planting as this will cause the plant to rot and wither. It is best to attach or wedge Bucephalandra on or between aquarium hardscapes such as aquarium driftwood and aquascaping rocks.

Add texture and fresh greenery to your planted aquarium with Rotala 'Bangladesh'. This aquatic stem plant features slender, narrow leaves in soft shades of green to light yellow-green, creating a fine, feathery appearance. Its upright growth and delicate foliage make it an attractive choice for the midground or background of an aquascape, where it adds textural contrast against broader-leaved stems and aquatic plants. It grows quickly (like other Rotala plants) and will readily branch when trimmed back. Botanical Note: Rotala 'Bangladesh' has also been sold under the names Rotala sp. 'Bangladesh' and Rotala mexicana 'Bangladesh'. Some aquarium plant references identify this form as Rotala wallichii 'Bangladesh'. The simplified trade name is retained here for consistency.

Add deep green to nearly black foliage to your planted aquarium with Bucephalandra ‘Dark Sky’. Its glossy, oval leaves sprout from vibrant red petioles, creating rich contrast, while gently wavy leaf edges add texture and visual character to an aquascape. Like other Bucephalandra, attach it to open gaps in the hardscape layout or along sparse areas of an aquascape. When placed under aquarium lights, the foliage may develop that subtle blue sheen as the plant matures.

Anubias Minima Mini is a small version of regular Anubias Minima. Belonging to the Anubias family, Anubias Minima Mini is fairly rare despite its common counterparts that are frequently used in all types of planted aquariums. Like other Anubias it can grow in a multitude of environments varying from aquariums to terrariums. Anubias Minima features slender leaves with a deep green coloration loved by planted tank hobbyists. This plant is suitable as a midground and background aquatic plant as the leaves are capable of growing quite long. This Anubias variant is a flowering plant that grows best when the rhizome is attached to a hard surface such as wood or stone. It benefits from consistent fertilization but light requirements are minimal as its leaves are susceptible to algae growth when placed under high lighting. CO2 is optional but can promote faster growth and robust leaves when used.

Anubias Spear Leaf is comparable in size and appearance to Anubias Nana Petite, but with a pointed leaf shape similar to sp. Pangolino. It is an easy aquatic plant that works well in nano aquariums. It features emerald tones and a distinctive midrib vein down leaf centers for some textural interest. Like most Anubias, Nana Spear Leaf is a great beginner aquarium plant. It is adaptable and tolerates a range of conditions. Being an epiphytic plant, it can be attached directly to driftwood, aquarium rocks, or any tank decor using cotton thread of glue. Keep the rhizomes above any substrate to prevent rot and that's nearly it! Propagation is easy and straightforward; simply cut or pull apart rhizomes to be replanted/reattached.

This specific Lagenandra is a rarer aquarium plant. Hailing from Sri Lanka, it develops upright slender leaves. The leaves feature a unique dark green base with a glimmer of silver sheen which differentiates it from other Lagenandra. Because of its slow growing nature, Lagenandra Thwitesii tends to remain small for quite some time. A fully grown mother plant will grow about 17 inches in height and is recommended for either the mid or background of an aquarium depending on tank size. In addition, Lagenandra Thwitesii tolerates higher temperatures ranging from 75 to 82 fahrenheit. It is also very suitable for emersed paludarium setups and other forms of jungle-like environments where tropical humidity can be replicated. It can be propagated by cutting the strong creeping rhizome. When grown out of water, this plant will also develop fluorescent red and burgundy coloration. Common Name Lagenandra Thwaitesii Lagenandra Care Moderate Lighting Medium to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Mid to Background Propagation Separate rhizome Growth Rate Moderate Height Varies

Bucephalandra Theia Red is a beautiful species within the Bucephalandra group. This specific species features long, thin leaves that are slightly wavy and bold in coloration. Like all Bucephalandra species, Buce Theia Red can be grown submerged in an aquarium tank or emersed in terrarium, paludarium, and vivarium-like setups. Bucephalandra as a species is very hardy and can adapt to a wide range of aquarium tank parameters. Those who are already familiar with Bucephalandra Catherinae may see similarities between the two as Buce Theia Red resembles a larger leaf version of Catherinae. Buce doesn't require excessive light either, making it an all-around wonderful choice for expert enthusiasts and beginner hobbyists alike. Bucephalandra Theia Red's care is comparable to that of Anubias species and its growth behavior is similar in that this aquatic plant does not need to be planted in aquarium soil to grow properly. Bucephalandra Theia Red is also a flowering species and it will do great simply being attached to aquarium hardscape material such as aquascaping stones or aquarium driftwood. Pruning is simple as well. All you need to do is separate the rhizome and replant it.

Ohko Stone, also commonly known as Dragon Stone, is an extremely popular hardscape choice in the aquarium hobby that is characterized by its notorious golden yellow dragon-like scale textures. The overall shape of the rock features numerous nooks and small craters that are great for anchoring aquatic plants and moss species while also providing a safe haven for sensitive or skittish fish and shrimp. Composed of a clay-like substance, Ohko Stone is extremely lightweight and fragile when compared to other rock options. It can be easily broken down into smaller pieces to suit a wide range of aquarium tanks and is inert so the water chemistry will not change when adding this stone into a planted tank. Alternatively, they can be used to tie aquatic moss species or attach plants such as Anubias and Bucephalandra, adding a sense of maturity to a newly planted aquascape layout. Accent stones are without limit and can be used to aquascape large aquarium tanks and nano aquarium tanks. Make sure to rinse before use to reduce debris and dust! Each order contains 2LB of Dragon Stone ranging from 1-3".

Lava Rock Gravel may be used for a wide variety of purposes. We recommend using it as an accent to a Black Lava Rock aquarium hardscape layout, filtration media, or as a tank substrate! The possibilities are endless! This lava rock gravel is inert and will not change water parameters. Black Lava Rock is a classic aquascaping stone that's often used in all types of aquarium setups such as planted tanks, freshwater, and brackish. Because of its highly porous nature, easy aquatic plants like moss, Anubias, Ferns, and Bucephalandra will readily attach themselves to these rocks. In addition, it's also great for the colonization of beneficial bacteria resulting in a healthier aquarium environment. TIP: Rinse before use.

These lead weights are commonly used when growing and storing aquarium plants. Easy to use, these weights are malleable and can be wrapped around the stem of an aquatic plant to prevent floating when storing plants for later use. Alternatively, they're the perfect weight for ensuring your aquarium plants stay put and also come in handy if extra weight is needed for aquarium decor! These lead weights are rust-resistant, non-toxic, and safe for use with live plants, fish, and shrimp species.

listings.commonName: Fittonia Albivenis on Christmas Moss Clay Ball
listings.description: Fittonia Albivenis is a beautiful plant that is best known for its striking foliage and prominent leaf vein pattern. Small to medium in size, Fittonia Albivenis does best when kept in bright, indirect light or in an area with dappled sunlight. Fittonia Albivenis does well when humidity is kept decently high making it a suitable choice for Wabi Kusa style planted setups or terrarium-like enclosures. Fittonia Albivenis commonly referred to as the Nerve Plant due to its vein pattern, is not an aquatic plant and should not be fully submerged as doing so will cause the plant to die. Propagation is simple and can be done through stem cuttings. This Fittonia comes in a decorative clay ball structure that is ready to plant in your enclosed garden setup. The ball itself is covered with Christmas Moss, a very popular aquarium moss! Please note, that y ou may receive Fittonia White, Skeleton, or Red depending on the current inventory.

Hemigraphis Repanda Green Dragon's Tongue is a beautiful plant that offers good texture and bright color to terrariums, paludariums, and vivarium style setups. This plant is not aquatic and should not be submerged, but it is relatively hardy and undemanding with care. Its interesting appearance, color, and texture make it a great addition to dish gardens, terrariums, and more. Alternatively, Green Dragon's Tongue may also be planted outdoors in shaded areas and will slowly create good ground coverage. Dragon's Tongue does best in medium to high lighting. It will tolerate low lighting, but this may reduce the vibrancy of colors and result in leggier and not as compact/robust growth. This Hemigraphis Repanda Green comes in a netted pot and is ready to plant in your enclosed garden setup once the rockwool is removed. Common Name Hemigraphis Repanda Green Care Easy Lighting Low to Medium Our terrarium plants are kept under strict and clean environments and are provided with ample humidity and lighting in their holding containers.

Begonia Arabian Sunset is a shrub-like Begonia that offers dense, bushy growth. Its leaves offer beautiful shades of dark bronze, reds and orange-toned hues. This Begonia does best when placed in stable conditions the preferably provide partial shade, indirect lighting, relative humidity, and a consistent temperature range. If provided with the correct conditions for health, Begonia Arabian Sunset is a beautiful species that will bloom bright pink flowers that hang together in small groups. The bold color tones on this plant pair well with fellow red tones or contrast beautifully against greens and variegated foliage. Begonia Arabian Sunset is NOT an aquarium plant. Submerging this plant in an aquarium will kill it! Begonia are notorious for being bad shippers. Potential leaf loss and signs of transit-shock are normal Common Name(s) Begonia Arabian Sunset Begonia Care Easy Lighting Low to Medium Growth Rate Slow Size Varies Depending on Conditions

Glass lids are the perfect addition to your Ultum Nature Systems rimless glass aquarium tank. They are great for minimizing water evaporation and keeping even the most skittish fish, safe - all without compromising the clean aesthetic of a rimless planted tank. Crafted with precision, they fit any UNS tank while ensuring proper room for essential equipment. Includes: Respective c lear plastic clips that fit directly onto the corresponding Ultum Nature Systems rimless glass aquarium tank. *Comes in a pack of 4* Note: To ensure you choose the correct size, please refer to the chart provided below. Noted are the minimum amount of clips needed to support the corresponding lid. The UNS 16C and UNS 16T do not require clips as the lid sits flush on the aquarium tank. These clips are intended to be used for UNS Glass Aquarium Lids - We cannot guarantee compatibility with alternative lids used.
