Bucephalandra Kedagang Japan is a variant in the Bucephalandra aquatic plant family. The term Kedagang describes Bucephalandra variants that are quite rare and small in size. Its leaves are slightly curved and grow quite densely. Like most Bucephalandra species, Bucephalandra Kedagang Japan is a great aquatic plant for beginners due to its easy care and undemanding nature. Bucephalandra comes in many varieties, shapes, colors and looks best when kept in clumps in a planted aquarium tank. This aquatic plant prefers lower lighting and will grow nice and dense if favorable conditions are provided. The stem and rhizome should not be covered when planting as this will cause the plant to rot and wither. It is best to attach or wedge Bucephalandra on or between aquarium hardscapes such as driftwood and rocks.

The Snail-Free Plant Bundle is an easy way to add live plants to a planted aquarium while avoiding the pest snails, algae, and common hitchhikers. Each bundle includes tissue culture aquatic plants grown in sterile conditions, making it a great option for hobbyists who want a clean start. Choose from foreground, midground, or background plant bundles depending on the area of the aquarium you are planting. Whether you’re aiming for a lush carpet, adding texture through the midground, or creating height and movement in the background, each bundle is designed to simplify plant selection while supporting a pest-free planted aquarium. What's Included (Bundle Options) Foreground (Monte Carlo): 5 Monte Carlo tissue culture cups that are ideal for thicker carpets and Iwagumi aquascapes. Foreground (Hairgrass): 5 Dwarf Hairgrass tissue culture cups that are best for nature-style aquascaping and Wabi Sabi layouts. Midground (Mixed): A curated mix of 5 tissue culture midground plants selected to add texture, depth, and color throughout the midground area. Background (Mixed): A curated mix of 5 tissue culture background plants selected to create height, movement, and a natural backdrop for a planted aquarium Tissue culture plants are typically grown emersed and may go through an adjustment period after being introduced to a new aquarium. Some melt or transitional growth is normal as plants adapt to submerged conditions. We recommend planting in fully cycled aquariums to help reduce transitional stress and melt. Plant varieties included in the mixed Midground and Background bundles are selected based on availability and may change at any time. Important Information: The plants included in these bundles are grown in sterile tissue culture conditions. Photos are representative of what you may receive. Natural variation in size, leaf shape, and growth stage should be expected with live aquatic plants.

Eriocaulon Setaceum is a beautiful aquarium stem plant that challenges its growers. In the wild, Eriocaulon Setaceum grows in stagnant and flowing waters in Southeast Asia and Australia. Comparable in care Tonina species, Eriocaulon Setaceum requires very specific parameters for successful growth. A quality substrate, soft water, high lighting, and CO2 injection are basic requirements to keep this Erio happy so this aquarium plant is recommended for seasoned aquarists. If successful, Eriocaulon Setaceum produces needle-like leaves that are very light green to almost white. This Erio has the ability to grow quite tall in cultivated settings and will happily produce lateral shoots to produce a bushy appearance when happy. Pruning can be done the same as other aquarium stem plants but should be done sparingly as Eriocaulon Setaceum does not respond well to trimming. One should also consider a consistent supply of micro and macronutrients as a key to its survival and growth. Common Name Eriocaulon Setaceum Care Advanced Lighting High CO2 Required Suggested Placement Midground to Background Propagation Separate and replant Growth Rate Moderate Height 5+" Our bunched stem plants are all kept and grown in high-quality substrate by Marfied Controsoil . A strict fertilizer dosing regime and CO2 are provided in their holding tanks.

listings.commonName: UNS Mini CO2 Dual Stage Regulator
listings.description: The UNS Mini CO2 Dual Stage Regulator is a compact, all-in-one CO2 solution designed for planted aquarium hobbyists seeking professional-grade performance in a smaller footprint. Compatible with standard refillable CO2 cylinders, paintball cylinders, and UNS disposable cartridges right out of the box, it eliminates the guesswork of finding the right adapters while giving hobbyists the flexibility to choose the CO2 system that best fits their aquarium. Best For - Nano and small planted aquariums - Aquarium stands with limited space - First-time CO2 users - Aquascapers using disposable, paintball, or refillable cylinders Why Choose the UNS Mini Regulator? While compatible with standard refillable cylinders, its compact size and cylinder flexibility make it especially popular for nano aquariums, smaller cabinets, and aquarium setups with limited space. Shop All CO2 Regulators

Drosera Rotundifolia, also known as the Round-leaved Sundew, is a lovely carnivorous plant that features signature circular traps. Its leaves are rounded, lime-green and lined with long red sticky tentacles. It is a medium-sized sundew and naturally grows in damp, boggy conditions with mottled sunlight. One of the best-known Drosera species, D. rotundifolia has been widely studied and used to better understand carnivorous habits. In ideal conditions, it blooms delicate white flowers and readily self-seeds, producing dense colonies over time. If you're looking for a plant that is functional and fun to observe, consider carnivorous species. They work beautifully in terrariums and vivariums, or as individual potted plants. Ensure they are planted in a consistently moist growing medium like sphagnum moss. If you live in drier conditions, consider placing them in a shallow dish of RO water. Common Name Sundew Care Easy Lighting Moderate to High CO2 Non-aquatic Terrarium Placement Bright & waterlogged Propagation Leaf or root cuttings Growth Rate Varies Size Varies

Green Filter Sponge (Fine Mesh) A reusable, fine-textured sponge that provides essential mechanical filtration in the first chamber. It works to trap detritus, waste, and plant matter in the early stages. Filter sponges are easy to remove, rinse and replace. Black Filter Sponge (Coarse Mesh) A secondary reusable, coarse sponge that serves as mechanical filtration. It captures large debris and organic matter. Easy to clean and a classic form of filter media. Compatibility: Ultum Nature Systems Delta 60, Delta 90 and Delta 120

Cryptocoryne Undulata is a beautiful but often overlooked aquarium plant. Native to Sri Lanka and Thailand, this lovely variety features textured leaves that can display a mixed palette of dark green and reddish-brown hues. Like most live aquatic plants, its colors are influenced by light and nutrients, making it somewhat of a mystery that unfolds as the tank matures. Appearance aside, it is a forgiving species and is often considered a beginner-friendly plant. Like other crypts, it is able to adapt to a variety of water conditions, but may experience melt in inital stages. Don't let crypt melt deter you. Plant yours in nutrient-dense aquasoil or use root tabs if you have sand and leave it alone. Once established, this family of plants is one of the hardiest around and come in a variety of shapes, sizes and colors. They're a great choice for midground placement in planted tanks and can fill out backgrounds of nano aquariums nicely. Propagation is easy when the plant matures and can be done by gently separating baby plants from the mother. If you're successful once, you'll have many to choose from for your next aquascape. (There's a reason why Cryptocoryne collectors exist!)

Littorella uniflora, commonly known as Shoreweed, is a unique foreground plant recognized for its short, chubby leaves with rounded bases and pointed tips. Its compact, upright growth gives it a distinct appearance compared to more traditional carpeting plants, adding bold texture and contrast to planted aquariums. As it establishes, Littorella uniflora spreads gradually through runners, forming a low, structured carpet over time. Its slow growth is easy to maintain, making it ideal for aquascapes where long-term stability and minimal maintenance are preferred. Its thick, fleshy foliage pairs especially well with finer carpeting species or can be used on its own for a more structured foreground. Adaptable to a wide range of conditions, including cooler water temperatures, Littorella uniflora can be grown both submerged and emersed. While generally easy to care for, an established environment and regular fertilization can support healthier, more consistent growth. CO2 injection can also be provided to support stronger growth but isn't required.

Rotala Manipurensis features narrow leaves and an overhanging, creeping growth. Quite similar to Rotala Sp. 'Green', it is most likely a variation of its popular counterpart, Rotala Rotundifolia. If grown in ideal conditions, the results are rewarding and Rotala Manipurensis features warm and rich color tones that will provide intense orange contrast when used as a background plant in nano planted aquariums or as a midground in larger sized planted tanks. If given a proper environment, Rotala Manipurensis is a fast-growing plant and will require consistent pruning to prevent the bottom leaves from dying off due to lack of lighting and to keep it growing lush. Common Name Rotala Manipurensis Care Moderate Lighting Medium to High CO2 Optional Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Fast Height 15-30 "

Riccia Fluitans, also known as Crystalwort, is a floating aquatic plant made popular by well known and respected nature aquarium master, Takashi Amano. He was the first individual to utilize this delicate plant as an epiphyte by attaching it to hardscape material such as stones and aquarium driftwood. Riccia Fluitans features a delicate texture and light green hue. It is well known for its extreme "pearling" or producing a large number of oxygen bubbles that looks beautiful underwater. Riccia Fluitans is commonly used for a carpet foreground aquatic plant in aquaria but has many uses. Alternatively, it can also be attached to hardscape material or left floating. When attaching it, it's important to note that this particular aquatic plant will not self-attach, meaning it will need to be maintained consistently to prevent it from floating away. CO2 is not required for the growth of Riccia, but it does fare better when CO2 injection is added. Easy to cultivate, Riccia Fluitans will grow quickly if it likes the water it is in. Young fish fry and shrimp also benefit from its coverage and will gladly nestle within its foliage. Common Name Riccia Crystalwort Care Easy Lighting Low to Medium CO2 Optional Suggested Placement All Propagation Cut or pull apart Growth Rate Varies Height Varies

We would also recommend adding more depth and detail to this nano tank by planting a taller grass-like background plant such as Eleocharis Parvulus Mini or Echinodorus Tenellus. Hydrocotyle Leucocephala is a unique aquarium plant that offers vine-like growth and floating bright green, lily-like leaves. Relatively undemanding, Hydrocotyle Leucocephala is similar to other Hydrocotyle species but typically tends to be on the larger side making it suitable for larger planted aquarium tanks or pond-style planted setups. This aquatic plant is easy to keep and is a great beginner plant due to its ability to adapt to a wide range of aquarium parameters. CO2 injection is not required but aids immensely in promoting lush, bushy growth. Growth is also quick and trimming will need to be done to keep it maintained. This version offers slightly variegated leaves with random shades of green and cream. To maintain variegation, higher light should be provided. It should be noted that variegated plants may revert! Common Name Brazilian Pennywort Care Easy to Moderate Lighting Medium CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Midground to Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 5-10"+

Vesicularia Ferriei Weeping AKA Weeping Moss is a beautiful aquatic moss species that features overhanging growth patterns. Its foliage is fleshy and dense with a teardrop-like shape that holds a vibrant light green hue. Like other aquatic moss species, Vesicularia Ferriei Weeping Moss can adapt to a wide range of aquarium tank conditions and can be readily attached to aquarium driftwood and rocks. In order to keep its overhanging appearance, trimming is recommended. We recommend using it in a jungle or forest aquascape layout for additional character, depth, and contrast.

A solid aquarium fish food to support stronger immune systems and vibrant coloration. Hikari Micro Pellets are ideal for Tetras, Barbs, and other small-mouthed tropical fish. These nutrient-rich, micro-coated pellets stay suspended in the water column for easy feeding. Free of parasites and harmful bacteria, Hikari offers a fresh, reliable, and cost-effective way to support optimal fish health. listings.commonName: Hikari Vibra Bites Tropical Fish Food
listings.description: One of our favorites! Our aquarium fish go crazy for Hikari Vibra Bites, an innovative tropical fish food designed to mimic live food. These worm-like pellets are highly attractive and perfect for fish that typically prefer live or frozen diets. Packed with nutrition, Vibra Bites help support strong immune systems, vibrant coloration, and healthy growth. Their slow-sinking behavior keeps food suspended in the water column, making them easy for fish to spot and feed on naturally. Ideal for a wide range of tropical fish, from small species like Tetras and Rasboras to larger fish like Discus and Angelfish. Product Highlights - Unique worm-like form for improved recognition and feeding response - Safe alternative to live blood worms - Packed with natural color-enhancing ingredients Size: 1.23oz Feeding Guidelines: Feed 1-2 times daily in small portions that can be consumed within a few minutes. Cryptocoryne Pontederiifolia is a classic Cryptocoryne species commonly used in the planted aquarium hobby. Known for its broad green leaves, Cryptocoryne Pontederiifolia is a medium-sized Crypt and suitable for larger planted aquarium tanks although it will likely adapt to nano-sized aquarium tanks as well given its easy-going nature. Like other Cryptocoryne species, C. Pontederiifolia has low light requirements and is a great aquarium plant for beginner aquarists. One should provide ample time for Cryptocoryne Pontederiifolia to adapt to its environment as moving it frequently may result in the death of the plant. Once settled, it has the ability to grow at a good pace. High lighting, CO2 injection and nutrient-dense aquarium soil will boost its growth and may alter its low-tech appearance as well. Final form, size, shape and color are determined by the tank it is placed in. Propagation is simple and can be done by gently separating the mother plant into smaller portions and replanting into quality aquarium soil intended for aquatic plant propagation and growth.

Anubias Minima Variegated is a variegated form of Anubias Minima. Belonging to the Anubias family, Anubias Minima is fairly rare despite its common counterparts that are frequently used in all types of planted aquariums. Like other Anubias it can grow in a multitude of environments varying from aquariums to terrariums. Anubias Minima Variegated features slender leaves with a deep green coloration accompanied by splashes of lighter green and yellow hues. This form is suitable as a midground and background aquatic plant as the leaves are capable of growing quite long and will require more light than its normal form to maintain its coloration. This Anubias variant is a flowering plant that grows best when the rhizome is attached to a hard surface such as wood or stone. It benefits from consistent fertilization but light requirements are minimal as its leaves are susceptible to algae growth when placed under high lighting. CO2 is optional but can promote faster growth and robust leaves when used.

Rotala Nanjenshan is described as a hybrid cross between Rotala Rotundifolia and Rotala Wallichi. It features dense stems with very thin leaves that give it a bushy appearance. Rotala Nanjenshan can be difficult to keep as it requires quality aquarium lighting and CO2 injection to thrive. It is also fairly fragile and should only be planted in an aquarium with smaller docile fish species as overly active or aggressive swimmers have the potential to damage the aquatic plant. If successful in keeping this aquatic plant, Rotala Nanjenshan grows dense and will require regular pruning to keep it in tip-top shape. Common Name Rotala Nanjenshan Care Moderate Lighting Medium to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Fast Height 5-10+" Tissue culture plants are grown in-vitro by laboratories who specialize in propagating aquatic plants. This makes them perfect for shrimp keepers and any planted tank enthusiasts alike. NOTE: It is important to remove the tissue culture agar gel before planting. Simply wash the gel away, divide, and plant.

Hygrophila Pinnatifida is a relatively rarer aquatic plant in the aquarium hobby. This aquatic plant features green and bronze hues on the upper side of its leaves and possesses a notorious deep red hue on the underside. A classic plant to use in aquascape layouts, Hygrophila Pinnatifida makes a beautiful addition to any planted aquarium tank. Its care requirements isn't too difficult so long as the water is kept clean and quality aquarium lighting is provided. Compact growth can be encouraged through frequent trimming and high light. Dosing additional nutrients, such as Iron, will also help to bring out the deep coloration that is, more often than not, the goal of keeping this aquatic plant. In addition, this unique aquatic plant can be attached to aquarium hardscape such as driftwood or rock instead of being planted directed in planted tank substrate. Rotala Narrow Leaf Red features narrow leaves with bright reddish hues. A new Glass Aqua favorite for red aquarium plants, this species of Rotala is relatively undemanding and easy to grow. Rotala Narrow Leaf Red's appearance is similar to Rotala Rotundifolia with slightly longer leaves. The ease in both obtaining and retaining bright, bold red colors with Rotala Narrow Leaf Red quickly makes it a favorite. We recommend providing standard care for Rotala species, and then some. High quality, nutritious aquarium soil, good LED lighting, CO2 injection and regular fertilizing are a great start for obtaining bushy, vibrant growth. Rotala Narrow Leaf Red would work beautifully in Dutch style planted aquariums or as a simple red aquarium plant accent in the background of nature aquariums. Propagation is the same as other Rotala species and aquatic stem plants in general. Snip along the stem and replant into the soil. Rotala are quick growing species and will require consistent pruning to prevent overgrowth and the shading of lower portions. Common Name Rotala Narrow Leaf Red Care Easy Lighting Medium to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Fast Height 15-30+ "

Echinodorus Chameleon is a gorgeous variety of Echinodorus, producing vibrant hues in a planted aquarium. When placed under high lighting, this species offers more compact growth and intense coloration. Varying hues of reds and greens are produced and offer great contrast in the background of planted aquariums. Like most Echinodorus, this species can grow quite large if given optimal conditions so we recommend using it in standard to larger sized aquariums, if possible. Like all aquatic sword species, Echinodorus Chameleon is easy to keep, fairly hardy and needs a minimum of a nutrient-rich aquarium substrate as these species of aquatic plant are heavy root feeders. Aside from this, Echinodorus species are fairly tolerable of varying water parameters and lighting conditions. While this little aquatic sword grows more compact, it is still a larger aquatic plant in general and should be pruned periodically to ensure smaller aquatic plants are not shaded from the light provided. Propagation is simple. Separate and replant. Common Name Amazon Sword Echinodorus Chameleon Care Easy Lighting Low to Medium CO2 Optional Suggested Placement Background Propagation Separate and Replant Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 4-12+"

Echinodorus Red Wild Grass is on the newer spectrum of Amazon Sword Plant species. Considered to be on the small side for Echinodorus, Echinodorus Red Wild Grass is a suitable sword plant choice for smaller planted aquariums. Newer leaves are a soft pink color with older leaves displaying vibrant green hues. Echinodorus Red Wild Grass is easy to grow both submerged and emerged with its emerged form displaying harder, coarse-textured green leaves. Echinodorus easy care makes it a great choice for beginner hobbyists and typically works great in Wabi Kusa setups as well. Like all aquatic sword species, Echinodorus Red Wild Grass is easy to keep, fairly hardy and needs a minimum of a nutrient-rich aquarium substrate as these species of aquatic plant are heavy root feeders. Aside from this, Echinodorus species are fairly tolerable of varying water parameters and lighting conditions.

Echinodorus Red Devil is a manmade cultivar that features smaller growth and bold red hues when grown in optimal aquarium conditions. Able to grow emersed, Echinodorus Red Devil appears larger in size and has coarse-textured, green leaves. When grown in an aquarium, its size is more compact, colorful and slightly wavy. Echinodorus easy care makes it a great choice for beginner hobbyists and typically works great in Wabi Kusa setups as well. Like all aquatic sword species, Echinodorus Red Wild Grass is easy to keep, fairly hardy and needs a minimum of a nutrient-rich aquarium substrate as these species of aquatic plant are heavy root feeders. Aside from this, Echinodorus species are fairly tolerable of varying water parameters and lighting conditions. Propagation is simple. Separate and replant. Common Name Amazon Sword Echinodorus Red Devil Care Easy Lighting Low to Medium CO2 Optional Suggested Placement Background Propagation Separate and Replant Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 4-12+"

PRO CO2 Manifold Block Multiple manifold blocks can be added to the UNS Pro Regulator to allow for CO2 injection into multiple planted aquariums. The manifold block consists of a detachable bubble counter, built-in check valve, and precise needle valve to lessen additional inline CO2 accessories. As a result, the combination of a single UNS Pro Regulator along with numerous manifold blocks creates a hassle-free and simplified planted aquarium CO2 injection system. Why CO2 injection is important in a planted tank: 3 main factors contribute to the optimal growth of aquatic plants. These factors include nutrients, light and carbon dioxide (CO2). If any of these are unbalanced, the results are algae growth or the withering of plants. The introduction of CO2 in a planted aquarium allows plants to thrive and grow more efficiently, while also giving them the ability to out-compete algae for nutrients. No matter what type of planted aquarium setup you have, we recommend CO2 injection for better aquarium plant growth. Includes: This listing is for ONE Manifold Block that is compatible with the Ultum Nature Systems Pro Dual Stage CO2 Regulator

Echinodorus Uruguayensis is a beautiful Amazon Sword plant that possesses many forms and cultivars throughout its time in the aquarium hobby. Readily available in the trade, Echinodorus Uruguayensis features varying green hues and leaf lengths depending on the plant purchased. Like most Amazon Sword plants, Echinodorus Uruguayensis has the ability to grow very large and is recommended for larger planted aquariums. Care standards are similar to other sword species with Uruguayensis being easy to keep. This aquarium plant is fairly hardy and needs a minimum of a nutrient-rich aquarium substrate as it is a heavy root feeder and will absorb nutrients in this manner. Aside from this, Echinodorus species are fairly tolerable of varying water parameters and lighting conditions. Propagation is simple. Separate and replant. Anubias Nana Pinto, also known as Nana Marbled White or simply Anubias Pinto, is a variegated aquatic plant perfect for planted aquariums and aquascaping! Its leaves are beautifully marbled, featuring a mixture of green, white, and cream hues. Each leaf is slightly different, making every plant one-of-a-kind. Similar in size to Nana Petite, Pinto is typically planted along the base of an aquascape. It is also an epiphyte, growing well when attached to porous structures like rocks or driftwood. Because of its variegation, it requires a little more light than other forms of Anubias, but it can still be added to low-tech planted tanks. If you enjoy variegated plants, consider adding Anubias Pinto to your aquascape—it will easily stand out as a focal point in any planted aquarium. When you have a larger plant, you can propagate it by separating gently along the rhizome.

Rotala Macrandra 'Mini Butterfly' is a delicate aquarium stem plant known for its vibrant red to magenta hues and dense form. Macrandra cultivars have been a longtime favorite for the aquascaping community—they come in a variety of colors, sizes, shapes and difficulty levels. Unlike Rotundifolia, Macrandra variations can be temperamental and will quickly reflect the conditions in a planted tank. Start with soft water, stable CO2 injection and high lighting. Rotala Macrandra ‘Mini Butterfly’ is best suited for high tech tanks and will also need a quality liquid aquatic plant fertilizer for proper growth and good color. Adjusting a main element, like lighting or nutrients, will produce different results. On top of this, keeping all parameters consistent is a must as any dips or fluctuations will easily cause stunted growth. If successful, it is a fast growing stem plant that will be a visual gem in any aquascape. When planting, be sure to give each stem enough space for even light distribution and uniform growth. Ammania Sengalensis is great for creating contrast amongst green aquatic plants. Characterized by thick stems and wavy oval leaves, its coloration includes a range of greens, yellows and reds. When provided with proper lighting and regular fertilization, Ammania Senegalensis can grow to an impressive size, making it a good choice for background zones in a planted aquarium.

Add a gradient of color to your planted aquarium with Ammania Gracilis. Depending on light intensity, this aquarium stem plant can develop a range of colors that include shades of green, yellow, red and pink. As it matures, its foliage becomes pointed and slightly wavy, adding extra texture and movement in an aquascape. It can grow to an impressive size, making it ideal for the midground to background zones of a planted aquarium. As a fast-grower, regular trimming will be required to ensure long-term health.

Utricularia Graminifolia is a popular carpeting plant! UG for short, this unique bladderwort is a carnivorous plant that can be spotted growing in marginal conditions in the wild. This gives it the ability to thrive fully submerged in a planted aquarium or above water in terrarium and paludarium-like setups. Be aware, Utricularia Graminifolia is considered a more advanced aquarium plant since it can be temperamental. You'll find plenty of methods and differing opinions on the best way to grow UG. These include nutrient-poor substrates, soft water and varying light exposures. We find that it grows best for us using the dry start method (DSM) . Because it doesn’t have a root system, giving it time to grow over itself is important. It provides that iconic carpet plant look and establishes a hold in the substrate to prevent floating when flooding the tank. From there, we strongly recommend moderate to high CO2 levels to maintain growth. If successful, UG becomes easy to grow and does not demand more than it gives. It also feeds on small insects or aquatic organisms. It is a tropical species and does not go through dormant periods!

Microsorum pteropus ‘Sunrise’, also known as Java Fern Sunrise, is a unique variation that stands out for its lighter, golden-green new growth and textured leaves. Its brighter coloration adds a subtle pop compared to standard Java Fern, making it a nice option for adding contrast in planted aquariums. Recently reclassified as Leptochilus pteropus , this plant is still widely known in the aquarium hobby as Microsorum pteropus. Like other Java Fern varieties, it is very easy to care for and adapts well to a wide range of aquarium conditions, similar to plants like Anubias, Bucephalandra, and Cryptocoryne. It grows well in low to medium lighting with good flow and a clean water column. While it will adapt in low tech setups, the addition of CO2 and regular fertilization will improve growth and overall appearance. Its slightly serrated leaves and fuller growth make it a great space filler, especially between driftwood or hardscape where it helps create a more mature, filled-in look. As an epiphytic plant, Java Fern Sunrise can be attached to driftwood, rocks, or placed into crevices within an aquascape. Be sure to keep the rhizome above the substrate to prevent rot. Propagation is simple—just divide the rhizome and reattach as needed.

Ardisia Tricolor is on the rarer side of the spectrum for commonly kept terrarium plants. Originating from Asia, this plant loves high humidity and low to medium lighting conditions. Coveted for striking foliage, Ardisia Tricolor offers bold hues of green with dark, prominent venation throughout its leaves. When placed under LED lighting, colors are stunning in a terrarium, vivarium or enclosed container garden. We recommend high humidity, partial-shade and a mixture of quality sphagnum or peat moss mixed with your choice of bark, perlite or alternative potting mediums. Stunted or deformed growth may signal nutritional deficiencies and browning edges are signs of insufficient humidity levels. Hygrophila sp. Chai is a rare pink aquatic plant! Known for its vibrant pink hue, its color comes from a rare mutation of the standard Hygrophila araguaia. Unlike other aquatic stem plants, Chai exhibits creeping growth that can slowly create bushy horizontal coverage in planted aquariums. Its leaves are slender and spindly, giving it a delicate appearance that looks great in colorful tanks. It is considered an advanced plant due to its sensitivity. For best success rates, it should be planted in mature tanks with stable parameters, high light, CO2 injection and a quality source of nutrients. Give this plant time to establish a healthy root system and good growth before attempting to propagate. Once mature, it can be propagated like other stem plants via trimmings. If you’re a pink plant lover and have a good understanding of balance in a planted tank, give this one a try! Common Name Hygrophila sp. Chai Care Advanced Lighting High CO2 Required Aquascape Placement Midground Propagation Trim and replant Growth Rate Slow Size 4-7+”

Cryptocoryne Dewitii is a rare species in the Cryptocoryne genus and Araceae family. This aquatic plant grows marginally in the wild and features a beautiful green hue with slightly puckered texture when healthy and mature. There isn't much information available for this Cryptocoryne species, so it can only be assumed that care follows the same general guidelines for Cryptocoryne plants. We recommend Cryptocoryne Dewitii as a mid to background aquarium plant and planting it in nutrient-dense aquarium soil to meet the requirements of heavy root-feeding plant species. Low to medium lighting with partial shade along with CO2 injection is likely preferable along with consistent maintenance habits. Like most Cryptocoryne species, Cryptocoryne Dewitii should not be bothered, if possible to prevent notorious Crypt melt. Propagation is simple and can be done by gently separating the mother plant into smaller portions and replanting into quality aquarium soil intended for aquatic plant propagation and growth.

Sporting a vibrant hue, Pilea Spruceana is a great choice for those who are looking to add pops of color into their terrarium or enclosed container gardens. A must-have for Pilea collectors, Pilea Spruceana may also be grown as a standard house plant, but we recommend having it near a humidifier as higher humidity levels are always appreciated. Microsorum Pteropus Fishtail is an oddball Java Fern for planted aquariums and aquascaping. This variety offers good texture and bright colors that include shades of green, yellow, pink and orange. Like other aquatic ferns, it is hardy and will forgive a range of water conditions. This makes it ideal for beginner aquariums where fluctuations can be more common. Recently reclassified as Leptochilus pteropus , this plant is still widely known in the hobby as Microsorum pteropus. Its split-end leaves are ideal for filling in empty space or just for adding extra visual interest in a low light aquascape! Its care is similar to other popular low-light aquatic plants like Anubias, Bucephalandra and Cryptocoryne. As an epiphyte, it grows best when attached to driftwood or porous surfaces.

Cryptocoryne Balansae is a unique species! It is known for its long, narrow leaves with a slightly crinkled texture. Its bold green coloration and taller grass-like growth makes it a great choice when you want to add height and movement to the background of a planted aquarium. Over time, it can grow quite large and tall, so its better suited for the midground to background of larger aquariums. As it settles in, it can develop dense groups that add flowing movement and coverage for tropical fish and shrimp. Like most Cryptocoryne, it doesn't like being moved once planted. Allow it to establish a healthy root system before attempting to propagate or reposition! Once established, it is easy to care for and will grow steadily in most conditions. High light and CO2 are not required to grow this aquarium plant, but Cryptocoryne are heavy root feeders, so we recommend using a nutrient-dense aquarium soil or providing it with targeted nutrients via root tabs. CO2, whenever possible, is always beneficial for aquarium plants!

Trichomanes Javanicum is a beautiful terrarium fern that originates from South East Asia. With little information available, this plant offers delicate foliage and texture to any terrarium, paludarium or vivarium enclosure. From experience, this terrarium fern, sometimes called the Borneo Fern, does best with higher humidity levels and low to medium lighting. This species is fairly slow-growing but is definitely a must-have terrarium plant for any fern collector, lover, or enthusiast. Insufficient humidity may present itself in the form of crisping leaf edges and/or slow decline of overall health. One of our favorites! Trichomanes Javanicum Fern is NOT an aquarium plant. Submerging this plant in an aquarium will kill it!

SL Aqua's Z3 BBA Remover is a freshwater aquarium tank treatment that aims to rid planted aquariums of pesky BBA. BBA, commonly known as black beard algae or black brush algae, is a stubborn form of algae that typically attaches to everything in a planted tank from aquarium plant leaves to hardscape material such as driftwood and stones. SL Aqua Z3 BBA Remover aims to remove this unsightly algae by simultaneously slowing down reproduction and killing spores. Z3 BBA Remover may also be used on other strains of algae commonly found in planted aquariums such as filamentous algae, blue algae and brown algae. When used correctly, Z3 BBA Remover will not harm aquatic plants or tropical fish inhabitants. We recommend using Z3 BBA Remover by SL Aqua in combination with good aquarium tank cleaning practices! Notes: Treatment cycles last 2 weeks. Add 2 drops for every 25L/6.6G of water once, daily. Do not change water or perform aquarium tank maintenance during this time. Algae will begin turning white. This is a sign the treatment is working! Complete a 30% water change weekly, minimum. Once the 2 week period is up, add the recommended dose once, weekly or as necessary for precautionary use. Do not use Z3 BBA Remover in an aquarium that contains invertebrates or snails. Recommended for freshwater use only. Size: 20ml

Hydrocotyle Verticillata is a beautiful species of Hydrocotyle that can be grown in both submerged aquarium settings and emersed environments. When grown in aquariums, this aquatic plant retains its trailing behavior and produces shield-like leaf pads that add varying texture to any planted aquarium tank. Optimal conditions include soft water, CO2 injection, nutrient-dense aquarium soil and medium lighting. This aquarium plant species may be used near the mid ground and can also be considered as a unique foreground aquatic plant. Hydrocotyle Verticillata, sometimes also known as Whorled Pennywort or Shield Pennywort, is a great aquarium plant for beginner hobbyists as well as experienced aquascapers who are seasoned in caring for aquatic plant species. Hydrocotyle Verticillata can grow quite large emersed and is a wonderful species to grow! Propagate by trimming stems and replanting. Alternatively, pull apart dense clumps, splitting the roots, and replant. New shoots can be trimmed anywhere along the stem thus allowing the plant to grow thicker and more compact. Common Name Whorled Marsh Pennywort Care Easy to Moderate Lighting Medium CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Midground Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 7-10+"

Bolbitis Heteroclita,commonly known as Asian Water Fern or Bolbitis Broadleaf, is an easy care fern that grows well in low light aquariums with emersed sections. Like other similar species, these plants benefit from elevated humidity to prevent drying leaves. Bolbitis Heteroclita features bright green color on broad, ribbed leaves. It is an epiphyte and will self-attach to porous surfaces like hardscape rocks and driftwood. Bolbitis can survive submerged in planted aquariums, but will need CO2 injection and a liquid plant fertilizer to support its growth. We find these plants are much happier when planted above the surface in terrariums or paludarium-like tanks. In this position, they have humidity, access to water and plenty of CO2. They are slow-growing, but with patience, will produce lush, leafy bushes of green in a planted setup when provided with consistent care and stable conditions. Propagate your Bolbitis easily by separating the rhizome gently.

Microsorum pteropus ‘Thor’s Hammer’, also known as Java Fern Thor’s Hammer, is a unique variation known for its bright green leaves with tips that resemble the shape of a hammer. This distinctive form gives it a unique, sculptural look compared to other Java Fern varieties. Recently reclassified as Leptochilus pteropus , this plant is still widely known in the aquarium hobby as Microsorum pteropus. However, like other Java Fern plants, it is hardy, easy to care for, and adaptable to a wide range of aquarium conditions. It grows from a rhizome and will do best when attached to driftwood, rocks, or placed into crevices within hardscape. Over time, it will naturally self-attach, adding texture and structure to an aquascape. Java Fern Thor’s Hammer grows well in low to medium lighting and is suitable for low tech planted aquariums. It can also be grown in high-humidity environments such as terrariums, vivariums, and paludariums. Be sure to keep the rhizome above the substrate to prevent rot. Propagation is simple—just divide the rhizome and reattach as needed.

Rotala Fujian is one of many Rotundifolia varieties. This aquarium stem plant features green emersed growth and will develop orange-pink hues in planted aquariums. It is a smaller pink aquarium stem plant and grows more compact than other cultivars, making it great for nano planted tanks and smaller aquascaping projects. Start with quality basics. A good aquarium LED fixture, nutrient-rich aquarium soil, CO2 injection and a liquid aquatic plant fertilizer. Rotala plants are great for nature-style aquariums! Mix and match various leaf shapes for a myriad of colors and textures. Periodic trimming will be necessary to allow light to penetrate to lower areas of the plant and to encourage branching. Replant healthy tops and you'll have a bushy section of Rotala in no time. Common Name Rotala Rotundifolia 'Fujian' Care Moderate Lighting High CO2 Necessary Suggested Placement Midground to Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate Height Varies depending on environment

Rotala Blood Red is another variation of Rotala Rotundifolia with higher demands and a finicky nature. When planted in the correct conditions, Rotala Blood Red has the potential to produce vivid, bold red hues, as its name suggests. However, this color only emerges when the aquarium plant is happy and provided with optimal growing conditions. Similar to other difficult to grow Rotala species, Rotala Blood Red requires CO2 injection, high lighting, softer water, a nutrient-dense aquarium soil and a quality fertilizing regiment. This variation of Rotala does not grow as quickly and exhibits an upright, straighter growth pattern that doesn't branch out as often when trimmed. Because of this, this aquarium stem plant will need to be trimmed and replanted more often to produce a bushy appearance. Rotala Blood Red is not a beginner aquatic plant, but for those are successful in growing it, rewards will be great! Common Name Rotala Rotundifolia Rotala Blood Red Care Difficult Lighting High CO2 Required Suggested Placement Midground to Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate Height Varies depending on environment

Nesaea Triflora is a rare aquarium stem plant that is sometimes referred to as Ammania Triflora, is a rarer aquarium stem plant that features a robust stem and broader leaves varying in tones of green, yellow, reds and oranges. Similar to other species in the same family, Nesaea Triflora also requires a good amount of quality aquarium LED lighting along with CO2 injection and more specific water parameters to promote lush, boldly colored growth. These factors make this aquarium plant slightly more advanced and not recommended for beginner hobbyists. When planting, Nesaea Triflora should be planted in quality aquarium soil with enough space between each stem to ensure lower levels receive an ample amount of lighting as well. Lack of lighting can result in dull coloration as well as the rotting of the lower portions. This aquarium plant can also be grown in emersed conditions. We recommend planting Nesaea Triflora in the midground of a planted aquarium tank. The style of this aquatic stem plant would work well for a classic Nature Aquarium Style planted aquarium or in a Dutch Style planted aquarium as well. The slight variation in deep orange and bronze tones would add a lovely contrast to groups of red, magenta and green aquarium stem plants. Simple to propagate, Nesaea Triflora can be treated the same as other aquatic stem plants: simply cut the stem and replant the trimmings into quality aquarium soil. Common Name Nesaea Triflora Ammannia Triflora Care Moderate to Advanced Lighting Medium to High CO2 Required Suggested Placement Midground or Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height Varies depending on environment

Limnophila Belem is a rare and attractive aquarium stem plant suitable for mid and background placement in a planted aquarium tank. This aquarium stem plant features lovely color with added texture from its serrated leaf edges. When properly taken care of, this Limnophila species branches well and will readily put out new growth, resulting in the need for regular pruning. While Limnophila Belem will survive without CO2 injection, the presence of it in the planted aquarium will noticeably encourage robust growth and better color. Along with CO2 injection, we recommend providing it with quality aquarium LED lighting and a nutrient-dense aquarium soil as a start. Like other aquarium stem plants, Limnophila Belem is simple to propagate and can be done by trimming anywhere along the stem and replanting it into aquarium soil. A great choice for medium to large-sized planted aquariums! Add fresh color to your planted aquarium with Ludwigia Marilia. This uncommon South American Ludwigia develops rounded leaves ranging from bright green to light red and warmer orange tones, creating a colorful group with a softer appearance than narrow-leaved stem plants. Ludwigia Marilia grows upright and can develop quickly under suitable conditions, making it a fine choice for the background of larger aquariums where its size has room to develop. Regular trimming helps control its height while encouraging additional side shoots, allowing individual stems to branch into fuller, denser groups. If allowed to reach the surface, stems can continue growing along the waterline and develop floating foliage.

Rotala Manipurensis features narrow leaves and an overhanging, creeping growth. Quite similar to Rotala Sp. 'Green', it is most likely a variation of its popular counterpart, Rotala Rotundifolia. If grown in ideal conditions, the results are rewarding and Rotala Manipurensis features warm and rich orange tones that will provide intense contrast when used as a background plant in nano planted aquariums or as a midground in larger sized planted tanks. If given a proper environment, Rotala Manipurensis is a fast-growing plant and will require consistent pruning to prevent the bottom leaves from dying off due to lack of lighting and to keep it growing lush. Episcias are beautiful plants belonging to the Gesneriad family. They have a stoloniferous growth pattern and produce plantlets along the length of its runners. Episcia Ruby Red Dress is a classic form of Episcia and features beautiful, bold coloration. Episcia make a great vining choice in terrariums or terrarium-like container gardens. Like most terrarium suitable species, Episcia Ruby Red thrives in higher humidity levels and prefer partial shade but will tolerate bright, indirect lighting sources. Direct bright light, or direct sunlight will dry and damage this plant. Signs of insufficient humidity levels will appear in the form of crisping or browning leaf edges. Normal pruning will be necessary to keep the plant in tip top shape as Episcia has the tendency to grow over itself and will result in a mangled appearance if not tended to. Episcia Ruby Red is NOT an aquarium plant. Submerging this plant in an aquarium will kill it! Labisia plants thrive in high humidity and low to medium lighting conditions. Labisia Musim features large, rounded leaves with high-contrast color tones that are characteristic of other Labisia commonly used for terrariums and vivariums. This humidity loving plant displays prominent venation that almost glows along with a wrinkled leaf texture that is comparable to aged leather or reptilian critters. Its high contrast color tones and stunning venation pattern are exaggerated when placed under plant LED grow lights making it a noticeable feature in any terrarium, vivarium or enclosed container garden. We encourage high humidity, partial-shade and a mixture of quality sphagnum or peat moss mixed with your choice of bark, perlite or alternative potting mediums for planting guidelines. Stunted or deformed growth may signal nutritional deficiencies and browning edges are signs of insufficient humidity levels. Labisia plants can grow quite large so we recommend having a sizeable tank or enclosure for this plant. This plant belongs on the rare vivarium plant collector's list! This plant will ship as a cutting that may or may not be lightly rooted Labisia Musim is NOT an aquarium plant. Submerging this plant in an aquarium will kill it! When placed under quality plant LED grow lights, this variation of Ardisia displays a metallic sheen combined of green, purple, maroon and golden tones. Its leaves are puckered in texture, adding to the exotic appearance Ardisia Dino provides. As basic guidelines, we recommend providing this rare vivarium plant with sufficient humidity levels and planting it in high-quality sphagnum moss or a mixture of bark and perlite. Since these substrates lack inherent nutrients, regular feeding is essential for vigorous growth. Signs of stunted or deformed leaves may indicate nutrient deficiencies or pest issues, while browning leaf edges could suggest inadequate humidity. This plant will ship as a cutting that may or may not be lightly rooted Ardisia Dino is NOT an aquarium plant. Submerging this plant in an aquarium will kill it! When placed under LED lighting, colors are exaggerated, allowing this plant to really shine. Appearance features rounded, tear-drop shaped leaves with coloration being a mixture of dark tones. When placed under LED lighting, Ardisia Black's metallic sheen is apparent, making it a beautiful addition to any vivarium, terrarium or enclosed container garden. As basic guidelines, we recommend providing this rare vivarium plant with sufficient humidity levels and planting it in high-quality sphagnum moss or a mixture of bark and perlite. Sphagnum moss, bark and perlite naturally do not contain any nutritional benefits, so it is essential to ensure this plant is given nutrients periodically. Stunted or deformed growth may signal nutritional deficiencies or the presence of pests. Browning edges may signal insufficient humidity levels. This plant will ship as a cutting that may or may not be lightly rooted Ardisia Black is NOT an aquarium plant. Submerging this plant in an aquarium will kill it! Common Name Ardisia Black Ardisia Care Moderate Lighting Low to Medium Growth Rate Slow Size Varies Depending on Conditions

Rhaphidophora Sp is a popular genus in the Araceae family that is commonly used in vivarium and terrarium enclosures. Loved by hobbyists for its wide range of growing dispositions, this Rhaphidorphora species presents a shingling growth habit and will happily climb or trail along the wall of a vivarium, terrarium or paludarium. As a basic guideline, we recommend providing this vivarium plant with sufficient humidity levels and a growing medium such as high-quality sphagnum moss or a mixture of bark and perlite. Sphagnum moss, bark, and perlite naturally do not contain any nutritional benefits, so it is essential to ensure this plant is given nutrients periodically. Alternatively, Rhaphidophora sp. will climb and trail around your enclosure when happy. Stunted or deformed growth may signal nutritional deficiencies or the presence of pests. Browning or crispy leaf edges may signal insufficient humidity levels. This plant will ship as a cutting that may or may not be lightly rooted Rhaphidophora sp. is NOT an aquarium plant. Submerging this plant in an aquarium will kill it! Common Name Rhaphidophora Sp. Care Moderate Lighting Low to Medium Growth Rate Slow to Moderate Size Varies Depending on Conditions

Add rich, earthy color to your planted aquarium with Cryptocoryne Cordata Var. Blassii. Broad leaves develop olive green to brown tones across the surface with contrasting wine-colored undersides, giving this Crypt plenty of color and dimension without relying on bright red foliage. Hardy and relatively undemanding once established, Crypt Blassii is a great choice for beginner-friendly and low-tech planted aquariums. Its broad foliage works especially well throughout the midground or in partially shaded areas beneath hardscape and taller aquatic plants. Like other Cryptocoryne, Blassii appreciates a nutrient-rich substrate and plenty of time to establish a healthy root system after planting. Avoid unnecessary moving or disturbance while it settles in, and allow new growth to gradually develop into a fuller group.

Anubias Barteri Butterfly is one of many forms readily available to the planted aquarium community. Favored for its dark green color and broad, textured leaves, this aquarium plant is a great introductory plant. Anubias have solid reputations in planted aquaria for being nearly indestructible. They're extremely hardy and will adapt to a range of conditions, making them suitable for low tech tanks, high tech planted aquariums, and even terrariums. An aquatic aroid, they are similar to Philodendron and Monstera plants. They're versatile with placement in aquascaping and will grow happily when attached to porous structures like rocks or natural driftwood. While it isn't required, providing CO2 and a quality plant fertilizer will noticeably boost form and growth speed. If you're looking for a beginner plant or need lush filler for your aquascape, consider Anubias plants!

Bucephalandra Titan is a lovely variation in the Bucephalandra family. At first look, Buce Titan is a small to medium sized specimen with ruffled leaves and varying color tones that mainly consist of olive green, bronze, and reddish hues. Like all Bucephalandra, Bucephalandra Titan produces exaggerated coloration when given proper care and placed under aquarium LED lighting. Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant and will sprout new growth from its rhizome. Bucephalandra does best in low to medium lighting and will grow nice and dense if favorable conditions are provided. CO2 injection along with a good flow and regular tank maintenance will promote quicker, more robust growth. The stem and rhizome should not be covered when planting as this will cause the plant to rot and wither. Care can be comparable to other popular aquatic plant species such as Anubias and Java Ferns, but Bucephalandra will not tolerate sudden changes well.

Aquatic plant decor offers an easy and convenient way to add live aquarium plants to your setup. These pieces feature live hardy plants that are readily attached to hardscape or recycled materials like ceramic, filter foam and more. This Buce Green Wavy comes pre-attached to a small piece of nano wood and ready to be added to planted tanks, terrariums, vivariums, and more! Green Wavy is a classic Bucephalandra known for its hardiness and adaptability to a range of water conditions. It is one of the more readily available varieties and is rarely harvested from the wild, making it a sustainable choice for aquascapers who like Bucephalandra. This versatile aquarium aroid can grow submerged or emerged, attaches easily to porous structures, and is great for adding instant greenery to sparse areas in aquascapes. While it is commonly associated with low-tech tanks, providing CO2, higher light, and balanced nutrition produces noticeable differences in its growth, color, and form.

Bucephalandra Godzilla is a lovely species of Bucephalandra! Easily recognized by beautiful ruffled leaves that vary in bold reddish-brown tones, Bucephalandra Godzilla later gains even deeper coloration as the aquatic plant matures. When provided with optimal conditions, Bucephalandra Godzilla produces dense bushes of Buce that will frequently flower, making for a beautiful addition to any planted aquarium tank. Like most Bucephalandra plants, Buce Godzilla is epiphytic and will grow happily attached to aquarium driftwood or stones in an aquascape layout. Low to medium lighting with partial shade is perfect for most Buce species and while this plant will tolerate other conditions associated with keeping a low-tech aquarium, we highly recommend providing Buce with CO2 injection and a quality source of nutrients to boost growth, help the plant outcompete algae and produce the iridescent hues Bucephalandra are known for. Overall, Bucephalandra Godzilla is a suitable plant for most beginner aquarists that have the basics of aquarium keeping down. Buce's stem and rhizome should not be covered or glued when planting as this can cause damage to the plant.

Anubias Nana Petite is one of the smallest Anubias varieties available in the planted tank hobby. With its thick, dark green leaves and compact growth, it's a great fit for tanks of all sizes—especially nano aquariums. Its hardiness is difficult to beat, making it a great aquatic plant for beginners. This listing includes a plant pre-attached to a small lava rock that can be conveniently be added to a new or existing aquascape! Anubias are flowering plants and grow best when attached to natural surfaces like driftwood or aquarium rocks. These plants will tolerate varying water conditions and don't require much to survive, but will benefit greatly if provided with a liquid plant fertilizer, CO2 injection and good maintenance habits. They're slow-growers, but eventually will produce side shoots that can be separated gently and replanted.

Anubias Nana Petite is arguably the most popular variation of Anubias used in the planted aquarium hobby. Easily recognized for its smaller foliage and rich green tones, Anubias Nana Petite is commonly used in planted aquariums of all styles. This variation of Anubias retains a bulletproof reputation in being an aquarium plant where effort is required to kill it. This quality makes it a fantastic choice for beginner aquarists who are building confidence with keeping live aquatic plants in the aquarium. At the same time, the overall appearance is equally loved by seasoned experts who have been keeping planted tanks for some time. Anubias Nana Petite requires seldom and is very easy to care for. This aquarium plant is typically available in plentiful portions making it a great filler where coverage is needed. Like most Anubias, Anubias Nana Petite will tolerate a wide range of aquarium conditions and also has the ability to thrive in both aquarium and terrarium-like enclosures. Anubias Nana Petite will sometimes produce blooms and is an epiphytic grower, meaning it can be easily attached to aquarium driftwood and stones. Low to medium light is sufficient, but the addition of CO2 injection and a nutrient source will produce a noticeable difference in growth and overall health. Propagation may be done by gently separating plants from the rhizome and reattaching or replanting.

Süsswassertang, commonly referred to as Subwassertang, is a timeless freshwater plant that is a little bit of an oddity! Scientifically, it is most closely related to Lomariopsis lineata, but could easily pass as an aquatic moss or liverwort. It is commonly compared to Monosolenium tenerum (Mini Pellia) but features darker green plant tissue that is slightly translucent. This hardy aquatic plant is very moss-like. It is easy to care for, great for low-tech tanks, low-light setups, and is particularly popular in breeding and shrimp tanks. Its growth form provides the perfect environment for tiny critters and also serves as a natural source of filtration. It grows in a similar fashion to moss and is typically left to settle on its own, but it can also be attached to driftwood or porous surfaces. In planted tanks with strong lighting, CO2, and fertilizer dosing, its growth will increase accordingly. Overall, Subwassertang’s delicate form adds unique texture and is both an ornamental and functional addition to any freshwater planted aquarium. Approximate Dome Size: 3" in diameter x 2" tall

Its characteristic grooves and indentations are caused by years of natural erosion, giving it a leathery, wrinkled appearance. With occasional depressions and concave areas, Elephant Skin Stone has a natural, organic look that pairs well with bright green aquarium plants. Unlike Seiryu Stone and other popular planted tank hardscape choices, it lacks jagged or sharp edges and is instead more rounded, producing a softer aethestic. Its also a good aquarium stone for fragile-finned fish like Betta splendens, Ranchu and Oranda fancy goldfish. Anubias barteri var. nana, simply called Anubias Nana, is well-known in the planted tank hobby ofr being one o the hardiest aquarium plants. Like other Anubias, it tolerates a wide range of conditions and adapts well to nearly all environments. Anubias plants are our top recommendation for aquascapers looking for easy aquatic plants that don't require CO2 injection but are equally attractive as some of the more demanding species in the hobby. It has a solid reputation for being nearly impossible to kill, but will still benefit from good habits like routine tank maintenance, moderate lighting, CO2 injection and a liquid plant fertilizer. It is an epiphytic plant, so it doesn't need to be planted in aquasoil and can instead be attached to driftwood or tucked into open spaces within the aquascape. Be mindful not to bury the rhizome or use too much adhesive as this can cause permanent damage over time. When you're ready to propagate, separate the rhizome (we recommend sharp aquascaping tools) and reattach as desired!

This plant is almost indestructible in any planted aquarium tank and will survive in a range of environments. However, if presented with optimal conditions, this plant will thrive. It's best when used as a mid-ground plant attached to stones or wood as an accent or centerpiece depending on tank size. We recommend Anubias Nana Long Wavy for any size aquarium and for those looking for a much more unique rhizome aquatic plant. It's a flowering plant that grows best when the rhizome is attached to hardscape material such as wood or stone. Regular fertilization is favorable and low to medium lighting is sufficient as high lighting will promote the growth of algae on its leaves. CO2 is not required but promotes faster growth and robust leaves. Propagation is straightforward; simply cut or pull apart rhizomes to be reattached.

Microsorum Pteropus AKA Java Fern Narrow Leaf is the skinnier cousin of the very common Java Fern. Its sharp and narrow leaves grow out to be only half an inch wide at most. This easy-to-grow beginner plant comes pre-attached to an aquarium-safe fibrous mat and can be used to fill the midground to background of most planted aquariums. Recently reclassified as Leptochilus pteropus, this plant is still widely known in the hobby as Microsorum pteropus. It can grow great in low light conditions and is forgiving in a wide range of water parameters. The plant can be attached directly onto driftwood, rocks or any aquarium decoration using thread or glue. Make sure to keep the rhizomes above your substrate or the plant can begin to rot. Propagation is easy and straightforward; simply cut or pull apart rhizomes to be replanted/reattached.

listings.commonName: Plant Pile - Assorted Aquarium Plant Bundle
listings.description: Have you ever ordered aquatic plants that end up being too big for your aquarium? Or, are you looking to fully plant your aquascape, but aren’t sure what to get? With so many species and variable information available, it can be difficult to choose the right aquarium plants for your setup. Our Plant Pile bundle contains an assortment of foreground, midground and background plants. You’ll receive live plants for each area of a planted tank that have been curated by our team to fit different aquarium sizes. Learn more about what each Plant Pile bundle contains below! Why should I have a fully planted aquarium? Fully planted aquariums provide many great benefits to the overall health of fish tanks. Live aquatic plants provide safe spaces for sensitive or shy tropical fish and shrimp. They also act as natural filtration, absorbing excess elements and nutrients in the water that can be harmful in elevated levels. Aquarium plants also provide oxygen for livestock and beneficial bacteria to thrive. Plant Pile Bundles Size Tank Volume Plants Included Tank Recommendations NANO 2 - 5G [1] foreground [2] midground [2] background Ultum Nature Systems 20C Ultum Nature Systems 3N Ultum Nature Systems 25C Ultum Nature Systems 3N MED 10 - 20G [3] foreground [3] midground [4] background Ultum Nature Systems 90B Ultum Nature Systems 30C Ultum Nature Systems 45U Ultum Nature Systems 40C LRG 20 - 30G [5] foreground [5] midground [5] background Ultum Nature Systems 60U Ultum Nature Systems 90L A Brief Overview of Aquascaping Zones Foreground Plants These aquatic plants are positioned front and center in most aquascapes. They are usually short in height and grow low in a horizontal manner for ground coverage. The term foreground plant is basically synonymous with carpeting aquarium plant and includes species like Monte Carlo, Hemianthus callitrichoides ‘Cuba’ (HC), Utricularia graminifolia (UG) and Eleocharis varieties (dwarf hairgrass). In-between plants, like Cryptocoryne parva or Marsilea hirsuta, are great choices for transitioning into the midground. Midground Plants The midground section of a planted aquarium is broad and varied, featuring plants of moderate height. Popular choices include shorter stem plants and clump-forming or rosette plants like Cryptocoryne species. It also includes plants attached to hardscape, such as Anubias, Bucephalandra, Java Fern, and various aquatic mosses. Compact stem plants like Hemianthus micranthemoides (pearl weed) and Staurogyne repens are also common choices. Although categorized as stem plants, they do not grow as tall or fast as other stems often planted in the background. Background Plants These are the tallest and largest plants in an aquascape, typically planted along the back panel and corners of rimless tanks. They create the lush backdrop for your aquarium. Species like Cyperus helferi, Vallisneria sp. (Jungle Vals), Rotala, and Ludwigia grow long, producing flowing foliage that fills the background and moves gently with the water flow.

CO2 Pressure Proof Tubing is one of the most overlooked yet essential part of getting the most out of your CO2 system. Pressure proof tubing does not allow penetration of CO2 gas and is the most efficient method of CO2 delivery for aquarium plants to absorb in a planted aquarium tank. Ardisia Black Type 2 is a variation of Ardisia Black. This rare vivarium plant has limited information available regarding its origin and care, but first impressions offer a tropical feel and rich color tones to any setup. The plant has elliptical leaves varying in deep olive, green and reddish-bronze hues. Texture is fleshy and rubbery, emitting a leathery shine when placed under LED lighting. If Ardisia Black Type 2 is similar to its counterparts, this plant will appreciate higher humidity levels and a consistently moist, not soggy, growing medium. Basic starter guidelines include, but aren't limited to, higher humidity levels and planting in high-quality sphagnum moss or a mixture of bark and perlite. These growing mediums naturally do not contain any nutritional benefits, so it is essential to ensure this plant is given nutrients periodically. Stunted or deformed growth may signal nutritional deficiencies or the presence of pests. Browning edges may signal insufficient humidity levels. This plant will ship as a cutting that may or may not be lightly rooted Ardisia Black Type 2 is NOT an aquarium plant. Submerging this plant in an aquarium will kill it! Cryptocoryne Nevillii is a compact Crypt featuring short, ovate leaves in green tones that can develop subtle brown undertones depending on growing conditions. Similar in size and appearance to other smaller Cryptocoryne, Nevillii grows slightly larger and faster than Cryptocoryne Parva while maintaining a low, compact growth habit. Its manageable size makes Cryptocoryne Nevillii easy to incorporate throughout the foreground and lower midground of planted aquariums. Plant individual rosettes between hardscape or group several together, allowing new growth to gradually create fuller coverage. Like other Cryptocoryne, allow Nevillii plenty of time to establish a healthy root system after planting and avoid unnecessary moving or disturbance while it settles in. New plantlets can eventually develop around established growth and may be separated and replanted for propagation.

Bucephalandra Red Blade is a medium-sized buce variety. At first glance, you'll notice this aquatic plant has attractive foliage! Its ruffled, oblong leaves include shades of green and reddish hues with a prominent central vein. When added to a planted aquarium, its colors and texture shimmer under tank lights. Like other species from this family, Buce Red Blade pushes out new growth via its rhizome. It is an aquarium epiphyte and will attach to natural materials like driftwood and porous stones (lava rock is great for this!). To get the best from your Buce, provide it with CO2 injection, nutrients and a spot that receives healthy flow. With hardy nature and easy care, it's easy to understand why Bucephalandra is one of the best aquatic plants for beginners. These plants are available in a wide range of color, size and texture to fit any aquascape with care comparable to Anubias!

Bucephalandra Arrogant Blue is a small to medium-sized variation in the Bucephalandra family. At first glance, Buce Arrogant Blue features a pronounced center vein and highly attractive iridescent speckled foliage. In some cases, newer leaves will produce unique dark green and hints of bright blue hues. Like all Bucephalandra, Bucephalandra Arrogant Blue will display unique coloration when given proper care and placed under aquarium LED lighting. This is the perfect Bucephalandra for any nano planted aquarium tank or for additional smaller plant details in larger aquariums. Bucephalandra is an epiphytic plant and will sprout new growth from its rhizome. Bucephalandra does best in low to medium lighting and will grow nice and dense if favorable conditions are provided. CO2 injection along with a good flow and regular tank maintenance will promote quicker, more robust growth. The stem and rhizome should not be covered when planting as this will cause the plant to rot and wither. Care can be comparable to other popular aquatic plant species such as Anubias and Java Ferns, but Bucephalandra will not tolerate sudden changes well.

Sporting color similarities to Malaysian Driftwood and surface structure to Dragon Stone (Ohko Stone), Dragon Wood has a distinct appearance that blends characteristics of classic aquarium hardscape picks. These features make Dragon Wood especially useful for aquascapers who enjoy including Bucephalandra, Anubias, Java Fern, and aquatic mosses in an aquascape. Rhizome plants can often be tucked directly into the wood's openings, reducing the need for glue, thread, or other attachment methods while creating more naturally planted results. Malaysian Driftwood is a classic hardscape material choice in the planted tank hobby. Well recognized for its rich coloration and lovely character, Malaysian Driftwood is a staple and is commonly chosen for bold nature aquarium style aquascape layouts. Its forest-like bark looks extremely natural and provides a realistic environment for tropical aquarium fish or shrimp species. Malaysian Driftwood pairs well with almost any aquatic plant choice and its dark coloration provides a lovely contrast allowing aquatic plants to pop in a planted aquarium tank. Naturally, on the larger side, we recommend Malaysian Driftwood Accent Stumps for nano and large sized aquarium tanks. Aquarium mosses such as Java, Christmas, Weeping or Flame Moss can be easily attached to these pieces for an added natural flare. All pieces are unique in shape and texture which also makes it a perfect choice for adding additional accents to an existing aquarium that utilizes larger Malaysian Driftwood hardscape. This specific type of aquarium driftwood is also quite prone to leaching tannins. Tannins within the water column produce the classic "tea" colored water commonly seen in black water setups and biotopes. This type of environment is thought to be favored by many species of tropical aquarium fish but can be an acquired taste for the modern fishkeeper. Tannic acid is not harmful to livestock but it will lower pH levels slightly. Alternatively, consistent water changes can be done and the effect of tannins will subside on its own naturally with time. Measurement Range: Provided measurements are rough estimates. Cryptocoryne axelrodi is an easy aquatic plant with narrow, pointed leaves that are a rich green to brown color. It is quite hardy and readily adapts to most water conditions, with its growth adjusting based on parameters. Like most Cryptocoryne, it is ideal for the midground zone in planted aquariums and can be used to break up groups of stem plants or create a subtle transition between various species. We recommend planting Cryptocoryne in tanks that are fully cycled to reduce shock or introductory melt. Once it roots in soil, it is low-maintenance and will slowly spread through the tank. At this point, baby plantlets can be gently divided and replanted as desired. Most Cryptocoryne are suitable for low-light planted aquariums, but stronger lighting, CO2 and routine fertilization will encourage faster growth and better color.

Overview: Seachem Flourish Excel provides a liquid source of organic carbon for aquatic plants. It is a great liquid additive for any planted aquarium especially when CO2 injection is not available. Flourish Excel is a source of bioavailable organic carbon. All plants require a source of carbon. This is typically obtained from CO2, but, may also be derived from simple organic compounds (such as photosynthetic intermediates). The use of either CO2 injection or Flourish Excel™ does not necessarily negate the use of the other. Because the processes of producing photosynthetic intermediates and building onto them occur simultaneously, one can derive a substantial benefit with the use of Flourish Excel™ either alone or in conjunction with CO2. The combination is particularly ideal for situations when continuing to add CO2 could result in dangerously low pH levels. Flourish Excel™ also has iron reducing properties which promote the ferrous state of iron (Fe +2 ), which is more easily utilized by plants than ferric iron (Fe +3 ). The reason plants need CO2 is to produce longer chain carbon compounds also known as photosynthetic intermediates. Photosynthetic intermediates includes compounds such as ribulose 1,5-bisphosphate, and 2-carboxy-3-keto-D-arabinitol 1,5 bisphosphate. Although the names are complicated, the structures are quite simple (5 carbon chains). Flourish Excel™ does not contain these specific compounds per se, but one that is quite similar. By dosing with Flourish Excel you bypass the involvement of CO2 and introduce the already finished, structurally similar compounds. It is in its structural similarity that Flourish Excel™ is able to be utilized in the carbon chain building process of photosynthesis. Simple chemical or enzymatic steps can easily convert it to any one to any one of the above named compounds (or a variety of others). Bottle size: 8.5 oz

Cloudy, discolored water is caused by overfeeding, biological blooms, gravel dust and other suspended particles that are too fine to be removed by mechanical filtration and stay in the water column. Fritz Clarifier rapidly clears water by pulling together (flocculating) fine particles, allowing them to be removed by the filter or settle to the bottom, leaving your aquarium crystal clear. Fritz Clarifier will not affect bio-filtration, pH or other important water parameters like other brands. Safe and effective for use in freshwater, saltwater, reef aquariums and ponds. 100% phosphate free; safe for all fish, plants and invertebrates; will not contribute to future cloudy water problems. Phosphate Free Does not impact biological filtration Will not alter pH Safe for reef, marine and planted aquarium tanks Size: 16 oz. Notes: Treats up to 960 gallons. Bottle cap measures 5mL volume. Instructions for use are outlined on the bottle. Shelf life: 3 Years.

Bucephalandra Apple Leaf, is a small species of Bucephalandra that produces small, rounded leaves that are primarily green in color. Newer leaves are lighter in color and mature into darker tones as the plant ages. When you take a closer look, Buce Apple Leaf has a slightly speckled appearance that surely pops when placed under quality aquarium LED lighting fixtures. Like other Bucephalandra, Buce Apple Leaf is epiphytic and grows best when attached to surfaces such as aquarium driftwood or aquascaping stones. We recommend low to medium lighting for this little Buce species along with good flow, quality aquarium plant nutrition and a well-maintained tank environment. CO2 injection isn't necessary for most Buce species, but it will surely help bring out the best colors that are commonly sought after when growing Bucephalandra. The stem and rhizome should not be covered when planting as this will cause the plant to rot and wither. Care can be comparable to other popular aquatic plant species such as Anubias and Java Ferns, but Bucephalandra will not tolerate sudden changes well.

We recommend this mat for aquarists who are interested in creating green walls or moss carpets in the aquarium, terrarium, vivarium or paludarium. As long as sufficient humidity and access to water is readily available, this piece of aquarium decor is versatile and can be repurposed for a wide variety of planted crafts. Aquarium plant decor offers a quick and easy way to add live plants to a new planted aquarium or an existing setup. They also make great gifts for the beginner hobbyist! Anubias can also grow marginally and will thrive above water in vivarium, terrarium, and paludarium setups as long as sufficient humidity is provided to prevent the plant from drying out. Bucephalandra Velvet 3 Color is a beautiful variation of Bucephalandra. This species ranges from a small to medium size and offers varying color tones and slender, ruffled foliage. Like most Bucephalandra, Buce Velvet 3 Color can be grown in aquarium settings as well as hybrid planted setups such as paludariums, vivariums, terrariums and more as long as sufficient humidity and transitional care is provided. When grown in the aquarium, we recommend CO2 injection, good flow and a quality source of nutrition to promote healthy growth and produce the iridescent qualities Buce is known and loved for in the aquarium hobby. Buce Velvet 3 Color is an epiphytic plant and like most aroids, sprouts new leaves along its rhizome. Propagation can be done by separating the plant along the rhizome. We recommend placing Buce within the cracks of a hardscape layout or attaching the plant to porous surfaces such as aquarium driftwood. Overall, Buce is generally perceived as beginner-friendly as it is fairly hardy and will adapt to most conditions.
