Add interesting texture to your planted aquarium with Potamogeton Crispus, commonly known as Curly-Leaf Pondweed. This aquatic stem plant features translucent, dark green leaves with distinctive wavy edges, creating a slightly ruffled appearance reminiscent of Bolbitis foliage. Its adaptability to lower lighting, cooler temperatures, and even slightly brackish water makes it a versatile option for a range of aquarium setups. Potamogeton Crispus can grow rapidly, developing tall stems and dense foliage that provide excellent background coverage. In higher-light aquariums with supplemental CO2, regular trimming is necessary to manage its growth and prevent it from crowing out surrounding plants. Please Dispose Responsibly: Potamogeton Crispus is considered invasive in many parts of the United States and may be restricted or prohibited in certain states. Never release this plant, its trimmings, or aquarium water containing plant fragments into natural waterways, ponds, or storm drains. Always collect unwanted plant material, including small fragments and reproductive buds, and dispose of it securely in household trash. Do not compost or discard it outdoors. Responsible aquarium keeping helps protect native aquatic ecosystems.

Cabomba piauhyensis, also known as Cabomba furcata, is an aquatic stem plant native to the Americas. This aquarium plant features lush, delicate foliage in shades of green, brownish-red, and wine red. Its fine, fan-shaped leaves add beautiful texture to planted tanks and provide cover for smaller tropical fish and invertebrates. When grown in a pond, Cabomba is also, arguably, one of the best aquatic plants for enjoying a lovely top-down view. It grows extremely fast and quickly absorbs available nutrients, providing natural filtration in aquariums or ponds and effectively reducing chances of algae appearing. Most Cabomba species are relatively easy to care for, but this variety is more demanding and requires stable conditions. Provide strong lighting, CO2 injection, and a full supply of macro- and micronutrients—whether through quality aquasoil, root tabs, liquid fertilizers, or a combination of these. Its form and coloration are also improved when grown in softer water.

Vesicularia Montagnei, more commonly known as Christmas Moss or X-mas Moss is arguably one of the most popular aquatic mosses commonly used in the planted aquarium hobby. Originating from Asia, Christmas Moss is closely related to Java Moss, another extremely popular aquatic moss, and is comparable in appearance with only slight differences in its fronds. Once established, Christmas Moss is a prolific grower and may require regular pruning to ensure it does not take over the aquarium. Manual removal is best, but if trimming is required, we recommend turning off filters and pumps to prevent the moss spreading to unwanted areas. Add luminous color and distinctive foliage to your planted aquarium with Echinodorus Iguazu. This iconic sword plant develops thick, oval-shaped deep green leaves traced with vibrant green veining. The combination packs a punch, giving the foliage an almost glowing appearance that makes Iguazu stand out easily in a planted aquarium. Unlike many larger Echinodorus, Iguazu stays more compact and grows very slowly. Its more manageable size makes it an excellent focal plant in Wabi Kusa-inspired setups or minimalist ponds. A long-time favorite in the aquarium hobby!

Rotala colorata is a vibrant variation of Rotala rotundifolia known for its range of orange, pink, and red hues, making it an ideal choice for adding color and contrast to planted aquariums. Similar in growth to other Rotala species, it develops fine, delicate leaves along upright stems, but with noticeably more intense and varied coloration. As it matures, Rotala colorata can be shaped through regular trimming to create dense, bushy groups in the midground to background. Its soft texture contrasts beautifully against broader-leaf plants and hardscape, adding balance and movement to the overall layout. One of its most appealing traits is its ability to develop warm coloration even under moderate lighting conditions, though stronger lighting, CO2 injection, and a complete nutrient supply will significantly improve its vibrancy. Under optimal conditions, it produces richer reds and more compact growth, especially in softer water. With consistent trimming and replanting, Rotala colorata can be maintained as a lush, colorful focal point or used in groups to create gradients and transitions within a planted aquascape.

Flat Bottom Seiryu Stones are hand-crafted with a flat bottom to produce instant aquascapes in the aquarium. These stones may be mixed and matched to create larger scapes in various tank sizes! Alternatively, placing them in smaller tank sizes also allow the tops of the stones to stick out above the surface allowing for emersed aquatic or terrestrial plant growth. Seiryu Stone is one of the most popular aquarium hardscape stones used for aquascaping. Known for its classic grey tones and natural textures, Seiryu Stone brings aggressive grooves, and jagged grooves to a planted aquarium tank and comes in a wide range of sizes and shapes. Application is very versatile and Seiryu can be commonly seen in both Iwagumi planted tanks as well as at the base of aquarium driftwood in Nature Style planted tanks. Seiryu Stone is a classic stone and we imagine it will remain a top choice for aquascapers! Measurement Range: Provided measurements are rough estimates. Flat Bottom Dragon Ohko Stones are hand-crafted with a flat bottom to produce instant aquascapes in the aquarium. These stones may be mixed and matched to create larger scapes in various tank sizes! Alternatively, placing them in smaller tank sizes also allow the tops of the stones to stick out above the surface allowing for emersed aquatic or terrestrial plant growth. Ohko Stone, also commonly known as Dragon Stone, is an extremely popular aquarium rock in the planted tank hobby. It's easy to spot thanks to its unique texture resembling dragon scales and rich color that contrasts well with bright green aquatic plants. It is a lightweight stone that gets you more stone per LB. Its numerous nooks and small craters are great for anchoring aquatic plants and moss species while also providing a safe haven for sensitive or skittish fish and shrimp. Dragon Stone's natural shape is typically favorable amongst aquascapers but can be easily broken down into smaller pieces to suit a wide range of aquarium tanks and applications. Vesicularia sp. 'Anchor Moss', often just called Anchor Moss, is a beautiful aquatic moss for planted tanks and aquascaping. It looks similar to Christmas Moss but grows more compact, which makes it great for creating tree or forest-inspired scapes, moss walls, or adding detail to wood and stones. When conditions are right, its color is a vibrant evergreen hue. Like most live mosses, you might see a bit of browning after shipping or when it’s adjusting to a new tank, but stable lighting and water conditions help it bounce back. Anchor Moss is a slow-growing variety, but it fills in dense over time. If you’re looking for a moss that adds natural texture, coverage, and color without demanding much, Anchor Moss is an easy one to enjoy.

Echinodorus Amazonicus is a popular Amazon Sword in the planted aquarium hobby, but doesn't seem to be as readily available as its popular relative, Echinodorus Bleheri. Like its name implies, Echinodorus Amazonicus is on the larger spectrum of sword sizes and is an ideal aquarium plant for the background area of the tank. When grown in optimal conditions, Echinodorus species can grow upwards of 2FT in height. Coloration is a bright green tone and leaves are quite sturdy, making them an all around solid plant choice for many styles of aquarium keeping. Like all aquatic sword species, Echinodorus Amazonicus is easy to keep, fairly hardy and needs a minimum of a nutrient-rich aquarium substrate as these species of aquatic plant are heavy root feeders. Aside from this, Echinodorus species are fairly tolerable of varying water parameters and lighting conditions. Lysimachia Nummularia, more commonly known as Creeping Jenny or Moneywort, is a beautiful marginal plant that can be grown in both aquarium settings or emersed in vivariums, terrariums, ponds and more. Creeping Jenny is characterized by its rounded leaves and low growing pattern, making it a great choice for those looking for good ground coverage in a planted setup. In aquarium settings, this plant tends to trail, producing an interesting look in the mid or background of the aquarium. It should be noted that this plant is a prolific grower and can be considered invasive in some areas, so periodic maintenance should be expected to keep its growth under control if a certain look is desired. Echinodorus Fancy Twist is an attractive variation of aquatic sword plant that is undemanding in care and grows moderately. When kept in submerged conditions, Echinodorus Fancy Twist offers bright color ranging from bright green to deep red tones with new leaves displaying a spotted pattern before maturing. When emersed, this aquatic plant is fully green with relatively tough foliage. Like other sword plants, Echinodorus Fancy Twist requires minimal care, but needs a nutrient-rich substrate and moderate lighting. Other than this, the plant will readily adapt to a wide range of parameters and is tolerant of neglect to an extent. Even so, providing the right conditions will allow this cultivar to shine in the aquarium. We recommend stable temperatures, a good maintenance routine, CO2 injection and quality source of both macro and micro nutrients for aquatic plant growth. Due to the size of this plant, Echinodorus make great centerpiece additions to Wabi Kusa setups or as a single species display. Echinodorus Fancy Twist would also work well in the background of a planted aquarium due to its size and height.

Cryptocoryne Schulzei is a rare Cryptocoryne found growing along small bodies of water within a specific region of Malaysia. With limited information available regarding its growth pattern, final size, and ideal aquarium conditions, this species is best suited for experienced hobbyists who are already familiar with Cryptocoryne care and requirements. Based on available information, Cryptocoryne Schulzei may develop narrower foliage when grown fully submerged and broader leaves when grown in marginal or emersed conditions. Younger leaves can display an attractive mottled pattern, while overall coloration ranges from green to brown tones. Final size, leaf shape, and coloration may vary depending on growing conditions. Like other Cryptocoryne, allow Cryptocoryne Schulzei plenty of time to establish a healthy root system after planting. Avoid unnecessary moving or disturbance while it settles in, and allow the plant to become well established before attempting propagation.

Named after the largest lake on the island of Sulawesi, Ammania Towuti is a rare cultivar with very limited information available on the plant and its care. From first impression, Ammania Towuti displays a bright green tone and serrated foliage that sprouts from a thick stem. Due to the lack of information available, we recommend this aquarium plant for hobbyists who have experience with Ammania or aquarium stem plants in general.

Echinodorus Red Diamond is a cultivar of Echinodorus that hybridizes Echinodorus Horemanii Red and Echinodorus Barthii. This aquarium plant is very attractive and produces ruby-red foliage that offers bold contrast to the planted aquarium. Size wise, Echinodorus Red Diamond falls on the conservative side and can be considered a medium size when compared to other variations in the Echinodorus family. Because of this, Echinodorus Red Diamond works well as a centerpiece or solitary aquarium plant species. We also recommend it for Wabi Kusa display as it can be easily grown in emersed conditions as well. Like other Amazon Swords, Echinodorus Red Diamond is a heavy root feeder and requires nutrient-dense aquarium soil to grow well. Other than this, it is relatively hardy and will tolerate a wide range of aquarium conditions. Medium to high light is preferable and will increase the plant's production of bright, ruby-red leaves. Anubias Chili Mini is an extremely rare variation of Anubias in the planted aquarium hobby. This aquarium plant is characterized by its small, evergreen leaves shaped like little chili peppers, making it a great addition to any Anubias enthusiast's collection. This Anubias variation exhibits compact growth and works fantastically for mid-ground placement in nano planted aquariums. Like other Anubias plants, Anubias Chili Mini is relatively undemanding and will tolerate a wide range of aquarium conditions. This aquarium plant can be grown submerged or emersed in terrarium-like conditions as long as moisture and humidity are sufficient. It should be noted that Anubias are slow growers, so some patience will be required to grow full portions! We recommend attaching Anubias Chili Mini to your favorite driftwood or in between the gaps of an aquascape layout. Anubias Chili Mini is sure to be popular amongst aquarium hobbyists who enjoy miniature plants! We recommend providing this aquarium plant with a light fertilizing routine, clean water, low to medium lighting, and CO2 injection. Propagation is straightforward and can be done by simply cutting or pulling apart rhizomes to be reattached.

Anubias Chili Jalapeño is an Anubias that hybridizes Anubias Chili and Anubias Minima. This cultivar is still rare in the planted aquarium hobby and exhibits small leaves shaped like jalapeño peppers and a rich green tone, making it a great addition to any planted aquarium tank. This Anubias variation exhibits compact growth and works fantastically for mid-ground placement in nano planted aquariums. Like other Anubias plants, Anubias Chili Jalapeno requires little care and will tolerate a wide range of aquarium conditions. This aquarium plant can be grown submerged or emersed in terrarium-like conditions as long as moisture and humidity are sufficient. It should be noted that Anubias are slow growers, so some patience will be necessary. We recommend attaching Anubias Chili Jalapeno to your favorite driftwood or in between the gaps of an aquascape layout. Anubias Chili Jalapeño is sure to be popular amongst aquarium hobbyists who enjoy miniature plants! We recommend providing this aquarium plant with a light fertilizing routine, clean water, low to medium lighting, and CO2 injection. Propagation is straightforward and can be done by simply cutting or pulling apart rhizomes to be reattached.

Must-have tool for keeping hardscape clean! Compact size makes this algae brush easy to use in a wide variety of tank sizes The algae brush is an underrated tool in the aquarium hobbyist's tool arsenal! This algae brush features coarse, durable bristles that are effective in removing stubborn algae from aquarium driftwood and stones. While it can be used for all types of algae, the algae brush is especially effective in removing difficult types such as Black Beard Algae or Staghorn algae. Once removed, siphon it out and keep maintaining the tank to improve results. TIP: Clean and dry the algae brush completely in between uses to avoid cross contamination between multiple tanks. This will also increase product longevity!

Cryptocoryne Ferruginea Sekadauensis is a rare Cryptocoryne variety with limited information available in the aquarium hobby. This plant naturally grows along the margins of bodies of water and can be grown in both submerged and emersed conditions when sufficient moisture is available. Its foliage displays natural variation in shades of green and brown. Best suited for hobbyists with experience growing Cryptocoryne, this variety appreciates a stable, established aquarium with low to moderate lighting and consistent access to nutrients. CO2 injection can be provided to support growth but is not required for keeping Cryptocoryne in every planted aquarium setup. Allow Cryptocoryne Ferruginea Sekadauensis plenty of time to establish after planting and avoid unnecessary relocation or disturbance. New plantlets can develop around established growth and may be separated for propagation once they are mature enough to do so.

Microsorum pteropus ‘Coral’ features random leaf splits and is comparable to Java Fern Trident in appearance. Its color is primarily green, with new growth showing a lighter pink to orange hue. Like other variations, it is beginner friendly and tolerant of a wide range of aquarium conditions. Recently reclassified as Leptochilus pteropus , this plant is still widely known in the aquarium hobby as Microsorum pteropus. When placed in an established aquarium with stable parameters, CO2 injection, and a consistent nutrient source, this plant really thrives. This easy-to-grow aquarium plant is a great choice for filling midground to background areas, especially in nano or smaller planted aquariums. Like other Java Ferns, it is epiphytic and can be attached directly to driftwood, rocks, or aquarium decor using thread or glue. Make sure to keep the rhizome above the substrate to prevent rot. Propagation is simple—just cut or separate sections of the rhizome and reattach as needed.

Anubias Nana Long Wavy is characterized by its unique wavy or ruffled-shaped leaves. As a result, its natural texture makes this plant highly sought after. Similar to other Anubias, it's a great choice for beginners due to its easy care and overall hardiness. This plant is almost indestructible in any planted aquarium tank and will survive in a range of environments. However, if presented with optimal conditions, this plant will thrive. It's best when used as a mid-ground plant attached to stones or wood as an accent or centerpiece depending on tank size. We recommend Anubias Nana Long Wavy for any size aquarium and for those looking for a much more unique rhizome aquatic plant. It's a flowering plant that grows best when the rhizome is attached to hardscape material such as wood or stone. Regular fertilization is favorable and low to medium lighting is sufficient as high lighting will promote the growth of algae on its leaves. CO2 is not required but promotes faster growth and robust leaves. Propagation is straightforward; simply cut or pull apart rhizomes to be reattached.

listings.commonName: Anubias Barteri Petite Round Lava Stone
listings.description: Anubias Barteri Petite Round is one of the many forms available in the Anubias family. It is a relatively new variation that resembles a cross between Anubias Round Leaf and Nana Petite. Barteri Petite Round is a smaller specimen that sprouts rounded leaves, a trait uncommon to the more readily available species. Like other Anubias, Barteri Petite Round is a great beginner aquarium plant. This genus is highly adaptable and will tolerate a wide range of aquarium conditions and water parameters. Anubias are epiphytic aroids, making them versatile with placement as they can be attached to aquarium driftwood and stones. This particular listing comes with the plant conveniently attached to a small lava stone and can be placed into an aquarium immediately. Alternatively, Anubias plants are capable of marginal growth and will work in terrarium, vivarium or paludarium-like enclosures as long as sufficient humidity is provided to prevent the plant from drying out. Anubias are flowering species and will bloom from time to time. With many different forms, shapes, and sizes available, Anubias plants are a classic staple in the planted aquarium hobby! When placing Anubias Barteri Petite Round into an aquarium, we highly recommend providing CO2 injection when possible. While it isn't required, the plant will produce quicker and more robust growth!

Looking for an easy aquatic plant or live aquarium decor? This Anubias Nana plant is conveniently pre-attached to a small piece of natural driftwood, and is ready to place in your planted aquarium when you are! Anubias Barteri var. Nana or Anubias Nana, is a popular choice for planted tank hobbyists. It's extremely hardy and will adapt to most conditions, making it a wonderful choice for anyone looking for live aquarium plants for their tanks. Use it in terrariums, paludariums or low tech aquascapes.

Bacopa Lanigera, commonly known as Hairy Bacopa, is a larger variation of Bacopa originating from Brazil. Appearance wise, Bacopa Lanigera is similar to Bacopa Caroliniana, but can be distinguished by slightly rounder leaves along with small white hair-like fibers covering the stem. This aquarium plant also has noticeable venation that is typically lighter than its leaves producing natural contrast. Due to its larger size, this aquatic plant is more suitable for larger sized aquariums, but may work in smaller tanks as long as it is pruned accordingly. When possible, we always recommend providing aquarium plants with CO2 injection to improve health, boost growth rates and increase color vibrancy. Bacopa Lanigera provides unique texture and frequent trimming will allow the plant to branch off, creating denser plant groups. At a minimum, we recommend using a nutrient-dense aquarium soil to help the plant establish a strong root system. Bacopa Lanigera is versatile and can be grown in terrariums, vivariums and paludarium setups as long as proper care is provided. When care is optimal, Bacopa Lanigera blooms blue-violet flowers above the surface. To propagate, cut along the stem and replant into the substrate.

Bacopa Madagascariensis is a rarer variety of Bacopa that can be difficult to find in the planted aquarium hobby. This plant can be grown in both submerged and emersed conditions, with its appearance changing significantly between forms. When grown above water, Bacopa Madagascariensis displays fleshy leaves with serrated edges and a more irregular growth pattern. In the aquarium, the serrated edges become less apparent, and the plant develops a more upright growth pattern. This variety of Bacopa is considered a more advanced plant and benefits from stronger lighting along with a complete supply of macro and micronutrients. Bacopa Madagascariensis can tolerate moderately hard water but generally does best in softer, warmer water. Like other aquarium stem plants, regular trimming is important to ensure the lower portions receive adequate light. Under suitable conditions, Bacopa Madagascariensis develops highly decorative foliage that adds color and visual interest to planted aquariums. Its uniform growth also makes it a great addition to Dutch-style aquascapes.

Ceratopteris Cornuta is a classic aquatic fern that is popular in the planted tank hobby. This species of Water Sprite produces broader leaf lobes and is light green in coloration. It is commonly used as a floating plant in breeding tanks, but can also be planted into aquarium substrate and treated as a normal stem plant. Ceratopteris cornuta is a prolific grower and is a great source of natural filtration as the plant readily absorbs excess nutrients in the aquarium. Water Sprite is undemanding and will tolerate a wide variety of conditions making it a favorite amongst beginner hobbyists and breeders. As Water Sprite grows quickly, it has the potential to grow unruly if not maintained and pruned regularly. We recommend this aquarium plant for the midground and background aquatic plant choices in a planted tank. It is suitable for the larger spectrum of nano aquarium tanks to larger standard sizes. Propagation is simple and trimmed stems can be replanted into quality aquarium soil.

Echinodorus Argentinensis, commonly referred to as the Argentine Sword, is a classic aquatic plant originating from South America. This species is a true aquatic and works best for larger aquariums given its size. Alternatively, Echinodorus work well for Wabi Kusa and as single specimen displays. Similar to other Echinodorus species, Argentinensis is a hardy plant that adapts to a wide range of parameters making it suitable for beginner hobbyists. It should be noted that aquatic swords are heavy root feeders and require hearty substrates to establish strong root systems for healthy growth as a minimum. Coloration is a bright green tone and leaves are quite sturdy, making them an all around solid plant choice for many styles of aquarium keeping. Propagation is simple. Separate and replant. Echinodorus Cordifolius features bright green, heart-shaped leaves. Often called Radican Sword, it can be found growing in water, swamps and along muddy banks. Like other Amazon Sword plants, it can reach impressive sizes, making it an excellent pond plant or a centerpiece addition to large planted aquariums with enough space for growth. Swords are a hardy bunch! They're suitable for all skill levels and various types of setups, including low tech aquariums. Start with a good substrate, clean water and moderate lighting. Once established, you'll have plants to replant or share in no time. This Java Fern is conveniently pre-attached to a small piece of aquarium safe driftwood! Microsorum pteropus, commonly known as Java Fern, is a classic genus in the planted tank hobby that consists of many variations and species. Recently reclassified as Leptochilus pteropus , this plant is still widely known in the hobby as Microsorum pteropus. Java Ferns are well-known for being hardy and suitable for beginner hobbyists looking to keep live aquarium plants. Highly adaptable, Microsorum pteropus plants will tolerate a wide range of aquarium conditions and water parameters. This aquatic plant is also epiphytic and will grow well when attached to porous surfaces such as aquarium driftwood or stones. This quality makes Java Fern a top candidate for filling in open spaces in an aquascape where additional greenery is desired. Its leaves are a rich green tone and contrast well against darker scape material. Like most aquarium plant species, Java Fern can be grown in low tech aquariums, but the addition of CO2 injection will produce a noticeable difference in growth rate and overall appearance. Care should be taken to ensure the rhizome is not buried to prevent damage to the plant. Once established, Java Fern will readily produce new growth that can be propagated by gently pulling new plants off and reattaching as desired. Average Size: Small: 3-4" Medium: 5-6" Large: 7-8"

This Java Fern ‘Windelov’ is pre-attached to a piece of aquarium-safe driftwood, making it an easy, ready-to-use addition to any aquascape. Microsorum pteropus ‘Windelov’, commonly known as Java Fern Windelov, is a popular variation recognized for its split leaf tips and bushy appearance. Recently reclassified as Leptochilus pteropus , this plant is still widely known in the aquarium hobby as Microsorum pteropus. Like other Java Fern varieties, it is extremely hardy and great for beginners. As an epiphytic plant, Java Fern grows naturally on hard surfaces like driftwood and stone. This piece allows you to instantly add greenery and texture to your layout without the need for planting. Its rich green color and detailed leaf structure make it a great option for filling in open areas and softening hardscape. Java Fern Windelov grows well in low to medium lighting and does great in low tech setups. While CO2 and added nutrients will improve growth, it will continue to thrive with minimal care. Be sure to keep the rhizome above the substrate if repositioning is needed. Over time, it can be propagated by dividing the rhizome and reattaching as desired. Average Size: Small: 3-4" Medium: 5-6" Large: 7-8"

Shop mixed bucephalandra pre-attached to aquarium safe bonsai driftwood. Bucephalandra is a popular genus of plants in the aquarium hobby. Bucephalandra come in a wide variety of sizes and colors, and are well-known for being fairly adaptable in aquarium settings. Bucephalandra are epiphytic aroids and grow well when attached to aquarium hardscape. They may also be grown on substrate as long as the rhizome is not buried. As mentioned, Bucephalandra are very adaptable and will tolerate a wide range of lighting spectrums and aquarium conditions. This particular listing offers a hand-crafted Bonsai Tree with a mixture of small-leafed buce readily attached. Bucephalandra are flexible and easy to care for. While it isn't required, we recommend providing Bucephalandra with CO2 injection to improve health and really bring out the iridescent colors Buce are known for. If kept in a tank without CO2, good maintenance habits will go a long way in preventing algae growth on leaves. Cooler water is preferable along with good flow as well. When ready for propagation, this plant's rhizome can be split and reattached elsewhere. Sizing Specifications (LxWxH): Please note, sizes provided are averages and may vary. Alternanthera Tricolor is a beautiful aquarium stem plant that provides beautiful pops of color to a planted tank. Primarily green in color with pink leaf edges, this stem plant may develop varying shades of pink, red and yellow. It is naturally lush, making it a great choice if your aquascape needs full plants. Most Alternanthera plants are suitable for midground and background placement where they have plent of space to spread out. Colors can vary and are highly dependent on aquarium conditions. To start, provide CO2 injection, quality aquarium plant fertilizer, nutritious substrate and moderate lighting. Common Name Alternanthera Amabilis / Tricolor Care Moderate Lighting Moderate to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Midground Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate Height 4-12"+

Cuphea Anagalloidea was initially introduced to the planted aquarium hobby as a variation of Rotala. Unlike many familiar aquarium plants, it belongs to a genus consisting primarily of terrestrial species, with Cuphea Anagalloidea being among the first successfully cultivated in submerged aquarium conditions. This relatively small stem plant can be demanding when grown submerged, requiring stable aquarium conditions to maintain healthy growth. It can also be grown emersed, where its foliage is generally larger and predominantly green. Under favorable submerged conditions, Cuphea Anagalloidea develops distinctive, slightly mottled leaves with shades of green and red, making it an interesting addition to planted aquariums. Like other aquarium stem plants, Cuphea Anagalloidea can be propagated by trimming healthy stems and replanting the cuttings into the substrate.

Cryptocoryne Striolata is a rare species of Cryptocoryne. It can be characterized by its unique leaves that display a dimpled surface with colors ranging from deep green to purple hues. Like most Cryptocoryne species, C. Striolata does not prefer to be disturbed and should be allowed to establish a healthy root system before attempting to propagate or relocate the mother plant. It can be quite finicky and is recommended for aquarium hobbyists who have experience growing Cryptocoryne species. As a base, we recommend planting this species in a fully established tank with a mature biological system. On top of this, CO2 injection, low to moderate lighting and a complete supply of macro and micronutrients should be administered. A nutrient-dense substrate and good maintenance habits will improve chances of success as well.

Cryptocoryne Silver Queen is a rare species of Cryptocoryne. It can be characterized by its unique leaves that display unique striations and a subtle pink undertone. Like most Cryptocoryne species, C. Silver Queen does not prefer to be disturbed and should be allowed to establish a healthy root system before attempting to propagate or relocate the mother plant. It can be quite finicky and is recommended for aquarium hobbyists who have experience growing Cryptocoryne species. As a base, we recommend planting this species in a fully established tank with a mature biological system. On top of this, CO2 injection, low to moderate lighting and a complete supply of macro and micronutrients should be administered. A nutrient-dense substrate and good maintenance habits will improve chances of success as well.

Add texture and uncommon foliage to your planted aquarium with Cryptocoryne Keii. This rare Crypt develops compact leaves with a heavily dimpled, almost hammered surface, creating pronounced texture throughout the plant. Deep green to earthy brown and darker tones give established growth an understated, natural appearance. Cryptocoryne Keii is best suited for experienced planted aquarium hobbyists who can provide a stable environment and a little patience. Give it time to establish a healthy root system after planting and avoid unnecessary moving or disturbance once it begins settling into the aquascape. A nutrient-rich substrate, consistent fertilization, and good aquarium maintenance can support healthy growth. Its compact size and unusual foliage make Cryptocoryne Keii especially interesting tucked between hardscape or grouped in the foreground to midground where its texture can be appreciated up close.

listings.commonName: Aqua Worx Omni Aquatic Plant and Coral Glue
listings.description: Omni is an instant gel adhesive for your favorite aquarium plants and saltwater corals. Formulated to be safe for various styles of aquarium keeping, Omni can be used with your favorite aquatic plants as well as in marine settings for corals! It features a super strong hold that may also be used to make basic repairs to plastic structures or decor. The texture is gel-like and is as simple as applying a small amount to the desired area then letting it cure. Packaged in an aluminum tube, Omni goes a long way and may be stored for extended periods of time when properly cleaned following each use. A single tube is usually enough for any nano tank setup as a little goes a long way. It adheres within seconds and has excellent control, hold, and durability. It can be used for aquascaping in freshwater or saltwater aquariums with coral frags. As with all aquarium-safe adhesives, we recommend allowing the glue to cure fully before submerging in water. Best used for attaching aquatic moss, Anubias, Bucephalandra, and Ferns. Be sure to check out this category of aquarium plants that are suitable for planting with this glue here. Size: 5 grams per tube

Black River Slate is a type of hardscape that isn't too commonly seen in the planted aquarium hobby. These flat stones are perfect for stacking cave structures or creating paths in the planted aquarium. Color tones are dark grey, almost black when submerged and provide lovely contrast against vividly colored aquarium plants. These stones are also easy to break apart for multi-use purposes and very ideal for wrapping your favorite aquatic mosses around them such as Riccia, Mini Pellia, Fissidens Fontanus, Christmas Moss and more. Alternatively, Black River Slate can also be used as a base hardscape for scapes that utilize intricate driftwood work.

Grey River Slate is an aquarium-safe hardscape that calls for creative application. Given a flat profile, these stones are great for aquascape layouts that require stacking or building. They can be glued together using aquarium-safe adhesives or placed atop as long as stability is double checked. Alternatively, Grey River Slate can also be used to increase stability beneath a layout that utilizes aquarium driftwood! These stones are super versatile and can also be broken apart to create paths or accents in the foreground. We recommend wrapping these stones with aquatic mosses such as Riccia, Pellia, Fissidens and more.

Black Slate is a solid stone that can be used for a variety of aquascaping layouts, creative plant projects and more. This stone features deep black and grey hues with small bits of white striation throughout. Because of Black Slate's flat profile, this multi-purpose project stone is suitable for stacking and layering to create taller structures, caves and more in an aquarium setting. While sturdy, these stones are relatively easy to break apart and can also be used to create paths or accents in the foreground. They also provide the perfect surface for creating moss-covered accent stones. Simply wrap your favorite aquarium mosses around it and place it in the desired location!

Lagoon Stone is a natural aquarium hardscape that offers features that can be found in both Wolf Stone and Icelandic Lava Stone. This aquarium rock is porous and offers an ideal base for attaching aquarium mosses or epiphytic aquatic plants such as Anubias or Bucephalandra. Coloration varies and includes shades of grey, white and black, easily making it a focal point in any aquarium. Given Lagoon Stone's irregular shapes, it can be easily stacked to create larger structures as well making it versatile layout material. Its darker tones are sure to pop against vividly colored aquarium plants and livestock! It should be noted that Lagoon Stone is relatively rough in texture, so it should be used with caution in aquariums that contain livestock with sensitive fins such as Betta Fish.

Its naturally open composition pairs beautifully with carpeting plants and low-growing species while capturing the texture and character of natural Seiryu stone. Made from lightweight, aquarium-safe resin, it offers a simple way to build a balanced, Iwagumi-inspired planted aquarium without the challenge of selecting and arranging individual stones. Strata Type 2 is safe for freshwater fish, shrimp, and aquatic plants, making it an excellent choice for beginners starting their first aquascape or anyone looking to enjoy the clean, minimalist beauty of Iwagumi with less time spent arranging hardscape and more time selecting plants and enjoying the finished layout. Its weathered appearance and horizontal striations create a distinctive look, making it an excellent choice for aquascapes inspired by cliffs, ridges, and gently eroded landscapes. Its semi-smooth surface and easy-to-stack shapes make it simple to arrange balanced hardscape layouts. Whether used as the foundation for a unique Iwagumi or paired with driftwood to create a beachside clearing, Sand Stone brings warmth and subtle character to layouts without overwhelming the surrounding aquatic plants. Best For - Layered cliff or clearing-inspired layouts - Warm, natural color palettes - Freshwater planted aquariums, terrariums, and paludariums Natural Variation Sand Stone is a natural material, so every piece will vary in shape, size, color, and layered texture. Create shelter, planted pockets, and unexpected details within your aquascape with Black Lava Rock Caves! Made from porous Black Lava Rock, each piece features one or more openings that can be positioned as caves for aquarium livestock or incorporated directly into your planting design. Turn an opening upward and treat it as a small planted pocket by adding aquasoil and aquatic plants for a Wabi-Kusa-inspired look. Lava Rock’s textured surface provides natural grip, making it a great option for stacking and building formations with planted pockets layered in at different heights throughout the scape. Use mosses and rhizome plants like Anubias or Bucephalandra to fill larger gaps and create a continuous, grown-in look. Alternatively, keep the openings exposed to create shelter and swim-through areas for small aquarium livestock. Boiling aquarium driftwood will speed up waterlogging and the release of tannins! Click here to shop all hardscape! Thorn Wood is a very unique aquascaping driftwood. It is the perfect aquarium hardscape for aquascapers who are looking to create a forest style planted aquarium. The “thornes”, when viewed underwater, can simulate straight horizontal branches which can provide a ton of depth in any planted aquarium aquascape. Thorne Wood is safe for aquarium, terrarium and paludarium use. When used in an aquarium, we recommend rinsing it off before use and weighing it down until waterlogged. Aquarium mosses can be attached to these pieces in order to provide a fully green underwater forest aquascape. This specific type of aquarium driftwood is also quite prone to leaching tannins. Tannins within the water column produce the classic "tea" colored water commonly seen in black water setups and biotopes. This type of environment is thought to be favored by many species of tropical aquarium fish but can be an acquired taste for the modern fishkeeper. Tannic acid is not harmful to livestock but it will lower pH levels slightly. Alternatively, consistent water changes can be done and the effect of tannins will subside on its own naturally with time. Like all aquarium driftwood, Thorn Driftwood is buoyant and we highly encourage allowing it to soak thoroughly or boiling the pieces to ensure they are fully waterlogged before designing and filling a planted aquarium tank. Measurements: Averages 18-25" TIP: Tannins leeched from wood will provide a natural tint to water, but will gradually dissipate based on the frequency of water changes

The natural texture is highly compatible with aquatic mosses and rhizome plants, offering so much room for creative expression. Whether used as a standalone piece for specimen display or combined with additional hardscape materials, Log Wood can be arranged to recreate fallen trees, forest floors, and natural woodland scenes within an aquarium, terrarium, or similar setup. Bucephalandra Mini Coin is a popular, relatively rare variation of Bucephalandra. At first glance, Buce Mini Coin offers tiny foliage that doesn't grow larger than 0.5 inches. Like other species of Bucephalandra, Mini Coin is capable of producing a myriad of hues that are dependent on aquarium conditions. Given its small blueprint, Bucephalandra Mini Coin is highly suitable for nano planted aquariums or any layout that demands small details. It is a very ornamental aquatic plant and is relatively hardy, making it a loved favorite amongst Bucephalandra collectors and enthusiasts. Bucephalandra Mini Coin is an epiphyte and can be grown in the cracks or crevices of your aquarium hardscape and while uncommon, it has been grown as a carpet as well. Time and patience are essential when growing Bucephalandra Mini Coin as this genus is known for being slow growing! Bucephalandra does best in low to medium lighting and will grow nice and dense if favorable conditions are provided. CO2 injection along with good flow and regular tank maintenance will promote quicker, more robust growth. The stem and rhizome should not be covered when planting as this will cause the plant to rot and wither. Care is comparable to other popular aquatic plant species such as Anubias and Java Ferns, but it should be noted that Bucephalandra will not tolerate sudden changes well.

Add rare, distinctive foliage to your planted aquarium with Fenestratarum Culum. Native to Borneo, this unusual rhizome plant develops long, narrow green leaves with a pronounced central midrib, creating a textured appearance that works especially well in jungle and forest-inspired aquascapes. Fenestratarum Culum grows from a creeping rhizome and can be attached to driftwood or stone rather than buried beneath the substrate. Its compact, slow-growing habit makes it easy to work between hardscape, where established growth can gradually form small groups of slender foliage. Overall, a unique choice for rare plant collectors and aquascapers who already enjoy Bucephalandra, Aridarum, and other uncommon rheophytic or rhizome plants.

Macodes Petola, more commonly known as the Jewel Orchid, is a very attractive plant that is well-suited for terrariums and other enclosed planted setups. This unique plant features bright golden venation that resembles lightning running across the surface of its leaves. It is one of the few species that is prized for its foliage in comparison to its flowers. This terrarium plant prefers warmer temperatures and increased humidity levels and providing it with optimal conditions will result in better growth and overall health. Macodes Petola is native to the tropics of Southeast Asia and typically grows quite compact. This makes it a top contender for smaller terrarium setups like the Natura Bioasis M, Aqua Worx Iota or a desktop nano or cube aquarium! When caring for this plant, growing medium should be kept moist but not wet as this may lead to root rot and damage to the plant. We recommend this beauty for anyone interested in starting a terrarium or looking for more plants to add to an existing setup. The Jewel Orchid is fairly forgiving and is tolerant of most standard household conditions. Macodes Petola is NOT an aquarium plant. Submerging this plant in an aquarium will kill it! Alternanthera Reineckii Bronze brings a warmer take on the classic red tones associated with AR. Commonly shortened to AR Bronze, this variety develops medium-sized, bright red leaves with bronze undertones that give established growth a rich, earthy appearance. With a little room to develop, AR Bronze produces vigorous stem growth that can fill out the background of medium to larger aquascapes. Regular trimming encourages new offshoots and helps build a fuller group, while its broader foliage creates substantial coverage between finer surrounding plants. Like standard Alternanthera Reineckii, AR Bronze is relatively forgiving for a colorful stem plant. Good lighting and consistent fertilization help support healthy, copmact growth and maintain stronger coloration.

Rotala Florida Sunset is a variation of Rotala Ramosior that isn’t as rare as it once was in the aquascaping community. It is a demanding aquatic stem plant that features saturated color when kept in stable, a high tech planted tank. In less than ideal conditions, color and form will quickly reflect the aquarium’s deficiencies. Sunset grows at a moderate pace and stays relatively small when compared to other fast-growing Rotala varieties. It is an upright stem plant and is a great choice for planted aquariums with high CO2, lighting and nutrients. It doesn’t readily branch out and will need to be trimmed then replanted to create denser groups. While it isn’t a beginner aquascaping plant, its care is straightforward and can be learned with time and patience. If you like pink, red or purple plants, add this Rotala to your list! Common Name Rotala Ramosior / Rotala Florida Sunset Care Advanced Lighting High CO2 Required Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate Height 3-7"

Anubias White Rose is a rarity in the planted aquarium hobby! This species of Anubias features fully white-creamish foliage that pops brighter than other variegated forms of Anubias more commonly known to the hobby. Because of Anubias White Rose's rarity, there is limited information available about this particular plant and it likely makes the wishlist for many rare aquarium plant collectors. Another trait that makes Anubias White Rose highly-coveted is its growth pattern. This aquarium plant has another mutation that causes it to produce smaller foliage that grows fairly compact and similar to a rose, earning its name. Care is comparable to other species of variegated Anubias and as long as you have experience caring for more finicky Anubias varieties, you should do just fine! Like other Anubias, Anubias White Rose is a great midground aquarium plant. It is epiphytic and will grow well when attached to aquarium driftwood or stones. Anubias are slow growers and will benefit from regular fertilization, CO2 injection and good aquarium maintenance habits. Additional care should be taken as its leaves are susceptible to algae growth when placed under too high lighting. CO2 is optional, but recommended as it will help encourage faster growth and robust leaves.

Soft, feathery foliage and fast-growing greenery make Ceratophyllum Demersum, commonly known as Hornwort or Coontail, a popular choice for planted aquariums, breeding tanks, and shrimp setups. This versatile aquatic plant features slender stems surrounded by dense whorls of fine, needle-like leaves, creating a fluffy, bushy appearance that provides excellent shelter for small fish, fry, and shrimplets. Unlike traditional aquarium stem plants, Hornwort lacks a structured root system and can be left floating freely throughout the aquarium or can be anchored into the substrate for a more organized appearance. Its rapid growth also helps absorb excess nutrients from the water column, making it a useful addition to aquariums where nutrient management and natural cover are priorities. Ceratophyllum Demersum is an undemanding aquatic plant that adapts to a wide range of aquarium conditions, making it an excellent choice for beginners.

Philodendron Pink Princess is arguably one of the most sought-after Philodendron plants. This beautiful variety features variegated color that includes shades of green, pink and maroon. The random pops of pink on classic heart-shaped leaves have put Philodendron Pink Pricess at the top of many rare plant collector's wishlists. While it is commonly confused for Philodendron Pink Congo, the variegation shown on Pink Princess is typically stable and the plant does not easily revert to fully green foliage. Philodendron Pink Princess's easy care makes it popular amongst beginner and seasoned house plant lovers alike. The plant isn't too demanding and is known to be more tolerant of normal household conditions. Even so, providing Philodendron Pink Princess with optimal care will pay off well. We recommend bright, indirect lighting, well-draining aroid mix that is rich with organic matter and increased humidity levels. This tropical aroid does best in warmer climates and should be kept away from colder areas and drafts. Philodendron tend to be mildly toxic and should be planted with care in households that have pets and children. In the wild, Philodendron are fantastic climbers and will appreciate a sturdy moss pole to climb on and traverse. When provided with optimal conditions, Philodendron put out aerial roots that may be air-layered for safe propagation once mature. Pruning does not need to be frequent, but older leaves or foliage with visible damage can be removed to encourage new growth. Common Name Philodendron Pink Princess Philodendron Care Easy Lighting Bright, indirect Propagation Cuttings Growth Rate Slow to Moderate

Cryptocoryne Florida Sunset, commonly referred to as a water trumpet, is a small to medium sized Cryptocoryne plant. This particular variation is a hybrid of Cryptocoryne Wendtii with highly variable pattern and color tone. Like most Cryptocoryne plants, Florida Sunset is primarily green but has the potential to produce cream, pink and golden hues depending on overall care and tank conditions. Like other varieties of Cryptocoryne, final size, color and overall form are heavily influenced by the plant's environment in which the plant is kept. This aquarium plant works well in low tech planted aquariums or in areas of a planted tank that are shaded by hardscape or light loving aquarium plant species. Like most Cryptocoryne species, Cryptocoryne Florida Sunset does not prefer to be moved once planted so being mindful of this will go a long way in preventing Crypt melt. Cryptocoryne plants are generally easy to maintain once established in a planted aquarium and will grow at a steady pace. While it isn't required, most aquarium plants will enjoy and experience much better growth in a planted tank that is fully established and is provided with CO2 injection, quality planted aquarium soil, and quality lighting. Common Name Cryptocoryne Florida Sunset Water Trumpet Care Easy Lighting Medium CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Midground Propagation Separate and plant Growth Rate Slow to Moderate Height 3-5"+

Add soft, feathery texture to your planted aquarium with Cabomba Aquatica. Commonly known as Fanwort, this South American stem plant features ornate foliage that fans out into its signature shape, creating soft, lush groups of greenery. Its voluminous growth is ideal for filling in the background of an aquarium, where it adds natural, billowing movement. Under stable conditions, Cabomba Aquatica can grow rapidly, requiring regular trimming to maintain its shape. Its potential size makes it especially suitable for larger planted aquariums, while its foliage also looks beautiful when viewed from above in freshwater ponds. Considered one of the less demanding Cabomba species, this aquarium stem plant still requires adequate lighting and consistent fertilization. Supplemental CO2 isn't strictly required but can help support denser growth and healthy, feathery foliage.

Philodendron Tortum is a unique specimen that is easily recognized and coveted for its foliage. Its rich green tone is consistent across its elongated thin leaves that branch out along the main stem. Philodendron Tortum is epiphytic and should be provided with means for climbing in the form of a stake or moss pole as the plant matures. Like other forms of Philodendron, Philodendron Tortum will appreciate increased humidity levels and warmer weather. Growing medium should be well-aerated and include a variety of organic and inorganic materials such as sphagnum, orchid bark, charcoal, perlite, coco coir and more commonly used ingredients. We recommend providing Philodendron Tortum with bright, indirect lighting. This can be in the form of indoor lighting with units like the ONF Aditya Plant Lamp or in a southern exposure. East-facing windows are good too along with western exposures, but the plant should be monitored to ensure lighting is not excessively direct as this may result in damage or burning of the plant. Pruning does not need to be frequent, but older leaves or foliage with visible damage can be removed to encourage new growth. Common Name Philodendron Tortum Philodendron Care Moderate Lighting Bright, indirect Propagation Cuttings Growth Rate Slow to Moderate

listings.description: Support healthy aquatic plant growth with Aquario Neo Essence Amino Acid Supplement. Formulated with highly concentrated natural amino acids extracted from plants, Neo Essence helps improve nutrient uptake, support photosynthesis, and promote healthy growth in freshwater planted aquariums. By improving the availability and absorption of nutrients, Neo Essence helps aquatic plants make better use of your existing fertilizer routine. Healthy, actively growing plants naturally compete more effectively for available nutrients, supporting a cleaner, more balanced planted aquarium. Best For - Freshwater planted aquariums - Supporting healthy growth and improved coloration - Supplementing existing fertilizer routines Size: 300ml / 1000ml Dosing Instructions: Shake well before use. Dose 5 mL per 60 L (approximately 16 gallons) of aquarium water. The 300 mL bottle cap measures 5 mL, while the 1000 mL bottle cap measures 10 mL. For best results, use alongside your regular fertilizer routine. Important Note: Neo Essence contains natural ingredients and may produce a slight odor, which is normal. Temporary cloudiness or visible natural ingredients may occur when added to the aquarium but will dissipate shortly after dosing. Overdosing may cause temporary cloudiness. Intended for aquarium use only. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Packaging Update: Aquario has updated the bottle design for this product. Anubias Minima Dragon Claw is a new hybrid variation more recently available to the hobby. This particular species features similar growth pattern and leaf shape but will, under the right care, produce leaves that are slightly different in color. This feature makes this plant extremely unique as a myriad of shades are certain to show when the plant is larger in size and mature. Like other Anubias plants, Anubias Minima Dragon Claw can be considered a hardy aquarium plant. This group of aquatic plants are tolerant to a wide range of aquarium conditions and will readily adapt to most environments making them a fantastic choice for the beginner aquarist or anyone interested in adding live aquarium plants to their tanks. Anubias Minima Dragon Claw is an epiphytic plant and can be attached to your favorite aquarium driftwood or between the crevices in hardscaping material making it versatile with tank placement and a great choice for areas of the aquarium that are lacking color. Despite Anubias' hardiness, we still recommend providing the plant with CO2 injection, if possible, along with a quality aquarium plant fertilizer. Good tank maintenance habits will also go a long way in ensuring the health of the plant and overall success.

Anubias Giant Stardust is a large-leafed aquatic plant characterized by prominent white venation that runs through its leaves. This feature creates beautiful contrast when grouped with other colorful aquarium plants. In addition, Anubias Giant Stardust has slightly speckled leaves and mottled coloration, earning its name. If you're looking for a rarer Anubias, this is a great one to add to your collection. Specific information is limited, so we recommend starting with basic Anubias care and making adjustments as the plant matures. Provide moderate flow, moderate lighting, and a liquid fertilizer that contains both macro and micronutrients. When kept in a planted aquarium under proper lighting, Anubias Stardust’s leaves are illuminated beautifully!

Echinodorus Hadi Red Pearl is a unique amazon sword plant that offers a low growing profile in the planted aquaria hobby. This particular variation offers higher levels of variegation and is sure to add an ornamental touch to any planted aquarium or planted setup. Like other Amazon Sword plants, Echinodorus Hadi Red Pearl Variegated has the potential to grow quite large so aquariums with enough space to accommodate its size are preferable. Alternatively, Echinodorus species make excellent single-specimen displays or as an addition to a Wabi Kusa planted setup. These aquatic plants are very versatile and can be grown in submerged conditions as well as emersed conditions. Ammannia Sulawesi is an uncommon Indonesian stem plant with a color palette that's difficult to pin down to just one shade. Under favorable conditions, its foliage can display a mix of soft green, orange, and pink tones along upright stems, giving established groups plenty of natural color variation. While Ammannia Sulawesi isn't necessarily difficult to grow, it appreciates consistency and is better suited for hobbyists with some experience keeping more particular stem plants. A mature, stable planted aquarium provides a better starting point than a newly established setup, where fluctuating conditions can make successful growth less predictable.

Microsorum pteropus ‘Gold Sparkle’, also known as Java Fern Gold Sparkle, is a newer variation of Java Fern known for its shifting green tones and lighter new growth. Fresh leaves emerge in a brighter shade and gradually deepen in color as they mature, giving the plant a subtle, changing look over time. Recently reclassified as Leptochilus pteropus , this plant is still widely known in the aquarium hobby as Microsorum pteropus. Like other Java Fern varieties, it is hardy and easy to care for, making it suitable for a wide range of planted aquarium setups. As an epiphytic plant, it can be attached to driftwood, rocks, or placed into crevices within hardscape. Over time, it will naturally anchor itself, making it a great option for filling in sparse areas and adding additional greenery to an aquascape. Java Fern Gold Sparkle grows well in low tech conditions, though the addition of CO2 and nutrients will improve growth rate and overall appearance. Be sure to keep the rhizome above the substrate to prevent rot. Propagation is simple—just divide the rhizome and reattach as needed.

Bucephalandra Brownie Phoenix is a beautiful species of Bucephalandra that offers iridescent, brownish-green pops of color. Its varying hues provide lovely contrast and its slightly ruffled leaves provide texture to a planted aquarium tank. Bucephalandra Brownie Phoenix looks best when placed in the mid-ground of planted aquarium tanks along with other Bucephalandra species that are similar in size. This aquatic plant prefers low to medium lighting and will grow nice and dense if favorable conditions are provided. CO2 injection along with a good maintenance schedule will promote quicker, more robust growth. The stem and rhizome should not be covered when planting as this will cause the plant to rot and wither. It is best to attach or wedge Bucephalandra on or between aquarium hardscapes such as aquarium driftwood and aquascaping rocks.

Bucephalandra Green Godzilla is a beautiful Bucephalandra plant. This particular species is a medium to large sized specimen and produces long leaves that are primarily dark green with a ruffled edge. Depending on the conditions the plant is kept in, Buce Green Godzilla has the potential to produce an iridescent glow in the planted aquarium and its pinkish orange stem adds additional contrast to the layout. Being a slow grower, Bucephalandra Green Godzilla is susceptible to growing algae on its leaves and should be placed in an area that provides slight shade. Higher lighting produces more compact growth, whereas lower lighting may result in the plant becoming leggy. Bucephalandra does best in low to medium lighting and will grow nice and dense if favorable conditions are provided. CO2 injection along with a good flow and regular tank maintenance will promote quicker, more robust growth. The stem and rhizome should not be covered when planting as this will cause the plant to rot and wither. Care can be comparable to other popular aquatic plant species such as Anubias and Java Ferns, but Bucephalandra will not tolerate sudden changes well.

Eleocharis Vivipara offers wispy background coverage in nature style aquariums or river inspired aquascapes. Remove this plant from its growing medium before planting. Click here to shop all aquarium plants! Eleocharis Vivipara is similar in foliage texure to the popular carpeting aquarium plant, Eleocharis Parvula aka Hair Grass. Eleocharis Vivipara, sometimes referred to as Umbrella Hair Grass, is a much taller variation of Eleocharis and offers excellent background coverage that will sometimes droop over and create a beautiful effect when it has reached the aquarium's water surface. We recommend this plant in river-style planted aquariums or in nature style aquarium tanks. It offers a semi-chaotic appearance and is extremely natural in any planted tank. A Glass Aqua favorite for background plant choice in a wide range of aquascapes! A pressurized CO2 system is not required to grow Eleocharis Vivipara, but will promote quicker, lush growth. Once established, Eleocharis Vivipara is a prolific grower and will happily spread to all areas of an aquarium. To prevent this, regular trimming will be essential in maintaining this plant's growth! Pogostemon Stellatus Dassen is a beautiful aquarium stem that produces long, narrow leaves that are primarily orange in color with varying shades of pinkish red depending on the conditions provided. This particular variation can be quite finicky and should be kept by aquarists who have experience growing difficult aquatic species. We recommend softer water conditions along with a nutrient-dense aquarium soil, CO2 injection and a complete macro/micro nutrient dosing regiment. Bucephalandra Boyan Mini Narrow is a rare Buce species that isn't commonly found in the planted aquaria hobby. This particular variation is a small to medium sized specimen that is primarily green in color with hints of purple undertones. Its leaves are slightly rounded with a pronounced central vein that runs down the center of each leaf. Like other Bucephalandra plants, Buce Boyan Mini Narrow is suitable for the midground area of a planted aquarium and can be grown in both low and high tech conditions. Because these plants are slow growers, they are more prone to algae growth when maintenance isn't consistent, so an area that provides a bit of shade is ideal. If placed under bright open light, maintenance must be consistent and thorough to prevent this. Leaves that older, have holes or are decaying can be pruned to encourage new growth. Bucephalandra Boyan Mini Narrow is epiphytic and grows best when attached to surfaces such as aquarium driftwood or aquascaping stones. We recommend low to medium lighting for this little Buce species along with good flow, quality aquarium plant nutrition and a well-maintained tank environment. CO2 injection isn't necessary for most Buce species, but it will surely help bring out the best colors that are commonly sought after when growing Bucephalandra. The stem and rhizome should not be covered when planting as this will cause the plant to rot and wither. Care can be comparable to other popular aquatic plant species such as Anubias and Java Ferns, but Bucephalandra will not tolerate sudden changes well.

Add glossy texture and vibrant green color to your planted aquarium Bucephalandra Fairy Sparkle. Its chubby, oval leaves display a subtle metallic sheen that shimmers when it catches the light, while its warmer-toned petioles create natural contrast against its foliage. Slow-growing like other Buce, it's easy to maintain and an ideal choice for adding detail to your hardscape, and shaded areas of an aquascape. With time and stable conditions, Bucephalandra develop into dense clumps that add color, texture and visual character that's hard to match in planted aquariums.

Bucephalandra Theia Green is a hybridized species cultivated in specialized aquatic plant labs. Theia Green is relatively small in size and offers a variation of dark olive green to light green tones depending on the environment in which it's grown. Like other Bucephalandra species, Buce Theia Green is fairly hardy and adaptable to many different aquarium conditions and growing styles. It can be grown submerged in a planted tank or emersed in terrarium and paludarium style enclosures. Because these plants are slow growers, they are more prone to algae growth when maintenance isn't consistent, so an area that provides a bit of shade is ideal. If placed under bright open light, maintenance must be consistent and thorough to prevent this. Leaves that older, have holes or are decaying can be pruned to encourage new growth. Bucephalandra are epiphytic and grow best when attached to surfaces such as aquarium driftwood or aquascaping stones. We recommend low to medium lighting for this Buce species along with good flow, quality aquarium plant nutrition and a well-maintained tank environment. CO2 injection isn't necessary for most Buce species, but it will surely help bring out the best colors that are commonly sought after when growing Bucephalandra. The stem and rhizome should not be covered when planting as this will cause the plant to rot and wither. Care can be comparable to other popular aquatic plant species such as Anubias and Java Ferns, but Bucephalandra will not tolerate sudden changes well.

This Java Fern is pre-attached to a natural fiber mat, making it easy to place, anchor, or integrate into your aquascape. Microsorum pteropus, commonly known as Java Fern, is a classic aquarium plant in the planted tank hobby. A fantastic choice for beginner aquarists, it’s known for being extremely hardy and able to tolerate a wide range of aquarium conditions. Recently reclassified as Leptochilus pteropus , this plant is still widely known in the aquarium hobby as Microsorum pteropus. Its bright green, broad leaves provide great coverage and are useful for filling in open areas of an aquascape. As an epiphytic plant, Java Fern grows best when attached to hard surfaces. This mat format makes it especially versatile, allowing you to lay it flat, tuck it into the aquascape, or secure it to driftwood or rocks. Like most aquarium plants, it can be grown in low tech setups, though added CO2 and nutrients will improve growth and overall fullness. Care should be taken to keep the rhizome above the substrate to prevent rot. Over time, the plant will continue to grow and can be propagated by dividing the rhizome and reattaching as needed.

This variation of Rotala is, like other Rotala plants, a prolific grower once established and will require routine maintenance to maintain the desired look. Because Rotala species are able to grow quite tall, we recommend planting them in groups in the background area of the aquarium. Results are improved with soft water as well. Rotala Colorata is an uncommon aquarium stem plant with leaves that range from orange to bright red and pink hues. It grows similar to other Rotala species but the leaves have much more vivid coloration, resulting in a very pleasing mid to background plant depending on the aquarium it's planted in. Like all aquatic stem plants, Rotala Colorata can be repeatedly trimmed and replanted to create a lush thick bush, making it a perfect addition to any planted tank that demands color. Unlike other Rotala species, this Rotala seems to produce intense colors even when in moderate lighting. However, to bring the best out of this plant, we recommend intense lighting, CO2 injection and a complete macro and micro-nutrient supply. Results are improved with soft water as well. listings.description: Please note: This item is final sale and cannot be returned or exchanged. Our recommended choice for Wabi-Kusa or desktop nano tanks! Height-adjustable, 360° swivel and dimmable. Click here to shop all lighting! A crowd favorite, the ONF Flat Nano Stand LED Light is a fantastic smart desktop plant lighting solution. Available in 3 colors, this LED light provides the optimal spectrum for growing lush, healthy terrestrial and aquatic plant species. ONF touts an exclusively customized LED range comprised of three wavelengths and full spectrum color. The Flat Nano Stand LED Light features adjustable height up to 14" and a 360° swivel to accommodate growing plants and easy maintenance. All models are dimmable and provide the clean aesthetic aquarium and plant hobbyists search for. Whether you are using this LED light for a pico aquarium tank, Wabi-Kusa or desktop plant setup, the ONF Flat Nano Stand LED Light is sure to impress. Shown in the video below is a Ultum Nature Systems 16T rimless tank with an ONF Flat Nano Stand LED Light: Simple to install, the ONF Flat Nano LED Light allows the user to adjust the height via a small rubber stopper for more or less light spread, making it a great aquarium lighting option for both low light easy aquatic plants to high light loving aquatic plants. With a smooth swivel, The ONF Flat Nano LED Light also allows the user to turn the light 360 degrees, keeping the lighting unit safe from water exposure and making aquarium tank maintenance quick and easy. The ONF Flat Nano LED Light features on/off, 3-level dimming via touch. Flat Nano's light output is the optimal spectrum for aquatic plant growth and suits various species of aquatic plants and their respective light requirements. Once a level is chosen, ONF Flat Nano LED Light has built-in memory and will display the level last chosen even when used with a timer. Coloration is extremely vivid, allowing the myriad of hues produced by aquatic plants, freshwater fish and shrimp to shine bright and clear. Abrupt on and off schedules have the potential to shock skittish fish, but the Flat Nano LED administers ramp up and down capabilities to mimic the rise and setting of the sun to provide the most natural experience for aquarium tank inhabitants. ONF Flat Nano Stand LED Light will fit under rimless aquarium tanks with foam mats. Featuring a lovely bright green hue, Limnophila Vietnam has star-shaped foliage that stays on the smaller side making it ideal as a midground aquatic plant choice in planted aquarium tanks. It's also a great choice for aquarists who are in the search of mini aquatic plants. When provided with quality aquarium lighting, Limnophila Vietnam can produce a faint purplish-red coloration that is sure to pop against other aquatic plant species. Rotala Rotundifolia is a classic aquatic stem plant that is commonly seen in a wide variety of planted aquarium tanks. This aquarium stem is a prolific grower and produces beautiful colors that include green, pink and orange tones depending on the conditions of the aquarium. Rotala Rotundifolia is commonly hybridized and is relatively undemanding, making it a popular choice for both beginner aquarists and seasoned aquascapers. Rotala Rotundifolia forms side shoots easily when pruned, making it a great contender for creating the compact and bushy effect in the background area of the tank. When mixed with other colorful aquarium stem plants, Rotala Rotundifolia is ornamental and is sure to impress. We recommend a nutritious aqua soil, CO2 injection and moderate lighting to start. Consistent maintenance habits will improve health and overall growth. Like other species of Rotala, Rotala Rotundifolia is versatile and can be grown in both submerged and emersed conditions making this aquarium stem a great choice for all styles of aquarium keeping and planted setups such as a classic Wabi Kusa. We recommend this plant for aquarists looking for a unique background or midground aquatic plant. Pruning is simple and can be done by replanting trimmed stems into quality aquarium soil. Anubias Jungle Star is a newer variation of Anubias with little information readily available about the specimen. Appearance-wise, Anubias Jungle Star is a small-leafed variant that is deep green in color with pointed leaves. Like other forms of Anubias, this aquatic plant is a great beginner aquatic plant choice and is a perfect introduction to keeping live aquarium plants. Anubias are known for being another bulletproof choice and will tolerate a wide range of aquarium conditions and water parameters. Anubias are epiphytic plants, meaning they sprouts leaves from its rhizome and can grow attached to aquarium hardscape such as aquarium driftwood or in the crevices between stone hardscape layouts. Anubias can also grow marginally and will thrive above water in vivarium, terrarium, and paludarium setups as long as sufficient humidity is provided to prevent the plant from drying out. Anubias are flowering species and will bloom from time to time. With many different forms, shapes, and sizes available, Anubias plants are a classic staple in the planted aquarium hobby! While it isn't required, most aquarium plants will enjoy and experience much better growth in a planted tank that is fully established and is provided with CO2 injection, quality planted aquarium soil, and quality lighting.

Cryptocoryne Spiralis Red is a unique aquarium plant that is suitable for the midground area of a planted aquarium. This Crypt variety is characterized by long, thin leaves that display an interesting pattern and are reddish brown in color. Cryptocoryne Spiralis Red is a medium to large sized specimen, making it a fantastic choice for transitioning the midground to the background area of the planted tank. Like other Cryptocoryne plants, Crypt Spiralis Red is relatively easy-going, but needs to become established first. We recommend planting this species in an aquarium that is already established as newly setup aquariums may contribute to chances of Crypt melt. Once this aquarium plant grows a solid root system, it is sure to standout in the aquascape layout! To support quicker and healthy growth, we recommend CO2 injection and a nutrient-dense aquarium soil. Moderate lighting along with nutrient dosing and good maintenance habits will go a long way!

Echinodorus Leopard is a beautiful Amazon Sword specimen that works well in the background area of a planted aquarium or as a single aquatic plant display. Echinodorus Leopard is primarily green in color with scattered spotting throughout its leaves. Spots are more apparent in younger growth and typically fades as the plant matures, producing a mottled appearance. Like other Amazon Sword plants, Echinodorus Leopard is a heavy root feeder and requires a nutrient-dense aqua soil to support healthy growth. Echinodorus species are typically very hardy and adaptable, making the species a great choice for beginner aquascapers. Echinodorus can be grown in submerged and emersed conditions, making the plant suitable for both aquarium settings and terrarium or Wabi Kusa applications. Propagation is simple. Separate and replant. Bucephalandra Sintang Green is a beautiful Buce specimen! This particular variety features compact growth and a rich green tone that adds character and texture to the midground of any aquascape layout. Sintang Green is a smaller variation, making it suitable for nano planted tanks as well. Its leaves are slightly ruffled and when grown in optimal conditions, Buce Sintang Green produces vibrant color with a metallic sheen when viewed at certain angles. Bucephalandra are typicaly found in fast-flowing waters in the wild and will appreciate good flow and consistent maintenance efforts. Because Bucephalandra are slow growers, they are susceptible to algae growth on their leaves when excess nutrients are present in the water column. Low to moderate lighting is sufficient and CO2 injection isn't necessary but will aid in promoting quicker growth that is lush and full. Lack of lighting may cause the plant to become leggy! Propagation is simple and can be done by gently separating the main rhizome and reattaching to aquarium driftwood or between cracks in the hardscape layout.

Rotala Vietnam is a delicate aquatic stem plant known for its fine, feather-like foliage and shades of green, bronze, and pink. Similar in appearance to Rotala Wallichii, this variety features slightly longer, narrow leaves that extend outward from reddish-brown stems, creating a soft, wispy appearance. Its intricate foliage and vibrant coloration make it an attractive choice for the midground or background of a planted aquarium, especially when grouped with contrasting leaf shapes and textures. Under favorable conditions, Rotala Vietnam can develop into dense, bushy groups that add height and dimension to an aquascape. This plant benefits from moderate to high lighting, consistent fertilization, and supplemental CO2 injection to support healthy growth and coloration. Regular trimming helps prevent overcrowding and allows light to reach the lower portions of the plant, while healthy stem cuttings can be replanted to encourage fuller growth.
