Customize your aquarium filtration with Aquario Neo Bag Filter Media. Available in four specialized formulas, Neo Bag provides an easy way to target specific water quality needs while supporting a balanced freshwater planted aquarium. Each media is pre-portioned in an aquarium-safe filter bag for convenient placement inside canister filters, hang-on-back (HOB) filters, or other high-flow filtration systems. Choose the formula that best fits your aquarium and goals. Best For - Freshwater planted aquariums - Targeted water quality management - Canister and hang-on-back (HOB) filtration systems Size: 12 × 8 cm (each filter bag) Contents: 8 filter bags per package Instructions for Use: Rinse the filter bag in clean water before use. Place 1 bag per 60 L (approximately 16 gallons) of aquarium water flat in an area of strong water flow, such as a canister filter or hang-on-back (HOB) filter. For faster results, an additional bag may be used. Important Note: Neo Bag performs best when placed in an area of strong water flow. Some temporary discoloration may occur during initial use and is normal. Neo Bag Minus and Neo Bag Zeolite can be regenerated for repeated use; refer to the comparison guide and included instructions for proper regeneration procedures. Filter media will gradually become depleted over time and should be replaced as needed. Intended for aquarium use only. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Bag Purpose Effect & Usage Plus Water Softener Lowers pH Best for: Freshwater aquariums with fish, shrimp, or aquatic plants that prefer softer, slightly acidic water. Minus Nutrient Remover Removes nitrite, nitrate, and phosphate Best for: Helping reduce excess nutrients that contribute to algae growth. Reusable: Can be regenerated for extended use. Carbon Activated Carbon Improves water clarity Best for: Removing discoloration, tannins, odors, and dissolved organic compounds from aquarium water. Zeolite Ammonia Remover Removes ammonia and heavy metals Best for: Established aquariums experiencing elevated ammonia levels or helping maintain stable water quality. Reusable: Can be regenerated for extended use. Regeneration Instructions: Neo Bag Minus and Neo Bag Zeolite can be regenerated for repeated use. Place the used filter bag in 300 mL of a 10% saltwater solution, gently agitate for approximately 10 minutes, then allow it to soak for 24 hours. Rinse thoroughly with clean water before returning it to the filter. Regeneration can be repeated multiple times, though the media’s effectiveness will gradually decrease with each cycle.

Starting a planted aquarium tank can be a challenging process simply due to the fact that all aquariums need to be in balance in order to thrive and start maturing. During this time, there is a likely chance that unsightly algae may appear. In order to minimize this occurrence without sacrificing the needs of aquatic plants, we have tested and recommended this liquid fertilizer combo. The main benefit of this Aquario liquid fertilizer combo is that there are absolutely no algae inducing elements. Adding to a planted tank may speed up aquatic plant growth, but they are not needed in the initial stages of a planted aquarium. Trace amounts of Nitrogen and Phosphorus can already be found in standard aquarium substrates, aquasoil and livestock waste. In addition, both elements are not additionally required in low light planted tank conditions as livestock waste byproduct is enough for aquatic plants with less demanding requirements. However, Nitrogen and Phosphorus will be needed once the nutrients from the substrate has been depleted for high demanding stem plants. Aquario Liquid Fertilizer Set Includes: Aquario Neo Solution K (Potassium) Aquario Neo Solution 2 (Micronutrients) Aquario Neo Solution is a full liquid fertilizer line designed for all planted aquarium tanks. The addition of liquid fertilizers to a planted aquarium tank can be for many reasons such as for general use, in response to decreased aquarium plant growth, combating specific aquatic plant ailments and increasing aquarium plant growth as needed for a specific look. Having healthy aquatic plants not only promotes a healthy ecosystem and looks good, but it also reduces chances for unsightly algae growth as planted aquarium algae types are typically opportunistic and will only appear when plant growth declines or little effort is made in regard to routine maintenance. Neo Solution liquid fertilizers for planted aquarium tanks can be used in conjunction with each other or separately to provide the results needed for a specific setup. As a planted aquarium tank matures, aquatic plant nutritional requirements respectively increase. Aquario Neo Essence provides a boost of essential amino acides while Aquario Neo Guard helps to safeguard your planted tank from algae blooms. The amino acids provided by Aquario Neo Essence Water Conditioner may not be found in a home aquarium! These amino acids are naturally derived and formulated to strengthen aquatic plant root structures, increase absorption of liquid fertilizers and enhance color vibrancy. The addition of this planted aquarium water conditioner indirectly supports the prevention of algae growth as aquatic plants that are growing vigorously will easily outcompete algae strains from reproducing. Aquario Neo Guard Water Conditioner's specialized formula eliminates unwanted algae outbreaks by reducing Phosphorus levels in a planted aquarium tank. When an excess amount of Phosphorus remains in an aquarium, algae will appear. Algae outbreaks generally occur in the first few months after starting a planted aquarium or when water parameters become unbalanced.

Maintaining an aquarium requires time and patience, but there are plenty of aquarium liquid conditioners that help make the aquarium hobbyist's life easier! A healthy planted aquarium includes the health of the livestock that inhabits the aquarium. When fish are healthy and water parameters are stable, live aquatic plants are also able to grow healthily, resulting in a well-balanced planted aquarium. Aquario Neo C Water Conditioner is a newly formulated tap water dechlorinator that will neutralize any chlorine, chloramine, ammonia and ammonium from water sources. It also contains trace minerals to improve aquarium livestock activity, digestion and long term health. This liquid aquarium water conditioner will also not disrupt the growth of beneficial bacteria and will instead aid in its exponential growth. Aquario Neo V Water Conditioner contains natural humic acids, trace minerals and amino acids that will reduce nitrates in an aquarium. When used as directed, livestock appetite and spawning rates will significantly improve.

Fire Stone is a unique aquarium rock that is suitable for an all rock hardscape layout or as a base beneath popular aquascaping driftwoods. The stone sports a warm-toned color pallete and serrated texture that provides plenty of crevices for the attachment of aquatic plants or mosses. Given its texture, the stone provides ample grip and is a good contender for hobbyists who are looking for stones that can be stacked. Fire Stone is sure to provide a solid base to any successful aquascape layout! Fire Stone is a fantastic choice for creating cave aquascapes, canyon style and mountain terrain hardscape layouts.

Its deep hue contrasts well against aquatic plants and its shape is ideal for creating Iwagumi style aquascape layouts.

Goliath Stone, also known as Rhino Stone, is a new aquarium stone that is versatile and can be used for a wide variety of popular aquascaping styles. The stone features a mixture of grey and brown tones along with plenty of textural character that is perfect for the greening method. The stone is comparable to other popular aquascaping stones but is more rounded rather than sharp, making it a good choice for planted tanks that contain livestock with sensitive fins. Goliath Stone can be used as a standalone hardscape material or as a solid base beneath popular planted tank driftwoods such as Malaysian Driftwood or Spider Wood. Its natural appearance also pairs well with aquarium carpet plants or with natural sand.

Striped River Stone is a smooth, rounded stone with a varying striated pattern. The stone displays a mixture of white, grey, brown and orange tones that provide a natural appearance. The overall texture of this stone is suitable for planted aquariums that contain sensitively finned livestock. Alternatively, Striped River Stone is a great choice for recreating river-style aquascape layouts. We recommend pairing this stone with simple aquatic plant species. Its natural appearance pairs well with an aquatic plant foreground or with cosmetic sand.

Hemigraphis Alternata Exotica, more commonly known as Purple Waffle, is a unique houseplant that is suitable for a terrarium, paludarium or vivarium. This plant features deep green foliage with bold purple undersides. Its foliage is crinkled in texture, adding textural and visual interest to the planted setup. Like other forms of Hemigraphis, the Purple Waffle plant prefers a consistently moist environment, but shouldn't be submerged in an aquarium. Whether being kept as a houseplant or in as an addition to the terrarium, Purple Waffle is a beautiful oddity that is sure to impress. Marsh Stone is a new aquarium hardscape that features similar characteristics that are found in Hakkai Stone. This stone is primarily light grey in color with random hints of cream and white throughout. Marsh Stone is a great choice for aquarists looking for a unique aquarium layout material that is versatile and safe for livestock with sensitive fins as well. The stone is softly rounded but doesn't lack the characteristic grooves and crevices that are commonly sought after when choosing an aquarium stone. The cracks and crevices provide additional texture and are perfect for attaching your favorite aquatic mosses and epiphytic aquatic plant species such as Anubias or Bucephalandra. We recommend Marsh Stone for a classic Iwagumi aquarium layout. Alternatively, it would work perfectly as a base to aquarium driftwood or in a community freshwater aquarium. Hydrocotyle tripartita ‘Mini’, often referred to as Hydrocotyle ‘Japan’, is a popular aquarium plant known for its bright green, clover-shaped foliage and vining growth habit. Originally popularized through nature-style aquascaping by Takashi Amano, it’s widely used for adding texture, shape and color in planted aquariums and terrariums. This versatile plant can be used in both the foreground and midground, where it spreads through runners to form dense bushes or trailing vines depending on how it’s trimmed. Its signature leaf shape and vibrant green color makes it an excellent choice for softening hardscape edges and filling in negative space with a natural, organic look. Hydrocotyle tripartita ‘Mini’ is generally undemanding, though sufficient lighting is important to maintain denser growth. In lower light conditions, it tends to grow more vertically, and can become leggy in an attempt to reach more light. With medium to high lighting, CO2 injection, and consistent fertilization, this dainty aquarium plant grows quickly and can become chaotic without regular trimming to maintain shape. Propagation is simple! Snip along the stem and replant into the substrate to encourage branching and fuller plant groups. Yokihi Medaka Rice Fish (Oryzias latipes) are a type of Japanese Rice Fish that bring movement, personality, and shimmering color to a planted aquarium or pond. We love these fish for their active swimming behavior, top-down viewing, and ability to flourish in a wide range of environments. Whether kept indoors or outdoors, Medaka are a fun fish that are rewarding to care for and easy to enjoy. Unlike many traditional aquarium fish, Medaka tolerate cooler temperatures and adapt well to planted aquariums patio ponds, planted tubs, and indoor pond setups. Their peaceful nature, low bioload, and hardy disposition make them a great option for beginners while still being appreciated by experienced hobbyists and breeders. Medaka Highlights Beginner Friendly: Hardy and adaptable, Medaka are often recommended for newer hobbyists looking for an active and easy care fish. Top-Down Viewing: One of the most enjoyable aspects of keeping Medaka is viewing them from above. Their colors and movement are ideal for shallow aquariums, ponds, and planted tubs. Peaceful Temperament: Medaka coexist well with other peaceful livestock and are an excellent choice for community aquariums and ponds. Medaka are social fish that should be kept in groups whenever possible. A group of six or more fish is recommended per 10 gallons to encourage natural behavior and activity. They prefer gentle water movement and will appreciate floating plants, live aquatic plants or additional cover, especially in outdoor setups. They may occasionally jump, so a lid or adequate plant cover s recommended. Stocking Recommendations As a practical guideline, plan for approximately one Medaka per gallon of water volume. Larger aquariums and ponds naturally provide more stability and swimming space. Avoid overcrowding as this can increase stress and make maintaining water quality more difficult. Feeding Medaka are omnivores and readily accept quality pellets, flakes, frozen and live foods. Feed only what they can consume in a few minutes and remove excess. Avoid overfeeding to help maintain water quality. If kept in outdoor setups, they will happily munch on mosquito larvae too! Arrival & Acclimation For best results, introduce new fish into a mature, cycled aquarium or pond. Spend extra time to float bags to match temperature before release. Once in the aquarium, pond or quarantine tank, give them time to settle in! Do not make any significant changes or move them during this time. Care & Compatibility Temperament: Peaceful Diet: Omnivore Group Size: 6 or more Important Information: If using tap water, always treat with a quality dechlorinator. Stable water conditions, regular maintenance, and appropriate stocking levels will help support long-term health and success. As with all live animals, natural variation in color, pattern, and size should be expected.

Horned Nerite Snails are small freshwater snails that are popular in the aquarium hobby for their unique appearance and algae-eating habits. Like other freshwater snails, Horned Nerites are generally peaceful critters and are easy to care for. We recommend adding these snails to covered planted aquariums as they can and will likely try to crawl out. The Horned Nerite can be identified by little protruding horns on the shell and are primarily brownish-black with hints of golden yellow. These snails do not breed in freshwater and can also be kept in brackish waters. Aquarium snails will help clean your aquarium glass, but will also happily turn over the substrate. They'll spend all day foraging, but we recommend providing quality sinking pellets as well. Warmer waters and stable pH levels are necessary, but other than this, Horned Nerites are generally easy to care for and will add interest to any aquarium tank. Tank size recommendation: 5-10G for 1-2 snails Aquarium snails are extremely sensitive to copper. If using tap, be sure to use a dechlorinator to ensure safety for your invertebrates. Horned nerites are peaceful.

Caridina multidentata , aka Amano Shrimp, is a powerhouse in the planted aquarium hobby and one of the best-known algae eaters. We add these shrimp to nearly every new tank setup to help manage diatoms and other early algae growth. They’re fairly hardy and will tolerate a wide range of water conditions, making them great for beginners and a must-have for new aquascapes. While they don’t breed in freshwater and require special conditions for reproduction, Amano Shrimp can live long, healthy lives with proper care. They are generally peaceful but can be more assertive than other species, making them well-suited for tanks with peaceful to semi-peaceful tankmates. (Essentially, they’re better equipped to defend themselves if needed!) Amano Shrimp also grow larger than most other Caridina, so keep this in mind when deciding if you want to add them to your aquarium. A favorite around here, Amano Shrimp are essential members of any planted aquarium algae squad! Tank size recommendation: 10G Shrimp are extremely sensitive to copper. If using tap, be sure to use a dechlorinator to ensure safety for your invertebrates. Amano shrimp are generally peaceful, but can be assertive.

Fire Red Cherry Shrimp are among the most popular freshwater shrimp in the planted aquarium hobby. Bred from the classic Cherry Shrimp, this hybrid variety develops vivid red tones that stand out beautifully against healthy aquarium plants—especially green ones! Fire Reds are a great introductory shrimp as they’re relatively hardy and don’t require the specialized care that more advanced species often need. Despite their popularity, they remain readily available and are an affordable, fun way to bring color and activity into any planted tank. Freshwater aquarium shrimp are also very small, meaning you can safely keep a good-sized colony even in a nano aquarium without overcrowding. While shrimp are often associated with algae control, Fire Reds shouldn’t be compared to the cleaning powerhouse, Amano Shrimp. Still, they spend their days grazing and foraging, making them both practical and fun to observe in planted aquaria. They also breed readily under most conditions, making them a great first time choice for beginner shrimp keepers. Tank size recommendation: 5-10G Shrimp are extremely sensitive to copper. If using tap, be sure to use a dechlorinator to ensure safety for your invertebrates. Fire Reds are peaceful. Keep them in an aquarium with non-agressive tank mates to ensure their safety.

listings.commonName: Aquario Neo Booster Plants Organic Carbon Supplement
listings.description: Support healthy aquatic plant growth with Aquario Neo Booster Plants Organic Carbon Supplement. Formulated with bioavailable organic carbon, Neo Booster Plants helps support photosynthesis, nutrient uptake, and healthy plant growth in freshwater planted aquariums. Available in Booster Plants and Booster Plants Ferti, both formulas can be used with or without CO2 injection and alongside your existing fertilizer routine. Booster Plants Ferti also contains natural amino acids for additional plant support. Healthy aquatic plants naturally consume more available nutrients, helping them compete with algae while supporting a balanced planted aquarium. Choose Your Formula Booster Plants Bioavailable organic carbon Supports photosynthesis and nutrient uptake Ideal for planted aquariums with or without CO2 injection Booster Plants Ferti Everything in Booster Plants Plus natural amino acids for additional plant support Best For - Freshwater planted aquariums - Supporting healthy aquatic plant growth - Supplementing existing fertilizer routines Size: 300ml / 1000ml Dosing Instructions: Shake well before use. The 300 mL bottle cap measures 5 mL, while the 1000 mL bottle cap measures 10 mL. Important Note: Neo Booster Plants is intended to supplement healthy plant growth and does not replace a pressurized CO2 system. Natural ingredients may produce a slight odor, which is normal. Booster Plants Ferti may appear cloudy in the bottle but will clear shortly after being added to the aquarium. Intended for aquarium use only. Keep out of reach of children and pets. listings.commonName: Aquario Neo Booster Tropical Ammonia & Nitrate Reducer
listings.description: Support a healthy biological filter with Aquario Neo Booster Tropical Ammonia & Nitrate Reducer. Designed for freshwater planted aquariums, Neo Booster Tropical provides organic carbon, trace elements, and essential nutrients that help beneficial bacteria establish and multiply. As beneficial bacteria become established, they naturally process ammonia and nitrate, supporting cleaner water and a more balanced aquarium. Neo Booster Tropical is especially useful during the early stages of aquarium setup, helping shorten the time it takes for biological filtration to mature. Best For - Freshwater planted aquariums - Supporting biological filtration - Helping maintain lower ammonia and nitrate levels Size: 300ml / 1000ml Dosing Instructions: Shake well before use. Dose 10 mL per 40 L (approximately 10 gallons) of aquarium water. The 300 mL bottle cap measures 5 mL, while the 1000 mL bottle cap measures 10 mL. Important Note: Aeration is recommended while using Neo Booster Tropical. Overdosing may cause temporary cloudiness; if this occurs, perform a water change. Contains natural ingredients and may produce a slight odor, which is normal. Do not use while treating fish or shrimp for disease or illness. Shake well before use. Intended for aquarium use only. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Packaging Update: Aquario has updated the bottle design for this product. During this transition, you may receive either the previous plain white bottle or the new printed bottle shown in our product images. The formula and contents remain unchanged.

Recreate the natural benefits of blackwater environments with Aquario Neo Black Water Conditioner. Formulated with humic acid, fulvic acid, and beneficial trace elements, Neo Black helps create conditions favored by many tropical fish, shrimp, and aquatic plants. By naturally lowering aquarium pH, Neo Black helps recreate soft, slightly acidic water conditions found in many natural freshwater habitats. The natural ingredients may temporarily tint aquarium water, closely resembling the appearance of blackwater environments. Best For - Creating natural blackwater conditions - Tropical freshwater planted aquariums - Biotope aquariums Size: 300ml / 1000ml Dosing Instructions: Shake well before use. Dose 10 mL per 40 L (approximately 10 gallons) of aquarium water. The 300 mL bottle cap measures 5 mL, while the 1000 mL bottle cap measures 10 mL. Dosage can be increased gradually if a lower pH is desired. Monitor pH levels regularly. Important Note: Neo Black naturally lowers aquarium pH, though the amount will vary depending on your aquarium’s water chemistry. Helanthium Tenellum, sometimes referred to as Echinodorus Tenellus, is a grass-like aquatic plant that is commonly used for its carpeting tendencies. Its appearance is similar to other popular carpeting aquarium plants like Dwarf Hair Grass and Lilaeopsis Novaezelandiae (Micro Sword). It propagates by sending runners throughout the substrate! This carpet plant is generally easy to keep and will spread readily in most tank settings. We recommend using it as a foreground or midground choice, but it can also be planted as a unique background plant in nano aquariums. Like other plants that spread via runners, regular pruning will be necessary to control spread. High lighting and CO2 injection are not required to grow this variety, but will yield quicker and fuller growth. To plant it, start by separating larger mats into small portions. Use quality aquarium tweezers to plant each portion an inch or so apart halfway into the substrate. Use it by itself or combine it with other species for a wabi sabi mix of carpeting plants in your planted aquarium.

listings.commonName: UNS Glass Aquarium Stabilizing Tank Mat - White
listings.description: Stabilizing leveling mats are essential and strongly advised when having a planted aquarium tank. Fully filled planted tanks are quite heavy and most, if not all, the weight is placed on the bottom glass panel resulting in a good amount of stress. Premium rimless glass aquarium tanks are constructed to withstand this so long as the surface they are placed on is level. Unfortunately, this is not true in most cases and the use of a leveling mat is crucial to help offset and absorb surface imperfections that have the potential to crack the bottom glass panel via stress points. Stabilizing tank mats are cost-effective and prevent the worst from happening! These aquarium tank mats are made from premium, absorbent material to ensure your planted aquarium tank doesn't slip, slide or move during or after setup. Tested to withstand considerable turbulence, these aquarium stabilizing tank mats by Ultum Nature Systems are the perfect solution for your planted aquarium. They are sleek, cut to size and ready to place beneath most aquarium tanks. Enjoy peace of mind knowing your planted tank and its inhabitants are safe on their stand, counter, nightstand or console. Mat thickness is 5MM. TIP: These stabilizing mats will fit other rimless aquariums in similar sizing and may also be cut to size. These leveling mats are not meant to be used over small gaps. Please ensure your stand can fully hold your aquarium with no part of the aquarium hanging over the edge. Cutting any excess foam material will keep your setup looking clean! Be sure to use a sharp blade and handle with caution if the mat needs to be trimmed further.

Regular water changes are one of the most important parts of the aquarium hobby. This gravel vac attachment creates a gentle flow that won’t disturb your aquascape and helps prevent fish or shrimp from being sucked up during maintenance. The slender and sharp leaves of Anubias Congensis differentiates this particular Anubias from that of the much more common Barteri or Nana variants. Vesicularia Montagnei, more commonly known as Christmas Moss or X-mas Moss is arguably one of the most popular aquatic mosses commonly used in the planted aquarium hobby. Originating from Asia, Christmas Moss is closely related to Java Moss, another extremely popular aquatic moss, and is comparable in appearance with only slight differences in its fronds. Once established, Christmas Moss is a prolific grower and may require regular pruning to ensure it does not take over the aquarium. Manual removal is best, but if trimming is required, we recommend turning off filters and pumps to prevent the moss spreading to unwanted areas.

Trichomanes Javanicum, more commonly referred to as Borneo Fern, is a beautiful fern plant that is commonly used in terrarium, paludarium and vivarium settings. While it is commonly sold for aquarium-use, this fern is not a true aquatic species and is not suitable for long-term fully submerged aquarium conditions. Limnobium Laevigatum, commonly known as Amazon Frogbit, is a floating aquatic plant that is commonly seen in freshwater ponds. This aquarium floating plant is fantastic for providing coverage to skittish aquarium fish or in breeding aquariums containing fry or shrimplets. Amazon Frogbit also provides shade and a natural source of filtration to the aquarium, improving the overall health and cleanliness of the aquarium's water column. Amazon Frogbit is easily recognized for lily-like appearance, rounded leaves and bright green hue. This aquatic floater plant is great for use in nano planted tanks or in planted enclosures with lower water levels like paludariums. Frogbit is extremely beginner-friendly and requires minimal care, making it a great choice for new hobbyists. This listing comes with 5 individual pods. What we like about Amazon Frogbit Natural Habitat Enrichment: Amazon Frogbit provides a natural element and look to any planted setup. Frogbit is a wonderful choice for natural filtration and it helps to regulate excess nutrients in the water column by absorbing it through its robust root system. This aquatic floating plant also provides shade and coverage to reclusive aquatic species, improving comfort and well-being of livestock. Prolific Growth: Frogbit is known for its quick growth, making it easy to propagate and add to other aquarium setups. Hardy Nature: Amazon Frogbit is extremely hardy and will adapt to a wide range of aquarium conditions, making it a fantastic choice for beginner aquarists or anyone looking for some added texture and character in the planted aquarium.

listings.commonName: Chihiros RGB Vivid Mini LED Aquarium Light
listings.description: The Chihiros RGB Vivid Mini LED Aquarium Light is a compact, potent lighting solution designed for planted aquariums. Delivering strong RGB output, it provides intensity strong enough for light-loving plants while also supporting healthy growth and boosting the vibrancy of aquatic plant and livestock colors. Available in both a standard mount and pendant configuration, the Vivid Mini can be customized to suit different aquarium setups. The standard version offers classic, rim-mounted installation, while the pendant version includes a hanging kit for a clean, floating look right out of the box. Built-in Bluetooth connectivity allows full control through the MyChihiros app, making it easy to customize brightness, color spectrum, and lighting effects such as sunrise and sunset transitions. Choose Your Setup Standard Mount A rim-mounted setup that can be paired with optional accessories like a shade or hanging kit. Pendant Mount (Hanging Kit Included) A clean, suspended setup that Improves light spread and provides easier access during maintenance right out of the box. RGB Vivid Mini Highlights - Delivers powerful RGB lighting in a compact, space-saving body that is ideal for tighter spaces - App-Controlled customization via Bluetooth connectivity allows users to control and customize brightness, color balance, and effects like sunrise and sunset through the MyChihiros app - Optional remote access and expanded control beyond Bluetooth range when used with the WiFi Hub - Available in standard or pendant configurations to suit different aquarium layouts and aesthetic preferences Shown below is our Ultum Nature Systems 75S planted aquarium with the Chihiros RGB Vivid Mini (pendant) and additional light shade installed What’s Included - Chihiros RGB Vivid Mini LED Light - Hanging Kit (included with pendant mount option) The Vivid Mini offers a balance of power and flexibility in a compact form, making it ideal for smaller, high-tech planted aquariums. It delivers the intensity needed for demanding plants while allowing you to personalize your setup through mounting options and accessory pairings. Add fine, grassy texture to your aquascape with Echinodorus Tenellus Micro. Despite its name, this variety isn't necessarily "micro" depending on aquarium conditions and maintenance habits. Instead, it develops noticeably thinner, narrow leaf blades that grow from compact rosettes that can gain considerable height as they mature, creating a grassy appearance throughout the foreground and lower midground of a planted aquarium. Rather than forming a dense, traditional carpet, Echinodorus Tenellus Micro spreads through runners that develop into new rosettes around the mother plant. Its growth works especially well tucked around stone and driftwood, where individual clusters can soften hardscape and create a natural transition between planted areas. Echinodorus Tenellus Micro is relatively adaptable and can be grown without CO2 injection, although moderate lighting, consistent fertilization, and supplemental CO2 will support stronger growth. As runners spread, they can be trimmed and replanted to control placement or develop additional groups throughout the aquascape. Plant Name Note: Naming varies by grower. Depending on the selected tissue culture, this plant may arrive labeled Echinodorus tenellus 'Micro' or Helanthium tenellum ‘Micro’ . Black Star Lava Rock is a unique variation of the classic aquascaping stone, Black Lava Rock. Black Star Lava Rock features a uniquely rounded shape that is much smoother than other Lava Rock varieties. This characteristic makes the round aquarium stones great for scaping in tanks that contain livestock with sensitive fins such as Fancy Goldfish, Betta Fish and more. Black Star Lava Rock still sports a porous texture that will support a variety of aquarium plants that are commonly grown on aquarium hardscape. Black Star Lava Rock works great as a base stone with driftwood or alone. We recommend wrapping them with aquatic mosses for additional greenery wherever desired! Another benefit of having Black Star Lava Rock in a tank is its ideal habitat for the colonization of beneficial bacteria resulting in a healthier aquarium environment. The best thing about Black Star Lava Rock is that due to its relatively lightweight, you'll get more volume per pound.

White Elephant Skin Stone is a natural aquarium rock that features a mix of cream and beige tones rather than commonly seen grey colors. Its lighter color palette contrasts beautifully against vibrant aquatic plants, tropical fish and various aquarium substrates like sand, gravel, or soil with a full aquarium carpet. Its unique grooves and heavily textured surface provide a good foundation for attaching aquarium plants or aquatic mosses for extra detail and visual appeal. Whether you’re aquascaping and searching for aquarium hardscape or building a lush terrarium, White Elephant Skin Stone is a versatile, solid choice!

Dark Blue Slate is a flat stone that can be used for a variety of aquascaping styles, terrariums, vivariums, paludariums and more. Dark Blue Slate sports a deep color palette that becomes substantially darker when exposed to water. It is primarily a blue-ish charcoal color that includes random striations throughout. Its flatter shape makes it ideal for stacking, adding stability or creating a sturdy base underneath aquarium wood such as Malaysian Driftwood, Pacific Wood, Spider Wood and more. They can be broken down into smaller pieces and wrapped with aquarium mosses or used in other planted projects with ease.

Cryptocoryne Wendtii Sindoor is a new variety of Cryptocoryne derived from Cryptocoryne Wendtii Brown. Like other lab-created Cryptocoryne plants, Crypt Wendtii Sindoor was carefully monitored to ensure a stable mutation that produces a more consistent color and form. Cryptocoryne Wendtii Sindoor features a deep maroon hue that may include shades of lighter red, pink, green and brown. It is a suitable aquatic plant for midground placement in an aquascape layout. Care is assumed to be similar to other forms of Cryptocoryne Wendtii and include a nutritious aquarium substrate, low to moderate lighting and CO2 injection, if possible. Cryptocoryne species are known for their sensitivity to newly cycled tanks and drastic parameter changes. To reduce chances of Crypt melt, allow Wendtii Sindoor to establish a strong root system in a mature planted aquarium before attempting propagation or movement of the plant. Once established, propagate by gently separating plantlets from the mother plant and replanting into the soil. Add rich purple hues to your planted aquarium with Bacopa Salzmannii 'Purple', also known as Bacopa Araguaia or simply Bacopa Purple. Its rounded leaves can develop beautiful shades of pink, violet, and deep purple, creating a colorful contrast against surrounding green aquatic plants. With its upright growth and distinctive coloration, Bacopa Purple is an eye-catching addition to the midground or background of an aquascape. Interestingly, Bacopa Purple can look quite different depending on how it's grown. Its emersed foliage typically remains green, while submerged growth under certain aquarium conditions develops the purple tones this plant is known for. Its relatively adaptable, but stronger lighting, consistent fertilization, and supplemental CO2 help support healthier growth and richer coloration. Its moderate growth rate makes it manageable with regular trimming, while healthy stem cuttings can be replanted to create fuller bushes.

Aglaonema Simplex, sometimes known as the Malayan Sword, is a tropical aroid that is extremely adaptable and easy to care for. It tolerates general household conditions, and unlike many common houseplants, Aglaonema Simplex is a hidden gem for paludariums, ripariums, terrariums, and emersed aquarium growth where its roots can remain consistently moist while its foliage grows above the waterline. Its deep green color is beautiful and its slow growth habit makes it an excellent choice for adding structure, size and height to planted displays. Like other rhizome plants, the rhizome should remain exposed and not be completely buried, as this may cause the plant to rot. Over time, established plants can be divided by separating sections of the rhizome to create new plants. Care requirements are comparable to other popular aroids such as Anubias, Bucephalandra, and many Philodendron species.

This listing incluldes a healthy portion of Monte Carlo readily attached to a stainless steel sheet, allowing you to quickly place it in your aquarium securely. It will then eventually anchor itself into the substrate naturally. Monte Carlo is a popular carpeting foreground aquatic plant that is commonly used in Iwagumi aquascape layouts and a variety of other planted tank styles. Known for being an easier carpet plant, Monte Carlo is loved by hobbyists of all skill levels. This aquarium plant is fairly forgiving, will grow in a wider range of aquarium conditions, and can adapt to low-tech planted tank settings. Its appearance is comparable to HC, Hemianthus Callitrichoides, but is slightly larger and less fickle. It should be noted that it will take much longer to spread when planted in a low-tech aquarium and may stretch upwards if the lighting is insufficient. The addition of CO2 injection, medium to high lighting, and quality aquarium soil will produce a noticeable difference in the growth and appearance of Micranthemum Monte Carlo. Once established, Monte Carlo is a prolific grower and will require periodic trimming. Using advanced technology, Aquario's Neo Media provides fine, yet unobstructed large pores within the filter medium allowing a variety of beneficial bacteria to live and thrive. The generous space allows water to flow smoothly, delivering nutrients and oxygen to beneficial bacteria colonies. This results in a thriving bacterial ecosystem inside of the Neo Media, keeping filtration cycles stable and improving overall aquarium tank health. Neo Media by Aquario goes through a grueling 5 step manufacturer process in order to produce high-quality aquarium tank filter media and is available in three different forms, making it suitable for any aquarium tank. Instructions & Notes: Gently rinse with clean water 2-3 times. Do NOT wash excessively. PH changes can vary depending upon water source and objects inside the tank. Vesicularia Montagnei, more commonly known as Christmas Moss or X-mas Moss is arguably one of the most popular aquatic mosses commonly used in the planted aquarium hobby. Originating from Asia, Christmas Moss is closely related to Java Moss, another extremely popular aquatic moss, and is comparable in appearance with only slight differences in its fronds. Like other aquarium mosses, Christmas Moss is extremely hardy and versatile with usage. Aquarium moss provides excellent shade and coverage for shrimplets and skittish fish who commonly search for refuge. Alternatively, it can be used to mimic foliage on Bonsai-style driftwood or attached sparingly to other types of driftwood for an aged look in the planted tank. Aquarium moss may also be grown in emersed conditions or found wrapped as the base on Wabi Kusa setups! Aquarium Moss is a fantastic choice for beginner aquarists and will tolerate a wide range of aquarium conditions and water parameters. Once established, Christmas Moss is a prolific grower and may require regular pruning to ensure it does not take over the aquarium. Manual removal is best, but if trimming is required, we recommend turning off filters and pumps to prevent the moss spreading to unwanted areas.

Anubias Barteri Broad Leaf is a full-bodied variation of classic Barteri. Its large, rounded leaves develop a waxy sheen at maturity, creating a dense, lush appearance that’s perfect for filling open space in planted aquariums and aquascapes. Anubias are hardy aquatic plants, well-suited for a variety of freshwater setups. Their thick leaves also withstand nibbling from fish like fancy goldfish or cichlids. Its abundant foliage provides safe hiding spots for smaller fish and invertebrates. Epiphytic in nature, they can be easily attached to driftwood, rocks, or nestled into crevices in your layout. Alternatively, it would work beautifully in Wabi Kusa displays, terrariums, or emersed sections in paludariums. While not required, Anubias Barteri Broad Leaf does best in mature tanks and will benefit from CO2 injection and quality plant fertilizers.

Anubias Glabra is an easy aquarium plant for planted tanks and aquascaping! A moderately sized variety, we recommend this one for nearly any setup that needs some greenery. Its hardiness makes it adaptable to a variety of setups, including betta fish tanks, shrimp tanks, low tech planted aquariums and more. This particular variation features slender, spear-shaped leaves, providing a different look with the same easy care requirements. While not required, Anubias Glabra will enjoy and experience much better growth in a planted tank that is fully established and is provided with CO2 injection, quality planted aquarium soil, and quality lighting.

Anubias Hastifolia is a unique species of Anubias that is easily distinguished by arrow-shaped foliage, an uncommon characteristic for most Anubias plants. This variation of Anubias can be considered medium sized and requires the same minimal care requirements as other popular varieties of Anubias. Its easygoing nature and adaptability makes it great for beginner aquarium hobbyists. A solid choice! While not required, Anubias Hastifolia will enjoy and experience much better growth in a planted tank that is fully established and is provided with CO2 injection, quality planted aquarium soil, and quality lighting.

Microsorum Pteropus Philippine is a decorative Java Fern with vibrant green color. Hardy and adaptable, this aquatic fern is ideal for filling in empty spaces in a planted aquarium. Recently reclassified as Leptochilus pteropus , this plant is still widely known in the aquarium hobby as Microsorum pteropus. Like other Java Fern varieties, it is hardy and easy to care for, making it suitable for a wide range of planted aquarium setups. Whether you have a low light planted aquarium, or are looking for a broad-leafed plant to fill in the gaps between hardscape, Java Fern Philippine is a solid pick.

Microsorum pteropus ‘Latifolia’, commonly known as Java Fern Latifolia, is a larger-growing variation of Java Fern with broad, ruffled leaves and rich green coloration. Its size and fuller texture make it a great choice for filling in open space in larger planted aquariums or terrariums. Recently reclassified as Leptochilus pteropus , this plant is still widely known in the aquarium hobby as Microsorum pteropus. Like other Java Fern varieties, it is very hardy and easy to care for, making it a great option for beginners. It grows well in low to moderate lighting and adapts to a wide range of aquarium conditions. As an epiphytic plant, it can be attached to driftwood, rocks, or aquarium decor using thread or glue. Its larger size makes it especially useful as a background plant or focal point in aquascapes where additional coverage is needed. Be sure to keep the rhizome above the substrate to prevent rot. Propagation is simple and can be done by dividing the rhizome and reattaching as desired.

Hedyotis Salzmannii, also known as Oldenlandia Salzmannii, is a vibrant green aquatic stem plant that is relatively easy to care for and great for midground placement in planted aquariums. Hedyotis Salzmannii is smaller in size and provides a delicate look, adding textural interest and character to planted tanks. It is similar in appearance to Bacopa varieties and grows in a creeping manner. When properly cared for, Hedyotis Salzmannii is a relatively quick grower and can be manicured into compact bushes. When grown emersed, its leaves are rounder, chubbier and work well for paludariums and Wabi Kusa displays. The plant will produce white to light purple flowers from time to time.

Tiger Lotus isn't a plant that stays quietly in its corner. Nymphaea Zenkeri develops broad, lily-like leaves in varying shades of green, red-brown, pinkish red, and deep maroon, often marked with darker spotting that makes each new leaf a little different from the last. Given enough room, Tiger Lotus can develop into a substantial centerpiece with long stems that reach toward the water's surface. Allow them to grow for a more dramatic, natural appearance, or regularly trim taller growth to encourage the plant to stay fuller and more compact below the surface. If left unchecked, mature surface leaves can eventually shade aquatic plants growing underneath. Its size and distinctive foliage make Tiger Lotus especially well suited for larger planted aquariums and freshwater ponds where it has room to develop. Strong lighting, consistent fertilization, and a nutrient-rich substrate support healthy growth, while CO2 injection can be provided but isn't required.

Looking for a Complete Setup? Pair your B Series light with a matching shade or hanging kit to create the ideal lighting solution for your planted aquarium. Shop Chihiros B Series Light Kits Product Highlights - Adjustable Positioning - Improved Light Spread - Integrated Design & Improved Accessibility Important Information: Designed for use with the Chihiros B Series LED lights. Lighting fixture sold separately.

Anubias Mini Coin is a smaller species of Anubias that features petite, rounded foliage and bold green coloration. This softer leaf edge provides an ornamental look and the plant's smaller size is great for filling in the midground areas of a nano planted aquarium tank. Like all Anubias, Anubias Mini Coin is fairly easy to care for and will adapt well to a wide range of aquarium tank parameters and is generally hardy and comparable in care to other Anubias, Bucephalandra, Cryptocoryne and aquatic fern species. Overall, Anubias Mini Coin is a great aquatic plant choice to add to any planted aquarium tank or Anubias enthusiast's collection and will give a beautiful pop of contrast against alternative aquatic plant species and aquarium tank hardscape.

The Ultum Nature Systems Pro Check Valve is a practical piece of equipment designed to handle high pressure while preventing back flow of aquarium water into air pumps and CO2 regulators. Installing this accessory provides extra security and protection for other commonly used aquarium equipment. Made from aluminum alloy, the Pro Check Valve offers a clean aesthetic that complements the rest of Ultum Nature Systems' planted tank accessories. Why CO2 injection is important in a planted aquarium tank: 3 main factors contribute to the optimal growth of aquatic plants. These factors include nutrients, light and carbon dioxide (CO2). If any of these are unbalanced, the results are algae growth or the withering of aquatic plants. The introduction of CO2 in a planted aquarium tank allows aquatic plants to thrive and grow more efficiently, while also giving them the ability to outcompete algae for nutrients.

The Hygger Submersible Aquarium Heater is an ideal fish tank heater for nano aquariums and standard tank sizes up to 25 gallons. This aquarium heater features a slim profile with two strong suction cups for easy installation. Its flat profile and versatile orientation makes it easy to disguise in-tank, ensuring both minimal distraction and safe water temperatures for your livestock. The device provides accurate heating with a variable range of 1 °F and will automatically turn on / shut off once the desired temperature is met. Available in several sizes to accommodate aquariums ranging in size from 1 to 25 gallons. Hygger Aquarium Heater Highlights - Safety Features: The Submersible Aquarium Heater will operate and shut off once the desired temperature is reached. It also prevents operation in the event water levels fall below safe operating conditions. Its small and slim profile is ideal for Betta Fish Tanks and more! Help restore balance to your planted aquarium with Dr. Tank Algae Remover & Prevention. As part of the Dr. Tank treatment series, No. 5 helps treat and control many common types of freshwater algae, including green algae, brown algae, hair algae, green brush algae, and green spot algae. When used as directed, it provides an effective solution for managing algae blooms in freshwater and planted aquariums. Algae Remover & Prevention works best when used alongside good, consistent aquarium maintenance. Excess nutrients, inconsistent maintenance, and strong lighting can all contribute to algae growth. Best For - Managing common freshwater algae - Planted aquariums - Routine algae control and prevention Product Highlights - One bottle treats up to approximately 500 gallons Size: 100 tablets Dosing Instructions: 1 tablet treats approximately 5 gallons. Tablets may be dissolved in water to create a concentrated solution for spot treatment or added directly to the aquarium approximately one hour before scheduled maintenance or water changes. Follow all manufacturer dosing instructions and do not exceed the recommended dosage. Important Notes: Dr. Tank Algae Remover & Prevention is intended for freshwater aquariums only. Keep out of reach of children and pets, and store in a cool, dry place.

Spot treat and address stubborn Black Beard Algae! BBA Remover (No. 4) is designed to target Black Beard Algae (BBA), one of the most persistent algae found in freshwater planted aquariums. When used as directed, it provides an effective spot treatment for reducing stubborn algae growth. Does My Aquarium Have BBA? Black Beard Algae (BBA), also known as Black Brush Algae, is a stubborn type of red algae that can appear in planted aquariums. It can be identified by its short, fuzzy tufts that range from dark grey to black. You’ll often notice it growing on the edges of plant leaves, hardscape, aquarium equipment, and even larger substrate grains. It clings tightly to surfaces and can be difficult to remove. Best For - Black Beard Algae - Black Brush Algae - Freshwater planted aquariums Product Highlights - Designed to specifically target BBA Size: 50 tablets Dosing Instructions: Dissolve 1 tablet in approximately 20 mL of clean water. Turn off the aquarium filter and apply the solution directly to affected areas as a spot treatment. Refer to the product packaging for complete application instructions. Important Notes: Dr. Tank Algae BBA Remover is intended for freshwater aquariums only. Keep out of reach of children and pets, and store in a cool, dry place.

Hottonia Palustris (Water Violet) is a bright-green aquatic stem plant. Its fern-like leaves fan out, producing a bushy appearance rather quickly. It is a medium-sized stem, making it a great option for the midground area of an aquascape. Its ability to fill empty space with instant texture offers good coverage and a unique transition between different areas of planted tanks. Easy to care for and less common in the hobby, Hottonia palustris is sure to add texture and color to any planted aquarium. Enjoy a clearer view of your aquarium with Dr. Tank Crystal Water. Treatment No. 6 helps improve water clarity and aims to address cloudy, green, or discolored water. When used as directed, Crystal Water gradually works to restore clarity in freshwater planted aquariums. Crystal Water works best alongside routine aquarium maintenance. While it helps improve water clarity, it’s not a substitute for regular water changes, filter maintenance, or addressing underlying causes of clouded or discolored water. Used together, good habits help promote a healthier, more balanced ecosystem. Best For - Cloudy aquarium water - Green or discolored water - Planted aquariums Product Highlights - Slow-dissolve formula Size: 50 tablets Dosing Instructions: Add the recommended number of tablets directly to the aquarium based on your aquarium volume. Tablets dissolve gradually over approximately four hours. Refer to the product packaging for complete dosing instructions. Important Notes: Dr. Tank Crystal Water is intended for freshwater aquariums only. Keep out of reach of children and pets, and store in a cool, dry place.

Regain control of nuisance snail populations with Dr. Tank Snail Remover. Snail Remover (Treatment No. 7) is a targeted freshwater treatment that helps reduce common pest snails, including bladder and pond snails, without copper-based ingredients. When used as directed, snail populations can be significantly reduced within 72 hours. While Dr. Tank Snail Remover effectively controls existing snail populations, long-term prevention depends on good aquarium maintenance. Pest snails reproduce quickly when excess food and organic waste accumulate, making routine maintenance and careful feeding the best way to keep populations under control. Otherwise, a few pest snails are a natural part of the aquarium hobby and generally aren’t cause for concern. But fear not! We understand that many hobbyists simply prefer a snail-free aquarium. Best For - Controlling pest freshwater snail populations - Planted aquariums - Community aquariums Product Highlights - Copper-free formula - Helps reduce snail populations within 72 hours when used as directed - Simple tablet dosing with no measuring required Size: 50 tablets Dosing Instructions: Refer to the dosage instructions on the product packaging. Complete directions and precautions are provided by the manufacturer Important Notes: Dr. Tank Snail Remover is intended for freshwater aquariums only. Follow all recommended dosing and water change instructions. Keep out of reach of children and pets, and store in a cool, dry place.

This unique color palette makes it an excellent choice for aquascapers seeking uncommon hardscape options or for anyone aiming to recreate specific nature or themed scenes. Like other aquarium stones, Joro Stone isn’t limited to aquarium use; it can be arranged in terrariums or paludariums and paired with non-aquatic or smaller house plants. Whether combined with driftwood or used on its own, Joro Stone is a versatile addition to any setup!

Verdant Stone offers a distinctive look with its muted hues. Primarily a grey-blue, this stone is accented by grey-cream tones and occasional rust-colored specks, adding visual interest and character. Its natural shapes make it ideal for building a solid base for driftwood or for stacking and arranging in Iwagumi style aquascaping. With a texture similar to classic Seiryu Stone, Verdant Stone provides an excellent surface for attaching aquatic mosses and other plants. Suitable for aquariums, terrariums, or any planted setup!

Caledonia Stone is an aquarium stone that resembles a cross between Seiryu Stone and Elephant Skin Stone. It provides a marbled look with a mixture of grey, brown and cream tones. Its natural shape is more boulder-like, making it a great choice for creating aquascapes that need some height or for creating borders within the tank. Available in a variety of sizes to accommodate popular aquarium sizes.

Yukon Canyon stone is a beautiful choice for aquascaping! With shades that range from greys and rich golden browns to soft beiges, Yukon Canyon stone provides an earthy, natural appearance in planted tanks or terrariums. Its neutral color palette blends well with a variety of setups, making it an ideal base stone or accent for biotope-style tanks, nature style aquascapes, and even Iwagumi layouts. The semi-flat and rounded form of this stone allow for easy stacking and stable arrangement for aquatic plants and driftwood. Suitable for aquariums, terrariums, paludariums or any planted project! This natural aquarium rock will darken in color when submerged! Our live aquatic plant recommendations for Yukon Canyon Stone: - Top selling aquarium plants - Grass-like plants - Easy, low light aquatic plants - Epiphytic rhizome plants

Vallisneria Spiralis, commonly known as Straight Vallisneria, Jungle Val, Eelgrass, or Tape Grass, is a popular background aquarium plant. Favored in the aquascaping community for its graceful, flowing leaves and low-maintenance care, Vallisneria plants thrive with minimal attention, making it ideal for beginners and seasoned hobbyists alike. Although it doesn't require CO2 injection, adding CO2 can enhance its growth rate and resilience. To support healthy growth, use nutrient-rich aquarium soil or supplement with aquatic plant fertilizers or root tabs. Propagation is simple as it spreads via side shoots and is easily separated. Regular pruning is recommended as this species can grow to the height of your aquarium easily and will also anchor deep into the substrate if given the opportunity to do so.

Vallisneria Americana, also known as American Eelgrass, Water Celery, Eelgrass and Tape Grass, is a background plant commonly used in the aquascaping hobby. The aquatic plant features long strap-like leaves that sprout from stoloniferous clumps. Vallisneria are known for their height and relatively easy care, making them a popular choice for a range of skills. Like other Vals, Vallisneria Americana will appreciate a nutrient-dense aquarium soil and good lighting. These plants are not too finicky, and while CO2 is not required, the addition of it will help improve health and growth rate. Propagation is simple as it spreads via side shoots and is easily separated. Regular pruning is recommended as this species can grow to the height of your aquarium easily and will also anchor deep into the substrate if given the opportunity to do so.

Hygrophila Corymbosa Stricta, sometimes known as Nomaphila Stricta, is a beautiful plant species that originates from Thailand. This variation is a prolific grower that is extremely hardy, making it a great beginner plant. Hygrophila Corymbosa Stricta grows easily in terrarium and aquarium conditions, making it versatile with placement. An ideal aquatic plant for filling space in an aquascape or for anyone who enjoys dense growth with rich color. While it is not required, we encourage providing low to moderate CO2 levels to support optimal growth and overall health. In addition, aquatic plant nutrients and low to moderate lighting should be provided. Vallisneria Gigantea Rubra is a hardy, eye-catching background aquatiic plant that is commonly seen in larger aquariums and ponds. Similar to other forms of Vallisneria, this variation is known for its height and massive size. When grown with care, Vallisneria Gigantea Rubra will reach the water's surface with ease and eventually begin drooping over, creating shade and a natural background if not maintained. Propagation is simple as it spreads via side shoots and is easily separated. Regular pruning is recommended as this species can grow to the height of your aquarium easily and will also anchor deep into the substrate if given the opportunity to do so.

Patagonia Stone brings a unique look to planted tanks, terrariums and paludariums. Its primary color is a soft brown, and its texture resembles Lava Rock, with plenty of pores and crevices that are perfect for attaching aquatic plants or greening with aquarium moss. With its varied sizes and shapes, this aquarium rock can be stacked and arranged easily on its own or as a base for aquarium driftwood. Cueva Stone features a rich grey base color with random white-cream striations and specks of brown throughout. Its appearance is similar to popular aquascaping rocks like Ryuoh and Seiryu Stone. Like these classic layout materials, Cueva Stone offers aquascapers abundant texture and natural shapes that are wonderful for creating dynamic rockscapes and Iwagumi layouts. When submerged in aquariums, its colors deepen and create beautiful contrast when paired with bright green aquatic plants or vivid red stem plants. Try it out for your next planted tank, freshwater aquarium, terrarium, paludarium and more!

Ashen Stone is a unique aquarium rock! It offers a smooth texture, pale tones, and rounded shapes, making it ideal for simple aquascapes, river layouts, or bare-bottom aquariums like fancy goldfish tanks. Its light color pairs well with lush green aquatic plants, achieving a minimalist, less is more, balanced look. Our live aquatic plant recommendations for Ashen Stone: - Top selling aquarium plants - Grass-like plants - Easy, low light aquatic plants - Epiphytic rhizome plants

UNS Plant Food MAX is a concentrated liquid fertilizer designed to support demanding planted aquariums. Formulated with a complete blend of macro and micronutrients, it promotes stronger, faster aquatic plant growth. It is ideal for established setups with dense plant mass and higher lighting, as well as aquariums with nutrient-demanding plant species. As plants mature beyond the initial acclimation phase, it provides the consistent nutrient support needed for continued healthy growth. Safe for most freshwater fish and shrimp when used as directed, Plant Food MAX is a reliable solution for aquascapers who want vigorous, vibrant plant growth. Choosing Between Plant Food MAX and MIN Plant Food MAX is ideal for aquariums with dense plant growth, nutrient-demanding species, and setups with higher lighting and CO2 injection. For lightly planted tanks or setups with nutrient-rich substrates, Plant Food MIN offers a toned down approach to maintaining plant health and steady growth. Plant Food MAX Highlights - Ideal for heavily planted aquariums and nutrient-demanding plant species. - Designed for established setups with increased nutrient requirements. - Supports faster growth, vivid color and helps address nutrient deficiencies. - Best used in balanced systems with higher lighting and CO2 injection. - Crystallization may occur in colder temperatures due to the concentration of the formula and does not affect product quality or effectiveness. - Looking for a gentler approach? Check out UNS Plant Food MIN! Size: 500ml / 16.9FL Oz. Dosing Instructions: Add 1 pump per 5 gallons of water every other day. Perform a 30–50% weekly water change for best results. Plant Food MAX is a concentrated formula. To avoid excess nutrients in the water column, follow dosing instructions and maintain regular water changes. In unbalanced tanks or setups with existing algae, excess nutrients may contribute to more algae growth. Hakkai Stone, also known as Pa-Hai Stone, is a rare and popular aquascaping stone. Coveted for its unique characteristics, Hakkai Stone is unlike any other aquascaping stone available. Hakkai Stone displays a mixture of blue, grey and green-ish hues in-tank and sports a smooth, rounded shape with natural grooves earning its alternative name, Bug Eaten Stone. This aquascaping stone is highly coveted and falls on the rare side as its characteristics are the result from years of natural erosion making availability limited when compared to other aquascaping stone choices. On the density scale, Hakkai is one of the heaviest stones available on the market, increasing its rarity further. If you enjoy river scapes, river-style planted aquariums or Iwagumi layouts, Hakkai Stone is a top contender! We recommend pairing this stone with delicate aquarium plant species or grass-like aquatic plants for a calm, scenic planted aquarium. Hakkai Stone is very dense and will weigh more when compared to other stone choices. We recommend increasing the amount ordered, if possible, to receive a multiple stones and/or a larger variety of sizes. TIP 1: Use Hakkai aquarium stone for creating unique riverscapes and pairing it with softer, wispy aquatic plant choices such as Dwarf Hair Grass , Utricularia Graminifolia , Blyxa Japonica , Potamogeton Gayi and more.

Madra Wood is a new type of aquarium driftwood that resembles Malaysian Driftwood, featuring a warm brown color with intricate textures, knots, and crevices. It pairs beautifully with epiphytic aquatic plants like Anubias, Bucephalandra, and aquatic ferns such as Java Fern. Available in various sizes, Madra Wood can be used on its own or atop stones to create unique aquascape layouts. Beyond aesthetics, aquarium driftwood like Madra Wood offers benefits such as providing shelter and softening water, creating natural conditions favored by aquatic plants and tropical critters. The Akula Protein Skimmer features a unique threaded outlet body, allowing users to make precise and reliable adjustments. Akula models also feature an innovative Easy Flip seal, enabling effortless removal of parts for maintenance. Eliminate unwanted planaria in your aquarium with Dr. Tank Planarian Zero. Treatment No. 9 is formulated to target planaria before they become a threat to shrimp, fish eggs, and other small aquarium livestock. When used as directed, it provides an effective solution for controlling outbreaks in freshwater and planted aquariums. Dr. Tank Planarian Zero helps eliminate existing planaria, but for the best long-term results, pair treatment with consistent aquarium maintenance. Best For - Eliminating planaria in freshwater aquariums - Planted aquariums - Community aquariums Size: 50 tablets Dosing Instructions: 1 tablet treats approximately 3.3 gallons. Treatment can be administered for up to three days depending on the severity of the infestation. Do not exceed the recommended dosage. Important Notes: Dr. Tank Planarian Zero is intended for freshwater aquariums only. Follow all recommended dosing instructions provided by the manufacturer and do not exceed the recommended treatment duration. Keep out of reach of children and pets, and store in a cool, dry place.

Treat white spot disease with Dr. Tank Ich Treatment. Treatment No. 12 (White Spot Out) is formulated to help control Ich (Ichthyophthirius multifiliis) in freshwater aquariums. When used as directed, it supports the recovery of infected fish while helping maintain a healthy aquarium environment. For the best results, begin treatment as soon as signs of Ich are observed and follow all dosing instructions carefully. Raising the aquarium temperature during treatment may help accelerate the parasite’s life cycle, improving treatment effectiveness when appropriate for your livestock. Best For - Treating white spot disease (Ich) - Tropical fish - Freshwater community aquariums - Planted aquariums Product Highlights - Targets Ich - Safe for most fish, shrimp, snails, and live aquatic plants when used as directed - Results may be noticeable within 3-6 days Size: 60 tablets Dosing Instructions: 1 tablet treats approximately 3.3 gallons. Follow the dosage instructions provided on the product packaging. For best results, maintain the recommended treatment duration and consider increasing the aquarium temperature when appropriate for your livestock. Important Notes: Dr. Tank Ich Treatment is intended for freshwater aquariums only. Keep out of reach of children and pets, and store in a cool, dry place.

Address cyanobacteria with Dr. Tank BGA Zero. Treatment No. 8 is designed to help control blue-green algae (BGA), more accurately known as cyanobacteria, in freshwater planted aquariums. When used as directed, it provides effective support for managing existing algae and reducing spread through the rest of the aquarium. BGA Zero works best alongside good maintenance and by addressing the conditions that encourage cyanobacteria to develop. Poor circulation, excess nutrients, and organic waste can all contribute to outbreaks, making routine cleaning an important part of long-term prevention. Does My Aquarium Have BGA? Despite its name, blue-green algae (BGA) isn’t actually an algae! It’s a type of cyanobacteria that’s easy to identify. It typically appears as slimy mats that range from blue-green to dark green and can quickly spread across the substrate, aquatic plants, hardscape, and aquarium equipment. Unlike many common algae, BGA often peels away in large sections and has a distinctive smell. Best For - Blue-green algae (BGA) - Freshwater planted aquariums Product Highlights - Designed to specifically target BGA Size: 30 tablets Dosing Instructions: Refer to the dosage instructions provided on the product packaging. Follow all manufacturer directions and do not exceed the recommended dosage. Important Notes: Dr. Tank Algae BGA Zero is intended for freshwater aquariums only. Keep out of reach of children and pets, and store in a cool, dry place.

Vallisneria Contortionist, commonly referred to as Corkscrew Val, Contortion val, or Twisted Val, is a popular aquatic plant that is very adaptable and commonly seen in the background of freshwater planted aquariums. This Val plant is recognized by its distinctive foliage that is subtly spiraled. Vallisneria Plants, also known as Eelgrass and Tape Grass, are background aquatic plants known for their height and relatively easy care, making them a popular choice for a range of skills. Like other Vals, Vallisneria Contortionist will appreciate a nutrient-dense aquarium soil and good lighting. These plants are not too finicky, and while CO2 is not required, the addition of it will help improve health and growth rate. Propagation is simple as it spreads via side shoots and is easily separated. Regular pruning is recommended as this species can grow to the height of your aquarium easily and will also anchor deep into the substrate if given the opportunity to do so.

Mayaca Fluviatilis is a soft, bushy aquarium stem plant. Its foliage provides a delicate texture that pairs well with larger-leaved aquatic plants. Often called Stream Bogmoss, for its moss-like appearance, this versatile aquatic plant thrives in moderate to high lighting. Once established, Mayaca is a prolific grower and will create lush, dense bushes that offer coverage and natural hiding spots for tropical fish and shrimp. An excellent choice for aquarium enthusiasts who appreciate unique, feathery plants. Its compact size also makes it ideal for nano tanks. Shipped Size: Rhizome cutting with 2-3 leaves. Davallia Parvula is a wonderful miniature epiphytic fern that can be commonly seen in terrariums, paludariums and vivariums. Like other Davallia species, Davallia Parvula produces delicate fronds and exhibits a creeping, climbing growth pattern. Like most fern plants, Davallia requires high humidity to thrive, making it an excellent plant choice for tropical environments. While relatively slow-growing, Davallia Parvula rewards patient growers with lush foliage when provided with the right growing conditions. This fern prefers moderate to high intensity lighting, indirect misting and natural vertical growing space like cork bark or driftwood to climb. Unlike some moisture-loving plants, it does best in consistently humid conditions without being directly misted. Davallia Parvula is perfect for tropical enclosures, dart frog tanks, and tropical plant enthusiasts! Care Recommendations: - Light: Bright, indirect to moderate lighting - Humidity: High humidity (thrives in tropical enclosures) - Watering: Indirect misting - Substrate/Growing Medium: Natural surfaces like dritwood - Growth Pattern: Epiphytic, ideal for vertical terrarium backgrounds Common Name Davallia Parvula Fern Care Easy Lighting Moderate to High CO2 Required (Non-aquatic) Suggested Placement Vertical Growing Surfaces Propagation Separate Rhizome Growth Rate Slow Height Varies

Shipped Size: Rhizome cutting with 2-3 leaves. Davallia Repens is an ornamental, medium-sized epiphytic fern that adds lush greenery to tropical terrariums and vivariums. While this species of Davallia requires a bit more attention than some other species, its arching fronds and rich color makes it a rewarding choice for patient growers. Although naturally epiphytic, Davallia Repens thrives when provided with a small amount of substrate, such as orchid bark or long-fiber sphagnum moss, to lightly root into. Davallia Repens prefers moderate to low lighting and requires from high humidity and indirect watering as it does not tolerate prolonged water exposure on its leaves. Care Recommendations: Humidity: High humidity but more adaptable than other species Watering: Indirect misting Substrate/Growing Medium: Natural surfaces like dritwood, Aroid mix Growth Pattern: Epiphytic, ideal for vertical terrarium backgrounds
