The Pantanal form of Ludwigia Inclinata var. Verticillata is a rare and highly coveted aquatic plant. Like another advanced Ludwigia, Ludwigia Cuba, Pantanal develops dense, narrow submerged leaves that easily become a statement in a planted aquarium with its rich color. When compared to Ludwigia Inclinata Cuba, the Pantanal variety requires more intensive care. This rare aquarium stem needs high intensity lighting, CO2 supplementation, soft water and a well-balanced supply of both macro and micronutrients. If successful, propagation is simple through cuttings, similar to other aquarium stem plants. When grown in an emersed state, Ludwigia Inclinata var. Verticillata 'Pantanal' produces broader foliage and yellow flowers. Common Name Ludwigia Pantanal Ludwidgia Inclinata Verticillata Ludwigia Pantanal Meta Pantanal Ludwigia Care Advanced Lighting High CO2 Required Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate Height 8-15"+

Bolbitis Difformis ‘Mini' is a small leaf variation of Bolbitis Heudelotii or Heteroclita. This variation is relatively slow growing with ornamental foliage that adds interesting texture to any planted setup. Care requirements are comparable to Java Fern, Anubias and Bucephalandra species. Bolbitis Mini is an epiphytic species and will sprout new growth via fiddle leaf heads from its rhizomes. This plant can be attached directly onto driftwood or porous stone and will grow happily as long as nutrients are available. Larger plants can be propagated by dividing along the rhizome and replanting or reattaching onto wood or stone. A total of 2 pots of Mini Bolbitis were used in the 3 gallon planted aquarium tank below:

Microsorum pteropus ‘Soft Leaf’, commonly known as Java Fern Soft Leaf, is a popular aquarium plant valued for its ease of care and more delicate appearance. This variety is recognized for its thinner, softer leaves compared to standard Java Fern, giving it a slightly lighter, more refined look in planted aquariums. Recently reclassified as Leptochilus pteropus , this plant is still widely known in the aquarium hobby as Microsorum pteropus. Like other Java Fern varieties, it grows well in low to moderate lighting and adapts easily to a wide range of water parameters, making it a great choice for both beginners and experienced aquarists. Its moderate size allows it to fit naturally into both nano and larger planted aquariums. It pairs especially well with plants like Anubias and Bucephalandra, where its softer leaf texture adds contrast. As an epiphytic plant, it can be attached to driftwood, rocks, or aquarium decor using thread or glue. Be sure to keep the rhizome above the substrate to prevent rot. Java Fern Soft Leaf can also be grown in humid environments such as terrariums or paludariums. Propagation is simple—just divide the rhizome and reattach as needed.

This listing includes a mature, mother plant specimen. Anubias Barteri is a popular aquatic plant that is frequently used in all types of aquariums. Like other Anubias it can grow in a multitude of environments varying from aquariums to terrariums. Its stems are slightly longer when compared to Anubias Nana but the overall shape and characteristics are similar. This plant is suitable as a midground and background plant as the leaves are capable of growing up to 3” long. This variant is a flowering plant that grows best when the rhizome is attached to a hard surface such as wood or stone. It benefits from consistent fertilization but light requirements are minimal as its leaves are susceptible to algae growth when placed under high lighting. CO2 is optional, but can promote faster growth and robust leaves when used. Pot Size Comparison!

listings.commonName: Anubias Barteri Broad Leaf - Mother Plant
listings.description: This listing includes a mature, mother plant specimen. Anubias Barteri Broad Leaf is a variation of regular Anubias Barteri. While very similar, Broad Leaf produces leaves that are considerably larger with a waxy sheen when mature. Like other forms of Anubias, Anubias Barteri Broad Leaf is very hardy and will readily adapt to various aquarium conditions, making it popular amongst beginner aquarium hobbyists. This aquatic plant is rich green in color and its large size makes it great for filling in empty aquarium space. It is epiphytic and will grow well when attached to aquarium hardscape or placed in between crevices of the hardscape layout. Alternatively, Anubias plants are great for Wabi Kusa display and are also suitable for terrariums or emersed conditions. While not required, Anubias Barteri Broad Leaf will enjoy and experience much better growth in a planted tank that is fully established and is provided with CO2 injection, quality planted aquarium soil, and quality lighting. Pot Size Comparison!

This listing includes a mature, mother plant specimen. Anubias Congensis stands out with its slender, sharp leaves, distinguishing it from the more common Barteri or Nana variants. Its deep green color and leaf size make it ideal for the mid-ground of planted aquariums. Like other Anubias, it’s perfect for beginners due to its hardiness and easy care, thriving in both aquariums and terrariums. It's a flowering plant that grows best when the rhizome is attached to hardscape material such as wood or stone. Regular fertilization is favorable and low to medium lighting is sufficient as high lighting will promote the growth of algae on its leaves. CO2 is not required but promotes faster growth and robust leaves. Propagation is straightforward; simply cut or pull apart rhizomes to be reattached. Pot Size Comparison!

This listing includes a mature, mother plant specimen. Anubias Heterophylla is a classic Anubias species that offers a medium to large sizes Anubias in a planted aquarium tank. In its natural habitat, Anubias can be found growing on rocks close to stream edges partially emersed and submerged making it a great choice for both aquarium tanks and terrarium-like, emersed setups. Anubias Heterophylla, like most Anubias, is quite forgiving in nature and is easily loved by hobbyists of all skill levels due to its hardy nature and ability to adapt well to a wide range of aquarium tank parameters. A single Anubias Heterophylla Mother Plant was used in an Ultum Nature Systems R60 40 gallon aquarium below: Pot Size Comparison!

This listing includes a mature, mother plant specimen. Anubias plants are hardy and beginner-aquarist friendly! Remove this plant from its growing medium before planting. Click here to shop all aquarium plants! Anubias Lanceolata is a hardy species known for its large growth and easy care. Like other Anubias plants, Anubias Lanceolata is undemanding and adaptable to various water conditions. This variety features long, pointed leaves that set it apart from other popular Anubias plants. It is a slow grower, like others, and does well in low-light, low-tech planted tanks and similar setups. Like most Anubias, Anubias Lanceolata is quite forgiving in nature and is easily loved by hobbyists of all skill levels due to its hardy nature and ability to adapt well to a wide range of aquarium tank parameters. Like other Anubias, Bucephalandra and Java Ferns, Anubias Lanceolata does best when attached securely to aquarium hardscape such as aquascaping stones or aquarium driftwood. Alternatively, it can also be placed between cracks in an aquascape layout and it will attach itself overtime. Care should be taken to ensure its roots are not glued when attaching as this can promote the rotting of the plant. Anubias benefits from consistent fertilization but light requirements are minimal as its leaves are susceptible to algae growth when placed under high lighting. CO2 is optional but can promote faster growth and robust leaves when used. Pot Size Comparison!

This listing includes a mature, mother plant specimen. Anubias Minima is a variation within the Anubias family. Like other Anubias, it can grow in a multitude of environments varying from aquariums to terrariums. Anubias Minima features slender leaves with deep green coloration that is loved by planted tank hobbyists. This plant is suitable as a background aquatic plant as the leaves are capable of growing quite long. This Anubias variant is a flowering plant that grows best when the rhizome is attached to a hard surface such as wood or stone. It benefits from consistent fertilization but light requirements are minimal as its leaves are susceptible to algae growth when placed under high lighting. CO2 is optional but can promote faster growth and robust leaves when used. Pot Size Comparison!

This listing includes a mature, mother plant specimen. Anubias Barteri var. Nana or simply just Anubias Nana is well-known in the planted tank hobby for being one of the hardiest aquarium plant options. Like other Anubias, Anubias Nana is tolerant of a wide range of aquarium conditions and will adapt to most environments it is placed in. We recommend Anubias to aquascapers who are in search of easy aquatic plants that do not require CO2 injection but are as equally beautiful when compared to some of the more finicky aquatic plant species available in the hobby. Anubias has a well-earned bullet-proof reputation, but will appreciate a well-maintained environment with clean water, CO2 injection and low to medium lighting. Anubias Nana is an epiphytic plant! This means that it does not require being planted in soil to grow and will do best when attached to aquarium driftwood or in the crevices of an aquascape layout. Care should be taken to ensure the rhizome is not buried as this may cause the plant irreversible damage over time. When ready for propagation, this plant's rhizome can be split and reattached elsewhere. Pot Size Comparison!

Best when used as a mid-ground plant attached to stones or wood as an accent or centerpiece depending on tank size. Echinodorus Bleheri, well-known by its common name, simply Amazon Sword is an aquatic plant that is well known for its bright green coloration and behemoth size. Echinodorus Bleheri is generally easy to keep and great for beginners. Aquarium Sword species are heavy root feeders and so long as nutrient-rich quality aquarium substrate is provided, it will do well in a wide range of planted aquarium tank conditions. As mentioned, this aquatic plant can grow quite large and regular pruning will be necessary for allowing light to filter through to the aquatic plant's bottom leaves. We recommend this aquatic plant for beginners as well as experienced hobbyists who have larger aquarium tanks suitable for its size. Propagation is simple. Separate and replant. Pot Size Comparison! Homalomena Sekadau South is a sought-after tropical plant native to the rainforests of Sekadau and West Kalimantan, Borneo. A member of the Araceae family, Homalomena is a well-known genus in the aquarium hobby and is also highly popular among terrarium enthusiasts and houseplant collectors. These plants are typically low-maintenance and well-suited for various plant-related hobbies, including aquascaping, terrariums, paludariums, and vivariums, while also being popular as houseplants. Similar to popular aquatic plants like Anubias and Bucephalandra, Homalomena is relatively easy to care for and can be grown in varying conditions. This variety of Homalomena features dark green coloration and more slender leaves than the regular H. Sekadau South. Live, golfball-sized chaetomorpha macroalgae for saltwater refugium. This is a live, aquatic organism. May come with pods. For best practice, always quarantine any new arrivals, regardless of the source, to ensure the health of your tank. Chaetomorpha, commonly referred to as Chaeto, is a popular choice of macroalgae for reef tank refugiums. Its fibrous structure effectively absorbs excess nutrients, such as nitrates and phosphates, helping to maintain optimal water quality. Chaeto's fast growth and low-maintenance care make it a favorite among reef hobbyists looking for a simple, natural solution to nutrient management without the need for complex equipment. It also provides shelter for beneficial organisms like copepods and is visually appealing, with some hobbyists even choosing to keep a portion in the main display tank, as it is usually left untouched by most marine life. In summary, Chaeto is easy to grow and maintain with proper lighting, offering a straightforward way to support a balanced and healthy marine aquarium. Common Name Chaeto Chaetomorpha Chaetomorpha Linum Spaghetti Algae Care Easy Lighting Moderate to High Salinity 1.020-1.026 SG Temperature 72-80°F Growth Rate Moderate

listings.commonName: Dr. Tank Green Algae & Lime Scale Remover
listings.description: Support a cleaner view of your aquarium with Dr. Tank Green Algae & Lime Scale Remover! Treatment No. 11 helps remove green algae and mineral deposits from aquarium glass, hardscape, and other hard surfaces. Green algae and mineral deposits are a natural part of owning an aquarium. When used alongside routine maintenance, accumulated buildup becomes easier to remove, helping keep your planted aquarium looking its best. Best For - Green algae on aquarium glass - Lime scale and mineral deposits - Routine aquarium cleaning Size: 50 tablets Dosing Instructions: Dissolve 5 tablets in 100 mL of clean water. For lime scale, spray the solution directly onto affected areas and wipe clean. For green algae, lower the aquarium water level until the affected surfaces are exposed, apply the solution to affected areas, and let it to sit for a few minutes before cleaning. Refer to the product packaging for complete instructions. Important Notes: Dr. Tank Green Algae & Lime Scale Remover is intended for freshwater aquariums only. Keep out of reach of children and pets, and store in a cool, dry place.

Best For - Supporting beneficial bacteria - New planted aquariums - Established planted aquariums - Long-term substrate health Size: 15 sticks Dosing Instructions: Insert individual sticks approximately 1 inch into the substrate. Bucephalandra Sanggau Mini Wavy, sometimes known as Sanggau Green or Buce Sanggau Green Jade, is a small-leafed variety of Bucephalandra native to West Kalimantan, Indonesia. It features small, pointed leaves with a mixture of green tones. When grown in optimal conditions, this tiny Bucephalandra is a true gem, displaying the iridescent quality the species is known for. Like other Bucephalandra varieties, Sanggau Mini Wavy is a slow grower, gradually forming dense, compact clumps over time. Eleocharis Parvula, more commonly known as Hair Grass is a staple foreground plant that is commonly used to produce "carpets" in a variety of aquariums. This particular variety of Hair Grass is most commonly used in the foreground area of a planted tank but is also great for using along the midground of an aquascape for textural contrast and interest. Eleocharis Parvula features thin stalks that grow vertically from roots and will moderately spread via runners throughout the tank. High lighting and CO2 injection are not necessarily required to grow most Hair Grass plants but are highly recommended as it produces a highly noticeable difference in growth rate and overall lush factor. To plant, gently separate the plant into small portions and plant each portion an inch or so apart halfway into the substrate. Once established, regular trimming will be required as once it sends runners out, the plant grows quickly.

Anubias is a widely popular aquatic plant genus, favored for its adaptability and versatility. Anubias plants are frequently used in all types of aquariums and similar environments varying from terrariums to vivariums, paludariums and more. Available in various shapes, sizes, and colors, Anubias is a staple among aquarium hobbyists. Anubias does best when its rhizome is attached to hard surfaces like aquarium driftwood or stone. It requires minimal lighting, as excessive light can cause algae growth on its leaves. While CO2 is optional, we recommend it to boost growth and improve overall health resulting in more resilient foliage. Regular fertilization further supports healthy development, making Anubias a low-maintenance yet rewarding choice for any setup.

Ophiopogon Japonicus 'Pusillus' (Dwarf Mondo Grass) is a hardy and versatile plant that is ideal for terrariums and paludariums. listings.commonName: Microsorum Pteropus Java Fern - Mother Plant
listings.description: This listing includes a large, mature Java Fern mother plant specimen. These plants are well-established and offer immediate impact compared to smaller, newly propagated plants. Microsorum pteropus, commonly known as Java Fern, is a classic aquarium plant in the planted tank hobby. A fantastic choice for beginner aquarists, it has earned a reputation for being extremely hardy and able to tolerate a wide range of aquarium conditions. Recently reclassified as Leptochilus pteropus , this plant is still widely known in the aquarium hobby as Microsorum pteropus. Its bright green, broad foliage makes it ideal for filling in larger areas of an aquascape right away. As an epiphytic plant, Java Fern grows best when attached to driftwood, rocks, or placed into crevices within hardscape. Its larger size makes it especially useful as a focal point or for quickly establishing a more mature look in planted aquariums. Like most aquarium plants, it can be grown in low tech setups, though CO2 and added nutrients will improve growth and overall appearance. Be sure to keep the rhizome above the substrate to prevent rot. Propagation is easy—simply cut or divide the rhizome and reattach as needed. Pot Size Comparison!

Live, 1-1.5" portion of dragon's breath (Halymenia Durvillei) macroalgae for saltwater refugium. This is a live, aquatic organism. For best practice, always quarantine any new arrivals, regardless of the source, to ensure the health of your tank. Dragon's Breath Macro Algae (Halymenia) is a popular macroalgae, known for its vibrant red and purple hues and branchy, ribbon-like structure. Its tips often fork, giving it the distinct shape and texture that make it a favorite among reefers. Like other macroalgae, Dragon's Breath provides reliable nutrient export, making it a solid choice for the refugium, but is also equally popular as a decorative feature in main reef displays and dedicated macroalgae aquariums. For optimal growth, Dragon’s Breath thrives in moderate to high flow and, when used in a refugium, benefits from a tumbling motion under strong lighting. If being used in an ornametal way, it should be noted that herbivorous and omnivorous marine life may graze and consume it! A beautiful pop of color for your reef aquarium and a tasty snack. Keep some extra growing in your refugium, just in case! In summary, Dragon's Breath is easy to grow and requires less maintenance when compared to other faster growing macro algae varieties. It provides a straightforward way to support a balanced and healthy marine aquarium. Common Name Dragon's Breath Halymenia Durvillei Dragon Breath Macro Algae Dragon's Tongue Algae Care Easy Lighting Moderate to High Salinity 1.020-1.026 SG Temperature 72-80°F Growth Rate Moderate

The Ultum Nature Systems new line of Bonsai Tree driftwood features hand-crafted pieces that are carefully made by skilled artisans. The UNS Bonsai 001 features a waved style, perfect for creating sweeping aquascape layouts. Aquascaping with Bonsai Trees has become popular and offers numerous benefits to the planted aquarium. Each tree features distinctive features and can be embellished with a variety of popular aquatic plant species such as Anubias, Bucephalandra, Java Fern, Aquarium Moss and more. The addition of bonsai tree driftwood to the aquarium also softens water, provides shelter and a source of food for smaller aquarium critters like caridina shrimp and snails. Almost all driftwood is buoyant. Before use, we recommend allowing your UNS Bonsai Tree to thoroughly soak to ensure the tree is fully waterlogged. If this step is not preferred, simply attach a weight to the bonsai tree to ensure it is weighed down when the aquarium is filled. Aquarium driftwoods release tannins and will discolor aquarium water, giving it a tea colored tint. This is temporary and will reduce gradually over time as water changes are performed. Tannins are 100% natural, providing several benefits to the aquarium such as softening the water and emulating natural conditions of many tropical fish. If you do not like colored water, adding this product to your filter system will leave you with crystal clear water quickly! This variety of Red Ogo, commonly known as Red Spaghetti Ogo, gets its name from its resemblance to other ogo seaweed variations. True to its name, Red Spaghetti Ogo (Gracilaria Pacifica) features a deep red-brown hue and a stringy growth pattern. Its texture allows it to form dense mats that are capable of absorbing excess nutrients, supporting a more balanced ecosystem. Relatively easygoing, Red Ogo isn't difficult to grow and will require intermittent harvesting. Harvested Gracilaria will be readily accepted by herbivores in the main aquarium. Overall, Red Ogo Spaghetti Macroalgae is an excellent choice for saltwater refugiums, as it efficiently consumes excess nitrates and phosphates. It also adds unique texture to dedicated macroalgae aquariums. However, keep in mind that if the aquarium contains herbivores, this macroalgae is likely to be consumed! Red Spaghetti Ogo offers a simple and effective way to maintain a balanced and healthy marine aquarium. This new variation of Bacopa produces variegated growth with a range of green, cream and silver hues. Depending on tank conditions, Bacopa Platinum can provide a dense growth pattern and is a great choice for aquarium hobbyists in search of a unique midground or background aquatic plant. Suitable for most hobbyists, Bacopa Monnieri Platinum grows well with moderate to high lighting to support its variegated leaves. Bacopa plants are typically tolerant of many aquarium conditions and are resilient for most freshwater aquariums. However, for best results, we recommend providing this aquarium plant with nutrient-dense aquarium substrate, CO2 injection and a quality aquatic plant fertilizer . To achieve a bushy look, regular pruning of Bacopa Monnieri Platinum is necessary to encourage more compact growth, off-shoots and a fuller group of plants. Propagation can be done by trimming along its stem and replanting into the substrate.

Unlike many upright-growing Rotala varieties, Rotala mexicana 'Goias' is a compact aquatic stem plant known for its creeping, horizontal growth habit. Its narrow, pointed leaves develop shades of green, olive, and soft reddish-pink, creating delicate clusters of foliage that add color and uncommon texture to an aquascape. As the plant becomes established, new shoots may begin growing upward, forming low, bushy groups with a naturally sprawling appearance. Rotala Mexicana 'Goias' is an attractive choice for the foreground or midground, where it can be planted in groups around hardscape or alongside other aquatic plants. Moderate to high lighting, consistent fertilization, and supplemental CO2 injection are recommended to encourage healthy, compact growth. Regular trimming helps maintain its low-growing appearance, while healthy stem cuttings can be replanted to expand existing groups.

Bucephalandra sp. Sekadau Bukit Betung is a gem for your next planted aquarium. Great for rare plant hobbyists and buce collectors, this variety of Buce is recognized by its rich green color, slightly waved leaves and iridescent shimmer. Depending on aquarium conditions, Buce sp. Sekadau Bukit Betung produces varying shades of blue, purple, green and bronze when mature and healthy. Like other forms of Bucephalandra, this little buce plant is a hardy epiphyte and is versatile with placement in aquascapes. Attach it to driftwood, lava rocks or between cracks in the layout. It will slowly attach overtime and eventually create dense clumps that are great for both system health and providing coverage to smaller livestock within the tank.

Anubias Barteri ' Emerald Bloom' A lush variation of Anubias with broad heart-shaped leaves and rich emerald green tones. Anubias Barteri 'Emerald Bloom' is a form of Anubias that features large, heart-shaped, emerald green leaves. Similar to other Anubias plants, Anubias Emerald Bloom is an easy aquatic plant that is extremely hardy and suitable for a range of plant-related hobbies. Anubias Emerald Blooom can add both texture and visual interest in your planted aquarium tank, terrarium, paludarium or vivarium tank. Anubias plants are epiphytes and grow well when attached to driftwood, rocks or tank decor. These aquatic plants adapt well and thrive in low-tech setups making them a popular choice for beginners and experienced plant hobbyists alike. CO2 injection is optional for Anubias, but recommended to boost growth and overall health. Anubias offers reward with little risk! We recommend providing this aquarium plant with a light fertilizing routine, clean water, moderate lighting, and CO2 injection. Propagation is simple and can be done by simply cutting or pulling apart rhizomes to be reattached as desired.

Hygrophila Pinnatifida 'UK' (Uttara Kannada Variation) Hygrophila Pinnatifida 'UK' is a newer form of Hygrophila Pinnatifida that originates from the Uttara Kannada district in India. This Hygrophila plant displays more intense red tones and noticeably deeper serrration on its leaves. The foliage on this Hygrophila typically grow a little longer than the original, giving the aquarium plant a more dramatic and textured appearance in planted aquascapes. Shown belown is Hygrophila Pinnatifida 'UK' planted in a 16 gallon aquarium Like the original form of Hygrophila Pinnatifida, Hygrophila 'UK' doesn't differ too greatly in regard to care requirements and growing conditions. This Hygrophila plant needs moderate to high lighting, CO2 injection and a well rounded supply of quality micro and macro nutrients. You can propagate Hygrophila Pinnatifida by trimming along its stem and replanting it into the substrate. Hygrophila is versatile and can also be attached to aquarium hardscape such as stones and driftwood. Provide your Hygrophila Pinnatifida 'UK' with regular maintenance to keep growth compact and healthy. Common Name Hygrophila Pinnatifida Uttara Kannada Care Moderate Lighting Medium to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Midground - Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Moderate Height 5-8"

Lemna Minor, commonly known as Duckweed, is a fast-growing, resilient and low-maintenance floating aquatic plant. Its petite, bright green leaves add a delicate botanical look to any planted aquarium or pond. As its name implies, Duckweed is a top floating aquarium plant pick that is well-known for its rapid growth. This makes it a great addition to aquariums or ponds with a high bioload. Through its tiny root system, Duckweed happily absorbs excess nutrients and is as a great source of natural water filtration. Beyond supporting improved water quality, aquarium floaters also create a layer of coverage and extra security for a variety of aquarium and pond fish. Many fish species, such as fancy goldfish, will also enjoy snacking on Duckweed! For a beautiful, nature-style look in your planted tank or pond, try mixing duckweed with other floating plants like Pistia stratiotes (water lettuce) or Phyllanthus fluitans (red root floaters). What to do with excess Duckweed Duckweed grows quickly, so it’s important to harvest and thin it regularly to prevent overgrowth and shading of submerged plants that need light to grow. When disposing of excess duckweed, please avoid releasing it into local waterways, ponds, or down your plumbing. We recommend composting it or allowing it to dry out completely before discarding. It can also be incorporated into soil mixtures! Thank you for helping protect native ecosystems.

Natural Cholla Wood – Versatile Decor for Aquariums, Terrariums, and Reptile Tanks Natural Cholla Wood is an excellent addition to aquariums, terrariums, and reptile tank enclosures. Each piece of this unique driftwood features a hollow core and plenty of holes, creating ideal hiding spots and shelter for small animals such as freshwater shrimp and fry. In reptile tanks, these pieces are commonly used for reptile perches. Beyond its structural appeal, cholla wood serves functional purposes—in aquariums, it encourages the growth of biofilm, a valuable food source for freshwater shrimp, snails and other bottom dwellers. Cholla will also gradually releases beneficial tannins into the water, similar to Indian almond leaves, which can help lower pH and soften water conditions. Cholla wood is equally popular as a plant holder—typically used for Tillandsia (air plants) and other decorative setups. Compared to standard straight-cut pieces, these cholla driftwood trees provide more vertical structure and branching, making them an ideal focal point. Aciotis Acuminifolia Aciotis Acuminifolia is a rare and uncommon stem plant that can be grown in aquarium and terrarium conditions. It made its debut to the aquarium hobby in the early 2000's, but is still not commonly seen in aquascaping or similar hobbies today. This unique stem plant exhibits a strict vertical growth pattern with foliage that features prominent venation. This aquarium plant's color palette offers a mixture of green, red, orange and yellow tones that will vary and shift depending on the aquatic plant's growing conditions. When kept submerged in a planted tank, Aciotis Acuminifolia will develop vivid red undersides of its leaves. New growth presents lighter in color with upturned leaves that slowly fan out and flatten as the aquarium plant matures. Aciotis Acuminifolia is an aquatic stem plant that we recommend for planted aquarium hobbyists that have decent experience growing aquarium plants that fall within an intermediate to advanced level. Aciotis Acuminifolia is a moderately sized aquarium plant and will grow anywhere between 3-15 inches in height with a 2-3" spread, making it a good choice for a range of popular aquarium and terrarium tank sizes. Aciotis Acuminifolia requires soft water conditions, moderate to high lighting, CO2 injection and a quality aquatic plant fertilizer that offers both essential micro and macronutrients. If successful, Aciotis Acuminifolia can be propagated similarly to other aquarium stem plants by trimming along the stem and replanting in nutritious aquarium substrate. If preferred, Aciotis Acuminifolia is suitable for terrarium conditions too! Its emersed growth prompts the display of bold red colors, serrated leaf edges and pink flowers. Common Name Aciotis Acuminifolia Sao Francisco Irecienu Care Advanced Lighting Medium to High CO2 Required Suggested Placement Midground - Background Propagation Trim and replant plant stems Growth Rate Slow Height 3-15"

Bucephalandra Brownie Ghost is a lovely buce specimen that is characterized by its iridescent quality and deep brownish red and purple-blue tones that shimmer under aquarium LEDs. This gem-like aquarium plant is an epiphyte, like all Bucephalandra, and features compact growth with soft wavy leaves. When grown in clusters, Bucephalandra provide visual interest, delicate texture and also serve as coverage for smaller aquarium critters like freshwater shrimp and fry. These aquarium plants grow best when attached to natural materials like driftwood or aquarium stones. While Bucephalandra species are adaptable and hardy, they thrive best in stable, mature aquariums. Bucephalandra tolerates most water parameters, but a slightly lower pH is preferred. This can be achieved by using pH-lowering aquarium liquids, indian almond leaves (IAL) or adding natural driftwood to the tank. Bucephalandra Brownie Ghost and other varieties of Buce benefit from steady water temperatures, CO2 injection and good flow. When choosing where to plant Buce, avoid dead zones in the aquarium as poor circulation combined with excess nutrients may result in algae growth on its leaves. Propagation is simple and can be done by gently separating the rhizome and reattaching as desired.

Hygrophila Difformis Pink Pest-Free Tissue Culture Aquarium Plant Hygrophila Difformis, commonly known as Water Wisteria or Water Sprite, is a fast-growing aquarium stem plant. This aquarium plant is ideal for beginner aquarium hobbyists for its rapid growth, easy care and ability to provide a natural source of filtration for aquariums. When compared to other aquarium plants, Water Wisteria generally takes well, even in newly set up aquariums. Water Wisteria grows quickly by absorbing nutrients in the water. If nutrient levels are absent, this aquarium stem plant provides visible indication via poor color and growth. Otherwise, Hygrophila Difformis is a great choice for filling in empty spaces in aquascapes or for other applications such as breeding aquariums, rehab and quarantine tanks. Its fluffy form provides plenty of coverage and shade for small aquarium inhabitants. Hygrophila Difformis also works great in pond setups! Common Name Hygrophila Difformis Water Wisteria Water Sprite Care Easy Lighting Low to Medium CO2 Optional Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Fast Height 10+”

Eriocaulon species have become more popular and common in the planted aquarium hobby. Eriocaulon Buergerianum, like other popular Erio plants, grows best when provided with soft water, a nutrient rich aquasoil, high lighting and elevated CO2 levels. While some aquarium plants are known for obtaining nutrients through the water column, Eriocaulon absorb through their root systems, making the use of a quality aquarium substrate or aquatic plant fertilizer tab necessary for better chances of successful growth. Proper growth for Eriocaulon presents as white and firm roots along with rate of new growth and overall uniformity. Eriocaulon species tend to grow in an organized manner and greying roots with lopsided growth may indicate poor health. Once familiar with Eriocaulon care and growth, these aquarium plants are moderate growers and can be split carefully. This family of aquatic plants are a solid choice for midground placement in mature aquascapes. Eriocaulon provide excellent texture and compact, tufted growth that is loved by many aquarists.

Cryptocoryne Spiralis 'Tiger' Cryptocoryne Spiralis 'Tiger' is a unique aquarium plant that features long ribbon-like leaves with a striped pattern that earns its name. Similar to other long leafed Cryptocoryne plants, Cryptoroyne Spiralis Tiger is an ideal aquarium plant for the midground to background area of a planted aquarium. Its vertical height combined with its mixture of reddish-brown to olive green leaves provides movement and a blended transition to other areas of a planted aquarium. Overall, Cryptocoryne Spiralis Tiger is a great choice for jungle-style or biotope inspired aquascapes. Cryptocoryne aquarium plants have a repuation for being easy care plants—this is true when the plant is mature and has developed a strong, healthy root system. In the beginning stages, Cryptocoryne plants can be susceptible to melt if moved too frequently or water conditions aren't stable. To mitigate effects, we recommend planting Cryptocoryne Spiralis Tiger (and other crypt plants) in an established, cycled aquarium when possible. Supplement this aquarium plant with moderate lighting and quality aquarium soil or aquatic plant root tabs if using sand / gravel. Additionally, CO2 injection and aquarium plant fertilizer will benefit all aquarium plants long term. When established and growing well, increasing lighting levels will help boost color! A great Crypt plant for hobbyists in search of a unique aquarium plant!

Male Galaxy Koi Betta Splendens (Betta Fish) Galaxy Koi Bettas have the marble gene variant and are known for their color-changing patterns. This gives each betta a unique personal color palette and marbled appearance that evolves over time, making each individual fish one-of-a-kind. The Koi Galaxy Betta often features a Halfmoon Plakat (HMPK) tail type, offering several advantages such as improved swimming ability and reduced fin nipping. Overall, Betta Splendens are a top fish pick for many aquarium hobbyists! Keep reading to learn more about Bettas. Sex: Male Type: Halfmoon Plakat (HMPK) Galaxy Koi Male Size: 2-3" Color/Pattern: Breeder's choice - May include shades of blue, red, orange, yellow, purple and more. Quick Introduction to Betta Fish Betta Splendens, commonly known as Betta fish or Siamese fighting fish, belong to a genus that includes over 70 recognized species. Popular for beginners, Bettas are often picked as a first pet fish thanks to their vivid color, interactive behavior and easy care. They are also great for those with limited space, as they don’t require large aquariums to thrive. While Bettas are generally hardy, this also makes them commonly mistreated. To help your Betta live a healthy and happy life, we’ve put together essential Betta fish care tips and tricks! How to care for Betta Fish The first step in proper Betta fish care is maintaining good water conditions. These fun fish prefer slightly acidic water around 6.8, but will tolerate a range between 6-8. In the wild, Bettas live in waters that are rich in organic matter that contribute to this preference. To emulate similar conditions, consider using materials in your aquarium tank that will naturally help lower pH. We like using natural driftwood or Indian Almond Leaves (IAL) to help gently lower pH levels. In addition, maintaining a clean and well-kept aquarium is essential. Always keep a dechlorinator to ensure chlorine and heavy metals are removed during routine water changes and tank maintenance. What type of filter does a Betta need? Quality aquarium filtration is key for all freshwater fish, and should never be overlooked. Modern Betta varieties are often bred to have large fins, which contribute to poor swimming and sensitivity to strong currents. Avoid aquarium filters that produce strong direct flow. Instead, opt for filters or outflow attachments that diffuse water to provide your betta with gentle flow. Ideal water temperature for Betta fish Betta fish originate from warm, tropical regions where temperatures range between 76°F and 80°F. Water that is too cold or too hot can lead to poor health, sluggish behavior and a weakened immune system. Bonus Betta Care Tips - Add live aquarium plants! Betta fish love to forage, explore and will greatly appreciate some coverage. Live aquatic plants also help with water oxygenation and purification. - Daily exercise. Use a reflective surface to encourage a good flare. Consistency helps your Betta stay strong and active. - Use an aquarium lid. Bettas are great jumpers, so a tank lid is recommended. Avoid sealed fits as Bettas need to come to the surface for air. Want to learn more about Betta fish care? Check out our blog for in-depth guides Part 1 - Tank setup, water preparation, aquarium cycling, filtration, heating, live plants and decor. Part 2 - Tank maintenance, Betta food, flare exercises, recommended tank mates, natural supplements, remedies, illnesses, diseases, medication and short overview.

Azolla Caroliniana (Mosquito Fern) Azolla is a small, fast-growing floating aquatic plant that forms dense surface coverage in planted tanks and pond setups. Also known as Mosquito or Water Fern, it’s a popular choice amongst aquarium hobbyists and pond enthusiasts. Its tiny overlapping leaves resemble miniature water ferns, making it a great option for anyone in search of a unique, low-tech floater. Azolla is primarily green, but can produce a reddish-purple hue when kept under high lighting. It is a very fast-growing plant that will require periodic harvesting to prevent light blockage. Floating plants offer several benefits such as algae control, improved water quality and a sense of security for tropical fish. Portion Size: 2" patch

Samolus Parviflorus Red (Lysimachia Parvifolia) Samolus Parviflorus ‘Red’ (also known as Lysimachia parvifolia) is a hardy, low-growing red aquarium plant ideal for the midground of a planted tank. When provided with moderate to high lighting and a nutrient-rich substrate, its leaves develop soft reddish-orange tones and a rounded, chubby shape. While it adapts well to low-tech aquariums without CO2, its growth form will be noticeably different with thinner, greener leaves. With a moderate growth rate, Samolus parviflorus ‘Red’ requires periodic trimming but is much easier to manage than faster-growing stem plants. Its forgiving nature, unique appearance, and soft color make it a great choice for aquascapers looking to add red tones without the extra care demands of more sensitive species. Common Name Samolus Parviflorus 'Red' Care Easy Lighting Moderate CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Midground Propagation Separate and replant Growth Rate Moderate

Rotala sp. 'Myanmar' Rotala is a diverse genus of aquarium stem plants that are loved for their vivid coloration, fast growth, and versatility in plant related hobbies. These plants feature delicate leaves that come in a myriad of colors including bright green, orange, red and pink tones. A classic name in the planted tank hobby, there is a Rotala for every aquascape. The most commonly known types like Rotala Rotundifolia and Indica, feature many cultivars within their respective groups. These aquatic stem plants are fairly adaptable, but grow best in planted tanks with CO2 injection, moderate to high lighting and nutrient-rich waters. When conditions are optimal, consistent maintenance is required to maintain a manicured look or to achieve the coveted bushy appearance. Once established, Rotala can be easily propagated by trimming its stems and replanting. Most species can also grow in emersed conditions, making them suitable for Wabi Kusa setups and terrariums! Common Name Rotala sp. Care Moderate Lighting Moderate to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Midground to Background Propagation Trim and replant Growth Rate Fast

Mopani Wood is a dense African hardwood commonly used in aquariums, paludariums, and terrariums. Its substantial weight and dense composition allow it to sink much more quickly than many traditional driftwoods, making it a popular choice for hobbyists who want less downtime spent waterlogging and more time building their layout. Known for its distinctive two-tone coloration, Mopani Wood features bold brown hues, natural knots, and gnarled texture that double as rich character and prime planting points. It’s super durable and resistant to decomposition, making it one of the longest-lasting natural woods available. It is a heavy tannin-releasing wood, so if tea-colored aquarium water isn’t up your alley, consider pre-soaking in advance. Best For - Aquascapers looking for wood that sinks quickly - Long-term hardscape layouts - African biotopes and Blackwater aquariums Natural Variation Mopani Wood is a natural wood and each piece is unique. Variations in shape, structure, coloration, and overall dimensions are normal and part of what makes each piece one of a kind. Custom size and shape requests cannot be guaranteed. Please use listed dimensions as general guidelines when selecting a size. All hardscape sales are final unless an incorrect item has been received. Size Dimensions S 7-10” M 10-16” L 16-22”

Persicaria Praetermissa, misidentified as Polygonum sp. 'Ruby', is a water knotweed that can be found growing in marginal conditions in tropical areas of Asia and Australia. This plant typically grows along the edges of wetlands, but can be cultivated under water. When grown in an aquarium, it takes on an entirely different form. Its leaves take on a slender shape with pointed tips and displays a mix of brownish-red and orange hues. If you're searching for a unique plant that can be grown multiple ways, try it out! Persicaria Praetermissa can be used in nature-style planted tanks or as an accent plant for your Wabi Kusa or emersed portion of your paludarium. It offers rich color and relatively easy care, making it a great choice for various aquascaping styles. Provide it with moderate to strong lighting, nutrients and CO2 injection if planting in your aquarium. Persicaria Praetermissa in our UNS 90L 20 gallon Iwagumi aquascape: Common Name Persicaria Praetermissa Rubra / Ruby Care Moderate Lighting Moderate to High CO2 Required Aquascape Placement Midground to Background Propagation Trim and replant Growth Rate Fast

Dipteracanthus Elastica is a low-profile terrestrial plant that's fantastic for all-purpose coverage in terrariums and similar planted setups. It may be easier to remember this one by some of its common names like bubble plant or popcorn plant! It earns these nicknames thanks to its small, round, puckered leaves. The bubble plant also features a naturally dense growth structure, providing an instantly lush look in exchange for minimal effort. Like most terrarium plants, Diptercanthus Elastica will appreciate good humidity levels and low to moderate lighting. Avoid placing it under strong direct lights to prevent burning it! If you're searching for an oddball plant for your terrarium, container garden or paludarium, try adding a Bubble Plant. Its rich green color, paired with its fun texture, is sure to add visual interest—and bonus! When the plant is happy, it may even bloom violet-blue flowers. Common Name Bubble Plant / Dipteracanthus Elastica Care Easy Lighting Low to moderate CO2 Required Suggested Placement Enclosed terrariums, paludariums Propagation Separate and replant Growth Rate Slow to moderate

Bucephalandra may not be the first plant that comes to mind when thinking about beginner-friendly aquarium plants, but it's on par with Anubias and Java Ferns! Buce for short, these aquatic rhizomes often feature iridescent leaves and are very easy to care for. They grow well in low lighting and come in a variety of sizes that are great for nano tanks or larger aquariums. While Bucephalandra is very forgiving, their growth and appearance is noticeabley different (in a good way) when you get the hang of caring for them. When happy and healthy, Bucephalandra easily becomes a focal point in a planted tank and it becomes easy to understand why so many aquarium hobbyists love these plants. While there is little specific information on sp. Sekadau Giant Blue, we imagine this aquarium epiphyte could very well surprise you and become one of your favorites.

Eriocaulon plants have become more prevalent in the planted tank hobby. With different plant hobbies becoming closer, many aquarists have started integrating terrestrial and marginal plant species into hybrid tanks. Eriocaulon Aquaticum lands into that section perfectly! In natural settings, this plant can be found growing along the water's edge of bogs and wetlands, making it adaptable and suitable for both submerged and emersed growth. Its rosette form offers structure and easy maintenance given its non-chaotic growth. So, if your planted tank or paludarium is in need of a grass-like plant that provides texture but won't take over like regular hair grass varieties, Eriocaulon might be the move. However, we'll throw caution to beginners! Like other species in the family, Eriocaulon Aquaticum is recommended for more experienced aquarium hobbyists. These plants need specific care that isn't difficult, but requires good understanding of water parameters, nutrition and lighting. If your Eriocaulon plant is growing happy, it will have white, firm roots and consistent uniform growth. Overall, Eriocaulon provide beautiful texture and neat, tufted growth that is loved by many aquarists.

Live portion of Sea Lettuce macroalgae. For best practice, always quarantine any new arrivals, regardless of the source, to ensure the health of your tank. Ulva Lactuca is a nutritious and easy to grow macroalgae for saltwater aquariums. Better known as Sea Lettuce, it is recognized by its bright green color and delicate structure that is semi-translucent throughout. Macroalgae use in marine tanks is commonly associated with nutrient export in refugiums, thanks to popular types like Chaeto or Dragon’s Breath. However, this super seaweed offers a different benefit: It is fast growing and nutritious. These qualities make it a solid, natural food to have on hand that most saltwater invertebrates and fish will happily snack on. It is also relatively hardy so long as it’s provided with strong lighting and moderate flow. When feeding, it’s best to offer it directly or use a device to keep it contained. The same goes for growing Sea Lettuce. Separate holding tanks or buckets are recommended since it can spread easily and root in the main aquarium display. Common Name Sea Lettuce / Ulva Seaweed Care Easy Lighting Moderate to High Salinity 1.020-1.025 SG Temperature 72-80°F Growth Rate Fast

Support healthy root development with Dr. Tank Substrate Root Fertilizer. As part of the Dr. Tank Nutritional Series, No. 0 slowly releases macro nutrients and trace elements directly into the substrate, providing up to two months of nutrition for rooted aquatic plants. Substrate Root Fertilizer is ideal for established planted aquariums where aquasoil may have become nutrient depleted, new setups that would benefit from a nutrient-rich base, or aquascapes using substrates that do not naturally contain nutrients. Best For - Nutrient-depleted aquasoil - Heavy root-feeding aquatic plants like Echinodorus and Cryptocoryne - Established planted aquariums Size: 30 tablets Dosing Instructions: Insert tablets directly into the substrate near heavy root-feeding aquatic plants. Refer to the product packaging for complete placement and instructions. Important Notes: Dr. Tank Substrate Root Fertilizer is intended for freshwater aquariums only. Keep out of reach of children and pets, and store in a cool, dry place.

Support healthy aquatic plant growth with Dr. Tank Iron Sticks. As part of the Dr. Tank Plant Nutrition Series, these slow-release substrate sticks provide iron (Fe), an essential micronutrient that supports chlorophyll production and photosynthesis. Healthy iron levels help aquatic plants efficiently use available light, supporting faster growth, resilience and vibrant foliage. Iron Sticks are ideal for planted aquariums using sand or gravel, or for aquariums that would benefit from additional iron supplementation. While iron plays an important role in plant health, it works best as part of a balanced fertilization routine and should not be the sole source of plant nutrition. Best For - Iron supplementation - Aquatic plants showing symptoms of iron deficiency Size: 15 sticks Dosing Instructions: Insert sticks directly into the substrate. Refer to product packaging for complete placement and use instructions. Important Notes: Dr. Tank Iron Sticks are intended for freshwater aquariums only. Keep out of reach of children and pets, and store in a cool, dry place.

Anubias Barteri is a wonderful aquarium rhizome plant that is commonly used in low light tanks. The cultivar 'Round Leaf' features chubby, spade-shaped leaves with noticeable veins throughout. Its ability to grow in low tech aquariums and general hardiness makes it popular amongst beginner hobbyists. It is very forgiving of many water conditions and still looks great without extensive or complicated care. Most Anubias are evergreen and provides rich color to freshwater planted tanks or terrariums.

Cryptocoryne Thwaitesii 'Kirindoya Brown' is a slow-growing aquatic plant that features textured, olive-brown tones and slightly ruffled leaves. Like other species in the same family, Cryptocoryne plants are fairly undemanding and don't require special care to grow properly. They are most commonly used as a midground aquarium plant in aquascapes due to their moderate size and low profile growth. When given the correct care, it will form dense tufts of foliage that will add a lovely touch to any planted aquarium. With all plants, we recommend using a quality aquarium LED light, CO2 injection and nutrient dense aquasoil to yield the best results. If your soil is low in nutrients, consider adding an all-purpose liquid fertilizer to support improved color and form. To propagate, simply cut off new plantlets growing from the mother rhizome.

Homalomena Sub Hasei Homalomena Sub Hasei is flowering plant genus in the aroid family. This particular species features a super unique look with its forest-green leaves that are covered in little hair-like spikes—an awesome pick for plant collectors who enjoy oddball plants! In general, most Homalomena plants appreciate warm, humid conditions with moderate lighting that is preferably indirect or filtered. They are pretty easy to care for and provide extra beautiful texture and interest with little effort. Plant your Homalomena in consistently moist aquasoil, provide it with plant food, keep humidity levels elevated and most will grow just fine! They’re great terrarium plants that are versatile with some being adaptable to fully submerged planted aquarium conditions! Common Name Homalomena Sub Hasei Care Moderate Lighting Moderate CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Terrariums or Paludariums Propagation Separate and replant Growth Rate Slow Height Varies

Bucephalandra, or Buce for short, can get overlooked when thinking about the best beginner plants—but these beautiful aquatic plants are easy to care for just like Anubias or Java Fern! They’re also generous with looks and often feature iridescent, speckled leaves that shimmers in a freshwater planted aquarium. With a wide range of species available to the aquarium community, Buce is a solid choice for everything from a nano tank to standard sized aquariums. Artemis is no different. It features subtle color that shines under aquarium LEDS. Its slightly waved leaves will add movement to your tank while giving small tropical livestock a place to rest or hide. Like other species, it is an easy care plant and can be planted in low light tanks with little fuss. If you want quicker results, add your buce to a high tech setup with CO2, moderate lighting and nutrients.

Bucephalandra Brownie Kapuas is a small variety that has deep, dark brown (nearly black!) leaves with an iridescent bluish-purple sheen when placed under quality aquarium LED lights. It is a small-leafed buce that is perfect for nano tanks or detailed work in larger planted aquariums. It grows slowly, but in a naturally dense manner that will eventually create patches of buce in your aquascape. Most Bucephalandra plants are low maintenance and will be fine in low light tanks. However, growth speed, form and color are significantly improved when these plants are given a little more TLC. When happy, its easy to see why bucephalandra has a loyal fanbase. These aquatic plants are some of the most eye-catching species in planted aquaria.

Bucephalandra are low maintenance aquatic plants that are similar to Anubias and other aquarium rhizomes. They often feature varying hues that change depending on light fixtures and viewing angle. This quality makes them a highly-coveted species amongst aquarists. They're ideal for planted tanks of all sizes and can also be planted in terrariums or high-humidity planted setups. Attach them to your favorite driftwood or stone and place in your tank as desired. Like other species, buce brownie purple offers easy care and can be added to low light tanks or high tech tanks. If planted in a low tech without CO2, keep the lighting low and ensure consistent maintenance is performed to prevent algae growth on leaves. For quicker growth and better color, CO2 injection, moderate light exposure and a quality liquid aquariumn plant fertilizer will produce noticeable differences.

Rotala Rotundifolia 'Shimoga' is an aquarium stem plant that stands out! This variation features slightly translucent, soft green leaves that curl upward to reveal baby pink undersides. Its a medium-sized Rotala that grows upright. This quality makes it a great background plant for standard to large planted aquariums. With its distinctive leaf shape and palette, Rotala Shimoga is a great aquarium plant that provides texture and pops of color to any aquascape. For the best form and color, plant it in a tank it with CO2, moderate to high lighting and a nutrient-rich aquasoil. Once established, try adding root tabs or liquid aquatic plant fertilizers for essential micro and macronutrients. You'll know your Rotala is happy when it starts growing fast and needs regular trimming. On the bright side, you can replant cuttings to achieve healthy bushes, start another planted tank or share! Common Name Rotala sp. 'Shimoga' Care Moderate Lighting Medium to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Fast Height 15+"

Myriophyllum elatinoides ‘Snowflake’ is a beautiful aquarium plant that features fine, feather-like leaves that fan out in patterns similar to snowflakes! Its form and rich green color bring natural texture and softness, making it a great choice for planted tanks and aquascapers who enjoy mixing and matching different aquarium stem plants. A fast-growing stem plant, Myrio plants are great for the midground or background of planted aquariums, where they have plenty of room to grow tall and sway with the flow. If you have a pond, the top-down view of this Myrio plant is special, and we highly recommend giving it a try. General care for Myriophyllum stem plants includes moderate to high light, CO₂ injection, and nutrient-rich aquasoil. When happy, you’ll need to trim it regularly. Replant healthy tops, and soon enough, you’ll have dense, feathery bushes in your planted tank or pond—your rice fish, tropical school, or shrimp will love it too. Overall, this aquarium plant is a solid pick for aquascaping, especially nature-style planted tanks, indoor ponds, or Dutch-style aquascape layouts! Common Name Myriophyllum / Watermilfoil Care Moderate Lighting Medium to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Midground to Background Propagation Trim and replant stems Growth Rate Fast Height 6-12"

Myriophyllum sp. ‘Roraima’ is a large, colorful aquatic stem plant. This special milfoil is best suited for bigger planted aquariums, where its needle-like leaves and intense colors can really shine in the background of an aquascape. The ‘Roraima Milfoil’ is a cultivar within the Myriophyllum genus that’s considered one of the easier types to care for—and it doesn’t fall short in the looks department. When grown in a healthy aquarium, its feathery whorls develop a vivid color palette that includes orange, yellow and deep red hues. It is a fast-growing aquatic stem plant that branches naturally and responds well to routine pruning. To get the best growth, provide this red aquarium stem plant with strong lighting, CO2 injection, and a well-rounded dosing regimen that includes both micro and macronutrients. With patience and consistent care, Myriophyllum sp. ‘Roraima’ brings color, texture and height to any aquascape. It’s a great fit for nature-style planted tanks, dutch-style aquascapes or large-scale freshwater ponds. Common Name Myriophyllum / Watermilfoil Care Easy to Moderate Lighting Medium to High CO2 Recommended Suggested Placement Midground to Background Propagation Trim and replant stems Growth Rate Fast Height 15+"

SL Aqua MORE Nature Aquarium Soil is a nutrient-rich, natural black aquasoil. The soil is sintered—a process where it is heated at a high temperature to create a strong bond, resulting in granules that are durable and won’t break down easily, yet remain porous enough to allow water and nutrients to pass through. It contains organic acids and essential nutrients that naturally lower pH and KH, creating ideal conditions for many live aquatic plants and tropical fish. MORE Nature aquasoil is easy to work with and can be used for many popular aquascaping styles. Use it to build sloped substrate hills for Iwagumi aquascapes or as a base layer for a colorful nature-style planted tank. What's the difference between normal and powder aquarium soil? Available in powder and medium granule sizes, its different grain options accommodate many popular plants. Fine powder substrate is great for small-rooted aquatic plants like Helianthus callitrichoides ‘Cuba’ (HC) or Eleocharis parvula ‘Mini’ (Dwarf Hair Grass), while the medium size works well for Cryptocoryne, Echinodorus, Rotala, Ludwigia, and more. How much substrate do I need? The general rule of thumb is one 3L bag per 5 gallons and one 8L bag per 10 gallons [Tank Length x Tank Depth x Desired Substrate Height (inches)] / 60 = Total liters of Aquarium Soil required

Persicaria hydropiper, also known as knotweed or marsh waterpepper, is a marginal stem plant with slender, lance-shaped green leaves and an upright, bamboo-like growth habit. Its delicate texture and growing form creates a subtle calming effect and planted aesthetic that many aquascapers can appreciate. It will soften emerged sections of an aquascape and can develop pinkish to purple hues under strong light and in nutrient-rich substrate. In nature, it grows along wetland edges, making it a must-have for ponds, paludariums, and hybrid planted tanks with emersed sections. If you're searching for a unique plant that can be grown multiple ways, try it out! Persicaria Hydropiper can be used in nature-style planted tanks or as an accent plant for your Wabi Kusa. It offers rich color and relatively easy care, making it a great choice for various aquascaping styles. Provide it with moderate to strong lighting, nutrients and CO2 injection if planting in your aquarium. Common Name Persicaria Hydropiper/ Polygonum sp. Care Moderate Lighting Moderate to High CO2 Required Suggested Placement Midground to Background Propagation Trim and replant Growth Rate Fast

Cryptocoryne Spiralis 'Jwala' This aquarium plant is a variation of Cryptocoryne Spiralis! Truthfully, information about this cultivar is still limited within the planted aquarium community. Based on the original species, it likely produces slender, elongated leaves in varying shades of green, brown, red, and olive. Like most Cryptocoryne plants, we believe it would work well in the midground area, where it will add texture and a good transition between different areas of an aquascape layout. Plus, Crypts look great at the base of stones and dritwood. This family of aquarium plants is known for being low-maintenance and beginner-friendly. However, this comes with caveats! Cryptocoryne should be planted in mature, cycled aquariums that are well-balanced between light and nutrient levels. Use quality aquasoil and allow them to send down roots before attempting to relocate or propagate to reduce chances of crypt melt!

Oryzias latipes "Black Medaka" Commonly called Japanese Ricefish or Japanese Killifish, Medaka are peaceful freshwater fish that are often enjoyed from a top-down view and have been bred into many color morphs. They are not often seen in planted aquariums and are more popular for indoor/outdoor ponds, patio tubs, and other top-view planted setups. They're hardy in nature, have low bioloads and can tolerate a wider range of water parameters so long as they're stable. Though they're a popular pond fish, Japanese Ricefish have calm temperaments and can definitely be a great addition to community tanks. Rice fish do best in groups, and generally occupy mid to upper levels of aquariums and ponds. They're active swimmers and easy to care for, making them a great choice for beginners as well. If being considered for a planted tank, provide gentle flow and live aquatic plants for coverage and reduced stress. Japanese Rice Fish are omnivorous and will readily accept quality flake, pellet, live, and frozen foods — and, as an added bonus, they will eat any mosquito larvae they find, making them both lovely and useful for outdoor planted tanks or ponds! Medaka Highlights Beginner Friendly: Hardy and adaptable, Medaka are often recommended for newer hobbyists looking for an active and easy care fish. Top-Down Viewing: One of the most enjoyable aspects of keeping Medaka is viewing them from above. Their colors and movement are ideal for shallow aquariums, ponds, and planted tubs. Peaceful Temperament: Medaka coexist well with other peaceful livestock and are an excellent choice for community aquariums and ponds. Medaka are social fish that should be kept in groups whenever possible. A group of six or more fish is recommended per 10 gallons to encourage natural behavior and activity. They prefer gentle water movement and will appreciate floating plants, live aquatic plants or additional cover, especially in outdoor setups. They may occasionally jump, so a lid or adequate plant cover s recommended. Stocking Recommendations As a practical guideline, plan for approximately one Medaka per gallon of water volume. Larger aquariums and ponds naturally provide more stability and swimming space. Avoid overcrowding as this can increase stress and make maintaining water quality more difficult. Feeding Medaka are omnivores and readily accept quality pellets, flakes, frozen and live foods. Feed only what they can consume in a few minutes and remove excess. Avoid overfeeding to help maintain water quality. If kept in outdoor setups, they will happily munch on mosquito larvae too! Arrival & Acclimation For best results, introduce new fish into a mature, cycled aquarium or pond. Spend extra time to float bags to match temperature before release. Once in the aquarium, pond or quarantine tank, give them time to settle in! Do not make any significant changes or move them during this time. Care & Compatibility - Temperament: Peaceful - Diet: Omnivore - Group Size: 6 or more Important Information: If using tap water, always treat with a quality dechlorinator. Stable water conditions, regular maintenance, and appropriate stocking levels will help support long-term health and success. As with all live animals, natural variation in color, pattern, and size should be expected.

Aponogeton longiplumulosus is an aquatic bulb plant that originates from Madagascar. It offers a bright olive-green color and large, fluted foliage that adds a delicate look to any planted tank. This aquarium plant grows large and tall, so we recommend it for larger tanks or even as a pond plant! When happy, it grows fast and adds lovely swaying motion and plenty of coverage for tropical fish and shrimp. This is an easy aquatic plant that adapts well to most water conditions. As a bulb plant, it will appreciate a nutritious aquasoil to support healthy growth. To plant aquarium bulbs, bury them partially into your substrate of choice and make sure the sprout tip remains above the surface. If you’re using sand, please ensure you have nutrient root tabs on hand. Be aware that some Aponogeton species go through dormant periods when new growth may slow or stop completely. This doesn’t mean your plant is dead—give it some time (typically a few weeks), and it should reboot if planted in the right conditions. This aquatic plant soft green color with hints of pink/purple depending on tank conditions. Its versatile with placement and can also be grown in emersed conditions (it produces a lovely scent above water!). General care is similar to other aquatic stem plants. Provide it with moderate to high lighting, CO2 injection and regular trimming once established. Use a quality liquid plant fertilizer and you'll have bushes of Limnophila in your aquascape in no time! Anubias Barteri var. Nana ‘Tropica’ is a hardy aquatic plant. Its moderate size is still suitable for nano aquariums, but can also be a great addition to larger planted tanks. It features more compact growth due to shorter stems, and broad, dark green leaves. Like other Anubias, it is easy to care for, making it a great choice for beginner aquarists. Anubias leaves are also on the thicker side, making them better choices in fish tanks that contain herbivores that may graze or snack on live aquarium plants. An aquatic rhizome, it can be attached to natural driftwood or stones. Its ability to grow without being planted makes it versatile with placement and an awesome choice for filling in empty spaces throughout an aquascape layout. Support faster growth and form with CO2 injection and a liquid plant fertilizer! Alternatively, if you’re searching for a good terrarium plant, consider giving this one a try. Its broad leaves are a perfect green filler and its hardiness is tough to beat.

Sagittaria subulata var. pusilla is a versatile aquatic plant known for its narrow, ribbon-like leaves that closely resemble Vallisneria. This dwarf arrowhead species is highly adaptable and can vary significantly in size depending on aquarium conditions, making it a flexible choice for a range of aquascaping styles. Under higher lighting, it tends to stay shorter and more compact, making it suitable for the foreground or as a transitional plant. In low light tanks, it can grow taller, gradually shifting into the midground or background while maintaining its soft, grassy appearance. As it establishes, it spreads through runners, creating natural horizontal coverage across the substrate. With occasional trims and maintenance, it can be controlled to produce a carpeting effect or allowed to grow more freely for a natural, organic look. Hardy and easy to care for, this plant adapts well to a wide range of aquarium conditions and is a reliable choice for both beginner and experienced aquascapers looking to add subtle texture and movement to their layouts.

Bucephalandra Mini Dark Needle, interchangeable with "Mini Needle Leaf," is a miniature aquarium plant. Its small, compact size makes it an excellent plant to pick for detailed work or tucked-away areas of an aquascape that you notice when viewing up close—aka the small details that make a big difference. Schismatoglottis sp. Mamasa is a rare tropical aroid that originates from regions in Southeast Asia. These types of plants are generally hardy and will do well when planted in a well-draining medium, such as a standard aroid mix or even sphagnum moss.
