Start by choosing your aquarium size, then move on to curate your stones, aquatic plants, and substrate. Iwagumi aquascaping is an iconic style known for strategic rock formations, minimal planting (often with carpeting aquatic plants), and open space where schooling nano fish take center stage. It remains one of our favorite planted aquarium styles, and we’ve gathered our top picks for the core elements of an Iwagumi setup. Pick your tank and get started today!

Aponogeton Ulvaceus is a large aquarium bulb plant originating from Madagascar. Its slight translucent, twisted rich green leaves create a beautiful focal point in planted tanks. Capable of growing up to 2ft, Aponogeton plants are best for large planted aquariums, ponds or setups that provide enough space for its height and expansive spread. Otherwise, as long as your tank is big enough, Ulvaceus is relatively easy to care for, hardy and will adapt to a range of water conditions. To speed up growth, adding CO2 will produce a significant difference. Like other fish tank bulbs, it may periodically enter periods of dormancy. During this time, its leaves may die off, but don't mistake it for plant death! Allow it some time to rest and it will resprout once it enters a growing cycle again. If you're looking for a fast-growing plant that adds lovely swaying motions and enrichment for your fish or shrimp, give Aponogeton Ulvaceus a go! Common Name Aponogeton Ulvaceus Care Easy Lighting Low to Medium CO2 Optional Suggested Placement Background Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 8-20+"

listings.commonName: Build Your Own Aquarium Kit - Nano Reef Tank
listings.description: Build Your Own Nano Reef Tank Customize your next reef aquarium with our BYOB aquarium kit. Start by selecting your tank, then piece together the main components of a successful reef tank! Add essential equipment like hardscape, lighting, and optional macroalgae for design, refugium, or both. Available aquariums feature Ultum Nature Systems’ line of Dual All-In-One rimless tanks with built-in filtration. Mix and match accessories to create a setup that works for you and your space.

Egeria Najas, often called Anacharis or Elodea Najas, is a fast-growing aquarium stem plant popular for many freshwater aquarium applications. It can be planted in the background of an aquascape to create a full, feathery backdrop, or used as a floating plant in shrimp tanks and breeding projects where it provides both shelter and filtration. Comparable to Egeria Densa, this species has finer, more delicate foliage with lightly serrated edges, adding soft texture and a natural look to planted aquariums. Easy to care for, Egeria Najas adapts well to a wide range of water parameters, making it suitable for beginners and hobbyists who enjoy live plants without extra effort. Its quick growth and nutrient uptake support water quality while contributing to a healthy, balanced aquarium. Please check your state’s regulations and protect the environment by disposing of excess trimmings or plant matter into the trash. Do not release this plant into drains or introduce it into local waterways. Common Name Anacharis / Waterweed Care Easy Lighting Low to Medium CO2 Optional Suggested Placement Midground to Background Propagation Trim and plant stems Growth Rate Fast Height 4-12”+

Saxifraga Stolonifera is an ornamental (and very cute!) plant. Commonly called Strawberry Begonia, it’s not actually a strawberry plant or a begonia, but gets its name from its physical traits and growth habit. Native to Asia, it is sometimes miscategorized as a geranium, though it belongs to the Saxifraga family, which also includes Jade Plants. In the right conditions, Strawberry Begonias will put out trailing stolons and baby plantlets. Its fuzzy leaves display a veined pattern with undersides that range from red to purplish hues. It's important to highlight that this is not an aquarium plant, but it would work beautifully in an open terrarium-like setup. It tolerates most household humidity levels and appreciates moderate to bright, filtered lighting. Intense direct sunlight or grow lights may scorch the plant and cause more harm than good. If you choose to pot it traditionally, ensure your mix drains well, avoid wetting the leaves, and prevent standing water. Otherwise, fertilize every two weeks or once a month. It is fairly easy going and will reward you with baby plants to propagate or share with friends and family. Common Name(s) Strawberry Begonia Care Easy to Moderate Lighting Medium to High [Filtered] Growth Rate Slow to Moderate Size Varies Depending on Conditions

Crinum Thaianum is a unique aquarium bulb plant that belongs to the lily family but closely resembles something else we all know. Its bulb looks like an onion—earning its common trade name, Thai Onion or Water Onion. When mature, this aquatic plant develops long, ribbon-like leaves that can grow very large if allowed. Due to its potential size, it’s a great option for anyone with a large planted tank or sizable pond where it can fully flourish! Important Note: This listing may or may not include a fully mature plant. Please ensure you are prepared to care for bulb plants at all growing stages. Aside from space requirements, Crinum Thaianum is an easy aquarium plant to grow and keep. It’s undemanding, and the reward outweighs the risk in this case. Established, mature plants will occasionally bloom fragrant lilies that rise to the water’s surface and last for some time. A great live plant for enthusiasts who enjoy keeping aquariums or similar setups long-term. Common Name Thai Onion / Water Onion Care Easy Lighting Low to Medium CO2 Optional Suggested Placement Background Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 8-20+"

listings.commonName: Build Your Own Rhizome Plant Pack
listings.description: Build Your Own Rhizome Plant Pack Have a low tech tank or thinking of starting one? Rhizome plants are ideal for low-light planted aquariums thanks to their hardiness and ability to grow in these conditions. Choose from a variety of popular Anubias, Bucephalandra, and Java Ferns to perfectly fill your aquascape. The best part about epiphytic rhizomes is that they don’t require aquarium soil to grow. Attach them to driftwood or rocks, and you’re ready to go! If you need plant-safe glue, tying thread, or plant weights, our Build Your Own Plant Pack includes everything you might need in one convenient, customizable bundle for your next aquascape. Browse a variety of shapes, sizes, textures, and colors—perfect for starting a new nano aquarium or adding to an existing setup. Most of these aquatic plants also make great terrarium plants!

Twinstar LightControl is an aquarium light controller for planted aquariums. Equipped with bluetooth capability, several settings can be controlled via Twinstar's app and intuitive interface. Compatible with a range of Twinstar LED lighting, aquascapers can easily upgrade older models and streamline light intensity and schdules for better aquatic plant growth. Product Highlights - 24HR timer for complete lighting cycle customization - Brightness control from 0 - 100% - Light Planner feature simulates natural circadian rhythms for a more dynamic growing environment for your fish and plants. Implement sunrise and sunset settings (up to 60min) each way for gentle, gradual light changes. Make simple and quick light adjustments straight from your phone. Whether you're running a nano aquarium or a show tank, LightControl is a great option for providing the right conditions for a healthy planted tank.

Echinodorus Major (Martii), commonly known as Ruffled Amazon Sword, is a bright green easy aquarium plant that is great for large freshwater aquariums and aquascaping. This sword plant grows broad, ruffled leaves that grow in an outward pattern like a fountain. Its impressive size makes it suitable for large setups or as a focal point in planted tanks. This amazon sword plant is popular for its easy care and large size. Like other Echinodorus, it is a heavy root feeder and will benefit from nutritious aquasoil and root tabs. Moderate lighting and CO2 injection will boost growing speed and form! Overall, this is an easy aquatic plant that's great for hobbyists of all skill levels.

A moderately sized Amazon sword plant for planted tanks and aquascaping! Echinodorus ‘Big Bear’ features a mixed color palette ranging from emerald green to crimson tones. Its colors change depending on the environment in which it is grown, making it an intriguing aquarium plant to cultivate. When grown above water, its leaves are rounded, more rigid, and primarily green. When grown submerged in aquarium conditions, the leaves soften, move with the flow, and develop deep burgundy tones. Like others in the family, this is considered an easy aquatic plant. It works well for low tech tanks or low light aquariums and will be resilient in most conditions. Sword plants are heavy root feeders and will benefit from nutritious aquasoil and root tab supplementation. To boost growth and form, provide moderate lighting and CO2 injection. Overall, Big Bear is easy going and is a great option for all aquascaping skill levels. We also like this one as a main plant for Wabi Kusa style setups!

Aponogeton Henkelianus is another bulb plant that is similar to Madagascariensis in appearance. However, this variety can be distinguished by solid green color throughout and narrower leaves. Not as readily available, this aquarium bulb adds beautiful texture to planted tanks when healthy. A solid pick for any aquascaper who loves unique aquatic plants. Important Note: This listing includes a bulb that may or may not be sprouted at the time of purchase. Please ensure you are prepared to care for either option. Provide a nutrient-rich substrate or supplement with root tabs to support this plant’s development. While most are relatively hardy, their leaves are fragile and should be handled with care to prevent tears. Start with moderate lighting, good water flow and CO2 injection if possible. Patience will be rewarded with this one! Common Name Madagascar Lace Care Easy Lighting Low to Medium CO2 Optional Suggested Placement Background Growth Rate Moderate to Fast Height 8-20+"

Green Jade Shrimp feature, as their name suggests, a mix of green tones that can carry hints of yellow, blue, or black depending on the individual shrimplet. They’re a unique addition to any planted aquarium and will happily forage throughout the tank all day. While their algae consumption isn’t as strong as Amano Shrimp, they breed easily, and large numbers grazing together can help clean obscure areas that are otherwise hard to reach. Like other Neocaridina shrimp, they are adaptable but can be sensitive to sudden changes. We recommend adding them to established setups. They prefer tropical temperatures and slightly soft water. As with any planted aquarium, a good filter is essential for maintaining water quality. Depending on what type of filter you have, consider getting an intake sponge or guard to prevent shrimplets from getting sucked up into the filter. (We've found entire colonies living in ours!) Tank size recommendation: 5-10G Shrimp are extremely sensitive to copper. If using tap, be sure to use a dechlorinator to ensure safety for your invertebrates. Green Jades are peaceful. Keep them in an aquarium with non-agressive tank mates to ensure their safety.

This clip-on aquarium LED light is a high-performance lighting solution for nano reef aquariums. Equipped with dimming capabilities and a full-spectrum tailored for marine setups, it supports healthy coral growth, calcium absorption and intensified display colors. Installation is quick and the light is compatible with glass thicknesses up to 1” max. The light fixture includes UV, violet, blue, green, red and white wavelengths. With each supporting a different function, the unit provides an even, full-spectrum coverage, for better health and beautiful lighting in saltwater aquariums. With its external controller, reef hobbyists can control brightness, LED colors and configure timer settings in alignment with the necessary schedule. HG088 Reef LED Highlights - 5 brightness levels (100-77-55-32-10%) to suit LPS, SPS corals, and marine fish - Choose from 6, 9, or 12-hour cycles to match your reef tank’s needs. - 60-degree lens and high-power output provides strong light penetration to deeper waters while remaining energy-efficient. - Easy installation, anti-rust design and flexible gooseneck to adjust directional lighting as needed. MODEL TANK SIZE POWER LUMENS HG088 30-45CM 30W 448LM Additional Specifications: - Color Temperature: 10,000K - LED Lifespan: 50,000HR depending on use

Twinstar S Line V Premium Aquarium Light for Planted Tanks The latest release in Twinstar’s most powerful line of lights for planted tanks, this series is designed for aquascapes with aquarium plants that require intense lighting. Available in six sizes, there is a model to illuminate everything from high-tech nano aquariums to large, nature aquarium show tanks. The device provides beautiful illumination and a carefully balanced spectrum, proven to support vibrant aquatic plant growth. The 600S V and larger models are compatible with the Twinstar Wire Kit. Smaller models are not compatible. Version 5 features six full-color LEDs along with specialized plant-growth LEDs, creating one of the widest spectral ranges available to aquascapers. This broad, balanced spectrum offers aquarium plants the perfect conditions for optimized photosynthesis, robust root development, and lush growth. Each light fixture includes Twinstar’s latest Bluetooth controller, LightControl Pro, unlocking a range of features and customizations—including color adjustment, brightness levels, timers, and more. If you're an aquascaper who doesn't need the strongest light out there, but you're still growing aquatic plants that have moderate light requirements and you like aesthetic equipment, this one is for you. listings.commonName: Build Your Own Aquarium - Shrimp Tank
listings.description: Build Your Own Shrimp Tank Looking to start your own freshwater shrimp tank? Whether it’s your first time or you’re a seasoned hobbyist setting up another, you’re in the right place! Curate your next setup in one place with our BYOB kit. Start by choosing your rimless tank, then add essentials like substrate, accessories, aquatic plants, and of course, the stars of the show—shrimp! These tiny critters are fun to watch and will graze on biofilm, algae, and debris all day. Peaceful and lively, they add interest and life to any nature aquarium.

Black King Kong first appeared in the planted aquarium hobby in the early 2000's. These freshwater aquarium shrimp feature black, white, and hints of blue hues, making them a high-contrast and beautiful addition to any planted tank. Their patterns can vary—some fully solid, others color blocked or slightly speckled. One of the classic Taiwan Bees, they're also commonly cross-bred with other popular species to create hybrids and unique color patterns. BKK shrimp are a little more sensitive, but still considered easy to care for. Basic care includes using remineralized RO water, stable temperatures, and pH levels between 6–6.5, along with quality nutrition. Many shrimp keepers prefer sponge filters for their gentle operation and aeration. Otherwise, these little critters make a great addition to any peaceful freshwater setup. They spend much of their time grazing and eating algae or biofilm from aquarium plants, glass, substrate, and hardscape. Tank size recommendation: 5-10G Shrimp are extremely sensitive to copper. If using tap, be sure to use a dechlorinator to ensure safety for your invertebrates. Black King Kong shrimp are peaceful. Keep them in an aquarium with non-agressive tank mates to ensure their safety.

Blue Dream Shrimp bring life and beautiful blue color to any planted aquarium. Selectively bred, this Neocaridina shrimp originates from Taiwan and is a popular pick for dwarf aquarium shrimp keepers! They stay relatively small, making them a great choice for nano aquariums or peaceful community tanks. We especially like watching them graze in tanks that have plenty of green aquatic plants. They spend the majority of their day grazing on algae and biofilm that's commonly found on plants or hardscape. Like other Neocaridinas, they are adaptable but can be sensitive to sudden changes. We recommend adding them to aquariums that are fully cycled and stable. They prefer tropical temperatures and slightly soft water. As with any freshwater setup, a good filter is key for maintaining water quality. Exclusive shrimp keepers enjoy using sponge filters, but if you opt for a canister, consider getting an intake sponge or guard to prevent shrimplets from getting sucked up into the filter. Tank size recommendation: 5-10G Shrimp are extremely sensitive to copper. If using tap, be sure to use a dechlorinator to ensure safety for your invertebrates. Blue Dreams are peaceful. Keep them in an aquarium with non-agressive tank mates to ensure their safety.

listings.commonName: Build Your Own Dutch Style Stem Plant Pack
listings.description: Build Your Own Dutch Style Aquarium Plant Pack Inspired by one of the oldest and most refined forms of aquascaping, the Dutch style aquarium celebrates dense aquatic plant growth, color contrast, and thoughtful composition. Our BYOB pack lets you customize and pick which stem plants you’ll strategically group and plant to create your own rendition of a classic style. Pick rom a wide selection of aquarium stems, rosettes and similar varieties that lend varying colors, textures, sizes, heights and leaf shapes. Whether you’re creating a contest aquarium layout or just love colorful plants, this customizable pack is for you!

Click here to shop all reef! Ready to solidify your reefscape? MR Powder is a natural, crushed rock powder designed to cover glued joints. Apply it while your glue is still curing to achieve a smooth, cohesive look that blends perfectly. Made from 100% aquarium-safe reef rocks, MR Powder is safe for reef tanks. Made by Marco Rocks, an environmentally conscious brand, this finishing powder is a great product to have on hand when creating your reef aquascape. MR Powder Highlights - Natural solution for covering glued areas in rock work. - Available in 3LB bags and two colors

Bucephalandra Pearl Grey is a lovely Bucephalandra plant that originates from Indonesia. This easy aquarium plant features broad, rounded leaves that display deep emerald tones with a silvery sheen when grown under aquarium lights. Like others in the family, this Buce is often considered beginner-friendly. It is hardy in most conditions and takes some effort to cause serious damage to the plant. Thanks to its resilience, it can grow happily in a wide variety of planted setups. Whether you have a low tech planted aquarium or a terrarium filled with rare aroids, this plant is a sure fit. To grow it, attach it to a porous surface like driftwood or rock and place as desired. In planted aquaria, we recommend choosing a spot with good flow and supplementing with CO2 and quality fertilizer. Once mature, Bucephalandra Pearl Grey can be propagated by separating the rhizome and reattaching. A great low-effort, high-reward aquatic plant!

Yellow Goldenback Shrimp (Neocaridina davidi) are a lovely dwarf shrimp you'll commonly see in freshwater planted tanks. Known for their bright yellow color, they stand out beautifully against aquatic plants and darker substrates. In peaceful aquariums, these critters spend most of the day foraging for biofilm and algae, making them both a lively and practical addition. These shrimp are peaceful and hardy in nature, making them great for beginner and experienced hobbyists alike. In safe, healthy conditions, aquarium shrimp breed fairly easily. When setting up a shrimp tank, make sure to provide plenty of shelter and hiding spots. Choose non-aggressive tank mates, and keep in mind that some fish may view shrimplets as food. Gentle filtration is best, and if you’re using a canister filter, consider an intake cover to protect young shrimp from being sucked in. Tank size recommendation: 5-10G Shrimp are extremely sensitive to copper. If using tap, be sure to use a dechlorinator to ensure safety for your invertebrates. Yellow Goldenbacks are peaceful. Keep them in an aquarium with non-agressive tank mates to ensure their safety.

Crystal Red Shrimp are one of the most popular dwarf shrimp varieties in the aquarium hobby. These freshwater aquarium shrimp are easy to spot thanks to their bold color and unique pattern. In a planted aquarium, they pop beautifully against live aquatic plants and are super fun to observe. They are not recommended for beginners and are considered more challenging to keep. Due to their specific water requirements and natural sensitivity to environmental shifts, crystal reds usually have dedicated setups. When successful, nurturing a colony is a highly rewarding experience! These shrimp are considered soft water shrimp and need slightly acidic conditions, extremely low TDS levels, and stable temperatures between 68–75°F. Provide gentle flow and ensure regular water changes to keep the tank clean. CRS will happily graze and forage, but also appreciate a varied diet whenever possible. Tank size recommendation: 5-10G Shrimp are extremely sensitive to copper. If using tap, be sure to use a dechlorinator to ensure safety for your invertebrates. CRS shrimp are peaceful. Keep them in an aquarium with non-agressive tank mates to ensure their safety.

Java Fern 'Windelov' Hybrid (Microsorum Pteropus) is a rich green aquatic plant that combines characteristics from popular species. While the exact parentage is unclear, this unique hybrid features Windelov’s classic split tips on overall thicker leaves. This aquatic fern also appears smaller in size, making it a nice choice for nano planted aquariums or aquascapes that need small plants to fill open spaces in a layout. Recently reclassified as Leptochilus pteropus , this plant is still widely known in the hobby as Microsorum pteropus. If Windelov Hybrid is like any other Java Fern, it is likely an easy aquatic plant that can add greenery and life to low-tech aquariums or setups with low lighting. Java Fern plants are known for their adaptability, making them a top recommended plant for beginners. Attach it to stones, driftwood, or aquarium decor and watch this naturally bushy plant grow!

Water Poppy (Hydrocleys nymphoides) is a beautiful aquatic plant known for its glossy, lily-like leaves and bright green color. In warmer conditions, it blooms cute yellow flowers that resemble poppies, hence its common trade name. If you're looking for pond plants that add character and texture to an outdoor or indoor pond, or a large planted aquarium with a marginal area, this one’s a great pick! Water poppies provide several benefits, including natural filtration and coverage for fish or shrimp. They are generally easy to grow when planted in nutritious soil and provided with high light. In outdoor setups, this aquatic plant loves full sun but does not tolerate colder climates well. When happy, regular trimming is necessary to manage its growth and spread, and it can be propagated easily by separating runners and replanting. Common Name Water Poppy Care Easy Lighting High CO2 Optional Aquascape Placement Background Propagation Separate runners Growth Rate Moderate Size 10+”

listings.commonName: Build Your Own Wabi Kusa Tank
listings.description: Build Your Own Wabi Kusa Tank Create your own Wabi Kusa display! This customizable aquascaping kit lets you design your setup from the ground up. Wabi Kusa is a Japanese art form inspired by nature and the philosophy of wabi-sabi, where beauty if found in imperfection. These planted displays typically feature a variety of aquatic plants growing on a spherical, moss-wrapped ball made from aquarium soil. Plants are intentionally mixed to create an organic mix of colors, textures, and leaf shapes. This type of planted tank is a great choice for small spaces and general plant enthusiasts. They require minimal maintenance, and offer a unique way to grow aquatic plants. If you enjoy organic, living art, this one is for you.

listings.commonName: Build Your Own Pro CO2 Kit
listings.description: Build Your Own Planted Tank CO2 Kit Ready to level up your aquascape or have multiple planted aquariums that need CO2? Customize your own pro kit to supply a single tank or multiple setups at the same time. Start by choosing your regulator, then add your cylinder, diffuser, and more. Each product featured in this aquarium kit has been tested and used by our team to ensure safe, consistent, and reliable CO2 for healthy aquatic plants and lush planted aquariums. Depending on what you choose, this all-in-one CO2 solution can support aquariums ranging in size from 5 to 250 gallons! Whether you're just starting out and want to introduce CO2 for the first time, or you're a seasoned aquascaper looking to upgrade your current setup, this customizable bundle has you and your tanks covered! How to use a drop checker for monitoring CO2 levels in your planted tank:

Cryptocoryne Mi Oya is most often planted in the midground area of an aquascape. Although a lovely Cryptocoryne plant, it is less commonly used when compared to more popular varieties like Lutea or Wendtii Green. This aquarium plant features similar care requirements and can be distinguished for its slender leaves and primary color palette of green and copper tones. Crypts aren't picky, but do best in stable, mature environments. This listing includes Mi Oya already nestled into a piece of aquarium-safe driftwood. Ensure your planted tank is cycled and the plant can be added as desired.

listings.commonName: Chihiros Nano LED Light - Universal RGB
listings.description: The Chihiros Universal RGB Nano LED Light delivers professional-grade lighting for small aquariums and nano planted tanks. Compatible with tanks ranging from 20-36cm, it’s a perfect choice for setups like the UNS 30C or UNS 5N rimless aquariums. Despite its compact size, it provides a powerful, balanced spectrum that supports healthy aquatic plant growth and amplifies colors found in planted aquaria. Available in two sizes, this aquarium light features a simple design and classic clip-on installation. It’s compatible with glass panels up to 10mm thick and also has an IP67 waterproof rating, making it reliable in humid environments. With built-in Bluetooth control, adjustments are convenient via the app! Set brightness, timers, or customize the spectrum and effects that are perfect for your aquascape. Universal RGB Nano Highlights - Suitable for 20-36CM aquariums. Use it to illuminate everything from planted tanks to shrimp tanks, miniature scapes, betta aquariums and more. - Full-spectrum RGB 3 in 1 LEDs produce beautiful color rendering and are energy-efficient. - Smart light that can be adjusted via Bluetooth and the mobile app. Make adjustments and tweaks straight from your phone. Model Specifications Model Dimensions (IN) W x D x H Lumens Power (WATTS) LED Bulbs Nano 20 7.09 x 1.89 x 2.48 850 13 12 Nano 30 11.02 x 1.89 x 2.48 1200 18 18

Drosera spatulata var. lovellae is a vibrant and easygoing sundew known for its compact form and rich red tones. Under bright light, its spoon-shaped leaves and sticky tentacles develop a scarlet hue that is sure to stand out in a terrarium or in any carnivorous plant collection. Like other Drosera, it captures small insects and is a fascinating plant to grow and observe. It grows best in consistently moist, bog-like conditions. If you decide to grow it on its own, you can keep its pot in a shallow dish of water. Alternatively, if you choose to add it to a planted setup, pick a spot where it has good access to water at its base. Drosera plants will do best with distilled, rain or RO water sources. Common Name Spoon-leaved Sundew Care Easy Lighting Moderate to High CO2 Non-aquatic Terrarium Placement Bright & waterlogged Propagation Leaf or root cuttings Growth Rate Varies Size Varies

listings.commonName: UNS Pro Aquascaping Tools - Straight Scissors
listings.description: The new Pro Straight Scissor by Ultum Nature Systems is designed for precise trimming of aquarium stem plants and general planted tank maintenance. Perfect for bulk trimming in large or densely planted aquascapes, straight aquarium scissor blades perform clean initial chops while minimizing damage to plant tissue. Straight scissors are also great for shape refinement, snipping dead leaves or older growth with accuracy and control. Tool Length: 10" TIP: Dry well after use to maintain tool longevity. The new design is ergonomic, lightweight and now includes a stabilizing tail that provides support and comfort during long trimming sessions. Like others from the line, each pro aquascaping tool is made from rust-resistant stainless steel and is available in two colors. UNS aquarium tools are reliable and essential all-purpose tools for aquascaping and planted tanks. Photo courtesy of Ultum Nature Systems

listings.commonName: UNS Pro Aquascaping Tools - Wave Scissors
listings.description: The Wave Scissor Pro Aquascaping Tool by Ultum Nature Systems aids with precision trimming of carpeting aquatic plants and low-growing species. Its unique wave-shaped blades allow you to trim at a higher angle, reducing strain and awkward hand positions. A great aquarium tool for anyone with a taller tank or aquascapes that are hardscape heavy with dense plant growth. If you have an Iwagumi aquascape, nature-style planted tank or nano aquarium, consider a pair of wave scissors! Tool Length: 10" TIP: Dry well after use to maintain tool longevity. The Pro version introduces a design change with two tail grips for more stability and comfort. Made from high-quality, rust-resistant stainless steel, these aquarium scissors excel at maintaining level carpets of Glosso, Monte Carlo, Dwarf Hair Grass and more. An essential aquarium tool for keeping a manicured, healthy planted tank! Photo courtesy of Ultum Nature Systems

Willow Moss (Fontinalis antipyretica) is a freshwater aquarium moss with intricate, delicate fronds and a cascading growth pattern. Although it grows slowly, it does so steadily, and with proper care, it will eventually form lush, fluffy mats of green in aquascapes of all sizes. Like other aquatic mosses, Willow Moss is exceptionally easy to propagate—any small piece that breaks off from the main mass will attach to a new surface and produce new growth. In aquascaping, live moss is commonly used in a variety of popular planted aquarium styles. It is ideal for softening hardscape edges and adding layered, textured dimension. Willow Moss is suitable for nano aquariums, low-tech tanks, and even terrariums where environments are consistently moist. Aquarium mosses are popular for their resilient nature and adaptability, tolerating a wide range of water conditions with minimal care requirements. This makes Willow Moss a top pick for beginner hobbyists. Use it in your nature aquarium, nano planted tank, low-light aquarium, betta tank, or shrimp tank. No matter what type of setup you have, Willow Moss is sure to add that extra bit of green your tank needs and aquatic life loves!

Selaginella pulvinata is a lovely evergreen perennial, commonly treated like terrarium mosses. This variety of club moss or spike moss forms dense, vibrant green tufts that grow in a rosette-like pattern. Depending on the age of the plant, it may also develop a "trunk", giving it a miniature tree appearance. In natural settings, S. pulvinata can be found growing on limestone rocks at high elevations, making it relatively hardy and resistant to drier conditions once mature. One of its unique traits is its response to changing environments. When dry, its fronds curl inwards, almost as if to preserve energy, and once moistened, they fan out and redevelop a rich green hue. Keep it in a growing medium like sphagnum moss or peat moss, and avoid waterlogging. Mist it daily and allow excess water to run off its leaves and into the medium. While it grows slower than other well-known Selaginella species, this moss-like plant is great for anyone looking to add an uncommong addition to terrariums, vivariums, or planted enclosures. Common Name Club Moss / Spike Moss Care Easy Lighting Low to Moderate CO2 Recommended Terrarium Placement On driftwood, rocks or decor Propagation Separate and replant Growth Rate Slow Size Varies

Bucephalandra is often regarded as a beginner-friendly aquarium plant for aquascaping, though it’s not chosen as frequently as other popular types like Anubias, Amazon Sword, or Java Fern. However, this family of aquatic aroid plants shouldn't be overlooked! Commonly called Buce, this flowering genus brings dynamic color, texture, shapes, and sizes to any planted tank. Freya is a variety we're not yet familiar with, but we like what we see. It features rounded, ruffled leaves with a distinct rib running down the center and bold green color that’s nearly black. Under the right aquarium light, it’s sure to produce beautiful contrast and the signature shimmer Bucephalandra are known for. Bucephalandra are a wonderful choice for everything from nano aquariums to large aquascapes and even terrarium enclosures. They’re highly adaptable and forgiving plants, with the rewards often outweighing any risks. When planted in nature aquariums, keep the rhizome above the substrate and attach it to driftwood, rocks, or any porous surface. Choose a spot in your planted aquarium that receives moderate light and good water flow. To increase growing speed and bring out the best colors in Buce, CO2 injection will go a long way.

Aquarium sponge filters are a classic form of filtration that have long been trusted in the aquarium hobby. They’re easy to clean and offer a no-fuss, reliable approach to aquarium filtration. The Hygger Sponge Filter features a dual-chamber: the sponge provides mechanical filtration, while the lower chamber is filled with bio-ceramic media that supports beneficial bacteria to help break down organic waste. Sponge filters work by using an air pump to pull water through the sponge that then traps particles that would otherwise contaminate the water. This tried-and-true method removes waste, keeps water clean, and helps prevent ammonia spikes that are dangerous for fish and shrimp. The integrated air stone creates the classic “bubbling” for water movement and essential oxygenation. This type of filtration is especially popular for shrimp tanks and similar setups that need gentle waters. Each filter includes an extra sponge, detachable container, ceramic bio-media, and is available in three sizes for tanks ranging from 5 to 125 gallons. (Air pump and tubing purchased separately) Sponge Filter Highlights - Combines mechanical and biological filtration for efficient waste removal and cultivation of beneficial bacteria. - Tried and true! Drosera spatulata, commonly known as a the Spoon-Leaved Sundew, is one of the largest groups of sundews found in nature. Native to many regions around the world, this carnivorous plant is highly adaptable and a favorite among collectors. It’s often recognized for its self-seeding behavior, sometimes becoming a “weed” in Drosera collections, but this trait also makes it easy to grow and share with friends or family. This sundew forms cute clusters of rounded leaves covered in glimmering, sticky tentacles that attract and trap tiny insects. Like other carnivorous plants, it grows best in nutrient-poor soils and obtains nutrition primarily from prey. A balanced mix of sphagnum moss with perlite or sand provides the ideal blend of aeration and moisture retention. Along with mostly moist conditions, Drosera prefer water that is low in minerals and salts like rain or RO water. These plants add beautiful color and texture to terrariums and appreciate bright light that isn’t too direct. Easy to grow and quick to flower, this sundew is a wonderful beginner-friendly introduction to carnivorous plants! Selaginella Kraussiana 'Aurea' is a variety of club moss well-known for its delicate, lacy foliage. Although these plants resemble ferns, they are not true ferns or mosses! They fall somewhere in between and have several nicknames like peacock fern, spike moss and more. Selaginella species make wonderful terrarium plants and are commonly used for ground coverage or as trailing vines in planted setups. Like other Selaginella species, this cultivar appreciates elevated humidity and well-draining substrate. It is also suitable for attaching to natural driftwood or porous structures, where it will slowly attach and spread. Avoid placing it too close to or exposed under direct, high light, as this can burn the plant. If you're looking for a low-maintenance terrarium plant that provides good coverage with beautiful texture, this is a great choice! Its growth can be random, so occasional pruning is recommended to maintain a neat appearance. Trimmings can be easily relocated or attached elsewhere to propagate the plant. Spirodela polyrhiza is a larger form of the notorious, fast-growing floating plant, Duckweed. Giant Duckweed features bright green, rounded leaves that float freely on the surface of planted aquariums or ponds, producing a serene, lily-like look. It is on equal footing with classic Duckweed and provides the same water-purifying power, but is a little easier to manage and thin out as needed. Alongside natural water filtration, floating plants are great for providing shade and shelter to aquarium fish or shrimp and indirectly help with algae control. It is relatively hardy, making it a favorite aquatic plant for beginner aquarium hobbyists. Overall, adding Giant Duckweed to your aquarium or pond is a great, low-maintenance way to grow beautiful and functional floating plants! Important Note! Giant Duckweed is naturally accompanied by regular duckweed, and the two become intermixed over time. Because of this, each order will include regular duckweed. Separating the two is not feasible and would result in unnecessary plant waste. What to do with excess Giant Duckweed This pond and aquarium floater grows quickly, so it’s important to monitor its growth and remove excess as needed to prevent shading of other aquatic plants that need light to grow. When disposing, please do not release it into local waterways, ponds, or down your plumbing. Try composting it or allowing it to dry out completely before discarding in the bin. It can also be incorporated into soil mixtures for house plants or gardens! Thank you for being a responsible aquarium hobbyist and helping protect native ecosystems!

Echinodorus Red Phoenix is a variety of Amazon Sword native to South America. With nicknames like Red Phoenix Sword, it is a popular sword plant thanks to its rich color palette, consisting of deep green to reddish tones. Like other Echinodorus species, this aquarium plant is extremely resilient, making it a solid pick for novice aquascapers or aquarium hobbyists just getting into planted tanks. To bring out more ruby tones, inject CO2, intensify lighting and supplement with quality aquatic plant fertilizer. However, this is all optional! Amazon Sword plants are well-loved for their adaptability and are also brilliant in Wabi Kusa style setups and low tech tanks. In these environments, the leaves tend to be firmer with a primarily green color palette. Overall, this is a versatile choice for any aquascape and friendly to all skill levels.

Bucephalandra Brownie Jade is one of many buce varieties. Like others, it is a resilient, slow-growing plant that is often dubbed a great beginner plant for its hardiness. While this is true, Bucephalandra have so much potential when provided with consistent care and stability in planted aquariums. To grow happy and healthy buce, go back to the basics. Tanks should be mature with fully established cycles to prevent melt and alleviate stress on the plant during transition periods. Plant your Buce in a spot that receives low to moderate lighting and good, indirect flow. CO2 injection and light fertilization can help improve form and color, but tank cleanliness is key! Overall, Bucephalandra is a genus loved by most. These aquatic rhizomes can grow in a variety of settings and observing the transition from emersed foliage to fully submerged growth is rewarding. Colors morph and many species (not all) feature the signature iridescent shimmer when placed under specific aquarium lights. Make sure to trim away old or dead leaves and keep up on tank maintenance!

Centrolepis drummondiana, commonly known as Blood Vomit, is a rare aquarium plant that is easy to recognize thanks to its subtle two-tone coloration. Native to Australia, this species has earned many names in the hobby, including Eriocaulon blood vomit and Trithuria species. Its unusual common name is certainly unique, but remains the most widely recognized trade name within the aquarium hobby. It is a true foreground plant that grows in tight rosettes. When fully submerged, it produces short, vibrant green leaves with a signature deep red base. Unlike many carpeting plants, it does not spread via runners. This quality allows for very controlled, intentional placement in aquascapes. Its root system can become extensive, often growing longer than the leaves themselves, making substrate choice especially important for long-term health. Blood Vomit is considered an advanced aquatic plant. Successful growth requires a quality aquasoil, high lighting, consistent CO2 injection, and soft water conditions. Pigmentation can be improved with a complete liquid plant fertilizer. Because of its slow growth, maintaining water quality is important to prevent algae from growing on its leaves. It won’t propagate on its own, but mature rosettes can be gently split into smaller sections and replanted. When grown successfully, Blood Vomit is a highly rewarding aquatic plant that adds beautiful detail and unique character to a planted aquarium. Common Name Blood Vomit Care Advanced Lighting High CO2 Required Aquascape Placement Foreground Propagation Separate and replant Growth Rate Slow Size <2”

Rhodobryum giganteum, commonly known as Umbrella Moss or Giant Rose Moss, is a unique moss species that produces flower-like growth. When happy and healthy, it forms dense clusters of tight rosettes that resemble tiny blooming umbrellas, adding sculptural texture and visual interest to terrariums and planted displays. In the wild, Umbrella Moss is typically found growing along the base of trees or on shaded rocks where airflow and stable moisture levels are present. Its growth spreads beneath the surface, with new rosettes emerging above the substrate over time. This live moss performs best in well-ventilated terrariums and similar setups. Plant it in sphagnum or a moisture-retentive substrate without waterlogging and place it in an area that receives filtered light. If you’re looking for a unique moss for a terrarium, vivarium, or paludarium, Rhodobryum giganteum offers an ideal balance of easy care and uncommon aesthetic. Tree Moss (Climacium dendroides) is an ornamental live moss that resembles tiny pine trees. Perfect for forest-inspired enclosures, it features a tree-like form with feathery, deep-green fronds. As it matures, it can expand into dense colonies, creating a neat woodland effect in terrariums, moss collections, or paludariums. This variety needs high humidity with consistent moisture. It will tolerate low-light conditions, making it a great choice for low-maintenance setups. In the wild, Tree Moss is often found growing on natural wood in consistently damp environments. If you’re looking for a unique moss for your planted setup, Tree Moss is sure to add unique character and texture.

Eriocaulon sp. “Feather Duster” is a rare, easy-to-grow Eriocaulon species with fine, grass-like leaves that are perfect for the background of a planted aquarium. Similar to popular choices like Vallisneria nana, Eleocharis vivipara, and Cyperus helferi, Feather Duster provides flowing texture with clean, controlled growth that’s easier to maintain. Despite the picky reputation of the genus, Feather Duster is surprisingly undemanding. Its clumping growth makes it easy to divide and propagate, and moderate lighting is usually sufficient. Stable water quality is key—Feather Duster prefers softer waters, and nutrients can be supplied either through the substrate or with a quality aquatic plant fertilizer. For stronger, faster growth, increase light levels and plant it in a tank with CO2 injection. It can easily reach the water’s surface, where you can let it swoop naturally or trim as needed, since it responds well to cutting. Overall, its form, soft movement, and lower-maintenance requirements make Eriocaulon Feather Duster one of our top recommendations for aquascapers who want a grass-like background plant.

Place Genki in a prominent spot near your planted tanks (or any aquarium!) as a reminder to stay focused, practice patience, and remain resilient. May your aquariums flourish with good fortune as your scaping skills continue to blossom. Genki is a mini figurine designed and made to bring a little joy to your aquascaping space. Genki does not sink or swim and is best placed near your aquarium, where he can keep an eye on things. Karp-e Diem, and keep scaping! APT 1 by 2HR Aquarist is an all-in-one aquarium plant fertilizer designed for new planted tanks or setups with lighter plant mass. Its balanced formula excludes nitrate and phosphate, helping reduce excess nutrients in the early stages when most freshly planted aquascapes simply don’t need them yet. If you’re looking for a no-fuss, easy-to-dose liquid fertilizer, APT 1 is one of our go-to choices. It provides comprehensive nutrition while keeping things simple, supporting healthy plant growth without overloading the system. Each bottle includes a calibrated pump and straightforward instructions, making it easy to stay consistent. One bottle is estimated to last approximately 3 months based on a standard 30-gallon planted tank. Choosing the Right APT Fertilizer APT 1 is designed for newly planted tanks or aquariums with lower plant mass and nutrient demand. As plants mature and nutrient requirements grow, APT 3 provide a more complete solutions with added nitrate and phosphate to support continued growth and demand. APT 1 Zero Highlights - Ideal for new aquascapes, Iwagumi layouts or lightly planted tanks, and aquariums that contain more fish and fewer plants - Nitrate and phosphate-free formula - Easy daily dosing with included calibrated pump - Looking for a stronger formula? Upgrade to APT 3! Size: 300ml / 10.14FL Oz. Dosing Instructions: Add 3 pumps per 26 gallons of water daily. Perform a 30-50% weekly water change. TIP! If you are starting off with a fresh aquascape or have a densely planted setup, start with APT 1 during the first 1-3 months. Monitor growth over time and when plants are mature and nutrient requirements increase, transition to APT 3 to support continued growth! APT Fix by 2HR Aquarist is a targeted algae treatment for planted aquariums! And from our experience, it’s one of the most effective (but gentle) solutions when you’re dealing with an algae bloom that’s grown beyond manual removal or natural control methods. Its fast-acting formula works directly on affected areas and biodegrades completely after treatment. APT Fix is especially effective against dreaded Black Beard Algae (BBA), BGA, Staghorn, and filmanentous types like green hair, fuzz, and string algae. Each bottle includes a spot-dosing pipette for precise and easy application to affected areas. When used as directed, APT Fix is safe for most freshwater fish and shrimp. APT Fix in action in our UNS 45U Iwagumi planted aquarium, showing targeted treatment of problem algae: APT Fix Highlights - Copper-free! Safe for fish and shrimp when used as directed - Fast-acting treatment for common aquarium algae - Gently biodegrades and will not disrupt aquarium cycle Size: 300ml / 10.14FL Oz. Dosing Instructions: Spot dose affected areas. Use up to 1ml per 2.5 Gallons TIP! Start with half the recommended dosage for 3–7 days before increasing if needed. When spot dosing plants, temporarily turn off filtration to stop flow. For hardscape treatment, partially drain the aquarium to expose affected areas before applying. After treatment, perform a water change to help maintain balance. Ingredients: 3% Epoxy Aldehydes

listings.description: Build Your Own Aquarium Kit - AIO Tank All-in-one aquariums simplify the process of building a beautiful planted aquarium by combining clean design with integrated filtration. Our Build Your Own Aquarium Kit - AIO Tank is designed for hobbyists who want a streamlined setup that reduces clutter while still offering the flexibility to create a fully customized aquascape. With filtration already built into the aquarium, AIO tanks make it easier to focus on the creative side of the hobby. Whether you’re setting up your first planted aquarium or need a desktop-friendly scape, this kit walks you through essential components needed for a balanced, healthy tank from substrate and lighting to CO2 and equipment upgrades. Our curated selections are designed to work together, helping you create a planted aquarium that’s clean and compatible from the start. New to planted aquariums? AIO tanks are one of the easiest ways to start, thanks to their integrated filtration and simple setup process.

Staurogyne repens “Variegated” is a variation of the classic S. repens that features bright green leaves marbled with cream and white hues. Its compact growth under higher lighting and signature foliage add contrast and bushy texture to midground areas of a planted aquarium. Like the standard form, this aquatic plant grows low and gradually forms dense groups when regularly trimmed and replanted. With good lighting and stable water conditions, S. repens is a fantastic choice for creating a natural transition between carpeting plants like Monte Carlo or dwarf hairgrass and taller background plants in planted aquariums. While generally considered an approachable plant to grow, variegated forms tend to develop more slowly due to reduced chlorophyll. Start with medium lighting levels, dose a complete aquarium plant fertilizer, and inject CO2 to encourage healthier, more compact growth. In setups where lighting is too low, the plant may become leggy, indicating that light levels should be increased. Pairs Well With - Fine-textured carpeting plants to contrast its broader, variegated leaves - Stone-based hardscape layouts like Seiryu Stone or Iwagumi aquascapes where its compact growth can form bushy groups along the base

Hydrocotyle tripartita ‘Mini’ Variegated is a variation of the classic form, featuring the same clover-shaped leaves accented with subtle cream and white tones along the edges. This added contrast brings a lighter, more delicate look while maintaining a similar growth habit to the original. Often used in the midground, this plant spreads through runners, forming bushy clusters with occasional trailing vines as it continues to grow. The variegated foliage stands out against darker green plants and contrasts beautifully with stone or driftwood! Hydrocotyle tripartita ‘Mini’ Variegated is slightly more sensitive than the standard form due to reduced chlorophyll, making stable conditions more important for long-term health. Provide medium to high lighting, CO₂ injection, and regular fertilization. With proper care, it will grow slowly and steadily. In lower light conditions, growth may become sparse or the plant may revert to its original coloration. Propagation is simple. Cut along the stem and replant into the substrate to encourage fuller coverage. Pairs Well With - Ornamental, standout plant for the midground area of planted aquariums - Filling in negative space with vining growth behavior and variegated color - Variegated plant species for mixed-toned planted setups

Star Wood Driftwood is a natural hardscape option for planted aquariums. Its long, straight branches with pointed tips create a more structured, minimalist look. With similarities to Manzanita and Spider Wood, it offers a nice balance of texture and neutral color, making it a great choice for wood-focused layouts while still being easy to work with. Its more predictable shape makes it ideal for center or triangular layouts with sloped substrate. Whether used on its own or combined with stone, Star Wood gives you a clean, organic look that works well for nature-style aquascaping. Pair it with a lush foreground or your own mix of aquarium sand and gravel, then finish it off with your favorite rhizome plants! Best For - Aquascapes that need structured flow or straighter branching - Attaching rhizome plants like Anubias, Bucephalandra, and moss Star Wood Highlights - Similarities to Manzanita and Spider Wood in texture, color and shape with straighter branches, making it easier to work with when creating a driftwood focused aquascape layout - Available in three sizes, making it ideal for standard aquarium sizes and larger What to Expect Each piece of Star Wood is unique in shape, branching, and orientation. Natural variations in size, structure and color should be expected. Pieces are selected by size category, but no two will be identical. This wood is naturally buoyant and will float when first introduced. Allow time for it to become fully waterlogged, or use hardscape, stones, or weights to hold it in place during the initial fill. Driftwood will also release tannins that tint the water, and a harmless white biofilm may develop during the first few weeks. Both are natural and temporary, and some fish and shrimp will happily graze! Alternatively, it can be removed with a soft-bristle brush and removed during routine maintenance. For a complete guide on preparing and managing driftwood, please refer to the section below. SIZE DIMENSIONS Small 16-19” Medium 19-24” Large 24-28”+

Echinodorus grandiflorus, also known as Giant Sword Plant or Burhead, is one of the largest Amazon Sword plants known for its broad green leaves and impressive size. Given the right conditions, it can grow exceptionally tall, making it best for large planted aquariums, ponds, or similar setups where its leaves can naturally extend above the waterline. This plant is very hardy and adaptable, making it suitable for aquarists of all experience and skill levels. Like other Echinodorus species, it is a heavy root feeder and benefits from a nutrient-rich substrate or regular root tab supplementation. Bright lighting and warmer temperatures will encourage faster growth and fuller development. Due to its eventual size, Echinodorus grandiflorus works best as a background or centerpiece plant in larger planted aquariums. Its large leaves help create a lush, natural look while also providing cover and shade for fish and shrimp. Once established, this Sword plant grows steadily and may require occasional trimming to help manage its size.

Echinodorus cordifolius ‘Marble Queen’, AKA Marble Queen Sword, is a large aquatic plant known for its marbled leaves. Its primary light-green color displays a mix of green and cream tones to add pops of contrast and texture to planted aquariums. Like other Echinodorus, this plant will grow large over time, making it best for larger aquariums, ponds, or open-top setups where it has room to spread out and fully develop. As it matures, it can easily become a focal species or centerpiece plant. Marble Queen is relatively easy to care for and adapts well to a range of aquarium conditions, making it an ideal introductory aquatic plant. It prefers nutritious substrate and benefits from regular root feeding due to its extensive root system. It's worth it to note that Sword plants produce large leaves and can shade surrounding plants if left untrimmed. Overall, Echinodorus cordifolius ‘Marble Queen’ is a hardy, statement aquarium plant that adds vibrant foliage and natural coverage to larger planted aquariums. Plant Care & Information

Available in a selection of popular UNS aquarium sizes, these limited edition tanks offer the same high-quality rimless construction in a unique presentation designed for modern planted aquariums. listings.commonName: UNS Substrate System - Soil, Sand & Base (Brown)
listings.description: The UNS Substrate System combines planted aquarium substrates designed to create a reliable aquascape foundation and support healthy aquatic plant growth. This bundled system pairs UNS Controsoil, UNS Controsand, and UNS Controbase together in one streamlined setup for planted aquariums. The rich brown tone of Controsoil creates a softer, more earthy appearance compared to traditional black aquasoils and pairs especially well with warm-toned hardscape and nature-style layouts. Choose between select UNS Controsand options to customize the final look of your aquarium while maintaining a clean, functional substrate system beneath the surface. Configure Your System Choose Your Sand Select from Mojave or Pacifica to complement the look of your aquascape. Mojave offers a warmer, natural sand tone, while Pacifica creates bold contrast against vibrant aquatic plants. Choose Your Soil Granule Size - Extra Fine: Ideal for carpeting plants, nano tanks and detailed layouts - Fine: All-purpose and balanced for most planted aquariums - Normal: Larger granules are best for large tanks and plants such as Echinodorus or Vallisneria How It Works A complete layered blend! This substrate system is designed to be used in three layers: 1. Controbase (Bottom Layer) Provides essential nutrients to support root development and long-term plant health and consistent growth. 2. Controsoil (Middle Layer) Buffers water parameters while supplying an ideal base for aquatic plants to absorb nutrients and establish groups. 3. Controsand (Top Layer / Decorative) Adds texture and contrast to the layout. Separates planted and open areas within the aquascape. What’s Included - 1x 10L UNS Controsoil Brown (granule size varies by selection) - 1x 8L UNS Controsand (type varies by selection) - 1x 2L UNS Controbase This system simplifies substrate selection by combining compatible materials into a single, proven setup. It supports healthy plant growth while giving you flexibility to customize the aesthetic of your final layout. Best For - Planted aquariums with defined foreground and background zones - Aquascapes that combine sand paths with planted areas - Hobbyists looking for a balanced and reliable substrate foundation for planted aquariums Important Information: We recommend rinsing Controsand before use. Do not rinse Controsoil or Controbase! This substrate system is designed for freshwater planted aquariums.

The Full Red Albino Guppy (Poecilia reticulata) is a stunning guppy variety recognized by its luminous red coloration, flowing fins, and red-tinged eyes. This variety is a great choice for hobbyists who want colorful, active fish in a planted aquarium or peaceful community tank. Traditionally, female guppies are more subtle in color compared to males, but Full Red Albino females often show more noticeable color when compared to other popular guppy varieties. Overall, these active swimmers bring constant movement and color to aquarium setups. They're easy to care for and hard not to love. Full Red Albino Guppies are sold as pairs (1 male, 1 female) Guppy Highlights Vivid Full Red Coloration: Saturated red color spans much of the body, creating beautiful contrast against live aquatic plants and natural hardscape materials. Excellent for Planted & Community Fish Tanks: Peaceful and active, Full Red Albino Guppies pair well with other non-aggressive fish and are safe for planted aquariums. Guppies are active swimmers that spend much of their time near the upper levels of an aquarium. They may occasionally explore other areas of the tank, but are generally considered a top-level fish species. They are social fish and are best kept in groups whenever possible. They are also capable jumpers, so we recommend a lid or adequate plant coverage such as floating aquatic plants. Guppies coexist well with other peaceful tank mates. Mature shrimp are generally safe, but they may consume shrimp fry if the aquarium lacks coverage. Stocking Recommendations As a practical guideline, we recommend a minimum group size of 4–6 guppies per 10 gallons of water. Avoid overcrowding, as this can increase stress and make maintaining water quality more difficult. Feeding Guppies are omnivores and readily accept quality pellets, flakes, frozen and live foods. Feed only what they can consume in a few minutes and remove excess. Avoid overfeeding to help maintain water quality. Arrival & Acclimation For best results, introduce new fish into a mature, cycled aquarium. Take extra time to float bags and match temperature before release. Once they are in the aquarium or quarantine tank, give them time to settle in and avoid making significant changes or moving them during this period. Care & Compatibility Temperament: Peaceful Diet: Omnivore Group Size: 4 or more Important Information: If using tap water, always treat with a quality dechlorinator. Stable water conditions, regular maintenance, and appropriate stocking levels will help support long-term health and success. As with all live animals, natural variation in color, pattern, and size should be expected.

Bucephalandra Spathulifolia ‘Neo’ is a dreamy Bucephalandra variety that features heavily ruffled leaves, deep green (nearly black) coloration, and a subtle shimmer. As the plant matures, newer growth may display bronze, copper, or darker tones that contrast against established foliage. Its textured leaves and dense growth habit make it a fantastic option for adding detail to driftwood, stone, and other hardscape gaps. Like other Bucephalandra species, Spathulifolia ‘Neo’ is an epiphytic plant that grows from a rhizome. Over time, it’ll slowly attach to porous surfaces and develop into a dense, textured colony. Established Bucephalandra colonies are among our favorite features in a planted aquarium, creating incredible texture while providing natural shelter for shrimp and other small aquatic inhabitants. While Buce can be grown in high-tech planted aquariums, we find they grow much better in shaded conditions and require less maintenance.

Start by selecting your driftwood, then choose moss, attachment supplies, and optional rhizome plants to complete your piece. Treat algae growth on delicate plants such as aquatic mosses, liverworts (including Riccardia and Riccia), Vallisneria, and newly established plants with APT Fixlite by 2HR Aquarist. Its biodegradable formula is gentle and effective for targeting Black Beard Algae (BBA), BGA, Staghorn, and most hair, fuzz, and string algae. Each bottle includes a calibrated spot-dosing pipette for easy application to affected areas. When used as directed, APT Fixlite is safe for freshwater fish, shrimp, and sensitive planted aquariums. Best For Mosses and liverworts (Riccardia, Riccia, etc.) Vallisneria (Tape Grass) Newly planted aquariums Black Beard Algae (BBA), BGA, Staghorn, and most filamentous algae Product Highlights Copper-Free! Safe for freshwater fish and shrimp when used as directed Fast-Acting Formula Biodegradable! Breaks down naturally without disrupting an aquarium cycle Choosing the Right APT Algae Treatment Choose APT Fixlite if your aquarium contains young plants, mosses, or other species with delicate foliage. APT Fix is ideal for established planted aquariums with hardy or mature aquatic plants, algae growing primarily on hardscape, or more stubborn algae blooms that require a stronger treatment. Size: 300ml / 10.14FL Oz. Dosing Instructions: Spot dose affected areas. Use up to 1ml per 2.5 Gallons TIP! Start with targeted spot treatments rather than broad dosing whenever possible. Temporarily turn off filtration during application to maximize contact time before restoring normal water flow. Manual algae removal and routine water changes can help improve long-term results. Ingredients: 2.5% Carboxylic Acids

Grow a vibrant terrarium, paludarium, or wabi-kusa with APT Dew by 2HR Aquarist. Its specialized formula delivers nutrients directly through plant leaves to support healthy growth, vibrant coloration, and lush foliage for mosses, ferns, aquatic, and semi-aquatic plants. Based on 2HR Aquarist’s proven Capstone formula, APT Dew provides complete macro and micronutrient coverage in an ultra-fine mist that’s easy for plants to absorb. Each 300ml bottle includes a precision nano-mist sprayer for easy application and uniform coverage. Best For Terrariums, paludariums and wabi-kusa Mosses and liverworts Ferns Emergent aquatic and semi-aquatic plants Product Highlights Direct leaf absorption for fast, efficient nutrient uptake Balanced blend of essential macro and micronutrients Safe for fish, frogs, insects, isopods, snails, and other terrarium and paludarium livestock when used as directed Size: 300ml Instructions: Spray evenly over plant foliage 2-3 times per week. TIP! For best results, apply APT Dew to clean foliage and avoid spraying directly under intense lighting. Start with fewer applications and gradually increase the frequency based on your setup’s needs. Once established, consistent application will help maintain healthy growth and vibrant foliage. Replenish calcium and magnesium in your RO or RODI planted aquarium with APT SKY by 2HR Aquarist. This helps ensure even mineral distribution throughout the aquarium. A healthy colony of beneficial bacteria is essential for planted aquariums, helping the cycling process (nitrogen cycle), improving long-term stability, and creating a healthier environment for aquatic plants and livestock. APT Balance is a concentrated beneficial bacteria supplement that can be used to boost a new setup or maintain an established system. APT Balance contains a unique blend of resilient bacteria cultures designed specifically for planted aquariums using aquasoil, where lower pH conditions are common. If you’re starting a new aquarium or restoring balance after filter maintenance, tank resets, or large water changes, it helps establish the biological foundation that allows planted aquariums to flourish. Best For New planted aquariums Faster aquarium cycling Routine aquarium maintenance Maintaining beneficial bacteria after filter cleaning or large water changes Product Highlights Two specialized bacterial blends for cycling and ongoing biological maintenance Designed specifically for planted aquariums using aquasoil Suitable for pH range 5.5-9.5 Shelf stable for convenient room-temperature storage What's Included 24 total sachets (12 Sachet A + 12 Sachet B) Each sachet pair treats approximately 100L (26 gallons) and will span 3-12 months of use for a 100L aquarium, depending on dosing frequency. Instructions New Aquarium: Add 1 Sachet A and 1 Sachet B per 100L (26 gallons) of aquarium water. For smaller aquariums, use a proportional amount. Maintenance: Use one pair of sachets monthly, after filter cleaning, aquarium resets, adding new livestock, or whenever you need to improve or restore microbial balance. Turn off UV sterilizers for 24 hours after dosing. TIP! APT Balance is also a great addition after filter maintenance, large water changes, or introducing new livestock. Adding more than the recommended amount is safe, though excessive bacteria may temporarily cause cloudy water or a thin surface biofilm that will naturally clear as the aquarium stabilizes. Ingredients: Advanced bacterial cultures in dry powder form

If you have a paludarium, a live moss wall, or you're looking for something to reduce manual misting, it offers a simple, effective way to automate humidity and support a healthier growing environment. listings.commonName: UNS Nano Aquarium & Glass Lid Bundle
listings.description: Create your next aquascape with a matching UNS Nano Rimless Aquarium and Glass Lid. Whether you’re keeping jump-prone fish like bettas or simply want to reduce water evaporation, adding a glass lid is a practical solution that maintains the clean, rimless aesthetic. Commonly shortened to Ludwigia Meta, its dense whorls of narrow leaves create a layered appearance that’s hard to miss. Depending on lighting, CO2, water quality, and nutrient levels, new growth can develop shades of orange, pink, and deep red, easily becoming the focal point of an aquascape. Nearly identical in appearance to Ludwigia ‘Pantanal’, this aquarium stem plant is often easier to grow, making it a more approachable choice for many hobbyists. This large stem plant appreciates room to grow, rewarding successful cultivation with impressive size, color, and form. This colossal Crypt features long, puckered leaves that create graceful movement while providing natural cover for fish and other aquatic life. Its impressive size makes it an ideal background plant that adapts well to a wide range of freshwater conditions. A true aquatic species, Cryptocoryne aponogetifolia is a solid pick for biotope-inspired aquariums, large planted tanks, and natural ponds where it has room to grow.

Add height and organic movement to your aquascape with Cryptocoryne spiralis 'Nari'. Its long, slender leaves move gently with the current, creating a grass-like appearance that’s ideal for the midground or background of nature-inspired planted aquariums. 'Nari' is resilient once established. It grows well under low to moderate lighting and doesn't require CO2, making it an approachable choice for new hobbyists. After planting, it’s not uncommon for Cryptocoryne to experience “Crypt melt,” but don’t let that deter you. It’s a natural transition process that’s often less pronounced in mature, stable planted aquariums. Depending on the age of your aquarium and the type of substrate you're using, we recommend adding root tabs to support healthy root development and long-term growth.

Schismatoglottis prietoi offers the familiar look and hardiness of Anubias with a unique twist. Its soft, almond-shaped leaves feature lightly ruffled edges and form dense, low-growing clumps over time, making it an excellent addition to low-tech planted aquariums. Unlike Anubias, Schismatoglottis prietoi grows best when planted directly into aquarium substrate, where it develops an extensive root system and spreads naturally by runners. It grows well under low to medium lighting without requiring CO2, making it an approachable choice for hobbyists ready to branch out into rooted aquarium plants.

Add texture and earthy color to your planted aquarium with Bucephalandra Alamanda. Its broad, oval-shaped leaves feature gently rippled edges and develop shades of deep green, olive, and bronze. Like other Buce, Alamanda works well for filling gaps throughout a hardscape layout and offers an interesting alternative for hobbyists who enjoy the easy care of Anubias but want something different. New growth displays varying tones before maturing, creating subtle color variation within established groups. Bucephalandra can also be grown in humid terrariums and paludariums, making this versatile plant easy to incorporate into a range of planted setups.

Add dark foliage and prominent texture to your planted aquarium with Bucephalandra Dark Phantom. Its deep green leaves feature noticeably rippled edges, creating a bolder shape than smoother-leaved Buce varieties. Dark Phantom is a great choice for adding contrast throughout driftwood and stone layouts, especially alongside brighter green plants, mosses, or groups of smaller-leaved Buce. Low to moderate lighting is suitable, while CO2 injection, good circulation, and regular fertilization can support healthy growth and stronger coloration.

Create contrast against bright green plants with the deep tones of Bucephalandra Dark Velvet. Its elongated leaves feature rippled edges and dark blue-green coloration with a subtle sheen that gives the foliage an almost velvety appearance under certain aquarium lighting. Use Dark Velvet throughout the midground, tuck it between stones and driftwood, or mix it with brighter Buce varieties to create variation in color and leaf shape. Its narrow, textured foliage is especially useful for adding detail to hardscape without taking up too much visual space.

Add soft, jewel-toned colors to your planted aquarium with Bucephalandra Maestro Blue. Its longer leaves help fill gaps in hardscape layouts while wavy edges add extra visual interest. Grow a colony throughout the midground or mix it with other Buce varieties for a combination of colors, shapes, and textures. Low to moderate light levels along with good flow are sufficient for healthy growth, but regular fertilization and CO2 injection can help improve growth rate and overall health. Like many Bucephalandra, Maestro Blue can display an iridescent sheen under the right lighting. While intense light isn’t necessary, a quality RGB aquarium light can help emphasize subtle blue, green, and jewel-like tones.

Looking for a compact Buce to fill the smaller spaces in your aquascape? Bucephalandra Pandora Queen features short, rounded leaves that grow into dense clusters of glossy green foliage. Its petite proportions make it especially useful for adding detail without covering up the hardscape around it. Tuck it into areas between stones, crevices in driftwood, or group several plants together to fill larger gaps. Its compact growth and chubby leaves work especially in nano aquariums where larger varieties can quickly outgrow the layout or disrupt scale.

Add deep, darker tones to your planted aquarium. With reddish undersides and broader leaves, Bucephalandra Red Central offers a bolder look compared to smaller, thinner-leaved Buce varieties. Use Buce Red Central in the midground area of an aquascape where its darker foliage can break up groups of brighter green plants and add variation throughout the layout. Its dense growth habit also works well for filling in open spaces where its subtle hints of color can be appreciated viewed up close. Like other Bucephalandra, Red Central grows slowly. This makes it easy to maintain and ideal for low to moderately lit planted aquariums. To boost growth rate and bring out better colors, inject CO2 and use RGB lighting.

Plant your driftwood-focused aquascape with Bucephalandra Hades. This moody Buce features broad, teardrop-shaped leaves with deep green and blue-green tones that vary as the foliage matures. We find its darker foliage pairs especially well with knotted wood bases, forest-inspired aquascapes, and dense jungle-style layouts. Tuck Hades into crevices throughout the hardscape or grow several together to create darker pockets that contrast against mosses, ferns, and colorful livestock. Hades is a slow-growing rhizome plant, making it manageable and well suited for low-tech planted aquariums and beginners as well. If you’re looking for a statement plant with the hardiness and easy care of other popular rhizome plants, this is a great pick.

Keep your aquarium glass clean and streak-free with the Chihiros Double-Sided Tank Cleaning Cloth. Designed specifically for aquarium maintenance, this reusable cleaning towel pairs soft deer suede with absorbent microfiber for two different cleaning tasks. The fine, flexible texture of deer suede gently wipes away fingerprints, water spots, and buildup and maintains its softness through repeated wetting and drying, while the microfiber side quickly absorbs water and spills. The cloth is compact enough to keep with your aquascaping tools while providing plenty of surface area for everyday maintenance tasks. Use it to wipe down aquarium glass, then flip it over to absorb spills after a water change. A convenient tool to keep on hand for any aquarium hobbyist!
